MOO_KitchenGnoll ' Barnabus' is a gnoll who works in the kitchen in Moonrise Towers during Act Two . “ *Soft hoot.* „ — 'Barnabus' Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Barnabus' and his fellow gnolls, 'Timothy' and 'Tomelia' , work in Moonrise Towers' kitchens, being trained against their vicious nature by Linsella to speak and behave courteously. After seeing a demonstration of Linsella's abilities, her controlling connection over 'Barnabus' can be broken by passing a DC 16 Wisdom Check . The gnolls attack and kill Linsella, then attack the party unless another skill check is passed. Asking Linsella to have 'Barnabus' speak, then failing the DC 16 Wisdom Check results in 'Barnabus' dying from a heart attack. If the Dark Urge severs Linsella's control over 'Barnabus', he grovels to his "Lord", and he and the two other gnolls become allies. The gnolls aid the party's assault on Moonrise Towers if they were befriended and freed from Linsella's hold (if the Harpers are involved in the assault; otherwise, they do not appear). Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 2~5 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Piercing Bite a target. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ranged Attack ( )   –   Longbow Damage: 4~11 1d8 + 3 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Seething Fury ( ) Let the rage build within you. Once it overflows, you'll be able to attack multiple times per turn. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursMouth_StreetGossiper_000 UUID bfbf3129-2634-4304-bddd-07115f910c04 Stats Dwarf_Commoner ' Bigmouth' Thimsen is a Baldurian citizen in the Lower City during Act Three . “ Look - I don't want your wares, I don't want to donate to anything, I'm just chatting with my friend. Excuse yourself. „ — 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Bigmouth' Thimsen is chatting with Margolenn near the entrance of Forge of the Nine . While Margolenn enjoys buying copies of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette for the illustrations, Margolenn prefers to read the articles. If interacting with him, Thimsen informs the party that he is having a conflab with his friend, and to leave them be. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Read the gazette today yet, mate? Margolenn Yeah, this edition looked better than ever! 'Bigmouth' Thimsen ... Better than ever? With all the articles about cults and war? Margolenn Oh, right. Nah. I don't read any of the gazette. I like the pictures, me. 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Wait, if you don't read the gazette, how do you stay informed? Margolenn I don't. Don't see the point - staying informed seems super stressful. 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Hearing you say that stresses me out more than the gazette, mate. Margolenn So, I was looking at the pictures in the gazette today... 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Rather than reading the articles, yeah. You said. Margolenn Well, they were in the gazette. Saw their pictures and everything. 'Bigmouth' Thimsen You're right - apparently they're these hero types.  (If Baldur's Mouth publishes a positive article on the party) 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Oh, shit - you're right. The article about Absolutists ... Bad news.  (If Baldur's Mouth publishes a negative article on the party) Margolenn Yeah, they looked real mean in the broadsheet illustration. 'Bigmouth' Thimsen Read the gazette today yet, mate?  (If Enver Gortash is killed) Margolenn Yeah, this edition looked better than ever! 'Bigmouth' Thimsen ... What do you mean better than ever? It was all about Lord Gortash dying! Margolenn Oh, right. Nah, I don't read any of the gazette. I like the pictures, me. 'Bigmouth' Thimsen But how do you stay informed about stuff? Dying lords, new wars, anything? Margolenn I don't. Don't see the point - staying informed seems super stressful. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursGate_Civilian_011 UUID af704b06-6d69-41ae-9636-7b7ef043036c Stats Human_Commoner ' Grumpo' Daggles is in the Lower City waiting to enter the Upper City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ It's supposed to be safe past the gate - if they ever let anyone in. Bastards. „ — 'Grumpo' Daggles Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Grumpo' Daggles is standing with Phrennog near the entrance of Facemaker's Boutique . They were waiting in the queue to head toward the Upper City but left due to feeling unsettled. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Phrennog Can't you feel it? 'Grumpo' Daggles Feel what exactly? Phrennog That weird... something. I dunno - it's like a tingle in my spine I can't shake. 'Grumpo' Daggles You sure it's not a trapped nerve? Phrennog I am , thank you. Grumpo' Daggles So you stopped queueing because you felt funny? Phrennog I mean yes, mostly. Why did you stop queueing, then? 'Grumpo' Daggles I couldn't take standing in that godsforsaken line a moment longer. Felt like I was gonna faint. Phrennog Fair enough. And they'd probably chuck you in the river if you did. 'Grumpo' Daggles Probably. Oh, unless... Grumpo' Daggles Do you think we could swim into the Upper City? Through the river, I mean. Phrennog Maybe. I dunno how closely they watch it. But there's probably grates and things down there to keep trash like us out. 'Grumpo' Daggles Nah, you're right. And I'm not the best swimmer anyway. Gods know what else is down there and all. Phrennog What do you mean 'what else is down there'? 'Grumpo' Daggles I dunno. Magic, innit? I'm just saying maybe there's a reason for that weird feeling of yours. Phrennog So you believe me, then? ## 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla
- **来源**: ['Loose Lips' Cyrilla](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/'Loose_Lips'_Cyrilla)
- **分类**: Characters

Not to be confused with Cyrella 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla In-game Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Lara Sawalha Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Elf Subrace Wood elf Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 8 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 12 m (40 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Features Darkvision Can see in the dark up to a certain distance. Fey Ancestry Advantage on saving throws against being charmed ; can't be put to sleep by magic. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_LOW_GossipingServant_002 UUID 409eae4a-4de6-491b-a839-9ff1f3dbd7cc Stats Elf_Commoner 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla is an elven servant to Lady Jannath who can potentially be found in Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Cyrilla can only be found in the kitchen storage of Lady Jannath's Estate if Oskar Fevras was never rescued from Brem in Act One . She is then seen gossiping with Hargin Jooli . If Oskar Fevras was rescued, the manor is haunted and Cyrilla has been sent away on a temporary leave of absence at the request of Chamberlain Mercer . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hargin occasionally chats with Cyrilla: Hargin Jooli How much you reckon Lady Jannath'll make out of those nobles upstairs? 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Oh, I don't know. More than I can count on my fingers, that's for sure. Hargin Jooli Surprised she's not showing the big one, though. That'd fetch a pretty penny. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla It was Master Oskar's favourite. She'll never sell that one. Hargin Jooli She should cut her losses. He ain't never coming back. Hargin Jooli You met that hoity-toity woman upstairs? She kept whinging that her wine tasted funny... 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla No you didn't... did you? Go on, tell me what you did. Hargin Jooli Let's just say it had more in it than a few grapes. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Oh, you're filthy. I bet she still drank every drop. Hargin Jooli Still think Lady Jannath'll make you a lady's maid? 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Oh, I've given up. I've scrubbed, I've washed, I've polished - all for nothing. She doesn't notice me. Hargin Jooli I think you'd make a great lady's maid. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Stop. You're making me blush. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla How's life in the kitchens? Hargin Jooli Piece of cake. I just turn up and chop what I'm told to chop. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Like being back in the Guildhall, eh? Hargin Jooli Don't know what you're talking about. Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayDoomSayer_Onlooker5 UUID afa8079e-c681-4ba5-8cb5-d0fba570e23c Stats Human_Commoner ' Plumes' Fronkin is in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I saw a Steel Watcher rip some poor sod clean in two - I guess we need that sort of thing on our side, the way things are going. „ — 'Plumes' Fronkin Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Plumes' Fronkin stands in the plaza between Elfsong Tavern and Baldur's Mouth . He is listening to Augur Harxkellan's speech on the city's savior Lord Gortash . Fronkin does not join in with the crowd and appears to reluctantly support Gortash, stating: "I don't really agree with Lord Gortash's methods, but the man does get things done." If Gortash is defeated, Fronkin and the rest of the crowd disappear, and are not seen again. v t e Baldur's Mouth Characters Flaming Fists Ernestus Glenvora Jerbold Guards Baalfe Hertvor Dremble Inocente Bramm Unilda Tiro Vlomina Wulf Outside Augur Harxkellan Bliggerillo Flant Borlley Flo Hurlburl Frothilda Frunilla Grent Grintly 'Gunny' Sacko Korrinna Koreena Juxon Lockhorn Lolo Fuzzletoes Manzarde Muttonchops Dorryss Phyria Gollus 'Plumes' Fronkin Sadar Illanov Trina Wuloona Dor Staff Bronte Delcan Ettvard Needle Falael Glimmer Whistleborn Jarlath Jelliwig Malek Stones Salene Freig Syril Valdemar Ty Willowbrook Zita Locations Newsroom Basement Quests Stop the Presses

Technical UID S_LOW_BloomridgeGhostWatch_Civilian2 UUID 98e8b486-cdfb-4821-a2c2-52a8011612fc Stats Halfling_Commoner ' Suspicious' Foont is a halfling civilian attempting to hunt ghosts in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Stand back! I can't have laymen disrupting the ephemeral intricacies of the spirit field! „ — 'Suspicious' Foont Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Foont is on the path to the House of Grief leading Kydden , Gor Falogen , and Gaff Garsem on a hunt for ghosts using a strange assortment of items. The group are completely oblivious to an entire house full of haunted spirits in Lady Jannath's Estate just behind them, if the ⁠ Free the Artist quest is active. Foont's attitude towards the party likely changes, depending on the outcome of the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Suspicious' Foont Gentlemen, I am quite certain that we are almost upon this most nefarious spirit! Gaff Garsem How, uh, how can you tell? 'Suspicious' Foont Can't you feel rich, unctuous gouts of necromantic energy simply coursing through the spirit field? Gaff Garsem Uh... I don't think so...? Gor Falogen That's because there's nothing here to feel. This is a colossal waste of time. Kydden I feel something! 'Suspicious' Foont Yes, my friend? What do you feel? Kydden My ears are cold! What does that mean? 'Suspicious' Foont Well, some spirits do communicate in a rather obtuse manner. 'Suspicious' Foont It could be inviting you to listen to the tale of its plight! 'Suspicious' Foont A sepulchral beckoning from beyond the veil! Gor Falogen Or his ears could just be cold. 'Suspicious' Foont Exercise caution! We do not yet know whether this spirit is malevolent or benign! Kydden Oh gods, what if it is malevolent? What if it's out to get us? 'Suspicious' Foont Worry not! I am well equipped to protect us in that eventuality. Gor Falogen You think that wand from that charlatan at Devil's Fee is going to protect us? Gor Falogen If there was anything we needed protecting from... 'Suspicious' Foont One must be prepared at all times - an unfortunate demise awaits the hasty. Kydden It's going to kill us, isn't it? Gaff Garsem You know, I'm not sure ghost hunting is for me... 'Suspicious' Foont Now, now - I'm sure it's much more scared of us than we should be of it. Kydden I've seen a real ghost snap someone in half! Kydden It squeezed their guts out of their ears like an overfilled sausage! Kydden Well, my cousin saw a real ghost snap someone in half. But they got better. Gor Falogen Well, I'm very glad they got better. 'Suspicious' Foont Hush! Too much cacophonous chatter and we'll scare away our quarry. MOO_KitchenGnoll ' Timothy' is a gnoll who works in the kitchen in Moonrise Towers during Act Two . “ Clean up your mess, Timothy. That gnome was not for eating. „ — Linsella , to 'Timothy' Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Timothy' and his fellow gnolls, 'Barnabus' and 'Tomelia' , work in Moonrise Towers' kitchens under Linsella , being trained against their vicious nature to speak and behave courteously. The party can free them from her thrall by succeeding a DC 16 Wisdom Check . If the gnolls are freed from their mental servitude, they ally with the party during the assault on Moonrise Towers. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_WineFestivalCivilian001 UUID 3a893643-8e1f-4b14-ae7a-d0a8e868d5de Stats Halfling_Commoner ' Zinfandel' [ 1 ] Gorse is a halfling wine taster. He is at the Wine Festival at Highberry's Home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ Why, I think I should 'sample' several more glasses, don't you agree? „ — 'Zinfandel' Gorse Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gorse mingles among the patrons of the wine festival if the party began ⁠ Investigate the Murders and the wine festival takes place. After Dolor reveals himself and attempts to kill Cora Highberry , Gorse runs off and is not seen again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Gorse occasionally chats with Dave Hosmo and Jaycen Borgu . Dave Hosmo Quite the turnout, don't you think? 'Zinfandel' Gorse You should've seen the cheese festival last year. Jaycen Borgu The streets were packed. The stench was... potent. Jaycen Borgu This is a welcome distraction from all the war talk. Dave Hosmo No, we're being too lax right now. 'Zinfandel' Gorse What do you mean? Dave Hosmo Refugees, wine festivals, we're wasting our resources. 'Zinfandel' Gorse I can't help but notice you're drinking anyway, Dave. Dave Hosmo Well, if the wine's here already, I might as well drink it. 'Zinfandel' Gorse So you think they shouldn't bring any more wine? That right? Dave Hosmo I mean, I didn't say that... Jaycen Borgu I wish you hadn't said anything. Dave Hosmo I just think we shouldn't be letting our guard down. Jaycen Borgu Why not? It's good to relax. Dave Hosmo These refugees are killers, apparently. And they're everywhere. 'Zinfandel' Gorse The only killer around here is going to be your hangover tomorrow, Dave. Technical UID S_GOB_PainPriest UUID cad1854b-8f41-4038-b640-156ee0272f81 Stats GOB_PainPriest Trs. GOB_PainPriest Abdirak is a human servant of the Maiden of Pain, Loviatar . He is at the Bloodied Shrine in the Goblin Camp during Act One . “ Let the sting of pain wash away your pain! „ — Abdirak Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act One 2 Dialogue 2.1 Fail to hold back the pain 2.2 Cry out for mercy 2.3 Telling him to hit harder 2.4 Use monk training 2.5 Using bard skills 3 Companion approval 4 Combat 4.1 Attacks and actions 4.2 Loot 5 Related literature 6 Notes and References Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Abdirak resides inside the Shattered Sanctum next to the torture room. He offers peace and serenity through pain. If the interacting party member accepts, Abdirak strikes them several times. If the player character is the Dark Urge , unique dialogue options are also available, and Abdirak may show sympathy for their plight. Regardless, if he is pleased with their performance, he blesses them with the permanent bonus Loviatar's Love , and the following inspiration: ⁠ A Kiss Without Mercy ( Acolyte background) ⁠ The Art of Agony ( Entertainer background) The player character must endure three strikes and pass each performance roll three times, each intimidation roll three times, or fail each constitution roll three times. These must be of the same type, passing one of each or any other combination does not grant the blessing. If the interacting party member wishes to fail the Constitution rolls, they can poison themselves by eating rotten food (found in the room next door). If the participant removes their armour first, they are granted Ardent Apostle – a temporary condition which grants a +4 bonus to Performance and Intimidation checks. If a party member reads On Receiving Her Grace , found on the nearby table, this unlocks the dialogue option, "I saw your book. Let me try some of those techniques" . This allows the party to choose which tool – mace, knife, or axe – Abdirak uses, and change the damage type inflicted to ⁠ Bludgeoning , ⁠ Piercing , or ⁠ Slashing respectively. This can be used to reduce the damage taken. For example, selecting the axe option and casting Blade Ward or equipping the Amulet of the Unworthy [ 1 ] to gain Slashing resistance. If all three ritual weapons are taken away, he casts Bone Chill instead. Afterwards, if present Torturer Spike bullies Lookout Grush into going up to the wall. Abdirak chooses a dagger, but gives up after two swings when Grush does not follow the ritual. Abdirak moves to leave the sanctum the first time he is loaded in after the party kill the goblin leaders or successfully defeat Minthara at the Emerald Grove . He is not brought into combat if the party members fight the goblins near him, instead opting to walk away. During the fight he moves in front of a burrow contemplating that he is too big to fit to escape. He carries the Ritual Dagger and Ritual Axe on his person from the Bloodied Shrine. After leaving the Shattered Sanctum Abdirak, unlike most other fleeing characters, does not despawn for a very long time. It is possible to follow him all the way out of the goblin camp, through the bridge, until only a bit south from Blighted Village where dirt road turns to stone, where he finally vanishes. Dialogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Fail to hold back the pain [ edit section | visual editor ] Must be failed all three times. I can't take it... it's too much! (DC 10  ) Telling him to hit harder [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 2 ] [INTIMIDATION]  Come on. A child can hit harder than that. (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  You look tired. Should I take over? (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  Hit me as hard as you can - or I'll return the favour. (DC 5) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  More. (DC 10  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  MORE. (DC 10  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  MORE!  (DC 5  ) Use monk training [ edit section | visual editor ] Always results in failure, as the player character does not react to the pain as Abdirak desires. [ 2 ] [MONK]  Slow your breathing to attain silence, inside and out. [MONK]  Slow your heart and sink deeper into the stillness. [MONK]  Let the world recede. You neither hear the priest nor feel the blow. Using bard skills [ edit section | visual editor ] Requires no checks, automatically succeeds. CRE_Gith_Generic Raider Add'ath is a githyanki in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ If I need to speak to a creature like you, I will do so. Begone. „ — Add'ath Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Add’ath is near the main gate of Rosymorn Monastery , where he and Warrior Ith’dul shepherd three Absolutist cultists into the crèche for questioning. When one of the cultists, Corliss Undertump , tries to flee, Add’ath shoots her in the back. After this cutscene, Add’ath and Ith'dul move to guard the area near the Crèche Trading Post . If a party member speaks with Add'ath, he tells them they are lucky they were not caught by the crèche; otherwise, the captain would hold them for interrogation. If the party member is githyanki, Add’ath suggests reporting to the captain immediately because her patience wanes. He becomes hostile if the party returns to the crèche after fighting with Inquisitor W'wargaz. Technical UID S_HAG_MurderousFrog UUID 307a4abf-cecf-4755-88e1-a20b306fc3a8 Stats HAG_MurderFrog Variant 1 UID QUEST_HAG_MurderousFrog_EnragedForm UUID 6f30fa2a-cf72-48b2-8d7f-aa38b2ca4547 Stats Familiar_Frog The Addled Frog is a frog in the Sunlit Wetlands in Act One . “ Green. Leaves. Shallow. Water. Argh. „ — Addled Frog , going mad Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Using Speak with Animals reveals that the frog seems to be in a state of painful madness, somehow caused by the corruptive magic of Auntie Ethel . If the hag is dead or forced out of the area, the frog regains her sanity and leads the party to a hidden stash of items at X: 7 Y: 294 as a reward. Otherwise, the pouch can be identified by passing a passive DC 20 Perception Check . If pestered for too long, she becomes hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Mirror Image ( + ) Create 3 illusory duplicates of yourself to distract attackers. Each duplicate increases your   Armour Class by 3. Whenever you successfully evade an attack, one of the duplicates disappears. Range: Self Reflective Mucus ( ) Increases Armour Class by 2, and reflects the first projectile flying towards it back at the attacker, after which the mucus is removed. Range: Self Recharge: Per turn Venomous Discharge ( ) Damage: 8~29 3d8 + 5 ⁠ Poison Spit out a venomous substance and possibly   Poison those it hits. CON Save Range: 12 m (40 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] None Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] The Addled Frog has an unusually high Armour Class due to her Reflective Mucus passive and Mirror Image ability. While she only has one attack, Venomous Discharge is a powerful AoE that can strike multiple party members at once. The frog also frequently uses Jump to create distance. Additionally, the first ranged attack or spell that strikes the Addled Frog is reflected due to Reflective Mucus. Notably, all missiles from the first Magic Missile spell are reflected. Her Toxic Secretions can inflict Madness on characters who attack the frog. While the Addled Frog can be quite deadly, she has relatively low health , and is vulnerable to the Sleep spell. After the initial projectile is reflected, using Magic Missile likely kills the Addled Frog due to her low health. Additionally, her only high saving throw modifier is dexterity , so she almost always fails saving throws with other abilities. v t e Sunlit Wetlands / Putrid Bog Characters Hag Victims Blinded Elf Connor Vinderblad Demir Efrin Hammerborn Johl Lorin Magron Mayrina Mask of Regret Mask of Servitude Mask of Terror Mask of Vengeance Traders Auntie Ethel Other Addled Frog Ancient Mud Mephit Gandrel Redcap Redcap Blood Sage Sheep Wood Woad Young Mud Mephit Locations Decrepit Sanctuary / Druid Sanctuary Overgrown Tunnel Riverside Teahouse / Gnarled Teahouse Quests Find a Cure Investigate Kagha Get Help from Auntie Ethel Save Mayrina Save the Refugees The Pale Elf

Technical UID S_LOW_HagSurvivors_Adrielle UUID aa38af5c-9c75-4b2e-89e3-0cc1b995dbd6 Stats LOW_HagSurvivor_Adrielle Adrielle is a human cleric of Helm who is in Old Garlow's Place in the Lower City during Act Three . She is part of the Anti-Hag Support Group , a group of people who have survived encounters with hags . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon entering Old Garlow's Place, the party finds Adrielle and the other members of the Anti-Hag Support Group. Adrielle initially threatens the party, believing them to be agents of a hag. She must be persuaded to back down through dialogue checks; if successfully pacified, she explains that the group is being menaced by Auntie Ethel . Otherwise, she and the Anti-Hag Support group attack the party; at this point, hitting Jatlo causes him to revert to his true form, and the other hag survivors then become hostile towards him and allied towards the party. If Mayrina died in Act One , then Adrielle is the group leader and directs the party to search the building for a cursed doll that the Hag had sent to threaten them. Upon destroying the doll, Jatlo is revealed to be a Redcap spy working for Auntie Ethel and immediately engages the party in combat. If Mayrina survived Act One, then Adrielle refers to her as their leader. She explains that the hag somehow hexed Mayrina by turning her into a sheep, and the group is desperately trying to find a cure. Proceeding upstairs and destroying the cursed doll ends the curse and reveals Jatlo as a spy. After Jatlo is dealt with, either Adrielle or Mayrina directs the party to a nearby safe with instructions for creating Hag's Bane and rewards them with Staff of Interruption . This initiates ⁠ Avenge the Hag Survivors . Once the party kills Ethel, they can return to Adrielle or Mayrina to complete the quest and be rewarded with Fey Semblance Amulet . PLA_Tavern_Paladin Fist Recruit Aelis is a human cleric and a recruit of the Flaming Fist . She is on the Risen Road in Act One . “ Stop gawking and look for a way inside! „ — Aelis (Fist Recruit) Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Aelis is at Waukeen's Rest , struggling to get inside the burning inn together with her fellow Fists - Fist Recruit Ito , Fist Recruit Pavel and Fist Recruit Tristan , along with Gauntlet Yeva . They are trying to rescue Counsellor Florrick and Duke Ravengard who are said to be blocked inside the building. If a party member helps the Fists to unblock the front door, Aelis with the rest of the squad runs upstairs to the room where Florrick is trapped, and descends back after the counsellor’s fate is resolved. If Florrick survives, Aelis receives her orders (with the other Fists) to search for the kidnapped Duke and, after leaving the Inn, is never seen again. Technical UID S_LOW_FireWizard UUID 5a4f7f77-43c9-4f84-b3f4-4076d876ccde Stats LOW_Sewers_Dragonborn_Red_Evocation_Wizard Aelis Siryasius is in the Lower City Sewers of Baldur's Gate in Act Three . “ This is Sarin's final resting place- and a killing ground for all who would disturb her. „ — Aelis Siryasius Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act Three 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Allies 2.3 Encounter details 2.4 Tactics 3 Loot 4 Related literature 5 Speak with Dead 6 Notes and references Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Aelis Siryasius inhabits an area surrounded by Grease Elementals , Grease Mephits , and Greaseballs . Upon approaching Aelis' grease summons, he warns the party to halt and accuses them of working with the Cult of the Absolute . Over the course of a rambling speech, he reveals he was one of the "three finest thieves in Baldur's Gate" alongside Bareki and Sarin before the trio broke into Enver Gortash's office. In doing so, they discovered the secret plot of The Absolute and were hunted by Absolutists until they fled into the sewers. They became increasingly paranoid until Sarin believed that Aelis and Bareki "had gone strange" and hid the treasure they stole from Gortash. Convinced she was taken over by the Absolute, Bareki decapitated her and Aelis burned her until only her skeleton remained. Aelis' account of what happened to Sarin hints that Bareki has Sarin's Skull . Throughout the conversation, Aelis repeatedly addresses a nearby Grease Elemental as 'his cousin' and pauses as if he can hear it speaking. He eventually reveals that he summoned his elementals to bear witness to Sarin's funeral and act as fuel for the fire. This conversation eventually leads to several dialogue options: [INTIMIDATION]  Your paranoia already killed Sarin. Are you so keen to follow her? (DC 18) [PERSUASION]  I'm not a cultist. And I don't think your friend was, either. Your paranoia turned you against one another. (DC 18) [PERSUASION]  If you're a thief, then you answer to Nine-Fingers. We're allies. (DC 18)  (If siding with Nine-Fingers Keene during Aid the Underduke ) [DECEPTION]  You need witnesses- I'm a witness. Just here to pay my respects. (DC 18) [CLERIC] [RELIGION]  I'm sworn to a better god than the Absolute. Why not let me say a prayer? (DC 15) Attack If the interacting party member fails any check, Aelis attacks. If they pass any of the checks, Aelis allows safe passage and cannot be spoken to again. Talking him and his allies out of fighting earns 3340 experience. If the party later re-enters the sewers and approaches Sarin's skeleton, Aelis becomes hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Fireball ( + ) Damage: 8~48 8d6 ⁠ Fire Shoot a bright flame from your fingers that explodes upon contact, torching everything in the vicinity for 8d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fire Bolt ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Fire Hurl a mote of fire. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fly ( ) Fly to a target position Range: 18 m (60 ft) Invigorating Flame ( + ) Ignite the corpses of nearby grease elementals with revitalising flame, resurrecting them as lava elementals to fight beside you. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Quarterstaff +2 Damage: 3~8 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Scorching Ray ( + ) Damage: 6~36 2d6 ⁠ Fire + 2d6 ⁠ Fire + 2d6 ⁠ Fire Hurl 3 rays of fire. Each ray deals 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Greaseball x7 Grease Elemental x2 Grease Mephit x9 Encounter details [ edit section | visual editor ] Aelis can cast ⁠ Fire damage spells igniting the ground which is covered in Grease . He also can use Fly to reach better positions on the battle field. On balanced difficulty, Aelis summons numerous Mephits , which can cast Heat Metal . The Mephits are summoned out of sight and can fly , allowing them to rapidly reach the party, where they cause an explosion of AOE fire damage when killed. However, some of his grease summons are far enough away that they cannot immediately join the fight. All of the grease summons are vulnerable to fire. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Fire damage spells such as Scorching Ray , Fireball , and Wall of Fire ignite the Grease and damage all his allies, decimating the grease summons due to their fire vulnerability, though Aelis himself has resistance to fire damage. [ 1 ] Initiating combat with a summoned Fire Elemental causes the grease to ignite (removing the slip hazard and applying incidental burning damage), and appears to draw most of the aggression onto the Fire Elemental; Aelis focuses on flying around and attacking the Fire Elemental. Aelis may be difficult to approach due to the grease on the ground, his many allies, and his ability to Fly (class action) away from threats. Using spells like Misty Step , Dimension Door , or Grant Flight can make it easier to reach him. Who are you? Aelis Siryasius Aeris... the Turnkey Three... The 'Turnkey Three'? What's that? Aelis Siryasius Sarin... Bareki... me... no better... thieves... What happened to Bareki? Aelis Siryasius Said I lost... my mind... then lost... his voice... What happened here? Aelis Siryasius Cult... took Sarin's mind... so we... took her head... Did Sarin have a parasite in her head? A tadpole? Aelis Siryasius *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* What were you doing down here? Aelis Siryasius Hiding... loot... from cult... Where is this loot now? Aelis Siryasius Sarin... paranoid... hid it... away... Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_Bonecloak_FF_001 UUID b6d526d6-a592-4db9-bcfd-3d04d4fab7fe Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Ranger Fist Aggralix is a dwarven ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is in the streets of Lower City in Act Three . “ Wouldn't want her to catch me stumbling home from the tavern on a dark night. „ — Aggralix , on Fist Elthira Gossen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Aggralix patrols the streets of Lower City with Fist Karoline , Fist Elthira Gossen and a Steel Watcher . They are near the Bonecloak's Apothecary at X:  Y:  , where Elthira has detained Drongo Bixworth and Florean Bixworth and is interrogating them, accusing both of being agents of the Absolute . Aggralix does not take part in the discourse but, if spoken to, looks utterly fascinated by Elthira's manner of dealing with suspects. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Aggralix disappears from the game along with both her mates and the detained citizens. Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_FlamingFist_002 UUID 971f5890-e0ae-49ef-9a04-5e69ebdf8159 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Defender Fist Aguta is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is in Lower City in Act Three . “ Chances are the constable will throw you down the stairs, but go ahead, citizen. I could do with something to break the monotony. „ — Aguta , letting the party through Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Aguta together with Fist Rusk is standing watch inside the Elfsong Tavern , in its northwest corner. They guard the stairs leading to Belynne Stelmane's private room, stopping civilians from entering the scene of the Duke’s murder until constable Gauntlet Devella Fountainhead finishes the investigation. When approached by the party, Aguta reasons with her fellow Fist, allowing the party to proceed upstairs after Rusk tries to turn the party away, keeping to the letter of the rule. This dialogue is enacted every time the couple of guards remain at the tavern, unless Rusk is defeated. In this case, Aguta also lets the player character go, telling them she has no patience to talk after losing her partner. Aguta (along with Rusk, and under command of Gauntlet Devella, if they are alive) moves to the Highberry's Home , if the party allows the serial killer to murder Cora Highberry at the Wine Festival. She is then inside the house, guarding the crime scene while the constable is working on it. CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Raider Ahu'u'rag regularly patrols the hallways of Crèche Y'llek during Act One . “ Kith'rak Therezzyn needs results soon, or the Inquisitor will have all our necks. „ — Ahu'u'rag Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ahu'u'rag continuously paces the hallways of the crèche, on patrol. She expresses open disdain toward non-gith and request her kin volunteer to help Kith'rak Therezzyn . If the party becomes hostile to Therezzyn in her chambers, Ahu'u'rag often joins the fight as a result of her patrols. Ailis Belt Lady of Baldur's Gate In-game Model Portrait Voice / Actor Debbie Chazen Family Belt (family) Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Technical UID S_WYR_KillDirectorGortash_Patriar_003 UUID 059d0242-62c5-436f-93d7-fa2db6135a3a Stats Human_Commoner Lady Ailis Belt is a Lady of Baldur's Gate who is present for Gortash's ordination as the Archduke of the city. “ An historic day. The city's first Archduke. „ — Ailis Belt , on Ravengard appointing Gortash the Archduke Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony she sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lady Ailis moves to the southern nave of the Audience Hall and stands near the first table with refreshments. If spoken to, she simply praises Gortash as the city's first Archduke. If the party confronts Gortash, Lady Ailis is slaughtered later along with all other invited guests and their retinue in the Audience hall. Gortash also kills them if the party enters the Lower City and returns. WYR_Circus_Djinni Akabi is a djinni in Rivington during Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . He is a performer at the Circus of the Last Days in Rivington , located at X: -68 Y: -75 where he hosts a Spin the Wheel game. “ APPROACH, UGLY ONE. „ — Akabi , when he first greets the player character. Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Winning the jackpot 1.2 Jackpot "prize" 1.3 Inspiration 2 Consolation prizes 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Loot 4 Related literature 5 Notes and references Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] When approached, Akabi invites the party to participate and Spin the Wheel for 500 gold, [ 1 ] loudly promoting the allure of winning the jackpot. Akabi magically rigs his game, guaranteeing that participants only ever get an item from one of the sixteen consolation prizes of questionable value, unless the party manages to cheat the djinn himself. Winning the jackpot [ edit section | visual editor ] A successful DC 20 Perception Check reveals that Akabi is cheating, manipulating the wheel to ensure no one wins the jackpot. He denies any accusations, offering the interacting party member to simply spin again instead. If provoked, Akabi uses Careful What You Wish For on the talking party member, transforming them into a Cheese Wheel for 20 turns. Akabi refuses to let anyone play who has been transformed by him in this way, but other party members may still participate. To win the jackpot, a party member must pickpocket Akabi for his Djinni Ring , without which he cannot rig the game. Bards can also distract Akabi ( DC 15 Performance Check ) with either a joke or a well-timed fart and win the jackpot. However, stealing the ring or the Bard distraction permanently locks the party out of winning future consolation prizes. Jackpot "prize" [ edit section | visual editor ] Regardless of how the party member wins, Akabi becomes enraged and accuses them of cheating. He transports the talking party member, alone, to a Jungle in the distant land of Chult . This is the only way to reach this area and to obtain the items within, notably the trident Nyrulna and the ring Band of the Mystic Scoundrel . Therefore, it is recommended that the party member chosen to win Akabi's jackpot be capable of heavy combat and / or stealth, to survive in the jungle. If obtained earlier, one may also give Summon Us to the party member, so they can summon additional help. They should also be able to pick a lock on the chest that contains Nyrulna. Akabi permanently closes down the game if one character wins the jackpot, all characters are turned to cheese, or if all consolation prizes are claimed by spinning the wheel 16 times. It is not possible to obtain all 16 of the consolation prizes and the jackpot as he shuts down the game on the 16th spin. He does not award the jackpot on the final spin, if he still has his ring or the bard option is not used. Inspiration [ edit section | visual editor ] Winning Akabi's "game" earns the following inspirations: ⁠ A Grand Prize! ( Sage background) ⁠ Cheating the Cheater ( Charlatan background) Consolation prizes [ edit section | visual editor ] There are 16 possible consolation prizes from Akabi. Although some have utility, most are either useless or even harmful. +1 Breastplate , a normal Breastplate. The description text reveals it is simply named "+1 Breastplate." Bag of Moulding turns all inserted food into moldy and rotten versions. [ 2 ] Boots of Very Fast Blinking grants a per turn free casting of Misty Step as a Bonus Action , and is arguably the most useful of Akabi's 'prizes', except the character is stripped naked down to their underwear on every use, with the stripped articles of clothing left on the spot the user teleported from. [ 3 ] Comeback Handaxe , as of patch 5 it "comes back" to the party member who throws it, but hits them upon doing so. Eternal Carafe of Wine (Or Sometimes Acid) inflicts the Caustic Brine condition on its user, dealing damage. Magical Walnut contains five walnuts for a total of ⁠10 Camp Supplies . Reverse Rain Cloak makes the wearer permanently Wet while worn. The wearer also has any accumulated blood and dirt washed away upon equipping due to the Wet condition. Staff of a Mumbling Wizard , when equipped, gives the user a cantrip similar to Fire Bolt , except it does not scale with the caster's level and always deals 1d10 damage. It has a 5% chance of instead spawning a Fireball centered on the target with every use of the cantrip. Pairs well with the Reverse Rain Cloak. Unlucky Thief's Gloves provides a +2 bonus to Sleight of Hand checks, and adds a piece of Charcoal to the wearer's inventory for each item they steal; after stealing 20 times, the next steal adds a Burning Coal Bucket instead. [ 4 ] Pairs well with the Reverse Rain Cloak. The other possible prizes are miscellaneous items with no further function: Akabi's Old Lamp Definitely a Broom of Flying Gem of Restitution Lonely Left Boot of Elvenkind Mirror of Ageing Sharess' Caress Voucher The Other Hand of Vecna Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Conjure Elemental: Air Elemental ( + ) The air elemental can use   Primordial Gales ,   Gushing Air , and can   Shock your foes. Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_Inkeeper UUID 81651113-d779-44e8-9d46-d49d5577453b Stats HalfElf_Commoner Alan Alyth is the owner and bartender of the Elfsong Tavern in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate. “ Oi oi, pull up a seat - if you can find one to spare, that is! „ — Alan Alyth greeting the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can ask Alan about Duke Stelmane's murder and about whether he has a free room. Alan remarks that the murder has spooked off many potential customers and offers to let the party stay in the whole upstairs floor until the panic subdues and people realize there is nothing to worry about. Alan asks for a mere 200 gold for the party to use the whole floor, though he can also be persuaded to make the room available for free through dialogue ability checks: Fair point. Here's the money. (200) [PERSUASION]  You want 200 gold to sleep next to a murder scene? Really ? (DC 18  )  (if the party know that there was a murder) [PERSUASION]  If I'm staying in this place, I'll make sure to protect it. (DC 18) [PERCEPTION]  Point out the tavern's obvious dirt and grime- that should get you a discount.  (DC 18) [ROGUE] [DECEPTION]  I'm with the Guild. You'll be giving me the Nine-Finger discount. (DC 20) [BARD] [PERSUASION]  Cut the price, and I'll spread word of this place for miles around. (DC 18) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  NO. FOR FREE . (DC 18) [SORCERER] [INTIMIDATION]  I could wave my hand and turn this place into rubble. (DC 18) [WIZARD] [HISTORY]  Recite Elminster's journal entry about his free stay at the Elfsong Tavern.  (DC 18) Failing any of the checks results in Alan raising the price to 300 gold. If the party spends gold or uses an ability check, the Elfsong Tavern campsite becomes the permanent camp while the party is in the Lower City , replacing the waterside back alley camp. Obtaining the room awards the following inspirations : ⁠ For Once, a Warm Meal ( Outlander background) ⁠ Perks of the Trade if a rebate was gained ( Charlatan background) ⁠ Proper Lodging, Finally ( Urchin background) ⁠ Veteran's Hotspot ( Soldier background) Alan Alyth's attitude towards the party often changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses quest. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_BoyWithDog UUID ab5e67c3-f0f4-4234-b36d-0bfad1592d09 Stats Human_Child Albert is a child with his dog in the Steeps district of Lower City in Act Three . “ Mam's going to be steamin' if we don't get home by second lunch. „ — Albert Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Albert arrived in Bloomridge Park to walk his dog Sparky . However, he is no longer able to catch him, as Sparky is running nonstop through the park. Albert stands at the stone-paved clearing, occasionally calling for Sparky to heel, but he believes he cannot catch him to return home in time for tea. If a party member speaks with him, Albert laments his short legs in preventing him fro catching Sparky. He asks them to catch Sparky instead, although he doubts the capacities of short characters like halflings and gnomes . If Albert is still present in the park when the party encounters the Bhaal cultists' ambush, he might become one of their victims. Alexander Rainforest In-game Portrait Identity Male Voice / Actor Glen McCready Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Elf Subrace High elf Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 8 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 12 m (40 ft) Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Features Darkvision Can see in the dark up to a certain distance. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_AlexanderRainforest UUID 18fe60a8-7235-4450-ac5b-fcbf15bdae88 Stats Elf_Commoner Alexander Rainforest was a citizen of Baldur's Gate. He was working as an ombudsman in Grey Harbour Docks in Lower City . When the party reaches him in Act Three , Rainforest is already dead. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Alexander Rainforest's corpse is on the second floor of the Rainforest's Home at X: -93 Y: -109 . Notably, his corpse is missing a hand. Rainforest is a victim of the serial killer Dolor , who is murdering people to become an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal , the God of Murder. Alexander's name is listed alongside other planned victims in Bloodstained Parchment , where he is marked as Killed . If spoken to via Speak with Dead , Alexander's corpse reveals that he was investigating the ownership history of Candulhallow's Tombstones . To unveil the truth, he watched the place himself, hired Zhentarim agents, and eventually became so keen on the matter that he even stopped mingling with friends. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Bloodied Note Bloodstained Parchment Cheese Record Record of Ownership Tombstone Shop Notes Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Investigate the Murders Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Alexander Rainforest's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Alexander Rainforest Alexander... Where are you from? Alexander Rainforest Baldur's Docks... Born and bred... What was your job? Alexander Rainforest Docks... Ombudsman... What in the hells is an ombudsman? Alexander Rainforest Sort... problems... check... everything... What happened to you? Alexander Rainforest Murdered... obviously ... Who killed you? Alexander Rainforest He was... short... Dressed... in red... What were you doing when you died? Alexander Rainforest Investigating... odd... records... What odd records? Alexander Rainforest Tombstone... shop... No owner... Decades now... Which tombstone shop? Alexander Rainforest Old... Candulhallow's... Why were you killed? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* What was your killer's name? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Ratin Sesescor , the rat dwelling in Rainforest's Home , refers to Alexander as 'cheese-dropper', but feels no remorse about eating his Technical UID S_DEN_Bard UUID 4a405fba-3000-4c63-97e5-a8001ebb883c Stats DEN_Refugees_Tiefling_Bard Eqp. EQP_Unarmed_Lute Trs. DEN_Refugee Alfira is a tiefling bard in Baldur's Gate 3 . She is at the Emerald Grove on a cliff overlooking the ritual, trying to compose a song. “ Dance upon the stars tonight... Smile and pain will fade away... Words of mine will turn to ash... When you call the last light down... „ — Alfira , composing a ballad Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.1.1 Performing together 2.1.2 Encouraging with words 2.1.3 The Weeping Dawn 2.1.4 Not helping Alfira 2.1.5 Celebration in the camp 2.1.6 The Dark Urge 2.2 Act Two 2.3 Act Three 3 Speak with Dead 4 Related items 5 Related literature 6 Related quests 7 Idle banter 7.1 Act Three 8 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira is part of the group of tiefling refugees who were exiled from Elturel, and Bardic apprentice to a woman named Lihala. On the journey to the Emerald Grove, they were attacked by gnolls and Lihala was killed. Alfira has since been trying to compose a eulogy for her. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira is on the hill overlooking the druidic shrine circle at the Emerald Grove . She is frustrated over a lack of progress in composing a song for her recently deceased teacher, Lihala. A party member can choose to help by inspiring her. Performing together [ edit section | visual editor ] If a party member offers aid by performing with Alfira, they receive Lihala's lute and can attempt to play along with her: Alfira Dance upon the stars tonight... Smile and pain will fade away... [PERFORMANCE]  Play along with her.  (DC 15) Alfira Words of mine will turn to ash... When you call the last light down... [PERFORMANCE]  Keep time with her.  (DC 10) Succeeding both checks (one failure allows a retry) helps Alfira make significant progress in composing her song. The party member who helped her gains Musical Instruments proficiency, if they did not have it already. Bards are not required to make ability checks to assist her. Encouraging with words [ edit section | visual editor ] If a party member offers aid by encouraging Alfira with words, she becomes inspired and a cutscene plays where she performs her near-finished song for the party. This does not reward the musical instrument proficiency. The Weeping Dawn [ edit section | visual editor ] After helping her in either way, she titles her song The Weeping Dawn and confesses in tears she was with her teacher Lihala when they were ambushed by gnolls , and has been struggling to create a worthy eulogy for her. The party can also gain the ⁠ A Bard's Muse inspiration ( Entertainer background). Alfira remains in this location, giving her song the finishing touches and singing it periodically. Not helping Alfira [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character or their companions choose not to help, they may leave, convince her to give up, insult her, or steal / destroy her lute with the following options: Slip the lute into your pack. [DEXTERITY]  Snatch the lute out of her hands and smash it.  (DC 10) You want honesty? Give up - you don't have the makings of a bard. You're holding yourself back. Start over with a blank slate. Here. I don't have time for this. Celebration in the camp [ edit section | visual editor ] If Alfira is still alive after the party returns from the Goblin Camp , she moves to the other tieflings who are preparing to leave for the Campsite . At the celebration , she talks to Lakrissa and, if spoken with, offers to compose a song about the player character and their deeds. After the party, Alfira leaves with the other tieflings and moves to the Last Light Inn in Act Two . During ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove , Alfira's corpse is with those of the tiefling children in the Tiefling Hideout . The Dark Urge [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Dark Urge is chosen as Origin , after crossing the bridge to the Blighted Village , whether she has been spoken with or not, Alfira visits the camp once the party prepares to short or long rest. Regardless of the player character's choice to allow her to spend the night at camp or not, they wake up to find her disemboweled by their own hands, earning the ⁠ Snipping the Chords inspiration. They can decide whether or not to hide the evidence, embrace their handiwork (which causes Paladins to break their Oath) or be horrified by it. To keep Alfira alive, she must be knocked out in the Emerald Grove before taking the short or long rest that triggers her visit. If Alfira is already dead, knocked out, or otherwise unavailable immediately prior to the party's committing to a rest, she is replaced by the dragonborn bard Quil . This event may be delayed by others. For example, if Karlach is recruited before Wyll, his arrival takes precedence as the camp event that night; Quil then arrives the following night instead. To ensure her survival (especially in honour mode) it may be necessary to either knock out Alfira more than once, or resolve any cutscenes prior to crossing the bridge to the Blighted Village, which appears to be the trigger for this event. [ verify ] Going to Wakeen's Rest does not trigger the scene on long rest. In this case, when the long rest is completed and Alfira survives the night, she can later be met at the camp celebration and again in Act Two . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act Two , Alfira is inside the Last Light Inn sitting by the fire at X: -66 Y: 142 . If spoken to, she recounts being ambushed by cultists of the Absolute and that some of the tieflings were taken to Moonrise Towers . This starts the ⁠ Rescue the Tieflings quest. Giving a hopeful response awards the ⁠ A Smile Better Suits... inspiration ( Folk Hero background). If Lakrissa is saved along with the other tieflings, Alfira rewards the Potent Robe and other loot to the party. If she survives to the end of Act Two, Alfira moves to Moonrise Towers. A conversation reveals that she wants to use her music to help calm the tiefling children in the room with her. If the active character is a Bard, they can speak with her again to gain the Improved Bardic Inspiration (class action) class action; it is not necessary to perform the song. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If she survives to Act Three , Alfira journeys to the rooftop of Elfsong Tavern . Reuniting with her awards the following inspiration: ⁠ Finding her Stage ( Entertainer background) ⁠ Safeguarding the Songbird ( Folk Hero background) If Lakrissa survives as well, she waits tables at the Elfsong, and may occasionally appear on the roof with Alfira. The two of them reveal they are dating, and that Alfira is planning on opening a bardic school. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Below is the available dialogue if Alfira is killed in camp by the Dark Urge . Who are you? Alfira Alfira... apprentice... bard... Did you have any valuables? Alfira Lihala's lute ... where is... where... Where were you going? Alfira Elfsong Tavern... Baldur's Gate... Why the Elfsong Tavern? Alfira To perform there... to sing... for Lihala... Did you come here alone? Alfira With... Lihala... but... but... Who is Lihala? Alfira Teacher... friend... everything to me. But gnolls... ripped her... apart... You met gnolls? How did you survive? Alfira Run when they... shriek. They call... for others... Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Lihala's Lute looted / given while playing music with Alfira in the Druid Grove Potent Robe reward for successfully completing ⁠ Rescue the Tieflings Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Folksongs of Faerûn Letter from Alfira Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Rescue the Tieflings ⁠ Save the Refugees Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira can be met on the roof of the Elfsong Tavern in Act Three where she has idle conversations with Lakrissa . Alfira How's your shift going? Lakrissa A rich arsehole sent his drink back three times - so I spat in his last one. Alfira Lakrissa! Lakrissa He said it was 'delicious'. Alfira Rent is due soon. I was thinking I could do some busking? Lakrissa No need, I picked up some extra shifts. Alfira You didn't have to do that. Lakrissa I know - I wanted to. You just focus on your music. Alfira We made it, Lakrissa. Lakrissa Damn right - and not even pissy druids or cursed shadows could stop us. Alfira Only because I had you. Lakrissa Nah - you'd have been fine without me. But the company was welcome. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira may have originally been intended as a potential companion. In the game files, she is defined in Origins.lsx , which lists the origin characters as well as non-origin companions, hirelings, and a few related characters such as Losiir . In the file, she is listed with the Entertainer background and the College of Lore subclass. Since the release of patch 7, Alfira can be recruited as a temporary companion. However, per Larian's notes for this patch, she is only recruitable if the Dark Urge is chosen as origin and there is room for her in the active party. Alfira has the level progression of a generic NPC_Wizard and has less-than-complete functionality as a playable character. Known limitations include: Not having the Dip , Help , or Hide actions (cannot use Stealth or Pickpocket ) Reduced hit point increases Lacking Bard spells Having a much higher Intelligence than Charisma Mods or console commands are required to allow Alfira to become a permanent companion or grant her standard companion functionality – such as normal actions, hit point increases, and skills. Otherwise, she remains unable to function properly. When Alfira joins the party, she has the Tiefling race applied to her a second time, granting her an 18 m (60 ft) movement speed . Despite having the colouration of a Mephistopheles tiefling , Alfira (along with every other Tiefling refugee ) is labelled an Asmodeus tiefling . As part of the quality of life improvements in patch 6, which added the possibility of choosing which companion to dismiss while accepting a new one into the party, Alfira's game files seem to have gained some empty and unused dialogue lines related to being dismissed from the party. Alia Durinbold Lady of Baldur's Gate In-game Model Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Fiona Sheehan Family Durinbold Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Elf Subrace Wood elf Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 8 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 12 m (40 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Features Darkvision Can see in the dark up to a certain distance. Fey Ancestry Advantage on saving throws against being charmed ; can't be put to sleep by magic. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_WYR_KillDirectorGortash_Patriar_002 UUID e03365dc-cb4b-4e80-b2fd-311b09e6986d Stats Elf_Commoner Lady Alia Durinbold is a Lady of Baldur's Gate who is present for Enver Gortash's ordination as the Archduke of the city. “ Ravengard has not once failed this city. If he trusts Gortash, then so do I. „ — Alia Durinbold Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony she sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lady Alia stays near the throne, discussing with Rugger Shattershield and Ulder Ravengard the unition of the Flaming Fist and the Steel Watch , but not taking part in the conversation too much. If spoken to, she says that she trusts Gortash if Ulder Ravengard does, not knowing Ulder Ravengard has been suborned by a tadpole. If the party chooses to confront Gortash, Lady Durinbold is later slaughtered along with all other invited guests, as well as their retinue in the Audience hall. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Ulder Ravengard Let us be resolved. Today, we name Lord Enver Gortash as Archduke of Baldur's Gate . Rugger Shattershield Aye! Alia Durinbold Aye! Dillard Portyr ...Aye. Ulder Ravengard The Council is unanimous. Let our walls be girded with steel! Enver Gortash ... we identify all enemies within our walls and within our ranks ...  (Part of Gortash's monologue) Dillard Portyr Enemies within? Who do you mean? Enver Gortash Traitors, Portyr. Any who dares speak ill of Baldur's Gate or its people. Rugger Shattershield Pardon me saying, Archduke, but do the people require such a heavy hand? Enver Gortash The people demand it. Is a Baldurian truly free when he fears for his future? Rugger Shattershield And if the Steel Watch can't protect us? What then? Ulder Ravengard The Flaming Fist stand ready. With Gortash at the head, they can't fail. Alia Durinbold Ravengard - you would give up the Fist's command? Ulder Ravengard The Watch and the Fist must unite under one authority. Gortash is uniquely qualified for the endeavour. Ulder Ravengard Under Gortash, the two will conquer the cult army and preserve our city and our heritage. Alia Durinbold The Steel Watch is disabled, Gortash. How do you intend to protect this city?  (If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed) Enver Gortash Are you so lacking in imagination, Durinbold? Enver Gortash A hiccup, nothing more. It is not steel that strengthens us, friends. It is courage . Enver Gortash Our courage. The Flaming Fist's courage. They have guarded Baldur's Gate for more than a hundred summers and winters. Ulder Ravengard I stand with Gortash. I would trust no other. Technical UID S_LOW_NecromancyBuyer UUID d33d47b9-299e-4be3-8867-eaf53b200b46 Stats Elf_Commoner Alice Althea is an elven customer hoping to buy necromantic charms in the Sorcerous Sundries in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ Do you think that zombie looks... fresh? Is fresh good? I never know with zombies... „ — Alice Althea Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Alice is in the necromancy area of the Sorcerous Sundries listening to the pitch being made by Cordrane the Recent . Cordrane attempts to sell her some necromantic charms to summon a fresh, 'completely safe' zombie to perform various menial chores, which Alice claims are beneath her. Upon approaching them the first time, Cordrane casts Animate Dead: Zombie on the nearby corpse as a demonstration, which causes Alice to note the peculiar appearance of zombies. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Cordrane the Recent I can tell you're a discerning customer - you're after nothing but the best. Cordrane the Recent And luckily for you, that's exactly what I have - the best necromantic charms in the city or your money back! Cordrane the Recent Just think of the possibilities once you have a fresh, high-quality, completely safe zombie at your disposal. Alice Althea Gods, but it stinks! And it looks like somebody melted most of its flesh off. Alice Althea I'd be a laughing stock with that lumbering 'round after me. Cordrane the Recent Now, now - you and I both know that being undead takes a toll on a corpse. Cordrane the Recent We also do a range of fetching liveries and complimentary perfume spritzers - all seasonal, of course. Alice Althea Complimentary, you say? Alice Althea So what can it do? I've a lot of domestic tasks that are quite frankly beneath me. Cordrane the Recent Oh. they excel at all those humdrum menial chores. Cordrane the Recent They're particularly good at cleaning - especially food disposal. Cordrane the Recent They'll happily eat anything you put in front of them. Alice Althea It is rather a pain to clean up after dinner parties... Cordrane the Recent Word of warning, mind: make sure you empty them frequently. Cordrane the Recent Otherwise you might have a gut explosion on your hands. Cordrane the Recent ...And everywhere else, really. Alice Althea Empty them? How? Oh. You know what - I'm not sure I want to know. Cordrane the Recent They also make excellent low-cost bodyguards - and you can't be too careful with the way things are going. Alice Althea It looks a little fragile to me... Cordrane the Recent Nonsense! They're tougher than they look. Plus, even if they lose a limb, they keep on going. Cordrane the Recent I sold one to a wonderful old gent for property protection. Cordrane the Recent A trespasser chopped its arms off but it still chewed right through their ankles. Cordrane the Recent They won't be trespassing anywhere else in a hurry! Or walking at all, for that matter. Alice Althea I see... Cordrane the Recent One more thing: I recommend getting at least a couple of scrolls of Turn Undead just in case. Alice Althea Just in case what? Cordrane the Recent Just in case you happen to lose control of your shiny new servant. Alice Althea Oh. Does that happen very often? Cordrane the Recent Not very. But it might. Cordrane the Recent It's very much a case of summoner error when it does - not our spellwork. Cordrane the Recent Tell you what, I'll throw one in for free with your purchase - limited time offer. Alice Althea I... Technical UID S_LOW_AllandraGrey UUID 32d78583-07c6-4160-9ec7-3a24b15149c8 Stats Human_Cultist_Umberlee_FloodTide Eqp. EQP_UmberleePriest_Sickle_Magical Trs. LOW_Umberlee_Cleric Flood Tide Allandra Grey is the Flood Tide of the Water Queen's House temple in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate. “ You have done the Bitch Queen's house a great deed - I pray that when you die, your lungs are blessed with her salted kisses. „ — Allandra Grey , after the completion of Avenge the Drowned Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] As the party approaches the Water Queen's House, a chorus of singing can be heard coming from within. Allandra and her priestesses are holding a funeral for the fallen Holli Dylford , who was blessed with the "divine mercy" of drowning. After Allandra acknowledges the party's presence, she asks for an offering for the deceased. She appreciates any tribute given, though certain classes have special options: I've brought gold I've brought a prayer. I've brought my weapon to help avenge her death. [CLERIC]  I will pray to my god for her salvation. [CLERIC OF BAHAMUT]  I will pray that the Platinum Dragon's shining light guides her spirit. [CLERIC OF CORELLON LARETHIAN]  I will pray to the Elffather for her. [CLERIC OF EILISTRAEE]  I will pray that Eilistraee guides her final dance. [CLERIC OF GARL GLITTERGOLD]  I will pray that Garl Glittergold protects her soul in death. [CLERIC OF GRUUMSH]  I will pray that Gruumsh grants her vengeance eternal. [CLERIC OF HELM]  I will entreat Helm to keep her in his watchful gaze. [CLERIC OF ILMATER]  She will suffer no more in death - the Rack-Broken Lord will ensure that. [CLERIC OF KELEMVOR]  The Lord of the Dead will smooth her soul's passage - I will ensure it. [CLERIC OF LADUGUER]  I will ask for Laduguer's aid in her passing. [CLERIC OF LATHANDER]  My prayers will grant her the Morninglord's shining light. [CLERIC OF LOLTH]  The Queen of the Dark Seldarine will see her soul safely to the afterlife. [CLERIC OF MIELIKKI]  I will ask the Forest Queen to find a safe path for her soul. [CLERIC OF MORADIN]  I will pray for her in the Dwarffather's name. [CLERIC OF MYSTRA]  I will ensure the Weavemistress watches over her soul. [CLERIC OF OGHMA]  I will pray that her soul holds Oghma's wisdom in death. [CLERIC OF SELÛNE]  A simple prayer - that the Silver Lady's light guides her soul. [CLERIC OF SHAR]  I will ask the Lady of Loss to guide her into the night eternal. [CLERIC OF TALOS]  I pray she rests in the stormy waves of Talos' embrace. [CLERIC OF TEMPUS]  It sounds like she died in battle - I will pray for Tempus to guide her soul. [CLERIC OF TIAMAT]  Tiamat's unholy flame - may its light guide her in death. [CLERIC OF TYMORA]  Tymora's luck - may your fallen carry it into the afterlife. [CLERIC OF TYR]  Lord Tyr will intercede for your dead. [CLERIC OF VLAAKITH]  Your pathetic dead will bask in the glory of Vlaakith's prayer. [CLERIC OF YONDALLA]  An intercession from the Lady of Plenty. [MONK]  I wish her soul the stillness of a calmed ocean. [BARBARIAN]  ROAR. Offering a tribute grants the ⁠ Sea Memorial to party members with the Entertainer background. The party may then ask for more information on Holli's death, and can offer to help find the beast who killed her or, if resolved earlier, say that the matter has already been taken care of. Entering Allandra's room upstairs causes her and her priestesses to become hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Ice Storm ( + ) Damage: 6~40 2d8 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 4d6 ⁠ Cold Impel a storm of hail and ice to crash from the sky, covering the ground and striking all objects and creatures within range, dealing ⁠ Bludgeoning and ⁠ Cold damage. It also creates an   Ice surface that lasts 2 turns. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Wavemother's Sickle Damage: 6~12 1d4 + 4 ⁠ Slashing + 1d4 ⁠ Cold Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ray of Frost ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Cold Reduces the target's Movement Speed by 3 m / 10 ft. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Water Whip ( ) Damage: 3~30 3d10 ⁠ Bludgeoning Possibly pulls a target 9 m / 30 ft toward you or knocks it Prone . DEX Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Avenge the Drowned Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Pearl Pearl Necklace Starfish Water Wavemother's Sickle Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Allandra is holding a ceremony for Holli Dylford : Allandra Grey Sing, sisters! Sing in Umberlee's name! Allandra Grey Glorious Wavemother, pour fury upon the beast responsible for this injustice! Allandra Grey Furious and merciful Umberlee, hear our prayer! Allandra Grey Praise her for this most holy death! Allandra Grey Leave its master a bloated carcass in the spume! Allandra Grey Rejoice as the Wavemother welcomes another daughter to the Deep Wilds! Allandra Grey Know that we too shall gladly follow when our time has come! Allandra Grey Flood the world with your word! Subsume us utterly! Related Literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Address Book Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Concept art by Tan Bur-Ci Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Allandra's title, Flood Tide , is equivalent to High Priestess . Allandra and her priestesses are allied with the Sahuagin , who worship Umberlee , too. The Sahuagin fight with the priestesses against the party when the treasure pile under the temple is disturbed. According to a note in the Sword Coast Couriers address book, couriers must only be sent with Water Breathing potions on hand. v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag Support ## Amanita Szarr
- **来源**: [Amanita Szarr](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Amanita_Szarr)
- **分类**: Characters

Amanita Szarr Lady Incognita Full Name Amanita Szarr Family Cazador Szarr (Uncle) Fistula (Grandmother) [ 1 ] Dralia (Great-aunt) Blovart (Cousin) Donnela Szarr Occupation Writer Stats Race Vampire or Vampire Spawn Amanita Szarr , later known as Lady Incognita , was a prolific author on vampiric matters. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Although Amanita is not encountered in any playthrough, her personal journals are inside Cazador's Palace . According to these notes, she was brought to the palace at thirteen years old and introduced to the ballroom for the first time. [ 2 ] She was later transformed into a Vampire , but refused to participate in what she called the family rites . [ 3 ] In punishment she was imprisoned in the attic. [ 4 ] Amanita rejected the name of Amanita Szarr after her damnation. She renamed herself Lady Incognita , and elected to remain in the attic. [ 5 ] The party can read some of the books Amanita wrote under her new name. WYR_SharessCaress_Mamzell Mamzell Amira is the human proprietor of Sharess' Caress in Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Amira is the proprietor of Sharess' Caress in on the bottom floor, near the front entrance. If spoken with, she tells the interacting party member that they look like the type who needs “a sturdy dwarf, a leather whip. She gives - you receive.” Regardless of the response, she says that it is a shame, as her 'Stern Librarian' Ffion Goldgrind is out for the day. Selecting “Will this 'Stern Librarian’ of yours be back tomorrow?” results in Amira admitting she does not know and that Ffion has gone missing. Selecting “You need help. Let me find Ffion for you.” has Amira graciously accepting the help. She provides Sharess' Caress Rooms Key , the key to Elminster's Library - Ffion's pleasure room. After finding out what happened with Ffion, the party can tell Amira “I found Ffion's corpse. She's been murdered.” Amira is grateful for the information, but saddened at the loss of coin. Choosing “I’m sure you can spare a little something for me, at least” results in her offering a free experience with one of the drow twins, Nym or Sorn Orlith as payment (or a discount with both together). PLA_Corpse_Zhent Amnos , named in-game as Dead Caravan Agent , was a human merchant who died along the Risen Road during Act One , near the bloated hyenas . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Amnos' corpse is along the Risen Road near the bloated hyenas at X: 27 Y: 525 . Using Speak with Dead reveals that he was traveling with the Zhentarim shipment caravan when they were attacked by gnolls . Rugan fled north with the chest, leaving Amnos behind to his fate. Monster_Eagle The Ancient Giant Eagle is a type of beast creature in her nest atop the roof of the Rosymorn Monastery in Act One . “ INTRUDER! In MY NEST! This area was meant to be SAFE! Xavier, get behind mummy. „ — Ancient Giant Eagle , indignant over unbidden guests Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Ancient Giant Eagle is perched in her nest with her son Xavier wandering around the roof. If the party approaches without Speak with Animals and are spotted, Xavier and his mother immediately screech and prepare to attack, unless the talking party member passes an animal handling check: [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Turn away from the eagle as you approach, indicating that you are not interested in its nest.  (DC 18) If a party member has Speak with Animals active, the Ancient Giant Eagle calls them intruders and tells Xavier to get behind her. The talking party member can then attempt to persuade her that they are only interested in the big device behind her: [PERSUASION]  I'm just interested in the big device, I promise to not meddle with the nest. (DC 15) Passing either check allows the party to explore the entirety of the roof area without interruption. Otherwise, the eagles immediately become hostile and attack. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] If combat begins, the Ancient Giant Eagle uses Cry for Help , summoning between 3-5 additional Giant Eagles using Signalling Cry the following turn.
