Gold_Meager Art Cullagh is a Flaming Fist at Last Light Inn X: -67 Y: 167 abed, unresponsive, and singing about Thaniel during Act Two . “ Know that my heart is full and happy, and I am grateful for my last moments. Do visit some day. And if you have time to stop by an old Flaming Fist's grave, I know I'd love to see you. „ — Art Cullagh bids farewell Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Lift the Shadow Curse and Wake Art Cullagh Over 100 years ago, Grand Duke Eltan assigned Art Cullagh with the mission to investigate the Thorm family and Reithwin's House of Healing to determine whether a Sharran cult was being established in the town. However, once Ketheric Thorm unleashed the Shadow Curse , Art became trapped in the Shadowfell for an extended period of time, causing his mental condition to deteriorate. Prior to the party's arrival, Art wandered out of the Shadowfell and was cared for by the Harpers and Flaming Fists at the Last Light Inn . If the party rescued Florrick from the burning building in Waukeen's Rest , Fist J'ehlar is tending to Art's wounds. The party can attempt to speak with Art as he lies unconscious and sings about Thaniel . He remains unresponsive but bringing this information to Halsin progresses ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse and initiates ⁠ Wake Art Cullagh . Halsin determines that the party must retrieve Art's Battered Lute from the House of Healing and play its music to wake him up. If the Battered Lute is recovered from Malus Thorm and played for Art, he wakes and desperately asks for Halsin's help. Art explains that he met Thaniel in the Shadowfell and while he cannot pinpoint Thaniel's location, he recalls that it always "smelled of lavender" around him. This information allows the party to lift the Shadow Curse and grants the ⁠ Strings of Fate to party members with the Entertainer background. Alternatively, Art may die during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction if Isobel is kidnapped or killed. Similarly, if Art is left unconscious before freeing the Nightsong and initiating the raid on Moonrise Towers , he will be left for dead and alone in the Last Light Inn . However, the party can still cast Speak with Dead to ask him about Thaniel, which skips Wake Art Cullagh and allows the party to lift the Shadow Curse anyway. After the party complete ⁠ Defeat Ketheric Thorm , Art can be found in Ketheric's throne room alongside several other characters. He thanks the party profusely if they successfully removed the Shadow Curse, but laments that his health is now rapidly deteriorating since it was sustained by the Shadowfell. During the epilogue, the party can receive Letter from Art if the Shadow Curse was lifted. Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Battered Lute Flaming Fist Writ of Command Letter from Art Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse ⁠ Wake Art Cullagh Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Art's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Art Cullagh Art... Cullagh of... the Flaming Fist. What are you doing here? Art Cullagh Investigating... Ketheric Thorm. Rumors of... Sharran cult. Worse... than we thought. What can you tell me about Ketheric Thorm? Art Cullagh He is... brutal. Cares for nothing... except... his daughter... What happened to you? Art Cullagh Curse... darkness... pain. Thaniel... have to help... Thaniel.. Thaniel? Who is that? Art Cullagh Spirit... of the Land. In the... Shadowfell. Look for... lavender. He needs... he needs... What does Thaniel need? Art Cullagh Halsin . I'm looking for Thaniel. Where is he? Art Cullagh Shadowfell... shifts... and changes. HAV_Survivor Harper Arthus is a gruff [ 1 ] high half-elf barbarian and Harper in Act Two . [ 2 ] “ Hold there! You can't just land and start unloading strangers - there are procedures, damn it. „ — Arthus , after refugees arrive at Last Light Inn. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Arthus can only be encountered at Last Light Inn after freeing the ⁠ Wulbren and the ⁠ tieflings from Moonrise Towers Prison , and escaping with them by boat. [ 3 ] Arthus addresses the party upon their arrival. Arthus clearly expresses disapproval, [ 4 ] remarking that there are procedures for every new arrivals. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] He pulls out a Mind Flayer Tadpole in a jar and addresses the unloaded prison escapees, telling them to get in line as to check them for signs of illithid infections, to the prisoners' utter confusion. [ 7 ] Arthus then proceeds to walk and stand in front of each freed prisoner. After finding no signs of tadpoles within the escaped prisoners, Arthus lets them go and walks away, and then completely disappears from the game once he is out of range. ## Arves

Arves In-game Model Portrait Full Name Arves Silvermount Identity Male Voice / Actor Mark Noble Family Moyra (wife, deceased) Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Technical UID S_LOW_ConfusedMerchant UUID b24e02bf-8c2c-40f3-82af-dd4fb20b2e17 Stats Human_Commoner Arves Silvermount is a human who can be found found outside the House of Grief in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ There was a squirrel in the tree. Marvellous creature. Inquisitive and nut-crazed! „ — Arves Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Investigate the House of Grief Arves is a splendidly-dressed merchant with a profoundly absent mind. Speaking to him is one way to initiate the quest Investigate the House of Grief . Despite his apparent wealth, he does not remember any details about his own life. Using Detect Thoughts reveals, that his memories are scrambled, but that the name "Moyra" occasionally peeks through the mess. It is possible to pass a DC 20 Deception Check to take advantage of his condition and convince him to give the party some of his gold. Knowing about Moyra gives Advantage on this check. Arves initially came to the House of Grief out of mourning after the death of his wife Moyra. They in turn removed all his memories of her — and many more, it would seem. According to the Client List , this is because he was through Mapping of the Heart determined to have a " melancholy heart ". If interacting with the Mirror of Loss within the Cloister of Sombre Embrace , it is possible to become imbued with Arve's memory of his lost wife. However, speaking to Arves after acquiring his lost memory yields no new dialogue options. EQP_Longbow_Greatsword Trs. DEN_Refugee Asharak is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . He is a combat and weapons trainer for the children. “ Remember: you have teeth and claws! Use them. „ — Asharak , teaching the children to defend themselves Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Asharak is in the training area of The Hollow inside the Emerald Grove, training Ide , Gan , and Umi to fight near Wyll . Asharak asks the player character to inspire the children to fight. If Zevlor dies during Act One, Asharak is one of his possible replacements. If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving Kagha's ritual the Rite of Thorns , the tieflings are expelled from the Emerald Grove and Asharak's corpse is among the pile of refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . In the event that Minthara and her raiding party is primed to assault the Emerald Grove, Asharak is among the first line of defence atop the gate, alongside Arka , Elegis , and Zevlor. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Asharak survives the events at Emerald Grove, his murdered body is in the Shadow-Cursed Lands at X: -9 Y: 54 among the tiefling refugees who did not make it to Last Light Inn . Alfira's testimony reveals that he was caring for the children when the fighting stopped, and was tortured by the Absolutists with the removal of his tongue and eyes before he was eventually killed or succumbed to his wounds. Guex Yes sir! Asharak I'm not 'sir'. I was a doorjack in Elturel. Pandirna ' Yes sir'. Guex Shut it, you - and help me with these barrels. Asharak Remember - get down to the cave as soon as you hear the horn. Guex What happens if they attack before we get the signal? Asharak I reckon you'll hear something. Asharak Almost done? Pandirna Nearly. We've ransacked the packs for anything that'll burn. Asharak Good. Reckon we can brave a few nights without lamp-light if it means burning these buggers. If the Grove prepare for a goblin raid during Act One, Asharak reviews Kaldani's barricade: Asharak Torm spare me, that thing looks fearsome. Kaldani Is that good or bad? EQ_Astarion Astarion Ancunín is an Origin character and recruitable companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. He is a high elven rogue with the Charlatan background. Astarion can be first found west of the Nautiloid Wreck during Act One . A vampire spawn previously under the control of Cazador Szarr until being abducted by the Nautiloid , Astarion is set on exacting revenge upon Cazador and becoming free, no matter the consequences. “ Keep your distance, darling. „ — Astarion , using a frequent tagline Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Companion quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Leaving the party 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 Gameplay 3.1 Proficiencies 3.1.1 Equipment proficiencies 3.1.2 Save proficiencies 3.1.3 Skill proficiencies 3.2 Unlockable bonuses 4 History 4.1 Pre-Vampirism 4.2 Life as Cazador's Spawn 5 Involvement 5.1 Act One 5.2 Act Two 5.3 Act Three 5.4 Endings 5.4.1 Zombie Astarion 5.4.2 Life as a spawn vigilante 5.4.3 Life as a vampire spawn leader 5.4.4 Life as a vampire lord 5.4.5 Life remaining as Cazador's spawn 6 Quest Rewards 7 Interactions & Scenes 7.1 In-Party Interactions & Scenes 7.1.1 Act One 7.1.2 Act Two 7.1.3 Act Three 7.2 Camp Interactions & Scenes 7.2.1 Act One 7.2.2 Act Two 7.2.3 Act Three 7.3 Speak with Dead 7.4 NPC Interactions 7.4.1 Act One 7.4.2 Act Two 7.4.3 Act Three 8 Loot 9 Achievements 10 Gallery 11 Notes and references 12 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion prowled the night as a vampire spawn for two centuries in Baldur's Gate, enslaved by a sadistic vampire lord named Cazador Szarr until he was abducted by mind flayers on the Nautiloid. Although living on borrowed time due to being tadpoled, he can now walk in sunlight, wade through water, enter homes uninvited, and resist his master's compulsions. Astarion has a chance at a new life where he can make his own choices and possibly gain the freedom and safety he previously dared not even hope for. Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before he is recruited, Astarion is a level 1 rogue with the following Ability Scores : 8 STR, 17 DEX, 14 CON, 12 INT, 13 WIS, 10 CHA. If recruited, Astarion reverts to a level 1 rogue with the standard ability scores for that class . Upon reaching level three, he defaults to the Arcane Trickster subclass. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion receives the Happy condition after using his Vampire Bite on a humanoid. [ 2 ] While not strictly labelled in-game as such, Astarion is immune to conditions and effects that most undead are, such as Mummy Rot , yet thanks to the side-effects of his tadpole , he is also immune to spells that would normally affect undead, such as Daylight . Companion quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion's personal quest as a companion is ⁠ The Pale Elf . As an origin, his personal quest is ⁠ Call of the Blood . His personal quest spans all acts of the game. In it, he explores his newfound freedom, how he can keep it, and the consequences of doing so. He also can choose how to come to terms with the abuse inflicted on him – and the harm he has inflicted on others. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Recruitable in Act One . Astarion can be found standing on the southern loop of the circular road west of the crashed Nautiloid and northwest of the broken pier in the Wilderness . When approached, a scene plays where he feigns asking for help in defeating an Intellect Devourer . Afterwards, he can be asked to join the party. Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] Handing Astarion over to Gandrel in the Sunlit Wetlands , staking him when he attempts to bite the player character (but failing the Strength check), breaking Yurgir's contract instead of killing him (and then failing to convince Astarion to stay), or interrupting his attempt to hijack the Ritual of Profane Ascension (without successfully talking him down) results in Astarion permanently leaving the party. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Astarion/Approval Astarion Approves Astarion approves of displays of power, degradation, and cruelty, and appreciates sarcasm and wit. He approves of the player character gaining access to areas or information by deceiving others, or when they avoid combat through persuasion or deception. The player character does not have to be "evil" to gain his approval, however: he approves when the player character is understanding of his past, makes choices that help him, supports his independence and autonomy, and helps certain people or animals he is fond of. Astarion disapproves of displays that imply weakness, as well as acts of kindness or charity which offer no reward. He also disapproves when the player character makes choices which may restrict or deny his personal agency or autonomy. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] See main article: Astarion/Romance Astarion can be romanced by characters of any gender. His romance deals heavily with his personal character growth, his relationship with intimacy, reclaiming his autonomy, and navigation of his newly found freedom. Astarion's romance has sharply different outcomes depending on the choices made at the end of his companion quest. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion is a high elven vampire spawn who appears to be in his late 30s despite being centuries old. [ 3 ] He is approximately 5'11" tall, [ 4 ] with a medium build and sharp facial features. He has pale skin and red eyes, as well as smile lines and a faint mark on his left cheek. Jaw-length silver hair curls around his long, pointed ears. He has a bite-mark scar on the right side of his neck from when his old master, Cazador Szarr , turned him into a vampire, as well as a myriad of scars carved by Cazador covering most of his back. Astarion is very interested in his overall appearance. Favouring extravagant attire, he wears an elaborate doublet, leather chaps and embroidered leather shoes when recruited. He takes meticulous care to maintain and repair the clothing that he owns. He is very mindful of his hygiene, especially his hair, nails, skin, and clothing. Default animations in camp regularly show Astarion tending to his appearance. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion's personality is heavily influenced by his background and his time spent as a vampire spawn slave. He is charming, eloquent, cunning, witty, and practical. But, having felt abandoned by the world and its heroes for centuries, Astarion can also be bitter, self-centred, manipulative, distrustful, prejudiced, and vengeful. Driven by fear, Astarion believes the world is divided into a predator-or-prey binary, and as such follows a "dog-eat-dog" philosophy, where his goal is to be on top to avoid subjugation. His main priorities initially are his own autonomy, safety, and revenge on Cazador, though he also prioritises the party's safety as a whole as a means to these ends. He is largely apathetic toward the feelings of others and typically has little interest in helping for no reward, as he feels that if he did not get help (literally for centuries), no one else should. He also holds a grudge against the Gur people and, perceiving them as weak, has a prejudice against small races such as gnomes. Despite his confident bravado and arrogant persona, subsequent conversations with Astarion reveal actions and plans that are arguably fear-motivated and reflect low self-worth. Astarion seemingly revels in the physical [ 5 ] and is among the first companions to offer sexual relations with the player character of their own accord, but this is likely due to seeking favour with the player character, if for no other reason than to have their protection from Cazador and other powerful enemies. He believes charm, seduction and sexual prowess are effective and proven paths to not only these goals, [ 6 ] but also one of the few ways he knows to form relationships with others. Astarion is willing to go to great lengths to gain power or an advantage, especially if he perceives it as required to secure his safety and wrest himself from Cazador's control, even if this means harming others or doing things he otherwise finds distasteful. Yet, even with these goals, Astarion's past has fostered a great reluctance for sacrifices involving bodily autonomy, even if it means getting something greater in turn. [ 7 ] Despite his traumatic past, Astarion can, depending on how he is guided during his questline, be encouraged to re-evaluate his ethos and develop and change as a person. If Astarion's beliefs and fears are challenged, he begins to deconstruct his cynical worldview, show empathy towards others and try to make amends, letting himself trust others and form genuine bonds. Conversely, if Astarion is encouraged to pursue power at the cost of others and his callousness and arrogance remain uncontested, Astarion gains tremendous power and freedom from the shackles of vampirism while reinforcing his starting worldview, motivating him to pursue plans to take over the city and even the world. [ 8 ] Gameplay [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion's default class is rogue . His default high elven cantrip is Fire Bolt , but if selected as an origin character, the player can choose any high elf cantrip they wish. As a vampire spawn, he has access to a unique Vampire Bite . However, this action does not appear as a companion until after the party finds out about his vampirism. If played as origin, this ability becomes available after waking up from the Nautiloid crash. Astarion can be spoken to with Speak with Dead . Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons Hand Crossbows Light armour Longbows Longswords Rapiers Shortswords Save proficiencies Dexterity Intelligence Skill proficiencies Acrobatics Deception Perception Performance Persuasion Sleight of Hand (x2) Stealth (x2) Unlockable bonuses [ edit section | visual editor ] The following bonuses and actions can be unlocked through certain decisions in Astarion's companion quest: Ascendant Bite Misty Escape Vampire Ascendant History [ edit section | visual editor ] Pre-Vampirism [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion was a young nobleman [ 9 ] magistrate in Baldur's Gate , until one day he was assaulted and almost killed by a gang of Gur because of a ruling he had handed down. The vampire lord, Cazador Szarr , approached Astarion while he was dying and turned him into one of his slaves – a vampire spawn. Life as Cazador's Spawn [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion's "family" in a D&D Supplement After being turned, Astarion and his vampire spawn "siblings" lived at the Szarr Palace in the Upper City. Being vampire spawn, Astarion and his "siblings" were completely subservient to Cazador, shackled to him through the bond of creator and creation. Cazador used this power to completely control Astarion and the others, and he imposed three main commands onto his spawn: "Thou must not drink from thinking creatures," "Thou must never leave my side, unless commanded," "Thou must obey me in all things." Astarion and the other spawn could not physically refuse these commands. Cazador used this power and these "rules" to physically and emotionally abuse and torture Astarion for centuries. Any form of attempted resistance or escape was met with harsh punishment. For example, Astarion was once entombed, starving in total darkness for over a year because he had tried to disobey one of Cazador's commands. The abuse inflicted on Astarion and the other spawn was brutal and frequent. They were, amongst other things: Physically tortured (sometimes even being compelled to injure one another) and had "poetry" carved into their backs by Cazador. Frequently emotionally abused as Cazador played mind games on them. Fed dead rats and bugs and starved for long periods of time. Forced to venture out into the Lower City to seduce and engage in sexual activity with people in order to lure them back to Szarr Palace and saved for future feeding by Cazador. However, while out in a city tavern seducing a young noble to bring back to Cazador, Astarion was abducted by the rogue Nautiloid and tadpoled alongside other victims. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] See main article: The Pale Elf The Pale Elf is Astarion's personal quest. It is added to the journal upon recruiting him and spans all three acts of the game. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion begins the story in Act One on the ravaged beach by the crashed Nautiloid, where he beckons the player character over to assist him in fighting an Intellect Devourer nearby in the bushes. However, it quickly becomes apparent that it is just a Boar . Depending on the player character's Perception, Astarion either pulls a knife on the player or tackles them to the ground with his knife at their throat while they are distracted, believing the player character to be in league with the mind flayers on the ship, as he saw them walking freely and speaking with the mind flayers while he was tadpoled and trapped in a pod. Astarion demands answers about what happened on the ship from the player character, who can explain the reality of the situation to him. Regardless of the outcome, Astarion ultimately backs off, apologises, and introduces himself. If the player character attacks Astarion and kills him before the introductory cutscene and then revivifies him, a slightly different greeting (without knife-threatening) takes place. Afterwards, Astarion can be recruited as a party member, and his companion quest, ⁠ The Pale Elf , is added to the journal. A few nights into adventuring, the player character wakes from a long rest to Astarion, hunched over them and preparing to bite their neck. Caught in the act, Astarion stops and tries to explain himself, but the player character successfully deduces he is a vampire. If allowing Astarion to live after this reveal, he asks the player character if they are willing to let him drink some blood to gain his strength. If they refuse, he stalks off into the night to hunt for animals. If they acquiesce, Astarion lays the player character down and begins to drink blood from their neck. [ 10 ] Immersed in his hunger, Astarion must then be persuaded or shoved off to end his feeding. If unsuccessful, the player character dies and must be revived . If successful, Astarion stops feeding and thanks the player profusely for helping him. The morning following either the attempted or successful feeding, the player character can talk to Astarion about a variety of topics. He divulges his past, revealing that he is a vampire spawn sired by the vampire lord Cazador Szarr over 200 years prior in Baldur's Gate . It was then that he handed down a ruling as a magistrate that a group of local Gur people took issue with. They attacked and beat him until he was near death in the street. Cazador Szarr then approached, offering him a second chance at life, which Astarion took in a moment of desperation. Cazador then turned Astarion into his vampire spawn and slave. Astarion also explains how vampire spawn are subservient to the vampires who created them, having all of the weaknesses of a full vampire but few of their powers. Amongst them is hypersensitivity to the sun, which Astarion has not experienced since the Nautiloid crash. He speculates that the tadpole has given him immunity to the sunlight and Cazador's compulsion. During this conversation, the player character can also discuss how Astarion may feed in the future. They can either agree to let him feed on the player character, let him feed on humanoid enemies, or relegate him to feeding on animals. In the Sunlit Wetlands (or Putrid Bog ), the party can encounter a Gur monster hunter, Gandrel . If previously revealed as a vampire, Gandrel explains that he is looking for a vampire spawn named Astarion on behalf of his tribe, and Astarion becomes visibly agitated. He argues with and insults Gandrel, ready to kill him in an act of self-preservation. The player character can let Astarion reveal himself and attack Gandrel or encourage Astarion to let it go, sparing his life. If Astarion's vampiric nature has not been discovered, Gandrel does not mention Astarion by name and instead says that he is looking for a vampire spawn. Astarion may kill Gandrel unprompted in this scenario if he is not talked down while agitated. The player character can also turn Astarion in to Gandrel, thus making him leave the party permanently. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act Two, Astarion explores the markings carved into his back by Cazador long ago and ponders their meaning. If his approval with the player character is high enough, or he is romanced, he reveals the scars to them. The player character may identify them as Infernal markings. If they are not identified, Astarion eventually comes to this conclusion on his own by slowly feeling them out. Either way, he says that he wants to discuss the subject with Raphael , who may be able to explain the scars to him. When talking to Raphael at the Last Light Inn , Raphael points out Astarion [ 11 ] and says he senses he has something to talk to him about. Astarion then confirms this fact. If Astarion has not revealed his scars, Raphael uses infernal magic to bare Astarion from the waist up and forces him to show his scars before continuing the conversation about Astarion's request. If Astarion has already revealed his scars to the player character, Raphael instead proceeds to think about Astarion's request. Raphael says he believes he can help explain his scars, but needs to think of something that Astarion can do for him first. He then departs, leaving Astarion to wait until they meet again. Astarion and the party encounter Raphael again in front of the Grand Mausoleum , where Raphael may [ 12 ] state he has thought of a way for Astarion to pay him for his services. Raphael tasks Astarion and the party to kill an old enemy of his, the orthon Yurgir , and affirms that if they do this, he will interpret Astarion's Infernal scars. If Yurgir is defeated per Raphael's request, Raphael comes to the Campsite and explains Astarion's scars. He reveals they are a part of a contract Cazador Szarr made with Mephistopheles , binding Astarion to the Rite of Profane Ascension. It is through this ritual that Cazador must sacrifice the souls of all of his vampiric spawn, including Astarion, to ascend to a new type of being, the Vampire Ascendant. The Vampire Ascendant will gain a new set of powers and lose all vampiric weaknesses, including the sensitivity to sunlight. However, the rite cannot be performed if any of the carriers of the scars are missing, and so Cazador cannot complete it while Astarion is gone. Astarion then realises that Cazador will never stop hunting him, and asks the player character to join him in taking the fight to Cazador in Baldur's Gate. On the road to Baldur's Gate, Astarion ponders the options he believes he will have in the city. He tells the player character that if they are to find Cazador, they should first find his "siblings", Cazador's other vampiric spawn. He states they will likely be found in the taverns and flophouses of the city, looking for prey for Cazador as per his orders. Astarion also speculates about the possibility of usurping the Rite of Profane Ascension for himself to gain its power, rather than Cazador. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] In Rivington , Astarion and the party may encounter Ulma and the other members of the local Gur tribe. Ulma recognises Astarion and reveals him as one of the vampire spawn who stole their children away in the night under Cazador's orders. She offers Astarion a chance for redemption: save their children from Cazador's clutches and bring them home. Agreeing starts the quest ⁠ Investigate Cazador's Palace , while refusing has Ulma and the other members of the Gur tribe become hostile. Later, in Fraygo's Flophouse , Astarion encounters two of his "siblings", Dalyria and Petras . [ 13 ] They discuss Cazador's ritual, falsely believing it will set them free. Astarion interrupts, calls them foolish for believing Cazador's lies, and demands to know where the ritual will happen. Dalyria and Petras reveal it is happening in a secret defiled chapel underneath Cazador's Palace before returning to Cazador. Astarion then continues to ponder if he can usurp the ritual for himself. Upon reaching the Lower City , some of Astarion's other "siblings," Leon , Aurelia , Violet , and Yousen , come to the party's camp in the night to capture Astarion. Astarion attempts to sway them to his side by lying and saying that if he controls the ritual, they can all name him their new master, and they will be set free. The player character can intervene and reveal the truth, but either way, Cazador's compulsion takes control of the spawn, and they become hostile. If Astarion is downed in combat, he is taken to Cazador's Palace and must be rescued, while if the spawn are defeated, Astarion remains with the party and emphasises the need to find Cazador. After finding and entering Cazador's Palace through a side entrance protected by charmed guards, Astarion finds out that the ritual is already underway, and presumes the way to the ritual is via the ballroom. However, the ballroom is sealed by an Arcane Lock spell, which only opens if a key is inserted and a set of words is spoken to it. Astarion then concludes that Godey , one of Cazador's servants, has the key, and suggests the party find him along with something that will help the party discover the passphrase. After obtaining the Szarr Family Ring from Godey and the Kozakuran Dictionary from one of Cazador's guest rooms, Astarion and the party may proceed into the ballroom, where they encounter a multitude of lycanthropes , wolves , bats , and rats . The creatures are hostile, as they wish to turn in Astarion to Cazador to gain favour with him. After defeating them, Astarion and the party can proceed to Cazador's study, where they find a nearby lift. Having just defeated Cazador, Astarion weighs his options. Upon taking the lift, it descends into Cazador's Dungeon , which was kept secret from all in the palace, including Astarion. Here, Astarion and the party encounter a large number of prisoners held in cells. One prisoner, Sebastian , recognises Astarion and speaks up. He says he remembers Astarion luring him back to the palace, where he was then turned into a vampire spawn by Cazador alongside many others there. In another cell, Chessa , one of the Gur children, also recognises him and speaks of how Astarion and other spawn kidnapped them from their camp and brought them to the palace, where Cazador turned them into spawn. Astarion then identifies others in cells who bear his mark, previous victims he brought to Cazador (either through lure or capture), but thought of as long dead, as Cazador told them he was feeding on those they brought back. It is after meeting the prisoners and seeing how they are marked with the same Infernal runes that Astarion realises Cazador means to sacrifice not just him and his "siblings", but the 7,000 souls suborned to his command. He starts to fully understand the true scope of the Rite of Profane Ascension, as well as struggle with the implications of his previous plans to usurp the ritual. After two centuries of suffering, Astarion is finally free. After leaving the main part of the dungeon, Astarion and the party confront Cazador in his lair, where the ritual is being prepared. Cazador gains control of Astarion through blood magic during the confrontation, forcing him into the ritual, and combat begins. If not rescued, Cazador ascends, and Astarion's essence, bound by an Archdevil's Infernal Contract, is consumed (along with 7000 others), killing him. If saved, Astarion joins combat. If defeated, Cazador retreats to his sarcophagus to regenerate. Astarion then rips him away and confronts him once and for all. Here, the player character can either talk Astarion down from usurping the Rite of Profane Ascension or assist him in completing it for himself – either choice and its outcome complete ⁠ The Pale Elf . Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] Zombie Astarion [ edit section | visual editor ] If given to the Gur in Act One, killed by the player character without recruiting him, or not freed during the fight with Cazador, Astarion is transformed into a zombie with red skin, exposed bones, and all of his otherwise defining physical traits gone. [ 14 ] Life as a spawn vigilante [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion as a spawn vigilante If the party stopped the ritual peacefully by persuading him to be better than Cazador or by killing one or more trapped "siblings" during the battle, Astarion's sunlight vulnerability spontaneously returns a few minutes after defeating the Netherbrain, ending the hope that his immunity via the tadpole might be permanent. After quickly saying goodbye, he is forced to run and find shade as another companion calls out to him, although the narrator reassures the player character that he will be safe. Back to a normal vampire spawn, Astarion continues adventuring on his own as a nighttime assassin, but a heroic one who only kills "the right people" who deserve it. Instead of grieving over his inability to be in the sun, he develops a renewed sense of self, accepting the dark as a part of him and being driven by his newfound inspiration of hope rather than fear. If spawn Astarion is romanced, the player character can join him in his adventures and explore Faerûn together. At the reunion party, he happily encourages the player character to mingle with their old friends and check in on their well-being. He reaffirms to the player character that he loves them and will always be there for them. If origin Karlach romanced Astarion, he instead offers to join her in Avernus . If a spawn origin Astarion romanced Karlach, however, he cannot convince her to go to Avernus because he is forced to run away from the sunlight before her ending cutscene; she dies while Astarion adventures alone. Life as a vampire spawn leader [ edit section | visual editor ] If Astarion is romanced and the vampire spawn in the dungeon are released to the Underdark , he and the player character can instead choose to find the spawn and help them adjust to their new lives. Both of them act as leaders alongside Astarion's "siblings." Astarion can also become a vampire spawn leader alone and without the player character, though this requires the player character to suggest they find the spawn in the Underdark, then break up shortly after. Astarion then goes to the Underdark alone and acts as a leader for the vampire spawn. Life as a vampire lord [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion as a vampire lord If allowed to complete the ritual, Astarion takes over Szarr Palace as his own and becomes an ascended vampire lord, rising in status and power in Baldur's Gate. When spoken to at the Reunion Party, Astarion brags about his rising status as the city's "puppet-master" and generally looks down upon the player character. He can be challenged on his new behaviour and compared to Cazador, but Astarion brushes off these comments. If romanced and turned into a vampire spawn, Astarion asks the player character to talk with the other companions at the Reunion Party, gather information, and share it with him later while he stays behind and drinks wine. Then, turning into a bat, he laments that he has not heard any interesting gossip. He is surprised to hear the others are somehow succeeding in life without his supervision, but is uninterested in engaging in conversation with them himself. If romanced as a mind flayer , the player character is simply an ally to Astarion, as they cannot be turned into a spawn (though his Reunion Party dialogue remains the same as if they were one). If origin Karlach romanced Astarion, she cannot be turned into a vampire spawn because of her engine running hot, and he breaks up with her during their next long rest after the ritual. However, there are a few ways for Astarion to end up as a vampire lord without taking over the palace. Like all other player characters, an ascended origin Astarion has the option to go to Avernus with Karlach in any relationship status, abandoning the vampire lord's life completely to fight demons by her side instead. Additionally, if an origin Karlach romancing Astarion does not rest between fighting Cazador and the Netherbrain (thus skipping the breakup scene entirely), he instead demands to bring her to Avernus himself. Life remaining as Cazador's spawn [ edit section | visual editor ] If Astarion's personal quest is not completed at the end of the story and Cazador is still alive, he loses his ability to walk in the sun and is forced to go into hiding to avoid being found, punished, and controlled by Cazador again. He is relegated to the sewers and other dark areas during the day, and returns to feeding on animals such as rats. At the Reunion Party, Astarion laments to the player character about the life he has to live. The player character can then choose to promise to help him defeat Cazador for good, which gives him hope. If Astarion reconciled with the Gur, however, they join forces against Cazador and easily kill him sometime after the events of the game, where Astarion is living a free but secluded life as a spawn by the time of the Reunion Party. Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] If Cazador is defeated: High Security Vault nº3 Key Rhapsody as loot from Cazador Szarr Family Ring Woe as loot from Cazador (unless the ritual was stopped by force and Astarion left the party, in which case he destroys Woe) If Cazador is defeated and Astarion does not complete the Rite of Profane Ascension: Aid of Ulma and the Gur for ⁠ Gather Your Allies If Cazador is defeated and Astarion completes the Rite of Profane Ascension: Aid of Astarion's servants of the night for ⁠ Gather Your Allies Astarion gains the passive feature Vampire Ascendant , which grants the actions Ascendant Bite and Misty Escape (Vampire Ascendant) and an additional 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage to weapon and unarmed attacks. He also cites his fear of bodily sacrifice as the reason he does not want to take the Astral-Touched Tadpole. ↑ Astarion states he wants to create a city of spawn and cast a fog over the world for his children; he tells the player character they could have "everything" , that "the world is ours for the taking" , and similarly wants to subdue the Netherbrain for reasons which may be seen as intent on world domination. When Astarion is told by The Dark Urge that they will spare him when they conquer the world, he says, "Not if I get there first". In the Epilogue , Astarion also remarks there is an entire world out there, ready for the taking. If the player character recognises that Astarion is aiming to conquer the world, he acknowledges with appreciation. CRE_Gith_Generic Youth Astyl is a member of a new githyanki generation hatched and raised in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Are you here to learn from our sa'varsh? He's so powerful and wise. No wonder Vlaakith puts such faith in him. „ — Astyl , giving an optimistic assessment of Sa'varsh Kethk Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Astyl and several other githyanki youths and children are training in the Crèche Classroom , watching their mentor, Sa’varsh Kethk , goad Youth Varrl to retaliate. After the situation with Varrl is resolved, Astyl resumes training with the other students. Astyl speaks highly of Sa'varsh Kethk and is grateful for his mentorship in improving her skills. If the interacting party member is a githyanki, she vows to dedicate her silver sword to Kethk. HAV_Survivor Aubree is a Flaming Fist led by Counsellor Florrick to rescue Duke Ravengard during Act Two . “ An extra blade could be the difference between rescuing Duke Ravengard or losing him forever. I hope you'll help us. „ — Aubree Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Initially on a mission led by Florrick to rescue Ulder Ravengard , Aubree and the rest of the Fists were waylaid by the dangers of the Shadow-Cursed Lands and found refuge with the Harpers at Last Light Inn . Aubree is within the inn, in the same room as several other Fists, and Art Cullagh . She is deeply loyal to Ravengard and is concerned for his safety after hearing stories about Moonrise Towers . [ 1 ] If Florrick is not rescued from Waukeen's Rest in Act One , Aubree never appears in the game. Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Aubree more often than not fails her saving throw and is Impaled for the remainder of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, Aubree and everyone in Last Light Inn turn into a Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira . After the battle, talking with Aubree results in her denouncing Marcus as scum, and swearing that she and the rest of the Fists are loyal to Ravengard. [ 2 ] Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn and the Nightsong is been freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Aubree is among the Fists left by Florrick to follow Jaheira to Moonrise Towers . However, Aubree is killed during the initial fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. Her corpse is on the bridge leading to Moonrise, implying she was amongst the first to fall in battle. ## Auntie Ethel
- **来源**: [Auntie Ethel](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Auntie_Ethel)
- **分类**: Characters、Bosses、Traders

Overview Combat Auntie Ethel Trader of Quirks and Sundries Sister of the Seeing Pearl In-game Model Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Rena Valeh Main Writer Rachel Ní Chuirc Role Trader Hometown Riverside Teahouse , Sunlit Wetlands Stats Size Medium Type Fey Race Hag Technical UID S_HAG_Hag UUID c457d064-83fb-4ec6-b74d-1f30dfafd12d Stats HAG_AuntieEthel Trs. HAG_Hag Variant 1 UID Humans_Female_HagDouble UUID 2ec6e2a6-2b93-4f7d-899c-bad10d93ea38 Stats Commoner Trs. DEN_Ethel Auntie Ethel [ 1 ] is a fussy trader of potions, lotions, quirks, and sundries who can be first encountered in The Hollow of the Emerald Grove . Later, she returns to her home at the Riverside Teahouse in the Sunlit Wetlands . “ Bollocks. You were supposed to rush to my defence, love. Fat lot of good you are. Some advice? You ever darken my door, you'd best have that head bowed and an apology at the ready. Bye-bye, now! „ — Auntie Ethel , dropping her mask Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act One 1.1.1 In the Druid Grove 1.1.2 In the Sunlit Wetlands 1.1.3 In the Riverside Teahouse 1.2 Act Three 1.2.1 In the Blushing Mermaid 2 Combat 3 Related literature 4 Related quests 5 Store 6 Loot 6.1 Act One 6.2 Act Three 7 Speak with Dead 7.1 With Tarnished Charm 7.2 Without Tarnished Charm 8 Notes and references Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] In the Druid Grove [ edit section | visual editor ] Auntie Ethel can first be found in The Hollow in the Emerald Grove , peddling "Potions and Lotions" to the Tiefling refugees. Upon first speaking, she quickly notices something is awry with the interacting party member and invites them to visit her at her home, the Riverside Teahouse . While in the Emerald Grove she also acts as a trader. Once the party reach the Sunlit Wetlands , Auntie Ethel moves from the Emerald Grove and appears in the Wetlands, and then eventually at the Teahouse. If a party member first [ 2 ] speaks with Pandirna before Ethel, she tells them Auntie Ethel gave her a potion to make her "strong and brave as a bugbear," but left her paralyzed instead. Immediately following this interaction, Auntie Ethel leaves her shop in the Emerald Grove. If Ethel is attacked or successfully pickpocketed while in the Emerald Grove, she exclaims, "Blast it all! I'm going home." and leaves for the Riverside Teahouse. The same result occurs if a hiding character is spotted by her. Auntie Ethel leaves the grove permanently once the conversation between her and Mayrina's brothers happens in the Sunlit Wetlands (see below). In the Sunlit Wetlands [ edit section | visual editor ] When the party first enter the Sunlit Wetlands from the east, Johl and his brother Demir are arguing with Auntie Ethel, demanding she tell them where their sister Mayrina is, and accuse Ethel of having taken her. This starts ⁠ Save Mayrina . The party can talk with the group to learn more: Mayrina has disappeared and the last person to see her was Ethel. Throughout the encounter, Demir pleads with her while she insists she is blameless, but "willing to help" them look for her. Eventually, the party can choose to take either side, or none at all. They can even walk right past, ignoring the trio altogether. If they side with Auntie Ethel, Demir and Johl accuse the party of working with her and attack. If they do not side with Ethel, she chastises them and disappears in a burst of magic. The party can then talk to the two brothers and attempt to convince them not to follow her into the swamp, which is futile. In the Riverside Teahouse [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party enter the Teahouse, they observe Auntie Ethel forcing Mayrina to eat. If the player character ⁠ seeks Ethel's help to remove the tadpole , she states her price: they must give up an eye in exchange for her removing the Tadpole . If the player character accepts her bargain, she reverts to her hag form, asks them to choose which eye to surrender and begins the procedure to remove the tadpole, only to soon stop and (truthfully) declare it has been modified by ancient Netherese magic. Having already Paid the Price , she refuses to reverse it despite failing to cure the player character. Allowing Auntie Ethel to take an eye of the player character irrevocably changes the appearance of the chosen eye. It cannot be removed and its appearance does not change with the Magic Mirror . It is not possible to take this deal if Volo has already replaced one of the player character's eyes or Wyll is chosen as origin . If the player character does not accept her bargain, and instead insists on saving Mayrina, then Ethel eventually reveals her true form and starts a fight, calling the redcaps from outside the teahouse to her side. During the fight Ethel first consumes a Potion of Invisibility , and then disappears through her fireplace in the teahouse. To save Mayrina the party must follow Ethel and infiltrate her lair in the Overgrown Tunnel . [ 3 ] In her lair, victims and thralls of the hag are found. Some of them can be freed, while others must usually be fought and are lost forever. Eventually Mayrina is seen in a cage in the Ancient Abode and can by saved by defeating Ethel. Alternatively it is possible to make a deal with Ethel , to acquire Auntie Ethel's Hair after which she disappears. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] In the Blushing Mermaid [ edit section | visual editor ] Auntie Ethel is part of the ⁠ Help the Hag Survivors , ⁠ Avenge the Hag Survivors , and ⁠ Save Vanra questlines whether the party accept her offer or kill her. She can be found posing as Captain Grisly in The Blushing Mermaid in Lower City . Her lair is located under this tavern and can be infiltrated through the basement. Auntie Ethel does not appear in Act Three if she remained in her lair at the Sunlit Wetlands and did not abandon it. It is ultimately revealed that Ethel is functionally unkillable while her life force is invested in her magic mushrooms, which is how can survived being killed in Act One. If she is killed there, she is more hostile to the party, preventing them from demanding a counter-offer to leave her alone. However, this does not prevent her from being acquired as an Ally for ⁠ Gather Your Allies if Lora is killed and Auntie Ethel is left to her schemes. It is recommended to begin the quest ⁠ Save Vanra by speaking with Lora prior to completing the Hag Survivors questlines and defeating the Hag. Failure to get this quest from Lora directly, even if Vanra is saved, locks the party out of its quest rewards. Killing Auntie Ethel in Act Three grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Estrangement of Ethel ( Urchin background) ⁠ Double-Tap ( Soldier background) - for killing her a second time ⁠ Re-tasting the Kill ( Haunted One background) Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Auntie Ethel/Combat Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Hag Spy's Note I Can Save Your Child Letter from Auntie Ethel Letter from 'M' Letter from Ethel Letter to Ethel Loving Note Report on Old Garlow's You Deserve To Feel Beautiful Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Avenge the Hag Survivors ⁠ Find a Cure ⁠ Get Help from Auntie Ethel ⁠ Help the Hag Survivors ⁠ Save Mayrina ⁠ Save Vanra Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds with DEN_Ethel Corellon's Grace The following items are restocked after a long rest: Elixir of Fire Resistance Elixir of Hill Giant Strength Potion of Greater Healing Potion of Healing Potion of Invisibility Water She also possibly sells the following alchemical ingredients: Autumncrocus Balsam Belladonna Daggerroot Mergrass Mugwort Weavemoss Items of following trader tables are possibly sold by Auntie Ethel: Rare Mushroom Supply Table Tiny Trader Table Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Auntie Ethel's Charm Auntie Ethel's Hair (obtained through mid-combat dialogue) Tarnished Charm Hag's Potions Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Ring of Feywild Sparks Soul Coin Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] If killed, Ethel's body can be spoken to using Speak with Dead . Ethel is unique in that her Speak with Dead dialogue changes depending on whether she still has the Tarnished Charm on her corpse when talking to her. Unlike most corpses, she is willing (but angry) to speak to her killer. With Tarnished Charm [ edit section | visual editor ] Narrator *A charm on the hag's body flashes a faint glow.* Auntie Ethel ARGH. You knuckle-dragging gobshite. Auntie Ethel You will bleed - you will choke on your own guts for this.  (if the caster is Ethel's killer) Auntie Ethel ARGH. Where is the knuckle-dragging gobshite that killed me?  (if the caster is not Ethel's killer) You're quite lively for a corpse. Auntie Ethel I'm a hag , you little snot - you think I didn't plan for this? Death and I are old friends. Auntie Ethel But I won't be a corpse forever - that I can bloody promise you. Tell me the truth - what did you want with Mayrina? Auntie Ethel I didn't want the girl, sweetie. I wanted her babe . Auntie Ethel I would have gobbled it up and given birth to my very own hag daughter. Auntie Ethel From my guts she would've come - my blood, my bile . It would have been glorious. Does being dead bother you?  (if the caster is not Ethel's killer)) Auntie Ethel You think this is the first time? I've found my way back before, and I will again. Auntie Ethel And then I will make the cretin beg, plead, weep for what will always be denied... Auntie Ethel ...The sweet release of death. You're dead and I'm not. Deal with it.  (if the caster is Ethel's killer) Auntie Ethel For now. Why are you so cruel? Auntie Ethel Please. It's you lot who come to me. All you do is want - to be prettier, to be richer, to be loved. Auntie Ethel People are their own worst enemies, petal. I just let them see it. What deal did you make with Mayrina? Auntie Ethel The brat's husband is dead . So sad. Auntie Ethel She wanted me to bring him back to life. Little fool thought it would fix everything. Do you have any regrets?  (if the caster is not Ethel's killer) Auntie Ethel Only one. Auntie Ethel And you'll never know. Do you have any regrets?  (if the caster is Ethel's killer) Auntie Ethel Only that I don't get to see the flesh melt from your bones, your guts dissolve, and your brain liquefy as you turn into a mind flayer. Auntie Ethel You'll weep, you'll beg, you'll plead - anything to make it stop. And once you stand tall, proud and tentacled? Auntie Ethel You'll butcher your friends and your loved ones LIKE THE ILLITHID SCUM YOU ARE. Without Tarnished Charm [ edit section | visual editor ] Auntie Ethel Bleed... choke on... your guts...  (if the caster is Ethel's killer) Auntie Ethel Kill them... kill them... all...  (if the caster is not Ethel's killer) Why did you want Mayrina? Auntie Ethel Didn't want... the girl... wanted her... babe . Auntie Ethel ... was going to... eat it... and make a... hag daughter... Are you the only hag around here? Auntie Ethel Where there's people... there's... hags. Where do you keep your valuables? Auntie Ethel In my... workroom... Why are you so cruel? Auntie Ethel Not me... that's cruel. It's... people. Auntie Ethel They want... and want... and want. I merely... give. Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_RitualRoom_Spawn_002 UUID a612de01-a750-491a-bacd-e09a67fc0de3 Stats Vampire_Spawn Aurelia is a vampire spawn enslaved to Cazador , and one of Astarion's siblings. She may appear at camp or Cazador's Dungeon during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] After reaching the Lower City , Aurelia, Violet , Yousen and Leon visit the camp at night and attempt to kidnap Astarion. Aurelia and the other spawn believe Cazador is going to include them all in the ritual, and that he will allow them to "cheat undeath". If Astarion or the player character successfully deceives or persuades the spawn to side with the party, Cazador compels them to fight anyway. Failing to defeat them before Astarion reaches one hit point results in their abducting him back to Szarr Palace . Astarion can then be found in the kennels with Godey . Aurelia and the other spawn can later be encountered in Cazador's Dungeon, trapped by ritual ruins as Cazador prepares for his ascension. Technical UID S_LOW_FireworksHouse_AverySonshal UUID 21359690-36ec-43d3-bfed-98c24f523fc7 Stats LOW_FelogyrFireworks_AverySonshal Avery Sonshal is a shopkeeper of the Felogyr's Fireworks workshop in the Lower City Baldur's Gate , during Act Three . He can be located and spoken with while following through the quest ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys . “ Remember, Felogyr's Fireworks accepts no liability for singed nails, toasted eyelashes, loss of limbs, scalded torsos or blown-off heads „ — Avery Sonshal 's disclaimer Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act 3 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Loot 3 Shop 3.1 Notable items sold 3.1.1 Dyes 3.1.2 Fireworks & grenades 4 Related Quests 5 Related Literature 6 Notes 7 External links Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Avery Sonshal is in charge of Felogyr's Fireworks , a workshop that sells various crackers and pyrotechnics to Baldurian citizens, including children. When approaching him, a cutscene triggers, during which he checks one of his underage clients', Willow , knowledge of the rules concerning safe usage of fireworks. As the cutscene continues, Avery addresses the next question to the party. He is tadpoled and aware of the cult, so he immediately recognizes fellow True Souls , calling them telepathically friends of Enver Gortash . Half of the conversation henceforth is kept up in the same manner. The party may ask Avery to give them a free sample of the workshop's production. He then gives them three Smokepowder Arrows . After that, there are several options within dialogue. The party may choose the line What else do you do for Gortash? . Sonshal then speaks aloud some gibberish, while again giving the real answer telepathically - he clearly does not want his dealings with Gortash to be exposed. This line allows to perform DC 15 Intimidation Check or DC 15 Deception Check , both concerning some 'last order from Gortash'. Avery tries to offer excuses, saying that his establishment keeps the schedule, and leaking a word by the way that Gortash is somehow connected with the Gondians . There is also an option to tell Avery the password wrested from Arfur Gregorio in Wyrm's Crossing . Hearing the password, Avery lets the party proceed to the first floor of the workshop, but forewarn them not to wander further upstairs. Saying this, he acts in an overly theatrical way, which allows to suspect that 'Uncle Felogyr' is a totally imaginary person. The party can also ask Avery to trade. However, speaking with him again after trading has the 'password' dialogue line still available. Avery Sonshal can be pickpocketed. Apart from trading goods, the party may also loot from him Felogyr's Fireworks Cellar Key , Fireworks Workshop Key , Counting House Vault nº5 Key , and a Soot-Stained Letter . As the quest ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys cannot be ultimately resolved in a peaceful way, Avery Sonshal joins the fight as soon as he notices any ill commotion, siding with the followers of Bane , who reside on the second floor of the building. He runs upstairs and attacks the party along with the other Felogyr's employees. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_RetiredFist_Elf02 UUID d7cd0aa5-7303-45c7-a9e2-fac6a458f63e Stats HalfElf_Commoner Avourel is a retired Flaming Fist who is still adjusting to retirement. Avourel is with a group of retirees in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Most elves don't oft retire. Guess I'm one of the lucky few. „ — Avourel Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Avourel is in Bloomridge Park discussing the state of the Flaming Fists with Eldaernth , Thokki , and Vistra . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Vistra ' Absolute ' this... 'end of the world' that... These young folk've no idea how good they've got it. Eldaernth Come off it, Vistra. You've been doing this same rant for years. Avourel Yeah, the first lot of young folk you said it about are old folk now! Vistra Piss off, the lot of youse. Eldaernth You're remembering the past pretty fondly, Vistra. Bit too fondly. Vistra What d'you mean? Eldaernth You telling me you'd have refused the Steel Watch's help on Returning Day a decade ago? Vistra You'll, uh... remind me? Eldaernth Big horrible beast? Slaughtered Duke Adrian? We could do bugger all about it? Thokki Lost a lot of good men that day. Vistra You make a good point, Eldaernth. Eldaernth You've known me long enough, Vistra. When haven't I? Vistra We could've used the Steel Watch back in the day. But that's because we fought actual threats. Back when the Fists were real Fists. Not bloody... Avourel Limp gloves. Eldaernth So, Vistra. You reckon we'd still be better Fists than the current cohort? Vistra Peace of piss, mate. Easy. Yes. Eldaernth Great. So let's get you out of that chair and into your chain mail, then? Show the young lot how it's done? Vistra Uh... Well... Thokki My armour's not fit for years. Avourel Yeah, to be honest? Thought of holding a pike makes my back ache. Eldaernth It's a young man's game. Right, Vistra? Vistra 'Spose. Vistra Look, all I'm saying is they've got it easier these days. Thokki Yeah, we didn't have these big metal bastards running the streets back in my day. Eldaernth Thanks to the bloody Iron Crisis we barely had any metal back then. Vistra You're right, you're right. We Fists had to proper fight back then. We knew how to watch each other's backs. Eldaernth Helm give me strength. Eldaernth Not seen action like that in a while.  (After the ambush in Bloomridge Park) Vistra Those cultists are lucky they were on the other side of the park. Lucky. Avourel You'd have taken them, would you, Vistra? Vistra Reckon so. Eldaernth Bollocks. These days we'd sooner throw our backs than a proper punch. Thokki Well, I, for one, count my lucky stars it happened elsewhere. Avourel Same here. ## Aylin
- **来源**: [Aylin](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Aylin)
- **分类**: Characters、Camp_Followers

Overview Combat Nightsong Singer of Sorrows In-game Render Model Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Helen Keeley Role Camp Follower Attached Follower Family Isobel Thorm (partner) Selûne (mother) Shar (aunt) Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Aasimar Class Paladin Subclass Oath of Vengeance Technical UID S_GLO_Nightsong UUID 6c55edb0-901b-4ba4-b9e8-3475a8392d9b Stats SHA_Nightsong Variant 1 UID Humans_Female_Strong_NightSong_Prison UUID 3690bd38-c4b3-4f3b-89e2-270f95283c90 Stats SHA_Nightsong Dame Aylin , also known by the moniker Nightsong , is an Aasimar and daughter of Selûne who appears in Baldur's Gate 3 . She is first introduced during Act Two , and her story plays a key role in the mysteries surrounding the Shadow-Cursed Lands and Moonrise Towers . She can become a Camp Follower and later an Attached Follower . “ Our Lady of Silver. Hear me! She Who Guides, the Moonmaiden Selûne - MOTHER OF THE SO-CALLED NIGHTSONG. THE NIGHTSONG IS NO MORE! „ — Nightsong , upon release Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Personality 1.3 Recruitment 1.4 History 2 Involvement 2.1 Act Two 2.2 Act Three 3 Combat 3.1 Equipment 4 Related quests 5 Related items 6 Related literature 7 Gallery 8 Datamined content 9 Notes 10 References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Dame Aylin is a daughter of the goddess Selûne , and therefore is effectively immortal. Many characters, including the necromancer Balthazar , sought to or participated in the imprisonment of Aylin to exploit this immortality for their own purposes. Aylin's story is closely intertwined with that of cleric Isobel . At the conclusion of Act Two, under the right circumstances, it is revealed that Aylin and Isobel are lovers. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Aylin embraces her emotions. She is passionate and fiercely protective of those she is close to and has no reservations with sharing her love of and desire for Isobel. As a paladin , Aylin personifies their values: she cherishes life and love, rewards friendship with loyalty, seeks to protect the weak, avenge the wronged, punish the wicked and uphold justice. She often speaks with and carries a lofty demeanor befitting her station as the daughter of the goddess Selûne. Finally, when angered, she may allow this feeling to flow through her as it influences her decisions and behavior. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Aylin can become a partial Camp Follower if she survives the events of Act Two, but eventually leaves camp again upon resolution of certain quests in Act Three. If Find the Nightsong is completed with Aylin freed, she becomes an ally as part of ⁠ Gather Your Allies . During the final quest, ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain , Aylin can be summoned with Sword of the Silverlight and become an Attached Follower . History [ edit section | visual editor ] Over a hundred years ago, Aylin was sent by her mother Selûne as an emissary to Isobel's town. The two met and fell in love at first sight. Ketheric Thorm , Isobel's father, was distrustful of Aylin's intentions. Aylin believed he was threatened by her and Isobel's love for each other, but both understood he was concerned for Aylin's status as an immortal. After Isobel died, a grief-stricken Ketheric turned to Shar . Under the influence of the Lady of Loss, he and Balthazar lured Aylin to the Shadowfell where they trapped and caged her. While trapped in the Shadowfell, Ketheric fed on Aylin's immortality as she was murdered again and again by Shar's Dark Justiciars as part of their trials to become anointed. Though imprisoned and having seen Isobel's dead body, she never stopped hoping the two would be reunited, dreaming each night that Isobel would return to her. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic During the final stages of act two, Dame Aylin is met by the party imprisoned in the Shadowfell , being used as a source of immortality for Ketheric Thorm. Balthazar is preparing to remove her from the Shadowfell and bring her to Moonrise Towers to keep Ketheric's immortality safe. Meeting Aylin grants the inspiration ⁠ Emblem of the Moonmaiden to party members with the Sage background. The party can either choose to aid Balthazar or fight him. If they aid him, Aylin is transported to Moonrise Towers and the party can return there for an audience with Ketheric. If they fight him, combat begins. If Aylin is killed during the fight with Balthazar, she respawns after a couple of turns. If Shadowheart is present, she can kill Aylin or spare and free her. If she is killed during the cut-scene with Shadowheart, Aylin's death is permanent. Shadowheart has a unique, additional approval mechanic, which influences her decision. See Nightsong Points . Aylin, filled with intense rage after a century of suffering from his plans, repeatedly crushes Ketheric Thorm's remains after his final defeat in the Mind Flayer Colony. If Aylin is freed, she flies to Moonrise Towers, where she assists the party in the first phase of Ketheric Thorm's fight atop the roof of Moonrise Towers but then must be freed once more during the second phase in the Mind Flayer Colony . After defeating Ketheric Thorm, Aylin reunites with Isobel (if alive), whom she believed dead. The two can become Camp Followers at this point. The following inspiration can be gained depending on choices made: ⁠ Blood Moon ( Haunted One background) - for allowing Shadowheart to kill Aylin ⁠ Damsel No More ( Folk Hero background) - for freeing Aylin ⁠ Good Deed of the Day ( Urchin background) - for freeing Aylin ⁠ Morally Grey ( Charlatan background) - for allowing her to be taken by Balthazar ⁠ Soldier of Faith ( Soldier background) - for freeing Aylin ⁠ Soldier of Fortune ( Soldier background) - for allowing her to be taken by Balthazar Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] While travelling in the city, the party can discover that the wizard Lorroakan is the one responsible for offering a reward for the Nightsong. Lorroakan can be deceived that Dame Aylin is dead. However, if Aylin is informed of his search, she flies to Sorcerous Sundries to face him, convinced that he will not stop searching for her. The party can finally side with Lorroakan and capture Aylin, or side with Aylin and attack him. If Lorroakan is killed, Aylin expresses sadness. Party members can offer their thoughts; that perhaps she is tired of revenge or was reminded of those who sought to use her in the past. It is hinted by Isobel at camp that Aylin's sadness is a result of the hurt she has experienced over the past century. After a long rest, she and Isobel depart from camp to help a Selûnite enclave outside the city. They later can be met at High Hall during the final fight to lend aid. If the party side with Lorroakan, Aylin kneels in prayer to Selûne who in turn blesses Aylin with a condition called Moonmother's Embrace and sends three powerful Moonlight Slivers to fight by her side, which makes for a significantly more difficult fight. If Aylin is allowed to be caged by Lorroakan, informing Isobel incites her to travel to Ramazith's Tower to rescue Aylin. With Aylin caged and Lorroakan now immortal, Isobel is ultimately killed by him. A heartbroken Aylin then vows that she will kill the player character's "children, and their children beside". If Lorroakan is defeated during the fight, after one long rest, Aylin leaves a threatening note in the tower and she and Isobel leave camp permanently. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Aylin/Combat Depending on the party's choices, Aylin can appear during several combat encounters as an allied, neutral, or hostile entity. Aylin cannot die in combat; if her HP reaches 0, she becomes Downed for one turn and attempts to regain 1 HP on the following turn. This healing can be prevented by certain effects, such as Bone Chilled , but she continues attempts to heal on subsequent turns until she finally stands up. Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Her equipment is not lootable or pickpocketable but can be accessed via mods / third party tools. Greatsword +1 Nightsong Boots Nightsong's Armour Nightsong Gloves Nightsong Helmet Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Daughter of Darkness ⁠ The Chosen of Shar ⁠ Find the Nightsong ⁠ Gather Your Allies Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Selûne's Spear of Night - reward for sparing Aylin during Shadowheart's personal quest. Shar's Spear of Evening - reward for Shadowheart killing Aylin during her personal quest. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Letter from Dame Aylin Letter from Isobel The Final Sacrifice of the Moon Daughter - found in the library in the Gauntlet of Shar An Assurance - found on the floor in Ramazith's Tower after a long rest if Aylin is sided against and killed, but Lorroakan is also killed during the battle Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Without helmet Render by Wayne Chu Renders by Wayne Chu Datamined content [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Aylin/Cut content According to the datamined content, the Nightsong was a cleric of Shar and was supposed to be a potential boss fight, her abilities and voice lines can be seen on YouTube. [ 1 ] Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The name Aylin is of Turkish origin, based on the root word "Ay" which means moon. The real-world name is pronounced EYE-leen , [ 2 ] similar to the unrelated Irish name Eileen, whereas the aasimar's name is pronounced AY-lin . Aylin has the tag Dragonborn . Despite being labelled by the game as an Aasimar , Aylin may be better be described as a Deva : Aylin is explicitly immortal, both in terms of not aging and resurrecting after death, whereas aasimar have finite lifespans similar to that of half-elves. She can use her wings for as long as she wishes as many times as she wants, whereas only one kind of aasimar can use theirs, and only a limited time per day. Her presence and the fact that she is explicitly Selune's child mark her as more divine than aasimars, whose divine parentage is usually extremely distant and seldom remarked upon in such a way. If Aylin participates in the fight against Lorroakan, her Child of the Moonmaiden passive is removed permanently, regardless of who the party sides with. References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ ⁠ The Nightsong, Halsin and Ketheric City | Baldur's Gate 3 Story Spoilers  – Chubblot Chubblot ↑ See ⁠ Aylin or any generic Turkish pronunciation guide. During the quest ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove , Azak is one of the goblins packed inside a Transport Barrel to be thrown to the ramparts of the Emerald Grove by an Ogre Brute . BG_Guard Fist Azari is human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is in Wyrm's Crossing during Act Three . “ What I wouldn't give to grab a flagon with the duke. The man's a living legend. „ — Azari Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Azari sits on a chair inside the guardhouse at the South Span Checkpoint (the entrance into it is from the Wyrm's Crossing only). Despite saying little to the party, Azari often initiates conversation with Fist Meadows , who is not very eager to keep the conversation up. Through idle banter, it is revealed that Azari looks up to Ulder Ravengard and is frustrated with being on sentry duty after two years of training. CRE_Gith_Generic Youth Ba’akreth is a member of a new githyanki generation hatched and raised in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Stop bothering me. I'm trying to concentrate! „ — Ba'akreth Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ba’akreth and several other githyanki youths and children are training in the Crèche Classroom . When the party arrive, everyone is watching their mentor, Sa’varsh Kethk , goad Youth Varrl to strike back. After the situation with Varrl is resolved, Ba’akreth continues to train on a dummy. If the party speak with her, Ba'akreth snaps at them for distracting her from training and threaten them saying she actually has a dagger in hand. However, should the player character speak to her after Varrl is spared or killed, Ba’akreth is the only youth in the classroom who acknowledges Varrl's fate. Depending on the player character's decisions, Ba'akreth might praise their technique, berate them for being too soft in fight, or simply call them a weakling. She can be found watching Lyrux Goldthroat performing on the far end of the Guildhall . Technical UID BADGER_PlayerWildshape UUID 47263893-8aab-48f1-96ad-13907d1e23e8 Stats Badger_Giant_Wildshape Badgers are a type of Beast creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Striped ponderous wanderers of the woods. „ — In-game racial description About badgers [ edit section | visual editor ] Badgers are burrowing beasts found throughout Faerûn , recognisable by their black-and-white striped fur and powerful digging claws. Only one named badger appears in-game: Postmaster Badger , who serves the Harpers by training messenger rats to gather and relay information throughout Baldur's Gate . Four dead badgers are near a mysterious hole in a ruined building at the Rivington Campsite . Druids can assume the form of a badger through Wild Shape: Badger .
