The Dream Guardian is a mysterious armoured figure that interacts with the player character and their party throughout the game. Their appearance is specific to each member of the party, with Karlach describing them as a "golden paladin" and Gale referring to them as female, while the player character sees a version created by the player which can be any gender and playable race except dragonborn. Their default appearance in character creation is a female Lolth-sworn drow . Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act One 1.2 Act Two 1.3 Act Three 2 Combat 3 Early Access 4 Gallery 5 References Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Dream_Visitor.webm I saved you... and I'm here to save you again The Dream Guardian first appears to the party shortly after their adventure begins while they sleep. They attempt to ease the player character into a sense of comfort, claiming to be the one protecting them from the influence of the Absolute , in addition to preventing their transformation into Mind Flayers . Throughout Act One, they encourage the player character to fully utilise the Illithid Powers , as well as encouraging them to use the Tadpoles of other infected hosts to further bolster their powers. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dream Guardian as a female tiefling in their camp clothing during an Act Two dream sequence. If a Long Rest is performed after arriving in the Shadow-Cursed Lands, the Dream Guardian appears to the player character once again in a dream, wearing their camp clothing (a Mellow Fruit -dyed Elegant Robe ) rather than their usual armour. The Dream Guardian shares that being in such close proximity to the Absolute is taking a toll on them, and the player character is given a number of different responses for how to react to this. More choices can be unlocked by noticing the Dream Guardian's distressed condition, accomplished by succeeding hidden Perception and Insight checks which the player character cannot modify. These additional conversation options will not be available if the party first progress to Moonrise Towers before long resting. After defeating Ketheric Thorm , and the Apostle of Myrkul , the Dream Guardian appears to manifest outside of the player character's dreams, congratulating them, but urging them to travel to Baldur's Gate to finally destroy the Elder Brain that is behind the Cult of the Absolute, as well as the rest of the Chosen of the Dead Three , Orin the Red and Enver Gortash . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] At the beginning of Act Three, while in camp, the party is disturbed by the sudden and nearly overpowering demands of the Elder Brain , and the Dream Guardian pleads for the party to help them. Upon the party's arrival into the Astral Prism , they meet not their hand-crafted Dream Guardian, but rather a Mind Flayer named the Emperor , who admits to having deceived the party in the form of the Dream Guardian. Should the party choose to free Orpheus and fight the Emperor, four versions of the Dream Guardian appear as enemies. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Dream Guardian/Combat Early Access [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Cut and unimplemented content#Dream Visitor Text above the Dream Visitor appearance options ask "Who do you dream of? Who attracts you?" while the narrator says "Tell me – Who do you dream of at night?" The Dream Guardian was named " The Dream Visitor " in the Early Access version of the game and " Daisy " in the game files of both versions. They wore their camp clothing during character creation and all scenes, while in the Full Release they appear in a set of armour for everything except one dream sequence in Act 2. In the Full Release the Guardian is supportive of the player character regardless of their decisions, encouraging the destruction of the Absolute while also utilising the strength of the tadpole. However, Larian appeared to have a very different story in mind for the Guardian initially because their presentation, behavior, and actions were more hostile and manipulative throughout the Early Access content. The visions granted by the Dream Visitor were of domination and power, and if the player character resisted these visions the Dream Visitor would become hostile. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The Dream Visitor would eventually attempt to seduce the player character, and this storyline was bolstered suggestions during the Guardian's character creation guiding the player to create someone the player character would be attracted to. The song Down by the River from the game's Original Soundtrack was likely related to these interactions as the dreams took place by a river and the song's lyrics ask the player character to stay there in the dream with them forever ( Don't wake me up, Just leave me there dreaming ). GOB_Goblin_Generic Drenn is a goblin who can be met at Moonrise Towers in Act Two . “ You creaking old bag of shit! „ — Drenn , snapping at Ketheric Thorm in despair Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Drenn can be found at Moonrise Towers undergoing a trial by Ketheric Thorm for her failures, if Minthara or Fezzerk do not survive Act One . In this case Drenn is accompanied by Darra and Racha . When the party approach the throne room in Moonrise Towers, a cutscene is triggered with Ketheric and Z'rell . Drenn claims that she and other subjects of the trial obeyed all orders. She offers explanations if Minthara or Fezzerk are not present. Z'rell and Ketheric provide their opposing opinion and ask the player character to evaluate the goblins' loyalty to the Absolute. Regardless of their response, Ketheric orders the goblins to be killed. Outraged, Drenn insults Ketheric, snatches a halberd from a guard, and hurls it into Ketheric's chest. The immortal general rips the weapon from his chest and drops it in front of Drenn, ordering her to "try again". Drenn strikes him in the neck, to no avail, and he smashes Drenn's spine with his bare hands, killing her. Ketheric leaves the hall, ordering Z'rell to dispatch the remaining goblins by the player character's hand. It is not possible for the party to speak with any of the goblins outside of the cutscene. The player character has several options for deciding their fate. If the party set them free, the surviving goblins flee from Moonrise Towers and disappear. After Drenn attacks Ketheric, Z'rell takes it as a personal mistake and says that "she is an unbeliever and outside her control". Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRock_MessHallGuard_001 UUID bca3d3e3-3ddc-4ba2-8ad5-58afec936933 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Dresten is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in Wyrm's Rock Fortress in Act Three . “ He'll clean up the city in no time. Got more backbone in his little finger than Ravengard has in his entire body. „ — Dresten (from the cut-out dialogue) Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Dresten is standing watch in the Mess Hall inside the fortress, accompanied by a single Steel Watcher . If spoken to, he allows the party to mind their own business - in due limits. There is also a cut-out dialogue with Dresten that supposedly would have been enacted if the party bypassed the conversation with Enver Gortash via the Steel Watcher (one occurring straight after entering the fortress). Throughout it, the automaton accompanying Dresten joins the dialogue and acts first mildly hostile to the player character, but then changes its attitude abruptly and invites them upstairs "to make acquaintance to Lord Gortash" (of which the Fist is quite surprised). In this case, Dresten also informs the player character about the ceremony upheld in the Audience Hall and compares Gortash against Ulder Ravengard , clearly not in favor of the latter. EQP_WYR_Circus_Hammer Fumm , disguised as Dribbles the Clown , works at the Circus of the Last Days as a clown. He can be found at the Circus in Rivington in Act 3 , as well as various locations around Baldur's Gate . “ Buddy the dog is my very best friend. Do you know why? Wa-hey! „ — Dribbles telling a joke at the Circus of the Last Days Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 History 2 Involvement 2.1 Act Three 3 Party interactions 3.1 Astarion 3.2 Gale 3.3 Halsin 3.4 Jaheira 3.5 Karlach 3.6 Lae'zel 3.7 Minsc 3.8 Minthara 3.9 Shadowheart 3.10 Wyll 3.11 Player character 4 Combat 4.1 Attacks and actions 4.2 Loot 5 Speak with Dead 6 Related items 7 Related literature 8 Related quests 9 References 10 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Dribbles the Clown, born Norris Greenie , [ text 1 ] is the "star" and one of the most popular shows at the Circus of the Last Days. Unfortunately, he is killed by cultists of Bhaal sometime before the party reaches Baldur's Gate and replaced by Fumm . History [ edit section | visual editor ] For a decade, Dumpty Dumpling was the headline act at the Circus of the Last Days. However, Dumpty's love of clowning was fading. During one of his performances, Norris Greenie volunteered himself when Dumpty called for one from the crowd. Norris quickly enthralled the crowd with his quick wit and one-liners. Lucretious, seeing his potential, offered Norris a job on the spot. [ text 1 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Dribbles the Clown' can first be encountered at the Circus of the Last Days doing a comedy routine. One member of his audience is Quinton . On approaching the stage 'Dribbles' calls upon a member of the party to join him on stage, where it is eventually revealed that this Dribbles is actually a Doppelganger named Fumm. Warlocks and Rogues can attempt to see through the clown disguise - passing the check allows the character to cautiously go on stage, allowing the party to preemptively strike the evil clown. Doing so also grants the ⁠ Taking the Spotlight inspiration to party members with the Entertainer background. After the fight, Lucretious asks the party to find Dribbles. The parts of his body can be found strewn across Baldur's Gate. After his parts are returned, Lucretious says she is able to resurrect him so that he can continue performing. “ Gods, I hate clowns. I'm not even sure clowns like clowns. „ — Shadowheart , on the prospect of being called onstage with Dribbles Party interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] The player character can suggest one of their party members go up on the stage when their group is called on. Some companions approve of being called up on stage, while others disapprove. The interactions are as follows: Astarion [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion: Oh good, puns. BG_Child Oyster Boy Dringo works at the kennel outside Sword Coast Couriers in Rivington during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Dringo is an apprentice to Angry Mar'hyah , who often verbally abuses him. He remains in his position because his dad thinks she will 'toughen him up'. He also heavily implies that she has used 'the rod' to discipline both him and the dogs. If the party summon Scratch to the kennel, Dringo is overjoyed to see him again. Should the party leave Scratch with Mar'hyah, Dringo promises to take good care of him. However, if the interacting party member successfully passes a DC 18 Intimidation Check or DC 18 Persuasion Check to convince Mar'hyah to allow Scratch to stay with them, Dringo mentions that she has a history of abusing all dogs, not only Scratch. The interacting party member can tell Dringo that they only care about Scratch, or they can attempt to pass a DC 18 Deception Check or DC 20 Intimidation Check against Mar'hyah. Failing the checks causes her to fire Dringo, forcing him to permanently leave the kennel, at which point Dringo will disappear and never return. Succeeding the check results in her leaving the kennel while Dringo releases all the dogs from their cages. He vows to care for them better than she ever did. Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_Bonecloak_Civ_001 UUID 137e9a88-bfdd-4e35-ac80-f8777bd45a36 Stats Human_Commoner Drongo Bixworth is being interrogated in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I just wanna go home. „ — Drongo Bixworth Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Steel Watch Foundry is intact, Drongo and Florean Bixworth can be found at Bonecloak's Apothecary being interrogated by Fist Elthira Gossen . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Florean Bixworth Look, we've got nothing to do with the Absolute . Fist Elthira Gossen I wouldn't expect you to admit your nefarious allegiance. You lot are sworn to secrecy, aren't you? Drongo Bixworth Please, just let us go and we'll be out of your way. Fist Elthira Gossen And what do you know about the Absolute, eh? Florean Bixworth Army's marching on the city! What else is there to know?! Fist Elthira Gossen Don't be smart with me. Fist Elthira Gossen And what about you? Drongo Bixworth I don't know nothing! We were just standing here! Fist Elthira Gossen Loitering's what you were doing. Loitering with intent , I shouldn't wonder. Florean Bixworth Loitering? I've got a gammy leg - that's just how I look! Drongo Bixworth Yeah, we weren't doing anything - just waiting for a friend! Fist Elthira Gossen So were you doing nothing or were you waiting for a friend? Which is it? Fist Elthira Gossen What, Lord Gortash is dead, and all you've got to do is stand around and stare? Looks suspicious, I think.  (If Enver Gortash is killed) Florean Bixworth Suspicious? What? How? I don't even know what that means. Drongo Bixworth Yeah, Florean's too dumb to do anything suspicious. He wouldn't know where to start. Fist Elthira Grossen So you're the smart one, then? GOB_GoblinKing_Warhammer Trs. GOB_King Dror Ragzlin is one of three bosses at the Goblin Camp who work for the Cult of the Absolute . The goblins threaten the Emerald Grove and tiefling refugees . “ You ever talk to a dead squid? Now's your chance. „ — Dror Ragzlin , squid whisperer Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.1.1 Shattered Sanctum 2.2 Act Two 2.2.1 Mind Flayer Colony 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Honour mode 3.3 Allies 3.4 Encounter details 3.5 Tactics 3.6 Loot 4 Related literature 5 Speak with Dead 6 Related quests 7 Quotes 8 Gallery Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Blessed by the Absolute and imparted the status of True Soul , Dror is a leader of the goblin forces in the Wilderness near the Emerald Grove. The Absolute instructed him to scour the wrecked remains of the Nautiloid to find a Mysterious Artefact . He is in the Shattered Sanctum attempting to speak with a mind flayer corpse . Depending on party choices, Ragzlin can become an ally or foe throughout Act One. Ragzlin, Minthara and Gut are True Souls and leaders of the goblins who threaten the Emerald Grove. Thus, Ragzlin must be defeated to save the Emerald Grove and the tieflings. Alternatively, the party can initiate the raid and double-cross Minthara without killing Ragzlin. If the raid is initiated but the goblins are instead defeated and Minthara is killed or Knocked Out , then ⁠ Defeat the Goblins is completed without killing Dror Ragzlin and Gut. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ragzlin and Minthara are first seen during the introductory cutscene to Act One , observing the Nautiloid's crash. Shattered Sanctum [ edit section | visual editor ] The first encounter with Ragzlin is during Act One in the innermost chamber of the Shattered Sanctum of the Goblin Camp , where he casts Speak with Dead on a dead mind flayer. The party can assist or hinder his attempt. After a brief dialogue, he delegates the party to Minthara while he deliberates his next move. Otherwise, the party can fight him, causing all characters in the Shattered Sanctum and Goblin Camp to become hostile, except Abdirak , Brakkal , Liam , Halsin , and Volo . If the party complete ⁠ Raid the Grove , regardless of whether they side with the tieflings or the goblins, Ragzlin and the rest of the camp will be gone from the Shattered Sanctum following the next long rest. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind Flayer Colony [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party allow Balthazar to take the Nightsong , the party is tasked with abducting Isobel . Killing or knocking her out grants an audience with Ketheric Thorm , who allows them to pray at the altar of the Absolute . Doing so results in the party to being imprisoned in pods within the Mind Flayer Colony where Balthazar tries to recycle the party into zombies. In the ensuing combat, the party must fight against Zombie Dror Ragzlin (if he died in Act One) and Zombie Minthara (if she died in Act One or was not rescued from Moonrise Towers Prison ). Range: 10 m (33 ft) Galvanise Bestow all allies within 5 m (17 ft) with an Action Surge they can spend. Range: Self Recharge: Per turn Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Booyahg Gnat Devout Cry Narvass Kagran Sharp-Eye Roo Warlock Bolt Warrior Huk Encounter details [ edit section | visual editor ] In combat, Dror Ragzlin is an aggressive barbarian who often attempts to engage in melee combat. He has access to various effects that buff nearby allies such as Leadership (and Galvanise on Honour mode), further empowering the goblin horde. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] It may be advisable to remove all of Ragzlin's allies first as they all have low hit points and are buffed by his skills if allowed to live. Afterwards, the party can face the hobgoblin himself. Ragzlin's throne room provides ample opportunities for the party to gain an advantage. One section of the room contains a wooden walkway with a "wooden support" that only has 1 hit point. Luring enemies onto the walkway and then destroying the support can be an easy way to trivialize the fight. The rafters near the ceiling provide high ground for spell-casters and archers to gain increased accuracy, as well as access to burning braziers with hinges that can be broken to drop onto enemies. Disabling or vision-reducing spells such as Darkness , Grease , or Hunger of Hadar allows the party to engage the enemy group safely from the rafters while the Difficult Terrain slows them down. If the party convince the Larger Giant Spider and Smaller Giant Spider to eat the goblins in the main hall and they survive, the spiders proceed to the area outside Ragzlin's throne room. Ragzlin can be lured out of this room to engage the spiders and give the party more allies, though this is not advised when playing Honour Mode due to the above described Arachnid Compulsion Legendary Action. There are also several Smokepowder Barrels and Firewine Barrels in the locked room near Roah Moonglow . It is possible to preemptively stack them around Dror Ragzlin and ignite them, killing him easily. Dror Ragzlin is also highly susceptible to Minor Illusion . He always returns to his throne after investigating, unless the throne is occupied by someone else, such as a party member. A series of Minor Illusions can be used to lure him to the nearby spider pit, where a Mage Hand can push him in before being dismissed. Her body is too damaged to use Speak with Dead on. Returning Droralias' Teddy Bear to the inventory of Droralias' corpse prompts special party banter. Using Speak With Dead on her sister Listelia's corpse beforehand is likely required to trigger this banter - in order to learn about the significance of the teddy bear first. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Druggag Never thought I'd end up taking in refugees. Larca Mena It's a good thing you're doing. More than most would do. Druggag I just pictured my own young'uns out on that road, no home, no shelter... It don't bear thinking about. Larca Mena How are your new guests settling in? Druggag Well enough, well enough. Though the city's been a shock to them, after all that time on the road. Larca Mena Must have been a hard walk from Elturel. They'll get used to it. Larca Mena Six children, four adults... it must be a bit of a squeeze. Druggag We manage. They didn't bring much with them, of course - not so much as a rattle for the babe. Larca Mena I can spare some things. Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayFoodCrisis_Farmer3 UUID 2388f62a-768c-41d8-a15f-37d55ff4cefe Stats Halfling_Commoner Drussuvissill is a farmer who recently arrived in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Lord Gortash promises us working folk the world then does things like this. I should've known. Arsehole. „ — Drussuvissill Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Drussuvissill is near the main entrance of Basilisk Gate Barracks in the Lower City . Alongside Asparagus Mhallie , Ploughman Zakk and Turnip Bubbs , the farmers are distraught that they must turn over their livestock to Kuthbert , who is enforcing Enver Gortash's decrees. Drussuvissill has a low opinion of Gortash and is doubtful that the farmers will be compensated for their livestock. If Gortash is defeated, Drussuvissill as well as the rest of the farmers leave, and cannot be found or interacted with again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Kuthbert Any complaints will be handled after you turn your animals over to the care of the ducal council. Turnip Bubbs And what good is that going to do us? How are we going to support ourselves? Drussuvissill My thoughts exactly - you're sentencing us all to a slow death. Ploughman Zakk Please, sir - we have children. We need to be able to provide for them. Fist Kuthbert Not my concern. Turnip Bubbs Not like we can even turn around and leave now - Absolute's hemmed us in good and proper. Fist Kuthbert Please provide a full inventory of any and all livestock before entering Baldur's Gate proper. Smuggling or any other form of deceit will not be tolerated. Drussuvissill What are you going to do - check under my skirt for any stray chickens? Fist Kuthbert All animals must be surrendered. Failure to do so will- Drussuvissill Result in a good hiding from Lord Gortash, got it. Thank you. Turnip Bubbs This is out-and-out madness. Ploughman Zakk Torm help us, what do we do? v t e Basilisk Gate Barracks Characters Civilians Amphol Asparagus Mhallie Bruha Oakhide Deeziks Tormo Drussuvissill Dryfle Doon Durm Goroy Eleganza Estra Stir Florrick Gasselblad Giftu Hudd Hasmet Hudd Hoogy Slone Kameros Lora Bergauz Luan Muttonchops Dexon Thatmatt Oakhide Thrastle Muria Turnip Bubbs Vince Torell Zakk Flaming Fists Anderson Arensen Arrinye Clover Corlos Crosse Eostre Koltz Kuthbert Liara Portyr Miller Murphy Seyama Smithwynn Thunder Williams Other Durm Goroy Florrick Vince Torell Traders Skittle Locations Heapside Prison Quests Free Counsellor Florrick Save Vanra

Technical UID S_LOW_BrokenFountain_Citizen_02 UUID ff77bda4-d645-4333-aced-9729e4d44166 Stats Dragonborn_Commoner Drybeldiyx is a dragonborn who is concerned about access to fresh water in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Bathing is going to be a problem. Last I checked, the Chionthar wasn't exactly clean. „ — Drybeldiyx Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Drybeldiyx and Garri Orne are southwest of the Blushing Mermaid , discussing their struggle to find fresh water in the Lower City . If the interacting party member is a dragonborn , Drybeldiyx suggests bathing in alcohol, except that even alcohol is no match for the humans in the city. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Drybeldiyx Don't bother. It's broken. Garri Orne This one too? This is the third fountain I've tried! Drybeldiyx Fourth for me. City's going to shit. Garri Orne Someone should report this to the gazette . Drybeldiyx If common sense can't sway them, perhaps a publicity disaster will. Garri Orne Always the way - no one fixes anything unless it hurts them personally. Drybeldiyx Can't blame them, I suppose. They've got armies to deal with. Garri Orne It's not that. It's that no politician ever went down in history for fixing the plumbing. Drybeldiyx Yes, but you do go down in history if your citizens die of thirst! v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag Support Group Adrielle Hydrangea Wubb Jatlo Kled Mayrina Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayRelief_TravelerA UUID 02f73074-a8e7-40a4-9afc-910cd0d4433f Stats Dwarf_Commoner Dryfle Doon travelled to Baldur's Gate with two companions during Act Three . “ I didn't think there'd be so many inns here - we're spoilt for choice. „ — Dryfle Doon Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Dryfle Doon arrived in the Lower City with Giftu Hudd and Hasmet Hudd . The trio fled from the Absolute and are in search of an inn. While Dryfle and Giftu are optimistic about reaching the city, Hasmet remains anxious and glum. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hasmet Hudd You do realise we can't stay here forever, don't you? Those walls might slow the army of the Absolute down, but they'll get through them sooner or later. Giftu Hudd Let's take it one day at a time, eh? You might feel differently after some food and rest. Hasmet Hudd Fools, the pair of you. Just be ready to leave when the time comes - or preferably before. Dryfle Doon Come on, old chap - I know you're hurting. But it won't bring her back, will it? Hasmet Hudd I know it won't. I just don't want to lose anyone else, all right? Giftu Hudd You won't lose us. We've come this far, haven't we? Whatever happens, we'll be right here with you. Hasmet Hudd I hope so. I really do. Giftu Hudd What's the first thing you want to do after we settle in? Dryfle Doon Sleep for a tenday. Or maybe two. Giftu Hudd Aren't you hungry? Dryfle Doon Pft, I can eat in bed. Hasmet Hudd I just hope somewhere has good dwarven beer. Don't think I'll be able to sleep without a decent drink. Dryfle Doon Look. Just look - we're finally here! We're safe. Hasmet Hudd Safe for now, at least. The army of the Absolute can't be more than a few days away. Giftu Hudd Don't be such a misery guts - we're here now, aren't we? Now they've got city walls and Steel Watchers to get through. Dryfle Doon That's the spirit! Next stop: Baldur's Gate cushiest inn! Technical UID S_MOO_Assault_PrisonMasterOfSouls_03 UUID 67e8eb20-2428-4c24-bdbd-bb19b962182a Stats Human_Cultist_Myrkul_MasterOfSouls Eqp. EQP_MasterOfSouls Trs. MOO_Cultist Duckie Verish is a necromancer [ 1 ] of the Cult of Myrkul found in Act Two . She appears in the Moonrise Towers Prison after the party launch ⁠ the assault on the cult . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Duckie is always hostile when met. Along with her allied necromancers Willinx Jindlebee and Sarabayle , she flanks the army of undead which confronts all trespassers into the prison. Unlike the Zealots, Adepts, and other members of the Cult of the Absolute , it appears Sarabayle and the other Mistresses of Souls are fully aware of what the Absolute is and the religious hoax they're perpetrating. [ 2 ] This greater understanding (and accompanying disdain) is shared by the other high-ranking Myrkulite necromancers serving Ketheric Thorm , with Kressa Bonedaughter bemoaning the weak servility of the infected she is presented with, and Balthazar using the player character's worm-infested status as an expletive. Winning the battle gains ⁠ A Bone To Pick for party members with the Soldier background. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bone Chill ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Necrotic Prevent the target from healing until your next turn. The target cannot help Downed characters. An undead target receives Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fireball ( + ) Damage: 8~48 8d6 ⁠ Fire Shoot a bright flame from your fingers that explodes upon contact, torching everything in the vicinity for 8d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Incubate Death ( ) Damage: 6~27 3d8 + 3 ⁠ Necrotic Spawn a skeletal involucre. After 1 turn, the involucre explodes, dealing 3d8 Necrotic damage and birthing a necromite. DEX Save Range: 24 m (80 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Myrkulite Scourge Damage: 3~15 1d8 + 1 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 1d6 ⁠ Necrotic Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Tenacity ( )   –   Myrkulite Scourge Damage ⁠ Bludgeoning When you miss an attack, deal ⁠ Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier anyway (minimum of 1). Tactician [ edit section | visual editor ] Shield ( + ) When you are about to be hit by an enemy, use your Reaction to increase your Armour Class by 5. You also take no damage from Magic Missile . These effects last until the start of your next turn. She can be found in the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Duddamoor is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Phanellis , Fist Halantow and a Steel Watcher . Their route runs up and down the stairs of the Heapside district, from the main entrance to Felogyr's Fireworks X: 16 Y: -123 to the entrance of the Baldur's Mouth X: 74 Y: -69 . Duddamoor and her mates do not respond to any attempts to speak with them, regardless of whether the Steel Watch Foundry is intact or destroyed. Cashguard Yonni Docks Sentry is the worst damn job at the House. Cashguard Dugg What's so bad about it? Cashguard Yonni It's boring, plus it's boring, and also it's boring. Cashguard Dugg I like it, though. Nice view. Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_Patrols_003_FF_002 UUID 49e23622-8969-445f-892a-21561ef3db80 Stats NPC_FlamingFist_Melee_Cleric Fist Healer Duranga is a dwarven healer and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found on the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Duranga is patrolling the streets of the Lower City with Fist Brandella , Fist Okralope and a Steel Watcher . Their route runs forth and back from the Stormshore Armoury , across the square in front of the Sorcerous Sundries and to the crossroads near the Devil's Fee (approximately from X: -16 Y: -21 to X: -31 Y: -85 ). Duranga and her fellow Fists do not respond to any attempts to speak with them, regardless of whether the Steel Watch Foundry is intact or destroyed. Technical UID S_LOW_RefugeeHostel_Child UUID b3c4924a-fb46-4c58-ae10-c239a0df4ff6 Stats Human_Child Dwindling is a human child who can be found in Nortale's Hostel in the Lower City in Act Three . “ The soap here smells funny. „ — Dwindling Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwindling and his father Dholber Greene are refugees speaking to the hostel's mistress, Pammella Nortale , in the hall of the establishment. The family lost their mother, and the father does not know how to properly care for Dwindling. The hostel mistress is ready to shelter both, but first wants them to get rid of the lice which the boy has caught on the way to the city. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale Rules are the same for everyone: clothes go in the fire, comb goes through the hair. We'll have no lice in here. Dholber Greene Burn my son's clothes? But I've nothing else for him to wear. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale We've plenty of donations. I'm sure you'll find something that fits. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale No need to look so glum. You'll be clean and comfortable in no time. Dholber Greene I'm so embarrassed. I - I'm sorry. We must have caught them riding on the ox cart. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale No sense apologising for what can't be helped. You made it here safely - that's what matters. Dwindling Dad - my head's itchy. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale Hot soapy water and a fine-tooth comb - that's all you need. Those lice will be gone in no time. Dholber Greene His mother was better with this kind of thing... BG_Bandit The Dying Stone Lord Thug is a Human character who is a member of the Stone Lord's crew in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dying Stone Lord Thug is on the shore of the River Chionthar , down the cliff and almost under the monumental bridge on which Wyrm's Crossing is located at X: -141 Y: 73 . He is sitting leaned against a low hedge with a knife deep in his guts. On approaching him, the party can speak to the Thug, but only to watch him inevitably die after a couple of phrases. However, the Dying Stone Lord Thug can be one of disguises that Orin the Red takes to mock and toy with the player character. [ 1 ] In this case, the dialogue with the Thug is longer and more meaningful. Throughout the dialogue, the player character has to roll a passive DC 20 Perception Check . If succeeded, they feel that the dying thug for some reason seems to be reveling in his miserable Gravely Wounded condition. As with other cases of her taking various disguises in Rivington , Orin tries to wheedle out from the player character any hint of shared understanding with her mindset, more so in case of playing as The Dark Urge origin. Whatever the player character chooses to say or to do, after three or four phrases Orin transforms to her true appearance and, after another couple of spiteful phrases, disappears. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ This can be determined with right-click on the character, choosing to 'Examine' him. If the Thug is actually disguised Orin, the character has her level, stats and passive features. Technical UID S_LOW_FireworksDare_Teen_02 UUID 8f6c2802-6dc2-421e-aaef-56d7c91fe5c7 Stats Human_Child Dyrovell is a human child in the Steeps district of the Lower City in Act Three . “ Twelve, thirteen, fourteen - rats, I'm short. „ — Dyrovell Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Dyrovell, together with her tiefling friend Rascal Borys can be found on a stone-paved space in front of Felogyr's Fireworks shop. They are standing near the main entrance to the fireworks shop, counting their pocket money, planning to buy a huge firework and throw it at some Flaming Fist guard or even a Steel Watcher . The idea seems to be their common interest, and now each is trying to persuade the other to do the actual mischief. However, both are lacking coin to obtain something they want. If spoken to, Dyrovell ponders on saving pocket money for another tenday to purchase a bigger firework than she can afford right now. v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag CRE_Gith_Generic Youth Dyrr'kas is a member of a new githyanki generation hatched and raised in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Maybe when the patrol comes back I can learn what the outside's like. „ — Dyrr'kas Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Dyrr'kas is in the Crèche Infirmary , wandering around the room and occasionally cleaning. If spoken to, he expresses interest in the player character’s appearance, alien to him, and also says that in his opinion wandering wherever you want is interesting. If the interacting party member is githyanki, Dyrr’kas mentions they differ from the Creche’s inhabitants, and supposes that he might learn what the world outside of the Crèche is like once the patrol returns. Technical UID S_WYR_SharessCaress_BoastingCrooks_RivingtonRat UUID 59f97331-f6bc-45b5-bf21-03ea4341e99e Stats WYR_SharessCaress_Dwarf_Rogue Eqp. EQP_Dagger_Leather Trs. BG_Commoner Earspoon is a dwarven member of the Rivington rats visiting Sharess' Caress in Wyrm's Crossing . He is whispering to Borgus Elamin . “ I want to be sandwiched between a pair of nymphs. „ — Earspoon when asked about Nine-Fingers History [ edit section | visual editor ] According to Wyrm's Rock Prison's Prison Log , Earspoon was previously arrested for indecent exposure but was released by Enver Gortash . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Earspoon is whispering to Borgus in the rear of Sharess' Caress. Approaching them triggers a passive DC 15 History Check (with Rogues and Baldurians having advantage) and a DC 10 Deception Check or DC 15 Perception Check to determine they are talking about Nine-Fingers Keene . The party can then ask Earspoon where Nine-Fingers is by passing one of these ability checks: [PERSUASION]  Come on, level with me. I'm not about to sell out another dwarf. (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  I bet a few coins would loosen your tongue. (DC 15) [ROGUE] [PERSUASION]  I'm looking to join the Guild. How about you point me the way? (DC 18  ) [FIGHTER] [PERSUASION]  I need work, and it sounds like Nine-Fingers needs steel.  (DC 18  ) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read the dwarf's mind. I need to talk to Nine-Fingers about Zenovia. He can be found in the Wyrm's Rock Fortress in Act Three . “ Absolute's army won't stand a chance. Gortash'll crush 'em like roaches under his boot. „ — Earthdigger Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Earthdigger with several other Flaming Fists ( Fist Bella , Fist Diallo , Fist Fernhollow , Fist Klaas , Fist Kyberos and Fist Quickstitch ) is standing watch in the Audience Hall of the Wyrm’s Rock Fortress at the ceremony of Enver Gortash being ordained as an Archduke of Baldur's Gate . He is guarding the door to an outer balcony at X: 15 Y: 190 . If spoken to, Earthdigger calls Gortash a true leader and expresses excitement with him achieving the title of an Archduke. He also is sure of the victory over the Absolute’s army under Gortash's marshalling. Technical UID S_END_LastStandGuard_004 UUID 99d89d39-9ef8-466b-8eb7-1776fed67b4a Stats END_CityWatchMelee_Human Watchman Ebber is a member of the The Watch in the Upper City in Act Three . He attempts to flee the High Hall's courtyard after it has been overrun by forces belonging to the Absolute . “ We're going back in - we're really going back in. I'm not ready... „ — Ebber Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the initial battle for High Hall, a large force of Absolutist cultists coming from the Upper City Sewers destroyed and routed the City Watch away from the keep, forcing what is left of the Watch to flee. [ 1 ] Faced with severe casualties, the last remnants of the Watch are composed of Ebber, Fry , Goodge , Gyordi , Matthew , and Preyn . A Mind Flayer kills Matthew and Preyn as the Watchmen try to flee from High Hall, before being confronted with the party. If a Mind Flayer (be it the player character, Karlach , The Emperor , or Orpheus ) is present, Ebber and the remaining Watchmen led by Gyordi are frightened of the party. Succeeding a passive DC 20 Insight Check allows the option to have the remaining Watchmen fight at the party's side. A Mind Flayer player character can convince them to partake in the ensuing battle as allies with a DC 18 Persuasion , Intimidation , or Strength Check . A non-Mind Flayer must pass a DC 20 Persuasion , Intimidation , Deception , or Strength Check to convince them. If the party's Mind Flayer is too far away and dialogue starts with the Watchmen oblivious to it, every class except Wizard also get either a special DC 20 Arcana , Insight , Persuasion , Intimidation , or Deception Check to convince them, or two generic DC 20 Wisdom or Persuasion Checks . If the interacting party member passes any of these checks, Gyordi rallies the rest of the Watchmen, and encourages them to fight with the party during the courtyard battle. Ebber and the rest of the named Watchmen's armour is similar in appearance to the Breastplate +1 dyed in blue, brown, and black colours, rather than the plate armour specifically designed and seen on the rest of The Watch . Ebber also wears the Watch's Helmet ; the only one to do so. Technical UID LOW_OskarsBeloved_KerriSpirit UUID b2fe9ed6-c6b4-43fe-af6a-e463c5ae33cd Stats LOW_OskarsBeloved_Spirit Echo of a Lost Love is the ghost of Kerri Evenfield who was Oskar Fevras's past girlfriend. “ Why does everything have to revolve around Oskar Fevras? „ — Echo of a Lost Love Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Once the party destroys the cursed portrait in the atelier in Lady Jannath's Estate during ⁠ Free the Artist , Kerri appears and rushes downstairs to confront Oskar Fevras and Lady Jannath . She is enraged at Oskar and wants to drag him back to the afterlife with her unless the party attacks her or convinces her otherwise using Persuasion or Intimidation. On a failed roll, she'll attack the party with two Vengeful Souls and two Tormented Souls . If the party chose to persuade or intimidate her instead of fight, then she becomes confused and starts to wonder why she is here in the first place. Oskar desires to know why she committed suicide and the party can either choose to let her leave or explain using Persuasion or Intimidation checks. If the check is passed successfully, Kerri reveals that she always just saw Oskar as a fling, nothing more. She killed herself out of depression rather than heartbreak, and is disgusted that Oskar dragged her all the way back to the land of the living because of his own vain assumption that her death was his fault. Kerri then leaves for the afterlife, happy to rest in peace at last. Technical UID S_LOW_MurderTribunal_MurderMerchant UUID 68a568cd-1e5e-46f1-9c5f-53d3eed23bd5 Stats LOW_Abazigal Eqp. EQP_Greatsword Trs. LOW_MurderTribunal_Merchant Echo of Abazigal is a ghost of a blue dragon Bhaalspawn . His ghost is disguised as a dragonborn. He was one of the members of the Five during the Bhaalspawn crisis . “ ...We led our worship by killing the weakest of our own line.... We hunted down his insipid fledglings in droves, until we were all that was left. All but Sarevok's own murderer, who murdered me in turn. „ — Echo of Abazigal , on his past life Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Backstory [ edit section | visual editor ] In life Abazigal was once a Bhaalspawn and a member of the Five, which was an alliance between five powerful Bhaalspawns formed by Amelyssan , Bhaal's high priestess, that sought to slaughter their siblings in exchange for power. Like the rest of the Five, he was defeated by his sibling and fellow Bhaalspawn "Gorion's Ward" and their party at his lair. Bhaal was resurrected a century after Abazigal's death. After this Sarevok Anchev was able to bring Abazigal back as an Echo to serve in the Murder Tribunal along with Illasera , Sendai and Amelyssan . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] After completing ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal and becoming an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal, Echo of Abazigal appears in the main chamber. There he can traded with and further questioned about The Five and his personal history. If killed during the fight with Sarevok his Bhaalspawn Essence: Abazigal causes Sarevok to do maximum damage with all his attacks. Also, his stock cannot be looted after the fight, since he is a spirit and thus disappears upon death. Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to LOW_MurderTribunal_Merchant . Abazigal cannot be pickpocketed normally. [ See Notes ] Bhaalist Gloves Bhaalist Armour Assassin of Bhaal Cowl Craterflesh Gloves Vicious Battleaxe Dolor Amarus Dread Iron Dagger Fleshrender Vicious Shortbow Crawler Mucus Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal ⁠ Investigate the Murders Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] There is an exploit to pickpocket Abazigal's inventory, despite not being able to pickpocket him directly. While talking to Sarevok , selecting the "I'm ready to be judged" dialog option results in the ghost of a previously killed character appearing before the tribunal. Switching to another character and pickpocketing this temporary ghost reveals a copy of Abazigal's inventory. Whether this is intentional or not is unknown, but it remains possible as of Patch 8 . Failing the pickpocket check turns the entire tribunal hostile. Technical UID S_LOW_MurderTribunal_Amelyssan UUID eca47258-a8ad-4453-a12a-3f39f8e1ca32 Stats LOW_Amelyssan Echo of Amelyssan is a ghost of the former high priestess of Bhaal . She was the main antagonist of Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal . “ I am Amelyssan the Blackhearted. I stood as Bhaal's high priestess - his eternal succour. Until I sought to usurp him. „ — Echo of Amelyssan Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Backstory [ edit section | visual editor ] In life, Amelyssan was once the high priestess of Bhaal . Before his death, Bhaal charged Amelyssan with the ritual needed to bring him back to life. When Bhaal perished in the Time of Troubles, Amelyssan sought to complete her task, not for her fallen god but for herself, as she had later discovered that the divine essence of the slain Bhaalspawn would flow through her, increasing her power. In her new guise as Melyssan, she sought to gather the Bhaalspawn by presenting herself as their kind protector. In secret, however, she convinced five powerful Bhaalspawn – Abazigal a blue dragon, Balthazar a human monk, Illasera an elven fighter, Sendai a drow cleric, and Yaga-Shura a fire giant – to unite and help her resurrect Bhaal with the promise that Bhaal would make them his right hand and they would rule as demigods. The Five unleashed their armies upon the Sword Coast killing Bhaalspawn and innocents alike in their path. Those Bhaalspawn that managed to escape the massacre were guided by Amelyssan to the city of Saradush in Tethyr , but the city was encircled by Yaga Shura and his army. In Saradush, Amelyssan met Gorion's Ward, the famous Bhaalspawn that had defeated Sarevok Anchev . She then began using Gorion's Ward as a tool to achieve her goal. She tricked them into meeting the ruler of Saradush who was also a Bhaalspawn which resulted in the latter's death and sent them to an old abandoned Bhaal temple where Yaga-Shura was raised, to discover a way to remove Yaga-Shura's invulnerability. Gorion's Ward succeeded in their task but returned too late, as Saradush and its inhabitants fell to the invading army due to Amelyssan having opened the way for Yaga-Shura. Gorion's Ward and their allies fought the fire giant and managed to put an end to him. After Yaga-Shura's death, Amelyssan convinced them to deal with the rest of the Five and revealed the locations of Abazigal and Sendai, telling them to use the village of Amkethran as their base of operations. She told them to seek her ally Balthazar, the ruler of Amkethran, for additional aid, who unbeknownst to Gorion's Ward was the the final member of the Five. While Gorion's Ward was away dealing with Abazigal and Sendai, Amelyssan approached Balthazar in his monastery, but the monk turned on her and tried to capture her, though she escaped. Gorion's Ward returned to Amkethran to deal with Balthazar at his monastery after they had learned that he was the last member of the Five. With Balthazar dead, Amelyssan now had all of Bhaal's divine essence and went to the Mana Forge in the Throne of Bhaal to begin her ascension into godhood. The empowered Amelyssan was confronted by Gorion's Ward and their allies at the Mana Forge and fought her, defeating the traitorous priestess. Gorion's Ward was given a choice on what to do with the essence of Bhaal and chose to be free of it and be locked away in the Upper Planes. A weakened Amelyssan tried to stop the divine essence from leaving, but died when the Mana Forge imploded. Bhaal was resurrected a century later after Amelyssan's death. After this Sarevok Anchev was able to bring her back as an Echo to serve in the Murder Tribunal along with Abazigal, Illasera and Sendai. However, unlike her fellow Echoes, she saw this as a slave sentence and punishment for her betrayal. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Amelyssan is in the Murder Tribunal, where she accompanies Sarevok . If the player character refuses to become an Unholy Assassin or performs any hostile actions she becomes hostile. If the player character instead completes ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal and becomes an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal, she can be questioned to learn more about her history. If the party chooses to fight the Murder Tribunal and the Echo of Amelyssan is destroyed before Sarevok, he gains the condition Absorbed Essence: Amelyssan . If Sarevok is killed first, the Echo of Amelyssan gains Retributive Justice instead. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Warding Bond ( + ) Ward an ally. They gain resistance to all damage, and a +1 bonus to their Armour Class and Saving Throws . Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Sanctuary ( + ) You or an ally cannot be targeted until you attack or harm a creature. You can still take damage from area spells. Until the affected entity attacks or harms another creature, it cannot be targeted by enemy attacks. However, it can still take damage from spells that influence a larger area. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Heal ( + ) Healing: 70 70 ⁠ Healing Heals a target's wounds and remove Blindness and any diseases. She was one of the members of the Five during the Bhaalspawn crisis and was the first of them to have been defeated by Gorion's Ward. “ I am Illasera the Quick. Child of Bhaal. Slayer of his idle children. Cut down before my time. „ — Echo of Illasera Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Backstory [ edit section | visual editor ] In life, Illasera was once a Bhaalspawn and a member of the Five which was an alliance between five powerful Bhaalspawns formed by Amelyssan , Bhaal's high priestess, that sought to slaughter their siblings in exchange for power. Illasera was tasked to kill the famous Bhaalspawn known as Gorion's Ward and ambushed them and their party at the Grove of the Ancients . The two fought, but Gorion's Ward ultimately defeated Illasera, making her the first of the Five to have been slain. Bhaal was resurrected a century after Illasera's death. After this Sarevok Anchev was able to bring her back as an Echo to serve in the Murder Tribunal along with Abazigal , Sendai and Amelyssan. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Illasera is in the Murder Tribunal, where she accompanies Sarevok . If the player character refuses to become an Unholy Assassin or performs any hostile actions she becomes hostile. If the player character instead completes ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal and becomes an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal, she can be questioned to learn more about her history. If the party chooses to fight the Murder Tribunal and the Echo of Illasera is destroyed before Sarevok, he gains the condition Absorbed Essence: Illasera . If Sarevok is killed first, the Echo of Illasera gains Retributive Justice instead. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Echo of Illasera can cast spells using up to Level 6 Spell Slots . Haste ( + ) Target yourself or an ally to become Hastened . The creature has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed is doubled, and can take one additional Action per turn. Range: 9 m (30 ft) Counterspell ( + ) Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Fly ( ) Fly to a target position Range: 18 m (60 ft) After Sarevok dies and Retributive Justice is gained [ edit section | visual editor ] Guiding Bolt ( + ) Damage: 4~24 4d6 ⁠ Radiant The next attack roll against this target has Advantage . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Spirit Guardians ( + ) Call forth spirits to protect you. Nearby enemies take 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant or 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage per turn, and their Movement Speed is halved. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_Edenosa_Cracklewall UUID 980f2182-100a-4c30-9965-5bbae804a511 Stats FlamingFist_Gnome_Cleric Manip Edenosa is a gnome cleric , a Manip of the Flaming Fist and a True Soul . She can found in the Lower City during Act Three . “ -- You know us - absolute WILL --- Absolute power --- „ — Edenosa , dominated by the Elder Brain Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Edenosa initially is standing watch at the western entrance to the Bloomridge Park , while her subordinates, Fist Pard and Fist Bella , patrol the area nearby. As a True Soul, she is quite aware of the Bhaal cultists preparing an ambush deeper in the park, but does not know that they have Orin's personal orders to eliminate the party in the first place, and anyone else as a collateral damage (and an offering to Bhaal) only. Depending on the party previous actions, the dialogue with Edenosa might run in several ways. If the party do not know about the cultists or failed the Perception check to spot an ambush, Edenosa warns them to leave the park, hinting that the area is a dangerous place right now. During the dialogue, the player character feels that Edenosa is infected with a tadpole. The Flaming Fist, in her turn, recognizes a fellow True Soul, tells them about "the Absolute's warriors at work" and asks not to interfere. If the party successfully spotted the ambush, but did not engage in the battle with the cultists, and try to report to Edenosa the suspicious activity in the park, she still reveals herself as a True Soul to them, but agrees to look into the situation or confirms that she knows about the cultists (depending on whether the player character has spoken to her previously or not). Regardless of the course of the conversation, if the party get into a fight with the cultists, Edenosa intervenes part way through the fight. The leader of the cultists calls her "defective", and the Flaming Fist joins the battle, siding with the party, along with any other Fist who patrols the park and spots the fight. If Edenosa survives the battle, the Netherbrain afterwards speaks to the player character through her, entreating the party to kill any remaining of the Dead Three . Edenosa then dies from the mind strain. Connecting with the Netherbrain in this manner grants the ⁠ Urgent Communications inspiration event to any party member with the Soldier background. After death, Edenosa can be looted for a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen . If Edenosa dies during the ambush, then Fist Griff is used by the Netherbrain to communicate with the player character in her stead, allowing mostly the same conversation to take place. Technical UID S_FOR_PriestConqueringGod_003 UUID 21507c79-dfea-421a-b149-4b5646d3941d Stats FOR_TrueSoul Eqp. EQP_Unarmed Trs. FOR_DeathOfATrueSoul_TrueSoul Edowin is a True Soul of the Absolute . He was searching the Wilderness with Andrick and Brynna for survivors of the Nautiloid Wreck to locate a weapon. “ They are a True Soul. Mind them. They will - they - they... „ — Edowin , commending his siblings to the player Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Edowin is in the Forest at X: 139 Y: 446 dying from wounds sustained from an Owlbear attack. When the party initiate a conversation with his siblings Edowin's tadpole can, with certain conversation choices, connect with that of the player character's. He asks them to protect Andrick and Brynna. Edowin inevitably dies from his wounds and cannot be saved by healing. After Edowin dies, the voice of the Dream Visitor prompts the player character to further examine his body and encourages them to recover a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen from him. If the player character declines to collect the tadpole, it attempts to flee, rushing down the hill and disappearing within one environmental turn. Turn-based mode can be entered quickly after interacting with Edowin's corpse to allow the party to attack the loosed tadpole. This grants 10 XP . Tadpole interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Let your body guide you - welcome the tadpole's influence. Gain Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen [STRENGTH]  The tadpole is toying with you. Resist it.  (DC 12) Success: The tadpole attempts to flee. Failure: Gain Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen [WISDOM]  Force your mind shut. You will not be influence by an illithid parasite.  (DC 12) Success: The tadpole attempts to flee. Failure: Gain Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen As The Dark Urge : There are different dialogue options which require no checks but have similar effects. Whatever the outcome, the party members are also rewarded 30 XP. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen Shaft of a Broken Spear Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Edowin can be spoken to with Speak with Dead . Who are you? Edowin Edowin... a True Soul... a Chosen... Who 'chose' you? Edowin The Absolute... the almighty goddess... What can you tell me about the Absolute? Edowin Do not... fight her. Power... such power... Is there anything valuable around here? Edowin Brynna... Andrick... Who are Brynna and Andrick? Edowin Sister... brother... my job... to protect them... What were you doing here? Edowin Looking... for Her weapon... the Absolute... What do you know about this weapon? Edowin Crashed... from the sky... taken... by infidels... What can you tell me about the Absolute? Edowin Do not... fight her. Technical UID S_WYR_South_Guard_004 UUID e572c6d1-3330-46fd-9ecc-da318f499956 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Cleric Eqp. EQP_Warhammer_Scalemail_Shield_Fist Trs. BG_Guard Gauntlet Edwynna is a human cleric and a member of the Flaming Fist . She guards the South Span Checkpoint between Rivington and Wyrm's Crossing during Act Three . “ Right. Article 30.1.5 of the Council's Decree on Extraordinary Wartime Measures. I am confiscating that. The city thanks you for your contribution. „ — Edwynna accepting the party's admission fee Contents 1 Involvement 2 Companion approval 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Loot 4 Related Literature 5 Notes and references Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Edwynna leads the squad guarding the South Span Checkpoint . She must be spoken with to use the gate entrance to Wyrm's Crossing. [ 2 ] If a party member tries to enter Wyrm's Crossing through the checkpoint, the nearby guards direct them to Edwynna for passage. Edwynna explains that refugees are not allowed to enter the city, but lets the party through with a 200 gold "fee" as a proof that they have the means to support themselves. She then asks for the player character's name and business in the city: I have an urgent message for Duke Ulder Ravengard. [DECEPTION]  I was born and raised in Baldur's Gate. This is my home. (DC 10) [DARK URGE] [DECEPTION]  I need to pass. I'm a Baldurian. My Father is already inside, he's waiting for me! (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  I need to pass. I was born and raised in Baldur's Gate. This is my home. (DC 10) [DARK URGE] [BALDURIAN]  I came from Baldur's Gate - my old home is there... somewhere... [DARK URGE] [BALDURIAN]  Please, let me pass. I need to find my old home. I'm a Baldurian! [BALDURIAN]  Baldur's Gate is my city, my home. [BALDURIAN]  Please, let me pass. Baldur's Gate is my city, my home. [FIGHTER]  I'm here to enlist - figured the Fist could use a hand. [WIZARD] [DECEPTION]  I am an envoy from the First Reader of Candlekeep. I come for knowledge. (DC 10) [MONK] [DECEPTION]  I'm on a pilgrimage to the city - I walked barefoot from the Rosymorn Monastery. (DC 10) [DRUID] [DECEPTION]  I wish to behold the Sea of Swords and commune with its water spirits. (DC 10) [RANGER] [DECEPTION]  I'm following the trail of a deadly beast - it escaped into the city.  (DC 10) [ROGUE] [DECEPTION]  I've been hired by Baldurian nobility for a task requiring discretion . (DC 10) [CLERIC] [DECEPTION]  My presence has been requested by the local temple. (DC 10) [BARD] [DECEPTION]  Baldur's Gate is the next stop on my Faerûn-wide poetry tour. (DC 10) [BARBARIAN] [DECEPTION]  I'm here for the Faerûn tavern brawl championships. (DC 10) [SORCERER] [DECEPTION]  I suspect the source of my limitless arcane power resides in this city. (DC 10) [OATHBREAKER] [PALADIN] [DECEPTION]  An immutable oath compels me to enter this city. (DC 10) [WARLOCK] [DECEPTION]  I'm just here to purchase an eldritch tome of immense magical power. (DC 10) Regardless of the option chosen, if the party does not attack they must submit to the nearby Steel Watcher , who performs a scan of the party, granting the ⁠ New Normal to party members with the Sage background. If they are found to be enemies of the Absolute , the interacting party member (usually the player character) must submit to arrest or attack. If the party successfully completed ⁠ Rescue Wulbren , then regardless of what dialogue is chosen, two Ironhand Gnomes , Nimble and Laridda , appear, throw a Flashblinder bomb, and then escape to Angleiron's Cellar . The blinded guards can then be bypassed. If the party cannot benefit from the gnomes' help and consents to be arrested, they are immediately moved to a cell in Wyrm's Rock Prison , where they can use various ways to escape. Any means of doing so imposes the Fugitive condition for 20 turns. After that, the party can freely explore the Wyrm's Rock Fortress and Wyrm's Crossing: the guards will treat them as other citizens eligible to cross the checkpoint in any direction. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Choosing certain options while speaking with Edwynna and further while being scanned by a Steel Watcher might grant following points of approval from various companions. Technical UID S_HAG_HagLair_Victim_001 UUID 48062828-eb14-43ab-ac97-3d7ed6cb2ecd Stats HAG_Victim_Fighter Eqp. EQP_GreatAxe_ScaleMail Trs. HAG_HagVictim_Traveler Efrin is one of Auntie Ethel's victims. He is in a petrified state in the Entrance Gallery of the Overgrown Tunnel near the Blinded Elf . “ My dearest Efrin, he begged me to halt the deadly disease that ravaged him. „ — Auntie Ethel about Efrin's fate Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] A party member can interact with Efrin when he is petrified, or after Auntie Ethel is killed. However, defeating Ethel without killing her - such as accepting Auntie Ethel's Hair in exchange for her freedom - does not lift the curse. Using a Basilisk Oil potion is needed to cure him of the status condition. Before or without killing the Hag [ edit section | visual editor ] When the party first meets Efrin, he is petrified . Using a Basilisk Oil potion at his feet cures him of the status condition and initiates a conversation with him. He reveals he has a disease called "The Bite" (also called Laduguer's Bite). Efrin yells at the party for 'saving' him while the disease is not cured and immediately dies. Casting Speak with Dead on Efrin after he dies provides more information about his life including his surname and family status. After killing the Hag [ edit section | visual editor ] After killing the hag, Efrin's curse is broken and his petrification ends. He begins a conversation with the party immediately, warning that he has a disease called "The Bite": Efrin I was on death's door. But now I feel... I feel great. How? [PALADIN OF ILLMATER] [CLERIC OF ILLMATER]  Search for any sign of Laduguer's Bite. [ARCANA]  Look for remnants of the hag's magic.  (DC 15) [MEDICINE]  Examine him for signs of Laduguer's Bite.  (DC 15)  (Non-duergar only) [DUERGAR] [MEDICINE]  Examine him for signs of Laduguer's Bite. (DC 10) [BARD]  In the tales, hags always cook up their victim's misery first, then sell them false hope. [SORCERER]  Attune with your blood and search him for magic. [SORCERER]  I can feel the hag's magic on you - it tastes of sickness. [WIZARD]  Mordenkainen warns us that hags often cause their victims' tragedies. [WIZARD]  Examine him for signs of magic. Picking one of the above options reveals the curse was actually a magical infliction caused by the hag, that Efrin is free and does not actually have Laduguer's Bite . He curses the hag, swearing that he will repay the party for his freedom, and escapes from the tunnel. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Bottle Gold Greataxe Scale Mail Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Efrin's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Cured? Were you sick? Efrin I'd the Bite... Laduguer's Bite... sickness worse than... death. Efrin Hag turned me... to stone. Stopped the... spread. What is your name? Efrin Efrin... Hammerborn... What happened to you? Efrin Got sick... had to leave home... leave my children... Efrin ... wonder what... they look like now... What can you tell me about the hag? Efrin She'll give you more... than you bargained... for... Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Efrin's family portrait. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_Reaper_05 UUID a2bcb302-7a7b-4206-ac93-54b755bcb4d8 Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_Reaper Reaper of Bhaal Eglantine is a human member of the Cult of Bhaal , found in the Bhaal Temple within the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . “ If you care for anyone up above - tell them to start running. I like a chase. „ — Eglantine , to the companion of the Dark Urge who embraced Bhaal Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can go to the Bhaal Temple in hopes of saving their companion from Orin . There they encounter Orin, who engages the party in combat by transforming into a Slayer . Eglantine, along with the rest of the reapers, begin channeling a ritual spell Bloody Favour , granting Orin a Boon of Bhaal at the start of every turn. If the player character is not the Dark Urge , and Orin is killed or disabled, Eglantine ends concentration and attacks the party as normal. If the player character is the Dark Urge and defeats Orin, Eglantine remains neutral to the party and moves to the foot of one of the stairs leading to the central altar ground. Her one-liners depend on whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. GOB_Goblin_Kid_Looter Eight is a goblin child in the Goblin Camp . “ Stupid, dead bastard. Give him a good kicin' - he deserves it! „ — Eight cursing at the body of his parents killer Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Eight is on the eastern most side of the Goblin Camp along the cliff where Brawler Rancer is stationed. Eight wears a Leather helmet and stands over the corpse of a dead adventurer, along with two other goblin children, Four and Five . Eight vents his anger on the dead adventurer for killing his parents. He invites Four and Five to join in kicking the body. Despite complaining about being an orphan, Eight has little care for his dead parents, who he views as weak for dying and even wants to kill them himself one day. If the party tries to loot the body, Eight confronts the party, claiming the corpse is his. The party can tell him off by passing an ability check: [DROW]  Nothing is yours. Find another corpse. [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  I'll do what I want - and you will find another corpse. [DECEPTION]  Boss' orders. I'm collecting his loot. (DC 15) [INTIMIDATION]  Or what? I'll run you through before you can cry for your mother. (DC 10) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  ROAR.  (DC 10  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Try and stop me.  (DC 10  ) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read the child's mind. You're wasting your time with this one. There are corpses outside with far more loot. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Eight, Four, and Five immediately escape without joining the fight when attacked, though they can still be killed during their escape. This is a rare exception to the game's standard treatment of minor NPCs; human and tiefling children can only be Knocked Out , and any narrative deaths they suffer (such as during the Raid on the Emerald Grove ) occur strictly off-screen. As a Small Humanoid of 10 kg, Eight's corpse is one of the lightest that can be used for both Fungal Infestation and Animate Dead . v t e Goblin Camp Characters Bugbears Bao'ek'nuk Stimk Teghun Camp Followers Owlbear Cub Volo Companions Halsin Minthara Goblins Aggy Azak Bal Bez Birka Bolt Brakkal Breg Clack Crub Crusher Cry Culk Druk Dullwill Eef Fezk Glomp Gnat Greez Gribbo Grikka Grush Gruz Gurd Gurk Huk Kirz Klagga Krolla Mirg Mrak Muzul Nass Neem Nik-Nuk Nozk Nrog Olak Piddle Plagg Plig Puce Puli Raagg Rancer Rindle Roo Rot Rozzak Sazza Shekt Sluck Snurd Spike Skrut Sul Tak Tiny Tizg Tozad Trinzas Tud Vrak Wasp Zami Zurga Zurk Children Eight Five Four One Three Goblin Leaders Dror Ragzlin Gut Minthara Ogres Gurgon Polma Traders Grat Roah Moonglow Other Abdirak Andrick Brynna Dishevelled Chicken Erna Ferr Larger Giant Spider Kagran Klaw Liam Narvass Smaller Giant Spider Small Klaw Smythin Taeglyn Tale Yerle Locations Bloodied Shrine Defiled Temple Goblin Camp Shattered Sanctum Worg Pens Quests Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Defeat the Goblins Find a Cure Find the Nightsong Raid the Emerald Grove Rescue the Druid Halsin Rescue Volo Save the First Druid Save the Goblin Sazza Save the Refugees Travel to Moonrise Towers

Her route runs forth and back from eastern to western entrance to the park, approximately from X: -90 Y: -61 to X: -128 Y: -51 . Elda can only be encountered if the party take a long rest after dispatching the Bhaalists’ ambush near the park fountain, replacing Fist Bella and Fist Pard , who patrolled the location prior. If spoken to, Elda asks the party to stay aware and also laments that extra guards would dissuade commoners from taking a stroll in the park. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_Cultist_01 UUID 9f7607e0-abae-4722-921a-e18ee01b8984 Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_NightBlade Night Blade Elda is a human Night Blade who can be found at the Bhaal Temple in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . “ Shhh. Silence is good. No screaming. No crying. No pleading. No air escapes. „ — Elda (Night Blade) Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Elda is in the Bhaal Temple in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . She patrols the upper balcony of the temple, near the entrance, and never descends to the central altar ground. When spoken with, Elda talks about how silence is good, and that when she "squeezes", she "makes sure they're quiet". Elda remains neutral to the party unless attacked, regardless of whether or not the player character is the Dark Urge or Orin is killed. Of all things, Elda likes silence most, and relishes in "making them all quiet". Thus, she prefers to strangle her victims. If the player character is the Dark Urge, she complains to them of Orin's endless prattle about them. After the fight, she is indifferent to whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy – the only thing she cares for is Orin's newfound silence. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_RetiredFist_Elf01 UUID 08d2d3a7-6d87-40e7-8649-750e9857dd3c Stats Elf_Commoner Eldaernth is a retired Flaming Fist who believes in the new Fist cohort. Eldaernth can be found with a group of retirees in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Don't listen to Vistra. She talks big for a short, old dwarf - those 'good ol' days' weren't all rosy. „ — Eldaernth Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Eldaernth is in Bloomridge Park attempting to challenge Vistra's views of the Flaming Fist. While Vistra is cynical of the current Fists, Eldaernth believes they are doing the best they can, given the circumstances. Avourel and Thokki occasionally comment on their views. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Vistra ' Absolute ' this... 'end of the world' that... These young folk've no idea how good they've got it. Eldaernth Come off it, Vistra. You've been doing this same rant for years. Avourel Yeah, the first lot of young folk you said it about are old folk now! Vistra Piss off, the lot of youse. Eldaernth You're remembering the past pretty fondly, Vistra. Bit too fondly. Vistra What d'you mean? Eldaernth You telling me you'd have refused the Steel Watch's help on Returning Day a decade ago? Vistra You'll, uh... remind me? Eldaernth Big horrible beast? Slaughtered Duke Adrian? We could do bugger all about it? Thokki Lost a lot of good men that day. Vistra You make a good point, Eldaernth. Eldaernth You've known me long enough, Vistra. When haven't I? Vistra We could've used the Steel Watch back in the day. But that's because we fought actual threats. Back when the Fists were real Fists. Not bloody... Avourel Limp gloves. Eldaernth So, Vistra. You reckon we'd still be better Fists than the current cohort? Vistra Peace of piss, mate. Easy. Yes. Eldaernth Great. So let's get you out of that chair and into your chain mail, then? Show the young lot how it's done? Vistra Uh... Well... Thokki My armour's not fit for years. Avourel Yeah, to be honest? Thought of holding a pike makes my back ache. Eldaernth It's a young man's game. Right, Vistra? Vistra 'Spose. Vistra Look, all I'm saying is they've got it easier these days. Thokki Yeah, we didn't have these big metal bastards running the streets back in my day. Eldaernth Thanks to the bloody Iron Crisis we barely had any metal back then. Vistra You're right, you're right. We Fists had to proper fight back then. We knew how to watch each other's backs. Eldaernth Helm give me strength. Eldaernth Not seen action like that in a while.  (After the ambush in Bloomridge Park) Vistra Those cultists are lucky they were on the other side of the park. Lucky. Avourel You'd have taken them, would you, Vistra? Vistra Reckon so. Eldaernth Bollocks. These days we'd sooner throw our backs than a proper punch. Thokki Well, I, for one, count my lucky stars it happened elsewhere. Avourel Same here. It can be spoken to using Speak with Animals . “ Rest, little one. But do not take long - I feel his shadow. „ — Elder Rothé warning the party about Ketheric Thorm Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Elder Rothé is a particularly long-lived rothé. It claims to have outlived its "mother, and her mother's mother, and many mothers beyond" . Speaking to either Elder Rothé or Deep Rothé Calf starts a joint conversation with them both. The rothé communicate using the spell Dancing Lights , which (if not using Speak with Animals ) the party can observe to discern the emotions of the Elder Rothé: pain, sadness, and a fear stretching back generations: [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Still your body and quietly observe.  (DC 10) [NATURE]  Pay attention to the lights.  (DC 15) [UNDERDARK] [NATURE]  Pay attention to the lights.  (DC 15  ) With Speak with Animals , the party can join in on the conversation. The Rothé speaks of Ketheric Thorm and his Dark Justiciar army, who have left their mark on the area: "the rock shivers from the sound. The Ketheric Thorm." The Elder Rothé has lived long enough that it worked during the time of Ketheric's war. It recounts the bloody battle and Thorm's army, and Yurgir , the "hellbeast that broke them." Technical UID S_DEN_Gatekeeper UUID 847717b3-82eb-45a7-b875-78665c12ce9a Stats DEN_Refugees_Tiefling_Ranger Eqp. EQP_Longbow_Dagger_RingMail Trs. DEN_Refugee Elegis is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . She becomes responsible for closing and opening the gate to the grove after Kanon's untimely demise. “ Glad you made it inside... doubt we'll be safe here for long though. „ — Elegis , after fending off the first goblin scouting party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Elegis is responsible for opening and closing the gate after Kanon's untimely death. She is usually near the gate winch and war horn at X: 203 Y: 441 . If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving Kagha's ritual the Rite of Thorns , the tieflings are expelled from the Emerald Grove and Elegis's corpse is among the pile of refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . If Minthara and her raiding party are primed to assault the Emerald Grove, Elegis is atop the ramparts, building barricades from the Emerald Grove's trees. Once the fighting starts, she moves away from the ramparts and joins the rest of the tiefling defenders in The Hollow . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Elegis survives Act One, her murdered body is in the Shadow-Cursed Lands alongside a dead ox, not far from the road to the Mountain Pass , far away from the other tiefling refugees who died in the cultist ambush. Passing a Perception check while inspecting her body reveals that they were gored. This can be also learned by reading her Refugee's Journal . Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Interaction: Talking to Elegis while she is on watch on the wall in Emerald Grove. You're scared of a few goblins? Pathetic.   +1   -1   +1   -1 [GITHYANKI]  If a few goblins scare you, you don't deserve to survive.   +1   -1   +1   -1 Best get to digging your own graves then.   +1   -1   +1   -1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Dagger Damage: 3~6 1d4 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ranged Attack ( )   –   Longbow Damage: 3~10 1d8 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Save the Refugees Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Refugee's Journal Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Elegis will nervously chat with Asharak just before the assault on the Emerald Grove: Asharak Holding up all right? Elegis I'm fine. You don't have to keep checking. Asharak It's this, or sitting and waiting. So I'll be back, if it's all the same to you. Elegis You've actually fought goblins before, haven't you? Asharak So have you, if I'm not mistaken. Elegis That wasn't - that's not the same. I was terrified the whole time. Asharak Hah - sounds exactly the same, then. Asharak Fine day for it, I reckon. Elegis What does that mean? Asharak Not a notion. Talking beats thinking, though. Elegis Yeah. Yeah, fine day for it. Elegis Nock. Draw. Breathe. Loose. Elegis Nock. Draw. Breathe. UND_Duergar_Officer Sergeant Thrinn is a duergar cultist at Grymforge in Act One . She has tasked several duergar to retrieve her stolen boots. “ Move, hoon. I don't have time for drugnin' outsiders. „ — Elenna Thrinn Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Free True Soul Nere Thrinn is in the duergar encampment in Grymforge at X: -643 Y: 300 , where she is organizing the rescue attempt to free Nere from the cave-in. She is in charge of the duergar in Nere's absence. If the party side with Nere, but he dies during the ensuing battle, Thrinn can be convinced to let the gnomes go: [ILLITHID]  Draw on the power within to enforce your will. [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  Call on the parasite, connect with Thrinn. 'The gnomes must go free.'  (DC 10) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  FREE THEM, OR ELSE.  (DC 10  ) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read Thrinn's thoughts. The gnomes won't survive the curse. What good is a gift of corpses? She can be given the Boots of Speed , thus completing ⁠ Find the Missing Boots . The party can choose either Bracing Band or Armour of Uninhibited Kushigo as a reward.
