## Eliette
- **来源**: [Eliette](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Eliette)
- **分类**: Characters

Eliette Hometown Whispering Depths (underneath Blighted Village ) Stats Type Humanoid Race High Elf [ 1 ] See also: Phase Spider Matriarch Eliette is a High Elf arachnomancer mentioned in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I will find solitude, and I will worship Lolth with my very soul. „ — Eliette , in the Bloody Journal Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Eliette is the author of multiple works which can be found in the Whispering Depths . She used to live above ground but due to her fascination for Lolth moved underground. In her works she refers to herself as a high elf. Her books tell the story of her regret at living on the surface for so long before moving to the Underdark , her capture by a group of drow , a vision of her escape when her captors' house falls, and being blessed with two gifts from Lolth: the Spiderstep Boots from a fallen drow "heretic", and the body of an Arachnomancer from which she copies the sigils scarred on its face to her own, and grants her the ability to shapeshift into a spider. Within the Whispering Depths she experimented with a method to transcend into a full spider form, after being unhappy with merely shapeshifting into one. It is strongly implied Eliette became the Phase Spider Matriarch . EQP_Crossbow_Dagger_ScaleMail Trs. HAV_Survivor Harper Elifer is a wood elf ranger who is part of the Harpers in Act Two . She guards the entrance to the Last Light Inn , stopping and questioning any newcomers that happen to arrive in front of the sanctuary. “ You there! Step forward and keep your hands off your weapons! „ — Elifer Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Elifer is at the Last Light Inn , where she guards the entrance to the sanctuary and main plaza from behind the main barricade, below Terradissia and a few steps away from Darragh . She is typically the first Harper within the inn proper to interact with the party. If the party saved Lassandra , Karrow , or Meygan from a Shadow ambush by going into the Shadow-Cursed Lands through the Grymforge lift, following them to Last Light Inn has the party's arrival be met with distrust from Elifer; the surviving Harpers attempt to vouch for the party, though it has little effect on the following conversation afterward as Elifer calls on Jaheira to interrogate the new arrivals. The same series of events happen even if the party comes to Last Light Inn through the Mountain Pass , with Elifer stopping the party and calling on Jaheira for further interrogation. When Jaheira sizes up the party, Elifer attempts to interfere, but is immediately silenced when the High Harper looks her way. Elifer does not react in the party's defence when Jaheira entangles the party, instead pulling her crossbow out at the ready. If the Tiefling refugees did not make it to Last Light, Marcus can instead vouch for the party. If the party then expose Marcus as a True Soul , Elifer is Stunned and joins the fight against his summoned Crawling Claws . Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during Resolve the Abduction , Elifer often fails the save and is Impaled for the remainder of the battle. If the party fail to protect Isobel, she and everyone in the Last Light Inn turn into a Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira. Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Infiltrate Moonrise Towers If the party prevent Marcus from capturing Isobel at the Last Light Inn and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Elifer follows Jaheira to Moonrise Towers . However, Elifer is killed during the fight against Absolute forces before the party members arrive, and her corpse is few steps past the Moonrise Towers main entrance, before the steps leading down to the main battle. BG_Guard Blaze Elin is a human wizard and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is at Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . “ Straight ahead, across the bridge. A blind ogre couldn't miss it. „ — Elin , letting the party into Wyrm's Rock Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Find a Way into Wyrm's Rock Fortress Elin is the commander of the Flaming Fist garrison in the Wyrm's Rock Fortress . She guards the South Drawbridge Checkpoint and prevents the party from entering unless they are in possession of a pass or can convince her by any means described below. Surprisingly for the commander of a whole fortress, Elin stands guard in person with Gai , Shah , and three Steel Watchers . [ 2 ] The party must speak with her to enter the city via the bridge. Based on the party's actions before approaching Elin, they might have the means to get the free passage into the fortress. Otherwise, the interacting party member must pass a difficult ability check (varying based on the character's features), fight, or leave. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Gaining the passage by any "free" means or by succeeding any ability check grants +1 approval from every possible companion present in the party. [ 3 ] Choosing the option " Leave. " after Elin asks for an admission grants   -1   -1   -1   -1   +1   +1   -1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Blight ( + ) Damage: 8~64 8d8 ⁠ Necrotic Deals 8d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage to a target. Technical UID S_SCL_Drider_Harper_Caster_000 UUID ef609a8e-08bf-4648-bbb4-380a7f4bc887 Stats SCL_Caravan_Ambusher_Elindale Eqp. EQP_Staff_Robe Trs. HAV_Survivor Harper Elindale is a cheerful Harper who guards the entrance to Last Light Inn during Act Two . “ I'm ready - I think. Am I? Yes. „ — Elindale Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party reach the Shadow-Cursed Lands through Grymforge , Elindale is at the Last Light Inn, south of the entrance into the inn proper, a few steps from Quartermaster Talli . After talking with Jaheira , Elindale moves to the bridge in front of Last Light Inn with Branthos [ 1 ] , Lassandra , Manus , and Skywin . They wait for the party so they can move in to intercept and ⁠ ambush a nearby absolutist convoy and acquire their source of protection against the Shadow Curse . Accepting the mission results in Elindale and his squad of Harpers casting Light on their weapons and moving to the Ruined Battlefield , where they lay in wait for the Absolutist convoy. The party can go with the group immediately or catch up with them later, as the ambush site is marked on their map. If the party speak with Isobel and trigger the fight with Marcus , Elindale will have already moved to the bridge, out of reach of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, Elindale dies immediately instead of turning into a Shadow-Cursed Undead . Ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] Talking to Branthos at the ambush site commences the ambush and spawns in the encounter. [ 2 ] Once Kar'niss and the convoy arrive, the party can attack immediately or hang back. If choosing to stay hidden and keep watching, Kar'niss kills Vez . From there, the party can either signal the Harpers or wait as they start the encounter themselves. After the fight, a Moonlantern can be found on the drider's corpse. Alternatively, the party can convince Kar'niss to relinquish the Moonlantern and consign the convoy members to their fate as Shadow-Cursed Undead . Either way, Elindale and his squad then depart amiably and return to Last Light Inn. If the party first enter the Shadow-Cursed Lands through the Rosymorn Monastery Trail , a goblin greets the party and sends them to a rendezvous point to wait for Kar'niss and the convoy to guide them to Moonrise Towers , where the party can ⁠ pass off as True Souls . This starts ⁠ Follow the Convoy . Kar'niss ferries the party, as well as the rest of the convoy, to Moonrise. During the trek, Branthos, along with Elindale, Manus, and Skywin ambush the convoy. The party can choose to turn on the convoy and help the Harpers, or protect the convoy in order to continue their cover as True Souls. If the party are meeting the Harpers for the first time, and Branthos dies while siding with them, Elindale tells the party to head to Last Light Inn, where they can obtain similar protection after speaking with Isobel. If they choose to remain with the convoy, Elindale and his squad turn hostile. After the Ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party side with Elindale and he survives, Elindale moves to the top floor of Last Light Inn, and is drinking wine with Branthos. He continuously attempts to break through Branthos' stoicism and get him to cheer, to no avail. [ 3 ] Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Elindale follows Jaheira there. However, he is killed during the fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. His corpse is in the Moonrise Towers Prison , surrounded by a Death Shepherd and a horde of Necromites . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Ellswort is rotting in an open grave in the Graveyard of the Lower City . Upon touching the corpse, it explodes due to the Grotesque Distention condition. A party member can safely pick up the corpse by right-clicking and selecting the pick up option, if they have sufficient strength. The corpse can also be "activated" to produce a poison cloud by looting it while held in inventory. PLA_ZhentHidehout_Guard Ellyka is a scout near the Mountain Pass entrance to the west of Waukeen's Rest in Act One . “ That bridge was going to be my passage to Baldur's Gate. To safety. Now I've to find another way. „ — Ellyka Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] At the entrance to the Mountain Pass, Ellyka warns the party about a group of githyanki on the road ahead. However, if the interacting party member appears to be a githyanki, Ellyka refers to them as 'flatface', and the party has a few unique dialogue responses. While speaking to Ellyka with a githyanki appearance, she attacks the party if they select: [GITHYANKI]  They may be my kin. I will investigate. [GITHYANKI]  First and last warning - lower that weapon. Ellyka is later captured and killed. Her corpse is in the cell room of Crèche Y'llek . Using Speak with Dead on it can reveal she traveled to Rosymorn searching for The Blood of Lathander , but was captured and tortured by the githyanki for information on Moonrise . If Ellyka is killed at the Mountain Pass, it is not possible to commune with her using Speak with Dead . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Leather Armour Longbow Potion of Healing Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Ellyka's corpse can be communed with at Crèche Y'llek using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Ellyka Ellyka... scout... Where are you from? Ellyka Elturel ... near Maiden's Bridge... Exiled... lost everything... How did you end up here? Ellyka Road to Baldur's Gate ... blocked... Took new path... found monastery... remembered... What did you remember? Ellyka A rhyme... Blood of Lathander... hidden... guarded by monks... Decided to... look for it... How does this rhyme go? Ellyka East... west... blood is blessed... Beneath... sun... it finds... its rest... What is the Blood of Lathander? Ellyka Powerful relic... valuable... wanted to sell... start again... Where can I find this Blood? Ellyka Hidden... inside... couldn't find... Who killed you? Ellyka Githyanki... slowly... painfully... What did they want with you? Ellyka Absolute ... Moonrise... couldn't understand... Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find the Blood of Lathander Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] While in combat with Ellyka, it is still possible for a character to enter the trigger zone for the usual cutscene that occurs at the Mountain Pass area. This abruptly ends the combat encounter, and Ellyka then flees from the location, but remains marked as 'hostile.' [ verify ] If Ellyka does not engage in combat with the party she is later captured and then killed by the Githyanki in Crèche Y'llek. If her corpse is examined there, she is level 5 and has an Extra Attack . v t e Risen Road Characters Companions Karlach Flaming Fists Aelis Bryanne Dain Dion Ephren Florrick Jacek Ito Marilla Pavel Rowan Tristan Wexford Yeva Githyanki Baretha Chost For'reth Voss Zastri Paladins of Tyr Anders Buckle Refugee Trynn Traders Brem Cyrel Zhentarim Amnos Bellar Garias Jarg Karad Olly Rugan Salazon Vol Zarys Other Benryn Ellyka Krug Marten Mirileth Oskar Fevras Sszaryn Vance Yul Animals and Creatures Bloated Hyena Flind Frightened Ox Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Indra Isbeth Istor Qudenos Locations Mountain Pass Toll House Waukeen's Rest Zhentarim Basement Quests Find a Cure Find the Githyanki Crèche Find the Missing Shipment Find the Nightsong Free the Artist Hunt the Devil Our Fiery Friend Rescue the Trapped Man The Blade of Frontiers The Githyanki Warrior Travel to Moonrise Towers Travel through the Mountain Pass

Technical UID S_GLO_Elminster UUID 75bb6396-1132-4064-bafe-205a3f156b9b Stats GLO_Elminster Eqp. EQP_Staff_Robe Elminster Aumar , commonly known as Elminster , is a legendary wizard who appears in Baldur's Gate 3 . He is one of the current Chosen of the Goddess Mystra and plays a key recurring role in the story of Gale . He is first encountered under the name Weary Traveller. “ Ho there, wanderer. Stay thy course a moment to indulge an old man. „ — Elminster , greeting the party Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Appearance 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.2 Act Two 2.3 Act Three 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 4 Related quests 5 Related literature 6 Gallery 7 Notes and references 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Elminster is a recurring character in the Forgotten Realms setting of Dungeons and Dragons, including previous entries in the Baldur's Gate series. The steeple-hatted wizard is of legendary renown across realmspace, having appeared in over twenty novels, four adventures, and each prior instalment in the Baldur's Gate series. [ 1 ] He is an old acquaintance of Volo and occasionally fact-checks his books, including Volo's Guide to Baldur's Gate . Gale describes him as being approximately "thirteen centuries old." Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Elminster wears a flowing orange-red robe with a matching hat, whose drooped steeple hangs backwards. Luscious silver locks of hair pour outward from the wide brim of his hat and blend into an equally long beard, between which sits a round, wizened face. A brilliant blue sash, decorated with jewels and signets, is draped between his right shoulder and left hip. Completing his finery is a necklace of gold and silver plates with a single blood-red jewel, along with a matching belt. In stark contrast to this opulent getup, he wields a single plain, unenchanted quarterstaff. Though bearing his normal appearance, the Elminster who appears in game is a construct . If defeated, it melts into a pile of water, strongly implying it to be a Simulacrum of the real wizard. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale must be alive and a party member or Origin for any encounters with Elminster to trigger. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] For Elminster to appear, Gale must have consumed at least one magic item. Elminster can then be encountered near the entrance to the Shadow-Cursed Lands from the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or inside the Shadow-Cursed Lands in the Sharran ruins into which the elevator from Grymforge exits. [ 2 ] At camp, Elminster delivers Mystra's message to Gale, entrusting him with a mission of detonating the Netherese orb within his chest in order to destroy "the Heart of the Absolute " in a suicidal attack. To help ease the task, Elminster also imparts a stabilising enchantment on Gale's orb, negating its need to consume more magical items. He then departs as quickly as he arrived, leaving Karlach (should she be in the camp) wondering if he was "Gale's grandad". After enchanting Gale, Elminster disappears from both locations and cannot be seen again until Act Three. If Elminster's construct is defeated, he does not appear again. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] So long as he has not spoken with Gale, Elminster may appear at camp during a long rest after entering the Shadow-Cursed Lands. He can also be encountered on the stone bridge right in front of Moonrise Towers , close to the waypoint . If Elminster never manages to speak with Gale to stabilise his orb, Gale leaves the party permanently any time he is spoken with after defeating the Apostle of Myrkul or when the party travel to Wyrm's Lookout . If Gale is present during the battle with the Apostle, he leaves immediately afterwards. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] After Gale reads The Annals of Karsus in the Sorcerous Vault during ⁠ The Wizard of Waterdeep , Elminster appears for a second time, either outside Sorcerous Sundries or in camp. He brings yet another message from Mystra, asking Gale to meet her at her holy shrine in the Stormshore Tabernacle . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] A direct confrontation with Elminster is ill-advised. To say nothing of his overlevelled stats relative to the party when he is first encountered, he also leaves no loot if defeated, and doing so permanently locks Gale out of progressing in his personal quest, causing him to permanently leave the party after Ketheric is defeated. If the party defeat Elminster in combat, they are awarded 1000 experience. Chain Lightning ( + ) Damage: 10~80 10d8 ⁠ Lightning Strike an enemy with lightning. Three more bolts will leap from the target, electrifying as many as three other enemies within range. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Disintegrate ( + ) Damage: 50~100 10d6 + 40 ⁠ Force If the target fails a Dexterity Saving Throw , and the spell reduces it to 0 hit points, it disintegrates into a crumbly ash. DEX Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Otiluke's Freezing Sphere ( + ) Damage: 10~60 10d6 ⁠ Cold Create a ball of churning ice that can be launched instantly to generate a frosty explosion or stored for later use. CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Polymorph ( + ) Transform a creature into a harmless sheep. If the sheep's Hit Points drop to 0, the target reverts to its original form with its original Hit Points. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Slow ( + ) Alter time around up to 6 enemies to Slow them. They won't get far, they can't do much, and they're easier to hit. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Sunbeam ( + ) Damage: 6~48 6d8 ⁠ Radiant A beam of brilliant light sears and Blinds all creatures in its path. Until the spell ends, you can recast Sunbeam without expending a spell slot . Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_Bonecloak_FF_000 UUID 1c25d7db-a379-4adc-9e06-3139e78356c1 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Elthira Gossen is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the streets of Lower City in Act Three . “ I wouldn't expect you to admit your nefarious allegiance. You lot are sworn to secrecy, aren't you? „ — Elthira Gossen , pressing on detained citizens Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Elthira Gossen is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Aggralix , Fist Karoline and a Steel Watcher . They can be found near the Bonecloak's Apothecary at X:  Y:  , detaining and interrogating Drongo Bixworth and Florean Bixworth . Elthira accuses them of being agents of the Absolute and tries to turn their words upon themselves. If spoken to, she asks the player character not to meddle in while she is carrying on her duties. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Elthira Gossen disappears from the game along with her fellow Fists and detained citizens. DEN_DruidServant Elwyn is a human druid in the Circle of the Emerald Grove in Act One . “ Feels like I've been holding my breath for a tenday. „ — Elwyn , finally relaxed. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Elwyn is at the Sacred Pool performing the Rite of Thorns . She becomes hostile if the party interact with the Idol of Silvanus . Although Elwyn does not fully agree with Kagha's methods to shut off the Grove, she is deeply concerned about the goblin attacks and believes that the Grove needs a leader and plan to survive. After rescuing Halsin , she is relieved she can stop thinking about goblins and tieflings so she can listen to the birds again. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Elwyn has two Wild Shape charges and can cast spells using up to Level Two Spell Slots . Cure Wounds ( + ) Healing: 1~8 + modifiers 1d8 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Healing Heal a creature you can touch. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Quarterstaff Damage: 2~7 1d6 + 1 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Moonbeam ( + ) Damage: 2~20 2d10 ⁠ Radiant Call down a beam of light that damages any creatures that enters the beam or starts its turn in the light. You can use an Action to move the beam 18 m (60 ft). CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Poison Spray ( ) Damage: 1~12 1d12 ⁠ Poison Project a puff of noxious gas, dealing 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Poison to a target. CON Save Range: 3 m (10 ft) Produce Flame ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Fire A flame in your hand sheds a light in a 9 m (30 ft) radius and deals 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage when thrown. Throwing the flame immediately after you conjure it does not cost an Action . Extinguishing or throwing it on subsequent turns costs an action. The throw has a range of 9 m (30 ft). Range: Self Wild Shape: Wolf ( + ) Assume the shape of a dire wolf that can   Incite allies and   Distract enemies. The dire wolf has a starting health of 18 hit points that increase every two druid levels. While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. You take on the attributes of your beast form - excluding your Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma scores. When your beast form drops to 0 hit points , you revert to your normal form. He and Conall were happily playing ball in the park, until Conall threw it far aside, right into the fountain bowl. Now both kids are arguing about which one of them should go and bring it back. If spoken with, Emen complains his friend threw the ball into the water and does not want to fetch it. However, he does not ask the party to do it instead of Conall. The party may take the ball themselves and return it to the boys, but if they do this, they risk stepping into an ambush set up by the Bhaal cultists. Overview Transcript Emmeline Hallowleaf In-game Render Model Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Angela Dixon Role Camp follower Faction Selûnite Family Arnell Hallowleaf (husband) Shadowheart (daughter) Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 106 AC 12 Initiative +2 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 15 (+2) 14 (+2) 13 (+1) 12 (+1) 12 (+1) 14 (+2) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA +4 +2 +3 +1 +1 +2 Features Darkvision Can see in the dark up to a certain distance. Fey Ancestry Advantage on saving throws against being charmed ; can't be put to sleep by magic. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_LOW_ShadowheartMother UUID d085272a-f1d0-4ff8-a498-80728030f83e Stats Human_Commoner Emmeline Hallowleaf is a Human Selûnite and the mother of Shadowheart . She can potentially become a Camp Follower . “ My darling girl. The last time I saw you cry, you cut your knee while chasing a frog. „ — Emmeline Hallowleaf , talking to Shadowheart History [ edit section | visual editor ] Emmeline Hallowleaf, and her husband Arnell Hallowleaf , raised Shadowheart , originally known as Jenevelle Hallowleaf, in a Selûnite household in the forests outside Baldur's Gate . [ 1 ] As a child, Jenevelle undertook a Selûnite coming-of-age ritual in which she was left alone in the woods and trusted to use Selûne's guidance to return to her family. However, the villagers discovered a Sharran spy near the village, and learned that his accomplices sought to abduct Jenevelle. Arnell took on his wolf form to quickly travel the woods to find Jenevelle, but she did not know about his curse, and panicked at the sight of the wolf, allowing enough time for the Sharrans to find and abduct both of them, as well as Emmeline. After their capture, Emmeline and Arnell were kept in the Cloister of Sombre Embrace for about 40 years as Shadowheart grew up there. During this time, Shadowheart was indoctrinated and made to 'practice' Sharran techniques, such as trickery, interrogation, and torture, on her parents. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Emmeline and Arnell are in the Cloister of Sombre Embrace . As part of Shadowheart's personal quest, Daughter of Darkness , she is forced to make the choice of letting them die and freeing herself of her incurable wound, or freeing them and having to live with the wound the for rest of her life. Both Arnell and Emmeline urge Shadowheart to let them die and free herself, but the player character can persuade Shadowheart to free them through a DC 20 Religion or Persuasion Check . If Emmeline and Arnell are freed, they become camp followers and reveal information about themselves and Shadowheart's past. Arnell is more talkative than Emmeline, as Emmeline is a human with a natural lifespan much shorter than Arnell's, and her memory is fading with age. Attacking Emmeline or Arnell at any point turns Shadowheart against the party. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Letter from Arnell Hallowleaf Letter from Emmeline Hallowleaf Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Daughter of Darkness Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Cinematic of Emmeline Hallowleaf References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Multiple things point to Shadowheart having grown in Moonhaven, the former name for the now ruined Blighted Village , such as her reaction when picking up the Old Schoolbook or her scene at the Selûnite statue behind the mill. However, this is difficult to confirm as different sources in-game indicate that the village was destroyed over a hundred years ago by Ketheric Thorm's dark justiciar army, and Shadowheart is estimated to be roughly fifty years old. Conflicting timelines regarding the village and its destruction also do not line up, thus, it is possible that the intent during development was that she and her family indeed lived in Moonhaven, but that these inconsistencies were never properly fixed for release. v t e Cloister of Sombre Embrace Characters Arnell Hallowleaf Emmeline Hallowleaf Viconia DeVir Justiciar Crusaders Nightmist Owltalon Fidelians Gloommask Gydd Hyrald Lamona Uttermask Novices Bluenail Dohna Dollay Garrigan Greymask Humboldt Monteith Tylda Sentries Baxta Fredrichk Hendly Imwise Traders Nocturne Locations Armoury Chamber of Loss Dormitory Night Orchid Cave Quests A Familiar Face Daughter of Darkness Investigate the House of Grief Surrender Shadowheart to Viconia

Beautiful. „ — Eni Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Eni is in the Bhaal Temple in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . He stands on the upper balcony of the temple and never descends to the central altar ground. Eni discusses with Mitchia Orin's victim, who is displayed in a side alcove – one of those whom Orin impersonated to speak to the party in Rivington . If spoken with, he confesses his skill is not refined, and is eager to learn from Mitchia, Orin, or the Dark Urge. His one-liners depend on whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. WYR_Danthelon_Trader Entharl Danthelon is the owner of Danthelon's Dancing Axe in Wyrm's Crossing during Act Three . “ What, by the Mordinsamman's curlies, went on down there? „ — Entharl Danthelon , after the event in the basement Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If Jaheira is recruited at the end of Act Two , she informs the party of a Harper safehouse in Wyrm's Crossing, which is hidden in a shop called Danthelon's Dancing Axe . The shop can be found on the west end of Wyrm's Crossing, across from Carm's Garms at X: -6 Y: 133 . Upon entering, Entharl Danthelon greets the party. If Jaheira is present, she tells him to skip the pleasantries, and Entharl offers the Rusty Key (Entharl) to the secret room at X: -18 Y: 138 , where the Harpers await at the end of the iron ladder. If Jaheira is not present, the interacting party member can inform him that they were sent by Jaheira to meet some Harpers. ## Enver Gortash
- **来源**: [Enver Gortash](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Enver_Gortash)
- **分类**: Characters、Bosses

Overview Combat Lord Enver Gortash Archduke Nominee In-game Portrait Full Name Enver Flymm Gortash [ 1 ] Identity Male Voice / Actor Jason Isaacs Family Dravo Flymm (father) Sally Flymm (mother) Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Deity Bane Technical UID S_GLO_Gortash UUID b878a854-f790-4999-95c4-3f20f00f65ac Stats WYR_Gortash Eqp. EQP_WYR_HeavyCrossbow_Dagger_Gortash Trs. Gold_Pocket_Wealthy Lord Enver Gortash , [ 2 ] [ 3 ] often just referred to as Gortash , is the Chosen of Bane , and one of the leaders of the enigmatic Cult of the Absolute . He serves as one of the main antagonists in Baldur's Gate 3 . Despite his humble beginnings, Gortash quickly rose through the ranks of society in Baldur's Gate with unbridled ambition and great cunning. Now, an influential figure and poised to become the Archduke of the city, he seeks to consolidate his power and become the ruler of the city and beyond, through whatever means are necessary. “ A mad dog understands the yank of the leash and the hand of its master, but it cannot be an equal. 'You' can be my equal. „ — Gortash , on masters and slaves Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Gameplay 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Early life 3.2 Rise to power 3.3 Chosen of Bane 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.2 Act Two 4.3 Act Three 5 List of interactions 6 Speak with Dead 7 Combat 7.1 Loot 8 Achievements 9 Related literature 10 Related Quests 11 Gallery 12 Notes and references 13 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Hinted at first through notes, he is properly introduced at the end of Act Two as one of the conspirators of the cult along with Ketheric Thorm and Orin the Red . Born from nothing and rising through the ranks of the city through hubris and sheer ambition, Gortash has positioned himself as a force to be reckoned with in Baldur's Gate. In the pockets of the nobility, with influence over the city's Flaming Fists and aided by his Steel Watch , Gortash now has the whole city in the palm of his hand. Gameplay [ edit section | visual editor ] Gortash is a level 9 Human boss and one of the main antagonists in the game. First mentioned in Act 1, he is introduced in Act 2, properly encountered in Act 3, and possibly fought there as well. Fighting him, or allying with him, is required in order to obtain his Netherstone and proceed with the story. In combat, he relies on his allies to protect him, while supporting them from afar through grenades and the hazards found in the combat arena. He can forge an alliance with the party to face the Netherbrain together. The party's encounters with him influence how friendly or hostile the city is. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] A man with a quick and easy smile, Gortash has short, dark hair, mussed in a choppy, tousled style. His facial features are rounded, and beginning to show the signs of age, with many creases around his eyes, and some scars. Gortash's style of dress is extravagant and reflective of his wealth; his wide open collar displaying gilded dragons, intricately designed gold gauntlets, and noticeably bright red and pointy steel-tipped boots. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Gortash is cunning and self-assured, arguably to a fault. He was noticed as intelligent from an early age. Highly ambitious and Machiavellian in nature, he uses whatever methods he deems necessary to achieve his goals, regardless of the impact his actions have on others. Described as needy and troublesome by his less-than-loving parents, [ 4 ] he grew up to be politically shrewd and ruthless in his business relations, leading him to a meteoric rise through Baldurian society. Despite his goals for domination, he is pragmatic and willing to engage in diplomacy when needed. Much like his patron god Bane , Gortash will work with others when it serves his interests, and is genuine, if not outright giving, with his alliances. [ 5 ] History [ edit section | visual editor ] Early life [ edit section | visual editor ] Enver Gortash was born to Dravo and Sally Flymm , the proprietors of Flymm's Cobblers in Baldur's Gate. The Flymms were mired in debt, and sold their son into slavery to pay them off. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] His parents describe him as a clever child, often found tinkering. They also described him as dreadful and wicked. [ 9 ] Mistaken by the Flymms as a warlock, Gortash was in reality sold to Raphael . Gortash became a pageboy in Raphael's and Nubaldin's service. [ 10 ] [ 11 ] He was physically abused and left on poor terms. [ 12 ] Rise to power [ edit section | visual editor ] Before acquiring the title of 'Lord', Enver Gortash started out operating as a black market weapons dealer, [ 13 ] before expanding his operation into other businesses. At some point, Enver Gortash hired a young Karlach as his bodyguard. He betrayed her later, striking a deal with Zariel to sell Karlach as a test subject for an implanted ⁠ Infernal Engine . [ 14 ] It is unknown what Gortash received in return. Rumours say that he had Helsik open a transplanar portal to Hell during this period. [ 15 ] Enver Gortash was able to supplant the Knights of the Shield as the leading black market dealer in Baldur's Gate, [ 16 ] but not without trouble. [ 17 ] His initial attempts to sway their client base by offering a more generous cut saw little success. Through generous bribes, Gortash began uncovering the nature of this resistance. [ 18 ] He was also able to supplant the Zhentarim position in the Chionthar Valley. [ 19 ] In time, he became known as a "Military Advisor" to Baldur's Gate Elite. [ 20 ] In his younger days, he had an affair with Lady Wisteria Jannath [ 21 ] likely the mother of Lady Fireliia Jannath . Chosen of Bane [ edit section | visual editor ] At some point, Gortash became the Chosen of Bane , and began taking more ambitious endeavors, further expanding his power and influence within the political structures of Baldur's Gate. After meeting the Dark Urge , the then leader of the cult of Bhaal in Baldur's Gate , they conspired together until they had a close and ambiguous relationship. Around this time, Gortash formed an alliance with Ketheric Thorm , Chosen of Myrkul , and the Dark Urge, the then Chosen of Bhaal. The Dark Urge was eventually deposed by his second in command Orin the Red and Gortash approved her joining the alliance in place of her predecessor. Pursuing both power and the aims of their patron deities, Gortash and his allies formulated a plot to enslave an Elder Brain underneath Baldur's Gate by using an ancient Netherese artifact, the Crown of Karsus , an item so powerful, it had granted its namesake a brief moment of Godhood. Gortash reveals the details of this plot during Act Two , and further explains it in Act Three . At some point, Enver Gortash returned to his parents for revenge. What resulted was Gortash eventually implanting Mind Flayer tadpoles into their minds, turning them into puppets who could do little more than praise their exalted son. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Though Gortash is not present in the first act of the game, his involvement in the plot is alluded to when the Absolute attempts to take over the party's mind and they see silhouetted images of Gortash, Ketheric Thorm and Orin the Red shortly before being repelled by the Mysterious Artefact . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Absolute_trinity.webm The Chosen of Bane Enver Gortash first appears alongside Ketheric Thorm and Orin the Red in the Mind Flayer Colony beneath Moonrise Towers . An argument breaks out between him and Ketheric and is stopped from becoming a fight due to Orin's intervention. After Orin plants an Illithid tadpole in Ulder Ravengard , Gortash, Ketheric and Orin each use their Netherstones and order the Netherbrain to march the Absolute's armies on Baldur's Gate . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] With Ketheric slain by the party and the Netherstones separated, Orin and Gortash's partnership falls apart and their control over the Elder Brain begins to falter, as evidenced by it emitting quakes that reverberate throughout Baldur's Gate. While Gortash is having his picture painted by a servant, a shapeshifted Orin comes to Gortash's quarters and repeatedly threatens him. Though Gortash urges Orin to control herself and focus on reuniting the Netherstones, Orin no longer has any interest in cooperation. Realizing Orin can no longer be relied on, Gortash resolves to be rid of his former partner. Upon entering Wyrm's Rock Fortress , Gortash speaks through a Steel Watcher to the party inviting them to his coronation in the fortress' audience hall. After arriving, Gortash offers the party a pact; he will not attack so long as they do no harm to him or his Steel Watch. Further, he promises they will rule Faerûn together when the party returns with Orin's Netherstone. Should the party perform a successful Insight ability check, it is revealed that, should they form an alliance, Gortash is sincere in his offer and fully intends on sharing his rule with the party. Whether this would only be a temporary truce is unknown. “ I wish this city – the people running it – were smarter than me. Gortash isn't their salvation. He's the monster at the gate. „ — Karlach , on Gortash's danger to the city after his installation as Archduke Gortash can explain the Chosen of the Dead Three's plot to the party, detailing everyone's role. Each individual had their own part to play in their plan, which would occur sequentially. The Chosen of Bhaal , Orin , would carry out a series of murders within Baldur's Gate, thinning out any forces not already under Gortash's control. The Chosen of Myrkul , Ketheric Thorm , would raise an army consisting of cultists of the Absolute , monstrous humanoids such as goblins , ogres , bugbears , and undead , marching from Moonrise Towers . Finally, the Chosen of Bane , Enver Gortash himself, would use his Steel Watch, commanding it in a rigged battle against the Absolute and winning in a way that indebts the city to him without damaging it beyond repair (and preventing him from ruling in prosperity). As parting words, Gortash warns the party not to return without Orin's Netherstone . If the Dark Urge is chosen as Origin , Gortash gives a much warmer welcome and greets his "favourite assassin". [ 22 ] He reveals that the original Chosen of Bhaal was not Orin, who he barely tolerates, but in fact the Dark Urge themselves, who he likes. Gortash continues, saying he and the Urge initiated the plot to steal the Crown of Karsus and use it to manipulate the Netherbrain, a plot that was going well until the Urge vanished and Orin proclaimed she would henceforth be speaking for the temple of Bhaal. Gortash then invites the party to witness his coronation where Duke Ravengard , under the Absolute's influence, crowns Gortash as Archduke. Witnessing the coronation grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Coronation of the Dreadmaster ( Sage background) ⁠ Personal Invitation ( Entertainer background) After attending Gortash's coronation and visiting the Lower City , the party can later meet Gortash upstairs in his office on top of Wyrm's Rock Fortress. After returning with Orin's stone, several possible outcomes can occur: If the party either destroys the Steel Watch Foundry or travels to the Iron Throne despite his warning them not to, Gortash sees this as a betrayal, and laments there is no hope of them becoming partners now. He then starts combat. [ 23 ] If the party upholds the deal, killing Orin, and bringing back her Netherstone, Gortash demands the party give both their Netherstones to him. If the party relents and hands them over, Gortash sees them as weak-willed and turns on them. Otherwise, after twice refusing, Gortash reveals he was testing them. The party's refusal proves they too are shrewd and headstrong, and a worthy ally. Gortash's intentions may be discovered through successfully reading his mind or passing an Insight check. If Gortash is killed during the Inauguration, the Iron Throne becomes unavailable, completing ⁠ Save the Gondians is not possible anymore, and the Steel Watch Foundry can no longer be entered. If Gortash remains allied with the party until the end, he meets them at the Morphic Pool , when it is time to confront the Netherbrain . As the party fails to dominate the brain, Gortash, already scared by the situation, pushes the party aside, trying alone to wield all three Netherstones. Too powerful to be controlled by only one of the Chosen Three, the Netherbrain inevitably kills him. Alternatively, Gortash can be fought at any point after meeting him in order to ⁠ obtain his Netherstone . If killed before reaching Orin, the party gains Gortash's Hand . Finally, killing Gortash grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Never Trust Those Above You ( Urchin background) - if Gortash was killed before a deal being made ⁠ Regicide ( Soldier background) ⁠ Shattering the Black Hand ( Haunted One background) List of interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Gortash is introduced at the end of Act Two, but cannot be interacted with until Act Three. During Act Three, the party has several opportunities to directly interact with Enver Gortash. While Enver Gortash is a neutral or allied entity, the party has several opportunities to start conversations with him. If provoked in certain conversations or deliberately attacked by the party, Gortash still becomes hostile. Enver Gortash is encountered in-person by the party at Wyrm's Crossing, during his inauguration as Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate. Despite previous hostilities, Gortash will be very open to cooperation with the party, even to the point of (possibly) offering them a place in his tyrannical rule. Gortash can be killed at Wyrm's Crossing, allowing the party to collect Gortash's Netherstone . However, if the party allies with Gortash, killing him is not necessary to continue. He accompanies them to the Netherbrain, attempting to command it once more. This, however, fails; he alone cannot effectively use all three stones to command the Netherbrain, and it uses its psionic might, killing Gortash instantly with a simple command: "Die." Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] If Speak with Dead is used on Gortash, he does not respond. Instead, Bane himself answers in his stead. (#1 First set) Lord Enver Gortash : You seek Gortash? His soul is already suffering at my hands. That is the fate of all those who fail me. If you're not Gortash, then who are you? (Jump to #2 Who are you?) Let him suffer, then. Isn't that the fate he deserves? Lord Enver Gortash : Yes. Because it is the fate you've given him. Lord Enver Gortash : A dead Archduke is of no use to me. A living explorer - [class/Wyll/githyanki/tadpole reference] , for example - is a different matter. (Jump to #3 Second set) You're much more coherent than most corpses. Why's that? Lord Enver Gortash : So naive for one with such cunning. Do you think it's Gortash speaking to you? (Jump to #2 Who are you?) Leave. (#2 Who are you?) Lord Enver Gortash : I am Bane, The Black Lord. I am the Ultimate Tyrant. I am Fear, I am Hate. Lord Enver Gortash : And you - you are the dagger that bled Myrkul's favoured. You are the thorns that prick at my sides. Lord Enver Gortash : Yet you are proof that I will still rise, and Bhaal and Myrkul will yield. (Jump to #3 Second set) (#3 Second set) Lord Enver Gortash : One question asked. Four still remains. You said I am proof you will rise. What did you mean? Lord Enver Gortash : You live for power. You have proven it with every fallen foe, every chest opened, every skill claimed. Lord Enver Gortash : As long as mortals and immortals vie for sharper blades and louder voices, I am strengthened. Lord Enver Gortash : So it is for Bhaal and Myrkul - and so it is for you. You make me eternal. I am no agent of yours. I seek power for proper ends, not for its own sake. Lord Enver Gortash : *Chuckle.* Narrator : The corpse says nothing more. You did not ask a question. Why did you ally with Myrkul and Bhaal? Lord Enver Gortash : Why do red dragons ally with the githyanki? Why did the Broken God befriend Tyr ? Lord Enver Gortash : Ah, but you already know the answer. By making one ally, you deny them to another." Lord Enver Gortash : And by turning mortals illithid, you deny their souls to their keepers. Lord Enver Gortash : You do not stoke fear by reaping your own fields, but by burning your foe's. What can I do to earn your blessing, Lord Bane? Lord Enver Gortash : You have already laid the foundation." Lord Enver Gortash : You gained my favour when you slayed Gortash. Your need for power exceeds even his. Lord Enver Gortash : Use the Netherstones to commandeer the brain and unleash your infected army, and I will count you among my chosen. Lord Enver Gortash : Or do not. Your lust for victory still brings you one step closer to me. How can I reach the Iron Throne? Lord Enver Gortash : Ah, Gortash's pet project. Iron Throne Headquarters once touched the sky, a monument to martial force. Lord Enver Gortash : It's been a century since it was submerged in Grey Harbour. You can reach it by a submersible beneath the harbour docks. Lord Enver Gortash : I look forward to your show of power. Can you help me find the headquarters of Orin the Red? Lord Enver Gortash : Of course you seek Orin, Bhaal's vengeful chosen. His temple is hidden even to my eyes. How fortuitous, then, that Orin seeks you. Lord Enver Gortash : Orin is too proud of her own handiwork to linger in your shadow. The vain don't like to be upstaged. Lord Enver Gortash : She'll make herself known to you - if she hasn't already, in her own special way. Leave. His defeat, or cooperation if so chosen, is required before facing the final threat of the game: the Netherbrain. PLA_Tavern_Paladin Fist Recruit Ephren is a human fighter and a recruit of the Flaming Fist . She is on the Risen Road in Act One . “ He of the Unsleeping Eyes. Grant me the might to carry this burden. Grant me the faith to face darkness without fear. „ — Ephren , praying to Helm Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ephren is at Waukeen's Rest inn, together with several other recruits - Fist Recruit Aelis , Fist Recruit Ito , Fist Recruit Pavel and Fist Recruit Tristan , as well as Gauntlet Dain and Gauntlet Yeva . She is kneeling in front of the dead body of Flaming Fist Jacek , uttering a prayer [ 1 ] . Ephren was part of the squad accompanying Duke Ulder Ravengard on his way from Elturel and staying at the inn when it was attacked by a horde of goblins and drow . If a party member decides to talk to her, they can ask a few questions on the attack, offer condolences or comment on the situation, depending on their character's class. Clerics of Helm have also an option to join Ephren's prayer. However, if the chosen party member is a Lolth-Sworn Drow , Ephren considers them an attacker and must be convinced otherwise, or fought. The player character then has several options that might placate the Fist: [DETECT THOUGHTS] [INTELLIGENCE]  Cast Detect Thoughts. I am no monster - I mean no harm to you. Tell me what happened here. [INTIMIDATION]  Think carefully, colnbluth [ 2 ] . Do you truly wish to anger Lolth's favoured? (DC 5) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Go on, try it.  (DC 5  ) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  TRY IT, WEAKLINGS.  (DC 5  ) [PERSUASION]  Be at ease. I didn't come seeking battle. (DC 5) If successful, Ephren asks the party to speak to Gauntlet (not clear which one) and leave her to her mourning. If the party undertake the task of rescuing all possible survivors (notably, Counsellor Florrick ) from the burning building, Ephren does not participate, remaining near Jacek's body, and stays there even after Florrick commands the Fist to search for Duke Ravengard, and all other Fists depart. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act Three , Ephren is only mentioned by Roger Highberry (if he survived the encounter with the serial killer at the Wine Festival). Sorting the correspondence, Roger finds a letter from Ephren, obviously bringing the word for Molly the Orphan about her father's death. EQP_Shortbow_Dagger_Leather Eramas is one of the tiefling refugees sheltering at the Emerald Grove in Act One . She is packing her belongings by the entrance to the Makeshift Prison . “ Easy now! Not going to let the goblins get you. „ — Eramas , calming the oxen. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Eramas is packing her belongings in the Grove near X: 190 Y: 575 . If the party converse with her, she expresses fear and panic around the recent goblin attack, suggesting to the party that they should also pack and leave. If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving Kagha's ritual the Rite of Thorns , the tieflings are expelled from the Emerald Grove and Eramas corpse is among the pile of refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party kill her   -10 Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Save the Refugees Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Eramas talks to herself as she packs her belongings in the Emerald Grove during Act One. Eramas Shoes. Where are my boots? Eramas Is that everything? I think that's everything. Eramas What to bring... Eramas Right, I've got food, water, my dagger... Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Despite wearing a hood in Early Access and in her portrait, Eramas in the final release of the game does not have any headgear or hood equipped. Eramas was once meant to be associated with a Cut and unimplemented content NPC named Spencer, who has since then been cut, removed, or entirely abandoned before Early Access. Erna is a member of the Zhentarim who guards Roah Moonglow alongside Yerle in the Shattered Sanctum and Moonrise Towers . “ Wouldn't go in there, 'less you fancy blowing your bones all the way to Baldur's Gate. „ — Erna , guarding a door Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] In the Shattered Sanctum , Erna and Yerle guard Roah Moonglow . Erna discourages the party from entering the room due to the high number of explosive barrels kept within. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] In Moonrise Towers , Erna only speaks with the party if they 'misbehave', and instead encourages them to speak with Roah. Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayDisappointment_Fist UUID 0b43f583-c9b9-450f-9732-db40d07d42e2 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Ernestus is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found on the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . “ If this lot have got a problem with the Gazette they should take it up with the editor, not make a scene in the streets. „ — Ernestus Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Ernestus is patrolling the streets of Lower City. He can be found at X: 43 Y: -71 , arguing with a group of Baldurians ( Saer Frunilla , Wuloona Dor , Porter Juxon , and Bliggerillo ). They are slandering aloud the contents of latest issues of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette and blaming the newspaper (and Gortash as well) for sweeping under the rug obvious crimes that happen in the city. Ernestus's reaction to the player character might differ depending on the positive / negative article printed about them in the Baldur's Mouth Gazette (or neither printed at all), as an outcome for ⁠ Stop the Presses quest. Also, he might notice if the party try to break in and enter any restricted areas nearby (e.g., Old Jol's house or the backdoor of the Nortale's Hostel ), and react accordingly. If Gortash is defeated, Ernestus and the rest of the group disperse, and cannot be found or interacted with again. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail Flaming Fist Helmet Halberd Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Wuloona Dor You see the latest issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette? Streets are safer than they've even been, apparently. Wuloona Dor Not a word on all the thefts and murders happening right on our doorsteps! Porter Juxon Nowhere's safe any more, no matter how many Steel Watchers Lord Gortash tries to jam down our throats. Wuloona Dor If you ask me, I don't think Gortash even deserves to be called a lord. Fist Ernestus That's enough of that! Lord Gortash has everything under control - we don't need agitators like you ruining morale. Wuloona Dor What are you gonna do? Arrest us? Fist Ernestus If that what it takes to keep the peace! Wuloona Dor If you say so, mate. Porter Juxon Why would they go to all that effort just to lie to us? Wuloona Dor It's obvious, isn't it? To placate us. To keep us all nice and obedient. Wuloona Dor They don't like it when we think too much - we might question their authority. Fist Ernestus I'm warning you... Porter Juxon There's one of you and four of us - do you really think you can take all of us at once? Fist Ernestus I... I can go and get back up. Wuloona Dor And do you think we're just gonna sit here and wait for you and your hog friends to come back and arrest us? Fist Ernestus Look, I'm just trying to do my job, all right? Porter Juxon So what can we do about it? All the lies they're publishing, I mean. Wuloona Dor Not a lot unless you want to set fire to the Baldur's Mouth Gazette headquarters. Fist Ernestus I'm still right here, you know... Wuloona Dor Tch, we do know, thank you - we just don't care. Wuloona Dor Besides, I don't think that'd achieve much in the long run. The problem's at the top - it always is. Porter Juxon Perhaps sending a strongly worded letter would be a good place to start? Wuloona Dor If by 'strongly worded letter' you mean a brick through a window, then aye. Porter Juxon I'm just not one for violence, you see... Errant Souls spawn randomly for a few seconds in the House of Hope in Act Three . “ Always read the fine print. „ — Errant Soul , stuck in the House of Hope Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Errant Souls are inside the House of Hope . They spawn randomly near the party and utter some words before disappearing again. They cannot be interacted with. Quotes [ edit section | visual editor ] "Creeping, stalking, walking, crawling. I see you." "I miss the sun. I miss the stars." "Hurt me. Please." "Time to wake up, time to wake up, time to wake up." "So many pretty things in the House of Hope. You're the prettiest of all." "Always read the fine print." "Raphael sees everything you do." "Raphael hears everything you say." "Can't sleep. So tired. Can't sleep." "I am air, I am light, I am free." "I deserve this. Thank you. Thank you." "Every day there is less of me." "I can't feel my legs... I can't feel my skin." "I made a mistake. I shouldn't be here. Let me take it back." "Am I alone here? I can't see, I can't hear, I can't feel." "Listen. LISTEN." "I was going to be married tomorrow. Or was it yesterday?" "The gods cannot see me here." "Such a beautiful house. Such a beautiful prison." "This place is all entrances and no exits." "It's hot. It's cold. It's hot. It's cold." "Never sign your soul away." "There was a shadow at my door, I opened up and am no more." Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Portrait variations

Technical UID S_WYR_CeremonyRoom_Patriar_006 UUID 8bbaa981-9b92-4f19-bc4a-b2b5cb63b8e5 Stats Human_Commoner Lady Eshvelt Guthmere is a Lady of Baldur's Gate who is present for Gortash's ordination as the Archduke of the city. “ An Archduke. Finally someone who'll stand up to those wretched Absolutists. „ — Eshvelt Guthmere Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony she sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lady Eshvelt stays near the throne, listening to several other guests discussing the Steel Watch with Gortash and Ulder Ravengard , but not taking part in the conversation. If spoken to, she deems Gortash as someone who can stand up to the followers of the Cult of Absolute. If the party choose to confront Gortash, they can later find Lady Eshvelt along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the Audience Hall. Technical UID S_HAV_HavenOutcasts_FountainGuards_Melee_2 UUID 271478dd-7efb-4ca7-b40c-593bbea91a85 Stats HAV_Harper_Gnome_Melee Eqp. EQP_Rapier_Studded Harper Essius is a confident [ 2 ] Harper at the Last Light Inn in Act Two . Depending on party choices in Act Two, he assists the party during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers . “ Jaheira will see us through this matter. She always does. „ — Essius Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Essius is at the Last Light Inn's plaza, chatting with Fist Ulthred next to the fountain. Whereas Ulthred is initially skeptical and doubtful of the party, Essius attempts to talk him down and be open to the party's help. As Ulthred displays some nervousness at being in the Shadow-Cursed Lands , Essius tells him he has seen worse alleyways in Baldur's Gate . [ 3 ] If Marcus is exposed as a True Soul , Essius is Surprised and joins the fight against his summoned Crawling Claws . Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Essius frequently is amongst the Harpers who avoid being Impaled , and runs up to fight the Winged Horrors . If Isobel is not saved, Essius and everyone in Last Light Inn turn into a Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira . Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn, and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise Towers , Essius follow Jaheira to the assault on Moonrise Towers, where he, along with Harper Antony , Lymn , and Naysa survive the first assault and assists the party in the remaining fight against Absolute forces. After the main battle, if Essius survive the fight, he guards the first floor of Moonrise with the remaining Harpers . Once Ketheric Thorm is defeated and the party progress to Act Three , Essius completely disappears. Technical UID S_GLO_Expeditioner UUID 5f4048ba-72ef-43c2-9528-1c9a12f3f82f Stats CRE_LadyEsther Eqp. EQP_Rapier_BreastPlate Trs. CRE_Expeditioner_Magic_Trade Lady Esther is a member of the Society of Brilliance , located on the Rosymorn Monastery Trail during Act One . “ I left your stupid crèche, why are you still chasing me? I don't even want your bloody eggs! <...> Well, not your eggs specifically... „ — Esther , when approached by a Githyanki character (including Lae'zel) Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Esther is an adventurer employed by the Society of Brilliance to acquire a githyanki egg for a long-term nurturing experiment. Upon meeting Esther, she asks the party to steal an egg from the crèche inside Rosymorn Monastery . The party can convince her to offer an advance payment by passing a DC 21 Persuasion Check , earning at least 200 gold with no effect on companion approval. The party can give Esther an Owlbear Egg and convince her it is a githyanki egg by passing a DC 21 Nature Check , convince her it is more valuable than a githyanki egg by passing a DC 21 Deception Check , or persuade her to trick her employers by passing a DC 21 Persuasion Check . If the entire Monastery is destroyed during ⁠ Find the Blood of Lathander , Esther witnesses the building's collapse from her camp. If she is spoken to afterward, she complains about this disaster ruining her plans, going so far as to brand the party as 'uncouth' if they claim responsibility for it. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If Esther is given a genuine Githyanki Egg in Act One, Esther is dead at the docks of The Lodge , killed by Ptaris who hatched from the egg. Several notes can be found along the docks about how she and her employers subjected Ptaris to an abusive upbringing until he finally killed them in retaliation. Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to CRE_Expeditioner_Trade . STR Save Range: Normal weapon range Second Wind ( ) Healing: 1~10 + modifiers 1d10 + Fighter level ⁠ Healing Draw on your stamina to protect yourself. You regain 1d10 + Fighter Level ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Esther can be a surprisingly dangerous opponent because of her relatively high dexterity, combined with Extra Attack , Duelling , and Menacing Attack (Melee) . She can easily burst down one of the party members if she is not killed quickly, especially if she uses Action Surge . Despite this, a full party should be able to easily finish her after her first turn. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursMouth_EstraStir UUID 0517dac3-e9f9-4d40-a863-2034f4a865fb Stats Human_Commoner Estra Stir is a gossip columnist for a newspaper in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ 'How' is such an overrated question. It's the who and the why that matter, darling. „ — Estra Stir , answering how she knows the player character. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Estra Stir works for the Baldur's Mouth Gazette in the Lower City . If Enver Gortash is alive, she informs the party they are the subject of the Gazette's next issue - the juiciest one to date. Estra refuses to elaborate and rejects any arguments about the party's consent to be written about. However, her statements initiate the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses . The party can investigate Baldur's Mouth by speaking to the editor, Ettvard Needle . If Gortash is dead, Estra informs the party that they should read the Gazette to learn the real story behind his death. If ⁠ Stop the Presses was not yet initiated, it is no longer possible to start the quest by speaking with Estra. She is one of many citizens forcibly transformed into a Mind Flayer by the Netherbrain upon collecting all three Netherstones . ## Ettvard Needle
- **来源**: [Ettvard Needle](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Ettvard_Needle)
- **分类**: Characters

Ettvard Needle In-game Model Portrait Identity Male Voice / Actor Andrew Spooner Hometown Baldur's Gate Occupation Editor in chief for the Baldur's Mouth Gazette Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursMouth_Ettvard_Needle UUID c171c8b4-acb9-4633-9de4-a09176d21d73 Stats Human_Commoner Ettvard Needle is the human editor in chief for the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . He is in the main building, the Baldur's Mouth , in the Lower City . “ Gods, the untold depravity... it is unprintable. I'll be out of syndication if I publish your gore-smut confessional. „ — Ettvard Needle after the Dark Urge tells him of his exploits Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] He claims to be close with Lord Gortash and abuses his position of power in journalism to print propaganda for him. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Talking to Ettvard starts the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses if the party has not already started it elsewhere. After conversing with him, Ettvard calls the guards to evict the party from the Baldur's Mouth, which makes the entire building a restricted area, making it harder to complete the quest. The quest also only becomes time sensitive after the party has spoken to Ettvard. If Gortash is dead, Ettvard loses interest in the party and exclusively publishes articles about Gortash's death, which makes the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses unavailable. Ettvard even calls the party "old news" and shoos them away, but this does not make the building a restricted area. If Ettvard is killed, Malek Stones is promoted to editor in chief. If Malek Stones is also killed, then a new character called Syril Valdemar takes their place after a long rest. According to the Sword Coast Couriers address book, Ettvard has requested a full-time courier for shipping purposes. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_LoversFemale UUID bf8d1fd2-53ea-4df4-9924-5136a4345ef3 Stats Human_Commoner Eugenie Kenridge is on an outing with her partner at Bloomridge Park in the Lower City during Act Three . “ I'm sorry for Wendel, he does get a touch, ah, over-effusive about our courtship. Pay him no heed. „ — Eugenie Kenridge Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Eugenie and Wendel Ashgrove are conversing at the centre of Bloomridge Park. Although the pair have dated for only one month, Wendel seems to have very strong feelings for her. Eugenie attempts to tactfully break up with him, but he misunderstands and agrees that both of them could get to know many more people around them. During the battle with the cultists, Eugenie can also help the party fight alongside her if they manage to protect her, for example by using Globe of Invulnerability . But if she survives, she disappears forever after the battle. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Wendel Ashgrove I still remember our first date in this park, you know. There were certainly less Fists about. Eugenie Kenridge It's only been a month, Wendel. Of course you remember our first date. Wendel Ashgrove But what a perfect month it's been - right, darling? Eugenie Kenridge Riiight. Wendel Ashgrove You know, I really don't think I've ever felt this way about someone before. Eugenie Kenridge I remind you again, Wendel. One. Month. Wendel Ashgrove I just think this park is so beautiful, don't you, darling? Eugenie Kenridge It's a bit loud, what with all these clanking guards. Wendel Ashgrove I could ask them to keep it down. Anything for you, dear. Eugenie Kenridge Listen, Wendel, I really think we need to have a chat. Wendel Ashgrove Are we not already having a chat, my angel? Eugenie Kenridge *Sigh.* Wendel Ashgrove You said you wanted to chat, my love? Eugenie Kenridge Yes... I did want to chat, Wendel. Wendel Ashgrove What did you want to talk about, my darling? Eugenie Kenridge Well... I asked you here because... Gods. Never mind. Wendel Ashgrove Come now, you know you can tell me anything. Eugenie Kenridge I just don't know how to say it... I think we should start seeing other people. There. Wendel Ashgrove Well, there's plenty of folk in this park we could get to know! Especially with all these new Fists. They'd be great craic, I bet. Eugenie Kenridge You are impossible sometimes, Wendel. WYR_OrinsImpersonation_Smith Exxvikyap is a brass dragonborn trader in Rivington during Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Hiiiiiiiii! Want a blade? Or a bow? Or a dagger? Or maybe a spear is more your thing? You look like you know how to use a spear. Buy a spear, whaddya say? Huh? „ — Exxvikyap , speaking to a customer Contents 1 Involvement 2 Notable items sold 2.1 Weapons 2.2 Armour 2.3 Arrows 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Exxvikyap is the shop assistant of the blacksmith shop and an avid fan of its proprietor, Gyldro Angleiron . She is in the Rivington General X: 8 Y: -32 within the Rivington area, between the Rivington and Wyrm's Crossing South Span waypoints . Exxvikyap enthusiastically greets the party and offers to sell them various items. If the party ask her more about herself then she explains how excited she is to be working for the shop of the legendary Gyldro Angleiron. She hopes that one day he will allow her a chance to use the forge. If Gyldro is impersonated by Orin the Red when the party first meet him, he disappears after a long rest. After Gyldro disappears or if the party kill the real Gyldro, Exxvikyap's dialogue changes, sounding depressed and wondering when the missing blacksmith will return. The party can discover Gyldro's body in the Temple of Bhaal , but there is no way to inform her of this. Notable items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to WYR_OrinsImpersonation_Smith . Technical UID S_WYR_South_GoldQuestGiver UUID ad4a43f4-a86c-4946-a696-43a4ba4e6b45 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Eqp. EQP_Halberd_Chainmail_HelmetMetal Trs. BG_Guard Manip Falcäo is a human [ 1 ] fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is in Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . “ Hey you. I've got a pest problem - and you look like the solution. „ — Falcäo , looking to hire adventurers Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Manip Falcäo is stationed at the South Span Checkpoint at X: 23 Y: 64 . If a party member gains access to Wyrm’s Crossing (regardless of whether the Ironhand Gnomes helped them or not), Falcäo calls them to come closer, promising a generous payment for some work. If spoken to, Falcäo offers the party a deal to kill the Ironhand gnomes and bring him Wulbren's Head [ 2 ] , whose crusade against the Steel Watch has made them a thorn in the side of the Fist. The party can agree or refuse to hunt down Wulbren , the gnomes' leader; their decision does not have any impact on how Falcäo and other Fists treat them. Upon completing the quest, Falcäo rewards the party with 800 gold and advises them to keep their noses clean, lest they suffer the same fate as the gnomes. Absolute deserves a church, not a ruin. „ — Falla Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Falla is in the Moonrise Towers throne room, and stands guard over the trial presided by Ketheric Thorm . Defending Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Nightsong is freed and the Harpers launch their assault on Moonrise Towers, Falla disappears from the game and cannot be found as an enemy or a corpse. Fallen Bhaalspawn is a dead dragonborn who can be found in the Chosen's Room in the Bhaal Temple within the Undercity . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Fallen Bhaalspawn can be found next to Orin's bed inside the Chosen's Room at the back of the Bhaal Temple inside the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . According to a book in a nearby locked chest Orin had a plan to put a worm inside the bhaalspawn to make it a mindless servant, but also mentions rebuilding the temple atop its festering corpse. Interacting with the corpse results in the player character remarking, "Orin relished tormenting this poor soul." The Dark Urge [ edit section | visual editor ] The Fallen Bhaalspawn only appears in the Chosen's Room if the Dark Urge is not picked as origin, implying it is the same character. Next to this, the bhaalspawn looks exactly like the default appearance of the Dark Urge, further implying this connection. Technical UID WYR_Wyrmsway_Skeleton_Mage UUID f8d34abe-68ce-4c45-961e-71a49fd64bcd Stats Undead_Skeleton_Caster A Fallen Wizard is an undead skeleton creature only found in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Fallen Wizards appear after failing any trial in The Wyrmway proposed by Statues of Balduran . One or two of them manifest near the party once they make a wrong decision or violate the rules of the trial, accompanied by several Fallen Fighters , Fallen Rangers , and a Fallen Champion . The same groups of skeletons, including Fallen Wizards, spawn simultaneously in every unfinished Chamber of Trials and also in the central hall of the Wyrmway. In the worst-case scenario there are 7 Fallen Wizards to be defeated. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Counterspell ( + ) Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Falura the Sous-Chef In-game Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Mara Allen Occupation Sous-chef Stats Size Small Type Humanoid Race Halfling Subrace Lightfoot halfling Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 3 HP 8 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +2 Movement 7.5 m (25 ft) Weight 35 kg (70 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Features Brave Advantage on saving throws against frightened . Halfling Luck When rolling a 1 on an attack roll , ability check , or saving throw , rerolls once and uses the new result. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_LOW_SousChef UUID 635592ec-64a4-4582-a038-aa78fb6a681e Stats Halfling_Commoner Falura the Sous-Chef is a halfling employee to Lady Jannath who can potentially be found in the kitchen of Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City . “ How did you become a chef, Chef? „ — Falura Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Falura can only be found cooking alongside her head chef Chef Marjoram if Oskar Fevras was not rescued from Brem in Act One . If spoken to, she tells the party she cannot talk right now. During idle dialogue, Marjoram humourously berates her for sending raw food to Lady Jannath in a clear reference to Kitchen Nightmares . If Oskar Fevras was rescued, the manor is haunted and Falura is sent away on a temporary leave of absence at the request of Chamberlain Mercer . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Falura has some interesting dialogue with Chef Marjoram, including a reference to the show Kitchen Nightmares : Chef Marjoram You served this to Lady Jannath? It's RAW! Falura the Sous-Chef Sorry, Chef. Chef Marjoram I can't serve apologies, can I? Make it again, and cook it this time. Falura the Sous-Chef Yes, Chef. Chef Marjoram Is your tongue half-baked too? Louder! Falura the Sous-Chef YES, CHEF! Falura the Sous-Chef How many more mouths will we have to feed? Chef Marjoram As many as Lady Jannath desires. So keep cooking! Falura the Sous-Chef How did you become a chef, Chef? Chef Marjoram I trained in Duke Ravengard's kitchens, under Chef Dinethaar Marsh. Falura the Sous-Chef Was Chef Marsh a good teacher? Chef Marjoram He was an efficient teacher. I have the burns to prove it. Falura the Sous-Chef Should I slice the radishes like this? Chef Marjoram No, no, no - thinner! Make them elegant, and make them count . Those are the last we have. Falura the Sous-Chef Can't we just use something else? Chef Marjoram Spoken like the cook you are. I'll never make a chef of you. EQP_Ogre_Club Trs. FOR_SchoolOgre_Dumb Fank is an ogre in the Blighted Village during Act One . “ No chicken. Taste like fish! „ — Fank discussing what a tiefling tastes like Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] See Lump the Enlightened for a detailed guide of this interaction. Fank is in the ruined schoolhouse of the Blighted Village with his companions Chock and Lump the Enlightened . The trio are feasting on a Dead Tiefling . If the party approach, the ogres ask the party to show a Brand of the Absolute from Priestess Gut . If the interacting party member is not branded, they must convince the ogres not to attack. On success, the party can also convince the ogres to work for them instead of the Absolute, which leads Lump to relinquish Lump's War Horn . LOW_CountingHouse_Guard Cashguard Artillerist Faona is a human member of the Cashguard, in the Counting House in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ Head Banker Glitterbeard! You look a little different today. Or - you're not him, which means this door isn't for you. Very sorry. „ — Faona Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Faona is on the first floor, guarding the door to Rakath Glitterbeard's office alongside Cashguard Basher Karol . Faona assumes that Karol is a member of the Guild . Karol tries to deny this. Word is he has Guild connections - that means Guild gold, nothing he can report stolen. Cashguard Basher Karol You need to get wise, young one. Pretty alone doesn't last. Cashguard Artillerist Faona You're Guild too, aren't you? Cashguard Basher Karol What makes you say that? Cashguard Artillerist Faona You're always guarding Glitterbeard's door, no matter who's on with you. You're definitely Guild - not that you'd tell me.
