Technical UID S_CRE_MainCheckpointMainGuard UUID 161701af-17b7-4def-b378-5f24e95d667f Stats Githyanki_Gish Eqp. CRE_MainCheckPointMainGuard Trs. CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Gish Far'aag is a githyanki gish who guards the entryway to Crèche Y'llek . Anyone seeking passage into the crèche's must first convince her to let them through. “ A ghaik thrall is something to eradicate, not reason with. „ — Far'aag Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Far'aag is initially friendly to the party, but can become hostile depending on dialogue choices taken during dialogue. Certain outcomes of Discover the Artefact's Secrets will also result in Far'aag becoming hostile. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] A conversation with this character is triggered shortly after entering the crèche through the front entrance. Depending on the outcome of the party's conversation with Kith'rak Voss , the party can have the option to say that they are carrying "the weapon" he was seeking. This has the benefit of allowing the conversation to conclude without mentioning the presence of any tadpoles in the characters' heads. Far'aag will ask the party to show them the artifact as proof. The response options to this include: Produce the artefact as evidence. [PERFORMANCE]  I SPEAK AS AN AVATAR OF QUEEN VLAAKITH. YOU WILL LET ME PASS, VIN'IISK.  (DC 30) [PERSUASION]  I was told to bring the weapon to the highest authority possible. That doesn't look like you. (DC 18) [GITHYANKI] [PERSUASION]  I will report to your kith'rak as protocol dictates. Do not forget yourself. (DC 18) Failing either of these checks will cause her and the nearby guards to become hostile. There is also the option to reveal that they seek a cure for their tadpole. Letting Lae'zel speak for the Party's behalf also causes her to do the same. The party can also simply demand to be let through: [INTIMIDATION]  Let me pass. Fighting me will end badly for you. (DC 18) [PERSUASION]  You githyanki hate illithid. I have proof that they're invading. We need your help. (DC 18) [DARK URGE] [INTIMIDATION]  I'm an unmatched killer. You want me as your ally. (DC 18  ) [RANGER] [INTIMIDATION]  I hunt monsters. Either that's you, or it's the mind flayers - your choice. (DC 18  ) [FIGHTER] [HISTORY]  Try to recall and invoke the ancient githyanki war rites of parley. (DC 18  ) One way or another, Far'aag relents without much convincing to let the players pass and seek out the ghustil in the infirmary, though her speaking tone becomes less friendly. LOW_CountingHouse_Guard Cashguard Captain Faril is the captain of the Counting House's Cashguard. “ Word is the Gondian guild has downed tools and gone walkabouts. „ — Faril Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Faril guards the door to the lower levels of the Counting House in the Lower City . She asks for a Vault Pass , and the party can either obtain one from Head Clerk Meadhoney and present it or attempt to bribe Faril to access the vaults: [PERSUASION]  All that gold you guard, and you never get a taste of it yourself? Seems unfair. (5000) (DC 18) [DECEPTION]  You've had stranger visitors than me today. I won't be noticed, and you can make a tidy profit. (DC 18)  (if the party has spoken to Meadhoney and learned about the cultists) [DECEPTION]  My pass was stolen. Truly. This is all the coin I have left. (5000) (DC 20) [INTIMIDATION]  You can make some gold, or die guarding someone else's. Choose. MOO_Cultist Pilgrim Farimorn is a half-elf in Moonrise Towers in Act Two . “ Not all of us survived the shadows to stand here. My wife, my sons... they were unworthy. „ — Farimorn Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Farimorn is in the main hall of Moonrise Towers at X: -163 Y: -176 . He is part a group of new Absolutist pilgrims, consisting of him and Iong , Nalira , Sul , and Taima . They are observed by Belub , who shows contempt for the pilgrims, and remarks on their lack of skills and usefulness. The party can either convince Belub to keep the pilgrims, or tell him to get rid of them. [PERSUASION]  They have potential. Great warriors have grown from less. (DC 14) It's not our place to question the Absolute's will. Then get rid of them. The undeserving should be purged. The first two options result in Belub sending them to the war camp west of Reithwin , where the pilgrims disappear. Telling Belub to get rid of the pilgrims results in their death. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pilgrim Nalira Where do you hail from, brother? Pilgrim Fairmorn I was a farrier in Dessarin Valley. Then the dreams came. Pilgrim Iong My brothers had the dreams too, same as me. But they wouldn't admit it. Pilgrim Nalira The Absolute calls us all to Her design. Your family will answer - eventually. Pilgrim Taima To stand this close to Her power... I never thought I'd make it. Pilgrim Iong I wouldn't have, if not for the lantern-bearer. To think the Absolute graces such a creature as that... Pilgrim Fairmorn We are each of us threads in Her design. Even those we once called monsters. Pilgrim Nalira Brothers. Sister. Pray with me while we wait. Pilgrim Fairmorn I'm not worthy. I... I never learned the words. Pilgrim Nalira Yes, you did. She gives them to you fully formed. Can you hear Her? Pilgrim Fairmorn Of many hearts, one soul. Of many thoughts, one mind... Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party go to camp between defeating the Cult of the Absolute members at Moonrise Towers and entering the rooftop, they may find Talli fighting against Farimorn and the other pilgrims of the Absolute Iong , Nalira , Sul , and Taima . Technical UID S_WYR_SmugglersCave_Guild_Leader UUID 2457049b-d7ee-43bc-932e-cc9e104933bc Stats WYR_SmugglersCave_Guild_Gnome Eqp. EQP_WYR_Farlin Trs. BG_Bandit Farlin is a member of the Guild and envoy of Nine-Fingers Keene . “ Nine-Fingers sends her love, arsehole. Your Stone Lord's a dead man walking. „ — Farlin Contents 1 Involvement 2 Speak with Dead 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Loot 3.3 Allies 4 Related quests 5 Notes and references Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Farlin is on the Western Beach west of the South Span Checkpoint in Wyrm's Crossing during Act Three at X: -212 Y: Y:87 . She and a group of Guild members are arguing with the Stone Lord's crew lead by Caïros near a docked ship from Moonrise Towers , accessible by taking the western path between the South Span Checkpoint and Open Hand Temple . Upon approaching the two groups, Farlin asks for help fighting the Stone Lord's men, promising that the Guild will pay. If the party agrees to help, the Guild joins them in a fight against the Stone Lord's men. Doing so grants the inspiration ⁠ Stacking the Deck for party members with the Criminal background. If the party declines to assist, appeals to Cairos, or prevents either side from fighting, both groups turn hostile. The party can also wait nearby for the fight to begin, join in, or wait for it to end. If the party sides with Farlin, she puts in a good word for them with Tusgront [ 1 ] who guards the entrance to the Guild. He then lets the party inside the Guildhall without requiring a dialogue check. If Caïros' side wins the fight and the party kills them afterwards, party members with the Criminal background gain the inspiration ⁠ Easy Pickings . After the combat, if Farlin's side wins, Farlin claims everything in the area for the Guild. If a party member asserts that the loot is theirs, she becomes hostile and attacks. However, if she is knocked out instead of killed, and a long rest occurs, she still puts in a good word with Tusgront. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] If Farlin is killed, her corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . She explains she was sent from the Guild to seize the Stone Lord's haul for Nine-Fingers Keene , though she did not know what it was besides being a valuable item. Who are you? Farlin Farlin... from the Guild... Who were you fighting? Farlin The Stone Lord's men... interloperes ... What were they here for? Farlin Don't know... something valuable... What were you doing here? Farlin Seizing their haul... for Nine-Fingers... Who is the Stone Lord? Farlin Fury... threat to... everyone... Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_DocksRoad_Sailor_001 UUID c5d28a10-3ed4-41f2-99bc-c421ada58001 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Felgi Diggums is attempting to make deliveries in the Lower City during Act Three . “ Even before they got those big metal bruisers, the Fists were obnoxious, but now... „ — Felgi Diggums Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Felgi and Kolobeg are two sailors near Grey Harbour Docks . They are trying to deliver their crates, but are prevented from accessing the area by Fist Gneiss and Fist Pantella . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Steel Watch Foundry is intact [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg We can't deliver our goods to the docks? Why? Fist Pantella New rule - it's a restricted area, top security. Felgi Diggums But I can see people down there on the docks going about their business! Fist Gneiss Oh, we'll get to them soon enough. Kolobeg We've got a job to do. These goods need to get delivered. Fist Pantella And I have a duty to the city and to Lord Gortash . So halt right there. Felgi Diggums Why this sudden restriction on visiting the docks, though? Fist Gneiss Somehow, citizen, Lord Gortash forgot to tell me. Isn't that strange? Kolobeg But I made a deliver to the docks just yesterday! Fist Pantella Sorry, citizen, the docks are now a restricted area. Felgi Diggums Talk straight. Are you really just looking for a bribe? Fist Gneiss Are you looking to get stomped flat by a Steel Watcher ? If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg The foundry's a wreck! There's nothing left to guard! Can we deliver our goods to the docks now? Fist Pantella Not just yet, citizen. The whole place is a crime scene. Felgi Diggums We just need to go past the foundry to make our delivery on the wharf. Fist Gneiss Don't split hairs with me. You go no farther. Kolobeg Come on, Saer Fist, let us past - these deliveries are urgent. Fist Pantella More urgent than justice? More urgent than the rule of law? Felgi Diggums Now you're just mocking us. Fist Gneiss Heh. You've got brains, for a dwarf. Kolobeg Look, we just need to go past the foundry along the docks. Fist Pantella My orders don't admit of any exceptions. Felgi Diggums You know, if you'd just look the other way for a minute... Fist Gneiss You trying to bribe me? If so, where's the bribe? If Enver Gortash is killed [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Pantella Security's tightened since Gortash's death. You stay in your designated district. Kolobeg Aw, come on, Saer Fist, we got urgent deliveries to make. Fist Gneiss Urgent, is it? Why, you could be trying to sneak Gortash's assassins out in your cargo. I'd better search your goods. Kolobeg You're joking, right? Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Felix Farrahd is buried in the Graveyard (Lower City) in the Lower City under the tombstone labelled "R. Sandryl" . The Official Will which is in his grave says that he was aware of his death being close. However, he rejected everything his family was going to do about this. I have clients to brief, and they're sharp as spoons. „ — Fentamia Viney Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fentamia Viney stands in the corner of reception room in the Wyrm's Rock Fortress. She is a lawyer, preparing to present her current case to a Flaming Fist investigator. While waiting, she practices a defensive speech with her clients, Arborio Rolfin and Civilian , but from time to time both let slip that they are guilty. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fentamia Viney Let's rehearse this one more time. Pretend I'm a Fist, and tell me what you were doing in the house. Civilian Well, your Fistliness, we broke down the door because it sounded like somebody was in trouble inside. Arborio Rolfin The house was on fire. We were rescuing people. Fentamia Viney I spoke to a witness who says you entered the house before the fire started. Civilian Who said that? I'll break their bloody legs! Arborio Rolfin Err, what my friend means to say is that the witness must have been mistaken. Probably a drunk. Fentamia Viney Better. LOW_CountingHouse_BhaalCultist Death's Head of Bhaal Feona is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , in the High Security Vaults in the Counting House in the Lower City . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the ⁠ The High Harper quest, the party can go to the Counting House in hopes of catching up to Minsc. Inside the vaults, the party can witness Minsc emerge from a Mimic and defeat it. 'Jaheira' then appears with a handful of Bhaalists including Feona, and teleports away with Minsc, leaving the cultists to attack the party and the staff. Death's Head of Bhaal Feona She... will find you... What does the cult want with Minsc? Death's Head of Bhaal Feona Minsc... is dead... Stone Lord... lives... WYR_SharranInformer_Basic Ferg Drogher is a human trader encountered in Act Three . He is an opportunist looking to make gold off the crisis in Rivington , buying heirlooms from desperate refugees in need of gold and selling their goods elsewhere with his shadowy supplier. “ Alas, you cannot eat grandmother's ashes, nor can you easily trade a golden candelabra for a bowl of soup. That is where I come in - liquidity. Their heirlooms, for my gold. „ — Ferg Drogher , explaining where his wares come from Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Ferg is at X: 45 Y: -95 when the party enters the refugee camp in Rivington . Though posing as an unscrupulous trader on the surface, Ferg is actually a Sharran lookout standing watch for Shadowheart's return. The party's interactions with him are entirely dependent on whether Shadowheart is nearby at the time, and whether or not she rejected Shar in The Chosen of Shar . If Shadowheart is nearby, he beckons to the party when they come close. If Shadowheart embraced Shar, he states that he has been waiting for her return and provides directions to the House of Grief. He hints at brewing unrest within the cloister, foreshadowing the upcoming fight with Viconia DeVir the Mother Superior. If Shadowheart rejected Shar, he threatens her and provides the same directions to the House of Grief for her to receive punishment. When this dialogue finishes, he walks away forever, locking the party out of his trade goods. If Shadowheart was given the Noblestalk , then she may ask about Rennald , the child she saw in her memories. Ferg replies that Rennald is no more, and that he will leave the rest for Shadowheart to figure out. Special stock [ edit section | visual editor ] Ferg has a special stock of goods. He can be convinced to sell it with a Persuasion check if Shadowheart is not nearby. If Shadowheart embraced Shar, having her near bypasses this check. The party can also bypass this check by using Speak with Dead on the Refugee Corpse on the cliffs of northeastern Rivington and learning about the Gemless Ring . Notable items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to WYR_SharranInformer_Basic . Cold Snap Dwarven Thrower Hellrider Longbow Special stock [ edit section | visual editor ] Nymph Cloak Robe of Supreme Defences Sethan Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and abiltiies [ edit section | visual editor ] Disarming Attack (Melee) ( + )   –   Shortsword Damage: 1~6 + modifiers 1d6 ⁠ Piercing + Superiority Die Focus your attack on your foe's hands and possibly force them to drop the weapons they are holding. They'll have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls and be unable to move. WIS Save Range: Normal weapon range Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Shortsword Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Leather Armour Ringless Gem Scroll of Confusion Scroll of Darkness Shortsword - 2x Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Although Ferg Drogher can be a fully functional merchant, he is not marked as such on the minimap. This may be a bug, or possibly intended, since the ability to trade with him depends on story choices Shadowheart made beforehand. If Ferg is Knocked Out and the party long rests, he cannot be spoken with later, though he can still be stolen from. If stolen from, Ferg quickly runs away and briefly disappears during the period in which traders normally search for the offending larcenist; he returns soon afterwards. v t e Rivington v t e Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRock_AudienceHallGuard_006 UUID 6cae7182-8327-4239-9de6-85e573a6df7c Stats FlamingFist_Halfling_Melee_Attacker Fist Fernhollow is a halfling fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the Wyrm's Rock Fortress in Act Three . “ Don't like the look of that Gortash. He's got nice hair. Only troublemakers got hair like that. „ — Fernhollow Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Ferhollow with several other Flaming Fists ( Fist Bella , Fist Diallo , Fist Earthdigger , Fist Klaas , Fist Kyberos and Fist Quickstitch ) are standing watch in the Audience Hall of the Wyrm’s Rock Fortress at the ceremony of Enver Gortash being ordained as an Archduke of Baldur's Gate . She is guarding the door to an outer balcony at X: 32 Y: 221 . If spoken to, Fernhollow is rather sceptical about Gortash being chosen to rule the city, saying that nobody asked her opinion on electing him, and doubting his good intentions. Fernhollow is one of two halfling members of the Flaming Fist who might be encountered throughout the game. The other one is Fist Anderson , who appears at the gallows only in case Counsellor Florrick is executed. Technical UID S_LOW_BramptonOrphan_Child UUID 6c4a9629-2719-4dcf-a79c-fcf90249065a Stats Tiefling_Child Fevrokis is a tiefling child who is distraught after finding the bodies of his dead parents in the Brampton district of the Lower City in Act Three . “ I'm scared. Why won't they get up? Why... „ — Fevrokis Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Fevrokis was in the Lower City with his parents when he followed a cat and became lost. When he returned to his parents Skulla and Vezrol , he found them both dead, murdered by an unknown assailant. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fevrokis can be found beneath an arch near Felogyr's Fireworks with two local thugs, Phelgro Dorph and Hari Nodles . The pair are trying to console Fevrokis, who is standing next to his parents' corpses. Hari wants to assume responsibility and help Fevrokis while Phelgro is afraid of the repercussions. Hari considers temporarily adopting Fevrokis until they can find permanent accommodation. Phelgro suggests bringing him to the Flaming Fist , but Hari believes that the Fists will hold them responsible for the death of Fevrokis' parents. Instead, Hari suggests bringing the child to the Guild , but Phelgro believes that the Guild is too busy with city matters to help them. With no other options, Hari attempts to soothe Fevrokis by offering to find someone to "help" his parents and then get him something to eat. Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] The vignette between Fevrokis, Hari, and Phelgro plays out as ambient dialogue while in the area. However, the party can also speak to them for some one-liners. If Halsin is in the party, he remarks, "This city fails those who need its aid the most. No child should be abandoned like this." Hari and Phelgro's reactions to the party will vary depending on the resolution of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fevrokis Mummy? Daddy? Please get up. Please! Hari Nodles Hey, hey - shh, all right? Look at me - it's gonna be okay. Phelgro Dorph Shit. We need to tell the Flaming Fist - get this kid some help. Hari Nodles And have them lock us up for two murders we didn't do? Hari Nodles They're too scared to come here anyway. We'd have better luck with the Guild. Phelgro Dorph Between the Steel Watch and the Stone Lord, the Guild have barely got the strength to look after their own. Fevrokis I'm scared. Why won't they get up? Why... Phelgro Dorph We can't get involved with this. Hari Nodles Don't listen to him, kid - we've got you. Hari Nodles Can you tell us what happened? Fevrokis I-I got lost. I was following a kitty. Fevrokis When I found them again - when I came back - they were lying here... Hari Nodles Hush, now - it's all right. We're gonna help you. Phelgro Dorph Oh, we are, are we? Hari Nodles Don't be such a heartless bastard. Phelgro Dorph I'm not! I just don't wanna get in trouble, that's all! Hari Nodles Kid's gonna need a family no matter what happens. Phelgro Dorph You want to adopt it? Hari Nodles Just until he has somewhere better to go. Hari Nodles And he's not an 'it'. Fevrokis I want to go home... Hari Nodles I know you do, kid. I know. Tell you what... Hari Nodles We'll try and find someone who can help your ma and da and then we'll get you something to eat, all right? Hari Nodles And it can be anything you want. I promise. Phelgro Dorph Help them? They're dead. Hari Nodles Shut up, would you? Fevrokis O-okay. Let's do that, please. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_FOR_GnomeGoblin1 UUID b2c582af-bc69-48b3-a004-648562dab404 Stats GOB_Goblin_Fezzerk Eqp. FOR_UnfortunateGnome_Golbin_HeavyAxe Trs. GOB_Goblin_Generic Fezzerk leads a gang of goblins at Blighted Village in Act One , tormenting an unfortunate deep gnome as part of the ⁠ Rescue the Gnome quest. Depending on whether he is spared, he can make a minor appearance in Act Two . “ Look what we got here - another little birdie wantin' to fly! „ — Fezzerk , when approached Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Fezzerk and his gang are on the western most side of the Blighted Village where the windmill is, laughing at Barcus Wroot who is strapped to the machine. This starts the quest ⁠ Rescue the Gnome . If approached, Fezzerk and his gang confront the party. The party can ask him what he is doing, or ask him to let them pass. If they ask what he is doing, they can that demand Barcus be let down, either by persuading Fezzerk to pick another victim or intimidating him. Asking to let the party pass results in Fezzerk demanding 1000 gold, which the party can decide to pay or haggle down. If paid, or convinced not to pay, Fezzerk lets the party leave, but if he is approached again a fight breaks out. Lastly, the party can attack Fezzerk and his gang. If during the fight Fezzerk is severely injured, he surrenders when near death, while the other members of his gang flee. It is then possible to interrogate him, demand that he gives up his belongings, or kill him. If spared, he makes a minor reappearance in Act Two . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Fezzerk survives Act One , he journeys to the Throne Room of Moonrise Towers . He, some other goblins, and potentially Minthara are being judged for the failure to retrieve the Mysterious Artefact . Whether he and the other goblins are spared or killed is left up to the interacting party member. That honour should fall to a daughter. „ — Minthara , on speaking to Ffion's corpse Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] A dominatrix of renown at Sharess' Caress , Ffion went missing and the party is tasked with finding her in ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Ffion's corpse is hidden underneath the bed in the secret room of Fraygo's Flophouse's attic. It can be found after inspecting the blood on the ground and passing a DC 10 Investigation Check , or destroying the bed. Reading the pieces of literature found throughout the room reveals that her death is closely related to the ⁠ Open Hand Temple Murders and the ⁠ spree of murders in Baldur's Gate . She was murdered by her own son Dolor , a Cultist of Bhaal who aims to become an Unholy Assassin. Fig In-game Model Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Ami Okumura Jones Faction Harpers , Jaheira's Family Family Jaheira (adoptive mother) Jord (adoptive brother) Tate (adoptive brother) Rion (adoptive sister) Jhessem (adoptive sister) Hometown Elerrathin's Home , Baldur's Gate Stats Size Small Type Humanoid Race Human Technical UID S_LOW_JaheirasHouse_JaheiraYoungestDaughter UUID 26cf6556-8d9a-4d10-b2af-3b1d497cc115 Stats Human_Child Fig is a human child in the Lower City in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Stand on your liver! „ — Fig , greeting the party [ 1 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Fig is Jaheira's adoptive child and lives in what is now Elerrathin's Home along with Jaheira's other children. He is the brother of Carmen Pennygood the owner of Carm's Garms in Wyrm's Crossing . “ Oh gods no. No no no. My friend, it is my turn to save you - from the disgusting tripe-garb my sister has adorned you with. „ — Figaro Pennygood , if he sees the player character wearing clothes from his sister's shop Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act Three 2 Store 2.1 Camp Clothing 2.2 Camp Shoes 2.3 Underwear 2.4 Hats 2.5 Very rare Dyes 2.6 Rare dyes 3 Notable loot 4 Related quests 5 Related literature 6 Speak with Dead 7 Notes Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Figaro stocks a large collection of clothing Dyes and expensive Camp Clothing . He is one of the murder targets during the quest ⁠ Investigate the Murders . If Dolor escapes at the Wine Festival , he travels to the Facemaker's Botique to kill Figaro. When walking in on this attempted murder, sneaking closer allows Dolor to kill Figaro, whereas announcing the party's presence saves him. Buying anything from Figaro grants the ⁠ Threads of Fame to party members with the Entertainer background. If Figaro is killed, his corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Figaro's assistant Phlanders Hort replaces him as the primary trader of the store. Figaro's attitude towards the party often changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Why were you killed? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Leon's Diary references making a deal for a "disguise" with "Figaro", most likely referring to Figaro Pennygood. The Forgery Kit in his basement next to The Last Will and Testament of Julio Facemaker suggests that he modified his father's will. After the encounter with Dolor, a character wearing clothing or shoes purchased at his sister Carmen's shop that talks with Figaro triggers a unique dialogue whereby he recognizes and disparages his sister's clothing. Figaro's name may be a reference to the central character of the same name from Pierre Beaumarchais' trilogy of plays: Le Barbier de Séville ou la Précaution inutile (1775), La Folle Journée, ou Le Mariage de Figaro (1778), and La Mère coupable (1793). The best known of the many operatic adaptations are Gioachino Rossini's Il barbiere di Siviglia, ossia L'inutile precauzione (1816) and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's Le nozze di Figaro (1786). v t e Lower Technical UID S_UND_HookHorror_Hermit UUID 2f00e363-09b2-4573-badc-f0995bef6610 Stats UND_HookHorrorHermit Eqp. EQP_Staff_Robe Filro the Forgotten is a hostile male drow wizard located in the Dread Hollow area of the Underdark . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Filro is located near the Sussur Tree in the Underdark . He is hostile toward the party from the start and fights alongside the Hook Horrors , that patrol around the Sussur Tree. Filro holds the Icy Crystal , one of the three pieces required to rebuild the powerful Mourning Frost . He can be communed with using Speak with Dead . History [ edit section | visual editor ] Xargrim , Filro, and Dhourn were trying to find the Adamantine Forge somewhere within the Underdark. Filro was tasked with learning about any defense mechanisms within the forge and learned of a guardian of the forge that could be injured while it was in magma, and was vulnerable to a "hot hammer". Abandoned by his companions after they turned on each other, Filro was found by a pack of Hook Horrors who took him in and cared for him. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who are you? Filro Filro... forgotten... forsaken... You lived among these creatures? Filro My pack... found me... fed me... gnome flesh... How did you come to be here? Filro Chasing... mystery... riddle... lie... the Adamantine Forge... The Adamantine Forge - what is that? Filro Workshop... of great Silouv... Yali... Filro Artefacts... beyond price ... Where would I find this forge? Filro Location... was Dhourn's task... I learned... of the Guardian... What's the 'Guardian'? Filro Protector... of the Adamantine Forge... Filro Born... from hellish heat... in hellish heat... destroyed... Who is this Dhourn your records mention? Filro Friend... enemy... like Xargrim The glowing tree - what is it? Filro It... stills the Weave... protects me from... the others... What others? Filro Xargrim... Dhourn... Filro Three seek... Adamantine Forge... only one of us... may find... Reading Filro's notes before speaking with his corpse unlocks the question "Your notes mention a 'Guardian' - what is it?" , which results in the same answer as above. If the party kill the nearby Hook Horrors , the interacting party member must pass a check first before Filro answers any questions: [DECEPTION]  You're confused. I would never harm something as beautiful as your beloved. (DC 20) [PALADIN OF KELEMVOR] [CLERIC OF KELEMVOR] [PERSUASION]  If you wish to see your beloved in the afterlife, I can smooth the way. (DC 10) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  ANSWER ME!  (DC 15  ) [WARLOCK] [SORCERER] [INTIMIDATION]  You are in my power. I do not ask, I command . (DC 15) If the check is failed while disguised , it can be removed and Speak with Dead can be re-cast as if the check was passed. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Fire Bolt ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Fire Hurl a mote of fire. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Hold Person ( + ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't Move , Act , or React . Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) [ verify ] Hypnotic Pattern ( + ) Hypnotise creatures that can see the pattern. They cannot attack you. They cannot move nor act. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Shield ( + ) When you are about to be hit by an enemy, use your Reaction to increase your Armour Class by 5. You also take no damage from Magic Missile . These effects last until the start of your next turn. Range: Self Tasha's Hideous Laughter ( + ) Leave a creature Prone with laughter, without the ability to get up. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Thunderwave ( + ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Thunder Release a wave of thunderous force that pushes away all creatures and objects in an area, while also dealing Thunder damage. CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Hook Horror - 4x Encounter details [ edit section | visual editor ] Filro uses the the height advantage he has among the cliffs and roots to throw down debilitating spells onto intruders for the hook horrors to pick off. He favors casting Tasha's Hideous Laughter to make his enemies fall Prone , leaving them open for a Hook Horror's deadly Multiattack (Hook Horror) . Grouping up near him on the high ground can also lead to a lethal outcome if he uses his Thunderwave to shove party members off the cliff. If the Bulette is still alive when the party begins the fight with Filro and the Hook Horrors, then there is a chance of it burrowing out of the ground to join the fight. Its Territorial passive leads to it attacking the Hook Horrors before going after the party. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Filro has low Wisdom and Charisma , making him weak to spells with such Saving Throws . A well aimed Shove can also instantly kill him via fall damage or by knocking him into a chasm, though in the latter case the Icy Crystal he carries will be lost. The party can also consider not fighting the Bulette until it makes its appearance during this fight. The Bulette and Hook Horrors deal good damage to each other, potentially weakening all of them enough for the party to make easier kills. Also, if Sovereign Glut is an Attached Follower , it can use its Animating Spores ability to revive a Hook Horror as a "Spore Servant", allowing use of their powerful natural abilities against the other Horrors and the insane wizard. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Icy Crystal Potion of Feather Fall Quarterstaff Scribbled Notes Scroll of Mirror Image Scroll of Misty Step Scroll of Sleep Simple Robe Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Tattered Scroll Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ The Adamantine Forge Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party kill Filro before encountering Dhourn, they can tell Dhourn this instead of discussing the Adamantine Forge. If the party deceive Dhourn into believing Filro had nothing of note, combat with Dhourn can be avoided entirely. Filro can be heard singing a song to himself before he is approached and triggers combat. The lyrics are: "The Bitch Queen shan't take me, my joy, ahoy / Bellows and swallows, my joy, ahoy / Melinda, my true love, my true love, my true... / Where have you got to, my darling, my joy" v t e Underdark Characters Attached Followers Glut Creatures Bulette Hook Horror Minotaur Spectator Decrepit Village Garmor Gekh Coal Holvik Lurgan Shattered Duergar Dread Hollow Baelen Bonecloak Filro Ebonlake Grotto Dead Myconid Sprout Deep Rothé Duergar Spore Servant (guard caster) Duergar Spore Servant (guard melee) Duergar Spore Servant (patrol melee) Duergar Spore Servant (ranged) Hook Horror Spore Servant Mossy Myconid Noxious Myconid Restless Myconid Spaw Thulla Xargrim Festering Cove BOOOAL Kuo-toa Kuo-toa Hunter Pooldripp Petrified Drow Arcagh Artimezt Dhourn Izwae Moy Tecothy Plants Barrelstalk Bibberbang Nightlight Timmask Torchstalk Traders Blurg Derryth Bonecloak Omeluum Other Animated Armour Bernard Dead Drow Locations Arcane Tower Decrepit Village Dread Hollow Ebonlake Grotto Festering Cove Selûnite Outpost Storehouse Quests Avenge Glut's Circle Cure the Poisoned Gnome Defeat the Duergar Intruders Deliver Nere's Head Find a Cure Find the Missing Boots Find the Mushroom Picker Find the Nightsong Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Reach Moonrise Towers

He appears to be lost and is near the Sorcerous Sundries in the Lower City during Act Three . “ You again? You must be as lost as we are. „ — Filson Vago , when talking to him a second time Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Filson Vago and his companion Saer Drana Hoyte have both stopped at a fork in the road and are discussing whether they should ask for directions. They are looking for the Facemaker's Boutique but are currently on the opposite side of town. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Filson Vago You're certain Figaro's is in this part of town? Saer Drana Hoyte I wouldn't say I'm certain . Just optimistic. Filson Vago We're lost, aren't we? Saer Drana Hoyte Why don't we just retrace our steps? Filson Vago Great idea. Do you remember which way we came? Saer Drana Hoyte Left, left, right, down the stairs and - or was it up the stairs? Filson Vago I'm going to ask for directions. Saer Drana Hoyte No, no - you mustn't! The city is full of criminals. We can't let them know we're vulnerable. Saer Drana Hoyte Fine. Technical UID S_DEN_ScoutCaptive UUID f5b5819f-1636-4f2e-82bb-709522cc399f Stats DEN_Findal Findal is a lightfoot halfling who can be found in the Underground Passage in Act One . “ Oh, thank you, thank you. I thought I was going to die down here. „ — Findal , after being rescued Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Findal is unconscious in the Underground Passage surrounded by Gresh , Gurza , Torrack , and Worm . The party can ignore him or enter the fray to defeat the goblins . If Findal's health is restored during combat, he joins the fight as an ally even if Sazza is in the party. He explains that he had been gathering herbs nearby when the Goblins captured him to interrogate him about a weapon, of which he knows nothing about. If Findal survives the encounter with the Goblins, he warns the party that the Underground Passage is trapped before departing for the Grove. This grants ⁠ A Timely Rescue for party members with the Folk Hero background. However, if Sazza is in the party, Findal realises he has stumbled upon a rescue attempt. The party can: Deceive Findal into believing that Halsin asked them to free Sazza DC 15 Deception Check Persuade Findal that Sazza will help them destroy the Goblin Camp DC 15 Persuasion Check Intimidate Findal DC 15 Intimidation Check Give Sazza to Findal Failing a check causes Findal to become hostile and attack. If Sazza is given to Findal, both of them enter combat with each other. If Findal is rescued before confronting Kagha in ⁠ Investigate Kagha , he will join the party in defeating the Shadow Druids . If the Goblin Camp is dismantled before the party explore the Underground Passage, Findal's corpse is found along the path, and the Key of the Ancients can be looted from him. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] After the party rescue Findal, he expresses his gratitude, to which the party can ask questions or threaten him. Don't thank me yet. I'm here to finish what they started.   +1   -1   -1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Cure Wounds ( + ) Healing: 1~8 + modifiers 1d8 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Healing Heal a creature you can touch. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Entangle ( + ) Vines sprout from the ground, turning it into Difficult Terrain and possibly Entangling creatures within. Entangled creatures cannot move. An ally can use its help action to try and tear away the vines. STR Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Poison Spray ( ) Damage: 1~12 1d12 ⁠ Poison Project a puff of noxious gas, dealing 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Poison to a target. CON Save Range: 3 m (10 ft) Thunderwave ( + ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Thunder Release a wave of thunderous force that pushes away all creatures and objects in an area, while also dealing Thunder damage. Technical UID S_LOW_Jannath UUID f64fa57e-8061-4eb4-8d46-1ac743e1852d Stats Human_Commoner Lady Fireliia Jannath is a Human in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Oskar, if you're still in there - listen to my voice! This is not you, please let me help you! „ — Fireliia Jannath , pleading to a possessed Oskar Fevras Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Free the Artist Lady Jannath is the fiancé of Oskar Fevras . She can be found at her estate in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . If the party rescued Oskar Fevras during ⁠ Free the Artist in Act One , he is possessed by a ghost in her bedroom, taunting Lady Jannath and claiming that he only married her for her gold. Three Poltergeists then appear and engage the party in combat. Once they are dealt with, Oskar falls unconscious and Jannath recognizes the party as Oskar's saviors from paintings he has made of them. She begs for help and explains that he has not been acting like himself since the wedding; she suspects that it has something to do with his atelier since that is the place where he spent most of his time. If the party agree to help her they can discover and burn the possessed portrait in the atelier with the Torch of Revocation . Once they do so, the Echo of a Lost Love is freed from it and she runs downstairs to terrorize Jannath and Oskar, leaving Lady Jannath unconscious. The party must deal with the ghost either through dialogue checks, fighting, or letting it take Oskar. If Oskar survives the incident, Lady Jannath is profusely thankful and encourages the party to go upstairs so that Oskar can paint them a Personal Portrait in his atelier. If Oskar died during Act One or was never freed from the Zhentarim during ⁠ Free the Artist , Lady Jannath instead hosts an art gallery and her mansion is not haunted by any ghosts. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Arno can be found in the Guildhall . When Roah Moonglow , Boss Friol , or Trinoda attempts to take over the Guildhall, Arno joins the fight alongside his Zhentarim allies against the Guild. Siding against the Zhentarim ends in Arno's demise, or in his disappearance if he is knocked out. Arno can be summoned with Gather Your Allies variant Black Fist Enforcers , if the party completed ⁠ Aid the Underduke and sided with the Zhentarim . GOB_Goblin_Kid_Looter Five is a goblin child in the Goblin Camp . “ Underdark too gloomy for ya, shroom-sucker? „ — Five , insulting a drow character Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Five is on the eastern most side of the Goblin Camp near the cliff where Brawler Rancer is stationed. Five stands over the corpse of a dead adventurer along with two other goblin children, Four , and Eight . Five only throws insults when spoken with. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Five, Four, and Eight immediately escape without joining the fight when attacked, though they can still be killed during their escape. This is a rare exception to the game's standard treatment of minor NPCs; human and tiefling children can only be Knocked Out , and any narrative deaths they suffer (such as during the Raid on the Emerald Grove ) occur strictly off-screen. She is at the Wine Festival at Highberry's Home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ There's some rather lovely vintages out today - I'd get in quick if I were you. „ — Flaerith Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaerith appears at her stall at the wine festival if the party began ⁠ Investigate the Murders and the wine festival takes place. After Dolor reveals himself and attempts to kill Cora Highberry , Flaerith runs off and cannot be seen again. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Farsea Marshwine x12 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaerith occasionally argues with Ontur , with Porter Oveer eagerly anticipating the fight: Flaerith You know, I really do think red is the best wine. Ontur What, on a hot summer's day? Madness. Flaerith ...Excuse me, how dare you?! Porter Oveer Oooh, I bet this'll be fun. Ontur Now, Flaerith - I'm just saying white wine is better. Flaerith Maybe for plebs. Porter Oveer Best not tell them I prefer a pink. Ontur At least white wine doesn't stain tongues and teeth. Flaerith No, they stain their drinker's reputation instead. Flaerith This red is the best wine in the entire Sword Coast. Ontur In the Sword Coast? In your dreams, more like! Flaerith Swallow a cork and die. Porter Oveer Fight, fight, FIGHT! Flaerith I think... I think I was too harsh, Ontur. My apologies. Ontur The only thing that's too harsh are these tannins. Flaerith You wound me, Ontur. Truly. Ontur I only jest, Flaerith! Porter Oveer Boring! Technical Stats FlamingFist_Human_Ranger Variant 1 Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Ranger Flaming Fist Archers are Hunter rangers of the Flaming Fist found guarding and patrolling the streets of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I've got my eye on you. And them over there, too. I don't miss a thing. „ — Flaming Fist Wearne Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaming Archers can be found throughout the entire city of Baldur's Gate , guarding strategic locations such as Wyrm's Crossing , Basilisk Gate Barracks , and Bloomridge Park . They can assist the party during certain public encounters, or fight against them should they be on the wrong side of the law. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaming Fist Archers are powerful ranger guards of the Flaming Fist capable of dealing large amount of AoE damage thanks to their high Dexterity and Volley action. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Ensnaring Strike (Ranged) ( + + ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Piercing Your attack summons thorny vines that possibly Ensnare your target. STR Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Ranged Attack ( )   –   Heavy Crossbow Damage: 6~15 1d10 + 5 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Volley ( ) Damage Normal weapon damage Fire a cascade of magical broadheads and bodkin arrows upon nearby foes. Range: Normal weapon range Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Arrow of Humanoid Slaying - 2x Heavy Crossbow Leather Armour Known Flaming Fist archers [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwarf [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Aggralix Fist Debin Fist Gneiss Fist Gonfalon Fist Larche Fist Loudstone Fist Magnolia Fist Rockbothem Human [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Arrinye Fist Clover Fist 'Deadeye' Mibbs Fist Equidna Fist Gai Fist Glenvora Fist Griff Fist Gummidge Fist Hagedorrn Fist Havard Fist Kyberos Fist Lionel Fist Madigan Fist Mîran Fist Olloa Fist Pard Fist Recruit Ito Fist Recruit Pavel Fist Recruit Tristan Fist Wearne Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The Flaming Fist employ many different races. The stats in this article reflect Humans only. There is a generic female Gold Dwarf simply named "Fist" that is also a Flaming Fist Archer despite the different name. She only appears when the party is caught committing crimes away from any existing Fists in the Lower City . It is possible to acquire the Flaming Fist Archer's unique Leather Armour in Naoise Nallinto's room in Sharess' Caress . The Fist Archer armour's icon is identical to the default leather armour, leading to potential confusion. v t e Creature Archetypes Absolutists Absolute Questioner Acolyte of the Absolute Adept of the Absolute Inquisitor of the Absolute Zealot of the Absolute Banites Black Gauntlet of Bane Fist of Bane Iron Consul of Bane Bhaalists Death's Head of Bhaal Invoker of Bhaal Night Blade Reaper of Bhaal Myrkulites Mistress of Souls Counting House Counting House Artillerist Counting House Enforcer Flaming Fist Flaming Fist Archer Flaming Fist Guisarmier Flaming Fist Healer Flaming Fist Protector Flaming Fist Wizard Gather Your Allies Gur Hunter Sharpshooter Gur Hunter Warrior (Handaxe) Gur Hunter Warrior (Scimitar) Harper Archer Hellrider Cleric Hellrider Paladin Ironhand Grenadier Watcher Guardian Githyanki Ardent Gish Gish'ra (caster) Gish'ra (melee) Raider Veteran Gish Veteran Raider Veteran Warrior Warrior Youth Gnolls Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Redcaps Redcap Boatswain Redcap Mystic Cannoneer Goblins Goblin Booyahg Goblin Boss Goblin Brawler Goblin Devout Goblin Sapper Goblin Sharp-Eye Goblin Tracker Goblin Warlock Goblin Warrior Sharrans Justiciar Crusader Sharran Fidelian Sharran Novice Sharran Sentry Umberlants Dark Breaker Savage Seawind Untaken

Technical Stats FlamingFist_Human_Caster Variant 1 Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Caster Variant 2 Stats FlamingFist_Gnome_Caster Flaming Fist Wizards are wizards of the Flaming Fist that can be found guarding and patrolling the streets of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaming Fist Wizards can be found throughout the entire city of Baldur's Gate , guarding strategic locations such as Wyrm's Rock Fortress , Basilisk Gate Barracks , and Bloomridge Park . They can assist the party during certain public encounters, or fight against them should they be on the wrong side of the law. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaming Fist Wizards are powerful spellcasters that have the spell slots of a level 12 caster. They are able to create diversions and debuffs to aid their fellow Flaming Fists through upcasted Slow and Conjure Elemental: Fire Elemental spells, as well as being able to shut down party spells through Counterspell . However, their damage output is low, consisting of upcasted Melf's Acid Arrow spells and Blight . Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Fire Bolt ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Fire Hurl a mote of fire. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Melf's Acid Arrow ( + ) Damage: 6~24 4d4 ⁠ Acid + 2d4 ⁠ Acid Shoot a green arrow that bursts in a spray of acid. Deals ⁠ 4d4 Acid damage immediately and ⁠ 2d4 Acid damage at the end of the target's next turn. If the spell misses, the target still takes half the initial damage, but no damage at the end of its next turn. Range: 18 m (60 ft) See Invisibility ( + ) Become able to see Invisible creatures, and possibly reveal them to others. DEX Save Range: Self Blight ( + ) Damage: 8~64 8d8 ⁠ Necrotic Deals 8d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage to a target. Plants take maximum damage from this spell, and have Disadvantage on the Saving Throw against it. CON Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Conjure Elemental: Fire Elemental ( + ) The fire elemental can use   Smouldering Touch ,   Erupting Cinder , and can make your foes   Burn . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per combat Counterspell ( + ) Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Slow ( + ) Alter time around up to 6 enemies to Slow them. They won't get far, they can't do much, and they're easier to hit. The Flaming Fist Wizard robe exists in the game as a Simple Robe , but is inaccessible to players without third-party tools. Technical UID S_GLO_IronThrone_Group7_Prisoner1 UUID 06d864d4-924a-4595-8155-d96df5b5f97e Stats LOW_IronThrone_Prisoners_Gnome Flansy Thornwhist is a lightfoot halfling member of the Church of Gond , held hostage at the Iron Throne by Enver Gortash . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party enter the Iron Throne, Enver Gortash remotely triggers explosions which soon collapse the building. Flansy is trapped in the cell immediately north-east of the central ladder. If freed, she dashes towards the Submersible to escape. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] The only action Flansy uses on any turn is Dash , with the help of the Glimpse of Freedom condition which is applied when the cage is opened. Dash ( ) Cover more distance this turn: double your Movement Speed . Range: Self Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail Difficulty differences [ edit section | visual editor ] Unlike other Gondian prisoners, Flansy has the standard 30% less HP on Explorer (instead of 50% more), and 30% more HP on Tactician. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_SHA_Necromancer_FleshGolem UUID 5d25116f-4e25-4f9f-bb7a-1d1fdfa8fd4f Stats FleshGolem Trs. SHA_Necromancer_Golem Flesh is a Flesh Golem , Construct [ 1 ] creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . It is found in the Gauntlet of Shar , working as a servant for Balthazar . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] After defeating various Dark Justiciars and Umbral Tremors outside Balthazar's room in the Gauntlet of Shar, the party can enter and talk with Balthazar. During the course of conversation, Balthazar can be asked about Flesh, and reveals that it is partly made up of pieces of his unborn twin brother. The party can gain the ability to summon Flesh as a temporary ally if they ask Balthazar for supplies and succeed a DC 14 Persuasion Check . He then gives the party the Summon Golem Bell which allows them to summon Flesh as an ally in battle anywhere inside the Gauntlet of Shar. [ 2 ] Doing so grants the ⁠ Meat Shield inspiration to party members with the Noble background. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Should the party wish to avoid fighting Flesh, Lyrthindor in rat form is an attractive option to dispose of him with minimal effort. A single party member can descend to the broken effigy, initiate the fight, summon Flesh in the first round with the bell, drink an Invisibility Potion , and stand back. Flesh and the Rats each have an AC of 11. Consequently he is virtually guaranteed to land his attacks on them and they on him. Their sheer number overwhelms him, as he only attacks one target per turn. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Flesh starts combat using only Slam, but after it reaches a certain health threshold it goes Berserk and begins using its Multiattack instead. Corpulent Rage Damage: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Thunder As your health diminishes, let out a bone-quaking roar that pushes back anyone near you, and go   Berserk . Tactician difficulty: In addition, you gain the effects of   Reckless Attack . STR Save Range: Self Recharge: Short rest On Tactician difficulty or higher, Corpulent Rage also grants permanent Reckless Attack . Multiattack ( ) Damage: 18~74 4d8 + 5 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 4d8 + 5 ⁠ Bludgeoning Aim multiple attacks at a target. If you have gone   Berserk , the target is also knocked   Prone . STR Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Slam ( ) Damage: 9~37 4d8 + 5 ⁠ Bludgeoning Hit a target with your bare fists. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Summon Golem Bell Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Model by Mohamed Abdelfatah Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Unlike the rest of Balthazar 's necromantic creations, Flesh is categorized as a construct rather than an undead due to being a Flesh Golem . ↑ Flesh cannot be healed by any spell or potion. [ verify ] If summoned by Balthazar's bell and Flesh is in, or enters the state of Corpulent Rage , it attacks the closest available target, including (former) allies. Therefore, if Flesh is in a state of rage when a combat encounter ends and the party returns to Balthazar, he and his retinue immediately become hostile and attack the party. v t e Gauntlet of Shar Characters Aylin Balthazar Flesh Hoarding Merregon Lyrthindor Nessa Yurgir Creatures Apostate Defender Apostate Destroyer Apostate Librarian Apostate Sentinel Ghoul Medic Justiciar Avenger Justiciar Crusader Justiciar Nightweaver Justiciar Soulhunter Merregon Legionnaire Necrotic Rat Rat Reconstituted Duellist Reconstituted Marksman Soporific Rat Locations Faith-Leap Trial Self-Same Trial Shadowfell Silent Library Soft-Step Trial Quests Break Yurgir's Contract Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic Find the Nightsong Kill Raphael's Old Enemy Lift the Shadow Curse The Chosen of Shar

PLA_ConflictedFlind_EA Variant 1 UID Gnoll_Flind UUID 406bdfdb-6063-448e-81cf-4b9ca76bcab3 Stats Gnoll_Flind Flind is a hostile gnoll warlord in The Risen Road Cave just west of The Risen Road Waypoint during Act One . [ 2 ] Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act One 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Allies 2.3 Tactics 2.4 Loot 3 Notes 4 Related literature 5 External links Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Flind is the warlord of a vicious band of gnolls gathered outside of The Risen Road Cave . The gnolls trapped Rugan and Olly , who are transporting goods for Zarys . [ 3 ] On her first turn in combat, if she moves near any party member, Flind mentally links with them, revealing that she is infected with a Mind Flayer Tadpole . The first Wisdom check made in dialogue with her can be bypassed through Illithid Persuasion if it has not already been used. The party can convince Flind to attack Rugan and Olly or search for the source of the Voice and then convince her to attack her fellow gnolls: [ 4 ] Divert her attention to the cave - perhaps there's more meat inside? Search her mind for the source of the Voice. [WISDOM]  Use the power within you to make her obey the Voice; to brave the flames and feast on the meat in the cave. [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  Conjure the mewlings of easy prey into her mind, centring it within the nearby cave.  (DC 12) Withdraw from her mind, and prepare to strike. A failed check triggers combat. Depending on the choices made in the dialogue tree, the following options may appear: [ 4 ] [WISDOM]  She wants meat? Command her to feast on the other gnolls.  (DC 15) [WISDOM]  Harness her anger - the meat in the cave must die.  (DC 10) [WISDOM]  You are of the same pack - command her to devour the other gnolls.  (DC 15) [WISDOM]  Urge her to obey the Voice; to brave the flames and feast on the meat in the cave.  (DC 10) [WISDOM]  Fight back, redirecting the gnoll's fury against her own pack.  (DC 20) [BARBARIAN]  Counter her rage with your own, unleashing your battle frenzy within her mind. [ 5 ] [BARD]  Fill her mind with a distracting joke. 'What's the difference between man and meat? [ 6 ] A failed check may trigger combat or further dialogue options depending on the check. The following options appear after she is ordered to kill the cave survivors: [ 4 ] [WISDOM]  Exert your mental power, commanding her to leave.  (DC 10) [WISDOM]  She wants meat? Dominate her mind, ordering her to feast on the other gnolls.  (DC 15) Sever the mental connection, and prepare to strike. A failed check triggers combat. The following options appear after she is ordered to kill the other gnolls (whether or not the cave survivors were killed): [ 4 ] [WISDOM]  Dominate her mind, commanding her to feast on herself.  (DC 10) [WISDOM]  Harness your willpower, and order her to devour herself.  (DC 15) [WISDOM]  Exert your mental power, commanding her to leave.  (DC 10) Sever the mental connection, and prepare to strike. A failed check triggers combat. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Multiattack ( )   –   Goblin Bow Damage: 9~24 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Piercing + 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Piercing + 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Aim three attacks at a target. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter - 3x Hyena - 2x Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Flind is a dangerous enemy who can be encountered early when exploring aimlessly. She has a respectable AC , a high amount of hit points , and powerful attacks, which altogether make her a deadly foe. Her unique flail attacks vary between dealing massive amounts of damage, paralysing, or turning a party member hostile for a time. The biggest threat is her frenzied state, which allows her to use all three of her unique flail attacks in one multiattack, possibly killing an opponent in a single round. Flind's high initiative almost always allows her to act first in combat. She immediately seeks out the first party member she sees to initiate a conversation, which presents an opportunity to use Illithid Powers to turn her against her pack. It is possible to command her to kill Rugan and Olly and then force her to turn against her pack afterwards. Turning her against her pack is recommended, as fighting Flind and her pack at the same time can be very difficult. It can be helpful to have the character interacting with Flind have a high Wisdom score while also receiving the benefits of Mark of the Shifter , Owl's Wisdom and Guidance to increase their odds of success. Once she is convinced to betray her pack, the party should focus on the Gnoll Hunters as they often target the party instead of Flind. Their frenzied multiattack arrow shots can be devastating, so it is best to kill them as quickly as possible with AoE attacks like Cloud of Daggers or Alchemist's Fire before they can frenzy. The best way to engage Flind is to sneak up behind her and sneak attack the hunters in front of her to initiate combat. It is important to have Flind be able to initiate conversation on her first turn to ensure the party interact with her as described above. When alone, direct combat with Flind is avoidable by passing the two Wisdom checks to compel her to kill herself. If this option is unavailable, Flind is quite dangerous up close; in her frenzied state, she can easily kill party members in a single turn. One potential strategy involves restricting her movement with spells like Grease , Web and Entangle , and then pelting her at range. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen Shattered Flail Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ In the game's data, Flind is defined as a Gnoll Flind , which is a type of fiend; however, like regular gnolls , they are tagged as humanoid. Consequently, Flind can also be affected by spells that only affect humanoids, such as Hold Person . In D&D 5e, flinds were originally a type of humanoid, as published in Volo's Guide to Monsters (2016), but were changed to fiends in the later published Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse (2022). ↑ 'Flind' is not this creature's real name, but rather her race, gnoll flind ; she is a superior type of gnoll, which are physically more powerful and vicious than their lesser cousins. ↑ If the party approach close enough to spawn the caravan survivors and then take a long rest before engaging them, Flind's pack kills them off-screen and occupy the cave, preventing the mental link dialogue from triggering. ↑ 4.0 4.1 4.2 4.3 Dialogue file: Act1/Plains/PLA_ConflictedFlind_Flind ↑ This causes her to turn on the other gnolls. ↑ This results in three punchline options, each with a DC 18 Performance Check . On success, she and the gnolls turn hostile, but are Mirth-Wracked for two turns. WYR_OpenHand_Sarcophagus Flinster Sunseeker is a corpse in the crypt underneath the Open Hand Temple in Rivington . He is raised as a Greater Zombie , if the party refuses to take the curse from the Sentient Amulet (Rare) . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon reaching the Open Hand Temple, it is revealed that Shirra Clarwen died the previous year, and her spirit passed on. The monk's manifestation inside the sentient amulet laments the passing of her spirit, who would have born the curse, and asks the interacting party member if they will bear it instead. If they refuse, the spirit inside the amulet (now inside the body of Shirra Clarwen ) raises three nearby corpses, including Flinster Sunseeker, to attack the party. EQP_Staff_Robe Variant 1 UID S_GLO_Desire UUID 8b9fa503-7205-4ddd-bdfa-bfaa781d9ea9 Stats GLO_CounsellorFlorrick Variant 2 UID S_GLO_Desire_Hooded UUID d8ccafbc-7d82-48ff-9bec-fa63fe2dec04 Stats GLO_CounsellorFlorrick Variant 3 UID S_GLO_Desire_Bruised UUID 37f1bf91-106a-49f3-8c9f-16476109e885 Stats GLO_CounsellorFlorrick Variant 4 UID S_GLO_Desire_HangedPhysics UUID e7b4bc5b-3ca5-4579-8a54-2de1075cf5a3 Stats GLO_CounsellorFlorrick Act 3 differences and additions Balanced Tactician Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 11 HP 79 AC 15 Initiative +2 Proficiency +4 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 12 (+1) 14 (+2) 14 (+2) 20 (+5) 11 (0) 16 (+3) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA +1 +2 +2 +5 0 +3 Conditions Mage Armour Base Armour Class is 13 Tactician Difficulty Stats Level 11 HP 92 AC 15 Initiative +2 Proficiency +4 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 12 (+1) 14 (+2) 14 (+2) 20 (+5) 11 (0) 16 (+3) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA +1 +2 +2 +5 0 +3 Conditions Mage Armour Base Armour Class is 13 Counsellor Florrick is an elven wizard and advisor to the Archduke. Her loyalty to Grand Duke Ravengard is beyond question. Steady as Tyr's heartbeat, as upstanding as the Sword Mountains, [ 1 ] Florrick plays a notable role in the politics brewing within Baldur's Gate , mainly through the questline ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke . “ A scorched throat, a few hairs singed off. Nothing a bit of time and fresh air can't cure. „ — Florrick after rescuing her Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.2 Act Two 2.3 Act Three 2.4 Epilogue 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and Abilities (Act 1) 3.2 Additional Abilities (Act 3) 3.3 Allies 3.3.1 Act Three 3.4 Loot 4 Gallery 5 Related quests 6 Related literature 7 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Florrick is professional and dutiful in her role as a leading member of Baldur's Gate's government. While an advisor, she prefers to be direct and on-hand when it comes to handling problems which plague the city, such as the disappearance of Ulder Ravengard. Being straightforward and honest in her dealings makes her quite a rarity in the oft corrupt ranks of the city's elite. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Florrick can first be encountered at Waukeen's Rest on the Risen Road leading west towards the Mountain Pass . Upon the party's arrival, the place is on fire after an attack by goblins and drow serving the Cult of the Absolute . Trapped on the second floor in the east-most room of the inn, Florrick can be rescued from the blaze. Once saved, she informs the party of Duke Ravengard's recent kidnapping by the cultists, assuming they took him west to Moonrise Towers . This starts ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke . She urges the party to help in saving the Duke, more so if Wyll is present. Upon recognizing him, she inadvertently reveals that he is Ulder's son. Upon rewarding the party for saving her, she departs from Waukeen's Rest, taking the (remaining) Flaming Fist soldiers with her to personally lead the mission to find the missing Ulder Ravengard . If Florrick is not rescued from the fire in time, she dies and is removed from the game, making it impossible to obtain Florrick's Cohort as an ally in the final battle, although the ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke quest can still be obtained in Act Three. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Florrick survives Act One, she travels to the Last Light Inn and, upon journeying through the Shadow-Cursed Lands , the party can meet her there, in the north-eastern room on the ground floor, where she and her Flaming Fist troops are still planning a rescue for Ravengard. However, without a safe way through the cursed shadows surrounding Moonlight Towers, her efforts unfortunately are in vain, as are their attempts to get information from Art Cullagh . While there, the party can speak with Florrick, and gain some news from the city and its new Lord, Gortash . She then informs the party of her plans and departs for Baldur's Gate the next day, intending to convince the council to send reinforcements for rescuing the duke. Once the party reach Moonrise Towers , Florrick and her retinue depart for Baldur's Gate, leaving a note on the table in Last Light Inn. Thus visiting Moonrise before Last Light Inn results in finding only her note. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act Three, Florrick is moved to Wyrm's Rock Prison , resigned as she awaits execution after being found guilty of crimes against the city of Baldur's Gate by none other than Ulder Ravengard. If the party decide to rescue her, she is reinvigorated, pledges her aid in the final battle and Florrick's Cohort becomes one of the allies the party can call upon. Party members with the Criminal background also gain the inspiration ⁠ Wrongly Convicted . If Florrick is not rescued within five long rests after ⁠ Free Counsellor Florrick starts, she is executed by hanging and her body remains suspended from the gallows at the Basilisk Gate. If Wyll breaks his pact with Mizora during ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers and forsakes his father, Florrick approaches Wyll and the party while they are in Baldur's Gate, with the intent to avenge Ravengard. A fight can be avoided by passing a DC 18 Persuasion Check or a DC 15 History Check . If she is convinced, and presuming Ravengard is dead, Florrick gives Wyll The Legend of Ansur [ 2 ] and directs the party to the next step of his personal quest. If all attempts to reason with Florrick fail, she and her retinue of Flaming Fists become hostile. In this case, the book must be acquired by other means. Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] If ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers is completed, and Wyll chooses to ascend politically as the next Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate, he mentions during the epilogue party that Florrick is now the Grand Duke of the Crossing, The Face of Devotion. [ 3 ] If Ulder Ravengard is dead, Wyll entrusts the command of the Flaming Fist to Florrick, and mentions that she has pardoned most Fists, having said "With a few exceptions, Florrick's pardoned every last Fist." . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Oddly, Foharell is listed as a gold dwarf but appears to be a duergar and has duergar racial abilities. Captain Goldwake Gods, I've barely enough to keep my ship sailing - let alone extra for Umberlee. Captain Goldwake She's gonna send me to the bottom of the sea, isn't she? Cashguard Captain Faril A mood? Mate, he was nervous. Cashguard Basher Forstum What for? The big bald fellow he was escorting? Cashguard Captain Faril With the half-elf, aye. New clients, maybe? Either way, Glitterbeard was fit to fill his trousers. Cashguard Basher Forstum Heh. Just as well he's going down to special deposits. Cashguard Captain Faril All right. Calm down. Cashguard Basher Forstum Agh. Cashguard Captain Faril What's wrong with you now? Cashguard Basher Forstum Shoulder. Glitterbeard kept checking this one chest in the vault, over and over - nearly dropped a door on me. Mustn't have seen me. Cashguard Captain Faril Or maybe he did. Cashguard Basher Forstum Mark the notice in the barracks, by the way. The anti-magic whatsit is banjaxed. Cashguard Captain Faril Aye, I heard. Word is the Gondian guild has downed tools and gone walkabouts. Cashguard Basher Forstum Striking, I bet. Lazy gits. GOB_Goblin_Kid_Looter Four is a goblin child in the Goblin Camp . “ You look like you think you're hard. Mess with us, and you'll end up like this bleeder. „ — Four , threatening the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Four is on the eastern most side of the Goblin Camp near the cliff where Brawler Rancer is stationed. He stands over the corpse of a dead adventurer along with two other goblin children, Five , and Eight . Despite his age, he proves to be overly aggressive, doling out threats to everyone who initiates conversation. If the talking party member has War Paint on their face, Four comments that they smell like they have been "kissin' a worg's backside" . Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Four, Five, and Eight immediately escape without joining the fight when attacked, though they can still be killed during their escape. This is a rare exception to the game's standard treatment of minor NPCs; human and tiefling children can only be Knocked Out , and any narrative deaths they suffer (such as during the Raid on the Emerald Grove ) occur strictly off-screen. As a Small Humanoid of 10 kg, Four's corpse is one of the lightest that can be used for both Fungal Infestation and Animate Dead . Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_Franc_Peartree UUID 1556e29c-a876-4853-9ea7-283a48703a56 Stats Human_Commoner Franc Peartree is a Baldur's Gate citizen. He was working as a cook in Basilisk Gate Barracks in Lower City . By the time party reach the Act Three locations, Peartree (if encountered) is already dead. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] The corpse of Franc Peartree without a hand, can be found on the floor of Peartree House near main entrance at X: 32 Y: -96 . The only thing that can be looted from it is a threatening letter. Franc Peartree is a victim of the serial killer Dolor , who murders people in order to become an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal , the God of Murder. Peartree's name can be found on a Bloodstained Parchment among other planned victims, marked Killed . If spoken to with the Speak with Dead spell, Peartree's corpse does not tell anything important, except from that he had been feeding the barracks' inhabitants and was impelled to retire after injury. Everything else concerning him and the possible causes of his murder may be discovered while visiting the basement of his house. Letters which can be found in the basement hint that Enver Gortash contacted Peartree after his retiring and blackmailed him into his covert armsdealing, presumably due to Franc's multiple contacts among Flaming Fists of different ranks. The threatening letter found on Peartree's body claims that the man was killed for helping the lordling . As it goes, this scornful moniker is used by Orin the Red when speaking of Gortash. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who are you? Franc Peartree Franc Peartree... What happened to you? Franc Peartree Killed... murdered... How were you killed? Franc Peartree Limbs... locked up... then hand... cut off... What did your killer look like? Franc Peartree Bastard... dwarf... red... shirt... Where are you from? Franc Peartree Basilisk's... Barracks... Got injured... discharged... What were you doing when you died? Franc Peartree Makin'... me soup... ruined now What was your job? Franc Peartree Feedin'... barracks... Why were you killed? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* What was your killer's name? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] An Offer Enhanced' Weapons - Sales Ledger My Gratitude Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Investigate the Murders Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] A copy of threatening letter addressed to Franc Peartree can be found in the mailbox of the Rainforest's Home (house of another murder victim), - obviously a mistake. Technical UID S_WYR_TerrifiedLocal_Woman UUID adcbb246-87d6-46b8-a1a1-56ffced39b72 Stats Human_Commoner Sister Franchot is in Wyrm's Rock Fortress in Act Three . “ If we could just talk to one of the Fists, it'd be as clear as day that we're not criminals. „ — Franchot Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Sister Franchot stands in the middle of reception room in the Wyrm's Rock Fortress, waiting for her case to be brought on before a Flaming Fist investigator. Her brother Bering Gahorst is accused of bumping a patriar while driving his cart on a road. Bering is very nervous about the upcoming trial and afraid of possible confinement. Although Franchot tries to cheer him, it is clear she feels just as uneasy as he does. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Bering Gahorst Are they going to arrest us? What if they throw us in jail? Franchot Calm down, dear. It won't happen, I swear. Bering Gahorst Our cart barely grazed that patriar. He wasn't even hurt! Franchot That's why nothing's going to happen to us. We'll tell them what happened, and we'll be home in no time. Bering Gahorst You've been saying that for ages, and we're still here. What are they waiting for? Franchot I don't know dear, I don't know. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_Harper_03 UUID a5964a5e-8086-445e-989f-d9c7f32e32b6 Stats LOW_HarperConfrontation_Druid_Halfling Harper Freddo is a lightfoot halfling druid and a member of the Harpers in Act Three . He joins Jaheira in the battle against the Dark Urge , should the latter choose to accept and embrace their heritage. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Temple of Bhaal [ edit section | visual editor ] Should the Dark Urge defeat Orin the Red , embrace Bhaal's gift and become Bhaal's Chosen, the Harpers set up an ambush at the entrance of the Temple of Bhaal , provided Jaheira is alive. Led by Jaheira and accompanied by Minsc (if rescued), the Harpers stand guard on the bridge leading out of the temple, preventing the party from leaving. The player character then has a brief exchange with Jaheira concerning their role as the Dark Urge and Chosen of Bhaal . Also, if Minsc is present, the Dark Urge has the ability to psionically control him into stabbing Jaheira in the back through his Mind Flayer Tadpole . Doing so immediately kills Jaheira and triggers combat with Minsc, Freddo, and the rest of the Harpers. [WISDOM]  Ease his confusion. Try to control him.  (DC 25) Alternatively, if the Dark Urge withdraws from Minsc's mind, Jaheira can potentially convince Gale (if under 20 approval), Karlach (if under 40 approval), or Wyll (always) to turn to their side, forcing the party to kill their former companions in the ensuing fight with the Harpers.
