Freida Oberon Lady of Baldur's Gate In-game Model Portrait Voice / Actor Nneka Okoye Family Oberon Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Balanced Explorer Tactician Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 6 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Explorer Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 4 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +4 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Tactician Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 7 AC 10 Initiative 0 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Technical UID S_WYR_KillDirectorGortash_Patriar_007 UUID 1f626306-2d28-4a64-93a8-67a35a03416e Stats Human_Commoner Lady Freida Oberon is a Lady of Baldur's Gate who is present for Gortash's ordination as the Archduke of the city. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony she sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lady Freida moves to the northern nave of the Audience Hall and stands near the table with refreshments at its far end. She engages in a casual conversation with Lady Beatrice Provoss , discussing Gortash's low-born origins, information on the Cult of the Absolute available in patriars' libraries, and the need to call the City of Candlekeep for help. If spoken with, she toasts to Gortash and says that she sees the bright perspective of Baldur's Gate. If the party confront Gortash, they can later find Lady Oberon's corpse – unlike those of all others who attended the ceremony – at the rocky footing of the Wyrm's Rock, to the right of the drawbridge from Wyrm's Crossing . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Beatrice Provoss After enduring Ravengard's slovenly manners for so long, I was rather hoping our next duke might be of high-born stock. Freida Oberon Gortash may be low-born, but if he is half the man Ravengard has proven to be, Baldur's Gate can count itself fortunate twice over. Freida Oberon Doesn't matter if a Duke comes from decadence or dirt, as long as they have the city's interests at heart. Beatrice Provoss We should request aid from Candlekeep while there's still time. Freida Oberon I hardly think Lord Gortash needs the assistance of ink-stained librarians. Everything is under control. Beatrice Provoss I hope these formalities don't last long. Freida Oberon Aren't you enjoying the refreshments? Beatrice Provoss The refreshments are fine, but I won't feel safe until I'm back in the Upper City . Behind solid walls. Beatrice Provoss I've studied every book in my library and can find no mention of the Absolute anywhere. Freida Oberon Hardly surprising. Your library is almost entirely made up of tawdry chivalric romances. Freida Oberon Still, even among the educated this Absolute is quite the mystery. Why do I even bother? „ — Frenello Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Saer Frenello recently lost his position as an event planner in the Upper City . He can be found drinking at one of the outdoor tables at the Elfsong Tavern, occasionally chatting with Rowan Elkfriend . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Saer Frenello Event planner for the Auld Patriars' Club! I'll never have a job that good again. Rowan Elkfriend I know it. Everyone knows it. You won't shut up about it. Saer Frenello As my friend, you should help me find a new job. Rowan Elkfriend Just because I lend you money sometimes doesn't make me your friend. Saer Frenello I know! I'll plan a jobs fair event so I can find myself a new job. Rowan Elkfriend Whoa, Frenello, that's brilliant. Or stupid. One of those. Rowan Elkfriend I'm fed up with this brown-ass town. I'm going back to the woods. Saer Frenello The woods! Do you think they could use an event planner there? Rowan Elkfriend Did you hear that? Lord Gortash has been killed! Who would do such a thing?  (If Enver Gortash is killed) Saer Frenello Whoever it was, they did me a big favour! The council is going to need to plan a state funeral. Rowan Elkfriend Of course. And here you are, an event planner just looking for work. Saer Frenello Exactly! Technical UID S_PLA_Tavern_OxAlive UUID c69aa4c1-bac2-401f-b4ec-cce8d545ba7c Stats Ox Frightened Ox is an ox which can be found near the entrance to the Zhentarim Basement at Waukeen's Rest in Act One . “ Monsters... everywhere... kill... „ — Frightened Ox Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Approaching the Frightened Ox in the barn behind the inn triggers a conversation. He thinks the party are part of the raiders and then tries to attack if the party choose one of the following options: Back away. Defend yourself. Otherwise, the party can try to perform an Ability Check to pacify him: [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Interpret his behaviour.  (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  Hold out your hands peacefully.  (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  Square your stance and face him directly.  (DC 10) [BERSERKER] [PERFORMANCE]  Stare down the beast.  (DC 5) [BARBARIAN] [PERFORMANCE]  Stare him down, as you have so many beasts in the wild.  (DC 5) [RANGER] [DRUID] [PERFORMANCE]  Bow deeply - a submissive gesture.  (DC 5) If using Speak with Animals , the check is slightly easier and no animal handling check is required: [PERSUASION]  Look at me - I'm not a monster. (DC 5) [INTIMIDATION]  Stay back. I don't want to hurt you, but I will. (DC 5) [DRUID] [PERSUASION]  Calm, friend. I won't harm you. (DC 5) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  BACK DOWN, BEAST.  (DC 5) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Back down. Or else.  (DC 5) However, he attacks Drow on sight, if using Speak with Animals. v t e Risen Road Characters Companions Karlach Flaming Fists Aelis Bryanne Dain Dion Ephren Florrick Jacek Ito Marilla Pavel Rowan Tristan Wexford Yeva Githyanki Baretha Chost For'reth Voss Zastri Paladins of Tyr Anders Buckle Refugee Trynn Traders Brem Cyrel Zhentarim Amnos Bellar Garias Jarg Karad Olly Rugan Salazon Vol Zarys Other Benryn Ellyka Krug Marten Mirileth Oskar Fevras Sszaryn Vance Yul Animals and Creatures Bloated Hyena Flind Frightened Ox Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Indra Isbeth Istor Qudenos Locations Mountain Pass Toll House Waukeen's Rest Zhentarim Basement Quests Find a Cure Find the Githyanki Crèche Find the Missing Shipment Find the Nightsong Free the Artist Hunt the Devil Our Fiery Friend Rescue the Trapped Man The Blade of Frontiers The Githyanki Warrior Travel to Moonrise Towers Travel through the Mountain Pass

Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Mace +1 Damage: 6~11 1d6 + 5 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. They'll have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls and be unable to move. WIS Save Range: Normal weapon range Frode receives 5 Superiority Dice in order to use Menacing Attack. Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail Hand Crossbow Mace +1 Shield Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Talis Losers' List Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Frode occasionally chats with Gudrun: Fist of Bane Gudrun You were fortunate to work shifts on the prison transport, were you not, Dread Brother? Fist of Bane Frode Indeed. The trip took my breath away. Fist of Bane Gudrun I've not had the pleasure of seeing the prison with my own eyes. Fist of Bane Frode Your time will come. Only Lord Gortash's most trusted may guard the Iron Throne. Fist of Bane Gudrun Dread Brother, is it true the transport hit and killed someone? Fist of Bane Frode It was only a waveservant - a minor inconvenience. Fist of Bane Gudrun You do not fear they will retaliate? Fist of Bane Frode If they do, we will deal with them in a manner befitting the Black Hand. Fist of Bane Frode Something is on your mind, Dread Sister - speak. Fist of Bane Gudrun The body of the dead waveservant. Has it been located? Fist of Bane Frode It is lost - why do you ask? Fist of Bane Gudrun If it is found, it could pose a risk to our operations. Fist of Bane Frode Such thoughts are above your station - focus on your tenets, Dread Sister. v t e Steel Watch Foundry Characters Gondians Bala Ofran Clore Falson Droo Falbo Frell Olsin Genshu Ofran Grindo Biggs Lanpos Biggs Lowa Lu La Forza Manser Biggs Menalda Zanner Toobin Black Gauntlet Borri Paver Indora Ralston Hahns Rives Ifran Tamia Holzt Iron Consul Chadd Malik Marten Moosk Yoonce Fist of Bane Aminah Anouk Bagdog Frode Gasper Throaks Gudrun Polandulus Zana Hade Locations Main Floor Lab Level Control Centre Quests Avenge the Ironhands Disable the Steel Watch Save the Gondians

Technical UID S_LOW_GeniusGortash_Supporter_02 UUID 9e5c50fb-8f98-4721-9e41-2caac6f16e88 Stats Elf_Commoner Frothilda is in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Ah, the wide-eyed gaze of someone new to Baldur's Gate! Well, you've reason to be excited, friend. „ — Frothilda Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Frothilda is an avid supporter of Enver Gortash . She and Saer Manzarde can be found next to Baldur's Mouth , discussing the finer points of Gortash's charisma and good will. If Gortash is defeated, Frothilda and Saer Mazarde leave, and cannot be interacted with again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Frothilda It's a shame Gortash's interview didn't touch on how the Watchers talk. Saer Manzarde That's just a gimmick. The Steel Watch don't need to talk. They're guards. Frothilda Sure, Gortash didn't need to make them speak - but that's precisely why he's a genius! Not only that, they're polite. Have you any idea how hard it is to make an automation have manners? Saer Manzarde As long as they do their jobs, they can sing sea shanties for all I care. Frothilda Did you see Lord Gortash's latest interview in the Baldur's Mouth ? Saer Manzarde Speaks well, that Enver Gortash. An excellent rhetorician. Frothilda He's a man of the people, too. Promised at least a hundred more Watchers before the year is out. Saer Manzarde Good. But once Gortash clears off the cultists, he'll still have to clean the rabble off the streets. Frothilda He'll manage. There's nothing that man can't do. Frothilda To think, for decades, all we needed to build the Steel Watch has been sitting right there. Saer Manzarde Gortash is a visionary, sure enough. But his vision has cost a pretty penny. Frothilda We have Steel Watchers promenading the streets and you're worried about the price of bread? Saer Manzarde He's delivered, yes, but these tax hikes are enough to make my eyes water. Frothilda Once the Watchers see off the cultists, we'll recoup what we've lost, and then some. Frothilda Dear gods above! It's hot off the press - Lord Gortash is dead!   (If Gortash is killed) Saer Manzarde Don't say that, Frothi. It isn't funny. Frothilda It's no joke, it's the truth! He's been taken from us, Manzarde - so young, so handsome, and gone, just like that! Saer Manzarde Shade of a lich! This is going to play merry hell with commodity prices. I'd better get over to the grain exchange. v t e Baldur's Mouth Characters Flaming Fists Ernestus Glenvora Jerbold Guards Baalfe Hertvor Dremble Inocente Bramm Unilda Tiro Vlomina Wulf Outside Augur Harxkellan Bliggerillo Flant Borlley Flo Hurlburl Frothilda Frunilla Grent Grintly 'Gunny' Sacko Korrinna Koreena Juxon Lockhorn Lolo Fuzzletoes Manzarde Muttonchops Dorryss Phyria Gollus 'Plumes' Fronkin Sadar Illanov Trina Wuloona Dor Staff Bronte Delcan Ettvard Needle Falael Glimmer Whistleborn Jarlath Jelliwig Malek Stones Salene Freig Syril Valdemar Ty Willowbrook Zita Locations Newsroom Basement Quests Stop the Presses

Technical UID S_END_LastStandGuard_003 UUID 0e5ae266-ba26-48ac-9c2a-c9a461f1352d Stats END_CityWatchMelee_Human Watchman Fry is a member of The Watch in the Upper City in Act Three . He attempts to flee the High Hall's courtyard after it has been overrun by forces belonging to the Absolute . “ Not sure how much fight I've got left in me, but I'll give it my best shot. For Baldur's Gate. „ — Fry Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the initial battle for High Hall, a large force of Absolutist cultists coming from the Upper City Sewers destroys the keep and routs the City Watch away from it, forcing what remains of the Watch to flee. [ 1 ] Faced with severe casualties, the last remnants of the Watch are composed of Fry, Ebber , Goodge , Gyordi , Matthew , and Preyn . A Mind Flayer decimates Matthew and Preyn as the Watchmen try to flee from High Hall, before being confronted with the party. If a Mind Flayer (be it the player character, Karlach , The Emperor , or Orpheus ) is present, Fry and the remaining Watchmen led by Gyordi are frightened of the party. Passing a passive DC 20 Insight Check allows for the option of having the remaining Watchmen fight at the party's side. A Mind Flayer player character can convince them to partake in the ensuing battle as allies with a DC 18 Persuasion , Intimidation , or Strength Check . A non-Mind Flayer must pass a DC 20 Persuasion , Intimidation , Deception , or Strength Check check to convince them. If the party's Mind Flayer is too far away and dialogue starts with the Watchmen oblivious to it, every class except Wizard also get either a special DC 20 Arcana , Insight , Persuasion , Intimidation , or Deception Check to convince them, or two generic DC 20 Wisdom or Persuasion Checks . If the interacting party member passes any of these checks, Gyordi rallies the rest of the Watchmen and encourages them to fight with the party during the courtyard battle. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Greatsword Helmet Plate Armour Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Fry and the rest of the named Watchmen have identical stats to the Watcher Guardians that can be summoned through the Gather Your Allies action The Watch . Fry and the rest of the named Watchmen's armour is similar in appearance to the Breastplate +1 dyed in blue, brown, and black colours, rather than the plate armour specifically designed and seen on the rest of The Watch . Fry also wears the Adjustable Steel Helm with the visor raised. MOO_Cultist Adept Furek is a drow Adept of the Absolute in Moonrise Towers during Act Two . He is stationed outside the main throne room, alongside Adept Dorikel . “ Praise the Absolute. Serve the General. „ — Furek Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Furek is on the ground floor hall of Moonrise Towers , up on the staircase leading into the throne room and watching over the hall. Defending Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Nightsong is freed and the Harpers launch their assault on Moonrise Towers, Furek is part of the remaining forces defending Moonrise, and is on the ground floor hall standing in the same place he was before the assault. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_NightBlade_01 UUID 7a82cf11-57a2-4796-8b3a-d3409c0cbe9e Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_DeathsHead Death's Head of Bhaal Fustian is a human Death's Head of Bhaal . “ I would lick the viscera from your boot, Bhaalspawn. It is all I deserve. „ — Fustian , to the Dark Urge who embraced Bhaal Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fustian is found in the Bhaal Temple in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . Initially she accompanies Orin the Red on the central altar ground, trying to distract her from torturing the player character's companion she abducted. If the player character is not the Dark Urge , Fustian takes part in the fight against them, allying with Orin. If the player character is the Dark Urge and defeats Orin, Fustian remains neutral to the party and moves to the top of the destroyed stairways leading to the central altar ground. Her one-liners depend on whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Fyl Baragezian is a refugee near the Rivington waypoint. He is urging his recalcitrant son Charl Baragezian to continue their journey to Baldur's Gate . His wife Nonah Baragezian is trying to convince Charl as well by promising sweets. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fyl Baragezian Nearly there now. You can see the city, up on the hill. Charl Baragezian I see it, but it's up there, and we're down here! Nonah Baragezian That's why we need to walk just a little more. One foot in front of the other. Charl Baragezian You have been saying that for days. My feet hurt! Fyl Baragezian I know, little one. But you'll be in a big, cosy bed soon enough. Nonah Baragezian And you'll have anything you want for supper. All the treats your tummy can handle. Charl Baragezian I'm never allowed sweet things right before bed. Fyl Baragezian This one time we'll make an exception. As long as you stop sulking and start walking right now. v t e Rivington v t e Characters in Rivington Refugees Arne Jacobson Belron Strongstep Ben Golewits Bex Billigan Indigo Billy Bobby Brekka ST_MusicInstrument_Common Fyodor is a bugbear who works at the Circus of the Last Days as a bouncer in Rivington , during Act Three . “ No. „ — Fyodor Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party tries to trespass behind the clown tent to the staff-only area, Fyodor staunchly refuses them entry. Technical UID S_LOW_BramptonDeal_Civilian2 UUID 2359a8f4-2b8a-4996-a852-e99b925046f8 Stats HalfOrc_Commoner Fyrd Nuugh is a half-orc food merchant. He is conversing with Beulla Sandfoot on a pier gazebo outside of Philgrave's Mansion in the Lower City during Act Three . “ You look like an upstanding sort. Surely you can turn a blind eye to a little... food-bartering, eh? „ — Fyrd Nuugh Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fyrd and Beulla are trading large quantities of food under the gazebo, in an attempt to avoid the Guild's watchful eyes. If approached, Fyrd chastises the party for interrupting a private conversation. Fyrd's attitude towards the party changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fyrd Nuugh So... still got the goods? Beulla Sandfoot Wouldn't be here if I didn't, would I? And you? Keeping up your end? Fyrd Nuugh Uh-huh. Flour - nine whole sacks. Just don't think too hard about where they came from. Beulla Sandfoot Did some Upper City type wake up to find an empty larder this morning? Fyrd Nuugh Better than not waking at all. Good quality stuff, too. Not a weevil in sight. Beulla Sandfoot Pity. I like a little crunch. Fyrd Nuugh Anyway, what do you have for me? Beulla Sandfoot Side of salted pork, some barley, and six dozen eggs, assuming none broke. Fresh as you'll get. Fyrd Nuugh Fresh, you say? I checked the last lot in a bucket of water - they all floated. Beulla Sandfoot That means they're good. Fyrd Nuugh Means they're old . Still, though... I'll take old over none at all. Beulla Sandfoot I told my third husband the very same on our wedding night. Beulla Sandfoot Nine-Fingers still keeping out of our little arrangement? Fyrd Nuugh For now. You'd think something like this would be below her. Beulla Sandfoot Nothing's below her - not if she thinks she's owed a cut. Let's just keep our heads down. Fyrd Nuugh Easier for you to say. Fyrd Nuugh Maybe we should meet somewhere different next time. Folk'll get suspicious. Beulla Sandfoot Over what? As far as they're concerned, we're just a couple of friends, discussing the weather. Fyrd Nuugh If we get careless, the Guild will come for its cut - and if it doesn't come out of our purses, it'll come out of us. Beulla Sandfoot Came down - nobody's killing anyone over a few eggs. LOW_SteepsTrader_Weapons Fytz the Firecracker is a weapons trader in the Lower City in Act Three . She is also an old friend of Karlach . “ My weapons won't be beat. Tell your friends - hells, tell your enemies if you like. „ — Fytz Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fytz is a small-time weapons retailer located in the Stormshore Armoury of Baldur's Gate at X: -38 Y: -83 . Talking with her as Karlach, or with Karlach in the party, yields special dialogue. She reveals she once worked for Gortash alongside Karlach, but left once she became concerned with his increasingly cruel methods. Fytz went on to get married with Gregor and is expecting a baby, whom she invites Karlach and the party to come meet in the future. Fytz's attitude towards the party often changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Blacksmith's Chest Key Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to LOW_SteepsTrader_Weapons . Some of the listed items may not be available after every restock. Features Advanced Unarmoured Movement Difficult Terrain doesn't slow you down and you can Jump an additional 6 m (20 ft) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield . Deflect Missiles Use your reaction to reduce the damage from a ranged weapon attack by 1d10 + your Dexterity Modifier + your monk level. Evasion Successful DEX saves nullify damage; failed DEX saves reduce it by half. Extra Attack Can make an additional attack after an unarmed or weapon attack. Ki-Empowered Strikes Your unarmed attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming enemies' Resistance and Immunity to non-magical damage. Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike After making an attack with a melee Monk weapon or while unarmed, you can make another unarmed attack as a bonus action. Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks Attacks with Monk weapons and unarmed attacks scale with your Dexterity instead of your Strength if your Dexterity is higher. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Psionic Empowerment Your attacks deal an extra 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage - the scars of illithid enslavement run deep. Slow Fall When you fall, you can use your reaction to gain Resistance to Falling damage. Stillness of Mind If Charmed or Frightened , automatically cast Stillness of Mind to remove them. Unarmoured Defence Your reflexes are as effective as any armour . While not wearing armour, you add your Wisdom Modifier to your Armour Class . Unarmoured Movement Your movement speed increases by 3 m (10 ft) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield. Technical UID S_INT_GithRoyalGuard03 UUID b8492256-64d0-44a0-b289-eb8387b98f5f Stats Githyanki_Gishra_Melee High Gish'ra G'imre is a Gish'ra encountered in the Astral Plane at the beginning of Act Three. He is part of Orpheus' honour guard, and is fighting to free him. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During a long rest at the end of Act Two , the party members are suddenly woken to an attack by various githyanki monks. They are then called into a portal by the Dream Guardian , where it is revealed it is The Emperor . It asks for the party's help, as G'imre and the other monks are invading the Astral Prism to free the son of Gith himself Orpheus, who as it turns out is being held prisoner within the prism. The githyanki attack the party, regardless of the answer given to the Emperor. CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Raider G'r'ath is a githyanki in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Crèche Y'llek welcomes you, ra'stil . „ — G'r'ath Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] G'r'ath can be first met if party approach Crèche Y’llek through the Cliffside entrance . She is one of the sentries who questions them if they try to infiltrate the Crèche through the hidden tunnel. Dialogue choices are similar to those available when speaking with Gish Far’aag at the Monastery Basement entrance. The options differ depending on if the interacting party member is a githyanki: If the party member is a githyanki: [GITHYANKI]  I simply seek to meet more of my kin, it has been too long. [GITHYANKI]  Kith'rak Voss said you're looking for a weapon, I've brought it with me. [GITHYANKI]  A ghaik parasite has infected me. Your crèche's will offer me sanctuary, as is its mandate. [GITHYANKI]  Ghaik have infected these lands. I need this crèche's help stopping them. [GITHYANKI]  Took a wrong turn - I'll just be leaving. Otherwise, the following options allow the party to pass: Lae'zel? Perhaps you could intervene?  (if Lae'zel present) Wait! I've been infected by an illithid, and I need your help. I have the weapon Captain Voss was looking for. [PERSUASION]  I have not transformed yet, and it's been ages. Your medics would find me useful. (DC 21) Captain Voss won't be happy you killed the person who found your lost weapon. [DECEPTION]  Captain Voss told me to find the item you've been searching for. I have it. (DC 18) [INTIMIDATION]  Let me past. It'll save both of us time and you a lot of blood. (DC 21) [PERSUASION]  Wait! A nautiloid crashed on your doorstep. People are getting infected by mind flayers. I need help. (DC 18) After the party infiltrates the Crèche, G'r'ath and Warrior Qen guard the same pass above the Trade Post of the Crèche. She becomes hostile to the party if they fail in their attempt to infiltrate the Crèche, or choose to walk back through the Crèche after speaking to the Inquisitor and start a fight. Emmet Of course - he never travels without his friends. Let's go! Technical UID S_LOW_BloomridgeGhostWatch_Civilian4 UUID 2235302d-9677-4aa2-aa10-5b25044f40b6 Stats Human_Commoner Gaff Garsem is a human civilian attempting to hunt ghosts in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I'd go home if I were you - I think the halfling in charge is the most haunted thing here. „ — Gaff Garsem Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Gaff is on the path to the House of Grief being led by 'Suspicious' Foont on a ghost hunt with Kydden , and Gor Falogen . Gaff is skeptical, but nevertheless paid to be on the ghost hunt. The group are completely oblivious to an entire house full of haunted spirits in Lady Jannath's Estate just behind them, if the ⁠ Free the Artist quest is active. Gaff's attitude towards the party changes, depending on the outcome of the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Suspicious' Foont Gentlemen, I am quite certain that we are almost upon this most nefarious spirit! Gaff Garsem How, uh, how can you tell? 'Suspicious' Foont Can't you feel rich, unctuous gouts of necromantic energy simply coursing through the spirit field? Gaff Garsem Uh... I don't think so...? Gor Falogen That's because there's nothing here to feel. This is a colossal waste of time. Kydden I feel something! 'Suspicious' Foont Yes, my friend? What do you feel? Kydden My ears are cold! What does that mean? 'Suspicious' Foont Well, some spirits do communicate in a rather obtuse manner. 'Suspicious' Foont It could be inviting you to listen to the tale of its plight! 'Suspicious' Foont A sepulchral beckoning from beyond the veil! Gor Falogen Or his ears could just be cold. 'Suspicious' Foont Exercise caution! We do not yet know whether this spirit is malevolent or benign! Kydden Oh gods, what if it is malevolent? What if it's out to get us? 'Suspicious' Foont Worry not! I am well equipped to protect us in that eventuality. Gor Falogen You think that wand from that charlatan at Devil's Fee is going to protect us? Gor Falogen If there was anything we needed protecting from... 'Suspicious' Foont One must be prepared at all times - an unfortunate demise awaits the hasty. Kydden It's going to kill us, isn't it? Gaff Garsem You know, I'm not sure ghost hunting is for me... 'Suspicious' Foont Now, now - I'm sure it's much more scared of us than we should be of it. Kydden I've seen a real ghost snap someone in half! Kydden It squeezed their guts out of their ears like an overfilled sausage! Kydden Well, my cousin saw a real ghost snap someone in half. But they got better. Gor Falogen Well, I'm very glad they got better. 'Suspicious' Foont Hush! Too much cacophonous chatter and we'll scare away our quarry. EQP_HeavyCrossbow_Leather Trs. BG_Guard Fist Gai is a human ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is at Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . “ Can't keep an eye on all of them. Someone's bound to slip past. „ — Gai , speaking to Fist Shah and Blaze Elin Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gai is stationed together with Fist Shah , Blaze Elin and three Steel Watchers at the bridge leading from Wyrm's Crossing into Wyrm's Rock Fortress . They guard the entrance and prevent anyone from going into the fortress (and, by extension, the Lower City of Baldur's Gate ) except those who have decent reason to pass. Gai refuses to discuss anything with the party, sending them to Elin to try and be allowed to pass. After gaining access into Wyrm's Rock Fortress (whichever way available), Gai treats the party as citizens eligible to cross their checkpoint in any direction. Technical UID S_GOB_AttackOnDen_Sapper_004 UUID 1b6dba51-be8b-47ac-a73b-94c29e56bbad Stats GOB_GoblinSapper Sapper Gald is a goblin sapper in Act One . “ Let's just keep out of her way. She's smiling. I get scared when she smiles. „ — Gald , on Minthara Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Gald only appears if Minthara launches a raid on the Emerald Grove . If Minthara learns of the Grove's location such as through the party, Liam's interrogation, or Sazza , she gathers a group of goblins to attack the sanctuary. Gald does not appear in the Goblin Camp and is only encountered during this raid. As a sapper, Gald's only purpose is to act as a suicide bomber against enemy targets. EQ_Gale Gale Dekarios is an Origin Character and recruitable Companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. He is a human wizard with the Sage background. Gale can be first found at the Roadside Cliffs waypoint during Act One . A scholar and prodigy in the arcane arts, Gale is committed to unlocking the secrets of the Weave no matter the cost. “ There's a gust of Weave about you, but it's a mere breeze. I need a tempest. „ — Gale 's hunger for powerful magic Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Personal quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Act One 1.5.2 Leaving the party 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Life in Waterdeep 3.2 Blackstaff Academy 3.3 Chosen of Mystra 3.4 Seclusion in Waterdeep 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.2 Act Two 4.3 Act Three 4.4 Endings 4.4.1 Gale's Sacrifice 4.4.2 Professor Dekarios 4.4.3 The God of Ambition 4.4.4 Elysium 4.4.5 Failed Ascension 5 Quest rewards 6 Interactions 6.1 Companion interactions 6.1.1 Act One 6.1.2 Act Two 6.1.3 Act Three 6.2 Unique interactions 6.2.1 Act One 6.2.2 Act Two 6.2.3 Act Three 6.3 Speak with Dead 7 Related literature 8 Related quests 9 Loot 9.1 Starting equipment 10 Achievements 11 Gallery 12 Notes and references 13 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] For a full overview of Gale's starting features, see the articles Wizard , Evocation School and Human . Background [ edit section | visual editor ] A prodigy of magic, Gale is a wizard of great talent and equally great ambition. Once a Chosen of Mystra , his quest to prove himself to his goddess resulted in him being cursed with a long-forgotten form of magic, a ticking time bomb with an all-consuming hunger. Now bereft of Mystra’s favor and condemned by a tadpole in his head, Gale must find a way to free himself from both the curse and this unwelcome guest. Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before he is recruited, Gale is a level 1 Wizard with the following Ability Scores : 8 STR, 13 DEX, 14 CON, 15 INT, 10 WIS, 12 CHA. If recruited, Gale reverts to a level 1 Wizard with the standard ability scores for that class . He has a balanced repertoire of 6 spells and 3 cantrips , allowing him to act both as an offensive and supporting caster. Upon reaching level two, he defaults to the Evocation School subclass, giving him access to a wider arsenal of offensive spells. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] In order to sate his arcane hunger, Gale must consume magic items periodically for a total of three times. If he does not then he becomes afflicted with "Arcane Hunger" which has three different stages of severity: Arcane Hunger gives him disadvantage to Constitution saving throws . Greater Arcane Hunger gives him disadvantage on all attack rolls and saving throws. Severe Arcane Hunger gives him disadvantage on all attack rolls and saving throws and his movement speed is halved. After reaching the third stage, if not fed Weave, Gale's netherese orb explodes leading to a Game Over screen. [ verify ] For recommendations on which items to give Gale for consumption, see the list of consumable items and the guide Snacks for Gale . If slain, Gale's corpse emanates a Necrotic Aura , dealing 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage every turn to those around it until he is revived . Leaving him dead for more than three long rests leads to a Game Over screen, as his netherese orb detonates without magic to sustain it. Cursed by netherese magic, Gale can cast Netherese Orb Blast , obliterating everything in the vicinity and leading to a Game Over screen. Gale can create the Shadow Lantern in Moonrise Towers , a unique item that allows summoning a Shadow . Alternatively, he can reject the ritual, receiving Mystra's Benevolence instead, granting him advantage on Concentration checks until the next long rest. When chosen as an origin character, Gale can either cleanse or consume the Shadow Weave from the corpse of Malus Thorm , Gerringothe Thorm or Thisobald Thorm , granting him one of the following boons: Consumed Shadow Weave gives Gale an additional Level 3 Shadow Spell Slot that recharges on long rest if he consumed the Shadow Weave. Mystra's Blessing gives Gale partial immunity to ⁠ Acid , ⁠ Cold , ⁠ Fire , ⁠ Force , and ⁠ Thunder damage if he cleansed the Shadow Weave. When played as an origin character, Tara , Gale's tressym, joins him in the Campsite as a Camp Follower . If Gale chooses to ask for Mystra's forgiveness during their meeting at the Stormshore Tabernacle in the Lower City , she grants him Anointed in Splendour which permanently gives him a +2 bonus to all saving throws. He is the only party member who does not need to make an offer at one of the statues at the Stormshore Tabernacle to obtain this condition. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale's personal quest as companion is ⁠ The Wizard of Waterdeep . As an origin his personal quest is ⁠ The Wizard of Waterdeep (Origin) . His personal quest is spanning all acts of the game. In it, Gale must come to terms with the consequences of his unbridled ambitions. Primary among these: his fall from grace with Mystra and the ticking time bomb in his body. Two further subquests are available that tie into his personal quest: ⁠ In Case of Death... , in which the party must deal with Gale's protocol for his untimely death, and ⁠ Balthazar's Experiment , where Gale can decide to finish the work of a dangerous necromancer. Completing ⁠ In Case of Death... with a Sage background character grants the ⁠ Reanimator inspiration. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale can be recruited as a permanent companion during Act One . Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale can be found when approaching the Roadside Cliffs Ancient Rune Circle , north of the Ravaged Beach . If investigated, Gale sticks his hand out from inside the circle and asks for help. A successful ability check is required to pull him out, with multiple options available: [KARLACH] [STRENGTH]  You'll have to remain extremely calm to touch him without burning him. Take a deep breath, then pull.  (DC 7) [DARK URGE] [STRENGTH]  Ignore the urge to maim. Grab the hand and pull.  (DC 7) [STRENGTH]  Grab the hand and pull.  (DC 7) [WIZARD] [INTELLIGENCE]  Whisper to the Weave roiling within the sigil. Attempt to calm it down.  (DC 7) [WARLOCK] [SORCERER] [BARD] [CHARISMA]  Attune yourself to the sigil's magic, then bid it to quiet down.  (DC 7) [CLERIC] [DRUID] [WISDOM]  Let flow some words of prayer to soothe the sigil's magic.  (DC 7) [CLERIC OF MYSTRA] [WISDOM]  Let flow some words of prayer to soothe the sigil's magic.  (DC 7  ) [ROGUE] [SLEIGHT OF HAND]  With a keen, but calculated twist, you attempt to sabotage the sigil.  (DC 12) If the first check is failed, a second one may be attempted with increased difficulty: [KARLACH] [STRENGTH]  Take a deep breath. Stay calm and cool. When you're sure your flames won't hurt him, pull again.  (DC 12) [STRENGTH]  Pull again, as hard as you can.  (DC 12) [STRENGTH]  Muster your strength and yank harder.  (DC 7)  (if class-specific check) Failing two checks, or choosing to leave him to his fate, results in Gale falling back into the rune circle and locks him out from recruitment. Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale moves to leave the party if the goblins are sided with and the Emerald Grove is raided successfully. After the slaughter, he confronts the player and says his goodbyes, though he may be retained through dialogue. If neglected or ignored for too long, he leaves the party without much fanfare, leaving only a small note behind. [ 1 ] On meeting Gale the first time as the Dark Urge , the player character has a special option on where they fantasize about cutting off his hand. If selected, the fantasy is not merely imagined, but acted out in real time: Gale loses his hand to the Dark Urge's unrestrained impulses and falls back into the circle, permanently barring the party from recruiting him. Also, doing this is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of any Oath subclass . If attacking and killing Elminster at the start of Act Two instead of talking to him, Gale leaves the party at the end of the Act, stating that his condition has worsened to the point that he can longer satiate it, and wishes to find somewhere remote to end his life. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Gale/Approval Gale Approves Gale generally approves of doing good and helping those in need, as well as solving conflicts with tact and pragmatism. He approves of those who appreciate the arcane arts and are willing to learn from him, as well as those who support his grand ambitions. Gale dislikes harming innocents and using unnecessary violence when diplomacy is an option. As a scholar, he disapproves of destroying or wasting valuable knowledge. Those who criticise his convictions and goals earn his disapproval. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Gale/Romance Gale may be romanced by characters of any gender. In his relationship, Gale must reconcile his newfound feelings of love with the tragic consequences of his past involvement with Mystra, as well as deal with his impending death. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale has a simple, yet refined style to him, with clothes well-made but never ostentatious. His mousy brown hair is straight and shoulder-length, swept back with an elegant flair. His eyes are chestnut brown, his gaze soft but confident, and he keeps his facial hair neatly trimmed. On his left ear, Gale wears a silver earring shaped in the form of an eight-pointed star, the holy symbol of Mystra, perhaps representing his former relationship with the goddess or just his affinity with magic. In the middle of his chest, a dark circle with wispy tendrils can be found, the result of absorbing Karsus' netherese magic. These tendrils extend all the way to under his left eye, faint, but ever present. [ 2 ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale is an intelligent, articulate and thoughtful practitioner of the arcane arts, with a good-hearted and peaceful nature. Despite his scholarly and slightly pompous manner of speaking, he is friendly and always willing to lend his ear to friends. As an accomplished wizard and eternal scholar, he is proud of his arcane knowledge and feats achieved as an erstwhile Chosen. Yet it is precisely this pride, combined with his ambition, which overshadows his otherwise exemplary ability to reason and risks his repeating grave mistakes from his past. Still, Gale can be sensible, and if convinced by friends, is willing to reconsider (or at least think twice) before jumping to rash actions. Furthermore, he is good to his companions, being attentive of their problems and taking care of them however he can, often by assuming cooking duties for the camp. [ 3 ] Though outwardly confident and easy-going, Gale still carries the physical and emotional wounds of his former relationship with Mystra and the consequences of dabbling in forbidden magic. As such, he is sensitive to criticism, and often reacts defensively when confronted with his past actions. All of this leads him to be willing to do anything to earn Mystra's forgiveness, even if it means sacrificing his life to do so. He also seems to hide somewhat behind his Gale of Waterdeep persona, built to project this image of a great and powerful wizard as opposed to, the way he sees it, the more mundane Gale Dekarios. [ 4 ] History [ edit section | visual editor ] Life in Waterdeep [ edit section | visual editor ] Born to Morena Dekarios and an unknown father, [ 5 ] Gale was raised in the city of Waterdeep . A prodigy of magic from a young age, Gale learned to manipulate the Weave like a skilled virtuoso plays music, his talents and abilities manifesting in many occasions, though often with unintended consequences. One time, forbidden from having a cat of his own by his parents, Gale summoned Tara , a tressym that would become not only his lifelong companion, but also family. [ 6 ] Such was their bond that Gale disallowed any attempts at referring to Tara as his pet. After Gale's departure from home, Tara kept mother Dekarios company throughout the years. Other less successful attempts resulted in a fiery meeting with a Magma Mephit , though he kept in touch with them over the years, nonetheless. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] In time, Gale enrolled at the prestigious Blackstaff Academy , an educational institution for promising wizards and sorcerers. [ 9 ] Blackstaff Academy [ edit section | visual editor ] The academy seemed the perfect place to nourish his talents, as Gale deeply believed he was destined for greatness despite being only a child. Still, young Gale's misadventures would continue even at the academy. Irritated with everyone's lack of faith in him, he attempted to cast a portal spell with the Blackstaff itself. Though it worked, rather than returning to his dormitory as he intended, the resulting portal pulled him into Limbo , facing a rather angry Death Slaad. Before Gale could face the slaad, the current Blackstaff Archmage pulled Gale back, and punished him with months of tedious work. [ 10 ] Chosen of Mystra [ edit section | visual editor ] At some point, Gale was mentored by Elminster Aumar , one of the most powerful and famous wizards of Faerûn and a hero to Gale. The Sage of Shadowdale guided Gale, furthering his mastery over the Weave and arcane arts, and over time became something of a parental figure to him. [ 11 ] Gale's talent eventually drew the attention of the Goddess of Magic, Mystra , who made him one of her Chosen. Mystra became a teacher, muse, and eventually lover to Gale. [ 12 ] When Mystra's passion waned, Gale sought the rekindle her interest by showing he was her equal. But the Goddess of Magic refused his every plea. Having learned of Karsus' Folly and his attempts at reaching godhood via his Netherese magic, Gale searched for a tome containing a scrap of Weave, hoping to impress Mystra by returning a long-lost part of her. [ 13 ] Yet when he opened the book, a writhing mass of darkest black leapt at him and fused with his body, creating within him an insatiable hunger for magic. To keep the orb from exploding with enough force to level an entire city, Gale needed to consume magic constantly in order to feed this gnawing emptiness. Yet the most painful punishment for his hubris would be to lose his position as Mystra's Chosen. When she learned of Gale's recklessness, Mystra ceased all contact with him and ended their relationship for good without adding another word, leaving Gale to face the Netherese orb within him on his own. Seclusion in Waterdeep [ edit section | visual editor ] Abandoned and with a doomsday device in his body, Gale moved back to his tower in Waterdeep to live in quiet seclusion. As much as he wished to be alone, Tara was there to accompany him even in his lowest of lows, [ 14 ] and together, they spent most of their time locating magic items for Gale to consume. Being forsaken by Mystra turned him into somewhat of a recluse, with few friends remaining. For unknown reasons, Gale left the tower in a hurry after some time, and shortly after he was abducted by the rogue Nautiloid and tadpoled along other victims. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] See main article: The Wizard of Waterdeep The Wizard of Waterdeep is Gale's personal quest. It is added to the journal upon recruiting him and spans all three acts of the game. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale can be found at the Roadside Cliffs rune circle . Likely trapped as he hastily escaped the crashing Nautiloid , he asks the party for assistance in getting him out. Once free, he recognizes the party as other victims of the Illithid aboard the besieged ship and quickly offers his services as a wizard of great renown. As the party travel together, Gale begins displaying signs of sickness, and if friendly enough with his companions, eventually asks them to bring him magical artefacts. When pressed for reasons why, he mentions it is a condition he has which requires feeding from the Weave but is reluctant to say more. He asks them to trust him and stresses how important treating his affliction is. Refusing to aid Gale progresses his sickness, eventually resulting in a Game Over screen. When brought certain magical items, Gale consumes them. Upon doing so his sickness is temporarily treated and he looks visibly better. Gale asks for magic items three times in total. The first time he is left satisfied, and assures answers will be given soon. The second time he notes the effects are diminishing but is grateful nonetheless. The third and final time he is distressed as the effect is barely noticeable and finally reveals the truth. Gale explains he was a magical prodigy, being able to control and sculpt the Weave at a young age. This gained him the attention of Mystra , the goddess of magic, who became his teacher, muse, and eventually his lover. However, with Mystra, Gale witnessed magic that was beyond mere mortals and seeing the powers he was denied, he begged her for more, only to be rejected each time and told to be contented with what he had. Seeking to prove himself a peer to Mystra, Gale eventually found a magical tome from the ancient empire of Netheril. Within it was contained a fragment of Weave that had been lost following Karsus' Folly , suspended in time and out of Mystra's eyes. Gale believed that by returning the fragment to Mystra, he would earn her favor and be granted the powers he desperately wanted, yet once he opened the tome, the fragment of raw Weave lodged itself within him, an insatiably hungry orb of netherese magic. Secluded and locked away in his tower in Waterdeep , Gale was able to manage the condition, but in the wilds, it risked becoming uncontrollable. If the orb was not sated, it would detonate with the power to level a city the size of Waterdeep. With the truth out, and concerned about his current predicament, Gale begins looking into more permanent solutions to sate the netherese orb. As the party continues their travels, they eventually encounter an old man in the trail leading to the Shadow-Cursed Lands in the Rosymorn Monastery Trail . Gale recognizes the man as none other than Elminster Aumar , the legendary Sage of Shadowdale and a former mentor of his. Elminster announces that he comes to deliver an important message to Gale, and asks to speak in peace back at camp. There, he reveals Mystra has been watching over Gale and following the movements of the Cult of the Absolute with great concern. Mystra sees the Absolute as a credible threat to the world, and believes the only person able to stop them is Gale. Thus, she offers a bargain her former Chosen cannot resist: redemption in exchange for his life. Elminster explains the power of the netherese orb lodged within Gale can be harnessed as a weapon to destroy the Absolute for good and stabilizes Gale's orb [ 15 ] , controlling its hunger pangs and allowing Gale to detonate it at will. Gale considers the proposition solemnly, and thanks Elminster for his words. With the message imparted, Elminster wishes Gale and the party the best of luck in defeating the Absolute and departs. When spoken to, Gale seems to be shocked at Mystra's directive, but considers it seriously. This is the chance he has been hoping for: redemption in Mystra's eyes, albeit at the cost of martyrdom. The party can support or dissuade him from following this path. As an origin, when Tara is told about the plan, she disapproves of the idea, and presses Gale to promise her he will find another way. If Gale dies at some point during his adventures, his body starts emanating a necrotic aura, harming those near his corpse. The first time this happens, a projection of him appears nearby which begins ⁠ In Case of Death... . The projection gives precise instructions on how to revive Gale, and stresses the importance of doing so before it is too late. Following the instruction grants a Scroll of True Resurrection , reviving Gale results in his gratitude and some information on his condition. If Gale dies again, the party must find other means to revive him. If left dead for three long rests, a Game Over screen appears as the netherese orb within him explodes after being left unsatiated for too long. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] While exploring the Shadow-Cursed Lands , Gale and the party can find a hidden chamber belonging to Balthazar in Moonrise Towers . The chamber is clearly used for the necromancer's experiments, and upon inspecting a nearby table, Gale attempts to make sense of the writings on it, beginning the quest ⁠ Balthazar's Experiment . He reveals the sigils are used in the fabrication of Moonlanterns and that given enough time, he can create a better one himself. The ritual does require using dark magic forbidden by Mystra, leaving the decision up to the party whether to encourage or dissuade Gale from finishing the necromancer's work. Allowing Gale to complete the lantern results in the party gaining a Shadow Lantern , a dark reflection of the regular Moonlanterns found, while destroying the sigils rewards Gale with Mystra's Benevolence until the next long rest. After reaching the Mind Flayer Colony , the party finally comes face-to-face with the truth of the Absolute: a gargantuan Elder Brain controlled by the Chosen of the Dead Three ; Ketheric Thorm , Enver Gortash , and Orin the Red ; using the fabled Crown of Karsus . With the Elder Brain and the Chosen all gathered in a single location, Gale decides that no better opportunity will present itself and prepares to detonate his netherese orb as ordered by Mystra. The party can encourage Gale to go through with Mystra's directive, destroying everything in the vicinity, including the Absolute and the Chosen, as well as the party. Because this course of action does not destroy the Elder Brain beneath Baldur's Gate nor remove the tadpoles already implanted in the victims around the Sword Coast , it causes a mass ceremorphosis as the tadpoles wake from their stasis. Without anything controlling them, rampant illithid ravage the lands, infecting and destroying everything they see, leading to an early Game Over screen. Gale can be convinced to do otherwise, however, by passing certain dialogue ability checks for him to stand down. Alternatively, he can be left in camp when adventuring through the illithid colony, skipping his interactions. Though he is disheartened at having defied Mystra and thus eschewed redemption in her eyes, he quickly shifts his focus to the artefact controlling the Elder Brain. Gale identifies it as as the Crown of Karsus, one of the regalia of the ancient archwizard Karsus, and an exceptionally powerful arcane object thought long lost. Convinced it is the key to defeating the Absolute for good, he asks the party to help him find more information about it. Since the group's destination is Baldur's Gate, he believes the famous Sorcerous Sundries must have information on netherese magic, making it worth a visit. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Mystra's statue in the Stormshore Tabernacle, bright with transporting channel for Gale Once at Baldur's Gate, Gale recommends visiting Sorcerous Sundries with haste, sure that the renowned bookstore will have tomes on netherese magic that can be of use in defeating the Absolute. There, when inquired about possible books on the matter, Tolna Tome-Monger answers that a tome containing information on Karsus' Folly and Netheril exists, yet it is kept under lock in the vaults as the information is too sensitive for most readers and access is strictly forbidden. The party can convince her to volunteer information on how to reach the vaults, or break in themselves through subtlety. Whatever the case, once in the vaults, the party must follow the correct path to reach Karsus' vault, containing the ancient tome The Annals of Karsus . If given the tome after reading, Gale exclaims it not only contains information on the Crown of Karsus, but also details on how it was constructed, making it possible to reforge it after destroying the elder brain. Gale's ambitions grow at the prospect of the power he could wield with the Crown, speculating that he could become a god strong enough to challenge even Mystra. The party can support his plans to be free from the yoke of Mystra, or challenge him about them, warning against treading down the same path Karsus once did before the fall of his empire. Whatever the outcome of the discussion, Elminster will visit the group once more upon leaving Sorcerous Sundries with a message from Mystra. The goddess of magic is willing to grant Gale an audience as she knows he not only defied her orders, but read the tome of Karsus as well. With Elminster's encouragement, the party must reach the Stormshore Tabernacle and let Gale interact with Mystra's altar there. Before departing, Gale can be encouraged to stand up to himself, whatever his final goals may be, or seek reconciliation with Mystra and possibly even redemption. Gale is transported to Mystra's domain where he finally meets his former patron and lover. An origin Gale can actively participate in the conversation as usual, while a companion Gale will converse with her on his own. Mystra informs Gale the piece of Weave he sought to return to her is actually a part of the Karsite Weave and it carries within it Karsus’ relentless ambition. This new form of Weave was born during Karsus' final moments, as he wrestled magic away from Mystryl and briefly ascended to godhood. It cannot be contained, it will never be sated and in order to prevent it from detonating and releasing a wave of destruction, Mystra allowed it to feed on the true Weave while she devised a solution. Knowing the Crown's reforging is a very real possibility, she implores Gale to return it to her, as its danger cannot be understated. She promises to cure Gale's condition if he does so, even offering him to become her Chosen once more. Unsure of what to do, Gale thanks Mystra and leaves pensive. Back on the mortal plane, Gale recounts what transpired in Mystra's realm, and says there is not much they can do until they defeat the Elder Brain. As the battle for Baldur's Gate rages on, the party arrives at the Elder Brain's brainstem. While they prepare for the final battle, Gale may be approached to discuss the imminent fight and the netherese orb he still carries within. Depending on past interactions with him, Gale may offer the party, or can be convinced, to deal with the Elder Brain on his own, doing as Mystra instructed and detonating the orb inside to destroy the Absolute for good. If deciding to go through with his plan, Gale says his goodbyes and teleport them away. He climbs the stem on his own and stabs himself in the chest, triggering a magical explosion that annihilates the Elder Brain for good. If his offer is declined, the party battles the Elder Brain instead and Gale is present during the Absolute's downfall. As it crashes in the river Chionthar, the Crown of Karsus breaks into pieces, sinking to the depths of the river. While the party gathers victorious, Gale announces his intentions to search the river for the pieces of the Crown. Depending on how he was treated in past conversations, and whether the party supported his ambitions or not, he may intend to reforge the Crown to ascend to godhood or simply to return it to Mystra. Whatever the case, he first desires to celebrate their victory in a nearby tavern, completing his companion quest. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale's Sacrifice [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale alone atop the Netherbrain “ Thrall? No, I think you're mistaken. The name's Gale of Waterdeep. A pleasure to make your acquaintance. Though our time together will be exceptionally brief. Farewell, and happy landing. „ — Gale 's last words before letting his Orb explode Gale can sacrifice himself before the final encounter with the Elder Brain. When approaching the brain's brainstalk, Gale may offer to do one last act of penance, complete Mystra's command and detonate the orb within him. If accepted, Gale teleports the party away before confronting the elder brain alone and destroys it with the power of the netherese orb. Unlike the choice of sacrificing himself during act 2, this martyring does deal with the tadpoles as they perish along their controlling brain, leading to the Endings and Epilogue . Professor Dekarios [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale as Professor Dekarios After beating the Elder Brain, Gale reforges the Crown of Karsus after fishing up the pieces from the river Chionthar. If pushed to become a man of his own and forsake Mystra's approval, he receives an audience with Mystra and returns the Crown to her in exchange of being cured from of the affliction of the netherese orb. Mystra fulfills her end of the deal and Gale returns to Waterdeep. Months later at Withers reunion gathering, Gale introduces himself as professor Gale of the Blackstaff Academy, seemingly teaching young prodigies in the ways of Illusion magic . Though cured of the netherese orb, he has not revealed this to his students as he finds his explosive reputation useful in controlling his pupils. He will offer a guest lecture to the player, an opportunity to regale his students with his exploits in the past months. When romanced, Gale will additionally abandon his Gale of Waterdeep persona to be content with plain Gale Dekarios . The God of Ambition [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale bringing the player character to Elysium If Gale's ambitions were given wind throughout the adventures together, after reforging the Crown of Karsus, Gale uses it to complete Karsus' half-formed netherese Weave and ascend to godhood, becoming the God of Ambition . Unlike Mystra, who keeps a tight leash on her divine boons, Gale intends to be there for all of his devouts, good or evil, spurring their desires and dreams whether they be a fledgling adventurer or a dreaded necromancer. With shrines in Thay and construction of a temple beginning in Amn , Gale's divinity is already spreading across Faerûn. Depending on whether or not he was pushed to be vindictive against Mystra, Gale may attempt to battle the goddess of magic for supremacy. In the end, Gale's ambition proves too much and Mystra deals with him decisively. If he fails, a Spectral Voice is left behind instead. If romanced, Gale can offer his partner to ascend to his new divine realm and rule it together. If accepted, Gale does as promised and ascends his partner to oversee the ambitions of mortals together in bliss. Whatever outcome of divine Gale, Tara will be disappointed with her former friend, sorry that he could not learn from his past follies. Elysium [ edit section | visual editor ] If an origin Gale transformed into an illithid to defeat the Elder Brain, he is granted a final audience with Mystra. Mystra can offer to cure him both of the netherese affliction and his illithid status if he accepts to go to Elysium with her. If he accepts, Mystra fulfills her promise and Gale is taken away from the Material Plane. Failed Ascension [ edit section | visual editor ] Having never learned the secrets of Karsus and his netherese regalia from The Annals of Karsus , Gale perishes attempting to reforge the destroyed Crown of Karsus to reach godhood. At Withers gathering, his projection gives his final farewells to his former companions and hands over an Improvised Letter , regretting having sacrificed everything for a chance at divinity. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Scroll of True Resurrection — reward for following Gale's instructions as part of the quest In Case of Death... . Shadow Lantern — reward for finishing Balthazar's experiment as part of the quest Balthazar's Experiment . Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale can be spoken with Speak with Dead , and has unique dialogue interactions as a companion available after certain events. Whenever one is available, he has a floating [ ! ] icon above him. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character intervenes in the confrontation between Arka and Sazza standing in harm's way for the goblin, Gale reminisces about a similar situation he saw in the Yawning Portal . Gale seeks out the player character when he requires a new magic item to feed on. This can occur thrice. After saving Mirkon from the harpies near the grove, Gale reminisces about his childhood with the party. If intervening on behalf of Arabella when facing Kagha's judgment and manages to have her spared, Gale is happy about the outcome of the confrontation. Upon receiving Mystra's orders via Elminster , Gale can be spoken with to learn more about his feelings on his new mission. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] None. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] After meeting Tara on the rooftop of the Open Hand Temple , Gale expresses his happiness over seeing her once more, and can be questioned about his surname. Unique interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Either as an origin , or in the party as a companion , Gale has unique interactions and special dialogue with the following characters, listed by the act they are first encountered in. Technical UID S_GLO_GurHunter UUID 0e47fcb9-c0c4-4b0c-902b-2d13d209e760 Stats HAG_GurHunter Eqp. EQP_Gandrel Trs. Hag_GurHunter Gandrel is a human Gur monster-hunter who is southwest of the Riverside Teahouse waypoint in Act One . He arrived in the Sunlit Wetlands to ask Auntie Ethel for help with his current hunt. “ I wish I had half the power settled folk think my people possess. Alas, I am a simple wanderer. „ — Gandrel Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act One 1.2 Act Three 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Tactics 2.3 Loot 3 Related quests 4 Speak with Dead 4.1 If talking as Astarion: 5 Notes Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] If Astarion is present, Gandrel reveals he is hunting for Astarion, whom he believes is a vampire spawn that attacked their village and abducted a child. Otherwise, the party can learn this information by passing a DC 15 Persuasion Check or DC 20 Intimidation Check . The party can choose to give up Astarion or protect him. Giving up Astarion results in his permanent removal from the party. Preventing Astarion from killing Gandrel earns Astarion's disapproval. If spared, Gandrel happily trades with the party, though he offers little besides some Arrows , Torches , Potions of Healing and a Supply Pack . If a party member speaks with Gandrel and chooses not to betray Astarion or kill Gandrel, it can be arranged so that Astarion dies; if the party then speaks with Gandrel again, there is no option to disclose who Astarion is. If Astarion is revived, and he is nearby, the option to betray Astarion remains available. If the player character talks to Gandrel as an Origin Astarion, they can reveal themselves to him; this initiates combat. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If Gandrel survives Act One, he appears with the Gur caravan in Act Three . If the party turned Astarion over to him in Act One, he is hostile and the rest of the Gur are dead, having been slaughtered by Cazador when the vampire lord reclaimed Astarion for his diabolic ritual. If the party did not turn over Astarion, then he is at the elevator up from Cazador's Dungeon alongside the other Gur once the fight with Cazador has concluded. If the vampire spawn in Cazador's captivity are freed after this, Gandrel moves to the Lower City Sewers with his children, Chessa and Kass . The party can speak to him regarding his children's hunger. Approaching while having any effect that produces sunlight, such as The Blood of Lathander or Daylight triggers his children's sunlight hypersensitivity and causes him to become hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Boar Companion ( ) Summon a boar that can sweep through the battlefield and knock enemies off their feet with its Charge . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Short rest Hail of Thorns ( + + ) Damage: 1~10 Normal weapon damage + 1d10 ⁠ Piercing Shoot a volley of thorns. The thorns deal weapon damage to the target and then explode. The explosion deals an additional 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage to the target and surrounding creatures. On miss, the thorns still explode. On save, targets still take half damage from the explosion. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Hunter's Mark ( + ) Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Weapon Mark a creature as your quarry to deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Weapon damage whenever you hit it with a weapon attack. If the target dies before the spell ends, you can use Reapply Hunter's Mark to mark a new creature. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Dagger Damage: 5~8 1d4 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Ranged Attack ( )   –   Gandrel's Aspiration Damage: 6~15 1d10 + 5 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Sacred Munitions ( )   –   Gandrel's Aspiration Infuse your crossbow bolts with holy energy. For the rest of your turn, your ranged weapon attacks inflict Turned against undead . Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Despite fighting alone, Gandrel is a capable combatant due to his high Strength , Dexterity , Hit Points , and ability to use Extra Attack . He can fire the arrows in his inventory to strike multiple party members in a small area, which become more effective at low health due to his Scar of Fury passive which causes constant critical hits . Additionally, several of his ranger spells can apply negative conditions or deal AoE damage. If a grouped party member attacks him, this results in a "temporarily hostile" cutscene, and Gandrel is given an attack sequence. If an un-grouped summon attacks him, such as Shovel, the cutscene is skipped, allowing the player to take Gandrel by surprise. Due to his reliance on ranged attacks, it is possible to position a party member next to him to apply the Threatened condition to lower his ranged accuracy. If Astarion is present, Gandrel focuses his attacks on him. Although Gandrel is a formidable foe, ensnaring him or knocking him prone are effective ways to limit his mobility and hold him in melee range. It is also possible to prevent him from using arrows and potions during combat by purchasing them in advance or pickpocketing him. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Arrow of Acid - 2x (if unused) Arrow of Fire - 2x (if unused) Gandrel's Aspiration Potion of Healing - 2x (if unused) Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Investigate Cazador's Palace ⁠ The Pale Elf Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Gandrel's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Gandrel Gandrel... hunter... What are you hunting? Gandrel Vampire... Astarion ... What's your business with Astarion? Gandrel Our children... he knows... where they are... What brought you to this place? Gandrel Wise... woman... questions... Who is this wise woman? Gandrel Dread... creature... but not the one... I hunt... Do you have anything of value? Gandrel Much. Nothing... you can spend... If talking as Astarion: [ edit section | visual editor ] Who sent you? Was it Cazador? Gandrel No... Ulma ... leader of my tribe... What were you going to do to me? Gandrel Capture... return... Baldur's Gate... Why did you need me alive? Why not destroy me? Gandrel Our children... you know... where they are... Technical UID S_LOW_BlushingMermaid_BosunGannet UUID d6f07cae-779b-4f10-b87c-c8117bfa1fe9 Stats Human_Commoner Bosun Gannet is a human who serves food and drinks in the Blushing Mermaid tavern in Lower City of Baldur's Gate. “ If yer here to complain' that the booze tastes like piss - I know. Anything else? „ — Bosun Gannet Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] He is obviously a former sailor (probably a pirate) and partook in erstwhile crew of tavern's owner, Captain Grisly . Bosun Gannet also acts as a trader, selling various types of food and wine, and Supply Packs . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Bosun Gannet can be found at the bar counter inside the Blushing Mermaid at X: -145 Y: -100 . He is one of the characters who advance ⁠ Save Vanra quest, which is the logical follow-up for the ⁠ Avenge the Hag Survivors quest. Though Gannet can advance the quest, it is recommended to speak to Lora Bergauz . When the story about the kidnapped child is revealed, the party can speak to Gannet to dig out some details. Bosun tells the party that they are not the first ones who ask about the lost kid, little Vanra Bergauz . The first one was the girl's mother, Lora, who may be found later at the Basilisk Gate Barracks hassling the Flaming Fist in charge. Gannet also tells the party that Lora had been making a real racket about her missing daughter and eventually was thrown out of the tavern by its owner, Captain Grisly. As the quest continues, Bosun Gannet remembers some things about what had been really happening in the tavern, after false Captain Grisly has begun to run the show there. The first point when he might be approached about the details is after true identity of 'Grisly' has been revealed, and the party defeated the Tipplesome Patrons inside the tavern (Bosun himself and other tavern patrons do not take part in the battle until attacked or unintentionally damaged, e.g. by an AOE spell). However, he is obviously suffering from a memory-tampering charm and after spilling out a piece of secret 'changes his mind' and tries to convince the party that nothing unusual is happening around. After Auntie Ethel in her hag form has been defeated, Gannet's reactions differ depending on whether real Captain Grisly survived or died. If Captain Grisly survives, Bosun tells the party that he regrets not being able to help and protect her, because all that had been happening was like being stuck in a fog. He also welcomes the party 'aboard', saying that they are part of Mermaid's crew now. If Captain Grisly is killed when clearing The Blushing Mermaid - Basement , Gannet nonetheless does not put the blame on the party. He is aware of the hag who had been nesting in the tavern, and sincerely mourns the death of his former captain. He tells the party that he is running the tavern from now on, and he welcomes the party there any time. Whatever has happened to Grisly, if extending sympathy to her fate, Bosun Gannet becomes their ally and henceforth is outlined in green. However, if using only the 'trade' line after the quest has been finished, the bartender remains neutral to the party. After speaking with the party about the outcome of ⁠ Save Vanra , the only possible interaction with Gannet is trading. Technical UID S_WYR_MurderVictim UUID 3d23b55b-b1da-4075-a695-ecdd19f7d335 Stats Human_Commoner Trs. Gold_Meager Garrett is a human refugee in Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Garrett was killed in the refugee camp in Rivington after he created a scene. Garrett's brother and his husband Dairow Vin fled Elturel for a better life. At some point they separated, Dairow taking work with the Guild , and his husband travelling with a group of refugees. [ 1 ] After losing contact with his husband, Dairow contacted guildmaster Nine-Fingers Keene to try and find information on his whereabouts. The Guild were able to track the latest refugees he was travelling with, but after crossing paths with the Absolute's forces, the entire group went missing without a trace. [ 1 ] Grieving the loss and probable death of his husband, Dairow consumed a large quantity of Potions of Sleep , falling into an impenetrable slumber in the city sewers. Information supporting the assertion that Garrett's brother was the husband of Dairow can be learned by using Speak with Dead Dairow through which he reveals that he fled from the Absolute's army with his brother. Additional evidence includes the Our Offer Remains Open note on Dairow Vin's body, which shows his husband was also a refugee. Also on the refugee's body is the Gemless Ring which, when combined with the Ringless Gem held by Ferg Drogher , creates a Tarnished Ring . If Garrett is asked about the ring using Speak with Dead, he answers that the ring belonged to his brother – who died on the road. Finally, if a party member pickpocks or kills Dairow Vin, a similar tarnished ring can be found. All of these details lend credence to the theory that Garrett’s brother was Dairow’s husband, and the Tarnished Rings are their wedding bands. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Gemless Ring Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who are you? Garrett Garrett... What happened to you? Garrett Pushed... felt bones break... darknesss... Do you have any next of kin? Garrett None... Where are you from? Garrett East... fled armies... lost everything... What's the last thing you remember? Garrett Man... buying heirlooms... vulture. Challenged him... Tell me about the gemless ring I found with you. Garrett Brother's... died on the road... man tried to buy... Just like the rest of our public services. „ — Garri Orne Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Garri Orne and Drybeldiyx are southwest of the Blushing Mermaid , lamenting the sorry state of Lower City drinking fountains. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Drybeldiyx Don't bother. It's broken. Garri Orne This one too? This is the third fountain I've tried! Drybeldiyx Fourth for me. City's going to shit. Garri Orne Someone should report this to the gazette . Drybeldiyx If common sense can't sway them, perhaps a publicity disaster will. Garri Orne Always the way - no one fixes anything unless it hurts them personally. Drybeldiyx Can't blame them, I suppose. They've got armies to deal with. Garri Orne It's not that. It's that no politician ever went down in history for fixing the plumbing. Drybeldiyx Yes, but you do go down in history if your citizens die of thirst! v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag Support Group Adrielle Hydrangea Wubb Jatlo Kled Mayrina Technical UID S_TWN_Hospital_ZealousAssistant_001 UUID e2c2a930-2eb5-419f-9020-c141a0fd0753 Stats Surgeon_Nurse Sister Geanne is an undead nurse in the town of Reithwin during Act Two . “ Scalpel. First cut. Make the cut. „ — Geanne Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Sister Geanne is one of the Zealous Assistants of Malus Thorm in the House of Healing . She and several other undead nurses are learning to grasp the science provided by Thorm on a struggling Distressed Patient . If the party encounter Geanne or the other nurses, a dialogue with Malus Thorm is immediately triggered. During the dialogue, the interacting party member can convince Thorm to order the nurses to kill each other or to operate on himself. If they choose the latter, Geanne remains neutral after the surgeon's demise. She wanders the auditorium, offering philosophical ramblings about patients, healing, and Thorm's fate. If the party attack her, the other undead nurses also become hostile.
