UND_Duergar_Officer Gekh Coal leads a group of duergar slavers in the Decrepit Village in the Underdark during Act One . “ Too loud, sun-scum. Heard you stumbling. Can hear you blinking. „ — Gekh Coal , noticing the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Gekh is hiding via invisibility inside the Decrepit Village along with Garmor , Holvik , and Lurgan . If the party approach from the high ground, then one of his hidden companions reveals themselves and tells Gekh that "someone is sneaking up on them". If the party approaching from the beach, Gekh immediately addresses the party himself. Gekh then threatens to kill the party, but combat can be avoided by passing one of the following: [ 1 ] [BRANDED]  Show him your brand. [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  Stand down. I am a True Soul. (DC 2) [TRUE SOUL]  Stand down. I am a True Soul. [RELIGION]  Stand down - I'm a follower of the Absolute, just like you. (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  I can be discreet. No need for bloodshed. (DC 15) [INSIGHT]  Read the duergar's thoughts.  (DC 10) [DARK URGE] [INTIMIDATION]  I'm a rabid dirty dog, and I bite.  (DC 10) [BARBARIAN] [NON-DARK URGE] [INTIMIDATION]  Back down, or bleed.  (DC 15) [DROW] [DECEPTION]  I'm here at the Absolute's bidding. That's all you need to know. (DC 10) [DUERGAR]  I'm a duergar, idiot - we're practically kin. [FIGHTER]  Fights tend to make quite a racket, if that's what you want to avoid. [NON-UNDERDARK] [NON-BARBARIAN] [NON-HALF ORC] [INTIMIDATION]  Take your hand off that axe before you lose it. (DC 15) [HALF-ORC] [INTIMIDATION]  I'm hungry for a fight, but you're barely a morsel. Choose your next move carefully. (DC 10) Gekh explains that his group is searching for the Boots of Speed belonging to Sergeant Thrinn . The boots were stolen by Thulla , who was last seen near Ebonlake Grotto . The party can either offer to help him recover the boots or refuse. If they refuse then Gekh and the other Duergar become hostile and attack. If they agree to help and successfully take the boots from Thulla (whether through stealing them or as a reward for healing her), Gekh congratulates the party and allows them to use his raft to travel to the Adamantine Forge . If the player character is a deep gnome or the party is accompanied by Glut , then the duergar are immediately hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Gekh Coal usually casts Animate Dead immediately on the nearby shattered duergar corpses, reviving them as Reanimated Corpses . BG_Agent Geraldus is a new recruit for the Harpers , who has been looking into the recent Bhaalist activity in the city on Jaheira's orders. He is in Danthelon's Dancing Axe in Wyrm's Crossing . History [ edit section | visual editor ] Bhaalist Resurgence [ edit section | visual editor ] After rumors of Bhaalist activity surfaced in Baldur's Gate , Jaheira ordered her Harpers to look into the machinations of the Cult of Bhaal, letting them uncover as much information as possible while she led another force of Harpers into the Shadow-Cursed Lands to defeat Ketheric Thorm . However, as Jaheira ordered the Harpers to concentrate their efforts in finding the Rashemaar , Geraldus' Harper cell was killed or captured by Bhaalist doppelgangers , only to be brought to Orin . Geraldus was the only Harper left alive by the doppelgangers, to be used as live bait for Jaheira and the party to contact. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Hostage to Bhaalists [ edit section | visual editor ] While in Wyrm's Crossing with Jaheira and following ⁠ The High Harper , she points out Danthelon's Dancing Axe, a store run by Entharl Danthelon , and front for a Harper safe house. After Jaheira speaks with Entharl, he gives the party the key to a secret room beneath the store, where Geraldus and a group of impersonated Harpers are waiting to give Jaheira new information from their scouting. Once below, Geraldus greets the party, saying "May Selûne's Tears shine on this meeting." Jaheira immediately recognises the old Harper code, and tries to communicate to the player character that the Harpers present are traitors. Attacking the Harpers reveals all but Geraldus to be Bhaalist doppelgangers, their originals murdered, and Geraldus left alive as bait. If Geraldus dies during the fight, his corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead , and informs the party about the doppelganger treachery from the cult of Bhaal, Orin and Gortash's war with each other, and that he was here to give Jaheira information on the Rashemaar. If Geraldus survives the fight, and Jaheira is prsent, he explains the Harpers were searching for cultists of Bhaal in the city, and all was quiet until they began asking after the Rashemaar on Jaheira's latest orders. The cult struck during the night, capturing the others and bringing them back to Orin . Jaheira then chastises Geraldus on bringing danger to Entharl's shop, and suggests that maybe he is not cut out for the job. If the player character agrees, Jaheira and Entharl make plans to send Geraldus home to his mother in the Dalelands. If they disagree, or lecture Jaheira on sending the Harpers out on too dangerous a job, Jaheira apologises and instructs Geraldus to lie low and rest if he can; he is now the last Harper operating in the city who she can rely on. If Jaheira is not present, Geraldus gives them his report, assuming they were sent on Jaheira's orders. If the target dies before the spell ends, you can use Reapply Hunter's Mark to mark a new creature. ## Gerringothe Thorm
- **来源**: [Gerringothe Thorm](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Gerringothe_Thorm)
- **分类**: Characters、Bosses

Overview Combat Gerringothe Thorm Accursed Keeper of Coins In-game Model Identity Female Voice / Actor Penelope Rawlins Family Ketheric Thorm [ 1 ] Malus Thorm Thisobald Thorm Isobel Thorm Hometown Reithwin Town Stats Size Medium Type Undead Race Undead Technical UID S_TWN_Tollhouse_TollhouseMaster UUID 3b460226-8ca2-4bbc-9bd7-8bb947aa2c06 Stats TollCollector Gerringothe Thorm is a unique intelligent Undead, the toll-master of the Reithwin Tollhouse . “ I REQUIRE GOLD „ — Gerringothe Thorm , about everything Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 2.1 Dialogue 3 Combat 3.1 Loot 4 Related literature 5 Gallery 6 Notes 7 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Seemingly made of gold, Gerringothe is driven by endless greed and is relentless in enforcing the toll to cross the river to Moonrise Towers . Her greed is not limited to just her mannerisms; she also wields powerful abilities which are influenced by the amount of gold a character is carrying. As well, her Visages grant her coin armour, increasing her total hit points . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] When approached, Gerringothe quickly demands gold from the party. Besides attacking, the party can toss her some gold, though she demands more. When asked for a clear price, she demands all of the party's gold. However, if given anything short of 5,000 gold, Gerringothe claims she was given too little and attacks. If paid at least 5,000 gold, Gerringothe gives the party the Signed Trade Visa which can be used to cast the unique and powerful one-use spell: Flesh to Gold . This peaceful resolution also earns the same experience as if defeating her and all her Visage minions. Interacting with Gerringothe Thorm as well as Ketheric Thorm's other family members, grants the inspiration ⁠ Thorm Family Secrets to party members with the Sage background. Dialogue [ edit section | visual editor ] If the interacting party member chooses "I have no more gold" or "I have no more money to give" , she starts combat. Otherwise, a variety of Skill Checks can be used to avoid this: The player character can attempt to persuade Gerringothe that gold is not everything: [PERSUASION]  Why stay in this rotted building? Take your gold and be free. (DC 18) [PERSUASION]  Says who? Seems to me there's no one here to oversee you. (DC 21) [DECEPTION]  Haven't you heard? The local authority has decreed the gold belongs to the toll collector - you. (DC 21) [INTIMIDATION]  Not anymore. (DC 21) [MONK] [PERSUASION]  The happiness gold grants is temporary at best. Do not let your need for gold trap you here. (DC 18  ) [EVIL CLERIC] [PERSUASION]  I know lust and avarice when I see it. You'll never be happy, no matter how much gold I give you. (DC 18  ) [PERSUASION]  Your obsession with gold is hurting you. If you leave this place, maybe you can still be saved. (DC 18  ) [WARLOCK] [PERSUASION]  Gold is such a limited desire. With the right help, you could become so much more. (DC 18  ) [PERSUASION]  Gold, indeed - not for the toll, but for yourself . Isn't that right? (DC 21) [INTIMIDATION]  It's over. Stand down. Now . (DC 21) [DECEPTION]  Requesting more than one toll per traveller is quite illegal, per the relevant statutes. What is your defence? (DC 21) Rogues get a special dialogue path: [ROGUE] [PERSUASION]  The 'toll collector' scam is old and uninspired. Give it a rest - figure out a new trick. (DC 18  ) [DECEPTION]  Yes, a trick - you're a trickster! You don't deserve the gold! (DC 18) [PERSUASION]  Look, I've run this scam myself - I know it's a trick. A basic one at that. (DC 18) [INTIMIDATION]  I require passage - or your throat will be cut. (DC 18) Optionally, the player character can attempt to use Deception to convince Gerringothe she has been fired and replaced: [BARD] [DECEPTION]  I'm afraid I'm actually your replacement. You've been fired as toll collector - terribly sorry. (DC 18  ) [DECEPTION]  I'm here to replace you as toll collector. (DC 18) [DECEPTION]  You've been promoted! You'll collect gold from a much better tollhouse (DC 21) [PERSUASION]  You've done a great job here. Really set the standard. But I'll take it from here. (DC 21) [INTIMIDATION]  You dare to question their decision? Leave this place at once! (DC 21) If the player character is a Paladin or Druid , OR they have found and read Gerringothe's Logbook (located in the basement), they can accuse her of corruption using Intimidation : [PALADIN] [INTIMIDATION]  You're an endless pit of avarice. I won't bow to your corrupt demands. (DC 18  ) [DRUID] [INTIMIDATION]  Enough! You're an embodiment of the curse and its corruption. You get nothing from me. (DC 18  ) [INTIMIDATION]  You're corrupt. I don't take kindly to such tactics. (DC 18) [PERSUASION]  Gold, indeed - not for the toll, but for yourself . Isn't that right? (DC 21) [INTIMIDATION]  It's over. Stand down. Now . (DC 21) [DECEPTION]  Requesting more than one toll per traveller is quite illegal, per the relevant statutes. What is your defence? (DC 21) If the player character has no gold at all (because it was stashed away), all available conversation options eventually lead to a fight. Whichever approach is taken, success leads to her having a moment of clarity where she states she will "pay it back" , then she seemingly kills herself. This (relatively) peaceful resolution earns the same experience as if defeating her and all her Visage minions, as well as the full amount of gold magically bound to her. It also grants the ⁠ The Best Offence is Virtually Nonsense inspiration to party members with the Soldier background if not already earned yet. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Gerringothe Thorm/Combat Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Twist of Fortune 600 Gold dropped near her, if defeated through skill checks. Otherwise a stack of 100 drops each time a layer of her armour is removed, up to six times. If paid earlier, she also drops the amount given. If no gold was given to her, party members with the Noble background are granted the inspiration ⁠ Taxes? Never Heard of 'Em . Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] BAN LIST , Gerringothe is listed as banned from the Waning Moon distillery Gerringothe's Logbook Heavy Book , a teller is surprised when Gerringothe appreciates something besides "the cold clink of gold." Inspector's Memo Scribbled Note (Last Light Inn) , a traveller during Ketheric's Shar-following days notices something is awry Tollhouse Ledger (Reithwin) , a dwindling record of traders passing through the town Unsigned Trade Visa Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Insufficient GOLD! Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ It is unclear what degree of kinship Ketheric and Gerringothe share. While she can be presumed to be his aunt given Malus’s situation, notes and narration mention Ketheric dug up many of his ancestors’ tombs, which could mean that she is a much older relative if necromancy was practiced on her corpse as well. If the speaking party member does not have the Baldurian tag, Gethin reacts negatively and calls them an outsider. Otherwise, Gethin tells the interacting party member if the refugees give them any trouble, to come to them. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Iwan The boys ready? Gethin They're damn near chomping at the bit. What's the plan? Iwan Look for refugees travelling alone, or any stupid enough to leave camp. Iwan Remind them that this is our city - and we don't take kindly to parasites. Gethin They let in another horde of refugees this morning. When is it gonna stop? Iwan It won't. Soon the bastards will outnumber us. They'll come for our homes, our jobs - everything. Rhett Kick 'em all out! Iwan We won't need to. If we do this right, they'll run for the damn hills. Rhett Can I come on patrol with you later? Iwan Not a chance - your mother would kill me. Gethin Let the kid come. He wants to teach them refugees a lesson, right? Rhett Right! Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_Exterior_Patron_002 UUID 31d1b1ba-5d49-438a-849b-f6554bb361f9 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Gherva Minedale is a dwarven patron at the Elfsong Tavern in Act Three . “ Breaking the knees of debtors for the Guild isn't honest work, and you know it - that's why you're giving it up. „ — Gherva Minedale Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Gherva is in the Elfsong Tavern in the Lower City arguing with her brother Stug Minedale about Stug leaving The Guild to join her order of Helm called the Vigilant Knights. Her brother is finishing a job for Uktar , where he pressures the Guild’s debtors to pay what they owe, using tactics than can include breaking their knees. The party can advise him to finish the job or abandon it. If abandoned, Stug returns the payment to Uktar, who hopes he will only have one of his knees broken. Regardless of the choice, Slug decides to remain at the Elfsong Tavern with Gherva, claiming he is not yet ready to face up to what he must do. v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Technical UID S_LOW_UndercityRuins_Cultist_Sniper UUID 876c18d6-fcf3-4934-abc1-c0939872c093 Stats LOW_Chasm_Sniper Farslayer of Bhaal Ghislev , also referred to as Farslayer Ghislev , is a character who can be encountered in the Undercity Ruins area of Baldur's Gate 3 , during Act Three . “ The trial begins. Best me and pass, or die „ — Farslayer of Bhaal Ghislev Contents 1 Involvement 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Allies 2.3 Encounter details 2.4 Tactics 3 Related Quests Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Ghislev serves as part of a "test" to any characters who want to enter the Temple of Bhaal . When the party enter the area past the Undercity Ruins Waypoint a combat encounter is triggered, where Ghislev takes a very early spot in the initiative order, and applies one round of surprised to all party members. This condition can be avoided by passing a DC 30 Perception Check at approximately X: -115 Y: 958 to spot the cultists or by otherwise moving close enough to the Farslayer to begin combat with him alone. It can be prevented as well by means such as the Alert feat, the Feral Instinct feature or the effect of specific items like the Elixir of Vigilance . On Ghislev's first turn, he casts Bhaal's Power Word Kill Ritual . Ghislev gains the condition Ritual Chant: Bhaal's Power Word Kill , and applies a separate condition to all friendly party members within 55 meters of Farslayer called Bhaalist Ritual Target . Both of these conditions have a duration of seven rounds on Explorer difficulty, six rounds on Balanced difficulty and five rounds on Tactician difficulty. The chanting range area of 55 m (183 ft) of Ghislev's spell is marked with a wall of bright-red fire. This border does not stop party members from crossing it. If a party member leaves the spell's area, its countdown is stopped for them, and resumes again once they re-enter the area; it continues as that of the party members who are already affected by it. The same happens to any party member who is left behind the spell area initially and enters it later. Ghislev's ritual has the same one-cast-per-game feature as the basic Power Word Kill spell. If the party manage to survive the initial countdown of turns without killing Ghislev, they can continue fighting without risking an instant death. Many Invisible Bhaalist cultists in the area gain the condition Entranced Murderer , and attack alongside him once the party get close enough to reveal their locations. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Benign Transposition: Teleport ( ) Teleport to a nearby, unoccupied space, or swap places with an ally. Range: 9 m (30 ft) Recharge: Long rest Bhaal's Power Word Kill Ritual ( ) Begin a ritual that will end in you casting   Power Word Kill upon the next eligible target you see. Cloud of Daggers ( + ) Damage: 4~16 4d4 ⁠ Slashing Conjure a cloud of spinning daggers that attack anyone inside. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Ice Knife ( + ) Damage: 3~22 1d10 ⁠ Piercing + 2d6 ⁠ Cold Throw a shard of ice that deals 1d10 Piercing damage. It explodes and deals 2d6 Cold damage to anyone nearby. It leaves an   Ice surface. On miss, the shard of ice still explodes. This spell can be cast while you are   Silenced . DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Spear Damage: 4~9 1d6 + 3 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ray of Frost ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Cold Reduces the target's Movement Speed by 3 m / 10 ft. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Slow ( + ) Alter time around up to 6 enemies to Slow them. They won't get far, they can't do much, and they're easier to hit. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Devastator Lizabett Devastator Stropes Invoker of Bhaal Ellice Manglin' Abby Night Blade Abraxa Night Blade Comina Night Blade Corniche Night Blade Flange Night Blade Garithon Night Blade Hervyl Night Blade Maireadh Night Blade Majjo Night Blade Zeironymous Reaper of Bhaal Flo-Flo Reaper of Bhaal Gruntman Reaper of Bhaal Varneela Strangler Luke Encounter details [ edit section | visual editor ] All enemies aside from Ghislev are hiding invisibly around the arena. They join the fight if the party get close enough to them. 3x Reaper of Bhaal archers are hidden on a ledge across the chasm to the right of the party as they enter the area. 2x Devastator mages are hidden on a ledge to the left of the party as they descend. The Invoker of Bhaal is hidden directly on top of the gate to the left. Strangler Luke and 3x Night Blade archers are hidden on the roof of a ruined building to the left of the bridge. 3x Night Blade archers are hidden next to a Smokepowder Barrel on the upper floor of the ruined building to the left of the bridge. 3x Night Blade dagger throwers are hidden on the lower floor of the ruined building to the left of the bridge. Manglin' Abby is hidden by the exit on the far side of the bridge at ( X: -100 Y: 1019 ). The party members become surprised after Ghislev begins chanting his ritual. Despite the lack of a concentration indicator, the ritual spell does require concentration . Disrupting this concentration causes Ghislev to begin using regular spells against the party instead of restarting the ritual. If a party member gets close to Ghislev, he uses Benign Transposition: Teleport to teleport to the exit near Manglin' Abby. Every Night Blade archer is equipped with at least one Arrow of Roaring Thunder . All enemies leave the fight on their turn after Ghislev has been defeated and their corpses also instantly disappear upon his death. This can prevent the party from acquiring the Bonespike Gloves from Strangler Luke. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] The stone bridge across the chasm is the most dangerous location in the fight since it is very easy to be knocked off of it. Both Manglin' Abby and Strangler Luke attempt to Shove the party members off, while their ranged allies rain down Arrows of Roaring Thunder on the party. However, the bridge is not the only means of crossing the chasm. The party can also use Misty Step , Dimension Door , Grant Flight , or Arrow of Transposition to cross it and attack Ghislev directly. Knocking Ghislev prone or using the Silence spell automatically interrupts his concentration on the ritual chant spell, preventing him from completing the chant. A sufficiently upcast Magic Missile can take out Ghislav's Unstoppable charges all in one go, since each missle takes out a charge. Further, any missiles after the fifth do full damage. The Smokepowder Barrel on the upper floor of the ruined building near the bridge can be ignited with a Fireball to damage and kill the 3 archers on that floor. Ghislev has a relatively low Constitution Saving Throw, thus an effective strategy is to cast Flesh to Stone as soon as the fight starts, and he turns to stone before he can complete the chant, cancelling the spell and rendering him immobile and vulnerable. If the caster gets surprised and cannot apply the spell on the first combat round, there still is enough time to turn Ghislev to stone by successfully casting the spell on round two. A Myrmidon who is hastened can reach Ghislev in a single turn by first using Dash , then Fly to reach the Reapers' cliff, then Elemental Warp over to Ghislev's platform. If the rest of the party stays in the starting area, this prevents any further enemies joining. An Air Myrmidon in particular can then stun Ghislev with Electrified Flail , preventing him from teleporting around. invisible characters do not trigger the Farslayer or the ambush. An invisible character in turn based mode can easily dash through the whole arena and make it out the other side. There are no enemies (though there are traps) between the exit of the arena and the Temple of Bhaal Waypoint . Once the waypoint is active, the party can be reunited and continue on, skipping the encounter completely. Alternatively, all four party members can take on invisibility in turn based mode and stroll to the waypoint together. A third possibility is for an invisible character to move within range of his platform and cast Cloud of Daggers or similar area of effect damage over time spell. This will cause Ghislev to teleport immediately, without casting the spell. Careful uses of hiding allows for hit and run tactics that will kill him and none of the other denizens in the area will spawn, even when visible characters pass through the abbey or over the bridge. MOO_Cultist Adept Ghulen guards the stairs leading up to the ground floor's main hall of Moonrise Towers Prison in Act Two . “ Cover your nose by the cells. Those gnomes smell like labour . „ — Ghulen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Ghulen can be encountered in Moonrise Towers Prison , immediately after descending from the ground floor or a few steps away from the docks entrance. He stands by the stairs which lead up to the ground floor. If a party member speaks with Ghulen, he complains about the prisoners' incessant cries and screaming, as well as the smell of the gnomes. Minthara's escape [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Decide Minthara's Fate If Minthara is saved from Jasin and Sumera's torture and escorted out, Ghulen usually is the first Absolutist the party encounter upon leaving the area. If they seek to avoid conflict, he must be convinced to let Minthara go. Defending Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Nightsong is freed and the Harpers launch their assault on Moonrise Towers, Ghulen is killed during the subsequent battle in a Harper flanking attack from the docks entrance. His corpse remains next to the stairs leading up to the ground floor, exactly where he stood previously. Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayRelief_TravelerC UUID 5a5bac2c-8b34-4728-9157-09f6b82cbc98 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Giftu Hudd travelled to Baldur's Gate with two companions during Act Three . “ Thank Helm we made such good time! The army of the Absolute at your back certainly encourages a brisk pace. „ — Giftu Hudd Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Giftu Hudd arrived in the Lower City with Dryfle Doon and Hasmet Hudd . The trio fled from the Absolute and are in search of an inn. While Giftu and Dryfle are optimistic about reaching the city, Hasmet remains anxious and glum. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hasmet Hudd You do realise we can't stay here forever, don't you? Those walls might slow the army of the Absolute down, but they'll get through them sooner or later. Giftu Hudd Let's take it one day at a time, eh? You might feel differently after some food and rest. Hasmet Hudd Fools, the pair of you. Just be ready to leave when the time comes - or preferably before. Dryfle Doon Come on, old chap - I know you're hurting. But it won't bring her back, will it? Hasmet Hudd I know it won't. I just don't want to lose anyone else, all right? Giftu Hudd You won't lose us. We've come this far, haven't we? Whatever happens, we'll be right here with you. Hasmet Hudd I hope so. I really do. Giftu Hudd What's the first thing you want to do after we settle in? Dryfle Doon Sleep for a tenday. Or maybe two. Giftu Hudd Aren't you hungry? Dryfle Doon Pft, I can eat in bed. Hasmet Hudd I just hope somewhere has good dwarven beer. Don't think I'll be able to sleep without a decent drink. Dryfle Doon Look. Just look - we're finally here! We're safe. Hasmet Hudd Safe for now, at least. The army of the Absolute can't be more than a few days away. Giftu Hudd Don't be such a misery guts - we're here now, aren't we? Now they've got city walls and Steel Watchers to get through. Dryfle Doon That's the spirit! Next stop: Baldur's Gate cushiest inn! Technical UID S_CHA_Exterior_Bandit_Melee_01 UUID 538e38b9-e3a4-452a-8369-60eb1fe8c40d Stats CHA_Bandit_Gnome_Melee Eqp. EQP_Longsword_ScaleMail Trs. CHA_Exterior_Bandit_Leader Gimblebock is a gnome bandit leader who is looting the Overgrown Ruins in Act One . “ ... You're both twice as tall as me but have half the bloody backbone! „ — Gimblebock , talking to his crew Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Gimblebock is at the Chapel Entrance with Quelenna , Taman , and Warryn . Upon approach by a party member, he automatically engages them in conversation and demands that they leave. [ 2 ] The party can attack the looters or use one of several Ability Checks to convince Gimblebock and the others to leave peacefully: [ 3 ] [DARK URGE] [STRENGTH]  I don't want to hurt you, but provoke me, and I'll keep stabbing long after you're dead. (DC 5) [DARK URGE]  I am not competition. I am annihilation. (begins combat) [PERSUASION]  That ship is full of monsters. I wouldn't go near it. (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  I think that ship's an invasion force. Run while you can! (DC 12) [INTIMIDATION]  The only thing you own is your life. Leave before I take that, too. (DC 10)  (if not Astarion, a Barbarian, or a Paladin) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  MINE.  (DC 10  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Not yours - mine. Leave. Now.  (DC 10  ) [INTIMIDATION]  Just grin, baring your fangs. (DC 10  )  (Astarion only) [PALADIN] [INTIMIDATION]  Selfish cur - there might be survivors, yet you think only of loot. Leave before I make you leave. (DC 10) [MONK] [INSIGHT]  Your words hide fear, confusion. Looting that ship will bring you no peace. (DC 10) [WARLOCK]  That ship's full of poisonous vapours. Probably demonic. I'd stay away. Attack. (begins combat) If the party meet Gimblebock after exiting the crypt while using Detect Thoughts , they learn he is wondering what happened to his crew inside the crypt – though he is more concerned with whether the player character has the upper hand than his allies' lives: [ 4 ] [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read the gnome's mind. Leave, before I gut you like I gutted Mari and Barton . [DECEPTION]  You have awoken me from my slumber - now I crave your blood! (DC 12) [DECEPTION]  You have awoken me from my slumber - now I crave your blood! (DC 5)  (Astarion only) [INTIMIDATION]  It's mine now. Leave, before things get ugly. (DC 10)  (if non-Barbarian) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Mine now. Leave.  (DC 10) Attack. Resolving the situation peacefully rewards 50 XP and lays the condition to acquire ⁠ Cheese Your Way Through for characters with the Charlatan background (to obtain it the party must also trick the bandits inside the chapel to let them in). Triggering the encounter from the balcony with Warryn does not lead to any approval increase no matter which option is chosen. To gain approval, the encounter must be started from the lower area near Gimblebock and Taman. Fighting the bandits grants 70 XP and the opportunity to take all their gear. The party can also defeat the bandits after convincing them to leave, granting a total of 120 XP. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Selecting any of the "peaceful" or "scare away" options:   +1   -1   +1   +1 Choosing to attack:   +1   +1   +1   +1 Upon exiting the crypt:   +1   +1   +1   +1 Choosing to attack:   +1   +1   +1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Longsword Damage: 3~10 1d8 + 2 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Second Wind ( ) Healing: 1~10 + modifiers 1d10 + Fighter level ⁠ Healing Draw on your stamina to protect yourself. You regain 1d10 + Fighter Level ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Quelenna Taman Warryn Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Longsword Scale Mail Shovel Gold Random Gemstone Random Camp Supply Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Explore the Ruins Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Gimblebock There could be all sorts of loot in that thing - don't you want to be rich? Taman Of course I want to be rich - but not if it'll get me killed. Gimblebock You'll die a bloody pauper unless you take a few risks. Taman Why don't we just wait a while? Make sure it's safe. Gimblebock Either we act now, or someone else will pick that wreck clean and leave us nothing. Taman Haven't seen anyone but us. It's just wilderness out here. Gimblebock Hells. Pity you aren't as good at graverobbing as you are at excuses. Taman Just being careful. Like my mum always said, fools rush in. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Gimblebock can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Gimblebock Gimblebock... What is your profession? Gimblebock Thieving. Looting. Cutting throats... wherever there's gold... Do you have any valuables? Gimblebock Looking for valuables... chapel... What were you doing here? Gimblebock Looting... chapel ruins... Did you find valuables in the ruins? Gimblebock Some... but lower crypt locked... How do I get into the crypt? Gimblebock Door sealed... can't break it... can't pick it... must be something. What's inside this place? Gimblebock The others, searching... chapel ruins. Can't get into lower crypt... Do you have many people inside? Gimblebock Handful... Andorn guarding the door. The rest searching... Did you know you were breaking into a chapel dedicated to Jergal ?  (If the party successfully identify the statue in the Dank Crypt ) Gimblebock No. Doesn't matter... if his loot's good... Who was this chapel dedicated to?  (If the party fail to identify the statue in the Dank Crypt) Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Gimblebock in Early Access Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ As of Patch 1 , Gimblebock's race is simply "Gnome", without having a subrace specified (unlike his fellow bandit Warryn who is listed as a Rock Gnome). Seawind Raheni A salty breeze. Seawind Raheni Swallowed a load of water, woke up with the Flood Tide standing over me. Done. Seawind Raheni How about yours? Dark Breaker Gira Started to panic, didn't I? Took three waveservants to hold me under. Dark Breaker Gira Don't think they would've minded if I didn't wake up afterwards. Dark Breaker Gira She's just a demanding lady. But so am I. Seawind Raheni Ain't that the truth? Dark Breaker Gira Watch it, you - there's no guarantee Umberlee'll save you from a second drowning. Dark Breaker Elonia We can only hope. Seawind Raheni All right, you two - I get it. BG_Commoner_Poor Gizelle Flintsplitter is a Dwarf in the Rivington refuge camp. “ Can't stand her can't stand her can't stand her! My sister-in-law: all law and no sister. Grr! „ — Gizelle Flintsplitter on Kristeen Hazel Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Gizelle is in the refugee camp with the rest of her family: her husband Garron Flintsplitter , along with Garron's sister Kristeen Hazel and mother Ramona Flintsplitter at X: 87 Y: -88 . Technical UID S_WYR_MerchantsHouse_Thug_002 UUID e7fc87a2-2320-43fc-83b3-5c9bc2076efe Stats WYR_MerchantsHouse_Human_Barbarian Eqp. EQP_Maul Trs. BG_Bandit Gleeful Clong is a member of Zenovia's gang and member of The Guild . He is outside Arfur Gregorio's mansion in Rivington . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gleeful Clong and the rest of Zenovia's gang were paid by Arfur Gregorio only to bring him safely home, but he now demands that they also evict the refugees who are currently squatting in his mansion. Zenovia reminds him that she and her group were only paid to act as caravan guards and anything more will cost extra. If Arfur is antagonized, or the intimidation of him fails, he calls on Zenovia to remove the refugees by force. If the party intervene, a fight can break out and Gleeful Clong then becomes hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Enraged Throw ( )   –   Handaxe Damage: 5~10 1d6 + 4 ⁠ Slashing Pick up an item or creature and throw it at a target, dealing additional damage and knocking it Prone . Your Strength affects the additional damage and how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the Thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. You also deal additional damage based on your Strength . Available only when Frenzied . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Frenzied Strike ( )   –   Maul Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning As a bonus action, make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Will cause a stack of Frenzied Strain on the barbarian. Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Per turn Frenzy ( + ) Your Rage turns into a frenzy! You gain Frenzied Strike and Enraged Throw . You can also make an Improvised Melee Weapon attack as a bonus action. Deal 2 extra damage with melee and improvised weapons, and throwing. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Range: Self Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Maul Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Reckless Attack ( )   –   Maul Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning Throw all caution in the wind to gain Advantage on your melee Attack Roll . Until your next turn, you have advantage on attack rolls, but enemies also have advantage on attack rolls against you. Range: Normal weapon range Tenacity ( )   –   Maul Damage: 4 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning When you miss an attack, deal ⁠ Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier anyway (minimum of 1). Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_BaldursMouth_FF_000 UUID d25b7709-2d37-406e-be4d-a2f24390cf68 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Ranger Fist Glenvora is a human ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . “ These writers sure do have a lot to say. The amount of trees they must have cut down to print all these papers... And people complain about the Steel Watch taking up resources. „ — Glenvora Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Glenvora is watching over several employees of the Baldur's Mouth , accompanied by Fist Jerbold and a Steel Watcher . They can be found near the entrance to the building at X: -12 Y: -51 , guarding Trina , Zita , Falael , Bronte , Delcan and Jarlath , who are counting, packing and loading freshly printed issues of Baldur's Mouth Gazette . Unlike Jerbold, Glenvora harbors no illusions on the newspaper contents, plainly claiming that the Gazette only prints "lies and drivel". After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Glenvora tries to put up a good front, saying that the inactive Watcher is "experiencing a temporary reset". He joins Jaheira in the battle against the Dark Urge , should the latter choose to accept and embrace their heritage. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Temple of Bhaal [ edit section | visual editor ] Should the Dark Urge defeat Orin the Red and embrace Bhaal's gift, becoming the latter's Chosen, the Harpers set up an ambush at the entrance of the Temple of Bhaal , provided Jaheira is alive. [ 2 ] Led by Jaheira and accompanied by Minsc (if rescued), the Harpers stand guard on the bridge leading out of the temple, preventing the party from leaving. The party then have a brief exchange with Jaheira concerning the Dark Urge's role as the Chosen of Bhaal , and should Minsc be present, have the ability to psionically control him into stabbing Jaheira in the back through his Mind Flayer Tadpole . Doing so immediately kills Jaheira, and triggers combat with Minsc, Glist, and the rest of the Harpers. [WISDOM]  Ease his confusion. Try to control him.  (DC 25) Alternatively, if the Dark Urge withdraws from Minsc's mind, Jaheira can potentially convince Gale (if under 20 approval), Karlach (if under 40 approval), or Wyll (always) to turn their side, forcing the party to kill them in the ensuing fight with the Harpers. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Fog Cloud ( + ) Create a cloud of dense fog to Heavily Obscure and Blind creatures within. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Ranged Attack ( )   –   Longbow Damage: 5~12 1d8 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Wolf Companion ( ) Summon a wolf that can inflict devastating wounds and knock down enemies with its Lunging Bite . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Short rest Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira Captain Leafsong Blaird Freddo Sulian Minsc (if present) Wyll (if present) Gale (if turned) Karlach (if turned) Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Arrow of Arcane Interference Arrow of Lightning - 2x Elixir of Heroism Longbow Studded Leather Armour Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Unlike other Harpers , Glist and the nearby Harpers do not conform to their organization's brown and blue colour patterns. Instead, Glist and Blaird wear armour identical in appearance to Studded Leather Armour in green and tan colours, and a Red Carmine Mask . ↑ If Jaheira is dead but still a member of the party when the Dark Urge embraces their heritage, Glist and his companions may still be found at the gates but do not attack, and Jaheira (and Minsc, if he is a party member) is permanently removed as a companion. Me too. „ — Glourik Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Glourik appears on the second floor of Moonrise Towers. Depending on whether Ketheric Thorm is still in the throne room, she is either standing outside of Balthazar's room, or beside Radija and several Necromites guarding the door leading to the rooftop altar. After the cutscene with Ketheric and Z'rell downstairs, Z'rell is with Glourik upstairs. If Glourik is with Z'rell, approaching her triggers a dialogue in which Z'rell interrogates the party and explains that the Absolute granted her the power to 'cut the thread of life with a thought'. The following dialogue options causes Z'rell to instantly kill Glourik with her mind: Show me the power She gave you. That's a little bit abstract - show me something real. Convincing Z'rell to demonstrate her powers grants the ⁠ Know thy Clientele inspiration to party members with the Charlatan background. Otherwise, if Glourik is not killed, she moves to guard the area near Z'rell's desk. Technical UID S_UND_Myconid_BroodingSovereign UUID 82af0858-d739-4c9d-84c8-5e6760e22e46 Stats UND_Myconid_Burly_Sovereign Trs. UND_Myconid_SovereignCorpse Sovereign Glut is a Myconid and an Attached Follower . It is the sole survivor of a Duergar attack against its circle, now taking refuge at Ebonlake Grotto , a myconid colony in the Underdark . “ I am the danger, and I am the cure. they erased my people; I will erase theirs. „ — Glut Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Glut was the sovereign of a myconid circle, now displaced after duergar killed its people. Without a circle, Glut took shelter with Sovereign Spaw's in the Ebonlake Grotto. However, it holds resentment towards Spaw for not giving aid despite its pleas during the attack. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] A brooding Glut can be found just inside the western entrance to the Ebonlake Grotto . Walking close to it starts a dialogue. Recently displaced, and without a home or circle, Glut asks the party to describe their own home. Depending on race and origin , the party can answer in several ways. Afterwards, Glut shares its memory of its fellow Myconids slain by the duergar. If the party already spoke with Sovereign Spaw and accepted the quest, Glut asks to travel with the party and kill the duergar , or if they have already been slain, to see their corpses. Once they have been defeated, Glut rejoices at the sight of the dead duergar, and proclaims that it is now the "Age of Glut". It asks the party to eliminate Spaw , as there can only be one Sovereign of the Grotto. The party can aid Glut or refuse, in which case it becomes hostile and must be defeated. If Spaw is killed, Glut declarers itself "King of Kings" and takes control of the circle, beginning a new song – a chant of war. This grants the inspiration ⁠ New Management to party members with the Haunted One background. Supporting Glut in his plans for a coup and then picking either side earns another inspirational event: ⁠ Warmonger ( Charlatan background). Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Glut can reanimate creature corpses as spore servants using Animating Spores , keeping up to one spore servant at a time. High-value targets that can be re-animated include: Bulette Hook Horror Minotaur Phase Spider Matriarch - unavailable in Tactician and Honour mode: if pushing her down the central chasm - landing location is near the Minotaurs / Selûnite Outpost It is also possible to reanimate creatures that only appear in other areas by carrying their corpses into the Underdark in a character's inventory and dropping them on the ground for Glut to access. This must be done with caution, as dropping corpses can turn nearby creatures hostile. Once killed, spore servants cannot be reanimated again. They can be healed by spells and by throwing potions at them, which is particularly helpful as they spawn at partial health If it turns hostile, Glut empowers itself with Frenzied Spores , increasing its size, health, damage, and spell pool – adding Haste Spores , Timmask Spores and Bibberbang Spores to its repertoire. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Animating Spores ( ) Release spores at a corpse to animate it as a spore servant under your command. Range: 3 m (10 ft) Recharge: Per turn Fist ( ) Damage: 4~24 2d8 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 2d4 ⁠ Poison Lash out with a fungal hand. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Multiattack ( ) Damage: 12~52 2d8 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 2d4 ⁠ Poison + 2d8 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 2d4 ⁠ Poison Aim multiple attacks at a   Prone target Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Avenge Glut's Circle ⁠ Deliver Nere's Head Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Champion's Chain - reward for delivering Nere's head to Glut Winter's Clutches - reward for Avenge Glut's Circle Featherlight Boots - an Early Access item, once received as a quest reward from Glut, which is now unobtainable through normal means Ring of Fire - an Early Access item, once received as a quest reward from Glut, which is now unobtainable through normal means Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Glut does not trigger the effects of hazardous mushrooms such as Bibberbang or Torchstalk when passing near them. As such, rescuing Baelen Bonecloak as part of ⁠ Find the Mushroom Picker is a trivial task for Glut. He can be controlled directly, using the move action with the backpack and Noblestalk to transport it back to the party. [ verify ] Spore servants raised by Glut have their spellcasting blocked. However, if Death Ward is cast on them, and they are then killed, they lose the spore servant tag. They appear as ordinary attached followers (albeit ones only available when Glut is also attached) and can cast spells. There is no known way for them to long rest (and thereby recover their spell slots), but they can drink potions set on the ground, including potions of arcane cultivation. Tested on (Patch #8, Hotfix #34) [ verify ] Glut only follows the party while they remain in the Underdark. When traveling to the Campsite from an Underdark location, Glut accompanies the party, though at the camp it is not directly controllable and just wanders around. It can be re-recruited while in camp, allowing control of it and any spore servants. Should the party long rest, Glut returns to his spot in the Myconid colony. Tested on (Patch #8, Hotfix #34) Casting silence on the party and then fast traveling to the surface brings the spore servant along, but not Glut, rendering them uncontrollable. Tested on (Patch #8, Hotfix #34) If Glut dies while a spore servant is active, the spore servant persists as long as it has hit points remaining, but is no longer controllable does not follow the party. Unless harmed, it remains neutral and hangs around the area where it was when Glut died. The party can continue to use Glut as an ally after it has seen the dead Duergar by simply not talking to it. This does preclude re-recruiting it should the party leave the underdark and return. v t e Party and camp Companions Origin Astarion Gale Karlach Lae'zel Shadowheart Wyll The Dark Urge origin Non-Origin Halsin Jaheira Minsc Boo Minthara Temporary Alfira Losiir Attached Followers Armoured Owlbear Counsellor Florrick Glut Hope Omeluum Orpheus Sazza The Emperor Ulder Ravengard Us Zanner Toobin Camp Followers Permanent Owlbear Cub Scratch Withers Temporary Arnell Hallowleaf Barcus Wroot Dame Aylin Emmeline Hallowleaf Isobel Tara Ulder Ravengard Volo Yenna Grub Hirelings Brinna Brightsong Eldra Luthrinn Danton Jacelyn Kerz Kree Derryck Maddala Deadeye Sina'zith Sir Fuzzalump Varanna Sunblossom Ver'yll Wenkiir Zenith Feur'sel Personal Quests Cazador Szarr Dream Visitor Elminster Enver Gortash Mizora Oathbreaker Knight Orin the Red Quil Raphael Sceleritas Fel Viconia DeVir v t e Underdark Characters Attached Followers Glut Creatures Bulette Hook Horror Minotaur Spectator Decrepit Village Garmor Gekh Coal Holvik Lurgan Shattered Duergar Dread Hollow Baelen Bonecloak Filro Ebonlake Grotto Dead Myconid Sprout Deep Rothé Duergar Spore Servant (guard caster) Duergar Spore Servant (guard melee) Duergar Spore Servant (patrol melee) Duergar Spore Servant (ranged) Hook Horror Spore Servant Mossy Myconid Noxious Myconid Restless Myconid Spaw Thulla Xargrim Festering Cove BOOOAL Kuo-toa Kuo-toa Hunter Pooldripp Petrified Drow Arcagh Artimezt Dhourn Izwae Moy Tecothy Plants Barrelstalk Bibberbang Nightlight Timmask Torchstalk Traders Blurg Derryth Bonecloak Omeluum Other Animated Armour Bernard Dead Drow Locations Arcane Tower Decrepit Village Dread Hollow Ebonlake Grotto Festering Cove Selûnite Outpost Storehouse Quests Avenge Glut's Circle Cure the Poisoned Gnome Defeat the Duergar Intruders Deliver Nere's Head Find a Cure Find the Missing Boots Find the Mushroom Picker Find the Nightsong Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Reach Moonrise Towers

Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_DocksRoad_FF_001 UUID 8a109c28-d87a-4268-90a7-a021f42b1045 Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Ranger Fist Gneiss is a dwarven ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the streets of Lower City in Act Three. “ You trying to bribe me? If so, where's the bribe? „ — Gneiss Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Gneiss is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Pantella and a Steel Watcher . They can be found at X: -228 Y: -79 , arguing with Kolobeg , Felgi Diggums and Earno Diggums about restricted access to the Grey Harbour Docks . However, the patrol does not stop neither the party nor any other citizen and refugees from walking around them back and forth. More so, the "blocked" alley is far not the only way to reach the harbour area. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Gneiss remains at the same place, warily proposing to look into the building wreckage once the flames douse. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Steel Watch Foundry is intact [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg We can't deliver our goods to the docks? Why? Fist Pantella New rule - it's a restricted area, top security. Felgi Diggums But I can see people down there on the docks going about their business! Fist Gneiss Oh, we'll get to them soon enough. Kolobeg We've got a job to do. These goods need to get delivered. Fist Pantella And I have a duty to the city and to Lord Gortash . So halt right there. Felgi Diggums Why this sudden restriction on visiting the docks, though? Fist Gneiss Somehow, citizen, Lord Gortash forgot to tell me. Isn't that strange? Kolobeg But I made a deliver to the docks just yesterday! Fist Pantella Sorry, citizen, the docks are now a restricted area. Felgi Diggums Talk straight. Are you really just looking for a bribe? Fist Gneiss Are you looking to get stomped flat by a Steel Watcher ? If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg The foundry's a wreck! There's nothing left to guard! Can we deliver our goods to the docks now? Fist Pantella Not just yet, citizen. The whole place is a crime scene. Felgi Diggums We just need to go past the foundry to make our delivery on the wharf. Fist Gneiss Don't split hairs with me. You go no farther. Kolobeg Come on, Saer Fist, let us past - these deliveries are urgent. Fist Pantella More urgent than justice? More urgent than the rule of law? Felgi Diggums Now you're just mocking us. Fist Gneiss Heh. You've got brains, for a dwarf. Kolobeg Look, we just need to go past the foundry along the docks. Fist Pantella My orders don't admit of any exceptions. Felgi Diggums You know, if you'd just look the other way for a minute... Fist Gneiss You trying to bribe me? If so, where's the bribe? If Enver Gortash is killed [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Pantella Security's tightened since Gortash's death. You stay in your designated district. Kolobeg Aw, come on, Saer Fist, we got urgent deliveries to make. Fist Gneiss Urgent, is it? Why, you could be trying to sneak Gortash's assassins out in your cargo. I'd better search your goods. Kolobeg You're joking, right? You couldn't fit a kobold in our cargo! Silent This creature can't speak or cast spells that have a verbal component Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_Kennel_Skeleton UUID f2a457d8-f2e5-430b-9a53-85746171482f Stats LOW_CazadorPalace_Kennel_Skeleton Godey is an Undead Skeleton in the service of Cazador Szarr . “ If I had my way, I'd saw off your legs - that'd put a stop to your wandering. „ — Godey Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Godey is in the kennels of the Szarr Palace where he tortures Vampire spawn for Cazador. The kennels are on the lowest floor of the palace, just around the corner from the bottom of the stairs. The door is disguised as red and gold wallpaper in an arch on the wall. If the party fail their Perception checks , the room can still be accessed by lighting the brazier immediately north of the room (to the left of the door) at X: -1293 Y: 989 . If the party enter the kennels, Godey confronts them. If Astarion is present, Godey mocks him and reminisces on all the times he tortured him. If defeated, Godey drops a Szarr Family Ring , which can open various doors throughout the palace. Godey can be persuaded to hand over the ring willingly by passing a DC 15 Deception or Intimidation Check , followed by a DC 20 Persuasion , Deception , or Intimidation Check . Passing both checks awards 95 XP. If the party kill him afterwards, the full 210 XP can still be gained. Wyr_GurHunter Godfrey Mordels is one of the Gur , the human nomadic tribe. He is in the Gur Camp in Rivington in Act 3 . “ My people do not die in our beds. It is not our way. „ — Godfrey Mordels at the Gur Camp in Rivington Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Godfrey Mordels is in the Gur Camp attending a funeral for the fallen from a recent offence on Cazador's palace. Godfrey with his fellow Gur, all members of a group of monster hunters lead by Ulma , are looking for their children, who have been kidnapped by Cazador's spawns. The nomads have camped in Rivington, and are trying to mount a rescue or seek revenge. Ulma asks the party to help defeat Cazador and discover the fate of their abducted children. Once Cazador is defeated, Godfrey along with Ulma and the other Gur move near the waypoint in Cazador's Dungeon . He attacks the party if the ritual held in the dungeons is completed. If Astarion was turned in to Gandrel in Act One and kidnapped, then in Act Three Godfrey and all of his fellow Gur (except Gandrel) are dead. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_FakeBalthazar UUID 0a522d54-ac41-43ac-bf33-e4b3d7f85ee0 Gohumberry Tresp is a dead Human whose corpse is in the Lower City in Act Three. “ This is meant to be Balthazar - a Bhaalspawn we faced in years past. The 'artist' did not think much of him. „ — Jaheira , upon exploring the scene Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gohumberry Tresp's corpse is in the premise resembling a bathhouse adjacent to the Basilisk Gate Barracks . Gohumberry was killed by Orin the Red . His body was used as a component of Orin's "art" as an effigy to Balthazar , a monk Bhaalspawn defeated more than a century ago. He is decapitated, and his body is clad in monk-like robes. Gohumberry's corpse can be looted for one of ⁠ Dribbles' body parts and the fifth of Orin's Ritual Notes . Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find Dribbles the Clown ⁠ Investigate the Murders Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Clown's Severed Pelvis Balthazar, the Fifth Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Gohumberry Tresp's in-game model, as well as the model of Quelat Quimms (another dead human depicting Balthazar in the Undercity Ruins ), is designed to copy Balthazar's image from the previous Baldur's Gate games. Technical UID S_LOW_Golbraith UUID 86b3c253-a6ab-445b-830a-3ecaab137fff Stats LOW_Golbraith Golbraith Stredivas is a human who can be found on the first floor of his house in the Lower City . He is loosely based on a fan of Baldur's Gate 3 , who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Golbraith is a retired mind flayer hunter, and leading expert on mind flayers and counter-illithid strategies. He is currently dedicating his time to tracking those that have infiltrated the city, having passed the mantle and illithid-hunting responsibilities down to his son. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Golbraith is found on the first floor of his home, a building north of The Blushing Mermaid X: -148 Y: -60 . If the player reassures him that they know how to deal with mind flayers, he will give them a shield originally gifted to him by Abdel Adrian, Abdel's Trusted Shield . [ 3 ] However, if the party tells him "You should be out there fighting- not hiding in here!" Golbraith will lament his inability to help his son (due to his age) and demand that the party leave his house. There is also a locked chest on the first floor with some (not-detailed) correspondence between him and his son, and a book inside a chest in the heavily-trapped basement titled Confidant of a Duke , which recounts his first encounter with Abdel on the Elfsong's terrace. Golbraith's mail box also has a letter from The Lodge , asking for a consultation on illithids, and some fanmail from someone who used his techniques to best an illithid. FOR_Courier Gomwick's corpse is in the Forest , protected by his dog Scratch in Act One . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Using Speak with Dead can reveal that he was a courier delivering letters to Baldur's Gate . Until Scratch calms down, the dog does not allow Gomwick's body to be looted. It is possible to return the letters which Gomwick was carrying to Sword Coast Couriers in Act Three . There is no reward for this, but Danzo Arkwright expresses his sorrow at hearing of Gomwick's demise. North of Gomwick's corpse is a small island which allows the party to jump across the river and bypass the Blighted Village to reach the Risen Road . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Gold Leather Boots Personal Note (Gomwick) Red Apple Soft Letter Tough Letter Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Personal Note (Gomwick) Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Gomwick's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Technical UID S_LOW_HeapsideGuardTower_FlamingFist1 UUID e1cefbcf-18ce-4524-87ef-196b969fab4e Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Ranger Fist Gonfalon is a dwarven ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . “ Why don't you climb those stairs and see if the Absolute's army is at the gates? „ — Gonfalon Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gonfalon together with Gauntlet Soapstone is guarding the entrance to the Central Watch Tower in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . Gonfalon’s reaction to the player character might differ depending on the positive/negative article printed about them in the Baldur's Mouth Gazette (or neither printed at all), as an outcome for ⁠ Stop the Presses quest. Technical UID S_END_LastStandGuard_002 UUID 73c547aa-fd47-4c4d-b907-316ad0af4d21 Stats END_CityWatchMelee_Human Watchman Goodge is a member of The Watch in the Upper City in Act Three . He attempts to flee the High Hall's courtyard after it has been overrun by forces belonging to the Absolute . “ I'm not doing this for you, I'm doing this for Matthew . He was the best of us. He loved this city. „ — Goodge , to the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the initial battle for High Hall, a large force of Absolutist cultists coming from the Upper City Sewers destroys the keep and routs the City Watch away from it, forcing what remains of the Watch to flee. [ 1 ] Faced with severe casualties, the last remnants of the Watch are composed of Goodge, Ebber , Fry , Gyordi , Matthew , and Preyn . A Mind Flayer kills Matthew and Preyn as the Watchmen try to flee from High Hall, before being confronted with the party. Goodge yells Matthew's name in shock as Matthew dies. If a Mind Flayer (be it the player character, Karlach , The Emperor , or Orpheus ) is present, Goodge and the remaining Watchmen led by Gyordi are frightened of the party. Succeeding a passive DC 20 Insight Check allows for the option of having the remaining Watchmen fight at the party's side. A Mind Flayer player character can convince them to partake in the ensuing battle as allies with a DC 18 Persuasion , Intimidation , or Strength Check . A non-Mind Flayer must pass a DC 20 Persuasion , Intimidation , Deception , or Strength Check check to convince them. If the party's Mind Flayer is too far away and dialogue starts with the Watchmen oblivious to it, every class except Wizard also get either a special DC 20 Arcana , Insight , Persuasion , Intimidation , or Deception Check to convince them, or two generic DC 20 Wisdom or Persuasion Checks . If the interacting party member passes any of these checks, Gyordi rallies the rest of the Watchmen, and encourages them to fight with the party during the courtyard battle. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Greatsword Helmet Plate Armour Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Goodge and the rest of the named Watchmen have identical stats to the Watcher Guardians that can be summoned through the Gather Your Allies action The Watch . Goodge and the rest of the named Watchmen's armour is similar in appearance to the Breastplate +1 dyed in blue, brown, and black colours, rather than the plate armour specifically designed and seen on the rest of The Watch . Goodge also wears the Blackplume Helm . Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_BasiliskGate_Civilian_002 UUID 2e746867-2f83-477a-b14e-24b84ecd480a Stats Dwarf_Commoner Scribe Goosequill is in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ What did she even do? I bet nobody knows. I didn't see her do anything wrong. „ — Goosequill Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Scribe Goosequill and Baz Hopbank can be found near the entrance of Stormshore Tabernacle at X: 113 Y: -47 , vouching for Gulster Boyes , who was knocked unconscious by a Steel Watcher . Gummidge claims that Gulster is a thief and her name was on a list, but both Baz and Gulster insist that she is innocent. [ 1 ] Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Baz Hopbank Whoa, that metal monster don't look so big now.  (If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed) Scribe Goosequill The Watchers are history! Think for yourself and show some mercy. Fist Gummidge I still have my duty. Now step back, I know how to use this bow. Baz Hopbank Let her go! Lord Gortash is dead, you have no right to hold her now!  (If Gortash is dead) Fist Gummidge How does the death of Gortash change anything? Duty is duty. Baz Hopbank Yeah, but orders are orders, and whoever is in charge now must have new orders for you. Right? Baz Hopbank That thing damn near busted her skull! I didn't see her make no trouble. Scribe Goosequill I know her, that's Gulster, she's no thief! Fist Gummidge Stay back and stay calm, I'm warning you. She was on the list. Baz Hopbank Come on! At least let us take her to a doctor! Scribe Goosequill That's my friend's niece! Let her go! Fist Gummidge Back off. She goes into the clink unless Lord Gortash tells us otherwise. Technical UID S_LOW_BloomridgeGhostWatch_Civilian3 UUID baaa4da1-5d5e-49f7-9800-0f7087599185 Stats Elf_Commoner Gor Falogen is an elven civilian attempting to hunt ghosts in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I'd go home if I were you - I think the halfling in charge is the most haunted thing here. „ — Gor Falogen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Gor is on the path to the House of Grief being led by 'Suspicious' Foont on a ghost hunt with Kydden , and Gaff Garsem . Gor is highly skeptical, and very critical of Foont's ability to find ghosts. The group are completely oblivious to an entire house full of haunted spirits in Lady Jannath's Estate just behind them, if the ⁠ Free the Artist quest is active. Gor's attitude towards the party changes, depending on the outcome of the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Suspicious' Foont Gentlemen, I am quite certain that we are almost upon this most nefarious spirit! Gaff Garsem How, uh, how can you tell? 'Suspicious' Foont Can't you feel rich, unctuous gouts of necromantic energy simply coursing through the spirit field? Gaff Garsem Uh... I don't think so...? Gor Falogen That's because there's nothing here to feel. This is a colossal waste of time. Kydden I feel something! 'Suspicious' Foont Yes, my friend? What do you feel? Kydden My ears are cold! What does that mean? 'Suspicious' Foont Well, some spirits do communicate in a rather obtuse manner. 'Suspicious' Foont It could be inviting you to listen to the tale of its plight! 'Suspicious' Foont A sepulchral beckoning from beyond the veil! Gor Falogen Or his ears could just be cold. 'Suspicious' Foont Exercise caution! We do not yet know whether this spirit is malevolent or benign! Kydden Oh gods, what if it is malevolent? What if it's out to get us? 'Suspicious' Foont Worry not! I am well equipped to protect us in that eventuality. Gor Falogen You think that wand from that charlatan at Devil's Fee is going to protect us? Gor Falogen If there was anything we needed protecting from... 'Suspicious' Foont One must be prepared at all times - an unfortunate demise awaits the hasty. Kydden It's going to kill us, isn't it? Gaff Garsem You know, I'm not sure ghost hunting is for me... 'Suspicious' Foont Now, now - I'm sure it's much more scared of us than we should be of it. Kydden I've seen a real ghost snap someone in half! Kydden It squeezed their guts out of their ears like an overfilled sausage! Kydden Well, my cousin saw a real ghost snap someone in half. But they got better. Gor Falogen Well, I'm very glad they got better. 'Suspicious' Foont Hush! Too much cacophonous chatter and we'll scare away our quarry. Technical UID S_LOW_KurwinCoffin_DogGhost_03 UUID b40c5e21-4aba-4252-b8e6-219ac1764814 Stats Dog_Ghost Variant 1 UID S_LOW_KurwinCoffin_MausoleumDogCorpse_02 UUID 8945ba9c-a8d5-4bea-aac2-3e5a924424cd Stats Dog Gordis is an Undead Dog which can be found in the Durinbold Mausoleum in Baldur's Gate's Lower City . “ Fearless Gordis, who would chase any prey and helped bring in our greatest trophies. „ — Plaque adorning his sarcophagus Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] He and his two ghastly canine comrades Zina and Rocky , plus their minder, Houndmaster Pol , attack the party if their sarcophagi are disturbed with a successful DC 15 Strength Check . Sir Gorran Penghyst In-game Portrait Identity Male Voice / Actor Brian Bowles Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats HP 8 AC 10 Initiative 0 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) 10 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 0 0 0 0 0 Features Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_LOW_AngryNoble_002 UUID 24376c44-ee3e-4131-86b1-25b738aee446 Stats Human_Commoner Sir Gorran Penghyst is a human noble that can potentially be found in Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City . “ Say that again, you... you... peasant . „ — Gorran Penghyst Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gorran can only be found in the dining room if Oskar Fevras is not rescued from Brem in Act One . He can be seen arguing with Lord Delwaer Jeth about a painting Delwaer sold him, that Gorran claims is a counterfeit. Delwaer believes Gorran should have known it was a fake, while Gorran believes he should not have sold a fake in the first place. If not intervening, the pair agrees to duel and heads out to a balcony. Combat starts between the two and only ends once one of them is dead. The party can intervene to stop the duel: [INTIMIDATION]  Stop this, or I'm sticking both of your heads through that bloody painting. (DC 18)   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 [PERSUASION]  Why not just sell the fake to another gullible fool? (DC 18)   +1   +1 [OATH OF DEVOTION]  Do not sacrifice your lives on such petty grounds. They are too precious.   +1   +1 Or, the party can let the events play out [HALF-ORC]  This can't be solved with words - only blades. Fight! WIN!   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 [FIGHTER]  You are clearly novices, but I will serve as second for you both, if you wish.   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Sounds like a duel is the only answer. [OATH OF VENGEANCE]  Such actions demand retribution. It is only right you deliver it. [OATH OF VENGEANCE]  Sounds like a duel is the only answer. Or, if failing a check, can also attack them both. If Oskar Fevras is rescued, the manor is haunted and the art exhibition does not happen. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_WineFestivalCivilian005 UUID e6f2dd59-7fee-4ae7-a913-940ceef7fb52 Stats Gnome_Commoner Gorrka Bekoone is a gnome wine taster. She is at the Wine Festival at Highberry's Home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ I'm trying to enjoy a glass of wine. In peace. Thank you. „ — Gorrka Bekoone Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gorrka mingles among the patrons of the wine festival if the party began ⁠ Investigate the Murders and the wine festival takes place. After Dolor reveals himself and attempts to kill Cora Highberry , Gorrka runs off and is not seen again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Gorrka will occasionally chat with Muttonchops Oreelly and Aran Elomar . Muttonchops Oreelly Now, did I mention that I set this entire festival up myself? Aran Elomar How... fascinating. Now, I must say, this vintage is - Muttonchops Oreelly These barrels aren't light, I'll tell you that for free. Gorrka Bekoone No... I'd imagine not. Muttonchops Oreelly Are you enjoying the festival so far? Gorrka Bekoone Oh yes, it's a lovely - Muttonchops Oreelly Well, I'm glad! It really wasn't easy to set it all up myself. Aran Elomar Yes, you've made that very clear. Muttonchops Oreelly I can get you both some free wine if you'd like. Aran Elomar Really?! Gorrka Bekoone They're called free samples. We can all get some. Aran Elomar Say, if you set this up, you probably know the best wine here, right? Muttonchops Oreelly Who - me? 'Fraid not - I'm a cider man myself. Gorrka Bekoone Makes sense. Technical UID S_LOW_KurwinCoffin_BuriedMan UUID 4cb2ab0d-35f5-4168-a5dc-292bbcac597c Stats Human_Commoner Gothric Rillyn is a human who has been buried alive in a plot at the Lower City graveyard during Act 3 . “ 'Stone Lord' he calls himself. More like Stone Shite . „ — Gothric Rillyn Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] While walking in the lower city graveyard, the party can notice a pipe jutting out of the ground with a Perception check. Upon clicking on this pipe, the party can hear someone yelling from beneath the ground and the unearthed Dirt Mound becomes interactable. After digging him up, Gothric explains that he stole something from the Stone Lord and was buried in retaliation. In thanks for saving him, Gotheric lets the player loot his coffin, which contains two enchanted items ( Rapier +1 and a Magical Pike ) alongside miscellaneous cosmetics. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] No new dialogue occurs if Minsc talks alone to Gothric. Technical UID S_LOW_KurwinCoffin_KelemvorPriestess UUID 74f08242-30d7-4ad5-a0d7-36aa75b213cc Stats LOW_KelemvorPriestess Mortarch Gracie Scyre is a human cleric located in the Graveyard in Baldur's Gate 3 . She is a devotee of Kelemvor and manages the graveyard. “ Breath it in - the damp. The decay. The smell is sweeter than roses - for death is a gift worth cherishing. „ — Gracie Scyre Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Gracie Scyre can be found patrolling the graveyard to prevent anyone from disturbing the dead. If attempting to steal from or dig up the graves, she stops the party and loses attitude . She also reacts to other things which the party do in the graveyard: If teaching Nina Dortmell how to revive her deceased brother, she joins the party in combat to defeat Garret Dortmell and the other undead. Afterwards she scolds the party and asks them to leave. Alternatively, if convincing Nina to give up on reviving her brother, she praises the party. She can also be told about Nina, after which she herself convinces Nina to give up on reviving her brother. She offers Nina to help her through the mourning process each night. Afterwards, she thanks the party for alerting her. If digging up Bugthimble , she joins the party in combat against him and his fellow Kobolds. Afterwards she thanks the party for their help. If persuading Ulkov Sully to make a coffin for Anita and Elias Fischer , she praises the party for their kindness. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursGate_FlamingFist_Melee_002 UUID 7fbbdc48-5a94-4fc3-bf75-2bc9427d53b9 Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Melee_Attacker Fist Granitdatter is a dwarven fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ I'm here to watch the line, not vice versa - you can look for entertainment elsewhere. „ — Granitdatter Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Granitdatter is standing watch on the far end of the bridge at the Upper City Gate Checkpoint . She watches over the queue of residents trying to make their way into the Upper City . Having received orders to not let anyone into the Upper City, Granitdatter and her fellows: Fist Healer Darbonna and Fist 'Deadeye' Mibbs , are trying to keep the queue orderly and prevent anyone from entering. If spoken to, Granitdatter, just as most other guards in the cordon, takes the player character for a citizen who tries to make their way through the gate ahead of the queue and looks very annoyed with this. If the party return to the city after acquiring all Netherstones , three infected refugees near the queue transform into Mind Flayers and attack the bypassers. Granitdatter is Surprised , but fights alongside the party. Once the Mind Flayers are dead, she and all the Fists around run away to warn their superiors, before completely vanishing from the game once far enough. Technical UID S_LOW_Guildhall_Zhent_Mercenary_004 UUID 6e6853b1-b422-4c18-b08b-e4c3a96b3b0e Stats LOW_Guildhall_GravediggerKarcen Gravedigger Karcen is a human fighter and Zhentarim mercenary that can be found in the Guildhall , during Act Three . He guards and patrols the southern half of the Guildhall in the event of a possible Stone Lord attack. Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Protecting the Guildhall 1.2 Battle for the Guildhall 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 3 Loot 4 Related quests 5 Idle banter 6 Notes 7 References Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Protecting the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] Karcen can be seen patrolling the southern and southwestern half of the Guildhall , as well as the central pit. Him and the rest of the Zhents in the Guildhall having been hired by Nine-Fingers Keene in order to deter and resist any future Stone Lord intrusions, he nevertheless makes his displeasure for the boring posting known to the party and that he'd prefer it if they attacked the Harpers instead. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] If Jaheira is in the party and rebukes him, Karcen will be intimidated and uncertain, not realizing that Jaheira was one until she spoke up. [ 3 ] On his patrol route, Karcen will often stop by Carlorina the Wolf , scheming and telling her to be sharp and to be ready for a signal. [ 4 ] Battle for the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] When Roah Moonglow , Boss Friol , or Trinoda attempts to take over the Guildhall, Karcen will join the fight alongside his Zhentarim allies against the Guild on the south-western side, facing against Lady Flux . Siding against the Zhentarim will end in Karcen's demise, or in his disappearance if he's knocked out. Provided the party aids the Zhentarim win the battle, and he survives the fight in Guildhall, Karcen will stand at the door leading into the guildmaster's office. Talking with him afterwards will have him mention that he'd actually like to stay here, and will request a posting in the Guildhall as there is good money to be made. [ 5 ] If either Fishbait Arno or Slick Inatra perished during the battle in the Guildhall, Gravedigger Karcen can take their place and be summoned with Gather Your Allies variant Black Fist Enforcers , if the party completed Aid the Underduke and sided with the Zhentarim . Carlorina the Wolf Any news, 'Digger? Gravedigger Karcen No. Watch for the signal . Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Carlorina the Wolf and Gravedigger Karcen are seemingly meant to be on alert for an unexplained signal, potentially the one to turn on the Guild , even though their local leader Slick Inatra seem to be unaware. If sided with, Gravedigger Karcen is one of the most powerful Zhents during the battle, and is the Zhentarim' biggest damage-dealer. However, his damage is off-set as he usually battles Lady Flux , whose Rage: Wolf Heart diminishes his slashing damage. Unlike most Fighter NPCs in the game, Gravedigger Karcen doesn't rely on the NPC variants of Superiority Die attacks that allow them to use their Manoeuvres once per round without needing or expending a Superiority Die. Instead, he uses the player variant that allows him to use Manoeuvres as much as he wants, at the cost of Superiority Die resources. Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_Servant_004 UUID 2776a0f5-def2-4714-a830-6561cc96eb53 Stats HalfElf_Rogue Greenfern is a Wood Half-Elf servant of the Szarr Palace in Baldur's Gate . “ I must be busy. Busy busy busy. Master might see me! Master might approve! „ — Greenfern Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Greenfern wanders back and forth the corridor in the lower part of the Szarr Palace, one that divides the Kennels and the spawn dormitories. From time to time he rubs and cleans walls and pieces of furniture around. If spoken to, he behaves as if thoroughly brainwashed, not even paying much attention to who he is talking to. The player character can ask Astarion (if he is in the party) about Greenfern and other servants in the palace, particularly about their strange behaviour. Astarion describes them all as "fanatics, here of their own free will and utterly devoted to Cazador <...>, idiots who brought this on themselves" [ 1 ] . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] If entering combat with the residents of the palace, Greenfern joins them against the party. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneak Attack (Melee) ( ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Weapon Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. You shall bring us true children of the Gate into the light! Muttonchops Dorryss Lightbringer Gortash! Grent Grintly Crush our enemies without mercy! Phyria Gollus Hail Lord Gortash! Hail the Steel Watch ! Augur Harxkellan Submit to Lord Gortash! Submission is salvation! Only Lord Gortash can protect us from the world-ending monstrosity of the Absolute!
