EQ_Halsin Variant 1 UID S_GLO_Halsin UUID 7628bc0e-52b8-42a7-856a-13a6fd413323 Stats DEN_Archdruid_Boss Halsin is a recruitable Companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. He is a wood elf and a Circle of the Moon Druid with the Outlander background. Halsin can first be found in the Shattered Sanctum during Act One as an attached follower or as a camp follower . Halsin seeks to create a harmonious balance between nature and civilisation as well as find a cure for the Shadow Curse that has haunted his home for the past century. “ I'm 350 years old. Of course there have been lovers. Just because I love nature doesn't mean I'm betrothed to it... „ — Halsin , on his sex life Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Personal quest 1.4 Recruitment 1.5 Approval 1.6 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 4 Gameplay 4.1 Skills with Proficiency 4.2 Temporary companion features 4.3 Permanent companion features 5 Involvement 5.1 Act One 5.2 Act Two 5.3 Act Three 5.4 Endings 5.4.1 Alone with the Shadow Curse 5.4.2 Life as a new father 6 Speak with Dead 7 Related literature 8 Related Quests 9 Loot 9.1 Starting equipment 10 Gallery 11 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin is the Archdruid of the Emerald Grove and an accomplished healer. Before he went missing, Halsin and his apprentice Nettie were researching the recent cases of illithid tadpole infections. Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before he is recruited, Halsin can first be met in the Worg Pens of the Shattered Sanctum as a level 5 druid , wildshaped into a bear with the following ability scores : 20 STR, 10 DEX, 16 CON, 10 INT, 17 WIS, 13 CHA. If he is freed and met later in the Emerald Grove , his ability scores are: 16 STR, 11 DEX, 14 CON, 10 INT, 17 WIS, 13 CHA. If he is recruited in Act Two , Halsin reverts to a level 1 druid with the standard ability scores for that class . His subclass is Circle of the Moon , specialised in wildshaping into various creatures to attack enemies or support allies in combat. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin does not have a Companion Quest . He is, however, deeply tied to ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse , and it cannot be successfully completed without his assistance. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] To recruit Halsin, the quests ⁠ Defeat the Goblins , ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin , and ⁠ Save the First Druid must be completed with him alive, and he must agree to join the party as they travel to the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Halsin can be recruited in Act Two after the party progress in the quest to lift the Shadow Curse to a certain point. However, if they proceed to Act Three without fully completing the quest, Halsin stays behind in the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Recruiting Halsin grants the ⁠ Patrician of the Grove inspiration to party members with the Noble background. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin Approves Main article: Halsin/Approval Halsin only gains or loses approval once he joins the party as a full companion. He likes those who are kind, especially to animals or children, and dislikes any decisions that involve harming the natural world or supporting corruption and cruelty. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Halsin/Romance Halsin can be romanced . Though the majority of his romance occurs in Act Three , he can be flirted with in prior Acts. He is polyamorous and is the only companion who may be romanced in later stages alongside Astarion , Shadowheart , or Karlach – with their consent. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] As a wood elf, Halsin stands out among his people, having an unusually tall and heavy athletic build. His chest and shoulders are broad, and his body thick with muscle, yet he retains a relaxed but ready stance. He has a deep, even voice and typically keeps a calm demeanour as reflected by his undisturbed face. He has warm two-toned eyes, gray with a touch of brown, along with a square jaw, straight nose, high cheekbones, and long, pointed ears. He has large calloused hands and sun-browned skin, marked by a few pale scars along the arms and ribs. He has chestnut brown hair, worn long and usually tied back, with a few loose strands at the temples. His movements are unhurried and balanced, the stride of someone used to long days in the wild. Despite (and perhaps because of) these traits, his presence typically feels steady and protective rather than aggressive. With all of these qualities, Halsin is generally found quite attractive and handsome and, like many who are so desired, has had his share of trials as a result. At camp, he favours simple leathers and a green cloak with a fur-lined collar, worn over a shoulder harness and bracers. Oak leaf clasps, a druidic torc, and a bear claw charm finish the look. When travelling, he switches to sturdier druid leathers in forest shades with leaf and root motifs, tall boots, and practical belts for pouches and tools, all of which add to his imposing outdoorsman presence. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Despite his tenacity in combat, Halsin is a gentle, honest elf who treasures the sanctity and beauty of nature. Despite being a powerful healer with a lofty title, Halsin is humble and patient – though he is willing to act with force if the need arises. One of Halsin's core beliefs is that desire should flourish wherever it finds purchase. He views carnal pleasures as a natural calling and monogamy, while something to be cherished, as something which suits others more so than himself. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Many years ago, when Halsin was younger and far more foolhardy than he is now, he ventured to the Underdark to experience the beauty of its unworldly flora. Instead, he found himself captured by a noble Drow house – in his words, "something between guest, prisoner, and consort". The house's matron and patron took an interest in him, seeing a bristling, well-formed wood elf from the surface as quite the novelty, and he spent nearly three years chained in their bedchamber. Halsin did what was necessary to survive the experience, though he does not look negatively upon it, because while he feared for his life, he is proud he was able and willing to wait for the chance to regain his freedom. That chance came when his captors' rivals attacked, as Lolth's noble houses are constantly at each other's throats. While the drow were distracted by the battle, he escaped, though he never learned what became of his 'hosts'. One hundred years before the events of the game, Halsin was part of the Emerald Grove's forces in the attack against Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers . However, shortly after Ketheric's body was interred within the Grand Mausoleum , the shadow curse took hold. In the chaos that followed, Halsin lost contact with Thaniel , his childhood friend and the living spirit of the land. Worse still, the Archdruid of the Emerald Grove was lost to the curse, leaving Halsin to take command and lead the survivors to safety. Gameplay [ edit section | visual editor ] For full information on Halsin's starting features, see Druid and Elf . As a druid, Halsin is capable of filling a variety of roles in the party. He can debilitate enemies with control spells, support the party with spells that enhance himself and his allies, and deal damage with elemental damage-dealing spells. His Wild Shape feature allows him to wade into battle as a melee combatant or sneak and scout as a small animal. Skills with Proficiency [ edit section | visual editor ] Animal Handling Nature Perception Stealth Survival Temporary companion features [ edit section | visual editor ] As a temporary companion, he knows the following spells: Call Lightning Healing Word Misty Step Thunderwave Wild Shape: Cave Bear Permanent companion features [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin always has Wild Shape: Cave Bear , which can be used by a non-druid Halsin by equipping the Shapeshifter Hat for the Wild Shape Charge . If Halsin has no 2nd-level spell slots, Lunar Mend can be cast at 1st level without expending a spell slot. Halsin also always has the Healing Word and Thunderwave spells prepared, even if he is not a spellcaster. As long as he has no 2nd-level spell slots (including warlock spell slots and spell slots from an Elixir of Arcane Cultivation ), these spells are free to cast. For example, if Halsin is a level 12 monk, a barbarian 10/druid 2, or an Arcane Trickster 6/Battle Master 4/warlock 2, he can cast these two spells for free. As soon as Halsin gets a 2nd-level spell slot, the spells consume spell slots normally. At druid level 3, Halsin gets Misty Step always prepared; this spell is free of cost as long as he has no 3rd-level spell slots. This means that Halsin as a druid 3/paladin 2 can use Misty Step for free, but he does not have it for free as a druid 3/wizard 2. Finally, Halsin has Call Lightning always prepared at druid level 5. Similarly, the spell has no cost as long as he does not have 4th-level spell slots. When respeccing and levelling up Halsin, his innate spells may need to be added to his hotbar from his spellbook. When casting these spells with without spell slots, they are always cast at their base level. When cast with spell slots, they can be upcast as normal. These four spells are considered 'granted' spells, so they use Halsin's current spellcasting ability at the time he receives them. Halsin loses access to these spells when he changes form, including using Wild Shape and Disguise Self , though not Starry Form . When Halsin returns to his normal form, all these spells are re-granted, which causes all of Halsin's granted spells to change to the spellcasting ability of the most recently acquired class (See Item spellcasting ability for a detailed explanation). Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin joined Aradin's ill-fated expedition to find the Nightsong , hoping to find a way to reach Moonrise Towers and the Shadow-Cursed Lands . However, he was captured and can be saved by the party; he is imprisoned in the Worg Pens within the Shattered Sanctum , and is being harassed by nearby goblins, who throw stones at him while he remains in wildshape . When his cage is approached, a dialogue cutscene is triggered. The goblins Three , One and Brawler Birka harass the wildshaped Halsin, thinking he is just a bear, and plan to kill him to feed the worgs . If a party member has Speak with Animals active, they can speak to the 'bear', who will ask for help. Various outcomes are possible: The party can join the harassment and throw a stone at him, in which case he breaks free of the pen, instantly kills Birka, and attacks the goblins and the party. The goblins then are allied with the party in this fight. The goblins can be urged to stop their harassment, but they refuse, and as in the previous case, Halsin breaks free and instantly kills Birka. In the fight that breaks out, Halsin is allied with the party against the goblins. A party member can use the Illithid Persuasion to order the goblins to stop and release the bear. The pen is unlocked, and Halsin immediately moves to kill the goblins. The party can chose to join him and attack the goblins, attack him and join the goblins, or leave him at the mercy of the goblins, which counts as allying with the goblins. If the party ally with him, Halsin offers to help in seeking a cure for their tadpole problem, but first asks them to ⁠ defeat the goblin leaders to protect the Grove. While he can join the party as a temporary companion at this point, he attacks the rest of the goblins on sight, so if discretion is preferred, he can be asked to wait in the Worg Pens. If the party kill the goblin leaders before they enter the Worg Pens for the first time, Halsin may break out by himself and return to the Emerald Grove. If Halsin is killed, ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin can be progressed by using Speak with Dead on his corpse. After the goblin leaders are defeated, Halsin returns to the Emerald Grove , where he confronts Kagha based on the party's choices when they ⁠ investigate her actions . The morning following the tiefling's celebration , Halsin tells the party about the two leads he has on how to reach the Shadow-Cursed Lands: travelling through the Mountain Pass , which would be less dangerous at first but would mean a longer journey through the shadow curse, or exploring the Underdark in search of an alternative route, which would bypass some of the shadow curse but comes with all the dangers inherent there. Regardless of which option the player character suggests exploring, Halsin accompanies the party as a Camp Follower in the hopes of travelling to the Shadow-Cursed Lands and lifting the Shadow Curse afflicting the region. If the party proceed to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before rescuing Halsin from the Goblin Camp , his dead body remains in his cell. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin provides vital assistance in the process of lifting the Shadow Curse , and it cannot be completed if he dies. He asks that the party keep an eye out for any information regarding a boy called Thaniel , who is in fact the land's spirit. Once Halsin is given a lead to Thaniel's location by Art Cullagh (whether through waking him or using Speak with Dead on his corpse), he performs a ritual to open a portal to the Shadowfell and leaves to retrieve the boy. If the party fail to protect the portal from the waves of shadow-cursed creatures, it closes, and Halsin is lost to the Shadowfell forever. If Thaniel is successfully rescued from the Shadowfell and Thaniel's other half, Oliver , is also convinced to reunite with him, Halsin offers to join the party for the remainder of Act Two. He becomes a permanent companion if Ketheric Thorm is defeated and the Shadow Curse is lifted upon leaving the Shadow-Cursed Lands. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin has no direct involvement in any Act Three storyline, though taking him out of the Lower City campsite and speaking with him has him express fear that balancing nature and civilisation may not even be possible. He is also one of two companions (alongside Astarion ) who can have a foursome at Sharess' Caress without having been romanced, and he tells the player character about his experience with the noble drow after participating. Lastly, he is added to ⁠ Gather Your Allies , harnessing Thaniel's strength to provide the Spirit of the Land condition once the party reaches the Upper City . Halsin is also one of Orin's potential abduction targets . If Lae'zel is dead, romanced, or in the active party upon first long resting in the Lower City , Orin instead captures Halsin and infiltrates the camp disguised as him, pretending to have gone mad and almost killed Scratch . Depending on how this scenario is resolved, he either gets killed by Orin before the player character's battle with her or returns to the party afterwards. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] Alone with the Shadow Curse [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party fail or neglect to complete ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse , Halsin stays in the Shadow-Cursed Lands and continues studying the curse on his own. He sees the player character off at the Road to Baldur's Gate , but he is never seen again in Act Three . If the player character recruits Halsin by freeing Thaniel but does not reunite Thaniel with Oliver, Halsin still permanently leaves the party, taking whatever equipment he is currently wearing with him. Life as a new father [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin during the epilogue Otherwise, if the party lift the Shadow Curse and Halsin is not killed by Orin, he returns to Reithwin Town after defeating the Netherbrain to help the former Shadow-Cursed Lands continue healing. He keeps in touch with Thaniel and Oliver, resumes his hobby of whittling, and converts Moonrise Towers into an orphanage, where he adopts and raises nine wagons of children who were orphaned by the Shadow Curse and the Absolute. When spoken to at the Epilogue reunion celebration, he asks the player character for bedtime story ideas and gifts them a Whittled Duck ; the player character can ask him to take the Owlbear Cub in return as a pet for the children. If the player character romanced Halsin, they can offer to move in with him and help with the children, and at the reunion party, he asks if they are comfortable having settled down after adventuring for so long. If the player character also partnered with Astarion or Shadowheart , they maintain a long-distance relationship with whichever partner they did not stay with. If the player character also partnered with Karlach , however, they cannot stay with Halsin unless she dies. If the player character instead went to Avernus with Karlach (as a friend or as a second partner), they can apologise to Halsin at the reunion party for leaving so abruptly, but he forgives them and says he will always be there when they get back. The player character can respond by embracing and kissing him or by amicably thanking him; either way, Halsin then shares about his new life as he would if not romanced. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . The dialogue varies depending on whether he was abducted and killed by Orin or not, as well as on how far the story has advanced when he is killed: Who are you? Halsin Halsin... First Druid... What happened to you?  (Act 1 only) Halsin Captured... goblins... drow... killed... What can you tell me about ceremorphosis? Halsin Altered... arrested... unnatural magic... Magic? What magic? Halsin Someone controls the parasites... controls the cultists... Who controls the parasites? Halsin Unknown... powerful magic... Moonrise Towers... Moonrise Towers? How do I get there? Halsin Follow Chionthar... but beware... danger ahead... darkness... Darkness? What do you mean? Halsin Curse... made of shadow... all succumb to it... find another way... Halsin Secret tunnel... entrance hidden... Selûne temple... Where are your valuables? Halsin Study... hidden... Emerald Grove... If Halsin was abducted and killed by Orin: Who are you? Halsin Halsin... First Druid... surely you knew that by now...? How did you end up here? Halsin Orin... abducted me from camp... so strong... How did you meet your end? Halsin Orin's blades. Halsin I hoped my loved would save me...  (if romanced) Halsin I hoped my friends would save me...  (if not romanced) What was your purpose? Halsin Stop the Netherbrain. Help my friends... as they helped me. Do you have any regrets? Halsin Thaniel and Oliver... I never said goodbye. Never saw their land flourish... Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Druid Note Halsin's Journal, Vol I Halsin's Journal, Vol II Hastily Written Note (Druids Grove) Letter from Halsin Logbook XII: 1371 Notes on Drow Parasite Rancid Note Scribbled Note (Druid Grove) Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Defeat the Goblins ⁠ Gather Your Allies ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse ⁠ Rescue Orin's Victim ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin ⁠ Save the First Druid ⁠ Wake Art Cullagh Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Starting equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Alchemy Pouch Camp Supply Sack Druidic Bracers Druid Quarterstaff Halsin's Druid Leather Armour Halsin's Grove Garments Halsin's Tasteful Boots Halsin's Underwear Grovetender Boots Potion of Healing – 2x Scroll of Revivify Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin's camp model Halsin's underwear model Early Access model (different tattoo) Epilogue model Bear wildshape model Steam Trading Card Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin was not originally slated to be a companion, but due to his popularity among fans, Larian Studios decided to add him as one. Halsin did not obtain his large facial scar in battle, but rather was marked by a she-bear encountered while in wildshape during mating season, who attacked after being rejected. This can be brought up as his greatest failure during the Test Your Love game with Zethino , though he will be disappointed and scold that "Rejecting unwanted advances is no failure, even if it earned me some scars." Halsin is noted to be much larger than normal for a wood elf, and speculates he may have some orc in his family tree. Halsin's surname is Silverbough according to his main writer John Corcoran : "While there’s nothing in the game itself, an earlier character outline stated it was Silverbough. This is probably semi-canon at best as there’s nothing supporting or contradicting it in the game." He goes on to note: "I do still like it as it alludes to an aspect of Celtic mythology that has nice thematic resonance for Halsin and Thaniel (the silver bough or branch granting access to the land of eternal youth)." ( Twitter/X post from November 30, 2023 and the subsequent post ) There is a cut out camp scene in which Halsin demands Minthara to be kicked out of the party, despite knowing this would result in her being enthralled by The Absolute , as she would no longer be protected by the Mysterious Artefact . The scene is scripted, animated, and voiced, but left out of the game. If the player character chose to let Minthara stay, Halsin would say he will remain until the Shadow Curse is dealt with. EQP_Longsword_ScaleMail Trs. HAV_Survivor Harper Hangfar is a Harper who patrols the northern side of Last Light Inn during Act Two . “ You look well-equipped. Good. You wouldn't believe the state of some of these lads. „ — Hangfar Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Hangfar is at the Last Light Inn, where he patrols the same northern side route of the docks area as Naysa . Speaking with Hangfar reveals that he thinks some Harpers at the inn are under-equipped. [ 1 ] Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Hangfar usually fails his saving throw and is Impaled for the remainder of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, Hangfar and everyone in Last Light Inn turn into a Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira . If Marcus is defeated, talking with Hangfar after the battle lets him mention to the party that he played cards with Marcus, and thought they were friends. [ 2 ] Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Hangfar follows Jaheira to Moonrise Towers . However, Hangfar is killed during the fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. His corpse is in Moonrise nestled in a nook between a wall and the staircase leading down from the entrance. He's found at the party site during the Epilogue Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Happy was caught stealing from the battlesite of the Battle for Baldur's Gate by Minsc . Minsc held him over the edge of High Hall for over 2 hours, until they both were transported to Withers' party. When initially speaking to Happy, conversation begins with Minsc instead. Minsc berates Happy for being a scoundrel who does not deserve to be in the presence of so many heroes. Still, the Rashemaan believes Happy could make better of himself, but ultimately it is up to Boo whether he lives or dies. When spoken to again, Happy quivers in fear of Boo.

Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_GithyankiShield_Paladin UUID 54467aa9-33dd-41c4-bd77-87a71ed22c16 Stats LOW_Githyanki_Paladin Eqp. LOW_GithyankiShield_Paladin Ch'r'ai Har'rak is a githyanki paladin [ 1 ] in Knights of the Shield Hideout in Act Three . She has been sent by Vlaakith to learn more about the mysterious Emperor . “ Your story ends here. We will reclaim the Astral Prism, purge it of the illithid interloper, and restore it to our queen. „ — Har'rak Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If a party member approaches her without Lae'zel, Har'rak accuses them of being the Emperor's puppets. She reveals that the Githyanki have been tracking the Emperor ever since it escaped with the Astral Prism and are well aware it is hiding inside. The interacting party member can attempt to reveal the presence of Orpheus , over the objections of the Emperor, but Har'rak says she already knows and desires glory for recapturing the "Traitor Prince". At this point, nothing the party says dissuades Har'rak and she attacks. If Lae'zel is present then a unique alternate dialogue plays out. Har'rak addresses Lae'zel instead of the player character and revels in the imagined rewards Vlaakith will give for delivering "the false heir's head" . Depending on her choices within the main story, Lae'zel either defends Orpheus or claims that she will be the one to deliver the prism to Vlaakith. Har'rak then turns her focus to the player character and threatens to annihilate them until nothing is left but "meat and bone". At this point, two options appear: [INTIMIDATION]  Strike me and die, a failed warrior forgotten by your people. (DC 18)   +5 [PERSUASION]  Vlaakith entrusted Lae'zel with the Prism. Interfere, and the queen's sure to punish you. (DC 18)   +5 [ 2 ] On a successful roll, Har'rak backs down and reveals her jealousy that a young warrior like Lae'zel could come so far despite the fact that she herself has served Vlaakith for a thousand years. She then leaves with her retinue, skipping the battle entirely. On a failed roll, Har'rak attacks the party instead. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] In combat, Har'rak functions as an Oath of Conquest paladin . Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Astral Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Conquering Presence ( + ) Exude a terrifying presence that   Frightens nearby enemies. WIS Save Range: Self Githborn: Flying Boots ( )   –   Boots of Psionic Movement Bestow the ability to   Fly upon yourself. Recharge: Long rest Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Githyanki Greatsword (Psionic) Damage Normal weapon damage Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Misty Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Long rest Wrathful Smite ( + + ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Psychic Your weapon absorbs your wrath as you strike, possibly Frightening your target. WIS Save Range: Normal weapon range Honour Mode [ edit section | visual editor ] Legendary Action: Tu'narath's Embrace Once per round, Ch'r'ai Har'rak can spend a Legendary Action to cast Tu'narath's Embrace on an ally to prevent an Incapacitating Condition . Tu'narath's Embrace Protect an ally that is targeted by an incapacitating condition [ See Notes ] with an Embrace that also grants 50 temporary hit points . Recharge: Per turn Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Gate Master Ri'zel Gate Master Zyrlak Veteran Gish Ghush'ins Veteran Gish Zhendila Veteran Raider Ly'iss Additional Veteran Warriors and Veteran Raiders each turn as long as the Astral Rifts remain open: Raider Kharyk Raider Zeddi'in Raider Zerentha Warrior Dor'il Warrior Ma'aryk Warrior Ni'ima Encounter details [ edit section | visual editor ] Ri'zel and Zyrlak are holding open Astral Rifts that allow more Githyanki to enter the fight. Each round, one of the two summons a new Veteran Warrior or Veteran Raider . This ability can only be used every other turn but they take turns doing it so that a new Githyanki is summoned each turn. The rifts disappear when they are defeated or lose concentration on the spell. Har'rak will be accompanied by W'wargaz and Tska'an if they were not killed in the previous Acts of the game. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] As previously noted, this fight can be skipped by bringing Lae'zel in the party and passing the DC 18 Intimidation Check . Enhance Ability and Guidance can help the player character beat this check. If the party engages Har'rak in battle then it is important to kill the two Gate Masters as soon as possible. Otherwise they will slowly flood the battlefield with reinforcements and make the fight more difficult. Calm Emotions can help counter Har'rak's Conquering Presence ability. Dwarven Resilience Advantage on saving throws against being poisoned and resistance to poison damage. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_LOW_GossipingServant_001 UUID 32024a4d-f4c4-4d6f-9032-7bf58fe28e90 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Hargin Jooli is a dwarven servant to Lady Jannath who can potentially be found in Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City . “ If you're hungry, go to the kitchen. I'm on a break. „ — Hargin Jooli Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Hargin can only be found in the kitchen storage of Lady Jannath's Estate if Oskar Fevras is not rescued from Brem in Act One . He can be seen gossiping with 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla . If Oskar Fevras is rescued, the manor is haunted and Hargin is sent away on a temporary leave of absence at the request of Chamberlain Mercer . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hargin occasionally chats with Cyrilla: Hargin Jooli How much you reckon Lady Jannath'll make out of those nobles upstairs? 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Oh, I don't know. More than I can count on my fingers, that's for sure. Hargin Jooli Surprised she's not showing the big one, though. That'd fetch a pretty penny. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla It was Master Oskar's favourite. She'll never sell that one. Hargin Jooli She should cut her losses. He ain't never coming back. Hargin Jooli You met that hoity-toity woman upstairs? She kept whinging that her wine tasted funny... 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla No you didn't... did you? Go on, tell me what you did. Hargin Jooli Let's just say it had more in it than a few grapes. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Oh, you're filthy. I bet she still drank every drop. Hargin Jooli Still think Lady Jannath'll make you a lady's maid? 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Oh, I've given up. I've scrubbed, I've washed, I've polished - all for nothing. She doesn't notice me. Hargin Jooli I think you'd make a great lady's maid. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Stop. You're making me blush. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla How's life in the kitchens? Hargin Jooli Piece of cake. I just turn up and chop what I'm told to chop. 'Loose Lips' Cyrilla Like being back in the Guildhall, eh? Hargin Jooli Don't know what you're talking about. Technical UID S_LOW_BramptonOrphan_Civilian1 UUID 0ad943fa-51be-4141-83c5-feca43e8a62a Stats Human_Commoner Hari Nodles is a human civilian. He is attempting to comfort Fevrokis after he found the bodies of his dead parents in the Brampton district of the Lower City in Act Three . “ Some people truly have the blackest hearts. Poor mite. „ — Hari Nodles Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Hari Nodles is beneath an arch near Felogyr's Fireworks with Fevrokis and Phelgro Dorph . They are trying to console the tiefling child, who is standing next to his parents' corpses. Hari wants to assume responsibility and help Fevrokis while Phelgro is afraid of the repercussions. Hari considers temporarily adopting Fevrokis until they can find permanent accommodation. Phelgro suggests bringing him to the Flaming Fist , but Hari believes that the Fists will hold them responsible for the death of Fevrokis' parents. Instead, Hari suggests bringing the child to the Guild , but Phelgro believes the Guild is too busy with city matters to help them. With no other options, Hari attempts to soothe Fevrokis by offering to find someone to "help" his parents and then get him something to eat. The attitude of Hari Nodles towards the party changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fevrokis Mummy? Daddy? Please get up. Please! Hari Nodles Hey, hey - shh, all right? Look at me - it's gonna be okay. Phelgro Dorph Shit. We need to tell the Flaming Fist - get this kid some help. Hari Nodles And have them lock us up for two murders we didn't do? Hari Nodles They're too scared to come here anyway. We'd have better luck with the Guild. Phelgro Dorph Between the Steel Watch and the Stone Lord, the Guild have barely got the strength to look after their own. Fevrokis I'm scared. Why won't they get up? Why... Phelgro Dorph We can't get involved with this. Hari Nodles Don't listen to him, kid - we've got you. Hari Nodles Can you tell us what happened? Fevrokis I-I got lost. I was following a kitty. Fevrokis When I found them again - when I came back - they were lying here... Hari Nodles Hush, now - it's all right. We're gonna help you. Phelgro Dorph Oh, we are, are we? Hari Nodles Don't be such a heartless bastard. Phelgro Dorph I'm not! I just don't wanna get in trouble, that's all! Hari Nodles Kid's gonna need a family no matter what happens. Phelgro Dorph You want to adopt it? Hari Nodles Just until he has somewhere better to go. Hari Nodles And he's not an 'it'. Fevrokis I want to go home... Hari Nodles I know you do, kid. I know. Tell you what... Hari Nodles We'll try and find someone who can help your ma and da and then we'll get you something to eat, all right? Hari Nodles And it can be anything you want. I promise. Phelgro Dorph Help them? They're dead. Hari Nodles Shut up, would you? Fevrokis O-okay. Let's do that, please. Technical UID S_END_HarperSummon001 UUID 97e7a9d6-4f11-4de9-bda2-7197d5647971 Stats END_HarperRanger_Elf Variant 1 UID S_END_HarperSummon002 UUID 7518e757-234a-4a16-899b-873c749d06ad Stats END_HarperRanger_Elf Variant 2 UID S_END_HarperSummon003 UUID 753a3cf7-4718-4715-b963-5eb6e74bfac7 Stats END_HarperRanger_Halfling Harper Archers are summonable, failsafe allies that provide ranged support in Act Three . “ We fight for the fate of the city. „ — Harper Archer 's battle cry Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Harper Archers can be summoned with the Gather Your Allies variant, Silver Harp Squadron , provided Jaheira is an ally and all previous incarnations of the Harpers are dead. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Dagger Longbow Ring Mail Armour Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Female Wood Elf model Lightfoot Halfling model Female Wood Elf portrait Lightfoot Halfling portrait Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Some members of this archetype may have slightly different passives, movement speed, weight, and size due to being members of different races. The Harper Archers wear a set of armour identical in apperance to the Ring Mail Armour +2 and Leather Helmet dyed in Harper colours, but are actually equipped with the default Ring Mail Armour . The only way to summon Harper Archers are if Naysa , Lymn and Antony die in Last Light Inn , and their replacement Grenywald , Lanni and Olys die in the Assault on Moonrise Towers . These Harper Archers are stronger than all previous incarnations of the Harper summon, as Naysa, Lymn, and Antony lack the ability to use their Extra Attack feature, and Grenywald, Lanni, and Olys are only level 6. v t e Creature Archetypes Absolutists Absolute Questioner Acolyte of the Absolute Adept of the Absolute Inquisitor of the Absolute Zealot of the Absolute Banites Black Gauntlet of Bane Fist of Bane Iron Consul of Bane Bhaalists Death's Head of Bhaal Invoker of Bhaal Night Blade Reaper of Bhaal Myrkulites Mistress of Souls Counting House Counting House Artillerist Counting House Enforcer Flaming Fist Flaming Fist Archer Flaming Fist Guisarmier Flaming Fist Healer Flaming Fist Protector Flaming Fist Wizard Gather Your Allies Gur Hunter Sharpshooter Gur Hunter Warrior (Handaxe) Gur Hunter Warrior (Scimitar) Harper Archer Hellrider Cleric Hellrider Paladin Ironhand Grenadier Watcher Guardian Githyanki Ardent Gish Gish'ra (caster) Gish'ra (melee) Raider Veteran Gish Veteran Raider Veteran Warrior Warrior Youth Gnolls Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Redcaps Redcap Boatswain Redcap Mystic Cannoneer Goblins Goblin Booyahg Goblin Boss Goblin Brawler Goblin Devout Goblin Sapper Goblin Sharp-Eye Goblin Tracker Goblin Warlock Goblin Warrior Sharrans Justiciar Crusader Sharran Fidelian Sharran Novice Sharran Sentry Umberlants Dark Breaker Savage Seawind Untaken

Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursGate_FlamingFist_Caster_001 UUID 02a89b77-07fe-4cc2-90d6-a7d5102f4cf7 Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Caster Fist Wizard Hartlebury is a dwarven wizard and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ Don't try and sweet talk me - I've heard it all before. Get in line. „ — Hartlebury Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Hartlebury [ 1 ] is standing watch on the bridge at the Upper City Gate Checkpoint . She watches over the queue of residents trying to make their way into the Upper City . Having received orders to not let anyone into the Upper City, Hartlebury and her fellows: Fist Grassley , Fist Magnolia , Fist Nudelmann and Fist Qirahe , accompanied by a Steel Watcher , are trying to keep the queue orderly and prevent anyone from entering. If spoken to, Hartlebury, just as most other guards in the cordon, takes the player character for a citizen who tries to make their way through the gate ahead of the queue. If the party return to the city after acquiring all Netherstones , three infected refugees near the queue transform into Mind Flayers and attack the bypassers. Hartlebury is Surprised , but fights alongside the party. Once the Mind Flayers are dead, she and all the Fists around run away to warn their superiors, before completely vanishing from the game once far enough. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Blight ( + ) Damage: 8~64 8d8 ⁠ Necrotic Deals 8d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage to a target. Plants take maximum damage from this spell, and have Disadvantage on the Saving Throw against it. CON Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Conjure Elemental: Fire Elemental ( + ) The fire elemental can use   Smouldering Touch ,   Erupting Cinder , and can make your foes   Burn . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Counterspell ( + ) Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Fire Bolt ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Fire Hurl a mote of fire. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Quarterstaff Damage: 1~5 1d6 - 1 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Melf's Acid Arrow ( + ) Damage: 6~24 4d4 ⁠ Acid + 2d4 ⁠ Acid Shoot a green arrow that bursts in a spray of acid. Deals ⁠ 4d4 Acid damage immediately and ⁠ 2d4 Acid damage at the end of the target's next turn. If the spell misses, the target still takes half the initial damage, but no damage at the end of its next turn. Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_HarvardWilloughby UUID 8a69560f-3a7a-4e6e-81df-eb77de816197 Stats LOW_Hardvard Harvard Willoughby is a human comedian at the Elfsong Tavern . “ Hel-LO, Baldurians! You know, I wouldn't be here tonight, except my wife ran off with a cambion. That's right, I got fiend-zoned. „ — Harvard Willoughby telling a joke Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Willoughby hosts the contest Laff Riot at the Elfsong Tavern , and is watched by his son Belford Willoughby . Laff Riot [ edit section | visual editor ] The contest can be won with these choices: Willoughby the comedian, folks! Were his jokes good, or did he just smell funny? I tried sleeping with a dragonborn the other night, but it didn’t work out – he had a reptile dysfunction. Our cleric tried to cast Healing Word on a ham, but it was already cured. It is possible to try to intimidate the audience into applauding ( DC 20 Intimidation Check , then DC 25 Intimidation Check ), but even if succeeding the player character loses the contest. Death [ edit section | visual editor ] Harvard Willoughby's death is one of three conditions that must be met for the summoning of Harvard Willoughby (Nature's Vengeance) . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Harvard Willoughby You know why they're called Steel Watchers , right? They're watching to see if you're stealing . Heh. Heh? Harvard Willoughby What do you get if you cross an owlbear with a bugbear ? An... owlbug! Geddit? Hey, would it kill you to laugh a little? Harvard Willoughby Hey, you know why it isn't wrong to fart in the Stormshore Tabernacle ? It smells divine! Harvard Willoughby Whoa-ah! Yeah, I got the kind of thing you like, if you like this kind of thing! Harvard Willoughby Asked my wife why she was fooling around with a wizard. She said, ' Mage Hand is a cantrip - he can keep casting it all night long .' Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] Harvard Willoughby has a DevNote in the internal files reading, "This is a tribute to our favorite sheep". CHA_FL1_Bandit Haseid is one of the bandits raiding the Overgrown Ruins in Act One . “ No such thing as coincidences when there's loot to be had. „ — Haseid Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Haseid is in the Refectory inspecting the library for loot together with Cefrey , Barton , and Torgga , while Mari patrols the antechamber and Andorn guards Chapel Entrance. Barton and the others are instantly hostile to the party. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatclub Damage: 3~10 1d8 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Rage ( + ) Deal 2 extra damage with melee and improvised weapons, and throwing. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Range: Self Reckless Attack ( ) Damage Normal weapon damage Throw all caution in the wind to gain Advantage on your melee Attack Roll . Until your next turn, you have advantage on attack rolls, but enemies also have advantage on attack rolls against you. Range: Normal weapon range Throw ( )   –   Javelin Damage: 3~8 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. Your Strength affects how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayRelief_TravelerB UUID c7716111-3aff-41db-9b95-f86ccbddf491 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Hasmet Hudd travelled to Baldur's Gate with two companions during Act Three . “ Gods, we should have just kept going - this place isn't any safer than the last. „ — Hasmet Hudd Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Hasmet Hudd arrived in the Lower City with Dryfle Doon and Giftu Hudd . The trio fled from the Absolute and are in search of an inn. While Dryfle and Giftu are optimistic about reaching the city, Hasmet remains anxious and glum. He is especially anxious about losing more people close to him. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hasmet Hudd You do realise we can't stay here forever, don't you? Those walls might slow the army of the Absolute down, but they'll get through them sooner or later. Giftu Hudd Let's take it one day at a time, eh? You might feel differently after some food and rest. Hasmet Hudd Fools, the pair of you. Just be ready to leave when the time comes - or preferably before. Dryfle Doon Come on, old chap - I know you're hurting. But it won't bring her back, will it? Hasmet Hudd I know it won't. I just don't want to lose anyone else, all right? Giftu Hudd You won't lose us. We've come this far, haven't we? Whatever happens, we'll be right here with you. Hasmet Hudd I hope so. I really do. Giftu Hudd What's the first thing you want to do after we settle in? Dryfle Doon Sleep for a tenday. Or maybe two. Giftu Hudd Aren't you hungry? Dryfle Doon Pft, I can eat in bed. Hasmet Hudd I just hope somewhere has good dwarven beer. Don't think I'll be able to sleep without a decent drink. Dryfle Doon Look. Just look - we're finally here! We're safe. Hasmet Hudd Safe for now, at least. The army of the Absolute can't be more than a few days away. Giftu Hudd Don't be such a misery guts - we're here now, aren't we? Now they've got city walls and Steel Watchers to get through. Dryfle Doon That's the spirit! Next stop: Baldur's Gate cushiest inn! Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party enter the Iron Throne, Enver Gortash triggers explosions which soon collapse the building. Hastar Biggs is trapped in the southern-most of the two western cells, alongside Featherweight Falson and Phoenix Lubbins . If freed, he dashes towards the Submersible to escape. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] The only action Hastar uses on any turn is Dash , with the help of the Glimpse of Freedom condition which is applied when the cage is opened. Technical UID S_WYR_Rivington_FlamingFist_000 UUID 2f0d4a81-4bc3-432b-a201-71bdacc34160 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Ranger Fist Havard is a human ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in the streets of Rivington in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Havard is patrolling the streets of Rivington with Fist Ingram . Their route runs a vast circle between the Rivington General and the Requisitioned Barn past the following points: X: 1 Y: -107 (entrance to the refugee camp upon starting the Act Three) X: -42 Y: -105 ( Sharran lookout's post ) X: 58 Y: -58 (crossroads) X: 62 Y: -10 ( Abandoned Windmill ) X: 33 Y: -3 (backside of the Sword Coast Couriers kennels) X: -1 Y: -27 ( Angleiron's Smithy ) X: -18 Y: -76 ( Circus of the Last Days ) Havard and his mate do not respond to any attempts to speak to them. Technical UID S_LOW_Havkelaag UUID 8f24c3d5-33cd-4e4f-8c34-4fbc8863862d Stats LOW_TheLodge_Havkelaag Havkelaag is a member of the Society of Brilliance in the Lower City in Baldur's Gate 3 . He can be found at The Lodge in Act Three . “ You find yourself in the cradle of all knowledge relating to the Underdark: the Society of Brilliance „ — Havkelaag Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] In Baldur's Gate, he can be found inside The Lodge just past the main door. If completing the ⁠ Steal a Githyanki Egg quest and having the egg in the inventory, then Havkelaag offers to purchase it for 1000 gold to perform an experiment on raising a githyanki child from birth. If having given the egg to his colleague Lady Esther , Havkelaag is dead along with the rest of the members of the Society of Brilliance, having been killed by Ptaris - the child he raised from the egg. According to the Sword Coast Couriers address book, Havkelaag has a 'philosophical objection' to postal service, and all letters must be address to Golbraith instead. The party can ask Havkelaag to become a member, however he will decline and say new memberships are on hold due to the Absolute . Party members with the Sage background will nevertheless gain the inspiration ⁠ Membership Admittance . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Ice Knife ( + ) Damage: 3~22 1d10 ⁠ Piercing + 2d6 ⁠ Cold Throw a shard of ice that deals 1d10 Piercing damage. It explodes and deals 2d6 Cold damage to anyone nearby. It leaves an   Ice surface. On miss, the shard of ice still explodes. This spell can be cast while you are   Silenced . DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Ice Storm ( + ) Damage: 6~40 2d8 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 4d6 ⁠ Cold Impel a storm of hail and ice to crash from the sky, covering the ground and striking all objects and creatures within range, dealing ⁠ Bludgeoning and ⁠ Cold damage. It also creates an   Ice surface that lasts 2 turns. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Ray of Frost ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Cold Reduces the target's Movement Speed by 3 m / 10 ft. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Notable Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Havkelaag's Key Quarterstaff +2 Simple Robe The Ptarian Code Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Address Book Havkelaag's Journal Havkelaag's Notes Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Havkelaag may only be spoken to while dead if he had been killed by Ptaris: Who are you? What were you doing? Havkelaag Proving theory... genetic morality... I was right. Why were you killed? Havkelaag Careless... skipped... precautionary termination. Where is your killer now? Hazelnut I don't want to do chores anymore. Mama Falice So you just disappeared? Do you know how worried I was? Hazelnut Why do we have to stay here? All we do is work. Mama Falice Everyone has to contribute, my darling. We all have to take care of each other. Mama Falice Once the washing is finished, you can play all you like. Mama Falice You must never, never run away like that again. Do you understand? Hazelnut I just wanted to go home. Mama Falice One day we will. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_SCL_ServantOfTheRaven_ShadarKai UUID a66dd998-1e87-433b-b147-359c0572e700 Stats SCL_HeWhoWas Eqp. EQP_Spear_Leather Trs. SCL_ServantOfTheRaven_Inventory He Who Was is a Shadar-kai on the Ruined Battlefield at X: 129 Y: 106 . He gives the quest Punish the Wicked and has a Raven companion. “ The murdered lie silent. The raven asks - will you be their voice? „ — He Who Was quotes the Raven Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] As a shadar-kai, He Who Was is a servant of the Raven Queen . Shadar-kai were formerly elves before being trapped in the Shadowfell and transformed. The Raven Queen, who is obsessed with collecting memories and essences (typically of loss and grief), sends the shadar-kai to retrieve mementos of tragic events, whether they are physical tokens, memories, or the souls of the dead. In doing so, they are guided by ravens; the raven companion of He Who Was is one such bird. Shadar-kai are typically as cold and emotionless as their queen, but for reasons unknown (possibly the effects of the Shadow Curse) He Who Was has become petty and cruel, taking pleasure in tormenting people while gathering their memories. Ambient dialogue between He Who Was and his raven companion implies that he is no longer following orders given by the Raven Queen , which the raven is displeased with. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] He Who Was is at a ritual circle he set up to commune with a corpse of the dwarven woman Madeline . Approaching him starts ⁠ Punish the Wicked . He initially tells the interacting party member to clear off, but the white raven suggests they might be able to help. He explains the dead woman was a murderer, and asks them to find Madeline's Ledger at the tavern she worked in and bring it back so that the murderer may be brought to justice and her victims given peace. If a party member gives the ledger to He Who Was, he is able to channel the spirit of Madeline through his body. The party member can then ask Madeline about the details of what happened, and decide what punishment – if any – she deserves. If the interacting party member makes Madeline stab herself once, or shames her for being a coward, He Who Was is satisfied. This causes Paladins with an Oath of the Ancients , Oath of the Crown , or Oath of Devotion to break their oath. ⁠ No Rest for the Wicked is granted for party members with the Acolyte background. Otherwise, if the interacting party member passes the Persuasion checks to forgive her, or makes her stab herself a second time, He Who Was becomes enraged and attacks, granting the ⁠ Let Sleeping Dogs Lie inspiration to Acolyte party members. Forgiving her breaks the oath of Vengeance Paladins. Each stabbing inflicts 5 damage, which persists into combat. Failing the Persuasion check on the forgiveness option also satisfies He Who Was, without breaking any Paladin oath. [ verify ] He Who Was is not marked with on the map and there is no dialogue to open trading interface when talking to him, though he has more useful items for sale than other characters. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bane ( + ) Up to 3 creatures receive a -1d4 penalty to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . CHA Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Confusion ( + ) Befuddle a group of creatures, causing them to attack at random, wander around aimlessly, and occasionally skip turns in the stupor. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Darkness ( + ) Create a cloud of magical darkness that Heavily Obscures and inflicts Blind to creatures within. Creatures cannot make ranged attacks into or out of it. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fear ( + ) Hostile targets drop everything and become Fearful : they have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls . If the target ends their turn where they can't see you, they can make another Saving throw to shake off their fear. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Shadow Spear ( )   –   Spear Damage: 5~54 1d6 ⁠ Piercing + 4d12 ⁠ Necrotic Deal an additional 4d12 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic with your equipped melee weapon. Technical UID S_LOW_Client_005 UUID bf5f19cd-638f-4011-ae3d-45007163c637 Stats Halfling_Commoner Hector Roba is an upset halfling customer of the Sorcerous Sundries shop in the Lower City in Act Three . “ I'm not moving from this spot until Lorroakan comes and speaks to me personally. I will be heard! „ — Hector Roba Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Hector is talking about the state of the Sorcerous Sundries to Cappa Delourese in the main lobby. He demands to see Lorroakan because he is unable to find any of the herbs he is looking for. Idle dialogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Cappa Delourese Find what you're looking for? Hector Roba No, I did not find what I'm looking for. Did you? Cappa Delourese Not a dicky bird. It's really quite disappointing. Hector Roba I've good mind to march up there and speak to Lorroakan myself. Cappa Delourese You might want to be careful - I've heard he's not really one for customer service. Hector Roba What do you mean 'not one for customer service'? Cappa Delourese I saw somebody go up to Lorroakan's tower last tenday - looked a proper fright when they came out. Hector Roba Surely you can't just go roughing up your customers? Especially if you're the one at fault! Cappa Delourese Apparently Lorroakan can. Hector Roba This is ludicrous! My complaints will be heard! Cappa Delourese Well, it might just be there's not much left - the Absolute's making people panic. Hector Roba Absolute or not, I still need my full complement of herbs - how am I supposed to do any healing without them? Cappa Delourese I'm sure you'll manage - it's not as if your cupboards are bare just yet. Hector Roba I shouldn't have to wait until I've got nothing left - I need to be prepared. Technical UID S_LOW_Client_001 UUID 9504e91f-b535-411b-ac3b-b4047150f93f Stats Human_Child Heder Cross is a human child gawking at the elementals inside the Sorcerous Sundries shop in the Lower City in Act Three . “ You look like you could drink an entire water elemental in one go! „ — Heder Cross Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Heder Cross, together with his mother Thalita Cross , are observing the water and lava elementals exposed in the hall of the magic shop. While doing so they discuss the elementals and some petty household problems. If spoken with, Heder tells the interacting party member he would like to have an elemental as a pet. He promises that if this happens, he will not let the new pet die "like a goldfish" . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Heder Cross Mumbus, why are lava elementals so hot? Thalita Cross Because they're made of fire, darling. Heder Cross If a lava elemental is made of fire, what am I made of? Thalita Cross Many things, I suppose. Blood, bile, phlegm, chocolate... Heder Cross Chocolate?! Thalita Cross Why of course, darling. Heder Cross Mumbus, if I were a lava elemental, I'd get a job in a restaurant. Thalita Cross Would you now? Heder Cross Mmhmm, 'cause I could cook food right on my body so I wouldn't even need an oven. Thalita Cross You make a fine point. Very efficient, you'd be. Heder Cross No fish, only chicken, beef, and vegetals. No pork either. Thalita Cross It'd be your body; you'd make the rules. Heder Cross Mumbus I'm bored. Thalita Cross Hello, bored, I'm your mother. Heder Cross That's not funny. Thalita Cross I think it's very funny. Heder Cross Well you're wrong. Thalita Cross If you're bored and I'm wrong, where have Jaremy and his mother gone? Heder Cross UGH! Heder Cross Can we go now? Thalita Cross In a little. I've got a bit more shopping to do. Heder Cross Then where are we going? Thalita Cross Figaro's , to pick up some hair ointment for your father. Heder Cross But dad doesn't have any hair. Thalita Cross That's why we need the ointment. Technical UID S_MOO_AssaultFlamingFist_002 UUID a442887f-71ed-415e-92b2-58ffa6e029a5 Stats MOO_FlamingFist_Gnome_Melee Eqp. EQP_Javelin_ScaleMail Trs. HAV_Survivor Fist Helena is a rock gnome Flaming Fist in Act Two . She can help the party during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers . “ Taking on a tower with no siege engines. Wonderful. „ — Helena Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn , and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise Towers , Helena, along with the Flaming Fists Hadenwell , Nipawa , Rhed and Ulthred survive the first assault and assist the party in the remaining battle against the Absolute forces. [ 2 ] but she nevertheless acquiesces by making a wry remark about how Jaheira could help them turn the odds anyway. [ 3 ] After the battle, provided she survives, she and the remaining Fists scout the Moonrise Towers Prison and enter a second battle against the Myrkulites Duckie Verish , Sarabayle , and Willinx Jindlebee , as well as a Death Shepherd and a horde of Necromites . The party can assist the Fists in this optional battle. If the Fists survive, they guard the prison until Ketheric Thorm is defeated. After Ketheric Thorm is killed and the party leave for Act Three , Helena disappears from the game entirely. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_OrinsMother UUID 178bc423-a543-4cf9-99cb-ef4e93a1056e Stats Stats_Placeholder Helena Anchev , also known as Orin's Mother Helena , is the daughter of Sarevok Anchev and both the mother and half-sister to Orin the Red , the latter of whom was born through an incestuous relationship between Sarevok and Helena. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The corpse of Orin's Mother Helena is found in The Chosen's Room in the Bhaal Temple at X: 96 Y: 991 during ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone . Using Speak with Dead , Helena reveals that Sarevok Anchev ordered her to kill Orin as a offering to Lord Bhaal. Desperately needing Sarevok's approval and wanting to become Bhaal's chosen, Helena attacked Orin when she was only seven years old, but Orin retaliated and killed Helena instead. Helena's corpse was then put on display in Orin's room. With this information it is possible to prevent Orin from killing whomever she ⁠ kidnapped , without passing any ability checks. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Helena can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Orin’s Mother Helena Helena... Anchev... daughter... of... Sarevok... Orin’s Mother Helena Mother... of... Orin... Why did you try to kill your own daughter? Orin’s Mother Helena I... wanted... to be... Bhaal’s... Chosen... Orin’s Mother Helena Sarevok... told me... she... must be... my... offering... Orin’s Mother Helena I... was... close... my hand... around... her throat... Orin’s Mother Helena I... failed... Did Orin know that Sarevok ordered you to kill her? Orin’s Mother Helena No... she... worshipped... him... loved... him... Orin’s Mother Helena So... did... I... Who killed you? Orin’s Mother Helena Orin... my... daughter... Orin’s Mother Helena I tried... to kill... her... but she... killed me... first... What happened to you? Orin’s Mother Helena Orin... my... daughter... Orin’s Mother Helena I tried... to kill... her... but she... killed me... first... Where are you from? Orin’s Mother Helena Baldur’s... Gate... Brampton... district... Why were you put on display like this? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ While Helena is listed as human on her character sheet, a memoir written by Sarevok Anchev describes her as a "shapeshifting beauty", implying that she, like Orin, was a changeling or part doppelganger. Technical UID S_LOW_DevilsFee_Helsik UUID 299a1c00-ff53-415e-ad8e-9bcbbae55597 Stats LOW_DevilsFee_Helsik Helsik is a diabolist who owns the Devil's Fee in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . She trades in magical equipment, alchemy ingredients, dyes, potions, and scrolls. As a diabolist, Helsik can also open a portal to the Hells . “ I welcome thee to the Devil's Fee, where every hellish curio's a rarity! So merry be - and shop with glee. „ — Helsik greeting the party Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 2.1 Act Three 2.2 Breaking into the House of Hope 2.3 After returning from the House of Hope 3 Store 3.1 Regular items 3.2 Curated selection 3.3 On the desk in front of her 4 Combat 4.1 Attacks and actions 4.1.1 Tactician only 4.1.2 Loot 5 Speak with Dead 6 Related literature 7 Related quests 8 Bugs 9 Notes and references 10 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Helsik is a warlock in service to the archdevil Mammon , possibly the richest being in existence and a miser loyal only to coin. At the Devil's Fee, Helsik trades in curios and information, offering a large and rare collection of Hellish items accumulated through her occupation as a diabolist. However, Helsik was not satisfied with the coin she was bringing in from the curios, and decided to diversify her skills into providing "access". [ 1 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Helsik initially only offers Alchemy ingredients, Grenades , and Dyes but the party can unlock trading access to her " Curated Selection " by passing multiple DC 5 Perception Checks to notice the diabolic curios in her collection and at least one DC 15 Arcana Check to identify the items as genuine. The interacting party member can say "Must be a diabolist running this shop with so many devilish artifacts" to unlock curated selection dialogue. These Arcana checks have a DC of 0 for Karlach due to her time in the Hells. At first, Helsik only has dialogue options to trade with the party, but if ⁠ Deal with the Devil , ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss , or ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior are sufficiently progressed, and at least one Arcana check is passed, it is revealed that she is a diabolist, which unlocks special dialogue options to talk about the House of Hope . Should a character have high Attitude with Helsik, such as by gifting her enough gold through trade, the character is bestowed the Infectious Greed buff in her presence. Breaking into the House of Hope [ edit section | visual editor ] Helsik can help the party break into the Hells in exchange for 20,000 gold. The party can pay the full price or convince her to reduce the cost to 10,000 gold by passing a DC 25 Intimidation Check or if the player is a warlock a DC 25 Persuasion Check . Instead of paying her gold, it is also possible to agree to steal the Gauntlets of Hill Giant Strength from the House of Hope for her, which initiates ⁠ Acquire the Gauntlets for Helsik . Upon convincing her to aid them, Helsik gives the party a Grimoire Bound in Imp Skin , Opening a Hell Gate , and Ritual Pouch containing the items needed to open the portal. She directs the party upstairs to a pentagram that opens a portal to the House of Hope . If the party previously stole from Helsik before she offers the ritual items, she angrily kicks the party out of the store and seals the door. Attempting to return to the store causes her to become hostile. After returning from the House of Hope [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon returning from the House of Hope, if the party agreed to obtain the Gauntlets of Hill Giant Strength through ⁠ Acquire the Gauntlets for Helsik , Helsik demands the gauntlets or the original proposed fee of 20,000 gold. The party can pass a DC 10 Intimidation Check to keep the Gauntlets without Helsik turning hostile. Helsik only asks for the gauntlets after the party finished all related quests in the House of Hope. Otherwise, if the party did not agree to obtain the gauntlets for her, they can keep or sell them to Helsik. Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to LOW_DevilsFee_Diabolist_Trade_Magic . Technical UID S_LOW_Bartender UUID 626fc1ed-c1ff-4dcd-a986-068a12cb7974 Stats HalfOrc_Commoner Tender Henk is the owner of The Singing Lute , a restaurant in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Jableeda. [ 1 ] „ — Henk Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Tender Henk can be found standing behind the counter of his restaurant. If spoken to, he might offer to trade with the party. He sells many types of alcoholic drinks and other beverages, but he does not initially carry gold. Henk is rather cranky, but nevertheless has a vena poetica and a creative bone. On the second floor of The Singing Lute , Henk's home contains musical compositions and song drafts. The restaurant's mailbox contains a Crumpled Letter that references troupe gatherings that Henk participates in. However, a note titled READ HENK suggests that Honk is not happy with his aspirations. If the player character romances Karlach , she may ask them out on a date early in Act Three . They rendezvous at the Singing Lute, where Tender Henk acts as a boorish waiter. He begins casting a ritual spell to kill the party after a certain number of turns, and his minions (including Hervyl) appear and attack the party as they attempt to cross the bridge to stop Ghislev. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Hextra is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Malayah , Fist Madstene and a Steel Watcher . Hextra and her mates do not respond to any attempts to speak with them, regardless of whether the Steel Watch Foundry is intact or destroyed. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_Reaper_04 UUID c01e3dc3-4323-4a50-a378-ae6c0b8a062a Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_Reaper Reaper of Bhaal Hiila is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , found in the Bhaal Temple within the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . “ Bhaal's will is clear - this world is ripe for the plucking. If you are not strong enough to lead us, another will. „ — Hiila , to the Dark Urge who rejected Bhaal Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can go to the Bhaal Temple in hopes of saving their companion from Orin . There they will encounter Orin, who will engage the party in combat by transforming into a Slayer . Hiila, along with the rest of the reapers, will begin channeling a ritual spell Bloody Favour , granting Orin a Boon of Bhaal at the start of every turn. If the player character is not the Dark Urge , and Orin is killed or disabled, Hiila ends concentration and attacks the party as normal. If the player character is the Dark Urge and defeats Orin, Hiila remains neutral to the party and moves to the foot of one of the stairs leading to the central altar ground. His one-liners depend on whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. Technical UID S_LOW_StelmanesDeath_Citizen_02 UUID 78dbf885-7452-452a-a541-85c823b742f8 Stats Gnome_Commoner Hilario Varota is in Baldur's Gate during Act Three , discussing the gorier aspects of a recent murder case. “ You've got to talk to the locals if you want the true story about Stelmane's death. The gazette would never print all the juicy details. „ — Hilario Varota Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Hilario Varota and Megthanet are at the western entrance of Elfsong Tavern in the Lower City . They are discussing the most gruesome details of Duke Stelmane's murder. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Hilario Varota I heard it happened right here in the Elfsong. Sliced clean through Stelmane's neck. Megthanet I heard her guts were placed on the ground in the shape of the Absolute's mark! Hilario Varota I always said the Elfsong was haunted. Now it's doubly so. Hilario Varota They never found the head. Makes me wonder how they knew it was Stelmane. Megthanet You can tell all sorts with technology these days. I'm sure she left some hair. Or teeth. Megthanet What would you do with a decapitated head anyway? Not like you could sell it. Hilario Varota I can think of a thing or two. Nothing good, though. Megthanet I'm never eating at the Elfsong again. What if there were bits. If Enver Gortash is killed: Hilario Varota First Stelmane, and now Gortash! If the higher-ups aren't safe, what hope do we have? Megthanet I heard Gortash was strangled with a piece of his own intestine! Hilario Varota As if Stelmane's death wasn't horrid enough. Hilario Varota I wonder who will take charge now that Gortash is gone. Megthanet Whoever it is, good luck to them. Those Absolutists won't stop just because there's a power vacuum. Hilario Varota Probably responsible for his death, if you ask me. Megthanet I always said he was doing too good a job. Better than Stelmane, in any case. Megthanet Do you really think it was Absolutists that killed him? Hilario Varota Them or a disgruntled citizen. Megthanet These dukes need to start improving their security. If they can't keep themselves alive, how can we expect them to protect us? v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag Support Group Adrielle Hydrangea Wubb Jatlo Kled Mayrina Technical UID S_HAV_GnomeCat UUID 33e545f6-9a0a-48ae-88b4-896a0c21c8ca Stats Cat His Majesty is a hairless ⁠ Sphynx cat with blue eyes in the Shadow-Cursed Lands during Act Two . “ Hiss! I say: HISS! „ — His Majesty Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] His Majesty is on the ground floor of the Last Light Inn . He is rather stand-offish and hisses immediately when approached and more throughout any interactions with him. Rangers immediately recognise him as territorial. Without Speak with Animals: [ edit section | visual editor ] A party member without Speak with Animals active may try to call the cat to them with a DC 14 Animal Handling Check and, at their own peril, attempt to pet him: His Majesty *Hiss!* [DARK URGE]  MREAOW! [DARK URGE] [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Try to muster some kindness, and calm the creature.  (DC 14) [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Here, kitty kitty. (DC 14) [BARBARIAN]  WOOF!   +1   -1   -1   -1   +2   -1   -2   -1 While using Speak with Animals: [ edit section | visual editor ] If Speak with Animals is active, a party member can ask him why they are so angry at them: His Majesty Hiss! I say: HISS! Easy, kitty. I mean you no harm. What's got your whiskers in a twist?  (if not a Ranger) [INTIMIDATION]  Hiss! (DC 14) [RANGER] [ANIMAL HANDLING]  I do not seek your territory, noble beast, only a few moments of your time. (DC 10)   +1   +1   +1   -1   -1   +1   +2   +1 The player character can either intimidate him or tell him they mean him no harm. His Majesty then expands further: His Majesty This is my territory. And you're in it. Apologies. I'll keep my distance. His Majesty Indeed, you will. Or you'll find my claws planted firmly in your dangles. My intentions are pure. I only wanted to admire you up close.   +1   +1   +1   +1   -1   +1   +2   +1 I see your point. You'll see these points unless you retreat! Barcus is permitted and I'm not?  (if Barcus met in Moonrise Towers Prison) Precisely! The party character can then either apologize, or express that their intentions are pure and that they only wish to admire him, after which he allows the party member to stay and chat a little longer: His Majesty Hmm. His Majesty I'll allow it. Quite the specimen you are. How did you come to this place? I slinked, of course. Quietly admire the cat.   +1   +1   +1   +1   -1   +1   +2   +1 You seem like someone who knows what he's about. Heard anything interesting around here? His Majesty Good of you to notice. For my part, I have noticed the cleric is a liar. His Majesty She promised me a bit of milk. But do you see any milk? Do you? Nor do I. Disgraceful. When asked if he has heard anything interesting, His Majesty relays his belief that Isobel is a liar because she promised him milk but he has yet to receive any. The party can corroborate this story by finding a milk bowl in Isobel's room. However, stealing it and presenting it to His Majesty does not improve favour with him, nor results in him drinking it. If the interacting party member decides to intimidate him instead and passes the ability check, they can immediately ask a few questions or demand he get out: How did you get to this place? Heard anything interesting around here? What's your name? I could use someone like you in my camp. Care to join? You're in my territory. Get out.   +1   -1   -1   -1   +2   -1   -2   -1 Speaking with His Majesty grants the ⁠ Noble Feline to party members with the Noble background. Meeting Steelclaw as well also grants the ⁠ Alley Cats inspiration to party members with the Urchin background. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] His Majesty's model. (Patch #3 to Hotfix #8) His Majesty sleeping. (Patch #3 to Hotfix #8) His Majesty. (Patch #3 to Hotfix #8) Appearance changes [ edit section | visual editor ] His Majesty was hairless when he was first implemented in Early Access and through launch. However, Larian gave him the fur of a long-haired cat in Patch #3 on September 22, 2023 with the following patch note: "Updated the visuals of His Majesty, who previously looked like Steelclaw . His Majesty's appearance now befits his name and nature." This resulted in players complaining that they felt the Sphynx cat breed perfectly fit the character of His Majesty. Larian restored his appearance soon after in Hotfix #8 on October 3, 2023, deciding to change Steelclaw's appearance instead of His Majesty's: "Shaved His Majesty, who is once again a Sphynx. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_DeathsHead_02 UUID adf3d591-4442-4543-86fd-9ca5b1cb73d2 Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_Invoker Invoker of Bhaal Hivune is a human follower of Bhaal . “ He allowed you - an unfaithful whelp - to behold him... Only for the Bastard Child of Murder to spurn him. Blasphemy. „ — Hivune , to the companion of the Dark Urge who rejected Bhaal Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Hivune is in the Bhaal Temple within the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . Initially he accompanies Orin the Red on the central altar ground, trying to distract her from torturing the victim she abducted from the campsite. If the player character is not the Dark Urge , Hivune takes part in the fight against them, allying with Orin. If the player character is the Dark Urge and defeats Orin, Hivune remains neutral to the party and patrols the chamber of Bhaal's Chosen. His one-liners [ 1 ] depend on whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. If the Dark Urge embraces Bhaal, and Jaheira and Minsc were recruited and did not leave the party up to the moment, they both confront the player character on their way back from the temple. In this case, Hivune joins the fight as the party's ally. SHA_MerregonTrader Hoarding Merregon is a Merregon and trader that dwells in Yurgir 's chamber in the Gauntlet of Shar . It serves as the Orthon's quartermaster. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Hoarding Merregon can initially be found taking part in Yurgir's ambush. If Yurgir has been pacified, it lounges beside a campfire at X: -664 Y: -760 . Using Detect Thoughts on it, reveals that it has slightly more self-will than other Merregons and that its driving purpose is to keep feeding the Displacer Beast and protect and grow Yurgir's stock. The party can then tell the Merregon that they are tending the Displacer Beast now, which makes the Merregon give them five Merregon Potions which can be thrown to befuddle the enemy. Store [ edit section | visual editor ] The Hoarding Merregon sells items from the following item tables. This corresponds to SHA_MerregonTrader treasure table. Coating Table Poor Trader Table Potion Table Scroll Table Spoiled Supply Table Unlike most traders, the Merregon has a "gold stash", similar to enemies, rather than a "trader gold supply". I serve... Umberlee... What happened to you? Holli Dylford I was... swimming... I was... attacked... Do you remember what happened before you were attacked? Holli Dylford Just... black blood... everywhere... What killed you? Holli Dylford Metal... monster... Tell me about this metal monster. Holli Dylford Big... fast... hit my head... everything went... black... Where were you attacked? Holli Dylford I was... swimming... in Grey Harbour... UND_Duergar_Generic Holvik is one of the duergar accompanying Gekh Coal to the Decrepit Village in Act One . “ Half the squad dead for the sake of one runaway. Gh'rack. „ — Holvik Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Holvik is part of Gekh Coal's task force to retrieve Sergeant Thrinn's stolen boots. If a party member speaks with him as a non- drow , Holvik expresses disgust at their casualties, which were caused by Myconid hallucinations that led members to leap to their deaths. Technical UID S_LOW_Bartender_RomanceSceneBackup UUID d3e6a655-b69d-4db7-9b59-dc0a9cdbfc26 Stats HalfOrc_Commoner Tender Honk is a situational character in the Lower City of the Baldur's Gate , a tender in The Singing Lute restaurant. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Honk appears within the game only if the Singing Lute's owner, Tender Henk , died before the player character went on a date with Karlach . Otherwise, his presence is indicated only by the note found in Henk's pockets. If this note is to be believed, Honk does not approve of Henk practicing music before the store closes. If Henk died, Tender Honk is the waiter catering to Karlach and her partner during their date at The Singing Lute in Act Three . He does the same actions as Henk does during the date with one exception; instead of saying, "Jableeda" , as Henk does when Karlach addresses him about the order, he says "Jablooda" . Unlike Tender Henk, Honk does not act as a trader within the game.
