Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_Player_Jaheira UUID 91b6b200-7d00-4d62-8dc9-99e8339dfa1a Stats HAV_Jaheira Eqp. EQP_Jaheira Trs. GLO_Jaheira Variant 1 UID HalfElves_Female_High_Jaheira UUID 7c7e6552-3fc0-4495-bb11-4b9f9a8e71fc Stats HeroHalfElfFemale Eqp. EQP_Jaheira Jaheira is a recruitable companion . She and Minsc return from both Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn and are the only two recruitable companions who cannot be romanced . [ 1 ] She is a high half-elf and a druid [ 2 ] with the Soldier background, and can be first found at the Last Light Inn during Act Two . Having become High Harper in the century since her first adventures, wherein her husband Khalid was killed, Jaheira is deadset on maintaining her Harper network, taking down the Cult of the Absolute , and later reuniting with Minsc , her closest friend. Jaheira is known for her sharp wit and dry humour, and also serves as a mentor figure to the rest of the party. “ Nature's servant awaits. „ — Jaheira 's catchphrase Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Starting class 1.2 Personal quest 1.3 Recruitment 1.3.1 Leaving the party 1.4 Approval 1.5 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 Backstory 3.1 The Iron Crisis & Shadows of Amn 3.2 Crusade against Ketheric 3.3 Life in Baldur's Gate 3.4 Last Light Inn 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.2 Act Two 4.2.1 Isobel's abduction 4.2.2 Assault on Moonrise Towers 4.3 Act Three 4.3.1 Meeting the Harpers 4.3.2 In the Guildhall 4.3.3 The vaults of the Counting House 4.3.4 The Sewers 4.3.5 Facing Minsc 4.4 Ending 4.4.1 Retirement from the Harpers 4.4.2 Remaining the High Harper 4.4.3 Other dialogue at the reunion party 5 Speak with Dead 6 Related literature 7 Related quests 8 Loot 8.1 Starting equipment 9 Gallery 10 Trivia 11 Bugs 12 Notes and references 13 See also 14 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] When first encountered, Jaheira is a level 8 druid with the following ability scores : 15 STR, 14 DEX, 17 CON, 10 INT, 16 WIS, 15 CHA. If recruited, she reverts to a level 1 druid with the standard ability scores for the class . Her default subclass is the Circle of the Land . Jaheira has the Soldier background. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] If recruited, Jaheira has a companion quest called The High Harper . Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira can be fully recruited near the end of Act Two , after Ketheric Thorm retreats to the Mind Flayer Colony . Until then, she is only available as an attached follower . However, if the Last Light Inn is destroyed and the party is still allied with Jaheira after Ketheric is defeated, she can be offered a place at camp . Although she accepts, she is, in this case, not available as a companion until Act Three . If Jaheira dies before she is recruited as a full companion, she remains Dead and cannot be recruited. If she is killed by the Dark Urge's hand, they earn the inspiration ⁠ Forced Retirement . Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character kills Minsc during her quest line , refuses to recruit him if he is freed, sacrifices him for Sarevok , kills any of her children, kills Isobel , intimidates her into leaving after obtaining the Slayer form, or – as the Dark Urge – embraces taking up the mantle of Bhaal's Chosen following their fight with Orin , then Jaheira permanently leaves the party. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira Approves Main article: Jaheira/Approval Jaheira favours direct approaches and eschews flattery. She loves snarky jokes, even at her own expense. [ 3 ] Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Unlike in Baldur's Gate II , Jaheira cannot be romanced in Baldur's Gate 3 . Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] A profile picture of Jaheira after a battle in Danthelon's basement. Her seasoned affect, elven ancestry and calm manner are readily apparent. Tall and lean, Jaheira wears her silvery-chestnut hair in neatly braided rows wrapped in blue cloth, with silver ringlets at their temples. Her green-gold eyes, high cheekbones and tapered ears lend her hawk-like profile an air of alert poise, revealing her elven ancestry. Approximately 150 years old when the game's events start to unfold, faint war lines etch the skin at the corners of her mouth and brow, softening only when a rare smile surfaces. Battle and age have sharpened her insight and weathered her frame, but not dulled her agility or the blades of the two curved scimitars she carries on her back, marking her as both warrior and druid. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaded and strengthened by her past, Jaheira is a formidable, headstrong and opinionated woman. Charismatic and insightful, she has a sharp tongue, and her wit can be deprecating to those for whom it is meant. She tends to make jokes out of serious situations and approves of the player character doing so. [ 4 ] Despite being a wizened veteran of numerous wars, she maintains a healthy sense of humour and does not mind when she is the butt of a good joke. [ 5 ] Jaheira, after realising that she was the butt of a good joke. As a result of Jaheira's experiences during her long life, she is rarely surprised and; except for what concerns those close to her heart, like Minsc; takes unexpected events calmly and in stride. Her initial testing of the player character with truth-telling drugs, as well as her inquisitive reaction to the Dark Urge revealing their nature as a Bhaalspawn, shows that she is very cautious with whom she extends her trust. But once the party prove themselves, Jaheira is a loyal and stalwart ally who sees them as equals, never afraid to speak her mind and not sugarcoating the truth. However, although Jaheira outwardly displays assuredness, confidence, and steadfast certainty of Harper virtues, such as hope and bravery prevailing in the face of evil, she may, like many leaders, reveal doubts about these things if approached in moments of self-reflection or great significance to her. [ 6 ] As one of the eldest and strongest of Baldur's Gate's Harpers , she commands the respect of most of the organisation. Speaking to Harpers with Jaheira in the party reveals that they almost always defer to her strength and experience. Her military background shows in her professionalism and cold analysis when dealing with most situations. One of the few exceptions to this is her old friend Minsc , whom Jaheira initially believed to be dead due to a combination of Minsc's recklessness and her own desire to put the safety of all Baldur's Gate above individual lives. She becomes enraged when it is revealed he was alive and being manipulated by Orin's Doppelgängers using her face. Once they reunite, their relationship is initially strained due to Jaheira not believing Minsc could be so easily manipulated, though they do eventually reaffirm their friendship. Backstory [ edit section | visual editor ] See Jaheira for full backstory [ 7 ] Jaheira was born in the nation of Tethyr to one of the nobles loyal to the king. When she was only a year old, a Tethyrian civil war broke out, and her family was killed by a mob of angry peasants. One of the servant girls took Jaheira, fled into the forest of Tethyr, and stumbled upon an enclave of druids. They took her in and raised her as their own. Jaheira grew up very headstrong and militant in her beliefs that the only way to protect nature is to have an active role in the world. At some point, Jaheira was introduced to the Harpers and joined them. There she met and fell in love with another half-elf named Khalid , whom she saved from an attempted assassination by the Shadow Thieves . And though they had completely different characters, they married soon after and travelled the Sword Coast together. The Iron Crisis & Shadows of Amn [ edit section | visual editor ] During the events of the first Baldur's Gate game, Jaheira and Khalid were sent by the Harpers to investigate the Iron Crisis and the Nashkel mines. In the Friendly Arm Inn , they waited for their old friend Gorion but met his ward instead. They travelled with Gorion's Ward (the protagonist of the previous Baldur's Gate games) to investigate the crisis which led to their confrontation with the culprit – Sarevok Anchev . Sometime after Sarevok's defeat, the group parted ways for a while until they once again joined up alongside their friends, Gorion's Ward, Imoen , Minsc , and Dynaheir . After they left Baldur's Gate, they were captured by Shadow Thieves and imprisoned in a dungeon beneath the city of Athkatla in Amn . She, Minsc and Imoen survived, but Dynaheir and Jaheira's beloved husband Khalid were killed. Their captor was Jon Irenicus – an elven wizard who wanted to steal the Bhaalspawn essence for himself. She eventually helped Gorion's Ward defeat him. Crusade against Ketheric [ edit section | visual editor ] About 20 years later, Jaheira, alongside Harpers and druids of the Emerald Enclave , fought Ketheric Thorm and his forces of Shar at Moonrise Towers . Their unified forces managed to defeat Thorm and imprison him within his family's Mausoleum in Reithwin Town . The united army was scattered when Ketheric brought down the Shadow Curse upon the surrounding lands, twisting them into a horrifying place of deadly shadows and cursed beings. Life in Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira's home in Baldur's Gate At some point later, Jaheira made herself a home in Baldur's Gate , where she raised her foster children: Jord , Rion , Jhessem , Fig and Tate . Yet, a Harper's life demanded she spend much time away from her home and children. She has a private basement that looks like a Druid's cavern, and it is heavily trapped. The basement is inhabited by the Postmaster Badger and his messenger rats, whom he trains to be harper spies. Jaheira keeps a key under a trapped bookcase. It unlocks a secret door hidden behind the bookcase, where she keeps some of her most private items: Rite of the Timeless Body , Belm , Staff of the Ram , and Khalid's Gift . [ 8 ] After Minsc was rescued from his stone prison, they reunited once again. They were the first to uncover information about the threat of the Absolute . Due to Minsc's impulsivity and eagerness to fight, he was captured by the cultists. Jaheira, realising they were severely unprepared against the cult, decided to leave him in order to warn others with news about the cult. She later regretted how easily she made the decision to leave him behind, knowing he would never have done the same to her. Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] After learning of Ketheric's return, Jaheira quartered herself with a squad of Harpers at Last Light Inn , in the middle of the Shadow-Cursed Lands . From there, her scouts ventured forth to keep a close watch on the cult's forces at Moonrise Towers . Since she left her family for Last Light Inn, they received only one sending message from her. It read: "I'm sorry, you know what to do." Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] “ Unshackled from shadows, she will rise in moonlit glory and carve a path of brightness to the accursed one's second death. So sayeth the wise Alaundo . „ — Jaheira on Dame Aylin Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Although she is not present during Act One, the party can stumble across a hint to her. In Grymforge , they can find a dead drow named Jhaam in one of the cages near Murmath at X: -632 Y: 388 . It is possible to use Speak with Dead on her, revealing she was sent by Jaheira to investigate rumours of Absolutist activity in Grymforge, as well as their attempts to find potential weapons . If Jaheira has not been met yet, the companions comment on whether or not they recognise her name. Only Karlach knows exactly who she is, while Astarion and Wyll have heard of her and Lae'zel , Shadowheart , and Gale have no clue. [ 9 ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] "We fight, we die, and when our time comes we just hope that there is someone else to take our place." On reaching the Last Light Inn , Jaheira is instantly wary of the party and summons vines to stop the player character. [ 10 ] She produces a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen . [ 11 ] Suspicious that the ensnared player character may be a True Soul , she demonstrates how the tadpoles react to those infected by bringing the specimen up to their face. It moves excitedly in its bottle, reinforcing her belief that the party is comprised of True Souls. Either Mol (if the tieflings were saved) or Marcus (if not saved) comes to their aid, vouching for them. Jaheira is shocked at how anyone clearly infected somehow manages to have free will and demands answers. She insists on knowing the whole truth. If given vague answers, a DC 21 Persuasion Check is required to convince her to back down, while showing her the Mysterious Artefact convinces her to relent without a check. She then invites the party inside the inn for a drink, granting the ⁠ Living Legend inspiration to party members with the Entertainer background. If the wine is smelled first, a hint of Klauthgrass is detected – a truth serum: [MEDICINE]  Smell the wine first.  (DC 10) [DRUID] [MEDICINE]  Smell the wine.  (DC 6  ) [ROGUE] [INSIGHT]  Meet her stare head on as you examine her body language.  (DC 6  ) [MEDICINE]  Sniff the wine to see if it's been tampered with.  (DC 6  ) The party can still down the wine, even knowing there is a truth serum: [CONSTITUTION]  Despite knowing you're under the effects of a drug, try to deny the tadpole has any influence over you.  (DC 6) Depending on the option chosen, the following inspiration can be gained ⁠ From One Hero to Another ( Folk Hero background) – for downing the drink ⁠ Not My First Time ( Charlatan background) – successfully passing the constitution check to resist the wine ⁠ Wary of Strangers ( Urchin background) – for refusing the drink Jaheira's trust can be earned regardless of whether her altered drink is consumed, and her query is the same: Is the parasite changing the party? Jaheira refuses to believe an assertion that the parasite isn't doing anything, but does believe a statement that the player character is resisting the urge to change. Once Jaheira trusts the party, she explains the situation: that the leader of Moonrise Towers is Ketheric Thorm , who is immensely powerful and gifted with immortality. The Harpers are attempting to find a way to stop the cult and kill Thorm once and for all. They have had little luck, but Jaheira believes the party can make a difference by infiltrating Moonrise as a True Soul. She asks the party to go upstairs and meet Isobel , the one responsible for shielding the Last Light Inn. Isobel's abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] After Jaheira starts to trust the party, she refers them upstairs to gain a blessing from Isobel. When Marcus arrives to abduct her, the party can help him or try to stop him, which starts ⁠ Resolve the Abduction . If Isobel is captured or killed, everyone in the tavern except for Jaheira and the party is killed and turned into a shadow-cursed zombie. The party can lie to Jaheira, telling her they tried to stop Marcus. Jaheira can be invited to stay at their camp, but she does not become a companion until ⁠ Infiltrate Moonrise Towers is complete. Assault on Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved, Jaheira continues to operate from Last Light Inn until the party is ready to defeat Thorm once and for all. When ⁠ Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic is complete, Jaheira and her Harpers have already started the assault on the Moonrise Towers. [ 12 ] If Dame Aylin is spared, Jaheira sees her assaulting Moonrise Towers. Jaheira can be invited to join the party as an attached follower until getting to the tower top and defeating Ketheric for the first time. If not invited, she fights alongside the party in the assault. Jaheira is neither shy about wading into melee combat nor discriminating about who she engages (e.g., against enemies who deal significant damage). As such, it is quite easy for her to die, and, because she is not a companion at this point, she cannot be revived if killed here. If the party intend to have her as a companion later, it is advisable to keep her well protected, or not invite her (as an attached companion) to participate in the battle. When Ketheric escapes to the Mind Flayer Colony , Jaheira can be recruited as a full companion. If not recruited, but acting as an attached follower, she stays at the tower top until his defeat. After Ketheric Thorm is defeated there, she can be found on the main floor, where she may ask to join the party on her own. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Meeting the Harpers [ edit section | visual editor ] In Danthelon's Dancing Axe If Jaheira is recruited and in the party when they reach Wyrm's Crossing , she asks to visit the Harper safehouse in a shop called Danthelon's Dancing Axe . This starts her companion quest, ⁠ The High Harper , to rescue her old friend Minsc . Upon entering the shop and speaking to the shopkeeper, Entharl Danthelon greets the party, although Jaheira tells him to skip the pleasantries if she is present. Entharl gives the key to a secret room at X: -18 Y: 138 , where the Harpers are waiting down the iron ladder. Once down below, Harper Geraldus greets the party with a strange greeting – "May Selûne's Tears shine on this meeting." He again emphasises Selûne's Tears a few moments later. A successful Insight check reveals that Geraldus is not nervous, but terrified, and is using Selûne's Tears as a code. Jaheira mentions that the Harpers remind her of Marcus , implying they are traitors laying a trap. Choosing to strike while Jaheira has them distracted makes the enemies Surprised . After the Harpers are defeated, they revert to their natural form as doppelgangers . Geraldus explains that the rest of the Harpers were murdered or dragged away, while he was only kept alive to lay a trap for Jaheira. Disillusioned at this revelation, Jaheira suggests the life of a Harper might be unsuited for Geraldus, as he endangered Entharl and others by going along with the doppelganger's plans, but she can be persuaded to think otherwise. Either way, Geraldus leaves, and Jaheira explains the main reason she sought out the Harpers was for more information on Minsc of Rashemen , who she had sent them after. Previously, Minsc and Jaheira had been investigating the cult together, but were separated, and Jaheira had to leave him behind so she could spread word of the cult to others. Geraldus speaks in code. With the Harpers gone, Jaheira needs a moment to think. She tells the party she has some ideas on how to proceed, but wants to consider whether this is truly her last resort. After arriving in the Lower City , she explains her plan to enlist the help of the Guild and Nine-Fingers Keene . In the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] Keene is in her office, well aware of the Harpers' entrance into her territory. She informs the party that she already knows of Minsc, who is going by the new title of the Stone Lord, that he now works for the Absolute, and is decimating the members of the Guild. As he threatens the Guild, she intends to take him down, but refuses to let the party confront Minsc themselves. However, there are plenty of other members with loose lips who eventually reveal the Guild's intention to ambush Minsc at the vaults of the Counting House . The vaults of the Counting House [ edit section | visual editor ] “ That old elf took two guards by herself. And she wasn't even scratched . „ — Cashguard Morra , commenting on Jaheira's combat prowess after the battle in the vaults Minsc is nearly swallowed by a Mimic. Once inside the vaults, the deepest area of the room is straight ahead. The party must move forward beyond the locked door. Minsc can then finally be seen in the flesh. Unfortunately, Minsc disappears before he can be confronted, and a group of Bhaalists attack the party as a parting gift. Once the Bhaalists have been defeated, the party must search for clues on where Minsc went. Approaching the large vault at the end of the room X: -691 Y: 873 (which was completely smashed by Minsc) with a successful perception check shows mud from the sewers. The Sewers [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc can be found in the Abandoned Cistern . There are two ways to find Minsc: belowground and aboveground. The valves that open the sluice gate Belowground, it is necessary to jump the pipes above the caustic water at X: -186 Y: 883 and defeat the Bhaalists guarding the area. Going north, there is an area with a Sluice Valve, which is stuck. A successful athletic check opens it. Otherwise, it is necessary to interact with the temperature valve and the water level valve, timing them properly to open the door. The sluice tunnel leads to Minsc. Pressure plates in the "Keep Out" room. Aboveground, there is a garden area north of the Steel Watch Foundry with a door that says, "Keep Out." There are two pressure plates on the north and south walls of the room. Moving a party member (or one of the crates in the room) on each of them at the same time opens the door to a secret area. In this area is an ornate hatch which leads to the area where Minsc is. Facing Minsc [ edit section | visual editor ] After finding Minsc again, he is under the control of a tadpole and does not see reason. He immediately attacks the party, along with a number of doppelgangers, cultists, and a Zhentarim. All Absolutists must be defeated. Taking down the "Jaheira" doppelganger elicits some panicked voice lines from Minsc. If the Zhentarim survive, they are found later in the Guildhall. If Minsc dies here, Jaheira becomes enraged, slanders the party, and leaves permanently, concluding the quest. To avoid this, Minsc must be knocked out with a non-lethal attack. The Emperor initially refuses to bring Minsc under his protection, stating he is too far gone to help. However, he can be convinced to bring Minsc under protection, particularly with Jaheira present. If Jaheira is not present, Minsc can still be shown images of Jaheira alive and well, allowing him to be recruited. If Jaheira is dead, Minsc cannot be recruited. If the player character agrees with the Emperor on not saving Minsc after he is knocked out, or decides to kill him themselves, the outcome is the same as if Minsc is killed in combat: Jaheira leaves the party. If she is not present in the Abandoned Cistern, she automatically starts a dialogue upon the party's return to camp, and permanently leaves afterwards. If Minsc is successfully recruited, he rushes off to find his friend Boo , smashing through several walls to the north. Following him and subsequently talking to Minsc and Jaheira resolves the quest ⁠ The High Harper . At some point after recruiting Minsc, Jaheira and Minsc have an argument where the latter refers to her as his wychlaran , and the player character must intervene. They have the option here to try convincing Minsc to rely more on Jaheira, and this choice determines which of two possible outcomes Jaheira's story has, leading to slight differences in her dialogue and behaviour at the dinner party in the Epilogue . Ending [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira's ending depends on whether or not she decides to retire from the Harpers after a very long lifetime of fighting for Baldur's Gate. In order for her to retire, the player character must find the Rite of the Timeless Body in the secret basement of Elerrathin's Home with her in the party, and then speak with her about it. Depending on whether the player character has at least 60 approval with her, Jaheira may either keep the scroll or burn it. If she decides to keep the scroll, the player character may try to speak with her about it again at a later point after her approval has increased. Retirement from the Harpers [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheria's appearance if she retires If the player character has sufficient approval, she decides to burn the scroll, feeling that Baldur's Gate is in safe hands. She retires from the Harpers and settles down as a stay-at-home mother. When spoken with at the reunion celebration, Jaheira shares that she has done much more sitting down than she would like, but has been heavily involved in the lives of her children, who have proven themselves capable of restoring the city on their own. She confesses that she misses adventuring and that Baldur's Gate is, in fact, her home, but she remarks on how one only realises someplace is home once they leave it and look back. Remaining the High Harper [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character did not convince Jaheira to retire, she keeps the scroll, which allows her to extend her life further, as she feels she is not done protecting Baldur's Gate yet from the Dead Three. When spoken with at the reunion celebration, Jaheira states that she has to house people and rebuild the Harper network; she has little love for Baldur's Gate, but she chose to keep serving the city for her family. Other dialogue at the reunion party [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character speaks with Jaheira during the reunion celebration, regardless of ending, Jaheira talks of Baldur's Gate's reconstruction efforts and the roles her children, the Harpers and Minsc, have to play in it. She reveals that Jord has joined the Harpers and is planning crop cycles in Wyrm's Crossing. Rion has temporarily joined the Flaming Fist , but she mostly spends her time incarcerating corrupt Fists. If the player character asks her if they may join the Harpers, she always agrees, even if they are a mind flayer; otherwise, she asks the player character what "home" means to them. She then either teases or comforts the player character based on their response before dismissing herself to ensure no one tampers with the drinks. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira has Speak with Dead dialogue that unfolds depending on events that have passed: Who are you? Jaheira Harper... Jaheira... What happened to you? Jaheira Stood... against... Bhaal...  (if witnessed the player accept Bhaal) Jaheira Stood... against... Absolute... Did you find Minsc? Jaheira Too... far... gone... What were you doing? Jaheira Hunting... Absolute... hunted... in turn...  (if in Act Two) Jaheira What... needed... to be done...  (if witnessed the player accept Bhaal) Jaheira Helping... a friend... What should I tell your family? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* I saw you with Minsc in the Counting House - what happened? Jaheira Shape... shifter... sworn to... Orin... Any regrets in life? Jaheira ...HAH!... How do I save the city? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. Her face in Baldur's Gate 3 matches her portrait from Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn . Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaheira is supposed to turn hostile whenever Isobel is attacked by a playable character in Moonrise Towers . However, because the game does not check the source of the attack, Jaheira turns hostile whenever Isobel is harmed or takes damage from any source after defeating Ketheric on the Moonrise Towers Rooftop (e.g., walking over Caustic Brine set by Absolute Zealots when entering Moonrise Towers after Ketheric is killed). If Jaheria is recruited, a bug may manifest which causes her to, in many respects, not be considered a party member (or even an ally), though she remains fully controllable as one. It can trigger as early as her being recruited after the party return to Moonrise Towers from the final defeat of Ketheric Thorm. The bug appears to make Jaheira almost always remain a neutral non-combatant, even when she clearly should not remain so, and all other party members are scripted or flagged to enter combat. Once activated, this "neutral flag" remains until she makes an attack, which commits her to turn-based combat mode. The following are some detailed examples of the effects of this bug: Spells targeting allies cannot be cast on her (in case of target selection) or do not include her (in case of AoE party buffs) unless she is the one casting the spell. Enemies usually do not consider her a member of the party and thus ignore her, and allow her to remain out of combat, unless she herself attacks. She remains free to roam these areas, interact with objects there, and cast non-combat spells while otherwise avoiding combat. If the other party members enter turn-based combat automatically due to starting a conflict, she remains out of combat unless she was the one starting the conflict. If the party enter an area where conflict automatically starts against them (e.g., the Ancient Lair or the Counting House High Security Vaults ), she remains out of combat unless she attacks. If a scripted event that begins combat specifically designates Jaheira as a target, as with Sarevok Anchev at the Murder Tribunal , then she enters combat as normal. If Jaheira is not in combat, she can make a single attack against creatures under the effect of Sanctuary . If the other party members are in combat while Jaheira is not, and she then stealthily attacks, passes the required checks to remain hidden, and lands a killing blow on her first attack, she remains out of combat. This makes her an ideal candidate to respec as a high-level rogue and use sneak attacks to finish off sufficiently weakened opponents, while the rest of the party remains in turn-based combat. The Ancient Lair exhibits further unusual behaviour: If Jaheira is alone there (an area where combat begins automatically) and she attacks in stealth mode while passing the required Stealth checks to remain hidden, she can then immediately leave stealth without consequence; the opponents there will continue to ignore her and search for the assailant, even if she is right next to them. This behaviour usually does not manifest elsewhere. However, if Jaheira attacks at a close enough range where the target (if they survive) or others notice the attack, combat then begins for her as normal. If Jaheira kills an opponent out of combat (even while the rest of the party are fighting the same targets), it is treated as a crime by – for example – the Flaming Fist . Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Unlike other companions, Jaheira and Minsc were revealed in a trailer at the Video Game Awards 2022. ↑ In previous games, she was a Fighter/Druid multiclass under the D&D 2e ruleset. ↑ If spoken with at camp during Act Three about rescuing Minsc, Jaheira mentions how he stood petrified as a monument in Baldur's Gate for over a century before being serendipitously freed, and that before being freed, she visited him to reflect on old friends and the fights ahead, adding, "And during all my self-serious brooding that big, dumb, insufferable buffoon was staring me in the face." The player character can respond by observing, "You have to admit, that's a little funny," earning her approval and a sly retort. ↑ After the player character is released from Jaheira's vines and interrogation upon entering the Last Light Inn , she says, "I'll not pretend to understand what that artefact is, but I'm old and wise enough to recognise a sliver of hope when it crawls out of the dark." and then asks, "Tell me, why have you come here?" Answering with, "I'm here on holiday," earns the reply, "You're just in time for Happy Hour," and approval is earned. ↑ If Jaheira is present in the basement of the Counting House after her doppelganger departs and the party is victorious, she can be spoken with, admitting, "I grow tired of these false faces. Every corner we turn, another - and now it is 'my' face they use to turn Minsc against us. I am sorry, but... I am just tired." The player character can respond with, "Of course you're tired - you're 'ancient'. But we still have work to do." Jaheira then bursts out in approving laughter, "...Ha. Hahahahahahaha." Then, realising the truth behind the joke, adds half seriously, "Bastard." ↑ Possible examples of Jaheira expressing concerns include immediately after meeting her doppelganger , who is manipulating Minsc, in the Counting House and after reading the Rite of the Timeless Body in her home . ↑ Jaheira has multiple references to her past in her voice lines , such as "Nature's servant awaits". Having her in the party during Act Three offers many unique interactions which heavily reference the prior Baldur's Gate games. ↑ If she has been recruited to the party, the player character can have an illuminating conversation with Jaheira after reading her scroll Rite of the Timeless Body in her sanctuary in Act Three . Similarly, she reminisces about her husband after the player character picks up Khalid's Gift . ↑ Comments of the companions concerning Jaheira: Astarion: "The name sounds familiar - I hope we didn't meet on one of my little excursions." Gale: "Hmmm, that name doesn't ring a bell." Lae'zel: "I'm not familiar with that name. A Harper leader, perhaps." Karlach: "Hang on... High Harper Jaheira?! Saviour of Baldur's Gate? Incredible." Shadowheart: "Jaheira? Can't say I know the name." Wyll: "The name sounds familiar. A Harper leader, if I recall." ↑ In the cutscene with Jaheira, the player character is ensnared in her vines as she interrogates them. This entanglement is unavoidable, regardless of any spell used or item equipped. While a player character (and the entire party) may avoid the cutscene by, for example, sneaking into the Last Light Inn , its occupants become hostile if an intruder is discovered and Jaheira is not first spoken with at the inn's entrance. ↑ The only other Harper seen to personally hold a Mind Flayer tadpole to check for potentially infected people is Arthus . However, like Arthus, the Mind Flayer Parasite mentioned in her conversation is for plot purposes only; if Jaheira is killed, no tadpole is in her inventory. ↑ Before going into Moonrise Towers , she quotes Alaundo the Seer (...so sayeth the wise Alaundo) . His prophecy was a central point in the first Baldur's Gate game. EQP_Jaheira_Not Gozz , disguised as ' Jaheira' in-game, is a doppelganger pretending to be Jaheira to fool tadpoled Minsc into obedience. Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] During the ⁠ The High Harper quest, the party can go to the Counting House in hopes of catching up to Minsc. Inside the vaults, the party witnesses Minsc emerge from a Mimic and defeat it. 'Jaheira' then appears with a handful of Bhaalists and teleports away with Minsc, leaving the cultists to deal with the party. If the real Jaheira is in the party then 'Jaheira' calls her a fake and a shapeshifter. After finding Minsc again in the Abandoned Cistern , he refuses to see reason since his tadpole is still controlling him and he is confused by 'Jaheira'. Minsc believes the real Jaheira to be fake or an "uglier sister". When 'Jaheira' is killed during the ensuing conflict, Minsc cries out in rage, believing the real Jaheira has died. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Janina is buried in the Graveyard (Lower City) in the Lower City . She was one of the victims of the serial killer Dolor . Her child Billyum is aside her grave mourning. The Diary which is also in Janina's grave (apparently written by her) says she was overwhelmed by the household routine and tried to run away from it. She seems to have chosen the wrong companion for the endeavour. MOO_Cultist Questioner Jasin is charged with interrogating prisoners in Moonrise Towers Prison with Sumera during Act Two . “ Plant one foot in front of the other. Head forward, back straight. Make them fear you. „ — Jasin Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Torturing Minthara [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Decide Minthara's Fate If Minthara is present in the prison, Jasin can be found alongside her sister, Questioner Sumera , working to break Minthara's mind. Without Minthara [ edit section | visual editor ] If Minthara did not survive Act One, Jasin is still found in the prison. She wonders aloud to Sumera when they will get new "playthings." Defending Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Nightsong is freed and the Harpers launch the assault on Moonrise Towers, Jasin is killed and her body can be found amongst the dead bodies on the entrance bridge. Nightwarden Minthara Minthara Baenre. Questioner Sumera We will take it from you soon. Nightwarden Minthara Queen of Spiders, I beseech of you the strength to destroy my foes. Questioner Sumera Lolth cannot hear you. She has forsaken you. Questioner Jasin There are no gods left to you, Minthara. You are alone. Questioner Sumera You are despised, Minthara. Questioner Jasin A blemish in the Absolute's design. Questioner Sumera We will cleanse you. Questioner Jasin How can you hope to resist the voice of a god? Nightwarden Minthara It is no god. Technical UID S_LOW_HagSurvivors_HagSpy UUID 0cb0a73b-1f97-4481-b320-b8fff88cfe0f Stats LOW_HagsSurvivors_Jatlo Jatlo (dragonborn disguise) In-game Model Portrait Stats Type Humanoid Race Dragonborn Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Initiative +3 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 18 (+4) 16 (+3) 18 (+4) 10 (0) 12 (+1) 9 (-1) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA +4 +3 +4 0 +1 -1 Technical UID S_LOW_HagSurvivors_HagSpyDisguise UUID 81c1f9dc-e942-492f-a105-a2d28648cfa3 Stats Dragonborn_Melee Jatlo is a redcap disguised as a dragonborn, who resides in Old Garlow's Place in the Lower City . He is a member of the Anti-Hag Support Group . “ Well aren't you a clever one, scale-pest. Faster than these idiots, at least. They mean to hurt Auntie - the best and most beautiful hag in the Realms. „ — Jatlo Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Jatlo is in Old Garlow's Place, where he is working with a group of hag survivors. Their leader, Mayrina has been polymorphed into a sheep. After Mayrina's curse is lifted, she exclaims that Jatlo was the one who cursed her. If Jatlo is confronted, he drops his ruse and reveals himself as a servant of the hag and a Redcap . He also reverts back to his Redcap form if he is simply attacked. If the party gets into a fight with the hag survivors before discovering Jatlo's identity, or if they fail to persuade the group, hitting Jatlo causes him to revert to his Redcap form. The other hag survivors become hostile towards him and ally with the party. If Auntie Ethel is killed before meeting any of the hag survivors, Jatlo will already be dead, having killed himself when Ethel died. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_WineFestivalCivilian002 UUID 4396e623-f09b-4599-91f3-63900a0c3382 Stats HalfOrc_Commoner Jaycen Borgu is a half-orc wine taster. She is at the Wine Festival at Highberry's Home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ You know, festivals like this give me a bit of hope. Everyone's so happy. „ — Jaycen Borgu moments before disaster Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaycen mingles among the patrons of the wine festival if the party began ⁠ Investigate the Murders and the wine festival takes place. After Dolor reveals himself and attempts to kill Cora Highberry , Jaycen runs off and is not seen again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Jaycen occasionally chats with 'Zinfandel' Gorse and Dave Hosmo . Dave Hosmo Quite the turnout, don't you think? 'Zinfandel' Gorse You should've seen the cheese festival last year. Jaycen Borgu The streets were packed. The stench was... potent. Jaycen Borgu This is a welcome distraction from all the war talk. Dave Hosmo No, we're being too lax right now. 'Zinfandel' Gorse What do you mean? Dave Hosmo Refugees, wine festivals, we're wasting our resources. 'Zinfandel' Gorse I can't help but notice you're drinking anyway, Dave. Dave Hosmo Well, if the wine's here already, I might as well drink it. 'Zinfandel' Gorse So you think they shouldn't bring any more wine? That right? Dave Hosmo I mean, I didn't say that... Jaycen Borgu I wish you hadn't said anything. Dave Hosmo I just think we shouldn't be letting our guard down. Jaycen Borgu Why not? It's good to relax. Dave Hosmo These refugees are killers, apparently. And they're everywhere. 'Zinfandel' Gorse The only killer around here is going to be your hangover tomorrow, Dave. ## Jelliwig
- **来源**: [Jelliwig](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Jelliwig)
- **分类**: Characters

Jelliwig In-game Portrait Voice / Actor David Alwyn Hometown Baldur's Mouth Basement , Baldur's Gate Occupation Printing press Stats Race Pixie Jelliwig is a pixie who runs the printing press for the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . “ I am no chattering contraption, I am a person. An artist . Name's Jelliwig. „ — Jelliwig Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Stop the Presses Jelliwig can be found in the Baldur's Mouth Basement in the Lower City , Baldur's Gate . To finish ⁠ Stop the Presses , the Jelliwig must be convinced to change the negative article which is going to be printed about the party. While trying to switch out the article block in the printing press, the press begins to speak with the party. If asked about their art or if they are a talking printer, they introduce themselves as Jelliwig. If the party freed Dolly Dolly Dolly during Act Two , Jelliwig immediately wishes to help them. Otherwise, they must be persuaded. If successful, Jelliwig tells the party to look for a neutral or favorable article to swap out for the negative one that is going to be printed about them tomorrow. DEN_DruidServant Jeorna guards the entrance to the Sacred Pool in the Emerald Grove during Act One . “ You're testing my patience. Leave, unless you want to see my other face. „ — Jeorna Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Jeorna is tasked with guarding the Rite of Thorns from interference. This ritual will seal the Grove from outsiders, forcing the tiefling refugees into the Wilderness to fend for themselves. If Kagha is persuaded to turn against the shadow druids, Jeorna sits just outside the entrance to the Inner Sanctum . If Minthara and her goblin hoard are ⁠ defeated , Jeorna then moves near the winch that operates the Overgrown Portcullis. Range: Self Wild Shape: Boar ( + ) Take the shape of a Boar . It has 11 hit points . While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. EQP_Spear_Chainmail_Shield_HelmetMetal_Fist Trs. BG_Guard Fist Jepsen is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is in Rivington in Act Three . “ Get moving, unless you want a belly full of steel. „ — Jepsen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Jepsen is stationed together with Fist Richter , Fist Mîran , Gauntlet Edwynna and a Steel Watcher at the South Span Checkpoint . They guard the actual entrance to the Wyrm's Crossing , preventing refugees from entering Baldur's Gate through it. Jepsen is reluctant to discuss anything with the party, sending them to the Gauntlet to discuss whatever they want. If a party member gains access to Wyrm's Crossing with the help of Ironhand gnomes, Jepsen chases them (to no avail) together with Fist Richter to the wooden footway edge where Manip Falcäo stands, and remains there for some time, trying to suss out the gnomes. After gaining access to Wyrm's Crossing (by any means) and taking a long rest, Jepsen treats the party as citizens eligible to cross the checkpoint in any direction. Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_BaldursMouth_FF_001 UUID 6fdc06e0-9c81-4853-9a08-f9d3ebf5a0eb Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Jerbold is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in the streets of Lower City in Act Three. “ No, we're not censoring the Mouth - we're simply doing a routine inspection. And no, I cannot sell you a copy. „ — Jerbold Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Jerbold is watching over several employees of the Baldur's Mouth , accompanied by Fist Glenvora and a Steel Watcher . They can be found near the entrance to the building at X: -12 Y: -51 , guarding Trina , Zita , Falael , Bronte , Delcan and Jarlath , who are counting, packing and loading freshly printed issues of Baldur's Mouth Gazette . Jerbold occasionally chats with Trina, who is working closest to his post. If the player character speaks to him, Jerbold orders them to be on their way, preemptively denying charges in the Fist censoring the newspaper. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Jerbold is found trying to placate Korrinna Koreena and Flo Hurlburl , who are worried about their safety now that the Steel Watch is fallen. UND_Duergar_Generic Jerris is a duergar ranger who is a part of Corsair Greymon's crew in the Underdark during Act One . “ One wrong move, and you're goin' in the lake. „ — Jerris Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] After boarding the boat from the Underdark beach, a boat captained by Corsair Greymon sails up alongside the party's boat. Greymon comes aboard, and the player character must pass a check to convince him to let the party through to Grymforge . If they fail the check, or choose violence, Greymon attacks and Jerris joins the battle on his side. UND_KC_ExecutedDrow_Random Jhaam , named in-game as Executed Drow , is a dead drow [ 1 ] and Harper in Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Jhaam's corpse is in Grymforge in one of the cages near Murmath at X: -632 Y: 388 . She was sent by Jaheira to investigate rumours of ⁠ Absolutist activity in Grymforge as well as find out what they "might seek amidst the ruins" . [ 2 ] Jhaam had orders to bring word of the cult's deeds back to Last Light Inn , but she was caught and killed by Murmath . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Creased Letter Engraved Pin Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Creased Letter Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Jhaan's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Executed Drow Jhaam... Harper scout... What were you doing here? Executed Drow Cultists... threat to Baldur's Gate... Jaheira's orders... What happened to you? Executed Drow Caught... interrogated... hanged... Who killed you? Executed Drow Duergar cultist... True Soul's command... Where are you from? Executed Drow Last Light... safe haven... in shadows... What is your profession? Executed Drow Scout... Harper... Where are your valuables? Executed Drow Have... none... Technical UID S_LOW_DeadOfNight_FlamingFist UUID 7f9e4158-f16e-4ac5-a4c6-0e718a9ec326 Stats FlamingFist_Dwarf_Melee_Attacker Fist Jimi Borleas is a dwarven fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in the streets of Lower City in Act Three . “ What do you want me to do? Arrest a smell? „ — Jimi Borleas , to the gnome bidder Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Jimi Borleas is patrolling the streets in the Heapside District of Baldur's Gate . He is standing near Philgrave's Mansion , across the back entrance to the Felogyr's Fireworks , and is talking to Battrick Degronce , a citizen reporting to him of suspicious activity and foul smell spreading around the mansion. However, Jimi does not actually want to investigate the complaint, preferring to find an easy and convenient explanation to talk the gnome down. If spoken to, Jimi Borleas takes the player character for yet another bidder on the same issue, and reacts accordingly – trying to placate them, too. Battrick Degronce I don't rightly know. But they was up to no good, lurching this way and that. Fist Jimi Borleas Walking funny isn't a crime. Battrick Degronce What about the smell? Nothing to concern yourself with. „ — Jitters Corbwell Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Jitters Corbwell and Pythonicus are in an alley near the entrance of Candulhallow's Tombstones . They speak in hushed voices. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Jitters Corbwell You want how much? It was half a tenday ago. Pythonicus We've had supply issues. You got a problem - take it up with Nine-Fingers . She loves it when people complain. Even better when she gets to shut them up. Pythonicus How 'bout this? You hand over everything you've got on you, and I'll give you three ounces. Jitters Corbwell But - but - that's twice what you just said. Pythonicus I'm doing you a favour. You don't want it - it's no scales off my back. Jitters Corbwell I could pay half now, and half tomorrow. Pythonicus Do I look like I was born in a bathtub? If you can't afford it, stop wasting my time. v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag Support Group Adrielle Hydrangea Wubb Jatlo Kled Mayrina Baldur's Mouth Gazette Baalfe Baz Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Acid Splash ( ) Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Acid Throw a bubble of acid that damages each creature it hits. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Eldritch Blast ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Force Conjure a beam of crackling energy. Deals 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to a target. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fear ( + ) Hostile targets drop everything and become Fearful : they have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls . If the target ends their turn where they can't see you, they can make another Saving throw to shake off their fear. WIS Save Range: Self Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Shatter ( + ) Damage: 3~24 3d8 ⁠ Thunder Damages all nearby creatures and objects. Creatures made of inorganic material such as stone have Disadvantage on their Saving throw . CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Aideen Ni Chuirc Hiero Lue Inku Neza Maggie Ni Chuirc Ulumpha Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Dagger Simple Robe Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Aideen Ni Chuirc Since you're all too cowardly to say it, I will - what if the Steel Watch storm this place? Hiero Lue We run for our lives - I'm not dancing with one of those murder machines. Jivin Mizzrym What if some strays decide to take refuge here? Or worse, the owners? Maggie Ni Chuirc We kill them. Obviously. Aideen Ni Chuirc We are in agreement. Anyone who sets foot in here? They die - swiftly and silently. Maggie Ni Chuirc This place is a dump. Hiero Lue I'm sorry, your highness. I didn't know you shat on a throne of gold? Aideen Ni Chuirc Cease your squabbling - the Steel Watch are onto us. We need a plan. Maggie Ni Chuirc I say we hole up here - let things cool down a bit. Jivin Mizzrym For once, I agree with the luddite. This 'dump' is a perfect hideout. Maggie Ni Chuirc Any sign of the Watch? Hiero Lue The cheek of you asking that - they're only on our arses because of you! Maggie Ni Chuirc It wasn't me who blew our cover, it was the bloody warlock. Jivin Mizzrym Me? A feral gnoll in the throes of mating is quieter than you, you blundering luddite! Aideen Ni Chuirc My friends, do you wish to bring a Steel Watcher down on our heads? HAG_Brother Johl is searching for his sister in the Sunlit Wetlands in Act One . “ She could shoot fireworks out of her backside for all I care; the hag has Rina. „ — Johl Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Johl and his brother Demir are at the east entrance to the Sunlit Wetlands, asking Auntie Ethel where she took their sister Mayrina . If the party interact with them, they learn that Mayrina disappeared and the last person to see her was Ethel. Throughout the encounter, Johl demands to know where Mayrina is and warns the party not to trust anything Ethel says. Ethel insists she has never met their sister but is willing to help look for her. The party have the choice of siding with Ethel to defend her, siding with the brothers, or refusing to get involved. If the party defend Ethel, Johl and Demir accuse them of working with her and attack. The brothers must be defeated, but their lives can be spared by toggling on Toggle Non-Lethal Attacks before landing a final blow. In this case, their corpses do not appear in the swamp, and the party can later tell Mayrina that her brothers were merely knocked unconscious. However, due to what appears to be an oversight in the game's dialogue files, she still cries out as if they are dead, and the quest journal receives the same entry as when she is told of their death. If the party side with the brothers, Ethel chastises them and disappears in a burst of magic. The party can attempt to convince the two brothers not to pursue her into the swamp. While Demir is willing to take the party's advice if they offer to look for Mayrina instead, Johl refuses and drags his brother into the wetlands with him. In this case they die, and their bodies appear later in the wetlands. If their bodies are not found, Ethel may later claim that she sent them off to "Sutton Farm" north of Baldur's Gate, but voice actor notes in the dialogue files reveal that this is a lie and confirm that she has killed them. If the party refuse to get involved during the initial confrontation between Ethel and the brothers, they are killed on the spot by Ethel with a poison spell. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Letter from Mayrina Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Save Mayrina Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Johl's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Johl Johl... cattle... farmer. How did you die? Johl Looked so... innocent. But the teeth... How did you plan on killing this hag? Johl With pitchforks. Stupid... Maybe Mayrina wants to stay with Ethel? Johl Course... 'cause she promised... to bring Rina's husband ... back. But hags... lie... How do you know your sister is even here? Johl The... note... What drove your sister to leave? Johl She's scared she won't be... a good mum. But... she will. I know it... Is the food here safe to eat? Johl Apples... so red... so delicious but... ngh. I found Mayrina's note. Why didn't you stop her? Johl Tried. But Connor's death... was horrible. Guts... everywhere. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursMouth_PaperBoy_Docks UUID 7a5ba740-76cb-4c29-a190-ae7cb8658c81 Stats Human_Child News Hawker Jonah is a newspaper seller who can be found in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ 'The Baldur's Mouth Gazette. When the Mouth barks, the Fist bites...' Uh... I forget the real slogan, but you get the idea. Now, buy a copy or leave. „ — Jonah Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Jonah is posted at a bridge in Lower City near X: -200 Y: -41 . He is very reluctant to sell copies of the Baldur's Gate Gazette , referring to it as a rag. If asked, he informs the party that his father forces him to work as a news hawker. The party can persuade Jonah to relinquish a free copy of the gazette, but he becomes annoyed and accuses the player character of being a "cheap bastard". Technical UID S_LOW_JaheirasHouse_JaheirasEldestSon UUID ebfe9029-2a74-40eb-bbd1-8e5d0ec8fe1f Stats LOW_JaheirasEldestSon Jord is a half-orc druid in the Lower City in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I just let it... thrive in its own independence. You know, same way you raised us. „ — Jord , describing his approach to horticulture Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Jord is Jaheira's adoptive son. He lives in what is now Elerrathin's Home along with Jaheira's other children. Jaheira took Jord in as a ward when he was nine years old after a confrontation with a merchant. In her absence, Jord watched over Jaheira's plants, letting those in her study grow unimpeded. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Flame Blade ( + ) Conjure a flaming Scimitar in your hand for 10 turns that deals 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. It sheds a bright light in a 3 m (10 ft) radius and a dim light in a 6 m (20 ft) radius. The blade can be unequipped and equipped again, but must stay on the spellcaster's person. Range: Self Hold Person ( + ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't Move , Act , or React . Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Poison Spray ( ) Damage: 1~12 1d12 ⁠ Poison Project a puff of noxious gas, dealing 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Poison to a target. CON Save Range: 3 m (10 ft) Wild Shape: Fire Myrmidon ( + 2 ) Take the shape of a Fire Myrmidon. Your fire myrmidon shape has a starting health of 90 hit points that increases every two druid levels. It can cast Scorching Strike , Myrmidon's Immolation , and Cinderous Swipe . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Rion Where's the boy got to, Jord? Jord The boy is upstairs. The girls were a little rough in their play earlier. Rion Chauntea's cheeks, I told them to give him space. That's two volunteers for dishes later, then. Rion Throw some cabbage on your list for the market, Jord. Jord You know I could just grow it myself. Even a lowly apprentice can manage that much. Rion I know you can, brother. Just being careful - don't want the young ones going all weird from eating mystical greens. Jord What do you mean, 'weird' ? Rion Well. Fig . Jord Ah. Fig. Yeah, fair enough. Jord Telk says they shut the Church of Last Hope down. Rion And how did Telk see that, through the bottom of her drinking mug? Jord She was stone cold sober. Heard it from Mother Aramina herself - the Steel Watch said they were only 'encouraging the refugees into an unlawful gathering'. Rion Aye. A warm meal and a scrap of rags to sleep on must be very encouraging. Well, the mother knows - Jord That we have space to spare if she needs it. Aye, I passed it on. Technical Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Justiciar Justiciar Crusader is a generic title and archetype given to powerful warriors who serve Shar . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Two Justiciar Crusaders are in the Cloister of Sombre Embrace . Despite the similar name, they have different statistics, passives, and abilities from the Undead Justiciar Crusader enemy found in the Gauntlet of Shar . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Justiciar Crusaders use Subsume Shadow to enter Umbral Form , empowering their attacks with an extra 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic and making them immune to non-magical damage. This lasts until death. Although the Umbral Form passive grants an extra attack, this does not stack with their existing Extra Attack . Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayDisappointment_Civilian2 UUID 01d599a4-58f1-4da4-ace2-92faabc417f2 Stats Human_Commoner Porter Juxon is a human civilian upset at the propaganda being peddled by the Baldur's Mouth Gazette in the Lower City during Act Three . “ I just wish it was as safe behind the walls as the Gazette says it is... „ — Juxon Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Juxon confronts Fist Ernestus alongside Bliggerillo , Saer Frunilla , and Wuloona Dor about the contents of the latest issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . The paper claims that everyone is safe in Baldur's Gate but he does not believe it. If Gortash is defeated, Juxon, Ernestus, and the rest of the civilians disperse, not to be seen again. Juxon's attitude towards the party changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Wuloona Dor You see the latest issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette? Streets are safer than they've even been, apparently. Wuloona Dor Not a word on all the thefts and murders happening right on our doorsteps! Porter Juxon Nowhere's safe any more, no matter how many Steel Watchers Lord Gortash tries to jam down our throats. Wuloona Dor If you ask me, I don't think Gortash even deserves to be called a lord. Fist Ernestus That's enough of that! Lord Gortash has everything under control - we don't need agitators like you ruining morale. Wuloona Dor What are you gonna do? Arrest us? Fist Ernestus If that what it takes to keep the peace! Wuloona Dor If you say so, mate. Porter Juxon Why would they go to all that effort just to lie to us? Wuloona Dor It's obvious, isn't it? To placate us. To keep us all nice and obedient. Wuloona Dor They don't like it when we think too much - we might question their authority. Fist Ernestus I'm warning you... Porter Juxon There's one of you and four of us - do you really think you can take all of us at once? Fist Ernestus I... I can go and get back up. Wuloona Dor And do you think we're just gonna sit here and wait for you and your hog friends to come back and arrest us? Fist Ernestus Look, I'm just trying to do my job, all right? Porter Juxon So what can we do about it? All the lies they're publishing, I mean. Wuloona Dor Not a lot unless you want to set fire to the Baldur's Mouth Gazette headquarters. Fist Ernestus I'm still right here, you know... Wuloona Dor Tch, we do know, thank you - we just don't care. Wuloona Dor Besides, I don't think that'd achieve much in the long run. The problem's at the top - it always is. Porter Juxon Perhaps sending a strongly worded letter would be a good place to start? Wuloona Dor If by 'strongly worded letter' you mean a brick through a window, then aye. Porter Juxon I'm just not one for violence, you see... Wuloona Dor You'd better start acquiring a taste for it - it's only gonna get worse from here on out. v t e Baldur's Mouth Characters Flaming Fists Ernestus Glenvora Jerbold Guards Baalfe Hertvor Dremble Inocente Bramm Unilda Tiro Vlomina Wulf Outside Augur Harxkellan Bliggerillo Flant Borlley Flo Hurlburl Frothilda Frunilla Grent Grintly 'Gunny' Sacko Korrinna Koreena Juxon Lockhorn Lolo Fuzzletoes Manzarde Muttonchops Dorryss Phyria Gollus 'Plumes' Fronkin Sadar Illanov Trina Wuloona Dor Staff Bronte Delcan Ettvard Needle Falael Glimmer Whistleborn Jarlath Jelliwig Malek Stones Salene Freig Syril Valdemar Ty Willowbrook Zita Locations Newsroom Basement Quests Stop the Presses

Evasion Successful DEX saves nullify damage; failed DEX saves reduce it by half. Extra Attack Can make an additional attack after an unarmed or weapon attack. Ki-Empowered Strikes Your unarmed attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming enemies' Resistance and Immunity to non-magical damage. Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike After making an attack with a melee Monk weapon or while unarmed, you can make another unarmed attack as a bonus action. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Psionic Empowerment Your attacks deal an extra 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage - the scars of illithid enslavement run deep. Slow Fall When you fall, you can use your reaction to gain Resistance to Falling damage. Stillness of Mind If Charmed or Frightened , automatically cast Stillness of Mind to remove them. Unarmoured Defence Your reflexes are as effective as any armour . While not wearing armour, you add your Wisdom Modifier to your Armour Class . Technical UID S_DEN_DruidLeader UUID 95eb2b0b-a522-4ea5-8167-c5f4d1418156 Stats DEN_ShadowDruid_Boss Eqp. DEN_Kagha Trs. DEN_DruidLeader Kagha is a wood elven druid in the Emerald Grove during Act One . She was Halsin's Second Druid, but has named herself First Druid in his absence. She started the Rite of Thorns to seal the Grove off, no matter the consequences. “ A viper bares her fangs defending her brood. Is it not her nature to strike at invaders? „ — Kagha , defending her actions Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Personality 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.1.1 Saving Arabella 2.1.2 Investigate Kagha 2.1.3 Kagha's fate 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Allies 3.3 Loot 4 Related literature 5 Related quests 6 Speak with Dead 7 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Kagha is willing to take drastic action to prove her authority over the Emerald Grove. She views the tiefling refugees as parasites and refers to them as devils and a rot to be cleansed. Kagha justifies her violent actions as those of a watchful broodmother. As such, Kagha admires drow and duergar for their culture of aggressive self-preservation. If the player character is a drow or duergar, she approves of their presence, calling it a gift. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Zevlor requests the party's aid on dealing with the acting Archdruid of the Grove, Kagha. He explains that she and the other druids are preparing a ritual to seal off the Grove from the rest of the world, endangering the tiefling refugees. Saving Arabella [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon entering the Inner Sanctum for the first time, the party finds Kagha reprimanding a tiefling child named Arabella for attempting to steal the Idol of Silvanus . The party and another druid, Rath , can intervene to ⁠ save her . If the player character fails to persuade Kagha or decides to not intervene, Arabella attempts to run, and Kagha's snake Teela bites her, killing her instantly. [ 1 ] Investigate Kagha [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can investigate and eventually confront Kagha. This must be done before Halsin is rescued from the Goblin Camp . Otherwise, the quest is cancelled early. Kagha's personal chest is hidden in a corner of the sanctum. Lockpicking it reveals a letter which advances ⁠ Investigate Kagha and guides the party to a covert location in the Swamp, where they can learn Kagha is secretly planning to offer control of the Grove to the Shadow Druids of Cloakwood. If the party returns and confronts Kagha about her plan, the Shadow Druids led by Olodan reveal themselves and order Kagha to attack the party and everyone else in the Sanctum. Telling Kagha that the party will not stay in her way is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of any Oath subclass . Kagha contemplates the error of her ways after helping the party defeat the Shadow Druids. The party can persuade Kagha to see her wrongs and instead side with the Grove's druids. This can be done by passing a number of Persuasion and Religion checks, or by having previoulsy read all of the frescos surrounding the sanctum. Doing so grants the ⁠ A Story for the Ages to characters with the Entertainer background. If Kagha survives, she shows remorse for her actions, thanks the party and allows the tieflings to remain in the Grove for as long as they need. If the player character is a druid, she bestows them the title of Faithwarden and gifts them Pale Oak . If the Shadow Druids are killed before confronting Kagha, she does not abandon her plans but remains neutral (non-hostile) and does not order the tieflings to be killed. The druids and tieflings in the grove then behave as if Kagha was defeated. Any remaining druids stop their ritual and sit dejectedly; Amek , Xeph and Rechel then come down into the grove to gawk as normal. Kagha's fate [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party does not kill Kagha themselves, her fate depends largely on whether she was persuaded to turn against the shadow druids, and whether Arabella died in her custody. Kagha repented Arabella lives, her parents live Halsin allows Kagha to remain in the Grove, however she is demoted to novice. If the party returns to the area later in Act One, she stands on the path overlooking the grove -- near where Zevlor and Aradin fought when the party first arrived.) Arabella died, her parents live Halsin leaves her fate in Locke and Komira's hands. They attempt to poison Kagha at the party, which kills her unless the party intervene. If the party can convince Locke and Komira to spare Kagha, the poison can be cured (e.g., with Lesser Restoration). Kagha thanks the party profusely and vows to improve herself. Kagha did not repent Arabella died, her parents live Halsin leaves her fate in Locke and Komira's hands. They attempt to poison Kagha at the party, which kills her unless a party member intervenes. If the player character convinces Locke and Komira to spare Kagha, the poison can be cured (e.g., with Lesser Restoration). Kagha then thanks the player character profusely and vows to improve herself. Arabella and her Parents died Kagha is exiled from the Emerald Grove, and all Groves of Silvanus . Convinced to let Arabella go earlier Kagha is demoted to the most junior rank of druid Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Kagha has an ability kit similar to a Level 5 druid , including the ability to cast spells using Level 3 Spell Slots . [ 2 ] Cure Wounds ( + ) Healing: 1~8 + modifiers 1d8 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Healing Heal a creature you can touch. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Heat Metal ( + ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Fire Cause a metal weapon or armour to glow red-hot and force the wearer to let go or receive Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks . If the creature is only wearing metal armour, it always receives Disadvantage. If the creature is still touching the metal, you can use a bonus action on subsequent turns to deal another 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire and force the creature to let go or receive Disadvantage. The dire wolf has a starting health of 18 hit points that increase every two druid levels. While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. You take on the attributes of your beast form - excluding your Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma scores. When your beast form drops to 0 hit points , you revert to your normal form. DEN_Refugee Kaldani is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . She overlooks the area in front of the grove's entrance from atop the gate. “ Aradin's back with his tail between his legs. I'm glad for your help, but I'd hoped you were Halsin. „ — Kaldani , welcoming the party to the Grove Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Kaldani guards the gate at the Emerald Grove. If a party member interacts with her, she comments that she had hoped they were Halsin instead. If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving Kagha's ritual the Rite of Thorns , the tieflings are expelled from the Emerald Grove and Kaldani's corpse is among the pile of refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Kaldani survives through Act One, her murdered body is in the Shadow-Cursed Lands X: -9 Y: 54 among the tiefling refugees who did not make it to the Last Light Inn . Let's not add to the problem. „ — Kali Hammerhand Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Kali and Neno Quilltop are shopping for supplies in Wyrm's Crossing after the Absolute's failed assault on Rivington . Kali attempts to calm Neno from panic shopping and to purchase only necessities. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Kali and Neno can be heard deciding on their purchases. Neno Quilltop Apples, loaves, butter - honey! We should stock up. Kali Hammerhand Honey is a luxury. We don't need honey. Neno Quilltop But I love honey. I love honey so much. Kali Hammerhand Woah, slow down, sweetie. Take a deep breath for me, yeah? Kali Hammerhand Ten loaves of bread? Are you sure? Neno Quilltop The neighbours said they had fifteen! Kali Hammerhand The neighbours are talking out of their arses. Besides our pantry is full . Neno Quilltop What if there's food shortages? Rationing? We can't leave anything to chance! Kali Hammerhand If it'll make you feel better, then fine - fifteen loaves it is. Neno Quilltop We should hit Rivington next - they might have something we've forgotten. Kali Hammerhand Like what? Neno Quilltop I don't know - but I'll know it when I see it! Kali Hammerhand Let's just stick to the list. Neno Quilltop If the Absolute's armies lay siege, they won't care about a stupid list. We have to be prepared! DEN_Refugee Kanon was one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . He was responsible for opening the gate to the grove but lost his life to a volley of goblin arrows, to his sister Arka's dismay. He can be communed with using Speak with Dead . “ .. killed... arrow... can't... breathe... „ — Kanon , on his recent encounter with goblins Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Little is known of Kanon due to his untimely death. However, his surviving sister Arka reveals he would disapprove of her killing Sazza. Arka carries Kanon's Handkerchief with her. It is also revealed through Rikka's prayer for Kanon that he was her confidant when she felt homesick. Despite never showing it, Rikka believes that he must have felt similarly. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act One, Kanon attempts to open the Emerald Grove's gate for Aradin , Barth , and Remira but is mortally struck by multiple goblin arrows. Shortly after the battle, his corpse is along the ramparts. The party can commune with him using Speak with Dead . Kanon's corpse is later buried in the grove at X: 175 Y: 445 . His belongings are nearby. If Minthara's raiding party is defeated at the gate, or if the goblins' leaders are killed, Arka and Memnos move to his grave, with Arka saying he has been avenged, and Memnos mentioning that Kanon would be proud of Arka. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who are you? Kanon ... Kanon... Where did you come from? Kanon ... I... we... from Elturel... left... Who left Elturel with you? Kanon ... sister... Arka... What is your profession? Kanon ...tailor before... guard... volunteered... What happened to you? Kanon ... killed... arrow... can't... breathe... Who killed you? Kanon ... there were... goblins... Aradin... followed... What were you doing when you were killed? Kanon ... guarding... gate... have... to open... Where do you keep your valuables? MOO_Cultist Kansif is a stoic and devoted member of the Cult of the Absolute encountered in Act Two . “ Don't you believe the Absolute will protect you? Or is your faith waning? „ — Kansif , to an Absolutist Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Follow the Convoy [ edit section | visual editor ] Kansif is initially found in the outskirts of the Ruined Battlefield , nearby the entrance from the Rosymorn Monastery Trail . He is a short jog away from the entry point, idly waiting for the arrival of a True Soul , and leading a small group of Absolutists composed of fellow half-orc Bedi , and the goblins Brawler Vez , Warrior Gronag , and Sharp-Eye Lora . Speaking with Kansif has him remark on the player character being a True Soul, and grants the opportunity to initiate ⁠ Follow the Convoy by playing the Spider's Lyre , which summons Kar'niss . The party can attack Kansif and the cultists, or follow the convoy to Moonrise Towers . Ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] Following the cultists takes them and the party through the Ruined Battlefield , where a nearby group of Harpers lay in wait to ambush the convoy in an attempt to acquire Kar'niss' Moonlantern . The Harpers immediately attack the convoy on sight, but momentarily give the party a chance to change sides and attack Kansif and the other cultists, which advances ⁠ Seek Protection from the Shadow Curse . Siding with Kansif allows the party to ⁠ Infiltrate Moonrise Towers , while siding with the Harpers leads to Kansif's death and has Branthos refer the party to Last Light Inn . Alternatively, if the party reach the Shadow-Cursed Lands through Grymforge , the party can encounter Kansif and his convoy for the first time mid-transit, with or without a Harper escort. The party can either ambush the convoy and seize the Moonlantern for themselves, let them pass, or convince Kar'niss to give them the Moonlantern. If they wait a little longer before attacking, Kar'niss slays Lora for venturing towards where the party and Harpers are hiding, to which Kansif calls for the drider to stop, to no avail. Convincing the cultists to part with the Moonlantern results in their walking into the Shadow Curse , only to be found later in the center of Reithwin as Shadow-Cursed Undead . They are automatically hostile to the party in this form and can only be fought. Arriving at Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party side with Kansif and he survives, Kansif arrives alongside the party at Moonrise Towers, where Kar'niss departs. Kansif remains in the towers' quarters, alongside Bedi and the goblins. Talking with Kansif lets him mention his mission to bring the party to Moonrise as successful, and his jokingly asking them to not forget him as they move up the ranks.
