SCL_Drider Kar'niss is a drider in service of the Absolute , whom he now serves after being cast out by Lolth, the Queen of Spiders . “ They must keep up. The shadows are hungry. „ — Kar'niss Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Kar'niss is a key character involved in the questline ⁠ Seek Protection from the Shadow Curse , since he carries a Moonlantern that holds the trapped pixie Dolly Dolly Dolly . He believes anyone who perishes to the Shadow Curse makes it stronger, and is starkly opposed to 'feeding' it. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Arriving from the Rosymorn Monastery Trail [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party arrive from the Rosymorn Monastery Trail a group of Absolute followers lead by Kansif are waiting for True Souls to arrive and summon the guide. The party can use a Spider's Lyre to summon Kar'niss, then ⁠ follow the convoy to Moonrise Towers . The party is then ambushed by the Harpers midway and has the choice to side with the convoy or the Harpers. Either choice leads to a combat encounter with the other group. Arriving from the Underdark [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party arrive from Grymforge and reach a large ruined building at X: 10 Y: -15 the convoy arrives without them and the Harpers are absent; the party can then reveal themselves or hide. If they stay hidden initially, Kar'niss murders Vez in anger as she is about to leave the light and feed the Shadow Curse further. If the party reveal themselves they can follow the convoy to Moonrise Towers without issue, attack the convoy or demand the Moonlantern for themselves. It is possible to avoid this scene by jumping up to a smaller ruined building along the eastern side and then reach Kansif, then summon the convoy as if they were arriving from the Monastery Trail. Once the party speak with Gronag , the caravan no longer triggers mid-transit without the Harpers. Harper ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] Finally the party may encounter Kar'niss' caravan mid-transit alongside the Harpers to ambush them and claim the lantern as part of a quest ⁠ Seek Protection from the Shadow Curse given by Jaheira at Last Light Inn . The party can choose to follow the convoy to Moonrise, kill Kar'niss and his followers to take his lantern, or convince him through dialogue to relinquish it and walk away to their deaths. Disarming Kar'niss causes him to drop the Moonlantern and grants the inspiration ⁠ Shiny Trinkets and Baubles to party members with the Criminal background. If Kar'niss and his convoy are convinced to leave without the Moonlantern, they can later be encountered as Shadow-Cursed Undead in Reithwin Town , south of the statue of Ketheric Thorm outside the Sharran Sanctuary and north of the bridge to Moonrise Towers . They are automatically hostile to the party in this form and can only be fought, although Kar'niss still appears as Temporarily Hostile if attacked. He is joined by several Shadows , undead Harpers , and undead prisoners. If Kar'niss survives the journey to Moonrise Towers, he runs up the tower to seek the Absolute's blessing on the rooftop, where he can be encountered one final time as he fights alongside Ketheric when they storm the tower at the end of Act Two . The Dark Urge will also receive ⁠ Fly-Swatter upon arriving with him to Moonrise Towers. EQ_Karlach Karlach Cliffgate is an Origin Character and a recruitable Companion [ 1 ] who can be romanced by characters of any gender. She is a Zariel Tiefling [ 2 ] and a Barbarian with the Outlander background. Karlach is on the Risen Road during Act One. Once a soldier in Zariel's army, Karlach has been given a new chance at life after the recent events. Now, freed from Avernus , she will make the most out of it, and no one will get in her way. In multiplayer sessions, if Karlach is chosen as an origin by a player, Wyll is locked out as an option to other players. “ Avernus was never my home. It was my prison. I'm free now. AND I'M NEVER GOING BACK. „ — Karlach , confronting servants of Zariel Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Personal quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Leaving the party 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Life in Baldur's Gate 3.2 Avernus and the Blood War 3.3 Escape aboard the nautiloid 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.2 Act Two 4.3 Act Three 4.4 Endings 4.4.1 A Blazing End 4.4.2 Return to Avernus 4.4.3 Life as a Mind Flayer 5 Quest rewards 6 Interactions 6.1 Companion interactions 6.1.1 Act One 6.1.2 Act Two 6.1.3 Act Three 6.2 Unique interactions 6.2.1 Act One 6.2.2 Act Two 6.2.3 Act Three 6.3 Speak with Dead 7 Related literature 8 Related Quests 9 Loot 9.1 Starting equipment 10 Achievements 11 Gallery 12 Notes and references 13 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] For a full overview of Karlach's starting features, see the articles Barbarian and Zariel tiefling . Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Trapped in Avernus under Zariel's banner due to the machinations of those she trusted the most, Karlach has been fighting in the Blood War for a decade, away from all that she loved. With the incursion of the nautiloid to the Nine Hells, fate would smile on her and give her a way out, only to turn on her just as quickly. Now, free at last, though with an unwelcome guest in her head, she must protect her hard-won liberty with her life as she seeks revenge on those who betrayed her many years ago. With a malfunctioning engine for a heart, and a burning desire to live , will she be able to save herself, or will the Hells finally catch up with her, sooner rather than later? Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before she is recruited, Karlach is a level 3 Barbarian with the following Ability Scores : 16 STR, 13 DEX, 14 CON, 8 INT, 12 WIS, 12 CHA. If recruited, Karlach reverts to a level 1 Barbarian with the standard ability scores for that class , with a focus on two-handed weapons. Upon reaching level three, she defaults to the Berserker subclass [ 3 ] granting her access to enraged attacks using a bonus action. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach can use Soul Coins to power up her mechanical heart, giving her the passive Infernal Fury , granting her additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage on her attacks when raging or her Hit Points drop below 25% Karlach's mechanical heart can be upgraded twice while progressing the story: The first upgrade grants Heart of Iron , giving her Advantage on Saving Throws against Charming effects The second upgrade grants Heart Ablaze , giving her immunity against Charming effects Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach's personal quest as a companion is ⁠ Our Fiery Friend . As an origin her personal quest is ⁠ Servant of None . Her personal quest spans all acts of the game. Throughout it, Karlach's past menaces ever closer, threatening her freedom just as she is beginning to enjoy it. Three sub-quests tie into Karlach's personal quest: In ⁠ The Hellion's Heart , Karlach and the party must deal with her mechanical heart and the problems it is causing her. ⁠ Hunt the Devil has her hunted by Zariel's agents. Wyll's companion quest, ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers , also features Karlach as an important character. An origin Karlach replaces Our Fiery Friend and The Hellion's Heart with Servant of None and Forging a Heart , respectively. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach is on The Risen Road , near the Toll House , at X: 111 Y: 503 . Cornered by Zariel's bloodhounds, she is nursing her wounds after the recent encounter. The party can talk to and recruit her, provided they agree to help do away with her pursuers. Returning to Anders and his team with Karlach in the party ultimately results in battle. However, Karlach refuses to join the party if, before meeting her, they side with the Goblins and ⁠ lay waste to the Emerald Grove , provoke a fight between the inhabitants of the grove, or they allow the Rite of Thorns to be completed. If Wyll is brought along for the first meeting with Karlach, the two confront each other. Wyll reveals that Karlach is the quarry he has been hunting for his patron, while Karlach claims to be a victim, not an agent of Zariel. Either of the two can be sided with, though siding with Wyll results in battle with Karlach. The situation can also be defused by convincing Wyll that Karlach's words are true, as backed by the vision everyone shares during the dialogue thanks to their tadpoles. Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party decide to side with the goblins before the raid on the grove, Karlach rebukes the player character and leaves – permanently. If the party side with the goblins during the raid on the grove, she assists until the fight at the gate is concluded. She then forcefully castigates the player character and permanently leaves the party. [ 4 ] Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Karlach/Approval Karlach Approves Karlach has a very strong, well developed and intuitive sense of right and wrong, not unlike that of a paladin. She enjoys helping innocents with their troubles, not expecting anything in return – something she finds in common with Wyll after their rocky first meeting. She approves of kind interactions with those in need, standing up for what is right, and being decisive with enemies. Setting her up for some fun, such as carousing or making some mayhem, also earns her approval. Being a compassionate friend to her, or a kind partner, is the easiest way of earning her trust and love. Karlach disapproves of indiscriminate violence and insensitivity to the plights of others, as well as being dismissive of her deleterious condition when she attempts to get closer. Also, as a result of her involuntary and deceptive conscription into the Blood Wars, dealing favourably with villains deeply offends her. As such, siding with Gortash , even if strategically sound, earns her contempt. Minimising her problems, especially that of her malfunctioning mechanical heart, is another sure way of breaking her trust. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Karlach/Romance Karlach can be romanced by characters of any gender. If romanced, Karlach's inability to touch her partner, and the pain of being physically isolated from everyone for so long, are issues that must be explored and overcome together. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach is tall and well-built, her body battled-toned after years of conflict in the first layer of the Hells. Her vermilion skin is covered in scars and burns received in Avernus, with tattoos adorning her left arm, upper back and parts of her abdomen. [ 5 ] Small exhaust vents on her shoulders billow steam whenever her ersatz mechanical heart flares up, its pulsating bright heat-outlines clearly visible beneath her chest. Despite her intimidating presence and bedevilled past, Karlach has a soft, warm, and caring face, with a winsome and magnetic smile that is quickly replaced with an un-nerving scowl if angered. Her pointed ears angle out and her left horn curves backwards and out, while the right one is broken off near its base, apparently the result of one of her countless battles in Avernus. She wears her dark-brown and reddish-accented hair long and mussed. A few simple braids adorned by metal discs fall along the right side of her neck, below the trimmed side of her head. Her piercing eyes are dark yellow, with distinctive tiefling-slit pupils. Light moles and freckles mark her nose and upper cheeks. [ 6 ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Despite her past, Karlach has managed to remain a kind, caring and passionate individual who strives to live life to the fullest. She does not mince words [ 7 ] and speaks excitedly regarding any of life's simple pleasures, whether that be food, drink, friends, or intimacy. Her demeanor is generally joyous and very forward, having no fear of loudly proclaiming her love of being alive and how much she cares for those close to her. Her positive disposition and infectious energy seem to allow her to make friends easily, even if her honesty can cause her to come off as somewhat naive at times. [ 8 ] Even so, as long as she is calm enough, Karlach has a knack for quickly, accurately and fairly judging most people she meets and situations she finds herself in. She is also very protective of her friends and companions, taking a genuine interest in them, especially Wyll, if transformed into a devil after defending her. Though oft friendly, Karlach is a very physical person with little-to-no reservations about getting into a brawl if provoked. She can be impulsive and easy to goad, and may lose sense and reason when confronting people she despises. Years in Avernus have made her lonely, compounded by the fact that her mechanical heart keeps her from having physical contact with others, let alone intimacy. When speaking of Gortash, beneath her outward rage, lies deep pain and a sense of betrayal, making her wary of trusting others as she once did. Despite their moral differences, she gets along well with Astarion due to them both wanting to forge their own lives outside of the shadows of their abusers. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Life in Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] Born to Pluck and Caerlack Cliffgate, [ 9 ] Karlach was raised in Baldur's Gate in a modest, but happy household in the Outer City . [ 10 ] Young and restless, Karlach frequently worked odd jobs as a means to support her parents, often getting into trouble in the meanwhile. Even as a child, she was joyous and full of life and, despite the hardships, she loved her life in the city, surrounded by family and friends. At some point, Karlach was hired by Enver Gortash to act as his bodyguard. Rising quickly through the criminal and political circles of the city, Gortash was beginning to paint a target on his back, and Karlach seemed like the ideal person to protect him. Lured initially by the money and a chance to support her parents financially, [ 11 ] Karlach eventually developed deep respect for Gortash, not only because he trusted her enough to put his life in her hands, but because he also made her feel valued. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] The pair worked well together for a while, until Gortash made a deal with the Archdevil Zariel , and sold Karlach to her for a grand sum of money in order to fund his plans for domination of the city. Zariel's interest in the tiefling was to test her new infernal machine, [ 14 ] while Gortash was confident she could handle it and believed she would also serve as an ideal prototype for his dreamed infernal automatons . [ 15 ] “ Zariel laughed. Said she paid him well for my services. She'd wanted to test her new machine, and he said I'd be able to handle it. He was right. Sometimes I wished he weren't. Evil, evil bastard. „ — Karlach , relating an unsatisfactory workplace experience Avernus and the Blood War [ edit section | visual editor ] Betrayed and sold to the devil, Karlach was taken to Avernus and quickly worked on. Happening faster than she could process it, Zariel ordered her heart to be replaced by an infernal machine, designed to test the limits of machine and soldier. The archdevil quickly put her and her new, infernal, mechanical heart to work, conscripting Karlach into her army to fight in the Blood War . Trapped and with no other choices at hand, Karlach would fight for ten years in the war, surviving day by day fueled by both vengeance and a desire to live free. She would prove to be an exceptional soldier, slaying great demons and becoming one of Zariel's prized fighters. [ 16 ] Both prisoner and champion of the archdevil, throughout it all she was alone, surrounded by devils and demons who offered no comfort, away from home and everybody she held dear. Escape aboard the nautiloid [ edit section | visual editor ] After a decade in the Hells, the sudden appearance of a Nautiloid presented itself as a chance for escape, and Karlach made good on the opportunity. Cleaving the devils around her, she made her way towards the hurtling ship before running into Wyll, brought to Avernus to hunt her. [ 17 ] The two battled briefly, Wyll giving chase as Karlach desperately reached for the ship, until they made it to the nautiloid before being separated during the siege. Captured by the mind flayers as the ship escaped Avernus, Karlach was tadpoled just as all other uninvited guests were, and awaited a slow transformation via Ceremorphosis . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach's personal quest is ⁠ Our Fiery Friend . It is added to the journal upon recruiting her and spans all three acts of the game. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] After the crash of the nautiloid, Karlach moves to the The Risen Road , near the Toll House occupied by paladins of Tyr . If Wyll is recruited to the party, his quest, ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers , adds a map marker that pinpoints Karlach's location. Otherwise the party will have a vague idea of where to find her. Anders , leader of the paladins, proclaims they are hunting a dangerous devil who has been hurting refugees, and that they must bring it to justice. When found, Karlach explains that she too was on the nautiloid and was infected with a tadpole, but she is not the monster she seems, and her current priority is to get rid of the paladins hounding her and spreading lies. At odds with what the paladins (or Wyll) told the party about her, the group can press her further. Karlach explains she escaped Avernus and the archdevil Zariel , and that the (false) paladins in the toll-house are nothing more than pacted bloodhounds sent to bring her back to the Hells . If brought along, Wyll confirms she is indeed his target and attempts to convince the party to aid him in slaying her. Karlach forcefully pleads she is no agent of Zariel but rather her victim, and that she took the first opportunity she had to escape Avernus and return home. The tadpoles infecting the group react to her heightened emotional state, prompting Karlach to share her memories of recents events, seemingly confirming her story. Regardless, the party can decide to side with Wyll (and indirectly with the paladins) and kill Karlach, claiming her head, or take her at her word and agree to spare her. Though initially intent on killing her, Wyll can be convinced to spare her after the visions are shared. If successful, he directs his anger at his patron for deceiving him. If Karlach is recruited before Wyll, he arrives at camp during a Long Rest to kill his quarry. In this scenario, the party may still side with Wyll and kill Karlach, or convince him to stand down and join the party. Alternatively, they can instead decide to challenge Wyll to a fight. Karlach will try to stop this, as she does not want Wyll dead. The party can still recruit Wyll as normal, or choose to go against Karlach’s wishes and attack Wyll anyway, much to her disapproval . If Wyll dies in this instance, Karlach mentions someone likely misguided him. [ 18 ] Bringing Karlach to the paladins leads to a confrontation. Anders eventually drops his act and confirms her words as true: the paladins are servants of Zariel, and the archdevil wants her favorite attack dog back. [ 19 ] After slaying them, a frenzied Karlach rages around the toll-house, setting it ablaze. If she is spoken with after she cools off, she confesses she has an infernal engine for a heart that allows her to burn as hot as the Hells, though it has been running overdrive since she left Avernus. She wants to find someone who has experience with infernal machines, and overheard one of the paladins let slip that one is in the area. This begins ⁠ The Hellion's Heart . Also, if she is spoken with after her fiery rampage, the player character can tell her she looks 'Hot'   +1 . The infernal mechanic turns out to be Dammon , a tiefling from Elturel who learned his trade when the city was taken to Avernus by Zariel and was forced to work on infernal engines for her army. Dammon explains that in order to stabilize her heart, the party need to find some Infernal Iron for him as it is the only material able to withstand the heat of her mechanical heart. When delivered, Dammon upgrades Karlach's heart, stabilizing it while still providing a boost to her abilities. He warns, however, that the solution is not perfect, and he needs more time to research and prepare a more permanent repair. Should they cross paths again, he promises to have a solution by then. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Dammon survives the events of Act 1 , he journeys to the Last Light Inn in the Shadow-Cursed Lands , aiding the Harpers in their stand against Moonrise Towers . If spoken to by Karlach, he explains that after further tinkering, he can give her heart another upgrade if the party has some more infernal iron to spare. After her second heart upgrade, a romanced Karlach shares a long-awaited kiss with the player character. Dammon tweaks Karlach's heart for a second time, adding an insulation chamber to cool it to the point that she can finally touch others again, something Karlach has been desperately longing to do for the last ten years. He also bears unfortunate news: her heart cannot keep going outside the Hells. Too hot to exist in the material plane, her infernal heart will burn her from the inside and consume her if she does not return to Avernus soon. Karlach dismisses the idea of ever returning to the Hells, content to celebrate her newfound ability to touch others for now. [ 20 ] . Later, when the party finally confront Ketheric Thorm , the battle eventually takes them down to the hidden Mind Flayer Colony beneath Moonrise. There, they spy Thorm consorting with Enver Gortash and Orin the Red , with the latter two leaving for Baldur's Gate to continue with their plans. After dealing with Ketheric, Karlach confesses she has a history with Gortash, letting out that it was because of him she was sent to the Hells and had her heart replaced with a mechanical one. Literally hell-bent on revenge, Karlach urges the group to hurry to Baldur's Gate and chase after her previous employer. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] After reaching the Wyrm's Rock Fortress outside Baldur's Gate, the party is notified that Gortash's grand ascension as Archduke of the city is taking place soon. When approached, Gortash briefly interrupts the ceremony to parlay with them and greets her nonchalantly. If present, Karlach immediately wants revenge and, if not stopped, is seized by Steel Watchers and thrown into the dungeon . If she is convinced against attacking Gortash, the party can listen to his proposition to an alliance. Karlach is against it, but can be persuaded to manage her temper for the good of the city. If Karlach is convinced to keep her hatred in check, the party can leave peacefully after Gortash's installation as Archduke. If the party then speak with any of the Steel Watchers , there is a unique dialogue as the Steel Watchers mistake Karlach as one of their own due to her infernal engine, but also detect hers badly overheating. The Watchers consider her a defective unit, and instruct the party take Karlach to the Steel Watch Foundry to have her "dismantled"; when asked if the engine can be repaired the Watcher mentions Karlach's engine is "very obsolete" and nearly impossible to repair, making Karlach wonder if she is a prototype for the Steel Watchers. If the partnership with Gortash is mantained up until the first encounter with the Netherbrain , he is killed as he attempts to control it. If present, Karlach lets out a celebratory laugh, mocking his ignominious end, yet the threat of the Elder Brain forces her to focus once more. Should the party antagonize Gortash, ally with Orin instead or simply wish to help Karlach get revenge, they ultimately face the Archduke and his minions. Confronting Karlach, Gortash coldly dismisses her grievances, infuriating her, until the quakes caused by the Netherbrain's attempts at freeing itself compell Gortash to attack the party for their netherstones in order to subdue it. After the battle, Karlach comes down from the excitement and is visibly upset. Though she has finally managed to kill the person who betrayed her and caused her so much pain, she feels no better: Gortash is no more sorry dead than he was alive, and her mechanical heart remains set to combust at any moment. Her impending doom and difficulty coping with overwhelming feelings of hopeless inevitability drives her near rage, and she leaves for camp. Back at camp, some time alone allows Karlach to better come to grips with her situation. Though still desperate, she is positive and instead decides to focus on the present and the time she has available, poised to save the city she loves. After the initial confrontation with the Elder Brain, it is made clear that the only path to success is to harness the true power of the netherstones, which only an illithid can do. Though it is possible for the Emperor to do so, the player character or Orpheus can sacrifice themselves and undergo ceremorphosis to become illithid instead. If Karlach is present during the discussion, she volunteers, arguing she is on borrowed time either way, and this way her death would have meaning. If the player character agrees, she transforms into a mind flayer and aids the party in their final battle against the Netherbrain. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] A Blazing End [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach burning up After defeating the Netherbrain, Karlach's infernal engine finally begins to overheat, signaling her end. With the setting sun on the background, Karlach thanks the player character for being there with her, and mourns not being able to join them in their celebrations and further adventures. If her wishes not to return to Avernus are respected and left unchallenged, they can stay with her until her engine finally combusts, leaving nothing but ashes where she once stood. At the Epilogue party Withers reveals that her soul in the Fugue Plane burns so brightly, it pains gods to look upon it. Return to Avernus [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach, returning from Avernus As Karlach's heart begins to enter its final stages of failure after defeating the Netherbrain, the player character can attempt to convince Karlach to return to Avernus before it is too late. Though initially against it, she can be persuaded to go if the player character offers to accompany her, assuring her that she will remain close to someone she cares deeply for and will not be alone again. Likewise, if Wyll completes his personal quest and becomes The Blade of Avernus, he too will offer to go with her. Back on the first plane of the Hells, Karlach and her companions prepare themselves to face the servants of Zariel. No longer alone, Karlach welcomes the challenge and readies her weapon in preparation of advancing imps. During Withers' gathering six months after the events of the game, Karlach mentions that she and her companions recently felled a high-ranking Cambion who carried blueprints for what could be a possible solution to Karlach's mechanical heart. Though the forge they intend to raid is likely well-guarded by Zariel's forces, she has an old contact, a guard named Flo, who might be able to help them. Regardless, she expresses joy at being able to see her companions once more, happy to receive the opportunity of a night's rest without the danger of being ambushed by devils. [ 21 ] If only Wyll accompanies Karlach to Avernus by the end of the game, she will also comment on how tough life is in Avernus, though having Wyll around is incredible and makes all the difference. [ 22 ] Life as a Mind Flayer [ edit section | visual editor ] Even as a mind flayer, Karlach still has her fire within. If Karlach sacrifices herself and becomes illithid in order to defeat the Netherbrain, she remains at Baldur's Gate, hiding and feeding from the dying patients of a local healer who wish to pass on with dignity instead of suffering. When spoken to at Withers' gathering, she explains she still remembers parts of herself, even using some of the expressions she once used in her tiefling form. Yet with every brain she feeds upon, she gains all the memories from it, slowly erasing her original identity. Still, she expresses gratitude and happiness at seeing many of her former companions, and bids the player a good evening. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach does not receive any particular items as reward for completing her quests. Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach has unique dialogue interactions available as a companion after certain events. Whenever one is available, she will have a floating [ ! ] icon above her. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] After killing Anders and his group, Karlach will rage inside the Toll House. When she cools off, she tells the group about her mechanical heart and how she needs to find an infernal mechanic. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] After upgrading Karlach's heart for the second time, she will express her joy and share her plans to celebrate. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] After finally killing Enver Gortash , Karlach will be overwhelmed by emotion, raging at Gortash's complete apathy until the very end, as well as the imminent loss of her own life and freedom. If a companion, Karlach will then affirm her love for the player character, feeling thankful before returning to camp. [ 23 ] [ 24 ] If spoken to at camp later, she appears to have recovered from the outburst, saying that despite the horrible situation, she is happy despite the circumstances. She then asks the player character to stay with her during the moment when her infernal engine finally gives out. Unique interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Either as an origin, or in the party as a companion, Karlach has unique interactions and special dialogue with the following characters, listed by the act they are first encountered in. Before the battle commences, Wyll and Karlach must be dead . Afterwards, their corpses must kept in the inventory of another active party member while making choices which improve their approval. The party member who carries the corpses must be in close vicinity when such events occur (see approval notes for more details on how approval works). Once their approval reaches or rises above -50, Karlach, Wyll or both can be revived. In this way, Karlach and Wyll live with the decision and stay, unless of course their approval drops below -50 again. ↑ The jagged black glyphs across Karlach’s upper back are a brand from her time serving Zariel in Avernus and spell out Demonsbane in infernal. These glyphs follow the official Infernal script first printed in Baldur’s Gate: Descent into Avernus and are used more precisely in the game's texture files. ↑ Throughout development Karlach had multiple design changes. In Early Access she only had a placeholder model created with the same assets as a custom character, with two horns and no scars and was a Fighter (with a datamined tag of a Paladin). Concept art shows different proposals for her face, initially planning to give her more scars and more aggressive features. She also had a few different starter armour designs with one repurposed to become Unwanted Masterwork Scalemail . Her other concept armour is on her Magic: The Gathering Card . ↑ If romanced by the player character at the tiefling night celebration and spending the night by the campfire after the others have gone to sleep, the player character can comment on her directness. ↑ Interactions with those who knew her prior to the events of the game's story imply that she has always been this exuberant, even as a poor child growing up in Baldur's Gate. ↑ Graveyard, Lower City , lines spoken by the narrator when inspecting her parents' graves. "Here lies Pluck Cliffgate - beloved husband and father." "Here lies Caerlack Cliffgate - beloved wife and mother." ↑ Campsite , line spoken by Karlach when recently recruited and asked about her past. "The year? Ten ere. The place? A sleepy little town called Baldur's Gate. Our hero? Karlach, a knock-kneed delinquent from the Outer City with everything to give and nothing to lose." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Karlach when talking to her after she's disclosed her relationship with Gortash. "One of my mates got wind of a bit of work guarding some indoorsy type with lots of enemies. Seemed like easy money, so I went in for it. (...) I kept him safe, and he paid me well. Well enough to move my folks to a better neighborhood and put something away for the future. My future." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Karlach when talking to her after she's disclosed her relationship with Gortash. "I respected him. Trusted him. And he returned that trust, that respect. His life was in my hands, and I took that seriously." ↑ Wyrm's Rock Fortress , lines spoken by Karlach when confronting Gortash after antagonizing him. "You make it sound like we were lovers. Or friends. But that wasn't it. I trusted you. I respected you. It was my job to protect you, and that's what I did." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Karlach when talking to her after she's disclosed her relationship with Gortash. "Zariel laughed. Said she paid him well for my services. She'd wanted to test her new machine, and he said I'd be able to handle it." ↑ Wyrm's Crossing , dialogue exchange between a Steel Watcher and Karlach. Steel Watcher: "Your unit is a highly outdated model. The ra-gnax casement protecting your metallurgised-ised valves is burning well outside the recommended temperature. Please report to the Steel Watch Foundry for dismantling." Player: "It thinks you're one of them, Karlach. Why?" Karlach: "(...) If it turns out I'm the fucking prototype for these things, I'll dismantle every single one of them. ↑ The Risen Road , lines spoken by Karlach when initially encountered and spared. "You already know I fought in the Blood War. I was good. Really good. Turns out I've got a knack for killing demons. That made me a valuable asset. Zariel - the archdevil herself - made me as her personal attack dog." ↑ It is never made clear when exactly Wyll arrives to Avernus or who really sent him. Though shortly before the events of the Prologue, Wyll could not have been hunting Karlach for long, as the time the nautiloid spent there before teleporting away was brief, and Karlach's escape was an opportunistic decision. It is possible Zariel sent Wyll after Karlach via Mizora, but as Karlach herself says, Mizora is largely inconsequential in Zariel's grand design. On the other hand, it is possible Mizora took the opportunity to remove Karlach as they both were in Zariel's inner circle and Mizora likely saw her as a rival. ↑ It is possible to recruit both Karlach and Wyll while still preventing his fiendish transformation. In addition, evading Mizora's punishment while also having Karlach in the party has no known deleterious impact on Wyll's storyline or other aspects of gameplay. To accomplish this, Wyll must be dead immediately prior to every long rest after Wyll and Karlach's confrontation at camp; he may be revived every morning after, if desired. While Wyll is dead, Mizora does not confront him for his disobedience. This arguably tedious routine is no longer needed once the party progress to Act Two . Upon first arriving in Act Two, Mizora is kidnapped and cannot transform Wyll, even if the party return to Act One and take a Long Rest there. After being rescued from the Mind Flayer Colony , Mizora no longer moves to punish Wyll. If one wants Wyll dead before long resting, it is advisable to have him die from falling damage by, for example, jumping from a great height (more than once if needed). If he is killed by damage from another party member, intended or not, approval is lost. ↑ If Karlach has been recruited and is in the active party, but is not nearby during the initial dialogue with Anders , he states that his scouts informed him the party members are her allies and initiates combat. ↑ In the end, despite having access to Dammon, a surplus of infernal metal, Gortash's schematics and even the help of both the Gondians and the Ironhand gnomes, there is no way to permanently fix Karlach's mechanical heart, save playing her as Origin, romancing Gale and ascending to godhood with him ↑ Epilogue , line spoken by Karlach if player went to Avernus with her. EQP_Crossbow_Dagger_Leather Trs. HAV_Survivor Harper Karrow is part of a small group of Harpers on a patrol expedition to the hills east of Last Light Inn during Act Two . [ 1 ] “ This might be the only peaceful spot for a league. „ — Karrow , on Last Light Inn Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Karrow can be encountered near the entrance to the Shadow-Cursed Lands from the Grymforge lift as part of a Harper expedition led by Lassandra , which consists of himself, Meygan , and Yonas . Shortly after meeting the party, Yonas is ambushed and corrupted by a Shadow , causing him to become a Shadow-Cursed Undead . Immediately after Yonas' demise, combat with the ambushing Shadows begins. Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lassandra survives the encounter, she speaks with the party and marks a safe location on their map, known as Last Light Inn . If both Lassandra and Meygan die in the fight, Karrow speaks with the party. However, he does not offer to mark the party's map. Instead, he instructs them to follow him to the Inn's safety. Karrow tends to seek and fight the two most distant ambushing Shadows. He is the only member of the group without an equipped light source. This leave him most vulnerable to the Shadow Curse and, as such, Karrow is more likely than the other Harpers to become corrupted. If the party start ⁠ Follow the Convoy instead, they can reach Last Light Inn and observe Karrow returning to the sanctuary with Lassandra and Meygan. If the party visit the Last Light Inn, Karrow and Meygan are mourning Yonas on a rocky ledge south of the docks. Provided Karrow and Meygan survive the ambush, he stands a few paces back from her, kneeling at Yonas' shrine, and observes Meygan grieving over Yonas' death. Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Karrow is too far away from the action to help in the ensuing fight. If Isobel is not saved, Karrow and everyone else at the Last Light Inn, save for Jaheira , turn into Shadow-Cursed Undead . Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Karrow, along with Lassandra, Meygan, and Mijah do not join the assault against Absolute forces. He remains at the Last Light Inn to patrol its outskirts, before completely disappearing once Ketheric Thorm is defeated. I'm so hungry. „ — Kass , talking to Gandrel Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Kass can be encountered in a prison containing Vampire spawn children in Cazador's Dungeon . If Cazador is later defeated, the party can then choose to consume the souls of all Vampire spawn or free them, the former resulting in her immediate death. If Kass is freed, she can later be seen in the Lower City Sewers with her father Gandrel . Wyr_GurHunter Katelyn Lerskin is one of the Gur , a human nomadic tribe. She is in the Gur Camp in Rivington in Act 3 . “ I will exterminate every last bloodsucker, I swear it. „ — Katelyn Lerskin at the Gur Camp in Rivington Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Katelyn is in the Gur Camp, attending a funeral for the fallen from a recent offensive on Cazador's palace. Katelyn, along with her fellow Gur – all members of a group of monster hunters lead by Ulma – are looking for their children, who have been kidnapped by Cazador's spawn. The nomads are camped in Rivington, and are trying to mount a rescue or seek revenge. Ulma asks the party to help defeat Cazador and discover the fate of their abducted children. Once Cazador is defeated, Katelyn Lerskin, along with Ulma and the other Gur move near the waypoint in Cazador's Dungeon . She attacks the party if the ritual held in the dungeons was completed. If Astarion was turned in to Gandrel in Act One and kidnapped, then in Act Three Katelyn and all of her fellow Gur (except Gandrel) are dead. Just wait for the next wave? Cassivora Dophir We cannot rush into their claws again. Another defeat will wipe us out. Oliver Quarlic What if this is it for our people? What if this is the end? Technical UID S_LOW_Park_FanclubMember01 UUID 32c18a38-6f75-4e72-8072-409dae627929 Stats Gnome_Commoner Kepli is a gnome in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Sorry, would you mind leaving me be? These books won't discuss themselves. „ — Kepli Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Kepli can be encountered in Bloomridge Park in the Lower City discussing books with Caerdwyn and Morgan during their book club. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Kepli, Caerdwyn, and Morgan discuss Dusk's Dark Desires at book club: Kepli So - Book Brigade. What did we think of Dusk's Dark Desires? Caerdwyn A thrilling read. Gave me goosepimples. Morgan Goosepimples are right - bits of the book were downright naughty. Kepli Morgan, please . We're in public, let's keep away from the book's racier parts. Morgan Racy? More like juicy. A very juicy read. Caerdwyn Yeah, the book was a lot more... lewd than its prequels. Kepli Please focus, we're the Book Brigade, not a smut symposium! Kepli Now, I personally loved the book's setting. Twisty corridors, flickering candlelight - oh, it's just such compelling reading. Morgan Nah, the blood and sex were the best bits. Of any book, really. Caerdwyn No, I'm with Kepli. The novel's sense of intrigue was its finest quality. Morgan Don't get me wrong - the book intrigued me. In all the right ways. Caerdwyn So, Kepli - who was your favourite character in the book? Kepli I really liked what the author did with Bedford. Caerdwyn I agree. Who'd have thought a were-cow could be written so beautifully? Morgan You're fools, obviously Dusk was the story's best character. Kepli The novel's protagonist is such a basic choice, Morgan. Listen, I know what I like - and the book delivered it in spades . Technical UID S_WYR_South_Guard_002 UUID 2df4c38e-db78-4a08-b78f-68882ef55a6c Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Eqp. EQP_Halberd_Chainmail_HelmetMetal Trs. BG_Guard Fist Kepso is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is in Rivington in Act Three . “ Wail all you want - we've got enough mouths to feed. We don't need your kind. „ — Kepso , to Horys Crysst Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Kepso is stationed together with Fist Wearne and Fist Silena outside the South Span Checkpoint and is responsible for addressing local complaints. They form the first line of guard, preventing refugees from entering Baldur's Gate through Wyrm's Crossing . Silena and Kepso argue with Noira Crysst and Horus Crysst , who fruitlessly beg to let them in. Like most other Fists at the checkpoint, Kepso abhors the presence of refugees. Unlike Silena, he does not mince words while expressing his opinion in their faces. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Halberd Damage: 6~15 1d10 + 5 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Sweeping Attack ( + )   –   Halberd Damage Superiority Die Swing your weapon in a rapid, sweeping arc to attack multiple enemies at once. Roll your superiority die for damage. Recharge: Per turn Throw ( )   –   Javelin Damage: 6~11 1d6 + 5 ⁠ Piercing Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. Your Strength affects how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Range: 3-18 m (10-60 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail Halberd Helmet Javelin - x2 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Kepso Citizens only. I won't say it again. Horus Crysst But - but we walked clear from Amn . There's nowhere else to go. Please - Fist Silena Orders are orders. We've got ours, you've got yours. I need you to step back. Noira Crysst There must be something - Fist Silena I said step back. Horus Crysst Please. My son - he's only a boy. You must understand - Fist Silena Sir. Sir. We can't let you in. Horus Crysst I - I thought we'd be safe in the Gate. I heard the stories. Fist Kepso Wail all you want - we've got enough mouths to feed. We don't need your kind. Horus Crysst Our - our kind? Fist Kepso Refugees. Outsiders. Fist Silena Enough, Kepso. Sir, you need to stay clear. Noira Crysst The Duke - Ravengard, I think. I heard he's a good man. Horus Crysst Let us talk to him. Please. If he could just - Fist Kepso We have the Duke's full support. For the good of the people. BGO_Supplies_Poor Keren is a monstrosity character in Act Three . Though appearing to be animal tamers for the Circus of the Last Days , Keren and Ryland are doppelgangers serving Orin and the Cult of the Absolute . “ Don't get too close, or Crimson here might decide you look tasty . „ — Keren Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Keren stands beside Crimson's cage in the Circus of the Last Days, at X: -57 Y: -34 . Keren reveals a violent streak if spoken to, voicing its wish that Crimson eat the fingers of any children who get too close to his cage. When the Dribbles impersonator signals the ambush to start (or combat with it otherwise begins), Keren and Ryland spend their first turns unlocking the animal cages holding Crimson and Shadow-Whiskers , unless they were were previously freed or pacified. After the cages are open, they use Morphic Ambush and revert to their native doppelganger forms. Tampering with the cages, including unlocking and opening them, turns Keren, Dribbles and Ryland Temporarily Hostile if detected. ## Ketheric Thorm
- **来源**: [Ketheric Thorm](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Ketheric_Thorm)
- **分类**: Characters、Bosses

Overview Combat Ketheric Thorm In-game Render Portrait Identity Male Voice / Actor J.K. Simmons Family Melodia Thorm (wife, deceased) Malus Thorm (uncle) [ 2 ] Gerringothe Thorm [ 3 ] Thisobald Thorm [ 4 ] Isobel Thorm (daughter) Hometown Moonrise Towers Reithwin Town (former) Stats Size Medium Type Undead Race Undead High Half-Elf (Possibly) [ 1 ] Class Paladin Subclass Oathbreaker Deity Selûne / Shar / Myrkul Technical UID MOO_Ketheric UUID bc4b5efc-cbd3-4f8f-a31e-d37f801a038c Stats SCL_Ketheric Eqp. MOO_Ketheric Variant 1 UID S_MOO_Ketheric UUID e9918f3e-5b87-40a3-a9bd-61545151573f Stats SCL_Ketheric Variant 2 UID S_MOO_Ketheric_Transforming UUID 5222b192-2ea3-4ecc-8434-79c9f28169f8 Stats SCL_Ketheric General Ketheric Thorm [ 5 ] is an Undead with elven ancestry and appearance, [ 1 ] the Chosen of Myrkul , and one of the leaders of the enigmatic Cult of the Absolute . He serves as one of the main antagonists in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Our darling will live again. What kind of man would I be if I didn't raze the world entire for her sake? „ — Ketheric Thorm in a diary entry Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Gameplay 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Governor of Reithwin 3.2 Conversion to Shar 3.3 Chosen of Myrkul 4 Involvement 4.1 Act Two 4.1.1 Moonrise Towers throne room 4.1.2 Atop Moonrise Towers 5 Combat 5.1 Loot 6 Related Quests 7 Related literature 7.1 Act 1 7.2 Act 2 7.3 Act 3 7.4 Books by Ketheric Thorm 7.5 Notes by Ketheric Thorm 8 Achievements 9 Gallery 10 Notes and references 11 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Once the governor of Reithwin Town , personal tragedy, loss and grief drove him down the path of darkness and violence, the eventual result of which was his defeat in battle a century ago by the combined forces of the Harpers and druids of the Emerald Grove . Now, risen from the grave to lead the Absolute's forces as their general, he seeks to destroy Baldur's Gate , spread the cult of the Absolute, and have his daughter Isobel with him once again. Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Risen from the grave a hundred years after the events that led to his downfall, Ketheric Thorm serves as the main antagonist of Act Two of the game, after being introduced during Act One through dialogue and in-game notes first. As the party members search for ways to cure their tadpole situation, many clues point towards Moonrise Towers and Ketheric himself and the party eventually must bring him down in order to rid the Shadow-Cursed Lands from its curse . By exploring Moonrise Towers, through subsequent battle with him, and later exploring the Illithid colony under the stronghold, an elaborate conspiracy behind the tadpoles in the party members's heads is unveiled. Ketheric's alliance with Enver Gortash and Orin the Red is also exposed, along with his plans to secure all three Netherstones for himself. [ 6 ] Also, during the fight against him it is revealed that it was Myrkul who brought Ketheric back from the dead. Gameplay [ edit section | visual editor ] Ketheric Thorm is a level 11 Undead boss who retains some features of his past life, and is one of the main antagonists in the game. He can be found throughout Act Two, while being referenced through dialogue and notes in Act One. Fighting him is required in order to obtain his Netherstone and proceed with the story. In combat, he is most similar to an Oathbreaker paladin , [ 7 ] able to cast a form of Smite with his attacks, as well as having access to Aura spells and able to raise Undead minions. Despite his status as a boss, Ketheric can still be disarmed, knocked prone or affected by other types of weapon abilities. True to his skill as a general, Ketheric commands his allies to focus their attacks on targets he deems especially troublesome via Deadly Orders . The outcome of the quests relating to the Nightsong , as well as dialogue checks, can influence the encounters with him. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Ketheric has a severe, weathered look - his face marked by age and a permanent scowl. He wears a plain circlet adorned with the skull of Myrkul, and a richly detailed suit of armor which clearly identifies him as the Chosen of the Lord of Bones. His Netherstone rests securely in an ornate golden cage on his chest armour. Ketheric's straight gray hair is tucked neatly behind his slightly pointed ears. A thick, full beard connects to his hair, which suggests he has only partly elven ancestry (according to the Forgotten Realms lore elves, unlike half-elves, cannot grow facial hair). [ 8 ] Despite this, in the first vision imposed upon the party by the Absolute near the Goblin Camp , the Narrator calls him "a mighty elf" among the Chosen Three. The Elder Rothé in Grymforge , if spoken to via Speak with Animals , also describes him in the same words. Companions' comments on murals surrounding Isobel's grave inside the Thorm Mausoleum (where the key points of Ketheric's story are depicted), too, refer to him as an elf. Presumably, Ketheric was first planned to be an Elf but was later changed to half-elf, and the (likely) erroneous mentionings as an elf are oversights by the developers. [ 9 ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Though best described as a man tormented and utterly transformed by grief [ 10 ] , his daughter Isobel speaks of a loving, doting father while she was growing up, one who had the admiration of his subjects for being just and fair, full of love for his wife who he adored more than anyone else. Tragedy, however, would turn him into a bitter, wrathful man, willing to cleanse Reithwin from any Selûnites to spite the Moonmaiden for abandoning him. Whatever the man he once was, the Ketheric the party encounters is a callous one, evident by his dismissal of Minthara and the goblins, ordering their torture and execution for failing him. Though courteous when needed, he will quickly condemn the party to death should they defy his orders. Above all, however, he is ruthless and relentless [ 11 ] in his pursuits, willing to burn the entire world just to be reunited with his daughter. [ 12 ] Though his loss and anguish moved him to change his patron god twice in search of relief, he proved to be an ardent believer of each while serving them: for Selûne, he built Moonrise Towers in her honour, for Shar , he built a grand temple under town in her name and for Myrkul , he amassed a great army ready to raze Baldur's Gate to the ground. Through it all, he kept a note from Isobel close to him, showing that deep down a small part of him still remembers the man he once was. History [ edit section | visual editor ] “ I pity you. Truly. „ — Isobel , addressing a bust of Ketheric Thorm while in her quarters at the Last Light Inn Governor of Reithwin [ edit section | visual editor ] A devout worshipper of Selûne , Thorm lived with his wife Melodia and daughter Isobel near the town of Reithwin as governor of the region. Such was his devotion to the Moonmaiden that he would commission a local mason, Morfred , to construct a grand bastion in her honour: Moonrise Towers . Yet disaster struck the Thorm family when Melodia passed away, leaving Ketheric to raise their daughter alone. [ 13 ] With a child in his care, Ketheric persevered, and though doubts plagued his mind, he kept the Selûnite ways. As Isobel grew older, their happy years had a sour note: he disapproved of a budding relationship between his daughter and an immortal Aasimar visiting the town, Dame Aylin , daughter of Selûne. The conflict would be cut short, however, as tragedy would befall Ketheric once more, and his daughter Isobel passed away. [ 14 ] Conversion to Shar [ edit section | visual editor ] Grief-stricken and unable to cope with his loss, Ketheric Thorm renounced the worship of the Moonmaiden and turned to Shar , the Lady of Loss. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] Moonrise Towers, once a bastion of Light, turned into a symbol of darkness and grief; Thorm systematically erased all Selûnite trace of the town, forcing all believers of the Moonmaiden to convert to Shar, flee, or die. [ 17 ] Those who remained devout to Selûne did so in secret, arranging a ⁠ fledgling resistance even as Sharran spies began to infiltrate their gathering places. [ 18 ] In Ketheric's downward spiral into darkness, Shar compelled him to build an army of Dark Justiciars beneath his home town in order to cleanse the world of Light. Ketheric lured Isobel's lover, Aylin, whom he had once quarreled with under Selûne , and trapped her in a prison. He had the immortal demigod serve as a perpetual sacrifice for Dark Justiciar initiates – a design of his closest confidante, the necromancer Balthazar . [ 19 ] [ 20 ] As terror gripped the town he had previously served so faithfully, the Harpers , a loose organization that roots out villainy, saw that Ketheric had committed "Murder, Slavery, and Desecration of Temples Most Holy." They began to seek an alliance to end his reign. [ 21 ] Reithwin soon became the site of a wintertime battle between Ketheric's army and the combined forces of the Harpers and druids of the Emerald Enclave . [ 22 ] Ketheric's Justiciars repelled the combined forces, and the Harpers unsuccessfully attempted surrender . [ 23 ] All the while a devil's bargain was struck with Raphael beneath the town by the Selûnite-in-secret Morfred as well as Yurgir and his merregons ; they then worked to annihilate Ketheric's Dark Justiciar army. In the end, the Sharran army was defeated, ⁠ virtually all Dark Justiciars were slain , and finally Ketheric himself perished [ 24 ] . And yet, before the final blow was struck and his defeat was sealed, he unleashed a Shadow Curse upon the land - a curse that would persist long after his demise, afflicting all battle survivors and any remaining inhabitants who did not flee. His body was later buried in the Thorm Mausoleum . Chosen of Myrkul [ edit section | visual editor ] “ I'll tell you a story, True Soul. About a man who sold himself piece by piece. „ — Ketheric Thorm More than a hundred years later, Thorm would be brought back from the dead by Myrkul as General Ketheric Thorm. The God of Death tasked the general to form an alliance with the apostles of the other two of the Dead Three and bring death to the world, offering in payment the resurrection of Ketheric's daughter Isobel. After reviving his daughter with help of Balthazar, Ketheric's plan at a family reunion failed: when the revived Isobel saw his broken visage, she fled into the darkness, protected by her goddess Selûne. The town had been ravaged by Ketheric's death rattle, the Shadow Curse. Looming over the town for a century, all within had either died outright from it or been twisted into horrific monsters. Undeterred, empowered by Myrkul, and granted immortality by the Nightsong, Ketheric began amassing an army of followers of the Absolute in order to march to Baldur's Gate and sow destruction. Tasked with the recovery of the mysterious artifact, the only object capable of thwarting the Dead Three's plans, he ultimately fails and falls at the hands of the party. [ 25 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Though the party learns about Ketheric during Act 1, his involvement in the Cult of the Absolute is only explored during Act Two, allowing them to meet Ketheric himself at Moonrise Towers either before or when it's sieged. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonrise Towers throne room [ edit section | visual editor ] The party's first encounter with Ketheric Thorm starts with the general judging members of the Absolute's forces from the Goblin Camp , including Sazza , Fezzerk , and Minthara if any of them are still alive. Should Minthara be alive, he sends her to the dungeons to be punished, before ordering for the goblins to be killed. Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers, answering in response to Drenn's first attempt to kill him. Outraged, Drenn insults Ketheric, snatches a halberd from a guard, and hurls it into Ketheric's chest. The immortal general rips the weapon from his chest and drops it in front of Drenn, challenging and daring her to "try again". Drenn strikes him in the neck, to no avail, and he smashes Drenn's spine with his bare hands, killing her. Ketheric then leaves the hall, instructing Z'rell to leave the fate of the remaining goblins to the player character's "particular creative genius." Ketheric moves to the rooftop of Moonrise Towers with orders not to disturb him under any circumstances. Although the party can visit him before the finale by sneaking into the rooftop, he is - if spoken with here - furious they did not wait as instructed and turns hostile. Remaining immortal at this point, he cannot be defeated. While speaking to characters such as Jaheira , Z'rell , and Balthazar , it is revealed, to some capacity, that a magical relic grants Ketheric immortality. Assisting Balthazar reveals that sometime between his life as a Sharran and his time serving Myrkul, Ketheric Thorm discovered the Nightsong and used it to render him unkillable. Atop Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] After killing or saving Aylin , the party must confront Ketheric during the assault on Moonrise Towers . This grants the ⁠ Top of the Ladder inspiration to party members with the Noble background. The party have the opportunity to make Ketheric see reason, by invoking Melodia's memory , or intimidating him into submission [ 26 ] . Doing so grants the ⁠ Eclipse of the Heart inspiration to party members with the Entertainer background. Whether or not Aylin is alive to interrupt the conversation, Ketheric concludes he has come too far to stop now and attacks the party upon discovering they have been in possession of the Prism all along. Once his health drops below 40%, Ketheric flees down into the Mind Flayer Colony , taking Aylin with him if she is alive. If, however, the party chose to let Balthazar take Aylin in the Shadowfell and helped abduct Isobel, the fight at the top of the tower is skipped. Should Isobel be dead, he recounts his life story, and his sacrifices, blaming the party for her death, but not punishing them, as he wishes to keep up the façade of the Absolute's judgement. The party is instead taken prisoner in the Mind Flayer Colony, where Balthazar is tasked with transforming them into zombies and retrieving the Artefact. It is then necessary to break out of the pods and defeat Balthazar to continue. Eventually, the party find Ketheric having a conversation with Enver Gortash and Orin the Red , revealing the true form of the Absolute. Gortash and Orin depart for Baldur's Gate, leaving Ketheric behind to deal with the party. Once he is defeated, the last portion of the fight will begin, this time against the Apostle of Myrkul . If asking Ketheric to repent by passing multiple Persuasion and / or Intimidation checks, both atop Moonrise Towers and in the Mind Flayer Colony, then the first half of his fight in the Mind Flayer Colony is skipped as he gives himself to Myrkul. Once the Apostle of Myrkul is defeated, Ketheric returns to humanoid form and mutters his daughter's name one last time before collapsing dead. After his death, his Netherstone is taken from his corpse by the party. The inspiration ⁠ Lesser of the Three is granted to party members with the Haunted One background for killing the Apostle of Myrkul. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Ketheric Thorm/Combat Ketheric serves as the main antagonist of Act 2 of the game and must be fought thrice in it. His defeat marks the end of the act and allows the party to proceed to their next and final destination: Baldur's Gate. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Early Design of the Chosen Portrait of Ketheric and Aylin Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 It is not exactly clear whether Ketheric Thorm is an undead Elf or Half-Elf. See the Appearance section. ↑ A Tissue and Organ Register written by Malus Thorm found in the House of Healing refers to Ketheric as nephew, thus it can be safely inferred that Malus is indeed his uncle. ↑ It is unclear what degree of kinship Ketheric and Gerringothe share. She is probably his aunt given Malus’s relation. However, notes and narration mention Ketheric dug up many of his ancestors’ tombs, which could indicate she is a far older relative if she was revived through necromancy. ↑ Ketheric's kinship with Thisobald is unclear. Though Thisobald calls Ketheric "Father" and introduces himself as "Son of Thorm" , neither Ketheric nor Isobel acknowledge him in dialogue or otherwise. In The Waning Moon: Consignments , Thisobald calls him "Father Ketheric" , which makes it more likely that Thisobald is referring to Ketheric as a principal figure of Shar rather than a literal parent, similar to how Shadowheart refers to Viconia DeVir as "Mother" . Another possibility, given that Ketheric and Balthazar desecrated the Thorm mausoleum and resurrected Isobel, is that Thisobald is another resurrected relative and uses "Father" not in the paternal sense, but as in "creator" . ↑ Though voiced by J.K. Simmons, Ketheric was mo-capped by other actors, Neil Newbon amongst them. ↑ Elder Brain Domination found underneath the floorboards by the bed in Ketheric Thorm's quarters. ↑ Ketheric is referred to as Shar's loyal paladin in the Sharran Registry and Scroll of Evidence . ↑ It is presumably for this reason that Cazador Szarr's early access facial hair was removed before launch ↑ In the Early Access version of the game, Ketheric had no beard and a more "elvish" appearance. In current game files he is tagged as a High Half‑Elf through "InheritsFrom": "HalfElves_Male_High_NotMessingAround" in his entry MOO_Ketheric . This tag was never contradicted by gamedev staff in any interviews or comments in various discussions. ↑ Graveyard Diary , and the diaries of Ketheric Thorm: volumes 1 , 2 , and 3 . ↑ Suelto's Ethics of War on the floor near a makeshift shrine to Myrkul in Kethric Thorm's quarters. ↑ Diary of Ketheric Thorm, Vol 3 ↑ Letter to Ketheric ↑ Mason's Log ↑ Diary of Ketheric Thorm, Vol 1 ↑ Tablet Fragment (3) ↑ From a Shadow Vestige : "An older man turns his head away in shame. His neighbors would not renounce Selûne - now they hang in the town square." ↑ Investigation Notes ↑ Ornate Letter ↑ Teachings of Loss: Dark Justiciar ↑ Scroll of Evidence ↑ The Price of Pride ↑ Harper's Testimonial ↑ Ketheric's first death, and the timeline of his immortality, isn't explained in the game. He survived a poisoning by the Harpers, and Thisobald wrote that it was because Ketheric was immortal. If that's true, it's not clear how he later was able to be killed. ↑ Missive from Gortash ↑ If in possession of Melodia's Letter to Ketheric the skill check to persuade Ketheric to stand down is DC 10. Otherwise, intimidating him into submission is DC 30. ↑ Available only if disarmed during the first encounter atop Moonrise Towers. ↑ This note contains the results of a Harper investigation, and the genesis of the plans to attack Ketheric with the Emerald Enclave. ↑ In this diary a disillusioned Reithwin citizen hopes for Ketheric's death on the eve of the Harpers' attack. ↑ In this journal a Mason discovers that the masonry has been raided, and everyone inside taken. ↑ This is Melodia's deathbed letter. ↑ In this log Selûnite resistance member asks Raphael to kill the Dark Justiciars . ↑ This a letter from Lord Gortash, describing the crash of the nautiloid and urging Ketheric find the Mysterious Artefact. ↑ In this journal an aasimar Harper records the first death of Ketheric, and the beginnings of the shadow curse. ↑ This book shows how Ketheric deals with those he regards as enemies. ↑ This is a letter from Ketheric to Lorroakan , explaining in general terms how his invulnerability stems from the Nightsong . CRE_CrecheTeacher Sa'varsh Kethk is an instructor in the Classroom of Crèche Y'llek during Act One . “ K'chakhi! Why do you keep hesitating? My instructions were clear! „ — Kethk , berating Varrl Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Kethk is a brutal taskmaster, not above killing his own students if it means hardening the survivors. He will do exactly this to Youth Varrl , unless interrupted by the party, who can step in to save the youth's life or kill the child themselves. Kethk firmly believes in survival of the fittest, and espouses his beliefs on child rearing and other tenets of traditional githyanki philosophy. He and his students become hostile if the party progress far enough in ⁠ Discover the Artefact's Secrets . Technical UID S_CRE_MainCheckpointWarningGuard UUID a6c0d21e-ce59-4dbb-9f64-1ec80b95c838 Stats Githyanki_Warrior Eqp. EQP_Shortsword_Robe_Gith Trs. CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Warrior Khunaruth is a githyanki in Crèche Y’llek in Act One . “ Halt. One step further and I end your primitive existence. „ — Khunaruth Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Khunaruth guards the entrance to the Crèche from Rosymorn Monastery Basement together with Gish Far'aag and Raider Ra'gur . They are accompanied by Ardent Lin'a'an , a member of Inquisitor W'wargaz's retinue, who was sent to the Crèche to locate and retrieve the ultimate mystical weapon against ghaik . As the party enter the Crèche, they might hear Khunaruth arguing with Lin’a’an about the Inquisition’s presence, and activities within the Crèche and its surroundings, Khunaruth scolding the warrior for negligence they notice almost everywhere and for lack of efforts to find the weapon. Khunaruth himself has little to say to the party. However, if for some reason Far'aag is dead by the time the party approach the entrance for the first time, he halts them and leads the questioning in her stead, with mostly the same options and possible outcomes. He becomes hostile to the party if they fail to explain their attempt to infiltrate the Crèche, or if they choose to walk back through the Crèche after speaking to the Inquisitor and having started a fight. MOO_Cultist Acolyte Kimmeral is resting in the barracks west of the ground floor in Moonrise Towers in Act Two . “ Don't mind Mig and her 'meat sounds'. It's just her brain slopping around in her skull. „ — Kimmeral Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Kimmeral is in the barracks of Moonrise Towers , which is situated west of the hall and throne room. He is resting there with Iogar and an ogre named Mig . Kimmeral warns the party about Mig and tells them the sounds the ogre alludes to are imaginary. Defending Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Nightsong is freed and the Harpers launch their assault on Moonrise Towers, Kimmeral is part of the remaining forces defending Moonrise Towers. Kimmeral then moves to the rafters above the ground floor's main hall, where he can harass the party and their allies. I'm not a baby. „ — Kimmy Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Kimmy is with her mother Monifa Diallo and Ha-yoon Kim just outside the well across from the Open Hand Temple . While Monifa is talking to Ha-yoon Kim about Steel Watchers , Kimmy simply wants to go home. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Monifa Diallo The Absolute's army will be here any day now. Ha-yoon Kim Stop fretting - the Steel Watch will put a stop to them. Monifa Diallo Those machines will form a circle 'round the upper city as soon as the fighting starts, mark my words. We'll be on our own. If Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed: Monifa Diallo The Absolute's army will be here any day now. Ha-yoon Kim Stop fretting - the Fist will stop them. Monifa Diallo They're too busy with their precious patriars. We're on our own. Monifa Diallo I've bags packed for myself and the kids, ready by the door. You should do the same. Kimmy But Mummy, I don't want to leave! Monifa Diallo I know, sweetie, but we'll be safe in the wilds, all right? Ha-yoon Kim The wilds? You throw a fit when there's no hot water - you wouldn't last a day out there! Monifa Diallo It's run or sit on my arse praying! And the gods don't give a damn about us. Ha-yoon Kim Why don't we talk about something else? Did you try that rye bread recipe I gave you? Monifa Diallo Really? The cult is on our doorstep and you want to talk about bread? Technical UID S_WYR_SharessCaress_Cat UUID 905545cf-04b9-4340-a501-f8f5fa201b87 Stats Cat Kira the Cat is a medium haired brown cat with blue eyes. She is in Sharess' Caress in Wyrm's Crossing . “ It's your lucky day. I am receiving compliments at this time, and you are most welcome to make an offering. „ — Kira Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If spoken with using Speak with Animals , Kira gives the party information on the customers of Sharess' Caress . If a party member compliments her, or if they leave the initial conversation without saying anything, then a party member can speak her again. If the party insults or tries to pet her, she does not converse with them anymore. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Kira was named after the cat of a character artist that worked on the cat model, using her own cats as references. Kira sadly passed away during production and was put into the game by the developers so she could forever roam the streets of Baldur’s Gate. Superior Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 24 m (80 ft). Technical UID S_UND_DuergarRebelMason_01 UUID d09aecce-fad1-4aa8-9c40-c370a0ac8835 Stats UND_KC_Duergar_Melee Eqp. EQP_Warhammer_Leather Trs. UND_KC_Trader_Utility Stonemason Kith is a duergar Trader who can be found at Grymforge during Act One . “ The past is nearer than we think. We simply must dig. „ — Kith Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Stonemason Kith is investigating the history of the Grymforge together with Gergerann at X: -660 Y: 375 . If the party speak with him, the first time they do so he asks for their assistance. A party member can examine the statue, rubble and general area. Upon passing each skill check, they discover that the statue is recent, implying two different eras of occupants to the fortress, and that the rubble and glassy stones within the debris indicate the nearby wall was smashed through by something large from the Hells. If the party member passes all three skill checks and reports to Kith, he gifts them a piece of Infernal Alloy and party members with the Guild Artisan background receive the ⁠ Expert Opinion inspiration. Otherwise, the infernal alloy can be purchased from his inventory. The interacting party member must pass three of the following skill checks: [INVESTIGATION]  Examine the fallen rubble.  (DC 10) [RANGER] [INVESTIGATION]  Examine the fallen rubble.  (DC 5) [PERCEPTION]  Survey the area for unseen curiosities.  (DC 10) [HISTORY]  Assess the statue for technique and composition. (DC 10) Bards only need to pass one skill check: [BARD] [HISTORY]  Try to remember the tome "Fables of Forges Grym".  (DC 10) Advantage [BARD] [DECEPTION]  I know everything about this place. In fact, it was hand-forged by a flumph called Grym... (DC 20) Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to UND_KC_Trader_Utility . Notable items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] Kith sells items from the scrolls and potions tables in addition to the following unique item: Infernal Alloy (if not given for free through passing conversation checks) Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Enlarge ( ) Grow in size to become stronger You gain Advantage on Ability Checks and Saving Throws using Strength, and weapon attacks deal an additional 1d4 damage. EQP_Longbow Kivak is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . “ Your courage is an inspiration to us all! „ — Kivak Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Kivak appears only at the tiefling camp celebration which happens during a long rest after successfully finishing ⁠ Defeat the Goblins . He takes the place of Ikaron , if he is dead. He appears as one of the dead tieflings at the Goblin Celebration if the quest ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove is completed. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Chatter between Kivak and Guex (if alive) Guex We're alive, Kivak. Alive! Kivak But the others... Guex Tonight we drink to them! Kivak I can't lie - I'm going to miss this place a bit. Guex One sight of the city, and you'll forget all about it. Kivak I thought you'd never been. Guex Ah, but I know. Kivak I feel like I can breathe for the first time in months. Guex Less air, more ale! Kivak and Rhy talking about various things Kivak What're you going to do in Baldur's Gate when we get there? Rhy More of this! Rhy Gods, it's good to be out of that damned grove! Kivak This, though! Night sky, warm fire... Rhy Prefer the city, being honest. Kivak How much ale you figure we have left? Rhy Not enough. Never enough! Kivak Never thought things would end up this way. Rhy Chin up! This is a celebration! Kivak Yeah... yeah. It is! Rhy To living! Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRock_AudienceHallGuard_005 UUID c3204c45-b2c8-45a7-bf68-24d64e98e593 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Klaas is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in the Wyrm's Rock Fortress in Act Three . “ A city is only as mighty as its leader. Under Gortash, no army can breach our walls! „ — Klaas Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Klaas with several other Flaming Fists ( Fist Bella , Fist Diallo , Fist Earthdigger , Fist Fernhollow , Fist Kyberos and Fist Quickstitch ) is standing watch in the Audience Hall of the Wyrm’s Rock Fortress at the ceremony of Enver Gortash being ordained as an Archduke of Baldur's Gate . He guards the door to an outer balcony at X: 16 Y: 227 . If spoken to, Klaas asks the player character to keep silence, as he doesn’t want to miss the ceremony. He also expresses utter loyalty to Gortash. GOB_Goblin_Generic Tracker Klagga is a goblin stationed in the Goblin Camp in Act One . “ Enjoying the view? Lookin' tasty in these new breeches, ain't I? „ — Klagga , greeting the player character Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Klagga is roasting the spit in the main outdoor area of the Goblin Camp. He is quite proud of his new breeches , which he looted from Brian , the dwarf whose corpse is currently being cooked. In addition to new breeches, Klagga also possesses a Dwarf's Poem which he also took from Brian. He is willing to trade for the poem or can be convinced to relinquish it. Reading the poem advances ⁠ Find the Nightsong and offers a hint to solve the puzzle in Selûne temple. Using Detect Thoughts reveals Klagga's fondness of poetry, although he hides this from his fellow goblins. He is the author of an undelivered letter meant to woo Minthara . He is probably also the author of an Unfinished Love Letter and some Love Letter Notes . Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Reading the dwarf's poem in Klagga's possession grants minor approval with Gale and Shadowheart.   +1   +1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Nimble Escape ( ) Retreat safely: moving won't provoke Opportunity Attacks .
