Technical UID S_LOW_WardingOffDecay_Druid UUID 0e50cc7a-ac91-4f77-93b5-86bd7a4cf1a9 Stats Dragonborn_Commoner Druid Klarrvox is a Dragonborn who is attempting to coax a dying sapling to bloom in Act Three . “ Awaken, little one - flower and bloom, as I know you can. „ — Klarrvox Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Druid Klarrvox is in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . He can be found next to Philgrave's Mansion and southwest of Felogyr's Fireworks at X: -8 Y: -143 , where he speaks to a withering sapling and calls for Chauntea , the goddess of life and agriculture, to save the sapling. Talking with Klarrvox as a dragonborn will have him greet the party member with 'kin', and vayemniri . Speculation [ edit section | visual editor ] It is possible that the sapling Klarrvox is trying to save is at risk of turning into a Blight , a plant-based creature that is usually tainted by evil forces, with the ability to turn entire landscapes into desolate blight-infested wastelands. [ 1 ] Blights originate and are created due to the influence of deep, dark, or evil forces in their premises. This evil "essence" can inherently corrupt vegetation, and either take control or wither existing healthy biomass, capable of tearing up entire buildings within days. As the sapling is located right at a crossroad between the Mummy Lord Mystic Carrion's necromantic home full of Undead and corpses, as well as down the road from the Szarr Palace's back entrance, where the Vampire Lord Cazador Szarr resides with his seven thousand Vampire spawns , this may explain the sapling's condition. Additionally, the first known origins of blights were from a vampire by the name of Gulthias , who was staked through the heart. The stake would eventually be corrupted by the vampire's blood and foul essence, eventually turning into roots and then a series of blights. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] As it is, there are no quests, mechanics, or content related to Klarrvox or his attempts at saving the withering sapling, and thus, no possible way of aiding the druid or saving the tree. Klarrvox' technical name within the engine is S_LOW_WardingOffDecay_Druid . WYR_Circus_GenericPerformer Klaus is a wood elf at the Circus of the Last Days . Along with Benji , he is tasked with sniffing people out. If Benji smells blood, they do not allow entrance to the circus. “ Welcome to the Circus of the Last Days - have fun, and be sure to catch the star of the show, Dribbles the Clown! „ — Klaus welcoming the party into the circus. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Klaus is with his tamed ghoul, Benji , at the entrance to the Circus of the Last Days at X: 22 Y: -75 . One of the following dialogue options grants access to the circus. [ 1 ] [ARCHFEY] [INTIMIDATION]  Unless you seek the wrath of the Seelie Court, you will let me pass.  (DC 18  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  You can smell the blood of my enemies, that is all. Monster_Worg Klaw is a named worg at the checkpoint just before the Goblin Camp during Act One . She is battle-tested and fierce, and has a litter of pups: Small Klaw , Ferr , and Tale . [ 2 ] “ Rip ya. Rip ya fer yer giblets. Got thick giblets. Want 'em. „ — Klaw Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Klaw guards the checkpoint leading to the Goblin Camp from the Blighted Village , alongside Olak and Small Klaw . If a party member talks to her using Speak with Animals , and they have War Paint on their face, Klaw comments that they are wearing "me muck", revealing the worg dung which makes up the War Paint came from her. Kled wants Lady Mayrina to be all better. „ — Kled Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon entering Old Garlow's Place , the party finds Kled and the other members of the Anti-Hag Support Group . They are being stalked by a hag and are initially suspicious of the party; they will attack unless pacified by a successful dialogue check. If Mayrina survives Act 1 , then Kled will talk about how much he admires her. Technical UID S_MOO_UpperGuard_002 UUID 638fe74f-aa4f-400c-85f9-69112a288300 Stats MOO_ZealotOfTheAbsolute_Human Eqp. EQP_Halberd_Plate_Shortbow Trs. MOO_Cultist Zealot Klen patrols the off-limits area of the first floor in Moonrise Towers in Act Two . “ Disciples may enter. All others are to be culled, by the General's decree. „ — Klen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Klen is on the first floor of Moonrise Towers , where he patrols the off-limits area connecting all the different first floor rooms. If he is till alive, intruding in the area causes Marcus to intervene in the party's favour. Otherwise Klen engages in trespassing dialogue. [DECEPTION]  Disciple Z'rell sent me with urgent news for the General. (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  I work for the General. Perhaps he should hear of your insolence. (DC 10) [ILLITHID]  Commune with your parasite, plant a thought: 'This one is a disciple.' Attack. Defending Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Nightsong is freed and the Harpers launch their assault on Moonrise Towers, Klen is killed during the subsequent battle. His corpse is next to the staircase leading into Moonrise Towers, at X: -159 Y: -137 . Technical UID S_LOW_FishAndGrime_Sailor_01 UUID b783dae8-e3d5-45ba-8937-1d7edcde5150 Stats Dragonborn_Commoner Klorrvank is a sailor sorting a haul of fish in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Trust me - you don't want to eat these. „ — Klorrvank Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Klorrvank is at the pier of the Grey Harbour Docks together with Nets Blandorf . Both he and Nets Blandorf notice a strange smell coming off the fish, and he minces no words in telling the party the fish found there should not be eaten. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Nets Blandorf Do these fish smell, erm, fishy to you? Klorrvank *Sniffs.* 'Course they do. They're fish. Nets Blandorf Very funny. I'm telling you - there's something off about them. Nets Blandorf Look at them - there's all black stuff in all the gills. Klorrvank I'm not surprised. The water's been grimy as anything recently. Haven't had a clean catch in a tenday or more. Klorrvank You'll have to wash them all. Marric will never let you sell them like that. Nets Blandorf Wonder what's causing it? Klorrvank I've fished these waters my whole life. Never known anything like it. Klorrvank Something's going on down there. Crossbow Expert: Point-Blank Crossbow attacks from melee range don't receive Disadvantage . Technical UID S_CRE_Caretaker UUID c61ac08e-addf-4f0e-8a0a-2fc026ec0224 Stats CRE_Githyanki_Varsh Eqp. CRE_Hatchery_Caretaker Trs. CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Varsh Ko'kuu is a githyanki charged with the Hatchery of Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ You? What do you know about githyanki child-rearing? „ — Ko'kuu , after asking him for the egg Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Steal a Githyanki Egg If a party member speaks with Varsh Ko'kuu, they can pass a passive DC 10 Insight Check to deduce that Ko'kuu has been waiting a long time for the last egg in the hatchery to hatch. If they pass the Insight check, they can attempt a DC 10 Persuasion Check to ask Ko'kuu why he really cares about this egg. If they fail the passive Insight roll, they can still ask Ko'kuu why he cares about one egg via a DC 14 Persuasion Check . On success, Ko'kuu reveals that he himself created the hatchery, despite being the last in his clutch to hatch. He believes there could be greatness in the unhatched egg. However, he grows weary and impatient because Kith'rak Therezzyn might inspect the hatchery soon and command him to destroy the egg. Upon learning this, the interacting party member can attempt to convince Ko'kuu to give them the last egg. Passing one of the following options results in Ko'kuu providing it: [PERSUASION]  Why risk its life at all? Give it to me - I'll take care of it. (DC 18) [DECEPTION]  You're out of time and clearly stalling - that's why Kith'rak Therezzyn sent me to bring it to her. Hand it over. (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  You're wasting time. Give it to me now or I'll tell her you're the weakling. (DC 18) If the interacting party member convinces Ko'kuu to relent the egg through a Persuasion check, he grants them Varsh Ko'kuu's Boots , which prevents the wearer from taking damage in the hatchery pool. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] After convincing Ko'kuu to relent the egg via a DC 18 Persuasion Check , he asks what the party will do with the egg. The following responses result in companion approval: I'll raise it as if it were my own flesh and blood. I'll find another crèche. One that's more forgiving. [GITHYANKI]  I'll see that it becomes the greatest ghaik -slayer you've ever seen. Any of the above:   -1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 I'll make the best omelette you've ever tasted. Depends, how much do you think these things sell for? Any of the above:   +1   -1   -1   -1   -1   -1 Note that choosing either of the above two dialogue options causes the hatchery to immediately become hostile. At the same time, Koll and the rest of the doppelgangers all re-disguise as Dolor, aiding his escape. Technical UID S_END_CircusTrader UUID c94a8e45-b601-4193-bb6a-aed77692c981 Stats Kobold_Inventor Koll the Red is a Kobold trader found in the Watch Citadel , an area within the Upper City accessible after travelling to the Morphic Pool . “ Bodies, bloods - this is the dream! Knew I was smarts to sneaks in. The skelly boy said I could stay if I solds ya stuff. So hurry up - BUY, BUY BUY. „ — Koll (kobold) Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Koll is the final trader encountered in the game. He is adamant that the party succeed in battle, lest he lose a customer. The table next to Koll is covered in various magical equipment and consumables. Taking these items counts as stealing and causes Koll to permanently vanish in a cloud of smoke along with the remaining items on the table. This also causes Beorn Wunterbrood and any nearby characters gathered as part of the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest to become hostile - preventing the party from using their Gather Your Allies abilities. Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_DocksRoad_Sailor_000 UUID 6cc199cb-d016-4995-bab4-944bc30d5cc1 Stats Human_Commoner Kolobeg is attempting to make deliveries in the Lower City during Act Three . “ I swear, this Fist is just trying to provoke me, but I'm not going to fall for it. „ — Kolobeg Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg and Felgi Diggums are two sailors near Grey Harbour Docks . They are trying to deliver their crates, but are prevented from accessing the area by Fist Gneiss and Fist Pantella . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Steel Watch Foundry is intact [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg We can't deliver our goods to the docks? Why? Fist Pantella New rule - it's a restricted area, top security. Felgi Diggums But I can see people down there on the docks going about their business! Fist Gneiss Oh, we'll get to them soon enough. Kolobeg We've got a job to do. These goods need to get delivered. Fist Pantella And I have a duty to the city and to Lord Gortash . So halt right there. Felgi Diggums Why this sudden restriction on visiting the docks, though? Fist Gneiss Somehow, citizen, Lord Gortash forgot to tell me. Isn't that strange? Kolobeg But I made a deliver to the docks just yesterday! Fist Pantella Sorry, citizen, the docks are now a restricted area. Felgi Diggums Talk straight. Are you really just looking for a bribe? Fist Gneiss Are you looking to get stomped flat by a Steel Watcher ? If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg The foundry's a wreck! There's nothing left to guard! Can we deliver our goods to the docks now? Fist Pantella Not just yet, citizen. The whole place is a crime scene. Felgi Diggums We just need to go past the foundry to make our delivery on the wharf. Fist Gneiss Don't split hairs with me. You go no farther. Kolobeg Come on, Saer Fist, let us past - these deliveries are urgent. Fist Pantella More urgent than justice? More urgent than the rule of law? Felgi Diggums Now you're just mocking us. Fist Gneiss Heh. You've got brains, for a dwarf. Kolobeg Look, we just need to go past the foundry along the docks. Fist Pantella My orders don't admit of any exceptions. Felgi Diggums You know, if you'd just look the other way for a minute... Fist Gneiss You trying to bribe me? If so, where's the bribe? If Enver Gortash is killed [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Pantella Security's tightened since Gortash's death. You stay in your designated district. Kolobeg Aw, come on, Saer Fist, we got urgent deliveries to make. Fist Gneiss Urgent, is it? Why, you could be trying to sneak Gortash's assassins out in your cargo. I'd better search your goods. Kolobeg You're joking, right? DEN_Refugee Komira is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter in the Emerald Grove in Act One . “ Argh. Let me through, mragreshem, or I'll rip your damned throat out! „ — Komira , trying to free her daughter Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Komira and her husband Locke are near the entrance of the Sacred Pool , attempting to reach their daughter Arabella , whom Kagha has taken prisoner after her failed attempt to steal the Idol of Silvanus . If the party interact with Komira and Locke, they can offer to speak with Kagha on their behalf. This initiates ⁠ Save Arabella . If the party return Arabella to her parents, Komira and Locke offer Komira's Locket as gratitude. If Arabella dies but Komira, Locke, and Kagha survive, the two of them move to poison Kagha at the camp celebration . The party can either allow them to poison her or try to convince them otherwise. If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving the Rite of Thorns, the tieflings are expelled from the Grove and Komira's corpse are among the pile of refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Arabella survives into Act Two , she moves to Reithwin Town , where she asks the party to ⁠ Find Arabella's Parents . The corpses of Locke and Komira are in the eastern wing of the children's ward at X: -185 Y: 12 within the House of Healing . Sister Lidwin is tending to their bodies but does not understand they are dead. Passing a Deception or Sleight of Hand check can convince her that her "patients" are cured. SCL_Corpse True Soul Korliss is a deceased True Soul of the Cult of the Absolute . Her body is on the Ruined Battlefield surrounded by lit torches in Act Two . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] At some point before the party's arrival, Korliss was indoctrinated into the Cult of the Absolute and made a True Soul . Charged by Ketheric Thorm with the mission to scout out and locate a nest of non-believers [ 2 ] , she set out east from Moonrise Towers to the ruins of the village by the Ruined Battlefield , where she was stalked by the shadows and attempted to evade them, though she still ultimately perished later. Casting Speak with Dead on her corpse reveals that she was attacked by Shadow Mastiffs but repelled them by lighting torches with the Continual Flame spell. Unfortunately, with her protected area surrounded by Shadow Mastiffs, she was unable to leave her safety cordon and soon died of hunger and thirst before accomplishing her mission. The party can destroy the torches which triggers an attack by three Shadow Mastiffs led by a Shadow Mastiff Alpha . Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Journal Log of True Soul Korliss Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Korliss' corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who were you in life? True Soul Korliss True Soul of the Absolute... Korliss by name... Where are you from? True Soul Korliss To Waterdeep born... to Moonrise called... What is your profession? True Soul Korliss Wizard... General Thorm's favoured... How do I destroy Ketheric Thorm? True Soul Korliss Ketheric Thorm... is unequalled... eternal... How did you end up here? True Soul Korliss Trapped... shadow mastiffs... repelled them with flame... How are the torches still burning? True Soul Korliss Spell... Continual Flame... How can I extinguish the torch flames? True Soul Korliss Destroy torches... How did you die? True Soul Korliss Unslaked hunger... unquenched thirst... Technical UID S_GOB_Warlock UUID d432aafd-f728-4d9d-9707-732e1cdd8297 Stats GOB_Dwarf_Warlock Eqp. EQP_Staff_Robe Trs. GLO_Warlock_Korilla Korrilla Hearthflame is a gold dwarven agent of Raphael's . She can be encountered briefly in Act One and Act Two . She later moves to Sharess' Caress , the House of Hope and potentially in the Elfsong Tavern during Act Three . “ Tr-tread carefully. You are still necessary. „ — Korrilla Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act One 1.2 Act Two 1.3 Act Three 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Loot 3 Idle banter 4 Related Quests 5 Related Literature 6 Bugs Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Korrilla's behavior during Act One and Act Two is not typical of most characters in Baldur's Gate 3, due to her nature as an agent of Raphael . If she spots the party getting too close to her, she disappears, with the player character making a remark about a 'bizarre' smell of sulphur. If they get close enough without being detected, the party member can pickpocket her for some common items and a small amount of gold, or trigger two lines of dialogue before she disappears. "You and I will have time aplenty to speak - but not tonight. This night is one of celebration - enjoy it while you can." Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] If Gut captures the party, Korrilla appears and kills the Goblin Priestess and her ogre guard Polma . She then frees the party and reveals that Raphael sent her. Korrilla then tells the party to watch their back, as Raphael will not always be around to save them. Regardless of potential interactions with Korrilla before, she can briefly be found at the Campsite , during the celebration at camp after completing ⁠ Save the Refugees . Shortly after the celebration starts, Korrilla teleports to the shoreline of the camp, to a spot between where Wyll and any hirelings hang out during the party. If the player character stands too close to her teleport location, she immediately disappears and sneaks towards the spot where Gale is camped; the party may briefly interact with her, before she disappears again. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Korrilla can briefly be seen spying on the party at the gates of the Mason's Guild . She teleports away quickly when the party gets too near. It is possible to trigger a brief dialogue if at least one party member is fast enough. She teleports away if the party attempts to attack, preventing all damage. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] She can be spotted and briefly spoken with in the Circus of the Last Days , between the tents near Lucretious and Popper . Later on, the party can finally encounter her on the ground floor of Sharess' Caress , her only relatively permanent location. After explaining her role under Raphael, she informs the party that Raphael is expecting them upstairs. If the contract is signed and she is not spoken with again in Sharess' Caress, Korilla shows up in the Elfsong Tavern and inquires about the meeting with Raphael. If the party enter the House of Hope , she can be found next to the Archivist in the Archive. Korrilla provides some background information on her sister, Hope , explaining that Raphael once offered both of them to serve him, but Korilla only continues to do so because Hope remains imprisoned and tortured for refusing. After the conversation, Korrilla teleports away. If the party steal the Orphic Hammer and attempt to leave the House of Hope, then Korrilla appears alongside Raphael and Yurgir to stop the party. She can be asked to betray Raphael but refuses and has no dialogue check to be convinced otherwise. Her low level and hit points make it easy to kill her, prompting Hope to mourn her sister when the fight is over. Recruiting Yurgir makes this more likely, as he cannot be controlled and is likely to involve and / or target her with sweeping area attacks. It is possible to minimize her risk of death by knocking her out with Non-Lethal Attacks or other means of crowd control. In this case, Hope will be happy if Korrilla survives. Then it's censoring, curfews - and soon we have to ask permission to just exist. „ — Korrinna Koreena Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Korrinna Koreena is outside of Baldur's Mouth . If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Korrinna and Flo Hurlburl demand answers from Fist Jerbold . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Korrinna Koreena What aren't you telling us? Flo Hurlburl Aren't you supposed to be on our side? Fist Jerbold Rest assured, citizens, Lord Gortash has the city's best interests at heart. Korrinna Koreena If you really wanted to keep us safe, you'd tell us what happened to the Watchers! Flo Hurlburl We deserve to know the truth! Fist Jerbold Your safety is of utmost importance to Lord Gortash. A full investigation is underway. Korrinna Koreena That's not an answer! Flo Hurlburl You're just trying to placate us! If the raid is successful, Kramp feels bad for killing the tiefling children, unlike his fellow goblins Rua and Sneem . Technical UID S_COL_Barracks_MistressOfSouls UUID 6068a46e-bbe4-4fc6-b955-cd8886fa5542 Stats Human_Cultist_Myrkul_MasterOfSouls Eqp. EQP_MasterOfSouls Trs. COL_Barracks_MistressOfSouls Kressa Bonedaughter [ 1 ] is a member of the Cult of Myrkul in the sanctum north of the Barracks in the Mind Flayer Colony . “ Kressa the Myrkulite necromancer patched you together... You were a tadpoled wreck down in this fleshpit. Nearly dead, head half-caved in. She said you were the first ever tadpoling victim. You're either one-in-a-million unlucky, or someone hated those stinking guts of yours to do such filthy work. Bloody vengeance seems appropriate. „ — Quest journal entry after speaking with Kressa Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Kressa is a Myrkulite necromancer [ 2 ] working under Balthazar , performing research and experiments on tadpolled victims in the Mind Flayer Colony. When met, she is rallying her fellow cultists, Hairy Henry , Ironfinger and Maghtew Budj . She provides the Myrkul's Gift buff. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] When approached by the party at the barracks, Kressa surmises that, because they are wandering around despite there being an active evacuation order from Ketheric Thorm , the party must be the attackers they were warned about. Unless a Deception dialogue option is chosen, combat starts. Otherwise, Kressa and her fellow cultists disperse towards their rooms in the barracks. [ 3 ] When spoken to again, she can give characters the Myrkul's Gift buff as well. The Dark Urge [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Dark Urge is chosen as Origin , Kressa instead recognizes the player character and reminisces about how the Urge used to be a captive at the colony before they were shipped away. She had found the Dark Urge close to death at this very sanctum, after they had been infected with a tadpole and opened them up endlessly for her research on the mind flayer parasites, thereby implying that the Urge was the very first tadpole victim. She displays an attachment to The Dark Urge because of a resilience that no other victim in the colony demonstrated. She inevitably attacks once this dialogue is concluded. The Dark Urge can pretend they are still docile but continuing the charade ends in combat with the added detriment of not getting any of the above exposition: [PERFORMANCE]  Play dumb - let her belive you lost your wits along with your memory.  (DC 10) After the battle, the Dark Urge remembers they were in the colony on their own business before someone ambushed them and left them to their fate. Unlike the Zealots, Adepts, and other members of the Cult of the Absolute , it appears Kressa and the other Mistresses of Souls are fully aware of what the Absolute is and the religious hoax they are perpetrating. [ 4 ] This greater understanding (and accompanying disdain) is shared by the other high-ranking Myrkulite necromancers serving Ketheric Thorm , with Kressa bemoaning the weak servility of the infected she is presented with, and Balthazar using the player character's worm-infested status as an expletive. HAV_Survivor Zealot Krizt is a Zealot of the Absolute stationed outside Moonrise Towers in Act Two . She guards the side entrance near the Moonrise Towers Docks , vetting new arrivals before they can enter. “ True Soul. A pleasure. What news from the field? „ — Krizt Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Krizt can only be interacted with if the party approaches Moonrise Towers for the first time. She probes party members through the use of her own Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen . Upon recognizing the player character as a True Soul , Krizt asks for news from the field; they can respond with a variety of dialogue options, but upon asking Krizt why she is on guard duty, she reveals that it is to recognise fellow True Souls. [ 1 ] Once the party enters Moonrise Towers, she returns to the towers and disappears. The party can later find her corpse in the Oubliette at X: 625 Y: -89 , where it can be looted. GOB_Goblin_Generic Krolla is a goblin stationed in the Goblin Camp in Act One . She is just left of the stage Volo is performing on, trying to organize a game of chicken chasing. If certain events have played out across the Wilderness , her 'chicken' will instead be the Owlbear Cub . “ Well now - you look like a tough'un. But 'ave you got smarts? Skill? Guts? „ — Krolla , challenging the player to take part in her game Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Krolla manages the chicken chasing game at the camp with the Dishevelled Chicken . If the Owlbear is dead and its cub is spared, Krolla alongside some other goblins capture it and debate if they should use it for their game. Considering it ate their only chicken, she sees it as a good replacement since it has feathers and a beak. When approached she invites the party to take part of the game with her setting a few ground rules. The chicken or owlbear must be lead between the posts across the obstacle filled courtyard to win the game. The course must be completed within 10 turns. The course must be completed alone by the creature. Buffs can be cast before they enter the course, but if anyone interrupts afterwards, the game is lost. A wager of 30 or 300 gold is required to start. If a party member agrees to play the game, the Owlbear Cub runs to X: -125 Y: 441 and Krolla climbs onto a nearby trunk. Once the party member approaches the owlbear in this spot, the game begins and a timer appears on the screen for 10 turns. It is recommended go into turn based mode as soon as it starts to plan movements, positioning and the use of jumps in a timely manner. The interacting party member must stay behind the chicken or owlbear cub to guide their direction. It is permitted to displace the trunks , crates , barrels and urns around the track to block the dead ends to force the owlbear towards the finish line. If a party member interacts with the Dishevelled Chicken or Owlbear Cub directly it is possible to bypass the game. Winning the game grants 35 Experience . Krolla congratulates the victor, but when she asked about winnings, she claims that only a goblin can win a chicken chasing, and refuses to give even return party's betting stake. A variety of skill checks can be made to convince her otherwise: [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  Then I'll write new rules - IN BLOOD AND GOBLIN-HIDE.  (DC 15  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Rules can be broken. And so can goblin bones.  (DC 15  ) [INTIMIDATION]  You mistook that for a request. My coin - now.  (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  We're having fun. Why ruin it now? (DC 18) [TRUE SOUL] [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  You'll be returning my coin - and all of yours. [ 1 ]   +1   +1   +1   +1 [DROW]  Goblins know to keep a civil tongue in the Underdark. Granted, most of them are slaves. [ 1 ] If a party member convinces the chicken or owlbear cub to attack the goblins (likely leading to their death), Krolla calls them out and demands compensation: I owe you nothing - I didn't kill it. (does nothing) [INTIMIDATION]  The game's not over. Maybe you can be the next chicken. (DC 10) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  ROAR.  (DC 10  ) [LOLTH-SWORN]  My people use goblin slaves for their games. They always die too. If a party member wages 300 gold, wins enough times or uses Illithid Powers on Krolla, then the game is closed. If they then interact with the owlbear cub and offer it to come to camp , it is possible to demand the cub itself as well as a prize without issue. UND_Duergar_Generic Stone Guard Kur is a duergar ranger who can be found in Grymforge during Act One . “ Drugnin' outsiders. You've got no business here. „ — Kur Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Kur is speaking with Brithvar in Grymforge. She seems to be his lieutenant. Stone Guard Kur is a loyal member of the Clan Flameshade. Should the party conspire with Brithvar against Nere , she joins them against the drow and duergar cultists. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Kur is predetermined to end the first turn of battle by retreating to the edge of a nearby lava pool, upon which Dalthar prioritises dashing and shoving her in over all other actions. If Dalthar is killed or blocked from pushing Kur into the lava, the remaining hostile cultists take that on as their main priority in a set order, starting with Greymon . Elder Brithvar Dead or alive, we ain't get our coin 'til Nere's dug out. Elder Brithvar Besides - I'd like to force-feed him some of that shit he's stirred up. Stone Guard Kur So say your chum blows Nere out of there. What then? Stone Guard Kur You sure we can trust 'em? Elder Brithvar Shit - 'course I ain't sure. I ain't even trust you most days. Elder Brithvar But we got nothin' to lose. It all goes to plan, and our arses get paid. Elder Brithvar If it goes belly-up? We got a scapegoat. It's Nere's game to lose. Elder Brithvar The gnome bolted. Saw it myself. Thrinn still ain't caught a whiff of her - slaves are paying the price. Elder Brithvar Those pricks'll get nowhere with just axes. Thrinn's gone touched in the head. Stone Guard Kur That's the cult's doing. Dunnol's joined up too. Stone Guard Kur Drugh. The cult-pricks are spreading like flies on shit. Stone Guard Kur See where the gnome sapper went? Elder Brithvar Thrinn ain't found a trace. Found a way past the rockfall, is my guess. Stone Guard Kur Skarjall still at it, then? Elder Brithvar Prick ain't stopped caning those beasts, last I saw. And he still ain't broke through. Technical UID S_LOW_EastwayFoodCrisis_Fist UUID af5e9de3-2f45-41bc-8406-fac8cb87b5f1 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Kuthbert is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in the streets of Lower City in Act Three . “ I said move along - unless you have a piglet up there somewhere, this doesn't concern you. „ — Kuthbert Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Kuthbert is stationed outside the Basilisk Gate Barracks , just aside the gate proper. He acts as a towncrier, announcing the confiscation of any remaining livestock from the citizen of Baldur's Gate "under the protection of the ducal council". Kuthbert is surrounded by a small group of farmers - Turnip Bubbs , Ploughman Zakk , Drussuvissill and Asparagus Mhallie , who take their outrage out on him for enforcing Enver Gortash's decrees. Kuthbert attempts to maintain peace, but is not actually interested in solving the bidders’ problems. If spoken with, Kuthbert tells the party to move along and leave him to placate the crowd. However, his attitude to the party might differ depending on the positive / negative article printed about them in the Baldur's Mouth Gazette (or neither printed at all), as an outcome for ⁠ Stop the Presses quest. Technical UID S_LOW_BloomridgeGhostWatch_Civilian2 UUID 579820b6-9fd1-4a5c-88bc-2c8e16ca2149 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Kydden is a dwarven civilian attempting to hunt ghosts in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Oh gods, I can feel them all around me! Ghosts! Like a horrible, slimy breeze! „ — Kydden Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Kydden is on the path to the House of Grief being led by 'Suspicious' Foont on a ghost hunt with Gaff Garsem , and Gor Falogen . Kydden is fearful, and claims to have seen and felt a ghost. The group are completely oblivious to an entire house full of haunted spirits in Lady Jannath's Estate just behind them, if the ⁠ Free the Artist quest is active. Kydden's attitude towards the party changes, depending on the outcome of the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Suspicious' Foont Gentlemen, I am quite certain that we are almost upon this most nefarious spirit! Gaff Garsem How, uh, how can you tell? 'Suspicious' Foont Can't you feel rich, unctuous gouts of necromantic energy simply coursing through the spirit field? Gaff Garsem Uh... I don't think so...? Gor Falogen That's because there's nothing here to feel. This is a colossal waste of time. Kydden I feel something! 'Suspicious' Foont Yes, my friend? What do you feel? Kydden My ears are cold! What does that mean? 'Suspicious' Foont Well, some spirits do communicate in a rather obtuse manner. 'Suspicious' Foont It could be inviting you to listen to the tale of its plight! 'Suspicious' Foont A sepulchral beckoning from beyond the veil! Gor Falogen Or his ears could just be cold. 'Suspicious' Foont Exercise caution! We do not yet know whether this spirit is malevolent or benign! Kydden Oh gods, what if it is malevolent? What if it's out to get us? 'Suspicious' Foont Worry not! I am well equipped to protect us in that eventuality. Gor Falogen You think that wand from that charlatan at Devil's Fee is going to protect us? Gor Falogen If there was anything we needed protecting from... 'Suspicious' Foont One must be prepared at all times - an unfortunate demise awaits the hasty. Kydden It's going to kill us, isn't it? Gaff Garsem You know, I'm not sure ghost hunting is for me... 'Suspicious' Foont Now, now - I'm sure it's much more scared of us than we should be of it. Kydden I've seen a real ghost snap someone in half! Kydden It squeezed their guts out of their ears like an overfilled sausage! Kydden Well, my cousin saw a real ghost snap someone in half. But they got better. Gor Falogen Well, I'm very glad they got better. 'Suspicious' Foont Hush! Too much cacophonous chatter and we'll scare away our quarry. Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRock_MessHallBodyguard_003 UUID 36078682-fde3-40cc-8f26-c238cb10c75e Stats WYR_MessHallBodyguard_03 Lady Durinbold's Attendant is a wood elven ranger who accompanies her mistress to the ceremony of ordaining Enver Gortash as an Archduke of Baldur's Gate in Act Three . “ Lady Alia says 'jump', and I jump. That's the way of things. „ — Lady Durinbold's Attendant Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Lady Durinbold's Attendant can be found at the mess hall, at the first floor of the Wyrm's Rock Fortress. She came with her mistress, Lady Alia Durinbold , and while waiting for her lady to descend from Audience Hall, spends time chatting with retinue members of other patriars. First time spoken to, she is discussing the Steel Watch with Lord Shattershield's Attendant and Lord Amber's Bodyguard , and asks the party's opinion on these automatons. She scolds Lord Amber's Bodyguard for his doubt in the Steel Watchers' abilities, saying that the constructs, unlike him, do the work better and without complaints. If talked with afterwards, she expresses utter obedience and loyalty to her mistress' demands. She repeats her lady's opinion that the Steel Watch and the Flaming Fist together are able to stop any army, even that of the Cult of the Absolute . If confronting Gortash, Lady Durinbold's Attendant can be found along with all other invited guests and their retinue slaughtered in the Audience hall. Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRock_MessHallBodyguard_003 UUID 36078682-fde3-40cc-8f26-c238cb10c75e Stats WYR_MessHallBodyguard_03 Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard is a half-orc battle master fighter who accompanied her mistress to the ordination of Enver Gortash as the Archduke of Baldur's Gate in Act Three . “ Cult army on the march, killer on the loose. And Mistress Durinbold still drags me hither and thither. „ — Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard is in the mess hall, on the first floor of the Wyrm's Rock Fortress . She came with her mistress, Lady Alia Durinbold , and while waiting for her lady to descend from Audience Hall, spends time chatting with retinue members of other patriars. She is engaged in casual conversation with Lady Oberon's Bodyguard , discussing the misfortunes of the Elturel tiefling exiles, and their fate in hands of Ulder Ravengard and Gortash. If spoken to, express worries for her mistress going about the city while there are dangers like cultists and serial killer around. Thinks that all those who hold power are the same, pureblood or not. If the party confront Gortash, Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard can be found along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the Audience hall. Range: Normal weapon range Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Longsword +1 Splint Armour Shield +1 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Lady Alia says the Absolute's army won't be causing trouble for Gortash - or for us. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard I'm not sure I believe her, but does it really matter? Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Meaning? Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard Meaning that in the games of generals and dukes, we're not even pawns, just dust on the board. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard What happens next is out of our hands. Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Gortash's got Ravengard on his side. That should tell you something. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard What? That every duke's just the same as the last, sticking up for each other as the sky falls around us? Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Gods, it must be exhausting to be so cynical. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard Not as exhausting as all that boot-kissing you've been doing. Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Ravengard's a hero! Elturel would still be stuck in the Hells if it weren't for him. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard Have you seen the tieflings at the south gate? Elturel's exiles, cast out by their own city. Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRock_MessHallBodyguard_006 UUID 6e383e38-7cde-4180-8eeb-b406ea90e365 Stats WYR_MessHallBodyguard_06 Lady Oberon's Bodyguard is a dragonborn battle master fighter who accompanies her mistress to the ordination Enver Gortash as the Archduke of Baldur's Gate in Act Three . “ You hear? M'lady says Absolute's army's on the march. Those Watchers will hold the line, you best believe. „ — Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Lady Oberon's Bodyguard is in the mess hall, on the first floor of Wyrm's Rock Fortress. She accompanied her mistress, Lady Freida Oberon and, while waiting for her lady to descend from Audience Hall, spends time chatting with the retinue of other patriars. She is engaged in casual conversation with Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard , discussing the misfortunes of the Elturel tiefling exiles, and their fate in hands of Ulder Ravengard and Gortash. If spoken with afterwards, she expresses confidence in the Steel Watch , repeating her lady's opinion. If the party confront Gortash, Lady Oberon's Bodyguard can be found along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the Audience hall. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard I'm not sure I believe her, but does it really matter? Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Meaning? Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard Meaning that in the games of generals and dukes, we're not even pawns, just dust on the board. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard What happens next is out of our hands. Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Gortash's got Ravengard on his side. That should tell you something. Lady Durinbold's Bodyguard What? That every duke's just the same as the last, sticking up for each other as the sky falls around us? Lady Oberon's Bodyguard Gods, it must be exhausting to be so cynical. EQ_Laezel Lae'zel of Crèche K'liir is an Origin Character and a recruitable Companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. She is a Githyanki Fighter with the Soldier background. Unless played as an origin character, Lae'zel is first encountered on the Nautiloid during the prologue, where she serves as a temporary companion, and can be properly recruited on the Roadside Cliffs in Act One . A ferocious warrior zealously devoted to the Lich Queen Vlaakith , Lae'zel will do whatever is necessary to end the terror of the Illithid and prove herself to her queen. “ Who am I? Your only chance of survival. „ — Lae'zel , introducing herself Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Personal quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Prologue 1.5.2 Act One 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Crèche K'liir 4 Involvement 4.1 Prologue 4.2 Act One 4.3 Act Two 4.4 Act Three 4.5 Endings 4.5.1 War against Vlaakith 4.5.2 Ascension 4.5.3 Life in Faerûn 5 Quest rewards 6 Interactions 6.1 Companion interactions 6.1.1 Act One 6.1.2 Act Two 6.1.3 Act Three 6.2 Unique interactions 6.2.1 Act One 6.2.2 Act Two 6.2.3 Act Three 6.3 Speak with Dead 7 Loot 7.1 Starting equipment 8 Achievements 9 Gallery 10 Camp animations 11 Notes and references 12 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] For a full overview of Lae'zel's starting features, see the articles Fighter and Githyanki . Background [ edit section | visual editor ] A fierce warrior from crèche K'liir, Lae'zel is a follower of Vlaakith, the Lich Queen of the githyanki. Sworn to obey her queen and serve as a blade against the Illithid, she was captured on her quest to present a Mind Flayer head to her crèche. Now, tadpoled and with few options at hand, she must find a way to rid herself of the parasite and finally prove herself as a worthy warrior to the Undying Queen. How she does it, and whether she remains loyal to Vlaakith, is something she can decide throughout the game. Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before she is recruited, Lae'zel is a level 1 Fighter with the following Ability Scores : 17 STR, 13 DEX, 14 CON, 11 INT, 12 WIS, 8 CHA. If she is recruited, Lae'zel reverts to a level 1 Fighter with standard ability scores for that class . She starts with a focus on two-handed weapons as is githyanki tradition. Upon reaching level 3, she will default to the Battle Master subclass, allowing her greater control of the battlefield and the ability to subdue foes with her martial prowess. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel does not have any special features unique to her. However, being the only githyanki companion, she can make the most out of exclusive passives and abilities that are available only to githyanki from their exclusive racial equipment found throughout the game. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel's personal quest as companion is ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior . As an origin her personal quest is ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior (Origin) . Her personal quest spans all acts of the game. In it, she explores her strong feelings of duty for her people, her zealous devotion to her queen, and where her loyalties should truly lie. Lae'zel's companion quest ties into two further, separate quests. In ⁠ Free Lae'zel , the party finds her trapped in a cage by a pair of tieflings, and must decide how to proceed. During ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss , Lae'zel must consider a proposition that promises to change the fate of her people forever. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel is recruited as a temporary companion during the Prologue on the Nautiloid by agreeing to fight with her when encountered; she can become a permanent companion during Act One. Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel is first encountered on the nautiloid while escaping from the ship; she joins the party as a temporary companion and leaves the party after successfully escaping. If Lae'zel is chosen as an Origin, she will be accompanied by Losiir in this encounter instead. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lae'zel survives the Nautiloid prologue, she can be encountered again in the Wilderness near the Roadside Cliffs at X: 242 Y: 370 . She has been captured and is being held in a wooden cage by two tieflings , Damays and Nymessa . If the party is able to free her, she can be invited to join them. If Lae'zel dies aboard the Nautiloid, her body will be found at the beach starting area. She can be brought back to life and recruited. Lae'zel can still be found in the cage if the party progresses to the Emerald Grove and triggers the initial attack scene at the gates. If the party progresses further into the game, Lae'zel breaks out of her cage and disappears, killing Damays and Nymessa if they are still alive. She can then be found later on and may still be recruited. After breaking out of the cage, if she is not admitted to the party until this point, she will show up when the party encounter the githyanki near the Mountain Pass . If not turned hostile during the encounter, she can be recruited at the end of the battle. If she dies during the battle as an ally or neutral, she can be revived and invited to join. If the player character misses or refuses all the recruitment opportunities above, she can be found again one final time near the first waypoint on the Rosymorn Monastery Trail where Crèche Y'llek is located for a final recruitment opportunity. Should the party proceed inside the crèche without having recruited Lae'zel, she will disappear from the mountain pass. When the party proceeds to the Shadow-Cursed Lands , they will find her as an Undead there, having gone the wrong way when trying to find the crèche. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Lae'zel/Approval Lae'zel Approves Lae'zel prefers direct approaches and is focused on quickly finding a solution to the tadpole infection, without wasting any time. She approves of direct solutions to problems, as well as avoiding unneccessary involvement in petty issues. Being resolute and displaying feats of martial skill also sit well with her. Lae'zel generally dislikes acts of mercy and compassion as well as showing submission, respect, or diplomacy when the simple use force is also a viable option. She does not agree with helping others for the sake of benevolence, despises showing weakness, and will vehemently disapprove of any form of neutral or positive interaction with Illithid of any sort. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Lae'zel/Romance Lae'zel can be romanced by characters of any gender. At first only about sex, the relationship will turn more serious as Lae'zel gradually learns to see the player character as an equal and then as a partner. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel has yellowish-green skin, with black accents below her ochre eyes, cheeks and neck. She has several scars, most prominent of all one that runs from her nose to her chin. These, along with her stern countenance, give her the look of a seasoned warrior that demands respect. Patterned black bumpy mottles adorn her face above her eyebrows and on her cheeks, and like all githyanki, she has a thin nose and long and pointed ears, with ridges protruding on the back edges. Her hair, kept shoulder-length, is auburn and straight, with a several adorned silver braids running along the side of her head and a small bun on the back. Though shorter than the rest of the companions, she stands proud and intimidating with a wiry, athletic frame. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel is depicted as xenophobic, arrogant, and quick to anger. Proud of her species, she frequently volunteers comments to the party detailing the nature of her people, often as a means to illustrate githyanki superiority. She can be rough in her expressions and often cares little for the feelings of others. In her mission to remove her mind flayer parasite, she will not hesitate to intimidate or harm those who would step in her way. Lae'zel is fiercely loyal to her queen Vlaakith , and is almost desperate in her determination to prove her worth. Over time, she can become more accepting of her companions [ 1 ] , though never losing her biting edge. Despite her often vicious behaviour, she is keenly observant and frequently understands the feelings of party members. As a seasoned warrior, Lae'zel is not above pragmatism either, willing to go along with a plan she finds distasteful or work together with someone she dislikes - as long as the party stands to benefit. She is still a juvenile to her people, which is shown in her youthful stubbornness at times. When romanced, Lae'zel will slowly begin to soften up to her partner and start enjoying the small things together with them, even seeing worth in Faerûn as a place to live in with her new lover. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Crèche K'liir [ edit section | visual editor ] While readily willing to boast of her people, Lae'zel is decidedly reserved when it comes to herself, and shares only fragments of her past before the conflict against the Absolute . She hails from crèche K'liir, also known as Stardock, [ 2 ] a githyanki enclave on an asteroid in the Tears of Selûne, an asteroid cluster near the namesake moon. [ 3 ] There, Lae'zel received the customary githyanki martial education, with lessons on how to battle, raid and plunder in the name of Vlaakith. This brutal training instilled a hatred for illithid in her, as well as turning her into a ruthless warrior, willing to do whatever is necessary to accomplish her missions. This indoctrination also reinforced her view of githyanki superiority and disdain (if not outright contempt) for other races. During her time in the crèche, she and her clutch battled beholders in a nearby asteroid and infiltrated a neogi spelljammer, slaying its entire crew. [ 4 ] Tested by battle, but still considered a youngling by her people, she sought to prove herself to Vlaakith as a worthy warrior, and be welcomed to the Astral Plane among her kin. [ 5 ] Thus, she set out in search of mind flayers, until then only heard of by her in stories, to battle and present her queen a severed illithid head as proof of worth. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Lae'zel is captured by the nautiloid during this mission, tadpoled in a cruel mockery of their ancestral feud. Kept in a pod, she awaited ceremorphosis , doomed to her fate. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel's personal quest is ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior . It is added to the journal upon recruiting her and spans all three acts of the game. Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel is first encountered during the battle aboard the nautiloid. Having escaped her pod, she ambushes the player character as they attempt to find an exit. Recognizing they are also free from illithid influence, she proposes a temporary alliance until they find a way out. After the ship crashes at the Ravaged Beach , she disappears leaving the party to fend for themselves until they find her again just north of the Roadside cliffs waypoint. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Once properly recruited by the player character to the party, Lae'zel discloses that her people know a way to rid themselves of tadpoles and that they must find a creche. While exploring the Hollow , a tiefling named Zorru can be encountered, who confesses to having run into a group of githyanki near the Mountain Pass . Upon reaching this location for the first time, a group of githyanki led by Kith'rak Voss skirmishes against a squad of Flaming Fists . The Fists are no match for Qudenos , Voss' mighty red dragon, who quickly dispatches them. Voss then turns to the party and interrogates them on the whereabouts of a Mysterious Artefact . Shadowheart and Lae'zel's presence can influence the result of this encounter, but regardless of the outcome, Lae'zel becomes angry that they are no closer to a cure for their parasites. Back at camp, Lae'zel confronts Shadowheart over the artefact she carries. Shadowheart refuses to part ways with the object, and mockingly suggests a duel at dawn - a duel she has no intention of participating in - to defuse the conflict. Instead, later that night, Shadowheart's true intentions for resolving their dispute become clear as the party is woken by a struggle between Shadowheart and Lae'zel, the latter pinned to the ground and Shadowheart with a knife at her neck. If the player character passes a skill check, their argument can be defused, with both agreeing to set their differences aside, at least for a time, and Lae'zel adopting begrudging respect for Shadowheart's resolute approach to conflict. Upon reaching the Rosymorn Monastery , some githyanki can be seen dealing with looters. Once inside, exploring the crèche can lead to an encounter with Ghustil Stornugoss at the infirmary. Stornugoss quickly diagnoses the party as being infected with tadpoles, and prompts them to use the nearby Zaith'isk , a device in fact used not for healing, but rather purification – through death. A determined Lae'zel at the infirmary, speaking after the Zaith'isk has exploded. The machine ultimately fails and, if a skill check fails to convince her otherwise, Stornugoss flees to inform the inquisitor. An audience is ultimately granted with Ch'r'ai W'wargaz , the inquisitor dispatched to the crèche to help them find the mysterious object Voss was after. The inquisitor quickly reveals he knows about the party and that they hold the artefact the githyanki are after. Whatever the outcome of this encounter, Vlaakith herself appears through a projection and reveals that the object is an Astral Prism, designed to contain someone. She demands the party kill the prism's inhabitant to earn her gratitude, and opens the way inside. If the player character does not volunteer, Lae'zel becomes angry, demands they comply, and threatens violence if they leave the room without first doing as her queen commands. Within the prism, the party can chose to spare or kill the Dream Visitor . Regardless of the party's decision while there, upon exiting, W'wargaz turns on them at the behest of Vlaakith, along with the rest of the crèche. At camp, Lae'zel mulls over the events at the crèche. Betrayed by her people, she believes it must be a test of faith from Vlaakith, yet seeds of doubt have been planted in her mind. Voss appears shortly after, asking to be heard. If given the chance, he asserts his firm conviction that Vlaakith is a pretender and the true son and heir of Gith , Orpheus , still lives. Voss leaves not long after, but not before asking the party to meet him at Sharess' Caress in Baldur's Gate . Lae'zel may then be guided down one of two paths: remain loyal to Vlaakith, or reject the Lich Queen and find Orpheus. Whatever her choice, the next stop in her quest is Baldur's Gate. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] At the end of Act 2, the party will be ambushed at their camp by githyanki monks . The Dream Visitor explains that they are under attack and opens a portal to the prism, urging the party to aid them. Inside, they find a Mind Flayer under attack by the same githyanki monks, the illithid quickly reaches out to the party, revealing that it is the Dream Visitor. Forced to aid it [ 7 ] , the party dispatches the githyanki and the mind flayer shares that it used the guise of the Dream Visitor to support them in their travels. Calling itself the Emperor , he explains the githyanki assaulted the prism in order to liberate its prisoner: Orpheus, and that the combined power of Orpheus and the Emperor is all that is keeping the party from becoming mindless thralls to the Netherbrain . As such, they have no other option but to side with him for the moment. Lae'zel shares her disbelief, explaining all githyanki have been told the Gith's son died to battle thousands of years ago - another one of Vlaakith's lies. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Arriving at Baldur's Gate, the party can proceed to meet with Voss at Sharess' Caress as pacted. There, they find Voss pleading with Raphael , who simply dismisses him. Raphael then explains he has the means to free Orpheus and is willing to assist Lae'zel and the party, for a price. Raphael's deal can be agreed to, in which case he gives the party the Orphic Hammer . Alternatively, he can be refused and his home, the House of Hope , can be raided instead to find it. Whatever path chosen, Voss will await the party in the Lower City Sewers for news of the hammer. At some point in camp, Vlaakith appears once more before Lae'zel, commanding Lae'zel to bow before her and comply with her decree to kill Orpheus. If Lae'zel previously rejected Vlaakith, she can be convinced to kneel to her queen and accept her once more. Lae'zel can also be inspired to remain true to herself and reject the Lich Queen for good, siding with the true heir of the Gith. With the hammer at hand, the party must bide their time until they can access the Astral Prism and Orpheus once more, as the Emperor refuses entry. This opportunity presents itself when confronting the Netherbrain at the Morphic Pool . Attempts to control it fail, and the Emperor pulls the party inside the prism in order to save them. Here, they can decide the Prince of the Comet's fate: staying loyal to Vlaakith and allying with the Emperor results in the mind flayer consuming Orpheus' brain in order to absorb his essence. The party members then must confront the Netherbrain with the Emperor as an ally. Alternatively, the party can reject the Emperor's offer, causing him to join the Netherbrain, and free Orpheus. Orpheus is initially hostile but, sensing the dire situation the world is in, changes his mind and quickly joins the party. He can furthermore decide to sacrifice himself to become illithid, or remain githyanki if a party member sacrifices themself. Whatever the case, Orpheus joins the party against the Netherbrain in the final battle for Baldur's Gate. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] War against Vlaakith [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel via an astral projection If Lae'zel betrays Vlaakith, allies with Voss and frees Orpheus, she joins the revolutionaries, bringing the fight to Vlaakith. If Orpheus becomes illithid, Lae'zel will call Quulos, one of Orpheus' dragons, and join Voss as they prepare to battle the Lich Queen. In the Epilogue, when spoken with through her astral projection, she mentions she and Voss will soon be meeting Zaerith Menyar-Ag-Gith , leader of the Githzerai , and is hopeful they can form an alliance and unify the Gith once more. If the player character romanced Lae'zel and destroyed the Netherbrain, they can choose to join her on her campaign, flying away together on a pair of red dragons. During the epilogue, both Lae'zel and the player character appear at Withers' gathering via astral projection. Ascension [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lae'zel remains loyal to Vlaakith, and fulfills her decree to slay Orpheus, she is welcomed back to Tu'narath, the Lich Queen's seat of power. There, she is ascended by the queen herself, a ritual reserved for only the mightiest heroes of the githyanki. A scene shows Vlaakith on her throne, welcoming Lae'zel nonchalant. From the shadows, githyanki zombies stare lifelessly as Lae'zel approaches, the queen using her psionic powers, forcing Lae'zel to kneel using her silver sword, grinning as she does. The camera slowly leaves the chamber as the doors close, Lae'zel's fate sealed. Withers can be asked her whereabouts in the Epilogue, to which he will reply she has ascended as she wished, but he can sense her presence no longer. He implies that she may have been consumed by the queen, as the rumours go, yet he cannot be certain. Life in Faerûn [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lae'zel sides with Orpheus but decides to stay in Faerûn, she launches a crusade to eradicate every Vlaakith-aligned Githyanki outpost on the Sword Coast, inviting the player character to join her in rooting out one of their last major strongholds in Chult. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Silver Sword of the Astral Plane — granted by Voss for showing him the Orphic Hammer as part of the quest ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss . Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead and has unique dialogue interactions as a companion available after certain events. Whenever one is available, she will have a floating [ ! ] icon above her. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] When first encountering Voss, if Lae'zel reveals she is infected with a tadpole, Voss sentences her to death. After dealing with the githyanki, Lae'zel expresses her anger at Voss, doubling down on finding the nearby crèche. After Vlaakith names Lae'zel a traitor upon returning from the first visit to the Astral Prism , she is distraught at her queen's betrayal. Lae'zel can be comforted or told it might be a test from Vlaakith. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Once Orpheus is revealed as the being trapped in the Astral Prism, Lae'zel can be spoken with. She will share her disbelief, and tell the party more about the long-thought-dead Prince of the Comets. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Unique interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Either as an origin, or in the party as a companion, Lae'zel has unique interactions and special dialogue with the following characters, listed by the act they are first encountered in. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Camp clothing model Underwear model Early Access model Astral projection model Alternate epilogue model Digital Artbook concept During the intro cinematic Steam Trading Card Appearance pre-release Digital Artbook armor concepts Camp animations [ edit section | visual editor ] While in camp, unless she is the selected active party member, Lae'zel periodically performs one of two idle animation routines. Both routines interact dynamically with her equipped gear: Combat dummy: Lae'zel unequips any off-hand item (storing it in her inventory) and strikes the combat dummy using her equipped main-hand weapon if it deals ⁠ Slashing damage and is not Light . If she has another weapon or none is equipped, she attacks unarmed. Swapping her main-hand weapon to a non-slashing or Light weapon while the routine is active causes her to briefly pause before transitioning to unarmed strikes. If her off-hand item is a weapon and is manually re-equipped there, Lae'zel briefly pauses the routine before unequipping it again and continuing. If the off-hand item is a shield, she may pause before ending the routine, or continue with the shield equipped. Weapon sharpening: If equipped with a qualifying weapon as described above, Lae'zel unequips her off-hand item and sharpens its blade at a whetstone wheel. The routine immediately ends if her main-hand weapon is removed, swapped to a non-qualifying type, or if the off-hand item is manually re-equipped. While either animation is active, opening Lae'zel's character sheet window displays her model holding only her main-hand weapon, as off-hand items remain suppressed in her inventory until the routine concludes and the off-hand item is automatically re-equipped. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 8 ] ↑ Lae'zel's relations and banter with Shadowheart is one example of how things may improve with those whom she initially despises. ↑ Baldur's Gate , party banter between Lae'zel and Minthara. Minthara: "I would like to visit your home one day, Lae'zel. Where is K'liir?" Lae'zel: "You may know it as Stardock. An asteroid, one of the Tears of Selûne. Its tunnels are home to all manner of creatures to hunt." ↑ Campsite , lines spoken by Lae'zel when asked about her hometown. "Next time you're able, look to the sky, watch the moon cross it. The Tears follow it. Rocky bodies tumbling through the Sea of Night. One of them is my crèche: K'liir." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Lae'zel when asked about her hometown. "My entire clutch battled beholders within the Eye of the Sky's tunnels. We infiltrated a neogi spelljammer and laid waste to its crew." ↑ 5.0 5.1 Mind Flayer Colony , party banter between Lae'zel and Wyll. Wyll: "Lae'zel - did you ever fight illithid creatures in your training days?" Lae'zel: "Never. The ghaik aboard the nautiloid was the first I ever witnessed in flesh." Wyll: "Really? I figured you would have joined your fellow gith in a colony raid." Lae'zel: "A young warrior is expected to fight their first ghaik with their cousins - kin hatched from the same clutch. The ones who triumph earn a place in githyanki society. The one's who don't, perish." ↑ Various locations, party banter between Lae'zel and Gale. Supplies_Vendor_Poor Lakrissa is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . “ We're tougher than we look. We've survived persecution. Survived Avernus. „ — Lakrissa on her fellow refugees Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Lakrissa usually guards one of the secret entrances into the sanctuary above the Secluded Chamber , in the Grove. If the party speak with her, Lakrissa responds with a sarcastic-pessimist attitude, saying their chances of survival are low. If the interacting party member obliges her, they can bet 10 Gold on whether they survive the trip to Baldur's Gate . If Lakrissa survives after the goblin leaders are killed, she attends the celebration and converses with Alfira . Lakrissa assures the player character that she has not forgotten of their bet (if they made one), but reminds them her people have not reached the city yet. The player character can then tell her to forget the bet and invite Lakrissa and Alfira to a drink instead, once they reach the city. If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving Kagha's ritual the Rite of Thorns , the tieflings are expelled from the Grove and Lakrissa's corpse is among the pile of refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lakrissa survives Act one she is later captured and moved to Moonrise Towers Prison with several other tieflings. Rescuing them from the prison advances ⁠ Rescue the Tieflings . If Alfira also survives Act One, reuniting them confirms they are romantically involved, and Alfira rewards the party with the Potent Robe . If Lakrissa is not freed from Moonrise Towers before the Nightsong is dealt with, or if the party visiting the Last Light Inn after releasing the prisoners but before Lakrissa makes it safely to the inn, then her corpse is in the Oubliette , together with those of all the other prisoners. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lakrissa survives to Act Three , she moves to the Elfsong Tavern where she waits tables. If the party bet her in Act One , party members with the Folk Hero background are granted the inspiration ⁠ A Bet Is a Bet . If Alfira also survives, the two of them are on the roof and where they share news of their relationship with the party. Should hold together. Kaldani Should ? Lakrissa Well. We won't be long finding out, I suppose. Lakrissa Goblins better bloody show up, after all this effort we're putting in. Kaldani Yup. Murderous is one thing, but late? Beshaba pass over. Lakrissa You think it'll make any difference? Kaldani What? Lakrissa All this . Getting ready, like. Kaldani I... I don't know. If the Grove prepare for a goblin raid during Act One, Lakrissa and Rikka visit Dammon for supplies: Rikka I do need some armour, you know. Lakrissa Me too. Dammon Can't outfit all of you at once. Dammon Anything else? Lakrissa Yes. A stiff drink. Rikka Make that two. Rikka I'm worried. I don't think we're ready. Lakrissa Ready as we'll ever be. Dammon Lakrissa's right. Can only do what we can. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira How's your shift going? Lakrissa A rich arsehole sent his drink back three times - so I spat in his last one. Alfira Lakrissa! Lakrissa He said it was 'delicious'. Alfira Rent is due soon. I was thinking I could do some busking? Lakrissa No need, I picked up some extra shifts. Alfira You didn't have to do that. Lakrissa I know - I wanted to. You just focus on your music. Alfira We made it, Lakrissa. Lakrissa Damn right - and not even pissy druids or cursed shadows could stop us. Alfira Only because I had you. Lakrissa Nah - you'd have been fine without me. But the company was welcome. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Lakrissa sells camp supplies, but is not marked as a trader on the map. In Act One she can only be traded with the first time she is spoken with. In Act Three she can be traded with normally. Technical UID S_LOW_LossDoorGuard UUID 90f9cb08-1019-424e-9b97-84d6a28898f2 Stats LOW_LossDoorGuard Lamona is a Sharran Fidelian within the Cloister of Sombre Embrace located at X: -421 Y: -1651 . “ This is a holy place - you would be wise to show respect. „ — Lamona Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character refuses to hand over Shadowheart Lamona fights alongside Mother Superior Viconia DeVir . Like the other Sharran Fidelians , she is primarily a spellcaster, and douses the battlefield in darkness to debuff the party. When the battle begins, she is the only one of all the sharrans who has the condition Temporarily Hostile . Therefore, if she is defeated with non-lethal attacks during the battle, she becomes neutral after a long rest and can then be spoken to. MOO_BugBearvendor_Trade Lann Tarv is a merchant on the ground floor of Moonrise Towers in Act Two . His special inventory is not available unless the party pass certain checks with Z'rell after the introduction scene further within Moonrise Towers. “ Hah! Bark, bark. Like a worg pup, you are. „ — Lann Tarv , mocking the player character Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act Two 1.1.1 Soul Coins 1.1.2 Getting lower prices 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Tactician and Honour mode 2.3 Loot 3 Store 4 Notes and references Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Soul Coins [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lann Tarv is approached with Karlach in the active party, there is an opportunity to receive three Soul Coins left with him on behalf of Florenta the Garrotter, on condition that Karlach listens to him while he tells the stories behind each of the three souls they contain. Although this is a devil's bargain, accepting these coins has no documented negative effects or approval changes. The player character can initially refuse the coins - offered by a devil - as "too risky" but still accept them after at Karlach's behest. Ultimately refusing the deal despite Karlach strongly suggesting otherwise causes -5 disapproval. If the party ultimately refuse the deal, or if Karlach is not present, the soul coins may still be acquired by theft or purchase. Getting lower prices [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can get better prices from him by suggesting he will not sell many wares with his attitude. Then, when he asks the interacting party member to prove their worth, they can respond: [HAG-EYED] [PERSUASION]  Bet the hag who ripped my eye out is howling from the grave. (DC 6) [PERSUASION]  If your stomach's strong enough, I'll tell you how I lost this eye. (DC 14) (if Volo removed eye) [WYLL] [INTIMIDATION]  The bastards who took my eye aren't singing. They're screaming in the Hells. (DC 14) [PERSUASION]  The Absolute is. I burned that druids' grove to the ground. (DC 6) [PERSUASION]  Dror Ragzlin isn't. I ripped him and his camp apart. (DC 14) [KARLACH] [PERSUASION]  The demons of the abyss sing my name and tremble. (DC 14) [INTIMIDATION]  You'll be shrieking my name if you keep asking innane questions. (DC 16) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  No songs. Just screams. (DC 16  ) [PERSUASION]  Nobody sings my name - I don't leave any witnesses. (DC 16) [EVIL CLERIC] [PERSUASION]  The gods - when I slit my enemies' throats and offer their lives up as tribute. (DC 16  ) [GOOD CLERIC] [PERSUASION]  Those who bathe in the warmth and light of the one I serve. (DC 16  ) [CLERIC] [PERSUASION]  Friends and enemies alike - for I wield the power of the divine with the ease of breathing. (DC 16  ) [WILD MAGIC] [PERSUASION]  Depends on what my magic summons - could be anything from a cow to a mephit. But they're all very musical, I assure you. (DC 16  ) [DRACONIC BLOODLINE] [PERSUASION]  My dragonblood sings every time I burn an enemy alive. (DC 16  ) [SORCERER] [PERSUASION]  The skies themselves - when they bow to my magic and unleash a tidal wave of power. (DC 16  ) [BARD] [PERSUASION]  Well, I mainly do the singing. Usually while beating my foes to a pulp - it's quite the sight. (DC 16  ) [ROGUE] [PERSUASION]  Nobody sings my name - I don't leave any witnesses. (DC 16  ) [GLOOM STALKER RANGER] [PERSUASION]  Footprints in untrodden places sing my travels and trials. (DC 16  ) [FIGHTER] [PERSUASION]  Check the calluses on my hands. Those come only from a steadfast grip on a weapon. (DC 16  ) [MONK] [PERSUASION]  Check my knuckles - I've felled plenty of foes with my fists alone. (DC 16  ) [OATH OF VENGEANCE] [INTIMIDATION]  The sinners who've fallen in the face of righteous justice. (DC 16  ) [OATH OF THE ANCIENTS] [INTIMIDATION]  Forgotten glades and eternal streams whisper their protector's name. (DC 16  ) [OATH OF DEVOTION] [INTIMIDATION]  Those I am sworn to protect. (DC 16  ) [OATH OF THE CROWN] [INTIMIDATION]  Citizens of the realm - everyone from paupers to kings. (DC 16  ) [OATHBREAKER] [INTIMIDATION]  Those who'd bind another to their will whisper my name in nightmares. (DC 16  ) [GALE] [PERSUASION]  Perhaps 'warrior' isn't the right word. But I could turn this tower to dust without twitching my finger. (DC 16) [LAE'ZEL] [INTIMIDATION]  Open shop, or it will be you howling my name and begging my mercies. (DC 16) [ASTARION] [DECEPTION]  Oh, no one sings it. But hundreds have died sobbing with my name on their lips. (DC 16) [SHADOWHEART] [INTIMIDATION]  Screaming my name, more like. I know how to inflict pain. Show respect, or I'll give you a demonstration. (DC 16) [DARK URGE] [INTIMIDATION]  I have cut from corpses a thousand tongues, and those thousand tongues sing of murder . (DC 16) [WIZARD] [PERSUASION]  The Weave itself - for I traverse its depths with the ease of breathing. (DC 16  ) [DRUID] [PERSUASION]  Nature's beasts - with fangs of fury and unsheathed claw. (DC 16  ) Doing so increases his attitude to the maximum (100) and grants one of the following inspirations: ⁠ Uncommon Recognition ( Folk Hero backgrounds) ⁠ Notched Armour ( Soldier backgrounds) Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Morningstar Damage: 4~11 1d8 + 3 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Technical UID S_MOO_AssaultHarper_001 UUID 1f0cddc9-db64-4f55-8bd8-53961c740e11 Stats MOO_Harper_Halfling_Ranger Eqp. EQP_Longbow_Dagger_Leather Trs. HAV_Survivor Harper Lanni is a lightfoot halfling ranger and Harper . Depending on if one of the original Harper allies are dead, she can take their place and help the party during the Assault on Moonrise Towers and be a potential ally during ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain . “ That figure... Selûne herself fights with us. „ — Lanni Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved in the Last Light Inn , and the Nightsong is freed from her cage to wage war against Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers , Lanni takes the place of one of the original Harper allies (either Antony , Essius , Lymn , or Naysa ) as a failsafe in the event that one of them has been killed before the Assault on Moonrise Towers . After the main battle, if she manages to survive the fight, she guards the first floor of Moonrise Towers with the remaining Harpers . [ 1 ] Speaking with Lanni after Ketheric Thorm has been defeated reveals her awe of the Elder Brain . She mentions how she fought a Mind Flayer before and lost half her squad to it. [ 2 ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Provided Lanni survives Moonrise Towers, she can be summoned as an ally through the Gather Your Allies variant Silver Harp Squadron , if ⁠ The High Harper is completed with Minsc alive, and either Antony, Naysa, or Lymn are dead. Technical UID S_LOW_DeadGondian UUID 41a7f5e2-c2d2-4fce-9fbb-4d534993e0b3 Stats Gnome_Gondian_Caster Gondian Lanpos Biggs is a dead member of the Church of Gond in Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Lanpos' corpse can be found in the lab level of the Steel Watch Foundry at X: -1948 Y: 422 . If using Speak with Dead , he reveals that the banites forced his husband Manser Biggs to beat him to death, because he discovered their sons Grindo and Hastar are held captive in the Iron Throne . Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Parchment (Steel Watch Foundry) Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Lanpos Biggs can be spoken to with Speak with Dead . Who are you? Gondian Lanpos Biggs Lanpos... Gondian... What is going on here? Gondian Lanpos Biggs Banites came... took over the Foundry... forced us to make... the Steel Watchers... How did you die? Gondian Lanpos Biggs The Banites had my husband beat me... for eavesdropping... What did you hear? Gondian Lanpos Biggs The prison... the Iron Throne... it's underwater. Submersible... under warehouse... docks... How many guards are in the building? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* How do I disable the Steel Watch? Gondian Lanpos Biggs Toobin ... only Toobin knows...
