TUT_Monster_Mindflayer The prologue Mind Flayer battles Commander Zhalk on the Nautiloid . “ Thrall. Connect the nerves of the transponder. We must escape. Now. „ — Mind flayer (prologue) Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] When the party enter the Nautiloid helm, the mind flayer orders them to connect the transponder before the ship crashes. Several fiends arrive and combat immediately commences. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind Blast ( ) Damage: 4~32 + modifiers 4d8 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Psychic Spew forth a conical wave of psychic energy and possibly   Stun targets within. INT Save Recharge: Long rest Tentacle Lash ( ) Damage: 6~24 2d10 + 4 ⁠ Psychic Lash out with your tentacles. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] The mind flayer joins combat as a party ally. It uses all its turns to fight Zhalk, ignoring all other enemies. It is possible to apply beneficial conditions like Bless to the mind flayer. However, if Zhalk and all imps and hellboars in the battle have died, the mind flayer claims that the party is no longer needed and becomes hostile. The prologue mind flayer is unique in that its health is slightly higher than mind flayers encountered later in the game. It also does not gain Charm on Tactician difficulty. Monster_Mindflayer The windmill Mind flayer is a notable mind flayer that is sleeping underneath the Abandoned Windmill in Rivington during Act Three . It is starved, as a result of its recent ceremorphosis . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If a party member interacts with the mind flayer, The Emperor informs them that it is a recently transformed mind flayer, and ushers them to kill it to consume its power. The party can sneak away via a Stealth check or awaken the mind flayer. Upon waking up, the mind flayer notices the party's tadpoles and asks for a fresh brain to consume, which initiates ⁠ Feed the Mind Flayer . The party can bring it a fresh corpse, tell it to find its own food, or kill it. The first and third options grant a free Illithid power. If the mind flayer is fed and not killed, it ventures to the Lower City and murders the Armbrust family and remains in their home until it is discovered by the guards. According to Absolute Orders: Newborn , which is carried by the mind flayer, its former name could have been Alyan, a member of the Flaming Fist . The following inspiration can be earned based on the choice to feed it or kill it: ⁠ Kill 'Em While They're Young ( Haunted One backgrounds) - for killing the mind flayer ⁠ Newfound Subject ( Noble backgrounds) - for feeding it ⁠ Unexpected Parenting ( Haunted One backgrounds) - for feeding it Providing the mind flayer with a dead body to feed on is considered an oathbreaking action for Vengeance Paladins , Ancients' Paladins , Paladins of Devotion , and Paladins of the Crown [ verify ] . Technical UID S_Player_Minsc UUID 0de603c5-42e2-4811-9dad-f652de080eba Stats Origin_Minsc Eqp. EQP_Minsc Variant 1 UID ORIGIN_Minsc UUID 9d5f838a-8595-490c-85d5-8a2a69414356 Stats Origin_Minsc Eqp. EQP_CC_Ranger Minsc of Rashemen is a recruitable Companion . He and Jaheira return from both Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn and are the only two recruitable companions who cannot be romanced . [ 1 ] He is a Human and a Hunter Ranger with the Folk Hero background. Minsc can first be found in The Counting House , where he has been tadpole-converted by the Absolute into a True Soul and criminal gang-leader known as the Stone Lord . He can be found again in the Abandoned Cistern ; knocking him out in the ensuing fight allows him to be freed from his brainwashing. After spending nearly a century Petrified together, Minsc and his beloved hamster sidekick Boo have finally been revived, and they seek a life of "butt-kicking" evil-doers to serve as a force of goodness, justice, and glory. Minsc is also the only character with access to the spell Find Familiar: Boo . Though voiced by Matthew Mercer, Minsc was motion-captured by other actors, Neil Newbon amongst them. “ If there is one thing Minsc hates more than beasts with bad breath - It is those who are tricksome with the truth! And turnips. But you are no turnip. Let that be of comfort, in your final moments. „ — Minsc , threatening Rakath Glitterbeard Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Starting class 1.2 Personal quest 1.3 Recruitment 1.3.1 Leaving the party 1.4 Approval 1.5 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 Backstory 3.1 The Iron Crisis 3.2 Shadows of Amn 3.3 Petrified for a century 4 Involvement 4.1 Act Three 4.2 Epilogue 4.2.1 Zhentarim Prisoner 4.2.2 Berserker Lodge 5 Speak with Dead 6 Related Literature 7 Related Quests 8 Loot 8.1 Starting equipment 9 Development 9.1 Changes from previous games 10 Minsc in official trailers 11 Gallery 12 Notes and references 13 See also 14 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] When first encountered, Minsc is a level 12 Ranger with the following Ability Scores : 20 STR, 15 DEX, 15 CON, 6 INT, 8 WIS, 9 CHA. If recruited he reverts to a level 1 Ranger with the standard ability scores for that Class . His default subclass is Hunter . Minsc has the Folk Hero background. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc does not have a personal quest, but he is directly tied to two others. First, he is the unwilling antagonist of Jaheira's companion quest ⁠ The High Harper , and completing this quest allows him to join the party. Second, his ending in the Epilogue is determined by the outcome of ⁠ Aid the Underduke , namely a conversation with Nine-Fingers Keene afterward. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc can be recruited during Act Three if Jaheira joined the party in Act Two. Progressing The High Harper leads to a fight with Minsc in the Lower City Sewers . To be recruited, he must be knocked-out on the final blow, otherwise Minsc dies without the possibility of being revived and Jaheira permanently leaves the party. The Emperor argues the Rashemi is too stupid to be of use but can be persuaded to extend the mind shield of the Mysterious Artefact in order to free Minsc from the Absolute's influence: [HISTORY]  His chaos saved the city before. We need him.  (DC 15) [INTIMIDATION]  You will do as I command, or I will find a way without you.  (DC 15) If Jaheira is dead, has not been recruited, or has left the party, the Emperor mentions he is "too far gone" and Minsc becomes hostile again with 1 hit point . After killing Minsc in this way, when spoken to, party members behave as though Jaheira had just left, even if she has never been with the party since Moonrise Towers . Approaching Minsc with the player character elsewhere and only Jaheira in the party may cause odd behaviour, possibly preventing him from being recruited. Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc's recruitment is tied to Jaheira and anything that causes her to leave will take Minsc along with her. This includes sacrificing her to Sarevok , killing her children or accepting Bhaal's blessing as the Dark Urge (or intimidating her to leave if they obtained the Slayer Form beforehand). Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Minsc/Approval Minsc Approves Minsc is not the brightest, but he is brave and loyal - and has the cutest familiar: Boo . [ 2 ] Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc cannot be romanced, remaining oblivious to any player character's possible attraction. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc, after freeing himself from a Mimic. Minsc is a towering, muscle-bound man; his clean-shaven scalp bears a vivid purple crescent that sweeps over his right brow and cheek, and his steel-gray eyes rest beneath heavy brows. Old nicks crisscross his broad arms like a map of hard-won battles. Plain silver-looped earrings, weather-stained studded leather beneath a scarlet sash, and a well-worn longsword slung across his back all underscore his Rashemi origins. Perched on his left shoulder sits a tiny brown hamster , whiskers twitching, the only soft edge to his otherwise imposing frame. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc is a skilled warrior who is otherwise blissfully bereft of the burdens of Intellect. He believes his friend Boo is actually a miniature giant space hamster and that he is the only one who can talk to him. He views the world in absolutes (no pun intended): if there is evil then it should be defeated. Despite her constant nagging, Minsc sees Jaheira as a dear friend and is very protective of her, going so far as to call her his honorary Wychlaran upon their reunion in Act Three . He intensely dislikes Viconia DeVir and Sarevok Anchev because of his history with the latter and because they are evil. Backstory [ edit section | visual editor ] See Minsc for a more complete backstory Minsc is a Rashemaar berserker from a matriarchal nation of Rashemen. As a young man, he went on a dajemma - a coming-of-age tradition for Rashemi men to travel the world accompanying his Wychlaran - a young witch Dynaheir . The Iron Crisis [ edit section | visual editor ] In their travels, they became separated and Dynaheir was snatched by gnolls . With the help of Gorion's Ward (the protagonist of the previous Baldur's Gate games) Minsc freed her and they travelled together, along with Imoen , Jaheira and Khalid . They resolved the Iron Crisis and defeated the culprit - Sarevok Anchev . Shadows of Amn [ edit section | visual editor ] Sometime after Sarevok's defeat, the group parted ways for a while until they once again joined up alongside their friends: Gorion's Ward, Imoen, Jaheira and Khalid. At some point in their travels, they were captured in a forest by Shadow Thieves and imprisoned in a dungeon beneath the city of Athkatla in Amn. Minsc, Jaheira and Imoen survived, but Dynaheir and Khalid were killed. Their captor was Jon Irenicus - an elven wizard who wanted to steal the Bhaalspawn essence for himself. Minsc eventually helped Gorion's Ward to defeat him. Petrified for a century [ edit section | visual editor ] https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Awaken,_my_Minsc1.webm Minsc's petrified statue https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Awaken,_my_Minsc2.webm Combat in front of the statue https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Awaken,_my_Minsc3.webm Awaken, my Minsc At some point in their travels, Minsc and Boo were ambushed by an unknown individual, petrified, and left in the middle of marketplace in the Upper City of Baldur's Gate . For a long time, Baldurians (including Jaheira) believed it was a statue, commissioned by a merchant to commemorate the city's renowned heroes. It became a popular landmark under the title "Beloved Ranger". 80 years later, a wild mage named Delina tried to defend herself against a gargoyle and accidentally struck the statue with a wild magic surge . The surge dispelled the petrification, and Minsc and Boo returned to life, unaware of the passing of time. They joined forces and travelled together for a time. Approximately 10 years later, Minsc reunited with Jaheira. Together, they worked to uncover the mysterious Cult of the Absolute and were the first to reveal information about this threat. Unfortunately, Minsc's impulsive eagerness to fight resulted in his capture by the cultists and Jaheira, realising that they were severely unprepared and unarmed against this cult, decided to leave him in order to share news about this growing threat. Captured by the cult, Minsc was infected with a Tadpole and brainwashed into following a Doppelganger imitating Jaheira . Under the tadpole's influence, he became a feared murderer under the moniker "Stone Lord". Minsc was also separated from Boo as the tadpole suppressed his memory of the hamster. Their latest crime is robbing the Counting House . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] During Act Three, should the party arrive at the Counting House and delve into the vaults, they encounter Minsc accompanied by a doppelganger imitating Jaheira, with Minsc revealing himself by tearing his way out of the maw of a Mimic . When encountering Minsc in the Counting House he immediately leaves the building. Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc's appearance and dialogue at the party depend on the outcome of ⁠ Aid the Underduke and the subsequent conversation with Nine-Fingers Keene . Ambient chatter from Minsc in either ending has him impressed with the quality of meat Withers provides, though neither he nor Boo knows where Withers sourced it. Zhentarim Prisoner [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc in prisoner rags If Minsc is not present for the conversation with Nine-Fingers, he refuses to make amends with her or the player character sides with the Zhentarim , he arrives looking worse for wear, decked in rags. Without knowing the gravity of his situation, he reveals he has been kidnapped by the Zhentarim and was nearly about to be executed until Withers rescued him by spiriting him away for the party. Berserker Lodge [ edit section | visual editor ] Well dressed Minsc in the epilogue If Minsc agrees to help the Guild as their "berserker lodge", he appears well-dressed and accompanied by a halfling from the Guild, Happy Hoarson , whom he was in the middle of terrorizing for looting corpses. Minsc commends the player character and their companions for being ideal heroic role models, the kind of people Happy should strive to be more like. He also says that he no longer sleeps in "that" sewer; instead he has found a much nicer sewer to sleep in. An additional line of ambient chatter from Minsc in this ending has him exclaiming to Boo that Happy must be treated nicely if he is to reform. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc can be spoken to with Speak with Dead , although several dialogue options only show up based on if the player knows that information already. Mentioning Boo turns his focus towards it and nothing else If Minsc was not saved from the Absolute: What is your real name, Stone Lord? Minsc Minsc... of... Rashemen... What did you want in the Counting House? Minsc Zhentarim... precious... treasure... Did you have anything of value worth taking? Minsc ...Boo... BOO... BOO!... You were paying the Zhentarim? What for? Minsc ...Boo! BOO!...  (If Boo mentioned) Minsc Kill... Nine-Fingers... seize... Guildhall... If Minsc witnessed the Dark Urge accept Bhaal: Why did you make me kill you? Minsc ...Boo...  (If Boo mentioned) Minsc Believed... in you... wrong... How did your Harpers know to wait in ambush? Minsc ...Boo...?...  (If Boo mentioned) Minsc Jaheira... smarter than you... smarter... than Minsc... If Minsc was reunited with Boo: What will happen to Boo without you? Minsc ...Boo... BOO... BOO!... Related Literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Domovoi Invocation Register of Goods Received Stolen Property - Reward Offered! The Stone Lord's Sketches Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Aid the Underduke ⁠ The High Harper Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Starting equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Alchemy Pouch Camp Supply Sack Leather Boots Leather Gloves Longsword Minsc's Fantastical Relaxation Garb Minsc's Leather Armour Minsc's Tasteful Boots Minsc's Underwear Potion of Healing Scroll of Revivify - 2x Development [ edit section | visual editor ] Unlike other companions, Minsc, alongside Jaheira , was revealed in a trailer at the Video Game Awards 2022. Minsc was initially slated to be a playable origin , his scrapped content was datamined back in 2020. Tieflings in the Emerald Grove had special dialogue reactions to him and his hamster. Changes from previous games [ edit section | visual editor ] Unlike Jaheira, whose stats remained fairly consistent through the games, Minsc's Ability Scores in Baldur's Gate 3 differ heavily from his stats from Baldur's Gate 1 & 2 . In previous games, he is depicted as immensely strong, being able to punch through walls and break himself out of cages. However, his stats as a companion in Baldur's Gate 3 do not reflect this. This is likely due to the fact that while previous games use stat rolling, Baldur's Gate 3 uses 27 Point-Buy; it also allows his Ranger abilities to function more reliably due to his high Wisdom. If one seeks to emulate Minsc's ability scores from prior incarnations of the game, an arguably close approximation is: STR 17, DEX 15, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 8, CHA 10. This distribution leaves only STR and WIS as unattainable outliers at the start of the game, as his previous STR is 18, (requiring an ASI) and his WIS 6 - which would be problematic for a Ranger in Fifth Edition. The NPC Version of Minsc encountered in the Sewers uses a stat-block reminiscent of the previous entries in the series: STR 20, DEX 15, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 6, CHA 9. He swaps to his playable version after the conversation introducing Boo to the party. In Baldur's Gate 3, Minsc is voiced by Matthew Mercer , replacing Jim Cummings from previous games. GOB_DrowCommander Trs. GOB_DrowCommander Nightwarden Minthara [ 1 ] Baenre is a recruitable [ 2 ] Companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. She is a Lolth-Sworn Drow [ 3 ] and an Oath of Vengeance Paladin with the Noble background. Ruthless in service of the Absolute , she commands a camp of goblins planning an attack on the Emerald Grove in the name of their god. Initially hostile, she can be re-encountered during Act Two and saved from execution. “ Bhaal , Lolth ... the Absolute . They do not have followers - they only have victims, and they reward devotion with death. „ — Minthara , on gods Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Personal quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Act One 1.5.2 Act Two 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Menzoberranzan 3.2 Indoctrination and time in the Cult 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.1.1 Save the Refugees 4.1.2 Raiding the Grove 4.1.3 Double-Crossing Minthara 4.2 Act Two 4.2.1 Decide Minthara's Fate 4.3 Act Three 4.3.1 Get Orin's Netherstone 4.4 Endings 4.4.1 Return to Menzoberranzan 4.4.2 Baldur's Gate 5 Quest rewards 6 Interactions 6.1 Companion interactions 6.1.1 Act Two 6.1.2 Act Three 6.2 Unique interactions 7 Combat 8 Loot 8.1 Starting equipment 9 Idle banter 10 Speak with Dead 11 Related literature 12 Related Quests 13 Gallery 14 Notes and references 15 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] For a full overview of Minthara's starting features, see the articles Paladin , Oath of Vengeance , and Lolth-sworn drow . Background [ edit section | visual editor ] A member of the ancient House Baenre , Minthara is a True Soul in service of the Absolute. She is one of the three leaders of the Goblin Camp in the Wilderness . She and her fellow True Souls, Priestess Gut and Dror Ragzlin , set up a base of operations in an old Selûnite temple in search of a Mysterious Artefact by order of Ketheric Thorm . [ 4 ] Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before she is recruited, Minthara is a level 6 paladin with the following Ability Scores : 16 STR, 15 DEX, 14 CON, 10 INT, 12 WIS, 17 CHA. If recruited, Minthara reverts to a level 1 Oath of Vengeance paladin with the standard ability scores for that Class , and a focus on dual-wielding one-handed weapons. This presents an offence-oriented toolkit with many ways to control and debuff foes. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara's passive Soul Branding allows her to grant herself or an ally an additional 5 m / 17 ft of movement and 2d4 + 1 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage on their next attack. She also bears the Brand of the Absolute and can fully benefit from items with this effect. Furthermore, she has access to the following illithid powers : Charm Concentrated Blast Favourable Beginnings Psionic Backlash Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara does not have a personal quest like other companions. However, she is directly involved in other important quests. As part of the main-quest ⁠ Save the Refugees , the party can decide which side to support in the conflict between the goblins and druids of the grove. If siding with the druids and refugees, Minthara becomes hostile and is an objective of ⁠ Defeat the Goblins . If siding with the Absolute, she appears as an ally during ⁠ Raid the Grove . If the grove remains sealed the day of the raid, she instructs her raiders to kill the party. In ⁠ Decide Minthara's Fate , the party can decide what happens to Minthara after her trial at the hands of Ketheric Thorm and Disciple Z'rell at Moonrise Towers . [ 5 ] . After recruiting Minthara, she has a personal interest in destroying the Cult of the Absolute and killing Orin the Red for revenge, therefore completing ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone . Orin killed Minthara's drow companions and tortured and enslaved her to the Cult of the Absolute through implanting a tadpole in Minthara's brain. The Cult of the Absolute forced Minthara to commit massacres on their enemies. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Although Minthara can be first encountered in Act One , she cannot be recruited as a permanent companion before reaching Moonrise Towers in Act Two . [ 6 ] [ 7 ] If the party side with Minthara during ⁠ Save the Refugees and raid the grove with her, no additional steps are needed to ensure she appears at Moonrise Towers. If the party side with the druids, Minthara must be Knocked Out when fought. This can be done in the Shattered Sanctum or when defending the grove from the goblin attack. [ 8 ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Minthara survives the events of Act One, she can be found at Moonrise Towers facing trial by Ketheric Thorm for failing to find the Mysterious Artefact. Sentenced to death, Minthara is taken to Moonrise Towers Prison to be tortured until her execution. The party can help her escape and, if invited to camp, she can be recruited to the party. “ The drow is unpredictable, uncompromising. I respect her almost as much as I distrust her. „ — Lae'zel , speaking to the player character after Minthara is recruited Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Minthara/Approval Minthara Approves Minthara approves of displays of power and control, often in the form of violent, if not efficient, solutions to problems. She respects those with the strength to follow their own will, and enjoys cruel irony on occasion. [ verify ] Minthara dislikes shows of compassion, especially towards those she considers weak. She disapproves of any form of benevolence without something to gain for it, as well as senseless violence that does not aid the party in some way. Above all, she despises acts of weakness and any worship of Lolth . Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Minthara/Romance If the player character sides with the Absolutists and successfully raids the Emerald Grove , they can have a one-night stand with Minthara while celebrating their victory. Should Minthara be saved and recruited, she can be romanced by characters of any gender. Though initially cold, Minthara may eventually reveal some of her deepest fears to her partner, and may also display a more romantic, if not jealous, side of her. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara has an imposing presence. With a stern countenance, piercing eyes, and a low, regal and steady voice, Minthara has an imposing presence. Like most drow, she has purplish-blue skin, crimson eyes, pointed ears, and is lithe of frame with delicate features. Familiar with combat, she remains trim and fit, and carries herself with a measure of confidence not uncommon to many nobles. Her hair is silver with light gold highlights kept in a loosely arranged top bun, with stray strands adorning the sides of her face. On the left side of her neck, she bears the seal of House Baenre in black, marking her a member of the ancestral house. Her equipment is of the finest quality, and her at-ease clothes reflect some of her noble upbringing. Given all of these things, Minthara is found quite attractive by many and, like Shadowheart , she is fully aware of these perceptions. [ 9 ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] As a Lolth-sworn drow and follower of the Absolute, Minthara typically has a highly hostile and cruel attitude towards other beings, [ 10 ] considering almost everyone as inferior. She has a special disdain for those who do not share her beliefs, and holds other drow in high regard. Her upbringing as a noble in Menzoberranzan further compounds her superiority complex. Aligned with the Absolute, she is willing to do whatever it takes to serve it. Prideful, [ 11 ] Power hungry [ 12 ] and a product of her drow upbringing, she is always looking for ways to increase her standing among her peers. Previously a follower of Lolth, she also knows that violence, deception, and cruelty are effective tools to obtain what she wants, and are tools she has considerable experience with. Despite her overt dislike for others, as a result of her constant striving for power and influence, Minthara knows to "read the room". She: Is observant, always studying those around and surrounding her Often understands the plights of her companions, even if she may not care for them Is always willing to offer a solution in her own way; though her methods are sometimes extreme, they always have sound reasoning Does not support mindless cruelty if it serves no purpose, and even shows a weak spot for Scratch If romanced, Minthara may reveal that she harbours doubts about her life and circumstances. Whether due to her looks, power and influence or attitude, Minthara concedes she has had several past lovers [ 13 ] and, unbeknownst to her, even has a few suitors amongst the goblins. [ 14 ] [ 15 ] If recruited and freed from the Absolute's influence, Minthara's cruelty becomes more tempered, and her fury is aimed solely at other leaders of the Cult - particularly Orin the Red . She becomes contemplative of her actions under the Absolute's influence, and rues their exploitation of her fears and yearning for belonging to use her as a tool. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Menzoberranzan [ edit section | visual editor ] Born into the ancient House Baenre of Menzoberranzan, Minthara was raised as a noble of the city in Qu'ellarz'orl , a plateau above the city expanse. [ 16 ] Taught in the ways of Lolth , she rose to be an important house matron, enjoying all the luxuries of her birthright. [ 17 ] She survived her first assassination attempt as a child, and another at the hands of her mother when she came of age. [ 18 ] Sometime during her life there, Minthara encountered a True Soul and two novices preaching the message of the Absolute . Minthara hanged and displayed them as a warning against heresy, [ 19 ] but curiosity got the best of her and, after using necromancy on the corpses to find their base of operations, she prepared a retinue of warriors to strike at Moonrise Towers . Indoctrination and time in the Cult [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara recalls the story of her joining the Cult of the Absolute Minthara gathered her allies to battle the absolutists. Yet, when they arrived at the Moonrise Towers, they were met with a lavish feast and a welcome fit for a house matron. Ketheric Thorm had been expecting her, and invited her to partake of his feast alongside Orin the Red . He explained that he wished to form an alliance between Moonrise and Menzoberranzan, flattering Minthara and playing to her pride. [ 20 ] Lowering her guard, Minthara was unable to react in time as Orin jumped on the table and sliced her men's throats as she approached her. Standing before her, Orin expressed her interest in Minthara, and Ketheric approved, ordering her to be taken to the Mind Flayer Colony . [ 21 ] There, Minthara was held for some time, helplessly watching as her men were processed for food or turned into thralls. Eventually, Orin returned and placed a tadpole in Minthara's eye, sealing the drow's fate as part of the Cult of the Absolute . [ 22 ] Under orders of her new god , Minthara participated in many massacres carried out by the cult, mostly against religious communities who refused to be converted. She became a zealot, and in time, even began to admire Orin. Orin would manipulate her further, telling her lies of how she was a True Soul, chosen by the Absolute as her greatest weapon. [ 23 ] For Minthara, the Absolute was more than just a god, it was everything she ever truly wanted. [ 23 ] With a new purpose, Minthara proceeded to the Wilderness in search of a powerful weapon her new goddess desires, hungry to prove herself. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara is first encountered at the Shattered Sanctum within the Goblin Camp , planning an attack on Emerald Grove at the behest of the Absolute . When spoken to, she quickly identifies the player character as a fellow True Soul , and reveals she believes the druids are hiding a powerful weapon that the Absolute desires. She has been surveying the land in search of the weapon, sending scouts to track the leader of the grove, Halsin. [ 24 ] Minthara probes the party's minds with her tadpole, possibly exposing the grove's location. Save the Refugees [ edit section | visual editor ] Though Minthara does not have a personal quest, she is deeply involved in ⁠ Save the Refugees . The party can kill Minthara as part of the quest ⁠ Defeat the Goblins . With one of the three goblin leaders dead, Dror Ragzlin and Priestess Gut would be next. Raiding the Grove [ edit section | visual editor ] Alternatively, the party can agree to disclose the grove's location and raid it with the Absolutists, which initiates ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove . [ verify ] Minthara then moves to the inner gates of the Shattered Sanctum and disappears from there after being spoken with. She also disappears if the party venture to another area (i.e. the Worg Pens or the Goblin Camp or using fast travel). Even if she is knocked out before disappearing, the raid still triggers. Dror Ragzlin and Gut can still be killed after Minthara has left without her becoming hostile. The raid on the grove begins after the next Long Rest . Completing the raid causes Karlach and Wyll to permanently leave the party. After the grove is destroyed, Minthara and the goblins join the party at their camp to celebrate slaughtering the druids, even though they failed to find the weapon the Absolute desired. Minthara also offers a casual night of pleasure with the player character. Rejecting her offer angers her, but carries no negative consequences. After the celebrations, Minthara urges the party to join the Absolute at Moonrise Towers in the Shadow-Cursed Lands . She gives the party her Spider's Lyre to summon a guide that helps them through the deadly shadows, and she departs shortly after. Double-Crossing Minthara [ edit section | visual editor ] After initiating the raid on the grove, it is possible to double-cross her. To do so, during the raid of the Emerald Grove, the party must side with the tieflings. If the goblin forces are defeated and Minthara is killed or knocked out, then the quests ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin and ⁠ Defeat the Goblins are completed without having to kill or knock out Dror Ragzlin and Gut. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Decide Minthara's Fate [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara reacts with fear and outrage at Ketheric Thorm's death sentence for failing to retrieve the Mysterious Artefact. Should Minthara survive Act One, whether friendly or hostile, she can be encountered in Moonrise Towers on trial by Ketheric Thorm for failing to retrieve the Mysterious Artefact . The party can intervene on her behalf, but Ketheric sentences her to death regardless of what is said. This begins the quest ⁠ Decide Minthara's Fate . As Minthara is dragged away by the guards, the party can follow and find her at the Moonrise Towers Prison , undergoing torture by two gnome inquisitors. If both gnomes are killed beforehand, they will be replaced with the human and half-orc Absolutist clerics Nola and Mola . The party can join the questioners in erasing Minthara's mind, turning her into a witless thrall of the Absolute, or help her escape, either by slaying the gnomes or through dialogue. If Minthara is freed, the party must escort her out of the prison, through any combination of stealth, dialogue or violence. [ 25 ] Once freed, Minthara can leave or be permitted to join the party, at which point she joins the camp. However, she temporarily leaves the party whenever they venture back to regions in Act One . If told to go her own way, Minthara disappears, and does not return until after defeating Ketheric Thorm at the end of Act Two. After taking the portal from the mind flayer colony, she can be found sitting on his throne inside Moonrise Towers. At this point there is another opportunity to accept her as a companion or tell her again to go her own way, rebuffing her offer once more. [ verify ] Freeing and recruiting Minthara gains the following inspirations: ⁠ Nobleborn as Below, so Above ( Noble background) ⁠ Twice Scorned, Twice Abandoned ( Urchin background) If the party locate Isobel for the Absolutists and allow Balthazar to take the Nightsong during ⁠ Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic , an audience is granted with Ketheric Thorm, who allows the party to pray at the altar of the Absolute. Doing so ultimately results in the party's imprisonment in pods in the Mind Flayer Colony , where Balthazar attempts to turn them into zombies at his service. In the ensuing fight, the party may battle a Zombie Dror Ragzlin and Zombie Minthara , if either died during prior events. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara is one of the possible victims of Orin's kidnapping during Act Three as part of ⁠ Rescue Orin's Victim . If so, once Orin is defeated and Minthara rescued, she comments on the entire ordeal. Additionally, she expresses feeling disheartened after killing her former abuser. Although Orin could only copy the surface characteristics of her victims, Minthara saw herself in Orin's bloodlust and madness, a shattered but possible version of herself had she not broken free from the Absolute's control. Get Orin's Netherstone [ edit section | visual editor ] Having been indoctrinated into the Cult of the Absolute by Orin herself, Minthara has a personal stake in the quest ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone . Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] When spoken to in either ending, Minthara bemoans the party's lack of extravagance and asks if the player character regrets their decision not to control the Absolute. Ambient chatter from Minthara has her wryly suspecting there have been other reunions to which she has not been invited, that all the heroes gathering together paints a target on the party for hostile attack, and that she is becoming accustomed to the taste of surface-grown plants. Return to Menzoberranzan [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara can be encouraged to return to Menzoberranzan, to which she will agree, suggesting they put the gnomes back to work to rebuild the Steel Watch , returning as conquerors to found a new noble House. Six months after the fall of the absolutists, Minthara mentions the war against House Baenre is going well, but she welcomes the distraction of Withers' party. Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] Otherwise, if encouraged to stay in Baldur's Gate, Minthara proclaims Baldur's Gate needs new leadership which she is happy to provide. She shares that she has been scheming in the shadows and the political intrigue has been enjoyable. She asserts that the people will learn from her or bow to her. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Assassin's Touch - given by Minthara for escorting the goblin Sazza to the Goblin Camp and convincing her to spare her life. Gift from the Absolute — given by Minthara for siding with the absolutists and raiding the grove. Spider's Lyre — given by Minthara after the camp celebration upon successfully raiding the grove, or looted from her if killed or knocked out during Act One. Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] I will never tire of sitting on dead men's thrones. Minthara has unique dialogue interactions as a companion available after certain events. Whenever one is available, a floating [!] icon is visible above her. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon arrival at the camp as a companion, she has dialogue about her time under the Absolute and her vow of vengeance. If she joins the party while she still has unfinished dialogue, she asks the player character for privacy and cuts them out of this dialogue. After defeating Ketheric, Minthara sits on his throne, gloating. When spoken to, she reveals more about her indoctrination into the Cult, and her plans after the Cult is destroyed. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon reaching Rivington , Minthara comments on the state of the refugees and city's refusal to let them in. If pursuing a romance with her, she asks about the player character's thoughts on her. Unique interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] As a companion, Minthara has unique interactions and special dialogue with Viconia DeVir in Act Three. She also has has special dialogue if Viconia is mentioned with her in Act Two. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Minthara/Combat Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Minthara possesses the same items as her starting equipment, except for her underwear . If knocked unconscious, she neither drops a Mind Flayer Parasite nor a supply pack. [ 26 ] If all equipment and clothing are looted from her and she is left unconscious, she reappears in Act Two at Moonrise Towers in a new set of camp clothes including camp shoes and underwear. Starting equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] If looted: Minthara's At-Ease Clothes Minthara's Tasteful Boots Minthara's Underwear If not looted: Alchemy Pouch Boots of Striding Camp Supply Sack Dagger Drow Leather Gloves Mace Minthara's At-Ease Clothes Minthara's Tasteful Boots Minthara's Underwear Spider's Lyre Spidersilk Armour Supply Pack Xyanyde Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] At the goblin camp, Minthara can be found talking to Rozzak : Rozzak Wot are we waitin' for? Spears are sharp, the lads are all riled up an' ready! Nightwarden Minthara You have already failed me once, and now you dare question me? Rozzak I, er... didn't mean nothin' by it, yer ladyship. Honest I didn't. Nightwarden Minthara Your life, much like your words, is meaningless, whelp. End the latter to save the former. Nightwarden Minthara The village to the east - it's abandoned? Rozzak Looks that way. But scouts said they heard somethin' movin' around out there. Somethin' big. Nightwarden Minthara It's not our concern. Our prey are elsewhere. Nightwarden Minthara How many raiders do we have? Rozzak Plenty of lashers, loads of hunters... and a few pariahs to carry the powder kegs. Nightwarden Minthara These pariahs - they're prepared to fight for the Absolute? Rozzak What they do ain't exactly fightin'. All they gotta do is light up their powder and burn. Nightwarden Minthara Then they're prepared to die for the Absolute. Good. Rozzak Dyin's the only thing they're good at. Rozzak Prisoner'll talk, yer ladyship. Spike always makes 'em talk.  (After Zurga reports to Minthara) Nightwarden Minthara If he doesn't, I'll cut out his tongue. Rozzak If he don't have a tongue, he can't tell us nothin'! Nightwarden Minthara The prisoner can keep his tongue - it's Spike's I'll be removing. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who were you before the Absolute claimed you? Nightwarden Minthara Destined to be... matron mother... House Baenre... Why did you abandon Lolth? Nightwarden Minthara For the Absolute's lie... What were your ambitions before you died? Nightwarden Minthara To find a home... Where are you from? Nightwarden Minthara Menzoberranzan... How do you want to be remembered? Nightwarden Minthara The commander I was... not the slave... I became... Have you left anything unsaid or undone? Nightwarden Minthara Murdering Orin... Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Drow's Letter Love Letter Notes Note to Self Parchment Unfinished Love Letter War Map Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Decide Minthara's Fate ⁠ Defeat the Goblins ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Save the First Druid ⁠ Save the Refugees Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Camp clothing model Underwear model Early Access post-Patch 6 model Early Access Patch 5 model Early Access pre-Patch 5 model Epilogue model Alternate Epilogue model At the start of Early Access Patch 5 of Early Access Steam Trading Card Patch 6 of Early Access Digital Artbook concept Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 27 ] ↑ In traditional Drow names, the prefix "Min-" means "lesser", "minor", or "second", while the suffix "-thara" means "glyph", "marker", or "rune". Owen K.C. Stephens, "By Any Other Name: The Drow", Dragon 267 (January 2000): 28-31 ↑ Minthara went through some recruitment changes during development and after release. Intended to be recruited only if the grove was destroyed, prior to Patch 5, an exploit could be used to recruit Minthara when siding with the grove. Minthara had to be knocked out temporarily in Act 1, recovering after a long rest. Once the party reached Act 2 and acquired the spells Polymorph and Dominate Beast , they had to return to Shattered Sanctum , turn her into a sheep and dominate her. The party then had to fast-travel back to the Moonrise Towers and then had to move Minthara as a sheep into the throne room, where the judgement continued as if Minthara was alive. After the cutscene she would be transported to the dungeon. The party had to attack her quickly once imprisoned as she would begin to run away otherwise, and then turn invisible and exit combat. Minthara was then part of the interrogation scene and her recruitment could proceed as normal. When Patch 5 was introduced, Minthara could be recruited if she was knocked out temporarily at her camp in the Shattered Sanctum, dealing with the rest of the goblin camp without long rests in-between as the game files checked for both conditions in order to trigger her scene at Moonrise Towers. Patch 6 removed the requirement for Minthara being temporarily hostile / knocked out. The game no longer checks for that condition. It became possible to recruit Minthara through knocking her out when defending the grove from the goblin attack. However, if Minthara was knocked out in the goblin camp, the quest ⁠ Defeat the Goblins had to be finished prior to taking a Long Rest . Since Patch 7, all methods of knocking her out result in a recruitment opportunity. ↑ If the player character is a Lolth-sworn drow , many unique dialogue options are available, one of which includes condemning Minthara and attacking her for abandoning Lolth. ↑ Attracting Drow Exiles in Kethric Thorm's quarters. ↑ If Minthara is recruited as a companion and returns to Moonrise Towers while Ketheric Thorm is still alive, and she is not near the player character or another tadpole-infected companion, she will be (whether disguised or not) attacked if seen by tower guards or other principal followers of the Absolute . If other party members are nearby, they may be drawn into the conflict as well. The exact range required to avoid a fight is not yet known, but if avoiding one is desired, it is recommended that companion Minthara remain within sight of a tadpoled party member while in Moonrise Towers. ↑ If recruited, returning to Act One areas with Minthara in the active party causes her to leave the party. This can be circumvented by casting Silence on her before doing so. Minthara's limitation on travel between Acts and areas may have arisen because it is possible that, during development, she was intended to be a companion earlier than she ended up being for release. Therefore, travelling to Act One (once recruited in Act Two), while likely an originally intended behaviour for Minthara, was later revised and can now only be accomplished by exploit. This assertion is supported by the following: Point one: Minthara refuses to travel to Act One with the party unless silenced immediately prior. Normally, just prior to travel there, Minthara says, " If you intend to stray from Moonrise while Ketheric still lives, I shall remain at camp, strategising his downfall. " The player character may respond with, "I have unfinished business to attend to before dealing with Ketrheric", upon which she replies, " I do not. All that I did before you rescued me was as a puppet of the Absolute - it is behind me. Until Ketheric falls, only vengeance remains. " Point two: if the party returns to Act One without Minthara, all unequipped items in her inventory are removed and placed in a backpack in the inventory of the player character. Point three: Minthara has exploration lines for Rosymorn Monastery and the destruction sequence of the weapon on the rooftop. She also has an exploration line at the Nautiloid . Additionally, coded into the game's dialogue files are various points in Crèche Y'llek where the player character can gain or lose approval with Minthara, even though she can only be recruited later in Act Two and cannot travel back to Crèche Y'llek without use of an exploit. Point four: if the party returns to Act One with Minthara, she has no tent at camp. ↑ There is currently a bug involving Minthara if the party return to Act One. [ verify ] It works as follows: If Minthara is recruited while the player character is disguised and the party venture to an Act One area without Minthara in the active party roster, upon returning to Act Two, at camp Minthara behaves as if being a merchant who has -45 attitude with the player character. She does not speak with the player character (and therefore cannot rejoin the active party roster) until given enough gold or items of value through the barter window until her attitude is -19 or better (i.e., in the "yellow" area of the approval scale). Once this threshold is passed she can be brought back into the active party and interacted with as normal - and with her normal approval. To avoid this bug, either Minthara must be silenced before proceeding to Act One and have her in the active party or , upon returning, have the player character speak with her in the same disguise form they were using when she was recruited. ↑ As long as she is knocked out in the Shattered Sanctum , it is possible to complete ⁠ Defeat the Goblins after several long rests without compromising her recruitment in Act Two . ↑ In Act Three, if playing the Dark Urge , the player character can reveal they are a Bhaalspawn to Minthara and, via their tadpole, share visions of their grotesque thoughts and deeds with her. After doing so, she remarks in awe, " Elgg-hor... duk-tak ... slayer. There are many names for you, and all of them inspire dread. You are exquisite ." If responding with, "So are you", Minthara answers with a grin, "I know." ↑ If Minthara is recruited and asked about her thoughts on Shadowheart, then asked what she has against Shar , she reveals, "I have performed a thousand interrogations, squeezing out the most-guarded secrets held in heart, mind and soul. I can tell you this – when the trivial parts have been whittled away and I have sifted out what remains, in most cases a person amounts to nothing at all." ↑ If, after the party vanquish Ketheric Thorm for good, a recruited Minthara is asked about how she first encountered the Absolute , she relates how a true soul acolyte and their novices visited her in Menzoberranzen, preaching togetherness. After hanging them, she went to investigate Moonrise Towers with the intent of waging war on the Absolute. If the player character responds with "Given how we met, it's safe to say you failed" , Minthara irritably replies, "It is never safe to point out my shortcomings, iblith. " Later in the same conversation when Minthara explains how she was captured there, the player charater can point out "Pride can be a great weakness" , to which Minthara agrees, "I recognise my flaws - pride is certainly among them." ↑ If Minthara is rescued from Moonrise Towers and joins the party, the player character can speak with her about her paladin vows. If they do and challenge her vows as being hypocritical, Minthara ultimately responds, "I do not know what will happen to with my vows when I defeat all those who serve the Absolute. I do know that when I take the Absolute's power, I will not lose control of it as our enemies have. I will harness it to create a more perfect world. Any who object to the laws of that world will have no place in it, of course, and I will gladly eradicate them." ↑ Various locations, party banter between Minthara and Karlach. ↑ Parchment (Goblin Camp) ↑ Unfinished Love Letter by Klagga ↑ Campsite , line spoken by Minthara to a drow noble player character. "Like you, I lived in Qu'ellarz'orl, high above the city's sprawl." ↑ Prior to Patch 8, Hotfix 31, if Minthara was killed and then spoken with by Speak with Dead , there were two dialogue lines which revealed that she had a daughter. However, those line came from an old, cut pregnancy subplot that Larian shelved before release and has since confirmed as unused content. On their community Discord and in support‑ticket replies shared by users, Larian staff have said the daughter line is “legacy text that slipped through” and that Minthara does not have a child in the shipped narrative. ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Minthara when inquired about her upbringing in Menzoberranzan. "(...) I survived my first assassination attempt while I still suckled at my mother's breast. (...) When I came of age, she tried to take my life herself, and I gave her fresh scars to match those she earned protecting me." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Minthara when asked how she was indoctrinated. "A True Soul came to my city preaching a message of togetherness, accompanied by two novices. Menzoberranzan is not fertile grounds for such messages. I killed them, and hanged their bodies in my garden." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Minthara when asked how she came to be indoctrinated. "I expected a battle, but found a fully-laden feast table, and a welcome befitting a house matron. (...) Ketheric proposed an alliance between Moonrise and Menzoberranzzan. I admit, I was captivated by him." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Minthara when asked how she came to be indoctrinated. "Then, quick as lightning, she climbed onto the table, a dagger in each hand, and skipped toward me, slicing the throats out of my men as she passed them. (...) I want this one , she said. Ketheric nodded his permission, and I was taken below." ↑ Moonrise Towers , lines spoken by Minthara in the throne room after slaying Ketheric Thorm. "There was no god. Orin held me down in a cocoon of flesh, while a mind flayer forced a parasite into my brain. And she laughed at my fear." ↑ 23.0 23.1 Moonrise Towers, lines spoken by Minthara in the throne room after slaying Ketheric Thorm. "When I first visited Moonrise, I stood before the Absolute in awe. It was more of an idea than an entity. Pure love, total power. Orin was by my side. She told me that god had chosen me to be a True Soul. Blessed and adored." ↑ Drow's Letter by Minthara ↑ Any dialogue in which the party members are challenged for Minthara's presence includes the character to whom she is attached, and any skill checks are performed by that character. ↑ Prior to Patch #7, Minthara's Underwear could be looted, too. Since Patch #7 this is not possible anymore. However, her Underwear is still shown on her looted body. ↑ Minthara is the subject of BG3 themed Magic The Gathering cards External links [ edit section | visual editor ] House Baenre on the GOB_Goblin_Generic Sharp-Eye Mirg is a goblin stationed in the Goblin Camp in Act One . “ Bloody arm is killin' me. 'Ere's to the best sedative there is - BOOZE. „ — Mirg , complaining about an injury Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Sharp-Eye Mirg is in the main outdoor area of the Goblin Camp, complaining to Puli about a recent injury from a raid. If a party member successfully poisons the booze tub in the Goblin Camp, Mirg proposes a toast and encourages them to drink. The party member can then attempt to convince all the goblins to drink. Down the drink. ( DC  15 Constitution Saving Throw to avoid taking 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Poison for Duration: 10 turns) [SLEIGHT OF HAND]  Spill the beer, then pretend to drink from the empty cup.  (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  After you! I shouldn't drink before the host. (DC 10) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  Show off an elaborate bartending trick.  (DC 10  ) Failing any of the above checks allows another chance to avoid suspicion: Down the drink. (same as above) Drink quickly to squash their suspicions. (same as above) You caught me. It's poisoned. (this will turn the whole camp hostile) [PERSUASION]  I'm simply being a good guest, that's all. (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  I was checking none of you idiots had spilled anything foul in there. (DC 10) [PERFORMANCE]  Aw, c'mon. I've already had a few cups... can barely see straight. (DC 7) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read her mind. Don't be stupid. You might be able to drink all day - the Absolute needs me sober. If the party member is successful in tricking the goblins, Mirg is one of many who die from the poison. Technical UID S_LOW_GriefAttendant UUID 2d74b412-6ed8-438a-b229-6cee7a48acca Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Caster Mirie is a Sharran Fidelian who manages the front desk at the House of Grief during Act Three . “ Please enter. The Mapping of the Heart will begin once you are seated. „ — Mirie Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Investigate the House of Grief When approached, Mirie asks the interacting party member if they are here to become Unburdened. She senses they need help and recommends The Unburdening to ease them of their woes. Passing a DC 10 Insight Check reveals that she genuinely wants to help, but there may be caveats: [INSIGHT]  Usually a god would've been mentioned by now - is this a scam? (DC 20) To become Unburdened, the interacting party member must pay 1,000 gold. Mirie then leads the party through the locked doors to the Mapping Room . If Shadowheart is present, Mirie recognizes her and greets her differently depending whether she rejected or embraced Shar in ⁠ The Chosen of Shar . Shadowheart voices her desire to see the Mother Superior, but Mirie interjects that she must submit to a Mapping of the Heart first. Mirie then leads the party to the Mapping Room without requiring a fee. After killing or banishing Viconia DeVir , Mirie remains neutral and does not trade with any party member except Shadowheart, provided she remains loyal to Shar. If Shadowheart's parents are freed or killed, the three followers of Shar next to her become hostile and attack the party. PLA_Tavern_Civilian Mirileth's corpse is in Waukeen's Rest in Act One . “ It's for her sister's wedding. I made a stupid joke about keeping it. We argued about it for hours. Then she took the dowry and left. She said I'd never see her again. She was right. „ — Benryn , recounting their final interaction Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Mirileth was killed during the Absolutist raid on the inn. Her body is on the upper floor of the inn's west building at X: -85 Y: 600 . If a party member uses Speak with Dead before finding Benryn , she asks them to rescue him through a nearby door. After successfully retrieving him, Benryn rushes to her body and collapses in grief. If a party member uses Speak with Dead at this time, Benryn asks her about a Dowry Ring . She reveals that the ring is hidden in the barn behind the inn. After finding it, the party can keep it or return it to Benryn, which completes ⁠ Rescue the Trapped Man . He remains next to her corpse even after the quest is finished. Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Rescue the Trapped Man Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Mirileth's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Mirileth ... Mirileth... farmer... Why were you at the inn? Mirileth ... from Elturgard... travelling... sister's wedding... How did you die? Mirileth ... finding... husband... Benryn... inside... Mirileth ... door... locked... trapped... fire... Where is Benryn? Mirileth ... inside... room... top floor... Did you have any valuables nearby? Mirileth ... dowry... for sister... in barn... Where is your sister's dowry? Mirileth ... dowry... for sister... in barn... Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dowry Ring's inscription and the Quest Log refer to Mirileth as "Miri". After Benryn's rescue, looting her body in front of him becomes a crime . Looting her body yields a small amount of gold (10-15) and a bottle of wine. v t e Risen Road Characters Companions Karlach Flaming Fists Aelis Bryanne Dain Dion Ephren Florrick Jacek Ito Marilla Pavel Rowan Tristan Wexford Yeva Githyanki Baretha Chost For'reth Voss Zastri Paladins of Tyr Anders Buckle Refugee Trynn Traders Brem Cyrel Zhentarim Amnos Bellar Garias Jarg Karad Olly Rugan Salazon Vol Zarys Other Benryn Ellyka Krug Marten Mirileth Oskar Fevras Sszaryn Vance Yul Animals and Creatures Bloated Hyena Flind Frightened Ox Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Indra Isbeth Istor Qudenos Locations Mountain Pass Toll House Waukeen's Rest Zhentarim Basement Quests Find a Cure Find the Githyanki Crèche Find the Missing Shipment Find the Nightsong Free the Artist Hunt the Devil Our Fiery Friend Rescue the Trapped Man The Blade of Frontiers The Githyanki Warrior Travel to Moonrise Towers Travel through the Mountain Pass

Hellish Resistance Resistant to all Fire . Technical UID S_DEN_CharmedKid UUID 3b92c689-6024-4446-a6c9-584e9e8d77ca Stats DEN_Mirkon Trs. DEN_Kid Mirkon is a tiefling child near the Emerald Grove . He is listening to a mysterious song. “ No, no. It's just a bit of water. I only want to listen. Just a little closer... Yes, everything's gonna be fine... once I get there... „ — Mirkon , entranced by harpies Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Mirkon is in a strange trance at the Secluded Cove near the Emerald Grove, and is central to the quest ⁠ Investigate the Beach . Exploring the beach or speaking to Mirkon reveals several harpies as the source of the alluring song. If a Rogue party member steals from him ( DC 5 Sleight of Hands Check ) while he is charmed by the song and before the conflict begins, party members with the Criminal background receive ⁠ The Allure of Coin inspiration. Upon approaching a bit closer, the harpies attack the party. If Mirkon survives the encounter, he provides the password to the Tiefling Hideout and tells the party to visit Mol . This grants the ⁠ Slaying the Piper inspiration to party members with the Urchin background, and the ⁠ Protector of the Small inspiration to party members with the Folk Hero background. The inspirations ⁠ The Allure of Coin and ⁠ Slaying the Piper are mutually exclusive. Multiple triggers can cause Mirkon's death. If any are activated, he is killed by the harpies and his corpse is left in their nest. Known causes include: Using a Long Rest after entering Mirkon's range on the beach Killing the Goblin Camp leaders Betraying Minthara after luring her to the Grove Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Rolan is persuaded to stay with the tiefling refugees, Mirkon moves to the room near the bar of Last Light Inn and chats with Harper Bor . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Mirkon moves with Mattis near the Requisitioned Barn in Rivington . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act Two inside the Last Light Inn . Mirkon This might be cheating, but have you seen any treasure? Bor Can't say I have, but if I do, you'll be the first to know. Mirkon Promise? Bor Heh. I promise, kid. Mirkon I really want to win the treasure hunt. Ide always wins. Bor Well, my coin is on you. Just do your best, all right? Mirkon I will! Bor How goes the treasure hunt? Mirkon I haven't found anything yet, but I will! I can feel it. Bor No doubt. Just keep your eyes peeled. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_UnholyAssassin_02 UUID cec194b2-0e8d-4d38-a136-0e9b1c38c684 Stats LOW_UnholyAssassin Unholy Assassin Mitchia is a member of the Cult of Bhaal . She is found in the Temple of Bhaal , in the Lower City Sewers , during Act Three . “ So, you too passed Sarevok's tribunal. Make sure your standards do not slip - we have a reputation to maintain. „ — Mitchia , to a player character who has become the Unholy Assassin Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Mitchia is in the Bhaal Temple in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . She stands on the upper balcony of the temple and never descends to the central altar ground. Mitchia discusses with Eni Orin's victim displayed in a side alcove – one of those whom Orin impersonated to speak to the party in Rivington . If the party speak with Mitchia, her comments depend in part on whether they took part in the Murder Tribunal . If the Dark Urge is present, she may state that she looks forward to watching the duel between them and Orin , believing it will be instructive for her. Regardless of the outcome, Mitchia remains neutral to the party. Later in the Act Three , if the Dark Urge accepts their fate as Bhaal's chosen, she, along with Rycke and {CharLink|Sarevok Anchev}} move to the High Hall . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Mitchia has a uniquely deadly combination of abilities. Her Dread Embrace bonus action can paralyse a target which then guarantees a critical hit from her level 11 sneak attack. This combination deals 2d4 + 12d6 + 6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage and is then doubled again due vulnerability from her Aura of Murder resulting in a total of 40~172 damage; an average of 106 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage. Furthermore, she is protected by Sanctuary and Unstoppable so it can be difficult to kill her before she has a chance to unleash this combo. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Dread Embrace ( ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't move, act, or react. Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . WIS Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Sneak Attack (Melee) ( )   –   Murderous Cut Damage: 8~16 1d4 + 6 ⁠ Piercing + 1d6 ⁠ Weapon Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. Also works if you have an ally within 1.5 m (5 ft) of the target and you don't have Disadvantage . If you were Orin , how would you have killed it? Mitchia I would never dare to compare myself to Lady Orin. Mitchia But if it were my kill... Well. It would've been slower. Eni You'd have poisoned your prey? Seems a bit... dull. Mitchia Not if the poison made the skin leak blood and the eyes weep pus. Be creative. Eni I believe Orin first made an incision in the upper left clavicle. Mitchia I am afraid I must disagree. Orin's first cut was quite clearly the throat. Eni But... would she not toy with the victim? Why begin with a death blow? Mitchia A proper cut throat does not kill right away. It bleeds the victim. Eni Like a prize piglet, trussed up for the slaughter... Yes. You're quite right.
