Gold_Pocket_Modest Variant 1 UID UNI_WYR_DapperDrow_Sister_Naked UUID a5fb4957-29c1-4f58-a0e4-6ced8efccb0d Stats WYR_DapperDrow_Sister Trs. Gold_Pocket_Modest Nym Orlith [ 1 ] is a Seldarine Drow sex worker employed at Sharess' Caress , where she works alongside her twin brother, Sorn Orlith . “ With Baldur's Gate preparing for war, the Caress feels like the final flicker of a beautiful flame before darkness falls. „ — Nym Orlith , when asked about Sharess' Caress History [ edit section | visual editor ] Hailing from the Underdark , Sorn was originally employed as a courtesan, and Nym as an artisanal masseuse. The pair fled the Underdark due to the matriarchy's mistreatment of men, ultimately coming to work in Baldur's Gate. Nym says that life is easy in her line of work, and refers to Sharess' Caress as an "oasis of calm" within the "chaos" of Baldur's Gate. A Lolth-sworn Tav or Dark Urge can question the validity of their claims about their background by pointing out that Nym and Sorn are Seldarine Drow. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Services from Sorn or Nym individually cost 500 gold, and from both together cost 1000 gold. Completing ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion , then reporting back to Mamzell Amira and requesting a reward results in Mamzell Amira offering the party the drow's services at a discount; the player character can then hire one of the twins for free, or both for 500 Gold. All of Sorn and Nym's sex scenes are voice-only over a black screen, without any visuals; the lights in the room are turned off as "part of the experience." Sorn and Nym Orlith can be hired by the player character individually, or as a pair together with additional companions, although - in most cases - this is only possible if said companions are romanced. [ 2 ] If the player character is in a romance with Shadowheart and her final romance scene has not been triggered yet, she rejects the invitation, wanting the first time to be just her and the player character. After that scene, she enthusiastically agrees to have sex with Sorn, Nym, and the player character. Astarion , when romanced, only agrees after ⁠ The Pale Elf is completed. However, as the night unfolds the narrator notes that while Astarion plays his part enthusiastically, he either has "a look <...> that reveals he's a million realms away" or "in his eyes there is <...> an intensity that makes you [ 3 ] shiver" (depending on the quest outcome). A romanced Gale can be convinced to participate with DC 25 Persuasion Check , but once the scene begins, he ducks out and leaves behind an Astral Projection to participate in his stead. Halsin , when romanced, also always agrees, and if romanced at the same time as Shadowheart or Astarion, can join in alongside them. If Halsin joins alongside another romanced companion and increases the number of participants to five, Sorn observes that in Qu'ellarz'orrl custom, a group of five or more is "legally" an orgy, while four or fewer is simply a gathering. Other companions reject Sorn and Nym's invitation. However, Karlach admits that while having a foursome sounds appealing in theory, the reality of doing so with the twins is not. However, if the player character backs out as well and hires only one twin, she happily encourages them to have fun and save some for her later. While Sorn has a variety of comical and strange scenes available, Nym, as the less "extreme" option, has a single, fairly simple scene available. Nym only offers to commence activities once all non-participating party members have left the room. If any are present, she admonishes the player character, stating, "Look, you didn't sign a treaty permitting you to march a warband through my lands. You paid for sex." [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Once either or both of the twins are met in their room, the player character can also change their mind and decide not to go through with the act, which results in either sibling returning the fee paid. Receiving the service from either of the drow grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Alternative Vocations ( Guild Artisan background) ⁠ Carnal Rituals of Sharess ( Acolyte background) ⁠ Giving a Private Performance ( Entertainer background) Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Acid Splash ( ) Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Acid Throw a bubble of acid that damages each creature it hits. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Cloud of Daggers ( + ) Damage: 4~16 4d4 ⁠ Slashing Conjure a cloud of spinning daggers that attack anyone inside. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Darkness ( ) Create a cloud of magical darkness that Heavily Obscures and inflicts Blind to creatures within. Creatures cannot make ranged attacks into or out of it. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Long rest Knock ( + ) Unlock an object that is held shut by a mundane lock. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Lesser Restoration ( + ) Cure a creature from Diseased , Poisoned , Paralysis , or Blinded . Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Poison Spray ( ) Damage: 1~12 1d12 ⁠ Poison Project a puff of noxious gas, dealing 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Poison to a target. CON Save Range: 3 m (10 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Key Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ In Drow language, "Nym" means "lost", "skeleton", or "skull". See Owen K.C. Stephens, "By Any Other Name: The Drow", Dragon 267 (January 2000): 28-31 ↑ Astarion is the only known exception to this rule. If the player character has never slept with Astarion, is not romancing him, and he is present when Nym or Sorn is spoken with about the prospect of sleeping with her and Sorn together, Nym declares, "In that case, we will require two of you . And indeed, I suggest it because I have never seen a creature as fair as this beau beside you." To this Astarion replies, "What a world. I never dreamed I'd be on the paying end in a brothel. But, our leader here has made the mistake of failing to sleep with me so far, and it's a mistake I've been aching to correct." Astarion gives this rejoinder even if ⁠ The Pale Elf has not been completed, and the player character may then accept Nym's invitation for them all together as a foursome. ↑ I.e., the partnering player character ↑ A glitch sometimes occurs if Scratch is summoned when the player character and Shadowheart approach Nym and Sorn in their Private Room to initiate the sex scene. If manifesting, Nym and Sorn roll for initiative and combat begins. Dismissing Scratch solves this problem. Leave it for the goblins to kill. „ — Nymessa , about Lae'zel Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Nymessa and Damays disagree on their next steps for Lae'zel , who is trapped in an elevated cage. Nymessa argues that it is safer to leave "it" in the cage, but Damays argues that Lae'zel should be brought to Zevlor in the Emerald Grove . If the party approach, Lae'zel telepathically demands that the party free her, initiating ⁠ Free Lae'zel . The party can convince the tieflings to leave the area or offer to help kill Lae'zel. If Nymessa and Damays are not dispatched through intimidation, the party can ask about nearby healers. They suggest seeking out Nettie , which advances ⁠ Find a Cure and ⁠ Get Help from Healer Nettie . Attacking Damays and Nymessa by any means, including options that occur through the dialogue, is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of any Oath subclass . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Bleeri What's the matter with you, freshie? I know you're green, but you don't have to turn green, heh! Oaknuzzle He attacked that bottle like someone was going to give him a medal for it. Dickon Urgh... I feel like I'm going to die. Bleeri Nah, nah. Hold on until after training, then at least you'll get paid for dying. Or your next o' kin will, at least. Dickon I don't have a... ugh... I don't have a sweetheart. Oaknuzzle Wonder why, with you being such a catch right now. Bleeri Don't you worry about that, freshie. Soon you'll have a handsome new uniform, coin in your pocket, and the pick of the finest strange the city's got to offer! And the first round can be on you. Dickon Don't even mention drink... Oaknuzzle You've gone and done it now. Bleeri He's a big boy, supposedly. Not like I forced it down his neck. Bleeri You done yet? Don't even have any chunks to blow - it's all water! Oaknuzzle Water? Bleeri Well, liquid anyway. Dickon Where's it all coming from? There was just the toast, then a chaser, and one for the road... Bleeri It was quite a road, as I remember. Had to refuel a few times. Dickon Never again... Oaknuzzle Never again, until next time. Bleeri Deep breaths, laddie. You'll be right in no time. Oaknuzzle Good, because we have no time - this leaky wineskin's due back at barracks. Bleeri Half the new recruits will be in the same way - there's no rush. Bleeri Keep sucking in that sea air. Good for what ails you. Dickon Ale? Don't even say it... Dickon I think... I think I'm better now. Can't miss my first roll call for the Fists. Oaknuzzle You might want to wash up, first. Got a few souvenirs from the night stuck to your chin. Bleeri Aye, and you smell like that place down the docks where they dump out the fish guts. Technical UID S_GLO_OathbreakerKnight UUID 3939625d-86cc-4395-9d50-4f8b846c4231 Stats GLO_Oathbreaker_Paladin The Oathbreaker Knight is an Undead Oathbreaker in Baldur's Gate 3 who will appear before Paladin players who have broken their oaths, becoming a temporary Camp Follower . “ To know the reason for your fall is, perhaps, to know the shape of things to come. „ — Oathbreaker Knight , speaking with the fallen Paladin Breaking your Oath [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Paladin The Oathbreaker Knight appears to paladin party members who have broken their Oath, and tells them that he waits at the campsite. Questioning the Oathbreaker about his story and duties reveals he was the first Oathbreaker, who broke his oath when he disagreed with the cruel ways of his patron, for which he was shamed. Since then, he has guided other Oathbreakers after they failed to fulfill their oaths. Restoring your Oath [ edit section | visual editor ] If a character breaks their Oath by accident or otherwise wishes to re-dedicate themselves to their Oath, must speak to the Oathbreaker Knight in Camp . He offers to restore the Oath for a fee of 1,000gp. This allows the character to once again use their Channel Oath abilities. However, should they break their oath again, the cost to restore the oath increases to 2,000gp. If breaking the oath a third time, the price increases to 10,000gp. It then stays at 10,000gp for each subsequent oath restoration after the third one. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] “ "You're DONE FOR. Hear that? To arms!" „ — Oathbreaker Knight , when attacked It is possible to fight the Oathbreaker Knight in the Campsite . Doing so turns all nearby Camp Followers (including Scratch and the Owlbear Cub ) and Companions (who are not in the active party) hostile unless the Oathbreaker Knight is the one who starts combat (which can occur if a party member is caught pickpocketing him). His body cannot be looted upon defeat, but he will drop a Greatsword +1 , an Elixir of Heroism , and three Javelins on the ground when slain, and a Pouch containing a Plate Armour spawns at the location of where corpse was after a Long Rest . Withers still refuses to respec an Oathbreaker paladin if the Oathbreaker Knight is dead. Because the Oathbreaker does not respawn in camp after long rests, this effectively locks any Oathbreaker character out of re-specifying for the rest of the playthrough. Reclaiming an oath, then killing Oathbreaker Knight, then breaking the oath again permanently locks a paladin into a Oath Broken state, as there is no Oathbreaker Knight who can induct the character into the Oathbreaker subclass. Abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] Oathbreaker Knight has the typical ability kit of a high-level Oathbreaker paladin wielding a Greatsword, including one Channel Oath Charge and 10 Spell slots . Dreadful Aspect ( + ) Let your darkest emotions burst forth as a menacing pulse to   Frighten nearby enemies. WIS Save Range: Self Hellish Rebuke ( + ) Damage: 2~20 2d10 ⁠ Fire React to your next attacker with flames that deal 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. On a successful save, the target still takes half damage. Compelled Duel ( + ) Force an enemy to attack only you, giving it Disadvantage against other targets. WIS Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Control Undead ( + ) Use the power of your Oath to gain control over an undead creature. The undead will follow you around and attack your enemies. WIS Save Range: 6 m (20 ft) Crown of Madness ( + ) Instil madness in a humanoid enemy, making them attack the creature closest to them (other than you), even if it's allied. At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Lay on Hands: Greater Healing ( + 2 ) Healing 4 × (Paladin level) ⁠ Healing Imbue your hands with divine power to heal an ally. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Wrathful Smite ( + + ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Psychic Your weapon absorbs your wrath as you strike, possibly Frightening your target. WIS Save Range: Normal weapon range Spiteful Suffering ( + ) Damage: 6~9 1d4 + 5 ⁠ Necrotic Steep an enemy in the darkness that churns within you. The target takes 1d4 + Charisma Modifier Necrotic damage each turn and Attack Rolls against it have Advantage . Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_Reaper_03 UUID 97c90688-1181-4893-a497-141e816a4c4a Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_Reaper Reaper of Bhaal Ogga is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , found in the Bhaal Temple within the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . “ Lady Orin misjudged the weight of Bhaal's favour. She slipped, and it crushed her. Tread carefully, Chosen. „ — Ogga , to the Dark Urge who embraced Bhaal Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can go to the Bhaal Temple in hopes of saving their party member from Orin . There they encounter Orin, who engages them in combat by transforming into a Slayer . Ogga, along with the rest of the reapers, begins channeling a ritual spell Bloody Favour , granting Orin a Boon of Bhaal at the start of every turn. If the player character is not the Dark Urge , and Orin is killed or disabled, Ogga ends concentration and attacks the party as normal. If the player character is the Dark Urge and defeats Orin, Ogga remains neutral to the party and moves to the foot of one of the stairs leading to the central altar ground. His one-liners depend on whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. DEN_Trader_Food Okta is an elder of the tiefling refugees sheltering in the Emerald Grove in Act One . She is Ikaron's mother. “ Best to fill your belly now - while we still can. „ — Okta offering food to the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Okta is usually preparing stew for the refugees at X: 195 Y: 550 . When a party member speaks with her for the first time, she offers them a bowl of Gruel . Lae'zel, Astarion, Karlach and Shadowheart can chose to say: "A bowl of grey goo. Reminds me of home." When a party member answers Okta's question "You been on hard times too, huh?" with "It's all in the past" , they are given one extra portion. Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to DEN_Trader_Food . The Fancy Trader Table is worth a total of 55.5 + # Camp Supplies on average. Food [ edit section | visual editor ] Rolls two or three times. Worth 14.8 Camp Supplies on average. Item Quantity Chance Supply Pack 1 Always Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Save the Refugees Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Okta occasionally talks to Ikaron : Okta There's barely any rations left. Ikaron We'll make it last. We always do. Okta I can't thin the broth much more than this. Ikaron It'll have to do. Okta If I'd known they were leaving, I would have given them an extra helping. Ikaron They're cowards, mother. You don't owe them anything. Okta But can you really blame them? After Elturel... Ikaron We can't run forever. I'd rather stand and fight. If the Emerald Grove is assaulted, Okta huddles with Bex, Danis, and Ikaron: Okta So you have experience treating the wounded? Bex Well... not exactly. Okta Just good with a needle and thread? Bex Sure. Were you a cook in Elturel? Okta You've had my food, right? Answer's in the gruel. Ikaron Look on the bright side, mother - should be fewer mouths to feed after today. Okta Ikaron, please. Bex Danis can hunt! Sharp as an elf with that bow, aren't you love? Danis Well. In a pinch. Ikaron Then why aren't you on the wall? Danis Rabbits don't shoot back, do they? Danis Would you... like to pray, or something? Ikaron No. Danis Right. Silence it is. If the tieflings prepare to leave for Baldur's Gate, Okta continues talking to Ikaron : Okta Do you need help, Ikaron? Ikaron Nn-! No. I've got it! Okta Don't be breaking your back before we get to Baldur's Gate. Ikaron I won't. I'm not ten anymore. Okta Don't I know it. But there's two more boxes after this one. Ikaron Ugh. Okta What do you think of opening a cart in Baldur's Gate? Ikaron A cart? Like on the street? Okta Exactly. Noble types won't want a tiefling cookin' for them, but common folk... Ikaron A cart sounds fine, but do I have to haul it around? Okta Until we make the coin for a proper ox, maybe. Ikaron *Sigh.* Ikaron Do you think we'll stay in Baldur's Gate long? Okta Of course. It's a big city, lots of opportunity. Ikaron But Elturel... Okta Don't let that place cast a shadow on your head forever. Ikaron I guess things are already better. I've learned a lot. Okta There we go, boy. Now back to packing. Technical UID S_GOB_Checkpoint_Guard_001 UUID 6d69a347-9b3f-4b64-818e-013f849c6ae4 Stats Goblin_Melee_Strong Eqp. EQP_Goblin_Axe_Shield_Absolute Trs. Humanoid_Ranger Sentinel Olak is a goblin stationed at the checkpoint just before the entrance to the Goblin Camp during Act One . Olak and Warrior Puce constantly argue with each other. Despite the title of sentinel, Olak shares the same stats as other goblin warriors, except for a higher AC granted from a Scrapwood Shield . “ We're celebratin' a raid. No better time in camp than this. Get yourself a bit of fun before it dries up. „ — Olak Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Sentinel Olak questions anyone who approaches the checkpoint and attacks those who appear to be trespassing. It is possible to avoid combat by by bringing Sazza , disguising as a drow , using Illithid Persuasion , or passing an Intimidation Check . [TRUE SOUL] [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  Stand aside (DC 5) [FIGHTER] [INTIMIDATION]  To offer my sword to your boss. You can be my first demonstration, if you like. (DC 10  ) [INTIMIDATION]  I'm a hired sword - employer's inside. Stand aside. Now.  (DC 15) [MONK] [INTIMIDATION]  I could best all of your sentinels with my bare hands. Let me pass. (DC 15  ) [RANGER] [DRUID] [NATURE]  Beautiful animal. Does she belong to the Nordiland worgata family? (DC 5) [NATURE]  Glossy coat on that animal. Does she belong to the Nordiland worgata family? (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  Your leader summoned me. (DC 15) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read the goblin's mind. I'm a messenger - here to see Minthara. If the interacting party member attempts to gain entry to the Goblin Camp through a skill check other than Intimidation, or they fail a check, Olak asks them to smear Worg dung on their face to show their "war colours": Grimace and do what you have to do. Smear the dung across your face. It's not your first time. [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  That's nature's bounty. Helps the trees grow. Eat it, or else. (DC 15) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  I said. EAT IT.  (DC 15  ) Follow the rules. Wink, gather the dung, and fling it at all four guards. [ATHLETICS]  Scoop up the warm dung and fling it at Olak's face.  (DC 10) Smearing worg dung on their face grants the War Paint condition to the talking party member. Olak then laughs and lets the party through. Passing the intimidation check grants access without the condition. Lastly, flinging the dung at Olak begins combat, with Olak being Blinded . A party member can opt to play with the nearby war drum, either by slamming the drum head with a flat palm or by passing a Performance check which grants the ⁠ Feel the Beat inspiration to characters with the Entertainer background. In either case, Olak remarks that he enjoys the rhythm but the party just raised the alarm. If the party member uses their flat of their palms to strike the drum head or they fails their Performance check, reinforcements arrive and Olak lets combat begin. If the check is passed, Olak additionally says that he will not let the reinforcements kill the party... this time. He then informs the arriving reinforcements that it was a false alarm and "just a bit of music" . Features Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_TWN_AasimarSurvivor_DeadAasimar UUID f210c0f6-a8ec-44d9-8114-4ecbfd8ac0dc Stats Human_Caster Trs. SCL_AasimarSurvivor_Body Olam [ 2 ] is a dead [ 3 ] aasimar [ 4 ] Harper whose corpse is in the House of Healing Morgue . He attempted to lift the Shadow Curse more than a hundred years before the events of Act Two , until he eventually succumbed to the darkness. “ 'All beings should walk free of fear', I was taught. Oh, if only were I granted such a fine fate. „ — Olam , in his journal. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Siege of Reithwin [ edit section | visual editor ] When Ketheric Thorm amassed an army of Dark Justiciars to plunge the world into shadow at the behest of Shar , Olam was part of the combined forces of Harpers and druids from the Emerald Grove intent on stopping him. Their crusade suffered setbacks and defeats at first, but the combined might of the Harpers and druids, along with the involvement of Yurgir and his merregons , eventually whittled down and destroyed the entire Dark Justiciar army. Ketheric Thorm was then finally killed in battle and sealed in Reithwin's Grand Mausoleum by the Harpers - but not before he uttered his final curse. The Harpers and druids were scattered when Ketheric's final words brought the Shadow Curse upon the surrounding lands, afflicting any survivors from the battle and all the town's remaining inhabitants. Shadow Curse [ edit section | visual editor ] Over the period of a few short days, the now- Shadow-Cursed Lands fell into darkness, causing harm to any who remained or ventured in it, and transforming into undead any who remained too long. Olam survived the first few days, protected by his armour, while his fellow Harpers fell to the curse and rose as Shadows . He hid and set up traps , with the company of his familiar , Corvin. On the fifth day, Olam set out searching for artefacts or scrolls in hopes of finding ways to ward off the Shadow Curse , as well as any other survivors. For the next weeks, his searching lead him to books, scrolls, and artefacts, but none of them useful in protecting against the curse. Olam mentioned hearing sounds from the House of Healing , but did not enter as the source of those were Shadow-Cursed Undead . Instead, he took comfort in his familiar Corvin's presence, and attempted to remove the Shadow Curse through spellcraft . [ 5 ] Though his research was inconclusive - his efforts instead culminated in his turning his gear into living armour. [ 6 ] Eventually, on his third tenday in the Shadow Curse, Olam made his way into the House of Healing Morgue where he continued his research. During his last hours, he summoned his familiar Corvin for comfort and affection, despite the Shadow Curse tormenting the two of them. Olam soon succumbed to the Shadow Curse, leaving behind his journal and Research Notes (House of Healing) and Shadow-Animated armour behind. Technical UID S_LOW_BeachSahuagin_Civilian_Fishmonger UUID ecba853d-f96a-4252-912e-3bf030b10482 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Old Troutman is a shield dwarven trader at the docks east of Philgrave's Mansion in the Lower City . “ Our hero's back! Fancy any celebratory seafood? „ — Old Troutman Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Old Troutman sells fish. If dropping any of the Netherstones anywhere in the Iron Throne and leaving the area without recovering them, and the Sahuagin encounter near Old Troutman has already been resolved, he has the missing Netherstones in his inventory. He is unaware of their true nature, referring to them as "shiny bits" he found while fishing, and sells them to the party for some gold each. The exact value depends on the interacting party member's Charisma and Persuasion modifiers. Shop [ edit section | visual editor ] Gold [ edit section | visual editor ] Old Troutman has a small amount of gold for offer. Item Quantity Chance Gold [ 1 ] 144 - 576 Always Fish [ edit section | visual editor ] Rolls 10-12 times on the Fish Supply Table . The average drop from the Fish Trader Table table is worth 49.0 Camp Supplies . Quantity 10 11 12 Chance 1/3 1/3 1/3 Item Quantity Chance Fish (big) 1 1/13 Fish 1 4/13 Fish 1 4/13 Fish 1 4/13 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Old Troutman Thought I'd be used to the smell of fish by now. Not this smell. Ugh. Hucinda I think I might've had my fill of fish for the next few tendays. Old Troutman Having these things lying around is bad for business... Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Old Troutman has a rare and unusual developer comment in the code that's shared with all nearby characters in the docks/beach area, simply describing him as "POTENTIAL SIMPLE CHARACTER". Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_DoppelgangerGiveQuest UUID 30e834cb-f029-424b-b787-12f10fe474d7 Stats Doppelganger Variant 1 UID LOW_SerialKiller_Doppelganger_GiveQuest UUID c1ace95e-806a-4e83-9cd0-45fffd293ede Stats Human_Commoner Olfaith Olumssdottir is a doppelganger serving the cult of Bhaal . “ Would you like to be more than a common murderer? To become an avatar of slaughter? „ — Olfaith Olumssdottir Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Olfaith approaches the party if they kill a name listed on the Bloodstained Parchment or one of two Flaming Fist officers investigating the murder cases, Valeria and Devella Fountainhead . He encourages them to slay one more target (or two, if a Flaming Fist officer was murdered instead) in order to become an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal, as part of the quest to ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal . If the party kill two murder targets from the list, Olfaith appears again, and tells the party to visit Candulhallow's Tombstones and giving them the password: Sicarius . If the party choose to attack Olfaith, he reverts to his Doppelganger form. In combat, he is a generic Doppelganger. The Tombstone Shop Key for Candulhallow's Tombstones can be found on his corpse, as well as a letter titled An Unexpected Talent which hints that the Murder Tribunal is hidden within the tombstone shop. If Olfaith is killed during his first appearance, he still appears again if the party kill a second target on the list. However, in this appearance he has a different voice actor, implying that this is actually a different Doppelganger who has assumed the same false identity. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Doppelganger ( ) Take the shape of a small or medium creature you've seen. Range: Self Recharge: Per turn Morphic Ambush ( ) Undergo a shocking transformation to startle your foes. Successfully   Ambushed entities are more susceptible to your attacks. Range: Self Recharge: Per combat Multiattack ( ) Damage: 12~32 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning Descend on an   Ambushed creature to eviscerate it with your doppleganger claws. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Per turn Ranged Attack ( )   –   Hand Crossbow Damage: 5~10 1d6 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If Olfaith shows up by murdering up Valeria or Devella Fountainhead instead of a target on the murder list, he does not reappear if two targets from the list have been murdered. Olfaith can show up even if the quest ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal has been completed, including if the party have slain the entire murder tribunal and / or Orin . v t e Lower City v t e Characters Technical UID S_SCL_OliversDiary_OliverShadow UUID 4f6e63a1-b143-46b1-ac0e-834494dfdc6a Stats SCL_Oliver Oliver is in the House in Deep Shadows , within the Shadow-Cursed Lands region in Act Two . “ Someone's coming. Someone new. Maybe they want to play. „ — Oliver , upon hearing the party approaching Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Appearance 2 Involvement 2.1 Act two 2.2 Playing with Oliver 2.2.1 "Round One" 2.2.2 "Round Two" 2.3 Lifting the Shadow Curse 3 Combat 3.1 Allies 3.2 Encounter Details 4 Related Quests 5 Related items 6 Companion approval 7 Bugs 8 Gallery Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Oliver appears to be a small olive-skinned tiefling child with grotesque shadowed gashes infecting his right eye and torso. If the interacting party member passes an Arcana check to sense his true nature, the aesthetics of the Shadow Curse are wiped from his body. Subsequently, he resembles more of a typical tiefling child, with his heterochromia still intact. Certain classes gain bonuses to this check, while Monks can choose an alternative Insight check. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act two [ edit section | visual editor ] Oliver is in the House in Deep Shadows . If a party member approaches, he asks them to 'play with' him. If humored, Oliver says he wants to play hide-and-seek, and turns himself invisible to go "hide." When a party member first enters the ruined house a Perception check is made, failing it lets the conversation start. They can study the boy if they do not already know he is Thaniel: [ARCANA]  Study the boy. Try to understand his true nature.  (DC 14) [DRUID] [WISDOM]  A familiar magic exudes from the boy. Try to commune with it.  (DC 14  ) [MONK] [INSIGHT]  The child's ki feels... uneven. At odds. Why? (DC 14) Oliver insists on playing hide and seek, and if refused, summons Daddy , Mummy , and Doggy , who initiate combat. Playing with Oliver [ edit section | visual editor ] While 'playing' with Oliver, walking up to his invisible model usually causes him to become 'found'. Automatic perception checks may be rolled, but for unknown reasons, these checks (on failure) do not always seem to disqualify the party from "finding" Oliver. "Round One" [ edit section | visual editor ] After 'finding' Oliver for the first time, he immediately starts a conversation with the party member who found him. He is upset but can be invited to play again, which he happily accepts but with additional "rules to the game", while adding "you are better than the others" , presumably referencing the Githyanki corpses littered around the house. "Round Two" [ edit section | visual editor ] Oliver vanishes while starting the "second round" of his game, triggering turn-based mode for all nearby characters, and three hostile shadow-like entities appear; 'Daddy' , 'Mummy' , and 'Doggy' . Among other tactics, it is possible to use a Potion of Invisibility and run to the house. If the party is able to sneak past his 'family' and speak with him again, he gives the Ring of Shadows as a prize, even though he suspects the party cheated. If his 'family' spots party members but they are defeated in combat, Oliver claims he won and awards the party with a 'second prize' – the same ring. If the party manages to pickpocket the Ring of Shadows from Oliver during the second round of hide and seek, a mundane silver band (worth 18 gold) is given instead as a reward. His 'family' then disappears. Playing both games of hide and seek with Oliver grants the following inspirations: ⁠ Child at Heart ( Urchin background) ⁠ Child's Play ( Outlander background) Lifting the Shadow Curse [ edit section | visual editor ] Advancing through the quest ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse with Halsin ultimately requires that the party return to Oliver and convince him to reunite with Thaniel . Regardless of whether Oliver's game was played, the party can confront him with their new information about Thaniel and his identity. Oliver becomes upset, summons a portal, and disappears through it. The party can interact with this portal to travel to his new location, upon which combat begins. Oliver's new location is near the center of Reithwin Town at X: -152 Y: -26 . Once his protective dome is destroyed, Oliver complains about being disturbed and says he does not want to go back to Thaniel, who he perceives as having abandoned him. The party can choose to be kind when convincing Oliver to rejoin Thaniel and be whole again, or be aggressive; they can also let Halsin handle it. Oliver always agrees to rejoin with Thaniel, but being aggressive about it causes Halsin to lose approval, while allowing him to handle it or being kind gives a large boost to his approval. Talking with Thaniel in camp reveals the Shadow Curse may only be lifted after Ketheric Thorm is defeated once and for all. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Daddy Mummy Nightdome Shadow Plush - may be summoned as often as every other round after the first Shadow Friend - 5x (5 additional Shadow Friends are summoned each round by Oliver) Encounter Details [ edit section | visual editor ] After running away Oliver moves to a protective magic bubble called the Nightdome , which reflects double damage back at the attacking party member. During this fight, Oliver does not leave his bubble. However, once per round he uses Friends Until The End . This ability summons five Shadow Friends . After the first round, use of this ability can summon a Shadow Plush into the fight. Failing to kill these shadow entities results in a growing number of them on the battlefield. The Nightdome must be destroyed to resolve this combat encounter. Defeating Oliver's summoned Shadow allies reduces the health of the Nightdome without it retaliating against the party. Defeating Daddy, Mummy, or Shadow Plush deals 60 ⁠ ⁠ Force to the dome, while defeating the Shadow Friends deals 10 ⁠ ⁠ Force . Thus it is not necessary to attack the Nightdome itself as it is destroyed by killing enough of Oliver's shadow summons. Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Oliver's Diary Ring of Shadows Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Confronting Oliver regarding his identity as Thaniel ( I know who you really are, and where you really belong. ):   +1 Agreeing to play with Oliver   +1   -1   +1   +1   +1 After agreeing to play with Oliver, change your mind   +1   -1 Agreeing to play a second round with Oliver   +1   -1   +1   +1   +1 Finding Oliver without alerting the shadows   +1   +1 Finding Oliver after fighting the shadows   -1   -1   +1 Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If Oliver's Nightdome is destroyed directly instead of through his summons, Oliver remains hostile and the subsequent dialogue where he returns to Thaniel does not trigger. This seems to render ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse impossible to complete. A possible fix is using Dominate Person after breaking the Nightdome if Oliver remains hostile and on turn order. If the party members are physically unable to initiate dialogue with Oliver (e.g., from being behind a strategically-placed barricade), Oliver remains hostile until someone leaves the barricade and becomes able to do so. Once dialogue is initiated, the fight does not end until all remaining summons are destroyed. Technical UID S_WYR_GurCamp_Hunter_006 UUID 4c42f14a-c99a-4ba0-891c-136bf7ed38bb Stats WYR_GurHunter_Ranged Eqp. EQP_Longbow_B_StuddedLeather_B Trs. Wyr_GurHunter Oliver Quarlic is one of the Gur , a human nomadic tribe. He is in the Gur Camp in Rivington in Act 3 . “ Ulma insists the tribe is not cursed, but I have my doubts. „ — Oliver Quarlic at the Gur Camp in Rivington Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act Three 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Loot 3 Idle banter 4 Related quests Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Oliver Quarlic is in the Gur Camp attending a funeral for the fallen from a recent offensive on Cazador's palace. Oliver with his fellow Gur, all members of a group of monster hunters lead by Ulma , are looking for their children, who have been kidnapped by Cazador's spawn. The nomads are camped in Rivington, and are trying to mount a rescue or seek revenge. Ulma asks the party to help defeat Cazador and discover the fate of their abducted children. Once Cazador is defeated, Oliver along with Ulma and the other Gur move near the waypoint in Cazador's Dungeon . He attacks the party if the ritual held in the dungeons is completed. If Astarion was turned in to Gandrel in Act One and kidnapped, then in Act Three Oliver and all of his fellow Gur (except Gandrel) are dead. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Ensnaring Strike ( + + ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Piercing Your attack summons thorny vines that possibly Ensnare your target. Ensnared creatures cannot move and take 1d6 ⁠ Piercing damage at the start of each turn. An ally can use their Help action to try and tear away the vines. Who will stand between them and the innocent? Cassivora Dophir If we do nothing, the innocent will suffer just the same. We have no good choices. Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_BasiliskGate_FF_001 UUID 0f84f1c1-2321-47f9-be8b-46df8f5f1dec Stats FlamingFist_Human_Ranger Fist Olloa is a human ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . “ If all these folks can just keep their shit together, maybe nobody else will get hurt. Maybe. „ — Olloa Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Olloa is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Gummidge , Fist Nateen and a Steel Watcher . They can be found near the Baldur's Mouth building at X: 113 Y: -47 , guarding the unconscious Gulster Boyes , prostrated on the ground after being knocked out by the automaton. Several citizens - Baz Hopbank , Scribe Goosequill and Eefa Barlow are vouching for their associate, but to no luck. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Olloa ruefully concludes that the Fist now have to use the old-fashioned ways to keep the order in the city. PLA_Cave_Zhent_Survivor Olly is a human Zhentarim agent accompanying Rugan during Act One . “ Good to see you. Killed any more beasts out there? „ — Olly , encountering the party again in the hideout Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Olly and Rugan are sheltering in a cave near The Risen Road while under attack from Flind's pack of gnolls. As the leader, Rugan orders Olly to leave the heroics to others, and neither of them engage the party until all the gnolls are defeated. After the battle, Rugan thanks the party for their assistance and reveals that their cargo caravan was ambushed en route to Baldur's Gate . During this interaction, the party can recognise Rugan and Olly as part of the Zhentarim merchant network. Regardless, Rugan offers the password to enter the Zhentarim Hideout at Waukeen's Rest . It is possible to persuade or intimidate Rugan into relinquishing the chest. If the party obtain the chest through either of these means, Olly is later killed for failing to deliver the cargo. If a party member kills Olly, they do not need to disguise themselves to speak to his corpse. Who are you? Olly ... Olly... Zhentarim agent... What happened to you? Olly ... ambush... gnolls... Olly ... you... YOU happened...  (If killed by the party) Where were you heading? Olly ... hideout... beneath... Waukeen's Rest... What were you transporting? Olly ... chest... locked... dangerous... EQP_Shortbow_Dagger_Leather Olodan is a halfling druid in the Emerald Grove during Act One . “ No one joins the Shadow Druids. Oh, no - their presence is requested. „ — Olodan Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Olodan is a prominent member of the Shadow Druids and is conspiring with Kagha to overtake the Emerald Grove in the name of their violent order. As a cold-hearted fanatic to the ideals of the Shadow Druids, Olodan views others as 'untouchables'. She does not share the same ideals on harmony as the druids of Silvanus' Grove , and has no qualms in using underhanded methods to achieve her goals. In pursuing the Shadow Druids goal of taking control of the Grove, she beguiles Kagha into adopting violent views on protecting nature and convinces her to unleash the Rite of Thorns to seal off the Grove. Cruel as she is, she shows compassion towards Kagha if their plot is exposed and is open about their intentions. However, even if the party allows the shadow druids to overtake the Grove, she does not spare them for exposing her plot. If Kagha turns against her, Olodan displays bitterness at the acting Archdruid's last moment reversal. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Olodan is in the Inner Sanctum with her fellow Shadow Druids Pinta and Wren , all of whom are Wild Shaped as rats. If the party interacts with them using Speak with Animals , they remain silent and non-threatening. When enough evidence of Kagha's schemes are revealed, Olodan and her druids reveal themselves and admit to their plans. She orders Kagha to join them in killing the party and taking over the druid circle. Unless Kagha is persuaded otherwise, she joins Marcoryl and Loic against the party. The badger has a starting health of 13 hit points that increases every two druid levels. While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. You take on the attributes of your beast form - excluding your Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma scores. When your beast form drops to 0 hit points , you revert to your normal form. ## Oloric Witmirth

Oloric Witmirth In-game Portrait Voice / Actor Ben Crowe Role Playwright Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_Oloric UUID 8083ab20-4877-4e16-adca-7f4f400ed87b Stats Human_Commoner Oloric Witmirth is a human playwright who can be found suffering from writer's block at the Elfsong Tavern . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Oloric appears in a list of characters provided as Elfsong Tavern regulars in the tabletop adventure Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus , where he is described as "an impoverished playwright who scribbles his private thoughts and observations in a small book". In Baldur's Gate 3 , his fortunes appear unchanged. He can be found sitting at a table with a pamphlet of the House of Grief , Surrender your Burdens , and he doesn't seem sure whether or not he actually knows the player character. The Client List confirms he was determined by the Mapping of the Heart to have a " melancholy heart " and had his memories removed. The events of Descent into Avernus were probably too traumatic. v t e Lower City v t e Characters in the Lower City Anti-Hag Support Group Adrielle Hydrangea Wubb Jatlo Kled Mayrina Baldur's Mouth HAV_Survivor Harper Olys is an Asmodeus tiefling ranger and Harper . If one of the original Harper allies is dead, he can take their place and help the party during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers and be a potential ally during ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain . “ Wish I'd used the latrine. Always need to, before a battle. „ — Olys Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn , and if the Nightsong is freed from her cage to wage war against Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers , Olys takes the place of one of the original Harper allies (either Antony , Essius , Lymn , or Naysa ) as a failsafe if one of them has been killed before the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers . Speaking with with Olys results in him nervously revealing that he wished he had used the latrine before going to battle. If he survives the main battle, Olys guards the first floor of Moonrise Towers with the remaining Harpers. Talking with him again reveals his signs of nausea from seeing a tadpole crawl out of a corpse, [ 1 ] and he pleads with the party to finish the fight. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Provided Olys survives Moonrise Towers, he can be summoned as an ally through the Gather Your Allies variant Silver Harp Squadron , if ⁠ The High Harper is completed with Minsc alive, and either Antony, Naysa, or Lymn is dead. Technical UID S_GLO_SocietyOfBrilliance_MindFlayer UUID 1f9937ef-9207-4db6-a833-e4083d571f53 Stats UND_SOB_Mindflayer Eqp. EQP_Robe Trs. UND_SocietyOfBrilliance_Mindflayer Variant 1 UID S_IRN_Omeluum UUID df88c3a5-9ee1-4a23-a7b6-34c07cef8a33 Stats MindFlayer Omeluum [ 1 ] is a friendly Mind Flayer and trader in Baldur's Gate 3 who comes to the Ebonlake Grotto in the Underdark after being contacted by Blurg . It is a member of the Society of Brilliance and can be asked to help ⁠ remove their tadpole . “ But not to worry. Should you transform, I will happily perform a new examination. „ — Omeluum , making a somewhat less than helpful offer Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.1.1 Meeting Omeluum 2.1.2 Helping Omeluum investigate the parasite 2.2 Act Three 2.2.1 Omeluum has vanished 2.2.2 Rescuing Omeluum 3 Shop 3.1 Notable items sold 4 Combat 4.1 Attacks and actions 5 Idle banter 6 Related quests 7 Related literature 8 Gallery 9 Notes and References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Omeluum [ 2 ] was born with a propensity for arcane magic, [ 3 ] giving it the strength to resist the elder brain and defect. Following its ambitions to better the world, Omeluum joined the Society of Brilliance, and now conducts research with its friend and fellow member, Blurg. [ 4 ] Currently, they are working to improve living conditions in the Underdark, as well as researching a means to subdue mind flayer 'appetites' in hopes of reducing its need to consume brains from one per month to perhaps one per year. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Meeting Omeluum [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can first meet Omeluum after talking to the Hobgoblin trader Blurg at the Myconid Colony at X: 111 Y: -89 . Blurg is a fellow scholar of the Society of Brilliance , who calls for Omeluum to help the party. Omeluum wonders what is so important that he be pulled away from tending to his Zurkhwood samples. Blurg then explains that the party are infected with tadpoles but have not yet begun to show any symptoms of ceremorphosis . There are several opportunities to attack Omeluum during dialogue, and some Companions might actually suggest it. Still, if the interacting party member listens to Omeluum, it reveals it is a rogue Mind Flayer, and was born with an affinity for magic which allowed it to resist the control of the Elder Brain of its colony. Omeluum feeds on the brains of creatures of the Underdark "who oppose the Society's goals", and wishes to help others of his kind by discovering a brain-free diet. Helping Omeluum investigate the parasite [ edit section | visual editor ] Omeluum suggests investigating the player character's tadpole. Agreeing to this starts ⁠ Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite . The mind flayer then asks the party to find some rare mushrooms to prepare its special decoction. The recipe includes Tongue of Madness and Timmask Spores , both of which can ostensibly be found in the Underdark. However, Blurg interjects and suggests the party might obtain them in the Arcane Tower of a local cleric, Lenore De Hurst . Upon bringing Omeluum the required ingredients, it attempts to remove the tadpole. However, Omeluum not only fails, but also makes the tadpole more powerful (granting Survival Instinct to whomever drinks the potion). The Mind Flayer is surprised and worried about the power of the tadpole, and apologizes for not being of service. Unable to bring the tadpole issue to a close, Omeluum then offers the party the Ring of Mind-Shielding , which can limit the powers of the tadpole. It is then possible to make an offer for the ring. Obtaining the ring by any means completes the quest ⁠ Help Omeluum investigate the parasite , and Omeluum can then be traded with. [ 5 ] Purchasing the book On Illithids, Volume XXVI from Omeluum and reading it earns the Inspirational Event The Forbidden Arcane ( Sage background). Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three differences Balanced Explorer Tactician Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 8 HP 71 AC 15 Initiative +1 Proficiency +3 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 11 (0) 12 (+1) 12 (+1) 19 (+4) 17 (+3) 17 (+3) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 +1 +1 +4 +3 +3 Explorer Difficulty Stats Level 8 HP 49 AC 15 Initiative +1 Proficiency +5 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 11 (0) 12 (+1) 12 (+1) 19 (+4) 17 (+3) 17 (+3) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 +1 +1 +4 +3 +3 Tactician Difficulty Stats Level 8 HP 92 AC 15 Initiative +1 Proficiency +3 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 11 (0) 12 (+1) 12 (+1) 19 (+4) 17 (+3) 17 (+3) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 0 +1 +1 +4 +3 +3 Omeluum has vanished [ edit section | visual editor ] If ⁠ Steal a Githyanki Egg was resolved without Lady Esther receiving the Githyanki Egg , the party can meet Omeluum's companion Blurg at the Society of Brilliance Lodge . Blurg informs the party that they both returned to Baldur's Gate to report to the Society of Brilliance their findings about the party's condition. However, shortly afterwards Omeluum decided to investigate the situation on its own and disappeared. Blurg explains that his friend believed the problem to be connected to the Cult of the Absolute . While not appearing overly concerned with Omeluum's whereabouts, Blurg agrees if the party propose to track the illithid down. This starts the quest ⁠ Retrieve Omeluum . Rescuing Omeluum [ edit section | visual editor ] There are no clear hints as to where to start searching, apart from Blurg's vague assumptions. However, if the party help Zanner Toobin or the servants of Umberlee (quests ⁠ Save the Gondians and ⁠ Avenge the Drowned respectively), Omeluum connects to the party telepathically when they dock at the Iron Throne . It altruistically prompts the party to save Duke Ravengard , who is also held in the underwater prison, and bides the party not to be concerned with its own fate. Nonetheless, it is possible to save Omeluum along with Ravengard and some (or even all) Gondian captives. Omeluum is held in a separate cell in the south-west corner of the Iron Throne, behind a locked door ( DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check ) and restrained to a surgical bed. If helped, it becomes an Attached Follower with the ability to Teleport to Submersible . Once rescued, Omeluum teleports to the Lodge. Unlike Blurg, it can no longer be traded with, although it can be pickpocketed. To finish the quest ⁠ Retrieve Omeluum , the party must speak with the illithid once more. Omeluum explains that the Society of Brilliance will not actively help the party in its further battles. But, in gratitude for being saved, it provides the party with a Pouch called Omeluum's Boon which contains several items selected from the Society' vaults: Fungal Bamboozler Potion of Supreme Healing Scroll of Dimension Door Scroll of Sunbeam Wizardsbane Oil Shop [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to UND_SocietyOfBrilliance_Mindflayer . Notable items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] As a trader, Omeluum sells the following items: Boots of Stormy Clamour Creation's Echo On Illithids, Volume XXVI Pearl of Power Amulet Ring of Salving The Shadespell Circlet Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] In the Underdark , Omeluum does not fight back and, along with Blurg , teleports away on its turn if attacked or if it catches a party member stealing from it. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Blur ( + ) Attackers have Disadvantage on Attack rolls against you. Doesn't affect creatures that don't rely on sight or that can see through illusions. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Hold Person ( + ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't Move , Act , or React . Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Levitate ( ) Float effortlessly to a destination. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) (Only while in the Iron Throne) Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Blurg and Omeluum occasionally chat while at Ebonlake Grotto in Act One . Blurg How is your more... personal research progressing? Omeluum Not well. The nutrition my species receives from other minds is difficult to emulate. Blurg Worry not, friend. You'll find the key soon enough. Blurg Have you spoken with Skriss lately? Omeluum Yes. She is cataloguing kuo-toan fertility rituals. Blurg Oh? Perhaps after I finish my research here, I'll join her... Omeluum Are you sure it was an illithid larva, Blurg? Blurg I'm not sure what reason there would be to lie. Omeluum True. If only I could see into their mind... Omeluum I have never seen anything like it, Blurg. Is my species evolving? Blurg Perhaps. But at such an accelerated rate? Omeluum Hm. It simply shouldn't be possible. Blurg and Omeluum catch up with each other at the Lodge in Act Three in case Omeluum is saved. Blurg So your escape from the Iron Throne was a narrow one? Omeluum Indeed! I find I now have an irrational fear of deep water. Blurg How do you pass through the city streets without exciting opprobrium? Omeluum I adopt the illusory appearance of someone else. You, for example. Technical UID S_LOW_Traders_JewelVendor UUID d68c344d-e491-4ca6-b88e-959e68445bb8 Stats Human_Commoner Omotola is a human trader who manages The Glitter Gala in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ My darling, you need my gems. They'll brighten even a ghoul like yourself! „ — Omotola , greeting the customer Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Omotola trades gems and jewelry in her store. Despite Omotola's words about selling some enchanted items, all her stock is non-magical. Omotola's Attitude towards the party often changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses quest. As evidenced by a Detailed Ledger , a portion of Omotola's business revenue is sourced by Lord Enver Gortash . Items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] Assorted precious gems, common rings and necklaces. Technical UID S_GOB_WolfPens_Kid_001 UUID dff4432a-85b4-4d5c-95b5-6d1179dbabf4 Stats Goblin_Kid Trs. GOB_Goblin_Kid One is a goblin child in the Goblin Camp in Act One . “ Again! Again! Make it squeal again! „ — One Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] One is in the Worg Pens of the Shattered Sanctum , eagerly pelting at a Cave Bear with rocks, together with Three . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Nimble Escape ( ) Retreat safely: moving won't provoke Opportunity Attacks . Throw ( ) Damage Normal weapon damage Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. Your Strength affects how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Range: 3-18 m (10-60 ft) Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] One alongside Three can be actively fought and killed by the party in plain sight. This is a rare exception to the game's standard treatment of minor NPCs; human and tiefling children can only be Knocked Out , and any narrative deaths they suffer (such as during the Raid on the Emerald Grove ) occur strictly off-screen. In combat, if One or Three are able to flee through the Worg Pen's exit, reinforcements enter the area. However, this does not cause the entire Goblin Camp to become hostile. If the party has an animal with them such as a Ranger's Companion , One and Three chuck rocks at it. This can be facilitated by luring them away from the cave bear's cage with Perform or a similar action. Each rock deals 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning . As a Small Humanoid of 10 kg, Eight's corpse is one of the lightest that can be used for both Fungal Infestation and Animate Dead . v t e Goblin Camp Characters Bugbears Bao'ek'nuk Stimk Teghun Camp Followers Owlbear Cub Volo Companions Halsin Minthara Goblins Aggy Azak Bal Bez Birka Bolt Brakkal Breg Clack Crub Crusher Cry Culk Druk Dullwill Eef Fezk Glomp Gnat Greez Gribbo Grikka Grush Gruz Gurd Gurk Huk Kirz Klagga Krolla Mirg Mrak Muzul Nass Neem Nik-Nuk Nozk Nrog Olak Piddle Plagg Plig Puce Puli Raagg Rancer Rindle Roo Rot Rozzak Sazza Shekt Sluck Snurd Spike Skrut Sul Tak Tiny Tizg Tozad Trinzas Tud Vrak Wasp Zami Zurga Zurk Children Eight Five Four One Three Goblin Leaders Dror Ragzlin Gut Minthara Ogres Gurgon Polma Traders Grat Roah Moonglow Other Abdirak Andrick Brynna Dishevelled Chicken Erna Ferr Larger Giant Spider Kagran Klaw Liam Narvass Smaller Giant Spider Small Klaw Smythin Taeglyn Tale Yerle Locations Bloodied Shrine Defiled Temple Goblin Camp Shattered Sanctum Worg Pens Quests Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Defeat the Goblins Find a Cure Find the Nightsong Raid the Emerald Grove Rescue the Druid Halsin Rescue Volo Save the First Druid Save the Goblin Sazza Save the Refugees Travel to Moonrise Towers

LOW_CountingHouse_BhaalCultist Reaper of Bhaal Onilla is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , in the High Security Vaults in the Counting House in the Lower City . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the ⁠ The High Harper quest, the party can go to the Counting House in hopes of catching up to Minsc. Inside the vaults, the party witnesses Minsc emerge from a Mimic and defeat it. 'Jaheira' then appears with a handful of Bhaalists including Deera, and teleports away with Minsc, leaving the cultists to attack the party and the staff. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_Ontur UUID 381a8770-5f64-454b-aa6f-ef8c57341c57 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Ontur is a dwarven wine merchant who can be found at the Wine Festival at Highberry's Home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ Glorious summer day, is it not? Perfect, in my opinion, for a light, refreshing tipple! „ — Ontur Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Ontur appears at his stall at the wine festival if the party began ⁠ Investigate the Murders and the wine festival takes place. After Dolor reveals himself and attempts to kill Cora Highberry , Ontur runs off and is not seen again. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Wine x12 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Ontur occasionally argues with Flaerith , with Porter Oveer eagerly anticipating the fight: Flaerith You know, I really do think red is the best wine. Ontur What, on a hot summer's day? Madness. Flaerith ...Excuse me, how dare you?! Porter Oveer Oooh, I bet this'll be fun. Ontur Now, Flaerith - I'm just saying white wine is better. Flaerith Maybe for plebs. Porter Oveer Best not tell them I prefer a pink. Ontur At least white wine doesn't stain tongues and teeth. Flaerith No, they stain their drinker's reputation instead. Flaerith This red is the best wine in the entire Sword Coast. Ontur In the Sword Coast? In your dreams, more like! Flaerith Swallow a cork and die. Porter Oveer Fight, fight, FIGHT! Flaerith I think... I think I was too harsh, Ontur. My apologies. Ontur The only thing that's too harsh are these tannins. Flaerith You wound me, Ontur. Truly. Ontur I only jest, Flaerith! Porter Oveer Boring! ## Orin

Overview Combat Orin Deathbringer of Bhaal In-game Render Full Name Orin the Red Identity Female Voice / Actor Maggie Robertson Main Writer Adrienne Law Faction Cult of Bhaal Family Bhaal (great-grandfather and grandfather) Sarevok Anchev (grandfather and father) Helena Anchev (mother and sister) The Dark Urge (great-uncle/aunt and uncle/aunt) Hometown Temple of Bhaal Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Human / Changeling Class Rogue Subclass Thief Deity Bhaal Technical UID S_GLO_Orin UUID bf24e0ec-a3a6-4905-bd2d-45dc8edf8101 Stats GLO_Orin Eqp. GLO_Orin Variant 1 UID LOW_Slayer_Orin UUID ced6bfeb-8f6f-47d0-943f-77833f643318 Stats GLO_Orin_Slayer Orin the Red is the Chosen of Bhaal and one of the leaders of the enigmatic Cult of the Absolute and serves as one of the main antagonists in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Come to me, Father. Set my flesh to your unholy purpose. „ — Orin the Red, about Bhaal Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Gameplay 1.3 Appearance 1.4 Personality 2 History 2.1 Bhaalist upbringing 2.2 Orin's betrayal 3 Involvement 3.1 Act One 3.2 Act Two 3.3 Act Three 4 Orin's shapeshifting 4.1 Disguises 5 Combat 5.1 Loot 6 Related Quests 7 Related literature 8 Achievements 9 Gallery 10 Notes 11 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] A daughter of Bhaalspawns and a devout practitioner in the arts of murder and pain, Orin has painted the streets red in her father's name for many years. Yet to be caught thanks to her shapeshifting abilities, she now prepares to make out of Baldur's Gate the biggest bloody offering to her father yet. Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Hinted at first through notes, Orin is properly introduced at the end of Act Two as one of the three conspirators of the cult, along with Ketheric Thorm and Enver Gortash . Through cunning and murderous devotion, she and her allies have established a solid Bhaalist foothold in the city of Baldur's Gate . Now, empowered by a Netherstone and with the cult's plans in motion, she intends to paint the city crimson with blood in a mighty offering to Bhaal. Gameplay [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin is a level 12 Changeling boss and one of the main antagonists in the game. First mentioned in Act One , she is introduced in Act Two , and properly encountered and fought in Act Three . Fighting her is required in order to obtain her Netherstone and proceed with the story. In combat, she uses her deadly powers given by Bhaal himself to deal large amounts of damage quickly while being supported by her cultists. Her encounter can go differently depending on the choices made by the party and whether or not the player character is the Dark Urge . A truce with her and her Bhaalists can be brokered if the party agrees to slay Gortash first. She can trick the party with her disguises and will kidnap someone important to the player character. Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin has pale blue-grey skin with swirling, smoke-like plumes of red undulating across it. The iris and pupils of her eyes are a soft milky white, almost melding with the sclera, contoured by dark eyeliner, giving her an intimidating look. Her straw-colored, braided hair falls to the backs of her knees in a fastening reminiscent of a flail. Her form-fitting armour is bright blood-red, rigid, and rough like chitin. She adorns her head with an ornate silver tiara with a centrepiece in the form of a person supplicant, a single crimson gem adding some colour. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin is cruel and sadistic, but artistic and creative in her own twisted way. [ 1 ] Her demeanour is immature and almost childish; Orin easily loses her composure when things do not go her way, enacts small rebellions against the authority figures in her life, and enjoys toying with her victims. [ 2 ] She derives sadistic pleasure from taunting her victims with the gory details of her deeds. When she impersonates another character with her shapeshifting abilities, she is initially able to convincingly mimic their personality. Her true nature tends to break through the mimicry, however, as she is often unable to contain her bloodlust, resulting in her becoming more openly violent and sadistic, invoking threats and fantasies of extreme violence and grotesque brutality before shifting back into her base appearance. Her deranged devotion to Bhaal hides her true desire for acceptance and belonging as she constantly seeks validation and approval from him. Though uncommon, she extends admiration to those she respects, such as her grandfather Sarevok. Her confident and vicious demeanour shatters, however, when confronted with the truth of her origins, and she displays genuine fear when forced by Bhaal to become his tool instead of doing so willingly. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Bhaalist upbringing [ edit section | visual editor ] Raised believing that Sarevok was merely her doting grandfather, Orin was, in truth, born of an incestuous relationship between Sarevok Anchev and his daughter Helena Anchev , intended to be the perfect offering to the Dread Lord. [ 3 ] Though he routinely mistreated and abused them, both Helena and Orin worshipped and loved Sarevok, enduring the hardships of growing up as Bhaalists. Orin received the bloody teachings of Bhaal, in time becoming the youngest Unholy Assassin to follow the steps of the God of Murder. Such were her gifts in killing that she was anointed Bhaal's Chosen. When Orin was still a child, Sarevok, knowing Helena desired to be Bhaal's Chosen, ordered his daughter to kill Orin as an offering to Bhaal. [ 4 ] Helena attacked Orin, but she was overcome by her daughter, who ultimately cut her down. Bhaal deemed the young changeling exceptional and ordered Sarevok to look after her henceforth. [ 5 ] [ 1 ] Orin served Bhaal directly under the Dark Urge as their second in command, though the two were often at odds about the correct way of making offerings to Bhaal. Orin believed that the Dark Urge butchered their victims without consideration, and what their father truly wanted was beauty and thoughtfulness in a kill. [ 6 ] The Dark Urge, on the other hand, understood that Bhaal cared only for the quantity of murder performed, nothing more. [ 1 ] Yearning for respect and status, but dismissed and looked down upon by Bhaal and Sarevok alike, Orin brooded as she waited for an opportunity to become her father's favourite. [ 7 ] Orin's betrayal [ edit section | visual editor ] The Urge joined forces with Bane's Chosen Enver Gortash , and together, they formulated a plan to steal the Crown of Karsus , an ancient, arcane object of immense power, and subjugate an Elder Brain with it in order to create a soulless army to destroy the world with. [ 8 ] After recruiting Ketheric Thorm , Myrkul's Chosen, Orin joined the three in the raid to plant the Crown on the brain beneath Moonrise Towers . It was during this time that Orin saw her opportunity and struck, driving a dagger through the Urge's skull and planting an Illithid tadpole in them. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] With her former rival left to die with a tadpole devouring their brain, Orin took the Dark Urge's place as Bhaal's Chosen and the third member of the conspirators. [ 11 ] Orin would prove undisciplined in her role, however, as her bloodlust could not be contained, and she rapidly grew to be disliked by the other two, who saw her as little more than a necessary nuisance for their plan. [ 12 ] At some point between the betrayal and the events of the game, Ketheric and Orin tricked Minthara into a trap where Orin murdered her allies and captured her. She then used a tadpole to convert Minthara into a True Soul . The dying Dark Urge was found by Kressa Bonedaughter , saved from death, and held captive in the Mind Flayer Colony for some time as she experimented on them, [ 13 ] until they were shipped away onto a Nautiloid . [ 14 ] If the Dark Urge is chosen as Origin , they later awaken during the Prologue . If the Dark Urge is not chosen as Origin, their corpse will be found in Orin's chamber during Act Three, tortured to death by their sister. [ 15 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Though Orin is not present in the first act of the game, her involvement in the plot is alluded to when the Absolute attempts to take over the party's minds, and they see a vision of the Chosen shortly before being saved by the Mysterious Artefact . The player character can also see a vision of Orin manipulating an enthralled Minthara upon first meeting the drow in the Shattered Sanctum . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin first appears alongside Ketheric Thorm and Enver Gortash in the Mind Flayer Colony beneath Moonrise Towers. [ 16 ] An argument breaks out between Gortash and Ketheric, and is stopped from becoming a fight due to her intervention. Having successfully kidnapped Ulder Ravengard , she also plants a tadpole in the duke's eye as part of their plan to take over the city. She then joins the other Chosen and uses her Netherstone , the Lash of Bhaal , with them to order the Netherbrain to march the Absolute's armies on Baldur's Gate . She and Gortash leave for the city, while Ketheric stays behind to deal with the party. “ I will find her, I will murder her. And I will smile. „ — Minthara , swearing to take revenge on Orin for her treachery Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin, standing over a captive Lae'zel. With Ketheric slain by the party and the Netherstones separated, Orin and Gortash's partnership falls apart along with their control of the Elder Brain. While Gortash is having his picture painted by a servant, a shapeshifted Orin comes to Gortash's quarters and repeatedly threatens him. Though Gortash urges Orin to control herself and focus on reuniting the Netherstones, Orin no longer has interest in cooperating. If the Dark Urge is in the party, she also tells Gortash of her intention to kill them. After reaching Rivington , the party can encounter Orin in person for the first time. She reveals that she is aware of their objective to confront her and Gortash and gather the Netherstones, and threatens to follow the party from now on, watching their every step before disappearing once more. If engaged by The Dark Urge, she reveals their relationship as siblings mockingly and taunts them (granting the inspiration ⁠ Personal Relations in the process). From then on, she begins harassing the party, using her changeling abilities to shapeshift into different characters. When speaking with these seemingly innocuous characters, the conversation slowly turns more violent until Orin drops the disguise to goad the party to violence and, ultimately, a bloody encounter with her. Gortash may offer an alliance with the party if spoken to before confronting Orin. Tired of her theatrics and unreliability, Gortash offers to join forces to subdue the Netherbrain for good and rule the Sword Coast together if the party slays Orin and ⁠ brings him her Netherstone . To convince the party, he also reveals their camp has been compromised by Orin, who is masquerading as a party member. [ 17 ] If bargained with, Gortash proves true to his word if his conditions are fulfilled. Upon entering the Lower City , Orin kidnaps a member of the party unbeknownst to the rest of the group. Who she kidnaps, when, and how it is revealed depends largely on the player character's relationships with their companions. Orin then confronts the party and announces that she has a hostage, demanding they deal with Gortash first and face her in combat, where the winner takes all. This encounter initiates the quest ⁠ Rescue Orin's Victim . To get Orin's Netherstone, the party must visit the Murder Tribunal in the Undercity Ruins , as the Temple of Bhaal is open only to those deemed worthy by Bhaal. At the tribunal, the party is welcomed by Sarevok Anchev . He reveals how the Bhaalists survived the events of years prior, as well as his connection to Orin as her grandfather. If confronted by The Dark Urge, he further elaborates on Orin's involvement in their fall from Bhaal's grace, excited at the prospect of a Bhaalspawn duel in the ranks of the cult. He offers passage to the Temple of Bhaal if the player character proves themselves worthy by becoming an Unholy Assassin , which requires impressing the tribunal with a killing, and then sacrificing a celestial being (though the Dark Urge is allowed to skip straight to the sacrifice). Alternatively, the party can simply decide to fight Sarevok, a prospect he welcomes eagerly. Whether granted to a worthy Bhaalist or looted from Sarevok's corpse, with the Amulet of Bhaal in hand, the party can finally confront Orin. Orin can be found within the Temple of Bhaal, at the altar. There, she is toying with her kidnapped victim, surrounded by Bhaal cultists. When approached, Orin threatens to kill her hostage, though she can be convinced otherwise through dialogue. If the The Dark Urge is chosen as origin , they must challenge her to one-on-one duel with neither of their comrades interfering per the Bhaalist tradition. If the Dark Urge refuses to duel Orin, she immediately executes the hostage. The party must then fight the standard version of the boss encounter; following the battle, the story proceeds as if the Dark Urge had lost the duel. Alternatively, if the party use Speak with Dead on Helena Anchev's corpse, they can discover that Sarevok ordered her to sacrifice Orin. Revealing this to Orin causes her to completely lose focus on killing her victim. The same can be achieved by exposing Sarevok as her father by reading A page from Sarevok's book . If the party then choose dialogue options without ability checks, Orin becomes enraged and calls on Bhaal's power to transform into the Slayer . However, the party can also choose to taunt her further by succeeding a DC 25 Deception , Persuasion , or Religion Check , which causes Orin to completely break down since she is unable to cope with the truth. Bhaal then speaks to her through the giant skull effigy carved into the temple wall, commanding her to fight and unnaturally forcing her body into the Slayer form. Regardless of the outcome of the conversation, Orin attacks when it concludes. Once defeated, the party can loot her corpse and obtain her Netherstone . The Dark Urge gains the ⁠ Securing Your Line inspiration if present. Orin's shapeshifting [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin uses her shapeshifting abilities to harass the party twice, using one of the disguises listed below. Following the second transformation, all further interactions with the characters below are genuine. Meeting one of Orin's impersonations for the first time as the Dark Urge grants the ⁠ Personal Relations inspiration. Orin can only be in one place at a time: if a disguised Orin stays in the visual range of a party member, she cannot take the appearance of other characters elsewhere and thus is effectively pinned in place. This way, it is possible to talk to the other genuine characters without triggering Orin's apparitions. These characters, with the exception of the dying Stone Lord thug, can also be 'saved' by not speaking to them until reaching Gortash at Wyrm's Rock . Once Gortash informs the party that Orin has compromised their camp by shapeshifting into one of their companions, she only impersonates the dying Stone Lord thug. Lastly, it is possible to identify when a character is actually Orin as they are then level 12, though without the large amount of hit points that would be expected from that level. When examined, these characters can be observed to have Orin's passives (e.g. Immutable Form ), giving away their true identity. If attacked straight away, Orin transforms and disappears without her usual threats, but still taunts the party. Her defeat is required before facing the final threat of the game: The Netherbrain . Technical UID S_LOW_VoloFate_Thug_Melee_01 UUID 9f9763b8-6294-4301-ae1c-eb532945c43b Stats LOW_VolosFate_Thugs_Melee_01 Ruffian Ormo is a human character in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . He can be found near the Grey Harbour Docks , as part of Churg Elvek's mob, ready to bring Volo to "justice". Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] When approaching the Steel Watch Foundry , the party can come across Churg Elvek and his mob, as well as Volo who is tied up to some Smokepowder Barrels . Upon approaching, a cutscene plays out where Churg accusses Volo of harmful lies, conspiracies and fear mongering. The party can opt to intervene or simply draw their weapons after which Churg and his mob attack.
