Technical UID S_LOW_SteepsHarborhandCrew_Civilian1 UUID cc0b24db-6621-426d-baea-f10248bf28a3 Stats Human_Commoner Ormont is intent on forming an employee strike in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ They grind you down to a nub in these parts. Work you into an early grave, then don't even send flowers to your widow. „ — Ormont Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Ormont and Tugelnhorn are members of the Harborhand crew. While Ormont is intent on striking, Tugelnhorn is wary that their living conditions will worsen. The pair are in the Lower City , north of Old Garlow's Place . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Tugelnhorn It ain's so bad - could be a damn sight worse. You've got a job and a place to rest your head - Ormont - When they bloody let me rest my head. Tugelnhorn Well plenty don't even have that, have they? What about all those refugees? They've got nothing. Ormont What about them? You want them flooding in here, driving down our wages even more? Tugelnhorn Well... no. Wouldn't want that. Ormont It ain't right - they're pushing folk too far. Tugelnhorn I know, but moaning isn't helping anyone, is it? Ormont Helps me - good to get it off your chest. Anyway, we just going to let what's-his-name and his toy soldiers take over the whole city? Tugelnhorn He's not gone that far. Not even close. And if you keep talking the way you're talking, the Fists will start breaking heads. Ormont Good - I might get some sleep if I took a crack on the noggin. Ormont There ain't no one coming to help us - we ought to be helping ourselves. Tools down, banners up! Tugelnhorn And what if it doesn't work? Ormont We keep going until it does work. They'll give in soon enough, once their coffers run empty. Tugelnhorn I'm more worried about what happens when my belly runs empty. Tugelnhorn Find yourself a stage, why don't you? Always bloody drama with you. Ormont Drama? This is sense. Half the crew are dead on their feet, while the others are ready to drop everything and leave. We need to stand up. The longer they treat us like this, the harder it'll be to force some change. Tugelnhorn There's a right time for a strike - but it ain't now. Not when the whole city's in danger. Ormont Bah - there'll always be an excuse. Anything to keep us in our place.
## Orpheus
- **来源**: [Orpheus](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Orpheus)
- **分类**: Characters

Overview Combat Orpheus The Prince of the Comet Identity Male Voice / Actor Tommy Sim'aan Role Attached Follower Family Gith (mother) Hometown Astral Plane Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Githyanki Class Monk Subclass Way of the Four Elements Technical UID S_GLO_Orpheus UUID 47c90728-af68-4cbc-baaa-6497eebd8d7e Stats INT_Orpheus Orpheus is a Githyanki who appears in Baldur's Gate 3 , playing a central role in Act Three and Lae'zel's personal quest, ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior . As the son of Gith herself, he acts as the supposed true ruler of the Gith Empire. However, he has been captured and imprisoned in the Astral Plane by Vlaakith . Being a githyanki, he seeks to destroy the mind flayers , and as the githyanki prince, he strives to remove Vlaakith from power. “ Quickly now - even here, we do not have infinite time. „ — Orpheus , after being freed from his prison. Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One & Act Two 2.2 Act Three 2.2.1 Battle in the Astral Prism 2.2.2 Acquiring the Orphic Hammer 2.2.3 Deciding the Prince's Fate 2.2.3.1 The Prince Assimilated 2.2.3.2 The Prince Freed 2.3 Endings 2.4 Epilogue 3 Combat 3.1 Loot 4 Related quests 5 Related literature 6 Gallery 7 Notes 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] According to the inscribed discs, banned and deemed heretical by followers of Vlaakith, Orpheus is the first and only son of Mother Gith, the leader of the rebellion that freed the races which would bear her name from the Illithid Empire. Gith's impressive psionic power allowed her to disrupt elder brain control, a power that her son inherited. At some point during the rebellion, Gith's advisor, Vlaakith, made a deal with the dragon goddess Tiamat , in which the gith and red dragons became eternal allies, and a small contingent of red dragons would serve the gith as steeds. It was only after the split between the githyanki and githzerai that the true cost of Vlaakith's deal was revealed, as Gith was summoned to the Nine Hells and never returned. Tiamat's red dragon consort, Ephelomon , came to the githyanki and decreed that Vlaakith was to be their new ruler. Outraged at this turn of events, Orpheus led a rebellion against Vlaakith I's rule, assembling an honour guard and declaring himself the rightful ruler of the githyanki. This "War of the Comet" was said to have ended with Orpheus' death at the hands of Kith'rak Voss , with Ephelomon devouring his corpse. [ 1 ] In truth, Orpheus and his honour guard were imprisoned in a corner of the Astral Plane accessed using the Astral Prism . Orpheus himself was restrained by infernal chains, so that Vlaakith could exploit his elder brain disruption powers. The fact that Orpheus still lives was known only to Voss, the current and past Vlaakiths, and a few secret devotees of the Prince of the Comet throughout githyanki society. The artefact containing Orpheus soon came to the attention of The Netherbrain , who wanted to use it to overthrow the Chosen of the Dead Three in control of it. It sent a team of illithids to find and take the artefact from the githyanki. However, the leader of the group (a mind flayer known as The Emperor ) seized the opportunity and went rogue, taking the artefact and hoping to use it to overthrow the elder brain. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One & Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Orpheus – and his role in the greater story of Baldur's Gate 3 – is hinted at throughout the game, but not truly revealed until the beginning of Act Three . Notably, he is referenced in the "Orpheus, Prince of the Comet" series of discs, which recount his attempted rebellion against the first Vlaakith and form the backbone of the quest ⁠ Discover the History of Prince Orpheus . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Battle in the Astral Prism [ edit section | visual editor ] While resting at Wyrm's Lookout , the active party members are ambushed by githyanki warriors. The Dream Guardian opens a portal into the Astral Prism for them to enter, lest they fall under the Absolute 's influence. There, the Dream Guardian reveals their true form as a mind flayer free from hivemind control, and asks the party for their aid against the githyanki, which starts ⁠ Help Your Protector . Though there is an option to attack the mind flayer, doing so leads to a Game Over , as the player character and all party members fall under the control of the Absolute or are killed by the githyanki. After the battle, the Dream Guardian reveals that the source of the party's protection is the imprisoned Orpheus, and the githyanki who attacked are his honour guard, imprisoned alongside him by the first Vlaakith. Completing this encounter completes both ⁠ Discover the History of Prince Orpheus and ⁠ Discover the Artefact's Secrets ; it also starts ⁠ Free Orpheus . Acquiring the Orphic Hammer [ edit section | visual editor ] While visiting the party's camp in Act Two , Kith'rak Voss directs the party to meet him at Sharess' Caress in Wyrm's Crossing . Upstairs, in the Devil's Den , he is attempting to make a deal with the devil Raphael , who eventually dismisses him. Talking to the devil reveals he has the Orphic Hammer , a magical hammer with the ability to free Orpheus from his infernal chains. This starts ⁠ Deal with the Devil . He promises to give the artefact to the party in exchange for the Crown of Karsus , signing a Soul-Sworn Contract with the player character if they accept. There are four main paths here: The player character refuses the deal but chooses to acquire the Orphic Hammer anyway. The party must then infiltrate the House of Hope to steal the Orphic Hammer, which leads to a fight against Raphael. The player character accepts the deal, starting both ⁠Escape the Deal and ⁠ Fulfill the Deal , and does not betray Raphael. Before the final battle, when trying to free Orpheus, Raphael appears and hands over the Orphic Hammer. As his deal involves the party giving up the Crown of Karsus, this prevents Gale from either giving the crown to Mystra or using it to become a god. Afterwards, Raphael appears at the celebration in the Epilogue . The player character accepts the deal, but ultimately decides to break it. The party must then infiltrate the House of Hope and steal the contract; the Orphic Hammer can also be stolen here. This also leads to a fight against Raphael. The player character refuses the deal and does not steal the Orphic Hammer. Without the Orphic Hammer, it is impossible to free Orpheus, though Raphael's offer remains open as long as he is still alive; he even appears in the Astral Prism near the end of the game to offer his terms one last time. Showing the Orphic Hammer to Voss completes ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss and he rewards the Silver Sword of the Astral Plane . Deciding the Prince's Fate [ edit section | visual editor ] At the Morphic Pool , the player character attempts to wield the Netherstones and control the Netherbrain, but is overwhelmed. The Emperor brings the party into the Astral Prism and tells them that only an illithid can successfully wield the Netherstones. Here, Orpheus' fate must be decided, with most decisions depending on whether or not the party acquired the Orphic Hammer. The Prince Assimilated [ edit section | visual editor ] Orpheus can be "assimilated" by either the Emperor, a mind flayer player character, or a mind flayer Karlach . Assimilating Orpheus results in several high DC skill checks being presented; failing to pass any of them results in combat and has a significant impact on the final outcomes of the game: If Orpheus is assimilated and Lae'zel has rejected Vlaakith and embraced Orpheus, the player character must pass a DC 30 Persuasion Check , or she turns hostile. Speaking with her again before entering the High Hall gains her scorn, and a DC 30 Persuasion or Intimidation Check must then be succeeded for her not to change her mind and attack the party. Upon leaving the Astral Prism and reaching the High Hall, an enraged Voss turns hostile unless convinced not to, which requires a DC 30 Persuasion or Deception Check , with an additional prerequisite DC 25 Persuasion or Intimidation Check if the player character was the one to assimilate Orpheus. If Voss turns hostile, he can no longer be recruited as part of ⁠ Gather Your Allies . The Prince Freed [ edit section | visual editor ] The party can refuse to allow the Emperor to assimilate Orpheus. Additionally, a mind flayer player character can refuse to assimilate Orpheus, though a check is required to prevent their hunger from getting the better of them. Either choice causes the Emperor to defect to the Netherbrain, and the party can then free Orpheus. If the player character made the deal with Raphael and did not betray him, then he shows up and gives the Orphic Hammer to the party. If the party has not obtained the Orphic Hammer by this point, then Raphael appears and makes his offer again. Refusing the offer causes a Game Over; survival then requires the party to ⁠ Fulfill the Deal . Regardless, Orpheus is freed and offers an alliance to the party, though he scolds them for not freeing him sooner. He may also scold them for stealing the Githyanki Egg , causing Crèche Y'llek's destruction, or fornicating with The Emperor. Like the Emperor, he tells the party that the only way to wield the Netherstones is to become an illithid. There are several options at this point: The player character or Karlach agree to become a mind flayer. Orpheus lowers his psionic defences to allow the order for their transformation to proceed. Alternatively, if the party obtained the Supreme Tadpole from the Emperor , then he does not lower the defenses but instead declares that they would consume this Tadpole when the moment comes. [ 2 ] If the player character and Karlach refuse to become mind flayers, Orpheus offers to make the sacrifice instead. Lae'zel is dismayed but does not turn hostile. The player character and the party decide to fight Orpheus. Winning or losing this battle immediately results in a Game Over, as the party either dies or loses Orpheus' protection and becomes dominated by the Absolute. Regardless of who transforms, Orpheus joins the party as an Attached Follower for the final battle. Depending on who is transformed, Voss expresses either confusion or dismay, but also does not turn hostile. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] This section contains sensitive content , including brief descriptions of self-harm and suicide. Orpheus' role in the ending depends on whether or not he transforms into a mind flayer. If Orpheus turns into a mind flayer, he appears on the docks and asks Lae'zel to lead the githyanki fight for freedom without him, as he is now an abomination and seeks death. Orpheus asks either the player character or Lae'zel to kill him. If his request is not fulfilled, he kills himself unless the player character convinces him to refrain with a DC 20 Persuasion Check . If they pass the check, Orpheus leaves the docks for places unknown. If the player character or another party member turned into a mind flayer, he appears on the docks and thanks the party's illithid for their sacrifice. Now ready to begin a new rebellion against Vlaakith's tyranny, he calls two red dragons and invites Lae'zel to join him in his new war against the Lich Queen. Lae'zel can either join Orpheus, be convinced to stay in Faerûn if the player character is not a mind flayer, which requires a DC 30 Persuasion Check , or – if the player character is romancing Lae'zel – take the player character along with her. Regardless of what choice Lae'zel makes, Orpheus flies atop his red dragon into the sky and away from Baldur's Gate. Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] This section contains sensitive content , including mentions of or allusions to self-harm and suicide. If Orpheus does not transform into a mind flayer, the player character finds a letter from him in the Chest of Grateful Words , titled The First Protocol . In it, he praises the player character as Mla'ghir ( Gith for "liberator"), and tells them of the success of his ongoing rebellion against Vlaakith. If Orpheus transforms into a mind flayer but is convinced not to kill himself, then a unique dialogue option asking about him is present when talking to Lae'zel. Her response indicates that Orpheus has disappeared and gone into hiding, but she holds out hope that he might re-emerge one day. It is also worth noting that his tattoos are read counterclockwise, as Githzerai tir'su is, despite his parentage (though given his age, it is possible that such differences did not exist in his youth). It is not known whether these tattoos were intended as acts of spite towards Vlaakith by Orpheus or were an oversight in development. ↑ Datamined by Chubblot ↑ Orpheus is also the name of ⁠ a demigod in Greek mythology who traveled with Jason and the Argonauts in pursuit of the Golden Fleece, but is primarily famous for his journey to the Underworld to save his love Eurydice. Features Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Fist Orvil is a deceased human member of the Flaming Fist . His body can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ ...each one of your scales is a gem, your eyes shine brighter than your throat-fire „ — Orvil , expressing his feelings to Quil Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Orvil's headless body can be found in the Bhaalist Crypt underneath the Candulhallow's Tombstones in Baldur's Gate . It is lying in one of the cells behind Sarevok Anchev's private chamber , at X: -1244 Y: 548 . Orvil cannot be spoken to via Speak with Dead . An unfinished letter addressed to Quil Grootslang can be found on Orvil's body. In it, the Fist confesses his deepest affections for the Dragonborn bard and asks Quil to meet him outside the Blushing Mermaid . He also writes that he pre-ordered a copy of Quil's love-chants songbook, which was due to be released in current year. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Dear Quil Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] It is unclear whether Orvil had been abducted by the Bhaalists or came to a sticky end after Humanoid_Melee Oskar Fevras is a human and well known painter in the city of Baldur's Gate , who is being trafficked by the Zhentarim . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] The Zhentarim Hideout [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Free the Artist Oskar is first located in the Zhentarim Basement , where he is being held captive for ransom or sale by Brem due to his skill and renown as a painter. The party can attempt to purchase him as a slave, persuade Brem to release him, or kill all the Zhentarim in order to free him. This starts the quest Free the Artist . If the interacting party member purchases Oskar and speaks with him as if he was bought to be a slave, he runs away. If they purchase Oskar and then free him, he asks for money to use along his way home. It is not necessary to pay the additional 200 gold "for the road" when freeing Oskar for him to show up in Act Three and continue the questline. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] A bug can occur when the quest is ended, saying "We left Oskar with the Zhentarim" , when entering the Shadowfell . [ verify ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Lady Jannath's Estate [ edit section | visual editor ] If Oskar is freed by the party in Act One , he returns home to Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City, Baldur's Gate. Upon entering Lady Jannath's Estate, the party can discover that Oskar is possessed by a ghost and the whole estate is haunted. After a brief fight with some Poltergeists , Oskar falls unconscious and Lady Jannath explains that he became possessed after their recent marriage. She then directs them upstairs to Oskar's atelier, where he had spent most of his time before the possession. In the atelier, the party can discover a possessed painting and the Letter to Oskar Fevras which directs them to Mystic Carrion at Philgrave's Mansion . Once they acquire the Torch of Revocation from him, they can return to burn the possessed painting and release the Echo of a Lost Love imprisoned within. The ghost rushes downstairs, knocking Lady Jannath unconscious and threatening to drag Oskar back to the afterlife with her. She reveals her name is Kerri Evenfield, a former girlfriend of Oskar's, and that he made a deal with Mystic Carrion to bring her back from the afterlife to figure out if it was his fault she committed suicide. The interacting party member can choose to either allow Kerri to drag Oskar into the afterlife, pass a DC 15 Persuasion Check or DC 15 Intimidation Check to get her to stand down, or defeat her in combat. If one of the dialogue checks is successful, they can either choose to let her return to the afterlife without answering Oskar's question or pass a DC 15 Persuasion Check , Intimidation, or Deception check to reveal the truth: she was only a fling and nothing more. If the party save Oskar's life and Lady Jannath does not break up with him as a result, he offers to paint a Personal Portrait of a party member in his atelier. The subject of the painting is determined by the party member starting the conversation. It is possible to obtain multiple paintings by talking to Oskar with different party members. The Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] If he is not freed in Act One, Oscar moves to the Guildhall after persuading the Zhentarim that he is more valuable when not kept in captivity and now makes a living making forgeries of paintings. He seems to have accepted his new life but is still quite unhappy about the party abandoning him in Act One. The party can buy an expensive, forged painting from Oskar, albeit at a high price due to a significant attitude penalty. It deals 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage, or 2d8 ⁠ Acid , ⁠ Cold , ⁠ Fire , ⁠ Lightning or ⁠ Poison damage and creates a surface . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Hold Person ( + ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't Move , Act , or React . Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Oskar has Speak with Dead dialogue if he is killed inside the Zhentarim Hideout: Who are you? Oskar Fevras Oskar Fevras... greatest artist... alive... You do know you're not alive anymore, right? Oskar Fevras ... peculiar... sense of humour... Where did you keep your valuables? EQP_Spear_Chainmail_Shield_HelmetMetal_Fist Trs. BG_Guard Fist Osmund is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is in Rivington in Act Three . “ There's no reason for me stick my neck out against armies of cultists when we can send mountains of steel instead. „ — Osmund Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Osmund is stationed together with Fist Lionel at the northern gate of Rivington. Both Fists are under orders to prevent anyone from walking past the barred gate – behind it the gruesome results of a recent battle between the Flaming Fist and Absolutists can be seen. Unlike Lionel, Fist Osmund is rather eager to chat with the party. If a party member speaks with her, Osmund freely reveals details about the attack: prior to the party's arrival in Rivington, a band of cultists nearly destroyed the gate into Rivington, which was narrowly prevented by the Steel Watch . Osmund talks with pride about the automatons, which were victorious in the battle, and attributes the city's safety to Enver Gortash . Although Cleric characters can attempt to reason with her using class-based options, she remains fixed in her views on the issue. Technical UID S_WYR_WyrmRockPrison_Prisoner UUID 55f621e8-c702-45d8-89a7-d38d1a4ebb1d Stats Human_Commoner Otto Ott is a human found inside a cell in Wyrm's Rock Prison during Act Three . “ I don't need to escape. I've got food, water, privacy. And I mean to keep it that way. „ — Otto Ott , adamant on staying put Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Otto Ott can be spoken with in his cell. The party can threaten or offer to help him escape, but Otto rebukes that in prison he has food, water and privacy and does not want to leave. Breva Brightmoon , the sleeping guard at the main door of the prison, can be heard talking about "Old Man Otto" by passing a Perception check. She mutters that he is "back here again" . If the party pass this skill check they can say that Otto is their father to gain access to the prison. A guard on break in the adjacent room can be overheard saying that Otto has been talking in his sleep about a dragon sleeping beneath Wyrm's Rock. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_WineFestivalWorker01 UUID 07663ad2-237c-4d11-9b55-fac1ac8e90ee Stats Dwarf_Commoner Porter Oveer is a dwarven worker. She is at the Wine Festival at Highberry's Home in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ You see, the key is to have enough drink to be cheery, but not so much you fall over. „ — Oveer Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Oveer mingles among the patrons of the wine festival. If the party arrives before beginning the quest ⁠ Investigate the Murders , Oveer is setting up tents and talking to Muttonchops Oreelly . She tries to keep Oreelly focused on the work, but he seems focused on simply enjoying life. After Dolor reveals himself and attempts to kill Cora Highberry , Oreelly runs off and is not seen again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party encounters them before beginning the quest, Oveer occasionally speaks with Muttonchops Oreelly. Porter Oveer Will you please keep your eyes on what you're doing? Muttonchops Oreelly Eh? I'm trying to enjoy the festival. Stop bothering me. Porter Oveer We're not supposed to be enjoying the festival - we're working! Porter Oveer Are you drunk? Muttonchops Oreelly Not drunk enough to listen to your prattle. Muttonchops Oreelly I wonder if we'll get free wine again this year. Porter Oveer That wine wasn't supposed to be free. You stole it. Muttonchops Oreelly Stealing is the best way to get things for free. Muttonchops Oreelly How many barrels of wine will we need? Porter Oveer Enough to make the guests forget how dangerous Baldur's Gate is. So... lots. Porter Oveer Hurry it up! We need these stalls ready sharpish. Muttonchops Oreelly You need to slow down and learn to enjoy life. After the wine festival begins, Oveer will overheer Flaerith and Ontur argue over whether red wine or white wine is better and becomes excited at the prospect of a fight: Flaerith You know, I really do think red is the best wine. Ontur What, on a hot summer's day? Madness. Flaerith ...Excuse me, how dare you?! Porter Oveer Oooh, I bet this'll be fun. Ontur Now, Flaerith - I'm just saying white wine is better. Flaerith Maybe for plebs. Porter Oveer Best not tell them I prefer a pink. Ontur At least white wine doesn't stain tongues and teeth. Flaerith No, they stain their drinker's reputation instead. Flaerith This red is the best wine in the entire Sword Coast. Ontur In the Sword Coast? In your dreams, more like! Flaerith Swallow a cork and die. Porter Oveer Fight, fight, FIGHT! Flaerith I think... I think I was too harsh, Ontur. My apologies. Ontur The only thing that's too harsh are these tannins. Flaerith You wound me, Ontur. Truly. Ontur I only jest, Flaerith! Porter Oveer Boring! Technical UID S_FOR_OwlBear_Cub_001 UUID c66b2865-6613-4372-b97a-e330c1d75d09 Stats Owlbear_Cub Variant 1 UID Owlbear_Cub UUID ffb05cca-cf38-4586-981f-7dca89092ff5 Stats Owlbear_Cub Owlbear Cub is a Beast [ 1 ] and a potential Camp Follower in the Owlbear Nest with his mother in Act One . “ Like it here. Warm fire. Scratch reminds me of big brother. „ — Owlbear Cub chatting in camp Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Owlbear Cave 1.2 Goblin Camp 1.2.1 Chicken Chase 1.2.1.1 Without Speak with Animals 1.2.1.2 With Speak with Animals 1.2.2 Saving the Owlbear Cub 1.3 Owlbear Cub is Hungry 1.3.1 Without Speak with Animals 1.3.2 With Speak with Animals 1.4 Owlbear Cub is Injured 1.4.1 Without Speak with Animals 1.4.2 With Speak with Animals 1.5 Act Three 1.6 Epilogue 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 3 Companion approval 4 Inspiration 5 Achievements 6 Gallery 7 Notes 8 External Links Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Owlbear Cub can be recruited as a pet Camp Follower and remains in the Campsite afterwards. Owlbear Cave [ edit section | visual editor ] To recruit the Owlbear Cub, the Owlbear Mother must be encountered in the Owlbear Nest in the Forest , near the Blighted Village . It does not matter whether the Owlbear Mother survives the encounter, but the cub must be spared to be available as a camp follower later. The principal scenarios to recruit the Owlbear Cub include: Meeting the Owlbear Mother in a cutscene, then retreating without combat. After long resting, the party can return to the cave and find the Owlbear Mother killed by a goblin hunting party. The cub survives and reappears in the Goblin Camp after the next long rest. Meeting the Owlbear Mother in a cutscene, then fighting and killing her. A second cutscene in which the cub begins eating its mother gives the party an opportunity to spare the cub. The cub survives and reappears in the Goblin Camp after the next long rest. [ 2 ] Attacking the Owlbear Mother from stealth, skipping the initial conversation cutscene with her. In this case, the second cutscene with the cub eating his mother after she is killed is not triggered, and the cub remains hostile. To save the cub in this scenario, it is necessary to flee from combat while the cub is still alive. After a long rest, if he survived, he reappears in the Goblin Camp. Downing the cub with non-lethal combat does NOT spare him for this purpose. If not in turn-based mode, a party member can launch a ranged attack, then be seen by the Owlbear Mother and trigger her cutscene before the ranged attack lands. In this case, the first cutscene ends when the ranged attack hits or misses, and combat begins. When it ends, the second cutscene with the cub eating his mother is still triggered, and the party can spare him. In Honour mode , the Owlbear Mother summons her Owlbear Mate if not immediately defeated or Silenced . During scenarios 2 and 4 described above, if the Owlbear Mother is killed before her Owlbear Mate, there is no second cutscene, and the party must flee, as in scenario 3, to save the cub. If the Owlbear Mother is killed after her Owlbear Mate, the second cutscene plays normally. Goblin Camp [ edit section | visual editor ] If he is successfully spared in one of the above scenarios, then after long resting, the Owlbear Cub moves to the Goblin Camp , where Krolla invites the party to play the Chicken Chase game to earn a bit of money. Playing Chicken Chase is not required to recruit the Owlbear Cub. Chicken Chase [ edit section | visual editor ] During the chicken chase game, a party member can talk with the Owlbear Cub in an attempt to influence the game towards victory: Without Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 3 ] [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Coax the cub toward the goalposts.  (DC 15) [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Guide his gaze to the goblins - they deserve to die.  (DC 15) [ 4 ] [RANGER] [DRUID] [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Nod to the goalposts - he'll be safe there.  (DC 10) With Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 3 ] [PERSUASION]  See those posts? Run toward them. (DC 15)  (if not a Druid or Ranger) [RANGER] [DRUID] [PERSUASION]  They won't hurt you if you run to those posts. (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  The goblins are responsible for your pain. Kill them. (DC 15)  (non-Barbarian only) [BERSERKER] [PERSUASION]  The goblins hurt you - CRUSH THEM.  (DC 10) [ 4 ] [BARBARIAN] [PERSUASION]  The goblins tried to hurt you. Show them what hurt really means. (DC 10) [ 4 ] Saving the Owlbear Cub [ edit section | visual editor ] Whether participating in Chicken Chasing or not, the party can talk to the Owlbear Cub to invite him to their camp. [ 3 ] Beckon him closer. [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Kneel down - you won't hurt him.  (DC 10) Offer him your hand. He can follow your scent to your camp in the wilderness.   +1   +1   +1 I have a camp. You're welcome there.   +1   +1   +1 However, before the Owlbear Cub can be freed, the goblins must be dealt with. They can either be killed or Krolla can be convinced to let the party leave with the Owlbear Cub. [ 5 ] [INTIMIDATION]  You love this game enough to die over it? (DC 10)  (non-Barbarian only) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Feel differently? How about you feel dead?  (DC 10  ) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  ROAR.  (DC 10  ) [PERSUASION]  I'd be doing you a favour. Keeping such a large beast fed isn't easy. (DC 10) [DRUID] [RANGER] [PERSUASION]  I'd be doing you a favour. The beast will only get bigger - and tougher . (DC 5  ) [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  I don't care what you think. I'm not asking. (DC 5) I'm saying I want to buy it. (500 gold) If a party member plays and wins the Chicken Chase and intimidates or convinces Krolla into giving them their winnings, she does not have to be intimidated again to let the party leave with the Owlbear Cub. The cub does not seem to appear in the Goblin Camp if Devout Mezzka is killed before a long rest or if the Goblin Camp is poisoned through the Booze Tub . [ verify ] Should the party kill the entire Goblin Camp before encountering the owlbears, then the mother is killed by a goblin hunting party, and the cub shows up at the campsite after a couple of long rests. If the party calls Lump the Enlightened to participate in combat with the Goblin Camp exterior when the cub is present, then the Owlbear Cub becomes hostile to the three Ogres and, by extension, the party. If this happens, recruiting the cub is likely not possible anymore, as it is difficult to prevent the Ogres from eventually killing him. Even if the cub is knocked out using non-lethal attacks, he still disappears after a long rest. The final cut-off point for recruiting the Owlbear Cub is entering the Mindflayer Colony at the end of Act Two . Owlbear Cub is Hungry [ edit section | visual editor ] As long as the cub is spared and not stuck in the Goblin Camp (i.e., the party freeing him or clearing the camp before he is captured), the cub appears at the campsite one evening. Feeding him and keeping distance encourages him to be a friend, while taunting him or approaching him causes him to attack. If he appears to be ready to charge, the party can attempt to "hoot softly" as a last-ditch effort to calm him down. [ 6 ] [DEXTERITY]  Move out of the way.  (DC 10) [PERFORMANCE]  Hoot softly to calm him down.  (DC 10) (he becomes a friend) Brace yourself to meet his charge. (begins combat) Without Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 6 ] Fetch a piece of food from your bag.   (if the party have food) [ 7 ]   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Toss the food to the owlbear. Keep the food held out in front of you. Eat the food. [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Wait for him to approach you.  (DC 10) [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Beckon him closer.  (DC 10) Keep your distance. (becomes friend) Move closer. With Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 6 ] I have food. Would you like it?  (if the party have food) [ 8 ]   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Go ahead. Eat. Come on, then. Take it. On second thought, I'll have it myself. Are you injured? You are strong. (becomes friend) You don't look very strong to me. [ACROBATICS]  Step away from the beast.  (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  No, you will not bite. (DC 10) Then prove it - defend yourself. (begins combat) Owlbear Cub is Injured [ edit section | visual editor ] He reappears after another long rest, but is injured. A party member can attempt to heal the injury: Without Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 9 ] Owlbear Cub *Hoo. Squawk!* Wave your arms to scare the cub away. (begins combat) [ 9 ] [NATURE]  Inspect his wound.  (DC 10)   +1   +1   +1   +1 [MEDICINE]  Attempt to heal the injury.  (DC 10)   +1   +1   +1   +1 [SURVIVAL]  Try cleaning the wound.  (DC 10)   +1   +1   +1   +1 With Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 9 ] [PERSUASION]  You're hurt. Let me see. (DC 5)  (If he is not a friend) [PERSUASION]  I can help you. Just stay calm. (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  Let me see, or the leg will fall off and I'll eat it for dinner. (DC 5) [INTIMIDATION]  Behave, or you'll end up like mother. (DC 15)  (non-Barbarian only) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  SHOW ME.  (DC 15  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Show. Me. Now. (DC 15  ) If he is already a friend: [ 9 ] [MEDICINE]  Hold still. I'll make it better. (DC 5) [PERSUASION]  It's barely a scratch. You'll be fine. (DC 5) [SURVIVAL]  Come here. I'll clean it for you. (DC 5) Successfully passing a check recruits him for good. The cub quickly acclimates to camp life. At some point after recruitment, a long rest is interrupted by a noise. If Speak with Animals is active, it is revealed that the cub had a nightmare, and Scratch is trying to calm him down. The cub also remarks that Scratch reminds him of his older brother. If asked about that, the cub says that he used to have an older brother, but his mother ate him. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If the cub is a camp follower and Dammon survives until the game's finale, then Dammon transforms the cub into a battle-ready beast before the group arrives in the Upper City . Dammon feeds the cub potions to accelerate his growth and outfits him with steel armour, granting him the Dammon's Special Brew condition and transforming him into an Armoured Owlbear . The party can summon the owlbear to assist in the final battle using Gather Your Allies , though he is one of two major characters who can permanently die in this fight and be removed from the Epilogue , the other being Zevlor . Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] If the cub survives the final battle, he appears at Withers' reunion celebration still armoured. The player character can pet him, tell him that it is good to see him, to which he becomes flustered, and ask what he is up to, though his answer is mistaken for dancing. If the player character uses Speak with Animals , the cub reveals that he was never invited but instead followed the player character's pleasant smell to join the gathering. Speak with Animals casters can also comment on the cub being so much larger than his "big brother" Scratch and ask again what he has been up to, to which he shares that he made new cat, turtle, and kraken friends but killed the kraken after it ate the cat. If the cub survived but was not upgraded by Dammon, due to not completing ⁠ The Hellion's Heart or because Dammon is killed at any point, he still appears as a juvenile owlbear and shares the same story of what he has been up to. However, he lacks the enhanced strength or armour, so he instead says that he had to run away when the kraken ate his cat friend. Either way, the player character then has the opportunity to let a former party member adopt the cub: either Halsin , Shadowheart (if she turned away from Shar ), or the player character themselves if they romanced Selûnite Shadowheart or Halsin [ 10 ] in Act Three and went home with one of them. Regardless of who adopts him, the cub says that he likes the player character's choice and will go to them after the party. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] After killing the owlbear in the Owlbear Nest : Let the creature live.   +1   +1   +1   +1 Attack.   -1   -1   +1   -1 The first time the cub comes to camp: Feed the cub something from your pack   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Tell the cub to go away, or attack him (with Speak with Animals)   -1   -1 Attack (without Speak with Animals )   -1   -1   -1 The second time the cub comes to camp: Nature , Medicine , or Survival check to heal him   +1   +1   +1   +1 Scare him away (without Speak with Animals)   -1   -1 Attack   -1   -1 Inspiration [ edit section | visual editor ] Interacting with the Owlbear Cub grants the following inspirations: ⁠ Born Innocent ( Urchin background) – for saving the Owlbear Cub in the Goblin Camp ⁠ Chicken Chase Extraordinaire ( Entertainer background) – for playing the Chicken Chase game in the Goblin Camp ⁠ Cub Tamer ( Outlander background) – for healing and recruiting the Owlbear Cub at the campsite Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] You Have Two Hands for a Reason Pet Scratch and the owlbear cub at the same time - the greatest joy an adventurer could ask for. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Owltalon is a Justiciar Crusader for Shar and, as such, possesses fearsome combat prowess. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Owltalon will use Subsume Shadow to enter her Umbral Form , empowering her attacks with an extra 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic and making her immune to non-magical damage. This lasts until death. Note that while the Umbral Form passive grants an extra attack, this does not stack with Owltalon's existing Extra Attack . Technical UID S_LOW_DiminishingWorkforce_HumanWorker UUID 29fc6976-5fea-4fa0-a1b4-ab4c0409b6f3 Stats Human_Commoner Paddo Garrard is a human stone mason. He is near the Lower City Central Wall in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ You aren't a stone mason by any chance? No, I suppose not. „ — Paddo Garrard Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Paddo and his fellow stone mason Buntter are chatting, wondering where the third stone mason Tamrin could be as he did not show up for work. The pair remark that it is unusual as his tools are here, but then again he is not the first worker to have skipped out on the job. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Buntter Where in the hells has Tamrin got to? Paddo Garrard Wish I bloody knew. This job's a six-hander - we can't do it without him. Buntter Another one who can't take a bit of hard work. Paddo Garrard First one to give up before he got paid though. Paddo Garrard Come to think of it, Tamrin really didn't seem the type to just bugger off... Buntter Neither did Berrk. Or Perral. Didn't stop them running. Paddo Garrard Tarrin worked harder than they did. He was still chipping away when I left last night. Buntter Never saw when he left though, did we? He could be propping the bar in the Elfsong for all we know. Buntter That's funny... Tamrin's tools are still here. Paddo Garrard Maybe he is coming back then. He'd never leave them behind. Buntter Chisel, hammer, trowel... Nothing missing at all. Paddo Garrard If he doesn't come back, I'm having his chisel. Mine's bloody useless. Paddo Garrard Think we can get the wall built, just the two of us? Buntter I doubt it. But we'll try. Paddo Garrard I really thought Tamrin would stick it out. He was a good mason. Buntter A good mason turns up for work. She can be found in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Pagnola patrols the streets of Lower City with Fist Norys , Fist Togarr and a Steel Watcher . Their route runs back and forth from the Singing Lute to the Beehive General Goods (approximately from X: -124 Y: -117 to X: -75 Y: -105 ). Pagnola and her mates do not respond to any attempts to speak with them, regardless of whether the Steel Watch Foundry is intact or destroyed. Technical UID S_LOW_RefugeeHostel_Worker UUID 325b4356-4de4-4f6a-8f3b-9ed2b55e214a Stats Halfling_Commoner Pammella Nortale is a halfling in Baldur's Gate . “ Welcome. If you've need of a bunk or a bath, you'll find them upstairs. „ — Pammella Nortale Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Pammella owns and manages Nortale's Hostel in the Lower City . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pammella Nortale will occasionally chat with Dholber Greene : Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale Rules are the same for everyone: clothes go in the fire, comb goes through the hair. We'll have no lice in here. Dholber Greene Burn my son's clothes? But I've nothing else for him to wear. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale We've plenty of donations. I'm sure you'll find something that fits. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale No need to look so glum. You'll be clean and comfortable in no time. Dholber Greene I'm so embarrassed. I - I'm sorry. We must have caught them riding on the ox cart. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale No sense apologising for what can't be helped. You made it here safely - that's what matters. Dwindling Dad - my head's itchy. Hostel Mother Pammella Nortale Hot soapy water and a fine-tooth comb - that's all you need. Those lice will be gone in no time. Dholber Greene His mother was better with this kind of thing... I'll do my best. Technical UID S_DEN_Tiefling_005 UUID e5319db6-ea86-43cc-9fd0-5ec1e0eab492 Stats DEN_Refugees_Tiefling_Melee Eqp. EQP_Shortsword_Leather Trs. DEN_Refugee Pandirna is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . With her legs paralysed from a dodgy brew, she is given the duty of guarding the refugees' storage hut. “ Never buying a potion off that old bat again. „ — Pandirna , on her recent shopping experience Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Pandirna was married to Almara, who passed away prior to Act One. In letters to her late wife, Pandirna expresses regret in not being able to prevent Almara's death. She now feels obligated to protect those around her. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Pandirna guards the storage hut in the Emerald Grove. She drank a potion from Auntie Ethel , who claimed she would become "as strong as a bugbear ". Although the potion worked it also caused Paralysis in Pandirna's legs, relegating her to guard duty. Pandirna can be reached by lockpicking the front door or entering through the rear roof. Behind Sazza's cage, a path leads around the cavern toward the rear of the storage hut. If the party attacks Pandirna, pickpockets her, or loots the nearby crates, she becomes hostile and calls for the guards. To receive the dialogue option to offer Pandirna a cure, the party member who interacts with her must be a bard , cleric , druid , or paladin . The paralysis can be cured with Lesser Restoration or the Amulet of Silvanus . After being cured, Pandirna allows the party to wander the room, but not to touch anything. The Dark Urge has the unique option of breaking Pandirna's legs, which kills her without alerting the guards. This is an oathbreaking action for all Paladins . If the party cause hostilities in the area, Pandirna is Knocked Out and Paralysed , and they cannot interact with her. This can be done after promising to cure her, getting approvals, then telling her to wait. [ verify ] If Minthara and her raiding party are primed to assault the Emerald Grove, Pandirna will be fit once more and be atop the grove's ramparts alongside Guex , busy filling up empty barrels with oil . If the raid is beaten back or the goblins ' leaders are dead, Pandirna moves with the other tieflings near the entrance of the Grove, and makes preparations for the road ahead. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] [THE DARK URGE]  Break her legs and kill her.   +1 [NON-BARBARIAN]  Tell her you'll snap her neck if she keeps talking.   +1   -1   -1   +1   -1 [BARD] [CLERIC] [DRUID] [PALADIN]  Offer to heal her paralysis.   +1   +1   +1 [BARD] [CLERIC] [DRUID] [PALADIN]  Offer to heal her paralysis, but only if she pays you.   +1 ...and then pocket the money and leave.   +1   -1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Shortsword Damage: 4~9 1d6 + 3 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Pandirna's Diary Storage Key Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Save the Refugees Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] During the Emerald Grove assault, Pandirna will be rallied by Asharak : Asharak Looking well, folks - keep it up. Guex Yes sir! Asharak I'm not 'sir'. I was a doorjack in Elturel. Pandirna ' Yes sir'. Guex Shut it, you - and help me with these barrels. Asharak Remember - get down to the cave as soon as you hear the horn. Guex What happens if they attack before we get the signal? Asharak I reckon you'll hear something. Asharak Almost done? Pandirna Nearly. We've ransacked the packs for anything that'll burn. Asharak Good. Reckon we can brave a few nights without lamp-light if it means burning these buggers. Pandirna can also be seen chatting to Guex while filling barrels of oil: Pandirna Gods, this oil bloody stinks. Guex Not so bad as burning goblin will, I'd wager. Pandirna It seems... cruel, when you say it like that. Guex Cruel? Imagine what they'd do to us, given half the chance. Pandirna Can we just get this done, please? I want to get below before - Guex Before what? Afraid you might actually have to fight? Pandirna Look. Asharak already picked who he wanted on the walls, right? And it wasn't us. Guex You might be afraid of your own shadow, but some of us - Pandirna Puff out your chest all you like - I'm going where it's safe. Guex Would you be careful? We're going to spill if you don't stop shaking. Pandirna I'm not shaking. Guex Please, you're trembling like - Pandirna I'm not. Shaking. Guex All right... Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_DocksRoad_FF_000 UUID 6e40bdc8-b4c1-4d60-b986-60517ced3400 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Pantella is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the streets of Lower City in Act Three. “ Foundries can explode, the whole world can change, but if my orders stay the same, I stick to them. „ — Pantella Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Pantella is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Gneiss and a Steel Watcher . They can be found at X: -228 Y: -79 , arguing with Kolobeg , Felgi Diggums and Earno Diggums about restricted access to the Grey Harbour Docks . However, the patrol does not stop neither the party nor any other citizen and refugees from walking around them back and forth. More so, the "blocked" alley is far not the only way to reach the harbour area. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Pantella remains at the same place, claiming she will keep to her duty until receiving new orders. Recharge: Per turn Throw ( )   –   Javelin Damage: 6~11 1d6 + 5 ⁠ Piercing Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. Your Strength affects how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Range: 3-18 m (10-60 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail Halberd Helmet Javelin - 2x (if unused) Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Steel Watch Foundry is intact [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg We can't deliver our goods to the docks? Why? Fist Pantella New rule - it's a restricted area, top security. Felgi Diggums But I can see people down there on the docks going about their business! Fist Gneiss Oh, we'll get to them soon enough. Kolobeg We've got a job to do. These goods need to get delivered. Fist Pantella And I have a duty to the city and to Lord Gortash . So halt right there. Felgi Diggums Why this sudden restriction on visiting the docks, though? Fist Gneiss Somehow, citizen, Lord Gortash forgot to tell me. Isn't that strange? Kolobeg But I made a deliver to the docks just yesterday! Fist Pantella Sorry, citizen, the docks are now a restricted area. Felgi Diggums Talk straight. Are you really just looking for a bribe? Fist Gneiss Are you looking to get stomped flat by a Steel Watcher ? If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed [ edit section | visual editor ] Kolobeg The foundry's a wreck! There's nothing left to guard! Can we deliver our goods to the docks now? Fist Pantella Not just yet, citizen. The whole place is a crime scene. Felgi Diggums We just need to go past the foundry to make our delivery on the wharf. Fist Gneiss Don't split hairs with me. You go no farther. Kolobeg Come on, Saer Fist, let us past - these deliveries are urgent. Fist Pantella More urgent than justice? More urgent than the rule of law? Felgi Diggums Now you're just mocking us. Fist Gneiss Heh. You've got brains, for a dwarf. Kolobeg Look, we just need to go past the foundry along the docks. Fist Pantella My orders don't admit of any exceptions. Felgi Diggums You know, if you'd just look the other way for a minute... Fist Gneiss You trying to bribe me? If so, where's the bribe? If Enver Gortash is killed [ edit section | visual editor ] Fist Pantella Security's tightened since Gortash's death. You stay in your designated district. Kolobeg Aw, come on, Saer Fist, we got urgent deliveries to make. Fist Gneiss Urgent, is it? Why, you could be trying to sneak Gortash's assassins out in your cargo. I'd better search your goods. Kolobeg You're joking, right? Technical UID S_LOW_Park_FlamingFist2 UUID be3b99d0-b8ed-4d39-92e1-848f09e022c3 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Ranger Fist Pard is a human ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ I wasn't even supposed to be on duty today - had plans to go fishing. „ — Pard Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Pard is guarding the Bloomridge Park with Fist Bella , under the command of Manip Edenosa . His patrolling route runs forth and back from the western entrance to the park to the backside of the Facemaker's Boutique , approximately from X: -131 Y: -50 to X: -154 Y: -34 . If spoken to, Pard is annoyed with his bad luck, both of serving under command of a rather strict superior officer and of being dispatched into patrolling on his free day. If the party take a long rest after dispatching the Bhaalists’ ambush near the park fountain, Pard (along with Bella), if not killed, disappears from the game for good. He is replaced by Fist Brottor , Fist Elda , Fist Moss , Fist Ulinn and a Steel Watcher . BG_Guard Fist Patrick is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is in Rivington in Act Three . “ Keep a sharp eye out - redcaps are on the loose, ones deemed 'too violent' to work. And not one of these circus folk seem bothered by it. „ — Patrick Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Patrick stands at X: -14 Y: -86 , questioning Edmundis Magarus – an employee of the Circus of the Last Days – who reported him about several Redcaps gone on the loose. However, Edmundis himself does not consider the missing Redcaps to be a concern. Patrick asks why the Redcaps were being caged and how many are missing, but Edmundis is evasive or defensive in his answers [ 1 ] . PLA_Tavern_Paladin Fist Recruit Pavel is a human ranger and a recruit of the Flaming Fist . He is on the Risen Road in Act One . “ Watch it, that was my foot! „ — Pavel , pushing against a door Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Pavel is at Waukeen's Rest , struggling to get inside the burning inn together with his fellow Fists - Fist Recruit Aelis , Fist Recruit Ito and Fist Recruit Tristan , along with Gauntlet Yeva . They are trying to rescue Counsellor Florrick and Duke Ravengard who are said to be blocked inside the building. If a party member helps the Fists to unblock the front door, Pavel with the rest of the squad runs upstairs to the room where Florrick is trapped, and descends back after the counsellor’s fate is resolved. If Florrick survives, Pavel receives his orders (with the other Fists) to search for the kidnapped Duke and, after leaving the Inn, is never seen again. Technical UID S_WYR_CeremonyRoom_Patriar_002 UUID 5b5795b8-2bcb-4121-b978-65a1c244af00 Stats Human_Commoner Admiral Peil Hullhollyn is an Admiral of Baldur's Gate , present at the ceremony of Gortash's ordaining as an Archduke of the city. “ A good leader knows when to step aside. Ravengard did the right thing. „ — Peil Hullhollyn , on Gortash becoming Archduke Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony he sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Admiral Hullhollyn moves to the norther nave and stays near the first table with refreshments. If spoken with, he says that Ulder Ravengard , as a good leader, has chosen the right moment to step aside and let Gortash rule. If the party chooses to confront Gortash, they can later find Admiral Hullhollyn – along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the audience hall. Technical UID S_WYR_OpenHand_FakeIllasera UUID fb1b68cf-52f1-46ce-8328-d7db26c7fbf3 Stats HalfElf_Commoner Penela Lumpensicks is a dead Half-Elf whose corpse is in Rivington in Act Three. “ This... stirs a memory. Some sick creature was playing out the death of Bhaalspawn, Illasera. „ — Jaheira , upon exploring the scene Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Penela Lumpensicks' corpse is in the cave underneath the Open Hand Temple . Penela was killed by Orin the Red and her body (along with bodies of Blue Connor Balkosc , Benferlaen Plum , Enris Kellem and Liron Dustclotter ) used as a component of Orin's "art" as an effigy to Illasera , a Bhaalspawn defeated more than a century ago. Penela's corpse can be looted for one of ⁠ Dribbles' body parts and the first of Orin's Ritual Notes . Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find Dribbles the Clown ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders ⁠ Investigate the Murders Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Clown's Severed Torso Illasera, the First Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Penela's in-game model, as well as the model of Echo of Illasera (Illasera's ghost at the Murder Tribunal ), is designed to copy Illasera's image from the previous Baldur's Gate games, save for her hair color. Technical UID S_WYR_VampireSpawns_Petra UUID 6fb6e85e-ccd0-42ef-a37d-1e256a433f3b Stats Vampire_Spawn Trs. BG_Commoner_Wealthy Pale Petras is a Vampire Spawn enslaved to Cazador , and one of Astarion's siblings. He may appear at Fraygo's Flophouse or Cazador's Dungeon during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Petras can first be encountered on the first floor of Fraygo's Flophouse in Wyrm's Crossing , where he is hunting with Dalyria . [ 1 ] If Astarion is present, the three have a confrontation about Cazador and his intentions for the ritual. If Astarion is not present, the party can eavesdrop on their conversation: [STEALTH]  Listen in.  (DC 15) [ROGUE] [STEALTH]  Listen in.  (DC 15  ) Whether or not the check succeeds or fails, the party can interject by stating they know Astarion or they are interested in the 'party'. The spawn invite the party and then leave. Petras later can be encountered with the other spawn in Cazador's Dungeon, trapped and suspended while Cazador prepares for his ritual. Like the other spawn, he can be spared or killed after the ritual, or allowed to be consumed as one of its sacrifices. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 6~21 1d6 + 3 ⁠ Piercing + 2d6 ⁠ Necrotic Sink your fangs into a target and Sap its blood. Subsequent attacks that sap blood will further reduce the target's maximum hit points. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Claws ( ) Damage: 5~11 2d4 + 3 ⁠ Slashing Lash out with deadly claws. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Multiattack ( ) Damage: 10~22 2d4 + 3 ⁠ Slashing + 2d4 + 3 ⁠ Slashing Aim multiple attacks at a target. Each attack deals 2d4 Slashing damage. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Per turn Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pale Petras Not long before we leave scouring places like this behind. Part of me will miss it. Dalyria I will not. It is our chance to start over, and I will gladly do so. Pale Petras Do you think the master plans to expand his territory? Take Candlekeep - maybe even Amn ? Dalyria Oh, I'm sure he has plans. But I wouldn't dare guess at them. Dalyria Haven't we lingered long enough? We should return for the ceremony. Pale Petras We have time - the runaway is still missing, after all. Nothing happens until he's found. Pale Petras Just think - soon we'll feel the sun on our skin. After all this time... Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ The Pale Elf Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Pale Petras and Dalyria vanish if they are affected by Lathander's Light due to their Sunlight Hypersensitivity . Technical UID S_WYR_CeremonyRoom_Patriar_007 UUID cc7ec874-9dc0-4750-8346-3c14797e2174 Stats Elf_Commoner Lord Petric Amber is a Lord of Baldur's Gate , present at the ceremony of Enver Gortash's ordaining as an Archduke of the city. “ Times of strife produce the finest leaders. Archduke Gortash will be no exception. „ — Petric Amber Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony he sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lord Amber moves to the southern nave of the Audience Hall and stands near the first table with refreshments. If spoken with, he calls Gortash a strong leader who came up in times of strife. However, he means to support him only as long as Gortash "holds up his side of agreement". If confronting Gortash, the party can find Lord Amber along with all other invited guests and their retinue slaughtered in the Audience hall. The lights are much more interesting. „ — Phantaizha Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Phantaizha can be found inside the Elfsong Tavern in the Lower City as part of the audience in the Laff Riot contest. When spoken with, the talking party member realizes that she is a Silkroot abuser and can use the following dialogue options: Silkroot is no joke. You should go home - it's not safe to be out and about like this. Phantaizha Don't get all high and mighty with me, I hear the potions jingling in your pack. Don't talk to me. You're in the wrong place, silkhead. Your kind belong in the back alleys. Phantaizha Wow. And here I thought you looked like a nice one. Guess I was wrong. Have any for me? Phantaizha Noooooo, mate. I'm all out. Technical UID S_LOW_PaperboyBreakTime_Girl UUID c8d0f0b4-706c-43c4-8e3d-b5507ca336b4 Stats Human_Child Pharnilla is a human child in the Heapside district of the Lower City in Act Three . “ Bet these breaks would go quicker if I could read... „ — Pharnilla Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Pharnilla can be found in the alley not far from the Crimson Draughts shop. She is arguing with her friend Dellys about having proper time for breaks in their work. Both kids are working as newspaper sellers for Baldur's Mouth Gazette . However, the party cannot buy a sheet from either of them. Pharnilla tries to return to work, mustering different arguments for Dellys, while he holds his ground, trying to act like an experienced person who knows his "rights". Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pharnilla What if I gave you my break? Can I go back to selling gazettes then? Dellys No. Boss says we can't take the breaks of other Gazetteers. Trust me, when you're older, you'll appreciate the breaks. Pharnilla You're only a year older than me - and I sell more broadsheets. Pharnilla But whyyyyy can't I keep selling broadsheets? I'm bored. Dellys If you keep skipping your breaks, Mr Needle's going to take mine away too. Pharnilla Pfft. You're just mad I sell more copies than you. Pharnilla Come on, if I can't sell broadsheets, I'll be oh-so hungry... Dellys That patter works on punters, but I know you spend your wages on sweets. Pharnilla Harumph. Mr Needle doesn't even pay enough for the good sweets. Pharnilla Oh, come on. Give me half your remaining broadsheets. With Gortash dead, they're selling like crazy!  (If Enver Gortash is killed) Dellys If you sell my broadsheets, how'm I going to make my quota? Huh? Pharnilla If you weren't such a duff seller, Del, you wouldn't need the help! Dellys And if you weren't such a pest, Pharni, I might do it. Phase Zhentarim In-game Model Portrait Identity Male Voice / Actor Jack Maddison Faction Zhentarim Stats Size Small Type Humanoid Race Gnome Subrace Rock gnome Class Monk Subclass Way of Shadow Balanced Explorer Tactician Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 12 HP 97 AC 16 Initiative +4 Proficiency +4 Movement 7.5 m (25 ft) Weight 35 kg (70 lb) Darkvision 12 m (40 ft) XP reward 400 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 8 (-1) 18 (+4) 13 (+1) 10 (0) 14 (+2) 12 (+1) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA +3 +8 +1 0 +2 +1 Resistances (info) Additional Resources 12 Features Advanced Unarmoured Movement Difficult Terrain doesn't slow you down and you can Jump an additional 6 m (20 ft) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield . Darkvision Can see in the dark up to a certain distance. Deflect Missiles Use your reaction to reduce the damage from a ranged weapon attack by 1d10 + your Dexterity Modifier + your monk level. Evasion Successful DEX saves nullify damage; failed DEX saves reduce it by half. Extra Attack Can make an additional attack after an unarmed or weapon attack. Fast Hands Gain an extra bonus action . Gnome Cunning You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma Saving Throws . Ki-Empowered Strikes Your unarmed attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming enemies' Resistance and Immunity to non-magical damage. Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike After making an attack with a melee Monk weapon or while unarmed, you can make another unarmed attack as a bonus action. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks Attacks with Monk weapons and unarmed attacks scale with your Dexterity instead of your Strength if your Dexterity is higher. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Purity of Body You are Immune to Poison damage and can't be Poisoned or affected by disease thanks to the purifying ki flowing through your meridians. Shortened Stride Your movement speed is 7.5 m (25 ft). Slow Fall When you fall, you can use your reaction to gain Resistance to Falling damage. Stillness of Mind If Charmed or Frightened , automatically cast Stillness of Mind to remove them. Unarmoured Defence Your reflexes are as effective as any armour . While not wearing armour, you add your Wisdom Modifier to your Armour Class . Unarmoured Movement Your movement speed increases by 3 m (10 ft) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield. Gnome Cunning You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma Saving Throws . Ki-Empowered Strikes Your unarmed attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming enemies' Resistance and Immunity to non-magical damage. Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike After making an attack with a melee Monk weapon or while unarmed, you can make another unarmed attack as a bonus action. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks Attacks with Monk weapons and unarmed attacks scale with your Dexterity instead of your Strength if your Dexterity is higher. Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Purity of Body You are Immune to Poison damage and can't be Poisoned or affected by disease thanks to the purifying ki flowing through your meridians. Shortened Stride Your movement speed is 7.5 m (25 ft). Slow Fall When you fall, you can use your reaction to gain Resistance to Falling damage. Stillness of Mind If Charmed or Frightened , automatically cast Stillness of Mind to remove them. Unarmoured Defence Your reflexes are as effective as any armour . While not wearing armour, you add your Wisdom Modifier to your Armour Class . Unarmoured Movement Your movement speed increases by 3 m (10 ft) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield. Technical UID S_LOW_Guildhall_Zhent_Mercenary_006 UUID 9a307843-3958-4c07-ace9-f1c04b5af558 Stats LOW_Guildhall_Phase Eqp. EQP_Dagger_B Phase is a rock gnome monk and Zhent working as a mercenary for the Guild and Nine-Fingers Keene . He is at the southwestern corner of the Guildhall , standing guard in the event of an attack by the Stone Lord . “ The Guild's no army, however tough they act. Just twenty different thieving crews, come to hide behind Nine-Fingers' skirts. „ — Phase Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Protecting the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] Phase is first seen at the Guildhall , working as a mercenary for the Guild and guarding the Guildhall in the event of a potential attack by the Stone Lord . He is not blind to Nine-Fingers Keene looking down upon him and the rest of the Zhentarim, but despite this, he is certain that the guildmaster would nonetheless be glad to have him once the Stone Lord attacks, [ 1 ] and is eager to take the fight to the Stone Lord. [ 2 ] Phase stands guard at X: -40 Y: 738 , occasionally chatting with Slick Inatra whenever she stops by. In fact, he is often chastised by her for his lack of hygiene and his tendencies for placing bets. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] He also seems completely unaware of the Zhents' true purpose at the Guildhall. Battle for the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] When Roah Moonglow , Boss Friol , or Trinoda attempts to take over the Guildhall, Phase joins the fight alongside his Zhentarim allies against the Guild. Siding against the Zhentarim ends in Phase's demise, or in his disappearance if he is knocked out. [ 5 ] If the party members side with the Zhentarim, win the battle, and he survives the fight in Guildhall , Phase moves to guard the door leading into the guildmaster's office. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Dagger Damage: 5~8 1d4 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Sneak Attack (Melee) ( ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Weapon Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. Also works if you have an ally within 1.5 m (5 ft) of the target and you don't have Disadvantage . Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Per turn Stunning Strike (Melee) ( + ) Damage Normal weapon damage Spend a Ki Point to deal normal weapon damage and possibly Stun the target. CON Save Range: Normal weapon range Shadow Step ( ) Teleport from shadow to shadow. Afterwards, you have Advantage on your next melee Attack Roll . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Aid the Underduke Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Slick Inatra I told our clients we'd be on our best behaviour. Everyone playing nice here? Phase Not playing at all, boss. Slick Inatra Even better. Slick Inatra Make sure the others keep to themselves. This place is jumpy - better to give the Guildies their space. Phase 'S not like we're bloody diseased, boss. Slick Inatra Worse, Phase - we're Zhentarim . Phase What are we waiting for, Inatra? If we're meant to fight this Stone Lord, then let's bloody be about it. Slick Inatra See my uniform, Phase? It's nicer than yours, agreed? And not just because I don't sleep in it. Slick Inatra That's because I outrank you. So when I say that I haven't even been told our orders yet, I want you to believe me. Phase Yes. Sergeant. Slick Inatra I'd also like you to bathe sometime this tenday. Phase Yes, sergeant. Phase The locals going to kick us out, sergeant? Slick Inatra Just you, Phase. You rob the place of its glamour. Phase No loss. Last time I was here they had dice, blood-bouts, the works. Now it's just a lot of sulking pickpockets. Slick Inatra Those sulks are paying us, Phase. So chin up, make your coin, and you can lose it somewhere else. Aye? Technical UID S_LOW_BramptonOrphan_Civilian2 UUID 0ad943fa-51be-4141-83c5-feca43e8a62a Stats Halfling_Commoner Phelgro Dorph is a halfling civilian. He is attempting to comfort Fevrokis after he found the bodies of his dead parents in the Brampton district of the Lower City in Act Three . “ Poor kid found his parents like this. It's a tragedy, yeah, but it's not like we can look after him. „ — Phelgro Dorph Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Phelgro Dorph is beneath an arch near Felogyr's Fireworks with Fevrokis and Hari Nodles . They are trying to console the tiefling child, who is standing next to his parents' corpses. Hari wants to assume responsibility and help Fevrokis while Phelgro is afraid of the repercussions. Hari considers temporarily adopting Fevrokis until they can find permanent accommodation. Phelgro suggests bringing him to the Flaming Fist , but Hari believes that the Fists will hold them responsible for the death of Fevrokis' parents. Instead, Hari suggests bringing the child to the Guild , but Phelgro believes the Guild is too busy with city matters to help them. With no other options, Hari attempts to soothe Fevrokis by offering to find someone to "help" his parents and then get him something to eat. Phelgro Dorph's attitude towards the party may change depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Fevrokis Mummy? Daddy? Please get up. Please! Hari Nodles Hey, hey - shh, all right? Look at me - it's gonna be okay. Phelgro Dorph Shit. We need to tell the Flaming Fist - get this kid some help. Hari Nodles And have them lock us up for two murders we didn't do? Hari Nodles They're too scared to come here anyway. We'd have better luck with the Guild. Phelgro Dorph Between the Steel Watch and the Stone Lord, the Guild have barely got the strength to look after their own. Fevrokis I'm scared. Why won't they get up? Why... Phelgro Dorph We can't get involved with this. Hari Nodles Don't listen to him, kid - we've got you. Hari Nodles Can you tell us what happened? Fevrokis I-I got lost. I was following a kitty. Fevrokis When I found them again - when I came back - they were lying here... Hari Nodles Hush, now - it's all right. We're gonna help you. Phelgro Dorph Oh, we are, are we? Hari Nodles Don't be such a heartless bastard. Phelgro Dorph I'm not! I just don't wanna get in trouble, that's all! Hari Nodles Kid's gonna need a family no matter what happens. Phelgro Dorph You want to adopt it? Hari Nodles Just until he has somewhere better to go. Hari Nodles And he's not an 'it'. Fevrokis I want to go home... Hari Nodles I know you do, kid. I know. Tell you what... Hari Nodles We'll try and find someone who can help your ma and da and then we'll get you something to eat, all right? Hari Nodles And it can be anything you want. I promise. Phelgro Dorph Help them? They're dead. Hari Nodles Shut up, would you? Fevrokis O-okay. Let's do that, please. - **分类**: Characters

Technical UID S_GLO_HiddenGnome UUID 6cacd488-c479-47a9-9a39-1cfb2bf6836e Stats GLO_HiddenGnome Variant 1 UID WYR_HiddenGnome UUID e0dc09f2-9193-4af2-b578-ddf44b97aca9 Stats GLO_HiddenGnome Eqp. EQP_Dagger_Robe Trs. WYR_Ironhand_Worker Philomeen is a Deep Gnome in Baldur's Gate 3 . She can give the party a Runepowder Vial . “ Hold it. I swear to Ironhand, one more step and I blow us to chunks! „ — Philomeen 's greeting Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Brithvar mentions that a deep gnome fled with some smokepowder. This gnome is Philomeen, who was fed up with the Duergar's cruelty towards her and her people. She managed to escape taking a Runepowder Barrel with her, and hid. Philomeen wants to bring the Runepowder - an explosive of immense power handed down to them by their war-god, Gaerdal Ironhand - back to Baldur's Gate . She wants to have her clan with her, but she knows that the mission must come first. She considers her fellow clan members to be freedom fighters and believes they need this powder to "prove a point". It is advisable for the party to calm her down using one of the following options: [PERSUASION]  Laridda sent me. The gnomes need your help. (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  If I was a True Soul, you'd be dead. Stand down before you hurt yourself. (DC 15) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  KILL THE FIRE. OR DIE. PAINFULLY.  (DC 15  ) [PERSUASION]  Smile sincerely and hold out your hand.  (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  Are you sure about this? Once you're dead, that's it. It's over. (DC 15) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [INTELLIGENCE]  Cast Detect Thoughts.  (DC 12) You will not serve Ironhand in death. But you might still serve him in life. If calmed, she refuses to give up the barrel but agrees to give the party a Runepowder Vial . If she is not calmed down, she ignites the barrel. In addition to losing the barrel as a useful item later on, the resulting explosion delivers enormous area of effect damage, killing Philomeen and (likely) any party members nearby. If the Nere situation is resolved before reaching her, she escapes Grymforge, and can be encountered in Act Three . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If she escapes, Philomeen journeys to Angleiron's Cellar with the rest of the Ironhand Gnome resistance. She shares the same zeal as the rest of the clan in its plans for the city, and confirms that she broke up with Laridda for good. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and Abilities (Act 3) [ edit section | visual editor ] Burning Hands ( + ) Damage: 3~18 3d6 ⁠ Fire Each flammable target is hit with 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: Self Fire Bolt ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Fire Hurl a mote of fire. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands ⁠ Deal with the Gnomes ⁠ Deliver Nere's Head ⁠ Free True Soul Nere ⁠ Save the Grymforge Gnomes Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Runepowder Barrel - pickpocketed, looted or bartered during dialogue options in Angleiron's Cellar after discussing the fate of the Gondians with Wulbren . (After completing the dialogue with Philomeen the party is locked out of trade with her. [ verify ] ) Runepowder Vial - obtained via dialogue options in Grymforge Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Hand-Drawn Map Slaver's Inventory Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Philomeen in Act Three Model in Act Three Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] To acquire the barrel: Select a speaking and a thieving party member, and unlink them. Initiate the dialogue with the speaker. There is a critical threshold just past the top of the stairs. If Philomeen spots the theiving party member crossing it, she ignites the barrel. Once across the threshold the barrel can be safely stolen. Being spotted at this point has no consequences. Being caught stealing the barrel or pick-pocketing Philomeen turns her temporarily hostile. However, she does not ignite the barrel even if it is present. If the vial is pickpocketed before Philomeen offers it in dialogue, she becomes permanently hostile. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Philomeen asserts that the player character must be a True Soul because she witnessed them "sail in" and be greeted by the Duergar, even if the party initially entered Grymforge through the elevator from the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Sometimes. „ — Phinn Truscott Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Phinn Truscott and Bellora Truscott are in the park south of Lady Jannath's Estate , remembering their daughter who passed away. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Phinn Truscott Remember when she fell down the stairs and split her chin? Bellora Truscott I felt horrible about that one. Could barely sleep for a tenday. Phinn Truscott She couldn't wait to show off the scar to her friends at school. Bellora Truscott When she was little, I couldn't wait for a time when she would stop needing us so much. What I'd give to be needed now... Phinn Truscott I still need you, love. I always will. Bellora Truscott Do you ever think we should have had another one? Phinn Truscott Doesn't matter what we think now - it would have broken us back then. Bellora Truscott But if we'd only made the effort, if we'd only pushed through... Phinn Truscott I know, love. I think about it too. Phinn Truscott You know what got me thinking about her today? The news about the death of Lord Gortash. I never even met him, but it started me thinking.  (If Enver Gortash is killed) Phinn Truscott I know. Every loss diminishes us further. And I'm afraid many more are on the way. What can we do? Phinn Truscott We've kept going so far, despite... our loss.
