Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_Figaro_Assistant_000 UUID b503ab77-c714-47de-9def-2a07aaf51d9f Stats Human_Commoner Phlanders Hort is an assistant employee in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I'm ever so glad Master Figaro was saved - I'd have been out of a job otherwise! „ — Phlanders Hort Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Phlanders Hort is employed by Figaro Pennygood at Facemaker's Boutique in the Lower City . If Dolor escapes at the Wine Festival, he travels to the shop to kill Figaro, who is one of his murder targets in the quest ⁠ Investigate the Murders . If Figaro is killed, Phlanders takes his place as a trader . Before and after this assassination attempt, he is mostly discussing slogans with fellow shop assistant Bobula Hanvers . Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to LOW_Figaro_Assistant , similar to Figaro's store but with a smaller selection. Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Facemaker Fashion Basement Key Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Investigate the Murders Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Phlanders Hort 'To look all sharp like a mover and shaker, get your garbs from Figaro Facemaker!' Bobula Hanvers Master Figaro isn't paying you extra to come up with slogans, you know. Phlanders Hort 'For clothes that are pig ment to last, come to Figaro Facemaker!' Bobula Hanvers Please start fitting customers , not slogans. You know, your job . Phlanders Hort How about: 'Welcome back to Figaro Facemaker - where the clothes are to dye for!' Phlanders Hort Do... Do you get it? To dye for? Clothes? Bobula Hanvers I get the joke like one gets dysentery. Can we please get back to work? After the assassination attempt on Figaro Pennygood the banter changes to: Phlanders Hort 'Get a killer look when you shop Facemaker Fashion!' Bobula Hanvers That's the most tasteless slogan you've come up with yet. Great job. Phlanders Hort You know, I heard it was a Bhaalist that tried to kill Master Figaro. Technical UID S_GLO_IronThrone_Group2_Prisoner1 UUID aede3e82-f02b-4d6c-a92f-e9418b1b0e37 Stats LOW_IronThrone_Prisoners_Gnome Phoenix Lubbins is a rock gnome member of the Church of Gond , held hostage at the Iron Throne by Enver Gortash . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party enter the Iron Throne, Enver Gortash remotely triggers explosions which soon collapse the building. Phoenix Lubbins is trapped in the southern-most of the two western cells, alongside Featherweight Falson and Hastar Biggs . If freed, she dashes towards the Submersible to escape. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] The only action Phoenix uses on any turn is Dash , with the help of the Glimpse of Freedom condition which is applied when the cage is opened. Dash ( ) Cover more distance this turn: double your Movement Speed . Range: Self Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] A Plea to Gortash Scale Mail Explorer only [ edit section | visual editor ] Phoenix Lubbins has 50% more HP and cannot be pushed or shoved. Technical UID S_LOW_Guildhall_Visitor_006 UUID 227941fa-8264-4a8f-b3b6-2ae0f7ec3356 Stats Gnome_Commoner Phostlethwaite is a guest of The Guild , drinking with Tut Thistlebog in the Guildhall at X: -16 Y: 739 . “ Don't care about Stone Lord, Tut. Don't care about some ambush. I asked - d'you eat my last pickled ooze? „ — Phostlethwaite , to Tut Thistlebog [ 1 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party succeed a passive DC 18 Insight Check , or have Jaheira in the party, it is revealed that Phostlethwaite is not actually drunk but just pretending to in order to keep Tut out of trouble. If the party fail the check, it is neccessary to pass a DC 15 Constitution Check to resist Tut's belching. If all checks are passed, Tut reveals that the Stone Lord is going after The Counting House , which is a trap by Nine-Fingers Keene to catch him. If the Stone Lord's plans are revealed by Uktar , Tut will tell the party to "G'WAY" , with Phostlethewaite mentioning he's all riled up. No further information can be obtained from them. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursGate_Civilian_005 UUID 2dcd714d-7516-4be1-b598-86cbd0f6c5bf Stats Gnome_Commoner Phrennog is in the Lower City waiting to enter the Upper City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ I was queueing with the others and then I started feeling... wrong. No, thanks. „ — Phrennog Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Phrennog is standing with 'Grumpo' Daggles near the entrance of Facemaker's Boutique . They were waiting in the queue to head toward the Upper City but left due to feeling unsettled. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Phrennog Can't you feel it? 'Grumpo' Daggles Feel what exactly? Phrennog That weird... something. I dunno - it's like a tingle in my spine I can't shake. 'Grumpo' Daggles You sure it's not a trapped nerve? Phrennog I am , thank you. Grumpo' Daggles So you stopped queueing because you felt funny? Phrennog I mean yes, mostly. Why did you stop queueing, then? 'Grumpo' Daggles I couldn't take standing in that godsforsaken line a moment longer. Felt like I was gonna faint. Phrennog Fair enough. And they'd probably chuck you in the river if you did. 'Grumpo' Daggles Probably. Oh, unless... Grumpo' Daggles Do you think we could swim into the Upper City? Through the river, I mean. Phrennog Maybe. I dunno how closely they watch it. But there's probably grates and things down there to keep trash like us out. 'Grumpo' Daggles Nah, you're right. And I'm not the best swimmer anyway. Gods know what else is down there and all. Phrennog What do you mean 'what else is down there'? 'Grumpo' Daggles I dunno. Magic, innit? I'm just saying maybe there's a reason for that weird feeling of yours. Phrennog So you believe me, then? 'Grumpo' Daggles Stranger things have happened in Baldur's Gate is all I'm saying. I'd love a gander at those schematics... „ — Phyria Gollus Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Phyria Gollus can be found in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate between the Elfsong Tavern and Baldur's Mouth . Augur Harxkellan is giving an inspiring speech to a crowd of Gortash supporters. If Gortash is defeated, Phyria and the rest of the crowd disappear, and are not seen again. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Augur Harxkellan Oh wise and merciful Lord Gortash, we give thanks to you! We know you will drive back the army of the Absolute and raise our city to its pinnacle! We stand with you - and for you! Our lives are yours, and our enemies' are forfeit. You shall bring us true children of the Gate into the light! Muttonchops Dorryss Lightbringer Gortash! Grent Grintly Crush our enemies without mercy! Phyria Gollus Hail Lord Gortash! Hail the Steel Watch ! Augur Harxkellan Submit to Lord Gortash! Submission is salvation! Only Lord Gortash can protect us from the world-ending monstrosity of the Absolute! As the Absolute's forces stalk ever closer, take solace in his brilliance and know that we will be protected! And know that those who oppose Lord Gortash will burn in the all-consuming radiance of the one true light! Grent Grintly Hail Lord Gortash! Muttonchops Dorryss Death to the Absolute! Phyria Gollus Long live Lord Gortash and the Steel Watch! Augur Harxkellan Who will save us from certain destruction? Phyria Gollus Lord Gortash! Augur Harxkellan And how will we step into his new and brilliant dawn? Muttonchops Dorryss Lightbringer Gortash will show us the way! Augur Harxkellan And what will happen to those who oppose us? Grent Grintly They'll be burned by the one true light! Technical UID S_GOB_NerdyGoblinSage UUID 5f5c8416-8118-4619-8fc9-442304ff0a3d Stats Goblin_Caster Eqp. EQP_Goblin_Staff Trs. GOB_Goblin_Generic Booyahg Piddle is a Goblin Booyahg reading a book in one of the ruined towers of the Goblin Camp in Act One . “ Sez here that 'goblinoids are obstreperous and malodorous'. What's that mean? „ — Piddle , trying to sort out notes in Volo's book draft. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Piddle is quite intelligent and has an interest in books; he is currently reading the book Volo was working on about the Absolute and goblin-kind. He also gives insights on about goblin magic, booyahg. When approached, Piddle questions about Volo's meaning behind his complicated choice of words. He further explains how the famed chronicler was captured as he arrived and asked questions, being quickly accused of being a spy before being used as entertainment. He also shares how since the tribe converted to the Absolute the power of their leaders such as Priestess Gut and Dror Ragzlin has increased. If a party member asks about getting Volo's manuscript, he refuses, stating has not finished reading it, though he can be convinced to hand it over: [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  You will give me the book. (DC 2) [HALF-ORC] [INTIMIDATION]  Your lifetime gets shorter every second you keep that book. (DC 15  ) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  MANUSCRIPT. NOW.  (DC 15  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  A lifetime can be very short. Hand over the manuscript. (DC 15  ) [INTIMIDATION]  It'll be a very short lifetime if you don't hand me that manuscript. (DC 15) [PALADIN] [CLERIC] [DRUID] [PERSUASION]  You should spend your time in prayer - not reading this nonsense. (DC 5) [PERSUASION]  You should spend your time in prayer - not reading this nonsense. (DC 10) [BARD] [DECEPTION]  We both know this book's rubbish, Piddle. Write your own, and I'll edit it for you. (DC 10) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Scan his mind. You're an authority on the Absolute - you should be the one writing about it. Whatever the method used, if successful, he hands over On Goblins: My Life Among the Conquering Host and then departs. If the party fights the whole goblin camp, he makes his escape and runs away – never to be seen again. Technical UID S_DEN_ShadowDruid_003 UUID 53b08334-9f79-4bb5-b580-2662355d54ad Stats DEN_ShadowDruid_Ranger Eqp. EQP_Shortbow_Dagger_Leather Pinta is a halfling druid in the Emerald Grove during Act One . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Pinta is one of the Shadow Druids conspiring with Kagha to overtake the Emerald Grove in the name of their violent order. Pinta is in the Inner Sanctum with her fellow shadow druids Olodan and Wren , all of whom are Wild Shaped as rats. If the party interact with them using Speak with Animals , they remain silent and non-threatening. When enough evidence of Kagha's schemes are exposed, Olodan and her druids reveal themselves and admit to their plans. Regardless of whether persuading Kagha to turn on them or not, Pinta fights to the death alongside the Shadow Druids. UND_Duergar_Generic Ward Pistle is a Flameshade duergar in Grymforge during Act One . “ My mug's gone dry, Stickshit. „ — Pistle Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ward Pistle is at X: -606 Y: 384 , where she and Magmar guard the elevator leading to the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Pistle and Magmar maltreat an enslaved deep gnome named Skickpit , repeatedly demanding he fetch more beer from the barrel at the foot of the stairs. Pistle is a loyal member of Clan Flameshade. Should the party conspire with Brithvar against Nere , Pistle joins them against the drow and duergar cult novices. However, she is positioned too far from the possible location of the battle with Nere and his allies. Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] In life, Pol was the houndmaster of the patriar Durinbold family, of Durinbold Cheese Wedge fame. He and his three ghostly dogs ( Gordis , Rocky , and Zina ) attack the party if their sarcophagi are disturbed with a successful DC 15 Strength Check . Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] To Clotilda Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Polandulus occasionally chats with Aminah: Fist of Bane Aminah It's been an age since Gortash's last visit. Fist of Bane Polandulus Lord Gortash - you have not earned such familiarity. Fist of Bane Aminah Forgive me, Dread Brother. I simply... wish to look upon Bane's Chosen once more. Fist of Bane Aminah I heard the Black Hand's favoured can command the room with a single word. And that he knows no fear. Fist of Bane Polandulus Instead of sharing idle gossip about Lord Gortash, I suggest you focus on your duties. Fist of Bane Aminah Of course, Dread Brother. Fist of Bane Aminah Have you ever spoken to him? Fist of Bane Polandulus Lord Gortash? Only once. I felt the Black Hand's power in every word. Fist of Bane Aminah To speak to him, face-to-face? The very thought sends chills up my spine. Technical UID S_LOW_FlorrickConfrontation_Goon02 UUID 6d0c04b2-81d4-4d34-96d5-d5304dc889e8 Stats LOW_FlorrickGoon_Melee Eqp. EQP_LOW_FlorrickGoon_Melee Trs. BG_Guard Pollo the Muscle is a high half-elf fighter and ally of Counsellor Florrick . He is part of the retinue that confronts the party after Wyll breaks his pact with Mizora . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] After Wyll breaks his pact his Mizora during ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers and forsakes his father, Mizora manipulates Counsellor Florrick (or her replacement, Cordula Eltan ) into believing Wyll intentionally killed his father Ulder Ravengard ; this subsequently results in Pollo and the rest of the retinue under Florrick approaching and confronting the party the next time they are in the Lower City . A party member can then convince Florrick (or Eltan) to stand down through dialogue checks, and receive the The Legend of Ansur . Failing any of the checks results or attacking the retinue turns Pollo and the rest of the retinue hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Action Surge Immediately gain an extra Action to use this turn. You die! „ — Polma , upon realizing her victim has broken free Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Polma guards Priestess Gut's chambers in the Defiled Temple . Convincing Polma to allow the party safe passage through the room requires a DC 22 Ability Check of Persuasion , Intimidation , or Deception . It is possible for the party to avoid combat by sneaking behind Polma during her patrols or using the rocky crevice shortcut in the storeroom, guarded by Erna and Yerle . If the player character is captured by Gut, forced to sleep , and fails to break free once captured, Korrilla rescues the party and kills both Gut and Polma. Even if the whole Goblin Camp turns hostile, Polma remains non-hostile so long as the above ability check is passed. UND_KuoToa_Boss Pooldripp the Zealous is a Kuo-toa in the Underdark during Act One , leading the worship of BOOOAL . “ Our blood to fill your oceans, oh blessed BOOOAL! Our bones to build your temple in the deep! „ — Pooldripp while worshiping BOOOAL Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: BOOOAL Pooldripp is among other Kuo-toa in the Festering Cove , worshiping the alleged Kuo-toa God of Murder, BOOOAL. The player character can reveal BOOOAL's true identity, which angers him and starts a fight against only him. Killing BOOOAL frightens the Kuo-toa, and they quickly proclaim the player character to be Mahkloompah , their new god, and ask what to do next. The player character can tell the Kuo-toa to find a better name, build an army, stop their blood rituals, study the teachings of the player character's god, or carry on with what they were doing until then. Regardless of what is picked, Pooldripp attempts to comfort the player character stating the Kuo-toa will spread the player character's word violently . Additionally, the ⁠ Tipping the Scales inspiration is granted to party members with the Acolyte background. Should the party fail to reveal BOOOAL's true identity, the Kuo-toa aid BOOOAL in his fight against the party. Convincing Pooldripp to build an army leads to the party gaining Kuo-Toa Acolytes during the final battle in Act Three as part of ⁠ Gather Your Allies . I've got a prison cell with your name on it. „ — Poole , spotting a party member in the guarded area second time Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Poole, together with Fist Rowan , Fist Madigan , Fist Varone , and Fist Broadhorn , under command of Manip Nestor , guards the goods donated to the benefit of refugees, put into storage inside the Requisitioned Barn . Poole accompanies Manip Nestor near the front entrance to the barn. If any party member is spotted by Poole while trying to sneak into the barn without permission or is caught inside, he orders them to speak with the Manip (which immediately moves the party to the entrance). Being caught a second time leads to them being arrested. Unlike some other members of Manip Nestor's squad, talking to Poole does not grant any changes in approval. Technical UID S_WYR_Circus_Merchant UUID 60e4431d-dee5-4af4-a05e-65896ec64f2f Stats WYR_Kobold_Popper Trs. WYR_Circus_KoboldMerchant Popper is a Kobold at the Circus of the Last Days in Rivington . He sells items he has looted from corpses. “ I die. You die. We all die. Big woof! Have a treato - it'll make it better. „ — Popper , expounding on his philosophy of life Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Find Dribbles the Clown Popper has the Clown's Severed Hand on display in his shop. If caught stealing it, rather than calling the guards, Popper instead tries to barter for the item, offering it to the party for 10,000 gold claiming it has " artisinal bite marks". A party member can then pass an Intimidation or Persuasion check to convince him to part with the hand. If they pass a Deception check and claim they can get a hand from elsewhere, Popper lowers the price to 100 gold instead. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Note from BUSINESSLORD POPPER Notable items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to WYR_Circus_KoboldMerchant . She attempts to flee the High Hall's courtyard after it has been overrun by forces belonging to the Absolute . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the initial battle for High Hall, a large force of Absolutist cultists coming from the Upper City Sewers destroys the keep and routs the City Watch away from it, forcing what remains of the Watch to flee. [ 1 ] Faced with severe casualties, the last remnants of the Watch are composed of Fry , Ebber , Goodge , Gyordi , Matthew , and Preyn. A Mind Flayer decimates Matthew and Preyn with a Mind Blast as the Watchmen try to flee from High Hall, before being confronted with the party. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursMouth_Wanderer_05 UUID d3d4cf1f-e542-437f-b08f-5164fecd12f4 Stats Dragonborn_Commoner Pritt Yellowbreath is a brass dragonborn civilian who can be found near Bonecloak's Apothecary in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Can you believe it? They removed the Baldur's Mouth puzzle section. That was the best bit. And for what? An interview with some lord? I don't care what he's done - I just want my lettergames back. „ — Pritt Yellowbreath Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Pritt can be found circling around Bonecloak's Apothecary in the Lower City . If spoken to, Pritt expresses incredulity that the Baldur's Mouth Gazette dropped the puzzle section in its recent issue. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pritt can be occasionally heard lamenting the Baldur's Mouth Gazette. Pritt Yellowbreath I'm apoplectic. Furious. Frankly, I'm puzzled. Pritt Yellowbreath Interviews, politics, gossip - all of it gets in that bloody Baldur's Mouth rag. Pritt Yellowbreath Except what the people actually want in a broadsheet - puzzles. Pritt Yellowbreath Can't bloody believe it. No more puzzles. A travesty . If a positive article is published [ edit section | visual editor ] Pritt Yellowbreath Can't believe all this pandering nonsense the Mouth is printing. Pritt Yellowbreath I don't care which necromancer they've killed - it's taking up too many pages. Pritt Yellowbreath Forget adventurers - you know what'd be really heroic? Pritt Yellowbreath Someone bringing back the bloody puzzle section. Pritt Yellowbreath I mean, don't we have enough Heroes of Baldur's Gate already? Pritt Yellowbreath It's all just fluff pieces in the Mouth these days. Give me a break. If a negative article is published [ edit section | visual editor ] Pritt Yellowbreath Some lunatics enter the city and suddenly it's all the broadsheet will print. Pritt Yellowbreath Those folk in the Baldur's Mouth headlines recently... Horrible. Pritt Yellowbreath While they're hogging broadsheet pages, the puzzle section shrivels and dies. Pritt Yellowbreath I know the Mouth thinks this Absolutist Adventurer beat is gold. Pritt Yellowbreath But that's no reason to gut the rest of the broadsheet. If Gortash was killed [ edit section | visual editor ] Pritt Yellowbreath Gortash this, Gortash that - nothing but the dead duke in the Gazette right now. Pritt Yellowbreath The real tragedy here is the Baldur's Mouth cutting its puzzle section. Pritt Yellowbreath That bloody Gazette - nothing but death, death, death. Pritt Yellowbreath What the people want in a broadsheet is something fun . Puzzles, for instance. Pritt Yellowbreath I'm apoplectic. Furious. Frankly, I'm puzzled. Technical UID S_LOW_GithKid UUID 10403a03-aa9c-4c68-8a52-cbb381627906 Stats LOW_Githyanki_Prodigy Ptaris is a Githyanki located in the Society of Brilliance Lodge in the Lower City during Act Three . He will only be there if the stolen githyanki egg was given to Lady Esther as part of the quest ⁠ Steal a Githyanki Egg . Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 History 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.2 Act Three 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Honour Mode 3.3 Tactics 3.4 Loot 4 Related Quests 5 Related Literature 6 References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Ptaris is the adult, who has grown up from Githyanki Egg , whose growth was accelerated in order for the Society of Brilliance researcher, Havkelaag , to prove his theory on genetic morality. As part of this, Ptaris was raised under the Ptarian Code, the teachings of which led him to kill the members of the lodge in his quest to cure them of evil. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Ptaris was laid at Crèche Y'llek's hatchery. He was the last of his brood in the hatchery, taking longer than expected to hatch. Though most caretakers would have crushed him, the hatchery overseer Varsh Ko'kuu had begun life in a similar way, and wanted to give the egg as much of a chance as he could. [ 1 ] Ptaris' egg was eventually taken from the hatchery by a group of adventurers who were passing through the crèche, and brought to Lady Esther, a member of the Society of Brilliance who was on an expedition to obtain a githyanki egg for her fellow researchers. Esther brought the egg back to the Lodge in Baldur's Gate. There, it was taken on by the researcher and philosopher Havkelaag, who was trying to prove his theory on genetic morality by observing that a githyanki raised in a peaceful, nurturing environment could overcome their "violent nature". [ 2 ] Havkelaag wrote down what happened with Ptaris in Havkelaag's Journal . In order to complete their research in a shorter amount of time, the Society created a means of accelerating the growth of Ptaris. [ 3 ] As the basis of their research, Ptaris was raised under his namesake, The Ptarian Code , a strict moral code decreed by the dragon god of justice, Bahamut . Some of the core ideals of the code were to uphold the highest ideals of justice and good, and correct those who would oppose these ideals. [ 4 ] As he grew, Ptaris showed a "diligence, attentiveness and hunger" for knowledge, learning and following the Ptarian doctrine almost obsessively. [ 5 ] While Ptaris was true to how he enacted the code, his interpretation became too inflexible to consider the broader consequences and morality of his actions. [ 6 ] Ptaris became more and more obsessive and compulsive, until he took action against Havkelaag and the Society. He believed himself to be absolutely good and able to determine who was "bad". Ptaris believed his father and the Society to be immoral, and in accordance with his code, attempted to "make them better". When this failed, he tried torture, and finally, death, massacring the members of the Lodge. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ptaris is first met while he is just an egg, incubating in the hatchery of Crèche Y'llek under the watchful eye of Varsh Ko'kuu. Ko'kuu explains to the party that the egg is taking a longer time than expected to hatch. The party can then persuade him to let them take the egg, or steal it. If the egg is given to Lady Esther along the Monastery trail, she takes it back to the Society of Brilliance Lodge, where it grows into Ptaris. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Arriving at the Society of Brilliance Lodge, the party find a scene of devastation, blood coating the floor and the lodge members murdered. Upstairs and in the bedroom there is a portal, which leads down to the Lodge's docks, where a full grown Ptaris has just killed Lady Esther. Ptaris introduces himself, and says that he is "good". He reveals that he was raised by a dwarf named Havkelaag, his growth accelerated and raised under the Ptarian code. Ptaris reads the player character's mind and sees them giving him as an egg to Esther, and blames them for the harm his 'father' caused him. Meeting Ptaris grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Alien in the Big City ( Entertainer backgrounds) ⁠ Nature of the Beast ( Outlander backgrounds) At this point, the party can try and talk down Ptaris: [DECEPTION]  I thought I was saving you. I had no idea what they were planning. (DC 25) [INTIMIDATION]  I never should have saved you. But I'm happy to rectify my mistake. (DC 25) [PERSUASION]  You would have been destroyed if not for me, I saved you. (DC 25) [BARBARIAN] [PERSUASION]  I wield my anger like a blade, but it does not rule me. I am no more 'bad' than you are. (DC 20) [GITHYANKI] [PERSUASION]  Ungrateful yank. Our kin would have destroyed you if it wasn't for me. (DC 20) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Probe the boy's mind. You feel strange, don't you? That's your conscience. It's telling you to stop. [WARLOCK] [PERSUASION]  I gave you what my patron gave me - a chance at something more . (DC 20) If passing one of the checks, he reacts by saying that he was born evil and his father cured him. Ptaris realizes that his code is flawed, and becomes inconsolable as he comprehends the reality of his actions. If failing to convince Ptaris, he becomes hostile and attacks. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Astral Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Sapping Images ( ) Creates magical effigies that steal 2 points of Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom from nearby targets. Destroying a mental effigy restores the ability points. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Vacuum Missile ( ) Damage: 4~32 4d8 ⁠ Psychic Pierce a foe with a psychic dart and possibly drag other foes towards the target. STR Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Honour Mode [ edit section | visual editor ] In Patch #7 , Ptaris gained a legendary action that lets him apply a pacifying aura to a foe that strikes him, once per round. This pacifying aura reduces the stats of all allies within 5 meters for 2 turns. It also grants 50 temporary hit points to the person with the aura, and if not removed after 2 turns, it will spawn a Ptaris' Mental Image . Legendary Action: Ptarian Dogma Once per round, after being hit, Ptaris can spend a Legendary Action to surround his attacker in Ptarian Pacifism . Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Ptaris can be a surprisingly challenging fight. He is Level 12 and creates a number of mental images that sap the strength of allies and can potentially cause them to become Atrophied if not dealt with quickly. He generally uses Astral Step and Shunt Through Space to keep his distance from the party, while attacking them from a distance with Vacuum Missile and creating more images. However, Ptaris has no resistances and can be focused down rather quickly if the party has high damage dealers. Melee party members can counter Shunt Through Space by baiting Ptaris into wasting his reaction on an opportunity attack before attacking him themselves. Wyr_GurHunter Pumler Grejit is one of the Gur , the human nomadic tribe. He is in the Gur Camp in Rivington in Act 3 . “ We shed tears today, so we may shed blood tomorrow. „ — Pumler Grejit banter at the Gur Camp in Rivington Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Pumler Grejit is in the Gur Camp attending a funeral for the fallen from a recent offence on Cazador's palace. Pumler with his fellow Gur, all members of a group of monster hunters lead by Ulma , are looking for their children, who have been kidnapped by Cazador's spawns. The nomads have camped in Rivington, and are trying to mount a rescue or seek revenge. Ulma asks the party to help defeat Cazador and discover the fate of their abducted children. Once Cazador is defeated, Pumler along with Ulma and the other Gur move near the waypoint in Cazador's Dungeon . He attacks the party if the ritual held in the dungeons is completed. If Astarion was turned in to Gandrel in Act One and kidnapped, then in Act Three Pumler and all of his fellow Gur (except Gandrel) are dead. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Action Surge Immediately gain an extra Action to use this turn. Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Second Wind ( ) Healing: 1~10 + modifiers 1d10 + Fighter level ⁠ Healing Draw on your stamina to protect yourself. You regain 1d10 + Fighter Level ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail Greatsword Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pumler Grejit talks to Ulma and Dominica Arsetz in the Gur Camp: Dominica Arsetz Forgive me. I know tears will not bring our children back. Ulma There is nothing to forgive. It is only right to mourn. Pumler Grejit We shed tears today so we may shed blood tomorrow. Dominica Arsetz What will we do? There are so few of us left. Ulma Our strength was never numbers, but the bonds we share. And they are stronger than ever. Pumler Grejit As long as we stand together, we can never be truly broken. Ulma We let emotion cloud our judgement and it almost doomed us. We need strategy and cool heads. Dominica Arsetz Should we fortify the camp? Wait for the vampires to strike here? Pumler Grejit And let them marshal all their strength against us? I do not like our chances. Pumler Grejit Cazador's nest of serpents must be exterminated. Nothing less will do. Dominica Arsetz And if our children still live? What will happen to them if we attack? Ulma I share your fear, but we cannot build plans on fear. We will have to act, for all our sakes. Initiating scans and stuff. „ — Punkins Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Punkins plays with her friends on a small stone-paved space at X: -166 Y: -75 . She and her two mates, Cinnamon and Slow-Butt , are standing near Golbraith's Home . She is pretending to be a Steel Watcher scanning Cinnamon and Slow-Butt, to check their 'records'. If spoken to, Punkins tries to copy the automaton behavior, addressing party members as "citizen" , imitating mechanical buzzes and sounds. The party may then take part in children's game, agreeing or declining to be scanned. If Cinnamon is spoken with first and candy is detected in her pocket, they may rat the girl out to the "steel watcher" , allaying suspicions from themselves. Either option earns minor approval from Karlach , Jaheira , Gale , Wyll , Minsc and Halsin . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Punkins Halt, citizen! Prepare to be scanned! Cinnamon I am holding very still! Go ahead and scan, Watcher ! Punkins Humm humm humm zip! Punkins Hold still, citizen. Initiating scans and stuff. Cinnamon Go ahead! I am totally not an Absolute spy! Punkins Humm zip humm humm zip! Punkins Violation! Violation! Whoop whoop! Cinnamon No way, hee hee! I know my rights and I have nothing to hide! Slow-Butt Ha ha! Fun at last! Punish her, Watcher! Slow-Butt Aw, come on! When is it my turn? Punkins Be patient, citizen. CRE_Gith_Generic Youth Pyrindath is a member of a new githyanki generation hatched and raised in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ So far not one patrol has found the device. But so far not one patrol has had me in it. „ — Pyrindath Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Pyrindath is in the Crèche Infirmary , kneeling to the right from the entrance, watching two kids honing their Mage Hand skill. If spoken to, she anxiously mentions that if she is seen talking to an istik , the captain will not allow her to join the patrol. If the interacting party member is githyanki, Pyrindath bitterly comments that the mysterious weapon has not been found because she has not yet taken part in the search, and hopes the captain will send her next time. Technical UID S_CRE_HiddenCheckpointWarningGuard UUID 970d10ed-8092-463b-8446-223fe4cf2d68 Stats Githyanki_Warrior Eqp. EQP_Greatsword_HalfPlate_Gith Trs. CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Warrior Qen is a githyanki in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Leave me alone. The watch must remain undisturbed. „ — Qen Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Qen is first encountered if the party approach Crèche Y’llek through the Cliffside entrance . He is conversing with Raider G'r'ath , and is one of the sentries who question the party if they try to infiltrate the Crèche through the hidden tunnel. Dialogue choices are similar to those available when speaking with Gish Far'aag at the Monastery Basement entrance. Depending on player choices and Ability checks, Qen might allow the party passage or attack. If convinced, he bids them to report to Kith'rak Therezzyn immediately. After the party infiltrate the Crèche, Qen and G'r'ath guard the same passage above the Crèche Trade Post . Qen and the other githyanki become hostile if the party fail to explain their infiltration into the Crèche or return to the Crèche after fighting with Inquisitor W'wargaz. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursGate_FlamingFist_Melee_001 UUID db0f9ee3-bdda-43f9-82e3-27f7e5ae6da9 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Qirahe is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ Watch yourself - I'm on my third spat of the day with dogs who don't think the rules apply to them. „ — Qirahe , warning the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Qirahe is standing watch on the bridge at the Upper City Gate Checkpoint . She watches over the queue of residents trying to make their way into the Upper City . Having received orders to not let anyone into the Upper City, Qirahe and her fellows: Fist Grassley , Fist Wizard Hartlebury , Fist Magnolia and Fist Nudelmann , accompanied by a Steel Watcher , are trying to keep the queue orderly and prevent anyone from entering. If spoken to, Qirahe, just as most other guards in the cordon, takes the player character for a citizen who tries to make their way through the gate ahead of the queue and looks very annoyed with this. If the party return to the city after acquiring all Netherstones , three infected refugees near the queue transform into Mind Flayers and attack the bypassers. Qirahe is Surprised , but fights alongside the party. Once the Mind Flayers are dead, she and all the Fists around run away to warn their superiors, before completely vanishing from the game once far enough. Technical UID S_GLO_GithDragon UUID 9e21fba4-5a6d-4ca0-9738-2add3c967b3f Stats Dragon_AdultRed Qudenos (Disguised) In-game Model Technical UID S_LOW_VossDragonborn UUID 7952187b-7636-418f-884c-adfdd33fda8b Stats LOW_VossSewers_Red_Dragonborn_Qdenos Qudenos is a red dragon who can be first encountered at the Mountain Pass . He serves Kith'rak Voss , a legendary Githyanki knight in search of the Mysterious Artefact . “ Call me Qudenos. Master of Flames, Splitter of Skies. „ — Qudenos providing proper introductions Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Qudenos is a red dragon who has lived for many centuries, bearing the weight of uncounted battles. Under a pact with the goddess Tiamat , he serves as mount and companion to Kith'rak Voss. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Qudenos can first be spotted flying around the Mountain Pass in his dragon form, when a party member uses the telescope at the Emerald Grove . Upon reaching the pass, he flies overhead carrying Kith'rak Voss on his way to meet Sarth Baretha and her fellow githyanki. The sight of Qudenos causes party members to become frightened unless they pass a saving throw. After speaking to Voss at the mountain pass, he and Qudenos fly off together. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Qudenos, this time in his humanoid form as a dragonborn, and Voss can both be met later in the Lower City Sewers , if Voss is alive and the quest ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior is in progress. While speaking to Qudenos, he reveals that he is one among many red dragon rebels, loyal to the githyanki people but not to Vlaakith . After freeing Orpheus, Qudenos plans to carry Voss into battle to defeat Vlaakith. If attacked, Qudenos and Voss teleport away at their turn. However, even if Qudenos is killed before managing to teleport away, he can still be a potential ally in ⁠ Gather Your Allies during ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Qudenos has an idle conversation with Voss inside the Lower City Sewers in Act Three. Qudenos Even with Prince Orpheus to guide us, we are too small in number to defeat Vlaakith alone. Kith'rak Voss We will not be alone, Qudenos. Kith'rak Voss For a thousand years, we have been planting the seeds of revolution. Kith'rak Voss In every crèche, many young whisper Orpheus' name. They do Vlaakith's duty, but out of fear, not faith. Kith'rak Voss When the Prince of the Comet blazes his path, they will follow. And so will countless others. Kith'rak Voss The time is soon upon us, Qudenos. I will not forget your loyalty, friend. Qudenos The lich queen has shackled the red dragons as surely as she has shackled the githyanki. Qudenos You will be the first to battle. And I will be the one to carry you. Qudenos This Lae'zel and her allies. Can they be trusted? Kith'rak Voss You ask the wrong question. It is not a matter of 'can'. It is a matter of 'must'. Kith'rak Voss Whether by fortune or necessity, fate made its choice. Kith'rak Voss Lae'zel was the opportunity we prayed for. This may be our one chance to secure githyanki freedom. CHA_Exterior_Bandit_Caster Quelenna is a high-elven bandit who is looting the Overgrown Ruins in Act One . “ Well, that's one less greedy bastard to share the loot with. „ — Quelenna Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Quelenna is at the Chapel Entrance with Gimblebock , Taman , and Warryn . She walks between a vantage point over the Chapel Entrance and occasionally down the stairs south of her. Quelenna carries Talis: Divination without Magic , which suggests she may have an interest in Talis divination and a burgeoning relationship with a Talis diviner named Alys. When approached by a party member, Gimblebock automatically engages them in conversation. Depending on the outcome of this conversation, Gimblebock and his crew either leave or attack the party. If one of Quelenna's crewmates dies, she is dismissive of the fatality, commenting that there is more loot to go around. Technical UID S_LOW_BlushingMermaid_QuenoraGrizly UUID 9d475536-34f0-4a6f-9191-3a635b81a232 Stats LOW_QuenoraGrizly Captain Grisly , also known as Quenora Grisly , is the owner of The Blushing Mermaid . She can be found in the Lower City during Act Three and is too hungover to speak to the party, unless they discuss Vanra . “ Well, if it isn't the hag-killer. If you're here to see how I am - don't. My crew has been acting like I'm bloody made from porcelain. I'm this close to kicking in a few teeth - just to show I've still got it. „ — Quenora Grisly , when visited after her rescue Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Save Vanra If the party speak to Grisly about Vanra's disappearance, she claims that Lora Bergauz has gone mad and is dangerous, threatening her customers. She states Vanra is not real, and is a delusion that Lora cooked up. Believing Lora to be a threat, she intends to put a hit out on her, and offers 3000 gold to the party if they are willing to take her out. Rogues can ask for double the amount, to which Grisly agrees. If, after being given Grisly's offer, the interacting party member chooses the dialogue option Absolutely not - I refuse to do your dirty work. then "Grisly" drops the act and reveals herself as Auntie Ethel , a hag. Grisly's true identity can also be exposed by finding a note in the Blushing Mermaid which contains a report on Old Garlow's, using terms like "Auntie". The note is inside a rosewood desk in the same room as Grisly at X: 123 Y: -93 . Afterwards, the party can confront Grisly on the note they found; in doing so she instantly drops the act. Save Grisly [ edit section | visual editor ] The true Grisly can be found in Ethel's lair in The Blushing Mermaid , enthralled by a Whispering Mask accompanied by Mask of Vengeance , Mask of Terror and Mask of Servitude . While Ethel lives, Grisly is hostile on sight. If the party permanently dispatch Ethel and her Pearlspore Bells , Grisly comes to her senses and thanks the party for saving her, granting the ⁠ The Returned Cap'n inspiration to party members with the Sage background. Another approach is to knock her out which, unlike pickpocketing, allows a party member to remove the mask from her body, thus dispelling the hostility and she will wake after a long rest. According to a Ransom Note , Auntie Ethel blackmailed Grisly into wearing the mask by kidnapping Grisly's beloved Bosun Gannet . No Ethel [ edit section | visual editor ] Auntie Ethel does not appear in Act Three if she remained in her lair at the Sunlit Wetlands and did not abandon it. In this case, the real Captain Grisly is upstairs from the beginning and Vanra is not missing. Technical UID S_DEN_Bard_Backup UUID 8ef4c8ea-317d-4539-aa5b-c5e899cf0f31 Stats DEN_Refugees_Tiefling_Bard Quil Grootslang is a silver dragonborn singer and composer in Baldur's Gate 3 . She is a temporary Camp Follower , found at the party's campsite if playing as The Dark Urge . “ Well met. Goblins roughed me up and stole my hose when they heard me singing Hatchling Love. „ — Quil Grootslang Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Quil is a singer-songwriter, travelling to Baldur's Gate to publish her manuscript of love-chants, Affairs in Ancient Abeir: Songs of Draconic Love , throat-sung in Tymanther style. She is a bit of a romantic, recently made homeless after her clan-name was struck. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Quil only appears in place of Alfira to progress the Dark Urge Origin's personal quest line, if Alfira is somehow rendered unavailable (e.g. by her being killed or knocked out ) for the scene before the party long rests after crossing the bridge towards the Blighted Village or the stream next to it leading to the Owlbear Nest . Quil is travelling to Baldur's Gate to publish a new song she has written. She has recently escaped an encounter with the nearby band of goblins who robbed her of her belongings and pants, and requests to stay at the party's camp for one night. Before the party long rests, they can learn a little about dragonborn culture, her talent for throat-singing, and her desire to roam free, away from the restrictive clan-centric culture of her people. She also discusses love with the player character, and asks if they feel anything for anyone within the camp. Upon commencing a long rest on the night Quil appears at the camp, a cutscene occurs, showing the Dark Urge has murdered her in much the same way Alfira would have been, had she appeared instead. The rest of the cutscene plays out exactly the same as if it were Alfira. Like Alfira, rejecting Quil's request to spend the night does not change the outcome of the scene; the Dark Urge tracks her down and drags her back to camp before disembowelling her. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] The bard Lyrux Goldthroat , found in the Lower City Guildhall , can be asked if she knows any of Quil's songs. Lyrux replies "Of course I do", implying that Quil is a renowned musician, at least among dragonborn. Additionally, a letter addressed to Quil can be found on Fist Orvil in the Bhaalist Crypt , asking Quil to meet the Fist outside the Blushing Mermaid . It is unfinished. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Dear Quil Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ The Urge Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira and Quil's identical statistics. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Quil's stats are identical to Alfira's, even her Hellish Resistance and Darkvision, despite silver dragonborn having neither. Conversely, Quil is also missing the Cold Resistance and breath weapon. Quil expresses some passive attraction towards the player character upon first meeting if they are a dragonborn. The player character does not have a chance to reciprocate this, or pursue a romance with her. Quil Grootslang's last name possibly derives from a real-world legendary creature of the same name , said to be a huge serpent that lives in a deep cave in Richtersveld, South Africa. The word "Grootslang" is Afrikaans for "Big Snake". Quil is the only Dragonborn character to appear in Act One of the game. The search must be going badly. „ — Qun'irel Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Qun'irel stands in the corridor to the west from the entrance with Tra'an , warily discussing the arrival of the Inquisitor and uneasiness within the Crèche evoked by his arrival. Speaking to Qun'irel (the dialogue involves both her and Tra’an), the player character might learn details about the current situation within the Crèche, and about the role of Inquisitors in gith society. The player character can roll a DC 14 Intimidation Check (or a DC 14 Deception Check if they are a githyanki; the Dark Urge origin has unique formulation on both rolls) to fish out more information about why the Inquisitor was sent to the Crèche, about tensions between him and Kith’rak Therezzyn , and also about how the search is going. At least until the ch'r'ai inquisition is over. „ — Ra'gur Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Ra'gur together with Gish Far'aag and Warrior Khunaruth guard the entrance to the Crèche from Rosymorn Monastery Basement. He stands on the high ground above the makeshift prison, to the left from the entrance. The three sentries are accompanied by Ardent Lin'a'an , a member of the retinue of Inquisitor W'wargaz , who was sent to the Crèche to locate and retrieve the ultimate mystical weapon against ghaik . If the party speak to Ra'gur, he resents the presence of strangers poking around the Crèche, as well as the inquisition. However, if the player character is a githyanki, Ra'gur tells them that he is going to keep out of the captain's sight until the Inquisitor leaves. Technical UID S_CRE_MageHandKid02 UUID 840d6525-88ba-462a-944c-a74975afa695 Stats Githyanki_Child Ra'jak is a githyanki child who can be found in Act One . Open the chest! ...Please? „ — Ra'jak Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Ra'jak and his friend Zel'i are playing in the Crèche Infirmary . They are honing their Mage Hand skill, shoving locked Traveller’s Chest back and forth. When being hit, the chest emerges wailing sounds that can be heard far beyond the Infirmary. If the player speaks to Ra'jak, this will initiate a dialogue with both kids, which (apart from those letting them continue their game) might lead to one of two outcomes: either Zel'i hits the player character with her Mage Hand, or both children run away to the right-central alcove of the Infirmary and chuckle, allowing the player to lockpick the chest ( DC 18 Sleight of Hand Check ) and face the consequences. Should the player speaks with Ra'jak afterwards, he will mock them, happy with their ‘joke’. GOB_Goblin_Generic Sharp-Eye Raagg is a goblin stationed in the Goblin Camp in Act One . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Raagg is at the northern edge of the Goblin Camp with several other goblins and bugbears who have fallen into a drunken slumber. If the party attack the cracked wall to gain entry into the Shattered Sanctum , it causes all nearby enemies to wake up and initiate combat. Unlike the other goblins nearby, Raagg cannot be calmed down if awakened and immediately attacks the party alongside the nearby bugbears and goblins. GOB_Goblin_Generic Racha is a goblin who can be met at Moonrise Towers in Act Two . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Racha can be found at Moonrise Towers undergoing a trial by Ketheric Thorm for her failures, if Minthara or Fezzerk do not survive Act One . In this case, Racha is accompanied by Darra and Drenn . It is not possible for the party to speak with any of the goblins outside of the cutscene. The player character has several options for deciding their fate. If the party set them free, the surviving goblins flee from Moonrise Towers and disappear. Technical UID S_MOO_AccessCultist UUID 7f0f8d11-9d1e-4210-bbcb-41aa05666d58 Stats Human_Cultist_Myrkul_MasterOfSouls Eqp. EQP_MasterOfSouls Trs. MOO_Cultist Radija is a necromancer [ 1 ] of the Cult of Myrkul . She is on the first floor of Moonrise Towers in Act Two . “ It is not your time yet, blessed one. The rooftop chapel is reserved for the General's private contemplation - save for those he chooses to ascend. „ — Radija Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Radija is just outside the ornate door which leads to the rooftop . If Ketheric Thorm is already on the roof, a party member can ask for an audience with him, which she refuses. Unlike the Zealots, Adepts, and other members of the Cult of the Absolute , it appears Sarabayle and the other Mistresses of Souls are fully aware of what the Absolute is and the religious hoax they're perpetrating. [ 2 ] This greater understanding (and accompanying disdain) is shared by the other high-ranking Myrkulite necromancers serving Ketheric Thorm , with Kressa Bonedaughter bemoaning the weak servility of the infected she is presented with, and Balthazar using the player character's worm-infested status as an expletive. Radija hints that the Cult of the Absolute goes well beyond mind flayer infections. These effects last until the start of your next turn. Range: Self Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Radija is a wizard who is joined by the Necromites . She usually casts Fireball and uses her Bonus Action to create another necromite with Incubate Death . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Myrkulite Scourge Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Despite being named as necromancers at several points, all Mistresses of Souls are Evocation Wizards. ↑ When a party member talks to Radija , if they pass a DC 14 Wisdom Check or try to link with her own parasite, it is revealed that she does not have one and that she (along with Kressa Bonedaughter ) views party members with scorn for being unwitting infected tools. Gold_Meager Rags Deelarma is a human beggar just outside the entrance to the Counting House , in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ It sounds like you might have some coins to spare? Just a few, saer? Please? „ — Rags Deelarma Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Rags Deelarma, a resident of Nortale's Hostel , is begging in front of the Counting House . She complains about Vrindula Mardassus counting money right in front of her while she has fallen on hard times. The party can either give a single coin, angering her, or 10 coins which results in praise. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] If a party member gives a handful of coins (10):   -1   +1   +1   -1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Rags Deelarma Excuse me madam. Hello? Vrindula Mardassus ...four, five, six, seven, eight... Rags Deelarma Excuse me, saer? Could you spare a little gold? Vrindula Mardassus ...nine... ten... eleven... Rags Deelarma It sounds like you might have some coins to spare? Just a few, saer? Please? Vrindula Mardassus ...Please stop interrupting me... eleven... twelve... Rags Deelarma We've fallen on hard times is all, what with everyone scaled 'cause of the Absolute . Vrindula Mardassus Urrrggh! Now I have to start again thanks to you. Rags Deelarma I'm sorry to ask again, but my family's starving. Vrindula Mardassus One... two... three... four... Rags Deelarma You're not even very far in yet! Vrindula Mardassus That's because you keep interrupting me! Vrindula Mardassus Gods, I knew I should've done this before I got here. Vrindula Mardassus Now, there's thirty in that pouch, forty in that one, eighteen, no, seventeen - wait. Vrindula Mardassus Ugh, that won't do. One at a time, then. Here we go. HAV_Survivor Fist Rahir is a Flaming Fist under the command of Counsellor Florrick to rescue Duke Ravengard during Act Two . “ You're heading into the Towers, are you? Good. I pray it's not too late for Duke Ravengard. „ — Rahir Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Initially on a mission led by Florrick to rescue Duke Ravengard , Rahir and the rest of the Fists were waylaid by the dangers of the Shadow-Cursed Lands and found refuge with the Harpers at Last Light Inn . Rahir is within the Last Light Inn, in the same room as several other Fists, and Art Cullagh . If Florrick is not rescued from Waukeen's Rest in Act One , Rahir never appears in the game. Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Rahir is incapacitated by a Winged Horror before the party can react, and becomes Impaled for the remainder of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, he and everyone in Last Light Inn turn into a Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira . After the battle, talking to Rahir reveals that he and Marcus were close, and that he is in disbelief at how easily Marcus turned against him. [ 1 ] He acknowledges Marcus' treachery, but mourns the loss of him as a friend. [ 2 ] Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise Towers , Rahir is among the Fists left by Florrick to follow Jaheira to the ⁠ assault on the fortress . However, Rahir is killed during the initial fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. His corpse is on the bridge leading to Moonrise, implying he was amongst the first to fall in battle. LOW_CountingHouse_Clerk Rakath Glitterbeard is the dwarven head banker of the Counting House , in the Lower City in Act Three . “ Yes sir, Stone Lord , sir. Shall we open the account in your name, or the Absolute's? Just step this way to your special deposit box - don't mind the teeth. „ — Rakath Glitterbeard , exhibiting exemplary customer service Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Return Rakath's Gold When the party first enters the lower area of The Counting House vaults, a cinematic conversation triggers, which leads to a combat encounter. If Glitterbeard survives, he reveals that he works for the Guild and that Nine-Fingers Keene instructed him to lure the Stone Lord into the vaults and kill him with a mimic . However, the plan has failed, and he asks the party to retrieve the 10,000 stolen gold. The party can pass a dialogue check to convince Rakath that the Guild should pay for half of it. If the party loots the high security vaults around the room, Rakath may occasionally rebuke the party, but he never becomes hostile. [ verify ] If a party member returns Rakath's gold, he rewards them with the High Security Vault nº9 Key , which unlocks a vault containing Elegant Studded Leather . Alternatively, a party member can pickpocket the key from him or lockpick the vault itself. WYR_OpenHand_Sarcophagus Raloric Windbane is a corpse in the crypt underneath the Open Hand Temple in Rivington . He is raised as a Greater Zombie if the party refuses to take the curse from the Sentient Amulet (Rare) . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon reaching the Open Hand Temple, it is revealed that Shirra Clarwen died the previous year, and her spirit passed on. The monk's manifestation inside the sentient amulet laments the passing of her spirit, who would have born the curse, and asks the interacting party member if they will bear it instead. If they refuse, the spirit inside the amulet (now inside the body of Shirra Clarwen ) raises three nearby corpses, including Raloric Windbane, to attack the party. GOB_Goblin_Generic Brawler Rancer is stationed on the eastern side of the Goblin Camp in Act One . “ I'll be a big ol' - big ol' boy. „ — Rancer Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Brawler Rancer wanders the easternmost area of the Goblin Camp next to the cliff's ledge, occasionally urinating or puking over the chasm from drunkenness. Rancer confronts the party if they are caught attempting to sneak into the Goblin Camp. It is possible to avoid conflict by passing one of the following ability checks or dialogue options: [BERSERKER] [ILLITHID] [INTIMIDATION]  I am a True Soul. Question me, AND DIE.  (DC 5  ) [BARBARIAN] [ILLITHID] [INTIMIDATION]  I am a True Soul. Doubt me at your peril.  (DC 5  ) [ILLITHID] [INTIMIDATION]  You're speaking to a True Soul. Step aside. (DC 5) [ILLITHID] [INTIMIDATION]  Step aside. I command you. (DC 5) [DECEPTION]  Just nosing around for a drink. (DC 10) [STEALTH]  Sneak away.  (DC 10) [ROGUE] [STEALTH]  Melt into the shadows.  (DC 5) [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM]  Read his mind. [DROW]  I'm doing whatever I please. [HUMAN] [HALFLING] [DWARF]  Pretend to hold up a mug. Cheers! [TRUE SOUL]  You're speaking to a True Soul. Step aside. He is listening to complaints about the treatment of their letters at the Sword Coast Couriers during Act Three . “ I'd suggest holding onto your letters until things get back to normal around here. „ — Randalf Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Randalf is outside the Rivington General across from the Open Hand Temple chatting to Balgor and Sylvie Summerworth . Sylvie complains that her letters were lost, while Randalf and Balgor attempt to reassure her, hopping the problem will resolve itself. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Sylvie Summerworth 'To Send and to Serve', they say. Well I say poppycock! I cannot believe they lost my letters. Randalf I'm sure your letters will turn up - have patience. Sylvie Summerworth This is the third time in the last tenday! Balgor Maybe it has something to do with the army about to invade the city. Sylvie Summerworth Don't believe everything you read in the broadsheets. That so-called army is probably no more than a pack of goblins and bugbears. Randalf What did the postmaster say? Danzo , isn't it? Sylvie Summerworth He muttered a bunch of excuses, but I wasn't having it. He has one job - deliver my post. So do it! Balgor Actually, the pigeons do the delivering. Why don't you take your complaints to them? Sylvie Summerworth You know - that's an excellent idea! I should go straight to the source. Balgor Never thought I'd feel sorry for a flock of pigeons. Balgor Instead of complaining to me, why don't you find a different delivery service? Sylvie Summerworth I checked - it's the Sword Coast Couriers or nothing. Can you believe it? Balgor I think that's what they call a monopoly. Technical UID S_WYR_CeremonyRoom_Patriar_001 UUID 8363e570-a4b9-4e98-99c8-380a68caeb7f Stats Human_Commoner Lord Randolf Vammas is a Lord of Baldur's Gate who is present for Gortash's ordination as the Archduke of the city. “ With Gortash in charge, this city will thrive. As will we all, of course. „ — Randolf Vammas Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony he sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lord Vammas stays at the central nave of the Audience Hall, but moves closer to its end. He engages in casual conversation with Lady Winstra Hullhollyn , discussing the after-ceremony soiree. He tells her he is going to discuss with Gortash several business proposals he sent him earlier. If spoken to, he calls Gortash a man who knows well how to do business. If the party confront Gortash, they can later find Lord Vammas along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the Audience hall. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Randolf Vammas Gortash will likely call on me soon - I've sent him many a business proposal. Winstra Hullhollyn Do invite me along, darling. We could have afternoon tea! Randolf Vammas Lady Winstra, we'll be discussing business - hardly your realm of expertise. Winstra Hullhollyn I could say the same thing about you, darling. Winstra Hullhollyn A man like Gortash knows the path to people's hearts - a glorious evening of drinks and dancing.. Randolf Vammas So long as business comes first - parties don't pay for themselves. Winstra Hullhollyn They do when I throw them. Winstra Hullhollyn I'd love an evening with Gortash. He's be a most fascinating host, I'd wager. Randolf Vammas More fun than Ravengard , for sure. Winstra Hullhollyn That's hardly difficult. Randolf Vammas Business has been slow, but it is hardly my fault! This ' Absolute ' has people in a flap! Winstra Hullhollyn Every gala, ball, and brunch has been cancelled due to that nuisance of a cult! It's a disaster. Randolf Vammas I think Gortash is more concerned about the economy than he is your parties, my lady. Then down came the claw and that, love, was that. „ — Raphael , reciting a lullaby Raphael is a cambion / devil who first appears disguised as an enigmatic human, but quickly reveals his true form and intentions. Contents 1 Overview 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 The Crown of Karsus 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.1.1 Encounter Location 4.2 Act Two 4.3 Act Three 5 Companion approval 6 Combat 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 Related quests 10 Gallery 11 OST 12 See also 13 Notes and references 14 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael delights in enticing mortals with offers, especially to those whose circumstances leave them with few options. Back home in the hells, Raphael resides in the House of Hope , a lavish and seemingly welcoming place where he brings potential clients. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael has dark hair and faintly red skin, which deepens into a brighter red when he sheds his human disguise. In his true form, he has the tell-tale characteristics of a cambion; significantly with thick and decorative curved horns, and a set of pointed wings with visible membranes, similar to those of a bat. While fiendishly ascended, Raphael's form forgoes its remaining humanoid qualities. Wreathed in flame and two sloping horns, his head is an amalgamation of three animalistic faces with skin stretched tight over bone. His faces total three glowing, yellow eyes, each with tusked gums and open nasal cavities, exposing bloody muscle. His body visibly glows with hellfire, laced with dark, bone-like structures that lead down his arms, torso and digitigrade legs. [ 1 ] Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael is cunning, manipulative, and very sure of himself [ 2 ] , though he angers easily when undermined. Although his station grants him power and rank higher than many other devils, he hungers for more; plotting, manipulating and scheming - for over the past thousand years - to unite the Nine Hells under his control. As the game begins, he sees events unfold and realizes he now has the tenable possibility of finally achieving this goal. [ 3 ] Raphael enjoys poetry and his own theatricality, as well as tormenting and toying with people in creatively cruel ways. He is also narcissistic to the point that his father sent an incubus, who could appear as a more youthful version of Raphael, to distract him. [ 4 ] History [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael is heir to the archdevil Mephistopheles , a status granting him power and rank above that of other devils. He is proprietor to the House of Hope , a falsely welcoming home used to lure in those he wishes to bind into his service with infernal contracts. The nature of Raphael's contracts are such that the contractee will inevitably owe him a debt. These individuals eventually become Eternal Debtors . One such contractee was the architect of Moonrise Towers , who bargained to end Ketheric Thorm's Dark Justiciar army in exchange for their soul. [ 5 ] Raphael contracted Yurgir and his legion of Merregons , who destroyed all but one of the Justiciars, who himself made a deal with Raphael to guarantee his survival in the form of many rats. As designed, Yurgir did not technically complete his end of the bargain, and remained trapped in the Gauntlet of Shar and under contract of Raphael. The Crown of Karsus [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael bore witness to the fall of Netheril through Karsus' Folly ; a magocracy destroyed by Karsus' inability to control the Crown of Karsus . However, Raphael saw also Karsus' ambition for creating a "better world" and ever since, coveted the crown for use in uniting the Nine Hells under his rule as Archdevil Supreme. [ 6 ] Before he could retrieve the crown, however, his father Mephistopheles archived it to one of his vaults. He continued to monitor the crown, observing later how the Dead Three managed to steal it from its vault, and then use it to control an Elder Brain and subsequently its tadpoled servants. At some point, likely after the fall of Netheril, Raphael's father sent him an incubus, Haarlep , to distract him from an unknown task (possibly his designs on the crown, though this task is not expanded upon anywhere). This was met mostly with success, thanks to Raphael's arrogance and narcissism. [ 4 ] Raphael finally saw his chance to obtain the crown when a group of adventurers who had been implanted with tadpoles under the Dead Three's plan, managed to retain their autonomy. He met with them soon after their escape from a Nautiloid ship, and began to set in motion an exchange for the crown through an infernal contract. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael introduces himself to the party during Act One, [ 7 ] not long after the fall of the Nautiloid . He appears disguised as a human with an enigmatic personality, and the party can act diplomatically or hostile about his presence. He teleports the party to the House of Hope where he reveals himself as a cambion . The fiend then offers them to lavishly partake on the supper he prepared and speaks in riddles, as he is fully aware of the party's condition . Raphael offers a deal: to remove the tadpole in exchange for the player character's soul. He warns them that when their luck and time runs out, he will appear one last time. While in the Wilderness, one of Raphael's agents, Korrilla , is keeping an eye on the party. If the player character is captured by Gut , Korrilla kills her instantly. She then frees the player character and reveals that Raphael sent her. Korrilla tells the player character to watch their back, as Raphael will not always be around to save them. Regardless of having interacted with Korrilla before, she can briefly be found at the Campsite , during the 'Celebrate at Camp' stage of the quest ⁠ Save the Refugees . Shortly after the party starts, Korrilla appears to teleport into the northern part of the camp and can briefly be found sneaking around, towards where Gale is camped, before disappearing. If the character gets too close, she disappears, and the player character makes a remark about a "bizarre" smell of sulphur. If they get close enough without being detected, it is possible to pickpocket her for some common items and a small amount of gold, or trigger two lines of dialogue before she disappears. Encounter Location [ edit section | visual editor ] The first encounter with Raphael is triggered the first time the party visit any of the following locations [ 8 ] after completing one of the sub-quests of ⁠ Find a Cure [ 9 ] , returning Halsin to the grove, accepting Halsin's request to kill the goblin leaders, or recruiting Lae'zel [ 10 ] at the Mountain Pass or along Rosymorn Monastery Trail . [ 11 ] The Harper outpost southwest of the druids' grove at X: 155 Y: 365 The path leading from the Sacred Pool to the Secluded Cove and Alfira at X: 270 Y: 524 The broken bridge between the Blighted Village and Waukeen's Rest at X: -7 Y: 476 The upper rafters of the Shattered Sanctum at X: 313 Y: -26 Accessible directly from the Goblin Camp by collapsing the corridor wall at X: -105 Y: 478 The Selûnite Outpost in the Underdark at X: 154 Y: -243 Camp while traveling to Rosymorn Monastery [ 12 ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] During Act Two, Raphael can first be found at the Last Light Inn , playing lanceboard with Mol , if she survived. If Astarion is in the party, Raphael offers him a deal for information about his scars. Sometimes, regardless of Astarion's presence, Raphael may disappear before the party has a chance to talk to him, claiming to have "urgent business with another client" and saying that he will be around as needed for his "favorite client", leaving it ambiguous as to whether he is indicating the player or Astarion. Regardless, Mol can be spoken to after Raphael disappears, and will tell the party she is considering making a deal with him. Korrilla too can be briefly spotted and spoken to outside the Reithwin Masons' Guild in the Shadow-Cursed Lands , still keeping an eye on the party. Raphael later can be encountered outside the Grand Mausoleum , practising a monologue. After approaching him, he immediately strikes up a conversation with the party. He warns them of a creature within the Mausoleum, and asks for it to be killed. Killing the creature also acts as payment for Astarion's deal. This starts ⁠ Kill Raphael's Old Enemy . Finding the creature inside the Mausoleum, the party discover that Raphael's enemy is Yurgir , an orthon who is trapped in a contract with Raphael. If his contract is successfully broken, Raphael appears to take Yurgir back to the House of Hope to discuss a new contract. If he is killed, Yurgir returns back to the House of Hope. If Astarion made a deal, Raphael appears at camp to fulfil his side of the bargain. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] After reaching Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three, Korrilla can be encountered at the bar of Sharess' Caress . Talking with her lets her try to convince the party to take Raphael's deal. Upstairs in the Devil's Den , Raphael is speaking to Voss , who wishes to make a deal with him in exchange for the Orphic Hammer . He is uninterested in anything Voss has to offer, but instead offers it to the party in exchange for the Crown of Karsus . Raphael wants to unite the hells using the crown, and rule over them. This starts ⁠ Deal with the Devil . The party can take this deal, or attempt to steal the Hammer from Raphael's House of Hope . It is also possible to just visit (or loot everything but the hammer from) Raphael's house. In the House of Hope, it is revealed that Raphael keeps Korrilla's sister, Hope , captive, and that he prefers to have sex with an incubus who looks like a younger version of himself, Haarlep . If the party take his deal, Raphael has a short cutscene at the end of the story, where he reveals his ambitions to take his rule further than just the hells. If the party instead steal the hammer, Raphael confronts them when they try to leave, and must be killed. After Raphael is defeated, the party can interact with a Crystal Ball in the Devil's Fee to see that he is dangling, bloody and beaten, above the giant mouth of Mephistopheles and about to be devoured. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] When meeting Raphael for the first time: "I'll do anything to get rid of the tadpole."   -5   -1   -1 "I need to think this over."   +1   +1   +1 "You're mad if you think I'll make a deal with a devil."   +1   +5   +1   +5   +5 "Then fix it. Or die by my hand!"   +5   +1   +5   +1   +1 If the character who triggers Raphael's appearance is sufficiently distant from the rest of the party, that character will be teleported to the House of Hope alone; however, the above options will still trigger approval or disapproval as normal even though the relevant companions are not physically present. Privacy Policy Continue Dismiss See also [ edit section | visual editor ] Haarlep Korrilla ⁠ House of Hope Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Raphael's appearance has mostly remained the same throughout the lifespan of the game with the exception of his hair color. During the Early Access and the Release of the game, Raphael had dark, brown hair. In Patch 3, this was changed to black. Sometime in a later update, however, his hair was reverted back to its previous state. ↑ In Act Three , the party can speak with Raphael on the upper floor of Sharess' Caress , where Voss is pleading with him for the means to free Orpheus . If the player character chooses the conversation line, "What makes you think you'd succeed in using the Crown where Karsus couldn't?", Raphael indignantly replies, "I AM NO MORTAL. And I do not fail." ↑ In a conversation with Raphael and the player character at Sharess' Caress , when discussing the Crown of Karsus , certain dialogue choices result in Raphael revealing, "The archdevil Mephistopheles snatched up the Crown and squirreled it away in one of his vaults. He's naught more than a frigid archivist. So much power and potential kept inert. He made a miracle into a museum piece. I raged - but only for a decade or so - then I waited, ever watching, for more than a thousand years, for a mistake, a mishap, a misadventure. And these Chosen who have caused you so much trouble accidentally did me a favor. They brought the Crown back into play." ↑ 4.0 4.1 Haarlep's dialogue using Speak with Dead ↑ Mason's Log by Morfred ↑ Raphael in the Devil's Den ↑ When Raphael is met for the first time, before being transported to the House of Hope, it is possible to set the stage for early acquisition of his legendary and highly desirable Helldusk Armour early on for use in rest of the game. This guide explains how. ↑ Reports that Raphael can also appear along the Risen Road near Karlach or at the bridge leading into the Blighted Village from the east could not be replicated, and do not appear to be reflected in game files. ↑ Specifically seeking help from Nettie , Ethel , Gut , or Omeluum . ↑ If Lae'zel is otherwise recruited, the relevant flag "PLA_GithChokepoint_State_MonitorIntroRequirementMet" is not set. ↑ There is an additional flag marked as a potential trigger "GLO_Halsin_Quest_ToldAboutMoonrise" but it is marked as removed for being redundant. Presumably with "GLO_Halsin_Quest_AskedKilledLeaders". ↑ Which flags, if any, need to be set to trigger this encounter are unknown. Technical UID S_LOW_FireworksDare_Teen_01 UUID c110d443-6cb8-4541-9314-dab65ebfb648 Stats Tiefling_Child Rascal Borys is a tiefling child in the Steeps district of the Lower City in Act Three . “ I love the smell of fireworks. Reminds me of grandma's stories of home. „ — Rascal Borys Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Rascal Borys together with his human friend Dyrovell can be found on a stone-paved space in front of Felogyr's Fireworks shop. They are standing near the entrance to the fireworks shop. They are counting their pocket money, planning to buy a huge firework and throw it at some Flaming Fist guard or even a Steel Watcher . The idea seems to be their common interest, and now each is trying to persuade the other to do the actual mischief. However, both are lacking coin to obtain something they want. If spoken to, Rascal Borys expresses childish certainty that the dangers posed by fireworks are a fib concocted by adults "to make us not want to play with them". v t e Lower City v t e Characters in
