EQ_Shadowheart Shadowheart (born Jenevelle Hallowleaf) [ 2 ] is an Origin character and a recruitable companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. She is a high half-elf and a Trickery Domain Cleric with the Acolyte background. Shadowheart can be first found on the Nautiloid during the prologue where she serves as a temporary companion, and can be properly recruited at various points in Act One . As a loyal servant of the goddess Shar , Shadowheart can be cold and calculating, willing to do whatever is necessary to serve the Dark Lady with utter devotion. “ We're in this together, but I'll happily go it alone. My faith will keep me company. „ — Shadowheart 's strong devotion Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Personal quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Prologue 1.5.2 Act One 1.5.3 Leaving the party 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 1.8 Nightsong points 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Early life 3.2 Life as a Sharran 3.3 Hunting after the mysterious artefact 4 Involvement 4.1 Prologue 4.1.1 As an origin character 4.2 Act One 4.3 Act Two 4.4 Act Three 4.5 Endings 4.5.1 Adventures throughout the Sword Coast 4.5.2 Life at a country farmstead 4.5.3 Mother Superior of the Sharran cloister 5 Quest rewards 5.1 Rewards for slaying the Nightsong 5.2 Rewards for sparing the Nightsong and defeating Ketheric Thorm 6 Interactions 6.1 Companion interactions 6.1.1 Act One 6.1.2 Act Two 6.1.3 Act Three 6.2 Unique interactions 6.2.1 Act One 6.2.2 Act Two 6.2.3 Act Three 6.3 Speak with Dead 6.3.1 If she dies before being recruited 6.3.2 If she dies off-screen after a long rest 7 Related Literature 8 Related Quests 9 Loot 9.1 Starting equipment 10 Achievements 11 Gallery 12 Datamined content 13 Bugs 14 Notes and references 15 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] For a full overview of Shadowheart's starting features, see the articles Cleric , Trickery Domain and High Half-Elf . Background [ edit section | visual editor ] A devout follower of the Lady of Loss, Shadowheart is the sole survivor of a holy mission undertaken on the Mistress of the Night's behest. She alone is left to deliver a relic of immense power to her coven in Baldur's Gate while threatened by a strange new magic that is burgeoning from within. Her faith plays an important part in her story throughout the game, and she can be steered towards or away from it. Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before she is recruited, Shadowheart is a level 1 Cleric with the following Ability Scores : 12 STR, 13 DEX, 14 CON, 10 INT, 15 WIS, 8 CHA. If Shadowheart is recruited, she reverts to a level 1 Cleric of the Trickery Domain , with the standard ability scores for that subclass . This gives her access to Spellcasting – with a particular focus on Illusion magic – and Blessing of the Trickster , a class action that grants another creature advantage on Stealth checks. This makes her an ideal support character, albeit with few offensive options. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart has the passive Fear of Wolves : whenever a wolf approaches her, she must make a Wisdom saving throw or become Frightened . Shar , Shadowheart's goddess, plays an integral part in her story, and is far more involved in her life than the standard Cleric class experience. Shar's patronage grants Shadowheart resistance to mild exposure to the Shadow Curse in the Shadow-Cursed Lands , though she will still need protection in areas where the curse is strongest. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart's personal quest as companion is ⁠ Daughter of Darkness . As an origin her personal quest is ⁠ Daughter of Darkness (Origin) . Her personal quest spans all acts of the game. Throughout it, Shadowheart will uncover fragments of her shrouded history, re-examine her relationship with her goddess Shar and decide her own future: whether to remain in the dark embrace of the Lady of Loss or free herself from her past. Three further subquests are available that tie into her personal quest: ⁠ The Chosen of Shar , in which Shadowheart's faith is tested, ⁠ A Familiar Face , where parts of her past can come to light, and ⁠ Surrender Shadowheart , in which the party considers a treacherous proposition. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart can be recruited as a temporary companion during the Prologue on the Nautiloid by freeing her from the mind flayer pod; she can become a permanent companion during Act One . Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart is first encountered on the Nautiloid during the Prologue, trapped inside a mind flayer pod. She can be freed by interacting with the nearby console or as a Barbarian, using one of the dialogue options below: [BARBARIAN]  Grip the pod's lid and pull. [BERSERKER] [STRENGTH]  RIP THE POD OPEN.  (DC 10) [BARBARIAN] [STRENGTH]  Don't give up. Tear this thing open.  (DC 10) If she is freed, Shadowheart joins the party as a temporary companion. Upon escaping the nautiloid, she leaves the party. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart can be found a second time at the Ravaged Beach in the Wilderness . If freed from the pod during the Prologue, she is seen lying unconscious on the ground and wakes up if interacted with. If she is not freed, she can instead be found attempting to gain entry to the nearby Dank Crypt . Either way, she can be invited to join the party after speaking with her. If Shadowheart is not spoken with immediately at the Ravaged Beach, she moves to the Druid Grove on her own searching for a healer; she can be spoken with there and invited to join the party. If the party enter the Goblin Camp without recruiting Shadowheart, she shows up and saves the party from the Voice of the Absolute using the Mysterious Artefact . If she is not recruited then, she can be convinced to wait there, or fought to the death. If the party ignore the Goblin Camp and walk toward the Mountain Pass , Shadowheart shows up there and saves the party from the Voice as they attempt to cross the bridge into the main area. If the party ignore both the Goblin Camp and the Mountain Pass, and enter the Underdark without her, Shadowheart ultimately appears there and saves the party from the Voice of the Absolute as they enter the elevator to the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character enters the Shadowfell without her, offers her to Viconia DeVir in exchange for Sharran aid in fighting the Absolute, or kills her parents after rescuing them in Act Three , she permanently leaves the party. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Shadowheart/Approval Shadowheart Approves Shadowheart prefers finding pragmatic and efficient solutions to problems. Accordingly, she appreciates discretion, creativity, and open-mindedness. She generally responds well to acts of heroism. While Shadowheart is afraid of wolves, she loves animals and will always react favourably to positive interactions with them and negatively to cruelty towards them. As a devout Sharran, Shadowheart also approves of acts against Selûne and Selûnites in general. Shadowheart greatly values her privacy. She dislikes those who pry for details on her personal life, her faith or (should they learn of it) disapprove of her worship of Shar, as well as those who press for responses to questions she has already declined to answer. Shadowheart also has has a dry, witty, [ 3 ] cynical, and often biting sense of humor, which may soften somewhat towards the player character if she is romanced . A romanced Shadowheart teases a Selûnite player character with the promise of a kiss. She does not like needless cruelty or violence and can respond unfavourably to others being too open with untrustworthy or unknown individuals. Straying from Shar's mandates results in Shadowheart being punished through the wound in her right hand, a reminder to follow Shar's wishes. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Shadowheart/Romance Shadowheart can be romanced by characters of any gender, and is one of the few characters willing to have a casual relationship. Throughout it, she will have to deal with the topic of her identity and how the idea of love fits the Sharran concept of self-sacrifice for their goddess. If she is romanced by a Selûnite cleric, Shadowheart has unique dialogue and behavior options available. [ 4 ] Nightsong points [ edit section | visual editor ] Unlike other Companions, Shadowheart has a unique secondary approval system, influencing the choices in ⁠ Find the Nightsong and ⁠ Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic . For more information, see Nightsong Points . Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Lithe of frame, well dressed and with meticulously managed features, Shadowheart is not unattractive [ 5 ] [ 6 ] and may, if mentioning this to her (e.g., if romanced ), acknowledge this matter-of-factly. [ 7 ] She has straight, coal-black hair and a long, flowing ponytail fastened in segments by elaborately crafted silver loops. Her fringe hair is kept short and straight, revealing her brows beneath and a scar running from her nose to her right cheek. Hair adorns her face on the sides, reaching past her chin, her pointed ears barely peeking through them, and her eyes, light-green with speckles of yellow, are contoured by dark make-up. Though rarely seen, she has a black circular mark on her right hand, a wound given by Shar, causing Shadowheart pain whenever she engages in behavior the Lady of Sorrows disapproves of. Though appearing youthful due to her elven heritage, she is over 40 years old. [ 8 ] Shadowheart complements her Sharran attire with a silver circlet worn above her fringe. It is simple, yet elegant, displaying her goddess' holy symbol, a black disc, as well as an ornate argent hairpiece at the base of her ponytail, reminiscent of the decorations found in Sharran temples. After the events of ⁠ The Chosen of Shar , if Shadowheart turns away from Shar, she will dye her hair silver and part her fringe off-center, showing more of her forehead. If she remains faithful, however, she will maintain her black hair but part it nonetheless. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Zealously devoted, independent and headstrong, Shadowheart prefers pragmatic solutions to problems, decisive action in the face of uncertainty and remaining uninvolved in the affairs of others. While she initially seems guarded and reserved – hesitant to reveal information about herself – she is in fact amnesiac, with little memory of her own past. Fiercely devoted to Shar, she does not tolerate slights against her goddess, often reacting defensively. Trained in Sharran ways, she is also not above forceful, ruthless actions, duplicity or even killing in order to achieve her goals. Still, given her youngest years of upbringing, Shadowheart displays traits that are often at odds with her Sharran training. She has a fondness for flowers and animals, disapproves of indiscriminate violence, prefers relatively peaceful resolutions to conflicts when possible and often sympathizes with the plights of party members. She can be as sarcastic as Astarion and does not shy away from dark humour. She is introspective and often harbours doubts as can be seen by romancing her, and when guided away from Shar, she is much more open and honest with her feelings. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Early life [ edit section | visual editor ] A girl in the woods. Born to parents Arnell and Emmeline Hallowleaf , Jenevelle, as she was named, was raised in a Selûnite household in the forests outside Baldur's Gate . [ 9 ] Devout followers of the Moonmaiden, they worshipped her in quiet seclusion away from the city, raising young Jenevelle in the ways of Selûne. In time, she would take part of an ancient Selûnite initiation rite: abandoned in the wilds, she would have to rely on her skills and faith to fend for herself, proving herself as a devout believer once she returned. [ 10 ] Yet Shar , Selûne's dark sister, had other plans for the child and commanded Viconia DeVir (along with her cadre of Sharrans) to kidnap her, turn her to Shar, and groom her to replace Viconia as Mother Superior of Baldur's Gate. [ 11 ] Arnell had learned of the first part of this plan - the kidnapping ploy - after capturing a Sharran spy. Taking his wolf form, he then raced towards Jenevelle. But young Jenevelle never learned of her father's curse of lycanthropy, and instead of being rescued by her father, all she saw was a great wolf hunting her. [ 12 ] The Sharrans caught up to the pair and kidnapped both, taking them to a secret cloister of the Dark Lady in Baldur's Gate. Life as a Sharran [ edit section | visual editor ] Jenevelle was brought to the Cloister of Sombre Embrace , a Sharran temple in Baldur's Gate set up and run by Mother Superior Viconia DeVir after her previous endeavours in Waterdeep were ended. [ 13 ] Viconia then undertook Shar's command to mould young Jenevelle into a champion of the Dark Lady and her eventual successor as Mother Superior . At first Jenevelle resisted the indoctrination, but the brutal training she was put through, being lied to that her parents perished defending her from wolves, as well as repeated forced use of the temple's Mirror of Loss , slowly erased her past and in time forged her new identity as Shadowheart. Her conversion to Shar ultimately took almost half a century. [ 14 ] The Mother Superior was especially cruel with Shadowheart, forcing her to use the Mirror of Loss more than any other acolyte. Under Viconia's watchful eye and no longer recognizing her parents, Shadowheart was forced to repeatedly torture and practice her newfound skills on them. [ 15 ] Still, Shadowheart was able to retain a few memories from her past thanks to Rennald, a young Tiefling acolyte undergoing similar training. Any time she was subjected to mirror training, he did his best to remind Shadowheart who she was afterwards. [ 16 ] Thanks to him, and whatever scattered notes Shadowheart was able to jot down between mirror trainings, [ 17 ] Shadowheart was able to retain some parts of her own identity, such as her fondness for flowers and animals. The two became good friends, and one of the few blessings during Shadowheart's time in the cloister. Hunting after the mysterious artefact [ edit section | visual editor ] At some point during Shadowheart's last stages of training, whispers of the rise of a mysterious cult reached the Mother Superior's ears. This Cult of the Absolute as it was being called, was quickly gaining traction among the populace and threatened Sharran influence over the city. [ 18 ] As luck would have it, the Sharrans captured a Githyanki scout who, [ 19 ] after being subjected to merciless torture, revealed the existence of a githyanki artefact of immense power such that the cult became desperate to find, lest it be used against them. [ 20 ] Such an artefact could prove an asset for the Sharrans in thwarting the absolutist presence in the city, so the Mother Superior quickly formed a party of elite devouts, tasking them with its retrieval. [ 21 ] Though deemed a suicide mission, Shadowheart and four other companions set out to fulfil what they believed were Shar's commands. The group was able to locate the Mysterious Artefact though at great cost: Shadowheart was the only survivor. [ 22 ] Disaster would not stop there, however, as she soon found herself captive at the hands of Mind Flayers . How and where she was captured is never explored, however, and at some point during her capture she was tadpoled and imprisoned in a pod, awaiting Ceremorphosis . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart's personal quest is ⁠ Daughter of Darkness . It is added to the journal upon recruiting her and spans all three acts of the game. Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart is typically first encountered during the battle aboard the Nautiloid . Trapped in a mind flayer pod, the party can decide whether to free her or not. If she is released, she joins the party as a temporary companion until they escape the ship. As an origin character [ edit section | visual editor ] As an origin character, Shadowheart wakes up in the pod where all player characters start. The artifact is on the floor nearby, and she is prompted to pick it up and bring it to Baldur's Gate. There is no one in the pod where Shadowheart is usually found. On the Ravaged Beach, Shadowheart is the only one present. As a result, there are only two intellect devourers to fight, rather than the usual three, but it can be a significantly more difficult fight if other companions are not recruited first. The fight can be bypassed by climbing rocks on the right of the location where the intellect devourers are found. If she returns later with at least one other party member, then there will be three intellect devourers. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart explains her dream of becoming a Dark Justiciar. During the first act of the game, the mystery of the artefact Shadowheart carries is slowly uncovered, as well as the mission that led her to find it. Shadowheart eventually reveals she is a devout of Shar and her mission to deliver the artefact to her cloister in Baldur's Gate. She also reveals that, as part of the operation, she had her memories suppressed so she would not betray Shar, who exerts her influence over her through the wound in Shadowheart's hand. As the party approach the Mountain Pass the first time, they can encounter Kith'rak Voss , who informs them the githyanki are searching for an object very similar to Shadowheart's artefact. Whatever the outcome of this encounter, Lae'zel confronts Shadowheart about the artefact later in camp. As a result, Shadowheart judges Lae'zel a critical threat to her mission and attempts to kill her in her sleep the next long rest , though she can be convinced to desist and put grudges aside. Shadowheart may also slowly reveal parts of her past. Upon an encounter with wolves, if she is asked about her apparent fear of them, she may, depending on player approval, show a memory of her younger self being saved from a wolf attack by Sharrans. Similarly, if she is given the Noblestalk from the Underdark , Shadowheart remembers a young tiefling boy named Rennald, who she was friends with during her initiate years and who she thinks may still be in Baldur's Gate. [ 23 ] This adds the quest ⁠ A Familiar Face to the journal. Should the party learn about Dark Justiciars , Shadowheart, if asked more about them, states that they are elite warriors of Shar and that she dreams of becoming one some day. This adds the quest ⁠ The Chosen of Shar to the journal. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart can become defensive when asked about her resistance to the Shadow Curse. Upon first arriving in the Shadow-Cursed Lands the next conversation with Shadowheart has her comment on how the Shadow Curse does not seem to affect her as much as others and that she must be blessed by Shar. She can be challenged or supported about this and, regardless of how she is approached, comments on how this protection must have been granted for a reason and that she needs to be on the lookout for any place dedicated to Shar. Having high approval with Shadowheart lets her at some point reveal that one of her favourite flowers is the Night Orchid . One such flower can be found in the Ruined Battlefield in the Shadow-Cursed Lands and given to her. If one is given to her, Shadowheart expresses her gratitude and laments not having anything to give in return. Within the Grand Mausoleum the party finds the Gauntlet of Shar , ancient proving grounds for Dark Justiciar aspirants. Shadowheart expresses excitement about the possibility of proving herself to her goddess, and urges the party to complete the trials and allow her to become a Dark Justiciar. Completing the trials leads the party to the Shadowfell and the confrontation with the Nightsong . Shadowheart's fate greatly diverges depending on the choices made here. If Shadowheart is allowed to slay the Nightsong, Shar is greatly pleased with her, and finally names her Dark Justiciar, granting her powerful rewards. Shadowheart is elated she has finally achieved her dream, and vows to serve Shar faithfully until death. Alternatively, Shadowheart can be convinced to spare the Nightsong, thereby abandoning Shar to forge her own future. In doing so, the Nightsong is freed and Shadowheart is abandoned by her goddess. Finally, if the party choose to not bring Shadowheart to the Shadowfell or surrender the Nightsong to Balthazar , Shadowheart becomes furious and either attacks or permanently leaves the party. Either of these outcomes completes ⁠ The Chosen of Shar . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] “ Loss is a gift, girl. Do you still not understand that? „ — Mother Superior to Shadowheart If Shadowheart remains in the party, whether commanded by Shar as a Dark Justiciar, or guided by Aylin , her next destination is the Cloister of Sombre Embrace in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate. A Dark Justiciar Shadowheart is commanded by Shar to cleanse the cloister from corruption, while a Shadowheart who freed Aylin and turned against Shar is spurred by the hope she may find her parents alive there. There, Shadowheart encounters Viconia DeVir , the cloister's Mother Superior who saw to her training as an initiate. Viconia demands the mysterious artefact and the surrender of Shadowheart. Once more, Shadowheart's fate can go different ways depending on choices made. The party can agree to surrender Shadowheart to Viconia, losing her as a companion but gaining the Sharrans as allies for the final battle. Hearing Viconia's offer out begins the subquest ⁠ Surrender Shadowheart to Viconia . Alternatively, the party can confront Viconia and the Sharrans, resulting in their demise. If Shadowheart is surrendered to Viconia, the main quest (and corresponding subquest) is completed. While exploring the cloister, the party may run into Nocturne , a tiefling who recognises Shadowheart. If Shadowheart recovered some of her memories by eating noblestalk, she realises Nocturne is the young tiefling friend from her past, now a transgender woman. Shadowheart and Nocturne then reminisce about growing up in the cloister, and this encounter completes ⁠ A Familiar Face . If Viconia is refused and defeated, the party can enter the Threshold of Loss, Shar's hidden sanctum. There, Shadowheart comes face to face with her parents, long thought dead. Shar's ultimate test for a Dark Justiciar requires her to slay them. In doing so, Shar blesses Shadowheart, wiping her memory and tasking her with rebuilding the cloister. Shar's faithful become available as ⁠ allies for the final battle . If she abandoned Shar, Shadowheart has a difficult choice to make: save her parents but be forever bound to Shar's curse, or sacrifice her parents and sever the curse at last. Either choice completes ⁠ Daughter of Darkness . [ 24 ] During the party's next long rest, Shadowheart is found waiting for the player character at a statue of Selûne. Shadowheart is in tears, overcome by grief and shame. If Shadowheart turned from Shar in Act Two or saved her parents as a Dark Justiciar, she reflects on her feelings now that she truly knows who she is. If her parents are alive, she worries they will not be able to look her in the eye after the tortures she put them through. If her parents are dead, she is overwhelmed by her first feelings of true loss and laments the loss of her younger self since there is no one left to remember her. She breaks down crying for a while, possibly in the arms of the player character (if they select " Embrace her "), or her parents if they are alive. After calming down, she ultimately decides to keep and reclaim the name Shadowheart for herself, stating, "You can't cast a shadow without some light." If Shadowheart as an origin character saved her parents, her mother, Emmeline Hallowleaf , says this line instead to show her support of the decision. Otherwise, if Shadowheart remained a Dark Justiciar, overthrew Viconia, and killed her parents, she mocks Selûne and vandalizes the statue, covering it in Aylin's blood. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] Adventures throughout the Sword Coast [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart during the epilogue If Shadowheart turned from Shar and lost her parents in the process, she embarks on adventures throughout the Sword Coast , visiting the House of the Moon in Waterdeep , battling Sharran assassins and even befriending an Imp named Bing Bong . Though she travels alone (unless romanced), Shadowheart appears to be happy with her new life; she also says that she still feels the presence of her parents in their moonmotes and looks forward to reuniting with them when she dies. Life at a country farmstead [ edit section | visual editor ] If she turned from Shar and rescued her parents, Shadowheart moves to a country farmstead to live surrounded by flowers, pets [ 25 ] and family. There, she is finally able to live the life she wanted, surrounded by love. If Shadowheart is romanced, the player character lives with her and her family, a quiet life after adventures. From time to time Shar inflicts pain on Shadowheart through the wound on her hand but, now at peace and surrounded by those she loves, she no longer minds and notices those events becoming more infrequent as of late. Mother Superior of the Sharran cloister [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart as the Mother Superior during the epilogue If Shadowheart chooses to remain in Shar's embrace, she becomes the new Mother Superior of the Sharran cloister in Baldur's Gate, operating from the House of Grief. In the months since, word of the Lady of Loss has spread far and wide, thanks to the efforts of Shadowheart. If romanced, Shadowheart ends the relationship prior to this, explaining that she needs to be fully devoted to her goddess. She agrees to be kissed for old times' sake, but remains faithful to Shar. Shadowheart also expresses sympathy for Viconia's fate, now able to understand what she went through as Mother Superior. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Rewards for slaying the Nightsong [ edit section | visual editor ] As part of the quests ⁠ Find the Nightsong and ⁠ The Chosen of Shar Dark Justiciar Boots Dark Justiciar Gauntlets Dark Justiciar Half-Plate Shar's Spear of Evening Rewards for sparing the Nightsong and defeating Ketheric Thorm [ edit section | visual editor ] As part of the quests ⁠ Find the Nightsong , ⁠ The Chosen of Shar , and ⁠ Infiltrate Moonrise Towers Moonlight Glaive Selûne's Spear of Night Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart has unique dialogue interactions as a companion available after certain events. Whenever one is available, she will have a floating [ ! ] icon above her. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Shadowheart abandons Shar and spares the Nightsong, upon taking the portal out from the Shadowfell Shar will keep Shadowheart hostage for a time before releasing her. The party can ask what kept her; she will explain Shar wanted to punish her and make sure she knew she was forsaken henceforth. Choosing Shadowheart as an origin is the only way in which players can watch the punishment directly. Shar insults her and inflicts so much pain in her hand that she falls unconscious before being thrown out of the Shadowfell, where she eventually wakes up as she would in other origins. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Unique interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Either as an origin , or in the party as a companion , Shadowheart has unique interactions and special dialogue with the following characters, listed by the act they are first encountered in. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Isobel Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Ferg Drogher Mirie Viconia DeVir Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] If she dies before being recruited [ edit section | visual editor ] Who are you? Shadowheart Shadowheart... What happened to you? Shadowheart Returned. Punished. My mission failed... What was your purpose? Shadowheart To serve. To repent. Do you remember me? Shadowheart No... What is your dream? Shadowheart To serve Lady Shar... What happened to you? Shadowheart The artefact... I felt it burn... The artefact burned? What do you mean? Shadowheart I felt it. It didn't want to stay with me... I failed... If she dies off-screen after a long rest [ edit section | visual editor ] What is your profession? Shadowheart Cleric... A cleric? Who do you worship? Shadowheart It is forbidden What is the artefact you had? Shadowheart A secret. My mission. Must keep it safe... What was your mission? Shadowheart Protect the artefact. Deliver to Baldur's Gate... How do I get rid of the artefact? Shadowheart Cannot. Must not. Too important... Where are you from? Shadowheart Baldur's Gate... Where do you keep your valuables? Shadowheart On me. Always in reach... Starting equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Alchemy Pouch Camp Supply Sack Circlet Keychain Leather Boots Mace Potion of Healing x2 Shadowheart's Chain Shirt Shadowheart's Clothes Shadowheart's Tasteful Boots Shadowheart's Underwear Scroll of Detect Thoughts Scroll of Revivify Studded Shield Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] To Bloom in Darkest Night Gift Shadowheart a night orchid - her favourite flower. Always knew she was a softie. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Camp clothing model Underwear model Early Access model Epilogue model Mother Superior model Digital Artbook concept Promotional art Steam Trading Card Appearence pre-release Digital Artbook early face concepts Shadowheart on the cover of Baldur's Gate III soundtrack Datamined content [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Shadowheart/Cut content Shadowheart had at some point in development a vastly different backstory and storyline that was completely revamped prior to the game's release. This previous version of Shadowheart had a high elven mother named Eliriana and a human father named Sebastian and had been acquainted with a Mother Superior (different from Viconia DeVir ), a Sister Superior , and a Sharran torturer . Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] After rejecting Shar, the hair on Shadowheart's model turns white, but the hair color on her portrait and in the initiative tracker remains black. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 26 ] ↑ In the Early Access version her background was Urchin . ↑ According to performance director Aliona Baronova, the name "Jenevelle" was selected by Shadowheart's writer John Corcoran as a deliberate reference to actress Jennifer English: ⁠ Shadowheart's Actor and Director Take a Shadowheart Quiz  – FallDamage ↑ In Act Two , in the foyer of Moonrise Towers , just east of the stairs leading from the main door, is a ladder which can be used to access the rafters. If passed, Shadowheart remarks in double entendre, "Careful, in future - you can't just stick your hand in every strange hole you come across." ↑ After being given the Idol of Shar by the player character romancing as a Selûnite cleric, and being challenged to "Kiss me like you hate me" , one of Shadowheart's possible responses includes teasing the player character with the promise of a kiss as she slowly circles them from behind, kissing them a few times on their backside, before finally sharing a passionate kiss face-to-face. ↑ In Act One , in the evening before long resting at camp, when Astarion laments over not being able to see his reflection, the player character can compliment aspects of his appearance. Just tell me I'm beautiful and we can call it a day." The player character can then reply, "You're fine. But you're sweet to notice." ↑ Cloister of Sombre Embrace , ambient line spoken by Shadowheart upon reading No Price Too High in the dormitory. However, it is difficult to confirm as different sources in-game indicate that the village was destroyed over a hundred years ago by Ketheric Thorm's dark justiciar army, and Shadowheart is estimated to be roughly fifty years old. Conflicting timelines regarding the village and its destruction do not line up, thus, it is possible the intent during development was that she and her family had indeed lived in Moonhaven, but the inconsistencies were never properly fixed for release. EQP_Spear_Chainmail_Shield_HelmetMetal_Fist Trs. BG_Guard Fist Shah is a dwarven fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is in Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . “ They just keep coming. Send them to Amn, make them Athkatla's problem. „ — Shah , talking to Elin Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Shah is stationed together with Fist Gai , Blaze Elin and three Steel Watchers at the bridge leading from Wyrm's Crossing into Wyrm's Rock Fortress . They guard the entrance and prevent anyone from going into the fortress (and, by extension, the Lower City of Baldur's Gate ) except those who have sufficient reason to pass. Shah is reluctant to discuss anything with the party, sending them to Elin to try to obtain permission to pass. After gaining access to Wyrm’s Rock Fortress (by any method or path), Shah treats the party as citizens eligible to cross their checkpoint in any direction. This tin toy may decide to go off duty, but we still have a job to do. „ — Shargil , after the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Shargil is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Larche , Fist Nephel and a Steel Watcher . They can be found near the Stormshore Armoury at X: -44 Y: -101 , guarding Courier Hara , Moorino and Burzenberg , who are being "evaluated" by the Steel Watcher. If spoken with, Chargil tells the player character that they are "rooting out disloyal elements" among the citizenry. After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Shargil remains at the same place, concluding that their duties are same with or without the Watcher's company. After a long rest, she disappears from the game along with her mates and all "evaluated" citizens. Technical UID S_LOW_BaldursMouth_Cynics_000 UUID 4bee2c69-6b73-4cec-bc58-ad2fd18ceb1e Stats Elf_Commoner Sharlz Molar is an exasperated reader of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette who appears in Act Three . “ What you staring at, pal? You dropping eaves? Get gone. „ — Sharlz Molar Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Sharlz Molar and Iza Blouin are in Baldur's Gate next to the Lower City waypoint at X: -50 Y: -55 . Like many Baldurians, Sharlz and Iza are concerned about the state of the city, but neither are assured in the gazette's reporting of actual issues. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Sharlz Molar Gazette has a transcript of a conversation with Archduke Gortash . Iza Blouin What's he got to say for himself? Sharlz Molar Lots of talk about the brilliant future of Baldur's Gate, city of steel and justice. Iza Blouin Does he say anything about the horrible present of Baldur's Gate, city of crime and chaos? Sharlz Molar No. He mostly avoids that topic. Iza Blouin Huh. Now that's something you don't see in the Mouth every day.  (If the Gazette publishes a positive article on the party) Sharlz Molar What's in this edition? More Absolute scaremongering? Iza Blouin A positive headline. About a group of adventurers, no less. Sharlz Molar Adventurers, necromancers, cults... Where's the reporting on real things? How do 'adventurers' help us normal folk? Not one bloody bit, that's how. Iza Blouin Adventurers aid Absolute ... Reckon there's any truth to that?  (If the Gazette publishes a negative article on the party) Sharlz Molar Truth? In the Baldur's Mouth Gazette? Iza Blouin The Gazette can't be wrong all the time. Adventurers are basically mercenaries. Stands to reason some of them would side with a mad cult if it paid well enough. Sharlz Molar What difference does it make? Cults come and go, and so do adventurers. The Gazette never prints anything that'll affect us regular folk. S'all a distraction. Iza Blouin Gods, you'd hink the late Lord Gortash was a saint the way the Gazette goes on about him.  (If Enver Gortash is killed) Sharlz Molar Yeah, they've really made a meal out of the 'Death of Gortash' stuff. Iza Blouin Won't tell us how Gortash died though, will they? Classic Baldur's Mouth. Sharlz Molar Shoddy journalism indeed.

Two friendly Sharran Fidelians are summoned by using Gather Your Allies: Nightbringer's Shadow Adepts . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] The Sharran Fidelians summoned with Nightbringer's Shadow Adepts are permanently affected by Bless , Protection from Energy: Fire , and Protection from Evil and Good . They are otherwise identical to those found in the cloister. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Beckoning Darkness ( ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Necrotic Curse a creature to be haunted by darkness. It takes 2d8 Necrotic damage if it enters or starts its turn in a Lightly or Heavily Obscured area. CHA Save Range: 4 m (13 ft) Bone Chill ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Necrotic Prevent the target from healing until your next turn. The target cannot help Downed characters. An undead target receives Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Darkness ( + ) Create a cloud of magical darkness that Heavily Obscures and inflicts Blind to creatures within. Creatures cannot make ranged attacks into or out of it. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Shadow Step ( ) Teleport from shadow to shadow. Afterwards, you have Advantage on your next melee Attack Roll . Technical Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Melee Variant 1 Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Melee_Human Variant 2 Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Melee_Elf Variant 3 Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Melee_Dwarf Variant 4 Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Melee_Gnome Variant 5 Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Cultist_Melee_Halfling Sharran Novice is the title given to initiate followers of Shar . “ *First you took apples from stalls, then gold from purses. Once, you even lifted a necklace right off a matron's throat. The other novices were in awe of you.* „ — Shadowheart regaining memories of her time as a Sharran novice Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Eight Sharran novices are in the Cloister of Sombre Embrace during the encounter with Viconia DeVir . If the party sides with Viconia or if Shadowheart takes command of the cloister, the party gains the Sharrans as allies during the final fight. This grants the ability Nightbringer's Shadow Adepts which summons two Sharran novices and two Sharran Fidelians during the final confrontation . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Sharran novices are basic, low-level fighters who cannot use any actions beside the standard set of Dash , Jump , and Main Hand Attack . However, they can still be dangerous due to their passive Shadow Ambush combined with Sharran Fidelians casting Darkness on the party. The novices summoned with Nightbringer's Shadow Adepts are permanently blessed , have Protection from Energy: Fire , and Protection from Evil and Good . Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Mace Damage: 3~8 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. UND_Duergar_Generic Shattered Duergar is a dead character whose corpse is on the beach area of the Underdark during Act One . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] The duergar's corpse is near the Decrepit Village at X: 11 Y: -198 . He was hunting the slave Thulla who stole Nere's boots but unfortunately met his end thanks to the Myconids who caused him to kill himself. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] The shattered duergar can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Shattered Duergar Hunter... reaver... warrior of... the Absolute... What happened to you? Shattered Duergar Myconids... made me... hurt myself... Did you have anything valuable? Shattered Duergar Me... no. Gnomes... were fiddling... with rubble... yonder. Where did you come from? Shattered Duergar Across... the... Ebonlake... What were you doing when you died? Shattered Duergar Hunting... runaway slave... What was your profession? Technical UID S_WYR_SentientAmulet_Zombie_Shirra UUID cc15a9d4-b600-4e82-b981-3a0038a62c6c Stats WYR_SentientAmulet_Zombie_Shirra Trs. WYR_OpenHand_Sarcophagus Sister Shirra Clarwen is the dead granddaughter of the Monk's Manifestation and follower of Ilmater , who lived in the Open Hand Temple in Rivington . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon reaching the Open Hand Temple , it is revealed that Shirra died the previous year, the year 1491 DR. Shirra was a sister and one of the trained deadspeakers at the Open Hand Temple. She was to endure the mania of her grandfather, the cursed monk of the Sentient Amulet , as was Ilmater's wont. Her corpse is in the crypt beneath the temple, accessed through a hatch in the kitchen. Shirra's corpse is inside the farthest sarcophagus on the left when entering the crypt. Inside is an inanimate zombie, now but a husk, her spirit having already departed. LOW_CountingHouse_BhaalCultist Reaper of Bhaal Shrev is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , in the High Security Vaults in the Counting House in the Lower City . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the ⁠ The High Harper quest, the party can go to the Counting House in hopes of catching up to Minsc. Inside the vaults, the party witnesses Minsc emerge from a Mimic and defeat it. 'Jaheira' then appears with a handful of Bhaalists including Shrev, and teleports away with Minsc, leaving the cultists to attack the party and the staff. Technical UID S_LOW_Client_002 UUID 91a348f4-a6a4-423d-8f3c-c48ceeb7383d Stats Dwarf_Commoner Shuna Huanje is a dwarven customer of the Sorcerous Sundries shop in the Lower City in Act Three . “ Have you seen how much the prices have risen? Might as well be throwing my gold straight into the lava elemental! „ — Shuna Huanje Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Shuna Huanje and her partner Lester Farrower are looking at shelves and a table full of alchemical ingredients. She and Lester are both stress buying, as supplies of certain ingredients appear to be running low. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Lester Farrower Gods, the shelves are practically picked bare. Shuna Huanje Some people are so selfish. Lester Farrower Bloodstaunch, jewelweed, mothersleaf - all gone. Typical. Lester Farrower Not everyone can just wave their hands and be healed. Why aren't they rationing anything? Shuna Huanje Gold. It's all about profits, my love. Lester Farrower It certainly is at that - but what'll we do in the meantime? Lester Farrower We really should've planted that herb garden, you know. Shuna Huanje Ah, well, it's too late for that now, isn't it, dear? Shuna Huanje We might have a bit of that catnip decoction left - as long as Lord Pawtash hasn't gotten into it. Lester Farrower I really wish you hadn't called the cat that. It feels a little... improper? Shuna Huanje Impropriety's the least of our worries with that mad cult on our doorstep. Lester Farrower I just think we should be careful what we say in public, is all. Lester Farrower So what do we have? Shuna Huanje Weavemoss... mugwort... incense... Shuna Huanje Six handfuls of assorted mushrooms. You can never have too many mushrooms. Lester Farrower Perhaps we ought to ask what they have in the back? If anything... Shuna Huanje I don't think it'd hurt - they'll probably have even less tomorrow. Lester Farrower Madness. Utter madness. Technical UID S_COL_TadpolingCentre_Manip UUID 6e52b75e-4e1d-46d7-b324-f08551475960 Stats COL_TadpolingCenter_Prisoner_HalfOrc_Caster Manip Shuurga is a half-orc wizard and an officer of the Flaming Fist. She can be encountered in the Mind Flayer Colony in Act Two . “ Hurr, what a stench. I'm beginning to think I should have stayed in that pod. In there it only smelled like me. „ — Shuurga , after being freed from the pod Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] In the end of the Act Two , Shuurga can be found in the Mind Flayer Colony , imprisoned in a pod within the Tadpoling Centre . Upon interacting with the Neural Apparatus controlling the pods, it is revealed that Shuurga has been captured and consigned to the future transformation, but is still not tadpoled (as well as Zevlor and Gauntlet Yeva in other pods around the room). Choosing to release Shuurga and other pod captives immediately leads to a battle with several victims already transformed into Mind Flayers and all Intellect Devourers that spot the fight. Provided she survives, Shuurga expresses the strongest concern about Duke Ravengard , whom she obviously came here to rescue. Afterwards, she presumably escapes the colony with Zevlor and Yeva, and is never met again throughout the game (as well as anywhere before exploring the colony). Shuurga is presumably the Manip that Counsellor Florrick ordered Gauntlet Yeva to report to for reinforcements in order to rescue Ravengard. The only other plausible alternative is Manip Vidor , who remains at Florrick's side throughout her presence in Shadow-Cursed Lands . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Dagger Damage: 3~6 1d4 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Dagger Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Shuurga has none of the racial features that come with being a half-orc. Also, her portrait is special in how it has a unique pose that is not found in any other half-orc portrait in the game. ↑ Despite being a wizard, having a caster archetype, and eight level's worth of spell slots, Shuurga has no spells or cantrips to cast and thus is forced to fight with melee. She also is mechanically naked and wears no armour; the Flaming Fist chain mail that she wears is purely cosmetic. v t e Mind Flayer Colony Characters Apostle of Myrkul Balthazar Chop Gortash Hairy Henry Ironfinger Ketheric Thorm Kressa Bonedaughter Maghtew Budj Mizora Nimias Orin Slack-Skinned Head The Netherbrain Ulder Ravengard Us Yeva Zevlor Zombie Dror Ragzlin Zombie Minthara Zombie Wulbren Creatures Death Shepherd Greater Zombie Reconstituted Arcanist Winged Horror Zombie Locations Barracks Morgue Necrotic Laboratory Tadpoling Centre Quests Defeat Ketheric Thorm Find Mol Find Zevlor Lift the Shadow Curse The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke The Wizard of Waterdeep

Technical UID S_LOW_BlushingMermaid_Patron_01 UUID 4e7b519f-3e47-45d7-b2d1-20001a522bfe Stats Dwarf_Commoner Siggy is a gold dwarf in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Mate, you'd be late to your own funeral. Look, skip the date, and I'll take you out next time we port, all right? „ — Siggy , to Svend Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Siggy is in the Blushing Mermaid in the Lower City attempting to convince Svend to skip his date because their ship leaves port at first light. Svend insists he will return on time, despite the recent dangers in the city. A party member can interact with them to convince Svend to go on his date or stay with Siggy. A passive DC 15 Insight Check reveals that Siggy has more feelings for Svend than just those of a friend. Passing a DC 7 Persuasion Check convinces Svend to stay and grants the ⁠ Playing Sune inspiration to party members with the Entertainer background. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Siggy You know the captain won't wait for you, right? Svend Yes, I have sailed with him before. Many times. Siggy Just be sure you're back before dawn. Svend Yeah, yeah. Svend Stop worrying. Siggy I'm not! Svend Yes you are - that's your worried face. After Svend is convinced to cancel his date and stay inside the Mermaid, the banter between him and Siggy changes. Svend Are you sure you don't want another drink? Siggy Only if you're buying. Svend You know there might be room in the hammock tonight for two? Siggy I'm sure the cook would be happy to share with you - so long as you like the smell of ham. Svend You wound me! Siggy So do you every time you speak. Now finish your drink. v t e The Blushing Mermaid Characters Other Auntie Ethel Chalara Mask of Servitude Mask of Terror Mask of Vengeance Nesha Leesha Vanra Wrint Sprigley Patrons Angevin Troy Bleeri Bortun Dickon Grimbus Gurira Madalitso Merri Fairweather Nafula Oaknuzzle Siggy Slog Svend Syllabub Fran Taslim Tongs Stoneheart Tud Whetstone Verryn Vin Dorgo Zena Redcaps Bert Adams Blunder Bob Flaming Pete Maggoty Jim Silas Silvertongue Two-Toes Rischer Staff Bruno Indomicus Captain Grisly Traders Gannet Locations Basement Quests Impress the Murder Tribunal Save Vanra

Technical UID S_LOW_FireworksHouse_BaniteGuard01 UUID cb956cc3-0e77-4a2b-8500-7a37486348b4 Stats Human_Cultist_Bane_Fist Feloguard Sigurd is a human who can be encountered in the Felogyr's Fireworks workshop in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate , in Act Three of the game, while following through the quest ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Feloguard Sigurd can be found on the ground floor of Felogyr's Fireworks . He guards the Reinforced Metal Door inside the pyrotechnics shop, that leads to the first and second floors of the building. The term "feloguard" is unique, it cannot be found elsewhere in the game. It corresponds with the name of the establishment. However, Sigurd himself has stats and most abilities of another type of Bane followers - a Fist of Bane . While going through the quest, the party may obtain a password to get onto the first floor of the Felogyr's Fireworks . Sigurd, alongside with the Felogyr's shopkeeper Avery Sonshal , may accept the password and let the party proceed upstairs. As the ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys quest cannot be ultimately resolved in a peaceful way, Sigurd joins the fight as soon as he notices any ill commotion, siding with the followers of Bane, who reside on the second floor of the building. He might remain at the ground floor of run up the stairs, and attack the party along with other Felogyr's employees. Technical UID S_WYR_South_Guard_003 UUID e93fa1a6-9999-45a9-9a91-3e7dc00908c1 Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Eqp. EQP_Halberd_Chainmail_HelmetMetal Trs. BG_Guard Fist Silena is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is in Rivington in Act Three . “ Orders are orders. We've got ours, you've got yours. I need you to step back. „ — Silena Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Silena is stationed together with Fist Kepso and Fist Wearne just outside the South Span Checkpoint , charged with resolving local complaints. They form the first line of guard, preventing refugees from entering Baldur's Gate through Wyrm's Crossing . Silena and Kepso are arguing with Noira Crysst and Horus Crysst , who fruitlessly beg to let them in. Like most other Fists at the checkpoint, Silena resents the presence of refugees, but occasionally tries to somewhat soften Kepso's harsh words. Noira Crysst There must be something - Fist Silena I said step back. Horus Crysst Please. My son - he's only a boy. You must understand - Fist Silena Sir. Sir. We can't let you in. Horus Crysst I - I thought we'd be safe in the Gate. I heard the stories. Fist Kepso Wail all you want - we've got enough mouths to feed. We don't need your kind. Horus Crysst Our - our kind? If he could just - Fist Kepso We have the Duke's full support. For the good of the people. DEN_Thieflings_Pickpocket Silfy is a tiefling child in Act One . She assists her brother Mattis in his scams for Mol's gang of tiefling refugee children through pickpocketing passersby. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Silfy is standing near her brother Mattis pretending to be his guard. If the talking party member steals Mattis' ring and then tries to buy something from Mattis, Silfy tries to steal back the 'magic' ring as well as some of the talking party member's belongings when looking at his wares. The talking party member can catch Silfy in the act if a passive Perception check is passed. If failed, another passive Perception check triggers, which, if passed, starts the quest ⁠ Find Your Belongings . If Silfy is caught stealing, the party can confront her, and optionally shake her down to recover their belongings. Otherwise, the party can question her if she saw anything suspicious as a guard. If Silfy is successfully intimidated, she gives away Mol's name and threatens to call her but realizes that this would be a mistake. She then runs away through the rocky crevice into the Tiefling Hideout . If the party travel to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before resolving Kagha's ritual the Rite of Thorns , the tieflings are expelled from the Emerald Grove and Silfy's murdered corpse is among the bodies of all the other refugees near the bridge to the Blighted Village . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Silfy moves next to the Heapside Strand Waypoint at X: 20 Y: -138 , selling the Baldur's Mouth gazette . If the party speak to her for the first time here, she timidly tries to sell them a copy. Over time (through long rests), she tries more charismatically, prompting the player character the option to remark her that her sales technique is improving. If this option is chosen, she credits the party for her newly found courage. Technical UID S_WYR_CeremonyRoom_Patriar_005 UUID 97631bfb-69f6-41ff-9f12-a76a0b6da398 Stats Human_Commoner Lady Silifrey Sashenstar is a Lady of Baldur's Gate who is present for the ordination of Gortash's as the Archduke of the city. “ What are they thinking, giving a fellow like that such power? I give him a year at most. „ — Silifrey Sashenstar , misjudging Gortash's lifeline at his coronation Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony she sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lady Silifrey moves to the northern nave of the Audience Hall and stands near the first table with refreshments. If spoken to, this elderly woman turns out to be virtually the only guest who doubts that Gortash will be able to keep the reins for more than a year. She also resents the other patriars who agreed to give him power. If the party choose to confront Gortash, the party can later find Lady Silifrey along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the Audience hall. According to research of the Black Hand of Loyalty , Lady Silifrey Sashenstar is one of the nobles who may easily fall in line with the cult via bribery, blackmail, or direct threats. [ 1 ] In retrospect, it is eventually revealed that this particular aspect of their research was not entirely correct. Technical UID S_TWN_Hospital_Reception_Receptionist UUID 3baf6794-2c83-4bd3-b2dd-70b4a9f98503 Stats Surgeon_Nurse Sister Sinda is an Undead Nurse who works at the House of Healing during Act Two . “ Here to see the doctor? Are we poorly? Are we desperately poorly? Not so well. But well enough to wait. Join the line, and you will be seen. „ — Sinda , tending to the non-existent line at the House of Healing Contents 1 Involvement 1.1 Act Two 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Loot 3 Related literature 4 External links Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Sister Sinda tends the front desk of the House of Healing, and addresses the party when they enter. She notes the party as "poorly", but well enough to wait in a line that does not exist. The party can convince her that their malady is important enough to be tended to by passing a check: I don't have time to wait - I need to see the doctor right now. [CLERIC] [DECEPTION]  I'm not a patient - I've been hired as a new healer. (DC 16  ) [MONK] [DECEPTION]  I am no patient - I've been hired as a spiritual advisor. (DC 16  ) [WIZARD] [DECEPTION]  I am no patient - I've just been hired as an expert in maladaptive necromantic malaise. (DC 16  ) [ROGUE] [DECEPTION]  I'm no patient, your surgeon heard I have the steadiest hand this side of Faerûn. (DC 16  ) [DECEPTION]  I'm not a patient - I'm the doctor's new assistant. (DC 16) [ROGUE] [PERFORMANCE]  Mimic the symptoms of Assassin's Blood, a well-known poison.  (DC 16  ) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  Feign the symptoms of a disease most terrible.  (DC 16  ) [DECEPTION]  Pretend to be ill.  (DC 16) [PERSUASION]  Wait! My wounds may not be visible on the outside, but I still need help. (DC 16) [RANGER] [PERSUASION]  Every monster you can imagine, man or beast, has tried to kill me. I should really see the doctor. (DC 16  ) [SORCERER] [INTIMIDATION]  You can let me in or I can burn, electrify, or freeze this place - maybe even all three. Your choice. (DC 16  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  ROAR AT THIS INJUSTICE.  (DC 16  ) [GREAT OLD ONE] [DECEPTION]  I'm sick with a deep malaise, one that came from a place beyond the stars. (DC 14) [ARCHFEY] [DECEPTION]  I've broken out in weird, singing hives - a sure sign of faerie infection. (DC 14) [FIEND] [DECEPTION]  I've picked up a diabolic disease - the symptoms are quite hellish. (DC 14) [THE HEXBLADE] [DECEPTION]  I cut myself on an otherworldly weapon - I think the wound's infected. (DC 14) [ASTARION]  My dear lady - look at my complexion. I am at death's door.  (automatic pass) If passing the check, Sinda directs the party to the Doctor, Malus Thorm . Otherwise, she insists that the party "wait in line", preventing them from entering past her into the lobby. The party can get around this by entering the building from any of the side entrances, or by taking the door immediately to the right of Sister Sinda, which exits outside to a short pathway leading to the children's ward. The children's ward can be entered either by breaking down the barricaded doors on the south side, or using the large vine ramps up to the roof to reach the north side. Alternatively, she can be killed, or controlled by an Oathbreaker Paladin ; the latter gives the party access to her powerful Mind Screech ability while the effect is active. If the Dark Urge is chosen as origin , a unique interaction becomes available. They can insist that there is something wrong with themselves, and allow Sister Sinda to inspect. She, in fact, notices the damage to the Dark Urge's mind, and allows the party to proceed to Malus Thorm without a Skill Check . This is also one of the events which confirms a key event in the history of the Dark Urge: the amnesia it suffers is a result of actual cranial trauma, separate from the Mind Flayer tadpole. If the party defeat Malus Thorm without engaging Sinda, returning to her reveals a new dialogue line: "The doctor is absent today. Come back another time." Time those rothé got to work. „ — Skarjall Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Skarjall is abusing two Deep Rothé alongside Grundril and Morgya at X: -668 Y: 442 . After trying to coerce the party into helping them ⁠ Get Past the Rubble , he reveals a piece of Adamantine Slag , indicating that an Adamantine Forge is nearby. The party can fight the duergar or help them clear the rubble. If spoken to via Speak with Animals , the two deep rothé that Skarjall is whipping can be convinced to rebel against the duergar. Superior Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 24 m (80 ft). Technical UID S_UND_ElevatorGnome UUID 348c5bc8-c514-41d7-a997-c8e58814d765 Stats UND_DeepGnome_Commoner Trs. UND_Duergar_GnomeSlave Skickpit is an enslaved Ironhand deep gnome who was captured by duergar cultists . Skickpit toils in Grymforge during Act One . “ It's 'Skickpit', you pisspot. „ — Skickpit Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Skickpit is outside the elevator which leads to the Shadow-Cursed Lands , being harassed by Magmar and Pistle . The party can join in with harassing Skickpit, or try to assure him that they are trying to help. This requires a Persuasion check. If Wyll is chosen as Origin , Skickpit believes the party automatically. Paladins or Clerics under a good deity also do not need to pass a skill check. Skickpit can be saved without combat by poisoning the "stained cask" near the stairs before climbing. If the camp is cleared of duergar, Skickpit can be told to join the other deep gnomes. If the party interact with the elevator, Skickpit warns them about travelling to the Shadow-Cursed Lands without a Moonlantern . After Nere and / or Magmar and Pistle are dealt with, the party can convince Skickpit to take the elevator, which eventually kills him: [DECEPTION]  The curse is cleared. You'll be perfectly safe. (DC 10) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  MOVE. I WASN'T ASKING. (DC 10  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  I go where I like. Move.  (DC 10  ) [INTIMIDATION]  Just do it, before I cut out that profane tongue of yours. (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  Grymforge is even more dangerous. Stay at your own peril. (DC 10) [GNOME]  Trust me. Would a gnome steer you wrong? Technical UID S_LOW_Park_AfterCombatChild03 UUID f793b719-0925-46ed-a6ad-b3e169d9572d Stats Human_Child Skip and two other children visit Bloomridge Park in the Lower City during Act Three . “ M-maybe we shouldn't walk around here. „ — Skip Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Skip, Cyrella , and Tam are three children who appear in Bloomridge Park after the Bhaal cultist attack. Of the trio, Skip is most wary and hesitant of being in the park, but is mocked by Cyrella when expressing these feelings. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Cyrella This is it! This is the park! Tam Where all the fightin' happened? Really? Skip M-maybe we shouldn't walk around here. Cyrella Waaaah! Waaaah! I'm Skip, and I'm a little baaaabyyyyy. Skip Shu'up! I'm not scared! Tam This place is so cool , Cyrella. I think I saw a whole eyeball . Cyrella I know, right? Skip Y-y-yeah. Super... cool. Tam How did you find out about this place, Cyrella? Cyrella I'm not telling! Hah! Tam Come on Cyrella. Tell us! How'd you know there was a fight here? Skip Yeah, Cyrella. Pleaaaase? Cyrella Fine. My big brother was here when it happened. Tam Woaaaah. Is he all right? Cyrella Oh yeah. He killed all the bad guys on his own. Skip That doesn't sound true... Cyrella Shut up, Skip! You're just jealous 'cos you don't have a big brother! Skip I do have a big brother! Cyrella Yeah but he's not cool. Or strong. Skittle Model Portrait Voice / Actor Shaun Mendum Role Trader Stats Size Tiny Type Beast Race Rat Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 1 HP 32 AC 12 Initiative +2 Proficiency +2 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 1 kg (2 lb) Darkvision 16 m (53 ft) XP reward 1 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 4 (-3) 15 (+2) 13 (+1) 4 (-3) 10 (0) 4 (-3) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA -3 +2 +1 -3 0 -3 Features Darkvision Can see in the dark up to a certain distance. Technical UID S_LOW_Prison_Rat01 UUID 7ec18c86-b069-4e60-82dd-61a0263d46f0 Stats LOW_Prison_TraderRat Skittle is a rat merchant found inside a cell in Heapside Prison during Act Three . “ A new client? What a thrill - for you, rat-urally! „ — Skittle the rat Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Skittle's cell can be unlocked with the generic key found on Fist Corlos , or it can be accessed via a destructible adjacent wall. Skittle can also be spoken to from outside the cell. In order to trade with Skittle, Speak with Animals must be used. Rat puns [ edit section | visual editor ] Befitting of a character with Intelligence 4, they speak almost exclusively in puns. The player can respond in kind. Skittle: "Step up and marvel at the spec-rat-ular wonders on offer!" Party member: A mercantile rodent? How rat-ical! Skittle: Indeed, my mirthful mate. Care to take a squeak at my fan-rats-tical wares? Party member: Is this business rat-ified by the local merchant's league? Skittle: My enterprise is a more... covert sort. I do my dealings in squeak-ret. Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Elixir of Universal Resistance Counting House Safe nº2 Key Scroll of Invisibility Scroll of Dimension Door Scroll of Fireball Scroll of Knock Scroll of Grease Scroll of Firebolt Thieves' Tools Oil Flask Dagger Trivia [ edit section | visual editor ] Skittle's store has everything one would need to plan an escape. LOW_CountingHouse_BhaalCultist Reaper of Bhaal Skoan is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , in the High Security Vaults in the Counting House in the Lower City . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the ⁠ The High Harper quest, the party can go to the Counting House in hopes of catching up to Minsc. Inside the vaults, the party witnesses Minsc emerge from a Mimic and defeat it. 'Jaheira' then appears with a handful of Bhaalists including Skoan, and teleports away with Minsc, leaving the cultists to attack the party and the staff. He is unhappy about the service of the Counting House and remarks that Head Clerk Meadhoney used to 'run a tighter ship'. Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_Skoona UUID 9a4e3f08-739f-4576-a50c-e051ce5126d1 Stats LOW_Skoona Enforcer Skoona is a half-orc [ 1 ] employee of the Elfsong Tavern in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Skoona patrols the tavern between the front door and the rear door in the kitchen. If a party member talks to her, she warns them to not break anything; as a Barbarian she can be pushed back. Cheering her up instead with specific Barbarian or Monk lines yields companion approval. [BARBARIAN]  Well, I'm thinking about your arms - they're like tree trunks. I approve.   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 [MONK]  What does it matter what anyone else thinks? You decide your own fate - no one else.   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Regardless of the options, she does not turn hostile and continues her patrol. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Scimitar +1 Damage: 7~12 1d6 + 6 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Off-Hand Attack (Melee) ( )   –   Scimitar +1 Damage: 7~12 1d6 + 6 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your off-hand weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Reckless Attack ( ) Damage Normal weapon damage Throw all caution in the wind to gain Advantage on your melee Attack Roll . Until your next turn, you have advantage on attack rolls, but enemies also have advantage on attack rolls against you. Range: Normal weapon range Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Chain Mail +1 Handaxe - 2x Scimitar +1 - 2x Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Skoona By Gruumsh ! These customers look more ragged every day. Skoona When my break comes, I'm going to play with the kitchen cats, I don't care what Revoor [ 2 ] says. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Skoona is a mentioned character in Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus , where she is described a gruff female half-ogre (instead of the half-orc she is in-game). She is there to protect the other staff members, not the patrons, and does not break up a fight unless a staff member is involved. ↑ Likely referring to Roveer , this could either be intended or a typo on Larians end. EQP_Shortbow_Dagger_Leather Trs. HAV_Survivor Harper Skywin is a determined elven [ 1 ] ranger [ 2 ] of the Harpers patrolling the southern stairway of the docks in Last Light Inn during Act Two . [ 3 ] “ May the road rise to meet you, and the shadows keep at bay. „ — Skywin , saluting the party. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party enter the Shadow-Cursed Lands through Grymforge , Skywin is at the Last Light Inn, on the southern side of the inn, patrolling the stairway to the southern docks, and behind Quartermaster Talli's tent. After speaking with Jaheira inside the inn, Skywin moves to the bridge in front of the Last Light Inn with Branthos , Elindale , Lassandra , and Manus . They wait for the party so they can move in to intercept and ⁠ ambush a nearby Absolutist convoy and acquire their ⁠ source of protection against the Shadow Curse . Accepting the mission results in Skywin and her squad of Harpers casting Light on their weapons and moving to the Ruined Battlefield , where they lay in wait for the Absolutist convoy. The party can go with the group immediately or catch up with them later, as the ambush site is marked on their map. If the party speak with Isobel and trigger the fight with Marcus , Skywin will have already moved to the bridge, out of reach of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, Skywin turns into a Shadow-Cursed Undead . Ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] Talking to Branthos [ 4 ] at the ambush site commences the ambush and spawns in the encounter. Once Kar'niss and the convoy arrive, the party can attack immediately or hang back. If they choose to stay hidden and keep watching, Kar'niss kills Vez . From there, the party can either signal the Harpers or wait as they start the encounter themselves. After the fight, a Moonlantern can be found on the drider's corpse. Alternatively, the party can convince Kar'niss to relinquish the Moonlantern and consign the convoy members to their fate as Shadow-Cursed Undead . Either way, Elindale and his squad then depart amiably and return to Last Light Inn. If the party enter the Shadow-Cursed Lands through the Rosymorn Monastery Trail , a goblin greets the party and sends them to a rendezvous point to wait for Kar'niss and the convoy to guide them to Moonrise Towers , where the party can ⁠ pass off as True Souls . This starts ⁠ Follow the Convoy . Kar'niss ferries the party, as well as the rest of the convoy to Moonrise. During the trek, Skywin, along with Branthos, Elindale, and Manus ambush the convoy. The party can choose to either turn on the convoy and help the Harpers, or protect the convoy in order to continue their cover as True Souls. If the party are meeting the Harpers for the first time, and Branthos dies while siding with them, Skywin can tell the party to head to Last Light Inn, where they can obtain similar protection after speaking with Isobel. If they choose to remain with the convoy, Skywin turns hostile. After the Ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party side with Skywin and he survives, Skywin moves to the southern coastline of the Last Light Inn, patrolling the same route as before the ambush, circling between the stairway to the southern side of the docks and the back of Quartermaster Talli's tent. Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn, and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise Towers, Skywin follows Jaheira there. However, she is killed during the fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. Her corpse is in the Moonrise Towers Prison , surrounded by a Death Shepherd and a horde of Necromites . This got fixed with Patch 8 . ↑ Has an exact duplicate of her as a Shadow-Cursed Undead in the center X: 158 Y: -35 of Reithwin . The undead Skywin has the same appearance, outfit, and weapons as the original; yet this undead copy has the correct stat block for a ranged combatant: 12 STR, 16 DEX, and 12 CON. Slack-Skinned Head In-game Portrait Voice / Actor Ellie Heydon Role Brain reader Stats Race Elf Technical UID S_COL_BrainReader_Head_Character UUID 034ec7e7-948b-4c1e-9a38-82efbe459ee4 Stats Elf_Commoner The Slack-Skinned Head and Mind-Archive Interface are side-by-side in the Mind Flayer Colony . They are accessible after defeating a Death Shepherd , some winged horrors and various Zombies. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Various 'minds' in green jars can be found and inserted into the Mind-Archive Interface, which lets the player character have a conversation with the unfortunate creature via the Slack-Skinned Head. There are 2 minds to be found on the Nautiloid in the Prologue : Dark Mind Slave Mind There are 6 minds to be found within the Mind Flayer Colony in Act Two : Butchered Mind - on top of a set of shelves with discarded armour, in the Morgue where Chop works Closed Mind - on a shelf in Ironfinger 's room, in the north-western part of the Barracks Fresh Mind - on-top of a stack of mucilaginous boxes beside the elevator leading to the final area True Mind - in front of the head in the Necrotic Laboratory Waking Mind - is behind a door in the Necrotic Laboratory , only accessible after solving the brain mapping puzzle [ 1 ] Willing Mind - on a desk west of the head in the Necrotic Laboratory Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ The Waking Mind is unique because speaking to the head can grant the permanent buff Githzerai Mind Barrier . v t e Mind Flayer Colony Characters Apostle of Myrkul Balthazar Chop Gortash Hairy Henry Ironfinger Ketheric Thorm Kressa Bonedaughter Maghtew Budj Mizora Nimias Orin Slack-Skinned Head The Netherbrain Ulder Ravengard Us Yeva Zevlor Zombie Dror Ragzlin Zombie Minthara Zombie Wulbren Creatures Death Shepherd Greater Zombie Reconstituted Arcanist Winged Horror Zombie Locations Barracks Morgue Necrotic Laboratory Tadpoling Centre Quests Defeat Ketheric Thorm Find Mol Find Zevlor Lift the Shadow Curse The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke The Wizard of Waterdeep

Now it's mush . „ — Slarmy Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Slarmy is near the broken cart east of the Abandoned Windmill in Rivington . He is scavenging the cart together with Zeffy Softbluff and Tina Two-Thumbs . They condemn the people who have broken down the cart and looted it, although they themselves are scavenging the leftovers. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Slarmy The state of this cart - what were they thinking?! Zeffy Softbluff They wasn't thinking - starving folk tend not to. Slarmy If they'd just lined up and - and taken their fair shares, we'd have plenty for everyone! Zeffy Softbluff 'If' won't get us fed and watered. Slarmy Look at that - finest pie that fruit could have made. Now it's mush. Tina Two-Thumbs You remember that spiced apple loaf we had in Waterdeep? The big one? Slarmy Gods, I can practically smell it. Zeffy Softbluff Shut it. Scavenge whatever you can from this mess - we'll make something out of it. Zeffy Softbluff Take the wood from the cart too - that'll be good for a fire, if nothing else. Tina Two-Thumbs Finders bloody keepers, I say. Slarmy Bloody savages, the lot of them! Zeffy Softbluff We're as desperate as the rest of these 'savages'. Technical UID 91550f0a-a04b-4cb1-b0d9-3d83dc902dae UUID S_LOW_SteepsEvacuation_Sailor Stats Halfling_Commoner Captain Sleam is a sailor at Grey Harbour Docks of the Lower City in Act Three . “ The crew and I are risking our lives. We're not doing this for charity. „ — Sleam Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Captain Sleam can be found in the Grey Harbour Docks , near her sloop moored at the pier to the south of the Steel Watch Foundry docks. She argues with Dharin Brislen over smuggling him and his family of four out of the city. Unfortunately, the family lacks money to pay for four people aboard. The party can help the family by convincing Captain Sleam to take them all via check-based options or by paying her the needed sum. Should the party succeed in resolving the problem, Captain Sleam and the Brislen family are gone from the docks after the next long rest, giving place to another group of characters with their own vignette. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] The following dialogue options result in companion approval: Captain Sleam: This is life and death for me too, mate. You only get as many berths on my sloop as you can pay for. If I allow any freeloaders, my own crew will scrag me. Excuse the interruption, Captain, but can I pay for the father's berth? [PERSUASION]  Captain... Sleam, is it? It would be a shame to split up the family, don't you think? Let the father go with them. (DC 15) [INTIMIDATION]  I have news for you, Captain: you're going to accept four for the price of three and take the father aboard. Or I'll pitch you into the harbour. Got it? (DC 15) Any of the above:   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Captain Sleam You want four berths on the sloop, you pay for all four berths. Dharin Brislen We only have enough for three! We sold everything! Captain Sleam Slipping through the Absolute blockade is risking business. Everybody pays. Leepak Brislen Captain, we have two children, you can't make us split up the family. Captain Sleam The crew and I are risking our lives. We're not doing this for charity. Dharin Brislen Honey, you go with the girls. I'll find another way to Waterdeep. Leepak Brislen What? No! We can't go without you! Dharin Brislen It's the only solution. Trust me. I'll catch up to you. Leepak Brislen You'd better! You'd better catch up to us! Dharin Brislen All right, captain. Just these three, then. v t e Grey Harbour Docks Characters Angry Mob Antinia Vharranne Churg Elvek Dart Dirtwood Imprudence Nobster Ormo Civilians Asthena Blossom Bunny Cinna Brewcellar Dharin Brislen Deelia Falmor Duguir Flaerian Kaet Ling Leepak Brislen Marie Taylira Neeme Rabbelle Saff Fargoer Slorsha Grommer Volo Vhynce Yeller Dawg Flaming Fist Rockbothem Virry Sailors/Dockworkers Birta Grougg Darvis Djingo Dollivar Noot Fleer Gowlan Gratz Kadugan Klorrvank Listless Matey Tallhamper Nets Blandorf Pheebs Splayfoot Rox Flunter Sharley Sleam Smiley Gheef Yves The Guild Big Huido Galem Meats Jezzy Topps Lo Blank Victims Dizby Harfang Jorkens Penita Locations Flymm Cargo Lustrous Lass Quests Avenge the Drowned Save the Gondians

Looks just like a hollyphant , that does. Sledge Pettifeet You're supposed to be looking out for us, not the bloody skies. Terse Torvalt Not my fault. I've got an overactive imagination . Skeeve Stabwell Try and imagine doing your job properly, then. Sledge Pettifeet You ever get bored of standing in this alley? Skeeve Stabwell Oh no. I love it. It fills me with purpose. Terse Torvalt Nah, it's great getting paid to do nothing but scratch my arse. Dream job, this is. Skeeve Stabwell Not my dream. Terse Torvalt 'When I was lad I made merry, made merry - With a beautiful lass from the plains...' Skeeve Stabwell Oh gods, he's at it again. Sledge Pettifeet Oi! What have we told you about bloody singing? Skeeve Stabwell Spoil sport. Sledge Pettifeet Right. Here's one. Who's pocket would you rather pick - a druid's, or a cleric's? Skeeve Stabwell Cleric, any day. Last time I emptied a druid's pockets, all I got for it was a nest of bloody squirrels. Terse Torvalt Nah, gotta be druid. Clerics don't carry much gold on 'em. Always offering it to their bloody gods . Sledge Pettifeet You're both wrong. You pick the pocket of whatever mark you're asking.
