Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Taeglyn's corpse was crushed beneath rocks in the Worg Pens at X: 416 Y: -46 . Using Speak with Dead reveals that he was attempting to escape the goblin prison by digging a tunnel, but the tunnel collapsed and trapped him in rubble. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who are you? Dead Elf Taeglyn... carpenter. Father of two. How did you end up here? Dead Elf Heading to... Baldur's Gate . Didn't hear... goblin patrol. Why is there a heart on one of your shoes? Dead Elf My son Galean... did it. If I ever missed him... could look down and... remember him. There's a bear in one of the other cells. Where did it come from? Dead Elf Not... bear. Were you the only prisoner here? Dead Elf Goblins took... my friends. Cut them up... for the worgs . For meat. How did you get trapped in the tunnel? Dead Elf Digging... too quickly. Felt tunnel... collapsing. Kept going. Better dead than... worg meat. v t e Goblin Camp Characters Bugbears Bao'ek'nuk Stimk Teghun Camp Followers Owlbear Cub Volo Companions Halsin Minthara Goblins Aggy Azak Bal Bez Birka Bolt Brakkal Breg Clack Crub Crusher Cry Culk Druk Dullwill Eef Fezk Glomp Gnat Greez Gribbo Grikka Grush Gruz Gurd Gurk Huk Kirz Klagga Krolla Mirg Mrak Muzul Nass Neem Nik-Nuk Nozk Nrog Olak Piddle Plagg Plig Puce Puli Raagg Rancer Rindle Roo Rot Rozzak Sazza Shekt Sluck Snurd Spike Skrut Sul Tak Tiny Tizg Tozad Trinzas Tud Vrak Wasp Zami Zurga Zurk Children Eight Five Four One Three Goblin Leaders Dror Ragzlin Gut Minthara Ogres Gurgon Polma Traders Grat Roah Moonglow Other Abdirak Andrick Brynna Dishevelled Chicken Erna Ferr Larger Giant Spider Kagran Klaw Liam Narvass Smaller Giant Spider Small Klaw Smythin Taeglyn Tale Yerle Locations Bloodied Shrine Defiled Temple Goblin Camp Shattered Sanctum Worg Pens Quests Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Defeat the Goblins Find a Cure Find the Nightsong Raid the Emerald Grove Rescue the Druid Halsin Rescue Volo Save the First Druid Save the Goblin Sazza Save the Refugees Travel to Moonrise Towers

DEN_DruidServant Tahan is one of the druids performing the Rite of Thorns during Act One . “ We should be looking out for ourselves. „ — Tahan Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Tahan is at the Sacred Pool of the Emerald Grove . She is loyal to Kagha and resents both the party and tiefling refugees for bringing violence to their gates, a view she adheres to even if Kagha's alliance with the Shadow Druids is brought to light. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Tahan has two Wild Shape charges and can can cast spells using Level Two Spell Slots . Heat Metal ( + ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Fire Cause a metal weapon or armour to glow red-hot and force the wearer to let go or receive Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks . If the creature is only wearing metal armour, it always receives Disadvantage. If the creature is still touching the metal, you can use a bonus action on subsequent turns to deal another 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire and force the creature to let go or receive Disadvantage. CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Quarterstaff Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Mirror Image ( + ) Create 3 illusory duplicates of yourself to distract attackers. Each duplicate increases your   Armour Class by 3. Whenever you successfully evade an attack, one of the duplicates disappears. Range: Self Produce Flame ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Fire A flame in your hand sheds a light in a 9 m (30 ft) radius and deals 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage when thrown. Throwing the flame immediately after you conjure it does not cost an Action . Extinguishing or throwing it on subsequent turns costs an action. The throw has a range of 9 m (30 ft). Range: Self Thunderwave ( + ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Thunder Release a wave of thunderous force that pushes away all creatures and objects in an area, while also dealing Thunder damage. CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Wild Shape: Wolf ( + ) Assume the shape of a dire wolf that can   Incite allies and   Distract enemies. The dire wolf has a starting health of 18 hit points that increase every two druid levels. While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. You take on the attributes of your beast form - excluding your Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma scores. When your beast form drops to 0 hit points , you revert to your normal form. MOO_Cultist Pilgrim Taima is a human in Moonrise Towers in Act Two . “ You're one of Her blessed, aren't you? To hear Her voice... I cannot imagine. „ — Taima Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Taima is in the main hall of Moonrise Towers at X: -163 Y: -176 . She is part a group of new Absolutist pilgrims, consisting of her and Farimorn , Iong , Nalira , and Sul . They are observed by Belub , who shows contempt for the pilgrims, and remarks on their lack of skills and usefulness. The party can either convince Belub to keep the pilgrims, or tell him to get rid of them. [PERSUASION]  They have potential. Great warriors have grown from less. (DC 14) It's not our place to question the Absolute's will. Then get rid of them. The undeserving should be purged. The first two options result in Belub sending them to the war camp west of Reithwin , where the pilgrims disappear. Telling Belub to get rid of the pilgrims results in their death. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Pilgrim Nalira Where do you hail from, brother? Pilgrim Fairmorn I was a farrier in Dessarin Valley. Then the dreams came. Pilgrim Iong My brothers had the dreams too, same as me. But they wouldn't admit it. Pilgrim Nalira The Absolute calls us all to Her design. Your family will answer - eventually. Pilgrim Taima To stand this close to Her power... I never thought I'd make it. Pilgrim Iong I wouldn't have, if not for the lantern-bearer. To think the Absolute graces such a creature as that... Pilgrim Fairmorn We are each of us threads in Her design. Even those we once called monsters. Pilgrim Nalira Brothers. Sister. Pray with me while we wait. Pilgrim Fairmorn I'm not worthy. I... I never learned the words. Pilgrim Nalira Yes, you did. She gives them to you fully formed. Can you hear Her? Pilgrim Fairmorn Of many hearts, one soul. Of many thoughts, one mind... Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party go to camp between defeating the Cult of the Absolute members at Moonrise Towers and entering the rooftop, they may find Talli fighting against Farimorn and the other pilgrims of the Absolute Iong , Nalira , Sul , and Taima. HAV_HarperQuarterMaster_Magic_Trade Quartermaster Talli is a human Harper quartermaster at the Last Light Inn in Act Two . “ If you're all right by Jaheira, you're all right by me. „ — Talli Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Talli is in Last Light Inn's courtyard during at X: -30 Y: 128 , managing the Harpers' supplies. If Marcus is exposed as a True Soul , Talli gets Stunned and joins the fight against his summoned Crawling Claws . Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during Resolve the Abduction , Talli always fails the save and is Impaled for the remainder of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, she and everyone in Last Light Inn turn into Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira . Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn, and once the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Talli follows Jaheira to Moonrise Towers. There, she survives the initial off-screen assault, and moves near the entrance. She still can be traded with. Talli does not usually partake in the ensuing battle within Moonrise Towers itself. However, after the ensuing assault within Moonrise Towers' hall, Talli moves in and starts salvaging the equipment and remains there until the very end of Act Two . Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to HAV_HarperQuarterMaster and HAV_HarperQuarterMaster_Magic_Trade . Weapons [ edit section | visual editor ] Defender Greataxe Incandescent Staff Rapier +2 Scimitar +2 Shortsword +2 Armour [ edit section | visual editor ] Barkskin Armour Cindersnap Gloves Gloves of the Balanced Hands Hat of Uninhibited Kushigo Obsidian Laced Robe Shadeclinger Armour Shield of Devotion The Mighty Cloth Yuan-Ti Scale Mail Accessories [ edit section | visual editor ] Amulet of the Harpers Cloak of Protection Dyes [ edit section | visual editor ] Talli sells all dyes from the Dye Subtable and Rare Dye Subtable . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Light Hammer Damage: 4~7 1d4 + 3 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Light Hammer Leather Armour Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Infiltrate Moonrise Towers ⁠ Resolve the Abduction Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] As of Patch 7 , despite having Extra Attack , Talli is not able to attack twice during her turns. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party go to camp between defeating the Cult of the Absolute members at Moonrise Towers and entering the rooftop, they may find Talli fighting against Farimorn and the other pilgrims of the Absolute Iong , Nalira , Sul , and Taima . While Cyrella leads the exploration, Tam is excited and eager about the prospect of battle. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Cyrella This is it! This is the park! Tam Where all the fightin' happened? Really? Skip M-maybe we shouldn't walk around here. Cyrella Waaaah! Waaaah! I'm Skip, and I'm a little baaaabyyyyy. Skip Shu'up! I'm not scared! Tam This place is so cool , Cyrella. I think I saw a whole eyeball . Cyrella I know, right? Skip Y-y-yeah. Super... cool. Tam How did you find out about this place, Cyrella? Cyrella I'm not telling! Hah! Tam Come on Cyrella. Tell us! How'd you know there was a fight here? Skip Yeah, Cyrella. Pleaaaase? Cyrella Fine. My big brother was here when it happened. Tam Woaaaah. Is he all right? Cyrella Oh yeah. He killed all the bad guys on his own. Skip That doesn't sound true... Cyrella Shut up, Skip! You're just jealous 'cos you don't have a big brother! Skip I do have a big brother! Cyrella Yeah but he's not cool. Or strong. CHA_Exterior_Bandit_Melee Taman is a cautious bandit looting the Overgrown Ruins in Act One . “ But we don't know what thing even is! And what about the crypt? „ — Taman , arguing with Gimblebock Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Taman is at the Chapel Entrance arguing with Gimblebock on whether to abandon their post to search the Nautiloid . While Gimblebock insists on exploring the ship, Taman is wary that the Nautiloid will be the death of them. Nearby, Quelenna and Warryn also guard the ruins. Upon approach by a party member, Gimblebock automatically engages them in conversation. They can convince the looters to leave the area or attack them. Failing any of the ability checks causes Taman and the others to attack. Clerk Tamara In-game Model Portrait Identity Female Voice / Actor Zoe Mills Faction Cult of Bane Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Drow Subrace Lolth-sworn drow Class Wizard Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats Level 9 HP 44 AC 12 Initiative +2 Proficiency +4 Movement 9 m (30 ft) Weight 75 kg (150 lb) Darkvision 0 m (0 ft) XP reward 250 Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 9 (-1) 14 (+2) 30 (+10) 17 (+3) 12 (+1) 11 (0) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA -1 +2 +10 +7 +5 0 Additional Resources Features Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Technical UID S_LOW_FireworksHouse_BaniteClerk02 UUID 3d69c599-5218-4b3d-9845-3c19b8a14278 Stats LOW_FelogyrFireworks_AverySonshal Clerk Tamara is a trader of the Felogyr's Fireworks workshop in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate , during Act Three . She can be spoken with while following through the quest ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys . “ Smokepowder in its earthier forms. For purists only. „ — Tamara , describing her stock Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Clerk Tamara stands at the counter on the first floor of the Felogyr's Fireworks. Her main occupation is trade, but she also acts as a warder, keeping customers from peeking into true realities of Felogyr's business. However, she cannot see through Invisibility. As such, she can be walked around easily. Unlike other Drow in the game, Tamara does not have the Faerie Fire ability or other drow racial feats. Her stats follow those of a Human of the same level. Tamara can be pickpocketed. Apart from trading goods, the party may also loot from her a Scribbled Note . The note's text confirms that Tamara's boss Avery Sonshal was the one who blackmailed Arfur Gregorio into helping him. On Tamara's counter the party can find a book by Avery Sonshal titled Boom, Bang, Blast: The joy of fireworks . On the shelf beneath the counter lays Avery's Storage Key that opens the Wooden Chest in the basement. As the ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys quest cannot be ultimately resolved in a peaceful way, Tamara joins the fight as soon as she notices any ill commotion, siding with the followers of Bane , who reside on the second floor of the building. She stays near her counter and attacks the party along with the other Felogyr's employees. Technical UID S_LOW_BaneiteOfficer02 UUID de084b09-99c6-426e-9159-f692d180d418 Stats Human_Cultist_Bane_BlackGauntlet Tamia Holzt is a Black Gauntlet of Bane on the main floor of the Steel Watch Foundry at X: -292 Y: -147 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Tamia Holzt guards the Steel Watch Foundry and watches over the Gondians who are forced to work there to produce the Steel Watchers for Enver Gortash . When first encountered, the party can witness her coercing a Gondian by starting Prinski's Motivation Sequence which would detonate the Kill Collars worn by each Gondian if completed. In the Elfsong Tavern , the party can meet Blarson Throaks and his wife Clovia discussing how their son Gasper just got a new job working as a guard at the Steel Watch foundry, due to the help of Tamia Holzt. As the discussion continues, Clovia reveals that Tamia has become her new lover and she is leaving her husband. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] When engaged in combat, Holzt prioritizes casting Planar Ally: Deva (Banite) and activating her Motivator which must be quickly disarmed or every Gondian dies. Technical UID S_GLO_Gale_Tressym UUID ada7ee81-829d-48c7-ba73-9c9ec191d236 Stats Tressym Trs. WYR_Tara_Tressym_Treasure Tara is a Tressym , a cat-like Monstrosity . She is Gale's fluffy companion and assistant. “ We have a great deal of catching up to do. Eat that, wash your hands, and for the love of all that's dear, a shave. Then you can fill me in on what I've missed. „ — Tara , speaking to Gale Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.2 Act Three 2.3 Epilogue 3 Items sold 4 Loot 5 Related Quests 6 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale conjured Tara when he was ten years old, after his parents refused to give him a kitten. Tara and Gale's mother eventually became friends, with Tara visiting her after Gale left home. Tara affectionately refers to Gale as "the most expensive pet in Waterdeep" , and later states that they both belong to each other. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Tara first appears upon the first Long Rest of the game if Gale is chosen as origin . She notes Gale's somewhat ill appearance, and expresses concern. She also provides Gale with a magic item, the Ring of Evasion , that he can consume when he awakes, to prevent the Netherese Orb from detonating. She remains within the Campsite . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Tara appears - regardless of the player character - on the roof of the Open Hand Temple in Rivington . She is involved in the quest ⁠ Find the Missing Letters , and has unique dialogue when Gale is in the party. It is also possible to get the Ring of Blink here, whether Gale is present or not. After this encounter Tara can be found on the roof of the Devil's Fee in the Lower City , where she used to sell the Hat of the Sharp Caster . In order to progress Tara to her third location now, the party must acquire the Hat of the Sharp Caster from atop the entrance awning of Sorcerous Sundries (via Telekinesis or an Arrow of Roaring Thunder ), reverse pickpocket it onto her, buy it back from her, and then take a long rest. The third encounter takes place on the roof of Highberry's Home , where Tara sells the Slinging Shoes . Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Tara appears during the Epilogue , accompanying Gale to the celebration in most endings. If Gale reforged the Crown of Karsus and gave it to Mystra, then talking to Tara causes her to invite the player character to her and Gale's tower, remembering the player character as "the one who saved Faerûn alongside Mr Dekarios." If Gale reforged the Crown of Karsus and ascended to godhood, she expresses disappointment in her friend's transformation and failure to learn from his past mistakes. If Gale sacrificed himself to destroy the Netherbrain with his Netherese Orb, Tara mentions how much she misses him and invites the player character to visit Gale's mother in the future. If the player character transformed into an illithid to fight the Netherbrain, then Tara remarks they must have sacrificed quite a bit to save Faerûn. Items sold [ edit section | visual editor ] If spoken to with Gale present during the quest ⁠ Find the Missing Letters , Tara appears on various rooftops in Lower City , selling one magical item each time. After buying an item and taking a Long Rest, Tara moves to another rooftop, selling a new item. Tara accepts most magical items and any type of Fish in exchange for her items. The fish are exchanged for their gold value and must be outside of a Camp Supply Sack to appear in the bartering menu. Tara can also be pickpocketed for the item at each location. However it should be noted that pickpocketing the item stops her from moving to the next location; the item must be purchased on the roof of the Devil's Fee for Tara to appear again on Highberry Home's roof. Hat of the Sharp Caster – on the roof of the Devil's Fee at X: -29 Y: 6 Slinging Shoes – on the roof of Highberry's Home at X: 1 Y: -36 Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Tressym Collar Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find the Missing Letters ⁠ The Wizard of Waterdeep Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Tressyms usually are unable to speak. Tara, however, is capable of speech, likely as a result of external magical means. Tara refuses to stop using Gale's surname, referring to him as "Mr. Dekarios". Tara nags Gale about being single. Gale asked Halaster - presumably Halaster Blackcloak - to take care of Tara in his absence. If a party member offers fish or a magical item in the barter screen, then clicks on the "balance offer" button, money is used to make up the difference. The party can then remove the original item offered and press the balance offer button again to top up the offer with gold. v t e Party and camp Companions Origin Astarion Gale Karlach Lae'zel BG_Guard Fist Taraji is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in Rivington in Act Three . “ The cult of the Absolute - what else? They turned this place into a bloodbath. „ — Taraji Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Taraji together with Fist Wayne can be found standing in the Circus of the Last Days nearby the stage. The two only appear if all of the following occur: the party leaves the circus after battling with the doppelgangers during the circus act, the conflict results in the death of both the false Dribbles and the ringmaster Lucretious , and the party takes a long rest afterwards. If all the above are true then Taraj investigates the crime scene and, if spoken to, stops the party from entering it. She also might shed some light on what has happened, blaming the Cult of the Absolute for murdering the ringmaster, and promising to find the killer. Technical UID S_LOW_TarhunMnemonis UUID 2d1b98a0-01a9-4c21-8bc2-9738c47f6966 Stats Dragonborn_Commoner Tarhun Mnemonis is a white dragonborn and butler to Lady Jannath . He can be found outside the front door of Lady Jannath's Estate in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . “ I have more to do with dustbrushes than paintbrushes - I am Lady Jannath's butler. „ — Tarhun Mnemonis , if asked whether he is an artist himself Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Tarhun's dialogue changes depending on the state of ⁠ Save the artist . If Oskar Fevras was saved from Brem in Act One , the house is haunted and Tarhun explains that Lady Jannath sent away all the servants on vacation, including him. As he is on 'vacation', he cannot stop anyone from entering the estate, but he does warn against it. While the conversation is going on, screaming and banging can be heard from within the mansion. If Oskar was not saved and remains missing, Lady Jannath is hosting an art exhibition and Tarhun welcomes them to "Lady Jannath's celebration of the arts". If Oskar is dead, Tarhun says they can enter but they are in a state of mourning. Technical UID S_LOW_DeadAdventurer_001 UUID 98f5af07-74fb-49ae-be05-3834e0a23464 Stats HalfElf_Melee Taron named in-game as Dead Half-Elf , is a dead adventurer in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Taron is in the Ancient Lair of the Undercity. If the party commune with him via Speak with Dead , he reveals that Mystic Carrion had once promised him a better life, only to cause his slow and painful demise while trying to perform a ritual. [ 1 ] Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Taron can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Dead Half-Elf Beggar... vagrant... scum... my name was Taron... Where are you from? Dead Half-Elf Tumbledown... long ago... no home now... How did you get here? Dead Half-Elf Carrion... offered shelter... safety... I was desperate... Who is 'Carrion'? Dead Half-Elf Mystic Carrion... medium... monster... liar... Who killed you? Dead Half-Elf Carrion... What do you know about Mystic Carrion? Dead Half-Elf Mystic Carrion... medium... monster... liar... What lies did Carrion tell? Dead Half-Elf Promised... better life... given only death... What did Carrion do to you? Dead Half-Elf Bled... hollowed... emptied... alive... was still alive... Why didn't he kill you straight away? Dead Half-Elf A ritual... jars... hidden in flesh... I failed... died too quickly... Technical UID S_LOW_SoberingUp_Cashguard_01 UUID 4544476d-1260-4ddb-8155-64712ad44950 Stats LOW_CountingHouse_Melee_Human Cashguard Taslim is a member of the Cashguard for The Counting House in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ This uniform's neat, isn't it? But why am I - ohhh, wait - I had a shift at the Counting House. Oops. „ — Taslim Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Taslim is outside The Blushing Mermaid in the Lower City next to Cashguard Gurira , who is chastising her for drinking during their lunch break. However, Taslim seems unbothered by the possibility of being fired, and asks Gurira if they should grab a drink for the road. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Hand Crossbow Helmet Maul Plate Armour Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Taslim occasionally chats with Gurira: Cashguard Gurira How much did you drink, you idiot dokal ? Cashguard Taslim Just - just a bitta beer. And wine. And mead. Cashguard Gurira We have to go back to the Counting House! What were you thinking?! Cashguard Taslim Ah, don't be a dry-shite. No one will... will... yeah. Cashguard Gurira Could you at least try to stand up straight. Cashguard Taslim I am! Oh - oh, that was a bad idea. Cashguard Gurira Don't you dare puke on your uniform. Cashguard Taslim You - you want a drink? Let's get one for the road. Cashguard Gurira No, you moron . We could be fired for this! Cashguard Taslim Ah, sure, a bitta drink never killed anyone. Cashguard Gurira Tell that to Glitterbeard ! Tate In-game Model Portrait Identity Male Voice / Actor Rosie Jones Faction Harpers , Jaheira's Family Family Jaheira (adoptive mother) Jord (adoptive brother) Jhessem (adoptive sister) Rion (adoptive sister) Fig (adoptive sister) Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Size Small Type Humanoid Race Human Technical UID S_LOW_JaheirasHouse_JaheiraYoungestSon UUID 0d760747-8fab-414e-8ccc-a925ebb6da2c Stats Human_Child Tate is a human child in Lower City in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Jaheira! I d-didn't... didn't w-want to see. If you were r-really dead. They said...<...> Jord and Rion. They didn't think I c-could hear... „ — Tate , afraid of losing an adoptive family Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Tate is Jaheira's adoptive child and lives in what is now Elerrathin's Home along with Jaheira's other children. Tate is described as a "little sneak-thief" by Jaheira. He keeps to himself upstairs, eavesdropping on conversations. Tate has one of the pins that can be used to access Jaheira's Basement . Gold_Pocket_Random Harper Teebs is a Harper who patrols the southern side of the Last Light Inn docks during Act Two . “ Nice to see the dark's spitting out more than shadows. Welcome. „ — Teebs Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Teebs is at the Last Light Inn, where he is patrolling the southern side route of the docks area, with Naysa patrolling in the opposite direction. Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Teebs more often than not fails his saving throw and is Impaled for the remainder of the battle. If Isobel is not saved, Teebs and everyone in the inn turn into Shadow-Cursed Undead , save for Jaheira . Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn, and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Teebs follows Jaheira to Moonrise Towers . However, Teebs is killed during the fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. His corpse is in Moonrise Towers, down the staircase leading down from the entrance, in front of Disciple Z'rell . Technical UID S_DEN_Snake_001 UUID af2ff867-467e-4765-a66c-fed091af4a09 Stats Snake_Viper Teela is Kagha's death viper snake. She is loyal to Kagha, but may be willing to listen to reason over her owner. She is in the Emerald Grove during Act One . “ A new hatchling? Yes. They can be foolish. „ — Teela Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon entering the Inner Sanctum of the Emerald Grove, Teela, Kagha, and Rath are discussing Arabella's fate after she was caught stealing the Idol of Silvanus . Teela is poised to intervene if Arabella struggles or tries to escape. A party member can intervene to ⁠ Save Arabella . If a non-druid character tells Teela to stay at ease, she responds that she only takes orders from Kagha. However, she listens to druids , agreeing that hatchlings can be foolish. She tells Kagha, "Kagha si nay. Wux geou fulla wer fanol." which convinces Kagha to relent from punishing the child. Should Arabella struggle or try to run, Teela bites Arabella, who immediately succumbs to her venom. After the cutscene is resolved, Teela disappears and is not seen again. She is positioned atop the guard tower by the entry bridge. “ From up here, you can almost pretend Isobel's light is the sun. „ — Terradissia Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Terradissia guards the entrance to Last Light Inn atop a guard tower above Darragh and Elifer . If Marcus rescues the party but is exposed as a True Soul , Terradissia is Stunned and joins the fight against his summoned Crawling Claws . Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Terradissia frequently is amongst the Harpers who avoid being Impaled ; she then either runs up to fight the Winged Horrors , or stays out of combat range. If Isobel is not saved, Terradissia and everyone save for Jaheira in Last Light Inn turns into Shadow-Cursed Undead . Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise Towers , Terradissia follows Jaheira to the assault on Moonrise. However, Terradissia is killed during the fight against Absolute forces before the party arrive. Her corpse is in the Moonrise Towers Prison , surrounded by a Death Shepherd and a horde of Necromites . CRE_Gith_Generic Teth'ka , named in-game as Dead Githyanki Warrior , is a githyanki fighter in the Shadow-Cursed Lands during Act Two . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Teth'ka's corpse can is in the house where Oliver plays hide-and-seek. She was training to become a sarth when she was ambushed by shadows in the Shadow-Cursed Lands and killed. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Who were you? Dead Githyanki Warrior Teth'ka... warrior for my Queen... blade for my Kith'rak... How did you die? Dead Githyanki Warrior Foolish games... shadow... ambushed... Dead Githyanki Warrior Shameful death... dishonour to Vlaakith... Where are you from?  (non-Githyanki speaker) Dead Githyanki Warrior Crèche Y'llek... hidden among the mountains... veiled by ruins... What crèche do you hail from, kin?  (Githyanki speaker) Dead Githyanki Warrior Crèche Y'llek... hidden among the mountains... veiled by ruins... Are there other githyanki nearby? Dead Githyanki Warrior Not in the shadowlands... Atop the mountain, reaching to the sun... Why were you here? Dead Githyanki Warrior Training... becoming a sarth... leading my kin... How do I fight the curse? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. HAV_Survivor Fist Thadwick is a gruff Flaming Fist [ 1 ] under the command of Counsellor Florrick to rescue Duke Ravengard during Act Two . “ The cultists are among us, and you want to chat? Let the professionals handle this. „ — Thadwick , to the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Initially on a mission led by Florrick to rescue Ulder Ravengard , Thadwick and the rest of the Fists were waylaid by the dangers of the Shadow-Cursed Lands and found refuge with the Harpers at Last Light Inn . Thadwick is within the inn, in the same room as several other Fists, and Art Cullagh . He regards the party with disdain due to their infected nature and them not being a Flaming Fist. [ 2 ] If Florrick is not rescued from Waukeen's Rest in Act One , Thadwick does not appear in the game. Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Thadwick is not affected by the Impaled condition and is instead Surprised . He may join the battle on his own without being affected by any conditions if the door to the room he is in is opened after the encounter starts. If Isobel is not saved, Thadwick and everyone in Last Light Inn, save Jaheira , turn into Shadow-Cursed Undead . Leaving for Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] After a Long Rest , Thadwick, Manip Vidor and Fist Cyril journey towards Baldur's Gate with Florrick to seek reinforcements unaffected by the Shadow Curse : the Steel Watch . Thadwick is never seen again after departing. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Technical UID S_LOW_Client_000 UUID 9504e91f-b535-411b-ac3b-b4047150f93f Stats Human_Commoner Thalita Cross is a human customer of the Sorcerous Sundries shop in the Lower City in Act Three . “ Have you seen how much the prices have risen? Might as well be throwing my gold straight into the lava elemental! „ — Thalita Cross Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Thalita Cross and her son Heder Cross pause to see the water and lava elementals in the hall of the magic shop while Thalita looks for supplies. As they look, her son barrages her with a series of childish questions on elementals, and when they are going to go home. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Heder Cross Mumbus, why are lava elementals so hot? Thalita Cross Because they're made of fire, darling. Heder Cross If a lava elemental is made of fire, what am I made of? Thalita Cross Many things, I suppose. Blood, bile, phlegm, chocolate... Heder Cross Chocolate?! Thalita Cross Why of course, darling. Heder Cross Mumbus, if I were a lava elemental, I'd get a job in a restaurant. Thalita Cross Would you now? Heder Cross Mmhmm, 'cause I could cook food right on my body so I wouldn't even need an oven. Thalita Cross You make a fine point. Very efficient, you'd be. Heder Cross No fish, only chicken, beef, and vegetals. No pork either. Thalita Cross It'd be your body; you'd make the rules. Heder Cross Mumbus I'm bored. Thalita Cross Hello, bored, I'm your mother. Heder Cross That's not funny. Thalita Cross I think it's very funny. Heder Cross Well you're wrong. Thalita Cross If you're bored and I'm wrong, where have Jaremy and his mother gone? Heder Cross UGH! Heder Cross Can we go now? Thalita Cross In a little. I've got a bit more shopping to do. Heder Cross Then where are we going? Thalita Cross Figaro's , to pick up some hair ointment for your father. Heder Cross But dad doesn't have any hair. Thalita Cross That's why we need the ointment. Technical UID S_HAV_SpiritOfTheLand UUID 1403cdfd-0660-4592-90c6-bfe4607ccd3a Stats Tiefling_Child Thaniel is an unaging nature-spirit, appearing as a tiefling child, who embodies the spirit of the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Lift the Shadow Curse If Halsin joins the camp in Act One , he ultimately tells the party about how the spirit of the Shadow-Cursed Lands take the shape of a Tiefling boy -- Thaniel. Halsin reveals that Thaniel was his friend as a child: as Halsin grew into an adult, Thaniel stayed the same, and Halsin realised he had to become a protector instead of merely a friend. As a result of the Shadow Curse , Thaniel has been separated into two beings: an injured form of himself, who is unresponsive and asleep when first rescued by Halsin, and another who goes by the name of Oliver . Thaniel has been in contact with Art Cullagh over the time that Art has been trapped in the Shadow Curse, and Art can be heard singing about Thaniel until ⁠ Wake up Art Cullagh is completed. Art, much like Halsin, worries about Thaniel once he is awoken. Through the events of ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse , Halsin works with the party to rescue Thaniel, upon which he stays in the party's Campsite for the remainder of Act Two. Rescuing Thaniel is a prerequisite for recruiting Halsin as a Companion . Technical UID S_LOW_BasiliskGate_CrimeComplainer_001 UUID 461ce028-4293-4028-951b-a2c267b67216 Stats Dwarf_Commoner Thatmatt Oakhide is a shield dwarf at the Basilisk Gate Barracks in Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ If you're here to report something, don't bother - the Fist don't give a damn. „ — Thatmatt Oakhide Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Thatmatt is at the barracks with his wife Bruha Oakhide , looking to report an incident where he was struck on the head and mugged. Unfortunately for him, the Flaming Fist are making him wait to be heard. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Thatmatt chats occasionally with his wife Bruha Oakhide: Bruha Oakhide Ravengard's back, I heard. Bet he'll twist some arms, clean up the riffraff. Thatmatt Oakhide Duke-types don't care what goes on in our streets. Bruha Oakhide Ravengard's no upper-crust softie. He's in charge of the Fist, right? Thatmatt Oakhide If Ravengard had trained the Fist proper, they'd be out catching crooks, not turning a blind eye. Bruha Oakhide There's more Flaming Fist on the streets than ever - maybe they'll whip the place into shape. Thatmatt Oakhide Nah. They're too busy 'visiting' Mamzell's guys and gals. Bruha Oakhide They do that quite a bit, don't they? It's a shame. Thatmatt Oakhide A damn shame. Bruha Oakhide How's your head? That last mugger left a hell of a mark. Thatmatt Oakhide Still attached. Bruha Oakhide Har-har. We can come back another time, if you ain't feeling up to it? Thatmatt Oakhide Nah, let's see what Portyr has to say - she claimed she'd look into it. Thatmatt will also occasionally go to Manip Seyama to check on his status: Thatmatt Oakhide Oi - I've been mugged. I'm here about my case? Manip Seyama We're dealing with an increased number of complaints, sir - please wait your turn. Thatmatt Oakhide Right. I'll be outside. Thatmatt Oakhide Portyr herself said she was investigating my case? Manip Seyama Blaze Portyr will get to you when she gets to you. Thatmatt Oakhide I'm sure. Thatmatt Oakhide My wife and I have been waiting half the day - are you lot gonna help us or not? Manip Seyama Take that tone with me again, and you'll see no one. You'll be called when you're called. Technical UID S_LOW_Elfsong_FlamingFist_001 UUID 990ad029-d291-4788-86f9-dfceacdf771c Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Rusk is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ Move quickly and I'll let you go, stranger. We've had enough trouble for one day. „ — Thauniel Rusk Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Rusk together with Fist Aguta is standing watch inside the Elfsong Tavern , in its northwest corner. They guard the stairs leading to Belynne Stelmane's private room, blocking access to the scene of the Duke’s murder until Constable Gauntlet Devella Fountainhead finishes investigating it. When approached by the player character, Rusk tries to be strict and dismissive while turning them away, but Aguta reasons with him, allowing the party to proceed upstairs. This dialogue is enacted every time the couple of guards remain at the tavern, unless Aguta is defeated. In the latter case, Rusk also lets the player character go, telling them that the Fists have their share of problems already. Rusk (again along with Aguta and under command of Gauntlet Devella, if they are alive) can also be encountered at the entrance to Highberry's Home , in case the player character allowed the serial killer murder Cora Highberry at the Wine Festival. He is then found yelling warnings to the bypassers, so that they pass the place until the Constable is working on the crime. ## The Dark Urge
- **来源**: [The Dark Urge](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Dark_Urge)
- **分类**: Characters

This article is about the established character, and contains many spoilers.. For the more spoiler-free origin page, see The Dark Urge (origin) . This article contains sensitive content , including brief descriptions of realistic or graphic violence, cruelty toward animals, and sexual violence. The Dark Urge Main Writer Baudelaire Welch Role Special Origin Family Bhaal ("father"/creator) Orin the Red (Bhaalspawn relative) Sarevok Anchev (Bhaalspawn relative) Unnamed foster parents Minsc ("uncle", determinant) Hometown Baldur's Gate Stats Race Any, White dragonborn (default) Class Any, Sorcerer (default) Subclass Any, Storm Sorcery (default) Deity Bhaal Background Haunted One Character Origin The Dark Urge is an established character as well as a special origin in Baldur's Gate 3 . Suffering from amnesia, the Dark Urge remembers little but glimpses of their own past. “ My rancid blood whispers to me: kill, kill, and kill again. My ruined body yearns to reap death in this world, and when this foul Urge calls, it possesses my whole being. Injured beyond repair, I know nothing besides this: I must resist the Dark Urge, lest it consume my mind. I must discover who I was, and what happened to me. Before my twitching knife-hand writes a tragedy in blood. „ — The Dark Urge, fearing their dark desires in their Introduction cinematic. Contents 1 Description 2 History 2.1 Early life 2.2 The plan 2.3 Betrayal 3 The Urge 4 Past relationships 4.1 The Absolute 4.2 Bhaal and his Temple 4.3 Enver Gortash 4.4 Orin 4.5 Sarevok Anchev 4.6 Sceleritas Fel 5 Related Literature 6 See also 7 Quotes 8 Gallery 9 Notes 10 References Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Prior to their amnesia, the Dark Urge was a much more cold and calculated individual than their bloodkin, Orin the Red . [ 1 ] They believed in killing for killing's sake, preferring practical and simple methods over flair and grace, and took issue with extravagant or needlessly creative killings. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] They were deeply loyal to Bhaal and rarely disobeyed him. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] History [ edit section | visual editor ] “ The heart of a Bhaalspawn is a flipped coin that lands on its edge. Yours is a family set upon self-slaughter. „ — Volo , speaking to the player character on their dark inheritance Early life [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dark Urge is a Bhaalspawn, but unlike other Bhaalspawn, they were not born – Bhaal created them from a piece of his dead flesh. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] [ 9 ] They are the only Bhaalspawn who had the guarantee of murder, the Urge, woven into their blood. [ 10 ] The Dark Urge grew up outside the Cult of Bhaal , and was at some point taken in by a poor couple in Baldur's Gate . They had a relatively peaceful childhood for a time, before succumbing to the Urge and murdering their loved ones and foster parents. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] The plan [ edit section | visual editor ] Eventually, the Dark Urge became the leader of the Cult of Bhaal, and pledged to end all life in existence for their father Bhaal. [ 4 ] At some point, Orin the Red joined and became their second-in-command. [ 13 ] Enver Gortash contacted the Dark Urge after reestablishing worship of Bane , and the two formed an alliance upon discovering common goals. They were visited in their dreams by Bhaal and Bane, who named them their Chosen and commanded them to ally with Ketheric Thorm , the Chosen of Myrkul . Gortash and the Dark Urge hatched a plan to steal the Crown of Karsus in a heist at Mephistopheles' Vault by having Helsik open a gate to Mephistar for them. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] After the heist was successful, Gortash suggested that they use the Crown on the elder brain located in the illithid colony below Moonrise Towers . The Dark Urge agreed to the plan so that they could fulfil their pledge to their Lord: They would create an army of soulless mind flayers, and with the help of this army they would exterminate all life — including, as the last being alive, their own. Fully intent on eventually betraying the other Chosen, the Dark Urge joined Enver Gortash and Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers. [ 4 ] [ 13 ] [ 15 ] Betrayal [ edit section | visual editor ] At Moonrise Towers, the Dark Urge was treated like a god, [ 16 ] and although nobody knew their name or rank, they were shown the utmost respect. [ 17 ] The three Chosen initiated a raid on the mind flayer colony, and successfully used the Crown on the colony's elder brain, enslaving it to their will. [ 13 ] At some point during this, the elder brain came to respect the Dark Urge and intended to go along with their plan, impressed by their unmatched cruelty. [ 18 ] After the Dark Urge put the Crown on the elder brain, they were soon betrayed by their "sister" Orin the Red, who was jealous of Bhaal's favouritism. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] Orin pierced and opened the Dark Urge's skull with a dagger, and infected them with a tadpole which began to eat their liquidating brain, resulting in their amnesia, as well as them becoming the first True Soul. [ 21 ] [ 22 ] [ 23 ] [ 24 ] The Dark Urge was found by Kressa Bonedaughter who, impressed with their willpower and resistance to the elder brain's influence, began to study them. She cut them open and put them back together repeatedly over the course of several days in the Mind Flayer Colony , during which the Dark Urge was unable to speak or do anything but attempt to inflict violence on themselves or others. [ 25 ] [ 24 ] Noticing his wife's obsession and hoping to snap her out of it, Kressa's husband, Maghtew Budj , arranged for the broken and amnesiac Dark Urge to be sent off on the Nautiloid Ship , where they would soon wake up with no memories of themselves, or of their past. [ 26 ] [ 27 ] The Urge [ edit section | visual editor ] Disobeying Bhaal shreds his wayward child's mind completely See Also: The Dark Urge (Origin) and The Urge . The Dark Urge's unique quest, The Urge , has two distinct paths: The player character can either resist their urges or embrace them. If they resist the Urge and reject their legacy, Bhaal drains them of their unholy blood, resulting in their death, but Withers intervenes and brings them back to life, explaining that the loss of unholy blood through their heroism has not destroyed them but made them reborn as a new person. The rest of Act Three and its endings then play out the same as in other playthroughs beyond pre-existing dialogue differences from characters like the Netherbrain. If they embrace the Urge and accept their legacy, they become Bhaal's Chosen once again and are tasked with resuming their plan to control the Absolute and kill all other beings. If they follow through and take control of the Netherbrain, the Dark Urge is confronted afterward by either their romantic partner or the companion with the highest approval, who scolds or praises them (depending on who it is and how their companion quest ended) for bringing about the end of the world; they can either mercy-kill that companion, kiss them goodbye while stabbing them (if romanced), or release all the surviving companions, telling them to run away. The Urge then uses the Netherbrain's power to kill everyone in the city with conjured daggers, and as they do so they are given a premonition of their success, worshipping Bhaal under a blood-red moon as the last living thing in Faerûn. If they embrace the Urge but do not obey Bhaal's orders, Bhaal begins to shred their mind mere minutes after destroying the Netherbrain as the party is leaving to celebrate. The Dark Urge can either accept their fate, turn themselves into prison, attempt to fight back, or simply kill themselves before Bhaal gets the chance, reuniting with a proud Withers in the Fugue Plane. If the latter is not chosen, however, they show up in a shortened version of the Epilogue , bloodsoaked and insane due to the madness Bhaal has left them with, and they plot to kill all their former companions in their sleep while licking Bloodthirst . Past relationships [ edit section | visual editor ] The Absolute [ edit section | visual editor ] The Absolute, an Illithid Elder Brain evolved into a Netherbrain from the power of the Crown of Karsus , actually had a positive relationship with the Dark Urge before they were betrayed. The Dark Urge was the one who placed the Crown on the brain's head, and as such it revered them for giving it so much power. [ 28 ] [ 29 ] The brain especially respected the Dark Urge for the calculated cruelty of their plan to kill all living beings. It intended to follow the plan and let the Dark Urge control the army it would amass. [ 30 ] When the Dark Urge disappeared, the brain felt like it was abandoned as a slave to the other Chosen. [ 31 ] The Chosen fought like children without the Dark Urge's presence, so the brain changed its plan which would eventually lead to its freedom. [ 32 ] Bhaal and his Temple [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dark Urge commanded great respect, admiration, and devotion from the devotees at the Temple of Bhaal in Baldur's Gate. They inspired them with their sheer ruthlessness, staggering amount of victims, and the intelligence of their schemes and planning. [ 33 ] [ 34 ] Bhaal himself loved the Dark Urge the most of all his children as he had personally handcrafted the Dark Urge's body from his own flesh, and filled them with blood directly from his body, thus making them the perfect child in his eyes. [ 35 ] This also stands in contrast to the other Bhaalspawn who were born from myriad dalliances with mortal women of various races during the Time of Troubles . As such, the Dark Urge is considered a pureblood Bhaalspawn. [ 3 ] Bhaal's uncharacteristic level of love and concern for the Dark Urge is shown in the amount of attention that they receive from Bhaal, even after losing their memories. Most chaotic evil gods (including Bhaal) would discard a Chosen if they were no longer useful, such as Myrkul did with Ketheric after his defeat, but Bhaal went to great lengths to restore the Dark Urge to their former place, and made sure to guide and reward them until they returned to the Temple. [ 36 ] [ 37 ] Enver Gortash [ edit section | visual editor ] Enver Gortash and the Dark Urge had a close relationship, and Gortash considered the two of them to be friends. [ 38 ] [ 39 ] Gortash thought of the Dark Urge as his favourite Bhaalspawn and assassin, [ 40 ] [ 41 ] regarding them as one of his "nearest and dearest". [ 42 ] He respected the Dark Urge's cold-bloodedness and the slaughter they brought, [ 43 ] [ 1 ] as well as the mastery and control they had over their urges. [ 44 ] Gortash actually liked the Dark Urge while he only tolerated Orin. [ 45 ] The Dark Urge for their part always liked Gortash as well, [ 46 ] admiring his genius and the brilliance of his plans. Nonetheless, they did intend to betray him in the end when they would kill the world for Bhaal. [ 4 ] The two met when Gortash contacted the Dark Urge following his establishment of the cult of Bane. Gortash informed the Dark Urge that some of their ancestral torture racks and the bones of one of their relatives were displayed in the Hall of Wonders . The Dark Urge and Gortash teamed up to recover these artefacts, which eventually led to them forming an alliance when they discovered they had common goals. [ 13 ] [ 47 ] They shared coded correspondence with each other as they discussed the failures of previous Banites and Bhaalists and how they might avoid them. [ 14 ] [ 48 ] Gortash and the Dark Urge came up with the Absolute plot and worked together to steal the Crown of Karsus from Mephistopheles. [ 49 ] [ 13 ] When Orin betrayed the Dark Urge, Gortash was unaware of what had happened, only knowing what Orin had told him of the situation and that she had made a fool of the Dark Urge. [ 50 ] Gortash was unable to interfere as they had agreed not to meddle in each other's affairs. [ 51 ] When he reunites with the Dark Urge right before his coronation, Gortash is relieved to see them again and happily reminds them of their shared history. [ 40 ] [ 52 ] [ 53 ] He is eager to renew their old partnership and would be honoured to help the Dark Urge reclaim their birthright and kill Orin. [ 54 ] [ 55 ] Orin [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin was the Dark Urge's second-in-command, but the two of them always had a turbulent relationship. [ 13 ] Orin believed that the Dark Urge's murders were too mindless to be worthy of Bhaal and that the Bhaal Temple decayed because of them. She was jealous that the Dark Urge was the favourite of Bhaal even though their killing lacked beauty and talent, [ 19 ] while the Dark Urge thought that Orin did not understand that Bhaal only wanted death in numbers, and that she was wasting Bhaal's time by killing in an extravagant way. [ 3 ] When the Dark Urge started the Absolute plot with the other Chosen, Orin grew even more resentful. [ 19 ] She particularly despised Gortash's alliance with the Dark Urge, thinking that he was manipulating them. [ 56 ] In response, Orin decided to infect the Dark Urge with a tadpole so she could replace them and rebuild the Temple in her own image. [ 19 ] The Dark Urge was not aware of Orin's plan, as they believed that she worshipped them as much as all the other cultists. [ 33 ] After the Dark Urge placed the Crown of Karsus on the elder brain in Moonrise Towers , Orin attacked them, pierced their skull with a dagger and put a tadpole inside it. [ 21 ] She left them gravely injured on the floor of the Mind Flayer Colony , where the Dark Urge was found by Kressa Bonedaughter. She healed some of the Dark Urge's injuries to keep them from dying and began experimenting on them, unaware of who they were. [ 25 ] Orin eventually learns that the Dark Urge is still alive after they obtain the Astral Prism. [ 57 ] She abducts one of their party members and challenges the Dark Urge to a duel to the death in the Temple of Bhaal – the winner will be Bhaal's true Chosen and can claim her Netherstone. [ 58 ] Sarevok Anchev [ edit section | visual editor ] When the Dark Urge was the leader of the cult of Bhaal, Sarevok Anchev was Bhaal's Deathbringer and a Bhaalspawn relative of the Dark Urge. [ 59 ] He considered the Dark Urge to be the true master of murder, as they killed with no excesses or pretentions. [ 60 ] However, Sarevok was displeased that the Dark Urge did not have any children and hoped that they might one day have a child with Orin. [ 61 ] After the Dark Urge meets him again following their fall, Sarevok encourages them to fight Orin and believes they are the one to kill her. [ 60 ] Sceleritas Fel [ edit section | visual editor ] The fiend-like creature Sceleritas Fel served the Dark Urge and joined them during a series of grisly murders in Baldur's Gate. [ 62 ] He was sent by Bhaal on the day the Dark Urge reached their age of majority to guide them to their birthright as Bhaal's Chosen. [ 63 ] Sceleritas loved the Dark Urge dearly and revelled in their depravity. [ 64 ] [ 65 ] He particularly wants to be killed by the Dark Urge at one occasion. [ 66 ] His regular duties included managing the Temple of Bhaal, as well as helping the Dark Urge with torture and murder. [ 67 ] [ 68 ] The Dark Urge frequently needed Sceleritas' assistance, and Sceleritas believed the Dark Urge struggled to conduct themself properly without him. [ 69 ] [ 70 ] When the Dark Urge disappeared, Sceleritas missed them greatly and was deeply worried for their health. [ 71 ] Once he finds them again, he helps guide the Dark Urge and rewards them for murdering specific targets. [ 72 ] Sceleritas despises Orin and wants nothing more than for the Dark Urge to kill her and reclaim their position as Bhaal's Chosen. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dark Urge is a cannibal. [ 74 ] They can also eat the cooked dwarf meat from the Goblin Camp . According to Sceleritas Fel , the Dark Urge is a necrophiliac. [ 75 ] The Dark Urge has much in common with the protagonists of many other party-based RPGs, such as being an amnesiac and having a hidden connection to the villains of the game which is revealed over time. Notably, the protagonist of the previous Baldur's Gate games was also a Bhaalspawn. Even after being freed of the Urge, the Dark Urge still has access to unique, violent dialogue – with the Urge references removed – suggesting that at least part of the Dark Urge's available actions could be the result of their own character, rather than simply Bhaal's influence. [ 76 ] Immediately after the Dark Urge is brought back by Withers, the character can choose to revel in their freedom to be evil - without the Urge, and take joy in having fooled everyone to believe that they are innocent. The character can also embrace their goodness, which illustrates the virtue of a good-aligned Dark Urge, as they (and the player) truly choose to be good. Even if the Dark Urge gets rid of their father's blood, the Netherbrain still refers to the Dark Urge as "murder incarnate". [ 77 ] This may be in reference to Ed Greenwood's - the creator of the setting - revelation, prior to the game's release, that a Bhaalspawn can never fully remove Bhaal's essence. ( https://twitter.com/TheEdVerse/status/1396624159363448832 ). Or, otherwise, the Netherbrain just does not know, at this particular moment, that the Dark Urge was freed from Bhaal's essence. In a campaign where the Dark Urge is not chosen as an origin , the party can find the corpse in the Bhaal temple, which has the default appearance of the Dark Urge Origin, called " Fallen Bhaalspawn ", and was assumedly tortured and murdered by Orin . The Journal of Magthew Budj still references Kressa's obsession with the "pet" she used for her experiments, and the plot to have it sent to the Nautiloid Ship. Likewise, notes penned by the Dark Urge themself that refer to their collaboration with Gortash and a letter that berates Orin for her incompetence can be found regardless of whether the Dark Urge Origin has been chosen. If recruited, Minsc considers himself to be the Dark Urge's uncle. [ 78 ] References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 The Dark Urge's dialogue with Gortash during his coronation.
