EQP_Longsword_ScaleMail Trs. Gold_Pocket_Random Fist Ulthred is a human Flaming Fist at the Last Light Inn . He can help the party during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers . “ Hey. That's close enough. Artefact or no, I don't like the likes of you crashing our party. „ — Ulthred , after the party has been cleared. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Ulthred is at the Last Light Inn 's plaza. He arrived at the sanctuary on a mission to rescue Grand Duke Ravengard . He chats with Essius next to the fountain, and is suspicious of the party at first, not trusting them the slightest to rescue the Grand Duke from Moonrise. On the other hand, Essius attempts to talk him down and get him to open up to the party's aid. Through his chats with Essius, Ulthred appears to not trust Jaheira and seems eager to move out rather than sit idly. [ 1 ] If Marcus is exposed as a True Soul , Ulthred will be Surprised and join the fight against his summoned Crawling Claws . Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Ulthred frequently is amongst the Fists who avoid being Impaled , and runs up to fight with the Winged Horrors . If Isobel is not saved, he and everyone in Last Light Inn succumb to the Shadow Curse, save for Jaheira . Ulthred in particular, can be seen agonizingly transforming into a Shadow-Cursed Undead . Assault Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Isobel is saved at the Last Light Inn, and the Nightsong is freed from her cage and heads for Moonrise, Ulthred, along with the Flaming Fists Hadenwell , Helena , Nipawa and Rhed survive the first assault and assist the party in the remaining battle against Absolute forces. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] After the battle, provided he survives, Ulthred and the remaining Fists scout the Moonrise Towers Prison and enter a second battle against the Myrkulites Duckie Verish , Sarabayle , and Willinx Jindlebee , as well as a Death Shepherd and a horde of Necromites . The party can assist the Fists in this optional battle. If the Fists survive, they guard the prison until Ketheric Thorm is defeated. [ 4 ] After Ketheric Thorm is killed and the party leave for Act Three , Uthred disappears from the game entirely. All this standing around is making me antsy. Essius Got to have a plan first. Got to trust Jaheira to come up with one. Ulthred I don't. Essius I do. Ulthred That's why we're still standing around. Essius Duke Ravengard's still alive, you reckon? Ulthred He better be, or I'm a dead man walking. Essius Aren't we all? Ulthred Not as long as we can put up a fight, we're not. Essius Good man. Ulthred This place gives me the creeps. Essius Seen alleyways in Baldur's Gate that are plenty worse in their way. Ulthred Yeah? Essius Heapside narrows at night time? Two steps in and you're likely to become some dagger's new sheath. Ulthred Ain't my neck of the woods. Essius Count your lucky stars. All this standing around is making me antsy." - Ulthred "Got to have a plan first. Got to trust Jaheira to come up with one." - Essius "I don't." "I do." "That's why we're still standing around." ↑ Unlike the other Fists ( Helena , Nipawa , and Rhed ) that partake in the assault on Moonrise Towers , Ulthred is level 6 rather than level 7. ↑ Unlike the Harpers Antony , Essius , Lymn , and Naysa , Ulthred has no failsafe replacement Flaming Fist if he is killed before the assault. There is a Flaming Fist by the name of "Fist Hadenwell" in the game files, referred to as "S_MOO_AssaultFlamingFist_004" not too unlike the other Fists that appear during the assault. It is possible that this Fist was originally conceived as a replacement, or failsafe in the event of an untimely demise for Ulthred. ↑ Aubree , Gretta , J'ehlar , Rahir , and Ulthred are the only remaining Flaming Fists that can actually be found at Last Light Inn after Florrick and her retinue leave for Baldur's Gate. Technical UID S_LOW_HeapsideDarkGods_Civilian1 UUID 9e83c0a3-fc93-46e6-a856-615eedc07e99 Stats Elf_Commoner Umbrenne is an elven prophet of Talona , preaching to two civilians in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate during Act Three . “ Listen and submit to the Mistress of Disease! „ — Umbrenne Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Umbrenne is behind the Stormshore Tabernacle trying to convince Leary Dowse and Grundlgornn that everyone will die soon thanks to Talona, otherwise known as the Mistress of Disease . Leary is skeptical but Grundlgornn appears to fully believe the prophet. Umbrenne's attitude towards the party changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Leary Dowse Talona? You want to let Talona loose in our city? Umbrenne Poor, sweet fool - you speak as if the Plague-Crone is not already here, striding among us! Umbrenne Her power waxes, and soon the cycle will reach its zenith - should you want it to or otherwise. Leary Dowse And then what happens? Nothing good, I bet! Umbrenne And then all will perish so the cycle can begin anew! Grundlgornn Dear gods, he's right - it's too late to stop it now! Grundlgornn What do we do? What can we do? Umbrenne Embrace it! Umbrenne The Mistress of Disease loves us all - her fondest wish is to free us from the agonies we have created! Grundlgornn My lungs feel tight! It's happening already! Leary Dowse Oh calm down, would you? It's all in your head. Leary Dowse I've a good mind to get the Flaming Fist before people start chucking themselves into the Chionthar . Umbrenne All the Talontar await her blessings with open arms - and we pity those who would reject her. Umbrenne I will smile as her fevers sear me to my core. I will bask in her febrile radiance. Grundlgornn Oh gods, I don't want to die! Not yet! Leary Dowse You are not going to die. Umbrenne We are all going to die, my friend - some of us merely intend to do so in service of something greater. Umbrenne And to thank blessed Talona for the honour. DEN_Kid Umi is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . “ What? Oh yeah. 'Go for the heart.' „ — Umi , training at the Emerald Grove Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Umi is usually in the training area of the Grove alongside Gan and Ide . Of the three children, Umi seems most afraid and reluctant to train. The party can encourage or discourage him and the other children during an interaction with Asharak . If the party successfully dismantle the Goblin Camp , Umi packs for the road to Baldur's Gate and reveals that he left his training sword behind. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Umi survives into Act Two , he is seen dealing with Rolan alongside Ide at Last Light Inn's bar, where it is revealed that Rolan saved him and the other children. If ⁠ Resolve the Abduction is completed while Isobel is at Last Light, Mol is nonetheless kidnapped by a Winged Horror , and the tiefling children then argue about what to do. Umi is reluctant to search for her, stating that they do not know how to reach Moonrise Towers . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Umi travels to the refugee camp in Rivington with Ide. His attitude has changed dramatically since Act One, as he complains about doing chores when he should be killing cultists, while Ide is concerned about his behaviour. v t e Emerald Grove Characters CRE_Gith_Generic Gish Umr'a'ac is a gish in Crèche Y'llek during Act One . “ Ren'thil was examined in the zaith'isk recently. Haven't seen him since - perhaps he got sent back to scout Moonrise. „ — Umr'a'ac Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Gish Umr'a'ac can be initially found in the Crèche Y'llek Infirmary , near the bunk beds, pondering over a book. He viciously derides anyone infected with a ghaik tadpole, if spoken to as a non-gith; however, he reveals a softer side to gith characters, expressing concern over a colleague who went missing after using the Zaith'isk . He turns hostile after either of these circumstances: If Ghustil Stornugoss leaves her chamber after the encounter with the Zaith'isk , locking the party inside. ## Us
- **来源**: [Us](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Us)
- **分类**: Characters

Us In-game Model Portrait Voice / Actor Clare Corbett Role Attached Follower , Familiar Stats Size Small Type Aberration Race Intellect Devourer Us is an Intellect Devourer and possible Attached Follower which is in the Prologue of Baldur's Gate 3 aboard the Nautiloid , trapped inside the head of an Elf named Myrnath . “ Us. We are us. „ — Us , introducing itself Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] Us is trapped inside Myrnath, who is strapped to a chair with the top of his skull removed, in the second room aboard the Nautiloid. The player character or another party member can perform one of the following actions on it: [INVESTIGATION]  Inspect the exposed brain.  (DC 10) [MEDICINE]  Attempt a cerebral extraction, staying mindful of the swelling.  (DC 10  ) [STRENGTH]  Break the skull.  (DC 10) [DEXTERITY]  Gently prise the brain from the skull.  (DC 10) Passing an Ability Check frees it. If freed, it receives the Newborn condition for 10 turns after, temporarily lowering its max HP and AC. After the Devourer is freed, the interacting party member notices an opportunity to cripple it: [DEXTERITY]  Mutilate the brain.  (DC 15) [DARK URGE] [DEXTERITY]  Imagine a brain full of holes. A brain like your own.  (DC 15  ) Spare the creature - any injuries might weaken it. If one of the above checks are passed, Us becomes Lobotomised , reducing its Intelligence from 12 to 8, and its movement from 9 m (30 ft) to 6 m (20 ft). This condition is permanent and cuts Us from the rest of the hive mind, allowing it to attack other Intellect Devourers on the nautiloid without turning Us hostile. If the dexterity check is failed, Us flees instead, turning it and all other Intellect Devourers hostile. Once freed, Us urges the interacting party member toward the Helm . They can tell Us to go away, attack it, or ask it to join the party. Us disappears after the nautiloid crash at the end of the Prologue. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] If Us survives the Prologue, it moves to the Morgue within the Mind Flayer Colony . It has been labelled an aberrant and caged as a result. If freed, Summon Us allows the party to summon it as an ally once per short rest. As a summon, Us has 55 hit points and resistances to physical and Necrotic damage. Its appearance also changes; its veins become more pronounced and it gains an overall paler appearance, with a green glow on its underside. Its bonelike spines protrude more prominently, and its tendrils gain thorn-like protrusions. If Us is lobotomised in Act One, it retains this condition in Act Two. After leaving the Mind Flayer Colony, Us remains with the party. It mentions it will appear as a "kitty" to anyone besides the party. When asked if it wants to serve the Absolute, Us replies, "the Absolute does not care about Us, and we do not care about the Absolute" . LOW_CountingHouse_BhaalCultist Reaper of Bhaal Vagga is a member of the Cult of Bhaal , in the High Security Vaults in the Counting House in the Lower City . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During the ⁠ The High Harper quest, the party can go to the Counting House in hopes of catching up to Minsc. Inside the vaults, the party witnesses Minsc emerge from a Mimic and defeat it. 'Jaheira' then appears with a handful of Bhaalists including Vagga, and teleports away with Minsc, leaving the cultists to attack the party and the staff. Gold_Pocket_Wealthy Investigator Valeria is a Hollyphant who can be found in the Open Hand Temple . “ Another case closed, another bottle open! Huzzah to Valeri-AH! „ — Valeria Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders Valeria is investigating various murders happening in Baldur's Gate . Initially met while talking to Sister Yannis in the Open Hand Temple , she afterwards moves to Sharess' Caress , upstairs at X: 24 Y: 93 , getting drunk. Later on Valeria is kidnapped by members of the Cult of Bhaal . The party can find her at the Murder Tribunal , and either rescue or sacrifice her to Bhaal. If saved, Valeria is recruited for ⁠ Gather Your Allies . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Joyous Trumpet ( ) Blow air from your trunk, causing no damage at all but making a trumpet sound. Toot! Trumpet of Blasting ( ) Damage: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Thunder Blast a cone of celestial noise from your trunk that knocks creatures Prone . CON Save Recharge: Per turn Trumpet of Sparkles ( ) Damage: 4~32 4d8 ⁠ Radiant Blast forth a cone of celestial sparkles. Evil creatures have Disadvantage on the Saving Throw , and Good creatures take no damage. [ See Notes ] CON Save Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Investigation Priorities Letter from Devella Letter from Valeria Lower City Pass Mastodonian Memoirs, Vol. 1, Investigator Valeria (not actually dropped by Valeria, but found in a Traveller's Chest X: -1264 Y: 458 next to them in the Murder Tribunal ) Pending Tab: Investigator Valeria Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Valeria passing time at Sharess' Caress . Concept art by Jane Katsubo Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party defeat Sarevok Anchev and his minions at the Murder Tribunal and then move to rescue Valeria but do not promptly free her, she then constantly hurls insults and demands she be released immediately. Technical UID S_LOW_KurwinCoffin_Gravekeeper UUID 865e5b54-e3d6-4fa3-80b4-d5f0b31873d5 Stats LOW_KurwinCoffin_Gravekeeper Valmorba is a high half-elven gravekeeper in the Mortuary within the Graveyard in Baldur's Gate 3 . She is a devotee of Kelemvor and manages the graveyard. “ I am sorry for your loss, but it will be a tenday before I can take your departed. Maybe more. „ — Valmorba Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Valmorba is inside the Mortuary, preparing corpses to be placed in coffins. She tells the party she is busy, and that it will be a while before any new bodies can be buried. If the party have read Tough Letter back in Act One , Valmorba can be asked about the grave of an 'M Kurwin'. She gladly points out his grave "under the great willow with drooping branches" . If the party dig up and fight Bugthimble , and his fellow Kobolds, she is grateful that the bodies can rest now, but wishes there was another way instead of killing. The party can humorously ask for a Shovel and claim to tidy up the graves. [INTIMIDATION]  I'm not joking and I'm done asking. Give me a shovel. (DC 18) [DECEPTION]  The kobolds made a real mess out there. I'd like to help clean it up. (DC 15)  (If the kobolds have been met) [DECEPTION]  I need it to tidy up some of the older graves. I hate to see them neglected. (DC 18) Failing any check angers Valmorba such that she does not talk to the party again. Technical UID S_TWN_Hospital_ZealousAssistant_002 UUID a9e86a16-f426-4772-a187-39256c4568a1 Stats Surgeon_Nurse Sister Vanessa is an undead nurse in the House of Healing , situated in the town of Reithwin , during Act Two . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Sister Vanessa is one of the surgical assistants of Malus Thorm in the House of Healing . She and several other undead nurses are learning to grasp the science provided by Thorm on a struggling Distressed Patient . If the party encounter Vanessa or the other nurses, a dialogue with Malus Thorm is immediately triggered. During the dialogue, the interacting party member can convince Thorm to order the nurses to kill each other or to operate on himself. If they choose the latter, Vanessa remains neutral after the surgeon's demise, wandering the auditorium. If attacked afterwards, the other undead nurses become hostile. Vanessa is the only undead nurse who cannot be spoken to after Malus Thorm's death. Technical UID S_LOW_BlushingMermaid_Vanra UUID bfeac6a6-678e-46da-b873-cf7e4c7a1e4c Stats Human_Child Vanra , or Vanra Bergauz , is the subject of the quest Save Vanra . Vanra is Lora's daughter. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Save Vanra After meeting Lora and progressing her quest to save Vanra, the party can rescue Vanra from Auntie Ethel in the Blushing Mermaid . Ethel has eaten Vanra and is planning to let her stew in her belly until she has absorbed enough power to become a hag herself. Killing Ethel also kills Vanra unless steps are taken to prevent it. One way to do so is to craft the Hag's Bane using ingredients and a recipe acquired from a safe in Old Garlow's Place . This potion causes Ethel to become Nauseous and safely throw up Vanra. Alternatively, toggling Non-Lethal Damage and using unarmed or melee weapon attacks to knock Ethel unconscious allows the party to cut her open and free Vanra. Vanra is quite traumatized by this experience, quivering and calling for her 'mummy'. After a brief dialogue with the party she runs off to her mother at Lora's House . All of this only occurs if Ethel was denied access to Mayrina in Act One . Otherwise, Lora and Vanra are at their house in the Lower City and have little to say other than berating the party for barging into their home. Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_Servant_003 UUID b8109954-bc78-4fbd-ac69-ba22cf4775fa Stats Human_Rogue Varderola is a human servant of the Szarr Palace in Baldur's Gate . “ I scrub for the master. As you see. Tell the master I scrub for him. Always. „ — Varderola Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Varderola wanders back and forth along the far side of the foyer of the Szarr Palace. From time to time she falls on her knees and starts to rub the floor frantically, or cleans the statues guarding the side walls. If spoken to, she behaves as if thoroughly brainwashed, not even paying much attention to who she is talking to. The player character can ask Astarion (if he is in the party) about Varderola and other human servants in the palace, particularly about their strange behaviour. Astarion describes them all as "fanatics, here of their own free will and utterly devoted to Cazador <...>, idiots who brought this on themselves" [ 1 ] . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] If entering combat with the residents of the palace, Varderola joins them against the party. She and Vilhelm have the biggest chance to participate in combat in the Ballroom, as both are wandering about its door. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneak Attack (Melee) ( ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Weapon Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. Also works if you have an ally within 1.5 m (5 ft) of the target and you don't have Disadvantage . Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Per turn Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Dagger External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Varderola on the Forgotten Realms Wiki Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Despite Astarion's scornful and dismissive observations, in-game dialogue files for Varderola and other servants suggests that they too would likely have served their "new master" with the same ardour and humility. BG_Guard Fist Varone is a human wizard and a member of the Flaming Fist . She is in Rivington in Act Three. “ Not sure why you're poking around here. Just smells of pig piss. „ — Varone Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Varone, together with Fist Poole , Fist Rowan , Fist Madigan , Fist Lochan and Fist Broadhorn , under command of Manip Nestor , guards the goods inside the Requisitioned Barn , which have been donated for the benefit of refugees. Varone is one of three Fists stationed outside the barn; she looks over the side entrance. If any party member is spotted by Varone while trying to sneak into the barn without permission or is caught inside, one of the Fists orders them to go and speak with the Manip (which teleports the party to the entrance). Being caught a second time results in them being arrested. Unlike some other members of the Manip Nestor’s squad, speaking with Varone offers no changes to approval . CRE_Gith_Generic Youth Varrl is a student in the Classroom of Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Killing each other like this, it's stupid! „ — Varrl Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Varrl is in the midst of being reprimanded by his combat instructor, Sa'varsh Kethk . Kethk is disgusted by the youth's countenance, soft for a githyanki warrior, and seeks a challenger to fight the boy to teach him a lesson. If they are uninterrupted, a party member steps up to fight, or if an ensuing ability check fails, Varrl is killed. Alternatively, if the interacting party member persuades Kethk to spare him, or he is knocked out and then healed, Varrl can be spoken to afterwards. Varrl confesses his doubts on the teachings of Vlaakith but stops short of naming who the player character reminds him of. They can coax the name 'Orpheus' from him which causes him to reveal the story of Orpheus , and offers the party Orpheus, Prince of the Comet, Part Two: Sacrifice if he is persuaded to or he is shown the first part . The player character can betray Varrl's confidence by revealing his heretical education to Kethk, resulting in Varrl's death. Varrl may also reveal that he placed Orpheus' mark somewhere in the crèche, hoping to find another interested in Orpheus' story. The mark is on Vlaakith's portrait, a black line drawing of a streaking comet. More information about Varrl is in a book in the infirmary. Ghustil Stornugoss has healed Varrl 47 times, considers him a waste of resources, and asks Sa'varsh Kethk to "do something about him", which may have prompted the confrontation the party saw. When the crèche becomes hostile, Varrl disappears with the gith children, which may prevent the party from completing the quest. EQP_Longsword Vatas is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . “ Kind of you to open your camp to us. We'll have to return the favour in Baldur's Gate. „ — Vatas Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Vatas appears only at the tiefling camp celebration which happens during a long rest after successfully finishing ⁠ Defeat the Goblins . He takes the place of Danis , if he dies. He appears as one of the dead tieflings at the Goblin Celebration if the quest ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove is completed. Technical UID S_LOW_BhaalTemple_Cultist_02 UUID b69fe2eb-20ec-4d32-a146-ade9dc4df5eb Stats Human_Cultist_Bhaal_Reaper Reaper of Bhaal Velki is a human Reaper of Bhaal . “ A few hours on the rack and your hide should stretch to an acceptable proportion. A lampshade's worth at least. „ — Velki , to a Gnome non-Dark Urge character Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Velki is in the Bhaal Temple in the Undercity of Baldur's Gate . She patrols the upper balcony of the temple and never descends to the central altar ground. Velki remains neutral to the party unless attacked, regardless of whether or not the player character is the Dark Urge or Orin is killed. Velki is particularly interested in flaying her victims and tanning their skin afterwards. Unlike other Bhaalists, Velki cares only for her trophies. If the player character is not the Dark Urge, her one-liners before fighting Orin differ depending on their race. [ 1 ] If the player character is the Dark Urge , she asks they let her have Orin's carcass after the duel, and states she already asked Orin for the same favor in case the Dark Urge fails. After the fight, she is indifferent to whether the Dark Urge embraces or rejects their Bhaalspawn legacy. Technical UID S_INT_GithRoyalGuard04 UUID 3cce9a81-6755-44ce-a391-77fe4ffb68e2 Stats Githyanki_Gishra_Caster Zephyr Gish'ra Verik is a Gish'ra encountered in the Astral Plane at the beginning of Act Three. She is part of Orpheus' honour guard, and is fighting to free him. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] During a long rest at the end of Act Two , the party is suddenly woken to an attack by various githyanki monks. The party is then called into a portal by the Dream Guardian , where it is revealed it is The Emperor . It asks for the party's help, as Verik and the other monks are invading the Astral Prism to free the son of Gith himself Orpheus, who as it turns out is being held prisoner within the prism. The githyanki attack the party, regardless of the answer given to the Emperor. ## Verillius Receptor
- **来源**: [Verillius Receptor](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Verillius_Receptor)
- **分类**: Characters

Verillius Receptor is a High Inquisitor in service of Zariel , mentioned in Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Verillius Receptor is a Fiend who works as a High Inquisitor in service of Zariel . She has official permission to audit Raphael's collection. Verillius' true form is so ghastly and mind-scarring that she takes on guises when she comes to visit. Although she never appears in the game, she is especially feared by the Archivist in the House of Hope . Thus, the player character can deceive the Archivist by introducing themselves as Verillius, saying they are acting as Zariel's High Inquisitor. Successfully doing so allows the party to stay in the Archive without triggering an alarm. Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Deal with the Devil ⁠ Escape the Deal ⁠ Save Hope External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Verillius Receptor on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

Verryn But how could I ever choose? They're both... perfect. Verryn Red is so fresh, so exciting. She can be found near the Grey Harbour Docks , as part of Churg Elvek's mob, ready to bring Volo to "justice". Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] When approaching the Steel Watch Foundry , the party can come across Churg Elvek and his mob, as well as Volo who is tied up to some Smokepowder Barrels . Upon approaching, a cutscene plays out where Churg accusses Volo of harmful lies, conspiracies and fear mongering. The party can opt to intervene or simply draw their weapons after which Churg and his mob attack. Overview Combat Viconia DeVir Mother Superior of Shar In-game Model Identity Female Voice / Actor Jess Nesling Faction Church of Shar Hometown Cloister of Sombre Embrace , Baldur's Gate , Menzoberranzan in Northdark Stats Size Medium Type Humanoid Race Drow Subrace Lolth-sworn drow Class Cleric Subclass Trickery Domain Deity Shar Technical UID S_LOW_Viconia UUID b1ea974d-96fb-47ca-b6d9-9c85fcb69313 Stats LOW_HouseOfGrief_Viconia Eqp. EQP_LOW_HouseOfGrief_Viconia Trs. LOW_Grotto_Viconia Viconia DeVir is a drow cleric of Shar. She is the Mother Superior of the Shar enclave in Baldur's Gate . She is a returning character from Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn , where she was a companion. [ 1 ] “ L'il Alurl! For Shar! „ — Viconia's Battle Cry Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] For more detailed information see Viconia DeVir and Viconia DeVir . Viconia was born to House DeVir in the drow capital city of Menzoberranzan in Underdark . She was a priestess of Lolth for many years. To prove her faith, she was tasked with killing an infant in a ritual sacrifice to the Spider Queen. Viconia refused and her house fell out of Lolth's favour. It seemed that the only way for House DeVir to regain their goddess' favour was for Viconia to prostrate herself before the Spider Queen. Viconia became fed up with Lolth's ways and believed that she could survive without her. As a result, House DeVir was left vulnerable to attacks of other Houses. In desperation, Matron DeVir tried to sacrifice Viconia, but her wizard brother intervened and killed their mother. As punishment, Lolth turned her brother into a drider for his matricide and stripped Viconia of her clerical powers for breaking faith; Viconia then fled to the surface. Some time later, she found a new goddess to worship in Shar . Being a possible companion in the first and second Baldur's Gate game, she canonically at the very least met (if not traveled with) Gorion's Ward (the protagonist of previous games) and their group, as Jaheira and Minsc remember meeting her. Depending on the party's actions in those games, and if Viconia was their companion, she could have also met Sarevok . In the century that passed since Baldur's Gate II Viconia DeVir became the Mother Superior of the Sharran enclave in Baldur's Gate . She previously had a grander enclave in Waterdeep , but Lady Shar commanded her to raze it and kill all her loyal followers. As a reward for her loyalty, Viconia was charged by Shar with a new mission: take a daughter of Selûne and, in time, turn and raise them to be Viconia's replacement as the Mother Superior in Baldur's Gate. [ 2 ] At some point she likely surrendered a part of her memories to the Mirror of Loss . Viconia and her group then ambushed a Selûnite family in process of a coming-of-age ritual for their half-elven daughter Jenevelle Hallowleaf. Her parents were captured and imprisoned, while the girl was raised a cleric of Shar under a new name – Shadowheart . While obedient to her goddess' charge, Viconia has long been resentful of Shadowheart being chosen to replace her as Mother Superior and treated Shadowheart in a very harsh way. For example, Shadowheart always dreamed of becoming a Dark Justiciar , but Viconia thwarted any attempts at doing so. [ 3 ] Finally, shortly before the game is set to begin, Viconia tasks Shadowheart and other most skilled but expendable followers [ 4 ] with retrieving the Mysterious Artefact that can help the Sharrans against the Absolute . If Shadowheart happens to fail in this task, Viconia might still keep her place as Mother Superior and maintain plausible deniability with Shadowheart's demise due to Shar's known displeasure with those who fail her. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] “ Aluve „ — Viconia on departing after she has been spared by the party Viconia, as the Inquirer of Grief On pursuing ⁠ Daughter of Darkness , it is necessary to visit the Cloister of Sombre Embrace , which is located in Sharran Ruins under the House of Grief . Viconia DeVir, disguised as the Inquirer of Grief , resides there and provides the Mapping of the Heart for those in need of Sharran guidance. If the player character or Shadowheart undergoes the Mapping, Viconia reveals her identity by removing her hood, and invites the party to the cloister. She explains that she knows the party have the artefact in their possession and she needs it to destroy the Absolute. If Intimidation or Persuasion checks are passed, then Viconia relents. However, she demands Shadowheart to be handed over to her. The party can either agree, starting the ⁠ Surrender Shadowheart to Viconia quest, or refuse, starting a fight. If Shadowheart is a Dark Justiciar, she can convince some of the cultists to fight along with the party, taking over the cloister after Viconia's defeat. [ 8 ] In the room where the Mapping of the Heart takes place, Jaheira , Minsc , or both of them – if they are present – comment on the reunion with Viconia. If the meeting results in combat, Viconia manifests the fears that she learned from the party: turning into a wolf to scare Shadowheart or – if the player character told her their fear of becoming one – temporarily turns the player character into a mind flayer. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] If Shadowheart is handed over to Viconia, Viconia becomes an ally in the final battle providing Nightbringer's Shadow Adepts support. Alternatively, if Shadowheart replaced Viconia as the Mother Superior, the same support is provided by Shadowheart instead. If Viconia is still alive at the end of the fight, it is possible to speak with her again and either let her go or kill her. If they are present and not disguised , Jaheira or Minsc admonish her directly on how she lost her way. Choosing to spare Viconia earns approval with Jaheira, while choosing to kill her earns approval with Minsc (approval is not lost with the other, if both are present). If spared, Viconia says "Aluve" in reluctant gratitude as she departs, and is not seen again in the game. Changes to Viconia's backstory [ edit section | visual editor ] Viconia's state in Baldur's Gate 3 is partially reflective of her default ending in Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal , wherein she found a Sharran cult in Waterdeep. However several differences can be found: In her original epilogue [ 11 ] Viconia killed all cult members due to one's betrayal, shrugging off the admonishment of her goddess, which mirrors her early rebellious actions against Lolth . She then wandered the Realms and stopped several crises with the help of Drizzt Do'Urden , including saving the elven city of Suldanessalar, for which she received honours from Queen Ellesime . Her fate following the events above was unknown. In Baldur's Gate 3 , Viconia's motive behind the Waterdeep slaughter was changed to obeying Shar's order, and she remained obedient to her goddess ever since. Despite her having a history of refusing to sacrifice a child to another goddess, she performed all of Shar's tasks faithfully, such as abducting children and torturing their relatives, similar to what Lolth did to her beloved brother – which caused her nightmares in the previous game. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Viconia DeVir/Combat Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] It is not necessary to kill Viconia to obtain these items. If defeated, she can be looted before the final conversation cut-scene with her. Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_Bedrooms_DeadGirl UUID 3a033a94-5313-4f28-94ef-f1f784aa8d74 Stats Human_Child Victoria Onufrio is a deceased human child found in the Szarr Palace guest room during Act Three . She has the rather unusual condition Sapping Curse . Contents 1 History 2 Involvement 3 Speak with Dead 4 Related items 5 Notes and references History [ edit section | visual editor ] Victoria was the 'pureblooded' daughter of one of Cazador's Vampire Spawn , Leon Onufrio , who brought Victoria to the palace on Cazador's insistence. By consistently remaining his 'favoured spawn', Leon and Victoria were able to stay in the favoured spawn bedchambers together, where they were apart from the rest of the vampires. [ 1 ] While at the palace, Leon became fearful for Victoria's life as other spawn showed interest in her. As a Sorcerer , he imbued her with a counter-curse in the event of an attack against her person, making her a "necrotic booby-trap" . [ 2 ] Leon was finalising a deal with someone identified as Figaro, most likely Figaro Pennygood , to procure a disguise for Victoria's escape. [ 1 ] However, she was found by the spawn Dalyria , who brought her back to the palace. Dalyria was searching for a cure to vampirism and thought Victoria's young blood could help. [ 2 ] She bit into Victoria, killing her and triggering her necrotic curse. [ 3 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Victoria can be found in the Szarr Palace guest room, which as Astarion explains is where 'guests' were kept until Cazador took them. He notes that there had been no prior deaths in the room, and that "something strange happened to that girl" . Her body and curse behave as an obstacle to obtaining the Kozakuran Dictionary found in the guest room. The Sapping Curse can be removed with Remove Curse , or an Elixir of Necrotic Resistance can be used to move past her. If neither are available, as Victoria is a child and weighs little, she can be (somewhat morosely) tossed across the room, away from the rest of the objects within it. [ 4 ] If done in turn-based mode, this only incurs a single tick of damage. The door to the guest room has the condition Sinister Seal , which applies one round of sapping curse when opened normally. Opening the door with through Mage Hand avoids taking damage. Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] It was possible to use Speak with Dead on Victoria's corpse until Patch #5 . Some of her then removed dialogue potentially contradicted in-game lore, such as saying that she was an orphan brought to Cazador by Dalyria. Who are you? Victoria Victoria... orphan... How did you end up here? Victoria Lady promised me food... shelter... took me here... Do you know anything about the dictionary I found? Victoria Lady who brought me here carried it... Hid it from monster... What lady? Do you know her name? Victoria Dalyria... What did the monster look like? Victoria Tall... long hair... terrible eyes... What happened when you got here? Victoria She held me... bit me... blood everywhere... Did the lady kill you? Victoria Tried but... couldn't drink... retching and gagging... then monster arrived... Victoria Furious... she tried to disobey... not drink thinking creatures... he dragged her away... HAV_Survivor Manip Vidor is a senior Manip of the Flaming Fist . Appearing alongside Counsellor Florrick in Last Light Inn , he is her second-in-command during their attempted rescue of Duke Ravengard . “ I'd rather lend you my blade, but you'll have to make do with my luck. „ — Vidor , before his departure Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] Initially the commanding officer of a mission led by Florrick to rescue Duke Ravengard, Vidor and the rest of the Fists were waylaid by the dangers of the Shadow-Cursed Lands and found refuge with the Harpers of Last Light Inn . Vidor is at the inn, discussing with Florrick the possibility that Art Cullagh is their solution for rescuing Duke Ravengard. Vidor is unhappy with waiting and would rather lead a frontal assault on Moonrise Towers with reinforcements from the city, but lacks authority to contradict Florrick. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] If Florrick is not rescued from Waukeen's Rest in Act One , Vidor does not appear in the game. Resolve the Abduction [ edit section | visual editor ] When Marcus attacks the inn and attempts to kidnap Isobel during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Vidor is not affected by the Impaled condition and is instead Surprised . He may join the battle on his own without being affected by any conditions if the door to the room he is in is opened after the encounter starts. If Isobel is not saved, he and everyone in Last Light Inn, save Jaheira, turn into Shadow-Cursed Undead . Leaving for Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] After a Long Rest , Vidor, Fist Cyril and Fist Thadwick journey toward Baldur's Gate with Florrick to seek reinforcements unaffected by the Shadow Curse : the Steel Watch . Manip Vidor is not seen again after his depature. Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_Servant_001 UUID 61564290-a0f8-457e-aba1-3697ad9ea0d4 Stats Human_Rogue Vilhelm is a human servant of the Szarr Palace in Baldur's Gate . “ You're to witness the master's ascension? Oh what fortune. What blessed eyes! „ — Vilhelm Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Vilhelm wanders back and forth in front of the sealed Ballroom doors of the Szarr Palace. Unlike other servants, he does not clean or rub anything, though he might utter phrases about it while stalking around. Vilhelm is the only living servant of Cazador Szarr who can speak to the party in a coherent way. Through various Deception or Intimidation rolls while talking to him, the party can find out how to get downstairs (particularly, about the Szarr Family Ring ) and about Godey , who is in charge for keeping the doors shut throughout the ceremony. If Astarion is in the party, Vilhelm immediately recognizes him and asks why he is not attending the ritual. The player character can also ask Astarion about Vilhelm and other servants in the palace, especially their strange behaviour. Astarion describes them all as "fanatics, here of their own free will and utterly devoted to Cazador <...>, idiots who brought this on themselves" [ 1 ] . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] If fighting with the residents of the palace, Vilhelm joins them against the party. He and Varderola have the biggest chance to participate in combat in the Ballroom, as both are wandering about its door. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneak Attack (Melee) ( ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Weapon Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. Also works if you have an ally within 1.5 m (5 ft) of the target and you don't have Disadvantage . Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Per turn Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Dagger Key to Ramparts Door External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Vilhelm on the Forgotten Realms Wiki Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Despite Astarion's scornful and dismissive observations, in-game dialogue files for Vilem and other servants suggests that they too would likely have served their "new master" with the same ardour and humility. Technical UID S_WYR_SteelWatcherNerds_Gnome UUID 256dbbf7-237a-4ef1-a640-ba9585b0660d Stats Gnome_Commoner Vinegaroon is in Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . “ Imagine seeing a Watcher power-up for the first time - my heart flutters at the thought! „ — Vinegaroon Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Vinegaroon, together with Trinigan Gazotts and Slozy Arminifer , is standing near Carm's Garms , discussing spiritedly the technical features of the Steel Watchers . The three of them are fascinated by this latest novelty in maintaining order, and meet every day to discuss the automatons' specialties. Recently Vinegaroon tried to study a Steel Watcher's optical system. To that end, he climbed upon one of them, and was sent into a brief flight. He and his mates see this as yet another reason to be delighted with the invention. If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, idle banter of the three enthusiasts changes: they now are saddened because of it, and blame the cult (of the Absolute) for doing this. v t e Wyrm's Crossing Characters Cultists of Bhaal Gavv Hemm Lunn Zoll Flaming Fists Azari Edwynna Elin Falcäo Gai Meadows Mîran Shah Carm's Garms Naaber Slozy Arminifer Trinigan Gazotts Vinegaroon Danthelon's Dancing Axe Geraldus Limmy Safyre Somi Tairn Fraygo's Flophouse Bernyr Crak Dalyria Dashkent Moliver Drim Ffion Goldgrind Petras Rilia Rosanna Sharess' Caress Amira Arfur Gregorio Borgus Elamin Chapeau Chorizo Cillian Earspoon Embry Ghainemeir Hakeem Irenya Jara Kira Korrilla Laila Naoise Nallinto Nym Orlith Raphael Rhol Sorn Orlith Surixana Valeria Voss Other Kali Hammerhand Neno Quilltop Traders Carmen Pennygood Entharl Danthelon Glynda Oltower Griska Hoots Hooligan Queelia Arvis Roberon Silt Stylin' Horst Thodric Shedeveer Velson Oakes Locations Carm's Garms Danthelon's Dancing Axe Fraygo's Flophouse Sharess' Caress The Velveteen Elixir Quests Deal with the Devil Deal with the Gnomes Find a way into Wyrm's Rock fortress Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion Free Orpheus Help Kith'rak Voss Investigate Cazador's Palace Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders The Githyanki Warrior The High Harper

WYR_Circus_GenericPerformer Viola Silvertongue is a human Bard performing at the Circus of the Last Days in Act Three . “ Viola Silvertongue - at your service. Or I will be, once my set is done! „ — Viola Silvertongue Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Viola performs alongside Calliope Blingsdorf and plays the Flute . She is confident and charismatic. If a bard party member talks to Viola, she assumes they are another hire of Lucretious , views them as competition, and is quite rude and haughty, telling the talking party member to walk off a cliff. [ 1 ] Viola is known to be opposed to Lucretious hiring any other bards - other members of the circus may comment on this, including Klaus [ 2 ] and Medrash . [ 3 ] Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Combat Inspiration ( + ) Inspire an ally to add a +1d6 bonus to their next Attack Roll , Ability Check , Saving Throw , weapon damage, or Armour Class . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Perform (Flute) Play a tune to attract and delight those around you. Tasha's Hideous Laughter ( + ) Leave a creature Prone with laughter, without the ability to get up. Technical UID S_LOW_CazadorsPalace_RitualRoom_Spawn_004 UUID a4dc8e21-833c-4469-a72b-1969c688b8a4 Stats Vampire_Spawn Violet is a vampire spawn bound to Cazador , and one of Astarion's siblings. She may appear at camp or Cazador's Dungeon during Act Three . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] After reaching the Lower City , Violet, Yousen , Aurelia and Leon visit camp at night and attempt to kidnap Astarion. She and her fellow spawn can be persuaded that Astarion will help them, but are compelled to attack regardless. Failing to defeat them before reducing Astarion to 1HP results in their abducting him back to Szarr Palace . Violet and the other spawn are later encountered in Cazador's Dungeon, trapped by ritual runes as Cazador prepares for his ascension. Technical UID S_LOW_SWS_NearMermaid_FF_000 UUID f306cae3-65b2-4312-b52c-2bc53aa79fde Stats FlamingFist_Human_Melee_Attacker Fist Virry is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . She can be found in the streets of the Lower City in Act Three . “ These sad little citizens actually think we'll let them off the hook if they complain loudly enough. Ha! What dopes. „ — Virry , on the concerns of the traders whose wine they are confiscating Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Virry is patrolling the streets of Lower City with Fist Rockbothem and a Steel Watcher . She and her fellow Fists can be found at the Grey Harbour Docks at X: -171 Y: -102 , bullying traders Rox Flunter and Cinna Brewcellar and trying to confiscate the wines they brought to the city under the pretense of smuggled goods. Both Fists seem to feel their impunity, being accompanied by an automaton . After the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, Virry remains at the same place, complaining that shaking the civilians down was much easier with a Steel Watcher behind them. Saer Deelia , Flaerian and Yeller Dawg nearby try to reason with the guards, but to no avail. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Halberd Damage: 6~15 1d10 + 5 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Fist Virry You're a little slow, but you get the point eventually. Citizen. Rox Flunter But this wine is already paid for, it's due at the Elfsong Tavern! Fist Virry If it's already paid for, you lose nothing by delivering it to me instead. Right, citizen? Rox Flunter If this was ruby tonic, I'd let you have it. Fist Virry If this was ruby tonic, you could keep it. After the steel watch foundry is destroyed, Flaerian can be found talking to a couple of merchants: Saer Deelia I think it's outrageous that Fists should harass people in a nice neighbourhood! Fist Virry Formerly nice neighbourhood. Now back off, honey. Flaerian I think your methods are somewhat unorthodox, Saer Fist. Fist Virry Hard times, citizen. Let's not let them get any harder, eh? Flaerian Saer Fist, I think you should reconsider your tactics here. Please. Yeller Dawg Yeah, Saer Fist . Show him why you're called Flaming Fists! Hee hee! CRE_Gith_Generic Youth Vis'kiir is a member of a new githyanki generation hatched and raised in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Look, I don't have time to talk to you, istik - this place isn't going to clean itself. „ — Vis'kiir Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Vis'kiir stands in the corridor at its western T-junction, near the portrait of Queen Vlaakith . If the party vandalize the portrait by drawing a new face on it, Vis'kiir rushes over to clean the markings, muttering about what might happen if the Inquisitor notices. Vis'kiir is the only character who might catch the party vandalizing the portrait. If caught, he becomes upset, but this does not otherwise bear any negative consequences for the party. If Vis'kiir is spoken to without interacting with the portrait, he only says that the Crèche will not become clean on its own. If the player character is githyanki, the youth rants about his cleaning duties and ask the player character whether these were that bad at their own crèche. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_RetiredFist_Dwarf01 UUID a94d18f7-23ec-4f4b-868a-d6feaf9beaae Stats Dwarf_Commoner Vistra is a retired Flaming Fist who idealizes the past. She can be found with a group of retirees in the Lower City during Act Three . “ Fist these days cannae take a piss without a Steel Watcher helpin' them aim. It's pathetic. „ — Vistra Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Vistra is in Bloomridge Park lamenting the state of the Flaming Fists to Avourel , Eldaernth , and Thokki . She believes the Fists are too reliant on the Steel Watch and no longer know how to properly fight. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Vistra ' Absolute ' this... 'end of the world' that... These young folk've no idea how good they've got it. Eldaernth Come off it, Vistra. You've been doing this same rant for years. Avourel Yeah, the first lot of young folk you said it about are old folk now! Vistra Piss off, the lot of youse. Eldaernth You're remembering the past pretty fondly, Vistra. Bit too fondly. Vistra What d'you mean? Eldaernth You telling me you'd have refused the Steel Watch's help on Returning Day a decade ago? Vistra You'll, uh... remind me? Eldaernth Big horrible beast? Slaughtered Duke Adrian? We could do bugger all about it? Thokki Lost a lot of good men that day. Vistra You make a good point, Eldaernth. Eldaernth You've known me long enough, Vistra. When haven't I? Vistra We could've used the Steel Watch back in the day. But that's because we fought actual threats. Back when the Fists were real Fists. Not bloody... Avourel Limp gloves. Eldaernth So, Vistra. You reckon we'd still be better Fists than the current cohort? Vistra Peace of piss, mate. Easy. Yes. Eldaernth Great. So let's get you out of that chair and into your chain mail, then? Show the young lot how it's done? Vistra Uh... Well... Thokki My armour's not fit for years. Avourel Yeah, to be honest? Thought of holding a pike makes my back ache. Eldaernth It's a young man's game. Right, Vistra? Vistra 'Spose. Vistra Look, all I'm saying is they've got it easier these days. Thokki Yeah, we didn't have these big metal bastards running the streets back in my day. Eldaernth Thanks to the bloody Iron Crisis we barely had any metal back then. Vistra You're right, you're right. We Fists had to proper fight back then. We knew how to watch each other's backs. Eldaernth Helm give me strength. Eldaernth Not seen action like that in a while.  (After the ambush in Bloomridge Park) Vistra Those cultists are lucky they were on the other side of the park. Lucky. Avourel You'd have taken them, would you, Vistra? Vistra Reckon so. Eldaernth Bollocks. These days we'd sooner throw our backs than a proper punch. Thokki Well, I, for one, count my lucky stars it happened elsewhere. Avourel Same here. ## Vlaakith
- **来源**: [Vlaakith](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Vlaakith)
- **分类**: Characters

Vlaakith The Lich Queen Artwork Model Portrait Symbol Full Name Vlaakith CLVII Voice / Actor Bethan Dixon Bate Stats Race Undead , formerly githyanki Technical UID S_GLO_Vlaakith UUID 6b00f9fb-b932-4ac9-8ed8-1ca89dd7d247 Stats Githyanki_Melee Trs. CRE_Gith_Generic Vlaakith CLVII is the current and undying ruler of the Githyanki . She oversees their operations in all the planes, and at the time of the events of Baldur's Gate 3 , is actively seeking the Mysterious Artefact that was stolen from her. She can also be chosen as a patron deity by githyanki clerics . “ We are githyanki. We move mountains, we snuff out stars, we shake the planes. „ — Vlaakith Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Vlaakith is the imperious queen of the Githyanki. A deathless lich of nearly-divine strength, she has used the prior millennia to fashion githyanki society around her image, imbuing in her gith subjects a loyalty bordering on fanaticism. Being chosen by Vlaakith to 'ascend' is the ultimate reward for the conquest exacted by githyanki warriors. In reality, however, this 'ascension' is the utter consumption of the warrior's soul into Vlaakith's own life essence, providing the fuel that allows her to maintain undying life and furthering her relentless pursuit of divine power. Through commonly accepted lore, Vlaakith CLVII is the blood descendent of Vlaakith I, herself the successor of the original gith leader Gith . Vlaakith I built her inheritance on the claiming to possess the prodigious psionic powers that allowed Gith to liberate her people from Illithid slavery. However, this is a fable, carefully crafted and jealously guarded; Gith's son Orpheus was the only inheritor of her unique powers of Illithid suppression. To cement her power, Vlaakith I had Orpheus imprisoned in the Astral Prism and erased nearly all mentions of him from githyanki histories. The Lich Queen Vlaakith CLVII continues on her ancestors' legacy by doing all in her power to prevent the truth about Orpheus from becoming known, thrusting into motion the opening events of Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] After producing the Artefact for Ch'r'ai W'wargaz or slaying him in combat, Vlaakith appears as a massive planecaster projection before the party in Crèche Y'llek . Vlaakith, attempting to convince the party the Astral Prism has been corrupted. She orders the party to venture inside the Artefact, which she calls the Astral Prism, to kill its inhabitant, claiming they have corrupted the Prism. Defying Vlaakith by asking her to kill the being inside the prism herself, treating her with enough continuous disrespect, failing the Detect Thoughts check to read Vlaakith's mind, or revealing Shadowheart as the thief who stole the prism, results in her casting a Wish spell on the party, wishing for the party to End, resulting in an instant Game Over . If the party enter the Astral Prism with W'wargaz still alive, upon their return, it is revealed that Vlaakith has ordered him to execute the party, naming Lae'zel a traitor if she is present. This betrayal has a significant effect on Lae'zel's companion quest ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior . Act 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lae'zel is chosen as origin or kept as a companion , Vlaakith will project herself to the party once more during a Long Rest after they discover the truth about Orpheus. She reiterates her demand that Lae'zel kill Orpheus, this time promising to anoint Lae'zel as Baht t'Vlaakith , Vlaakith's Chosen. The decision Lae'zel makes at this point will, with finality, result in her embracing or rebuking Vlaakith. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lae'zel is selected as origin and she chooses to ⁠ Control the Elder Brain , she can rally the Githyanki to launch a direct assault on Vlaakith's domain with the power of the Absolute behind her, which results in Githyanki rebels invading Vlaakith's throne room and her composure starting to break. If Lae'zel remains loyal to Vlaakith and leaves to ascend, she meets Vlaakith in her throne room (potentially alongside her romanced partner), where Vlaakith consumes her soul for herself. Related characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Ch'r'ai Har'rak , Paladin of Vlaakith Ch'r'ai Tska'an , Avatar of Vlaakith Ch'r'ai W'wargaz , Inquisitor of Vlaakith Lae'zel Orpheus , Prince of the Comet Voss Related locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Crèche K'liir ⁠ Crèche Y'llek Quotes [ edit section | visual editor ] “ Vlaakith herself. She is both the sun that blinds us and the void that contains us. Praise be. „ — Lae'zel Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Warlocks have a unique bit of dialogue when Vlaakith is first encountered in Act One . The Warlock's Patron takes a distinct interest in Vlaakith and sizes her up, saying "Not quite a god, but not far off" , and advises caution. Also, he joins the fight as soon as he notices any commotion, siding with other followers of Bane . Technical UID S_GLO_Volo UUID 2af25a85-5b9a-4794-85d3-0bd4c4d262fa Stats GLO_Volo Eqp. EQP_Unarmed Trs. DEN_Volo_Trade Volothamp Geddarm , or Volo , for short, is a Camp Follower in Baldur's Gate 3 . He can be first found at the Sacred Pool during Act One , interviewing a bear. Volo is a recurring character in Forgotten Realms media and a returning character from Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal . “ Our fates are bound, my wisdom vast, I dearly hope our kinship lasts! „ — Volo 's dedication written in Volo's Guide to Baldur's Gate (Signed) Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.2 Act Three 3 Companion approval 4 Combat 4.1 Attacks and actions 5 Speak with Dead 6 Store 7 Related literature 8 Gallery 9 Notes 10 References 11 See also 12 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Volothamp Geddarm is a widely travelled wizard, most known for his guidebooks such as Volo's Guide to Monsters and Volo's Guide to Waterdeep . Elminster , an occasional fact checker and editor of his books - notably Volo's Guide to Monsters - has said he is prone to "exaggeration, misrepresentation, and flights of fancy". [ 1 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Volo is first located at the Sacred Pool in the Emerald Grove . If the player character interacts with him there, he requests an interview on the recent goblin assault against the Grove. Telling him a false story results in the ⁠ A Very Tall Tale inspiration to characters with the Entertainer background. He then departs for the Goblin Camp , intent on documenting goblin behaviour from the inside. The party later finds Volo as a captive to the goblins, who force him to act as their jester and "entertainment". After faltering his performance, Volo is locked in a cage inside the Defiled Temple . If rescued, the party can invite him to their Campsite and the following inspiration is gained: ⁠ The Bard with Nine Lives ( Folk Hero background) ⁠ A Man of Many Talents ( Noble background) If he is not freed before the conclusion of the Grove's quest line, Volo remains in the Goblin Camp awaiting rescue. If the goblins' drinks are poisoned before triggering Volo's cut scene, he is not imprisoned, but still awaits rescue. If Volo is pickpocketed during his dialogue after opening the cage door, he does not drink a Potion of Invisibility . Instead, he stands still and initiates combat with any patrolling goblin who sees him. The party members are not forced into combat, even after Volo dies. His attempted eye surgery having failed, Volo offers the player character a replacement. If Volo arrives at the party's campsite, he offers to remove the Mind Flayer Tadpole from the player character's skull via a highly questionable eye surgery. Agreeing to his eye surgery ends in catastrophe, but the player character receives Volo's Ersatz Eye as compensation, granting a permanent enhancement . This offer is only available during Act One and Act Two . If the player character accepts Volo's surgery, he leaves afterwards. If Wyll speaks with him, selecting the option "Sorry, but I have no eyes left to spare" causes him to leave camp as well, with no compensation. At the conclusion of the Emerald Grove questline, Volo attends the celebratory party regardless of which side the party aligned with. If the Grove was protected, he sings a song. If the Grove was attacked, he is kept in a cage (for his own protection) and asks the player character pointed questions as to how they justify slaughtering the refugees . If the player character does not allow Volo to perform eye surgery, he remains in the camp until the end of Act Two. He does not have any new dialogue, but he can act as a vendor via the "Trade" button in the dialogue UI. Like other traders, his inventory continually refreshes, in his case with five Potions of Animal Speaking and various scrolls which roughly match the party's level, including up to Level 6 spells. Being caught pickpocketing Volo has no consequence besides him briefly fleeing and losing some opinion towards the offending character. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] In Baldur's Gate , Volo is trapped in front of the Steel Watch Foundry near the Grey Harbour Docks , tied to a rail cart loaded with eight Smokepowder Barrels and with an angry mob ready to execute him. If the party rescue and speak with him after, he appears again at camp and offers the book Regarding the Slayer . Saving Volo again grants the inspiration ⁠ Saving a Fellow Tale-Spinner to party members with the Charlatan background. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Allowing Volo to perform his operation –   -1   -1   -1   -1 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Volo has no spell slots, but knows the following spells: Colour Spray ( + ) Blind creatures up to a combined 33 Hit Points . Range: Self Grease ( + ) Cover the ground in flammable grease. It becomes Difficult Terrain and creatures within can fall   Prone . DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Magic Missile ( + ) Damage: 6~15 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Force + 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Force + 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Force Create three darts of magical force, each dealing 1d4 + 1 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to its target. The darts always hit their target, and can each be targeted individually. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Volo can be communed with using Speak with Dead if he dies during Act One : Who are you? Volo Volothamp... Geddarm. My mother's... son... What were you doing here? Volo Investigating... the Absolute. Goblins'... new god... Who is the Absolute? Volo Unreal god... unheard of... spread like a plague... Do you have anything of value? Volo Quick mind... silver tongue... Do you have any unfinished business? Volo Manuscript. Story of... goblins... Absolute. Don't know... how it ends... Who is the Absolute? Volo Unreal god... unheard of... spread like a plague... Do you have any advice for me? Volo Use your voice... always... What was your greatest desire in life? Volo To be heard... What is it like to die? Volo Transforming... glimmering... 'Transforming'? 'Glimmering'? What do you mean? Volo The story... never told. The passing... beautiful... Store [ edit section | visual editor ] Corresponds to the DEN_Volo_Trade treasure table. Grease Bottle Potion of Animal Speaking Potion of Healing The Whispering Promise Thieves' Tools Volo also sells items from the following treasure tables Poor Trader Table Scroll Table Common Music Instrument Subtable In addition, he sells a random Scholar/Travel/Monster/Politics/Entertainment book. Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Balthazar Personal Notes: 3 Born to be Wild Dearest Elminster For the Attention of Volothamp Geddarm On Goblins: My Life Among the Conquering Host Volo's Complete Guide to the Behaviour of Nymphs Volo's Guide to Baldur's Gate Volo's Guide to Baldur's Gate (Signed) Volo's Guide to Spirits and Spectres Volo's Note Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Volo's appearance in Patch 7 Volo's appearance at the start of Early Access Volo's appearance in Patch 5 and 6 of Early Access Volo's appearance since Patch 7 of Early Access Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Volo is voiced by Stephen Hogan , replacing Rob Paulsen from previous games. Volo has appeared in multiple adventures, notably Tomb of Annihilation , Waterdeep: Dragon Heist and Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage , as well as several video games such as Neverwinter Nights 2: Storm of Zehir , Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal . Volo met the protagonist of the previous Baldur's Gate games twice, and even got his hands on Irenicus' notes on torturing the protagonist (see Regarding the Slayer ). If an instrument is played near Volo, he joins in by whistling. If Volo is approached in his cell at the Goblin Camp, he always recognises a character he spoke to previously at the Grove, even if they are using Disguise Self . This is likely a scripting omission, though it could also be intended and mean that he has some form of Truesight. In the Emerald Grove, Volo claims he never learned how to speak with animals, despite carrying and selling Potions of Animal Speaking . To get Volo's surgery and the enhancement on all four party members, after receiving the eye on the first party member but before the dialogue ends, a different party member must try to steal from Volo and fail at it. Volo then runs away, but comes back after a while, as usual when stealing from him. Then the next party member can get the surgery. Alternatively, the player character can first enter turn-based mode, cast Hold Person on Volo, then talk to him and let him perform the surgery. After finishing, Volo cannot immediately run away; other party members can then speak to him and also receive the surgery during their turn. SCL_Voss Kith'rak Voss is a determined Githyanki knight in the service of his queen, Vlaakith . He rides a red dragon named Qudenos . Contents 1 Background 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.1.1 Mountain Pass 2.1.1.1 Lae'zel 2.1.2 Campsite Visit 2.2 Act Three 2.2.1 Sharess' Caress 2.2.2 Lower City Sewers 2.2.3 Upper City 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Allies 3.3 Encounter - Rosymorn Monastery Trail camp 3.4 Encounter - The Upper City 4 Loot 5 Idle banter 6 Related literature 7 Gallery 8 Notes and references Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Voss is a legendary Kith'rak in githyanki society who reports directly to the lich queen Vlaakith CLVII. Per Lae'zel and lore found in-game, Voss has been the right-hand knight of Vlaakith and her predecessors, dating back to Vlaakith I, who succeeded the first githyanki leader Gith thousands of years in the past. Qudenos the Red Dragon is his mount and closest comrade. [ 1 ] Voss is direct and ruthless, expecting the deference due both his rank and possession of Vlaakith's personal silver sword. Other gith characters, including Lae'zel, hold him in esteem and may even be cowed by his presence. He still talks with – and may even be friendly to – non-gith, but githyanki party members or those who appear as a githyanki by use of Disguise Self have special interactions with Voss that reflect their place in gith society. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] For the transcript of Voss's Act 1 appearance, see Voss/Transcript . Mountain Pass [ edit section | visual editor ] During Act One , the party can first encounter Voss if they venture close enough to the Mountain Pass area to the northwest of Waukeen's Rest . A group of githyanki has just slain a Flaming Fist patrol, and Voss lands astride Qudenos to chide them and issue orders. Interacting with them advances ⁠ Find the Githyanki Crèche . If Kith'rak Voss or the other githyanki are approached by the party, he interrogates the interacting party member about the object of his mission, the Mysterious Artefact which he has been charged to retrieve for use against the Mind Flayers . [ 2 ] The interrogation is a gauntlet of ability checks . The interacting party member must first convince Voss not to kill them on the spot followed by an DC 10 Arcana Check check to perceive his hidden casting of Detect Thoughts , and then a DC 10 Wisdom Check check to resist it. Warlocks recognize the spell, bypass the Arcana check, and then only need a DC 5 Wisdom Check check to resist it. The interrogation can then end peacefully with a third successful check. Regardless of how the interrogation ends, Voss departs on Qudenos once the dialogue is concluded. He does not participate in combat and, if preemptively engaged, flies away with Qudenos at the first opportunity (usually immediately). Lae'zel [ edit section | visual editor ] If Lae'zel is present, she immediately runs to Voss without the party. [ 3 ] . If the player character follows her, the event proceeds as above. If the party leave, Lae'zel dies, Voss flies away, and the other githyanki under his command become hostile. Campsite Visit [ edit section | visual editor ] Once ⁠ Discover the Artefact's Secrets is complete, Kith'rak Voss makes a surprise visit upon the Party's first Fast Travel or Long Rest outside of the Crêche. He speaks directly to Lae'zel, attempting to reason with her about the truth of Vlaakith's tyranny after her own recent betrayal. Further, he claims to be opposing Vlaakith's reign, and that the occupant within the Artefact is the key to her being overthrown. A critical choice must be made: If the party choose to listen to him and reason with Lae'zel, he urges them to meet him again in Baldur's Gate at Sharess' Caress . Alternatively, it is possible to urge Lae'zel to attack him, leading to an optional boss fight. This has considerable consequences, yet earns the party Voss' Silver Sword [ 4 ] . The Letter to Voss on his body directs the party to Sharess' Caress, continuing ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior questline. If Lae'zel is has never been recruited, then she will be dead and Voss will therefor not visit to the Party's camp when leaving the Crêche region after completing ⁠ Discover the Artefact's Secrets . This impacts certain buffs (e.g. Morninglord's Radiance from solving the four weapons puzzle as part of the ⁠ Find the Blood of Lathander quest) by not clearing them since the forced Long Rest from Voss' visit—which would usually clear them—doesn't happen. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Sharess' Caress [ edit section | visual editor ] Voss moves to Sharess' Caress in Wyrm's Crossing , which starts the ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss quest, where he tries to make a deal with Raphael in the Devil's Den , but Voss has nothing to offer him. Raphael is in possession of the Orphic Hammer , a tool that can break the cage that holds Orpheus the githyanki prince and son of Gith. Orpheus has long since come to realize that Vlaakith I betrayed his mother. He led Gith's Honour Guard in a revolt and named himself the rightful king of the githyanki, triggering the War of the Comet . At the head of the Honour Guard mounted on red dragons, Orpheus fought Vlaakith's knights in a battle in the Astral Plane, where he praised Gith and accused Vlaakith. Yet he was overcome and defeated by Kith'rak Voss on Qudenos and imprisoned within the Astral Prism so that Vlaakith I (and her successors, now Vlaakith CLVII) could exploit the powers he inherited from his mother. Years later, Voss came to realise Vlaakith does not act in the interests of githyanki, and swore to free Gith's rightful successor. Lower City Sewers [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party sign the deal with Raphael, they can immediately show it to Voss, who then gifts the party a Silver Sword of the Astral Plane , a precious cultural item of the githyanki. Voss then departs to prepare his forces to take on the Elder Brain. If the party refuse Raphael's deal, Voss moves to the Lower City Sewers north and slight east of the City Sewers waypoint. There, he waits for the party to show him the Orphic Hammer and after this, he grants them the silver sword before leaving to gather his forces. If the party attack him in the sewers, he calls them traitors and teleports away on his turn, even if restrained, silenced, or merely incapacitated; he can still be killed if defeated in a single turn. Upper City [ edit section | visual editor ] Voss confronts the party as they approach High Hall . His reaction varies greatly depending on the choices that the party made inside the Astral Prism after their initial loss to the Netherbrain : If the party free Orpheus and either Karlach or the player character becomes a mind flayer, Voss is overjoyed at his prince's freedom. He then agrees to help the party as part of the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. If the party free Orpheus and allowing him to sacrifice himself to become a mind flayer, then Voss initially believes they betrayed him and killed Orpheus. He is shocked and horrified to learn his prince sacrificed himself for the cause, yet still offers to help the party as part of the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. If the party trust the Emperor and let him or Karlach consume Orpheus, Voss becomes enraged and the party must pass a DC 30 Persuasion Check or DC 30 Deception Check to prevent him from attacking them. If successful, Voss stands down and agrees to help the party as part of the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. If the party trust the Emperor and the player character becomes a mind flayer and consumes Orpheus, then an additional DC 25 Persuasion Check or DC 25 Intimidation Check must be passed before the DC 30 Persuasion Check or DC 30 Deception Check to prevent Voss from attacking and secure his aid in the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. Voss is accompanied by Voss' Raider . If Lae'zel was never recruited, this Encounter never happens. This impacts certain buffs (e.g. Morninglord's Radiance from solving the four weapons puzzle as part of the ⁠ Find the Blood of Lathander quest) by not clearing them since the forced Long Rest from Voss' visit—which would usually clear them—doesn't happen. Encounter - The Upper City [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party completed the ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss quest or disarmed him during Act One, then he wields Voss' Silver Sword instead of Silver Sword of the Astral Plane . Voss is accompanied by Veteran Gish , Veteran Raider , and Veteran Warrior . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Elixir of Heroism Githyanki Crossbow Githyanki Half Plate Letter to Voss Silver Sword of the Astral Plane or Voss' Silver Sword (depending on story/quest completion) Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Voss has an idle conversation with Qudenos inside the Lower City Sewers in Act Three . Qudenos Even with Prince Orpheus to guide us, we are too small in number to defeat Vlaakith alone. Kith'rak Voss We will not be alone, Qudenos. Kith'rak Voss For a thousand years, we have been planting the seeds of revolution. Kith'rak Voss In every crèche, many young whisper Orpheus' name. They do Vlaakith's duty, but out of fear, not faith. Kith'rak Voss When the Prince of the Comet blazes his path, they will follow. And so will countless others. Kith'rak Voss The time is soon upon us, Qudenos. I will not forget your loyalty, friend. Qudenos The lich queen has shackled the red dragons as surely as she has shackled the githyanki. Qudenos You will be the first to battle. And I will be the one to carry you. Qudenos This Lae'zel and her allies. Can they be trusted? Kith'rak Voss You ask the wrong question. It is not a matter of 'can'. It is a matter of 'must'. Kith'rak Voss Whether by fortune or necessity, fate made its choice. Kith'rak Voss Lae'zel was the opportunity we prayed for. This may be our one chance to secure githyanki freedom. If the interacting party member is githyanki, Vraalsith mentions they are not a hatchling anymore to be trained with the other youths. Vraalsith becomes hostile if the party attack anyone in the classroom, or upon their return from the journey into the Astral Prism , as part of Lae'zel's ⁠ quest . BG_Commoner Vrindula Mardassus is a civilian in front of the Counting House , in the Lower City during Act Three . “ Gods, I knew I should've done this before I got here. Now, there's thirty in that pouch, forty in that one, eighteen, no, seventeen - wait. Ugh, that won't do. One at a time, then. Here we go. One, two, three, four... „ — Vrindula Mardassus , in want of an abacus Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Vrindula Mardassus is outside of the entrance to the Counting House in the Lower City . She is counting her coins while standing in front of the beggar Rags Deelarma , who asks her to spare a little gold for herself. Vrindula Mardassus ...nine... ten... eleven... Rags Deelarma It sounds like you might have some coins to spare? Just a few, saer? Please? CRE_Supplies_Gith_NPC Warrior Vu’un is a githyanki in Crèche Y'llek in Act One . “ Watch your feet. Our hatchery does not treat strangers kindly. „ — Vu'un Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Vu’un and Raider Zar'an guard the Hatchery of the Crèche Y’llek. He stands watch at the low rocky cliff near the entrance of the hatchery. If spoken to, he resents that strangers are allowed to wander the Crèche's Hatchery, but nonetheless warns them about nearby traps. If the interacting party member is githyanki, Vu’un explains how gith eggs are nurtured in the hatchery, and that Varsh Ko’kuu is responsible for both tending the eggs and constructing the hatchery's defenses. Additionally, Vu'un warns the party not to approach the egg. Vu'un becomes hostile to the party if they try to sneak past him to steal the Githyanki Egg and trigger a trap, if they choose wrong options when speaking with Ko'kuu , or if they are permitted to approach and take the egg, but instead crush it (the latter option is not available for githyanki player characters). Honour mode [ edit section | visual editor ] W'wargaz receives the passive Legendary Action: Mind-Claw of Tu'narath on Honour Mode , enabling him to freely summon up to two Mind-Claws of Tu'narath per round, whenever he or his allies are attacked. Mind-Claw of Tu'narath Summon a vestigial echo of Vlaakith's ire as a wicked psionic blade. Recharge: Twice per round Whenever a summoned Mind-Claw strikes an opponent, W'wargaz can cast Mindsteal Link as a reaction on the target. All Mind-Claws are dismissed when W'wargaz is killed. The summoned Mind-Claws are not dismissed by knocking W'wargaz unconscious. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Prinski worked heavily with Enver Gortash in creating the Motivators to control the Gondians, and was instrumental in creating the Iron Throne alongside a rogue member of the Church of Umberlee , Dark Breaker Antiope who handled and controlled the Sahuagin . At some point, he likely ran afoul of Gortash, as his corpse is now in the Iron Throne.
