BG_Guard Wanda Tullermoor is a human wizard and ally of Counsellor Florrick . She is part of the retinue which confronts the party after Wyll breaks his pact with Mizora . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] After Wyll breaks his pact his Mizora during ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers and forsakes his father, Mizora manipulates Counsellor Florrick (or her replacement, Cordula Eltan ) into believing Wyll intentionally killed his father Ulder Ravengard ; this subsequently results in Wanda Tullermoor and the rest of the retinue under Florrick approaching and confronting the party the next time they are in the Lower City . A party member can then convince Florrick (or Eltan) to stand down through dialogue checks, and receive the The Legend of Ansur . Failing any of the checks results, or attacking the retinue, turns Wanda and the rest hostile. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Conjure Elemental: Water Elemental ( + ) The water elemental can use   Winter's Breath ,   Slam , and can mete out cold punishment upon foes with its fists. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Counterspell ( + ) Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Ice Storm ( + ) Damage: 6~40 2d8 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 4d6 ⁠ Cold Impel a storm of hail and ice to crash from the sky, covering the ground and striking all objects and creatures within range, dealing ⁠ Bludgeoning and ⁠ Cold damage. It also creates an   Ice surface that lasts 2 turns. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Invisibility ( + ) Touch a creature to turn it Invisible . Attacks against it have Disadvantage . It attacks with Advantage . Invisibility ends early if the invisible entity attacks, casts another spell, interacts with an object, takes an action or bonus action, or is damaged. Not another step, hear me? „ — Warryn , if approached by the party Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Warryn guards the Chapel Entrance with Gimblebock , Taman , and Quelenna . He maintains a vantage point over the area opposite of Quelenna. [ 1 ] Upon approach by a party member, Gimblebock automatically engages them in conversation. They can convince the looters to leave the area or attack them. Failing any of the dialogue checks causes them to attack. Warryn keeps his lower face covered, but has marks on his face which are remarkably similar to the characteristic pattern of partial-illithid veins on of those undergoing ceremorphosis . However, neither explanation is given or referred to in-game regarding his appearance, nor does he have any illithid-related powers. Technical UID S_END_WatcherSummon001 UUID 1f0ff035-b76b-4a2c-a172-ca088089cbba Stats END_CityWatchMelee_Dwarf Variant 1 UID S_END_WatcherSummon002 UUID 011f6bf8-87ab-46b7-bc70-546571df75ec Stats END_CityWatchMelee_HalfOrc Variant 2 UID S_END_WatcherSummon003 UUID 751f3dd2-70fe-4de0-bff5-10e00d4f6ffc Stats END_CityWatchMelee_Tiefling Watcher Guardians are summonable allies during Confront the Elder Brain , using their great weapon mastery to protect the city against the Absolutist forces' incursion. “ The City Watch will join you! „ — Watcher Guardian 's battle cry Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] During the initial battle for High Hall , a large force of infiltrated Absolutist cultists coming from the Upper City Sewers destroyed and routed the City Watch away from the keep, forcing what's left of the Watch to flee. Faced with severe casualties, what remains of the disposable City Watch forces available to retake High Hall are in the form of a small squad of Watcher Guardians under Constable Valeria's orders, and an incohesive group of panicked Watchmen attempting to escape the High Hall's courtyard. [ 1 ] These Watcher Guardians can be summoned with the Gather Your Allies variant, The Watch if Valeria has been saved and is an ally present for the final battle. Summons a male half-orc , a female tiefling , and a female gold dwarf to fight at the party's side. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Watcher Guardians are potent melee fighters capable of taking a generous amount of heat thanks to their high Armour Class and HP pool, as well as dishing significant damage thanks to their Great Weapon Master: All In passive. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 6~16 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Greatsword Helmet Plate Armour Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwarf model Tiefling model Dwarf portrait Tiefling portrait Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Some members of this archetype may have slightly different passives, movement speed, weight, and size due to being members of different races. These summonable Watcher Guardians have identical stats to the named Watchmen seen running away from the courtyard, those being Gyordi , Ebber , Fry , and Goodge . However, these named Watchmen' armour resemble that of the Breastplate +1 dyed in blue, brown, and black colours, rather than the armour specifically designed for The Watch that the Watcher Guardians and the Dead Watchmen wear. There are several other Watcher Guardian dead bodies strewn throughout the courtyard of High Hall , some of them being dyed in inconsistent schemes of blue and yellow, and blue and red hues. EQP_Spear_Chainmail_Shield_HelmetMetal_Fist Trs. BG_Guard Fist Wayne is a human fighter and a member of the Flaming Fist . He can be found in Rivington in Act Three . “ Show's over. Those Absolute bastards slaughtered the ringmaster - we're lucky there weren't more casualties. „ — Wayne Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Wayne together with Fist Taraji can be found standing in the Circus of the Last Days nearby the stage. The two only appear if all of the following occur: the party leaves the circus after battling with the doppelgangers during the circus act, the conflict results in the death of both the false Dribbles and the ringmaster Lucretious , and the party takes a long rest afterwards. If all the above are true then Wayne investigates the crime scene. Unlike Taraji, he is less talkative and, if spoken to, also puts the blame on the Cult of the Absolute , and orders the party to move along. EQP_HeavyCrossbow_Leather Trs. BG_Guard Fist Wearne is a human ranger and a member of the Flaming Fist . He is in Rivington in Act Three . “ I've got my eye on you. And them over there, too. I don't miss a thing. „ — Wearne Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Wearne is stationed together with Fist Kepso and Fist Silena just outside the South Span Checkpoint . They form the first line of guard, preventing refugees from entering Baldur's Gate through Wyrm's Crossing . While Silena and Kepso argue with several refugees who beg to let them in, Wearne walks back and forth across the path leading to the checkpoint and does not take part in the conversation. Unlike most other Fists at the checkpoint, Wearne does not express his opinion on the presence of refugees if spoken to, being keen on carrying on his duties. Technical UID S_LOW_Park_LoversMale UUID cc2aca46-3a9a-4637-98a4-dc812b71ff6d Stats Human_Commoner Wendel Ashgrove is on an outing with his partner at Bloomridge Park in the Lower City during Act Three . “ Right here, just one month ago, my Eugenie agreed to our courtship. It's a good place for romance, take it from me! Though I must admit - all the clankery from the Flaming Fists dampens the mood somewhat. „ — Wendel Ashgrove Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Wendel and Eugenie Kenridge are conversing at the centre of Bloomridge Park. Although the pair have dated for only one month, Wendel seems to have very strong feelings for her. When Eugenie attempts to tactfully break up with him, he misunderstands and agrees that both of them should get to know more people around them. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Wendel Ashgrove I still remember our first date in this park, you know. There were certainly less Fists about. Eugenie Kenridge It's only been a month, Wendel. Of course you remember our first date. Wendel Ashgrove But what a perfect month it's been - right, darling? Eugenie Kenridge Riiight. Wendel Ashgrove You know, I really don't think I've ever felt this way about someone before. Eugenie Kenridge I remind you again, Wendel. One. Month. Wendel Ashgrove I just think this park is so beautiful, don't you, darling? Eugenie Kenridge It's a bit loud, what with all these clanking guards. Wendel Ashgrove I could ask them to keep it down. Anything for you, dear. Eugenie Kenridge Listen, Wendel, I really think we need to have a chat. Wendel Ashgrove Are we not already having a chat, my angel? Eugenie Kenridge *Sigh.* Wendel Ashgrove You said you wanted to chat, my love? Eugenie Kenridge Yes... I did want to chat, Wendel. Wendel Ashgrove What did you want to talk about, my darling? Eugenie Kenridge Well... I asked you here because... Gods. Never mind. Wendel Ashgrove Come now, you know you can tell me anything. Eugenie Kenridge I just don't know how to say it... I think we should start seeing other people. There. Wendel Ashgrove Well, there's plenty of folk in this park we could get to know! Especially with all these new Fists. They'd be great craic, I bet. Eugenie Kenridge You are impossible sometimes, Wendel. BG_Guard Flaming Fist Wexford is a Flaming Fist who is killed by a githyanki patrol along the Risen Road at X: -145 Y: 570 . “ Stop wasting time, Baretha. You're not here to play with the locals. „ — Voss , commenting on her being taunted before her incineration Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Wexford is briefly seen as part of a squad of Flaming Fists opposing a githyanki patrol along the Risen Road, on a bridge nearby the Mountain Pass entrance. Faced with the githyanki, Gauntlet Dion demands they drop their weapons, but is swiftly rebuked by their leader Sarth Baretha . Before the Fists can respond, Qudenos swoops in from overhead and incinerates both the Fists and the nearby bridge. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Longsword Damage: 2~9 1d8 + 1 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Flaming Fist Bryanne Flaming Fist Rowan Gauntlet Dion Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Wexford cannot be looted, as she dies during the cutscene and her corpse cannot be found. Wexford cannot be interacted with, attacked, or even killed with Area of Effect attacks during the cutscene. Aiming at her simply shows an Invalid Target! prompt. Trust me. „ — Wilbur Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Wilbur wanders between the front entrance and front desk of the House of Grief in the Lower City . If Shadowheart interacts with him, Wilbur sneers that she is more wretched-looking than the rumours claimed, and that she will learn her fate as soon as she walks through the front doors. He can be found in Lower City in Act Three . “ Look at the body all you like - it'll be up for a while as a 'reminder'. „ — Williams Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Williams is standing at the gallows outside the Basilisk Gate Barracks . He only appears in the game if Florrick is executed. He and Fist Anderson are tasked with guarding Florrick’s body as a measure of increased security. Unlike Anderson, Williams completely agrees with the propaganda about Florrick’s treason, and is annoyed with being ordered to guard her corpse. He outrages if the party manage to steal the counsellor’s body. Technical UID S_MOO_Assault_PrisonMasterOfSouls_02 UUID 11570320-e45b-480c-a92a-4734f560edcf Stats Human_Cultist_Myrkul_MasterOfSouls Eqp. EQP_MasterOfSouls Trs. MOO_Cultist Willinx Jindlebee is a necromancer [ 1 ] of the Cult of Myrkul found in Act Two . She appears in the Moonrise Towers Prison after the party launch ⁠ the assault on the cult . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Willinx is always hostile when met. Along with her allied necromancers Duckie Verish and Sarabayle , she flanks the army of undead which confronts all trespassers into the prison. Unlike the Zealots, Adepts, and other members of the Cult of the Absolute , it appears Sarabayle and the other Mistresses of Souls are fully aware of what the Absolute is and the religious hoax they're perpetrating. [ 2 ] This greater understanding (and accompanying disdain) is shared by the other high-ranking Myrkulite necromancers serving Ketheric Thorm , with Kressa Bonedaughter bemoaning the weak servility of the infected she's presented with, and Balthazar using the player character's worm-infested status as an expletive. Winning the battle gains ⁠ A Bone To Pick for party members with the Soldier background. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bone Chill ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Necrotic Prevent the target from healing until your next turn. The target cannot help Downed characters. An undead target receives Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fireball ( + ) Damage: 8~48 8d6 ⁠ Fire Shoot a bright flame from your fingers that explodes upon contact, torching everything in the vicinity for 8d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Incubate Death ( ) Damage: 6~27 3d8 + 3 ⁠ Necrotic Spawn a skeletal involucre. After 1 turn, the involucre explodes, dealing 3d8 Necrotic damage and birthing a necromite. DEX Save Range: 24 m (80 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Myrkulite Scourge Damage: 3~15 1d8 + 1 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 1d6 ⁠ Necrotic Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Tenacity ( )   –   Myrkulite Scourge Damage ⁠ Bludgeoning When you miss an attack, deal ⁠ Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier anyway (minimum of 1). Tactician [ edit section | visual editor ] Shield ( + ) When you are about to be hit by an enemy, use your Reaction to increase your Armour Class by 5. You also take no damage from Magic Missile . These effects last until the start of your next turn. Technical UID S_LOW_FireworksHouse_ChildCustomer UUID 7564dced-44e3-41f0-8e1f-0c19c0f36585 Stats Human_Child Willow is a human child who can be encountered inside the Felogyr's Fireworks in Lower City of the Baldur's Gate , in Act Three of the game, while following through the quest ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys . “ That smokepowder smell - it smells so good . „ — Willow Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Willow participates in the cutscene that triggers upon first speaking to Avery Sonshal , the shopkeeper of the Felogyr's Fireworks. Avery checks the girl's knowledge of proper usage of fireworks. After Willow answers correctly, he also proclaims a warning about his establishment not being liable for any injuries caused by not following the rules. While the party members remain in the fireworks shop, Willow might run outside and return back to the ground floor. If spoken with, she tells the party that she is charmed by the smell of the pyrotechnics. Technical UID S_LOW_SerialKiller_Amelyssan_FakeAmelyssan UUID 8013105c-2bb0-43a1-9ede-fdcc9593969a Wilting Alex is a dead Human whose corpse is in the Lower City in Act Three . “ A 'tribute' to the Bhaalspawn of ages past. This is Amelyssan - and the five spawn she tricked into dying for her cause. It didn't help her, in the end. „ — Jaheira , upon exploring the scene Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Wilting Alex's corpse is in the Undercity Ruins , close to the Bhaal Temple . She was killed by Orin the Red . Her corpse was used as a component of Orin's "art" as an effigy to Amelyssan , a priestess of Bhaal defeated more than a century ago, along with the corpses of Lupir Neswaen, Hubersa Declensios, Isaan Thibault, Goxxoon, and Quelat Quimms. Wilting Alex's corpse can be looted for one of ⁠ Dribbles' body parts and the sixth of Orin's Ritual Notes . Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find Dribbles the Clown ⁠ Investigate the Murders ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Clown's Severed Head Amelyssan, the Sixth Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Wilting Alex's in-game model, as well as the model of Echo of Amelyssan (Amelyssan's ghost at the Murder Tribunal ), are designed to copy Amelyssan's image from the previous Baldur's Gate games, save for the haircut which only resembles her helm. Other corpses strewn around Wilting Alex's body resemble once more all the Bhaalspawn of the group known as The Five , led by Amelyssan slyly and subtly long time ago. Though not a Bhaalspawn herself, Amelyssan achieved almost a demigod status in her attempt to revive Bhaal. Technical UID S_WYR_CeremonyRoom_Patriar_003 UUID 3b7c5f23-a704-47bb-b064-5215ed4d531a Stats Human_Commoner Lady Winstra Hullhollyn is a Lady of Baldur's Gate who is present at Gortash's ordination as the Archduke of the city. “ Finally, a leader with some charisma. Ravengard was quite the dullard. „ — Winstra Hullhollyn , on Gortash becoming the Archduke Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the ceremony she sits among other patriars on the pews in central nave of the Audience Hall. After the ceremony ends, Lady Winstra stays in the central nave of the Audience Hall, engaged in casual conversation with Randolf Vammas , discussing the after-ceremony soiree. She expresses hope that Gortash will throw more interesting parties than Ulder Ravengard ever did. She is also outraged that most events have been cancelled due to the threat of the Absolute's army approaching the city. If spoken to, Lady Winstra calls Ravengard a dullard and says that in her opinion Gortash has much more charisma. If the party choose to confront Gortash, they can later find Lady Winstra along with all other invited guests and their retinue – slaughtered in the Audience hall. Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Randolf Vammas Gortash will likely call on me soon - I've sent him many a business proposal. Winstra Hullhollyn Do invite me along, darling. We could have afternoon tea! Randolf Vammas Lady Winstra, we'll be discussing business - hardly your realm of expertise. Winstra Hullhollyn I could say the same thing about you, darling. Winstra Hullhollyn A man like Gortash knows the path to people's hearts - a glorious evening of drinks and dancing.. Randolf Vammas So long as business comes first - parties don't pay for themselves. Winstra Hullhollyn They do when I throw them. Winstra Hullhollyn I'd love an evening with Gortash. He's be a most fascinating host, I'd wager. Randolf Vammas More fun than Ravengard , for sure. Winstra Hullhollyn That's hardly difficult. Randolf Vammas Business has been slow, but it is hardly my fault! This ' Absolute ' has people in a flap! Winstra Hullhollyn Every gala, ball, and brunch has been cancelled due to that nuisance of a cult! It's a disaster. Randolf Vammas I think Gortash is more concerned about the economy than he is your parties, my lady. ## Withers

Technical UID S_GLO_JergalAvatar UUID 0133f2ad-e121-4590-b5f0-a79413919805 Stats GLO_Jergal Withers is a mysterious Undead entity who joins the party on their adventures as a Camp Follower . He calls himself "a scribe, a seneschal - a keeper of records" . [ 1 ] He offers resurrection and Hireling services to the party, and also allows respeccing [ 2 ] of characters. “ What is the worth of a single mortal's life? „ — Withers Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Gameplay 1.3 Appearance 1.4 Personality 2 Services 3 History and identity 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.2 Act Two 4.3 Act Three 4.4 Epilogue 4.5 After Credits Scene 5 Combat 5.1 Loot 6 Related Literature 7 Related Quests 8 Achievements 9 Gallery 10 Notes and references 11 Bugs Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers [ 3 ] [ 4 ] is a camp companion who offers his various services to the party. Secretive, but wise and ever helpful, he can be found in the Dank Crypt in Act 1 and remains with the party throughout the game. If asked to leave or who he is, he declines to do so. Gameplay [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers is an Undead creature encountered in Act 1 who remains with the party throughout the game. He cannot be damaged or killed; he can be stolen from and does not react in any way if caught doing so. He is the only means of changing class and rearranging ability scores in the game. Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers has pale-brown, desiccated skin splotched with red spots. Strikingly, he lacks a nose but retains his other facial features. His outfit has been tattered by the passage of time, and he wears bandages around his arms and chest. His face, arms and parts of his collarbone are adorned with elaborate gilded strips of metal which, despite these other salient aspects of his appearance, give him a regal look. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Although he may seem cryptic at times, Withers appears genuinely invested in the party's success against the Cult of the Absolute . He offers his services to aid them, as well as information and guidance, though often vague. He is not intentionally rude, but usually very forthright when spoken to, especially when it comes to gods and divinity, yet he remains mysterious about his past. He respects those with the courage to stand up to fate and take destiny into their own hands, such as the Dark Urge if they reject Bhaal for good. At times, he also shows a rare kindness, as with Arabella , should she join the party as a camp follower. Withers comforts her after she finds out her parents are dead and guides her on her journey of understanding the Weave. He also organises the gathering during the epilogue of the game simply for the enjoyment of the companions, and even rescues Milil from the Fugue Plane, where he was trapped, seemingly just to provide music and entertainment. Furthermore, he seems to enjoy more mundane activities, as evidenced by his multiple luncheons with Tara and Gale's mother after the events of the game. In the epilogue, Withers can be seen speaking to the mural of the Dead Three not only with a familiar tone but also with great disdain, dismissing them as fools and vermin. Whatever his relation to them may have been, he clearly has no respect for them and chides them for their actions involving the Absolute. Services [ edit section | visual editor ] Resurrecting dead companions for 200 gold per resurrection. [ 5 ] Recruiting and resurrecting hirelings after reaching character level 3. [ 6 ] Respeccing [ 2 ] party members for 100 gold, setting them back to level 1 and allowing them to change class, subclass, ability scores, skill proficiencies, spells, feats, and other class-based level-up choices. [ See: Bugs ] Characters cannot change their race, gender, origin, appearance, or background with Withers; [ 7 ] the selectable aspects of any given race, such as a high elf's choice of cantrip, also remain fixed. Paladins who have broken their oaths must first restore their vows through the Oathbreaker Knight in order to access respeccing. History and identity [ edit section | visual editor ] Little is known about Withers' history prior to the game, although, through conversations with Arabella , it is revealed that Withers has always been a "bone man", in a sense, and he is neither living nor dead. Whoever he was, he was important enough to be laid to rest in a richly adorned sarcophagus, [ 8 ] alongside attendants to take care of the temple that serves as his resting place. Paladins and Clerics feel a divine energy coming from him, and he seems to have a deep understanding of gods and their natures. After resurrecting the Dark Urge , he says, "I know all, but to state truths is to interfere, for the minds of mortals are easily swayed." The fact that he is all-knowing but rarely interferes with mortals appears to imply that he is, in fact, a god . Though never explicitly stated in-game, it is heavily implied that Withers is actually Jergal , the erstwhile "Lord of the End of Everything" , and "Final Scribe" , the ancient god of death who willingly gave up part of his divine portfolio to three ambitious evil adventurers who then became the Dead Three . Since this grand bargain, Jergal carries out his remaining duties as a bookkeeper of the dead. In the Crumbling Journal , found in the Ancient Mausoleum in Act Three, the author tells of their meeting with Jergal, who asks them the same initial question that Withers asks the player character – "What is the worth of a single mortal life?" Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] “ Where matters of balance are concerned, I am eternally called. „ — Withers , answering a query on his presence in Moonroise Towers after the final defeat of Ketheric Thorm Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers is first encountered in the Dank Crypt – an ancient temple of Jergal. He is resting inside a sarcophagus within a hidden room. If released from it by the party, he asks the one who does so a cryptic question and then leaves. The Dark Urge is granted the ⁠ Unfamiliar Familiarity inspiration. Later, Withers appears at the campsite and joins as a camp follower . If the courtyard of the Goblin Camp is reached, or the story has progressed to a certain point [ verify ] without meeting Withers in the crypt, he nevertheless still appears at camp. If Withers arrives at camp in this way, the party can still visit the crypt and complete ⁠ Explore the Ruins , but his sarcophagus is then empty. This is the case even if the party have not been to camp since meeting the criteria for Withers to move there. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers moves to Moonrise Towers after defeating Ketheric Thorm , where he asks the interacting party member if they think illithids possess souls. Regardless of their answer, Withers affirms that they do not. [ 9 ] He also ponders why the Dead Three would amass an army of soulless beings when souls are what gods need to imbue them with power. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If the Dark Urge refuses to become the Chosen of Bhaal after killing Orin , Bhaal kills the Dark Urge. [ 10 ] [ 11 ] However, almost immediately after their final moment, Withers appears and invests a portion of his divine essence into the player character, returning them to life. He explains that Bhaal could only destroy the part of them he knew, the violence and brutality that he himself had imparted on them; he could not destroy the new self the player character had become by resisting their Dark Urge. He then pronounces them redeemed and free of Bhaal's influence. Withers moves to join allies and companions gathered in High Hall for the final battle against the Netherbrain . He offers his services as always, [ 12 ] and has some words of encouragement for the fight ahead. He also reassures the gathered allies that the Mind Flayer (either the player character, Karlach , Orpheus or The Emperor ) accompanying the party is on their side. Epilogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Six months after the events of the game, Withers extends an invitation to all companions for a celebratory party, gathering them all at the first campsite that served as home for many days. For this, he has prepared food and beverages, a fact many companions remark upon with surprise. He has also summoned Milil , a god who was trapped in the Fugue Plane, to provide music and entertainment. After the player character is done mingling with the guests, he can be spoken to and offers a toast to the heroes of Baldur's Gate, telling them that there may yet be a time when they are called to action once more. Tara , Gale's tressym, reveals that Withers has regularly joined her and Mrs Dekarios for luncheons in the past six months. If the player character attacks anyone, Withers banishes them to an unknown realm through a portal, and the game ends immediately. After Credits Scene [ edit section | visual editor ] In the after-credits scene, Withers is seen talking to a mural of the Dead Three, thoroughly disappointed in their actions and telling them that he overestimated them. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers cannot be damaged, is functionally invincible [ See: Bugs ] , and never engages in battle, even if provoked. If Withers is attacked, he responds in banter with one of the following: Ah, yes. Well struck. Thy accuracy would be lauded, had it a purpose. Hast thou considered this is a waste of mortal energy? When one tries and fails so many times, it is often named madness. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Withers cannot be killed or looted. [ See: Bugs ] Related Literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Crumbling Journal The Book of Willing Souls Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Explore the Ruins ⁠ The Urge Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Outsourcing Recruit a hireling. You can befriend them or use them as cannon-fodder - we won't judge. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance during Early Access. Official concept art by Jane Katsubo. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ When asked who he is after resurrecting the Dark Urge in the Temple of Bhaal. The full line is: "A scribe, a seneschal - a keeper of records. And now, thine advocate, both here, and in the City of the Dead." LOW_BhaalTemple_PostBattleDarkUrge_Resistance ↑ 2.0 2.1 "Respeccing" in role-playing games refers to the process of resetting or reallocating a character's skill points and / or abilities, allowing players to change their character's build or playstyle. This feature enables players to experiment with different strategies or correct mistakes in their character's development. ↑ There is never a point where Withers actually reveals that his name is Withers; this information is revealed purely via the subtitles. It is unclear how the party members themselves learn this. ↑ In Early Access, he was initially called The Hooded Skeleton, even though he had no visible hood. He was later renamed to Talkative Skeleton, and finally to Withers. ↑ Withers puts the gold that he receives for his services into a pickpocketable inventory, so it is possible to steal back any money paid. Unlike most NPCs, Withers does not react to failed pickpocketing, allowing unlimited attempts. ↑ If a party member speaks with a hireling, it is revealed that they themselves do not speak and that Withers instead speaks for them remotely. In a sense, this makes Withers indirectly a companion as well. ↑ Although The Dark Urge and Custom characters can change their appearance, this is done with the Magic Mirror , not Withers. ↑ If a party member interacts with the sarcophagus before the crypt skeletons are defeated, Withers tells them, "Dost thou think to rush fate? See to the dead first." This line is voiced by voice actor Brian Caspe instead of the usual voice actor Stephen Boxer . ↑ Mind Flayers (illithids) are generally considered not to have souls, at least not in the way typical humanoid races do. This comes from a mix of older and newer sources: The D&D 5e supplement, Volo's Guide to Monsters , mentions that illithids are soulless in the eyes of most gods, and that they themselves do not believe in gods, souls, or afterlives, and instead believe they will live on immortally in the mind of their Elder Brain after death. This is thought to be why they do not have afterlives or meaningful religious connections. The D&D 3.5e supplements the Player's Guide to Faerûn and the Expanded Psionics Handbook explain that on very rare occasions, illithids will choose to forgo merging with their Elder Brain after death to instead become petitioners in Ilsensine's divine realm. It is unknown whether there is any particular quality that separates these illithids who choose to enter an afterlife from those who do not, nor if the soul entering the afterlife is the same one possessed by the creature that underwent ceremorphosis to become the illithid. ↑ Upon the Urge's death, the The Narrator states, "In the end, your own death brought you more joy than any you wrought on this land. You are slipping into oblivion." and the Urge, upon being resurrected by Withers, can state "I just want to rest - death seemed so peaceful." ↑ Although completely drained of life by Bhaal, the Dark Urge does not 'die' as far as game mechanics reflect; any active buffs are retained, which is not ordinarily the case when Withers resurrects a fallen party member. Yet certain lines which can be spoken by Withers after his resurrection of The Dark Urge from their death at the hands of Bhaal imply this act was not like an ordinary resurrection of a fallen companion: Withers proclaims, "This intervention, the reclamation of thy soul, is beyond mine ordinary remit. But thou art extraordinary, and so are these times." ↑ In High Hall, Withers allows the player character to summon hirelings only if the party has fewer than four characters, and no longer permits respeccing. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Respeccing a character back to their same class(es) and level restores most depleted resources , such as spell slots , Luck Points , and War Priest Charges . This can be done as often as desired, as long as one has the gold to pay for it. Restoring Bardic Inspirations or War Priest Charges requires the character to start as a class other than bard or cleric before returning to that class to restore them. As of Hotfix 21, there is a bug where Withers can be killed in camp during Act Three by a partial-illithid character, via repeatedly using an Intelligence -based spell to trigger Ability Drain , bringing Withers' Intelligence to 1, and then using Absorb Intellect . If killed via this exploit, Withers only drops a regular Quarterstaff . If Withers is moved from Moonrise Towers to another waypoint [ verify ] using Improvised Melee Weapon (see notes on that page), he permanently disappears from camp. If The Dark Urge is in the party and rejects Bhaal, Withers will still appear in the Temple of Bhaal to resurrect them. This clears the bug, and Withers returns to camp. If the Dark Urge resurrection scene is not triggered, effects on Withers' appearance at High Hall and the epilogue are unknown. Certain hostile actions against Withers, if witnessed, can turn the camp hostile. Us using Devour Intellect on Withers is one such example. v t e Party and camp Companions Origin Astarion Gale Karlach Lae'zel Shadowheart Wyll The Dark Urge origin Non-Origin Halsin Jaheira Minsc Boo Minthara Temporary Alfira Losiir Attached Followers Armoured Owlbear Counsellor Florrick Glut Hope Omeluum Orpheus Sazza The Emperor Ulder Ravengard Us Zanner Toobin Camp Followers Permanent Owlbear Cub Scratch Withers Temporary Arnell Hallowleaf Barcus Wroot Dame Aylin Emmeline Hallowleaf Isobel Tara Ulder Ravengard Volo Yenna Grub Hirelings Brinna Brightsong Eldra Luthrinn Danton Jacelyn Kerz Kree Derryck Maddala Deadeye Sina'zith Sir Fuzzalump Varanna Sunblossom Ver'yll Wenkiir Zenith Feur'sel Personal Quests Cazador Szarr Dream Visitor Elminster Enver Gortash Mizora Oathbreaker Knight Orin the Red Quil Raphael Sceleritas Fel Viconia DeVir

She and her fellow goblins have captured Findal . “ Maybe we can set him on fire. „ — Worm Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon entering the Underground Passage, Worm is with Gresh , Gurza , and Torrack . EQP_Greatclub_Leather Wren is a lightfoot halfling druid in the Emerald Grove during Act One . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Wren is one of the Shadow Druids conspiring with Kagha to overtake the Emerald Grove in the name of their violent order. Wren is in the Inner Sanctum with his fellow Shadow Druids Olodan and Pinta , all of whom are Wild Shaped as rats. If the party interact with them using Speak with Animals , they remain silent and non-threatening. When enough evidence of Kagha's schemes are exposed, Olodan and her druids reveal themselves and admit to their plans. Regardless of whether persuading Kagha to turn on them or not, Wren fights to the death alongside the Shadow Druids. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Lunar Mend ( + ) Healing: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Healing Expend spell slots to regain Hit Points while wild shaped. You regain 1d8 hit points per spell slot level. Range: Self Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatclub Damage: 3~10 1d8 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Tenacity ( )   –   Greatclub Damage: 2 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning When you miss an attack, deal ⁠ Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier anyway (minimum of 1). Wild Shape: Bear ( + ) Assume the shape of a polar bear that can   Goad enemies into attacking it. The polar bear has a starting health of 30 hit points that increases every two druid levels. While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. You take on the attribution of your beast form - excluding your Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma scores. When your beast form drops to 0 hit points , you revert to your normal form. WYR_Ironhand_Worker Variant 1 UID UNI_WYR_Wulbren_Beheaded UUID e6e93b8a-6972-4338-a4af-64deb67ecf98 Stats MOO_GnomePrisoner_Leader Wulbren Bongle is a deep gnome who leads the Ironhand Gnomes . Wulbren despises the Gondians and the Steel Watch, and works to destroy the Steel Watch Foundry in Baldur's Gate and rid the city of Gondians. “ Fine. You want to try flapping your gums in the belly of the beast, be my guest. „ — Wulbren Bongle Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Wulbren is the leader of the Ironhand Gnomes and a close friend of Barcus Wroot , though their relationship becomes strained as events in the game unfold. He and the Ironhands were stationed in the Decrepit Village in the Underdark , which was raided by Duergar slavers sometime before the events of Baldur's Gate 3 . Wulbren has since gone missing, and Barcus has been searching tirelessly to try and find him. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Wulbren Bongle is a descendent of Wolverforce Bongle, a member of clan Ironhand who, it is claimed, was spoken to directly by Gaerdal Ironhand . Gaerdal implored Wolverforce to speak out against the Gondians who had falsely taken credit for the Ironhand's creations. [ 1 ] Wulbren himself has become obsessed with destroying the Gondians and restoring the name of clan Ironhand, possibly fuelled by his relation to Wolverforce. Wulbren and the Ironhands were stationed at the Decrepit Village in the Underdark, surveying the area in search of Gaerdal Ironhand's formula for runepowder. While they were there, the village was ambushed by duergar slavers in collaboration with the Cult of the Absolute , who caught most of the gnomes and moved them to Grymforge . Wulbren managed to find the formula in a small cache, but was captured as well. Recognised as their leader, and now possibly the only surviving person with the knowledge of how to make runepowder, he was taken to Moonrise Towers . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Rescue Wulbren Wulbren, Nickels and Nimble are in a cell in Moonrise Towers Prison . If they are rescued, they can be directed or escorted to Last Light Inn . Upon arriving at the Inn, Wulbren becomes absorbed in planning. Barcus can be informed of his arrival, but their reunion is icy. [ 2 ] If the party asks for a reward, Wulbren directs them to Barcus for a reward, if he is present; he otherwise gives some gold. Rescuing Wulbren gains the following inspiration: ⁠ Always a Way Out ( Criminal background) ⁠ Breakout! ( Folk Hero background) ⁠ Bugging Out ( Urchin background) ⁠ Simple Tools, Great Works ( Guild Artisan background) He later moves to the first room of Moonrise Towers after Ketheric Thorm is defeated, where he attempts to butter up the party to have them assist him in Baldur's Gate. If Wulbren is not freed from Moonrise Towers before the party deals with the Nightsong , his corpse is dropped in the Oubliette , along with those of all the other prisoners. Similarly, if Isobel is abducted by Marcus during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction or otherwise killed while Wulbren is present at Last Light Inn, he dies when the location subsequently falls to the shadow curse . However, this can be prevented by rescuing him after the Inn has already fallen. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If Wulbren is rescued from Moonrise Towers in Act Two, he later moves to Gyldro Angleiron's cellar in Rivington . Gyldro is sympathetic to the plight of the Ironhand Gnomes and has agreed to provide shelter while Wulbren and the rest of his clan seek to remedy the problem of their years in exile and deal with the Gondians. [ 3 ] If spoken with, Wulbren asks the party to help him to blow up the Steel Watch Foundry, using a Runepowder Bomb , which starts ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands . Once the Foundry is destroyed, he meets the party outside to kill any remaining Gondians. The party can side with Wulbren or against him. These choices can be accomplished peacefully, by defending the Gondians through intimidating him – or forcefully – by starting a fight. Alternatively, if Barcus survives up to this point, he can be pursuaded to stand up against Wulbren and talk down the other Ironhands, resulting in him taking up leadership and casting Wulbren out. If the party sides with Wulbren (in which case he leads them) or Barcus (who leads if convinced to oust Wulbren), the Ironhands assist in the final battle (see ⁠ Gather Your Allies ). If Enver Gortash is killed without disabling the Steel Watch first, the Elder Brain takes control of the remaining Steel Watch, which destroy the Foundry and kill all the Gondians before the party can meet them. If the party travels to the ruins of the Foundry after these events, Wulbren is there outside. He acts as if the party just sided with him against the Gondians and promises to assist in the final battle. The tombstone of Wulbren's father Antunio Bongle is at the Graveyard of the Lower City . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] When met in Moonrise Towers Prison , Wulbren has no equpiment, and can only use Throw Stone . When in Rivington he has equipment and corresponding weapon actions. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Throw Stone ( ) Damage: 6~9 1d4 + 5 ⁠ Bludgeoning Throws a sharp stone at a foe. Range: 9 m (30 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Half Plate Armour Longsword Shield Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] While in a cell in Moonrise Towers Prison , Wulbren, Nickels and Nimble discuss their predicament. Nickels The stone - I feel it. Hollow behind the back wall, and beyond... water? Wulbren Bongle I'd bet my last copper there's a pier nearby. Nimble This could be our chance, sir. Nimble We should leave - and soon. Wulbren Bongle That is the plan, Nickels. Nickels There's something evil here. Below, down, down... argh! Nimble Breathe - I've got you. Wulbren Bongle Unless this 'evil' can get us out of here, I don't want to hear about it. Wulbren Bongle It's only a matter of time 'til we're served up to the necromancer on a platter. Nimble We'll get you to Baldur's Gate , sir - I swear it. Wulbren Bongle Damn straight - without me everything will be for naught. The Ironhand Gnomes must succeed. Despicable. „ — Wuloona Dor Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Wuloona confronts Fist Ernestus alongside Bliggerillo , Porter Juxon , and Saer Frunilla about the contents of the latest issue of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . The paper claims that everyone is safe in Baldur's Gate but she does not believe it. If Gortash is defeated, Wuloona, Ernestus, and the rest of the civilians disperse, and are not seen again. Wuloona's attitude towards the party changes depending on the outcome of ⁠ Stop the Presses . EQ_Wyll Wyll Ravengard is an Origin Character and a recruitable Companion [ 1 ] who can be romanced by characters of any gender. He is a Human and a Fiend Warlock with the Folk Hero background. Wyll is first encountered just outside the Emerald Grove in Act One . Known as the "Blade of Frontiers" across the marches of Baldur's Gate , Wyll is a valiant hero who fights injustice and hunts monsters wherever they may hide. Though forever bound to his infernal patron Mizora , he has dedicated his whole life to protecting the city he loves. In multiplayer sessions, if Wyll is chosen as an origin by a player, Karlach is locked out as an option to other players. “ The frontiers demanded a blade. And so I heeded. „ — Wyll , on how the Blade of Frontiers came to be Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Background 1.2 Starting class 1.3 Special features 1.4 Personal quest 1.5 Recruitment 1.5.1 Act One 1.5.2 Leaving the party 1.6 Approval 1.7 Romance 2 Description 2.1 Appearance 2.2 Personality 3 History 3.1 Life in Baldur's Gate 3.2 A pact with the devil 4 Involvement 4.1 Act One 4.2 Act Two 4.3 Act Three 4.4 Endings 4.4.1 The Blade of Avernus 4.4.2 Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate 4.4.3 The Blade of Frontiers 5 Quest rewards 6 Interactions 6.1 Companion interactions 6.1.1 Act One 6.1.2 Act Two 6.1.3 Act Three 6.2 Unique interactions 6.2.1 Act One 6.2.2 Act Two 6.2.3 Act Three 6.3 Speak with Dead 7 Related Literature 8 Related Quests 9 Loot 9.1 Starting equipment 10 Achievements 11 Gallery 12 Notes and references 13 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] For a full overview of Wyll's starting features, see the articles Warlock , The Fiend and Human . Background [ edit section | visual editor ] Being the fabled "Blade of Frontiers" and the son of Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard , Wyll is bound by pact to serve the devil Mizora , a cambion in the service of the Archdevil Zariel . Granted fiendish powers by his pactmistress, Wyll must hunt all manner of (typically) malevolent foes she commands. [ 2 ] Prepared to sacrifice anything to protect Baldur's Gate , Wyll must struggle to maintain his integrity, desire to do good and protect the innocent against Mizora's machiavellian schemes which ultimately further her, and Zariel's, infernal plans. Starting class [ edit section | visual editor ] Before he is recruited, Wyll is a level 2 Warlock with the following Ability Scores : 8 STR, 13 DEX, 14 CON, 12 INT, 10 WIS, 15 CHA. If recruited, Wyll reverts to a level 1 Warlock with the standard ability scores for that class . He starts with the Fiend subclass, [ 3 ] giving him a chaotic and destructive set of skills. His baseline proficiency with rapiers also makes him a flexible companion who can adapt to any combat roles required. Special features [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll has the passive The Blade of Frontiers , granting him proficiency with rapiers regardless of class. Mizora, Wyll's patron, plays an active part in his story and can be interacted with to varying degrees when she appears. Wyll's choices when dealing with her (and her instructions) can lead to vastly different outcomes that impact his story. Personal quest [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll's personal quest as a companion is ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers . As an origin his personal quest is ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers (Origin) . His personal quest spans all acts of the game. Throughout it, Wyll must deal with what it truly means to be a hero, facing overwhelming odds and, at times, seemingly impossible choices as he struggles to embody the ideals instilled by his father. Two further quests are available that tie into his personal quest: ⁠ Hunt the Devil , in which Wyll's vow to slay all fiends will be tested, and ⁠ The Grand Duke , where Wyll must uphold his honour and reckon with the large shadow cast by his father, Ulder Ravengard. Recruitment [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll is first encountered when the party approaches the Druid Grove in the Wilderness . On approach, goblins launch an attack on the grove gate and Wyll participates in the battle, announcing himself as "the Blade of Frontiers" , as he defends the grove. If he survives the conflict, he moves to the The Hollow teaching tiefling children how to fight. Speaking with him there and agreeing to join forces brings Wyll into the party. If Wyll dies during the goblin battle, he can be resurrected with a Scroll of Revivify and recruited as normal. If Karlach is recruited first, Wyll appears at camp after taking a Long Rest , and immediately confronts her. Convincing him not to attack Karlach gains approval from nearby companions. If the Druid's Grove quest is completed, Wyll leaves the hollow. He instead appears in camp after Karlach is recruited upon taking a long rest. Wyll disappears from the game if Karlach dies before meeting him. [ verify ] Wyll does not join the party if a battle breaks out between the inhabitants of the Emerald Grove before recruiting him. If the party raids the grove without first recruiting him, Wyll's corpse can be found among those of the grove defenders after the battle. Should ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke be started by rescuing Florrick from a burning Waukeen's Rest without recruiting Wyll, his recruitment dialogue is entirely skipped and he makes conversation as if he has already joined the party. In this event, he can be recruited by simply asking him to join. Leaving the party [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll abandons the party if they side with the Goblins and lay waste to the Grove. If he accompanies the party during this siege, he turns on them. If the tieflings and druids are already dead, and the party directed Minthara towards the Grove or the party chooses to warn the grove of the attack and then betrays them upon her arrival at the gate without him present, he abandons the party once the goblin celebration commences. [ 4 ] Attacking his father at any point causes Wyll to turn against the party. Approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Wyll/Approval Wyll Approves Wyll approves of valiant acts of defending the innocent or the defenceless, and appreciates kindness towards children. Peaceful, but decisive actions resonate with him. Those who take a genuine interest in him and the struggles he faces are also appreciated. Wyll dislikes villainous acts and condemns participation in evil plans. He frowns upon wanton violence and disapproves of refusing or abandoning those in need. He is hostile to his infernal patron Mizora and disapproves of any kind of rapport with her. Romance [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Wyll/Romance Wyll can be romanced by characters of any gender. He is earnest in his romance, and takes a dim view of casual encounters with others, especially Mizora. Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll has dark brown hair kept in neat rows with cropped sides, a trimmed circle beard adorning his face. He claims his right eye is made out of Bloodstone carved from the Galena Mountains, which functions as a sending stone, gifted by Mizora as a replacement after losing his eye fighting cultists, doubling as a method to keep track of him. [ 5 ] Despite the scars adorning it, his face retains a youthful look, complimented by his friendly, yet determined gaze. He dresses modestly, his outfit suited for combat and hunting, with only his rapier hinting at his noble upbringing. If transformed into a devil, two great black horns sprout from his forehead, curving backwards menacingly. His face receives new scars on his cheeks and neck and his good eye turns black, with a crimson red pupil. In Act 3, Wyll reveals he is 24 years old, [ 6 ] having been exiled from Baldur's Gate for the past seven years since his pact with Mizora. Personality [ edit section | visual editor ] Heroic and kindhearted, but conflicted and ever struggling against his pactmistress, Wyll has dedicated most of his life to fighting on behalf of the people of the Sword Coast . He takes his duty and title seriously, and speaks boastfully of his skills and past as "the Blade of Frontiers" . Despite his determination to his cause, Wyll has a more playful side. He suggests the party stop to try drinks at The Waning Moon , and wistfully tells Karlach he would love to unwind and swim at the beach in Act 3. He retains some of his noble upbringing, not only in the manner of his speaking, but also in some pastimes he has, such as dancing and a fondness for good wine. [ 7 ] Still, while he is able to partake in the pomp and vanity of higher society, he prefers the simple life he leads now. [ 8 ] History [ edit section | visual editor ] Life in Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] The son of Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard , Wyll observed many of the political inner workings of Baldur's Gate while growing up. His mother, Francesca, [ 9 ] died in childbirth, [ 10 ] and he spent a largely happy childhood being trained by his father, who came from a working-class background, being taught practical skills such as swordplay. [ 8 ] Much of Wyll's principles come from his father, who instilled in him a sense of duty to the city of Baldur's Gate and its people. As his father rose through the ranks of nobility, Wyll took part of many noble gatherings, getting to know that side of the city well. A pact with the devil [ edit section | visual editor ] “ ... In his eyes, I invited a devil into our midst. I was a fool at best; a traitor at worst. And Grand Duke Ravengard suffers neither. „ — Wyll , relating the story of how his father came to banish his only child from Baldur's Gate When he was seventeen, Wyll felt a grave warning urging him to investigate the outskirts of the city, where he encountered Tiamat cultists ready to summon the tyrannical dragon goddess to the plane. Eager to stop them, but young and powerless against many armed cultists, Wyll's desperation attracted Mizora who offered him a solution: her powers in exchange for his eternal servitude. Wyll did not hesitate, and together they made quick work of the cult. [ 11 ] However, young Ravengard would soon realize the cost of dealing with devils, as one of the many clauses of the pact prevented him from disclosing what happened that night. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] Mizora never gave specifics for why she approached Wyll; all she revealed was that Tiamat's scheme was at odds with Zariel's plans. [ 14 ] When his father, Ulder Ravengard, returned from Elturel to find his son accompanied by a devil, he demanded an explanation, yet Wyll's tongue was unable to explain what happened, and the scene of the ordeal was conveniently cleaned up. With cold disappointment, his father cast him out from the city, forever exiled to the frontiers. [ 15 ] Ever since, Wyll has roamed the frontiers beyond Baldur's Gate, struggling to serve the city, protect the weak and fight for justice, as he carries out Mizora's infernal whims. Some of the clauses are revealed by Mizora throughout the game: Clause A § 2: 'Should soul-holder choose to abandon his patron, he is freed from his duty. His father, Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard, will be thus fated to die by an enemy's hand.' Clause F § 9: 'Soul-binder shall bestow reward or favour only upon soul-bearer's fulfilment of related obligation.' Clause G § 9: 'Targets shall be limited to the infernal, the demonic, the heartless, and the soulless.' Clause Z § 13: 'Should the promised soul refuse obeyance or neglect duty, the pact-holder shall cast the promised in Avernus as a lemure.' Clause Z § 13: 'If the soul-binder consents to separation, she will release the soul-bearer from all obligation within six months.' Addendum F: 'The Absolute must be avenged for the soul-binder's detention at Moonrise. The soul-bearer retains his gifts until such time as the Absolute is slain.' Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] See main article: The Blade of Frontiers The Blade of Frontiers is Wyll's personal quest. It is added to the journal upon recruiting him, and it spans all three acts of the game. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] At the start of the game, Wyll is on the hunt for Karlach, the latest target his patron Mizora wishes dead. Forced to obey as part of their pact, the hunt takes Wyll to Avernus , where he finds his quarry slaying scores of her own. Wyll's relentless pursuit after the fleeing Karlach eventually ends on a rogue Nautiloid , suddenly materialised before them. As they confront each other on the ship, they are captured by Mind Flayers and tadpoled, kept aboard awaiting Ceremorphosis . After the Nautiloid crashes, and without trace of his quarry, Wyll eventually arrives at the Emerald Grove. Moved by the plight of the refugees within, he stays to protect them from Goblin attacks. After fending off the goblin scouting party, Wyll can be spoken to in The Hollow. He recognizes the party as having been aboard the nautiloid. Depending on conversation choices made by the player character, Wyll agrees to join the party to hunt a devil (Karlach) or find a cure for the tadpoles together. If he joins to find a cure for the tadpoles, Wyll then reveals he is on the hunt for a devil escaped from Avernus, and knows she is somewhere nearby. Karlach is near the Toll House. If present, Wyll confronts her immediately. As Karlach defends her innocence, Wyll remains determined to slay her until their tadpoles connect and a vision of Karlach's escape from Avernus is shared between the party members. The vision shows her tearing through the Archdevil Zariel's forces, frantically seeking escape. She is a victim of the Blood War , not an agent of it. A choice is presented: ignore the warnings and help Wyll slay Karlach, or trust the events shared by her tadpole and spare the Tiefling. If spared, Karlach can be recruited and (if space is available) added to the active party. If slain, Karlach's head can be taken as proof of Wyll's successful hunt. Sparing Karlach opens the possibility of assisting in her ⁠ quest to slay false paladins of Tyr who are hunting her down. If Wyll is not present when Karlach is recruited, he confronts her at the next long rest. The party can now fight either of them or defuse the situation. If conflict is avoided, the player character gains approval with all nearby companions and, if spoken with after, Wyll alludes to unpleasant consequences from his decision to spare Karlach being revealed "one night soon". At camp, on the next Long Rest , Wyll warily announces the arrival of Mizora. She introduces herself to the party, greets everyone mischievously and reveals not only her role as Wyll's patron but that it was she who gave Wyll his mission to hunt Karlach. If Karlach was killed, she is pleased and rewards Wyll. If spared, however, Mizora reminds Wyll of the terms of their pact and his obligation to hunt the heartless , a description Karlach clearly meets. If he insists she remain spared, Mizora takes this as a breach of the pact, and transforms him into a fiend as punishment. The same result occurs if the party avoids Wyll's mission and ignores Karlach entirely. [ 16 ] Upon reaching Waukeen's Rest , the party can find a burning inn surrounded by Flaming Fists , mercenaries working as Baldur's Gate's enforcers. They quickly reveal Grand Duke Ravengard is trapped inside, and needs to be saved. Wyll quickly moves to help, rescuing Counsellor Florrick , the duke's advisor, in the process, but no signs of the duke can be found. Outside and safe, Florrick recognises Wyll and urges him to save his father, letting slip that Wyll is the son of the duke. Ambushed by Drow , the duke was kidnapped and taken to Moonrise Towers , the base of operations of the Cult of the Absolute . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] At some point during the adventures in the Shadow-Cursed Lands , Mizora appears before Wyll and the party, informing Wyll that cultists of the Absolute have captured an important asset of Zariel, a powerful devil, and that he must rescue them. Stressing the importance of the mission, Mizora disappears as quickly as she arrived. During this conversation the player character can pass a series of skill checks to allow Wyll the opportunity to earn his freedom from his pact with Mizora if he completes the mission. Afterwards, if they are successful in creating this chance, a conversation icon [!] appears above Wyll's head, and further approval can be gained. Wyll's anger is clear as he relates the danger to Baldurs Gate that may unfold from his father's subjugation to the Absolute. Zariel's asset cannot be found in Moonrise Towers proper, rather, they can only be saved upon entering the Mind Flayer Colony after the first battle with Ketheric Thorm . There, the party finds Mizora herself trapped within a pod in the Tadpoling Centre. Mizora can be freed from the pod or killed, though killing her also "kills" Wyll as per the terms of their pact, turning his soul permanently into a tortured lemure in Avernus. [ 17 ] If Mizora is freed, she can be persuaded to reward Wyll. If not accomplished earlier, Mizora can be pressed here to end Wyll's contract, to which she may relent yet stipulate its provisions still require he wait six months to actually be released. Rescuing Mizora lifts Wyll's restriction on speaking about his pact and allows the party to learn more about his deal with her. Following Ketheric through the colony, the party eventually finds him arguing with Enver Gortash and Orin the Red , with Duke Ravengard next to them. After the Absolute is revealed to be an Elder Brain under the control of the three Chosen, Orin takes the duke and forces a tadpole into his eye. Gortash and Orin leave for Baldur's Gate not long after, with a now enthralled duke in tow. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Arriving at Baldur's Gate and provided she was rescued from Moonrise, Mizora moves to wait for Wyll and the party on the main floor of Wyrm's Rock Fortress . She mocks Ulder Ravengard's fate and goads Wyll to hurry to the main chamber. When the party returns, Mizora announces she is ready to break the pact between her and Wyll, and will meet everyone back at the campsite. After the next long rest, Mizora appears, ready to bargain. If Duke Ravengard remains alive, Mizora offers his location in exchange for a sacrifice. Wyll is then presented with a choice: break the pact immediately, but sacrifice his father to his fate, or remain forever bound to Mizora in exchange for his father's freedom. If Duke Ravengard did not survive, however, Mizora presents a different bargain: bring back Wyll's father from the dead in exchange for young Ravengard's soul, or break the pact immediately. Mizora is pleased with whatever choice Wyll makes, remaining in camp as a Camp Follower . She then allows the party to speak with and learn more about her. If Wyll keeps his contract, she becomes available as an ally against the Absolute as part of the quest ⁠ Gather Your Allies . If alive, Duke Ravengard is moved to the Iron Throne , now an an underwater prison used by Gortash and his Banites. The party can attempt to break him out. However, if Wyll sacrificed him in exchange for his freedom, Mizora appears and attempts to murder the duke, ensuring the deal goes through as pacted between them. If the duke survives, Wyll and his father have a long overdue reunion, and can speak to Mizora, who is displeased at the outcome but does not otherwise punish Wyll for outfoxing her. Duke Ravengard then urges Wyll to find Ansur , a legendary dragon said to sleep under the city, ready to defend it during its time of greatest need. If Duke Ravengard is unavailable or dead, the mission to find Ansur is given to the party by Counsellor Florrick (or her replacement Cordula Eltan if she is not rescued from Wyrm's Rock Prison ) some time after travelling to the Lower City . Ansur is in The Wyrmway , below the fortress' prison. The legendary Balduran has prepared trials to test the mettle of adventurers before they may seek audience with Ansur. Wyll's upbringing proves valuable during these trials, and he can be consulted for possible solutions to them. With the trials completed, the party faces Ansur, yet all they find is the decayed corpse of the once-great wyrm. Reanimated, Ansur and the Emperor begin arguing, and it is revealed the mind flayer is none other than Balduran, turned illithid when he was captured near Moonrise Towers. Angered by Balduran's betrayal, Ansur attacks, forcing the party to put down the wyrm for good. Ansur's fate can then be revealed to Ulder Ravengard, if alive. He proposes Wyll become a Grand Duke of the city, following his father's steps, to which Wyll can agree or decline. Regardless of the choice, Duke Ravengard pledges his support for the coming battle. If the Duke is dead, Wyll decides his future on his own following the battle with Ansur. Endings [ edit section | visual editor ] The Blade of Avernus [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll as the Blade of Avernus If Wyll is transformed by Mizora and chooses not to become the Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate, he takes on the mantle of "the Blade of Avernus" and vows to hunt devils in their own homeland. By the time he is summoned by Withers for his gathering six months after the events of the game, Wyll has become a seasoned slayer of fiends, boasting about his many hunts. If his contract was broken, he also mentions he is working with a diabolist from Calimshan and is using his sending stone eye to track Mizora, setting his sights on his former patron. If still bound to her, he mentions Mizora has been surprisingly hands-off, sending him only after demons and devils per their agreement. If Karlach was convinced to return to Avernus with Wyll, they join efforts to find a cure for her mechanical heart and grow closer after travelling together for six months there. [ 18 ] Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll as the Grand Duke If Wyll chose to become the Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate, he oversees the reconstruction of the city, parleys with influential nobles for aid and tightens bonds with the other cities of the Sword Coast. If Ulder Ravengard lives, Wyll works with him to marshal forces for peace and renewal. The city's gates are opened to refugees, the Council of Four is reformed, and romanced player characters are extended an invitation to become a Duke. If Wyll never broke his contract with Mizora, she remains active in his life in her human disguise, enjoying the political intrigue and keeping him on a long leash for reasons unknown to him. If Astarion becomes Vampire Ascendant, he mentions that Wyll is a capable duke who makes it difficult for him to accrue power in Baldur's Gate. The Blade of Frontiers [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll as the Blade of Frontiers If Wyll either never completed his personal quest or was not transformed by Mizora and chose not to become the Grand Duke of Baldur's gate, he remains "the Blade of Frontiers" and wishes to share stories of his adventures. He shares that he has slain trolls, ghouls, a dinosaur, a lich, and a dragon. If his contract was broken, he also mentions he is working with a diabolist from Calimshan to use his sending stone eye to track Mizora, and has set his sights on his former patron. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Infernal Rapier — granted by Mizora for rescuing her from the Mind Flayer Colony in Act 2 and convincing her with a successful DC 14 Persuasion Check Infernal Robe — granted by Mizora for killing Karlach Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll has unique dialogue interactions as a companion available after certain events. Whenever one is available, he will have a floating [ ! ] icon above him. Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Once Wyll's confrontation with Karlach has been dealt with, if she is spared, he comments on being deceived, and alludes to a punishment he will soon receive. After the party's first encounter with Mizora, Wyll can be asked about his pact and history with her. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] As early as reaching the Shadow-Cursed Lands, Wyll expresses his desire for mutual trust, and reveals he is the son of Ulder Ravengard if not revealed earlier at Waukeen's Rest. Following Mizora's liberation from Moonrise Towers, Wyll expresses his annoyance at her duplicity but also happiness over his future freedom. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] After slaying Ansur, Wyll laments his failure to bring the dragon to the party's side and suggests speaking to his father if alive and rescued. Unique interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] Either as an origin, or in the party as a companion, Wyll has unique interactions and special dialogue with the following characters, listed by the act they are first encountered in. The party member who carries the corpses must be in close vicinity when such events occur (see approval notes for more details on how approval works). Once their approval reaches or rises above -50, revive Karlach, Wyll or both of them. In this way, Karlach and Wyll can live with this decision and stay, unless of course their approval drops below -50 again. ↑ Campsite , lines spoken by Wyll when he reveals the terms of his pact after saving Mizora. "I was seventeen. (...) That's when the Cult of the Dragon made its move." ↑ Various locations, lines spoken by Wyll when revealing his relationship with Ulder Ravengard. "Father's the son of a blacksmith, born with barely a coin in the coffers. (...) I spent more time duelling with father than I did rubbing elbows with lords. Not to say I didn't develop a taste for good wine and a talent for courtly dance." ↑ 8.0 8.1 Wyll's story was almost entirely rewritten for full release after fan feedback. In Early Access, he struggled with a brutal side and with living up to the title of the Blade of Frontiers, and had a particular hatred of goblins. His pact with Mizora was made due to his desire for vengeance after being attacked by goblins and losing his eye to one of them. His personality on release was rewritten to be more genuinely heroic and kind-hearted, with his personal struggles focusing more on his relationship with his father and with Mizora, and his hatred of goblins being swapped for a hatred of devils and their kind. ↑ Duke Ravengard's Longsword description. ↑ Campsite, dialogue exchange between the player character and Wyll after encountering Arabella in the Shadowlands and agreeing to find her parents. Player: "You've talked about your father, but not your mother. Why's that?" Wyll: "Because there's nothing to tell. She died when I was born." ↑ Campsite, vision of the events shared by Wyll when he reveals the terms of his pact after saving Mizora. Wyll: "A tenday after father left, I head a whisper as I slept. (...)" Narrator: "As the maelstrom howls, Mizora's lips press to your ear. 'She will destroy Baldur's Gate. Grant me your soul - and I will give you the power to save it', she whispers." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Wyll when he reveals the terms of his pact after saving Mizora. "I tried to tell him the truth, but my mouth couldn't form the words. I led him to the battlefield, but Mizora had swept it clean. After, he said only one word: 'Go'. So I did." ↑ Mind Flayer Colony , dialogue between the player character and Wyll after freeing Mizora. Player: "Mizora said you can talk about your pact and exile. It's time I know the whole truth." Wyll: "First, we kill Ketheric Thorm. Then I'll tell you everything you want to know." ↑ Campsite, lines spoken by Wyll when he reveals the terms of his pact after saving Mizora. "Tiamat made a play for power. Zariel had other plans." ↑ Campsite, line spoken by Ulder Ravengard when talking to him with Wyll present after rescuing him. "My son, you sold your soul to save Baldur's Gate - and I cast you out for it." ↑ It is possible to recruit both Karlach and Wyll while still preventing his fiendish transformation. In addition, evading Mizora's punishment while also having Karlach in the party has no known deleterious impact on Wyll's storyline or other aspects of gameplay. To accomplish this, Wyll must be dead immediately prior to every long rest after Wyll and Karlach's confrontation at camp; he may be revived every morning after, if desired. While Wyll is dead, Mizora does not confront him for his disobedience. This arguably tedious routine is no longer needed once the party progresses to Act Two . Upon first arriving in Act Two, Mizora is kidnapped and cannot transform him, even if the party returns to Act One and takes a Long Rest there. After being rescued from the Mind Flayer Colony , Mizora no longer moves to punish Wyll. If one wants Wyll dead before long resting, it is advisable to have him die from falling damage by, for example, jumping from a great height (more than once if needed). If hecis killed by damage from another party member, intended or not, approval is lost. ↑ Mind Flayer Colony, lines spoken by Karlach if Mizora died and took Wyll's soul. "But he isn't dead, is he? He's a blob of tormented flesh in the Hells. And that's all he'll be - forever." ↑ Epilogue , lines spoken by Karlach during Withers' gathering if only she and Wyll ended up in Avernus by the end of the game. "War is a dirty business, soldier, it's been exactly how you think. But having Wyll around is being incredible. Fucker's even better at killing devils than yours truly. We don't have much time to chat, but just knowing he's there makes all the difference. " or " Wish Wyll and I had more time to reminisce, but surviving Avernus is just non-stop. Still, having him there has been incredible. You really can get through anything with someone you love at your side. UND_MycoVillage_DeadDrowHermit Xargrim , named in-game as Pale Corpse , was one of the three drow explorers in the Underdark searching for the Adamantine Forge in Act One . “ Xargrim had no taste at all. But enough low cunning to use an illusion? Absolutely. „ — Dhourn , on Xargrim's book Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Xargrim's corpse is hidden in the vine-blocked section in Ebonlake Grotto next to Derryth Bonecloak at X: 55 Y: -90 . The door is unlocked as a quest reward for ⁠ Defeat the Duergar Intruders . This area can also be reached via Misty Step . Xargrim, Dhourn , and Filro were searching for the Adamantine Forge . Xargrim collected notes on the forge's operation, which he magically concealed under the guise Flumph Mating Rituals . Over time, the three explorers turned on each other, and Xargrim released a Spectator on Dhourn and his mercenaries at the Selûnite Outpost . At some point, Xargrim was likely imprisoned and killed by the Myconids in Ebonlake Grotto. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Flumph Mating Rituals Icy Metal Shadow of Menzoberranzan - next to corpse Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Flumph Mating Rituals Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Defeat the Duergar Intruders ⁠ The Adamantine Forge Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Xargrim can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Who are you? Pale Corpse: Xargrim... conjurer... seeker... How did you die? Pale Corpse: Battle... with rival... summoned spectator... What were you fighting over? Pale Corpse: Glory... we search... for the Adamantine Forge... What was your business down here? Pale Corpse: Glory... we search... for the Adamantine Forge... 'We'? Who were the others? Pale Corpse: ... Filro... Dhourn... each held knowledge... none... would share... What was your knowledge of the Forge? Pale Corpse: ... secret... to its operation... Pale Corpse: ... book... disguised ... by magic... What is this book I found next to you? Pale Corpse: ... the secret... to mastering the Adamantine Forge... Pale Corpse: ... book... disguised ... by magic... What is the Adamantine Forge?  (If party told about Grymforge) Pale Corpse: ... lost workshop... of Silouv Yali ... finest weapons... in all creation... Do you know where to find the Forge?  (If party hasn't seen Grymforge yet) Pale Corpse: Dhourn knows... but cannot tell... Where can I find this Dhourn?
