Technical UID S_DEN_Tiefling_011 UUID 77439e86-3f60-4456-bd55-931e2f45654f Stats DEN_Refugees_Tiefling_Ranger Eqp. EQP_Longbow_Leather Trs. DEN_Refugee Zorru is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One . Originally out on a scouting mission with Yul , he encountered a githyanki patrol on the Risen Road before fleeing back to the grove. “ We were s-scouting the road to Baldur's Gate. It saw us 'fore we saw it. Jammed its blade through Yul's belly, straight to the other side. And I just... I just ran. „ — Zorru , on the githyanki patrol killing Yul Description [ edit section | visual editor ] Zorru has a strong survival instict, which may override other duties and obligations. As a result, he often chooses flight over fight, such as when he abandoned his fellow scout to die after they had been ambushed by a githyanki patrol. He values humor, especially in difficult times, and occasionally makes fatalistic jokes. [ 1 ] He has grown to fear githyanki after watching one gut his friend. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] When Nymessa and Damays guard a captured Lae'zel , they comment that Zorru was right to describe the gith as "Yellow as a toad, and twice as ugly" and that one of them killed his squad. Upon arrival at the Grove, if Zaki sees Lae'zel, she comments Lae'zel is one of the toad-people Zorru saw. Either interaction may lead to Lae'zel insisting on finding and questioning Zorru about the gith he saw, with the hopes of finding their Crèche and curing the party of their tadpoles. Zorru is in The Hollow , next to the storage hut. If Lae'zel is present, he questions her presence, and Lae'zel orders Zorru to bow. If the player character allows this to happen, approval is gained with Lae'zel and lost with Shadowheart . If Zorru is not made to bow, Shadowheart gains approval instead, and Lae'zel gains disapproval. The player character can question Zorru over the whereabouts of the Githyanki Crèche , which results in his giving information that updates the map with a marker. This advances ⁠ Find the Githyanki Crèche . When the party approach the Mountain Pass, they can encounter the corpse of Yul , Zorru's friend and fellow scout. Using Speak with Dead reveals that Zorru left Yul to die. If Wyll is in the party, he calls Zorru a coward. After defeating all three goblin leaders , Zorru leaves the Grove before most of the tiefling refugees, and travels to Baldur's Gate on his own. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] If he survives to Act Three, Zorru is with several other tieflings in the refugee camp near the Requisitioned Barn , within Rivington . His dialogue with Cerys , Bex , or Danis reveals he miraculously made it to the city all on his own, but had some close calls with Absolutist cultists on the way there; nevertheless, he acquiesces that he did not have it as hard as the rest of the remaining refugees. [ 2 ] Despite his own cowardice, he despises Zevlor for failing to act under pressure during the attack by Absolute Cultists. [ 3 ] Depending on the player character's conversation with him, he may change his point of view to understand Zevlor tried his best in an untenable situation. Technical UID S_GLO_IronThrone_Group1_Prisoner1 UUID 18991627-0e38-44d0-a8ac-31e1105d5392 Stats LOW_IronThrone_Prisoners_Gnome Zumbo Pumbo is a rock gnome member of the Church of Gond , held hostage at the Iron Throne by Enver Gortash . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party enter the Iron Throne, Enver Gortash triggers explosions which soon collapse the building. Zumbo Pumbo is trapped in one of the western cells alongside Ogro Nettles and Ceres Olsin . If freed, he dashes towards the Submersible to escape. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] The only action Zumbo uses on any turn is Dash , with the help of the Glimpse of Freedom condition which is applied when the cage is opened. Dash ( ) Cover more distance this turn: double your Movement Speed . Range: Self Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Leather Armour Explorer only [ edit section | visual editor ] Zumbo Pumbo has 50% more HP and cannot be pushed or shoved. CRE_Gith_Generic Veteran Raider Zunii is a githyanki Veteran Raider who lies in wait to ambush the party near the Road to Baldur's Gate in Reithwin Town within the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party are marked for death by Vlaakith , Ch'r'ai Tska'an , Zunii, and the rest of their unit lie in wait to ambush them as they approach the western gate to Reithwin Town. Carrying the Qua'nith Psionic Detector allows the party to spot the ambush and surprise the githyanki instead. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Misty Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Manoeuvres [ edit section | visual editor ] Zunii can spend up to five Superiority Die on manoeuvres : Rally ( + ) Healing 8 Temporary ⁠ Healing Expend a superiority die to bolster the resolve of a friendly creature. GOB_Goblin_Generic Zurga is a goblin stationed in the Goblin Camp during Act One . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Zurga patrols the north-east area of the Shattered Sanctum , periodically reporting to Minthara at her command post. If the party initiates combat, Zurga rushes to the nearest war drum to rally reinforcements. If the party initiates combat with Minthara, Zurga joins the battle, potentially causing Bez and Druk to join in. It is possible for Zurga to climb one of the ladders scattered throughout the Sanctum to safely engage the party at range by throwing stones or tossing Acid Vials . If Zurga is alive when the party starts the quest ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove , she is packed inside a Transport Barrel to be thrown to the ramparts by a Ogre Brute Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Goblin Scimitar Damage: 3~8 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Reckless Warcry ( ) Increase your Strength by 3, at the cost of decreasing your Armour Class by 1. Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Throw ( )   –   Acid Vial Damage Normal weapon damage Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. Your Strength affects how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Range: 3-18 m (10-60 ft) Throw Stone ( ) Damage: 3~6 1d4 + 2 ⁠ Bludgeoning Throws a sharp stone at a foe. Range: 9 m (30 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Acid Vial -2x (if unused) Goblin Scimitar Spiked Shield Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove Idle banter [ edit section | visual editor ] Zurga occasionally chats with Gurd in the goblin camp: Zurga Don't get too comfortable, you 'orrible sacks of muck. Drow might need us any time. Brawler Gurd Ain't been comfortable since we been here. I miss the swamp. Brawler Gurd Proper nice that swamp was. Zurga and Neem also occasionally chat during the celebration at camp: Zurga Minthara's pleased. Neem First time for everything. Zurga If she hears you, it'll be the last. Zurga Get any good scars during the raid? Neem Nah. True Souls did most of the fighting. Zurga Oi! I was right in the thick of it. Zurga We should have raided another tavern. Neem We should have raided a town . Zurga A city! Zurga Where do druids store their liquor? Neem I'm not even sure they drink liquor. CRE_Gith_Generic Gate Master Zyrlak is a githyanki in the Knights of the Shield Hideout in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Zyrlak concentrates on holding an Astral Rift open to summon the githyanki reinforcements Kharyk , Ma'aryk , and Ni'ima . If she loses concentration during the fight, or after she has summoned all three aforementioned githyanki, and the fight is still going on, she can participate in it. Technical UID Bulette UUID 0ea356fc-7a6f-4c60-8017-86349e2777ab Stats Bulette Variant 1 UID S_UND_Bulette UUID 307934b5-6fb5-4fdc-a7ff-433a7ba175b3 Stats Bulette Trs. UND_Bulette Bulettes are a type of Monstrosity in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are armoured monsters that burrow through underground tunnels and can suddenly erupt from the ground to strike. A single bulette burrows through the Underdark in Act One . “ The bulette's deep burrowing and powerful leap makes it an apex predator in nearly every terrain it finds itself in. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Bulettes are dangerous monstrosities. Their natural armour consists of thick plates layered across their bodies. They are typically native to hill environments but can be found in many different locations. Bulettes are sometimes referred to as Landsharks . A bulette's Territorial passive feature causes them to prioritise other monstrosity creatures. This can be used to the party's advantage when luring the bulette to fight other creatures. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 8~52 4d12 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Bite a target and possibly push it back 1.5 m / 5 ft. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Corrosive Phlegm ( ) Damage: 5~19 2d8 + 3 ⁠ Acid Expectorate on a target. DEX Save Range: 14 m (47 ft) Deadly Leap ( ) Damage: 14~44 3d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 3d6 + 4 ⁠ Slashing Leap to your targets, pushing them back 4 m / 13 ft, and possibly making them fall   Prone STR Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn AI only [ edit section | visual editor ] Burrow ( ) Healing: 18~74 8d8 + 10 ⁠ Healing Burrow into the ground to escape combat and recover hit points. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Honour Mode [ edit section | visual editor ] Shredding Scales Damage: 3~18 3d6 ⁠ Slashing Expel crystalline scales outward, possibly causing targets to Bleed . DEX Save Recharge: Per turn Legendary Action: Shredding Scales Once per turn, the Bulette can spend a Legendary Action to use Shredding Scales after being hit if its Diamond Scales are active. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Bloodguzzler Garb Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Concept art by Tan Bur-Ci Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The Bulette in the Underdark has scripted appearances at X: 120 Y: -175 and X: 160 Y: -150 . The Bulette grants 150 XP when killed. Glut can reanimate the Bulette. It is one of the toughest and highest-damage creatures that Glut can control; however, due to its large size, it may struggle to navigate tight areas and cannot climb ladders or similar devices. Applying Bone Chilled or Arrow of Ilmater to the Bulette before it uses Burrow prevents it from healing as it exits combat. The healing only restores its real hit points, not the temporary ones it has in Honour Mode. Command does not stop it from burrowing, but the Command applies when it next appears. The Bulette is suggested to be the entity which speaks with the party when Speak with Animals is used on the deep hole in the Underdark. Polymorphing the Bulette in Honour Mode does not remove its temporary hit points or its legendary action gained from Diamond Scales, but it prevents the Bulette from fighting back, allowing for the removal of Diamond Scales while the Bulette is defenceless. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] In Honour Mode, any effect applied to a reanimated Bulette that contains a Passive within its code (for example, Enlarge or Elixir of the Colossus ), regains its Diamond Scales and allows the use of its Legendary Action Shredding Scales . This is due to the application of Passive s triggering the OnCreate functor context found in DefaultStatus_Bulette_DiamondScales . A Dominated Red Dragon can be encountered Atop the Netherbrain in Act Three . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Always hostile and psychically enslaved by the Netherbrain , it serves as a major enemy in the final combat encounter of the game. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dominated Red Dragon is a Githyanki Dragon cohort which has been mind-controlled by the Netherbrain into defending the Crown of Karsus . Befitting a dragon encountered at the very end of the game, its base level and statistics are formidable even for a full-level party. Technical UID S_FOR_OwlBear UUID e903a41f-8ef7-46dc-a847-7d0ec2804d08 Stats S_FOR_OwlBear Variant 1 UID OwlBear UUID 6cd57ec0-7f04-452c-8fb9-31cae384b916 Stats OwlBear Owlbears are a type of beast creature located in the Owlbear Nest in Act One as an optional boss fight. Resembling large feathered bears with the head of an owl, they are quick to anger, very strong and seemingly have voracious appetites. While highly territorial, the owlbear mother's recent injury from the Cult of the Absolute has left her notably weakened. If the second attack hits, the target is pushed back 1.5 m / 5 ft and knocked   Prone . STR Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Per turn Honour Mode [ edit section | visual editor ] Call Consort Summon your mate to protect you in battle. Range: Self Recharge: Long rest Legendary Action: Call Consort Once per combat, the Owlbear mother can spend a Legendary Action to summon her mate when she is attacked. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] While the owlbear mother is already damaged by 8 points and cannot make Critical Hits because of her recent injury, she is still a powerful and dangerous creature. She also has the Distressed condition. Many of her abilities knock others Prone , such as Crushing Flight, allowing her to attack with Advantage on successive hits against her prone victim. When taken to half health, her rage ability triggers, increasing her damage with improved Strength and Multiattack . She also has the support of her Owlbear Cub , though he is weak and may be ignored. It is best to ignore her cub if the party plans to recruit him for the Camp . However, he attempts to flee if badly hurt. The owlbear mother's injury imposes Disadvantage on Perception checks which should cause a -5 penalty to Passive Perception to detect hidden creatures. However, it is offset by an unlisted +5 bonus to Perception which counteracts this penalty. Additionally, Andrick and Brynna can be convinced to help in the fight. They can act as useful distractions and support. Spells, items or weapon abilities that require a Dexterity Saving Throw like Grease , Grease Bottle or Topple are effective in slowing the owlbear. When the owlbear mother is enraged, it is best to finish the fight quickly before her multiattack shreds through the group. Convincing the owlbear mother not to attack outright is helpful for pre-combat positioning and allows the party to prepare a stealth ambush. There are two Fissured Stalactites attached to the rock overhangs just above the mother and cub. They can be shot with ranged weapons and damage whatever is beneath them on the cave floor for 6d4+4 Piercing damage. If the owlbear mother is hit with one, she realizes who triggered its fall and attacks the party. In Honour mode, Silencing or Incapacitating the owlbear mother prevents her from using her legendary action. Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Head of a Broken Spear Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Owlbear Render by Bert Vanhengel Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The owlbear mother in the Owlbear Nest is killed by goblins after a Long Rest after entering the cave. In the 5th edition of Dungeons and Dragons, an owlbear is classified as a Monstrosity , not a Beast . Owlbears being classified as Beasts in Baldur's Gate 3 is more in line with 3rd and 4th edition, although the owlbears get their in-game physical appearance from 5th edition. It is a boss encounter in the Whispering Depths and possesses several powerful abilities. “ In Her form I find ecstasy. The spell is not enough. „ — Eliette , on her transformation Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] History [ edit section | visual editor ] The phase spider matriarch was once an arachnomancer named Eliette [ 1 ] and worshipper of Lolth . She wished to transform so as to "refashion myself in the Queen's image". Unless removed with Fire or Acid damage, this glob of web will eventually explode, dealing 10d8 ⁠ ⁠ Poison [ See: Bugs ] to the entombed creature. DEX Save Range: 30 m (100 ft) Recharge: Per turn Allies [ edit section | visual editor ] Phase Spider - 2x Phase Spiderling - 17x, maximum possible, in 3 groups of 6, 6, and 5. Encounter details [ edit section | visual editor ] When combat begins, the Matriarch attempts to hatch her nearby Phase Spiderling eggs. There are three groups of 6 spider eggs scattered throughout the chamber, two on top of the large stone platforms and one at the base of a platform. The Phase Spider Matriarch uses its phase abilities to teleport around the arena. At 50% or less Hit Points , the Matriarch casts Spider Queen's Wrath on itself, entering into an enraged state. Knocking the Phase Spider Matriarch into one of the side holes labelled 'Chasm' kills her and grant the party 250xp. However, knocking her into the centre hole (not labelled 'Chasm') does not grant experience , but its corpse can be found in the Underdark (X:140 Y:151) to loot and possibly animate with Glut . On Tactician and Honour mode, the Matriach cannot be knocked into any of these drops since it just teleport back to its former location. The Phase Spider Matriach has +1 bonuses to Strength and Dexterity on Tactician difficulty, with resultant bonuses to Initiative , Armour Class , Attack rolls , and Saving throws , making an already fairly fierce early game enemy even deadlier. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] The Matriarch's eggs can be destroyed before the battle begins if the party can stay hidden (which also allows for an easy Pest Control achievement). Failing that, area damage spells work well on their low Hit Points . It is preferable to destroy all the eggs in Tactician/Honour mode due to her legendary action, but in lower difficulties it can be beneficial to leave a single egg behind in a batch as the Matriarch then essentially wastes an action to summon a single Phase Spiderling. Destroying the eggs with an Arrow of Fire destroys nearby webs even though it does not deal damage to any webs. If any webs are destroyed, a Phase spider will cast Ethereal Jaunt to find somebody who recently touched the web. In Honour mode, Spiritual Weapon can be used to kill a Phase Spiderling and the Matriarch will then use Gossamer Tomb on the Spiritual Weapon, but due to the weapon being immune to this action, this will essentially waste the Matriarch's legendary action. When the Matriarch is on a web bridge, destroying the bridge using ⁠ Fire damage inflicts a significant amount of fall damage on her (~45, varying with height). The stone platforms they connect to have no loot on them and are mostly accessible even without the bridges, thus it is recommended to use this tactic whenever the opportunity presents itself. Almost all of the Spider Matriarch's damage is ⁠ Poison so the party can benefit from casting Protection from Poison or drinking Elixir of Poison Resistance before entering combat. The matriarch never initiated combat. Combat log showed 90 exp reward for knocking her down the chasm. Lump the Enlightened and his ogres can prove valuable allies in the battle. They can be recruited just up above in the Blighted Village through a Charisma check or paying them 500g. This can result in a win-win situation where Lump is killed in the battle or is significantly weakened allowing the opportunity to easily obtain the Warped Headband of Intellect . It is advisable to spread party members out. Her venomous discharge ability has a large AoE radius. Exploits [ edit section | visual editor ] The middle spiderweb bridge has a stone outcrop that, when the matriarch stands on and the bridge destroyed, effectively neutralizes her: she will be stuck in her falling down animation but never move and, therefore, never enter combat. The combat log gives experience as if she has fallen into the Underdark , but the player can still kill her normally with ranged attacks afterward — yielding the kill experience reward and loot. This was found on a tactician playthrough and should work for honour mode. A good portion of the matriarch collision size(?) indicator is outside of the ledge. Kill any minions. Having other starting combat for the queen snaps her back to normal. Kill the eggs then the phase spider, use Minor Illusion to draw them away and into kill-box. Use a rogue and equip them with the Haste Helm for hit-and-run. This should be easy, given all of them have -2 intellect saving throw. Best setup location is the ledge gated by web: draw a spider into the low-ground directly below, activate combat mode first before attacking. Any location with similar advantage is also acceptable. Lure the queen with Minor Illusion to the outcrop. Attack the bridge then kill her with ranged, as going into melee triggers normal combat. Gold_Combat_Leader_Strong Spectators are a non-playable Aberration race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They have four eyestalks that can each cast debilitating rays. The Spectator's multiple eyestalks allow it to cast up to two rays per turn. “ Aggressive and greedy aberrations that believe their own forms to be the ideal, and hold all others - be it other beholders or 'lesser beings' - in contempt. „ — In-game racial description Contents 1 About 1.1 Where to find 2 Combat 2.1 Attacks and actions 2.2 Immunities 2.3 Honour mode 2.4 Loot 3 Notes 4 Bugs 5 Gallery 6 External links About [ edit section | visual editor ] Spectators are a lesser type of Beholder . They are floating creatures with a single huge eye and four eyestalks from which they can cast damaging or debilitating ray attacks. They come in two varieties, a normal version and a stronger variant with increased stats and HP. As many as five spectators can be encountered throughout the game: One stalks near the petrified drow in the Underdark , one is trapped inside the Iron Flask , two guard Hope's prison in the House of Hope , and one is in the courtyard of the High Hall . Where to find [ edit section | visual editor ] Iron Flask ⁠ High Hall ⁠ House of Hope ⁠ Underdark Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Spectators use a special kind of resource for their actions called Eyestalk action and can perform two Eyestalk Actions per turn. Bite ( ) Damage: 4~18 2d8 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Bite a target. Range: 2 m (7 ft) Confusion Ray ( ) Shoot an eye ray that Befuddles its target. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Fear Ray ( ) Shoot an eye ray that Frightens its target. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Paralysing Ray ( ) Shoot an eye ray that Paralyses its target. CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Unpetrification Ray ( ) Turn a Petrified creature back to its organic form. CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Wounding Ray ( ) Damage: 7~35 4d8 + 3 ⁠ Necrotic Shoot an eye ray that deals immense damage. CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Immunities [ edit section | visual editor ] Maimed Prone conditions, such as Prone and Hideous Laughter All Surfaces Honour mode [ edit section | visual editor ] In Patch #7 , the Spectator gained a Legendary Action . When struck, the Spectator accumulates stacks of Paranoid Dreams . When it reaches 5 stacks, it uses its reaction to cast Ocular Nightmare . The Legendary Action can be avoided by removing stacks of Paranoid Dreams, either by waiting for it to cast a ray attack or by intentionally moving close to the Spectator to trigger Panicked Sentinel . Any ray attack reduces Paranoid Dreams counter by 1. Ocular Nightmare Damage: 7~35 4d8 + 3 ⁠ Necrotic Possibly Wound , Confuse , Paralyse and Frighten all foes within 20 m (67 ft) with your flailing Eye Rays. CON Save Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Burnished Ring - dropped by one of the Spectators located in Hope's Prison in the House of Hope . The Spectator Eyes - dropped by the Spectator located in the Underdark . Severed Eye - dropped by the Spectator located in the Upper City . Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Some combinations, such as Frightened and Fog , cause the Spectator to teleport even though there is no mention that they are able to do this. There is also no mention of this special movement in the combat log. However, if Blinded (by, for example, using Malice ) the Spectator does not teleport. A Spectator contained inside the Iron Flask may be used to acquire the Silver Sword of the Astral Plane upon first entering the Mountain Pass in Act One by use of this guide . Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Contrary to the description of Sanctuary , Spectators can target characters protected by it. ## Steel Watcher Titan
- **来源**: [Steel Watcher Titan](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Steel_Watcher_Titan)
- **分类**: Bosses

Overview Combat Steel Watcher Titan Gortash's Magnum Opus In-game Render Full Name Steel Watcher Titan Stats Size Large Type Construct Race Steel Watcher Technical UID S_LOW_SteelWatcher_Prototype UUID 51db791d-4378-448a-86ba-3e3ae2748db6 Stats Steel_Watcher_Quadruped Trs. LOW_SteelwatcherTitan_Legendary_Bow_Treasure Steel Watcher Titan is a powerful Construct in the Steel Watch Foundry in Act Three . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Titan is the ultimate Steel Watcher , created by Enver Gortash and his Gondian workers to guard the Control Centre of the Steel Watch Foundry. Upon approaching the center of the room, the Steel Watcher Titan rises out of the floor and immediately engages the party in combat to protect the Steel Watch Foundry . Defeating the Titan allows the party to access the Neural Switchboard behind it which can blow up the entire factory. On Honour mode the Steel Watcher Titan is renamed the Hellfire Steel Watcher Titan and has the same red appearance as the regular Hellfire Watchers . Its abilities also become more powerful. ## Fog
- **来源**: [Fog](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fog)
- **分类**: Areas

See also: Fog Cloud Fog is a cloud that blinds and obscures creatures within, and blocks sight, blocking NPC sight cones and preventing attacks and spells which require sight. Description Heavily Obscures and Blinds creatures within. Properties Type: Cloud Condition: Blinded Blinded Duration: Whilst on surface Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range of attacks and spells reduced to 3 m (10 ft). Attack Rolls against Blinded creatures have Advantage . Creation This area can be created by the following: Items: Cloak of Cunning Brume Hammergrim Mist Amulet Spells and actions: Fog Cloud Wild Magic: Fog Notes There is a known bug regarding the IgnoreSurfaceCover internal boost which manifests with Fog . Specifically, if a surface has the property CanSeeThrough = false but CanShootThrough = true (like Fog Cloud ), any active IgnoreSurfaceCover boost allows a creature to see through it. Conversely, if CanShootThrough = false (like Darkness ), the creature must have the specific IgnoreSurfaceCover(SurfaceDarknessCloud) boost to see through it. The result is that features which grant sight through Magical Darkness (e.g., Devil's Sight ) implicitly grant sight through Fog, but Fog-specific protections do not work against Darkness. The Sight mechanics page explains this bug in further detail.

## Ice (surface)
- **来源**: [Ice (surface)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Ice_(surface))
- **分类**: Areas

This article is about the slippery ice surface. For other uses, see Ice (disambiguation) . Ice is a type of area . Created in numerous ways, it can knock Prone anyone who travels over it. Description Difficult terrain - movement speed is halved and creatures may fall Prone. Properties Type: Surface Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. Condition: Difficult Terrain Difficult Terrain Duration: Whilst on surface Movement Speed halved Creation This area can be created by the following: Items: Snowburst Ring Arrow of Ice Spells and actions: Blade of Rime Chromatic Orb: Cold Death Burst (Cold) Explosive Icicle Ice Knife Ice Storm Icy Regurgitation Magic Allergy: Ice Bloom Otiluke's Freezing Sphere (Launch) Sleet Storm Sphere of Elemental Balance: Cold Interactions Ice can be formed when many "wet" surfaces are exposed to ⁠ Cold damage. Ice formed this way lasts for 2 turns and melts into water afterwards. These surfaces include: Blood Water Alcohol Acid Simple Toxin and other coatings Ice melts into Water when exposed to ⁠ Fire damage. Ice surfaces created (by any method) on top of existing surfaces behave differently from those made on normal ground. Ice surfaces on normal ground instantly trigger a saving throw to fall Prone on creation, while those made on other surfaces do not. Blood surfaces are produced by most instances of physical damage , so to ensure that creatures make an initial save to fall Prone when creating an ice surface beneath them, avoid dealing physical damage. Notes When an ice surface is made through converting another surface with ⁠ Cold damage or by the Snowburst Ring , it uses the attacker's spell save DC (i.e., the spell save DC of their newest class). When created by a spell, it uses the spell save DC of the class to which the spell belongs (i.e., Intelligence-based spells use Intelligence for the spell save DC). The exception is Sleet Storm , which always uses the spell save DC of the caster's newest class. A creature slipping on an ice surface attributes the source of the Prone condition to the character that formed the ice surface. This can trigger the Boots of Stormy Clamour and similar effects. The Arrow of Ice uses a fixed DC 12 save to avoid becoming Prone for any creature in range of the initial hit. This is a different save from the Dexterity save of the ice surface left behind afterwards, which behaves as a non-spell-created ice surface and uses the spell save DC of the attacker's newest class. If a creature succeeds on the saving throw to fall Prone, it can walk up to 4 m (13 ft) before triggering the next saving throw. If an ice surface is created on top of another surface, the first saving throw is only triggered after more than 1 m (3 ft) of movement. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] An ice surface on a grassy, paved path at dusk. An ice surface as seen in the prologue.

## Lava
- **来源**: [Lava](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lava)
- **分类**: Areas

Lava is an area . Characters passing through lava are slowed and receive massive fire damage per turn. Description Deals 10d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Properties Type: Surface Condition: Melting Melting Duration: Whilst on surface Takes 10d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Condition: Difficult Terrain: Lava Difficult Terrain: Lava Duration: Whilst on surface Movement speed halved. Creation This area can be created by the following: Spells and actions: Create Lava Notes NPCs that die from Melting burn to ash and: can no longer be targeted by Speak with Dead gain a charred appearance offset with patches of glowing orange when inspected may lose certain items Most notably Nere's Head becomes unavailable if he burns to ash by melting, failing ⁠ Deliver Nere's Head Characters do not burn to ash if they: are a party member die from damage other than ⁠ fire while standing in lava are displaced into lava through certain mechanisms and die immediately from the damage taken (i.e. on the displacer's turn). The key factor appears to be that "killed while downed" overrides burning to ash. A non-exhaustive list includes: being Thrown does not trigger burning to ash. Neither does Telekinesis . being Shoved does trigger burning to ash, as do Boot of the Giants and Mobile Flourish (Ranged) displacement methods that would otherwise trigger burning to ash do not do so if the target is already Prone

Wall of Thorns is an area created by Wall of Thorns . It creates a passable barrier that deals heavy Piercing damage to all who enter. Description Giant, twisted thorns have sprouted from the ground. They deal 7d8 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing per turn, and quarter the movement speed of all creatures walking through it. Properties Type: Summoned Condition: Wall of Thorns Wall of Thorns DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) Walking through a wall of pliable, twisted thorns. While within the wall, the affected entity's movement speed is quartered, and it takes 7d8 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage per turn. Condition: Difficult Terrain Difficult Terrain Movement Speed halved Creation This area can be created by the following: Spells and actions: Wall of Thorns Notes The tooltip is wrong. While it claims the movement speed is quartered, it is using the normal Difficult Terrain condition which only halves.
## Water (surface)
- **来源**: [Water (surface)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Water_(surface))
- **分类**: Areas

See also: Water Water is a type of surface that can be created by numerous ways and manipulated by other elements. Description Douses unprotected flames. Can be electrified or frozen. Properties Type: Surface Dippable Creation This area can be created by the following: Items: Bubbling Cauldron Carafe of Water Decanter of Nearly Endless Water Holy Water Jug of Water Trident of the Waves Water Water Barrel Spells and actions: Create Water Slam (Water Elemental) Minor Conjuration: Create Water Interactions Turns into Electrified Water for Duration: 2 turns after being exposed to lightning damage. Reverts back to water afterwards. Turns into Ice for Duration: 2 turns after being exposed to ice damage. Reverts back to water afterwards. Turns into a Steam Cloud for Duration: 2 turns after being exposed to a fire surface. Notes As of Patch #6 , can be created by interacting with a water pump . Dipping a weapon into this surface removes Dipped in Fire , Dipped in Poison , and Burning on the weapon, if applicable. Standing on a Water Surface cleans off dirt and blood, as does using these items: Soap Bar , Sponge , Sponge Tray , and Mattis's Holy Hand Soap Water of sufficient depth (i.e. Deep Water) is considered Difficult Terrain in game.
## Web (surface)
- **来源**: [Web (surface)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Web_(surface))
- **分类**: Areas

This article is about the sticky surface. For the spell that creates this surface, see Web . Web is a type of Surface . When stepped on, characters will move at half speed and they might become Enwebbed . Web surfaces can be created through the use of spells or grenades. In areas where spiders live, webbed surfaces may be present. Description Difficult terrain - Movement Speed is halved. Can Enweb creatures. Prevents Falling damage. Flammable. Properties Type: Surface Condition: Enwebbed Enwebbed Duration: 1 turn DEX Save ( DC  12) Cannot move. Attack Rolls against the creature have Advantage , while the creature's Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws are rolled with Disadvantage . Condition: Difficult Terrain: Web Difficult Terrain: Web Duration: Whilst on surface Movement speed halved. Creation This area can be created by the following: Items: Web Grenade Spells and actions: Web Web (Spider Wild Shape) Web (Spider) Web (Phase Spider) Notes Prevents fall damage Contact with Fire turns it into a Fire surface. Contact with Blood turns it into a Blood surface. The DC for the Enwebbed condition depends on the caster, if created by a character. When Web is first applied, it can immediately enweb creatures. After that, enwebbed creatures are always released at the begininng of their turn, and creatures on the web area can become enwebbed only when they walk on the web at least 1 m, not when they Jump , Fly , or take any other kind of bonus action or action. For enwebbed creatures there is a saving throw at the beginning of the next turn, but they are released no matter whether they succeed or fail the save. Throwing a character onto this surface does not cause them to make the Dexterity saving throw with disadvantage, despite the fact that, according to the battle log, Prone is applied before the Dexterity saving throw.

The view, looking West, upon entering the Ancient Temple area Grymforge Grymforge ↑ Abandoned Refuge ↓ Adamantine Forge (location) The Abandoned Refuge (also known as the Ancient Forge ) is a Location within the Grymforge in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is south of and adjacent to Grymforge , and home to the Adamantine Forge and serves as a connecting landmass between the former and the latter, and overlooks Ancient Temple . Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Regional locations 1.2 The Adamantine Forge 2 Points of interest 2.1 Mithral veins 2.2 Landmarks 3 Waypoints 4 Related quests 5 Notable characters 6 Notable loot 6.1 Quest items 6.2 Moulds 6.3 Other notable 7 Gallery 8 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Looking East, towards a Mithral vein, near the Adamantine Forge The terrain of the Abandoned Refuge consists of crumbling architecture interspersed with caverns and lava flows, which frequently require jumping, or similar measures, to navigate. In this area, the player may discover two Mithral veins, from which they can extract Mithral Ore . This can be used in the adjoining the Adamantine Forge location. The Adamantine Forge [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Adamantine Forge South-east of the Ancient Forge waypoint and down a set of broken stairs is the Adamantine Forge. The forge can be used to create armour or a weapon by loading it with a piece of Mithral Ore and a mould. There are only two pieces of ore available, so only two items total can be crafted. ## Adamantine Forge (location)
- **来源**: [Adamantine Forge (location)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Adamantine_Forge_(location))
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

This article is about the location. For the quest, see Adamantine Forge (quest) . The Ancient Forge. Grymforge Abandoned Refuge ↑ Adamantine Forge The Adamantine Forge is a Location within Grymforge in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ ...somewhere deep, loud, and hot as the Hells themselves. Within the Underdark's bowels, beyond an ancient stronghold, hovers a giant hammer, waiting to fall. „ — Reflections in Dhourn's Memory Shard Contents 1 Overview 2 Using the Adamantine Forge 2.1 Armour 2.2 Shields 2.3 Weapons 3 History 4 Waypoints 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Creatures 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 Gallery 10 References 11 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Adamantine Forge is an area inside Abandoned Refuge , adjacent to the Grymforge area, and shares the same region. From the area where the waypoint is located, a rocky path descends to X: -568 Y: 243 , to the forge mechanism. The forge itself is a gargantuan round platform with four lesser round daises, curved paths between them with gaps for the lava to flow down, and a crucible in the middle. It has two positions: upper (initial) and lower, to which it must be moved during the forging process. From the upper position, at X: -570 Y: 229 , the party can also jump onto a crumbled structure that leads to a lava lake with a Lava Elemental wandering about, where the quest ⁠ Help the Spirit of the Amulet can be started or progressed. Experience for discovering this medium-sized location is gained halfway down the broken staircase: 75XP, 150XP, or 180XP at character levels 4, 5, or 6, respectively. Using the Adamantine Forge [ edit section | visual editor ] The basic elements controlling the forging process are scattered around the platform: the mould chamber (with the lever that ejects the mould after crafting) is near the crucible, the lever which lowers the hammer is in the middle of one of the daises, and the valve that allows a portion of lava flow into the crucible is near the furnace, on a grate near another dais. When poured in, lava covers all the platform surface save for the four daises, curved paths between them, and the grates near the valve. The top of the crucible also remains uncovered - to receive the hammer's blow. Instructions for operating the forge can be found in a book obtained from Xargrim's corpse in the Ebonlake Grotto in Underdark : “ Place the ore and mould into their respective chambers. Pull the lever to lower the hammer and prepare the ore for smelting. Open the valve to allow lava into the crucible, and drop the hammer again to forge the product. „ — The Great Furnace of Grymforge tome Every recipe requires one Mithral Ore . However, there are only two pieces of ore available. One can be found southwest of the Ancient Forge Waypoint, following the path down to a lava flow. The vein is clearly visible on the opposite "shore" at X: -645 Y: 255 . The other can be found in a library-resembling area located east from the path leading down to the Forge platform. The vein is bulging from the archway at X: -558 Y: 278 . Therefore, the player character is able to craft any two items from the following list: Armour [ edit section | visual editor ] Name AC Slot Effect Mould Adamantine Scale Mail 16 Armour  ( Medium Armor ) Attackers can't land Critical Hits on the wearer. Magical Plate All incoming damage is reduced by 1 Adamantine Backlash When a melee attack hits you, the attacker is sent Reeling for 2 turns. Scale Mail Mould Adamantine Splint Armour 18 Armour  ( Heavy Armor ) Attackers can't land Critical Hits on the wearer. Magical Plate All incoming damage is reduced by 2. Intense Adamantine Backlash When a melee attack hits you, the Attacker is sent Reeling for 3 turns. Splint Mould Shields [ edit section | visual editor ] Name AC Slot Effect Mould Adamantine Shield +2 Off-Hand Melee  ( Shield ) Attackers can't land critical hits on the wearer. Shield Blow ( ) When a foe hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to knock it   Prone , unless they succeed a Strength saving throw . Adamantine Shield When a melee attack misses you, the attacker is sent Reeling for 2 turns. Shield Mould Weapons [ edit section | visual editor ] Name Slot Effect Mould Adamantine Longsword Main Hand Melee  ( Longsword ) Diamondsbane If an adamantine weapon hits an object, the hit is always critical. Lethal Weapon This weapon ignores Resistance to ⁠ Slashing damage. Longsword Mould Adamantine Mace Main Hand Melee  ( Mace ) Diamondsbane If an adamantine weapon hits an object, the hit is always critical. Lethal Weapon This weapon ignores resistance to ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. Mace Mould Adamantine Scimitar Main Hand Melee  ( Scimitar ) Diamondsbane If an adamantine weapon hits an object, the hit is always critical. Lethal Weapon This weapon ignores Resistance to ⁠ Slashing damage. Scimitar Mould Any mould can be used twice to craft two identical items. To do this, the party must first eject the previously used mould from the Mould Chamber via the lever, pick it up and place it inside again, and repeat the whole cycle. The first time the Lava Valve is used, Grym appears to defend the forge. Also, during the fight with it, several Magma Mephits emerge from surrounding lava. To raise the platform, a button located behind the hammer-operating lever can be used. Raising the platform to its initial position makes the forge nonfunctional. Therefore, if the platform is raised before a second item is created, further crafting becomes impossible until it is re-lowered using the platform control button. History [ edit section | visual editor ] Adamantine is an incredibly hard alloy, forged at very high temperatures by alloying an adamant ore with mithral. Due to the difficulty of creating it, adamantine is usually produced by dwarves. The Adamantine Forge was probably first constructed along with the Grymforge fortress in an unknown age by a group of Sharran followers. The inscription on the plaque at the entrance to the platform implies that the forge itself probably existed even before Ketheric Thorm's coming, as its wording melted away "several centuries" ago. After its take over by Dark Justiciars of Shar, the forge was redesigned by Silouv Yali , a gnome well known for his talents for wizardry and converted to the Sharran faith by the Sharran priestess Sister Ansar. After a sequence of experiments, he managed to find a way to bring its temperatures high enough to produce adamantine. However, Silouv Yali's magnum opus was not the forge, but Grym , a powerful construct said to be immune to both blades and spells, an eternal guard of the forge. Unfortunately for Dark Justiciars, Yali used most of the available adamantine for creating the automaton, and thus nearby veins became too scarce to provide enough metal for the Sharrans' armaments. [ 1 ] After all the Dark Justiciars were eliminated by an Orthon , the Adamantine Forge sank into darkness once more. ## Apothecary's Cellar
- **来源**: [Apothecary's Cellar](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Apothecary's_Cellar)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

Hidden laboratory within the Apothecary's Cellar. The Apothecary's Cellar is a Location within the Blighted Village in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ A hidden laboratory full of abandoned experiments. Colour me in my element. „ — Gale , entering the Necromancer's Lab Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 1.2 Main Cellar 1.3 Cavernal Antechamber 1.4 Necromancer's Lab 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters and Creatures 5 Loot 5.1 Hidden treasure 6 Literature 7 Achievements 8 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Access [ edit section | visual editor ] The Apothecary's Cellar is located underneath the Blighted Village and is accessible from a hatch in the abandoned apothecary building, which is near the entrance of the village at coordinates X: 32 Y: 379 . Inside the building behind the main counter on the floor is a Wooden Hatch through which the party can descend into the cellar. Main Cellar [ edit section | visual editor ] This section has a share of potions and alchemical ingredients scattered around in containers (mostly wooden barrels) and on the shelves, as well as in the wooden chest near the northern wall. On the desk next to the chest is a Healer's Log and Potion of Healing Recipe . Reading the former book helps to proceed into the Necromancer's Lab (see below). A lever is hidden behind a stack of crates at X: -704 Y: -353 . It is highlighted after passing a passive DC 15 Perception Check , but can also be found through normal investigation. Pulling it opens a hidden passage behind a bookcase at X: -695 Y: -350 , leading into the next chamber. Cavernal Antechamber [ edit section | visual editor ] “ The blacksmith. The teacher. The grocer. The baker. Little piggies to the butcher. „ — Shovel , when asked about the identities of the guardians This natural cavern has eight mouldering caskets scattered around. The casket closest to the tunnel entrance holds the Scroll of Summon Quasit along with two bottles of Alchemist's Fire and a Poo-Scraper . The scroll can be used to cast the spell immediately, or transcribed by a Wizard character. [ 1 ] Casting the spell summons Shovel - previously the familiar of the former owner of the laboratory. Talking to her sheds some light onto the personality of her master. Interacting with any of the other caskets caused a skeletal guardian to burst out of it, surprising the party. Apart from attacking the party, the skeleton tries to run off to the other caskets, breaking them open and spawning more undead. There can possibly be three Robust Guardians and four Agile Guardians in total. Attacking any of the caskets still causes the skeletons to emerge, but without surprising the party. Defeating all spawned skeletal guardians before they smash up remaining caskets prevents other guardians from appearing; extra xp and loot is then forfeited. An effective strategy for dealing with the guardians is to drag all the caskets (by clicking and dragging) into a pile or stack and use Cloud of Daggers or similar persistent ground attacks on them, breaking them all and wounding all guardians simultaneously and over multiple turns. This ensures loot and experience from all. Also, several fissured stalactites on the cavern vault can be shot down to damage whoever stands under them. At X: -669 Y: -318 a passive DC 15 Survival Check reveals hidden treasure. When the casket at X: -664 Y: -315 is opened or destroyed by a fellow guardian, a Dark Journal falls out. Reading it reveals more information on the lab owner, progresses the ⁠ Search the Cellar , and provides an additional option when interacting with the Ornate Mirror (see below). At the south end of the cave is a wooden platform with a magical Ornate Mirror on the wall. Interacting with it can open the way forward into the hidden lab. Convincing the mirror to let the party through earns the ⁠ Mirror Master for the characters with the Charlatan background. Failing to convince the mirror causes it to unleash a floating flaming sphere which circles around the room, leaving a trail of fire. It takes a route throughout the cavern and partly into the tunnel leading in before losing power and returning into the mirror. The sphere attacks any object on sight, dealing 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire , with a DC  12 Dexterity Saving Throw to halve the damage. After two appearances, its power dwindles, and it is possible to interact with the mirror again. This can be done as many times as needed. For the details and possible dialogue options to operate the mirror, see the Ornate Mirror page. Also, the mirror can be destroyed by attacking it or choosing certain dialogue options. Necromancer's Lab [ edit section | visual editor ] The lab itself is a vast hall with the main workspace in the centre and several smaller rooms around it. Various containers in the lab and in the rooms contain alchemical ingredients, notably Acorn Truffles , which can rarely be found freely while exploring. In the centre of the lab there is an alchemists's workspace, where a Scroll of Feather Fall and some Basilisk Oil can be taken. Also, several documents and books describing the lab owner's concerns can be found. The lesser rooms when coming around from most-eastern are: A storeroom (almost across the entrance) with several containers with alchemical components. A lever in the far end moves a wall section to get back into the main cellar [ 2 ] . On the shelf is a Rusted Key (Apothecary) . A room with a stuffed bear. A wooden chest at X: -679 Y: -370 contains several random scrolls. A small library. The gilded chest at X: -656 Y: -369 contains the Bracers of Defence . On the east side is a gated off cavernous area which holds the real prize of this lab, the Necromancy of Thay . A Marble Plate just before the rusted iron gate can be detected by a DC 15 Perception Check . It activates the traps inside: two Gargoyle Statues on the each side and a pressure plate on which the tome itself is placed. A DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check can pick the gate lock, or the party can use the Rusted Key from the storeroom shelves. Alternatively, spells like Misty Step or Mage Hand can be used to bypass the gate. Each of the four traps here can be disabled with a DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check . Otherwise, turn-based mode can be used to take the book and replace it with any other object, or simply rush out before the fire bolts from gargoyle statues are hurled. The first interaction with the book updates the ⁠ Search the Cellar quest, adding to the journal two subquests to it: ⁠ Unlock the Ancient Tome and ⁠ Destroy the Ancient Tome . Astarion , Karlach , and Wyll may prompt their opinion on the tome, if they are in the party. Once the Dark Amethyst is acquired, any party member can try to read the tome, binding it to them permanently. The full list of possible interactions with the book, as well as companions' approval towards each of them, can be found at the Necromancy of Thay page. ## Arcane Tower
- **来源**: [Arcane Tower](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Arcane_Tower)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The Arcane Tower overlooking the Ebonlake. Underdark Decrepit Village ↑ Arcane Tower → Selûnite Outpost The Arcane Tower is a Location within the Underdark in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . The tower overlooks the Ebonlake, and belongs to Lenore De Hurst . However, she has not returned home in over a decade. “ New sounds through damp and dark oppression break. Is it the foe, that foul, contemptuous heel? „ — Bernard , asking the rhymed parole Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 1.1.1 Dealing with the Arcane Turrets 1.2 Ground floor (generator room) 1.3 First floor (greenhouse) 1.4 Second floor (main entrance) 1.5 Third floor (bedroom) 1.6 The fourth floor (roof) 1.7 The basement (secret room) 2 Layout 3 Bernard's commands 4 Related locations 4.1 Torchstalk Gulch 4.2 Festering Cove 5 Related quests 6 Characters 7 Creatures 8 Loot 8.1 Ground Floor (generator room) 8.2 First floor 8.3 Second floor (main entrance) 8.4 Third floor (bedroom) 8.5 Fourth floor (roof) 8.6 Basement (secret room) 8.7 Alchemy 9 Literature 10 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Access [ edit section | visual editor ] The Arcane Tower is in the south-west corner of the Underdark map. This area is recognizable by its neatly built stone entryway that opens to a front garden featuring two Arcane Turrets . It can be reached through the Torchstalk Gulch, recognisable by its dark brown paths paved with deep red mushroom clusters and spots of Torchstalk that cast floating embers into the air. [ 1 ] The area is divided roughly into the entry area, each floor of the tower, and the garden outside the ground floor. Upon initial approach, the doors are shut and the central elevator is disabled; the floors must be accessed through other means. The party can use the fungus platforms growing around the tower to Jump their way down to the ground floor, starting either from the southern balcony of the Second floor, or from the breach in stone railing near entrance at X: 3 Y: -296 (just behind the turret). It is a good idea to cast Feather Fall to prevent unnecessary fall damage. Alternatively, using Fly or teleporting (via Misty Step ) also gets the party down without issues. Dealing with the Arcane Turrets [ edit section | visual editor ] An active Arcane Turret The Arcane Tower is guarded by automated Arcane Turrets . They are automatically hostile and shoot at the party whenever they are in the line of sight and in range; there is a targeting indicator which can show this. Anything that breaks this line of sight (e.g. solid obstacles or Fog Cloud ) effectively stops the attacks. The turrets shoot and attack in real-time exploration mode as well as in turn-based mode. However, it is recommended to turn on turn-based mode to make movement and controlling the party more manageable. In general, there are a few approaches to dealing with these the Arcane Cannons: Attacking - the cannons can be directly damaged and rendered inoperable. They have some resistances, and vulnerability to ⁠ Lightning . Override - the cannons can be shut down once restoring power on the generator on the ground floor. Running by / Stealth - this is best done in turn-based mode as it allows the party members to move cover-to-cover between turns. Anti-Magic - as the Arcane Cannons are magical constructs, they can be shut down by placing a Sussur Bloom near them, because of their Sussur Antimagic Field . Sussur Blooms can be found in the garden at the bottom of the Arcane Tower, or at the Sussur Tree in Dread Hollow . Attacking a Cannon while it is shut-down by the Anti-Magic field destroys it, as opposed to "knocking it out". Cannons which have previously been rendered inoperable but not destroyed can actually be revived by the Sussur Antimagic Field, by first placing and then taking back a Sussur Bloom near them. Ground floor (generator room) [ edit section | visual editor ] The door to the Ground floor is locked (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick). However, it can also be opened with a lever from inside, and a Hole at X: -50 Y: -304 (detected with DC 5 Perception Check ) allows any small summon (like Mage Hand ) to seep inside and use the lever. Once inside, the clues on how to restore power to the generator of the Arcane Tower are clear: several Withered Blue Petals on the floor near its furnace, and also a book titled Treatise on the Antimagic Properties of Sussur Tree Flowers on the workbench nearby. A Sussur Bloom must be inserted in the power generator. Sussur Blooms can be found at the Garden just outside the door, or taken from the giant sussur tree in the Dread Hollow . The party must interact with the Power Generator to bring up the crafting menu and use it to combine the machine with a Sussur Bloom. The Arcane tower comes to life, granting 25 xp and the inspiration ⁠ Regeneration for party members with the Guild Artisan background. Once the generator is powered, the Arcane Turrets power down, the Arcane Braziers become lit, and the elevator can be used to ascend and descend between the floors. At halfway from the generator room to the elevator chamber, at X: -53 Y: -284 , in a Gilded Chest lies the Uncovered Mysteries necklace. Also, the barrels and crates around the elevator and in the generator room contain a fair amount of alchemical ingredients, mostly of mushroom and crystal derivation. First floor (greenhouse) [ edit section | visual editor ] This floor can only be accessed by the restored elevator, by flying, or by using the platforms on the exterior fungus on the south side of the tower. This is a level that contains all the mushrooms required for the quest ⁠ Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite . The other notable item on this floor is the Threadbare Book containing the phrase: "How can I trust? How should I know? How can I show myself, my darkest me?" , which provides an additional option for interacting with Bernard on the roof. Second floor (main entrance) [ edit section | visual editor ] The main floor can be accessed directly through the front door of the tower, or via the elevator after it is powered. Opening the Main Door requires succeeding on a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check , or it can be broken down - it has Medium Toughness and 36 hit points. Alternatively, there is a broken window to the left of the door that can be entered. Opening this door prior to the restoration of power leads to a confrontation with two Arcane Turrets, one of which is stationed right across the broken window. A Dusty Book can be found on this floor. After reading, it changes its title to Evil's Ascent . On the northern balcony is the Chest of the Mundane , which is revealed as magical with a successful Arcana check. Taking the clutter from the chest in the inventory, or placing a Sussur Bloom near the chest, dispels the illusion to reveal some scrolls and Mystra's Grace . The latter can provide the party an additional casting of Feather Fall which can help them avoid some damage trying to access the ground floor. Observing the effects of the chest grants the inspirational event ⁠ Trash & Treasure for characters with the Guild Artisan . The southern balcony does not contain any notable items, but lets the party access the exterior fungus platforms to the lower levels. Third floor (bedroom) [ edit section | visual editor ] The Roads to Darkness book on Lenore's desk. This floor can only be accessed by the restored elevator or by flying. If wanting a peaceful interaction with Bernard, this floor contains documents the party can inspect prior to ascending to the fourth floor (roof). The book The Roads to Darkness can be found on the desk at the South-Eastern corner at X: -25 Y: -297 and a Torn-Out Paper on the table close to the elevator at X: -35 Y: -286 . The book contains a stance that leads Bernard to take the player character for the tower hostess, while the separate page provides them with an additional interaction with the automaton. The Orpheus, Prince of the Comet, Part One: Betrayal can be found on top of a bookshelf at X: -31 Y: -296 . If Lae'zel is in the party, she can read it straightaway; if she is not available, the disc can be read after picking up and using the The Careful Art of Tir'su Ciphers from the table near the elevator at X: -32 Y: -292 , or after succeeding on a DC 20 Intelligence Check . Also, the player character may discuss the disc with Lae'zel upon returning to the camp. Either way, deciphering the disc starts a quest ⁠ Discover the History of Prince Orpheus . Aside from the books and notes, the magical ring Mage's Friend can also be looted on this floor in a wooden chest by the bed, at X: -29 Y: -273 . Lastly, there is an interactable button at the north-eastern corner of the tower which appears to do nothing when pressed. To function, the party must retrieve and equip the Dog Collar from the grave at the Dread Hollow at X: -41 Y: -212 , prior to interacting with it. Doing so reveals the button served as a food dispenser for Lenore's pet, Myrna, as a piece of Raw Steak appears, but only if the button is pressed by the same party member who wears the collar. If the collar had been dug up, but was not equipped, or the button was pressed by another character, the party member currently having it in the inventory or wearing it comments, feeling it vibrating. The button can be pressed multiple time, but gives the treat only once and after that its mechanism is deactivated. The Handwritten Letter ( Letter from Amarith after the first reading) on Lenore's desk sheds some light on Myrna's story, and also on reasons that caused a Bulette to roam around the tower. If Myrna's grave in the Dread Hollow has not been inspected by the party by this moment, reading the letter adds an option to place an Autumncrocus on it, earning approval from Gale , Karlach and Wyll . The fourth floor (roof) [ edit section | visual editor ] This floor can only be accessed by the restored elevator or by flying. Upon arriving at the floor, a dialogue is triggered with Bernard , who is standing guard by the elevator along with a group of Animated Armours . Bernard speaks only in poetry, with the scattered lines found throughout the Arcane Tower serving as various command phrases for him. In the first meeting, if the party read The Roads to Darkness they can respond with "Or art though friend, a rescue from my lonely wake?" which prevents Bernard from becoming hostile and attacking. Of all character Classes, only Bards can roll a passive DC 18 History Check here, and if successful, they remember the correct line continuing the stanza. Successfully placating Bernard grants the party 50 XP, and also earns the ⁠ Heart of the Creator inspirational event to any party member with Entertainer . Afterwards, there are several dialogue options / commands the party can use with Bernard, depending on what they have read (see #Bernard's commands ). The Guiding Light ring can be obtained by reciting "How can I trust? How will I ever know? / How can I show myself, my darkest me?" from the Threadbare Book on the first floor, or by destroying Bernard in combat. It cannot be pick-pocketed. Destroying Bernard (or commanding them to drop their weapon) also grants the party the Light of Creation . There is also a lever next to a bookshelf at X: -40 Y: -296 , which can be noticed with a DC 18 Perception Check . This is an alternate way to open the wall on the first floor that leads to the basement. Lastly, there is the Stool of Hill Giant Strength at X: -26 Y: -272 , behind one of the Animated Armours. Party members can sit on the stool and notice its magical effect, as well as its disappearance once they stand up. If they break the stool, they can obtain the Club of Hill Giant Strength from its debris. The basement (secret room) [ edit section | visual editor ] Flying down to the secret basement room. There are several ways to access the basement: Using the elevator with Guiding Light equipped (an additional "Basement" button appears at the controls) Using Fly or Misty Step to go through a gap from the first floor Using Mage Hand or a ranged attack to activate a lever under the staircase to open the wall Activating the lever on the fourth floor hidden next to a bookshelf. In the basement, aside from more Tongue of Madness and Timmask Spores , the party can also find the Staff of Arcane Blessing leaning against a table, The Sparkswall in a gilded chest, and an assortment of scrolls in the chest and various rows of books. Layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Tower layout Level How to access Notable elements Ground floor (Generator) The exterior Garden can be access by flight , jumping or teleporting on outside the tower. The locked ground floor itself can be accessed by the Back Door or through a Hole in the wall. Contains the generator that allows you to restore power to the tower. The elevator itself is located on a mezzanine, with the rest of the basement beneath it. 1st Floor (Greenhouse) Can be reached by the elevator, flight, or by jumping or teleporting on the mushrooms on the tower exterior. Contains the quest related items Tongue of Madness , Timmask Spores ). If the party don't want to explore the rest of the tower, they only have to visit this one floor. 2nd Floor (Main Entrance) Can be accessed by the Main Door . Or flight and elevator if approaching from another level. Contains the Chest of Mundane with Mystra's Grace + two Scrolls ) and 2x Arcane Cannons . 3rd Floor (Bedroom) Can be reached by the elevator and / or flight . Contains key elements that allows the party to converse with Bernard and other constructs peacefully. 4th Floor (Roof) Can be reached by the elevator and / or flight . This level contains Bernard, and the Guiding Light ring which is one method to visit the basement. Basement (Secret Room) Can be reached by the elevator with the Guiding Light ring equipped, by flying or using Misty Step through a gap from the 1st level, by using Mage Hand to activate a lever under the staircase, by using a bow to activate the lever under the staircase through the staircase, or by activating the lever on the 4th floor hidden next to a bookshelf. Contains treasures - including the Staff of Arcane Blessing , The Sparkswall , and another set of the quest items Tongue of Madness, Timmask Spores). Bernard's commands [ edit section | visual editor ] Line Action Required book "How can I trust? How will I ever know? / How can I show myself, my darkest me?" Bernard gives Guiding Light to the player character. Threadbare Book (first floor / greenhouse) "These empty sheets are all that's left of you. / The last of all the thoughtless gifts you gave." Bernard gives the player character a Potion of Greater Healing . Patched Parchment (table next to Bernard, fourth floor) "The silence stretches on - I'm all alone. / Please, can I hold your hands, for just a while?" Bernard hugs the player character and reassure them. It speaks as if the player character is Lenore. Torn-Out Paper (third floor / bedroom) "Or art thou friend, a rescue from my lonely wake?" Bernard acknowledges the player character as their master, and remains passive. The Roads to Darkness (third floor / bedroom) "There is a light in every living thing. / It's crawling t'wards the surface to survive." Bernard and the nearby Animated Armours become hostile and attack. Evil's Ascent (second floor / main entrance, marked as Dusty Book before reading it) Related locations [ edit section | visual editor ] View from the South Torchstalk Gulch [ edit section | visual editor ] To the east of the tower, this unnamed area of the Underdark has deep red mushroom clusters and spots of Torchstalk that cast floating embers into the air. The corpse of an unfortunate Drow can be found, having been killed by an unexpected fall. The party can climb mushrooms along the wall to reach an upper level. Some of these mushrooms are illusions that de-materialise when stepped on or discovered with a DC 10 Investigation Check . There are also some mushroom circles, one behind an illusory wall, on the upper level and below. These connect to each other, until the circle in the Overgrown Tunnel is used. They can then be used to travel to the Overgrown Tunnel near the the Riverside Teahouse and back. Festering Cove [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: The Festering Cove The Festering Cove is a partially hidden location on a separate Underdark map, where Kuo-toa worship their "god", BOOOAL . It can be reached by climbing down the cragged rock in Torchstalk Gulch X: 80 Y: -241 . Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Discover the History of Prince Orpheus ⁠ Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Bernard Creatures [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Turret Animated Armour Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Notable items obtained in this location, whether looted, purchased, or obtained as a quest reward: Skybreaker inside a locked chest in-front of the tower X: 27 Y: -298 Ground Floor (generator room) [ edit section | visual editor ] Uncovered Mysteries First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Timmask Spores Tongues of Madness Second floor (main entrance) [ edit section | visual editor ] Broken Machineries Mystra's Grace inside the Chest of the Mundane Third floor (bedroom) [ edit section | visual editor ] Mage's Friend in a chest at the foot of the bed on the 3rd floor Fourth floor (roof) [ edit section | visual editor ] Broken Machineries Club of Hill Giant Strength from breaking the Stool of Hill Giant Strength on the 4th floor of the tower Guiding Light looted or gifted from Bernard after using the appropriate play line Light of Creation looted from Bernard (can also use Command: Drop ) Basement (secret room) [ edit section | visual editor ] Staff of Arcane Blessing The Sparkswall Timmask Spores Tongues of Madness Level 3 Spell Scroll (randomised) Alchemy [ edit section | visual editor ] Apart from Timmask Spores and Tongue of Madness , the latter of which can be looted only in the Arcane Tower, this location is the only place where the player character can obtain Broken Machinery (on the fourth floor and also in crates on the second floor) used to craft Elixir of Lightning Resistance .
