## Storehouse
- **来源**: [Storehouse](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Storehouse)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

An overview of the Storehouse Underdark Ebonlake Grotto ← Storehouse ↓ Selûnite Outpost The Storehouse is a Location within the Underdark in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ The Black Network's mark. Spies, murderers, and thieves ahead, I guess. „ — Astarion , recognizing the markings on crates [ 1 ] Contents 1 Overview 1.1 The Zhentarim storehouse 1.2 Minotaur hills 2 Related locations 3 Creatures 4 Loot 5 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Storehouse is located in the most north-eastern quadrant of the Underdark map. The unnamed area between it and the Selûnite Outpost features bright green grass and whimsical red mushrooms with swirling paths. This part contains two points of possible entering the Underdark. The party can use the elevator from the overland's Zhentarim Basement (which must be unlocked from upside), or land at X: 140 Y: -150 , after jumping into the hollow within the Whispering Depths (using means like Feather Fall are necessary to avoid immediate death). Entering the Underdark the latter way grants the ⁠ Abyss Jumper inspiration to party members with the Outlander background. This area does not have any interactable neutral or allied NPCs. The Zhentarim storehouse [ edit section | visual editor ] The Storehouse is crammed with various containers, mostly wooden crates and trunks, as well as several locked Rustic Chests, and also one locked and trapped Heavy Chest not far from the elevator. If the storehouse is reached from the other part of the Underdark, any party member can recognize the symbols on the crates at X: 141 Y: -100 as belonging to the Zhentarim (no Ability check is needed, but if entering the region through the elevator from the Zhentarim Hideout, a different remark is uttered). The area can be looted for a large amount of Valuables , Ammunition , alchemical resources, Camp Supplies and common weapons. If the party comes to tne Underdark by any means other than the elevator, unlocked from above, it cannot be used to leave the area. Approaching the entrance to the storehouse, the party may feel an earthquake. It does no harm, but a random party member comments on it. The Storehouse is divided from the other parts of the Underdark by the rope netting. The ground at the foot of the netting is trapped with several hidden Blast Mines , which can be noticed with a passive perception check. Triggering any of them starts a chain explosion that may eventually destroy the netting and alerts nearby Minotaurs . However, it is possible to climb up or descent through a series of jumps onto rocky steps and giant mushroom caps just aside. Minotaur hills [ edit section | visual editor ] While the Storehouse is free of any enemies, the adjacent territory features three wandering Minotaurs , which turn hostile on sight. However, if the party enter the Underdark through the Selûnite outpost, one of them may run to attack the iron portcullis and is then burned to death by the Moonstone rays of its magical defence. Most part of the area (all the way to the barricades before the Selûnite Outpost) is considered as demesne by the Myconids of the nearby Ebonlake Grotto colony, with the boundaries seen as purplish speckles in the air. When first entering the myconid-controlled area, the party feel the effect of Rapport Spores and are engaged into the dialogue with "Cryptic Voice" through it, warning them of the Minotaurs ahead. A successful DC 15 Nature Check helps to detect the spores, and any party member comments on it regardless of result. The path leading from the Minotaur Hills down to the Ebonlake Grotto is one of the places where the party might encounter a Bulette . Related locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Zhentarim Basement Creatures [ edit section | visual editor ] Minotaur Bulette - possibly Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Various alchemical resources, Ammunition , Elixirs , Valuables , and Camp Supplies Thieves' Tools and Trap Disarm Toolkits Buried chest at X: 140 Y: -120 In the locked and trapped Heavy Chest: Scroll of False Life - 3x Scroll of Speak with Dead -2x Looted from the Minotaur wielding a weapon: Amulet of the Unworthy Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ This remark, as well as similar ones from other companions, is heard only if approaching the Storehouse from the Underdark. v t e Underdark Characters Attached Followers Glut Creatures Bulette Hook Horror Minotaur Spectator Decrepit Village Garmor Gekh Coal Holvik Lurgan Shattered Duergar Dread Hollow Baelen Bonecloak Filro Ebonlake Grotto Dead Myconid Sprout Deep Rothé Duergar Spore Servant (guard caster) Duergar Spore Servant (guard melee) Duergar Spore Servant (patrol melee) Duergar Spore Servant (ranged) Hook Horror Spore Servant Mossy Myconid Noxious Myconid Restless Myconid Spaw Thulla Xargrim Festering Cove BOOOAL Kuo-toa Kuo-toa Hunter Pooldripp Petrified Drow Arcagh Artimezt Dhourn Izwae Moy Tecothy Plants Barrelstalk Bibberbang Nightlight Timmask Torchstalk Traders Blurg Derryth Bonecloak Omeluum Other Animated Armour Bernard Dead Drow Locations Arcane Tower Decrepit Village Dread Hollow Ebonlake Grotto Festering Cove Selûnite Outpost Storehouse Quests Avenge Glut's Circle Cure the Poisoned Gnome Defeat the Duergar Intruders Deliver Nere's Head Find a Cure Find the Missing Boots Find the Mushroom Picker Find the Nightsong Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Reach Moonrise Towers
## Sunlit Wetlands
- **来源**: [Sunlit Wetlands](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Sunlit_Wetlands)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The Sunlit Wetlands scape Wilderness Blighted Village ↑ Riverside Teahouse ← Sunlit Wetlands → Nautiloid Wreck ↓ River Chionthar The Sunlit Wetlands (also known as the Putrid Bog ) is a Location within the Wilderness in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ A fine sword and hat. And a fine adventurer at the bottom of the swamp, no doubt. „ — Astarion , stumbling upon the lost gear in the marsh Contents 1 Overview 2 Access 3 Dispelling the delight 4 Riverside Teahouse 4.1 False Fireplace 4.2 Connor's Coffin 4.3 The Well 5 Marshlands 5.1 The Gur Hunter 5.2 Local Fauna 5.3 Campsite carnage 6 Druid Sanctuary 7 Hazards 7.1 Spike traps 7.2 Barbed bulrush 8 Waypoints 9 Related quests 10 Characters 11 Creatures 12 Loot 12.1 Hidden treasure 13 Related Literature 14 Gallery 15 Notes 16 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of Sunlit Wetlands with the Druid Sanctuary The Sunlit Wetlands appear to be a peaceful and picturesque location south of the Blighted Village and of the Forest . It features a calm water stream, finding its way into a bigger river via a widespread, branched delta, and a small Riverside Teahouse , where Auntie Ethel , a trader from the Hollow , is waiting to welcome even the unexpected guest. The rivershore ends with a streak of sandy beach and a wooden dock, from which a series of jumps lead the party to the Druid Sanctuary on a small separate island. Several quests can be initiated, progressed and resolved here, including the main quest ⁠ Find a Cure , as well as ⁠ Investigate Kagha and ⁠ Save Mayrina . If Astarion is recruited in the party, his personal quest ⁠ The Pale Elf can also be evolved in the area. Access [ edit section | visual editor ] The Sunlit Wetlands can be accessed through the path at X: 47 Y: 315 , where the roads from the Blighted Village and from the Forest merge. Also, by progressing along the southern sidewalk to the Goblin Camp , through the fallen log at X: -20 Y: 319 , and then jumping down the cliff at X: -37 Y: 307 , using Feather Fall or Grant Flight to avoid damage. At the border of the Sunlit Wetlands Auntie Ethel can be seen arguing with two brothers Demir and Johl . Upon approaching, the player character is automatically engaged in dialogue with all three. Both men press upon Ethel, demanding she surrender their sister Mayrina . The party can take any side or refrain from intervening; this choice decides the fate of both brothers. Alternatively, the party can skirt around them, ignoring the conversation altogether. If this route is taken and the party returns to the spot, both men will be found dead on the ground. The Letter from Mayrina can be found on Johl's corpse. Regardless of the outcome, Ethel can be found later in the Riverside Teahouse, along with Mayrina. Dispelling the delight [ edit section | visual editor ] The Putrid Bog once the illusion has been broken Shortly after entering the Sunlit Wetlands, a cutscene triggers, where the player character feels something strange and unsettling about the environment, as it seems too pleasant to be natural. They can try to understand what disturbs them with a DC 20 Investigation Check . However, depending on the Class of the interacting character, the check might be easier: [ 1 ] [CLERIC OF MYSTRA] [ARCANA]  Search for any disruption in the Weave.  (DC 15) [DRUID] [RANGER] [NATURE]  Looks for signs of unnatural activity.  (DC 15) [NEUTRAL CLERIC] [MONK] [NEUTRAL PALADIN] [WISDOM]  Reach out with your senses - check the balance of this place. (DC 15) [OATH OF THE ANCIENTS] [CHARISMA]  Tap into the preternatural awareness granted by your oath. Seek the truth.  (DC 12) [OATH OF DEVOTION] [CHARISMA]  Something here is... unnatural. Reach out with your magic, seek its source.  (DC 12) [SORCERER] [ARCANA]  Attune your magic to find any disturbance. (DC 15) [WARLOCK] [ARCANA]  Draw on your pact to empower your sight.  (DC 15) [WILD MAGIC] [ARCANA]  Carefully probe with your magic. Is the disturbance around you, or within you? (DC 15) [WIZARD] [ARCANA]  Search for signs of magical interference.  (DC 15) If the initial attempt is failed, the illusion over the area can be broken later by any of the following actions: Speaking to one of the sheep pasturing in the middle of the wetlands, and passing a DC 15 Animal Handling Check . Attacking any "sheep". Causing Auntie Ethel to reveal her true form. Once the character in question realises that the bliss around them is an illusion, a murky, fetid swamp (laden with many traps) and poisoned food is unveiled and the sheep are revealed as Redcaps in disguise. The druidic fane turns into the Decrepit Sanctuary, and the teahouse becomes a dilapidated hut. The teahouse owner Auntie Ethel turns out to be a hag - a treacherous and ruthless Fey creature. Successfully dispelling the illusion grants the ⁠ Eyes of the Wild inspiration for characters with the Outlander background. Once the illusion is broken, the map name changes from Sunlit Wetlands to Putrid Bog ; the background music also changes. Riverside Teahouse [ edit section | visual editor ] Auntie Ethel's teahouse under illusion “ If my breath couldn't kill people already, it certainly can now. „ — A Dragonborn Tav after eating Auntie Ethel's treacle tart The Riverside Teahouse is located on a small hill at X: -40 Y: 270 . If the illusion over the area is broken, its map name changes to Gnarled Teahouse . Upon entering, the dialogue with Auntie Ethel and Mayrina starts automatically. The party realize the young woman is the one sought by Demir and Johl. However, they can choose to drop the matter or to intervene, mentioning the results of the outcome of the dialogue with the brothers at the area entrance. Regardless, Ethel eventually teleports Mayrina away. Depending on the party's choices within the dialogue, Ethel can talk to them peacefully, or attack, dispelling the illusion if it is still intact. In former case, Auntie Ethel makes her offer to try and heal the player character - in exchange for one of their "pretty little peepers." If the player character agrees, they receive the Paid the Price condition. [ 2 ] Trading an eye to Ethel is considered an oathbreaking action for Ancients' Paladins . Auntie Ethel can also act a Trader , featuring the same set of wares as in the Hollow , until the party annoy her somehow. [ 3 ] [ verify ] When Ethel is in the Teahouse, she can also be pickpocketed as normal, unlike in the Hollow. If combat is commenced, Auntie Ethel turns Invisible on her first turn and flees through the false fireplace (see below) to the Overgrown Tunnel . The party is left to fight her minions: two Redcaps and two Redcap Blood Sages , previously disguised as sheep. Ethel can also be attacked before the automatic conversation starts, with the same results: dispelling the illusion and Redcaps siding with her, while Mayrina also disappears from the teahouse. Attacking Ethel without first speaking with her is considered an oathbreaking action for Ancients' Paladins . After the battle is finished, the teahouse can be looted for several potions and alchemical ingredients , as well as some Camp Supplies . Eating any of Treacle Tarts (or both one by one) in the far corner of the house while the illusion is intact prompts a comment from the party member doing so; this varies widely depending on their origin and race. The locked door in the far end of the house leads to a small patch of the swamp with a Mushroom Circle and Connor Vinderblad's coffin (see below). It can be opened with a Teahouse Key , or with a DC 2 Sleight of Hand Check . False Fireplace [ edit section | visual editor ] The back of the fireplace in the Riverside Teahouse is an illusion. Approaching the fireplace causes the active party member(s) to roll a DC 10 Investigation Check to notice the illusion. The wall can be walked through, and leads to the Entrance Gallery of the hag's lair in the Overgrown Tunnel. Passing this wall without any means of stealth causes Auntie Ethel to become hostile. Connor's Coffin [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Barrier around Connor's Coffin The body of Connor Vinderblad, the husband of ill-fated Mayrina, lies in a coffin in the middle of a small ground at the backyard of the teahouse. While Auntie Ethel is still around, Connor's coffin is surrounded by an Arcane Barrier - a thick magical cocoon which stings back whomever attempts to touch it, resulting in 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. The character in question also receives the condition Hands Off, Petal for 10 turns. [ 4 ] After Ethel is killed or ousted from her lair, the cocoon dispels, allowing to interact with the body. If Mayrina survives and is not snatched away by Ethel, she can be found here mourning over her husband's corpse. Connor can be raised from dead using Bitter Divorce - a magical wand left by Ethel in her workshop in the Overgrown Tunnel. Doing this is considered an oathbreaking action for Ancients' Paladins . The Well [ edit section | visual editor ] South of the Teahouse entrance is a well that is deceptively altered by the illusion of the area. Interacting with it when the illusion is up has it appearing fresh with sweet-smelling water gurgling gently below. Without the illusion, the well's true nature is shown, with a fetid smell, and full of dead flesh. Despite the truth of what is in the water, drinking from it gives the Refreshed condition, which increases the character's maximal Hit Points by 10 until their next Long Rest , while any temporary hit points are removed at the same time. After a Long Rest, Refreshed is replaced with the Nauseated condition, which inflicts vulnerability to Psychic and Acid damage until another Long Rest. Drinking from the well again with the nauseated condition gives the Sickened condition. If drinking from the well prior to engaging in combat with Auntie Ethel, she changes the effect of refreshed to sickened during the fight. Drinking from the well brings approval from   +1 and   +1 , and disapproval from   -1 , regardless of whether the illusion is still intact or after the illusion is dispelled. Marshlands [ edit section | visual editor ] The Gur Hunter [ edit section | visual editor ] On the hill to the south of Ethel's teahouse at X: -25 Y: 241 stands a man named Gandrel . He introduces himself as a monster hunter and claims that he came to the swamp to ask help from the hag. The layout of the dialogue with him depends heavily on several conditions: Whether Astarion has been recruited; Whether he is currently in the party or not; Lastly, whether it has already been revealed that he is a vampire. If Astarion is in the party and his true nature is already known, Gandrel reveals the reason for his presence, explaining that he is hunting for a vampire spawn who attacked their camp and abducted the tribe's children. The player character can then choose to give up Astarion or to stand up for him. In the latter case, Gandrel becomes hostile. If Astarion's nature is unknown yet, he picks the right moment and kills Gandrel, stabbing him in the eye. He does not explain much afterwards. If Astarion is not in the party, the player character can convince Gandrel to reveal his target (requires a DC 15 Persuasion Check or DC 20 Intimidation Check ). Afterwards, they can choose to protect Astarion or betray him by showing Gandrel the way to their camp. Betraying Astarion in either way results in his permanent removal from the party. He can be met again in the Act Three as a zombie. If defeated, Gandrel can be looted for the Gandrel's Aspiration , and his backpack for gold, three Trap Disarm Toolkits and several Garlic bulbs. Local Fauna [ edit section | visual editor ] At X: -27 Y: 304 in a small coomb [ 5 ] an Addled Frog hops around the water edge. Speaking to her via Speak with Animals reveals her mental confusion. If pestered several times, the frog becomes hostile. Despite having a modest amount of HP, she is a dangerous enemy. If Auntie Ethel is killed or forced out of the area, the frog regains its sanity and rewards the party. Otherwise, her hidden treasure at X: 7 Y: 294 can be found with a successful DC 20 Perception Check . To the east of the teahouse approximately at X: 0 Y: 253 the party pass by two islands where, if the illusion is intact, several sheep pasture. Speaking to any of them and passing the Animal Handling check dispels the illusion. If the illusion already broken, the party see a pack of Redcaps [ 6 ] still pretending to be sheep. They are not hostile at first and bleat if spoken to. Bleating back at them earns companions' approval:   +1 ,   +1 and   +1 . Provoking them or angering Auntie Ethel makes the Redcaps hostile. If Demir and Johl survive the initial conversation with Auntie Ethel at the entrance to the Sunlit Wetlands, the corpses of both can be found near the Redcaps' "pasture". At X: -3 Y: 277 a Reinforced Greatsword protrudes from the marsh, with a Reinforced Helmet aside it, both items highlighted by a successful DC 10 Investigation Check . The party members comment on them upon noticing. Campsite carnage [ edit section | visual editor ] The marsh flares out to the river and a narrow sandy beach. At X: 85 Y: 273 is a campsite smeared in blood and gore, noticeable regardless of whether the illusion persists. The camp can be freely looted for Camp Supplies , gold, Valuables and random scrolls. Any party member comments on this, and the closest one to the carnage attempts a passive DC 10 Nature Check to identify the Redcaps being responsible for the attack. The check is made regardless of whether the illusion is still intact. In the far end of the camp a wooden chest is buried, containing the similar set of loot. From the nearby dock the party can reach the Druid Sanctuary via a series of jumps. Druid Sanctuary [ edit section | visual editor ] The sanctuary from the entrance point, under illusion The sanctuary occupies the largest one in a chain of rocky islands protruding from the water. If the illusion covering the area has been dispelled, its map name changes to Decrepit Sanctuary . The island is guarded by two Wood Woads and several Ancient Mud Mephits , which attack the party on sight. The area where the battle takes place features Deep Water , Twisting Vines and Mud . The mephits summon Young Mud Mephits ; both kinds create more mud patches through their Death Burst . In the sanctuary the ⁠ Investigate Kagha quest can be initiated or progressed by finding and reading the note from the Shadow Druids in the notch at X: 83 Y: 211 (requires DC 15 Perception Check to reveal). A Wood Woad Shield can be looted from one of the Wood Woads. The chest under the tree in the centre on sanctuary contains The Sparkle Hands . Also, at X: 66 Y: 223 a wooden chest is buried, containing gold, random potions and Camp Supplies (requires DC 12 Survival Check to detect). Hazards [ edit section | visual editor ] Spike traps [ edit section | visual editor ] Numerous spike traps are spread throughout the deeper water in the waterstream arms and can be detected with a DC 15 Perception Check . Activating these traps does not remove the illusion on the wetlands. When triggered, they inflict Bleeding and Open Wound with no Saving Throw . After the duration of latter expires, a DC  15 Constitution Saving Throw is needed to overcome the condition, otherwise it progresses into Rotting , and then to Flesh Rot . These conditions have the same saving throw requirements; Flesh Rot may be reapplied multiple times until a successful save is rolled. The Open Wound can be cured by any type of Healing , preventing it from worsening, but further conditions require treatment for one who is Diseased , such as Lesser Restoration , Lay on Hands , or Potion of Vitality . The traps are not removed when triggered, allowing them to continue harming the party unless being disabled with a DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check . Due to the high number of traps, it is recommended to avoid them by staying away from deep water instead of potentially wasting Trap Disarm Toolkits while doing so. Barbed bulrush [ edit section | visual editor ] Barbed bulrushes are scattered around the Wetlands. When interacting with the plants, the interacting character automatically attempts a DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check or risks getting an Open Wound , which can progressively worsen (as detailed above). It is recommended to avoid touching these plants. Regardless of the check result, the character in question loots an Juicy Apple (if the illusion is intact), which turns into Poisoned Apple after the illusion is dispelled. Consuming either type of apples applies Poisoned condition for 10 turns. Also, several wicker baskets scattered around the swamp also contain apples, which have the same aforementioned effects. These apples cannot be placed into the characters' Camp Supply Sack and thus cannot be consumed via Auto-Select function during the Long Rest. ## The Festering Cove
- **来源**: [The Festering Cove](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Festering_Cove)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The Ebonlake beach in The Festering Cove. The Festering Cove is a Location within the Underdark in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ We will spread word of Mahkloompah. Your glory will sing from ten thousand throats! „ — Pooldripp , hailing the party as their new god Contents 1 Overview and access 1.1 The Kuo-toa 1.2 Exploring the cave 2 Related quests 3 Characters 4 Creatures 5 Loot 5.1 Hidden treasure 6 Related literature 7 Notes and references Overview and access [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the Festering Cove The Festering Cove is a separate large cavern in the Underdark located beneath the general level of the region. It features several waterfalls and rocky cliffs descending to the subterranean water stream, and is scattered with giant mushrooms and adorned with fishing nets and various shells and conches. The entrance to The Festering Cove is hidden at X: 70 Y: -240 northeast of the Arcane Tower and south-east of the Decrepit Village . It requires the party to traverse a rift (e.g., by using two mushroom platforms) and then descend via a cragged rock. On the far end of the rift under a Torchstalk lies a skeleton with the Helmet of Autonomy on it. The Kuo-toa [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: BOOOAL The kuo-toa worshipping BOOOAL The Festering Cove is home to a tribe of Kuo-toa who worship their alleged "God of Murder" BOOOAL . Part of the tribe led by Pooldripp the Zealous are chanting near the makeshift altar, and several others are stationed up on the mushroom caps and cliffs around. Unless Pooldrip and those close to him are approached, none of them pay attention to the party, and it is possible to explore at least part of the cove by stealth. When the party approach the altar, at approximately X: -421 Y: 284 , where one of the kuo-toa is sacrificed, the dialogue with Pooldripp starts automatically. At the start of the conversation the interacting party member rolls a passive DC 10 Nature Check to recognize the creatures and the peculiarities of this race. The layout of the conversation depends heavily on whether the player character recognizes the true nature of the 'deity' they are fervently worshipping. Exploring the cave [ edit section | visual editor ] The Festering Cove features several gilded chests in plain sight. Most are not locked and contain gold, Valuables , and miscellaneous sea-themed items like Clamshells or Starfishes . There is one concealed chest, however, hidden on a rocky cliff. To approach it, the party must traverse (e.g., jump) several mushroom caps starting from X: -401 Y: 311 , on which the Torchstalks grow. The chest itself is trapped and locked (requires two subsequent DC 10 Sleight of Hand Checks to disarm and to lockpick), and contains the Slippery Chain Shirt . Under a Torchstalk nearby a Potion of Greater Healing lies in plain sight, but with high probability of being destroyed if the mushrooms explode. On the beach at X: -395 Y: 240 a highlighted rock protrudes from the water. It seems to be used as a fane to BOOOAL by the Kuo-toa, as its foot is scattered with gold coins, bottles and other offerings. Also here lies The Ecstasy of Murder - a scroll briefly describing Bhaal's doctrine. Behind this rock a wooden chest contains some alchemical ingredients . If the party explore the far end of the beach, at X: -394 Y: 264 a DC 5 Perception Check allows them to notice a "Message in a bottle" . Inside the bottle is a Curled Paper - a letter from Doni , one of tiefling children from the Emerald Grove , to his father (probably deceased). A heavy chest nearby at X: -396 Y: 233 contains gold and random valuables. ## The Hollow
- **来源**: [The Hollow](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Hollow)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The Hollow Emerald Grove Makeshift Prison ↑ Secluded Chamber ← Hollow → Sacred Pool ↓ Ravaged Beach The Hollow is a Location within the Emerald Grove in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is the section of the Emerald Grove where most of the tiefling refugees reside. “ Well, this seems like a lovely little spot. The sense of impending doom aside. „ — Astarion , upon entering the Hollow Contents 1 Overview 2 Entrance 3 Points of interest 3.1 The trading post 3.2 Entrance to the Sacred Pool 3.3 The training ground 3.4 The storage and the makeshift prison 3.5 Dammon's smithy and Auntie Ethel's shop 3.6 Adventurers' corner 3.7 Secluded Chamber 3.8 Tiefling Hideout 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Adventurers 6.2 Tieflings 6.3 Tiefling children 6.4 Traders 6.5 Other 7 Creatures 8 Loot 9 Related literature 10 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Combined map of the Hollow, with Secluded Chamber (left), Tiefling Hideout (right-up), and the Storage interior The Hollow is a connective hub area adjacent to the Emerald Grove . It provides easy access to the other parts of the grove and harbours several local traders. Close before the game events commence it became a temporary haven to a group of refugees from Elturel led by Zevlor , including several important characters. The Hollow is a vast cavern with paths forming an uneven ring, elongated from south to north. In the south, the Hollow is connected with an open ground right behind the ramparts and overgrown portcullis, which is considered a part of the Emerald Grove. The northern end of the cavern ends with an appendix where the makeshift prison can be found. To the east, a stone-paved stairs descend to the Sacred Pool - the central part of the grove. Wyll can be recruited as a companion here, along with Shadowheart - provided she has not yet joined the party. Entrance [ edit section | visual editor ] Apart from the main entrance at X: 204 Y: 501 , the Hollow may be also accessed from the Sacred Pool through its archway, and also from the Underground Passage , from where one of the stone doors lead to the fringe path behind the makeshift prison. Paths which lead from the Hollow into other locations, such as to the Forest and to the Risen Road (both starting from Zevlor's headquarters), can be difficult to access and use backwards, as they require use of spatial movement like Misty Step or Grant Flight to traverse. Points of interest [ edit section | visual editor ] The trading post [ edit section | visual editor ] The trading post is the first point of interaction which the party see after entering the Hollow from its main entrance. A round stone ground with an obelisk is in the middle at X: 204 Y: 519 ; it is tended by halfling druid Arron . Apart from trading, Arron can also shed some light on the opinion of most druids upon the refugees' presence and the ritual his fellows have initiated. Past the trading post two paths start, running through the Hollow along its eastern and western sides, meeting near the makeshift prison in the farmost northern point. Farther on the eastern path at X: 207 Y: 531 , a trio of tieflings - Rolan and his siblings Cal and Lia are arguing. They are not part of the refugees associated with Zevlor, and are debating whether to stay and help their kin, or to continue their way to Baldur's Gate . Rolan believes they have no responsibility toward the refugees and should leave for their own safety, while Lia fervently admonishes they should help because it is the right thing to do. Cal does not sway to either side, but quietly attempts to have them discuss the matter with cooler heads. The party can take either Rolan or Lia's side and convince the trio to stay or to leave. All possible dialogue options can be found on any of their pages. The player character's decision determines whether these characters can be met in other acts of the game. If convinced to stay, Rolan and his siblings move from the initial point deeper into the Hollow and stand near Okta's kitchen (see below). Entrance to the Sacred Pool [ edit section | visual editor ] Following the eastern path further is a stall with three oxen tied to it, and Toron foddering them from a nearby haystack. A DC 9 Perception Check allows to find a hidden gilded chest in the hay. It can also be found by talking to the Bored Ox via Speak with Animals . Looting this chest is not considered a crime. A DC 10 Insight Check gives the player character a hint that something is different about the Strange Ox here. It can also be spoken to in order to discern the reason for the player character unease. Dialogue options and possible results are listed on this creature's page. If Shadowheart has not yet been recruited to the party, she stands near the oxen stall and can join immediately. A bit farther the oxen stall at X: 230 Y: 550 the tiefling boy Doni stands. He does not react substantively to any attempts to talk to him, and his task on loitering exactly at this place becomes clear if the party receive an invitation to meet Mol in the Tiefling Hideout . Across Doni's watch post is a cart with a pair of Metallic Gloves in it. The locked travel-worn chest next to the cart also contains useful loot. Both can be looted without it being considered a crime. The way continues to descend towards the Sacred Pool, passing a small stand maintained by Mattis and his sister Silfy . If speaking with Mattis, he tries to show a trick with a "magic ring" to the interacting party member. Making a similar trick and snatching the ring through it earns the following inspirations: ⁠ Artful Dodger ( Urchin background) ⁠ Made You Look ( Entertainer background) If the interacting party member then decides to examine Mattis' wares, Silfy tries to rob them. On a successful DC 15 Perception Check , they can catch Silfy in the act and retrieve the stolen goods. On failure, Silfy retreats to the Tiefling Hideout via the ladder behind Mattis's shop, [ 1 ] and the ⁠ Find Your Belongings quest is initiated. A series of stone-paved stairs come down to the entrance to the Sacred Pool . Upon first time approaching, approximately at X: 260 Y: 540 , a cutscene triggers showing a group of tieflings led by Locke and Komira arguing with three druids who block their entering the sacred grounds of the grove. After initial dialogue, the tieflings stand back, and the party can speak to them to find out that the druids intend to "judge" one of tiefling children, Arabella , for her attempt to steal the Idol of Silvanus ; the ⁠ Save Arabella quest is then added to the journal. The training ground [ edit section | visual editor ] The training ground is at X: 207 Y: 544 . Several tiefling children: Gan , Ide and Umi , along with Guex are learning basic fencing moves against training dummies. If spoken with, their teacher Asharak asks the party member for a few worlds to cheer the children up. If Wyll survives the initial fight at the grove gate, he can be found here, explaining basic tactics and style to the children. Speaking with Wyll here allows recruiting him to the party immediately, adding ⁠ The Blade of Frontiers quest to the journal. If talking to Guex, the player character can help him train more effectively, passing Insight or Athletics check. Martial classed characters can also use their class-based options without rolling any checks. Giving a piece of advice to Guex earns companions' approval and also ⁠ To Arms! inspiration for the characters with the Soldier background. To the west of the training ground a wooden platform extends into a scaffold running around the rock. At its start X: 200 Y: 540 , a series of rocky ledges allow to descend deeper in the Hollow, to Auntie Ethel's shop. The storage and the makeshift prison [ edit section | visual editor ] Further down along the eastern path and past the turn to the Sacred Pool, at X: 200 Y: 574 is a small hut. Its door is locked and red-outlined; lockpicking it is considered a crime. However, the party still can get inside using the rocky shelves behind the makeshift prison. Malnourished Torchstalks are camouflaged along the path and explode if any party member comes too close. At X: 220 Y: 590 a pouch contains gold and random Valuables . A rat running back and forth from the hut entrance to the nearby smithy can be spoken to via Speak with Animals . It complains about chipping a tooth on an 'evil thing' inside the storage. Inside the storage hamlet the party meet Pandirna , a tiefling girl whose legs have been Paralysed . The player character may threaten her not to raise the alarm or – if they are a Bard , Cleric , Druid or Paladin – heal her by casting Lesser Restoration . Dark Urge characters have a unique interaction to kill Pandirna instead by breaking her legs; this is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of any Oath. The storage here can be looted for some potions and / or alchemical ingredients locked up in the Alchemist's Cabinet near Pandirna. The chest she is leaning on contains the Cabinet Key , gold and a random gem – the "evil thing" the rat was speaking of. Also, from various containers around some Camp Supplies can be looted. The northernmost part of the Hollow is separated by a wooden fortification where, at X: 190 Y: 585 , a makeshift prison can be found. There, in an iron cage, a goblin scout Sazza is imprisoned. Upon first approaching the prison, the party see Arka preparing to shoot Sazza dead. Arka wants revenge for her brother Kanon's death in the recent assault, while her friend Memnos tries to talk her down. The player character can decide Sazza's fate through the ensuing dialogue. If the goblin survives, a party member can talk to her again, progressing the quest ⁠ Find a Cure and initiating the quest ⁠ Save the Goblin Sazza . Sazza's cage can be opened with the Iron Cell Key [ 2 ] or by passing a DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check . The easiest way to help Sazza escape is to jump down the rocky ledge behind her cage and lead Sazza through the hidden stone door (requires a DC 5 Perception Check to find) into the Underground Passage at X: -438 Y: -140 . Saving Sazza from the grove is one of the first steps required to get the achievement "She cannot be caged!" . It also grants the ⁠ Jailbreaker inspiration to characters with the Criminal background. Letting Arka kill Sazza is considered an oathbreaking action for Oath of the Crown Paladins , while helping her escape breaks the oath for both Oath of the Crown Paladins and Oath of Vengeance Paladins . Dammon's smithy and Auntie Ethel's shop [ edit section | visual editor ] At X: 180 Y: 557 is a small smithy where Dammon can be found. He acts as a trader and perhaps is the only one of the refugees who displays feelings of ambiguity for the The Descent , as he learned much while being enslaved in the Hells. Speaking with him progresses the ⁠ The Hellion's Heart quest (or ⁠ Forging a Heart quest if Karlach is played as an origin). Near Dammon's smithy, at X: 186 Y: 570 stands Zorru , a tiefling scout who managed to run away in one piece after meeting a githyanki patrol near the Mountain Pass . Talking to him with Lae'zel in the party progresses the ⁠ Find the Githyanki Crèche quest. After being interrogated, Zorru walks to the storage entrance. Across the smithy, Auntie Ethel tends to her small shop of "lotions and potions". She can also be traded with, and if the player character allows her to "fuss around them", they can get a free Potion of Greater Healing . If the player character confesses to having a parasite in their head, Ethel invites them to her home to take a closer look. If stolen from, or if any conflict or fighting occurs in the Hollow or nearby parts of the Sacred Pool, Ethel leaves the Hollow and can be found later in the Sunlit Wetlands . Near Ethel's shop, a tiefling chef Okta cooks food for the camp. She can spare a bowl of gruel to any character who agrees to try it. Okta can also act as a trader, selling some Camp Supplies , but only through using the "Trade" option in the lower-left corner within the initial dialogue cutscene. Adventurers' corner [ edit section | visual editor ] The north-western corner of the Hollow at X: 171 Y: 540 is occupied by a group of adventurers lead by Aradin . Unless the argument between Aradin and Zevlor at the ramparts immediately after repelling the goblins ends with Aradin being knocked out, those who survive the battle remain here: Aradin and Barth sit at the table, and Remira tends to her wound nearby. If Liam has been saved from the Goblin Camp , he can also be found here sleeping soundly. Speaking to Aradin sheds some light on the reason of his crew coming to the grove. He can be convinced (without ability checks) to pass to the party the Stamped Handbill . Obtaining it initiates the ⁠ Find the Nightsong quest, which is deeply intertwined with the game plot and can be finished only in Act Three . If Aradin survives the battle and is knocked out at the ramparts, he and his crew leave the Hollow immediately after, leaving all their belongings behind in the adventurers' chest. Upon first approach to the adventurers a tiefling boy Meli robs Barth for a Brass Locket and tries to run away. Barth soon catches up with him up on the scaffolds, and the player character can follow both to choose and take either side. Depending on their choice, this encounter grants any one of mutually exclusive inspirations for Urchin background: ⁠ Family Comes First or ⁠ Protect Your Own . On a scaffold above the adventurers' corner a pair of young lovers, Danis and Bex can be met for the first time in the walkthrough. Secluded Chamber [ edit section | visual editor ] Zevlor resides in a small cavern called the Secluded Chamber behind a stone door at X: 166 Y: 539 . The cavern has two levels, of which the upper one features a watch post. From the watch post, it is possible to jump down back into the Hollow at X: 171 Y: 518 with minimal health damage. The watch post opens to the east onto a stone ledge over the river stream, from where the party can reach Forest through a series of jumps. The northern side of the ledge has a cragged rock that leads up to another rocky shelf with a heavy chest on it at X: 136 Y: 519 , containing gold and a random grenade. Past the chest, the party can also reach the Risen Road by jumping ( Feather Fall is recommended to avoid falling damage). If the Hollow is assaulted during the ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove quest, the Secluded Chamber is the place where the most helpless of the tiefling refugees gather, seeking protection. Tiefling Hideout [ edit section | visual editor ] The Tiefling Hideout is a subterranean cavern hidden under the south-western part of the Hollow . It is occupied by Mol and her tiefling children gang, [ 3 ] who use it as a base to run scams and other exploits. The party can find the hideout themselves after interacting with various members of Mol's gang, or they can be invited to visit it as a reward for helping or protecting the children. ## The Risen Road
- **来源**: [The Risen Road](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Risen_Road)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

An abandoned wagon on The Risen Road Wilderness Waukeen's Rest ← Risen Road → Emerald Grove ↓ Blighted Village The Risen Road is a Location within the Wilderness in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It runs parallel to the River Chionthar , and serves as an alternate route of trade. “ ... those who seek to journey to the coast from the interior regions lying to the east will typically seek out the Risen Road. Running parallel to the River Chionthar, the Risen Road provides an overland route all the way from Elturel to Baldur's Gate, and has proven tempting to travellers seeking an alternate to the river barges that sail the Chionthar. „ — Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. IV: The Risen Road Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Ravaged Caravan 1.2 Trapped in cave 1.3 Meeting Karlach 1.4 Toll House 1.5 Toll House Basement 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 Available to Speak with Dead 5 Creatures 6 Loot 6.1 Hidden treasures 7 Related literature 8 Notes and references 9 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Combined map of the Risen Road location The Risen Road is located to the north of the Blighted Village . It can be accessed from several points: From the Blighted Village - jumping across the broken bridge at X: -6 Y: 493 From the Forest - jumping at the stones across the stream at X: 78 Y: 489 (near the place where Scratch can first be met) From the Emerald Grove - climbing a ladder in the Secluded Chamber ( Zevlor's quarters) and descending the western cliff at X: 126 Y: 527 (means like Feather Fall or Misty Step are helpful here to avoid damage). In this location Karlach can be recruited. If traversing the Risen Road westward the party can reach the Mountain Pass . Ravaged Caravan [ edit section | visual editor ] When coming from the Blighted Village and moving eastward from the collapsed bridge, the results of a massacre can be clearly seen at X: 4 Y: 517 : broken wagons, blood pools and corpses strewn around. Several Bloated Hyenas lie here, exhausted. Approaching them, an automated dialogue with one of the hyenas starts, and the player character can understand what is happening to her by succeeding a passive Arcana check: a birth of a Gnoll ; they can prevent this by killing the beast. Clerics and Paladins can bless it instead, with the same result, while Dark Urge origins have additional unique choices. Regardless of the result, a fight with the rest of the hyenas starts. On its first turn, the only not-bloated hyena runs northward, where a pack of already born gnolls feast on corpses. Eliminating the gnoll pack grants the ⁠ Cursebreaker inspirational event for the characters with Outlander background. Gnolls, as well as hyenas, provide a rare alchemical ingredient, Hyena Ear , which can be occasionally traded for or obtained at higher levels further in the game. Also, looting the caravan wreckage provides Camp Supplies , as well as several potions . Among the corpses, the Dead Caravan Agent can be spoken to via Speak with Dead to find out that some of the caravan members managed to flee from the gnolls. On the lower path next to the river running under the broken bridge, there are several points of interest. A skeleton in a thick bush at X: 57 Y: 516 can be looted for a Smuggler's Ring . Knotted roots at X: 35 Y: 515 lead to the upper path, to another point where the dialogue with Bloated Hyenas may be started. At the end of the path, under the broken bridge, a couple of skeletons "sit" in an eternal embrace. Interacting with any of them prompts the player character to make a passive DC 10 History Check to recognize their armour as belonging to a Harper and a druid. [ 1 ] . Successful discerning the armour grants the ⁠ A Natural Alliance inspirational event for the characters with Sage background. [ 2 ] Trapped in cave [ edit section | visual editor ] Looking down into the Risen Road's cave A trail of beasts' pawprints leads northwards from the encounter with the gnoll pack. Following it, the party arrives to where the ambush survivors fled. At X: 30 Y: 576 the player character notices a symbol of the Absolute daubed onto a rockside with blood. In a cave at X: 32 Y: 608 , Rugan and Olly are defending themselves against another pack of gnolls, led by Flind . They are transporting a locked Caravan Strongbox containing an Iron Flask . Upon approaching the cave from outside, the battle between the party and the gnolls is commenced. Flind rushes to attack the nearest party member, but on its first turn links with them mentally, and the player character's tadpole responds. The player character then has a chance to change the odds: they may sic the whole pack onto the men in the cave or attack its pack, thus making Flind neutral to the party, through several Wisdom rolls (using the tadpole to compel her to eat her peers is only DC 2). After the initial order is fulfilled, the player character can speak to Flind again (if she is close to the party, she engages in a dialogue with the nearest party member automatically). The player character can then use Wisdom again to compel Flind to kill herself, attack the pack (if this was not initially ordered), or flee. Failing any of the rolls keeps Flind hostile to the party. If Flind is killed, a Shattered Flail and a parasite can be looted from its body. If Rugan and Olly remain neutral at the start of the battle, on their first turn both retreat deeper in the cave and disengage from the fight. The cave has also another mouth at X: 50 Y: 570 , but it is blocked by a wooden barricade, and is further inside trapped with two Tripwires , any of which, if triggered, sets loose a large round boulder to roll down. Disarming both Tripwires grants the ⁠ Rock Steady inspirational event to the characters with Outlander background. If entering the cave that way, Rugan considers them as allies and offers to fight back the gnolls. The player character may then agree to help or refuse, but the latter makes the survivors hostile, too, in addition to the beasts. Depending on the player character's choices made throughout the whole episode, they may discuss it with Rugan afterwards (the dialogue with him starts automatically), or speak to his corpse if he did not survive. In case Rugan survived, the party can find out about the important shipment which they are transporting, and succeeding a passive DC 10 History Check reveals that both men are agents of the Zhentarim . The party then can let the men go, or intimidate them into surrendering the cargo, or bargain with them on selling it and splitting the profits. If the conversation turns out in favourable way, Rugan tells the party the password to the Zhentarim Basement in Waukeen's Rest . Otherwise, it can be learned from his corpse while interrogating. [ 3 ] Getting payment from Rugan and Olly for saving them earns the ⁠ Hero for Hire inspirational event to the characters with Urchin background. If the Zhentarim are killed or the cargo is wrested from them, opening the strongbox and taking the flask grants the ⁠ Open for a Surprise inspirational event for the characters with Criminal background. Inside the cave at X: 37 Y: 644 , in a locked chest lie the Reason's Grasp gloves. The small ground in front of the chest is trapped with a Poison Mine . The corpse of an unnamed Dead Caravan Agent which lies nearby the cave mouth wields the Speedy Reply Scimitar. Meeting Karlach [ edit section | visual editor ] Approximately at X: 55 Y: 533 the upper path along the river and the path leading to the gnoll-sieged cave collide. From this point, a bridge goes towards the local Toll House, and another path goes eastwards and down to the river shore. If choosing to go the latter way, the party can encounter Karlach behind the log crossing the stream at X: 111 Y: 503 , trying to cope with the flames engulfing her. At this point, she can be recruited . If Wyll is in the party, he recognizes Karlach as his target and confronts her. On the way down to the shore, at X: 104 Y: 525 the player character can pick up the Toll Collector's Key . It is easily missed, as it is not highlighted by the Perception skill. To the north-east of the road collision point there is another bridge which leads to the Toll House and is also littered with gnoll corpses. Toll House [ edit section | visual editor ] The abandoned Toll House The Toll House was once used to collect tolls from travellers, but recently the toll collectors decided to abandon it due to the road's dangerous conditions. However, their guards fled instead of defending them, and the collectors were killed by goblins. [ 4 ] One of the dead bodies, Vance , lies on the road at X:  Y:  . The area in front of the Toll house features a Waypoint at X: 82 Y: 597 and a collapsed tunnel that might otherwise lead further onto the Risen Road. On approaching the rockfall, any party member comments on it, suggesting that the cave-in was not from by natural causes. As the Risen Road appears blocked, the party must use the Mountain Pass to continue their way towards Baldur's Gate overland. The abandoned Toll house recently became a temporarily base of operations for Anders and his crew, who are searching for Karlach under the disguise of paladins of Tyr . However, fighting with Karlach and with gnolls, they lost two members of the squad. The corpse of one of their mates can be found in the Toll house backroom, while the other might be Buckle, a Rock Gnome whose corpse was left on the bridge. The party can talk to Anders and his mates, Trynn and Cyrel about their mission, and also trade with the latter. Throughout the dialogue the player character may detect that Anders is deceiving them; Clerics of Tyr have an additional option to catch him on a lie, asking to recite a basic dogma of their faith. Also, the party can interrogate the aforementioned corpse of their fallen fellow to find out that in truth the crew serves Zariel , the Archduchess of Avernus . Once caught red-handed, Anders attacks the party. All these interactions are available only if Karlach is not in the party ; if already recruited and in the active party, any of Anders' subordinates attacks them on sight. Anders, however, has more composure and starts a dialogue first, trying to convince the party to turn on Karlach. Killing Anders grants the ⁠ Warrior of the Hells inspirational event to the characters with Soldier background, and the Sword of Justice can be taken from his body. Killing Anders without first learning his true loyalties is considered an oathbreaking action for Devotion Paladins , while eliminating him without talking at all breaks the oath of Ancients' Paladins . After the false paladins are dealt with, the party can descend to the Toll House basement, gaining various loot (see below). Also, on the open balcony of the Toll house at X: 109 Y: 551 lies a single Soul Coin , possibly left by Anders' crew to bait Karlach. If Karlach is in party, she rampages for 10 turns after defeating the false paladins inside the Toll house building, crushing everything that comes under her axe, and leaving a burning trail behind (which may damage the party members, should they stand in the way). Toll House Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Toll House basement can be accessed via a trap door in the same room where Anders initially resides. Until the false paladins are defeated, it is marked red-outlined. The basement consists of an antechamber, where a dead toll collector lies, and the locked vault. The vault cannot be lockpicked, although it can be opened by using Toll Collector's Key (see above), or destroyed. There is a Burrow Hole on the wall opposite the basement door, connecting to the hole just east of the Toll House. Past the door are two rooms with four Vents in each, which can be detected and disarmed, but do not trigger if stepped on. Various containers in these rooms, as well as in the antechamber, provide the party with Valuables , alchemical ingredients, Camp Supplies and various common armour and weaponry. At the end of the second room there are two stone thrones. Letting party members sit on both of them at the the same time, or placing items on both thrones, reveals a hidden treasury room behind a movable wall containing a Greataxe +1 , Gloves of Heroism , several piles of Gold and also several mundane weapons. Just behind the wall section a Marble Plate can be detected. If not disarmed but triggered, it makes the vents in all three rooms cover the floor with Simple Toxin . The movable wall section cannot be opened from within. ## Tiefling Hideout
- **来源**: [Tiefling Hideout](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tiefling_Hideout)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

Hidden Tiefling hideout within the Druid Grove. Emerald Grove The Hollow ↑ Tiefling Hideout The Tiefling Hideout is a Location within the Emerald Grove in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ The Gate will never see us coming. We're going to own that town. „ — Mol , bracing up her gang in the hideout Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Getting access 2 Interactions 3 Related quests 4 Characters 5 Loot 6 Gallery 7 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the Mol's gang base of operations The Tiefling Hideout is a subterranean cavern hidden under the south-western part of the Hollow . It is occupied by Mol and her tiefling children gang, [ 1 ] who use it as a base to run scams and other exploits. The party can find the hideout themselves after interacting with various members of Mol's gang, or they can be invited to visit it as a reward for helping or protecting the children. Getting access [ edit section | visual editor ] The hideout has two entrances: Through the Concealed Hatch at X: 227 Y: 553 in The Hollow , guarded by Doni The hatch is revealed by succeeding a passive DC 10 Perception Check while speaking to Doni, followed by passing a DC 10 Investigation Check . Rangers and Rogues have Advantage on this Investigation check. If Mirkon is rescued in ⁠ Investigate the Beach , he tells the party to speak with Doni and gives them the password which allows them in. Through the Rocky Crevice at X: 224 Y: 564 in The Hollow Silfy flees there after stealing, or being caught while attempting to steal the party's ⁠ belongings . The crevice is located on a rocky ledge beneath a wooden ladder and requires a DC 5 Perception Check to reveal. Only Small or tiny sized party members can fit through the crevice. This can be done by Gnomes , Halflings , as well as characters disguised as such or reduced . Characters who are shapeshifted into creatures of appropriate size and summons can also fit through. Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] To explore the hideout without consequences, the party must first earn Mol's favor. This can be done by helping out members of her children gang, or by protecting them from other characters, like Kagha or Barth . On the opposite, allowing others to abuse the kids or leaving them in danger makes Mol angry with the party. Entering the hideout without doing anything to befriend Mol causes her to demand the party leave in "a tencount". She begins to count audibly. If the party members do not leave in time, Mol runs away. After leaving the hideout, the party members are accosted by the guards outside, for 'threatening children'; the interacting party member must then pass a DC 20 Deception Check or be sent to prison. If having earned Mol's approval, the party can trade with her and can also start the quest ⁠ Steal the Sacred Idol . They can also show interest in her enterprise and offer an investment of 20 gold to found a Thieves' Guild when the tieflings reach Baldur's Gate . This grants the inspiration ⁠ Paying It Forward to party members with the Urchin background. In the hideout the party can find items stolen from their inventory during ⁠ Find Your Belongings . Possible peaceful options to get these items back if talking to Mol are listed on her personal page. The party can also try and steal their belongings back from the gang's stash at X: 94 Y: 74 in the hideout. Doing this without making enemies of Mol and her fellows earns the inspiration ⁠ Show Them How It's Done to party members with the Criminal background. Also Barth's stolen Brass Locket can be found here in a chest. It can be given back to him. At X: 52 Y: 59 a rift over the underground stream can be jumped over by any character with at least 15 Strength , or crossed by means of spatial movement like Misty Step or Grant Flight . Druid characters may also use Wild Shape: Badger to Burrow to the other side. A Wicker Chest on the other side of the chasm contains gold and random alchemical ingredients . It is free to loot, even if the tiefling children are still present in the hideout.
