## Tiefling Refugee Celebration
- **来源**: [Tiefling Refugee Celebration](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tiefling_Refugee_Celebration)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The celebration is in full swing. The tiefling refugree celebration is a special camp event which occurs after completing either ⁠ Defeat the Goblins or ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove , while siding with the tieflings . “ We can worry about the road tomorrow. Tonight, we drink! „ — Rhy , celebrating the victory over the goblins Contents 1 Overview 2 Companions 2.1 Astarion 2.2 Gale 2.3 Lae'zel 2.4 Karlach 2.5 Shadowheart 2.6 Wyll 3 Other interactions 3.1 The way forward 3.2 Alfira 3.3 Lakrissa & Zae 3.4 Barcus 3.5 A new name 3.6 A potential murder 3.7 Korrilla 3.8 The other tieflings 3.9 Other camp followers 4 Related quests 5 Characters 5.1 Companions 5.2 Followers 5.3 Notable characters 5.4 Tieflings 6 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] After the party defeated the goblin leaders or successfully defended the Emerald Grove , the tiefling refugees pack their belongings to leave the grove. Speaking with Zevlor – or to Cerys in case Zevlor has died – initiates the feast when the next Long Rest is taken. The event is mutually exclusive with the Goblin Celebration , which happens if the party side with the goblins during ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove . Zevlor and the tiefling refugees appear at camp and start a celebration before leaving for Baldur's Gate . The choices prior to this event determine who appears during the feast. This event allows the player character to possibly initiate romantic encounters with more than one companion, and at much lower approval rates than otherwise required; it also grants the ⁠ Guardian of the Forgotten to party members with the Folk Hero background. During the festivities, in addition to the party's regular camp followers , numerous characters can be interacted with. Companions [ edit section | visual editor ] Every recruited companion can be spoken with during the celebration, with a higher chance of romance. Typically a romance option is open if the player character has 20 or more approval and has either not started any romance or is involved in no more than one other active romance. Companions sometimes comment on who the player character is interested in or "commit to" during the party, influencing their dialogue afterward. During conversation a romance scene can be unlocked, but if there is more than one option, it is only upon going to sleep that the player character chooses among these potential romances. Depending on the player character's prior choices and which companion is spoken with first, more than one romance can be started (e.g., Shadowheart, then Lae'zel and then Karlach). In addition, all companions have dialogue if they are already being romanced by the player character, if a romance has been ended, or if their approval is not yet high enough. Companions can be found at their regular camp spot, except Wyll , who moves closer to the water side for this event. Astarion [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Astarion/Romance If this is the first time the player character engages in close relations with Astarion , it first triggers a dialogue with him stating the party was insufficiently rewarded for their heroics (and explaining what he would like to receive instead). If the player character agrees, Astarion becomes a romance option when they go to sleep. If he is picked a cutscene triggers as described on his romance page . If the player character slept with Astarion before the celebration, Astarion tries to entice the player character into another sexual encounter, paying compliments and finally even confessing his love (though admitting quickly and readily it is an obvious lie). Choosing "I think it's better if we leave last time as a once-off" ends the relationship with Astarion. If the player character agrees to spend the night, there is no additional romantic scene; it is simply implied. Gale [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale gazing at a conjured image of Mystra. See also: Gale/Romance If the player character has not yet triggered a romance scene with Gale , he thanks the player character upon initiating conversion for seeking him out. When going to sleep the player character can seek out Gale and his Mystra cutscene plays, as described on his romance page . If the player character is already romancing Gale, or has ended their romance, he instead talks about his companion Tara and their history together. Lae'zel [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Lae'zel/Romance The tiefling celebration night offers another opportunity to romance Lae'zel . If the player character agrees to her offer, and picks her as option when going to sleep, her cutscene plays as described on her romance page . If scene already happened, an exclamation point may appear above [!] her head. If spoken with, Lae'zel observes she has, on several occasions since their first night together, caught the player character looking at her "with lidded eyes" and perhaps, as she sees it, wants to sleep with her again. If the player character agrees with her assessment, she reminds them she never promised to be with them more than once. If they agree but promise to stop, she deflects, answering, "I did not say it was unwelcome." With either choice, she playfully challenges the longing player character with an offer: "Tempt me." Any response except declining results in approval. When they go to sleep an option think about Lae'zel can then be picked. Karlach [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Karlach/Romance The camp celebration is a key moment in Karlach's romance story. Regardless of approval, the player character can inform Karlach how much they like her and Karlach excitedly agrees to visit the player character after everybody else goes to sleep that night. Karlach's normal method of offering to start a romance is bugged and no longer triggers without mods. As a result, Karlach's romance can only start at this tiefling celebration. If there is an already-planned romance scene (having talked to another companion) Karlach comments on it. However, she still awkwardly asks if the player character wants to spend time with her later instead. If Karlach is chosen, when the player character goes to sleep, she visits and lies next to them. The player character is not able to actually touch Karlach yet, as her quest ⁠ The Hellion's Heart cannot be progressed past the first step in Act One . However, she can be convinced to try a brief kiss – which the player character can either end quickly or embrace the moment. Both options result in burnt lips, but with different dialogue. Shadowheart [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart, spending a quiet evening alone with the player character. She is hoping for a kiss. See also: Shadowheart/Romance At the celebration Shadowheart can be approached in conversation, during which she admits she has begun to care about the refugees and is confused by these unexpected emotions. She also confesses that she feels guilty toward her mistress, Lady Shar . If the player character is eligible for romance with Shadowheart she invites them to "share a bottle" with her. Picking her as option results in her waterfall cutscene unfolding as described on her romance page while going to sleep. The next day, the player character can speak with Shadowheart about the previous night. Her response varies depending on her approval level and on what did or did not occur during the encounter. Wyll [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll sulking by himself near the water. See also: Wyll/Romance Wyll is by the water during the celebration, secluded from the festivities and in a state of melancholy. The player character can talk to him and attempt to cheer him up through various dialogue options. They also have options to flirt with Wyll, including playing a guessing game, asking for a dance or asking for a kiss instead. The kiss requires a DC 15 Charisma or Persuasion Check , but failing does not lock the player character out of his romance. If the player character successfully flirts with Wyll, he responds with a promise: "There will be another time for us." This confirms they are now dating. Afterwards, the player character can select "hoping to dream of Wyll" when going to rest. Wyll rejects the player character during this conversation if they already agreed to spend the night with another companion, are double-dating or have less than 10 Approval with him. After the celebration, the player character can talk about their romantic moment regardless of the kiss or not; either way, Wyll states he has planned something for them. Other interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] The way forward [ edit section | visual editor ] Near the trunk serving as bridge across the water, Zevlor and Halsin stand near each other. When spoken to, Zevlor expresses his delight that his people are saved and happy. He thanks the player character for helping. In case Zevlor has died Cerys takes his place. Instead of simply enjoying the night, she is listing herbs for a hangover cure and plans to go foraging. Halsin urges the player character to enjoy the evening instead of worrying for tomorrow. Although he can be flirted with, his romance scenes are not available at this point. The morning following the tiefling's celebration, Halsin tells the party about the two leads he has on how to reach the Shadow-Cursed Lands : travelling through the Mountain Pass , which would be less dangerous at first but would mean a longer journey through the shadow curse, or exploring the Underdark in search of an alternative route, which would bypass some of the shadow curse but comes with all the dangers inherent there. Both routes are part of the overarching quest ⁠ Travel to Moonrise Towers which starts from this point onward. Alfira [ edit section | visual editor ] In the middle of the campsite Alfira is busy writing a new song. Her companion Lakrissa occasionally drops by and gives her some suggestions. If she is spoken to she says she feels inspired, wants to compose a new song about the player character and asks for input on what it should be about. Not really. I'm not much of a bard. How about courage? Classic song material. Have you seen this body? It would be a crime not to sing about it. Honestly? I'd rather you didn't. If I hear my name in a song, your life is forfeit. [BARD]  If I want a song about me, I'll write it myself. [BARBARIAN]  How about the goblin spines I'd ripped out with my bare hands? [CLERIC]  I don't deserve such praise. I serve a higher power. [FIGHTER]  Sing about my prowess in battle. [HALF-DROW] [HALF-ELF] [HALF-ORC]  Maybe a song about my mixed heritage? It's a point of pride for me. [LOLTH-SWORN]  Sing about surface elves - and how filthy and pathetic they are. [TIEFLING]  Sing about our people. We deserve it. [ASTARION]  There's just so much. Let's start with my physical beauty and go from there. [GALE]  I'd rather hear a song about Mystra. [KARLACH]  Make it a song for everyone who fought. Couldn't have done it alone. [WYLL]  Just mention the legend that is the Blade of Frontiers, the hardiest hero to ever travel the Sword Coast. Afterwards, Alfira mentions that things have begun spinning due to her wine and she will return to creating the song next morning. If Alfira does not survive to the time of the camp celebration, Chell shows up instead; she does not provide similar songwriting questions. Lakrissa & Zae [ edit section | visual editor ] Zae urging the player character on for a dance. If Lakrissa does not survive to the celebration, Zae replaces her. She is slightly intoxicated and asks the player character for a dance. Bards have a specific line to excitedly accept, while Githyanki can decline saying "I only dance the dance of death - in battle." . If the player character accepts Zae's invitation, the following options can be selected. Sway your arms and hips. [PERFORMANCE]  Spin in a circle - hands drifting through the air.  (DC 10) [PERFORMANCE]  Kick out a jaunty two-step.  (DC 10) [DRAGONBORN] [PERFORMANCE]  Perform an ancient waltz of victory.  (DC 10) [BARBARIAN] [STRENGTH]  Stamp the ground and ROAR.  (DC 10) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  Begin a classical Baldurian courtier's dance.  (DC 10) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  Improvise a unique dance.  (DC 10) The first option is deemed too boring by Zae – selecting any other option and dancing successfully grants the ⁠ Celebrant inspiration to characters with the Entertainer background. It also grants approval to some companions.   +1   +5   +1 Barcus [ edit section | visual editor ] Celebration fireworks from Barcus It is possible to have Barcus join the celebration at the campsite if he has been rescued from both the windmill at the Blighted Village and the dig at Grymforge . He must be asked to join the camp at Grymforge after which he becomes a camp follower . During the celebration Barcus can be asked to join the festivities, but he states its your victory, not his. He still worries about his friend Wulbren . Despite his reluctance, he can be persuaded to set off fireworks for the celebration. A new name [ edit section | visual editor ] Asking the player character pause for a while with him, Volo relates how he wants to do a naming for them, a so called "nom de guerre" . The player character can make a suggestion, like 'Grovekeeper' or 'Goblinsbane', but Volo wants something grander, more dramatic and then excuses himself to deliberate. A potential murder [ edit section | visual editor ] During the quest ⁠ Save Arabella the acting archdruid Kagha can let her snake kill the tiefling child Arabella . In this case she is present at the celebration, but so are Arabella's parents Komira and Locke . Whether or not she feels guilty depends on how the quest ⁠ Investigate Kagha is resolved and if she repented. Arabella's parents then poison Kagha and Komira tries to assault her with a knife. A conversation option is available to the player character to convince her to stop her attack ( DC 15 Persuasion Check ). The poison can be cured afterwards with for instance Lesser Restoration . Kagha thanks the party profusely and vows to improve herself. Korrilla [ edit section | visual editor ] Regardless of potential interactions with Korrilla before, she can briefly be found at the campsite. Shortly after the celebration starts, Korrilla teleports to the shoreline of the camp, to a spot between where Wyll and any hirelings are hanging out during the party. If the player character stands too close to her teleport location, she immediately disappears and sneaks towards the spot where Gale is camped; the party may briefly interact with her before she disappears again. The other tieflings [ edit section | visual editor ] Groups of tieflings are spread throughout the camp, and can be spoken with. The couple Bex and Danis are near a trunk which serves as bench. Bex attempts to dance but realises she has had several drinks too many. Githyanki characters get a unique "humorous" dialogue option, asking about cats. The siblings Cal , Lia and Rolan are nearby. Rolan performs a magic show for his brother and sister, and the player character can applaud his performance, though his siblings playfully chide him. The tieflings Ikaron and Guex occasionally banter together. Ikaron is rather unhappy about the festivities, thinking that the fallen tieflings should be commemorated. He can be persuaded to join the others with a DC 5 Charisma Check . Upon success he admits that drinking will make the situation more tolerable. Guex is excited for their destination Baldur's Gate, finally saying goodbye to caves, tents and running away, instead settling down in homes . Across the bridge next to Halsin and Zevlor on the waterside stands Mol . She has found a reclusive spot after having stolen some wine. Mol reveals she is planning on selling it for an expensive price once the attendees run out of drinks. If she was given the idol during the quest ⁠ Steal the Sacred Idol , but the idol is then pickpocketed or bought from her before the celebration, she instead comments that someone managed to steal the idol and she would like to them recruit if she finds out who it was. Other camp followers [ edit section | visual editor ] Despite the celebration, Withers stands at his usual spot, having dialogue options no different than normal. The potential pets Owlbear Cub and Scratch are also present, and excited about the many celebrating people around them. Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Save the Refugees ⁠ Defeat the Goblins ⁠ Raid the Emerald Grove ⁠ Travel to Moonrise Towers Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Since the celebration happens at the campsite , all companions and camp followers can appear if conditions are met (e.g., a companion is recruited). Companions [ edit section | visual editor ] Astarion Gale Lae'zel Karlach Shadowheart Wyll Followers [ edit section | visual editor ] Barcus Wroot [ 1 ] Oathbreaker Knight [ verify ] Owlbear Cub Scratch Tara [ 2 ] Volothamp Geddarm Withers Notable characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin Kagha [ 3 ] Korilla Zevlor Tieflings [ edit section | visual editor ] Alfira Bex Cal Cerys [ 4 ] Chell [ 5 ] Danis Guex Ikaron Kavil [ 6 ] Kivak [ 7 ] Komira [ 3 ] Lakrissa Lia Locke [ 3 ] Mol Rhy [ 8 ] Rolan Vatas [ 9 ] Zae [ 10 ] Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ If rescued from both the Blighted Village and Grymforge before the celebration starts. ↑ If Gale is chosen als origin . ↑ 3.0 3.1 3.2 Shows up if Arabella was killed by Teela . ↑ Shows up if Zevlor is dead ↑ Shows up if Alfira is dead ↑ Shows up if Bex is dead ↑ Shows up if Ikaron is dead ↑ Shows up if Guex is dead ↑ Shows up if Danis is dead ↑ Shows up if Lakrissa is dead
## Trapped Beacon
- **来源**: [Trapped Beacon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Trapped_Beacon)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

A Trapped Beacon on the side of the gallery in Grymforge A Trapped Beacon is a unique type of Trap that might be encountered in the Grymforge in Act One of the game. A Trapped Beacon is a defensive mechanism of clearly Sharran design, resembling a giant vertical ring chiselled of stone, with a brazier inside. There are five beacons standing in the plain sight on each side of the narrow gallery in Grymforge , that can be reached only after successfully resolving the ⁠ Get Past the Rubble : four in pairs across one another, the "pair" for the last one is destroyed. The whole gallery is thickly trapped with Marble Plates , both rectangular and round ones (these are planted between the Beacons), all working as a joint system. Triggering any of plates turns the whole gallery into a veritable obstacle course, as Trapped Beacons work in a certain accordant rhythm with Gargoyle Statues at the both ends of the gallery. Upon triggering any of traps here a Turn-based mode is started automatically. Once in two turns each Trapped Beacon projects a jet of flame that reaches the opposite side of the gallery, dealing 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage to any targets in its way. The paired Trapped Beacons produce the flame jets simultaneously, which allows the party to cross their "firing line" the next turn, when they take pause. The Gargoyle Statues, however, activate each turn , and unlike Beacons, their flame jets protrude for 15 meters and might make the target fall Prone along with taking the damage. Each Trapped Beacon must be detected as a trap and disarmed individually, but botching the Disarm Trap roll on any of them sets off the whole system of traps on the gallery. However, passing the gallery to its end and getting behind the iron gate is worth doing, as it allows to obtain two notable items: The Protecty Sparkswall (one of possible parts of the Sparkstruck set ). Idol of Shar , which can serve as a gift to Shadowheart to improve her attitude towards the player character. A Trapped Beacon can be disarmed with the help of Sleight of Hand skill, but the character must have a Trap Disarm Toolkit in their inventory. Difficulty Class requirement is a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check roll. After successful disarming, the very ring of a Trapped Beacon is depicted as crumbling into a stone rubble down from the gallery.
## Underdark
- **来源**: [Underdark](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Underdark)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The caverns of the Underdark. The Underdark is a region in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is a vast series of caverns and tunnels devoid of sunlight but full of dangerous creatures and even more dangerous mushrooms. It also contains a multitude of alchemical ingredients that are hard to find elsewhere. “ Ah, cries for help... I must be home. „ — Player character belonging to an Underdark race, upon hearing Baelen's wails Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Locations 1.2 Adjacent regions 1.3 Regional Waypoints 2 Access 3 Areas 3.1 Arcane Tower 3.2 Festering Cove 3.3 Decrepit Village 3.4 Carrion crawler nest 3.5 Dread Hollow 3.6 Ebonlake Grotto 3.7 Grymforge 3.8 Selûnite Outpost and Petrified Battlefield 3.9 Storehouse and Minotaur Hills 4 Related quests 5 Characters 5.1 Notable NPCs 5.2 Available to Speak with Dead 6 Creatures 7 Loot 7.1 Quest Items 7.2 Other loot 7.3 Alchemy 7.4 Hidden treasure 8 Literature 9 External Links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3 is only a small portion of the true Underdark. The Drow , Duergar and Deep Gnomes are native to the Underdark. Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Arcane Tower ⁠ Decrepit Village ⁠ Dread Hollow ⁠ Ebonlake Grotto ⁠ Grymforge ⁠ Selûnite Outpost ⁠ Storehouse ⁠ The Festering Cove Adjacent regions [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Shadow-Cursed Lands ⁠ Wilderness Regional Waypoints [ edit section | visual editor ] The following Waypoints are available within the Underdark. Underdark - Beach at X: 22 Y: -209 Underdark - Selûnite Outpost at X: 180 Y: -235 Underdark - Myconid Colony at X: 101 Y: -101 Underdark - Sussur Tree at X: 49 Y: -140 Underdark - Grymforge at X: -647 Y: 382 Underdark - Ancient Forge at X: -612 Y: 294 Access [ edit section | visual editor ] Due to its immense size, there are multiple access points into the Underdark from over-land. All of them involve travelling (or falling) deep into the depths of the world. The following are known options to access the Underdark: Climbing down a ladder from the Defiled Temple , arriving in the Selunite Outpost Using an elevator from the Zhentarim Hideout , arriving in the far end of the Storehouse Using a Mushroom Circle in the Overgrown Tunnel to a corresponding circle above the Torchstalk gulch Jumping into the hole in the Whispering Depths , arriving in the Minotaur Hills; Feather Fall must be used, or a cutscene shows the party falling to death. Areas [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Tower [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Arcane Tower The SW Quadrant of the Underdark, as seen on the map The Arcane Tower occupies the south-west corner of the Underdark region. This area is accessible through a neatly built stone entryway which opens to a front garden featuring several Arcane Cannons . Stains of scorched earth may warn the party members of the danger ahead. The cannons can be destroyed or disabled using the flowers of the Sussur Tree from the Dread Hollow (see below; the latter way grants the ⁠ Secrets of the Sussur Tree inspiration event for party members with the Sage background). In the front garden several Bronze Ingots can be looted, as well as undelivered letter from the tower hostess Lenore de Hurst to her beloved Yrre the Sparkstruck . The tower is forsaken and uninhabited, save for guarding mechanisms and creatures. Its powerbase is deactivated, too, and the party have to solve this riddle in order to explore the building thoroughly. Activating the tower earns the ⁠ Regeneration inspiration event for party members with the Guild Artisan background. The area just in front of the tower garden entrance features dark brown soil and spots of Torchstalks , as well as several deep burrow holes; DC 15 Nature Check helps to recognize the latter as the traces of a Bulette , but the beast never appears in this area. The southern cliff of this gulch features several giant mushroom caps, growing on a rock to resemble a makeshift ladder. Some of these, however, are mere illusions ( DC 10 Investigation Check to dispel each illusional "step"). The corpse of a Dead Drow scout at the foot of the cliff is a victim of an unexpected fall ( DC 10 Medicine Check to apprehend his wounds). It can be spoken to with Speak with Dead . "Upstairs" the party can find an illusional wall, same as they encountered in the Overgrown Tunnel . A DC 20 Investigation Check is required to detect it, but the wall can be walked through even in case of fail. A mushroom circle beyond it at X: 98 Y: -283 leads into the hag's domain. Another circle at the cliff top transports the whole party down. This is one of the points of gaining access to the Underdark, but it is locked if the hag is dead or has already fled her swamp. A character wearing a whispering mask may still walk through the door, even after the hag is dead. [ verify ] Festering Cove [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: The Festering Cove Just aside the illusional mushrooms' wall there is a rift half-concealed with a waterfall. Climbing down the Cragged Rock on its opposite side X: 80 Y: -241 , the party can reach the Festering Cove . It is a hidden location containing a pack of Kuo-toa , led by their priest Pooldripp in worshipping their god BOOOAL . Decrepit Village [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Decrepit Village Map of the Underdark, with the central area highlighted The Decrepit Village is the central area of the Underdark, gradually, but markedly descending from the average level of the region. It visually consists of two levels, with ramshackle wooden structures on the upper one, and rope nettings leading down to the sandy beach of the Ebonlake with two berths. The path leading to the village entrance is strewn with the bodies of dead Myconids and Duergar, and the village and its surroundings - with both Duergar and Deep Gnomes corpses. When first approaching the Decrepit village, a DC 20 Perception Check can help to detect an ambush of several Duergar warriors led by Gekh Coal . They are searching for Thulla , but will attack the party, too, if they are not placated through options of automatically started dialogue. The party may also promise to help Gekh, but if they attack his squad afterwards, it is considered an Oathbreaking Action for Devotion Paladin characters. Down on the beach, a skiff rests at one dock, ready to take the party to Grymforge based on the story path of their choosing. However, it cannot be used until the party somehow deals with Gekh Coal and his squad. In one of the shackles a journal belonging to Wulbren Bongle can be found, asserting his presence in the Underdark and the probability of his being captured by the Duergar. Carrion crawler nest [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Carrion crawler nest On the opposite to the Duergar's ambush side of the village, at X: 30 Y: -238 a carrion crawler nest can be found, resembling a bunch of holes in a steep rocky slope. Several of them are interactable, and recognizing what is what requires a DC 15 Survival Check . Regardless of the result, the player character may also reach into any of holes. If playing as a short race(or disguised as one), a player may reach into the nest and earn the ⁠ Nest Egg inspiration event for party members with the Outlander background and a random precious gem. Dread Hollow [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Dread Hollow Map of the Underdark, with the Dread Hollow and Bibberbang Grotto highlighted This area occupies western and north-western quadrants of the Underdark region. The Dread Hollow actually forms a ring-like territory around a chasm, with a large and brightly shining Sussur Tree growing in it. In the western corner a cave on a rocky cliff can be found, where a mad wizard Filro the Forgotten has made his haven. He becomes hostile to the party on sight, as well as several Hook Horrors roaming around. Speaking to Filro's corpse afterwards or successful examining Tattered Scroll looted from him may start the ⁠ Adamantine Forge (quest) , if it has not been started already, or progress it. If climbing onto a branch of the Sussur Tree at X: -14 Y: -138 , the party can obtain a piece of Sussur Tree Bark , which is necessary to complete the ⁠ Finish the Masterwork Weapon quest. Also, the flowers of this tree block caster characters from using any spells and cantrips, instilling the magic-sapping effect onto any character who comes close to the blooms or carries a fresh flower in the inventory. The eastern part of the Dread Hollow is one of areas where a Bulette can be encountered. Also, at X: -41 Y: -209 here lies the tombstone of Myrna , a pet dog of Lenore de Hurst . To the north-east from the Sussur Tree is a vast cave overgrown densely with dangerous Bibberbang mushrooms with highly flammable spores. Baelen Bonecloak is trapped among their stalks: he fell there from the stone perch engirdling the cave inside, holding a burning torch. The player character must decide whether to help Baelen or not, and also may try to collect a valuable Noblestalk mushroom, which grows in the far end of the cave and can easily be destroyed if even a single Bibberbang stalk is triggered to explode while a fire source is nearby. Helping Baelen to escape earns the ⁠ A Lethal Endeavour inspiration event for party members with the Folk Hero background. The Noblestalk, if successfully collected, can be used by Shadowheart or the Dark Urge to recover some lost memories from their past, and grants the ⁠ A Noble Endeavour inspiration event for party members with the Outlander background. Ebonlake Grotto [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Ebonlake Grotto Map of the Underdark, with Ebonlake Grotto, Myconid Minefield, and Giant Bird Nest highlighted This is the northern part of the region, most of it occupied by the Myconid colony. Several twisted alleys within it are side-lined by oversized mushrooms, with myconid guards and spore-animated corpses walking back and forth. Along the paths Barrelstalks grow, issuing clouds of spores in the air. Passing through such clouds instills Haste Spores on any character for one turn. In the colony, the party can meet several notable non-player characters: the colony leader Sovereign Spaw , traders Blurg and Derryth Bonecloak , Thulla the deep gnome, as well as illithid Omeluum , who can advance the ⁠ Find a Cure quest and act as a merchant, too. Hidden in a cave behind the magical vines, a corpse of a drow wizard Xargrim lays. Investigating it starts the ⁠ Adamantine Forge (quest) (if not started already), or progresses it. The Ebonlake Grotto can be entered at two points: X: 113 Y: -127 ("main entrance" to its south-east, resembling a rocky ladder and guarded by several Myconids) and X: 34 Y: -123 (with yet another guarded mushroom "ladder") leading to the Dread Hollow . Between the two entrances stands Glut - a myconid sovereign of a extinguished circle, who plans to use the party as a means to kill two birds with one stone: taking vengeance upon the Duergar for murdering his subjects and supporting his coup against Spaw for refusing to intervene while the slaughter of his subjects happened. The area in front of the first entrance is full of dangerous mushrooms - Timmasks alternated with Torchstalks. Together these species form a dangerous combination, as triggering or destroying any of Torchstalks starts a chain reaction of explosions. Destroying a single specimen from every type of dangerous mushrooms in Underdark (these two and also a Bibberbang) earns the ⁠ Mushroom Enthusiast inspiration event for party members with the Outlander background. A westward path from the dangerous area leads to the Decrepit Village . The narrow rocky cliff right beyond the mushroom field at X: 126 Y: -159 is one of areas where a Bulette can be encountered. At X: 43 Y: -141 the player character may reach the giant bird's nest by series of jumps. Looting the wooden chest inside the nest grants the ⁠ Clever Cuckoo inspiration event for party members with the Outlander background. Grymforge [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Grymforge Grymforge is an expansive and abandoned settlement on a separate map, including the Adamantine Forge . It can be reached for the first time via the skiff from the Decrepit Village beach. Recently it has been found anew by the Duergar Clan Flameshade . Some members of the clan have also been swayed to the cause of the Absolute by Ketheric Thorm's retainer, drow Nere , while others remained unconcerned. The player character may settle the conflict between two parts of the clan to their avail or oppose them both. Also, they must resolve the fate of several Deep Gnomes, enslaved by the Duergar. Finally, the party can gain access to the ancient Forge and craft an armour or weapon piece of a Very Rare grade. From Grymforge the party can travel into the regions belonging to Act Two of the game. Selûnite Outpost and Petrified Battlefield [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Selûnite Outpost Map of the Underdark, with the Selûnite Outpost and the battlefield highlighted The Selûnite Outpost is located in the south-east corner of the Underdark region. It resembles a small fortress with ramparts and portcullis, but looks abandoned long time ago. However, the magical defence remains functional. A statue of Selûne holds up a bright Moonstone , which channels energy to the two lesser statues just behind the gate to blast any approaching enemy. If any party member comes close to the raised portcullis, one of Minotaurs wandering near the Storehouse runs to attack them and feels the full impact of its ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage. Shattering the moonstone grants the ⁠ Shatter the Moon inspiration to party members with the Acolyte background. By the feet of the statue a tome titled In Search of the Nightsong lies; reading it progresses the ⁠ Find the Nightsong quest. The Outpost is another possible point of accessing the Underdark. It can be reached descending from the Shattered Sanctum . By several diaries and documents found around the outpost, as well as scattered wooden barricades and weapons left, it may be concluded that Selûnite devotees tried to establish a foothold in the Underdark, but their endeavour demanded an ever-growing amount of resources from over-world and finally failed due to hostility of local inhabitants (drow, according to diaries, but probably not only them), and also lead to the decline of the temple above. The surroundings of the outpost is one of areas where a Bulette can be encountered. The high cliff at X: 116 Y: -192 features the remains of a ritual revering the goddess Eilistraee . Using various checks, the player character can take the Phalar Aluve from its stone cradle, which earns the ⁠ Last Rites of the Dark Dancer inspiration to party members with the Acolyte background. The area to the west of the outpost, accessible through the ruined window section, is remarkable by several Petrified Drow and numerous glowing gems. When the party approach it, a cutscene starts, ending in the source of petrification revealing itself - a Spectator . After the battle with it is resolved, one of the formerly petrified drow, the wizard Dhourn (or his corpse), can be spoken with to start the ⁠ Adamantine Forge (quest) (if not started already), or to progress it. Otherwise, the player character may try to use the Memory Shard looted from Dhourn. On a cliff behind several layers of spider webs at X: 84 Y: -207 , the party can find a long-forgotten stash of Lolth-Sworn Drow . From a locked chest the party can loot Drow Studded Leather Armour , and read the On Educating the Faithful tome by matron Tarrae of Menzoberranzan on the stone "desk" nearby, which earns the ⁠ Secrets of the Matron inspiration to party members with the Sage background. Storehouse and Minotaur Hills [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Storehouse Map of the Underdark, with the Storehouse and Minotaur Hills highlighted The north-eastern quadrant of the Underdark consists of the Storehouse - a named area recognisable for its aging pale wooden interior crammed with various containers, and Minotaur Hills (unnamed area), featuring bright green grass and whimsical red mushrooms with swirling paths. The Storehouse is divided from the Minotaur Hills by the rope netting. The ground at the foot of the netting is trapped with Blast Mines , and triggering them may destroy the netting. However, it is possible to climb up through a series of jumps onto giant mushroom caps growing aside. This quadrant has two points where the party can enter the Underdark region. An elevator leads from the over-world's Zhentarim Hideout into the Storehouse. Also, if the party jumps into the hollow within the Whispering Depths (using means like Feather Fall to avoid immediate death), they land at X: 140 Y: -150 , on the fringes of the Minotaur Hills. Entering the Underdark this way grants the ⁠ Abyss Jumper inspiration to party members with the Outlander background. The Storehouse can be looted for a large amount of Valuables , alchemical resources, Camp Supplies and common weapons. If reached from the other part of the Underdark, any party member can recognize the symbols on the crates as belonging to Zhentarim (if entering the region through the elevator from the Zhentarim Hideout, the check is not rolled). The Storehouse is free of any enemies, while the Hills, as per name, feature three wandering Minotaurs , which turn hostile on sight (one of them may attack the Selûnite Outpost gate and be burned to death by Moonstone rays). Neither area has interactable neutral or allied NPCs. Most part of the area (all the way to the Selûnite Outpost) is considered as demesne by the Myconids of the nearby Ebonlake Grotto colony, seen as purplish speckles in the air. When first entering its boundaries, the party feel the effect of Rapport Spores and are engaged into the dialogue with myconids (warning them of Minotaurs) through it. A successful DC 14 Nature Check helps to detect the spores, and any party member comments on it regardless of result. Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] The following quests may all be found in unnamed areas of the Underdark region (additional quests are available in named locations within the Underdark): ⁠ Find the Nightsong ⁠ Find the Mushroom Picker ⁠ Find a Cure ⁠ Help Omeluum investigate the parasite ⁠ Reach Moonrise Towers Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] The list here does not include the characters that might be encountered in Grymforge . Notable NPCs [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Tower: Bernard Decrepit Village: Gekh Coal Garmor Holvik Lurgan Dread Hollow: Baelen Bonecloak Filro Festering Cove: BOOOAL Pooldripp Ebonlake Grotto: Blurg Derryth Bonecloak Glut Omeluum Spaw Thulla Xargrim - deceased Petrified Battlefield: Dhourn Available to Speak with Dead [ edit section | visual editor ] Dead Drow - found in the Torchstalk Gulch area Dead Myconid Sprout - found inside the Ebonlake Grotto Shattered Duergar - found in the Beach area Creatures [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Turret Animated Armour Bulette Deep Rothé (myconid colony) Hook Horror Kuo-Toa Minotaur Mossy Myconid Noxious Myconid Restless Myconid Spectator Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] The list here does not include items that can be obtained in Grymforge . Quest Items [ edit section | visual editor ] In Search of the Nightsong Memory Shard Noblestalk Scribbled Note Sussur Bloom Sussur Tree Bark Tattered Scroll The Great Furnace of Grymforge (this book is initially disguised by magic and seen as Flumph Mating Rituals ) Other loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Bloodguzzler Garb - looted from Bulette Club of Hill Giant Strength - after breaking the Stool of Hill Giant Strength in Arcane Tower Dog Collar - by digging up the grave in the Dread Hollow Drow Studded Leather Armour - in a chest in Lolth-Sworn Drow stash Explorer's Ring - on a skeleton X: -12 Y: -50 on a stone ledge in Bibberbang cave Exterminator's Axe - looted from Gekh Coal Icy Crystal - carried by Filro Icy Helve - carried by Dhourn Icy Metal - on the corpse of Xargrim Helmet of Autonomy Helmet of Smiting - in a locked chest in the Selûnite Outpost Light of Creation - looted from Bernard Luminous Armour - in a hidden section of the Selûnite Outpost Mourning Frost - on combining Icy Crystal , Icy Helve and Icy Metal Phalar Aluve X: 117 Y: -192 : by passing a Strength or Religion check to free this sword from a stone Sickle of BOOOAL - in the Festering Cove Shortsword of First Blood looted from the corpse of an executed deep gnome at X: 73 Y: -187 Skybreaker - in a locked chest in the garden near the Arcane Tower Slippery Chain Shirt - in the Festering Cove The Blast Pendant - worn by Dhourn The Spectator Eyes - looted from Spectator Alchemy [ edit section | visual editor ] The Underdark provides several unique alchemical ingredients that cannot be picked up anywhere else, only bought from various traders. However, collecting these ingredients sometimes requires certain Ability checks or preemptive measures. Nightlight Frond can be picked up from Nightlight mushrooms growing around the region after succeeding a DC 14 Nature Check Timmask Spores can be collected around triggered Timmask mushrooms by those party members who succeeded a Saving Throw against Befuddled caused by these fungi. The spore items disappear in a turn after triggering the mushroom. ## Underground Passage
- **来源**: [Underground Passage](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Underground_Passage)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

Not to be confused with Overgrown Tunnel The Underground Passage. Emerald Grove The Hollow ↑ Underground Passage → Enclave Library ↓ Forest The Underground Passage is a Location within the Emerald Grove in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I don't think that statue's eyes are glowing to provide illumination. Best be careful. „ — Shadowheart , spotting the guardian statue inside Contents 1 Overview 2 Guardian statues 3 Interactions 4 Related quests 5 Characters 6 Loot 7 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Underground Passage is a cavernous tunnel which runs roughly in parallel to the western side of the Hollow , connecting certain parts of the Emerald Grove with the Forest . It is trapped with several guardian statues which hurl flames at any trespassers in sight that deal 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage and inflict 3 turns of Burning on a failed DC  12 Dexterity Saving Throw . Map of the tunnel The Underground Passage can be accessed at several points, all of which are concealed by stone doors. In the Forest at X: 172 Y: 423 . This door requires a DC 10 Survival Check to find. It is located behind a mossy boulder and a fallen tree. In the Hollow , on a rocky ledge behind the Makeshift Prison at X: 204 Y: 604 . Detecting this door requires a DC 5 Perception Check . In the Enclave Library , opposite the other door, at X: -446 Y: -30 . Noticing the door requires a DC 5 Perception Check check and to unlock it a Key of the Ancients must be equipped by one of the party members. [ 1 ] It also has a small antechamber trapped with vents spilling poison clouds . Guardian statues [ edit section | visual editor ] There are five statues in the tunnel, two of them depicting bears, another two eagles, and the last one a wolf. [ 2 ] Of the statues, only three, one of each animal, are hostile and a DC 5 Perception Check is required to detect each threat. To turn them off, a character must directly interact with the rune that corresponds with the statue's animal shape. Unlike levers, the runes cannot be shot to deactivate them, though a Mage Hand can be used. This task can be accomplished without taking damage via Turn-Based Mode and using several Dashes or similar class actions to reach each rune. The rune locations are: Rune of the Bear at X: -432 Y: -173 Rune of the Eagle at X: -434 Y: -203 Rune of the Wolf at X: -456 Y: -183 The last rune is hidden on the side of a rocky outcrop protruding from the water, and reaching it requires jumping from the main path of the passage. Alternatively, the statues can be attacked and destroyed from a distance. Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party have not defeated the Goblin Camp , they find an unconscious Findal surrounded by several goblins. After defeating the goblins, the party can heal Findal or tell him they are going to finish the job. In the former case, he returns to the grove and can later be encountered in the Inner Sanctum . Defeating the goblins and healing Findal grants the inspiration ⁠ A Timely Rescue for characters with the Folk Hero background. However, if the party have Sazza with them, Findal realises he has stumbled upon an escape attempt and may become hostile. While still unconscious, Findal can be freely pickpocketed for the Key of the Ancients ; he does not later accuse the party of theft upon waking up. If the party arrive in the Underground Passage after defeating the Goblin Camp without having saved Findal, his corpse can be found along the path. When reaching the Rune of the Wolf, at X: -450 Y: -180 , a buried chest can be detected with a DC 12 Survival Check . It contains an Elixir of Fire Resistance , random alchemical ingredients , and gold. Near the rune itself, at X: -455 Y: -183 , a Charred Key and a Potion of Healing can be found on a corpse. [ 3 ] At X: -425 Y: -200 is a trapped heavy chest. A DC 10 Perception Check is required to notice the trap, and the chest needs a DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to disarm and a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to open. The lock can also be opened with the Charred Key. Inside is gold and the Nature's Snare . Two Oil Barrels lie beside the chest, massively increasing the damage of the trap, if triggered. Therefore, It is advisable to pick up or move the barrels before attempting to disarm the trap. A clutter of crates and barrels nearby contain random potions, scrolls, Thieves' Tools , and Trap Disarm Toolkits . In front of the Forest entrance, a backpack hidden at X: 167 Y: 418 , behind a log, contains a Grease Bottle , a Potion of Healing , and a set of Thieves' Tools . Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Raid the Grove ⁠ Save the Goblin Sazza ⁠ Save the Refugees Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Findal Gresh Gurza Sazza - conditional Torrack Worm Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Key of the Ancients Nature's Snare Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ The Key of the Ancients can be taken from Findal in the Underground Passage itself, or from Nettie in the Inner Sanctum . ↑ The tunnel also features the remains of a sixth statue of an elk, but there is no respective rune to be found. ↑ Prior to Hotfix #33 [ verify ] , the body was named "Charred Corpse", before being changed to "Dead Man" . ## Waukeen's Rest
- **来源**: [Waukeen's Rest](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Waukeen's_Rest)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The burning inn of Waukeen's Rest Wilderness Mountain Pass ← Waukeen's Rest → Risen Road ↓ Goblin Camp Waukeen's Rest is a Location within the Wilderness in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is an inn that serves passing travellers but has recently been sacked by goblins and drow . “ Your kind happened! Unless you're here to finish the job, get over here and push! „ — Yeva , to a drow or drow half-elf player character asking what has happened Contents 1 Overview 2 After the assault 3 Florrick and the Grand Duke 3.1 Quest Rewards and Consequences 4 Benryn and Mirileth 5 Zhentarim Hideout 6 Waypoints 7 Related locations 8 Related quests 9 Characters 9.1 Available for Speak with Dead 10 Loot 10.1 Quest rewards 10.2 Hidden treasure 10.3 Other 11 Notes 12 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Waukeen's Rest is a two-story inn with a central building and two wings on either side. Neatly built in a natural rocky alcove, its premises make for a secluded pocket of space, divided from the outer world by a gate. Such a layout could provide strong defences – or turn into a deadly trap for those inside if caught off guard. If the party have not already discovered Waukeen's Rest, they can first hear about it from Rugan , a Zhentarim agent cornered by a pack of gnolls on the Risen Road . After the assault [ edit section | visual editor ] The inn is on fire when the party first arrive. Any party member may see smoke and hear cries from afar and comment on it. Saving the possible survivors is a time-sensitive activity . The timer is set upon reaching the inner yard of the inn. Using fast travel (including simply returning to camp and back) or taking a long rest after it has started causes the flames to progress and all characters trapped inside the inn to die. There are many corpses of drow, goblins and Flaming Fists lying about. On one of the drow corpses, the party can find Faded Drow Leather Armour . Succeeding in identifying the armour grants the inspiration ⁠ The Spider's Gift ( Guild Artisan background). Upon the party's approach, they see several members of the Flaming Fist – Gauntlet Yeva , as well as the recruits Ito , Aelis , and Pavel – trying to break down the main door. Two more Fists, Tristan and Gauntlet Dain , run around trying to douse the fires with water from the fountain in the middle of the inner yard. Near the gate, Ephren kneels over the corpse of Jacek , praying to Helm for his soul. Paladins (except Oathbreakers ) and clerics of good-aligned deities have an option to pray with her, earning the inspiration ⁠ A Unified Spirit ( Acolyte background). Talking to Yeva near the main door starts the quest Rescue the Grand Duke . If Wyll is played as an origin or has been recruited as a companion , this also adds the subquest The Grand Duke to his personal or companion quest. The player character can then help the Flaming Fists to break the door by passing a DC 10 Strength Check . Paladins roll this with Advantage , while bard characters use Performance instead. There is only one attempt for the entire party; if it fails, Yeva suggests finding another way in. The actual task is to get inside the building and free Counsellor Florrick , who is trapped behind a broken door in a room on the first floor of the western wing. [ 1 ] Following Yeva's orders grants the inspiration ⁠ Chain of Command ( Soldier background). The interior of Waukeen's Rest can be accessed through several alternative routes if the main entrance is blocked: Western Wing: Enter through the room where Benryn is trapped. Front Gallery: A character with high Strength can jump to the gallery above the main doors ( X: -72 Y: 605 ) and enter by destroying the boarded-up window. Eastern Wing: Destroy the large wine barrel blocking the eastern entrance. Once inside, jump to the first floor or use nearby crates to construct improvised stairs. First Floor Suite: The locked door on the upper floor can be opened using the Suite Key , found on a halfling corpse outside at X: -88 Y: 610 . Alternatively, the door can be lockpicked ( DC 18 Sleight of Hand Check ) or destroyed. Once freed, regardless of the method, Florrick moves down to the inn entrance, telling the player character she will explain everything outside. Florrick and the Grand Duke [ edit section | visual editor ] After following Florrick outside the building, dialogue with her starts automatically. [ 2 ] The player character may then learn that Counsellor Florrick is the closest assistant to Ulder Ravengard , the Grand Duke of the city of Baldur's Gate . If Wyll is played as an origin or is in the party as a companion, he and Florrick recognise each other at once. After that, Florrick confirms that Duke Ravengard had been inside the inn, but was kidnapped by goblins and drow who assaulted it. She asks the player character to track down the attackers and rescue the Duke. At this point, refusing her or choosing to leave the dialogue is considered an oathbreaking action for Oath of the Crown Paladins. If she is rescued, Counsellor Florrick rewards the party with a choice of one of three lightning-themed weapons (see Rewards below). This reward is granted regardless of whether the party agrees to help her rescue Ulder Ravengard . Quest Rewards and Consequences [ edit section | visual editor ] Inspirations: Saving Florrick grants ⁠ Rescued from the Flames ( Folk Hero background) [ 3 ] and ⁠ Protector of the Duke ( Noble background). Departure: Following her rescue, she orders the Flaming Fist to regroup and track the kidnappers. NPC Dispersal: Most members of the Flaming Fist leave the area. While the text implies only Gauntlet Yeva appears later, others (such as Manus or Liara Portyr ) can be encountered in later Acts depending on player choices. If the party missed their chance to save Florrick (due to fast travel or taking a long rest), they return to the smouldering ruins of the inn. All the Fists are gone, except Ephren (still praying) and Gauntlet Dain, who wanders around the inner yard, trying to read the tracks of the raiders. The party may offer their help, which requires passing a DC 10 Investigation Check , or try to question her. Dain tries to conceal the real state of affairs, but the party can still find out through various checks that Duke Ravengard was the target and that his counsellor is dead. The party can also find Florrick's corpse upstairs, but she cannot be communed with using Speak with Dead . Benryn and Mirileth [ edit section | visual editor ] As the party come to the first floor of the burning inn at X: -71 Y: 624 , they feel the heat emerging from behind the doors nearby and comment on it. From behind the door, they can hear cries for help. However, breaking or opening the doors causes a backdraft effect; all nearby party members are thrown back approximately 12 m (40 ft), possibly gaining the Burning condition and falling downstairs, while the fires behind the door flare up and engulf both rooms. Inside, Benryn is Pinned to the ground with fallen beams. Entering the room starts the quest Rescue the Trapped Man . A party member can then make their way through the burning room to Benryn, help him up by removing the beams, which requires passing a DC 10 Strength Check ( barbarians have Advantage ), and escort him out of the room. All this must be done rather quickly, as Benryn has only 8 HP, the flames cover the whole room in three turns, and the only other way out is blocked with a wooden barricade. Therefore, it is recommended to use a single party member with high Strength, high movement speed and in turn-based mode . Once freed, Benryn runs past the player character to the next room in the eastern wing, where the corpse of a half-elven woman lies at X: -85 Y: 600 . Benryn recognises her as Miri and kneels beside her, consumed with grief. The player character may then ask him about her or interrogate her corpse using Speak with Dead to find out what happened. If the player character communes with her corpse prior to rescuing Benryn, she asks them to save him, initiating Rescue the Trapped Man. Letting Benryn burn to death under the fallen beams grants the inspiration ⁠ Fresh Kindle for the Fire ( Haunted One background). In the room adjacent to where Benryn was trapped is a wooden chest with some gold and also a locked gilded chest with Hamarhraft inside. The hammer and the gold can be obtained safely after a long rest, when the inn is burned down, and the fire is extinguished. The chest is then destroyed, but the loot remains intact. Zhentarim Hideout [ edit section | visual editor ] Behind the western wing of the inn, there are three barns. In the one to the right, at X: -102 Y: 621 , a hay stack can be inspected by passing a DC 15 Perception Check to find a Gilded Chest containing the dowry belonging to Benryn and Mirileth. This check can be reduced to 0 by asking Mirileth about the dowry using Speak with Dead . The left barn is a shed with two cows, an ox which has been killed, and another alive. As the party approach, dialogue begins with the Frightened Ox . If the interacting party member does not placate it with Persuasion via Speak with Animals or by using Animal Handling it attacks the party. If the player character is a drow or drow half-elf themselves, the ox attacks without speaking. The barn in the middle serves as a clandestine entrance to the Zhentarim Hideout . As the party approach, a DC 15 Perception Check allows a member to detect movement inside. Behind the shelves, Salazon is crouched and asks for a password, threatening to hurl a Fire Bolt at the several Oil Barrels and Firewine Barrels stacked inside near the entrance. The password ( "Little serpent, long shadow" ) can be obtained from Rugan if the party save him during the quest Find the Missing Shipment or via Speak with Dead if he dies. Alternatively, passing any of the dialogue ability checks with Salazon has him stand down. Rogue characters have an additional option: showing him a "profit" hand gesture, which earns approval from   +1 ,   +1 ,   +5 , and   +1 . If Salazon is successfully dealt with, he gives the party an Engraved Key and welcomes them to enter the basement through the trapdoor. The key opens a secret passage behind the wardrobe at the back of the basement, which leads to the hideout. If the attempt to convince Salazon is not successful, he ignites the barrels and moves to flee back to the hideout. In this case, the spare key to the secret passage may be found in a wooden crate at X: 382 Y: -258 . ## Whispering Depths
- **来源**: [Whispering Depths](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Whispering_Depths)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The Phase Spider Matriarch's lair in the Whispering Depths. The Whispering Depths is a Location within the Blighted Village in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is situated below the village. “ Those webs are huge. Tread lightly, or become dinner. „ — Wyll , after descending through the well Contents 1 Points of entrance 2 Overview 2.1 Arachnomancer's chamber 2.2 Central caves 2.3 Matriarch's den 3 Waypoints 4 Related quests 5 Creatures 6 Loot 7 Literature 8 Achievements Points of entrance [ edit section | visual editor ] Whispering Depths can be accessed from three points, all of which are located in the Blighted Village . The overgrown well in the centre of the village at X: 24 Y: 401 . To detect it as an entrance to the tunnels underneath any party member must first pass a DC 10 Investigation Check . Through the cellar of the blacksmith's workshop. There are two points where a weak wall of the cellar can be destroyed to get access to the location: near the forge itself at X: -447 Y: -367 , which requires DC 10 Perception Check to find or at X: -455 Y: -389 , which requires climbing up on the cavernous shelf. Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the tunnels with exits into the smithy The Whispering Depths are a vast system of tunnels, caverns and rocky rifts underneath the Blighted Village . Some of the caverns and rifts are located on different height levels, with cragged rocks to climb upon them. Some, however, stand separately, and the only way to reach them is using paths of thick cobwebs stretched between the edges. The ground in the tunnels is sporadically covered with Web , as well. Party members who step on the enwebbed area or onto a hanging cobweb path must immediately roll a DC  12 Dexterity Saving Throw , unless they have any equipment or ability which prevents their movement from being restrained. If failed, they receive the Enwebbed condition and cannot move until the next successful roll which is made once a turn. Even with successful rolls, the web surface is considered Difficult Terrain . More so, disturbing it echoes around the caverns, depicted as blood-red waves of "sound" running from the character, and attracts the web-weavers to their next potential meal. Finally, hanging web paths can easily be destroyed with fire, felling whatever is on its surface. This can be useful in a fight, but may also cause party members' serious injuries if used carelessly. In the Whispering Depths one of four possible ways to reach the Underdark can be found. To do this, the party must jump into the central green-glowing pit below where the Phase Spider Matriarch normally wanders, arriving approximately at X: 140 Y: -150 at an unnamed location dubbed Minotaur Hills . Feather Fall must be used, otherwise a cut-scene shows the party member(s) falling to their death. Entering the Underdark this way grants the ⁠ Abyss Jumper inspiration to party members with the Outlander background. Arachnomancer's chamber [ edit section | visual editor ] The tunnel starting at X: -505 Y: -402 leads into a small workshop, which previously housed a Lolth devotee named Eliette . She left four journals, which describe the story of her being captured by the drow, then enraptured with Lolth cult, and finally, her "transcendence". It is strongly implied that Eliette eventually became the Phase Spider Matriarch (see below). Eliette's journals are scattered around the cavern. Reading all four journals earns the ⁠ A Solitary Spider inspirational event for the characters with Sage background. A metal chest beside a writing desk contains Spiderstep Boots , which Eliette considered a gift from Lolth herself. Central caves [ edit section | visual editor ] North of the well is a section of caves guarded by two Phase Spiders and two Ettercaps . Both types of creatures are particularly sensitive to web disturbances, and proceed to the source as fast as they can. Several cragged rocks at the east-most side of the cave system lead to an upper-level path. This in turn eventually leads to both ways into the Blighted Village smithy. When exploring the caves, the player character can find several old backpacks with various supplies, gold and potions, as well as goblin corpses and skeletons. Also, the party can loot the numerous Spider Silk Cocoons which can be found along the way; those hanging high enough must be destroyed by any means except ⁠ Fire . Most of them (especially human-shaped ones) yield potions, gold, and plain weapons and pieces of armour. While the spiders in the cave (including the Matriarch) are still alive, all cocoons are red-outlined and, if looted, emit sound waves which attract nearby Phase Spiders and Ettercaps. At X: -494 Y: -364 lies the Apprentice's Pack , which contains the Apprentice's Journal , shedding some light on the story of Ilyn Toth and giving a hint where the keygem to the Necromancy of Thay is hidden. Matriarch's den [ edit section | visual editor ] At the western end of the depths is a large, open section where the Phase Spider Matriarch can be encountered, accompanied by two more Phase Spiders . The matriarch wanders along the cobweb "bridges", overlooking three clutches of eggs and hatches them out if attacked. Each clutch hatches into a pack of six Phase Spiderlings . Two egg clutches are laid on the tops of rocky ridges, connected by the cobweb paths at X: -569 Y: -355 and X: -557 Y: -337 , and the third one lies on the lower level of the cave at X: -549 Y: -375 . Being caught when destroying any of them makes all three spiders hostile. However, it is possible to destroy all three clutches by using stealth and / or Silence . It is also possible to destroy them in a single combat turn before the Matriarch can hatch them into spiderlings by dividing the party and using area-covering spells, grenades or arrows. At the feet of one of the rocky ridges at X: -565 Y: -356 lies the Dark Amethyst - the aforementioned keygem to the necromancer's tome. It is not hidden, and its purple glow can be seen from afar; it is possible to loot it without fighting the spiders. Waypoints [ edit section | visual editor ] This location contains the following waypoint : Whispering Depths at X: -584 Y: -384 Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Search the Cellar ⁠ Travel through the Underdark ⁠ Unlock the Ancient Tome Creatures [ edit section | visual editor ] Ettercaps Phase Spiders Phase Spiderlings - conditional Phase Spider Matriarch Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Notable items obtained in this location, whether looted, purchased, or obtained as a quest reward: Dark Amethyst - a quest item found just beside the central pit in the matriarch's den Poisoner's Robe - looted from the phase spider matriarch Spiderstep Boots Spurred Band The various Spider Silk Cocoons in the area contain random loot, corresponding to a Treasure Table with the UID FOR_Spiders_Cocoon . ## Wilderness
- **来源**: [Wilderness](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wilderness)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

A map of the Wilderness with some notable locations; Emerald Grove, Tollhouse, Waukeen's Rest, Goblin Camp, Overgrown Ruins and the Sunlit Wetlands highlighted. The Wilderness is a region in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Locations 1.2 Adjacent regions 1.3 Waypoints 2 Ravaged beach 2.1 Roadside cliffs 2.2 Overgrown ruins 3 North eastern locations 3.1 Emerald Grove 3.2 Secluded cove 4 Central locations 4.1 Forest 4.2 Blighted Village 5 North western locations 5.1 Risen Road 5.2 Waukeen's Rest 5.3 Mountain Pass 6 Southern locations 6.1 Sunlit Wetlands 7 Western locations 7.1 Goblin Camp 8 Characters 8.1 Companions 8.2 Notable non-player characters 8.3 Creatures 9 Loot 9.1 Hidden treasures 10 References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Wilderness is a heavily forested area in Elturgard [ 1 ] [ 2 ] , covering a segment of the Risen Road and the River Chionthar somewhere between Elturel and Baldur's Gate . Notable settlements in the region include the Emerald Grove , the Blighted Village and Waukeen's Rest . A tribe of goblins and several other types of monsters have settled in the Blighted Village and Temple of Selûne to the west. The Overgrown Ruins lie to the far east. The Wilderness also contains several entrances to the Underdark . The Wilderness Region as seen on the minimap. Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Blighted Village ⁠ Emerald Grove ⁠ Forest ⁠ Goblin Camp ⁠ Mountain Pass ⁠ Nautiloid Wreck ⁠ Overgrown Ruins ⁠ Ravaged Beach ⁠ Sunlit Wetlands / ⁠ Putrid Bog ⁠ The Risen Road ⁠ Waukeen's Rest Adjacent regions [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Rosymorn Monastery Trail ⁠ Underdark Waypoints [ edit section | visual editor ] The following Waypoints are available within the Wilderness region. Blighted Village  X: 34 Y: 394 Emerald Grove Environs  X: 246 Y: 423 Goblin Camp  X: -74 Y: 445 Overgrown Ruins  X: 276 Y: 298 Riverside Teahouse  X: -10 Y: 250 Roadside Cliffs  X: 222 Y: 326 The Risen Road  X: 82 Y: 597 Waukeen's Rest  X: -77 Y: 570 Ravaged beach [ edit section | visual editor ] The map areas that constitute the SE quadrant of the Wilderness. Main article: Ravaged Beach Located on the bank of the River Chionthar along the far south-east of the mini-map, the Ravaged Beach is dominated by the wreck of a Nautiloid . Corpses of fishermen and intellect devourers dot the area. Several makeshift docks once stood here, but both the docks and the fishing boats that used them appear destroyed. A door leading to the Dank Crypt lies to the north-west, while the Emerald Grove lies to the north. The player character arrives in this location immediately after the Prologue and is likely to encounter Shadowheart here. Roadside cliffs [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Roadside Cliffs The Roadside Cliffs sprawl north of the Nautiloid Wreck and south of the Emerald Grove, between the Forest to the west and the Overgrown Ruins to the east. Gale and Lae'zel can be rescued and recruited here. Waypoint : Roadside Cliffs X: 222 Y: 326 Overgrown ruins [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Overgrown Ruins North eastern locations [ edit section | visual editor ] The map areas that constitute the NE Quadrant of the Wilderness. Emerald Grove [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Emerald Grove The Emerald Grove , also known as Silvanus' Grove and Druid's Grove , is in the north-east. It encompasses the large cavern known as the The Hollow and the Sacred Pool . The Druids of the Emerald Grove are led by Kagha , who serves as the leader of the druids in the absence of First Druid Halsin . They provide temporary refuge for the tiefling refugees from Elturel, though tensions are high between the two groups. The Grove is on high alert due to the aggression of nearby goblins. Kagha has ordered for the Rite of Thorns to shut the grove off, which would also displace the tieflings. Secluded cove [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Secluded Cove The Secluded Cove is another segment of beach to the east of the Emerald Grove. Harpies have set up a nest in this location. They can be a dangerous encounter for unprepared party members. Central locations [ edit section | visual editor ] The map areas that constitute the Central Quadrant of the Wilderness. Forest [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Forest The Forest is located in the centre-most quadrant of the Wilderness map. This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable for its large canopy of shade trees and soil pathways speckled with grey rocks. This location contains the Blighted Village at its centre. It is located north of the Sunlit Wetlands, east of the Goblin Camp, south of The Risen Road, south-west of the Emerald Grove, and west of an unnamed area known as the Roadside Cliffs where the Nautiloid wreckage still burns. Blighted Village [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Blighted Village The Blighted Village is in the centre-most quadrant of the Wilderness map. This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable for its large windmill. The village is surrounded by the Forest on all sides. North western locations [ edit section | visual editor ] Risen Road [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: The Risen Road The Risen Road is located in the north and central quadrants of the Wilderness map. This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable for large groups of gnolls . This location is adjacent to the west of the Emerald Grove and to the north of the Forest. It contains a passage between Waukeen's Rest and the Mountain Pass to its west. Waukeen's Rest [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Waukeen's Rest Waukeen's Rest' is a location in the north-west quadrant of the Wilderness . This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable for the large fire that consumes its primary building as a result of a raid. This location is adjacent to the north-west of the Risen Road. Mountain Pass [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Mountain Pass The Mountain Pass is in the most north-west quadrant of the Wilderness map. This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable for a powerful group of githyanki . This area is adjacent to the west of Waukeen's Rest and the Risen Road. The passage leading farther westward leads to a separate region. Southern locations [ edit section | visual editor ] Sunlit Wetlands [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Sunlit Wetlands The Sunlit Wetlands (also known as the Putrid Bog ) is located in the most south-west quadrant of the Wilderness map. This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable for its beautiful pools of dappled waters that eventually give way to dead trees and foetid marsh. This location is adjacent to the south of the Forest. Western locations [ edit section | visual editor ] Goblin Camp [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Goblin Camp The Goblin Camp is a settlement location in the far west quadrant of the Wilderness map. This area is labelled on the player minimap and is recognisable by its goblin residents. This location is adjacent to the Forest to the west and the Sunlit Wetlands to the south. A passage farther westward leads to a separate region via the Mountain Pass. Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Companions [ edit section | visual editor ] The following companions may be found in the unnamed Wilderness region (additional companions are available in named locations within the Wilderness): Astarion is looking for help defeating an intellect devourer west of the crashed Nautiloid at X: 170 Y: 288 Lae'zel is trapped by two tieflings, Damays and Nymessa at X: 237 Y: 371 Gale teleports from the Roadside Cliffs waypoint Shadowheart is lying unconscious in the sand along the Ravaged Beach Notable non-player characters [ edit section | visual editor ] All other notable characters are contained within named locations. ## Worg Pens
- **来源**: [Worg Pens](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Worg_Pens)
- **分类**: Act_One_Locations

The Worg Pens Shattered Sanctum Worg Pens ↓ Shattered Sanctum The Worg Pens is a Location within the Shattered Sanctum in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is a separate sub-area which can be reached only from the Sanctum. “ Pardon the viscera. One should cherish all of nature's bounty... but goblin guts are quite far down the list. „ — Halsin , after being freed from the pens' cage Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Animal pens 1.2 Prison cell 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 Creatures 4.2 Available to Speak with Dead 5 Loot 6 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Worg Pens serve both as a place where the Goblin Camp's worgs are kept and also as prison for those party members who are arrested within the camp and Shattered Sanctum territory. The pens can be accessed from two points: The main entrance from the antechamber adjacent to Minthara's headquarters. A secret passage which can be opened after interacting with the Dead Elf corpse at X: 416 Y: -44 . After entering the Worg Pens, there are two small rooms on both sides. In the western one, a wooden chest contains some valuables, while in the eastern room a Potion of Healing can be taken and also three random scrolls from the broken cabinet. While the goblins in the pens are still alive, picking up any of these items is considered a transgression. Animal pens [ edit section | visual editor ] The Worg Pens are managed by Beastmaster Zurk and Butcher Vrak , who oversee the prisoners and occasionally feed the worgs with those who are no longer deemed useful. Warrior Plig patrols the area in front of the entrance. Two worgs, Ferr and Tale , are locked in the far pen. They are the offspring of Klaw in the Goblin Camp . Both pens are opened with levers on nearby walls. When the party visit the pens, the sole living creature contained in the other pen is Halsin , the First Druid of the Emerald Grove , disguised as a Cave Bear . Two goblin children, One and Three , throw sharp rocks at him through the pen gates, encouraged by their tutor Brawler Birka . Upon approaching the pen, the dialogue between the player character, the Cave Bear, Birka and the goblin kids starts automatically. The party can side with the bear or with the goblins, or leave the conversation without taking a decision. If the character speaking has the Speak with Animals effect active, the bear asks them for help. Also, the player character may choose to attack the goblins or shoot the lever which keeps the grate shut from afar without starting the conversation. Siding with the Halsin or aiding him in any way starts a fight with all the goblins in the pens and both worgs, with Halsin as an ally of the party. Aiding Halsin causes him to break free from his cell and kill Birka immediately. If the fight is started without interacting with Halsin at all, he breaks free on the first turn he gets and kills Birka if alive. Choosing to attack Halsin while he is still in bear form, throwing a rock at him, or leaving him to the goblins' mercy is considered an oathbreaking action for the Ancients' Paladins . At the start of the fight, the two goblin children try to flee and call for assistance. If successful, they draw in the guards outside the doors, Sharp-eye Neem , Sharp-eye Eef , and Sharp-eye Nass , but this does not turn the whole camp hostile. Once the fight is resolved, a surviving Halsin sheds his wildshape, and a dialogue with him starts immediately, progressing the quest ⁠ Save the First Druid and ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin . Otherwise, the Cave Bear corpse reverts to the dead druid, concluding the quest as failed. [ verify ] The wooden chest near the butcher's block at X: 377 Y: -44 contains Beastmaster's Chain amulet and several potions of health of various grades. From one of the wooden barrels nearby some Camp Supplies can be taken. On the adjacent table lay several pieces of Suspicious Meat , which can also be used as food for Long Rests, despite their questionable origin. Among these, a Prison Key which opens the Worg Pens cell can be found, while another can be looted from Plig. In the pen where the worgs were kept, a Worg Fang can be taken from a pile of bones. Prison cell [ edit section | visual editor ] Although most traditionally attitude -reducing crimes in the Goblin Camp trigger all-out hostility, a player character who is instead arrested is ultimately kept here. The cell is located upstairs on the eastern side of the Worg Pens. Under the stairs there is a storeroom where more Camp Supplies and some Potions of Healing can be found. Inside the cell, a Smokepowder Bomb and a Grease Bottle can be taken from the window sill, and another bomb can be obtained from the human-shaped Spider Silk Coccoon hanging up under the ceiling. At X: 416 Y: -44 , a corpse of a dead elf is tucked into a mysterious hole. Pulling it out does not require any skill checks. The corpse can be spoken to via Speak with Dead . The half-cleared mysterious hole can afterwards be destroyed to create a passage back to the Shattered Sanctum . The player character then emerges at X: 346 Y: 14 . It leads to the Worg Pens antechamber, but the exit is hidden behind stone shelves in its far corner. This passage cannot be opened from outside.
