## Baldur's Mouth
- **来源**: [Baldur's Mouth](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Baldur's_Mouth)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Facade of the Baldur's Mouth Lower City Elfsong Tavern ↑ Highberry's Home ← Baldur's Mouth → Nortale's Hostel ↓ Old Jol's Baldur's Mouth is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ A Gazette a day keeps the ignorance away! „ — Luan , hawking the latest edition Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Involvement 2 Building layout 2.1 Entrance 2.2 Newsroom 2.3 Baldur's Mouth Basement 2.4 Rooftop 3 Outside the building 4 Printing blocks 4.1 Positive Articles 4.2 Neutral Articles 4.3 Negative Articles 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Staff, employees and reporters 6.2 News Hawkers 6.3 Guards 6.4 Outside, near the building 7 Related literature 8 External links 9 Footnotes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Baldur's Mouth is a large building in the Eastway district of Baldur's Gate, located west of the Basilisk Gate waypoint. It is a publishing house which main purpose is printing the daily newspaper distributed in the city and its suburbs: the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . Also, Baldur's Mouth produces various posters which can be found hanging around the city. The building has several points of entrance: The main entrance is at X: 66 Y: -52 . On either side of the doors instead of doorplates is a gargoyle face with a scroll of paper hanging out of its mouth. The backdoor on the balcony at X: 39 Y: -52 is accessible by jumping, or by means of spatial movement such as Misty Step or Fly . This entrance is red-outlined, locked (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick or the Key (Inocente Bramm) to open) and guarded. At the south-eastern corner of the roof at X: 65 Y: -63 is a destructible barricade covering a hole. Being red-outlined as well, it lies out of sight of any NPCs. However, this way leads straight to the printing press elevator behind the iron gate, guarded by Guard Vlomina , so some means of invisibility is recommended. Despite its large size, location-wise the building has only a main floor with a large newsroom, a small editor's office and a basement where its printing press stands. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Baldur's Mouth Gazette is the only publication available for the city's residents and guests to keep up with the latest events. Unsurprisingly, it has become a powerful tool for swaying minds of baldurians for Enver Gortash in his pursuit of power over the city. To achieve this, the Archduke nominee won to his side Ettvard Needle , the editor-in-chief of the newsprint. Due to their collusion, in all ways that matter, the gazette covers the city events in favour of Gortash, while the juiciest rumors and gossips are cobbled into prejudiced and one-eyed articles. As the plot goes on, the party might become an object of such slanted opinion on their actions. When they learn about their planned defamation penning, the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses begins. However, the party can not only save their reputation, but use this opportunity to their advantage. Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Entrance [ edit section | visual editor ] The main entrance opens onto a small plaza with a large tree, with Nortale's Hostel lining up to it from the other side. Apart from the publishing house guards, the plaza is observed by two Flaming Fists and a Steel Watcher . Also, there are several loose packs of the gazette copies laying on the surrounding tables. Each contain the latest issue of the gazette (though on interaction it is called "dog-eared"), which changes after every Long Rest . These packs are red-outlined, but the papers inside can be read by the means of stealth or invisibility . Newsroom [ edit section | visual editor ] The newsroom, with its bridge lifted. The entrance to the publishing house opens into a single, large split-level hall, part of which is reserved for the editor's office. The upper part of the hall near entrance, houses an elevator with a locked gate in the south-east corner, which leads to the basement. The elevator is operated with a lever inside the cabin (see the Basement section below). In the middle of the room a bridge has been lifted by chains to the ceiling. The red-outlined lever can lower it, allowing the party to reach the opposite side of the hall, though doing so in plain sight alerts the guards. The lever on the opposite side operates the bridge mechanism as well. Double doors behind the bridge lead to the platform above the western balcony with a ladder to the rooftop. A flight of stairs in the main room leads to the newsroom where employees work on the next issue of the gazette . On a small dais is the editor's desk. The editor-in-chief, Ettvard Needle , is here, pacing around. [ 1 ] Speaking to him starts or progresses ⁠ Stop the Presses . However, if the quest is already underway, conversing with Ettvard results in the party being expelled from the building; the main entrance is locked, becomes red-outlined, and the entire building is considered off-limits for the party. Several desks are scattered across the room, behind them the reporters are working. On the western side is a locked door which leads to a small balcony where a guard stands. Two Steel Watchers monitor the area. Behind Ettvard's desk, under the upper part of the hall, is his locked office. It can be opened with the Silver Key , carried by Ettvard. [ 2 ] . Otherwise, it requires DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. On the table here lies a Key which opens the gate to the elevator. The locked Document Chest at X: 63 Y: -60 can also be opened with the Silver Key or a DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. It holds the Ink-Spattered Key , gold and a random arrow. Two other chests in the office - a Gilded Chest on the lowest shelf across and a Heavy Chest in the opposite corner - are unlocked and contain minor loot. To the south from the editor's office is a guarded stairway to the basement. Around the newsroom are several wicker baskets with papertrash, some of which also contain various printing blocks that can be used throughout the ⁠ Stop the Presses quest. The printing blocks can be used create a positive or negative article about the party, or dwell on neutral themes. The full list of printing blocks, hidden in different corners of the publishing house and sorted by their effect, is provided in the special article section below. Baldur's Mouth Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] The basement can be accessed via either of two routes: A locked metal door leading down a flight of stairs from the newsroom. The door requires DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check or can be opened with the Ink-Spattered Key . The elevator on the ground level of the building, behind the iron grate at X: 66 Y: -61 . The door requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick or the Key . While in the Baldur's Mouth Basement, the party cannot fast-travel or visit Camp , regardless of whether the ⁠ Stop the Presses quest is active. Both means of entry lead to a double corridor, patrolled by two Steel Watchers . Stealthy movement in turn-based mode or any means of invisibility is advised to avoid conflict. [ 3 ] On the northern side of the basement are two rooms filled with old gazette issues and paper rolls for the printing press. In the western room are two more printing blocks needed for the quest (one 'positive' and one 'negative'). On the counter near the door lies the "Broadsheet" - a test issue for tomorrow's paper with slanderous articles about the party. Interacting with this item triggers a dialogue cutscene, where a DC 10 Intelligence Check , if passed, gives a hint that the printing press can be altered. [ 4 ] The eastern room contains a locked Gilded Chest with five pouches, each containing a minor amount of gold – news hawkers' earnings from various city districts. The chest can be lockpicked, or opened with the Baldur's Mouth Chest Key carried by Guard Unilda Tiro in the newsroom. Darkroom where portraits of Gortash are printed On the western side is a darkroom, where new Heroic Portrait of Gortash posters are being printed. Two Silver Ingots and another article block are here. In the corridor across the darkroom, approximately at X: -1021 Y: 1035 a passive Perception check is made, but no item is highlighted. [ 5 ] On the southern side is the largest room with the printing press. Inside are several printing blocks of various regard toward the party. If the the actual press is interacted with, it turns out to be operated by a pixie named Jelliwig , who considers themself a "master pensman" . They can be convinced to change the article block for ⁠ Stop the Presses . All possible interactions with Jelliwig are listed on the quest page. Discovering Jelliwig in the basement of Baldur's Mouth grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Putting the Pen to Paper ( Guild Artisan background) [ verify ] ⁠ Rennaissant Ingenuity ( Sage background) Rigging the news in the party's favour grants the following inspiration: ⁠ A Pressing Heist ( Criminal background) ⁠ Defamed No More ( Noble background) ⁠ Making It Sing to Your Tune ( Entertainer background) ⁠ The News of My Deeds Was Greatly Exaggerated ( Charlatan background) Rooftop [ edit section | visual editor ] The Mouth's rooftop, with the planks over the hole in the covering. The rooftop can be reached from the outer sides of the building: By using series of wooden scaffolds on the southern side of the building at X: 53 Y: -67 . This way requires means of spatial movement such as Misty Step , Fly or Jump . From the platform a few more jumps get to the rooftop. The wooden platform on the western side is much higher, but has a ladder going to the rooftop and double doors leading into the main building, onto the far end of the movable metal bridge inside. However, unlike the first route, a character using this way can be spotted by the publishing house guard standing on the balcony below. On the roof at X: 48 Y: -54 is a loose plank (requires DC 15 Perception Check to spot) holding random potions, two sets of Thieves' Tools and two Trap Disarm Toolkits . The southeastern separate ground has a destructible wooden barricade covering an entrance into the elevator. While it is red-outlined, it remains out of reach of any possible witnesses who might accost the party. Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes around the Baldur's Mouth publishing house. In front of the main entrance, several employees are loading the copies with fresh issue of the newsprint. One of them, Falael , is counting the copies. Helping her or muddling her count earns approval from various companions. Near the plaza a dragonborn doom sayer Augur Harxkellan attracts the attention of a small crowd of bypassers by singing praises to Enver Gortash. After Gortash is defeated, Augur and his listeners disappear, not to be found again. If the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, three more characters: Korrinna Koreena , Flo Hurlburl and 'Gunny' Sacko appear at the plaza. They pester the Flaming Fists trying to learn what is happening from them firsthand. Almost across the entrance to the Elfsong Tavern Saer Manzarde and Frothilda discuss the latest interview with Gortash in the gazette. Both are delighted with the installation of the Steel Watch as the prime city guard and tend to dismiss problems like high taxes and prices. Behind the building, near Old Jol's house, Fist Ernestus tries to placate several citizens outraged by the gazette printing, in their opinion, obvious lies about the state of the city. However, the protesting civilians do nothing more than complain, so the Fist is unable to accuse them of anything illegal. Near the western side of the building Sister Lockhorn and Lolo Fuzzletoes dream aloud of a way to draw the attention of gazette reporters. Another citizen, Sadar Illanov , who constantly walks around the publishing house building, has higher aspirations, and is rehearsing an imaginary interview with Ettvard Needle himself. Printing blocks [ edit section | visual editor ] These blocks are hidden in various containers and on the shelves around the newsroom hall of the building and in the basement, any of which can be used to replace the slanderous article ready for publication, though some can make things even worse. ## Barren's Coop
- **来源**: [Barren's Coop](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Barren's_Coop)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Overview of Barren's Coop Lower City Peartree House ↑ Felogyr's Fireworks ← Barren's Coop → Guildhall Entrance ↓ Vonayn's Home Barren's Coop is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Snowstorms inside the house, blood weeping from the windows <...> I can't risk the neighbourhood just 'cause you were stupid enough to piss off a hag. „ — The eviction notice from the owner of Barren's Coop Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 3 Related locations 4 Related quests 5 Related literature 6 Footnotes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Barren's Coop is a small private building in the Eastway district of the city, located just before the part of the city controlled by the Guild . The owner seems to have been renting the place to other people. The only entrance is at X: 45 Y: -114 . It is locked, but not considered a restricted area. The door requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. The breach in the stone railing across the entrance and knotted roots hanging down allow to descend to the porch of the Vonayn's Home and further to the Heapside Strand beach. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Barren's Coop interior The current state of the place depends on the decisions made by the party in Act One during the ⁠ Save Mayrina quest. If the party saved Mayrina from the hag who tricked her, the building was briefly a place of gathering for the Anti-Hag Support Group , founded and run by Mayrina. However, the owner got fed up with the peculiar consequences of their struggle, and bid them to leave the place. They have found a new shelter in Old Garlow's House . Upon entering the house, a DC 10 Perception Check highlights the Eviction Notice from the building owner. However, the place can still be explored: the wooden chest in the far corner contains a journal with records on various stuff which the group tried to use against hags, and some alchemical ingredients. On the table in the opposite corner among several Anti-Hag Support Group Posters lies a note from one of the group members Kled , revealing their new base of operations. If the ⁠ Help the Hag Survivors quest is not active, reading any of the posters starts it. If the party sided with the hag in Sunlit Wetlands , or never encountered neither her nor Mayrina, there are no documents left by the Anti-Hag Support Group within the house, as well as no eviction notice. The research journal is replaced with a book called Calishem Awaits , in which Adrielle states she could not find enough other hag victims to band together against the hag, so she will try her luck in Calishem . ## Basilisk Gate Barracks
- **来源**: [Basilisk Gate Barracks](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Basilisk_Gate_Barracks)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Basilisk Gate city entrance Lower City Candulhallow's Tombstones ↑ Stormshore Tabernacle ← Basilisk Gate Barracks → Wyrm's Rock Fortress Basilisk Gate Barracks is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I have a city to protect, refugees to manage, and an army on my door - I do not have time to chat. „ — Liara Portyr , commander of the Basilisk Gate checkpoint Contents 1 Overview 2 Barracks layout 2.1 Training grounds 2.2 Barracks office 2.3 Heapside Prison 2.4 Execution grounds 3 Waypoints 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Flaming Fist 6.2 Other 6.3 Near the building 7 Loot 7.1 Secret Stash 7.2 Skittle sells 8 Related literature 8.1 Barracks and Execution grounds 8.2 Heapside Prison 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Basilisk Gate Barracks are situated just north of the Basilisk Gate - the point of first entrance to the Lower City, and the point of changing regions between the Lower City and Wyrm's Rock Fortress after that. The barracks are tucked into the city wall corner, but the wide open ground across it can also be designated as their part, as it is used as a place of executions, featuring a large gallows in the middle. The Basilisk Gate Barracks consists of of the Flaming Fist office with adjacent dormitory and kitchen, the open training ground, and the Heapside Prison located in its basement. A small unnamed bath-house nearby could be considered a part of the complex as well. The barracks are built higher than the average street level, probably to make room for the prison, and thus are reached by climbing up the stone stairs. Also, a wooden stairs outside the barracks wall ends with a side door which opens onto the training grounds. On the wall near the barracks' entrance is the Basilisk Gate Waypoint at X: 134 Y: -38 . Barracks layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Training grounds [ edit section | visual editor ] Inner court of the barracks This is an open space divided from the rest of the city by a stone wall with wooden ramparts atop it. The space around the training area itself is used as a storage. To the east is the entrance to the barracks' office. The place is guarded by several Flaming Fists and a Steel Watcher . Also, any citizens who come to state their concerns wait their turn to do it here. Near the entrance, Fist Murphy is standing on one leg, being punished in such a way for a felony by the barracks' commander Blaze Portyr . Fist Clover , who is patrolling the ramparts, checks on him when passes by, expressing mild compassion. A key , if pickpocketed from her, opens the wooden chest standing in the far end of the ramparts. It keeps several random Uncommon arrows and a bow. In the training area Fist Koltz and Fist Crosse are training hard under the watchful eyes of Gauntlet Thunder . Both receive the Exhausted condition from time to time. Fist Eostre wanders around, charged with counting the supplies and reorganizing them. Several petitioners are waiting to be heard out by the Fist officers. Fist Miller guards the office door and does not stop the party from entering the office. He can be pickpocketed for the Heapside Armoury Key . Interacting with most NPCs here and choosing certain dialogue options can bring small amounts of approval from various companions. The bath-house with its entrance at X: 123 Y: 4 is a part of ⁠ Find Dribbles the Clown quest: it is one of the murderous effigies left by Orin the Red in the city. The door is locked; it requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check [ 1 ] Inside the decapitated body of Gohumberry Tresp can be found. Barracks office [ edit section | visual editor ] The barracks inside consist of several rooms: an office, a small dormitory, and a kitchen where Cook Kameros is toiling. Upon first visiting the office the party see Blaze Portyr, accompanied by Manip Seyama . A woman named Lora tries to get through to the commander to get help with finding her missing daughter. Blaze Portyr, however, behaves herself strangely, speaking off the mark, and a passive DC 15 Arcana Check allows the observer to detect her being enchanted. Offering Lora help starts the quest ⁠ Save Vanra . The door to dormitories is red-outlined, but inside there is nothing significant to explore or loot. Blaze Portyr can be pickpocketed for the Office Storage Key . The door in the northern wall leads down to the Heapside Prison . Heapside Prison [ edit section | visual editor ] Heapside Prison cells area The Heapside Prison is a small (compared to the one in Wyrm's Rock) lockup in the Basilisk Gate Barracks Basement. A Letter addressed to Seyama suggests that it is used mainly for a brief imprisonment of alleged criminals before execution. However, should a party member get caught committing a crime by the Flaming Fist within the Lower City and agree to be arrested, the character in question is transported to a cell within Heapside Prison . [ 2 ] The prison consists of a cells area with a guardroom, and a small office with adjacent armoury. It is guarded by three Flaming Fists and a Steel Watcher, all of which move around the prison in a certain sequence. The guardroom here has a manhole and a pit latrine. Both, if used, transport the party member to the Lower City Sewers and back. [ 3 ] The prison cell where an arrested character is placed provides several options for a break-out. It has a breakable wall section and a hole (requires DC 5 Perception Check to notice), both leading into the guardroom. Also, a breakable barricade behind some crates allow them to move to the neighbouring cell, where Fist Smithwynn stands guard. The Key he keeps in his pocket opens both cells' doors. Inside the prison cell Skittle the rat trader runs around. If spoken via Speak with Animals , he acts as a trader. Among other goods, he sells Counting House Safe nº2 Key . Skittle speaks in rat-themed puns, and the interacting character can keep the conversation in the same style, earning approval from some companions. If the party come to explore the prison from the barracks, Skittle still can be spoken with through the cell grate. The wooden trunk at X: -1280 Y: 765 contains gold, a random gem, random scrolls and three Trap Disarm Toolkit sets - possibly confiscated from a prior prisoner. Another wooden trunk nearby holds two sets of Thieves' Tools . Both containers are red-outlined and guarded by Fist Arrinye . The prison office door is also red-outlined, and any attempt to enter it without means of concealment is stopped by the guards. Inside are two heavy chests containing random arrows and scrolls from Uncommon to Very rare grade. The larger can be opened with DC 18 Sleight of Hand Check , the smaller with DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check . Otherwise, both can be opened with the Office Storage Key , pickpocketed from Liara Portyr. The smaller chest also contains an old, partly censored Crumbling File concerning the Emperor 's activity in the city. Fist Corlos can be pickpocketed for the Barracks Office Key , which opens the outer door to the prison armoury. A copy of this key lies in the cabinet at X: -1286 Y: 782 , but the door leading into it from the office itself is unlocked. The armoury has another unlocked heavy chest behind the iron gate, which can be opened with the Heapside Armoury Key or with a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check . Inside are several health potions of various grades. The weapon stands here keep several Uncommon weapons with a +1 enchantment . Office desks contain documents concerning the criminal situation in the city, including Counsellor Florrick 's death sentence signed by the tadpoled Duke Ravengard . However, even if the ⁠ Free Counsellor Florrick quest is in progress, reading this document does not progress it. Execution grounds [ edit section | visual editor ] The focal point of this open space is a large gallows guarded by the executioner Fist 'Edge' Arensen . Talking to him reveals the biased authorities' view on the crime and punishment in the city, and may earn a small amount of approval from party members. If the ⁠ Free Counsellor Florrick quest has not been started yet, reading the Execution Notice pinned to the gallows' platform starts it. If the quest is already in progress, Arensen can let slip some information on her whereabouts. If Florrick is not saved during the quest, her body remains on the gallows for several Long Rests, guarded by extra Fists, Anderson and Williams . [ 4 ] Also, from time to time the bodies of other executed people appear hanging in the nooses. Several pillories near the waypoint, seemingly an alternative detention for culprits, are always empty. Near the gallows Estra Stir , a reporter of Baldur's Mouth Gazette , can start the quest ⁠ Stop the Presses . It is a time-sensitive quest which has the length of a single long rest. Its outcome directly influences the attitude of the various citizens towards the party throughout the Lower City, and also can affect the prices of certain traders around it. There are also several minor NPC vignettes around Basilisk Gate Barracks. Near the gate Fist Kuthbert declares the new order on all the citizens' livestock to be turned over into the authorities' hands. Several citizen are protesting against it, but Kuthbert, who guards the cages with already confiscated animals, pays them with trivialities. Behind the gallows three dwarves - Hasmet Hudd , Giftu Hudd and Dryfle Doon are discussing their plans after they have finally reached the Lower City. They celebrate being in security from the marching armies at last. News Hawker Luan is crying out the gazette slogans, attracting the customers. ## Beehive General Goods
- **来源**: [Beehive General Goods](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Beehive_General_Goods)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Street view of the Beehive General Goods. Lower City Lora's House ↑ Beehive General Goods → Flymm's Cobblers ↓ Old Garlow's Place Beehive General Goods is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Got grub, potions, a few nice vintages. Best stock up now before someone clears me out to fill their larder. „ — Oliver Tefoco , welcoming a customer Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 3 Tefoco's Home 4 Basement 5 Outside the building 6 Characters 7 Loot 8 Related Literature 9 External links 10 Footnotes and References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Beehive General Goods occupies the first floor of the three-storied building in the Steeps district of Baldur's Gate, with the main entrance at X: -76 Y: -112 and a back door at X: -71 Y: -121 . The upper stories serve as living space for the owner and merchant Oliver Tefoco and his family. The building has a basement as well, accessible via a locked hatch on the first floor. It is also connected to the neighbouring Rainforest's Home , with a small alley between the ground levels leading to the Old Garlow's Place and further to the Counting House entrance. The upper floors have their own location name "Tefoco's Home" (see below) and are also accessible through the door at X: -72 Y: -106 on a narrow bridge leading to it from Lora's Home and the Crimson Draughts . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] In Beehive General Goods the party can stock up with Camp Supplies , various potions and alchemical ingredients of herbal derivation. On the store counter stands a locked gilded chest (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick), containing gold and several Rare potions. Oliver can also be pickpocketed for all sellable goods, and for the Counting House Safe nº7 Key as well. [ 1 ] Under the stairs which lead to the upper floors is a locked hatch to the basement (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick). Both the gilded chest and the hatch are red-outlined. Tefoco's Home [ edit section | visual editor ] View of the upper stores of the building This is the living space of Oliver Tefoco's family. It is connected to the general store via a series of stairs and can also be entered through a small bridge from the opposite side of the street. According to the numerous books and letters scattered around the house, Tefoco and his spouse Kroyce have nine children and a granddaughter. None of them, though, are present in the city: the elder daughter is married and lives separately, three elder sons joined the Flaming Fist , two more became guards in the trading caravan, and Oliver's wife with the lesser kids fled the city to Beregost for safety from the threat of the Absolute . The door to the upper stories is locked and red-outlined. It can be opened with the DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check or with the key pickpocketed from Oliver Tefoco. Through the door the party gets access to the third floor of the building. Inside, a rosewood desk holds Tefoco's Hatch Key , and in the bottle rack near the stove is Tefoco's Basement Chest Key . In a locked wooden chest is some gold, a set of Thieves' Tools and a letter from Oliver's wife. The second store has nothing significant except another letter, this time from Oliver's sons who left the city as caravan guards. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] The basement of the Beehive General Goods features multiple shelves, containers and burlap sacks with fresh Camp Supplies and alchemical ingredients. [ 2 ] The upper shelf at X: -1952 Y: 620 contains random potions as well. There are several hidden containers here. A safe hidden behind the "Landscape" painting on the wall can be unlocked by using Tefoco's Basement Chest Key . It contains a wedding ring and a scroll of Hold Monster spell. At X: -1957 Y: 620 is a breakable Sturdy wall. An unlocked wooden chest is hidden behind, with a Blast Mine in front of it. Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes placed around Beehive General Goods. At X: -64 Y: -98 , under the bridge from Tefoco's Home door to Crimson Draughts two news hawkers, Pharnilla and Dellys , argue about their rights for having a break. They are "having a break" whenever the party approaches them. Behind the store two citizens, Pompton Norvath and Delyarna , discuss the strange company which occupied "the Albright place" after it was abandoned. Cressida Flint is constantly doing rounds from the Beehive General Goods and as far as Flymm's Cobblers . She praises aloud Enver Gortash and his governing style, though it appears most her opinions come from Baldur's Mouth Gazette articles. ## Bhaal Temple
- **来源**: [Bhaal Temple](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bhaal_Temple)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Altar at the centre of Bhaal Temple (by Martijn Petersen) Undercity Undercity Ruins ← Bhaal Temple The Bhaal Temple is a Location within the Undercity in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Gods, who knew such a vile abcess lurked in the bedrock of the city. The very stone reeks of misery and despair. „ — Gale , upon entering the temple Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 2 Temple layout 2.1 Outer perch 2.2 Altar ground 2.3 The Chosen's Room 3 Involvement 3.1 The Rescue 3.2 Fighting Orin 3.3 The Dark Urge 4 Waypoints 5 Related locations 6 Related quests 7 Achievements 8 Characters 8.1 Notable 8.2 Abducted companions / camp followers 8.3 Cult of Bhaal followers 8.4 Orin's victims 9 Related literature 10 Gallery 11 Notes and references 12 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The entrance to the Bhaal Temple. [ 1 ] Bhaal Temple is located deep under the city of Baldur's Gate, in the northeastern part of the Undercity Ruins . As such, it is accessible only through the Lower City Sewers and past the ruins itself. The temple is the innermost sanctum to the followers of the Cult of Bhaal . Though the cult has been destroyed in the past, [ 2 ] the temple's subterranean cavernous halls remain functionally intact. The temple was preserved by the efforts of Sarevok Anchev and the ghostly members of the Murder Tribunal [ 3 ] and now serves as a home base for the cult risen from its slumber. Currently the Cult of Bhaal is headed by Orin the Red . However, for the most time in the temple's recent history she had been only the second-in-command. Orin became the acknowledged leader of the cult after a treachery committed against the true Bhaal's Chosen - the Dark Urge . Thus, the events unfolding in the temple serve a culmination point in the story of this unique game origin . Access [ edit section | visual editor ] A large stone door prevents access to the temple and can only be opened with the Amulet of Bhaal , which can be acquired at the end of the quest ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal : as a reward for earning the title of the Unholy Assassin, granted from Sarevok Anchev , or looted from him, should the party confront the Murder Tribunal. The Dark Urge can enter the temple without the Amulet, as their butler Sceleritas Fel opens the door for them. When the doors to the temple are unsealed, one or more of the following inspirations is granted: ⁠ Forgotten, Bloodied, Halls ( Acolyte backgrounds) ⁠ Homecoming ( Haunted One backgrounds) ⁠ The Face of Evil ( Outlander backgrounds) While inside the temple the party cannot fast travel or go to camp . Temple layout [ edit section | visual editor ] The large effigy of Bhaal, which reinforces Orin during the fight (by Frédérick Senesael) The temple grounds consist of the outer perch with several alcoves along it. From the perch, three wide stairs lead down to the centre, where is the round platform with an altar in the middle (one of the stairs is destroyed). On the cavern wall above the altar a colossal bas-relief depiction of Bhaal's symbol is chiselled in stone. It takes a special part in the party's confrontation with Orin (see Involvement section). Another stone stairway from the altar leads down and into the archway beneath the symbol. Following it, the party can reach the Chosen's Room – the private chambers of the cult leader. Outer perch [ edit section | visual editor ] The Bhaal Temple consists of a large main area with a forked higher ground. This surrounds a lower situated platform upon which the Altar of Bhaal rests. The upper area has alcoves with bodies on display. The alcoves located in the northwestern corner at X: 35 Y: 1035 and the one in the southwestern corner at X: 35 Y: 976 both potentially contain up to two corpses of characters who Orin impersonated in Rivington during the current playthrough. Her potential victims are: Dying Stone Lord Thug Dorghan [ 4 ] Fist Rowan Gyldro Angleiron the Smith Lens the Journalist Zethino [ verify ] One of the alcoves on the upper level. On the right the 'library' can be seen. On the northern side around X: 43 Y: 1032 is a stack of scrolls with a plaque leaned against which calls it "A Lending Library" . Interacting with it prompts a comment from the Narrator. The stack contains only one item, The Ecstasy of Murder . One more alcove behind the library contains the skeleton of Manip Antyra Thorpe , executed by the cult for interfering in their activity in the city. In the northernmost side of the perch at X: 75 Y: 1032 is a hidden passageway which allows access to the Chosen's Room without going through the altar (and the potential fight). This allows the party to explore Orin's chambers before confronting her, giving additional options in that dialogue. Descending either of the extant stairways brings the party to the altar of Bhaal. Altar ground [ edit section | visual editor ] Situated at X: 59 Y: 1007 , the altar of Bhaal is at the center of the platform where Orin and her retinue of several cultists are waiting for the party to arrive. Orin's victim – if there is one –} is chained to the altar. The Altar itself can be opened using the Altar Key carried by Orin, lockpicked with a DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check , or opened with Knock . The main events concerning the ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone , ⁠ Rescue Orin's Victim and ⁠ The Urge unfold around the altar. Here the party must confront Orin and her allies, which inevitably leads to a fight. The layout of the initial dialogue with the Orin and of the resulting conflict depends on several conditions: Whether the player character is the Dark Urge Whether the party promised Orin to kill Enver Gortash first and whether they kept their promise Whether the party managed to find out the proof of Orin's incestous lineage while exploring the Murder Tribunal chambers or the temple itself Whether the party managed to free the victim unnoticed by Orin Further details on the consequences of each of these decisions are described in the Involvement section. The Chosen's Room [ edit section | visual editor ] The Chosen's Room in the back of the temple (by Martijn Petersen) A stairway behind the altar leads to the Chosen's Room, which serves as Orin's private quarters. It can alternatively be entered from the north side of the upper area, avoiding the altar, the entrance is around X: 75 Y: 1032 . Three cultists guarding the room pay no attention if the party explore it, even if they ferret about Orin's chest or interrogate corpses nearby. [ 5 ] In the northern part of the room is Orin's office with a desk, wardrobe, and an elaborated display case behind the desk. On the desk is Orin's Chest Key and a book containing Orin's vows to glorify Bhaal's cult. In the display case is the mummified corpse of Orin's mother Helena Anchev . It lacks one hand, which may possibly have born the idea of the ritual trophies taken from the cultists' victims. [ 6 ] The party can commune her via Speak with Dead to gain additional background information on Orin's childhood. The facts concerning Sarevok's part in orchestrating it can later be used to convince Orin to free her abducted victim. At the far end of the room is a bed. To one side of is the dead body of an imp-like creature named Cruor . The book laying aside it explains this creature played the same role to Orin as Sceleritas Fel plays to the Dark Urge, and relates of Orin's attempts to rid herself of the creature. If the Dark Urge was not picked as origin, a dead body of a white Dragonborn lies to the other side of the bed in a ritual circle. The circle is drawn in blood and mirrors the one which the Dark Urge (if played) uses to sacrifice Alfira in the campsite. Upon interacting with the body, any party member comments on its horrendous death. If the player character is the Dark Urge, there is no body and no circle, implying they are the same character. Next to the bed is a locked Wooden Chest which can be opened with Orin's Chest Key . It contains a skull and two random coatings from Uncommon to Very rare quality. The wardrobes contain several pieces of common jewelry. Several documents around the room concern Orin's and the Dark Urge's clash of opinions on proper worshipping Bhaal. A vase near Helena's body contains a note from Sceleritas Fel. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Bhaal Temple serves as base of operations for the followers of the Cult of Bhaal and their leader Orin the Red. It is the place where ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone and its sub-quest ⁠ Rescue Orin's Victim are resolved. A pivotal decision must be made for the Dark Urge in regards to their personal quest ⁠ The Urge . Whether or not the Dark Urge is picked also influences the way the other two quests are resolved. In the center of the temple lies the kidnapped victim of Orin, chained to the altar. Orin wanders around, bantering with the closest cultists. Her retinue consists of a Death's Head of Bhaal , an Invoker of Bhaal , and six Reapers of Bhaal . The Rescue [ edit section | visual editor ] The player character has several options to secure the abductee's life when they approach the altar: Succeeding a DC 25 Deception , Intimidation , or Persuasion Check during the initial conversation with Orin Distracting Orin from killing the victim by revealing her true lineage. Convincing her requires a DC 25 Deception , Persuasion , or Religion Check and information learned from A page from Sarevok's book and / or by speaking with the corpse of Helena Anchev in Orin's private chambers. Unlocking the victim's bindings (regardless of the way) while approaching the altar stealthily or using invisibility Beginning a combat with Orin by attacking her or any member of her retinue If the interacting player character chooses the dialogue options "Go ahead. I won't stop you." or "His/her fate is of no interest to me" , or fails any check, or (as the Dark Urge) refuses to duel, Orin immediately murders her hostage. If the abducted victim is a companion , and they are executed by Orin or die in the subsequent fight, they cannot be revived afterwards by any means, including Withers' resurrecting powers, and their personal quest (if active) is completed. If the victim is freed before or during the combat, they join the fight as a controllable ally (with available attacks and class actions but without access to the personal inventory). If they survive, they prompt a dialogue afterwards with the player character and leave for camp . Deceiving Orin about killing Gortash when the party did not do so is one of the possible opportunities to gain the ⁠ Always Trust a Dishonest Person inspiration for characters with the Charlatan background, if it was not earned earlier. [ 7 ] Fighting Orin [ edit section | visual editor ] Eventually, Bhaal claims Orin's body to confront the party See also: Orin/Combat As mentioned, fight with Orin occurs regardless of whether the Dark Urge is picked as origin or not. However, the layout of the battle depends on whether the Dark Urge is chosen as origin, and also on whether the party initiates the dialogue or attacks Orin and / or members of her retinue from afar. If the Dark Urge is not played as origin, Orin calls on Bhaal's power to transform into the Slayer and attacks (she may do so anyway depending on dialogue choices). If the party attacks first, Orin turns into a Slayer on her first turn. If the player character is the Dark Urge and acquired the Slayer form themselves before Act Three, they are given the option to transform into it during their dialogue with Orin before their duel, in which case she fights against them in her native humanoid form. If Orin does not duel with the Urge, there is a unique component to the battle. When the battle begins, the Reapers of Bhaal begin chanting a prayer to Bhaal, which activates the the Boon of Bhaal from the bas-relief effigy above the altar. At the end of the turn, it casts its spell, Boon of the Unstoppable , which renews Orin's Unstoppable condition up to full stack (7 charges on Explorer and Balanced difficulty levels, 12 on Tactician and above). This continues for as long as the cultists are chanting. The cultists start the battle with Sanctuary , but still can be disrupted by conditions such as Prone , Silenced , Hypnotised , Fearful , or Stunned , or killed with various area-of-effect. [ 8 ] None of the other cultists in the temple participate in the combat unless they are attacked directly. However, their reactions if spoken to differ depending on whether the interacting party member is not the Dark Urge, and – in the case of the Dark Urge – whether they reject or accept their legacy. Killing Orin grants one or both of the following inspirations: ⁠ Putting the Past to Rest ( Soldier backgrounds) ⁠ Securing Your Line ( Haunted One backgrounds) The quest ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone resolves upon looting Orin's Netherstone from her corpse. Although the player character loots Netherstone-Pommelled Bloodthirst from Orin's remains, it immediately separates into two components in the player character's inventory. The Dark Urge [ edit section | visual editor ] Before the duel, Orin tries to unsettle her Bhaalspawn rival, mirroring their form If the player character is the Dark Urge, Orin challenges them for a duel. To rile them up, she shapeshifts into their form and mocks them, revealing her treachery of ambushing them in the Mind Flayer Colony , mutilating and infecting them with a tadpole. If the Dark Urge is picked, Orin challenges them to one-on-one duel, with none of their comrades interfering per the Bhaalist tradition. If the Dark Urge refuses to duel, the party must then fight the standard version of the boss encounter. Following the battle, the story proceeds as if the Dark Urge had lost the face-to-face fight. If the Dark Urge accepts the challenge, at the beginning of the fight a visible cautionary ring arises around the altar, . If another party member passes it, the duel is cancelled and the battle continues as normal with the participation of the sanctuaried Reapers of Bhaal as well as the Boon of Bhaal . Additionally, if another party member passes the ring before either of the combatants is defeated, the battle continues after one is, as a regular boss fight. After defeating Orin, Sceleritas Fel appears at the altar platform, praises the Dark Urge and then is killed as several blades protrude from inside his body. His reflection in the pool of blood speaks to the Dark Urge as the Avatar of Bhaal. This serves as the event horizon for the Dark Urge's personal quest where they may restore themselves as Bhaals's Chosen, or refuse the title. If the Urge refuses to become Bhaal's chosen they are drained of their father's blood and essence and die immediately. However, they are soon brought back from death by Withers , who personally appears at the altar to revive them. He explains that Bhaal killed only the part of his wayward child known to him, while the rest can still be restored. Reborn anew, the player character is free of their Urge, and their ⁠ personal quest is complete. They lose access the Slayer form if they had previously obtained it in Act Two . If denied, Bhaal takes back all power he has bestowed onto his wayward spawn If the Dark Urge accepts their Bhaalspawn legacy, they are instead tasked to control the Netherbrain in the name of Bhaal, and gain access to the Slayer form if they did not already. Taking the ultimate decision concerning their legacy grants the Dark Urge one of the following mutually exclusive inspirations: ⁠ Bhaalspawn No More ( Haunted One backgrounds) ⁠ Return of the Bhaalspawn ( Haunted One backgrounds) Also, accepting Bhaal's gift and blessings is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of any Oath subclass , if they are the Dark Urge themselves. If the Dark Urge embraces their Bhaalspawn legacy while inside the temple, upon leaving it the party is confronted by Jaheira and Minsc , who appear on the bridge to the entrance, accompanied by a small squad of Harpers . Defeating Jaheira at this point grants the Dark Urge characters the ⁠ Forced Retirement inspiration as well. ## Bloomridge Park
- **来源**: [Bloomridge Park](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bloomridge_Park)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

View on Bloomridge Park from the Szarr Palace ramparts Lower City Facemaker's Boutique ← Bloomridge Park → Lavernica's Home ↓ The Blushing Mermaid Bloomridge Park is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I always loved this park. Spent a lot of time here as a boy battling imaginary monsters. „ — Wyll Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 2 Involvement 2.1 Bhaalists' Ambush 2.2 Encounters in the park 3 Characters 3.1 Civilians 3.2 Cultists 3.3 Flaming Fists 4 Loot 4.1 Hidden treasure 5 Related literature 6 Notes 7 External links 8 Footnotes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Bloomridge Park is a large community landscape located in the northern part of the Lower City . [ 1 ] It occupies vast territory between Facemaker's Boutique , Lower City Central Wall and The Blushing Mermaid . The park is tended by groundkeeper Lavernica and, according to her notes, is opened only in the daytime and closed throughout the night. It seems to be a beloved place of citizens' leisure, judging by several picnic spots which are scattered on its grounds. In the north-west corner of the park is a small natural pond with sandy shores, seemingly a part of the half-underground stream running along the border between the Lower City and the Upper City . This stream also feeds a small artificial waterfall in the north-east corner of the park. The paved part of the park is constantly patrolled by several Flaming Fists . Access [ edit section | visual editor ] There are four possible points of entrance to the park: The main entrance at X: -130 Y: 52 A side gate near the groundkeeper's house at X: -91 Y: -65 A wall breach behind The Blushing Mermaid at X: -107 Y: -71 A broken fence section near the Facemaker's Boutique at X: -167 Y: -21 Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Bhaalists' Ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] The park patrol is initially led by Manip Edenosa . In the park depths near the fountain, a group of Bhaal followers have laid an ambush . Edenosa is a follower of the Absolute and, if spoken to, recognizes the party as fellow True Souls . She is fully aware of the cultists hiding in the park, but she believes them to be warriors of the Absolute and does not know the true goal of the ambush. As the party approach the place of the ambush, two can be seen arguing near the waterfall pool in plain sight; all members roll a passive DC 10 Perception Check to detect the other hiding cultists: three Night Blades , a Reaper of Bhaal and two Death's Heads of Bhaal . This check is rolled regardless of whether the party spoke to Edenosa prior. Further course of interaction with the Bhaalists depends on whether the party have already bargained with Orin the Red or with Gortash against the other one. [ verify ] If the party agreed to ally with Orin, one of the ambushing cultists offer them to join the slaughter they are planning to start. The party can agree or decline; the latter choice start a fight with them. Otherwise, the Bhaalists kill as many civilians as they can and flee; the Flaming Fist do not stand up against them. If the party declined Orin's proposition of alliance or have not yet a chance to bargain with her, they become the cultists' target along with the civilians around (civilians remain the prime target). In this case, the Flaming Fist join the fight as neutrals. If any member of the party passed the Perception check, they can also sneak behind the revealed Bhaalists, climbing up the flowerbeds approximately at X: -135 Y: -5 or the stairs at X: -86 Y: -40 . Attacking the cultists first wins a surprise round. Surviving the fight against the Bhaalists grants the ⁠ Urban Jungle inspiration to the characters with the Outlander background. If a fight occurs, Manip Edenosa approaches the party after it ends. She chokes on words and behaves strangely. Throughout the conversation it becomes clear that her mind is possessed by the elder brain , which also makes advances towards the party, asking to help it break free from the Crown of Karsus . The manip's brain then collapses from the overstrain, and she dies. If Edenosa dies in the fight, Fist Griff takes her place. [ 2 ] If the party let the cultists act and flee, the dialogue with Edenosa is not triggered. Encounters in the park [ edit section | visual editor ] There are multiple NPC vignettes placed all around the Bloomridge park grounds and nearby. On the paved ground Albert is trying to take his dog Sparky home. Sparky is an excitable dog who can be convinced to return to his master. He moves quickly, so interacting with him may require using Turn-based mode. During the cultists attack Albert runs away, but Sparky may be killed. Near the statue of Balduran in the centre of the park Eugenie Kenridge and Wendel Ashgrove are having a date. In case of a fight, either or both usually become the first victims. At a table at the far end of the park sit four retired Flaming Fists - Eldaernth , Avourel , Thokki and Vistra - discussing current events and their past service. Near the side entrance to the park a group of book lovers - Caerdwyn , Kepli and Morgan - share opinions about the latest novel they read. Two children, Conall and Emen have come to the park to play. However, Conall has thrown their ball too far, and both are arguing on who must bring it back. The ball lies at the waterfall pool, but there is no interaction to give it to the boys and approaching the pool triggers the ambush cutscene. An elderly citizen couple, Bertram and Martina Kostaka , have come to the park for an everyday walk. Martina from time to time begs Bertram to return home, but he persists. As their route regularly comes close to the ambush, both may become the victims of the assault. Behind the park fence Druggag and Larca Mena are discussing a family of ten refugees from Elturel whom Druggag has recently sheltered in his house. After the encounter with the Bhaalists is resolved and the party have at least one Long Rest, the set of NPCs inside the park changes. New Flaming Fist patrol, reinforced with a Steel Watcher , appear: Fist Brottor , Fist Elda , Fist Moss and Fist Ulinn Near the waterfall, three children discuss the Bhaalist's attack. Cyrella claims her elder brother bested all the assailants alone, and while Tam and Skip barely believe her, they are eager to hear all the juicy details. There is no option to interact with these three. All are red-outlined; a single locked one requires DC 7 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. [ 6 ] Around the park grounds, near the waterfall and the pond multiple alchemical ingredients of herbal and fungal derivation can be picked up freely. Camp Supplies left on the picnic blankets are, however, red-outlined; picking them up is considered a crime. At X: -130 Y: -20 - requires DC 20 Survival Check to find. Inside is gold, a random potion and a random Very rare spell scroll. ## Bonecloak's Apothecary
- **来源**: [Bonecloak's Apothecary](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bonecloak's_Apothecary)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Front view of Bonecloak's Apothecary Lower City Devil's Fee ↑ Bloomridge Park ← Bonecloak's Apothecary → Highberry's Home ↓ Stormshore Armoury Bonecloak's Apothecary is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Bonecloak's. Get what you can before we have to shutter the place. „ — Derryth Bonecloak , if returned from the Underdark without noblestalk Contents 1 Overview 2 Apothecary layout 2.1 Ground Level 2.2 First floor 2.3 Basement 3 Outside the apothecary 4 Characters 4.1 Outside, near the building 5 Loot 5.1 Store 5.2 Basement 6 Related Literature 7 External links 8 Footnotes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Bonecloak Apothecary is a large apothecary which lines up the central square of the lower City together with Sorcerous Sundries and the Lower City Central Wall. It is a two-storied building with a basement and a greenhouse added to the western side. The apothecary is owned and run by a dwarven couple, Derryth and Baelen Bonecloak . Both can be first met in Act One in the Underdark , in the Myconid Colony . They went to the underdark hoping to gather some Noblestalk - a precious and valued type of mushroom. The state of their apothecary in Act Three directly depends on the fate of both Bonecloaks. If both Baelen and Derryth die in the Underdark in Act One, or if Derryth dies and Baelen is not rescued, the Bonecloak's Apothecary is closed, with a simple note left out front that says "Gone shroom hunting" . If Derryth and / or Baelen survived, they can be found in the apothecary. In this case, the default trader is Derryth, unless Baelen survived and consumed the Noblestalk. Either way, the party can stock up with potions and various alchemical ingredients . If the party picked up the Noblestalk and gave it to Derryth, she sells three pieces of it as well. Unlike the one found in the Underdark, these Noblestalk cannot be used by Shadowheart or Dark Urge to restore memories. Apothecary layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground Level [ edit section | visual editor ] The interior of Bonecloak's Apothecary The ground floor of the apothecary consists of a store and greenhouse. In the store, some common herbs can be freely taken. On a bookcase shelf at X: -20 Y: -33 lies the Bonecloak Apothecary's Chest Key . On the western side is a stairway to the first floor. If the party walk behind the counter and further to the west, they find the greenhouse. There, several herbal alchemical ingredients can be found and freely taken. In the middle is a red-outlined locked hatch to the basement ( DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick). Behind the wooden screen dividing the store from the path to the greenhouse stands a locked wooden chest ( DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check as well). Inside are several non-herbal alchemical ingredients. If Derryth returned from the Underdark without Baelen, she expresses her loneliness to the party. However, they can help her with this. There are three cats in different corners of the central square and around: Barsik , Malta , and Myshka . Each of them can be convinced to accompany Derryth via various skill checks. If convinced, the chosen cat resides in the apothecary afterwards. First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The first floor has a small bedroom which can be reached at the end of the hall. It contains no remarkable items except for Derryth's Journal , the contents of which depends on the fate of Derryth and Baelen, and an unsent letter from Derryth to her former suitor. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] The basement can be accessed through a locked hatch in the greenhouse. It has two rooms with multiple containers, which may contain alchemical ingredients of herbal and / or fungal derivation. In the second room is a locked Heavy Chest, which contains the Counting House Safe nº3 Key . It can be opened with a DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check or a certain key (see below). On the western wall is a notice that reads " Preparing brews. Feck off ", and several crates at X: 1453 Y: 843 which partially conceal a lever. Using the lever lowers the wall to provide entrance to the apothecary's underground laboratory. The lab contains more alchemical ingredients stored in crates and sacks, as well as an Elixir of Psychic Resistance and a Potion of Speed . Several Bibberbang are scattered throughout the room. At X: 1442 Y: 842 is a wooden chest which can be opened with a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check or with the first apothecary key from the bookshelf upstairs. Down the path at X: 1412 Y: 843 in a bottle rack lies the second apothecary key [ 1 ] which opens aforementioned heavy chest. Journals and notes left on workbenches shed some light onto Baelen's mind disease and his desperate attempts to cure it while he still could think clear. Outside the apothecary [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes around the Bonecloak's Apothecary. At X:  Y:  a Flaming Fist patrol consisting of Elthira Gossen , Fist Aggralix , Fist Karoline , and a Steel Watcher have detained and are questioning Drongo Bixworth and Florean Bixworth , accusing both of being the agents of the Absolute . If the Steel Watch is disabled, both the Flaming Fist and the detained civilians disappear, and their place is taken by Hyrla Sname and Peetri Sname , who are gawking at the broken automaton. Just across the apothecary entrance News Hawker Jason attracts the customers. Another trader, a gnome named Mohan , stands modestly near the greenhouse windows. Mohan sells various scrolls and coatings, and sets of Thieves' Tools as well. A brass dragonborn Pritt Yellowbreath walks around the apothecary building, ranting aloud about the contents of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . She is severely vexed at the paper's editors as they recently stopped printing puzzles. ## Bruc and Pishe's Emporium
- **来源**: [Bruc and Pishe's Emporium](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bruc_and_Pishe's_Emporium)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Front view of Bruc and Pishe's Emporium Lower City Guildhall Entrance ↑ Barren's Coop ← Bruc and Pishe's Emporium ↓ Vonayn's Home Bruc and Pishe's Emporium is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . Contents 1 Overview 2 Building layout 2.1 Ground floor 2.2 Basement 3 Outside the building 4 Related locations 5 Related Quests 6 Characters 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Bruc and Pishe's Emporium is a small building, one in the labyrinth of narrow alleys of the Brampton district of Baldur's Gate. It has one storey and a large basement hidden in the rocky cliff above the Vonayn's Home and the sandy beach beneath. The only entrance to it is across the Guildhall Entrance at X: 56 Y: -104 . It is locked (requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick), but breaking in is not considered a crime. On the old plaque near the entrance the former name of the establishment can be read: "Tina Turki's Good Time Bazaar" . The building is being used by the Guild as a storage area and a postal address for the correspondence, and its basement – as a makeshift office. Outside a ladder on the eastern side of the building leads to the roof. A patch of knotted roots can be used to climb on the roof to go one level higher, although nothing of interest is there. Behind the building is a winch with the elevator hanging over a half-flooded cavern mouth. Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground floor [ edit section | visual editor ] On the ground floor various miscellanous items are scattered around, as well as several letters addressed to the Guild concerning debts and services' offers. In a locked chest (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick) are Thieves' Tools (up to three sets) and / or Trap Disarm Toolkit , and the Guild Ring . None of items or containers inside is red-outlined. The Guild Ring can be used to enter the Guildhall : inserting it into the interactable wall slot at X: 59 Y: -97 reveals the entrance. Around the room are three named pouches, containing small amounts of gold. One of them holds the Patriar's Letter . Their owners are in the alley behind the building (see below). At the far end of the room a locked hatch leads to the basement. The lock requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] Bruc and Pishe's Emporium basement interior The main room of the basement is a makeshift office for the current Guild operations. On a large table here are various reports from minor gangs. According to these letters, the situation in the Guild's campaign against the Stone Lord looks dire. Containers around the basement may contain Camp Supplies , alchemical ingredients and useful items like Trap Disarm Toolkits or high-grade health potions. On the cupboard in the corner lies a copy of the File Under Diabolist (another one is in the Guildhall). This document hints on Helsik as a person who can provide passage into the Nine Hells. This information (if not obtained prior) updates all quests corcerning the party's dealings with Raphael and freeing Prince Orpheus . The southwest part of the room is used as storage. At its opposite ends two DC 15 Perception Checks reveal a trapped movable wall and a pressure plate. Removing the weight from the plate opens a hidden door on the east wall, behind it is a trapped chest ( DC 15 Perception Check to detect a trap, DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to disarm) which contains another Guild Ring , random spell scrolls and / or alchemical ingredients. Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] The alley along the Bruc and Pishe's Emporium and its roof is guarded by several Guild thugs. One of them, the half-orc Tusgront , initiates a dialogue when the party approach him for the first time (provided that they have not been in the Guildhall via the other way, through the Lower City Sewers ). All options to pass Tusgront by are listed on the location page. Behind the house are three burned corpses, on the ground – all members of various patriar families of Baldur's Gate. Three pouches inside the building belonged to them. Flaev Linnacker ( Flaev Linnacker on the Forgotten Realms Wiki ) Malghar Caldwel ( Malghar Caldwel on the Forgotten Realms Wiki ) Ulis Oberon ( Ulis Oberon on the Forgotten Realms Wiki ) On a crate nearby lies a Parchment from Mystic Carrion , addressed to one of the ill-fated patriars. It gives the passphrase which opens the door to the Philgrave's Mansion , if the party has no clues on it yet. Across the entrance to the Bruc and Pishe's Emporium is a ruined building, where the ground level is actually the Guildhall Entrance . Above it, on the intact porch is a mailbox with the Counting House Safe nº8 Key inside. ## Candulhallow's Tombstones
- **来源**: [Candulhallow's Tombstones](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Candulhallow's_Tombstones)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Candulhallows Tombstones entrance in the allew behind the Elfsong Tavern Lower City Graveyard (Lower City) ← Candulhallow's Tombstones ↓ Elfsong Tavern Candulhallow's Tombstones is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ There's just the occasional customer who enters and then stays inside for a while, sometimes for hours. <...> I'd swear I saw one go in and out in the same clothes but leave wearing a different face. „ — Alexander Rainforest 's observation notes concerning the building Contents 1 Overview 2 Building layout 3 Involvement 3.1 Candulhallow's Basement 4 Outside the building 5 Related locations 6 Related quests 7 Characters 7.1 Outside the building 8 Related literature 9 Bugs 10 Notes and references 11 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Candulhallow's Tombstones is a small trade establishment on the fringes of the Eastway district of Baldur's Gate. It is located on an alley behind the Elfsong Tavern , with the entrance at X: 74 Y: 25 . The building has one storey and a basement. The establishment trades in funeral services and respective goods and is conveniently set nearby the city graveyard . Although it may have been a legitimate business in the past, its current ownership and sources of maintenance are questionable. Despite the unknown fate of the last proprietor after her detention, all due municipal payments have since been made on time. [ 1 ] These pecularities drew attention of the city ombudsman Alexander Rainforest , which eventually cost him his life. In truth, the grim metier of Candulhallow's Tombstones has a compelling ground: the shop is a front for the Cult of Bhaal activity within the city of Baldur's Gate. In particular, it hides the Murder Tribunal – the entry point for any murderer who aspires to earn the title of Unholy Assassin. Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Candulhallow's Tombstone shop interior The entrance to the building is locked. It can be lockpicked (requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check ), or opened with a key . Copies of this key are carried by the would-be Unholy Assassin Dolor , and by members of doppelgangers' groups who assist him in Lower City . [ 2 ] The interior of the shop is a series of three small rooms with numerous stellages. On the shelves are caskets, coffins and tombstones offered for sale. Some tombstones already have names and epitaphs chiselled on their surfaces, directly naming or containing clear hints to Dolor's victims, as listed in the Bloodstained Parchment – including the murders which may have been prevented by the party. [ 3 ] Some caskets might contain common weapons or fresh Camp Supplies . In the last room a DC 25 Perception Check highlights the "Butterfly on Skull" painting at X: 87 Y: 15 . Behind the painting a button is hidden. If no party member passes the check, the scroll on the desk nearby can give a hint for the next actions. Another hint is hidden amongst the lines of the document carried by Dolor. [ 4 ] Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The painting that hides the button Pressing the button reveals a secret door in the opposite corner of the room. It is locked and cannot be lockpicked. On its surface is the symbol of the Absolute and a red text which reads as following: All are awaited, all are embraced, none shall escape. Interacting with the door starts a dialogue which offers the character two mutually exclusive checks: [HISTORY]  That text is vaguely familiar - try to recall its historical source.  (DC 20) [ See: Bugs ] [INVESTIGATION]  Examine the red symbol blazoned on the door. (DC 20) Passing a History check allows the interacting party member to recall that this text's source has Bhaalist origins. Neither of these checks opens the door. However, the door can be interacted with once by every party member, which affords several opportunities to pass a mostly perfunctory check, since the only way to get past the door is by knowing the passphrase, Sicarius . The passphrase can be obtained by: Reading the Dirge of the Unholy Assassin , looted or pickpocketed from Dolor Learning it from Olfaith Olumssdottir , after killing two murder targets listed on the Bloodstained Parchment Interrogating Devella Fountainhead's corpse via Speak with Dead , if she is killed in the Facemaker's Boutique Reading Orin's letter , left in camp after killing Gortash The Gilded Chest in the corner requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick; it contains random minor loot and a note , presumably addressed to the employee who conducts the covering. Candulhallow's Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] As the party enter the basement (marked as "Bhaalist Crypt") they find themselves on a brick path over a pool of dirty water. Across the entrance stands a metal shield emblazoned with the Flaming Fist symbol. Along the path are four human skulls affixed to the wall in a row, with inscriptions on them. If read one by one, they form a roughly-rhymed stanza, authored by Invoker Grimlark . [ 5 ] If the party come down to the water, they can find an unlocked elegant chest in the far corner at X: -1324 Y: 549 with minor loot. The path along the opposite wall is safe, unlike crossing the water: the area closer to the brick path is trapped with a Tripwire ( DC 18 Perception Check to find), which drops down a Fire Explosive and three Firewine Barrels ; the shores of the water pool are smeared with Grease . Following the brick path in the eastern direction leads to the antechamber door of the Murder Tribunal at X: -1302 Y: 520 . While the party are inside the basement of the Candulhalow's Tombstones, they cannot fast travel or move to the Campsite . Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes nearby the Candulhallow's Tombstones. Near the house adjacent to the Candulhallow's Tombstone Shop is Alembrosius , standing near a makeshift stall with various pottery and vases. He says the vendor will be back in a short time, letting slip this is his mother, but he does not sell anything himself. A letter in the house mailbox contains gratitudes for a repaired vase and some gold. Halfway to the graveyard Pythonicus and Jitters Corbwell are bargaining over some goods which are apparently not quite legal to distribute: both try to discourage the party from poking their nose into their dealings. Jitters is discouraged with the new price for the same service, while the dragonborn insists, appealing to the Guild politics. Related locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Lower City ⁠ Murder Tribunal ⁠ Rainforest's Home Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal ⁠ Investigate the Murders Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] Alembrosius Jitters Corbwell Pythonicus Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] Dirge of the Unholy Assassin Keeping Up Appearances Observation Notes Record of Ownership Seekers Speak your Loss The Superior Durability of Hardwood Tombstone Shop Notes Repairs Payment Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] When interacting with the secret door, attempting the History check blocks the Investigation check, but not vice versa. This is because in the corresponding dialogue file LOW_MurderTribunal_TombstoneShop_Password both checks set the identical flags, *_InvestigationSuccess or *_InvestigationFailed depending on the roll result. Combined with the jump-node scheme of the dialogue file, this effectively deprives the character from rolling checks in a sequence. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ As stated in Record of Ownership notes. ↑ Namely, Koll at the Highberry's Wine Festival and Soxx in Facemaker's Boutique . ↑ One of the tombstones' epitaphs runs as "Franc Peartree. Our Lady's Traitor. His life now given, gladly taken." ↑ Part of its text runs as "seek trigger hidden by a frame" . ↑ Grimlark can be met in the Temple of Bhaal . More of his Bhaal-inspired poetical creations are in the Undercity Ruins and the Abandoned Cistern . ## Carm's Garms
- **来源**: [Carm's Garms](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Carm's_Garms)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Street View Wyrm's Crossing Wyrm's Rock Fortress ↑ Danthelon's Dancing Axe ← Carm's Garms ↓ Sharess' Caress Carm's Garms is a Location within Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is a clothing store selling various camp clothing items, as well as dyes to diversify them. “ If it's genuine quality, and genuine taste, you're after - Carm's Garms has you covered. „ — Carmen Pennygood Contents 1 Overview 2 Characters 2.1 Outside the building 3 Loot 4 Literature 5 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Carm's Garms [ 1 ] is a two-storied building located in the north-east of Wyrm's Crossing , across from Danthelon's Dancing Axe . It has no cellar, featuring a subjacent tunnel instead, accessible from the outside wooden sidewalks of the Crossing bridge. Near the store building, three machinery enthusiasts - Trinigan Gazotts , Slozy Arminifer and Vinegaroon - discuss spiritedly the technical features of the Steel Watchers. The store is owned by Carmen Pennygood , the sister of Figaro 'Facemaker' Pennygood , the owner of Facemaker's Boutique in the Lower City . Their relationship is uneasy, as both are keen to carry on their deceased father's metier, but deem each other unapt in tailoring and fashion. One of the blackboards standing in the tradehall says that the proprietor does not take on mending clothes from the Facemaker's, as those are hopeless, while one of letters in the backroom states the same opinion of Figaro's on his sister's works. Carmen offers a fair amount of Camp Clothing to buy (from Common to Rich grades), as well as lots of Rare dyes . In several containers around the store, including the second floor, the party may also steal several random clothing items of the same quality. Inside the store the party can also meet Naaber , a meddlesome young man who starts to follow the player character once they enter, prompting them to talk. If talked to, he starts to imitate various character Classes one by one separately (therefore, it takes 12 times to hear out all his attempts). However, if the player character goes through it resignedly, Naaber rewards their patience with Absolute Confidence Amulet . Within the dialogues when Naaber is imitating a Bard and a dog (which comes instead of Druid class) the player character may also earn approval from their companions. Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Carmen Pennygood - trader Naaber Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] Slozy Arminifer Trinigan Gazotts Vinegaroon Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Absolute Confidence Amulet Seemingly Gleaming Ring - if the amulet above has been stolen from Naaber before trying out all his options Carmen sells a variety of dyes and Camp Clothing items.
