## Fraygo's Flophouse
- **来源**: [Fraygo's Flophouse](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fraygo's_Flophouse)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Fraygo's Flophouse - street view Wyrm's Crossing Sharess' Caress ↑ Fraygo's Flophouse → Sharess' Caress ↓ South Span Checkpoint Fraygo's Flophouse is a Location within Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . It is a three-storied building on the western side of the Wyrm's Crossing, just north from the ramparts of South Span Checkpoint . “ Great - we can bunk with ten other people and pray none of them have sticky fingers! „ — Rilia , refusing to lodge at the Flophouse Contents 1 Overview 1.1 First floor 1.2 Second floor 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 Outside the building 5 Related literature 6 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon approaching the building, any party member may pass a Perception check and recognize the flowery motif on the Flophouse patter, in case they have already found the Flowery Key in the tunnels beneath Open Hand Temple in Rivington . Near the entrance, Crak and Rilia are discussing the lack of decent places to stay in the city. The ground floor of the Flophouse consists of a mess hall and a kitchen. Between them is a wide stairs leading to the first floor. In the mess hall the player character can trade with Trader Griska , who has various potions and alchemical ingredients in stock. Also, speaking to the adventurers Drim and Rosanna can bring approval from some companions (available for all character classes except Sorcerer ). In the kitchen, the cook Queelia Arvis can sell some Camp Supplies . Also, a flophouse employee Dashkent Moliver walks back and forth between the reception desk and the kitchen. If the party has progressed the ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders quest far enough to know that the killer dresses in red, they can ask Moliver about it. First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The first floor is divided in two by the corridor starting from the stairs; both parts are lodgings with several bunks and a locked Wooden Chest near each one. The corridor is constantly patrolled by Worker Bernyr and ends with a locked door to the outer balcony to the west and a small bathroom to the east. All containers here (as well as the backdoor) are red-outlined, but the chests can be looted with the help of sight-blocking means like Fog Cloud . In the southern part of the room, two vampire spawns - Dalyria and Pale Petras - can be found arguing. These two are Astarion's siblings, and interacting with them progresses his ⁠ companion quest . The dialogue differs depending on whether the party know (or don't know) the true purpose of the scars on Astarion's back. However, the interaction itself is possible only if none of the party members has a light effect active, or an item with such effect equipped (such as Daylight or The Blood of Lathander ). Otherwise, both spawn receive Sunlight Hypersensitivity and teleport away [ 1 ] . If playing as Astarion Origin, interacting with the spawns grants some approval or disapproval, depending on the player character's choices during the dialogue. If Astarion is currently not present, the player character may eavesdrop on the spawns' conversation (requires a DC 10 Stealth Check for a Rogue character, or a DC 15 Stealth Check for all others). If successful, they hear Dalyria and Petras discussing their master, the pending ritual and Astarion's disappearance. Regardless of the roll result, the player character gets involved in the dialogue, and a carefully chosen bluff helps to fish the necessary information out of the heedless couple. Second floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Up a ladder on the second floor at X: -12 Y: 87 is an attic with a red-outlined wardrobe at X: -17 Y: 82 which can be opened with the Flowery Key . However, if the party have not obtained the key, they may lockpick the door with a DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check roll, or use the backdoor to the outer balcony at X: -29 Y: 80 , which is neither locked nor red-outlined, and thus available from outside by most means of spatial movement. The room inside, by several interior details and documents (like Bloodstained Note and Open Hand Temple Plans ), may be identified as the serial killer's hideout. A successful DC 10 Perception Check followed by a DC 10 Investigation Check allows the party to find bloody spots near the bed and find Ffion Goldgrind's body. Using Speak with Dead on her provides the party with some information on the serial murders. Several items here can be interacted with to gain more information about the Open Hand Temple murders. In particular, picking up a copy of the Bloodstained Parchment from the table to the right of the entrance is necessary to progress the ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders quest. Also, the room can be looted for some poisons and alchemical ingredients to derive them. ## Golbraith's Cellar
- **来源**: [Golbraith's Cellar](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Golbraith's_Cellar)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Street view of Golbraith's Cellar Lower City Bloomridge Park ↑ The Glitter Gala ← Golbraith's Cellar → Bloomridge Park ↓ The Blushing Mermaid Golbraith's Cellar is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ ...before or after you thundered into my home like a wounded umber hulk? Make no mistake - you're here because I allow it. „ — Golbraith Stredivas , after party advised him to worry about himself Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Golbraith's Cellar [ 1 ] is a small private house located directly across from the main gate to Bloomridge Park and north of The Blushing Mermaid . Though it seemingly consists of two adjacent dwellings, the door to the second one (with a separate mailbox) is blocked. The only entrance is at X: -154 Y: -55 . The building is two-storied and has a spacious basement. On a triangular ground outside Golbraith's Cellar three children, Cinnamon , Punkins and Slow-Butt are playing a game, imitating citizens being detained and scanned by a Steel Watcher. The party can talk to them and participate in the game. Layout [ edit section | visual editor ] First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The ground floor features a hatch leading to the basement (see below) and the ladder on the south-western corner, which leads to the first floor. However, the first floor room can also be accessed via jumping onto the balcony. The upper bookshelf at X: -154 Y: -62 contains a key . The nearby locked rustic chest, however, must be lockpicked ( DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check ) to be opened. It contains a book of letters between Golbraith and his son, some gold and a set of Thieves' Tools . The house owner Golbraith Stredivas is on the first floor. He is a retired monster hunter and an expert in countering mind flayers . He taught his son everything he knew about his metier, but is now concerned about him. Easing his mind about the mind flayers in the city and about his son's mettle as well grants approval from most companions (the formulation depends on the interacting character's Class and Race ). If the party choose a friendly course when speaking with Golbraith, he awards them with Abdel's Trusted Shield . Otherwise, the shield can be pickpocketed from him, along with the Golbraith's Hatch Key . Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] Basement of the house (by Martijn Petersen) In the north-eastern corner of the room is a locked hatch which leads to the basement. It requires DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check or aforementioned hatch key stolen from Golbraith. Descending through the hatch, the party first find themselves in a small cellar, where some containers may keep Camp Supplies or health potions of various grade. The western wall is movable; it is initially marked as a door and does not require any ability checks to detect. Behind the wall is the main part of the basement: a spacious hall with a study, a training ground, and multiple hunting trophies along the walls. The middle part of the hall is crossed with four Marble Plates which set off the vents emanating Cloudkill vapors. Each marble plate requires DC 15 Perception Check to find and DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to disarm. Also, a button on the wall at X: -2342 Y: 834 disables all traps. Containers around the room (including various vases) may keep gold, Camp Supplies , common weapons, random arrows, various potions and elixirs. The southern side of the room is a makeshift training ground. A Katana lies on a cupboard under a stuffed hyena head. The northern side has a small study with several books on Illithids and ways to track and fight them. In the far end of the hall, on a weapon stand and on the table are some common and Uncommon weapons. A locked gilded chest which can be opened with Golbraith's Chest Key contains gold and rare alchemical ingredients. The platter at the entrance, however, calls the building "Golbraith's Home", like most other private dwellings in the city.
## Gorion Mausoleum
- **来源**: [Gorion Mausoleum](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Gorion_Mausoleum)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Gorion Mausoleum - interior The Gorion Mausoleum is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . It can be accessed through the Graveyard of the Lower City. “ Here lies Lord Gregorion Gorion, First High Constable of Baldur's Gate, the city's protector. „ — Plaque in front of the sarcophagus of Lord Gorion [ 1 ] Access [ edit section | visual editor ] It can be accessed through the Lower City's Graveyard , almost at its center at X: 10 Y: 33 . It requires either Gorion Mausoleum Key or DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to open the gate. Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Overview of the mausoleum The aboveground to the mausoleum is through a locked gate beneath the graveyard's willow tree. A sarcophagus holds the remains of Lord Gregorian Gorion, First High Constable of Baldur's Gate. Gorion was known for his heroism, sage mind, and kind heart. [ 2 ] The hole east of the sarcophagus is used to access Durinbold Mausoleum , while the crumbling wall on the west end can be destroyed to access Hhune Mausoleum . Related locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Graveyard Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] A Plea for Freedom A Plea for Protection A Plea to the Gods Elixir of Heroism [ 3 ] Hymns for the Gone Patrons of our Hero Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Gregorion Gorion's corpse is unusually heavy, weighing 500 pounds (Reddit: quegurjin, Why in the Hells is Gregorion Gorion 500 lbs? , 2025-04-12). From game design perspective, it might be intended as an easy solution to access the hidden room in the Hhune Mausoleum. ↑ It is unclear whether Lord Gregorion Gorion is supposed to be the Gorion from Baldur's Gate 1, or somehow related to him. To prevent confusion, Lord Gregorion Gorion is referred to as Lord Gorion , and Gorion from Baldur's Gate 1 as Monk Gorion in the following notes. The city of Baldur's Gate dates back to at least the 5th century DR, and was already a widely recognized power in the 1200s. Monk Gorion, on the other hand, was born around 1300 DR. (See also the article on Gorion on the Forgotten Realms Wiki .) It seems very unlikely but not completely impossible that the city did not have its first High Constable until after ~1300 DR. Monk Gorion was an adventurer who traveled with the Harpers , and moved to Candlekeep around 1350 DR to raise Gorion's Ward . He lived there for about 20 years, until his death. It seems unlikely that he would have been employed as High Constable of Baldur's Gate at any point in his life. Monk Gorion died near Lion's Way , in the vicinity of Candlekeep, making a burial there more expedient than one in Baldur's Gate (located 120 miles north). Monk Gorion is never referred to by any other name or title. For example, he is never referred to as Lord Gorion or as Gregorian. The name Gorion generally seems to be used as his only name in Baldur's Gate 1 and 2. The only similarity between Monk Gorion and Lord Gorion, apart from the name, is that they were both heroes and sages renowned for their wisdom. There are various continuity and lore consistency issues between Baldur's Gate 3 and the previously established lore of the city of Baldur's Gate and the events of the past games. Therefore, it may have been intended that Lord Gorion and Monk Gorion be one and the same, despite the aforementioned inconsistencies. ↑ In Lord Gorion's sarcophagus v t e Lower City v t e Characters ## Graveyard (Lower City)
- **来源**: [Graveyard (Lower City)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Graveyard_(Lower_City))
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

The Graveyard in the lower city. A giant tree casting shade on the gravestones below. Lower City Devil's Fee ← Graveyard → Candulhallow's Tombstones ↓ Forge of the Nine The Graveyard is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . This article contains sensitive content , including brief descriptions of realistic or graphic violence, and physical or emotional abuse. “ Mum used to say there was no such thing as death. That there was only change. Dad thought that was a load of woo. That gone meant gone, unless you'd made a deal with one of the gods. Said he had better things to do in life than beg favors off immortals. „ — Karlach , reciting her parents' views on death Contents 1 Overview 2 Graveyard layout 2.1 Mortuary 2.2 Graveyard proper 3 Companion interactions 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Staff 6.2 Visitors 6.3 Creatures 6.4 Other 6.5 Corpses 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Lower City Graveyard occupies a large plot of land stretched across the northern part of the Lower City wall. It spans from Candulhallow's Tombstones to the walls of the Devil's Fee . The graveyard has three open entrances at X: -19 Y: 4 , at X: 21 Y: 13 and at X: 56 Y: 31 . It features several aisles with plain graves and four entrances to underground family tombs: Grand Mausoleum X: -9 Y: 36 [ 1 ] Durinbold Mausoleum X: 32 Y: 18 Gorion Mausoleum X: 10 Y: 33 Hhune Mausoleum X: 17 Y: 41 All mausoleums are locked. The key to Hhune Mausoleum can be found in the Knights of the Shield Hideout , the key to the Ancient Mausoleum can be pickpocketed from Gracie Scyre , and the key to Durinbold Mausoleum lies on a shelf in the upstairs bedroom of the Mortuary. Finally, the key to Gorion Mausoleum can be picked up from the ground, in the corner to the left of its entrance, hidden by a tuft of grass. Otherwise, each mausoleum door requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to open. Lockpicking the mausoleums is not considered a crime, although most of them contain traps and / or undead guards. The middle part of the graveyard is a mild hill, with the Mortuary atop it. It has two stories and a basement. Behind the mortuary is the cemetery carpenter's workbench. Also, a huge weeping willow in the middle of the graveyard is a major landmark, capturing the eye. Due to the series of murders which recently happened throughout the city, the graveyard staff has plenty of work to cater to the bodies of the newly deceased. Graveyard layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Mortuary [ edit section | visual editor ] The Mortuary building The Mortuary is located in the eastern part of the graveyard. On its porch, Anita and Elias Fischer are distraught at being unable to get a coffin made for their daughter Lily, her life cut short by a serial killer . The carpenter Ulkov Sully is behind the mortuary. He can be convinced to make a coffin for the child out of turn, or paid to do so. Convincing him and reporting back to grieving parents may grant the following inspirations: ⁠ Empathy for the Fallen ( Folk Hero background) ⁠ Part of Life ( Urchin background) Inside the building, the gravekeeper Valmorba prepares bodies for burial. If the party read the Tough Letter , carried by Gomwick in Act One , they can ask Valmorba where they can find "M.Kurwin"'s grave, and even ask her to borrow a shovel. The upper floor of the mortuary serves as Valmorba's dwelling. The only remarkable item there (apart from aforementioned mausoleum key) is her diary . At X: 31 Y: 21 a locked hatch beside the porch stairs leads to the mortuary's cellar. It can be opened with Kurwin's Mortuary Key carried by Valmorba, or DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check . Inside are three rooms. In the first are the gravekeeper's notes on Duke Stelmane 's body. Straight ahead is the embalmer's lab where a body is waiting to be buried. The room to the left is Valmorba's workshop. On the table stands the Jar of Mystic Carrion's Lungs , which she bought from an adventurer who found it in the Undercity Ruins . Some herbal alchemical ingredients can be picked up around the room. Graveyard proper [ edit section | visual editor ] Several potential encounters can be had with persons around the graveyard. Like the Fischer couple, all mourning visitors owe their grief to a serial killer . [ 2 ] Several have dialogue lines which change depending on the party's progress with ⁠ Investigate the Murders quest. Mortarch Gracie Scyre , a cleric of Kelemvor , is patrolling the graveyard to prevent anyone from digging up the graves. She joins the party in combat if they instigate a fight with either the undead or kobolds (see below). When she reaches the mortuary porch, she stops to speak to the unfortunate couple. At X: -12 Y: 32 Nina Dortmell is trying to resurrect her recently deceased brother. The party may either help her or convince her to leave him be. Both decisions bring approval or disapproval from various companions, and grant the following inspirations as well: ⁠ What Remains of the Dead ( Acolyte background) - for either option ⁠ Good Intentions ( Urchin background) - for assisting Nina with raising her brother Helping Nina spawns three Zombies , two Greater Zombies , two Skeletons , and Garret Dortmell , a Death Shepherd who buffs the other summoned undead with significant additional durability. If the party speak to Mortarch Gracie Scyre after helping Nina, she chastises them for teaching the little girl necromancy, comparing it to leaving a poisoned cake out in a park where a child can eat it. The party can, however, report Nina's attempts to the Mortarch preemptively. Around X: 3 Y: 23 the Strange Beggar Morbus is wandering back and forth, trying to play hide-and-seek with Pookums . She tries to explain to him that a graveyard is not the best place for such games. After the quest ⁠ Find Mystic Carrion's Servant is completed, both Morbus and Pookums disappear from the graveyard. Other visitors, Billyum and Droona Shveitz , are mourning over the fresh graves of their relatives. Near the western end of the graveyard Maude sells flowers. Some of her stock can be used for alchemical brewing. At X: 17 Y: 24 is a grave where a DC 10 Perception Check highlights a pipe sticking out of it. If clicked on, a voice can be heard from the pipe. This Dirt Mound is initially red like all other available for digging, but after interacting with the pipe end changes color to normal. Digging up the grave exposes a coffin, and opening it releases Gothric Rillyn , who was apparently buried alive by The Stone Lord as punishment for theft. At X: 7 Y: 25 is the grave marked "M. Kurwin" . The Dirt Mound in front of it can be dug up to reveal a kobold named Bugthimble who aggressively claims the treasures hidden in the grave. The party can then either intimidate or deceive Bugthimble to chase him away, while some character Classes (e.g., a Draconic Bloodline Sorcerer), have unique lines to placate him. Failing the check (or choosing the corresponding option) starts a fight with Bugthimble and their kobold allies. If intimidated or defeated, Bugthimble drops the Kurwin's Cauteriser . Securing the loot from this grave grants the ⁠ Grave Prospector inspiration for the characters with Charlatan background. Dark Urge characters have an additional option to indulge their Urge, burying Bugthimble alive. Doing this is considered an oathbreaking action for Vengeance Paladins , Ancients' Paladins , and Paladins of Devotion . [ verify ] After digging up the Dirt Mound at X: 29 Y: 16 a DC 5 Perception Check highlights a hole, through which a small or tiny creature (or disguised or wildshaped as such) can descend into the Lower City Sewers , landing near the entrance to Cazador's Dungeon . There appears no option to come back to surface from there. Several other graves around the graveyard are pictured like red-outlined Dirt Mounds, which still can be dug up, revealing caskets and coffins. From these containers various loot like gold, Valuables , and rare alchemical ingredients can be taken. The sarcophagus under the willow can also be looted if the DC 15 Strength Check is passed. However, this all must be done with certain means of concealment. Graverobbing in front of other NPCs is considered a crime and bears adequate consequences. Throughout the graveyard territory, several herbal alchemical ingredients can be freely taken, including Corpse Rose , Weavemoss , and Poppy Flower , a renamed copy of the Mergrass which can be mixed with it to obtain the usual extract. Companion interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several companion interactions which take place at the graveyard. Karlach and the player character, sharing a quiet moment after she visits her parents' graves. If Karlach is in the party, she points out her parents' graves to the party. They are in the middle aisle of the Graveyard at X: 5 Y: 31 . If interacting with any of highlighted tombstones, Karlach speaks to her parents' graves, telling them of what she has been up to. The player character can then ask to find out how Karlach's parents died and events which transpired afterwards. If Shadowheart is in the party, she comments on the grave of Allister Marnley, located at X: 25 Y: 15 next to the south entrance of the Graveyard with a "Happy Birthday" note. After this, she can be spoken with again and muses further on newly rediscovered bits of memories from her past in Baldur's gate. It is also possible to place a Night Orchid directly in front of the grave for her. Shadowheart's comment afterwards depends on whether her companion quest has been completed, and if it is - on its final outcome as well. Astarion dusts off the tombstone with his own name on it. The graveyard is also the location where the romantic scene with Astarion takes place, if he remained a vampire spawn upon completing his companion quest , and the player character is currently in partnership with him. To let his past go ultimately, he takes his partner to his own grave , which cannot otherwise be found in a regular playthrough. Judging by other cutscene landmarks, it seems to be located under the willow tree, next to the graves of Karlach's parents. Game dialogue files suggest there was another unique interaction for the Dark Urge origin as well, apparently not implemented. Upon digging up one of the graves, they could have restored a part of their memories and recall that the mutilated corpse buried there is their victim. However, the state of the body would give rise to mixed feelings with the rest of the party, from utter disgust (Halsin or Wyll) to mild sarcasm (Astarion or Minthara). [ 3 ] In current game version, the Dark Urge upon entering the graveyard simply says "Not enough graves. Never enough." ## Grey Harbour Docks
- **来源**: [Grey Harbour Docks](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Grey_Harbour_Docks)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

View of Grey Harbour Docks from the balcony under The Society of Brilliance Lodge Lower City The Lodge ↑ Steel Watch Foundry ← Grey Harbour Docks → The Counting House ↓ Water Queen's House Grey Harbour Docks is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I have no love for the sea, but the city would not be what it is without these ships. That lends them a kind of beauty, I suppose. „ — Jaheira , bantering with Lae'zel in the Docks Contents 1 Overview 2 Locations 2.1 Lustrous Lass 2.2 Passenger dock pier 2.3 Grey Harbour Docks Waypoint 2.4 Loading dock of the Steel Watch Foundry (secured) 2.5 Stairs to the Steeps district 2.6 Smugglers' corner 2.7 Embankment under the balcony of the Lodge 2.8 Fishermen pier 2.9 Flymm Cargo 2.10 Watchtower 2.11 Dock cranes 3 Waypoints 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Churg Elvek's gang 6.1.1 Onlookers 6.2 Sailors and dockworkers 6.3 Civilians 6.4 Flaming Fist 6.5 The Guild 6.6 Creatures 7 Loot 8 External links 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The map screen showing the Docks' layout This area consists of several docks and ships, with several locations that are considered restricted throughout Act Three , but can still be entered and explored. The major points of interest in the location are as described below (listed from the bottom-left corner, up and right, along the piers' line). Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] Lustrous Lass [ edit section | visual editor ] The Lustrous Lass docked. Main article: Lustrous Lass The Lustrous Lass is a quarantined ship that can be found at X: -193 Y: -233 with its dead crew on it. It has been towed into the docks for investigation. Passenger dock pier [ edit section | visual editor ] The dock pier can be found at X: -208 Y: -188 . Upon visiting the docks for the first time, the party can find a citizen named Dharin Brislen , arguing with Captain Sleam over smuggling his family of four out of the city. Unfortunately, the family is short of money, only being able to pay for three. The party can help the family by convincing Captain Sleam to take them all or by paying her the sum the Brislens are lacking. Helping the family by any means grants approval from some companions. If successfully resolving the conflict, after a long rest another group of characters can be encountered: Trader Djingo and his clients Kaet Ling , Smiley Gheef , and Pheebs Splayfoot . They can be spoken with as well, but these interactions have no further implications for the party. The far end of the pier has wooden stairs leading to the Water Queen's House entrance at X: -229 Y: -199 . Grey Harbour Docks Waypoint [ edit section | visual editor ] Near it, at the pier, at X: -219 Y: -155 , the party can find two sailors, brother and sister Gowlan and Fleer . Talking to Gowlan advances the ⁠ Avenge the Drowned quest, providing the party with some information about circumstances of the death of Holli Dylford . Loading dock of the Steel Watch Foundry (secured) [ edit section | visual editor ] The ship moored at this pier at X: -208 Y: -134 is guarded by two Steel Watchers , patrolling the small footway back and forth. The entrance to the pier is marked by Flaming Fist "Secure Area" signs. However, if any party member manages to make their way onto the ship's deck, they can find a disguised container at the stern X: -203 Y: -124 . To detect it, a DC 20 Investigation Check must be passed on two adjacent long wooden crates (however, if the check is failed, a direct attempt to loot any of these removes the guise). The crates are revealed to be a single container of clearly illithid design, resembling a closed nursery (as shown in the intro cutscene of the game). It can be looted for 6 Mind Flayer Parasite Specimens , accompanied by the Cargo Shipment from Ketheric Thorm . The container remains unclaimed throughout Act Three , thus the party can loot it freely after completing ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch . Stairs to the Steeps district [ edit section | visual editor ] This is one of several possible points to approach the Docks for the first time. If the party come to the Docks for the first time down from Lady Jannath's Estate , approximately at X: -230 Y: -145 they are engaged in the dialogue with Churg Elvek and his allies, who are preparing to execute Volo . Saving Volo from the grim fate grants the ⁠ Saving a Fellow Tale-Spinner inspiration to characters with the Charlatan background. Letting Churg Elvek and his gang execute Volo is considered an oathbreaking action for Vengeance Paladins and Paladins of Devotion . Smugglers' corner [ edit section | visual editor ] This point of interest can be approached either by the ladder near the end of the railroad track or by walking along the high stone-paved embankment directly below the Society of Brilliance Lodge . At the end of the embankment is a ladder which leads down to the smugglers' boats. Near the ladder, approximately at X: -221 Y: -109 , the automated dialogue with Big Huido , the leader of a gang under Guild protection, starts. The player character can attempt to convince Huido to surrender his cargo to them, fight the gang and loot the shipment afterwards, or simply walk away and let the smugglers be. Depending on the player character's decisions, various choices might gain approval from several companions. Embankment under the balcony of the Lodge [ edit section | visual editor ] Walking along the embankment, party members passing a DC 10 Perception Check detect a Loose Plank at X: -188 Y: -98 , which conceals a bottle of wine and a Sailor's Key . The key opens a wooden chest nearby, however, both the stash and the chest are red-outlined, and looting them without any concealment leads to unwanted attention from a group of Flaming Fist guards standing nearby. The chest contains a Trap Disarm Toolkit , a Thieves' Tools set, a Gold Ingot , and a minor amount of gold. Fishermen pier [ edit section | visual editor ] The pier is the footway forming the right bank of the docks. All containers here are red-outlined. However, at X: -179 Y: -101 between two interactable Drying Racks lies Pile of Rotten Fish (a unique type of Dirt Mound ). It can be spotted as an interactable object by passing a DC 10 Perception Check , but is available to loot even without it. Digging up the pile requires a DC 15 Constitution Check . Among the fish, a Reeking Pouch is buried, containing a Map to Buried Treasure and a Key to Buried Treasure , along with some gold and random alchemy components. The map leads to a piece of land just south of The Counting House at X: -98 Y: -201 where there is a dirt mound containing a wooden chest with 259 gold inside. Flymm Cargo [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Flymm Cargo The Flymm Cargo building is a large warehouse with several entrances, all locked and restricted (red-outlined). However, getting inside is crucial for accomplishing several quests, among them ⁠ Avenge the Drowned and ⁠ Retrieve Omeluum . Two of the entrances are in the plain sight of the Flaming Fist patrol accompanied by a Steel Watcher ; sneaking inside from the docks may not be a simple task. Watchtower [ edit section | visual editor ] The Watchtower environs are considered a restricted area, and are directly connected to the Counting House docks to the east. Unlocking the tower allows access to its roof and an excellent view of the docks and the river Chionthar, along with two Smokepowder Barrels . The pier can be reached from the deck of the Lustrous Lass or from the berth behind the Flymm Cargo building. However, the footway is constantly patrolled by two Steel Watchers and two Cashguards . Being spotted here results in an encounter with a Cashguard, which may end in teleporting to the entrance bridge of The Counting House or spill into a fight. Dock cranes [ edit section | visual editor ] One of these is standing near the stairs to the Steeps on the left bank, and two more near the Flymm Cargo building. All of these have Metal Crates clutched in their hooks. Despite being Sturdy , the hooks can be easily destroyed, causing the crates to fall. Inside some common items and / or Camp Supplies can be found. ## Guildhall
- **来源**: [Guildhall](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Guildhall)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Guildhall - view to to the bar and Nine-Fingers' office Undercity Lower City Sewers ↑ Guildhall The Guildhall is a Location within the Undercity in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ The Guildhall has one rule: All crime stays in the city streets, where it belongs. Break this rule and you die. „ — Plaque near the Guildhall entrance, if entering from the Lower City streets Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 1.1.1 Underground route 1.1.2 Guildhall entrance 2 Guildhall layout 2.1 Main Area 2.1.1 Secret Stash 2.2 Guildhall Bar 2.3 Nine-Fingers' Office 2.4 Secret Sewer Vault 3 Involvement 3.1 Major quests 3.1.1 Fight at the Guildhall 3.2 Lesser quests 3.2.1 Inspirations and rewards 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Notable 6.2 Guild Members 6.3 Visitors 6.3.1 Zhentarim Members 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 Bugs 10 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Guildhall [ 1 ] is a separate part of the Lower City Sewers . It is the underground headquarters of The Guild – the main criminal syndicate in Baldur’s Gate and the city suburbs. The Guildhall, however, is not choke-packed with thugs and thieves. It is more a joint management centre for disparate local gangs and solitary dealers, as well as a social space with shady characters and merchants dealing in "pre-owned stuff", illicit goods, services and leisures, and of course trading information. During the game's events, the Guild (and by extension the Guildhall) is run by the Guildmaster Astele Keene , also known as Nine-Fingers Keene or simply Nine-Fingers . When the party arrive to Baldur's Gate, the Guild's positions have already been substantively undermined by the actions of a newly-sprung gang led by the Stone Lord . To regain turf, Nine-Fingers struck a deal with the Zhentarim , a trading and mercenary organization with back-alley morals. For this reason, several members of the Zhentarim are also present in the Guildhall. Access [ edit section | visual editor ] Revealed entrance from Lower City to the Guildhall The Guildhall can be accessed either from underground via the Lower City Sewers or above ground through the Guildhall Entrance in the Lower City . Underground route [ edit section | visual editor ] The fastest route is using the manhole at X: 127 Y: -30 in the alley north of the Basilisk Gate Barracks and then smashing through the western wall at X: 38 Y: 784 ( DC 15 Perception Check to detect the wall). The party must then follow the path west to a locked door labelled No Entry - No Exit ( DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check ) to the Guildhall bar at X: -14 Y: 772 . Although the door is red-outlined, there are no repercussions to lockpocking or using it in either direction. Alternatively, the party can descend into the sewers from the Knights of the Shield Hideout . Behind the door is a room trapped with vents emitting poison clouds . The traps are disabled with a lever at X: 18 Y: 793 (can be triggered with a ranged attack). Jumping up into the wall breach above the lever leads the party into the same room with the door to the Guildhall bar. The vents' room is also accessible through the breach in the wall across the lever (where the sewer chute is from the Heapside Prison ). Finally, if the party find and unlock the movable wall section leading from the secret hideout of Nine-Fingers' office (see below), they can use it afterwards as another entrance into the Guildhall from the sewers. Guildhall entrance [ edit section | visual editor ] Above ground, the Guildhall Entrance is in a narrow alleyway in the Brampton district of Baldur's Gate. It hides in a half-ruined building at X: 62 Y: -99 , behind the Barren's Coop and across from Bruc and Pishe's Emporium , posing as a trading establishment, apparently used by the Guild as a correspondence addressee. The alley is guarded by Tusgront and several other Guild members. When the party approach Tusgront for the first time, he starts a dialogue. There are several options to get past him: If the party side with Farlin during the events on the Western Beach in Rivington , Tusgront recognizes them and allows entry. If Jaheira is present, selecting the option "Careful, that's the High Harper Jaheira you're speaking to" smooths the way. Succeeding a dialogue check. Full list of options when dealing with Tusgront is on the Aid the Underduke quest page. Alternatively, the party can find a Guild Ring and insert it into the wall slot at X: 59 Y: -97 to reveal the entrance. [ See: Bugs ] Two such rings are inside the Bruc and Pishe's Emporium . The entrance into it at X: 56 Y: -104 is locked (requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick), but breaking in is not considered a crime. Entering the Guildhall through either route for the first time grants one or more of the following inspirations: ⁠ Back into the Familiar ( Criminal backgrounds) ⁠ Beneath the Gate ( Outlander backgrounds) ⁠ Home Sweet Home ( Urchin backgrounds) ⁠ Underbelly Diplomat ( Noble backgrounds) Also, gaining peaceful access through the Tusgront's alley grants the ⁠ Friends in Low Places inspiration for characters with the Charlatan background. In the mailbox above the Guildhall Entrance is the Counting House Safe nº8 Key and a note concerning the sightings of shape-shifting creatures in the city. Guildhall layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Area [ edit section | visual editor ] The main area of the Guildhall where Guild members and Zhentarim congregate. The entrance from the Lower City leads through the southeastern door of the Guildhall into a large cavernous area with the bottom covered in sewer filth. A complex, multi-levelled scaffold system lines up the walls. Various levels of the scaffolds are connected with staircases, wooden ladders and rope nettings. Ladders and nettings – as well as wooden supports to some platforms – are destroyable, which can help or hinder the party if a fight begins. A heavy stone slab hanging on a coiled rope can be shot down as well. Destroying any of these outside of combat is considered a transgression by Guild members. At X: -28 Y: 753 a doorway leads from the main area scaffolds into the Guild bar and to the doors of Nine-Fingers' office. Most lower-rank members of the Guild are around the main area. Some of them appear only if the party made certain choices in the Act One, namely: Saving or raiding the Emerald Grove Saving Oskar Fevras from the Zhentarim in their hideout or leaving him there There are several points of interest around the main area: Most of the Zhentarim congregate in the southeastern corner. Some walk around the scaffolds, but no further than the doors to the Guildhall bar. They occasionally chat with various Guild members, but mostly between themselves, revealing they have specific orders and wait for some 'signal' to make a certain move. Tut Thistlebog and Phostlethwaite drink by a balcony at X: -15 Y: 740 . Phostlethwaite occasionally walks back and forth from there to the bar to refill their drinks. Beneath this balcony is a Rustic Chest with minor random loot. A merchants corner in in the northeast is the base for a gang of children called the Fetcher's Brats , [ 2 ] with Sticky Dondo acting as a trader. Sticky sells the Shade-Slayer Cloak . If Mol survived the events of Act One and Two , she is also here, claiming she runs the gang management. Unlike dealing with her in Act One, she cannot be traded with via dialogue options, though pressing the 'Trade' button when speaking with her still opens the trade menu. [ 3 ] If Mol did not survive, Li'l Fezmor takes her place. At X: -47 Y: 741 a trio of halflings consisting of Bad Twin Bubbins , Blades Bakstir and Three-Piece stand to the west of the main area. The party may have previously found mentions of Three-Piece: he is the one who tried to hire an Elfsong patron's son into the Guild ranks, and plans to take part in a revenge match of knife fighting with Babyjowls [ 4 ] . The Zhentarim Phase and Lugarrio stand out the lookout nearby. If Oskar Fevras was not saved from the Zhentarim in Act One , he resides in this corner of the Guildhall. He is busy drawing counterfeit pictures and sells a Fake Portrait of a Noble Before His Death for 1000 gp. He can act as a trader, but does not have any gold initially to buy anything from the party. If Oskar is present, he replaces Blades Bakstir. At X: -47 Y: 751 a dragonborn bard Lyrux Goldthroat plays the flute, attracting the attention of Cutter Violet and Mango who sometimes dance to the music. If Oskar Fevras was not saved from the Zhentarim, two more Guild members listen to Lyrux: Babyjowls and Cheeky Nora . At X: -22 Y: 748 , almost across the entrance to the bar, is an elf by the name The Professor . He serves as a confidant scout to the Guildmaster [ 5 ] and can give the party a hint on where to search for information on her campaign against the Stone Lord. Bursar Uktar is at X: -31 Y: 753 near the stairway leading to the Guildhall bar, accompanied by two bodyguards. He moves to this location after the party speak with Nine-Fingers Keene in her office for the first time. In the filth pit in the centre of the main area Doozy the Dunce looks for a lost ring. The ring is nearby and can be spotted with a DC 15 Perception Check and returned to Doozy, though he gives no reward for it. Doozy appears only if Oskar Fevras was not saved from the Zhentarim. Once the ring is returned, he runs away and disappears from the game. A child named Happy Hands patrols back and forth between the Brats' corner and the pit, behaving as if looking for the same ring. Secret Stash [ edit section | visual editor ] In the southwest corner of the main area is a secret stash on a balcony at X: -51 Y: 721 . Abilities such as Misty Step or Enhance Leap may be helpful in reaching the balcony. On the balcony are two Opulent Chests , containing: Gold, random Rare and Uncommon arrows and / or elixirs Gold, random precious gem and random alchemical ingredients Near the edge of the balcony on the floor lies a book titled Old notes , concerning the Emperor's dealings with Duke Stelmane , when they both ran the Knights of the Shield . Guildhall Bar [ edit section | visual editor ] The Guildhall's bar On the north side of the Guildhall is a bar run by the bugbear Severn . [ See: Bugs ] He sells a variety of food and drink, and as well the Drunken Cloth and Terazul . [ 6 ] Several visitors of the Guild drink or smoke near the bar counter and at the tables across the stairs. In the far corner behind the bar counter is a locked door labelled No Entry - No Exit which leads into the Lower City Sewers . It can be unlocked with Severn's Sewer Key carried by Severn or lockpicked with a DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check . Two members of Guildmaster Keene's personal guard keep sentry near the doors to Nine-Fingers' office. They can be discerned from other Guild members by the title 'Lady'. Another one, Lady Ague , patrols up and down the stairway to the bar, stopping from time to time at the wooden platform over the pit. Two sets of doors leading into the office remain unlocked, while the one right across the counter is locked and red-lined; it leads into Nine-Fingers' bedroom and is opened with the key owned by Nine-Fingers. Nine-Fingers' Office [ edit section | visual editor ] Nine-Fingers' Office Guildmaster Keene is in her office, working at her desk. Two more of her bodyguards protect the area. On the shelves behind Keene are multiple empty pouches. A wooden plaque declares that the shelves once kept a collection of rare Moonshae Zinfandel wines. Nine-Fingers stays in the office at all times except during the scene when the Zhentarim try to take over the Guildhall. She carries the key to High Security Vault nº7 , and those to her safe and bedroom . The two latter keys do not differ in appearance in Keene's inventory, so to get into Keene's Secret Sewer Vault the party must acquire both of them. Directly opposite to Nine-Fingers' desk is an alcove serving her as a bedroom. On the shelves behind the four-posted bed here lie multiple scrolls, containing dossiers on specific persons in Baldur's Gate and on the party themselves, though the actual contents of the dossiers cannot be read. There are several useful documents in the office and in the bedroom: Devil's Fee Observer's Report on the bedroom cabinet gives a lead on the diabolist Helsik , which updates all quests concerning Prince Orpheus and dealing with Raphael File Under Diabolist on Keene's working desk gives the same result From the Desk of Rakath Glitterbeard, Head Banker on the desk near the bed progresses the quests concerning Nine-Fingers' campaign against the Stone Lord , including Jaheira's personal quest The red-outlined bookcase at X: -42 Y: 765 in the bedroom is actually a locked hidden door to a secret area of the Guildhall. Moving the bookcase aside requires a successful DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. Alternatively, the key to it can be pickpocketed from Nine-Fingers. Secret Sewer Vault [ edit section | visual editor ] The secret vault behind the bookcase On the secret landing behind the bedroom bookcase, a Key is on a crate. This key opens a Heavy Chest located on the ground floor at X: -63 Y: 760 (impossible to lockpick). Inside is a small cache of supplies, including the rare Moonshae Zinfandel 1475 , gold, and random minor loot. Across the landing is a safe door, requiring DC 30 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. Otherwise, it can be opened with the same key which opens the bookcase. Behind the safe door is a vault containing two Opulent Chests with: Gold, random Valuables and / or alchemical ingredients Gold, random precious gem and several random Uncommon or Rare potions An internal double door here requires DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check or can be opened with the same key which fits the safe door. Opening this door triggers a trap which seals the outer safe door, [ verify ] trapping the party inside. To escape, the party must either pick the lock from the inside or press the button hidden behind a bookcase at X: -73 Y: 754 in the second room. This trap can be bypassed by destroying the internal door instead of unlocking it, or by fast traveling out of the room. The second room contains another Opulent Chest with more Gold and an Uncommon or Rare arrows or elixirs. Also, Mahogany Wardrobes in both rooms contain several pieces of expensive Camp Clothing . One of them contains the rare Moonshae Zinfandel 1466 as well. Outside the safe door at X: -64 Y: 778 a lever opens a stone door leading to the Lower City Sewers , to the southern end of the sewage raft line . This exit functions as a one-way path until the lever is pulled; it cannot be opened from the sewer side initially. Once opened, it can serve as another way inside the Guildhall. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Within Baldur's Gate 3 , the Guildhall serves as a narrative hub for several large quests, including those started before entering Lower City. It also has several minor interactions which serve as unlisted quests, or complete the active ones with or without consequences as the game unfolds. Major quests [ edit section | visual editor ] Much of the ⁠ Aid the Underduke quest unfolds within the Guildhall, intertwined with Jaheira's ⁠ personal quest . When the party visit Nine-Fingers Keene for the first time at her office, she is holding a council with Guild bursar Uktar about some missing payments from an orphanage. The cutscene continues with the party involved, and Nine-Fingers shows a remarkable knowledge of the party's recent activities. If Jaheira is present, Nine-Fingers recognizes her and has special dialogue, progressing both quests. Otherwise, Keene asks to bring Jaheira to her. In Jaheira's presence, Keene informs the party about her campaign against the new gang led by the Stone Lord and works for the Absolute . She intends to take him down, but refuses to reveal her specific plans to do so. Within the Guildhall there are multiple ways to learn of Nine-Fingers' plans: Bursar Uktar at his post reveals her plans if the option "The quicker I deal with the Stone Lord, the quicker Nine-Fingers gets back to business" is selected The Professor gives a hint to talk with Tut Thistlebog , who drunkenly gives away the information after several ability checks. The letter titled From the Desk of Rakath Glitterbeard, Head Banker in Keene's bedroom at X: -37 Y: 763 also gives away her plans (this note can be read freely and is a comparatively easy way to progress both quests). Either way, the party learn that the Guild intends to ambush the Stone Lord at the Counting House . Both major quests are progressed there, and afterwards in the Abandoned Cistern . Fight at the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] The fight between the Guild and the Zhentarim is about to break out “ Two sides, each itching to draw blades against the other. „ — Lae'zel When the party returns to the Guildhall, they find out the Zhentarim are ready to make their own move. Their leader starts a dialogue, prompting the party to pick a side in their coup attempt. This leader can be Roah Moonglow , Boss Friol , or Trinoda [ 7 ] The encounter unfolds based on the outcome of the Abandoned Cistern battle: Hostile Takeover: If Minsc is killed, or the Zhentarim leader (Roah or Friol) dies during the fight, the Zhentarim automatically attack the party and the Guild. Proposed Alliance: If the Zhentarim leader survives, they propose an alliance to overthrow Nine-Fingers Keene and install the Zhentarim as the city's new criminal underlords. The party can choose to accept this coup or side with the Guild and eliminate the Zhentarim. Failed Takeover: If the Zhentarim agents in the Guildhall are killed prior to this encounter, the leader is surprised by the lack of backup and cancels the takeover attempt entirely. Following the battle, the surviving faction leader pledges their support to the party for the final conflict against the Absolute . However, additional complications can still arise: Betraying the Zhentarim: If the party side with Roah Moonglow or Boss Friol , they can subsequently claim the Guildhall for themselves. This choice immediately triggers a new combat encounter with the Zhentarim. The Minsc Complication: If the party successfully recruit Minsc and side with the Guild while he is present, speaking to Nine-Fingers Keene after the battle triggers a tense confrontation. The player character must succeed in a dialogue check to convince Minsc not to attack her. Lesser quests [ edit section | visual editor ] If Roah Moonglow (or Boss Friol) dies during the fight, the party can loot a Stolen Gold Bag from their corpse after the battle. If the party sides with the Zhentarim, the pouch can be pickpocketed from either of them. It can then be returned to Head Banker Rakath Glitterbeard as part of the quest ⁠ Return Rakath's Gold . One of the Zhentarim agents, Slick Inatra , can take the Caravan Strongbox from the party, if they acquired it from Zarys to deliver throughout the ⁠ Find the Missing Shipment quest and never opened it. While the quest itself is completed in Act One one way or another, the reward of 975 gp can still be obtained from Inatra. This money cannot be looted from her if she is killed. Bursar Uktar offers gold for each High Security Vault Key of the Counting House , provided the contents of the corresponding vault remain untouched. He is not interested in the keys to the regular vaults of plain safes. If Mol is present, the quest ⁠ Find Mol can finally be resolved by speaking with her. She can be given her eyepatch if it was obtained in the Mind Flayer Colony . If the party have already been to the House of Hope and obtained Mol's contract with Raphael , they can hand it to Mol and talk about it. The party can also inform her about killing Raphael, which upsets Mol greatly. Otherwise, if she is not told about Raphael's demise, and the interacting party member expresses approval of her decision, Mol can be persuaded to help in the final fight (requires DC 15 Persuasion Check ). [ 8 ] Speaking with Cheeky Nora (if she is present) can start an unlisted quest to set straight the relationship between her and the bugbear Severn who runs the Guildhall bar. Nora is fixated on gaining Severn's attention as he recently broke off with her. Inspirations and rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Resolving the fight by picking either side gives the following inspiration: ⁠ The Wealth of Morality ( Noble backgrounds) Siding with the Guild in the fight grants the following inspirations: ⁠ Honour Among Thieves ( Criminal backgrounds) ⁠ Woman of Her Word ( Charlatan backgrounds) Siding with the Zhentarim grants the following inspirations (mutually exclusive with those provided by the other choice): ⁠ It's Just Business ( Criminal backgrounds) ⁠ Winged Serpent of Gold ( Charlatan backgrounds) If Mol promises to join in the final battle, the following inspiration is granted (if not obtained prior): ⁠ An Apocalyptic Deal ( Noble backgrounds) Depending on the party's choice, the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest is updated, adding either Black Fist Enforcers or Guildmaster Keene's Fixers to the list of possible options in the endgame. Convincing Mol to provide aid in the final battle adds the Fetcher's Favour buff in the endgame. ## Gur Camp
- **来源**: [Gur Camp](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Gur_Camp)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Street view of the Gur Camp Rivington Abandoned Windmill ← Gur Camp ↓ Requisitioned Barn The Gur Camp is a Location within Rivington in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Welcome, friend. You've joined us as we honour our fallen dead - a sombre time. And you have brought a sombre guest. I did not think you would willingly return, spawn. „ — Gandrel , hailing the party [ 1 ] Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Outside the camp 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 The Gur 4.2 Outside the camp 5 Related Literature 6 External Links 7 Footnotes and References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Gur Camp is the temporary home to a group of Gur monster hunters, led by Ulma . It is located on the top of the hill at X: 102 Y: -12 , north from the Requisitioned Barn and east of the Abandoned Windmill . The state of affairs in the Gur Camp depends heavily on the player character's decisions concerning Astarion and / or Gandrel in Act One . If Astarion was by any means betrayed by the party and turned in, all the Gur are dead, having been slaughtered by the vampire lord Cazador Szarr when he reclaimed Astarion for his diabolical ritual. Gandrel is the only one alive amidst the destroyed camp and becomes hostile to the party on sight. If the party defended Astarion from the monster hunter or never encountered the latter, they see the Gur performing a commemorizing ritual over a funeral pyre upon approaching. If Gandrel survives Act One, he is also present here. The same scene plays out if the party never recruited Astarion, or disposed of him in any other way before meeting the Gur, or he is not present at the moment. However, if Ulma is alive, she is always conducting the aforementioned rite upon the party approaching. A passive DC 15 Religion Check allows to recognize the meaning of the ceremony. [ 2 ] Conversation with her starts automatically. The layout of the dialogue also depends on whether Astarion is present in the party. Eventually, Ulma tells the story of her tribe and asks to help to ⁠ Investigate Cazador's Palace . If the party refuse, the Gur become hostile. Regardless of the outcome, the encounter may advance Astarion's personal quests, ⁠ The Pale Elf or ⁠ Call of the Blood . Bearing witness to the funeral ceremony may grant one or both of the following inspirations: ⁠ Skald's Song for characters with the Entertainer background ⁠ Solemn Farewell for characters with the Outlander background The Gur Camp after Cazador's assault [ 3 ] If defeated, Ulma drops The Undead Bane . If the camp has been massacred, most nomads' corpses can be looted for Uncommon varieties of weapons and armour as well. The barn in the far end of the camp is off-limits to enter. However, if a party member manages to get inside unnoticed (or if the camp has been massacred), a fair amount of arrows, potions, and Camp Supplies , as well as some alchemical ingredients in a locked chest (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check or having the Camp Chest Key ) can be looted from there. Outside the camp [ edit section | visual editor ] Behind the camp, three halflings - Tina Two-Thumbs , Slarmy , and Zeffy Softbluff are scavenging a broken cart, considering anyone who talks to them as competition for the food scraps in it. A bit farther from a cliff, an almost endless field with dozens of refugees' tents can be seen. Up on a hill to the of the camp, a beautiful vista on the River Chionthar , the Wyrm's Crossing bridge, and the city suburbs beyond the river opens. On a bench, a bottle of wine and abandoned locket can be taken. ## Hhune Mausoleum
- **来源**: [Hhune Mausoleum](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hhune_Mausoleum)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Hhune Mausoleum interior The Hhune Mausoleum is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . It can be accessed through the Graveyard of the Lower City. The aboveground entrance is on the northern side of the mortuary. Contents 1 Access 2 Overview 2.1 Hidden room 3 Related locations 4 Loot 5 External links Access [ edit section | visual editor ] The mausoleum can be accessed through the Lower City's Graveyard , on the northern side beside the mortuary at X: 17 Y: 41 . It requires either Hhune Mausoleum Key which can be found in the Knights of the Shield Hideout , in a Mahogany Wardrobe at X: -744 Y: 537 or DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to open the gate. Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Overview of the mausoleum The mausoleum contains one sarcophagus and several hidden ( DC 15 Perception Check ) tripwire traps. A hidden ( DC 20 Perception Check ) cracked tile east of the sarcophagus contains the Hhune Mausoleum Iron Key . Opening the sarcophagus requires passing a DC 15 Strength Check check. Inside the sarcophagus is the Hhune Mausoleum Golden Key and a note, THE LEGACY OF HHUNE , which states: "KNEEL WITH THE WEIGHT OF ALL YOU VALUE AT HIS FEET, AND HE WILL REVEAL HIMSELF." At the foot of the sarcophagus between two columns, a tile is highlighted on a Perception check. If party members stand on it with a combined inventory weight of at least 400 kg (800 lbs), a hidden door opens along the southeastern wall of the mausoleum. A crumbling wall on the west end can be destroyed to access the Gorion Mausoleum . Hidden room [ edit section | visual editor ] Inside the hidden room is a Knights of the Shield statue and a Journal written by one of the members of the Knights. In the journal, the writer mentions being introduced to the Emperor , who they believed would be a "boon" to the Knights. Beneath the statue is a gilded chest which can be unlocked with the Hhune Mausoleum Golden Key, containing random valuables. Beside it is a heavy chest which can be opened with the Hhune Mausoleum Iron Key, containing more random valuables. The shelves contain various silver valuables. ## High Hall
- **来源**: [High Hall](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/High_Hall)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

High Hall Entrance High Hall is a Location within the Upper City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . This area is accessible only after travelling to the Morphic Pool to begin the final quest of Baldur's Gate 3. Contents 1 Overview 2 Locations 2.1 Watch Citadel and Surroundings 2.2 High Hall Courtyard 2.3 Upper City Sewers 2.4 High Hall 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 Githyanki 4.2 Other characters 4.3 Available to Speak with Dead 5 Creatures and enemies 6 Loot 6.1 Sold by Koll the Red 6.2 On the table in front of Koll the Red 6.3 Other 7 Related literature 8 Gallery 9 Notes and references 10 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the High Hall. The High Hall is a location in the final sequence of the game. It is reached after travelling through the Morphic Pool and the Astral Plane . The location is named after its main building, the High Hall, which the party must reach in order to resolve the final quest ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain . The location consists of a few subareas: the Watch Citadel where the local law enforcement is stationed, an underground sewer system and the High Hall itself with its courtyard. The party cannot fast-travel or go to camp while in the High Hall. Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] After travelling through the portal in the Astral Plane, the party members enter the High Hall from the western side. After one or more party members walk the stairs Kith'rak Voss confronts them. His reaction varies greatly depending on the choices they made just before inside the Astral Plane. He can be ultimately persuaded to join, aiding in the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. Otherwise he turns hostile. Voss is accompanied by Veteran Gish , Veteran Raider , and Veteran Warrior . Right after the confrontation, the path leads to the Watch Citadel. Watch Citadel and Surroundings [ edit section | visual editor ] The Watch Citadel is a small area visited before the High Hall's Courtyard. Any allies gathered during the game as part of the quest ⁠ Gather Your Allies appear here, and give short lines of support dialogue. Koll the Red can be traded with for last minute supplies. The Flaming Fist Beorn Wunterbrood asks the player character to finish his speech. The table next to Koll is covered in various magical equipment and consumables. However, taking any of these items counts as stealing and causes Koll to permanently vanish in a cloud of smoke – along with his remaining items on the table. This also causes Beorn Wunterbrood and any nearby characters gathered as part of the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest to become hostile – preventing the party from using their Gather Your Allies abilities. [ 1 ] The citadel has two exits: One on the eastern side, from there the party can walk through a hallway towards the main stairway of the courtyard, or the party can jump down into a sewage stream, where a rusted iron gate can be destroyed, revealing an entrance into the Upper City Sewers. One on the northern side, going through a bell tower, this route also ends up at the main stairway. The bell tower itself can be climbed, atop is a Winged Horror and a locked chest ( DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check containing gold, a Silver Ingot , a Potion of Animal Speaking and an Uncommon arrow. While approaching the stairway multiple unnamed civilians flee downstairs, running towards the Watch Citadel. Among them is one named character called Wrenfrew the Barker . [ 2 ] While on the stairs a cutscene starts where multiple Watch guards flee from a Mind Flayer and run outside the gate. Two of them are killed. The party can then speak with the guards, lead by Watchman Gyordi , and persuade them to help in the coming courtyard fight. Before entering the large gate towards the courtyard the end-game party can go north and / or south. To the south are two civilians which turn into Mind Flayers and attack the party. To the north a platform can be jumped upon which eventually leads to the northern entrance of the sewers. The entrance is in a small room with a metal door. In the room is a locked ( DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check ) Gilded Chest containing gold, Pearl , Purple Worm Toxin , Elixir of Guileful Movement , Elixir of Psychic Resistance and a Potion of Angelic Reprieve . High Hall Courtyard [ edit section | visual editor ] The High Hall and its courtyard (by Joannie Leblanc) The High Hall Courtyard is a large area before the High Hall proper. It can be entered by going through a large opened gate. On the other side is a large host of enemies consisting of Absolutist cultists, Winged Horrors , Goblins , an Ogre , a Spectator , an Illithid Arcanist and several Mind Flayers . Entering the courtyard causes the enemies to attack. However, it is possible to bypass this battle by approaching the High Hall from the northern or southern routes – or taking the sewers. It is also possible to only fight parts of the host of enemies by not running too far into them. Just above the gate is a room where a lever opens and closes the main gate. In the northeastern end of the courtyard, behind a locked door, Civilian [ 3 ] , Tilly and Robyn have managed to stay hidden, paralyzed by fear. They can be fought or convinced to leave by talking to them through the door. Inside their hiding room is only a note to the kitchen staff . There is another locked door which leads to a balcony with a locked ( DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check ) Heavy Chest containing a Potion of Supreme Healing . While fighting through the courtyard the party must eventually reach the stairway which leads to High Hall proper, this is near where the Spectator is. A noble lies dead on the floor, and next to him are Legal Notes . On the wall next to him is a Memory Brain Jar . [ 4 ] At a small table on the north side of the stairs to high hall lies A Home for Every Working Baldurian! . Opening the large doors leads to the High Hall, where the party must climb up to reach The Netherbrain . Upper City Sewers [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the Upper City Sewers. Underneath the Upper City Courtyard lies the Upper City Sewers, its main purpose being an alternative route towards the High Hall proper. It can be entered in two ways: Directly outside of the Watch Citadel (where all allies have gathered) by jumping into the small sewage river to the south and breaking open the rusted iron gate at X: 258 Y: 33 . After it is broken down, the sewers can be entered from the south side. Going north from the Watch Citadel, head up the stairways – but turn left towards the north before entering through the lifted gate. A broken piece of road serves as a platform that can be jumped upon. Another jump forwards leads to a tower-like structure. The party can jump down on a balcony which leads to a small room with a metal door that can be used to enter the sewers (at X: 263 Y: 126 ). This route is patrolled by Winged Horrors . If the party enters via the southern entrance they find themselves in a sewage stream. Inside this room is a Traveller's Chest which contains a Potion of Angelic Reprieve . Nearby is a gate which can be unlocked by a lever (highlighted by a DC 5 Perception Check ). The room after the gate contains a Goblin Boss and three Cranium Rats . The metal door which is used as northern entrance also ends up in this room. At the east side of the room is a door which leads to the main area of the sewers. It is a large room with a tentacle protruding through the roof into a reservoir of sewage. The northern side features a blocked path where Merug 'Curly' Dugald is buried under a pile of rubble ( X: -1477 Y: 3160 ). He carries a High Hall Key , used to open the heavy oak doors while climbing the High Hall proper. The southern hallway remains open. Once a party member enters the room, all enemies there turn hostile and attack. They consist of Goblins , Necromites , multiple Followers of the Absolute , an Illithid Arcanist and the Death Knight Stalker Svignee . At the end of the main area another door leads to a small room, containing a locked Wooden Chest ( DC 7 Sleight of Hand Check ), contains gold, Scroll of Polymorph , Trap Disarm Toolkit and a Potion of Supreme Healing . There is a short stairway leading to another metal door, which connects to the back to the High Hall Courtyard. Ascending to the upper level brings the party to a hidden chamber and an alternative path into the heart of the citadel. A concealed button in the room unlocks a secret doorway which provides access to the courtyard. In the following room is a locked door that cannot be lockpicked; the only way out is walking up the small stairway and jumping out of the half broken wall. The party can jump down into the courtyard, or jump across a series of wooden platforms to bypass the main defenses and enter the High Hall directly. High Hall [ edit section | visual editor ] The High Hall proper (by Joannie Leblanc) The High Hall itself is located just past the courtyard, through a large double door. In the entry area party members can interact with the brain stem in the middle of the building. Doing so causes all party members to become Mindbroken thereby requiring several DC  20 Constitution Saving Throw to prevent becoming Stunned . The Netherbrain cautions that this is not the right place and the party must rise first to join it. On a small table lies a Court Register . Inside a display case is a Potion of Superior Healing and a Scroll of Phantasmal Killer . The way leads forward to doors on the left and right. Once a party member crosses either door or upon being sighted by enemies, combats starts with Intellect Devourers , Bhaal cultists , and a Nautiloid . The Nautiloid marks the floor in multiple places with either a glowing yellow circle or a smaller glowing white circle. The yellow ones will be blasted by a Nautiloid Airstrike and the white ones will receive Mind Flayer Reinforcements , consisting of one Mind Flayer and two Intellect Gluttons . The route going to the left (north side) is blocked by a heavy oak door, which can be unlocked with the High Hall Key or by lock picking. The path continues upward and a Gilded Chest is visible after a jump. It contains a Potion of Angelic Slumber . [ 5 ] The route going to the right (south) goes up similarly and at some point a Crumbling Statue blocks the way. It can be pushed over using Shove , succeeding a DC 20 Strength Check . After falling, the party can walk over it and continue. Both stairs lead to a door at the top of the High Hall. If at least one party member traverses through it towards the stem of the Netherbrain combat ends. Once here, the party can use a restoration pod (not available on Tactician or Honour difficulty , alternatives are advisable) to heal, and then traverse up the stem to the final area ⁠ Atop the Netherbrain . Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain ⁠ Gather Your Allies Characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Characters available are based on those recruited as allies (see quest: ⁠ Gather Your Allies ). ## Highberry's Home
- **来源**: [Highberry's Home](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Highberry's_Home)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Highberry's home - view from the front street Lower City Forge of the Nine ↑ Bonecloak's Apothecary ← Highberry's Home → Baldur's Mouth ↓ Sorcerous Sundries Highberry's Home is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ We're lucky to be blessed with a rather spacious one - seems cruel to let it go unused if there are children in need. „ — Cora Highberry , describing her house Contents 1 Overview 2 The house layout 2.1 Ground floor 2.2 First floor 2.3 Basement 2.4 Roof 3 Involvement 3.1 The wine festival 4 Related quests 5 Characters 5.1 Residents 5.2 Wine traders and workers 5.3 Patrons 5.4 Assassins 5.5 Other 6 Loot 7 Related literature 8 External links 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Highberry's Home is a large building located directly north of Sorcerous Sundries . It has two spacious stories and a basement. The main entrance to Highberry's Home is at X: 14 Y: -43 . The house has several more entrances from balconies at its backside and on the first floor at X: 0 Y: -30 , X: 1 Y: -37 , and X: 14 Y: -37 respectively, available via means of spatial movement such as Grant Flight or Misty Step . All entrances except the main one are red-outlined. Highberry's Home belongs to an elderly halfling couple, Cora and Roger Highberry , who recently adopted two orphaned children, Timmy and Molly . [ 1 ] As the party arrive in Baldur's Gate, the Highberrys are preparing to hold a wine festival to raise funds for their young wards. As Cora Highberry has been marked as a quarry for a serial killer , the actual state of the building depends on the state and (if started) progress of the party's involvement in the ⁠ Investigate the Murders and ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal quests. The house layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The ground floor consists of a spacious living room with an adjacent smaller kitchen. The wooden chest in the corner can be looted for gold and random rare alchemical ingredients. On the kitchen mantelpiece lies the Wine Cellar Key , which opens the red-outlined hatch near the kitchen entrance, leading to the house basement. First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] On the first floor is a small study with a desk; several letters concerning one of the Highberrys' wards, Molly, lie atop it. A red-outlined door leads to the bedroom, where another wooden chest with minor loot can be found. Both first-floor balconies lead into this room. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] The basement can be accessed through a locked hatch. Inside, a DC 15 Perception Check attracts the party's attention to a painting on the wall. If the party approach, another DC 20 Perception Check highlights a Loose Plank , which conceals Highberry's Strongbox Key . The strongbox itself is hidden behind the painting and contains an Elixir of Universal Resistance and a Potion of Flying . The half-round bottle rack in the far end of the basement contains several health potions of random quality. Other containers around the cellar may keep fresh Camp Supplies . Behind the door at the far end of the basement is a small study divided in two by a curtain. A stack of scrolls here contains a random scroll up to Rare grade. Behind the curtain is a trapped heavy chest ( DC 15 Perception Check to detect trap, DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to disarm it, and DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick) holds a pile of gold and a Gold Ingot , with another wooden chest aside it (not trapped, but requiring DC 20 Perception Check to lockpick) storing more gold. Roof [ edit section | visual editor ] The roof can be the place where Tara the tressym can be met for the third time in a playthrough, provided that two previous encounters (on the Open Hand Temple roof and atop the Devil's Fee ) already happened. If encountered here, she can sell Slinging Shoes . A loose plank on the roof at X: 0 Y: -40 is noticed with a DC 15 Perception Check . It hides several random useful items, possibly including Trap Disarm Toolkit , Thieves' Tools , potions of Flying or Speed , and some gold. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The wine festival [ edit section | visual editor ] Highberrys' wine festival in its height. If the party started the ⁠ Investigate the Murders and ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal quests, the Wine Festival is taking place on the front porch of the Highberrys' mansion. Several traders and connoisseurs offer their wines to the public. However, one of them, Master Meztli, is actually the disguised serial killer Dolor , who is planning to murder Cora Highberry (along with several other quarries) to become an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal . Among the festival patrons are four doppelgangers , who can be recognized by their signature four-letters names. If the party have any of the quests active and trigger the wine festival plot branch by approaching the event close enough , they can initiate dialogue with Cora and "Metzli" and try and prevent the murder. They may also allow Dolor to commit his crime. The former option leads to a fight with Dolor and his shapeshifted assistants. Dolor, however, accuses the party of "sullying the sacrifice with knowledge" and attempts to teleport away on his first turn. If he succeeds, the shapeshifters prefer to attack the party and not Dolor's marked victim, and Cora Highberry most likely survives. Revealing Dolor's murder plot may grant one or both of the following inspirations: ⁠ Soured Taste ( Guild Artisan backgrounds) - for detecting the poisoned bottle ⁠ Wine Connoisseur ( Noble backgrounds) - for warning Cora Highberry If the Wine Festival ends and Cora and Roger Higberry are not killed by Dolor, both might be found inside the house with two orphans for whom they provide care. If the party then speak with Cora Highberry, she thanks the party for saving her life and rewards them with gold. Roger Highberry can be pickpocketed for the Counting House Vault nº4 Key . If the plot branch was triggered, but the party never started a dialogue with Cora, after a long rest both she and her husband Roger can be found dead in their bedroom on the first floor. Both (now twice-orphaned) children wander around the ground floor. If neither quest is active, Dolor is not present, and the festival has not started yet. The Highberrys can then be found inside their house and spoken with about the upcoming festival.
