## Old Garlow's Place
- **来源**: [Old Garlow's Place](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Old_Garlow's_Place)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Overview of the Old Garlow's Place Lower City Flymm's Cobblers ↑ Beehive General Goods ← Old Garlow's Place → Felogyr's Fireworks Old Garlow's Place is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ A nice old man called Mr. Garlow used to live here, but his neighbour said he doesn't live here any more. „ — Kled , in a note left for his fellows in Barren's Coop Contents 1 Overview 2 Ground floor 3 First floor 4 Second floor and the roof 5 Basement 6 Outside the building 7 Related locations 8 Related quests 9 Characters 9.1 Anti-Hag Support Group 9.2 The Dead Eyes 9.3 Outside 9.4 Creatures 9.5 Previous residents 10 Loot 11 Related literature 12 Bugs 13 External links 14 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Old Garlow's Place is a house in the Heapside district of Baldur's Gate, standing on a rocky cliff on the shore of the River Chionthar . It has two stories, an attic and a basement. The property fell into disrepair after its previous owner Garlow left for Calimshan , and is now deemed unsafe for habitation by the city authorities. However, the city life abhors the vacuum, and the seemingly empty house turns out to be quite occupied, if the party explore it. The particular set of the current inhabitants of the Old Garlow's depends on the decisions taken by the party in Act One during the ⁠ Save Mayrina quest. If the party saved Mayrina from the hag who tricked her, the building has become a base of operations for the Anti-Hag Support Group , founded and run by Mayrina. However, the group leader herself is indisposed when first approached, and the party may investigate and help Mayrina and her newfound fellows-in-misery. If the party sided with the hag in Sunlit Wetlands , or never encountered neither her nor Mayrina, the house has become a hideout for a group of thugs calling themselves the Dead Eyes , who try to operate in the Lower City athwart the Guild . However, they do not know that the Guild is already watching them. Ground floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The entrance to the ground floor at X: -48 Y: -127 is locked (the door requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick). Inside, the first two rooms are empty, with old rickety pieces of furniture along the walls. A Traveller's chest at X: -43 Y: -138 contains minor loot. The house inhabitants (whoever they are) wait in the third room, which resembles a large salon. In this room, some containers may keep fresh Camp Supplies . Also, a bottle of Antidote can be taken from the fireplace shelf. At X: -59 Y: -142 is a hatch leading to the basement, and on the opposite wall a strongbox is clearly seen. The stairs above the hatch lead to the first floor of the building. If the building is occupied by the Anti-Hag Support Group, its members Adrielle , Kled and Jatlo can be found in the salon. Upon entering the main room, the dialogue starts automatically, and the party must succeed an ability check to convince them of their peacefulness, otherwise they attack. If Hydrangea Wubb was saved in Act One , she is also present in the room. She recognizes the party members and stops the others from hostility. Also, throughout the dialogue it can be seen that the only one who supports paranoid moods in the group members is Jatlo. If the Hag Survivors attack, it is enough to defeat him only to stop the fight. After the group is placated, they ask to check out for their leader Mayrina upstairs. If the building is occupied by the group of thugs calling themselves "The Dead Eyes" , they are hostile on sight. Of them, Inku Neza , Jivin Mizzrym and Ulumpha can be encountered on the ground floor, while Hiero Lue patrols the stairs back and forth. First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The first floor has a single room and a balcony running around two of its sides. In its middle there are two areas of destructable rotten floorboards, which can be used in the battle by any side. The only relatively new wardrobe here contains several sets of random Camp Clothing of medium and citizen quality. In case of Anti-Hag Support Group, their leader Mayrina can be found on the first floor, hexed into a sheep. If Connor Vinderblad was resurrected in Act One , he can also be found here. The vicious sniggers are heard in the room; if inspecting, the party quickly finds its source: a Voodoo doll . All possible ways to dispel the hex and the following actions are described at the ⁠ Help the Hag Survivors quest page. If the building became a hideout for the Dead Eyes, their leader Aideen Ni Chuirc is on the first with her sister Maggie Ni Chuirc . They turn hostile to the party with the rest of the gang. Second floor and the roof [ edit section | visual editor ] In the far eastern end of the room in the first floor at X: -46 Y: -145 is a ladder leading to the small attic. In the attic stands an unlocked heavy chest with minor loot. Some containers around it can be looted for fresh Camp Supplies. A door from the attic leads to the open space on the roof with nothing remarkable on it, except the scape of the riverside. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] The basement of the Old Garlow's Place Next to the stairs, a hatch at X: -59 Y: -142 allows access to Old Garlow's Basement. The basement consists of several rooms. In the central one, five Blast Mines are planted in the floor. The farmost door is locked. When approaching it, a DC 15 Perception Check highlights a Marble Plate in the northeast corner. Adding weight to it moves aside a section of the wall, opening a hidden cave. Inside is an unlocked opulent chest; the area in front of it is trapped by three more Blast Mines. One of mines is planted adjacent to the Acid Barrel , which most surely will be destroyed if the mine detonates. The chest contains gold, random valuables and the Old Garlow's Basement Backroom Key . The key opens the door to the locked room, which otherwise requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. Containers in the locked room may keep random potions, random arrows (possibly Rare or Very rare ), or various alchemical ingredients. The wooden chest contains minor loot. A letter from the previous owner of the building, Garlow , lies on the cupboard, addressed to any "new inhabitants". Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] There is a path winding around the western side of the Old Garlow's Place. Following it via a series of jumps leads down to a small stripe of the sandy beach, where approximately at X: -33 Y: -164 a DC 18 Survival Check allows to notice a Dirt Mound. The buried chest contains a random Very rare scroll, a random arrow, gold and random valuables. The narrow streight in the rocky cliff can be clearly seen from inside the basement (behind the opulent chest in the hidden cave), but is inactive and thus cannot be used as an entrance to the building or as the exit outside. In front of the building, two dock workers, Ormont and Tugelnhorn , are washing clothes in a street water basin and arguing about holding a strike among the dockers' crew. Ormont claims that the working conditions are unbearable unless the workers vouch for their rights, while Tugelnhorn tries to talk him down. ## Old Jol's
- **来源**: [Old Jol's](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Old_Jol's)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Overview of Old Jol's house Lower City Baldur's Mouth ↑ Sorcerous Sundries ← Old Jol's ↓ Guildhall Entrance Old Jol's is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ This is Jol's house. No letters, no clerics, no herb-sellers, no potion-peddlers and NO Steel Watch . „ — Plaque at the door of Old Jol's Home Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Old Jol's is a small one-storied private building located in Eastway district of Baldur's Gate, south of across the Baldur's Mouth . The only entrance is at X: 55 Y: -79 . It is red-outlined, and breaking in without means of concealment inevitably draws the attention of the guards. One of them, Fist Ernestus , stands constantly near the Baldur's Mouth corner, and the building is in his direct sight. Inside the house is a locked wooden chest (requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick). Further exploring the only room, a DC 15 Perception Check highlights Jol's Chest Key under the wardrobe, though it does not work on the chest. Inside the chest is gold and minor random loot. Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] On the stairs ground to the east of the Old Jol's Mama Falice scolds Hazelnut for running away from the place they both stay. On the stairs ground down the building are remnants of a destroyed Steel Watcher . It cannot be looted, but upon interacting the Narrator prompts the following: "Unit defective - return to the Steel Watch Foundry at the West Docks ." . This can help the party to locate the foundry if they do not have any hints on it yet. ## Open Hand Temple
- **来源**: [Open Hand Temple](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Open_Hand_Temple)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Scenic view of the Open Hand Temple Rivington South Span Checkpoint ↑ Open Hand Temple → Sword Coast Couriers ↓ Circus of the Last Days The Open Hand Temple is a Location within Rivington in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ You must be new here - quite the time to be passing through. Here, we give thanks to Ilmater. Well, we did , until our high priest... Until he... „ — Yannis , mourning Father Lorgan Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 1.2 Main nave 1.3 Infirmary, dormitories and kitchen 1.4 Graveyard 1.5 Roof 1.6 Other encounters nearby 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 Clergy 4.2 Other 4.3 Outside, near the building 4.4 Available to Speak with Dead 5 Loot 6 Related Literature 7 External links 8 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Front view of the Open Hand Temple The Open Hand Temple is a large shrine located south of the South Span Checkpoint and across the road from the Sword Coast Couriers . The temple is dedicated to the worship of Ilmater , and until recent events was a centre of healing, feeding and almsgiving for numerous waves of refugees fleeing the approaching armies of the Absolute . Yet worship here, and aiding the bereaved, has been suspended due to the recent murder of the head priest . The temple building consists of the large main nave, a back annex for the infirmary, dormitory and kitchen, and an inner courtyard. In the centre is a high belfry providing a fine vista onto the whole of Rivington and beyond. The temple's roof and underground area can be explored as well. The underground has a cellar with a crypt, connected to a large natural cave. Behind the temple is a small graveyard, adjacent to the Circus of the Last Days territory. Access [ edit section | visual editor ] The main entrance to the temple is at X: -44 Y: -6 . However, it can also be accessed at several points: A side door to the kitchen at X: -63 Y: 16 - accessible from the side path to the west of the South Span Checkpoint at X: -7 Y: 20 , or after climbing up the slope from the Western Beach, starting approximately at X: -84 Y: 61 , or using knotted roots at X: -50 Y: 73 An iron gate from the grounds of the Circus of the Last Days at X: -74 Y: -13 (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick) - leads into the inner yard of the temple An iron fence from the grounds of the Circus of the Last Days at X: -103 Y: -39 (requires DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick) Traversing (jumping) to the temple graveyard from behind the circus ringmaster's tent, approximately at X: -97 Y: -29 The iron fence and the jumping route from the circus lead into the graveyard, from where the temple dormitories can be entered via the door at X: -91 Y: 11 . It is red-outlined, but there is no one around to notice it. The inner temple structure is also accessible if exploring the cave area first, entering it from the riverbank at X: 5 Y: 74 . Inside, party members can use the lever at X: 28 Y: -1007 , which opens the movable wall into the temple cellar, or make a series of jumps from the cliff at X: 35 Y: -1034 to reach the cellar library. Either way, the ladder at X: 1 Y: -993 leads up into the temple through the kitchen hatch. Main nave [ edit section | visual editor ] Inside the main nave of the temple The main nave is a large rectangular building with a pool in the middle and several dining tables along both sides. The temple altar is at the far end of the temple. The doors to the infirmary and to the kitchen are to the left and the right from the altar respectively. Near the altar, Sister Yannis can be found arguing with Investigator Valeria over the crime committed within the shrine. Valeria, having found the most obvious explanation, does not want to look any further, while Yannis tries to convince her out of stopping the investigation. The party can speak to Yannis after Valeria leaves, and offer to conduct their own investigation. This initiates the quest ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders and may grant one or several of the following inspirations: ⁠ Assistant to the Extra-Planar Agent ( Sage background) ⁠ Drama Sleuth ( Entertainer background) ⁠ Trusting Your Instincts ( Folk Hero background) Sister Yannis explains where to find the crime scene and the bodies of both the murder victim and the refugee accused of killing him. She can also be asked for help finding Shirra Clarwen , to progress the quest ⁠ Help the Spirit of the Amulet . In the north-east corner of the nave, the party can encounter Brother Clements and Brother Bill discussing the tenets of their faith and Father Lorgan's death. Siding with Clements or Bill in the discussion grants one of the following mutually exclusive inspirations: ⁠ A Scorned Closed Heart ( Acolyte background) - for siding with Clements ⁠ A Wounded Open Heart ( Acolyte background) - for siding with Bill On the tables along the northern side of the nave, several Potions of Healing and Potions of Greater Healing can be stolen. Infirmary, dormitories and kitchen [ edit section | visual editor ] These three rooms form the back annex of the temple with the inner courtyard in the middle. The infirmary and the kitchen are adjacent to the main nave and to the belfry, while the dormitories circle the yard. The kitchen is on the northern side of the temple. Brother Donnick can be found here. Questioning him reveals that Lorgan was murdered in the nearby basement and Donnick often brought unusually large amounts of food down at his request. At X: -62 Y: 3 is an ornate wooden hatch leading to the cellar. Doors in the western and northern walls of the kitchen lead to the temple's dormitories and outside to the Western Beach . The infirmary occupies the southern half of the temple annex. Here Sister Rose the Penitent is tending to Father Lorgan's body at X: -59 Y: -23 . Initially, she takes the party for somebody in need for medical care. [ 1 ] However, if the ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders quest is in progress, she can give the party more details on the murder. Lorgan can be spoken to using Speak with Dead to gather additional information, and his chest key can be taken from him. The dormitories are in the farmost western part of the temple, with a door leading out to the graveyard. A wooden chest stands by the foot of each bed here (five total), all locked ( DC 10 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick, except the central one) and red-outlined (though no one walks in to notice any lockpicking). One of these chests contains Seraphic Pugilist Gloves . The central chest belonged to Father Lorgan. Unlike others, opening it requires his chest key or a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. After opening it a passive DC 10 Investigation Check is made to perceive a false bottom containing the abbot's journal . Bookcases and book shelves in the infirmary and in the dormitories are red-outlined, and may contain random spell scrolls of Rare and / or Very rare grade. Graveyard [ edit section | visual editor ] The graveyard can be accessed through the dormitories' door. Also, a locked iron fence leads into it from the grounds of the Circus of the Last Days . Thus, the temple graveyard can be used to bypass interacting with the circus guard to gain access to the circus. At X: -105 Y: -20 is a fresh Dirt Mound. From it, a casket with the body of the suspected murderer of Father Lorgan can be dug up. Brilgor can be spoken to with Speak with Dead to learn more details on the crime. Near the temple wall at X: -98 Y: -6 is a wooden chest with minor loot. Roof [ edit section | visual editor ] The scape of Rivington from the top of the temple belfry The roof can be accessed by climbing knotted roots starting at X: -50 Y: 11 . Alternatively, the party can also climb up the belfry through a door in the inner yard, and jump down to the roof using Feather Fall . In the middle area of the roof the tressym Tara can be encountered. The party's comments on seeing her and the layout of further dialogue with Tara depend heavily on whether Gale was recruited, and on whether he is present in the active party. If Gale was recruited, a passive DC 10 Perception Check is made to recognize Tara as his pet (regardless of his current presence). Talking with Tara progresses the quest ⁠ Find the Missing Letters . In her nest, she keeps a Bundle of Letters and a Ring of Blink . If Gale is in the party, she surrenders both items without much fuss, [ 2 ] and also agrees to stop eating carrier pigeons. If Gale is absent, convincing Tara requires several various ability checks with DC of at least 15. Retrieving the bundle of letters from Tara may earn either or both of the following inspirations: ⁠ Cat's Got Your Tongue? ( Outlander background) ⁠ Interrupted Communications ( Noble background) On the ground near the knotted roots leading to the roof, a DC 18 Survival Check highlights a buried treasure chest with random precious gems and a random spell scroll of the Very rare grade. Other encounters nearby [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes placed about the temple. Near the northern stairs to the temple entrance a news hawker yells out the latest events. One of her outcries mentions the death of Duke Stelmane , and the Emperor immediately reacts to this. Afar from the southern stairs leading to the temple doors two local civilians, Cormac and Brigid , discuss the robbery Cormac recently suffered from some bandits. They doubt it was the Guild , because the culprits have beaten the man as well. At the temple door a family of tiefling refugees led by Rozes Kallista beseech Novice Bramble to let them in, relying on the temple's charity to survive. ## Open Hand Temple Underground Area
- **来源**: [Open Hand Temple Underground Area](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Open_Hand_Temple_Underground_Area)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Open Hand Temple Cellar Rivington Western Beach ↑ Open Hand Temple ← Open Hand Temple Underground Area The Open Hand Temple Underground Area is a Location within Rivington in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I can go anywhere , but I still end up in crypts. Let's just find Shirra Clarwen and go. „ — Astarion , upon entering the temple crypt Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Cellar 1.2 Cave area 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 Cellar and crypt 4.2 Corpses in the cave area 4.3 Doppelgangers 5 Loot 6 Related literature 7 Footnotes and References Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The area beneath the Open Hand Temple consists of two distinctive parts: the temple cellar with a crypt, and adjacent large natural cave. The temple cellar can be accessed from the temple kitchen through the hatch at X: -62 Y: 3 . The caves under the temple have their own entrance from the Western Beach through the cave mouth at X: 5 Y: 74 . The party may need to move aside several boulders to enter the cave. Eventually these two areas connect with a movable wall at X: 28 Y: -1007 , which is opened with a lever on the wall or by pressing hidden buttons (see below). Otherwise, a series of jumps from the cliff at X: 35 Y: -1034 can be made to reach the cellar library (this route can be used in the opposite direction as well). Cellar [ edit section | visual editor ] Shirra Clarwen's sarcophagus. The hatch ladder initially leads into the storage, which in turn opens into a small prayer hall - presumably used for conducting the last rites for the dead. The small altar is smeared in blood - this is the place where the temple's high priest Father Lorgan was murdered. The prayer hall has two doors in its western and southern walls. To the south is a small library. There are a fair amount of lootable objects here: The bookshelf at X: 16 Y: -1024 contains several random scrolls The display case nearby contains a Elixir of See Invisibility . It is locked and trapped (requires DC 15 Perception Check to detect a trap, and two DC 20 Sleight of Hand Checks to disarm and lockpick it) The barrel behind it contains several healing potions of random quantity and grade. The bookcase at X: 10 Y: -1018 contains a Scroll of Arcane Lock , a Scroll of Dominate Person , and a vial of Holy Water . Behind the farmost bookshelf is a wall breach which can be used to reach the cave beyond. The room to the west of the prayer hall is a temple crypt. If the party have taken up the ⁠ Help the Spirit of the Amulet in Act One and currently have the Sentient Amulet in the inventory, the quest can be completed here by opening the sarcophagus where Shirra Clarwen is buried. In the central room are two buttons on the northeast and southeast walls, hidden behind movable Heraldic Signs. Both can be revealed with a successful DC 10 Perception Check . [ 1 ] Using these buttons grants access to the cave area. Opening the hidden door from the either side grants the inspiration ⁠ There's Always a Back Door for party members with the Criminal background. Cave area [ edit section | visual editor ] The natural cave behind the temple cellar When entering the cave from the temple cellar, the party come out on a stone ledge. In the middle of the cave is a large natural indenture, where three men are bantering about someone named Dolor , his weapons, and about searching "his place" located at the Flophouse . [ 2 ] . They become hostile on sight. During the fight, they are revealed as doppelgangers . One of them, Zomm , can be looted for the strange Flowery Key and spoken to via Speak with Dead . Asking them about the key gives a hint on where to continue the murders' investigation. After defeating them, the party can loot the part of the stone ledge behind the wooden doors at X: 42 Y: -1028 , which has been turned into a makeshift storage, and move on to the place where the shapeshifters were wandering. At X: 65 Y: -1029 lies the body of Penela Lumpensicks , which can be looted for Clown's Severed Torso and the note titled Illasera, the First . These items are the part of the ⁠ Find Dribbles the Clown quest. If already started, taking them progress the quest. Otherwise, party members simply comment on the scene and the gory loot. At X: 67 Y: -1017 is a hole, highlighted by a DC 5 Perception Check when approached. Inside is Stillmaker , a dagger which evolves the ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders quest upon picking up. Further in the cave at X: 89 Y: -1044 , the bodies of several tiefling refugees can be found in a makeshift camp. None of them can be spoken via Speak with Dead . The camp has several backpacks and a traveller's chest with minor loot. In the far end of the cave at X: 83 Y: -1004 is an unlocked wooden chest between two vents emanating the Cloudkill vapors. Also, at X: 24 Y: -1033 a heavy chest is hidden in cobwebs. Both chests contain random minor loot. ## Peartree House
- **来源**: [Peartree House](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Peartree_House)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Front door to Peartree House Lower City Baldur's Mouth ↑ Sorcerous Sundries ← Peartree House → Guildhall Entrance ↓ Barren's Coop Peartree House is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . Contents 1 Overview 2 Building layout 2.1 Ground floor 2.2 Basement 2.3 Outside the building 3 Related locations 4 Related quests 5 Characters 6 Loot 7 Related literature 8 External links 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Peartree House is a small private dwelling in the Eastway district of Baldur's Gate located close the huge outdoor staircase which leads from the Baldur's Mouth down to the Felogyr's Fireworks . It has one floor and a basement. The house belongs to Franc Peartree , an ill-fated agent to Enver Gortash's trade operations. However, Peartree is already dead by the time party reaches Act Three locations, and his housee is a restricted area. The only entrance to Peartree House is at X: 32 Y: -96 . The doors are nailed up, and a Flaming Fist 'investigation' triangle stands in front of entrance. The staircase and nearby streets are patrolled by a group of Flaming Fists accompanied by a Steel Watcher . They become hostile if they spot the party damaging the barricade or entering Peartree House. Using means of Invisibility or spells like Fog Cloud is recommended. In the mailbox lies a Soul Coin , which can be taken freely. Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Inside the only room lies the corpse of Franc Peartree, missing one hand. A note can be looted from his corpse which claims he was killed for helping the lordling . As the party may already know, this disdainful sobriquet is used by Orin the Red when speaking of Enver Gortash . The party can commune with Peartree using Speak with Dead . In the far corner, under the bench lies a copy of Bloodstained Parchment . Near the bench is a hatch leading to an important part of Peartree House. It is covered by a Traveller's Chest with minor loot inside, and must be moved aside to gain access. The hatch is locked can be opened with the key , hidden in one of the bookcases in the opposite corner or by DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. A DC 20 Perception Check reveals loose planks in the floor, where Peartree's Chest Key is hidden. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] Murder scene in the cellar The hatch leads to Peartree's basement, which consists of a study to the south and small workshop to the east. In the study (turned into a sacrifice chamber) lie the dead bodies of Courageous Little Kimmabeth and Cassie Wheynstown. Kimmabeth can be looted for of one of Orin's Ritual Notes , Yaga-Shura, the Second , [ 1 ] and the Clown's Severed Arm , which is a part of the quest ⁠ Find Dribbles the Clown . Also, a Longsword +1 can be pulled from his body. The workshop has several stands with several weapons, pieces of armour, and shields lying around (all common, except another Longsword +1). In the far corner is wooden chest with some gold. On the desk lies the ledger which sheds some light on Gortash's covert trade operations. [ 2 ] In the southern wall of this room is a built-in Strongbox , opened with Peartree's Chest Key or with a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check . It contains a Half Plate Armour +2 , a Shortsword +2 , and two Soul Coins . Outside the building [ edit section | visual editor ] Across the entrance to the Peartree House Saer Drana Hoyte and Filson Vago are speaking. They were trying to find Figaro's Facemaker's Boutique , but were misled by an explanation given by a citizen and got lost. They are considering whether to ask someone else or to try to retrace their own steps back. On the second level of the ruined belfry a bit farther lies a backpack with gold and random alchemical ingredients. However, as this race was not implemented in Baldur's Gate III , Orin had to use for his effigy heavyset, robust humans with light-ginger hair and beards. ↑ Two letters from Gortash found in the basement indicate that Peartree was blackmailed by the Archduke nominee into distributing weapons and armour for his armsdealing network, probably being chosen for his numerous connections among the Flaming Fists (as he served as a cook in the Basilisk Gate Barracks before retirement). Other books around the room suggest that the house owner deeply studied the matters of infernal planes and bargaining with their inhabitants. ↑ Two coins are in the basement strongbox and one more is ## Philgrave's Mansion
- **来源**: [Philgrave's Mansion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Philgrave's_Mansion)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Philgrave's Mansion from the waterside. Lower City Felogyr's Fireworks ↑ Philgrave's Mansion → Vonayn's Home Philgrave's Mansion is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Carrion calls himself a 'spirit medium'.<...> He has a mansion, down near the water. A forsaken place, dank and decayed as he is. „ — Lady Jannath , describing the whereabouts of Mystic Carrion Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 2 Mansion Layout 2.1 Ground Floor 2.2 First Floor 2.3 Top Floor 2.4 Basement 2.5 Outside, around the building 3 Heapside Strand beach 4 Waypoints 5 Related Locations 6 Related Quests 7 Characters 7.1 Strange beggars 7.2 Creatures 7.3 Outside, around the building 7.4 Heapside Strand beach 7.4.1 Non-player characters 7.4.2 Sahuagin assault 8 Loot 8.1 Mystic Carrion's sells 8.2 Buried Treasure 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Overview of the mansion and the adjacent beach. The decay of local flora is obvious Philgrave's Mansion is a large house located in the Brampton district of the Lower City , to the south of Felogyr's Fireworks and to the west from the Guild -controlled alleys. It has three floors and a basement. Philgrave's mansion is occupied by Mystic Carrion and his undead retinue. Their behaviour and foul odours concern the local citizens, though the Flaming Fist do nothing to investigate the problem. The trees and other plants around the mansion look blighted and dying as well, despite efforts to revive them. If both Astarion and Shadowheart are in the party, she initiates banter dialogue near the mansion, emphasizing the possible reason for this. Access [ edit section | visual editor ] Philgrave's Mansion can be entered via several ways: A locked door in a stone wall at X: -8 Y: -158 . It requires a DC 10 Perception Check to detect when first approached. When interacted with, a dialogue begins. Throughout it, another passive DC 15 Arcana Check reveals that the door requires a password to open. The only correct password "Secreta mortuorum" can be acquired reading either a Letter to Oskar Fevras [ 1 ] or a Parchment lying on a crate at X: 73 Y: -107 in the alley next to Bruc and Pishe's Emporium . [ 2 ] The door can also be opened by using the lever aside it in the mansion lobby. Finally, like most other doors, it can be lockpicked (requires DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check ), opened with Knock , or destroyed (having Medium Toughness ). A hole in the wall at X: 29 Y: -166 leads straight into the mansion basement. It is initially hidden behind several crates and requires DC 5 Perception Check to find. The crate covering it is red-outlined; moving it may be considered a transgression by the nearby NPCs. The hole can be used by Small and Tiny characters only (including those disguised and wildshaped as such). The balcony entrance at X: 17 Y: -169 allows entrance the third floor of the mansion. The balcony can be accessed by any means of spatial movement such as Misty Step or Grant Flight . A DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check is then required to lockpick the doors. Mansion Layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground Floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Combined map of the mansion: (1) Ground floor and surroundings (2) Basement (3) First floor (4) Top floor The ground floor is separated into the small lobby and the larger living room. A staircase from the lobby leads to the locked door (requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick) to the first floor. Mystic Carrion resides in the living room, accompanied by a Ghast named Ulnar . There are a number of caskets and coffins strewn about the salon. One is also placed in the lobby, under the stairs to the first floor. If any one is interacted with, the casket breaks open and an Ancient Servant breaks free. From time to time will-o-wisps resembling Soul Echoes appear in the room, and Carrion talks to them, calling them ghosts in his submission. The dialogue with Carrion starts automatically after entering the living room. Its layout differs, depending on whether the party have the ⁠ Free the Artist quest active and also on whether any party member succeeded in reading at least one page of the Necromancy of Thay (they need not be present at the moment). Otherwise, Carrion may act as a trader, selling several Very rare pieces of equipment. In the farmost part of the floor stands a locked wooden chest, containing a Torch of Revocation - a Story Item necessary to complete the ⁠ Free the Artist quest, as well as gold and random precious alchemical ingredients. The chest can be lockpicked DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check or opened with the key pickpocketed from Carrion. Otherwise, the torch is rewarded for completing the sub-quest ⁠ Find Mystic Carrion's Servant . It is possible as well to steal the torch from the chest using means of invisibility without ever speaking with Carrion. A small part of the first floor is completely separated by walls. Inside is a hatch which leads to the mansion basement. This area is accessed through a secret door on the middle floor. If the party have acted against Carrion, or if he is attacked, all the caskets in the room break open, releasing seven Ancient Servants, and combat begins with all characters on this floor, including Mystic Carrion and Ulnar. Attacking Carrion after agreeing to find his servant Thrumbo for him (but without siding with Thrumbo first) is one of the possible ways to earn the ⁠ Always Trust a Dishonest Person inspiration for the characters with the Charlatan background. Killing Carrion regardless of siding with Thrumbo grants the ⁠ An Overdue Slaughter inspiration for the Dark Urge characters. If the party side with Thrumbo in his conflict with Carrion, and kill Carrion, then Thrumbo and his fellow Strange Beggars come to the mansion and remain there in the living room, with Thrumbo acting as a trader from now on. First Floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The first floor of the mansion is a dusty salon with a staircase leading up to the top floor. It features several red-outlined bookcases, which may contain random spell scrolls. A ghoul named Ligus wanders between this floor and the top one. He does not react to the party breaking and entering the room, but stops them from accessing the stairs, telling them it is "not safe for guests" there. Repeated attempts to ascend the staircase against the warning make Ligus and his fellow creatures on the top floor hostile. The farmost end of the salon has a locked door ( DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check ), behind which is a macabre room filled with disfigured bodies and body parts. A Soul Coin can be found in the viscera on the table. A camouflaged stone door in this room at X: 16 Y: -154 (not highlighted by any ability checks) hides a ladder to the basement. Top Floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The upstairs area is inhabited by three more Ghouls - Carpal , Hamate , and Rectus ) and a Ghast Thenar . [ 3 ] In the far end is a locked door to the balcony. If entrance is gained from this point without any means of invisibility , Thenar asks the party to leave. He can be placated with a successful DC 15 Deception , Intimidation , or Persuasion Check . A failed check, or an attempt to proceed without one, makes all the ghouls hostile. A Gold Pendant is on the table upstairs next to the staircase, and a Red Carmine Mask on the table across the balcony. The room at X: 8 Y: -155 contains a Beggar's Portrait , which is highlighted by a DC 10 Perception Check . The portrait is warded with necrotic magic and requires passing a DC 15 Arcana Check . If the check is failed, the portrait issues a cloud of Darkness , and the interacting character suffers ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage, [ verify ] with DC  10 Wisdom Saving Throw . Success awards Thrumbo's Note , which progresses the ⁠ Find Mystic Carrion's Servant quest. There is also a wooden chest tucked in the corner. It contains gold, a random set of potions and / or spell scrolls, and a book titled Writin Exorcises penned by Thrumbo for his "brothers" to practice the alphabet. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] This is a separate location accessed either through the hatch in the isolated part of the ground floor, or through the hole from the rivershore outside. This is a laboratory which has seen use. Multiple alchemical ingredients can be found on the shelves and in containers here. The Bottle Racks in this basement are not empty, unlike similar containers elsewhere; they mostly keep useful elixirs and healing potions of various grade. A bookcase at X: -1502 Y: -130 may house random spell scrolls. On the working desk the stone reading easel contains the book titled A Mummy's Memories , which progresses the ⁠ End Mystic Carrion's Immortality quest, marking the entrance to the Ancient Lair on the map. A bottle of Elixir of Necrotic Resistance stands aside it. If the Dark Amethyst was not previously acquired in the Whispering Depths in Act One , it can be obtained here. Outside, around the building [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes placed around Philgrave's Mansion. Near the stairs leading to the Eastside district Druid Klarrvox is tending to a dying young tree, praying to Chantea to help it cure and bloom. In the alley between Philgrave's Mansion building and the Felogyr's Fireworks Battrick Degronce tries to make Fist Jimi Borleas see his concerns about the foul smell emanating from the house and strange lumping figures going out at night. Fist Jimi Borleas, however, is not interested in doing anything about the complaint and looks for the easiest explanation. Near the Heapside Strand Waypoint Silfy sells the Baldur's Mouth Gazette . Heapside Strand beach [ edit section | visual editor ] This is a short strip of beach going from the Philgrave's Mansion to the east, featuring several wooden berths with moored boats, a long wooden roadwalk ending with a round pergola, and a small fish market. Two stone stairs lead from the beach to the alley between Philgrave's Mansion and Felogyr's Fireworks shop. An Old Troutman here is a trader selling some seafood Camp Supplies . The only other building which has the exit onto the beach is Vonayn's Home , which is important to progress the quests initiated in the Philgrave's Mansion. Knotted roots from its terrace lead into the alleys controlled by the Guild . When the party approach the beach for the first time and reach approximately the X: 45 Y: -145 point, a pack of Sahuagin emerge from the sea. They focus on attacking the party, rather than nearby civilian NPCs. The Sahuagin Champion can be looted for random Valuables and a Smelly Bag , which contents the first (if veiled) mentioning of the Iron Throne in the game. Defending the locals from the sahuagin attack also results in a reward of gold from the nearest living NPC. The Heapside Strand beach also features several NPC vignettes. In the pergola in the end of a wooden berth Beulla Sandfoot and Fyrd Nuugh discuss the problems of smuggling food inside the city so that their business may remain unnoticed by the Guild and Nine-Fingers Keene in particular. Halfway up the stairs, on a landing, Glorissima is begging aloud for alms. Her son Meem Grayling looks sleepy and wants nothing except some rest. Two gnomes near the fish market, Rossina and Grout , are the only Forest Gnome NPCs found throughout the game. The Heapside Strand beach also provides a failsafe option [ verify ] in case the party have somehow lost one or more Netherstones while exploring the Iron Throne . In this case, the Netherstone(s) can be looted from the Sahuagin Champion, or bought off from the Old Troutman, or simply found inside a large fish lying on the sand between the farmost berths. Also, the corpses of any Iron Throne captives who were not saved from the underwater prison can be eventually washed out onto this beach. ## Rainforest's Home
- **来源**: [Rainforest's Home](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rainforest's_Home)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Front entrance to Rainforest's Home Lower City Crimson Draughts ↑ The Bibliophile ← Rainforest's Home → Beehive General Goods ↓ The Counting House Rainforest's Home is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . Contents 1 Overview 2 The house layout 2.1 Ground-floor and first-floor rooms 2.2 Ratin Sesescor 2.3 Rainforest's Basement 3 Related locations 4 Related quests 5 Characters 6 Loot 7 Related literature 8 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Backside of Rainforest's Home, more convenient for entering Rainforest's Home is a building in a row of private dwellings and small stores, which runs along Stormshore Street in the Steeps district of Baldur's Gate. It is built side-by-side with The Bibliophile and has two stories and a basement. The building can be entered both from the facade and from the backside. The front doors at X: -93 Y: -109 are locked and red-outlined. The street is overlooked by a patrol of Flaming Fists and a Steel Watcher . Guards will question the party member if they are spotted lockpicking the doors. Using means of Invisibility , spells like Fog Cloud , or entering turn-based mode can be helpful. Another way to get into the house is through the balcony at the rear side of the building (the balcony railing is broken, which allows party members to jump to it), or the party can try to find their way behind the fence using spells like Fly or Misty Step . The balcony door and the one under it at X: -88 Y: -124 are red-outlined, but not locked. Rainforest's Home was a dwelling of Alexander Rainforest , an ombudsman at Grey Harbour Docks . By the time the party reach Act Three , Rainforest is already dead. The house layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground-floor and first-floor rooms [ edit section | visual editor ] The corpse of the owner, Alexander Rainforest, lies on the first floor, empty of any loot and without one hand. His severed hand can be taken from the serial killer Dolor during the quest ⁠ Investigate the Murders . Alexander's corpse can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Under the spell, it tells that he was an ombudsman at the docks in life, but had been working for some time on an investigation into the peculiar ownership history of Candulhallow's Tombstones . A message from Alexander's friends lying on the cabinet nearby implies that his mates considered Rainforest to be totally obsessed with unveiling the truth about this building. Through the quest ⁠ Investigate the Murders , it is revealed that Alexander Rainforest was murdered by Dolor , a cultist of Bhaal , who wants to become an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal. On the ground floor, with a DC 10 Perception Check , party members can spot another copy of the Bloodstained Parchment with the list of murder targets, lying conveniently near the basement hatch. Ratin Sesescor [ edit section | visual editor ] Ratin Sesescor, the cheese lover Ratin Sesescor is a buoyant rat who is randomly running around the ground-floor and first-floor rooms within Rainforest's Home. If spoken to through Speak with Animals , it says that Alexander was their "cheese-dropper" until the "man in red" came and caused him to drop "some tasty red morsels" instead of cheese. The Cheese Record book lying on the table next to the bed sheds some light on Ratin's palate. If the player character asks whether Ratin realises that it ate human innards, they cynically mention that Alexander does not need them anymore. Should the player character continue trying to speak with Ratin, it will shoo them off with a minor threat, saying that the character's own smell is rather delicious and tempts them to taste the character's own "red morsels", even though this would not be very polite. Rainforest's Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] Murder scene in the basement The hatch under the stairs leads to the basement of Rainforest's Home. Upon descending into the basement, the party can spot a Blast Mine and the Tripwire which sets it off, both requiring DC 15 Perception Checks . Further ahead lies a ritual murder scene with a makeshift altar and two blue dragonborn victims. One of them, Winslow Reginol , can be looted of the Clown's Severed Foot and one of Orin's Ritual Notes . On the altar lies a Potion of Feather Fall , a Rope , and a Faded Scroll of Reversal . The door to the north leads into Rainforest's study, where a Traveller's Chest and a Stack of Scrolls can be looted. A Gilded Chest on the cabinet and another Traveller's Chest near it both contain a small amount of gold and minor random loot as well. Several documents regarding Alexander's investigation into Candulhallow's Tombstones are around the study. They describe suspicious activity around this establishment, including a letter from the Zhentarim agent Roah Moonglow . The eastern wall of the study, at X: 1424 Y: 1050 , is a disguised entrance to the rest of the basement; discovering it requires a DC 15 Perception Check . [ 1 ] Behind the wall, there is another series of traps (same combination as the basement entrance, same DC to spot). In the far corner of the hidden space, on a stone shelf, stands a Wooden Chest with minor loot. There are also some common weapons around the room. Near the chest lies Rainforest's Chest Key . A small storeroom to the south is also equipped with the same series of traps as the entrance. It has a Strongbox in the eastern wall that can be opened with the aforementioned key or by succeeding a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check . It contains gold and a random gem. ## Ramazith's Tower
- **来源**: [Ramazith's Tower](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Ramazith's_Tower)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

View from outside Ramazith's Tower is a Location within the Upper City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ I knew Lorroakan amassed knowledge like a dragon with its hoard, but never could I have imagined such wealth .<...> Study and catalogue it... Then share it with the Realms. After all, it does little good collecting dust in an old tower. „ — Rolan , after succeeding the tower to Lorroakan Contents 1 Overview 1.1 History and access 2 Building layout 2.1 Top floor 2.2 Middle floor 2.2.1 Weave Buttons 2.3 Bottom floor 3 Involvement 3.1 Rolan's fate 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 7 Creatures 8 Loot 9 Related literature 10 Gallery 11 Notes and references 12 External Links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Ramazith's tower is a major landmark of the city of Baldur's Gate, located in its Temples district. Its silhouette is clearly seen on the initial loading screen of the game. The tower is round and resembles a pagoda with its several concentrical levels decreasing in diameter from foundation to the top. Within the playthrough only three inner levels of the tower are accessible, as well as a balcony which encircles one of them and offer a marvellous vista on the whole city. The tower is connected to the magical shop of Sorcerous Sundries and to its vault , where the most precious items are stored. It is the location where the quest ⁠ Find the Nightsong which spans all three Acts of the game can be finally completed. The plot lines of several notable characters can also be brought to their conclusion here, updating the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. History and access [ edit section | visual editor ] As the tower name suggests, it was built by a famous wizard Ramazith Flamesinger more than a hundred years prior to the game events. After Ramazith disappeared, [ 1 ] the ownership of the tower (and of the magical shop as well) passed to an Amnian wizard Lorroakan . The latter, however, apparently saw both the tower and the shop only as a means to pursue his personal goals (as the party soon find out, the first and foremost of these is gaining immortality). The tower can be accessed only through a portal from the first floor of the Sorcerous Sundries. When they reach this part of the shop for the first time in a playthrough, they encounter Lorroakan's Projection at X: 14 Y: -72 . It opens four portals, each accompanied by a plaque. To reach the tower, the party must use the pale blue portal at X: 13 Y: -83 . The three others down and eject from the building whomever attempts to enter. The portal transports the party to the top floor of the Ramazith's Tower. Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Top floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The top floor of Ramazith's tower (by Stimona Milanova) The party arrive at the top floor of Ramazith's Tower via a portal in Sorcerous Sundries . Afterwards, they can return to the shop via the same portal. The top floor is a large, lavishly decorated round area, with walls lined up with seemingly endless bookshelves. Unfortunately, neither the shelves nor stacks of books around can be interacted with. On the tables and counters are various alchemical, astronomical, and magical devices. The top floor has several points of interest (listed here moving clockwise from the portal): At X: 4988 Y: 705 is an exit to the balcony, which can be used to move to the outer area of the middle floor of the tower via spells like Misty Step or Fly . Other such exits are at X: 4962 Y: 719 and at X: 4961 Y: 690 . At X: 4980 Y: 705 several pieces of furniture are magically suspended in the thin air. They also can be used as a bridge to jump down to the middle lever. However, if Lorroakan is alive, the furniture is red-outlined; jumping down is considered a crime. At X: 4977 Y: 693 is a runic circle prepared for the Nightsong, harmless for any other character to step over. The top floor features two small grounds above the main level, which can be reached via ladders at X: 4977 Y: 693 and X: 4975 Y: 719 . On the former is a Gilded Chest with gold and random Valuables , while the other has no remarkable items. Around the top floor are five small display cases and two large ones, which may contain random precious gems or Rare potions. One of the large cases in the centre ground always keeps a Potion of Supreme Healing . Middle floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The middle floor of Ramazith's tower (by Stimona Milanova) The middle floor consists of an indoor inner area and an outdoor outer ring. It can be reached by jumping down an aforementioned series of floating furniture, or using spatial movement spells from the top floor balconies. The inner area also consists of two concentrical rings connected with gilded metal stairs. When exploring this area, using the See Invisibility spell or potion is recommended. If no party member has an option to obtain the effect, they can take an Elixir of See Invisibility from a backpack on the outer ring (at X: 4979 Y: 704 ). The floor is densely trapped with Cloudkill vents and four Arcane Cannons . Detecting any of them here requires DC 15 Arcana Check , unlike most other locations. Around the area are several unlocked showcases, Opulent Chests and smaller Gilded Chests, which may contain gold, valuables, random alchemical ingredients and potions, as well as random arrows and very rare spell scrolls. The outer ring is available either via jumping through the windows on this floor or after demolishing the barricade at X: 4962 Y: 691 . Two Mage Hands roam constantly around the ring, casting Create Water on green patches lining the edges. The area has nothing of remark, except a patch of alchemical herbs at X: 4981 Y: 686 , and a Snakeskin Hat on the ground near the barricade. Weave Buttons [ edit section | visual editor ] The outer ring of the middle floor (by Stimona Milanova) Five pillars are scattered around this floor, each with a 'Weave Button' on the top and a plaque in front of them, which can be revealed with See Invisibility : At X: 4962 Y: 718 the Below button teleports the party to the bottom floor. At X: 4954 Y: 704 the Cleanup button activates gas vents around the room. At X: 4977 Y: 719 the Security button activates Arcane Cannons. At X: 4979 Y: 693 the Vault button teleports the party member who pressed it to the Sorcerous Vault . There is no way to teleport back to the Ramazith's Tower from there. The only pillar on the outer ring at X: 4995 Y: 706 is labelled as Artillery and fires a fireball from the top of the tower. Bottom floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The bottom floor, featuring two arcane barriers (by Stimona Milanova) The bottom floor is accessible via the Weave button marked "Below" on the middle floor. It can not be reached by jumping down from the middle floor; there is an invisible barrier blocking the way. This floor features two Globe of Invulnerability arcane barriers protecting the legendary staff Markoheshkir and the Robe of the Weave . In front of each is an invisible lever which can be revealed with See Invisibility and disabled by passing a DC 20 Arcana Check . Two stone statues labelled as Aspects of Athkatla are actually traps connected to these levers. If an Arcana check on a lever is failed, the statue casts Disintegrate on the interacting party member. Also, the failed check locks the party member in question out of another try for that lever; further attempts of this party member always result in the Aspect attacking them. Thus, the party has a limited number of tries to obtain the guarded items. A nearby display case is trapped ( DC 13 Perception Check to detect, DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to disarm) and contains the High Security Vault nº1 Key for The Counting House storage. Next to it is a Gilded Chest with gold, a Gold Ingot , random potions and the Sorcerous Sundries Mystery Door Key can be found here, which opens the door leading to the Southern part of the Sorcerous Vault . On the opposite side of the floor is another unlocked display case keeping the Scroll of Circle of Death . There is also a Weave button marked Above that teleports the party back to the middle floor. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] When the party teleport into the tower for the first time, a cutscene starts, showing Lorroakan and his retinue. The wizard is idling time while he awaits someone to bring him information on the Nightsong - or fetch the Nightsong herself. He is accompanied by an animated armour Krank , his servant Miklaur and his elemental myrmidons . The cutscene spills into a dialogue with Lorroakan, where they can inform him of the Nightsong's fate or bargain with him about bringing her to the tower. They can also deceive the wizard to win some time to make the ultimate decision. The layout of the dialogue directly depends on the party's choices in the end of Act Two . The party can also ask Lorroakan about the reasons he wants to lay hands on the "relic" and even make him to show the means he plans to use towards this end. If Gale is in the party, he chimes in and the two exchange mutually contemptuous phrases concerning true immortality. If Dame Aylin survives the events of Act Two and resides in the party's camp, she can be later informed about Lorroakan and his true intentions. In this case, she storms out of camp and moves to Ramazith's Tower. There, the quest ⁠ Find the Nightsong reaches its climactic conclusion. The party has options to side with Lorroakan or with Dame Aylin. Either way, the fight begins. If the party side with Aylin, she and Isobel add their unique aiding options to the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. Otherwise, the party receives 5000 gold from Lorroakan and his aid in the final battle. If the party betrays Dame Aylin to Lorroakan and later tells Isobel about this in camp, Isobel runs away to save Aylin, and her corpse can be found in the Ramazith's Tower after a long rest. The party's ultimate choice between siding with Lorroakan or with Dame Aylin may grant one or more of the following inspirations: ⁠ Always Trust a Dishonest Person ( Charlatan backgrounds) - for betraying Aylin ⁠ How High They Fall ( Haunted One backgrounds) - for killing Lorroakan ⁠ Never To Be Chained Again ( Folk Hero backgrounds) - for saving Aylin from Lorroakan ⁠ Stopping the Repetition of History ( Sage backgrounds) - for killing Lorroakan ⁠ The Karsus of Our Times ( Sage backgrounds) - for betraying Aylin Also, choosing surrender Dame Aylin to Lorroakan (regardless of bargaining about it with him prior) is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of the Crown and Paladins of Devotion . Rolan's fate [ edit section | visual editor ] If Rolan survives the events of Act One and Two , he is also present here. His choice of allegiance depends on whether the party saved his siblings from the Moonrise Towers Prison : if both were saved, he sides with the party. If either Cal or Lia died, he must be convinced via DC 20 Intimidation Check , DC 18 Persuasion Check , or DC 15 Arcana Check . Wizard characters have also an additional option via a DC 18 Strength Check check. [ 2 ] If both Rolan's siblings died, he inevitably sides with Lorroakan and cannot be convinced to reconsider. Rolan takes over the tower if he survives and the party side with Dame Aylin to complete ⁠ Find the Nightsong . He can be asked to help in the battle against the Absolute . [ 3 ] If he is asked about looting the tower, he allows the party to take whatever they like, save for books and scrolls. In this case, all containers on the three floors of the tower become available, and Rolan, despite his own words, does not object taking spell scrolls. After a long rest , Rolan becomes an ally for the ⁠ Gather Your Allies quest. If the party side with Lorroakan, but he is defeated in the battle, Rolan decides to capture Aylin himself. However, the task is beyond his strength: after a long rest, the party can find Rolan's corpse in Ramazith's tower and a threatening note from Aylin. [ verify ] If the party choose to attack Lorroakan themselves, Rolan instead confronts the party after Lorroakan is defeated, demanding to know what happened. To avoid another fight with Rolan, the party must succeed either a DC 18 Persuasion or Intimidation Check . ## Requisitioned Barn
- **来源**: [Requisitioned Barn](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Requisitioned_Barn)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Street view of Requisitioned Barn Rivington Gur Camp ↑ Arfur's Mansion ← Requisitioned Barn The Requisitioned Barn is a Location within Rivington in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ This isn't a glorious post, Fists, but it isn't a hard one, either. If you can't even guard a blasted shed, it's no wonder we're being replaced by Steel Watchers. „ — Nestor , berating his squad Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Guards 2 Donations 2.1 Looting the barn 3 Other encounters nearby 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 6.1 Flaming Fist 6.2 Traders 6.3 Refugees 6.4 Other 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Requisitioned Barn is located at X: 83 Y: -108 . It is currently in use as a storehouse for donations collected to be distributed among the refugees. The large rectangular building has several means of entry except the main one. At X: 99 Y: -114 are double doors, locked and guarded by a Flaming Fist. At X: 59 Y: -146 is the unguarded side door from a small balcony, overlooked from time to time by a patrolling guard inside. Guards [ edit section | visual editor ] The barn is guarded by a squad of the Flaming Fist under command of Manip Nestor . His subordinates are Fist Broadhorn , Fist Lochan , Fist Madigan , Fist Poole , Fist Rowan , and Fist Varone . Nestor (and presumably his whole squad) was previously based at Basilisk Gate Barracks , but has been temporarily assigned to Rivington. Fists Poole, Rowan and Varone guard the entrances to the barn outside, while Fists Madigan and Broadhorn patrol the building inside. Fist Lochan stands nearby, preoccupied with attempts to calm down a group of protesters led by Saer Grotpoll who demand the refugees be driven from Baldur's Gate. Fist Rowan is one of characters who might be chosen by Orin the Red as a disguise to threaten the party. [ 1 ] In this case, the corpse of real Rowan can be later found in the Bhaal Temple in Lower City . As with other possible disguises in Rivington , Orin tries to make the player character understand or agree with her mindset, but invariably takes her true form and, after some spiteful phrases, disappears. Donations [ edit section | visual editor ] Various goods donated to refugees Nestor and his squad are primarily charged with collecting and preserving various donations and distributing them among the refugees. The party can share some of their gold or food as a donation. While the money share is defined strictly as 500 gold , offering to share rations opens the generic barter window with Nestor. Passing a donation to Nestor may grant one or more of the following inspirations, depending on the party's choice: ⁠ Alms for the Unfortunate ( Noble background) - either money or food (any amount) ⁠ Food for the Soul ( Acolyte background) - food (at least 40 Camp Supplies ) [ 2 ] ⁠ Gifts of the Wilds ( Outlander background) - food only (any amount) ⁠ Sharing the Spoils ( Soldier background) - either money or food (any amount) ⁠ Spare What You Can ( Urchin background) - either money or food (any amount) Nestor can additionally be persuaded to gain passage into the barn, which would otherwise be considered trespassing . If the party have already started the ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys quest (see below), the roll requires DC 10. If they have not, they can ask Nestor to let them place their donations inside the barn themselves (and thus gain the entrance), but this requires a DC 20 roll. Any "donation" dialogue options are available when speaking to Nestor only before the party convinced him to grant access inside the barn. This possibility disappears as well if the party manage to sneak into the barn and are caught there. There are also several DC 20 checks on dialogue options for the party to explain their presence in the barn (or their need to enter); doing so grants the inspiration ⁠ Never Trust an Honest Person to party members with the Charlatan background. Fighter characters can also attempt a DC 18 Deception Check to convince Nestor that they are Flaming Fists reporting for duty. Looting the barn [ edit section | visual editor ] Inside the barn various containers are strewn about, keeping mainly Camp Supplies or simple camp garments. A live Pig occupies a small fold near the entrance, sincerely believing in his "emotional support role". The party can praise him, or call him "bacon". The party can try to stock up their own supplies from the barn, though all containers inside are red-outlined. Several of them may provide random Camp Clothing of Rich and / or Patriar grade. [ 3 ] Also, a backpack at X: 82 Y: -105 contains random potions and / or elixirs. If any guard spots a party member inside the barn, a dialogue is started automatically. Regardless of what is offered as an explanation, they are snapped to the main entrance, and the conversation continues with Nestor. If they are caught a second time, the only options left are to consent to arrest or to attack. [ 4 ] The crate with suspicious toys after detecting explosives inside The two major points of interest inside the barn are the Donations chest at X: 76 Y: -111 and the toy crate nearby. The Donations chest contains gold and random valuables. It is locked and requires DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick, or it can be opened with the Donation Chest Key kept by Nestor. Stealing donations from the chest may grant one or both of the following inspirations: ⁠ Donations Means 'Free' ( Criminal background) ⁠ Give Nothing Back ( Urchin background) The crate with stuffed bears nearby is a material part of the ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys quest. Upon approaching, a passive DC 15 Investigation Check is made; success marks the crate as a trap. If the quest has not been initiated yet, a successful check starts it. Disarming the chest requires DC 20 Sleight of Hand Check . Finding a box with the rigged toys grants the ⁠ Immoral Ingenuity inspiration to the characters with Guild Artisan background. If the trap was triggered, the explosion alerts all guards, and the player character almost inevitably needs to provide explanation for their presence in the barn. The Dark Urge in this case has an additional option to activate one of the remaining bears and toss it to Manip Nestor. Other encounters nearby [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several NPC vignettes placed around the barn. Near the main entrance stands a locked, red-outlined heavy chest. It can be opened with a DC 18 Sleight of Hand Check , or with a Munition Chest Key kept by Fist Poole . Inside is a Potion of Superior Healing , a Remedial Potion , an Elixir of Heroism and a Longsword +1 . Across the barn stands the trader Ferg Drogher . Interactions with him depend on whether Shadowheart is present in the active party - and if she is, on whether she remains loyal to Shar . If Shadowheart is not present, Ferg can be questioned about the source of his stock, and confesses to "purchasing" precious items from the refugees, in exchange providing them with real coin to meet their immediate needs. He then can be convinced through several ability checks to show his special goods. If Shadowheart is present and remains loyal to Shar, no convincing is needed. Regardless of her loyalties, interacting with him progresses Shadowheart's personal quest (both companion and origin). If Shadowheart is present and has abandoned Shar, he threatens her and directs her to the House of Grief to receive punishment. When this dialogue finishes, he walks away forever, locking the party out of the option to trade for his goods. At X: 59 Y: -126 stand Mattis and Mirkon (if they survived the events of Act One and Two ). Mattis recognizes the player character and confesses that he found some useful items to refill his stock in Moonrise Towers . He can be traded with afterwards. Several refugee children - Billy , Bobby , Elsa and Steffy play tag, running around a tree in front of Nestor's post. None of them can be spoken to, though if picked any of them cries out a random phrase as if the player character were playing with them. The refugee family Flintsplitter are standing around the bonfire near the barn. If spoken to, each of them reveal arguably stereotypical looks onto relationship between spouses and parents-in-law: Ramona Flintsplitter grumbles about her son marrying Kristeen Hazel , with Gizelle Flintsplitter echoing along on the matter. Garron Flintsplitter tries to talk down them both. At X: 108 Y: -109 a hobgoblin Toadbreath sleeps on a low wooden deck. A Traveller's chest near him contains gold and random valuables; it can be opened with Toadbreath Stash Key . The letter inside states that the hobgoblin tried to get inside the city on the ground of placing his fortunes into the Counting House vault, but was denied to do so.
