## Upper City
- **来源**: [Upper City](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Upper_City)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

The Upper City in the midst of Illithid Invasion Upper City ↓ Lower City The Upper City is a region in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Beyond that gate is the Upper City, housing the great and the good of Baldur’s Gate. „ — Astarion Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Access 2 Locations 2.1 High Hall 2.2 Ramazith's Tower 2.3 Szarr Palace 2.4 Upper City Sewers 3 Related quests 4 Notable characters 5 Related literature 6 Gallery 7 Notes and references 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Upper City is a region in Baldur's Gate in Act Three . It is the wealthy district of Baldur's Gate, that lays north of the city's oldest wall and its namesake gate. It is home to the city's noble patriar families, who typically live in estates. Contrary to the rest of Baldur's Gate where the Fist operates, the upper city has its own law enforcement called The Watch . The Watch are well-trained and authorised to use lethal force if patriars are threatened. [ 1 ] In-game, only a small part of the upper city is available, [ 2 ] although several places are mentioned. For example; the High House of Wonders [ 3 ] , the shops Dersu's Vintage Tipple [ 4 ] and Fine Fabrics [ 5 ] , as well as estates typically owned by patriars. [ 6 ] Access [ edit section | visual editor ] The main gate into the upper city Access to the Upper City is limited, the main gate at the Upper City Gate Checkpoint is closed due to the threat of the Cult of the Absolute. [ 7 ] The upper city can only be accessed during the final quest ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain by traveling through the Morphic Pool . Two buildings in the upper city can be accessed freely prior to the final quest through specific mechanics. Ramazith's Tower is linked to the ⁠ Sorcerous Sundries by portal. Szarr Palace has a door on its ramparts, which are in the lower city. [ 8 ] Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] High Hall [ edit section | visual editor ] The entrance to High Hall area Main article: High Hall The High Hall area is named after its main building, which serves as the spot where the party can reach The Netherbrain . The area contains a courtyard which is located in front of the hall. The courtyard is filled with enemies and has to be battled through. Alternatively the sewers underneath the area can be used to reach the hall. The high hall location is accessible only after traveling to the Morphic Pool and is the last area before the final battle of the game. Ramazith's Tower [ edit section | visual editor ] The outside of Ramazith's Tower Main article: Ramazith's Tower Ramazith's Tower is a three-level magical spire located within the Upper City . While geographically part of the Upper City, it is primarily accessed via a portal on the top floor of Sorcerous Sundries in the Lower City . Due to its magical concealment, the tower is largely obscured from view for those wandering the streets below. It is the home and stronghold of the wizard Lorroakan , and is tied directly to the quest ⁠ Find the Nightsong . Szarr Palace [ edit section | visual editor ] Szarr Palace as seen from Lower City Main article: Szarr Palace Szarr Palace is the home of Cazador Szarr and explored in the quest ⁠ Investigate Cazador's Palace . Although it is located in the Upper City , the palace only can be accessed from the Lower City by climbing stairs in the Central Watch Tower at the Lower City Central Wall Waypoint at X: -53 Y: -64 or by jumping (or similar) from the roof of the Devil's Fee to the palace's ramparts. In the palace fast travelling and resting is not possible. Upper City Sewers [ edit section | visual editor ] The upper city sewers, underneath the courtyard Main article: Upper City Sewers The Upper City Sewers is a transitional area accessible only during the High Hall sequence. It provides a strategic shortcut, allowing the party to bypass portions of the main courtyard on their approach to the The Netherbrain . Entrances : Ruined Tower: Through a metal door located in a tower along the pathway leading up to the courtyard. Sewage Gate: Through a destructible iron gate near the Watch Citadel. Inside the sewers the party must face enemies, one of them being the Death Knight Stalker Svignee . ## Upper City Gate Checkpoint
- **来源**: [Upper City Gate Checkpoint](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Upper_City_Gate_Checkpoint)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Overview of the Baldur's Gate checkpoint to the Upper City Lower City Upper City ↑ Upper City Gate Checkpoint → Facemaker's Boutique ↓ The Lodge Upper City Gate Checkpoint is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ No admission to the Upper City until further notice. Residents may queue up and wait. „ — Flaming Fist triangle standing in front of the checkpoint Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 3 Waypoints 4 Related quests 5 Characters 5.1 Gate guards 5.2 Civilians 6 Loot 7 Related literature 8 Footnotes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Upper City Gate Checkpoint (also designated as Baldur's Gate Checkpoint) is an unnamed part of the Steeps district of the Lower City, occupying the bridge leading to the Upper City gate. The bridge spans across the river stream, which runs from the far end of the Bloomridge Park towards the House of Grief . The eastern side of the street leading to the bridge is lined up with the Facemaker's Boutique and The Glitter Gala . On the western side of the street is the Baldur's Gate waypoint . The street runs down to the large plaza with a statue of Balduran in the middle. Another statue to him stands on the bridge, separating it (and both the patrols and the queue of citizens) approximately in two. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] With the armies of the Cult of the Absolute threatening the city, the power holders of Baldur's Gate have forbidden free entrance to the Upper City. This prohibition is still active when the party reaches the Lower City in Act Three of the game. As a result, the Baldur's Gate Checkpoint is heavily guarded by a squad of several Flaming Fists and a Steel Watcher , commanded (apparently) by Fist Darbonna . [ 1 ] They have been instructed to deny entrance to anyone in without proper authorisation (which effectively means no one at all). Several Upper City residents wait their turn to pass the checkpoint, forming a queue. However, there is one exception from the new-established rules – the party itself. If the party reach the gate proper and talk to Darbonna, her squadmate Fist 'Deadeye' Mibbs claims that the party "have special dispensation" and is about to let them in. Unbeknownst to everyone around, Mibbs and Darbonna are infected with Mind Flayer Tadpoles . The implications behind Mibbs' and Darbonna's actions, as well as passing a DC 15 Insight Check throughout the dialogue, reveal that Mibbs' behaviour is not his own, and both are likely being mind-controlled by the Netherbrain . The latter is trying to lure the party into the Upper City, so it can overwhelm the Emperor's defences and force the party's transformation. Going on the bridge without having acquired all Netherstones results in the Netherbrain attempting to take over the party members' minds, causing them to receive Mindbroken or Stunned conditions. These conditions are applied to every member of the party, even if only one of them tries to get to the end of the bridge separately. These conditions are not applied to the two infected Fists. While crossing the bridge, The Emperor chimes in several times, warning that the party are being fooled and urging them to turn back at once, even going so far as teleport them back to the beginning of the bridge. Ignoring the Emperor's warnings and proceeding beyond the gate potentially causes a game over screen . [ verify ] If the party return to the city after acquiring all Netherstones , three infected NPCs near the queue forcefully transformed into Mind Flayers via Ceremorphosis and attack the bypassers. The Flaming Fists are Surprised , but fight alongside the party. Once the Mind Flayers are dead, all the guards run away to warn their superiors, before completely vanishing from the game once far enough. However, their banter suggests they wanted to pass the gate but quit the queue due to feeling something unnatural or unnerving around. ## Vonayn's Home
- **来源**: [Vonayn's Home](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Vonayn's_Home)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Vonayn's home as seen from the beach side Lower City Barren's Coop ↑ Philgrave's Mansion ← Vonayn's Home Vonayn's Home is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . Contents 1 Overview 2 Building layout 2.1 Ground floor 2.2 Basement 3 Involvement 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Characters 7 Loot 8 Related literature 9 Gallery Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Vonayn's Home is a small private dwelling in the Brampton district of Baldur's Gate, located east of Philgrave's Mansion and down from Barren's Coop and Bruc and Pishe's Emporium . It has one story and a vast basement, opening into a natural cave half-filled with the waters of the river Chionthar . Vonayn's Home has the only entrance, located at X: 53 Y: -120 . It can be reached by taking the stairs up from the beach at the eastern docks or climbing down knotted vines hanging from a breach in the stone railing above, between the Barren's Coop and Bruc and Pishe's Emporium. Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Inside the house is a single room with a bed and a kitchen with a stove. Containers around the room do not keep any remarkable items, except the wardrobe (see Involvement section below). Atop the wardrobe lies the Beach House Hatch Key which opens an a locked hatch out on the porch at X: 61 Y: -123 and leads to the basement. Otherwise, the hatch requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to lockpick. Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] A map of the basement of Vonayn's home. The initial room has several empty boxes and an oak door leading to a hallway with numerous tripwires . Another oak door leads to a smaller hallway; at its end is a lever inside a small rock alcove. The lever must be hit from a distance, for instance by using a Ranged Attack . Hitting the lever opens a false wall revealing a living area with a makeshift dock and a half afloat rowboat. On a table in the corner is some gold. In the open area with the dock is a bed with a backpack X: 61 Y: -123 beside it, which contains the Counting House Safe nº6 Key . Several documents, like the Smuggler's Note on a table and To 'One-Eye' reveal that the house was previously used to smuggle goods and people in and out of Baldur's Gate. In the cave-area to the east is a trapped Wooden Chest with some gold and a random potion. It stands next to an Acid Barrel , causing a failed disarming to explode together with the chest. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Exploring the house is a pivotal point in the ⁠ Find Mystic Carrion's Servant quest – the runaway zombie Thrumbo is hiding here. Throughout the quest, the party can learn several "milestones" on where to search: Reading Thrumbo's Note in the Philgrave's Mansion "Thrumbo was going to get us a boat. He must be somewhere near the water." - from Strange Beggar Lumbar "Down the stairs, across the sand. Down the stairs, across the sand..." - from Strange Beggar Morbus "Thrumbo had a plan. He was going to find us an abandoned house, somewhere to hide away from Carrion. You have to search them thoroughly. Especially the wardrobes - Thrumbo said that's the smartest place to hide." - from Strange Beggar Sacrum Thus, the pieces of the puzzle eventually lead not only to the Vonayn's Home, but to the wardrobe inside. Opening the wardrobe causes Thrumbo to jump out and start a conversation. Afterwards, if a fight is not started, Thrumbo stays in the room until the quest is resolved. ## Water Queen's House
- **来源**: [Water Queen's House](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Water_Queen's_House)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Water Queen's House Lower City Grey Harbour Docks ↑ Water Queen's House → Lustrous Lass The Water Queen's House is a Location within the Lower City in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Queen Umberlee, the sea Herself, I dash myself upon the rocks of your favour, Let me drink the brine of your glory deep into my lungs, Turn my skull to shell, my ribs to reef, To earn your blessing, And to spare me the wrath of your sahuagin. „ — Supplications to Umberlee Contents 1 Overview 2 Building layout 2.1 Portico entrance 2.2 Main building 2.2.1 Upper floor 2.2.2 Southern exit 2.3 Water Queen's Cellar 2.3.1 Treasure room 2.3.2 Hidden cavern 3 Involvement 4 Waypoints 5 Related locations 6 Related quests 7 Characters 7.1 Notable 7.2 Umberlee's followers 7.3 Civilians 7.4 Creatures 8 Loot 9 Related literature 10 Notes and references 11 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Umberlee Fountain The Water Queen's House is a temple dedicated to the deity Queen Umberlee . It is a huge building in the southmost part of the Grey Harbour Docks , standing on a rocky cape pushing far into the waters of the River Chionthar . The temple consists of two parts: the portico lined up with a colonnade, used for offering and worship by commoners, with a fountain depicting The Bitch Queen [ 1 ] herself in the middle, and the actual two-storied building with a cellar in the rocky foot of the cape, used by the clergy. It has only one way of entering through the portico at X: -228 Y: -201 . The cellar of the temple is accessible through the passageway in the backside of the cliff at X: -254 Y: -265 . Umberlee's followers ( "Umberlants" as official term, and "waveservants" , by the common speaking) in Baldur's Gate are led by Flood Tide Allandra Grey . [ 2 ] Being a huge trading port, Baldur's Gate obviously has a fair share of Umberlee worshippers, notably the sailors and sea captains, who fear the wrath of Umberlee in their travels and seek her favour. Umberlee's clergy, though, care not only for spreading the influence of their goddess, but also of material basis for doing so, covertly accumulating wealth and taking into possession the city's docks and shipyards. [ 3 ] Building layout [ edit section | visual editor ] Portico entrance [ edit section | visual editor ] Path into the main building, archway across upper floor rooms can be spotted above. The portico gallery encircles the aforementioned fountain and serves to the commoner worshippers of the Sea Queen. It features an altar for those who want to pray at X: -222 Y: -223 . Several worshippers are in this area, praying, discussing the donations, or simply fancying the sea sights. An Offerings Chest for donations is on the opposite side at X: -233 Y: -226 , guarded by Seawind Star Stolitti , one of Umberlee's waveservants. Another waveservant can be occasionally seen emptying the chest, as she moves the contents to the temple cellar treasury. Party members placing any item or any amount of gold in the Offering Chest receive Umberlee's blessing until their next Long Rest . However, this can only be done once per party member and does not stack with other instances of Bless, such as Sweet Stone Features . It is removed if the character respecs . Interacting with the chest is not a crime, but taking any of the items out of the chest is . Stealing from the chest (or from the treasure pile in the Water Queen's Cellar (see below) angers Umberlee, causing her to cease blessing future party member donations (existing ones are not cancelled). Donating to the chest grants the ⁠ Offerings to the Waves inspiration to characters with the Acolyte background. Following the way underneath an archway brings the party to the main building. The southwestern corner of the portico approximately at X: -240 Y: -202 can be used to access the Steel Watch Foundry territory through a series of jumps (spells like Misty Step or Feather Fall help to avoid falling damage). Main building [ edit section | visual editor ] In the separate nave at the back of the temple the head priestess Allandra Grey is leading a funeral ceremony for the deceased Holli Dylford – her body lies on the mat in the centre, and several waveservants are chanting a song of lamentation. To the west a short stairway lead down to a kitchen area where two Untaken (i.e., novice clerics) are preparing drinks and food for the funeral. Some Camp Supplies and the book Sacred Shark Recipes are in the area. To the east, a stairway leads up to the first floor of the temple, while to the south another leads outside the temple onto a balcony and then to a small beach patch, where there is a passage to the temple cellar. Upper floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The interior of Flood Tide's chambers The upper floor consists of an entry office room and Allandra Grey's private quarters, connected with a bridge seen from the outside. Inside the entry room Vilmina stands guard, blocking further passage. Several containers here are not locked, but red-outlined: A Traveller's Chest and a small Gilded Chest on a desk at X: -213 Y: -245 contain gold, alchemical ingredients, and random precious gem. Two Opulent Chests keep gold, random precious gems, and (possibly) Valuables , random spell scrolls and / or potions. Through the door and across the archway is another room. Inside is Norya Baker who accuses the party of trespassing if she spots them here. On the wall is a fishing net decorated with lootable Starfishes and Pearls . At the far end of the room is an Opulent Chest containing the High Security Vault nº4 Key and the Wavemother's Cloak . Southern exit [ edit section | visual editor ] Exit to the small beach behind the temple. To the south of the temple a small stairway leads down. At X: -245 Y: -277 a DC 20 Survival Check highlights a buried chest containing a Rare arrow, a health potion ( Greater or Superior ), and a random book. On the beach three fishers chat about possibly catching a Sahuagin and what that might entail. Going past the group, a passageway can be spotted inside the rocks which leads to the Water Queen's Cellar. Water Queen's Cellar [ edit section | visual editor ] The cave beneath Water Queen's House “ You dare steal from the very sea that birthed you? Enjoy these breaths - they shall be your last. „ — Umberlee , when looting her treasure The Water Queen's Cellar is a cave located underneath the Water Queen's House. It can be accessed through a passageway at X: -254 Y: -265 from an aforementioned patch of sandy beach behind the temple. The cellar is considered a private area of the Church of Umberlee and cannot be explored without trespassing; the use of stealth is recommended. When the party enter the area they must pass a water stream, from which a stairway leads up and further into the cellar. As the Deep Water effectively breaks invisibility , this might be an obstacle to an unhindered exploration of the cave. Several Umberlants standing on the stairs and next to a table on the higher ground are discussing the recent death of Holli Dylford and apparently preparing a funeral repast, with a dead Kuo-Toa served as food. Next to the table is an unlocked chest with minor random loot. Treasure room [ edit section | visual editor ] Hidden cavern behind the destroyed Sandstone Wall The back of the cellar is separated with an unlocked iron gate. Behind it is a room with a treasure pile containing ~400 gp, a random gem, several pieces of jewelry, a bottle of wine and a Fish . Looting the pile earns the Wavemother's ire, triggering an Ice Storm upon the party, summoning hostile Sahuagin in the water pool further in the back and turning all the Waveservants in the cellar hostile (the clergy of the temple above do not turn hostile if the party pillage the cellar). Also, stealing Umberlee's donations here ends the party's ability to get blessed when making an offering at the Offering Chest in the Water Queen's House . In the far corner are another three dead Kuo-Toa. The corpse of Redhammer is here if the party sided with the Church of Umberlee and handed him over to Allandra Grey as part of the ⁠ Avenge the Drowned quest. Hidden cavern [ edit section | visual editor ] At X: -1840 Y: -78 in the far end of the cellar passing a DC 15 Perception Check reveals a nearby Sandstone Wall which can be breached. Behind it is another small room with waterfalls and a Wooden Chest containing gold, random valuables, and some alchemical ingredients and / or elixirs. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon the party's approaching the temple, Diomira Trellis starts a conversation. She relates that the funeral of one of recently deceased waveservant is underway and allows them to enter regardless of their answer; the ceremony itself can be found in the main building. Speaking with Allandra Grey allows the party to learn about the fate of deceased Holli Dylford . The priestess also ask the party of their offerings to the funeral ceremony. Choosing any answer except "I brought nothing" grants one or both of the following inspirations: ⁠ Offerings to the Waves ( Acolyte background) [ 4 ] ⁠ Sea Memorial ( Entertainer background) When speaking of the offerings to the funeral, Cleric characters can use either the generic class line or the line reflecting their particular deity. [ 5 ] Monks and Barbarians also have unique lines. The aforementioned inspiration (if available) is granted regardless. The full list of possible formulations is on Allandra's page . If the party agree to investigate Holli's death, the quest ⁠ Avenge the Drowned is started. It can only be initiated if the party has not yet visited the Iron Throne . Holli can be communed with using Speak with Dead . Also, Allandra mentions the sailors who caught Holli's body in their fishing nets. They are Gowlan and Fleer , who are near the docks waypoint. Refusing to help Allandra find Holli's murderer is considered an oathbreaking action for Vengeance Paladins if they are the one interacting with the priestess. If the party successfully finish the quest and sides with the waveservants , Allandra Grey moves up to her office. In this case, party members can get to her office without being stopped by the guards. For example, the "Untaken" is the common title for novices of the church, while the "Dark Breakers" and "Flood Tides" belong to the middle level in the table of ranks, and the "Savage Seawinds" are considered the senior clerics. Despite this, within the Baldur's Gate 3 plot Allandra Grey acts as the acknowledged leader of the temple and of the Umberlee's clergy. ↑ According to Acquisitions journal. ↑ This is another option to earn the inspiration if it was not obtained through donating to the chest in the portico gallery. ## Western Beach
- **来源**: [Western Beach](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Western_Beach)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Western Beach - smugglers' hideout Rivington Western Beach → South Span Checkpoint The Western Beach is a Location within Rivington in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Fighting ahead. Just once, it would be nice not to play the cooler head... „ — Jaheira , watching the conflict between gangs is brewing up Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Eastern slope 1.2 Western slope 1.3 Cave tunnel and the hidden bay 1.4 Smugglers' cave 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 4.1 The Guild 4.2 Stone Lord's men 4.3 Other 5 Loot 6 Related literature 7 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The beach is an unnamed location accessed by travelling west down the paths from both sides of the South Span Checkpoint , and then following along the shore of the River Chionthar . The steep slope descends from the grounds of the Gur Camp and the Sword Coast Couriers to the south from the checkpoint, and from the Open Hand Temple to the north of it. The slope consists of numerous rocky ledges connected with winding paths and patches of knotted roots, and has several entrances into cave which can be used to access some locations in Rivington. The northern end of the beach butts against the high rocky ridge; a tunnel leads through it to a secluded bay which is being used for smuggling operations by the Stone Lord and his men. Eastern slope [ edit section | visual editor ] Blocked entrance to the gnomes' cave This part of the western beach runs down to the river shore from the Gur Camp and the Sword Coast Couriers . There are several points of interest here, including the entrances leading into caves under various locations in Rivington: At X: 58 Y: 48 is the exit from the cave area under Rivington Well . It is initially blocked with a winch mechanism and must be opened from inside to be used in both directions. If none of the party members succeed a passive DC 20 Perception Check near the well, the area remains inaccessible. At the beach near the water end there are two buried treasures: the one at X: 67 Y: 88 requires DC 10 Survival Check to detect, and another at X: 46 Y: 82 requires DC 15 Survival Check . Near the first one, a backpack with gold and random valuables lie. At X: 30 Y: 29 is the exit from the cave leading to the Angleiron's Cellar . When the party first approach the cave mouth, a passive DC 15 Survival Check is made. Success results in noticing small footprints leading into the cave. A character belonging to an Underdark race, i.e. a Drow , Duergar or a Deep Gnome unmistakably recognizes them as footprints of a deep gnome. The cellar can be explored only if the deep gnomes of the Clan Ironhand survived the events of Act One and Act Two . If they were killed in Grymforge or perished in Moonrise Towers Prison , the cave mouth is laden with unmovable boulders, and the cave is inaccessible. At X: 46 Y: 67 a Refugee Corpse lies, which can be interrogated via Speak with Dead . He claims to have been murdered by a trader who wanted to purchase his valuable ring. Certain conversation choices with Ferg can reveal he is indeed the killer merchant of whom the corpse speaks. A Gemless Ring can be looted from the corpse, which can be combined with the gem bought or stolen from Ferg into a common ring. The rocky ledge at X: 32 Y: 45 provides a convenient point to traverse to the scaffolds surrounding the Wyrm's Crossing bridge - either by jumping, flying, or using any means of spatial movement like Misty Step . Once Wyrm's Crossing is reached, the guards at the South Span Checkpoint allow the party to pass freely back and forth, even if the initial dialogue with the checkpoint patrol was never initiated. At X: 3 Y: 71 (under the Wyrm's Crossing bridge) is the exit from the cave under the Open Hand Temple . To get close and enter, several boulders need to be moved aside. Near the cave entrance, some Valuables lay on the ground. Western slope [ edit section | visual editor ] View on the western part of the beach with the cave to smugglers' bay The northern part of the beach runs mostly along the Open Hand Temple grounds. This part of the Western Beach also has its points of interest. At X: -51 Y: 72 knotted roots allow the party to ascend to the path which eventually leads either up to the South Span Checkpoint or down to the old remains of a shipwreck. The roots end up on a small ground with a defaced statue, where a DC 20 Survival Check allows one to notice a buried chest with gold, a random arrow, and a random spell scroll of Very rare grade. Halfway up to the temple at X: -34 Y: 23 a pouch with gold and a Trap Disarm Toolkit lies. The path down leads to a wrecked ship at X: -90 Y: 85 , where on the foredeck a trapped Traveller's Chest can be found. It requires DC 15 Perception Check to detect the trap and two DC 15 Sleight of Hand Checks to disarm and lockpick the chest. Inside is a Necklace of Elemental Augmentation , gold and one or two healing potions of various grade. Another Heavy chest with minor loot is hidden under the opposite half of the wreck. It is visible only after highlighting it with "Show Item Labels" button. Near the broken statue at X: -118 Y: 103 a veritable obstacle course starts. The path here is covered with a Steam Cloud from a Vent , concealing 5 Blast Mines and several Tripwires which trigger them. The tripwires here require DC 18 Sleight of Hand Check instead of regular DC 10 to disarm. Several fresh corpses are strewn about, but none of them can be interrogated via Speak with Dead . At X: -141 Y: 73 the party can find the Dying Stone Lord Thug . He is sitting leaned against a low hedge with a knife deep in his guts. On approaching him, the party can speak to the Thug, only to watch him inevitably die after a few phrases. However, Dying Stone Lord Thug is one of the characters who might be chosen by Orin the Red as a disguise to threaten the party. [ 1 ] In this case, the corpse of real Thug can be later found in the Bhaal Temple in Lower City . If this is the case, the dialogue with the Thug is longer and more meaningful. Throughout the dialogue, the player character rolls a passive DC 20 Perception Check . If successful, they feel that the dying thug for some reason seems to be reveling in his miserable Gravely Wounded condition. Whatever the player character chooses to say or to do, after three or four phrases Orin reverts to her true appearance and teleports away. Cave tunnel and the hidden bay [ edit section | visual editor ] The ship from Moonrise moored in the smugglers' bay At X: -233 Y: 84 is an opening to a passageway under the rocky ridge. Inside, the straight path forward is littered with tripwires (each requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check ), also concealed with a Steam Cloud . Any of these tripwires trigger the eagle statue at the end of the passage to cast a Chain Lightning spell. The statue cannot be interacted with or disarmed. The safest way is to bypass the tripwired path using the wooden platform nearby (presumably used by the guards). The backpack left there contains minor loot. At the foot of the ladder lies a beheaded corpse; a DC 10 Medicine Check tells the party members this is a fresh kill. Although not all victims of a fierce fight are disfigured or decapitated, none of them are available to interrogate via Speak with Dead . When the party first approach the bay, they see a ship moored there and recognize it as previously seen at Moonrise Towers . On the shore they witness an argument between the Stone Lord's thugs and the members of The Guild , who have tracked the thugs down to the place. Regardless of the party's actions, a fight between two groups starts. If the party comes to the spot openly and quick enough, they can participate in the dialogue between the two groups leaders, Caïros and Farlin . By this moment Farlin sees she has underestimated the strength of her rivals, and asks the party to help, who then must pick a side. [ 2 ] If the party is hiding or remain far enough from the action, they can watch from a safe distance. Otherwise, they are engaged in the battle against the Stone Lord's men, with the Guild gang as neutrals. The party can then pick a side, confronting both gangs, [ 3 ] or resolving the fight in initial balance of forces. If the party supported the Guild or remained neutral, and Farlin survives the fight, a dialogue with her starts automatically. She awards the party with 665 gold . Questioning her about the operations in the bay starts or progresses the ⁠ Aid the Underduke quest. [ 4 ] The interacting character can also choose to instigate a fight with Farlin as well after taking the reward from her. If Farlin did not survive, the rest of her crew run away, and no reward is granted; the gold cannot be looted from her corpse. Depending on the party's choices, some of the following inspirations may be earned: ⁠ Backing the Established Players ( Noble background) - for supporting the Guild ⁠ Cleaning up the Scum ( Haunted One background) - for killing both groups ⁠ Easy Pickings ( Criminal background) - for killing both groups ⁠ Stacking the Deck ( Criminal background) - for supporting the Guild [ 5 ] If Minsc has already been recruited prior to this moment, siding with the Guild is considered an oathbreaking action for Paladins of Devotion . If he is present as party member, then some additional dialogue options are available. After the battle is resolved, the ship from Moonrise can be explored. Despite Farlin's claims that its cargo now belongs to the Guild, she does not object to looting the ship. At coords X: -214 Y: 131 on the deck is the ship's storage, where two Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen can be taken (they disappear after a Long Rest [ verify ] ). One more tadpole stands atop a barrel at X: -225 Y: 107 . Smugglers' cave [ edit section | visual editor ] At X: -234 Y: 85 is the entrance to the cave which is used by Caïros and his crew to smuggle cargo from Moonrise into the city. Inside a trapped chest at X: -1339 Y: -859 contain the Bonespike Boots . The trap requires DC 15 Perception Check to detect and DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check to disarm; the chest itself is not locked. From a tresure heap nearby gold and random Valuables can be looted. At the southern end of the cave a series of cragged rocks lead to the small dock with a rowboat. It cannot be used to travel to the city. A map on one of the barrels here adds a marker on the map of the Wyrm's Rock Fortress where a wall breach can be used to infiltrate the prison. Also here a pouch with Silkroot and a bottle of Dream Mist can be found. ## Wyrm's Crossing
- **来源**: [Wyrm's Crossing](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wyrm's_Crossing)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Wyrm's Crossing - side view from the east Wyrm's Rock Fortress ↑ Wyrm's Crossing ↓ Rivington Wyrm's Crossing is a region in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . Hemmed in between Rivington and the Wyrm's Rock Fortress , it must be crossed to enter the Lower City . “ Wyrm's Crossing is a chokepoint - if I wanted to intercept a new arrival, I'd find somewhere before the bridge, blend in amongst the crowds, and wait. „ — Shadowheart Contents 1 Overview 2 Locations 2.1 South Span Checkpoint fortifications 2.2 Fraygo's Flophouse 2.3 Sharess' Caress 2.4 Danthelon's Dancing Axe 2.5 The Velveteen Elixir 2.6 Carm's Garms 2.7 Bridge to Wyrm's Rock Fortress 3 Waypoints 4 Related locations 5 Related quests 6 Notable characters 6.1 Traders 6.2 Flaming Fist 7 Notable loot 8 Related literature 9 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyrm's Crossing - side view from the west Wyrm's Crossing occupies the wide stone bridge that connects Rivington and the Wyrm's Rock Fortress . It resembles an urban area much more than Rivington, and consists of several establishments of trade and entertainment, built up on both sides of the bridge and forming its borders. All buildings in Wyrm's Crossing have a purpose, and almost all are a part of one quest or another, directly pointed out while speaking with various NPCs in the walkthrough and mentioned in quest objectives. Otherwise, once inside the area the party may stumble upon non-playing characters who advance a quest in some fashion. Therefore, thorough exploration of this area may prove useful. Most buildings have open wooden decks and scaffolds at the backside, hanging somewhat precariously above the river; they can be used to move along the bridge and gain access to most establishments through back doors or open parts of walls. Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] The locations here are listed in order of approach if going from the South Span Checkpoint to the North, and from West to East. South Span Checkpoint fortifications [ edit section | visual editor ] Both wooden towers of the ramparts have an entrance from the Wyrm's Crossing, to both sides just behind the gate. Inside, the party can obtain several potions of health of various quality inside Wooden Chests and on them as well as Elixirs of Hill Giant Strength , a score of random arrows, and some Camp Supplies . All of these are red outlined but easy to take, as the only guards who consistently stay inside are Fist Azari and Fist Meadows in the ground-level room of the western tower. The western tower also has two Stacks of Scrolls with random scrolls and a Rustic Chest which requires a DC 30 Sleight of Hands Check to lockpick but contains only minor amounts of gold and random dyes. If the party gains access into the Wyrm's Crossing with the help of the deep gnomes of the Clan Ironhand , Manip Falcäo begins to call them out from a low wooden scaffold to the east of the ramparts, promising a reward for solving his ⁠ "pest problem" . If the gnomes do not appear for any reason (or after the party has taken a long rest ), Falcäo is standing in either of the ground-level ramparts' rooms. The checkpoint gate can also be bypassed altogether by a series of jumps or using most any means of spatial movement (e.g. Arrow of Transposition , Misty Step , Grant Flight ) from the rocky cliff at approximately X: 34 Y: 47 . On the way, a Heavy Chest at X: 32 Y: 50 can be looted. Fraygo's Flophouse [ edit section | visual editor ] Exterior view of Fraygo's Flophouse Main article: Fraygo's Flophouse This is a three-storied boarding house on the western side of the bridge. Near the building, trader Thodric Shedeveer offers to buy fresh fish from him. At X: -27 Y: 81 (on the upstairs balcony), there is a locked backdoor allowing to break inside the lodging area, and right above it is another door which leads into the serial killer's hideout. Near the entrance, Crak and Rilia argue about where to find a shelter to have a decent rest once they have reached the Crossing. Inside the party can find Trader Griska , who offers potions and alchemical ingredients, and Queelia Arvis - a Flophouse cook who can provide them with Camp Supplies . This location is involved in several quests: ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone ⁠ Investigate the Murders ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders Also, here the party might progress Astarion's ⁠ companion quest . Sharess' Caress [ edit section | visual editor ] Exterior view of Sharess' Caress Main article: Sharess' Caress "Sharess' Caress" is a pleasure house run by Mamzell Amira . The main entrance to it is located at the eastern side of the bridge. It occupies all three stories at the eastern side, as well as lodgings in the storey above the stone archway connecting two sides of the Crossing, and also two stories of the building on the opposite side. Most its rooms are engirdled with wooden balconies, which makes approaching various rooms even easier from the street, instead of running twisting stairs and corridors inside. The western pillar of the archway is actually a cellar for the western part of the pleasure house, but it is not connected with the upper level by ladders or similar means. Under the archway the party can trade with several vendors, offering various goods: Roberon Silt - paintings and dyes , and Velson Oakes - various plant-based Camp Supplies . Near the main entrance, on the wall, a Waypoint is located. Also, here the player character can witness several minor vignettes, all contributing to the Crossing's image as a place to find anything, any time. Near the entrance two citizens, Laila and Embry persuade their friend Hakeem to celebrate his birthday at the pleasure house, while at its far corner a Dragonborn Surixana tries to pawn off an "enhancement substance" to Cillian . To the West, Neno Quilltop , seemingly in a flap, is discussing with Kali Hammerhand whether they have bought everything necessary to flee from the city, while the latter tries to calm her down. Inside the player character can meet a number of notable characters. Also, several quests here might be started, progressed or resolved. ⁠ Aid the Underduke - started ⁠ Deal with the Devil - started ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion - started ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss - progressed ⁠ Investigate the Suspicious Toys - progressed ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders - resolved ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior - progressed In various rooms and corridors of the pleasure house the party can speak and deal with Raphael , Voss , Naoise Nallinto , Valeria , Hoots Hooligan , Arfur Gregorio , as well as drow twins Sorn Orlith and Nym Orlith . The full list of rooms, notable characters and possible interactions can be found on the location page. Danthelon's Dancing Axe [ edit section | visual editor ] Exterior view of Danthelon's Dancing Axe and The Velveteen Elixir Main article: Danthelon's Dancing Axe This building at the North-Western side of the bridge has two stories and a vast cellar beneath the level of the bridge's pavement. The cellar features a wide open scaffold at the outer side which can be reached by normal spatial movement. The ground floor of the building is occupied by a weapons and armour store owned by Entharl Danthelon , also serving as a Harper safehouse. Near the building Glynda Oltower offers her goods: various tools and instruments, along with Thieves' Tools and Trap Disarm Toolkits . Also, Safyre and Limmy are pondering on where to buy a nice garment to be introduced and dine with the former's parents. Visiting the store progresses Jaheira's ⁠ companion quest . The Velveteen Elixir [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: The Velveteen Elixir An alchemy and potions shop run by Stylin' Horst occupies the upper floor of the same building, right above Danthelon's Dancing Axe . Unlike all other establishments in Wyrm's Crossing, it is marked on the map simply as "Potion Shop". Horst sells a wide range of elixirs and potions, as well as a number of alchemical ingredients, including very rare ones. Also, the back room of the store (accessible from outside) may be also looted for ingredients. Carm's Garms [ edit section | visual editor ] Exterior view of Carm's Garms Main article: Carm's Garms A camp clothing and dye store owned by Carmen Pennygood - sister of Figaro Pennygood , a fashion dealer who can be met later in Lower City . Also, inside the store the party can speak to Naaber , a meddlesome "would-be adventurer". If ignored, Naaber follows until the party move far enough from Carm's Garms. Near the store building, three machinery enthusiasts - Trinigan Gazotts , Slozy Arminifer and Vinegaroon - discuss spiritedly the technical features of the Steel Watchers, as well as the latter's brief experience of acquiring an ability to fly after an attempt to study an automaton too close. Bridge to Wyrm's Rock Fortress [ edit section | visual editor ] The bridge to Wyrm's Rock Fortress is guarded by a Flaming Fist patrol (led by Blaze Elin ) and three Steel Watchers . To gain access to the further locations of Act Three the party must convince the patrol to let them pass into the Wyrm's Rock Fortress, which is currently closed due to extreme safety measures. Successfully getting into Wyrm's Rock grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Multipass ( Noble background) - using Urgent Report for Duke Ravengard ⁠ Procedures be Damned ( Noble background) - for sneaking in with spells or other abilities ⁠ Rock-Solid Alibi ( Charlatan background) - convincing the Flaming Fist ⁠ Through Nooks and Crannies ( Urchin background) - for sneaking in with spells or other abilities Waypoints [ edit section | visual editor ] This location contains the following Waypoint : South Span of Wyrm's Crossing at X: 15 Y: 74 Related locations [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ South Span Checkpoint ⁠ Rivington ⁠ Wyrm's Rock Fortress ⁠ Wyrm's Rock Prison Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Aid the Underduke ⁠ Deal with the Devil ⁠ Deal with the Gnomes ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion ⁠ Free Orpheus ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss ⁠ Investigate Cazador's Palace ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior ⁠ The High Harper ⁠ The Pale Elf Notable characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Arfur Gregorio Dalyria Ffion Goldgrind - ## Wyrm's Rock Fortress
- **来源**: [Wyrm's Rock Fortress](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wyrm's_Rock_Fortress)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

Wyrm's Rock Fortress - view from Rivington Lower City ↑ Wyrm's Rock Fortress ↓ Wyrm's Crossing Wyrm's Rock Fortress is a region in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Wyrm's Isle foot 1.2 Making the way inside 2 Layout of the fortress 2.1 Ground floor 2.2 Basement 2.3 First floor 2.4 Second floor 2.5 Top floor 2.5.1 Gortash's private chambers 3 Wyrm's Rock traps 4 Waypoints 5 Related locations 6 Related quests 7 Characters 7.1 Notable 7.2 Members of the Flaming Fist 7.3 Members of the Cult of Bane 7.4 Coronation attendees 7.4.1 Patriars in the Audience Hall 7.4.2 In the mess hall (first floor) 7.5 In the reception room 7.6 Other characters 8 Loot 9 Literature 9.1 Reception room 9.2 Barracks 9.3 Audience Hall 9.4 Gortash's Apartments 9.5 Other 10 Notes and references 11 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyrm's Rock Fortress Wyrm's Isle foot [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyrm's Rock Fortress stands on a rocky isle in the middle of the river Chionthar, taking up the whole space save for minor cliffs around. Wyrm's Rock Fortress is connected to the south to Wyrm's Crossing , and to the north to the Lower City by two drawbridges. As the legend goes, the isle once was home to a bronze dragon , who swore to defend the city from greatest dangers. The southern side of the cliffs can be reached using spells like Grant Flight or Feather Fall and similar means, and explored. To the west, a series of jumps and climbing the Knotted Roots lead down to a small beach with a Dirt Mound and a Mousehole that might be used to open the path to the Wyrmway , or up the wall to a balcony behind the Audience Hall, allowing to bypass the First Floor of the Fortress. To the east, the path leads to a wall breach which can be used to gain access to the Wyrm's Rock Prison via its storage room. A rope ladder hanging from the cliff leads to another beach with a trapped Wooden Chest standing openly. Also, a small amount of alchemical ingredients can be gathered around the cliffs. Making the way inside [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon approaching Wyrm's Rock Fortress for the first time, the party finds out that the drawbridge leading inside has been lifted due to extreme safety measures: the ceremony of ordaining Enver Gortash as the first Archduke of Baldur's Gate is about to start. The passage is guarded by several Flaming Fists, accompanied by three Steel Watchers : Fist Gai , Fist Shah and Blaze Elin . The latter is actually a commandant of the whole fortress, but she prefers to stand watch at the bridge in person, instead of tending to the stronghold's needs. However, there are several ways to get past the guards: Obtain an Admission Pass to the coronation , wrested from Arfur Gregorio or taken from the Nymph's Grotto in Sharess' Caress Obtain the Lower City Pass granted by Investigator Valeria Obtain the Urgent Report for Duke Ravengard (found at the Sword Coast Couriers in Rivington ) Bribe Blaze Elin (requires a DC 25 Persuasion Check and 20,000 gold pieces ) Let Wyll speak for the party as an Origin or as a party member (requires a DC 30 Persuasion Check , and only works if he was not turned into a devil) Several other options, based on the class of the player character (requires a DC 30 Persuasion or Deception Check ) Alternatively, the party can walk around the patrol by, for example, jumping down from the Wyrm's Crossing side onto the rocky footing of the fortress at X: 27 Y: 158 . Entering Wyrm's Rock Fortress for the first time earns following Inspirational Events , depending on the way that the party chose: Convincing the Flaming Fist patrol to let the party in ⁠ Multipass ( Noble background) - if using Urgent Report for Duke Ravengard only ⁠ Rock-Solid Alibi ( Charlatan background) - for using any dialogue option to get in past the patrol Getting in without a pass ⁠ Procedures be Damned ( Noble background) - this one includes the possibility of entering the fortress proper through the prison after being arrested ⁠ Through Nooks and Crannies ( Urchin background) Behind the drawbridge is a tunnel which traverses the fortress to the Lower City, guarded by three more Steel Watchers and another Flaming Fist patrol ( Fist Larys and Fist Serrik ) at the far end. The drawbridge leading to the Lower City is guarded by another Steel Watcher and Blaze Savora . Layout of the fortress [ edit section | visual editor ] Ground floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Combined map of the fortress's Ground Floor and First Floor The ground floor of the fortress consists of a vast tunnel joining two drawbridges, and two parts of the building itself, located at both sides of the tunnel. The tunnel is guarded by three Steel Watchers standing near each door. Regardless of the way the party gains access into the fortress proper, as soon as they approach the nearest Steel Watcher , an automated dialogue with it starts. The automaton informs the player character that their trespass will not be punished, after which Gortash himself connects to the Watcher and instead grants a personal invitation to his ordination. To the right is the door to the first floor of the fortress, along with Mess Hall and stairs to the Audience Hall. To the left are two doors, where Flaming Fists are quartered. The southern door leads into kind of a reception room. A Waypoint is on the northern wall, and there are stairs which lead to Wyrm's Rock Prison . The room is guarded by Fist Callaway , Fist Loudstone and Fist Broko , as well as Manip Cragbender and a Steel Watcher. Quartermaster Arkleia Oloril sits behind the counter. She can be convinced to show her stock of goods. Successfully doing so earns the ⁠ Nothing's Not for Sale for any character with Charlatan background. Also present are two groups of citizens waiting to be judged for transgressions. The reception room The northern door opens into Flaming Fist barracks. The plaque near the barracks states it is for authorized personnel only, but nevertheless the door is not red-outlined. Inside Manip Bakshi , Fist Debin and Fist Oriona are sleeping, while Fist Reynash , who is meant to be on duty, is trying to lockpick Bakshi's chest. The party can choose to deal with Reynash or to wake other guards and resolve the situation with them. Depending on the party member's choices, they might earn the following Inspirational Events : ⁠ Easing His Leave, and His Pockets ( Urchin background) - if intimidating / blackmailing the thief ⁠ Court Marshall ( Soldier background) - for turning in the thief Basement [ edit section | visual editor ] A corridor within the prison Main article: Wyrm's Rock Prison The basement of the fortress consists solely of the Wyrm's Rock Prison, which can be accessed from the reception room through the spiral stairs at the far corner of the reception room, or from the outside via the wall breach at X: 42 Y: 190 (requires a Perception check to detect). There the party can advance the ⁠ Free Counsellor Florrick , speak with Marvin the Unusual Skull [ 1 ] and also gain access to The Wyrmway , as a part of Wyll's ⁠ companion quest . Also, should a party member commit any transgression within Rivington , Wyrm's Crossing or Wyrm's Rock Fortress itself, they find themselves locked up in one of the cells of the said prison. First floor [ edit section | visual editor ] The mess hall with entrance to the audience hall The first floor consists of the vast Mess Hall and the kitchen. Upon first visiting the fortress, the party can encounter several bodyguards and attendants of patriars in the mess hall waiting for their masters to descend. Discussing the Steel Watch with Lord Amber's Bodyguard , Lady Durinbold's Attendant and Lord Shattershield's Attendant may result in approval changes with various companions. In the centre is a door which leads to the Audience Hall on the second floor. It is guarded by Fist Dresten and a Steel Watcher. Also, if Wyll is alive, Mizora stands nearby the door to the Audience Hall. Upon approaching her, dialogue starts automatically. She prompts the party to attend the ceremony, and, if Wyll is present, mocks him about Duke Ravengard's tadpoled condition. She dryly suggests that they speak to her again after returning from upstairs. Second floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Combined map of the Audience Hall and adjacent balconies The second floor consists of the audience hall and several adjacent balconies. No matter the time of their arrival, upon entering the Audience Hall for the first time, the party can witness the ordination of Enver Gortash as an Archduke of Baldur's Gate. Upon noticing the party, Gortash interrupts the procedure to have a chat with them. The dialogue itself differs depending on whether the lead player character is the Dark Urge , Karlach , Wyll as Origin, or if Wyll is present as companion party member. Within the dialogue, the player character is offered an opportunity to strike an alliance with Gortash. They can agree to the proposition, decline it or choose a neutral course of action, while other companions might have their own opinion on the subject. Also, at this point, the Emperor chimes in, prompting the player character to agree. Regardless of their choice, Gortash tries to aim their efforts onto locating and killing Orin by telling them about the shapeshifter spy in their camp. In playing the Dark Urge origin, the dialogue with Gortash sheds a fair amount of light on their pre-plot story and their personal participation in the whole of the conspiracy of the Dead Three. After discussing the possible alliance, Gortash offers the player character to witness the ceremony. To this, they may answer using a variety of lines, the results of which can result in approval changes with various companions. However, choosing rude options – or trying to decline and leave – leads Gortash to cause pain to the player character for a few moments through illithid forces and thus makes them stay. Lastly, the player character can react to Gortash's speech agressively and wage a fight. Doing so results in a confrontation with all Steel Watchers and Flaming Fists present (as well as the patriars' companions present, who run up the stairs to defend their masters [ verify ] ). The audience hall, with throne for the archduke After the cutscene with the ordaining ceremony ends, the party has a brief chance to speak directly to Ulder Ravengard . Unfortunately, the Grand Duke is under the tight grip of his tadpole, and usually does nothing except sing praises to Gortash and conduct his ordination as the new Archduke of the city. However, if Wyll is present, certain conversation choices indicate his subjugation to the Absolute is not yet fully complete. Speaking to him about Florrick does not shake off the Duke's delusion - but doing so starts a time-sensitive side quest ⁠ Free Counsellor Florrick , if she was not freed previously. This is the first chance to speak to Ravengard directly, and the last one if the party do not try (or succeed) to save him from the Iron Throne later. If the party descend from the Audience Hall without speaking to the Duke, they do not find him there again even if they return immediately. The following Inspirational Events can be earned, depending on the choices made through the dialogue: ⁠ Coronation of the Dreadmaster ( Sage background) - witnessing the ceremony ⁠ Personal Invitation ( Entertainer background) - witnessing the ceremony ⁠ Shaking Bane's Hand ( Acolyte background) - agreeing to make an alliance with Gortash Additionally, striking the alliance with Gortash lay the groundwork for gaining the ⁠ Always Trust a Dishonest Person inspirational event for Charlatan background, in case the player character chooses to betray the agreement later in their walkthrough (in case it was not acquired earlier) Top floor [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the rooftop of the fortress There are various ways to get on to the top floor: Use the main double doors in the southern wall Lockpick a side door in the western wall Climb up at the bell tower and use the doors there Descend via a ladder from the bell tower roof. The top floor consists of Gortash's personal quarters, a vast roof area surrounding it (with several side towers), and a bell tower (also including an inner room and a climable area onto the roof). After Gortash's ordination, he moves here and remains until the party chooses to confront him or fulfill the agreement, bringing him the Netherstones held by Ketheric and Orin. The top floor can be accessed multiple ways: from inside - through the door in north-west corner of the Audience Hall from outside - using scaffolds and ladders attached to the walls, as well as various means of spatial or enhanced movement: Grant Flight , Misty Step or Dimension Door spells, Potion of Glorious Vaulting and the like. In the centre of the rooftop is a two-storied building, where the first level is Gortash's personal chambers, and the second is a bell tower (with a square gallery inside around the bell mechanism). Along the crenellations several ballistas are stationed, and at the bell tower roof stands a trebuchet. Both eastern and western sides of the rooftop offer a magnificent vista onto the river Chionthar and on the riverside part of the Lower City afar. Around the rooftop and atop the bell tower are multiple containers which can be be looted for various kinds of uncommon, rare and very rare arrows and potions: X: 23 Y: 184 - Heavy Chest X: 22 Y: 184 - trapped Wooden Chest (accessible only via means of spatial movement) X: 29 Y: 218 - Metal Trunk and Metal Crate near the blue tent X: -26 Y: 200 - Wooden Crate X: -12 Y: 203 - Wooden Chest X: -1 Y: 208 - Heavy Chest (most upper ground, near the trebuchet) X: 21 Y: 236 - the Thief's Stash (disguised as a pile of stone blocks; its location can be wrested out of Reynash or requires an Investigation check to reveal otherwise) The rooftop is guarded by several Steel Watchers walking back and forth as well as being outfitted with several of Gortash's defensive inventions and Stunner Vents surrounding the Archduke's chambers. There are also three dead Bhaalists on the rooftop. One can be looted for Assassin's Instructions , a note which reveals that these cultists were sent by Orin to haunt and murder Gortash. Seemingly, they were no match for the Steel Watchers stationed there. Gortash's private chambers [ edit section | visual editor ] Combined map of Gortash's personal quarters and the bell tower gallery Gortash's chambers consist of his personal apartments and an antechamber. The antechamber features six busts of legendary leaders of Baldur's Gate. One of these busts depicts "The Cockeyed Stranger", as Bane who first appeared before Enver Gortash [ 2 ] . At the eastern wall is a movable ladder which is initially raised to the upper gallery but can be lowered via a lever up there. After his ordination, Enver Gortash waits for the party at the far end of his apartment guarded by Black Gauntlet Numia , Black Gauntlet Ulova , Iron Consul Jaxbock , Iron Consul Lo , and another Steel Watcher. The room inside is equipped with many of Gortash's devices. Gortash's personal quarters The course of the dialogue with Gortash depends on whether the player character has previously struck an alliance with him, whether they fulfilled the terms of agreement, and also on whether Karlach is present. Confronting and killing Gortash without Karlach in the party brings a fair amount of disapproval   -20 from her. Gortash's apartment has several chests (the locked one is opened with Gortash's Key , looted or pickpocketed from him). Inside the Helldusk Boots and the Servitor of the Black Hand Gloves can be found. Also, behind the picture at X: -34 Y: 202 a wall safe is hidden ( DC 15 Perception Check to detect). It is opened with the same key and contains High Security Vault nº5 Key and a unique Elixir of Health . Two more chests with some minor amount of gold and valuables are at the upper gallery. Also, a fair amount of books are on the conference table in the middle of the room, as well as at Gortash's desk and on a display box near it. In the safe is a copy of Shield Steward Interrogation Log , which provide the party with some facts on how Gortash figured out the lurking presence of The Emperor behind the Knights of the Shield leadership. On the table in the antechamber lies a receipt for a full-height portrait of Bane. The portrait itself is upstairs, with a modest altar beneath. The God of Tyranny is depicted here exactly the same as he is portrayed on a mural in the final after-Epilogue cutscene with Withers . Wyrm's Rock traps [ edit section | visual editor ] Gortash has outfitted Wyrm's Rock Fortress with a variety of traps. These traps only become active during combat. ## Wyrm's Rock Prison
- **来源**: [Wyrm's Rock Prison](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wyrm's_Rock_Prison)
- **分类**: Act_Three_Locations

A corridor in the prison with cells Wyrm's Rock Fortress The Wyrmway ← Wyrm's Rock Prison Wyrm's Rock Prison is a Location within Wyrm's Rock Fortress in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 . The prison occupies the fortress's basement. While inside, the party cannot fast-travel to a Waypoint or go to camp . “ Welcome to Wyrm's Rock Prison - the Fist nail, we jail. What's your business? „ — Breva Brightmoon , greeting the player Contents 1 Overview 1.1 Main corridor 1.2 Cells 1.3 Guardroom 1.4 Storeroom 1.5 Western block 1.6 Dealing with the unusual Skull 1.6.1 Meeting the skull 1.6.2 The game 1.6.3 Outcomes 1.6.4 Notes 2 Related locations 3 Related quests 4 Characters 5 Related Literature 6 Notes and references Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the prison Main corridor [ edit section | visual editor ] The main corridor has a rough T-junction form, with the main enfilade [ 1 ] connecting the cells' part and the entrance from the Wyrm's Rock Fortress. The side corridor connects it to the Storage Room, while through its short western appendix that grants the access to The Wyrmway . Both the main and side corridors are constantly patrolled by Fist Ivarus . Along the left row of the cells stand the Evidence Chest and the Equipment Chest, where all the inventory belongings of an arrested party member can be found. If multiple items are confiscated and stored, picking out each one of them prompts a single Stealth check. It is recommended to exercise care if using invisibility here. A bug with possessing the Necromancy of Thay has been reported several times: as the book is bound to the character who read it and cannot be removed from their inventory, it may disappear when the character in question is arrested and all their belongings are placed in prison chests. This effectively deprives the character from completing the ⁠ Unlock the Ancient Tome quest. Cells [ edit section | visual editor ] There are five cells in the prison, located in the far end of the main corridor. They might be occupied as described below: Western cell: (empty) Northwestern cell: occupied by Counsellor Florrick . She is imprisoned here upon initiating ⁠ Free Counsellor Florrick , and after that, for five days more (counted down by long rests), unless the party help her escape. Northern cell: cell is occupied by Arfur Gregorio's corpse. His corpse is here if the player character convinced the toymaker to turn himself in. Northeastern cell: occupied by Otto Ott , an elderly man who got into the habit of being jailed to have a guaranteed meal and place for sleep. The player character may call him their father to get access into the prison through the main entrance. Eastern cell: occupied by any party member should they commit a crime in Rivington, in Wyrm's Crossing or within Wyrm's Rock Fortress itself. Alternatively a party member can end up here if they drink Hoots' Hooch which results in Hoots' Hooch: Blackout in which case Fist Ivarus wakes them up and mocks them. A skeleton chained to the wall inside it can be looted for The True Life of 'Lord' Gortash note. Also, Marvin the Unusual Skull can be found in this cell (see below). Guardroom [ edit section | visual editor ] The guardroom is actually an empty cell which the guards ( Fist Saunder , Fist Creekrider and Fist Jagic ) occupy to while away the time of their duties. If a party member enters the prison by peaceful means, or makes their way inside stealthily, or convinces the guards that they have any plausible reason to be there, the guards will remain inside the guardroom, sitting and chatting around the table. Storeroom [ edit section | visual editor ] This is the room in the far end of the side corridor. It is locked and red-outlined; opening it from either side is, if noticed, taken as a violation by Ivarus. Inside are several barrels and containers of food. At the northern wall of the storeroom is a weak wall, which can be breached by weapons or magic. Generally, if the door to the storeroom is closed, the prison guards do not react to any suspicious commotion in the storeroom, including the sounds of wall stones crumbling down. Behind it is a short cave which leads to another breach, this time in the outer wall of the fortress, opening to the foot of the rock. This is one of the possible routes to escape the prison. Western block [ edit section | visual editor ] This is the short extension of the side corridor, laden with various barrels and boxes. On its southern wall are two dragon head torches. Lighting them anew with any ⁠ lightning damage allows the party to enter The Wyrmway, but casting spells or shooting arrows to do so is berated by Ivarus if he notices. However, he does not mind if the party walk through the wall (and back if needed) after successfully opening the way. Dealing with the unusual Skull [ edit section | visual editor ] “ The merriment laid before thee is born of trifling jest, wizardry - and whiskey. „ Meeting the skull [ edit section | visual editor ] Marvin the Unusual Skull If any party member commits a crime in Rivington , Wyrm's Crossing or within the walls of Wyrm's Rock Fortress and consents to arrest, they will find themselves in a cell of the Wyrm's Rock Prison . On the back wall of the cell are broken shelves, where the arrested party member can find the Unusual Skull . Even if not noticed at once, the skull attracts their attention with a cheerful greeting. If spoken to, the skull identifies itself as Marvin (called such hereafter) and explains it is imbued by a spirit of a wizard who was occupying this very cell "after a night of bacchanalian debauchery" somewhere far, far in the past. A successful DC 15 Arcana Check sheds some light on this peculiar enchantment. By default, Marvin uses florid speech with an abundance of archaic words that may be difficult to understand. However, he can be persuaded to speak more plainly (this option requires DC 18 Persuasion Check ). Marvin suggests the imprisoned party member a deal of sorts: for solving two riddles correctly it helps them escape. However, if they answer any of the riddles wrong, the skull plays a trick on them, though it warns them of this honestly. The game [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party member agrees to solve the riddles, Marvin asks them one after another, offering three possible answers for each (only one is correct). First riddle: I fly, yet not through the firmament. I bidst and biddeth and bidstseth farewell at night and welcome thee in the morn. I am part of thee, and follow whither thou guideth. I am clothened and claddened all in black, and flee the light. Yet apart 't, I wouldst be nought. Name me. Simple speech formulation: I fly, but not through the sky. I say goodbye at night and hello in the morning. I am part of you, and follow wherever you go. I wear only black, and run from the light. Yet without it, I couldn't exist. Who am I? Possible answers: "A child", "A raven", "A shadow" (correct). Second riddle: I am battered, but nev'r did bow. Mine coronet bears the blunt of endless blades, but I can nev'r move. I nev'r did sweat, even when the summertide sun didst fully heateth mine brow. Name me. Simple speech formulation: I am beaten and battered, but never break. My crown has felt the strike of endless blades, yet I can never move. I never sweat, even when the summertide sun shines upon me. Who am I? Possible answers: "An anvil" (correct), "A king", "A shield". Outcomes [ edit section | visual editor ] Possible outcomes of dealing with Marvin are as following: Both riddles solved. Marvin teleports the imprisoned party member out of the cell, placing them next to the Evidence chests, and casts Haste and Greater Invisibility on them for 10 turns. Only one riddle solved correctly. Marvin teleports the imprisoned party member out of the cell, next to the entrance to the guardroom, and casts Haste and Mirror Image on them for 10 turns. None of the riddles solved. Marvin teleports the imprisoned party member out of the cell, next to the entrance to the guardroom, and casts on Haste on them for 10 turns. However, regardless of their shrewdness, the party member also automatically receives the Fugitive condition for 20 turns (like any other jailbreaker). After teleporting, turn-based mode is not launched automatically. Should the imprisoned party member refuse to play the game at all, or choose to stop guessing once the first riddle has been asked, Marvin considers this as if both given answers are wrong, with consequences described above. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Once having played his game with the party member, Marvin 'remembers' the achieved result and uses it again should the party member (in the same lineup or another [ verify ] ) find themselves jailed anew. The whole plot with escaping the prison in exchange for solving riddles occurs only if and when a party member is arrested for a crime. Entering the prison by any other means (e.g., sneaking through the wall breach from outside) does not result in the above interactions with Marvin - it instead shoos them off in the same refined manner of speech. Successful solving each of the riddles, as well as successful persuading Marvin to speak in common language, grants a point of approval from all companions (up to three points total). Rage ( + ) Deal 2 extra damage with melee and improvised weapons, and throwing. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Unarmoured Defence Your body is as resilient as any armour. While not wearing armour , you add your Constitution Modifier to your Armour Class . Level 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] Reckless Attack ( ) Throw all caution in the wind to gain Advantage on your melee Attack Roll . Until your next turn, you have advantage on attack rolls, but enemies also have advantage on attack rolls against you. Danger Sense You sense when things aren't as they should be. You have Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , such as against traps, spells , and surfaces . To gain this benefit, you can't be Blinded or Incapacitated . Level 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Rage Charges : 3 Gain an additional Rage Charge. You can now Rage more times per long rest. Select a subclass [ edit section | visual editor ] All subclasses receive a special version of Rage that replaces the standard Barbarian class action. Level 5 [ edit section | visual editor ] Extra Attack You can make an additional free attack after making an unarmed or weapon attack. Fast Movement Your Movement Speed increases by 3 m (10 ft) while not wearing Heavy Armour . Cleric is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Clerics are representatives of the gods they worship, wielding potent divine magic for good or ill. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.1.1 Select a subclass (Domain) 5.2 Level 2 5.2.1 Subclass feature - Domain actions 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Domain Spells (always prepared): 5.4 Level 4 5.5 Level 5 5.5.1 Domain Spells (always prepared): 5.6 Level 6 5.6.1 Subclass features - Domain actions 5.7 Level 7 5.7.1 Domain Spells (always prepared): 5.8 Level 8 5.8.1 Subclass features - Domain actions 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Domain Spells (always prepared): 5.10 Level 10 5.11 Level 11 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable clerics 7 Notes 8 See also 9 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Clerics worship and enact their deity's will to the world, for better or worse. They channel the power of their faith to cast Spells . Clerics use Wisdom as their primary ability score. Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Cleric Subclasses, or Domains , are: Death Knowledge Life Light Nature Tempest Trickery War Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Cleric Class Progression Spell Slots per Spell Level Level Proficiency Bonus Features Subclass Channel Divinity Charges Cantrips Known 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 1st +2 Spellcasting Choose a subclass - 3 2 - - - - - 2nd Turn Undead Channel Divinity use 1 3 - - - - - 3rd - 2 Domain spells 4 2 - - - - 4th Feat - 4 4 3 - - - - 5th +3 Destroy Undead 2 Domain spells 4 3 2 - - - 6th - Subclass feature 2 4 3 3 - - - 7th - 2 Domain spells 4 3 3 1 - - 8th Feat Subclass feature 4 3 3 2 - - 9th +4 - 2 Domain spells 4 3 3 3 1 - 10th Divine Intervention - 5 4 3 3 3 2 - 11th - - 4 3 3 3 2 1 12th Feat - 4 3 3 3 2 1 Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Cleric's default armour Hit points At level 1: 8 + Constitution modifier On level up: 5 + Constitution modifier Key abilities Wisdom for Spells Constitution for Hit Points and Concentration checks Dexterity for Armour Class . Spellcasting ability Wisdom Prepared spells For a list of spells available to the Cleric, see: List of Cleric spells . You may swap your prepared spells at any time while out of combat, but can only have a certain number of spells prepared at a time. The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. Number of prepared spells = Cleric level + Wisdom modifier (Minimum of 1 spell.) Starting Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving throw proficiencies Wisdom , Charisma Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Flails , Morningstars Light armour , Medium armour Shields Skill proficiencies (Choose 2) History , Insight , Medicine , Persuasion , Religion You receive a bonus to every skill that you are proficient in. At character level 1, this proficiency bonus is +2. Starting equipment Mace , Chain Shirt , Studded Shield , Leather Boots Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment proficiencies Flails , Morningstars Light armour , Medium armour Shields Skill proficiencies (Choose 2 [ 1 ] ) Same list as Starting Proficiencies Level progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Through experience, you acquire new power. You gain the following traits. Level 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] Select Deity Bahamut Corellon Larethian Eilistraee Garl Glittergold Gruumsh Helm Ilmater Kelemvor Laduguer Lathander Lolth Mielikki Moradin Mystra Oghma Selûne Talos Tempus Tiamat Tymora Tyr Vlaakith Yondalla A Cleric's choice of deity provides access to some unique conversation options throughout the game, but have few gameplay implications otherwise. The deities that trigger the most unique options are Selûne and Mystra, mostly due to interactions with Shadowheart and Gale respectively. Some Cleric spells have visual effects that incorporate the chosen deity's symbol. Note that choice of deity is restricted by the race and subrace of the cleric. Only Githyanki have the option to choose Vlaakith as a deity, only Duergar have the option to choose Laduguer as a deity, Lolth-Sworn Drow may only choose Lolth as a deity, and Seldarine Drow cannot choose Lolth as a deity. The deity choice for Shadowheart is fixed, and the deity choice screen will not show when selecting the Cleric class. She will have Shar as picked deity. ## Druid
- **来源**: [Druid](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Druid)
- **分类**: Classes

Druid is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Druids channel the elemental forces of nature and share a deep kinship with animals. Mastery of Wild Shape allows them to transform into beasts from all over the Realms. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.2 Level 2 5.2.1 Select a subclass 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Subclass features 5.4 Level 4 5.4.1 Subclass Features 5.5 Level 5 5.5.1 Subclass Features 5.6 Level 6 5.6.1 Subclass Features 5.7 Level 7 5.7.1 Subclass Features 5.8 Level 8 5.8.1 Subclass Features 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Subclass Features 5.10 Level 10 5.10.1 Subclass Features 5.11 Level 11 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable Druids 7 See also 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Druids are closely attuned with nature and the animals that live in it. They utilize the power of nature to cast Spells and have the ability to transform into various creatures. Druids use Wisdom as their primary ability score. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Druid's default armour Hit points At level 1: 8 + Constitution modifier On level up: 5 + Constitution modifier Key ability scores Wisdom for spells Constitution for hit points and Concentration checks Dexterity for Armour Class Spellcasting ability Wisdom Prepared spells For a list of spells available to druids, see: List of Druid spells . You may swap your prepared spells at any time while out of combat, but can only have a certain number of spells prepared at a time. The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. Number of Prepared Spells = Druid Level + Wisdom Modifier (minimum of 1 spell.) Wild Shape: Badger ( + ) Assume the shape of a giant badger that can Burrow into the ground. The badger has a starting health of 13 hit points that increases every two druid levels. Wild Shape: Cat ( + ) Take the shape of a cat that can avoid attention and Meow to distract enemies. It has 2 hit points . Wild Shape: Spider ( + ) Assume the shape of of a giant spider that can   Enweb enemies. The giant spider has a starting health of 20 hit points that increases every two druid levels. Wild Shape: Wolf ( + ) Assume the shape of a dire wolf that can   Incite allies and   Distract enemies. The dire wolf has a starting health of 18 hit points that increase every two druid levels. Wild Shape Charges : 2 The number of times you can use your Wild Shape. Replenished with a Short or Long Rest .
