## Fighter
- **来源**: [Fighter](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fighter)
- **分类**: Classes

Fighter is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Fighters have mastered the art of combat, wielding weapons with unmatched skill and wearing armour like a second skin. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.2 Level 2 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Select a subclass 5.4 Level 4 5.4.1 Subclass features: 5.5 Level 5 5.6 Level 6 5.7 Level 7 5.7.1 Subclass features: 5.8 Level 8 5.8.1 Subclass features: 5.9 Level 9 5.10 Level 10 5.10.1 Subclass features: 5.11 Level 11 5.11.1 Subclass features: 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable fighters 7 See also Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Fighters use their martial expertise to fight enemies and support their allies in combat. Fighters use Strength or Dexterity as their primary ability score. Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Fighter subclasses are: Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Fighter Class Progression Level Proficiency Bonus Features 1st +2 Second Wind , Fighting Style 2nd Action Surge 3rd Choose a subclass 4th Feat 5th +3 Extra Attack 6th Feat 7th Subclass feature 8th Feat 9th +4 Indomitable 10th Subclass feature 11th Improved Extra Attack 12th Feat Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Fighter's default armour Hit points At Level 1: 10 + Constitution Modifier On level up: 6 + Constitution Modifier Key Ability Scores Strength for physical attacks. Dexterity for physical attacks with Finesse and Ranged weapons, Armour Class (non- Heavy armour ), and Initiative . Constitution for Hit Points (and Concentration Checks for Eldritch Knights ). Intelligence for Spells (Eldritch Knight and Arcane Archer). Spellcasting Ability Intelligence for the effective use of items, scrolls, and equipment. Starting Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving throw proficiencies Strength , Constitution Equipment Proficiencies Simple weapons , Martial weapons Light armour , Medium armour , Heavy armour Shields Skills proficiencies (Choose 2) Acrobatics , Animal Handling , Athletics , History , Insight , Intimidation , Perception , Survival You receive a bonus to every Skill that you are Proficient in. At character level 1 the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Starting Equipment Longsword , Scale Mail , Leather Boots Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment Proficiencies Simple weapons , Martial weapons Light armour , Medium armour Shields Level progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Through experience, you acquire new power. You gain the following traits. Level 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] Second Wind ( ) Draw on your stamina to protect yourself. You regain 1d10 + Fighter Level ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . ( Recharge: Short rest .) Fighting Style Choose a fighting style: Archery You gain a +2 bonus to Attack Rolls you make with ranged Weapons . Defence You gain a +1 bonus to Armour Class while wearing armour . Duelling When you are wielding a melee weapon that is not Two-Handed in one hand, and no weapon in the other, you deal an additional 2 damage with that weapon. Great Weapon Fighting When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack with a Two-Handed melee weapon, that die is rerolled once. Protection When you have a Shield , impose Disadvantage on an enemy who attacks one of your allies when you are within 1.5 m (5 ft). You must be able to see the enemy. Two-Weapon Fighting When you make an offhand attack, you can add your Ability Score Modifier to the damage of the attack. Level 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] Action Surge Immediately gain an extra Action to use this turn. ( Recharge: Short rest .) Level 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Select a subclass [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Gain Arcana proficiency. Gain Nature proficiency. Gain 4 Arcane Arrows Choose 3 Arcane Shots Gain one of the following cantrips: Guidance Light True Strike Gain 4 Superiority Dice Choose 3 Battle Manoeuvres Improved Critical Hit Weapon Bond New Spells: Gain two Level 1 Spell Slots Choose 2 Cantrips Choose 2 Spells (schools of Abjuration or Evocation only) Choose 1 Spell (any spell school) Level 4 [ edit section | visual editor ] Choose a Feat . ## Monk
- **来源**: [Monk](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Monk)
- **分类**: Classes

Monk is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Some reach enlightenment by languid meditation - others do so in the heat of battle. Monks manipulate ki to empower their own strikes and debilitate their foes. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.1.1 Martial Arts 5.2 Level 2 5.2.1 Step of the Wind 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Select a subclass 5.4 Level 4 5.4.1 Subclass features: 5.5 Level 5 5.5.1 Stunning Strike 5.5.2 Subclass features: 5.6 Level 6 5.6.1 Subclass features: 5.7 Level 7 5.8 Level 8 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Subclass features: 5.10 Level 10 5.11 Level 11 5.11.1 Subclass features: 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable monks 7 Notes and references 8 See also 9 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Monks are unarmed combatants capable of spending Ki Points to perform special abilities. Monk's key ability scores are Wisdom , Dexterity , and Constitution , and their core ability is Unarmed Strike . Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Monk Subclasses are: Way of the Drunken Master Way of the Four Elements Way of the Open Hand Way of Shadow Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Monk Class Progression Level Proficiency Bonus Features Ki Points Martial Arts Unarmoured Movement 1st +2 Unarmoured Defence , Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks , Martial Arts: Deft Strikes , Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike , Flurry of Blows 2 1d4 - 2nd Unarmoured Movement , Patient Defence , Step of the Wind: Dash , Step of the Wind: Disengage 3 + 3 m / 10 ft 3rd Choose a subclass , Deflect Missiles 4 1d6 4th Feat , Slow Fall 5 5th +3 Extra Attack , Stunning Strike (Melee) , Stunning Strike (Unarmed) 6 6th Ki-Empowered Strikes , Subclass feature , Improved Unarmoured Movement 7 + 4.5 m / 15 ft 7th Evasion , Stillness of Mind 8 8th Feat 9 9th +4 Advanced Unarmoured Movement , Subclass feature 10 1d8 10th Purity of Body , Improved Unarmoured Movement 11 + 6 m / 20 ft 11th Subclass feature 12 12th Feat 13 Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Monk's default armour Hit points At level 1: 8 + Constitution modifier On level up: 5 + Constitution modifier Key abilities Dexterity for bonuses to attack and damage rolls of unarmed strikes and monk weapons as well as Ki saving throw DCs . Constitution for more Hit Points. Wisdom for improved Armour Class . For Way of the Four Elements abilities, also improves Ki attack rolls and saving throw DCs . Monk weapons Monk weapons are weapons the Monk has Proficiency with (from any source, including race and multiclassing), and have neither the Heavy nor Two-Handed properties. Versatile weapons count as Monk weapons even if they are wielded with both hands. Monks can use Dexterity for those weapons, even if they do not have the Finesse property. Some Monk abilities, such as Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike , are limited to Monk weapons. Spellcasting ability Wisdom for the effective use of items, scrolls, and equipment. Most Monk features use the associated weapon ability (e.g., the better of Strength or Dexterity). However, Way of the Four Elements Monks use their spellcasting ability for their unique class features other than Fangs of the Fire Snake [ 1 ] and Water Whip . Starting Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving throw proficiencies Strength , Dexterity Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Shortswords Skills with proficiency (Choose 2) History , Insight , Religion , Acrobatics , Stealth , Athletics You receive a bonus to every Skill that you are Proficient in. At character level 1 the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Starting Equipment Quarterstaff , Monastic Robes , Monastic Boots Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Shortswords Level progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Through experience, you acquire new power. You gain the following traits. Level 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 2 You can spend these points to fuel various Monk abilities. Ki abilities which incorporate an unarmed attack use the higher of Dexterity or Strength for attack rolls and save DCs. This includes all offensive abilities outside of the Way of the Four Elements subclass. Recharge: Short rest Martial Arts [ edit section | visual editor ] Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks Attacks with Monk weapons and unarmed attacks scale with your Dexterity instead of your Strength if your Dexterity is higher. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike After making an attack with a melee Monk weapon or while unarmed, you can make another unarmed attack as a bonus action. Unarmoured Defence Your reflexes are as effective as any armour . While not wearing armour, you add your Wisdom Modifier to your Armour Class . Flurry of Blows ( + ) Punch twice in quick succession. Level 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 3 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Unarmoured Movement Your movement speed increases by 3 m (10 ft) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield. Patient Defence ( + ) Attack Rolls against you have Disadvantage , and you have Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws . Step of the Wind [ edit section | visual editor ] Step of the Wind: Dash ( + ) Double your movement speed. Jump no longer requires a Bonus Action . Step of the Wind: Disengage ( + ) Move without triggering Opportunity Attacks . Jump no longer requires a Bonus Action . Level 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 4 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning (previously 1d4) damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Select a subclass [ edit section | visual editor ] Way of the Drunken Master Way of the Four Elements Way of the Open Hand Way of Shadow Cheeky Tipple Drunken Performance Drunken Technique Harmony of Fire and Water Select 3 subclass spells from: Blade of Rime Chill of the Mountain Fangs of the Fire Snake Fist of Four Thunders Fist of Unbroken Air Rush of the Gale Spirits Shaping of the Ice Sphere of Elemental Balance Sweeping Cinder Strike Touch of the Storm Water Whip Flurry of Blows: Topple Flurry of Blows: Stagger Flurry of Blows: Push Shadow Arts: Hide Shadow Arts: Pass Without Trace Shadow Arts: Darkness Shadow Arts: Darkvision Shadow Arts: Silence Gain a free cantrip: Minor Illusion Deflect Missiles ( ) Reduce the damage from a ranged weapon attack by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level. If the damage is reduced to 0, you can use a Ki Point to   Deflect the Missile . Use your Reaction to reduce the damage from a ranged weapon attack by 1d10 + your Dexterity Modifier + your monk level. If the damage is reduced to 0, you can use a Ki Point to return the missile back to the sender. Level 4 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 5 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Choose a Feat . Subclass features: [ edit section | visual editor ] Way of the Drunken Master Way of the Four Elements Way of the Open Hand Way of Shadow Intoxicating Strike Life of the Party (none) (none) (none) Slow Fall When you fall, you can use your reaction to gain Resistance to Falling damage. Level 5 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 6 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Stunning Strike [ edit section | visual editor ] Stunning Strike (Melee) ( + ) Spend a Ki Point to deal normal weapon damage and possibly Stun the target. Stunning Strike (Unarmed) ( + ) Spend a Ki Point to deal normal unarmed damage and possibly Stun the target. Subclass features: [ edit section | visual editor ] Way of the Drunken Master Way of the Four Elements Way of the Open Hand Way of Shadow (none) (none) (none) Cloak of Shadows Extra Attack You can make an additional free attack after making an unarmed or weapon attack. Level 6 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 7 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Improved Unarmoured Movement Your movement speed increases by 4.5 m (15 ft) (previously 3 m (10 ft)) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield. Ki-Empowered Strikes Your unarmed attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming enemies' Resistance and Immunity to non-magical damage. Subclass features: [ edit section | visual editor ] Way of the Drunken Master Way of the Four Elements Way of the Open Hand Way of Shadow Leap to Your Feet Redirect Attack Select 1 spell from the Monk spell list. New Spells: Clench of the North Wind Embrace of the Inferno Gong of the Summit Manifestation of Body Manifestation of Mind Manifestation of Soul Wholeness of Body Shadow Step Level 7 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 8 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Evasion Your agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain spells. When a spell or effect would deal half damage on a successful Dexterity Saving Throw , it deals no damage if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail. Stillness of Mind If you are Charmed or Frightened , you automatically cast Stillness of Mind to remove the condition. Level 8 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 9 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Choose a Feat . Level 9 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 10 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes Attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks deal 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning (previously 1d6) damage, unless their normal damage is higher. Level 10 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ki Points : 11 You gain an additional Ki Point to fuel your monk techniques. Improved Unarmoured Movement Your movement speed increases by 6 m (20 ft) (previously 4.5 m (15 ft)) while you are not wearing armour or using a shield. Purity of Body You are Immune to Poison damage and can't be Poisoned or affected by disease thanks to the purifying ki flowing through your meridians. ## Paladin
- **来源**: [Paladin](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Paladin)
- **分类**: Classes

Paladin is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ A promise made so deeply that it becomes divine in itself flows through a paladin, burning bright enough to inspire allies and smite foes. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Oaths and Oathbreaking 5.1 Keeping Your Oath 5.2 Becoming an Oathbreaker 5.3 Restoring your Oath 6 Level progression 6.1 Level 1 6.1.1 Select a subclass 6.2 Level 2 6.3 Level 3 6.3.1 Subclass features - Channel Oath abilities 6.3.2 Oath Spells (always prepared): 6.4 Level 4 6.5 Level 5 6.5.1 Oath Spells (always prepared): 6.6 Level 6 6.7 Level 7 6.7.1 Subclass features 6.8 Level 8 6.9 Level 9 6.9.1 Oath Spells (always prepared): 6.10 Level 10 6.11 Level 11 6.12 Level 12 7 Notable paladins 8 See also 9 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Paladins are masters of a variety of weapons and armour. They channel the power of their sacred oath to heal the sick and injured and to smite their foes. Important Ability Scores for Paladins include Strength (or Dexterity ), Charisma , and Constitution . Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Paladin subclasses are: Oath of Devotion Oath of the Ancients Oath of the Crown Oath of Vengeance Oathbreaker Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Paladin Class Progression Spell Slots per Spell Level Level Proficiency Bonus Features Lay on Hands Charges 1st 2nd 3rd 1st +2 Divine Sense , Lay on Hands , Channel Oath , Choose a subclass 3 - - - 2nd Fighting Style , Spellcasting , Divine Smite 2 - - 3rd Divine Health , Subclass Feature 3 - - 4th Feat 4 3 - - 5th +3 Extra Attack 4 2 - 6th Aura of Protection 4 2 - 7th Subclass Feature 4 3 - 8th Feat 4 3 - 9th +4 Subclass Feature 4 3 2 10th Aura of Courage 5 4 3 2 11th Improved Divine Smite 4 3 3 12th Feat 4 3 3 Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Paladin's default armour Hit points At level 1: 10 + Constitution modifier On level up: 6 + Constitution modifier Key abilities Strength or Dexterity for physical attacks Charisma for Spells, Aura and Channel Oath Abilities Constitution for Hit Points and Concentration Checks. Spellcasting Ability Charisma Paladins are primarily martial fighters; they gain Spell Slots at 1/2 the rate of a full spellcaster. Prepared Spells For a list of spells available to the Paladin, see: List of Paladin spells . You may swap your Prepared Spells at any time while out of combat, but can only have a certain number of Spells prepared at a time. The Spells must be of a level for which you have Spell Slots. Number of Prepared Spells = Paladin Level + Charisma Modifier (Minimum of 1 spell). Starting Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving throw proficiencies Wisdom , Charisma Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Martial weapons Light armour , Medium armour , Heavy armour Shields Skills with proficiency (Choose 2) Athletics , Insight , Intimidation , Medicine , Persuasion , Religion You receive a bonus to every Skill that you are Proficient in. At character level 1 the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Starting Equipment Warhammer , Wooden Shield , Javelin x2, Scale Mail of the Ancients or Scale Mail of Devotion or Scale Mail of Vengeance or Scale Mail of the Crown , Leather Boots and Paladin Oaths and their Tenets Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Martial weapons Light armour , Medium armour Shields Oaths and Oathbreaking [ edit section | visual editor ] Keeping Your Oath [ edit section | visual editor ] Your choice of subclass during Character Creation determines the Oath you have taken. See Oath of the Ancients , Oath of Devotion , Oath of Vengeance , or Oath of the Crown for the full text of each Oath. The basic tenets can also be found embroidered on your starting Armour – except for Scale Mail of the Crown ; the starting armour of the Oath of the Crown has a bug where it displays the Oath of Devotion quote instead. As a Paladin, you must constantly adhere to the tenets of your Oath or you will lose the power it grants you. Taking any action that breaks your Oath will summon the Oathbreaker Knight and temporarily prevent you from using your Channel Oath abilities. (Other Paladin class features and always-prepared Oath spells will remain available.) Each subclass has different actions that will cause its oath to be broken. Here are some examples (see each subclass's individual wiki page for a more complete list): Oath of the Ancients: Killing a non-aggressive animal, raising the dead, or (in some cases) choosing an "Attack" dialogue option when more peaceful options are available. Oath of Devotion: Attacking a non-hostile creature, refusing to defend someone who is obviously in need of aid, or dishonorably deceiving your enemies (e.g., negotiating a peaceful resolution and then attacking anyway). Oath of Vengeance: Convincing someone not to take revenge on their transgressor, letting the guilty go without punishment, betraying those who were in need of vengeance and siding with their oppressor. Oath of the Crown: Breaking promises, siding against legitimate rulers, agreeing to (and following through on) criminal plots Becoming an Oathbreaker [ edit section | visual editor ] *A spasm grips your chest. Your strength falters. An emptiness grows within you, Paladin. Something has been lost.* Unlike the other Paladin subclasses, the Oathbreaker subclass is not available during Character Creation . Once you take an action that breaks your Oath, the Oathbreaker Knight will appear before you and let you know he will be waiting in your Camp . Speak with him to learn about Oathbreaking and, if you so desire, unlock the Oathbreaker subclass. This replaces the Channel Oath abilities and Spells from your previous Oath with new abilities and Spells available only to Oathbreaker . Withers will not respec a Paladin who has the Oathbreaker subclass. Restoring their original Oath (see below) will enable the respec service again. Restoring your Oath [ edit section | visual editor ] If you break your Oath by accident or otherwise wish to re-dedicate yourself to your Oath, speak to the Oathbreaker Knight in your Camp . He will offer to restore your Oath for a fee of 1000gp. This will allow you to once again use your Channel Oath abilities. However, should you break your oath again, the cost to restore your oath will increase to 2000gp. If you break your oath a third time, the price will increase to 10,000gp. It stays at 10,000gp for each subsequent oath restoration after the third one. Level progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Through experience, you acquire new power. You gain the following traits. Level 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] Lay on Hands Charges : 3 Recharge: Long rest Channel Oath Charges : 1 Recharge: Short rest Divine Sense ( ) Tap into your spiritual awareness to gain Advantage on Attack Rolls against celestials , fiends , and undead . ( Recharge: Short rest .) Lay on Hands ( + ) Use your blessed touch to heal a creature or cure it of all diseases and poisons . Select a subclass [ edit section | visual editor ] Oath of Devotion Oath of the Ancients Oath of the Crown Oath of Vengeance Oathbreaker Holy Rebuke Healing Radiance Righteous Clarity Inquisitor's Might Spiteful Suffering Level 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] Divine Smite ( + ) Your weapon deals an additional 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant DRS damage, increased by 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage when attacking Fiends or Undead . Fighting Style Choose a fighting style: Defence You gain a +1 bonus to Armour Class while wearing armour . Duelling When you are wielding a melee weapon that is not Two-Handed in one hand, and no weapon in the other, you deal an additional 2 damage with that weapon. Great Weapon Fighting When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack with a Two-Handed melee weapon, that die is rerolled once. Protection When you have a Shield , impose Disadvantage on an enemy who attacks one of your allies when you are within 1.5 m (5 ft). You must be able to see the enemy. Level 1 Spell Slots Unlocked: 2 You gain two Level 1 Spell Slots. Prepared Spells Choose a number of Spells = 2 (Paladin Level) + Charisma Modifier (Minimum of 1 spell.) Level 1 Spell Slots Unlocked: 3 You gain an additional Level 1 Spell Slot. Prepared Spells Choose a number of Spells = 3 (Paladin Level) + Charisma Modifier (Minimum of 1 spell.) Ranger is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Rangers are unrivalled scouts and trackers, honing a deep connection with nature in order to hunt their favoured prey. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.2 Level 2 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Select a subclass 5.4 Level 4 5.5 Level 5 5.5.1 Subclass features 5.6 Level 6 5.7 Level 7 5.7.1 Subclass features 5.8 Level 8 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Subclass features 5.10 Level 10 5.11 Level 11 5.11.1 Subclass features 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable rangers 7 See also 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] In tune with nature and their surroundings, Rangers utilize both their knowledge of the wilds and spellcasting to pursue their prey. Important Ability Scores for Rangers include Dexterity (or Strength ), Constitution , and Wisdom . Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Ranger Subclasses are: Beast Master Gloom Stalker Hunter Swarmkeeper Class progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Ranger class progression Spell Slots per Spell Level Level Proficiency Bonus Features Spells Known 1st 2nd 3rd 1st +2 Favoured Enemy , Natural Explorer - - - - 2nd Fighting Style , Spellcasting 2 2 - - 3rd Choose a subclass 3 3 - - 4th Feat 3 - - 5th +3 Extra Attack , Subclass Feature 4 4 2 - 6th Favoured Enemy , Natural Explorer 4 2 - 7th Subclass Feature 5 4 3 - 8th Feat , Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain 4 3 - 9th +4 - 6 4 3 2 10th Favoured Enemy , Natural Explorer , Hide in Plain Sight 4 3 2 11th Subclass Feature 7 4 3 3 12th Feat 4 3 4 Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Ranger's default armour Hit points At level 1: 10 + Constitution modifier On level up: 6 + Constitution modifier Key abilities Dexterity (or Strength ) for physical attacks Constitution for Hit Points and Concentration Checks Wisdom for Spells. Spellcasting Ability Wisdom Known Spells For a list of spells available to the Ranger, see: List of Ranger spells . Ranger Spells are Always Prepared. In exchange, Rangers know fewer Spells at low levels. Rangers are primarily martial fighters; they gain Spell Slots at 1/2 the rate of a full spellcaster. Starting Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving throw proficiencies Strength , Dexterity Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Martial weapons Light armour , Medium armour Shields Skill proficiencies (Choose 3) Animal Handling , Athletics , Insight , Investigation , Nature , Perception , Stealth , Survival You receive a bonus to every Skill that you are Proficient in. At character level 1 the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Starting Equipment Shortbow , Leather Armour (green variant), Leather Boots , Arrow of Ice Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Martial weapons Light armour , Medium armour Shields Skill proficiencies (Choose 1) Same list as Starting Proficiencies Level progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Through experience, you acquire new power. You gain the following traits. Creatures you hit with Ensnaring Strike (either ranged or melee) have Disadvantage on their Saving Throw . Investigation Proficiency Keeper of the Veil You specialize in hunting creatures from other planes of existence. You gain Proficiency in Arcana and can grant protection against aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. Arcana Proficiency Gain a free spell ( Recharge: Long rest ): Protection from Evil and Good Mage Breaker You have a history of battling spellcasters. Gain Proficiency with Arcana and True Strike , which gives you Advantage on Attack Rolls against a creature. Arcana Proficiency Gain a free cantrip: True Strike Ranger Knight You have sworn to serve a crown or nation and seek to bring its foes to ruin. Gain Proficiency with History and Proficiency with Heavy Armour . Heavy armour Proficiency History Proficiency Sanctified Stalker You swore to hunt the enemies of a holy or druidic order. Gain Proficiency with Religion and the Sacred Flame Cantrip , which deals 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage. Religion Proficiency Gain a free cantrip: Sacred Flame Natural Explorer Choose 1 Natural Explorer Natural Explorer Options Archetypes Description Grants Beast Tamer You have cultivated a strong bond with animals. You can cast Find Familiar as a ritual. Cast Find Familiar once per short rest Urban Tracker An expert at navigating the wild within the city, you gain Sleight of Hand Proficiency . Sleight of Hand Proficiency Wasteland Wanderer: Cold You have spent endless days surviving desolate tundras. Gain resistance to ⁠ Cold damage, taking only half damage from it. ⁠ Cold Resistance Wasteland Wanderer: Fire You have spent endless days surviving forbidding deserts. Gain resistance to ⁠ Fire , taking only half damage from it. ⁠ Fire Resistance Wasteland Wanderer: Poison You have spent endless days surviving fetid swamps. Gain resistance to ⁠ Poison , taking only half damage from it. ⁠ Poison Resistance Level 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] Fighting Style Gain 1 of the fighting styles: Archery You gain a +2 bonus to Attack Rolls you make with ranged Weapons . Defence You gain a +1 bonus to Armour Class while wearing armour . Duelling When you are wielding a melee weapon that is not Two-Handed in one hand, and no weapon in the other, you deal an additional 2 damage with that weapon. Two-Weapon Fighting When you make an offhand attack, you can add your Ability Score Modifier to the damage of the attack. ## Rogue
- **来源**: [Rogue](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rogue)
- **分类**: Classes

Rogue is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ With stealth, skill, and uncanny reflexes, rogues' versatility lets them get the upper hand in almost any situation. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.2 Level 2 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Select a subclass 5.4 Level 4 5.4.1 Subclass features 5.5 Level 5 5.6 Level 6 5.7 Level 7 5.7.1 Subclass features 5.8 Level 8 5.8.1 Subclass features 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Subclass Features 5.10 Level 10 5.10.1 Subclass features 5.11 Level 11 5.11.1 Subclass features 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable rogues 7 See also 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Rogues are well versed in the art of stealth and rely on their resourcefulness to be in control of any challenging situation. Rogues use Dexterity as their primary ability score. Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Rogue Subclasses are: Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Rogue Class Progression Level Proficiency Bonus Features Sneak Attack Damage 1st +2 Expertise , Sneak Attack (Melee) , Sneak Attack (Ranged) 1d6 2nd Cunning Action: Dash , Cunning Action: Disengage , Cunning Action: Hide 3rd Choose a subclass 2d6 4th Feat 5th +3 Uncanny Dodge 3d6 6th Expertise 7th Evasion 4d6 8th Feat 9th +4 Subclass feature 5d6 10th Feat 11th Reliable Talent 6d6 12th Feat Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Rogue's default armour Hit points At level 1: 8 + Constitution modifier On level up: 5 + Constitution modifier Key abilities Dexterity for physical attacks and Armour Class Constitution for Hit Points Intelligence for Spells (Arcane Trickster only) Charisma for "dirty trick" abilities (Swashbuckler only), (exception for sand toss) Spellcasting Ability Intelligence for the effective use of items, scrolls, and equipment. Starting Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving throw proficiencies Dexterity , Intelligence Equipment proficiencies Simple weapons , Hand Crossbows , Longswords , Rapiers , Shortswords Light armour Skills with proficiency (Choose 4) Acrobatics , Athletics , Deception , Insight , Intimidation , Investigation , Perception , Performance , Persuasion , Sleight of Hand , Stealth You receive a bonus to every Skill that you are Proficient in. At character level 1 the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Class Starting Equipment Shortsword , Leather Armour (purple variant), Leather Boots , Thieves' Tools , Grease Bottle x2 Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] Equipment proficiencies Light armour Skills with proficiency (Choose 1) Same list as Starting Proficiencies Level progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Through experience, you acquire new power. You gain the following traits. Level 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] Gain Expertise in 2 Skills you are Proficient in. Sneak Attack Sneak Attack (Melee) ( ) Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. ( Recharge: Per turn.) Sneak Attack (Ranged) ( ) Deal an extra 1d6 damage to a foe you have Advantage against. ( Recharge: Per turn.) Level 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] Cunning Action Cunning Action: Dash ( ) Cover more distance this turn: double your movement speed . Cunning Action: Disengage ( ) Retreat safely. Moving won't provoke Opportunity Attacks . Cunning Action: Hide ( ) Hide from enemies by succeeding at Stealth checks . Stick to the dark and avoid enemy sightlines. Attacking or casting a spell will reveal your location. Level 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneak Attack damage +2d6 (Your sneak attack gains an additional +1d6 damage.) Select a subclass [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Mage Hand Legerdemain Gain two Level 1 Spell Slots Gain Mage Hand Choose 2 Cantrips Choose 2 Spells (schools of Enchantment or Illusion only) Choose 1 Spell (any spell school) Assassin's Alacrity Assassinate: Ambush Assassinate: Initiative Fancy Footwork Rakish Audacity Rakish Sneak Attack (Melee) Rakish Sneak Attack (Ranged) Fast Hands Second-Story Work Level 4 [ edit section | visual editor ] Choose a Feat . Subclass features [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Gain one Level 1 Spell Slot Choose 1 Spell (schools of Enchantment or Illusion only) (none) Dirty Trick: Flick o' the Wrist Dirty Trick: Sand Toss Dirty Trick: Vicious Mockery (none) Level 5 [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneak Attack damage +3d6 (Your sneak attack gains an additional +1d6 damage.) Uncanny Dodge Use your lightning-quick reflexes to protect yourself. When an attack hits you, you only take half the usual damage. Level 6 [ edit section | visual editor ] Gain Expertise in 2 Skills you are Proficient in. Level 7 [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneak Attack damage +4d6 (Your sneak attack gains an additional +1d6 damage.) Evasion Your agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain spells. When a spell or effect would deal half damage on a successful Dexterity Saving Throw , it deals no damage if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail. Subclass features [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Gain one Level 1 Spell Slot Gain two Level 2 Spell Slots Choose 1 Spell (schools of Enchantment or Illusion only) (none) (none) (none) Level 8 [ edit section | visual editor ] Choose a Feat . Sorcerer is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Sorcerers are natural spellcasters, drawing on inherent magic from a gift or bloodline. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class progression 4 Class Information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level Progression 5.1 Level 1 5.1.1 Select a Subclass 5.2 Level 2 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Subclass Features 5.4 Level 4 5.5 Level 5 5.6 Level 6 5.6.1 Subclass Features 5.7 Level 7 5.8 Level 8 5.9 Level 9 5.10 Level 10 5.11 Level 11 5.11.1 Subclass Features 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable sorcerers 7 See also 8 External Links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Sorcerers use their innate magical powers to fight enemies and aid allies in combat. Sorcerers use Charisma as their primary ability score. Sorcery Points : 2 Recharge: Long rest Sorcery Points are the innate power of sorcerers. They can use these points to alter Spells or gain Spell Slots . You gain 2 Sorcery Points. Create Spell Slot ( + 2 ) Spend Sorcery Points to unlock a Spell Slot . Create Sorcery Points ( + ) Spend Spell Slots to gain Sorcery Points. The level of spell slot spent creates the equivalent number of Sorcery Points . Metamagic Choose 2 Metamagic: Metamagic Sorcery Points Grants Careful Spell 1 Allies automatically succeed Saving Throws against spells that require them. Distant Spell 1 Extends the range of a spell by 50%. Melee spells are increased to Range: 9 m (30 ft). Extended Spell 1 Double the duration of Conditions , summons, and surfaces caused by spells. Twinned Spell 1 per Spell Slot level (Cantrips are 1) Spells that only target 1 creature can target an additional creature. Warlock is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Bound by a pact to an all-powerful patron, warlocks trade their loyalty for supernatural abilities and unique magic. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.1.1 Select a subclass (patron) 5.1.2 Subclass Features - Expanded Spell List 5.2 Level 2 5.3 Level 3 5.3.1 Subclass Features - Expanded Spell List 5.4 Level 4 5.5 Level 5 5.5.1 Subclass Features - Expanded Spell List 5.6 Level 6 5.6.1 Subclass Features 5.7 Level 7 5.7.1 Subclass Features - Expanded Spell List 5.8 Level 8 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Subclass Features - Expanded Spell List 5.10 Level 10 5.10.1 Subclass Feature 5.11 Level 11 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable warlocks 7 See also 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Warlocks channel their patron's pact magic to fight enemies and aid allies in combat. Warlocks use Charisma as their primary ability score. Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Warlock Subclasses are: The Archfey The Fiend The Great Old One The Hexblade Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Warlock Class Progression Spell Slots per Spell Level Level Proficiency Bonus Features Invocations Known Cantrips Known Spells Known 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 1st +2 Pact Magic , Choose a Subclass - 2 2 1 - - - - 2nd Eldritch Invocations (+2) 2 3 2 - - - - 3rd Pact Boon 4 - 2 - - - 4th Feat 3 5 - 2 - - - 5th +3 Deepened Pact , Eldritch Invocations (+1) 3 6 - - 2 - - 6th Subclass feature 7 - - 2 - - 7th Eldritch Invocations (+1) 4 8 - - - 2 - 8th Feat 9 - - - 2 - 9th +4 Eldritch Invocations (+1) 5 10 - - - - 2 10th Subclass feature 4 11 - - - - 2 11th Mystic Arcanum (6th level spell) 12 - - - - 3 12th Feat , Eldritch Invocations (+1) 6 13 - - - - 3 Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Warlock's default armour Hit points At level 1: 8 + Constitution modifier On level up: 5 + Constitution modifier Key abilities Charisma for Spells Constitution for Hit Points and Concentration Dexterity for Armour Class For a list of spells available to the Warlock, see: List of Warlock spells . Spellcasting Ability Charisma Known spells For a list of spells available to the Warlock, see: List of Warlock spells . Warlock Spells are Always Prepared . In exchange, Warlocks know fewer Spells at low levels. Pact Magic Warlock spell slots (also known as "pact slots") are not like those of other spellcasters. Warlock spell slots are equal to the highest level of Spells the Warlock has access to. Casting a lower level Spell will always "upcast" it to the highest level available. Warlocks have a very limited number of spell slots, but also regain those slots by taking a Short Rest or Long Rest . As a result, Warlocks can cast fewer Spells per battle than other spellcasters, but also more high level Spells per day. At character level 1, the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Armour of Shadows You can cast Mage Armour on yourself at will, without expending a Spell Slot . Mage Armour increases your Armour Class when you are not wearing armour. Beast Speech You can cast Speak with Animals on yourself at will, without expending a Spell Slot . Beguiling Influence You invoke your patron's bewitching charm. You gain Proficiency in Deception and Persuasion . Devil's Sight You can see normally in darkness, both magical and non-magical, to a distance of 24 m (80 ft). Mask of Many Faces You can cast Disguise Self on yourself at will, without expending a Spell Slot . One with Shadows You learn how to cast One with Shadows . Repelling Blast When you hit a creature with Eldritch Blast , you can push the creature up to 4.5 m (15 ft) away from you. Wizard is a character class in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Wizards master the arcane by specialising in individual schools of magic, combining ancient spells with modern research. „ Contents 1 Overview 2 Subclasses 3 Class Progression 4 Class information 4.1 Attributes 4.2 Starting Proficiencies 4.3 Multiclass Proficiencies 5 Level progression 5.1 Level 1 5.2 Level 2 5.2.1 Select a Subclass (School) 5.3 Level 3 5.4 Level 4 5.5 Level 5 5.5.1 Subclass Features 5.6 Level 6 5.6.1 Subclass features 5.7 Level 7 5.8 Level 8 5.9 Level 9 5.9.1 Subclass Features 5.10 Level 10 5.10.1 Subclass features 5.11 Level 11 5.12 Level 12 6 Notable wizards 7 See also 8 External links Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Wizards channel magic through their extensive knowledge of the arcane to fight enemies and aid allies in combat. Wizards use Intelligence as their primary ability score. Subclasses [ edit section | visual editor ] The Wizard subclasses, also known as Schools , are: Abjuration Bladesinging Conjuration Divination Enchantment Evocation Illusion Necromancy Transmutation Class Progression [ edit section | visual editor ] Wizard Class Progression Spell Slots per Spell Level Level Proficiency Bonus Features Arcane Recovery Charges Cantrips Known Spells Learned 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th 6th 1st +2 Spellcasting , Arcane Recovery , Transcribing scrolls 1 3 6 2 - - - - - 2nd Choose a subclass 8 3 - - - - - 3rd - 2 10 4 2 - - - - 4th Feat 4 12 4 3 - - - - 5th +3 - 3 14 4 3 2 - - - 6th Subclass feature 16 4 3 3 - - - 7th - 4 18 4 3 3 1 - - 8th Feat 20 4 3 3 2 - - 9th +4 - 5 22 4 3 3 3 1 - 10th Subclass feature 5 24 4 3 3 3 2 - 11th - 6 26 4 3 3 3 2 1 12th Feat 28 4 3 3 3 2 1 Note: Proficiency bonus is based on character level , not class level. It is included in the table for convenience. Class information [ edit section | visual editor ] Wizard's default armour Scroll copying button on the Spellbook page Attributes [ edit section | visual editor ] Hit points At level 1: 6 + Constitution modifier On level up: 4 + Constitution modifier Key Ability Scores Intelligence for Spells Constitution for Hit Points and Concentration checks Dexterity for Armour Class Spellcasting Ability Intelligence Prepared spells You may swap your Prepared Spells at any time while out of combat, but can only have a certain number of Spells prepared at a time. The Spells must be of a level for which you have Spell Slots. For a list of spells available to the Wizard, see: List of Wizard spells . Transcribing scrolls A Wizard who finds a scroll for a spell they do not know may permanently copy that spell into their spellbook at the cost of the scroll and 50 gp per level of the spell. The spell must be on the Wizard class spell list , and be one for which the Wizard has a spell slot, even if they obtained it by multiclassing (so a L4 Cleric / L1 Wizard can transcribe Level 3 spells). For information about how this interacts with multiclassing , class changes, and unobtainable scrolls, see the dedicated page for this feature . At character level 1 the Proficiency Bonus is +2. Starting Equipment Quarterstaff , Simple Robe (green variant), Simple Boots Multiclass Proficiencies [ edit section | visual editor ] No proficiencies are granted when multiclassing into Wizard. Technical Stats MOO_MindTorturer Absolute Questioners are deep gnome Cult of the Absolute warlocks and capable torturers that specialize in a unique form of mental torture. Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Questioners are warlocks who adhere to the Absolute , whose main responsibility lies with the interrogation, torture, and conversion of prisoners held by the Cult of the Absolute. It's not clear if, like the zealots and adepts , the questioners are oblivious to the Absolute's standing as a false goddess, or like the Mistresses of Souls , if they are aware of the hoax-like nature of the Absolutist plot. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Two deep gnome questioners are initially encountered in the Moonrise Towers Prison , and under the circumstances that Minthara has reached Moonrise, they can be observed torturing and erasing her into a docile state. If not killed early, both questioners will automatically be killed during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers before the party can arrive. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Absolute Questioners are warlocks that with the abilities to inflict negative effects and cast Eldritch Blast on their opponents. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Blindness ( + ) Limit a foe's sight range. It is easier to hit, and the creature will miss more often. Attack rolls against it have Advantage and the foe attacks with Disadvantage . CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Cloud of Daggers ( + ) Damage: 4~16 4d4 ⁠ Slashing Conjure a cloud of spinning daggers that attack anyone inside. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Confusion ( + ) Befuddle a group of creatures, causing them to attack at random, wander around aimlessly, and occasionally skip turns in the stupor. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Eldritch Blast ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Force Conjure a beam of crackling energy. Deals 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to a target. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Known Absolute questioners [ edit section | visual editor ] Questioner Jasin Questioner Sumera Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] It's not clear who the questioners' patrons are, or if their warlock powers come from the Elder Brain itself. v t e Creature Archetypes Absolutists Absolute Questioner Acolyte of the Absolute Adept of the Absolute Inquisitor of the Absolute Zealot of the Absolute Banites Black Gauntlet of Bane Fist of Bane Iron Consul of Bane Bhaalists Death's Head of Bhaal Invoker of Bhaal Night Blade Reaper of Bhaal Myrkulites Mistress of Souls Counting House Counting House Artillerist Counting House Enforcer Flaming Fist Flaming Fist Archer Flaming Fist Guisarmier Flaming Fist Healer Flaming Fist Protector Flaming Fist Wizard Gather Your Allies Gur Hunter Sharpshooter Gur Hunter Warrior (Handaxe) Gur Hunter Warrior (Scimitar) Harper Archer Hellrider Cleric Hellrider Paladin Ironhand Grenadier Watcher Guardian Githyanki Ardent Gish Gish'ra (caster) Gish'ra (melee) Raider Veteran Gish Veteran Raider Veteran Warrior Warrior Youth Gnolls Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Redcaps Redcap Boatswain Redcap Mystic Cannoneer Goblins Goblin Booyahg Goblin Boss Goblin Brawler Goblin Devout Goblin Sapper Goblin Sharp-Eye Goblin Tracker Goblin Warlock Goblin Warrior Sharrans Justiciar Crusader Sharran Fidelian Sharran Novice Sharran Sentry Umberlants Dark Breaker Savage Seawind Untaken

Technical Stats MOO_AcolyteOfTheAbsolute_Human Variant 1 Stats MOO_AcolyteOfTheAbsolute_Elf Variant 2 Stats MOO_AcolyteOfTheAbsolute_Dwarf Variant 3 Stats MOO_AcolyteOfTheAbsolute_Duergar Acolytes of the Absolute are basic clerics that specialize in healing and supporting their fellow Absolutists . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Acolytes are devoted clerics of the Absolute, mainly specialized in healing and blessing their deadlier and more powerful allies. Like the zealots and adepts , and most other members of the broader Cult of the Absolute , acolytes are oblivious to the reality of the tadpoles and deceptive nature of the pretend-god, believing or being manipulated into believing that the Absolute is a new goddess. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Acolytes are primarily encountered within the halls of Moonrise Towers and in low numbers, serving as guards, and occasional handlers for new pilgrims. Each of the acolytes can be fought during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers if they were not killed before. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] A number of acolytes were initially present during the battle for High Hall , with all of them perishing during the City Watch's rout from High Hall. No living acolytes remain when the party arrives, with most being killed or incinerated by the Watch. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Acolytes are low-level clerics who focus on healing and blessing their fellow cultists during combat, only occasionally shooting their crossbows to harass their enemies when it is convenient to do so or when there are no allies to support. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bless ( + ) Bless up to 3 creatures. They gain a +1d4 bonus to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . Range: 9 m (30 ft) Cure Wounds ( + ) Healing: 1~8 + modifiers 1d8 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Healing Heal a creature you can touch. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Piercing Shot ( )   –   Light Crossbow Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Piercing Deal regular damage and possibly inflict Gaping Wounds which cause extra damage on attacks. Undead and constructs can't receive Gaping Wounds. CON Save Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Short rest Ranged Attack ( )   –   Light Crossbow Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Sacred Flame ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Radiant Engulf a target in a flame-like radiance. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Arrow of Ice Leather Armour Light Crossbow Known acolytes of the Absolute [ edit section | visual editor ] Belub Daine Kimmeral Marls Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Some members of this archetype may have slightly different passives, movement speed, weight, and size due to being members of different races. It is not clear who acolytes get their clerical spells from, as the Absolute is not a true god, and thus should not be able to grant its followers access to divine spells. v t e Creature Archetypes Absolutists Absolute Questioner Acolyte of the Absolute Adept of the Absolute Inquisitor of the Absolute Zealot of the Absolute Banites Black Gauntlet of Bane Fist of Bane Iron Consul of Bane Bhaalists Death's Head of Bhaal Invoker of Bhaal Night Blade Reaper of Bhaal Myrkulites Mistress of Souls Counting House Counting House Artillerist Counting House Enforcer Flaming Fist Flaming Fist Archer Flaming Fist Guisarmier Flaming Fist Healer Flaming Fist Protector Flaming Fist Wizard Gather Your Allies Gur Hunter Sharpshooter Gur Hunter Warrior (Handaxe) Gur Hunter Warrior (Scimitar) Harper Archer Hellrider Cleric Hellrider Paladin Ironhand Grenadier Watcher Guardian Githyanki Ardent Gish Gish'ra (caster) Gish'ra (melee) Raider Veteran Gish Veteran Raider Veteran Warrior Warrior Youth Gnolls Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Redcaps Redcap Boatswain Redcap Mystic Cannoneer Goblins Goblin Booyahg Goblin Boss Goblin Brawler Goblin Devout Goblin Sapper Goblin Sharp-Eye Goblin Tracker Goblin Warlock Goblin Warrior Sharrans Justiciar Crusader Sharran Fidelian Sharran Novice Sharran Sentry Umberlants Dark Breaker Savage Seawind Untaken

Technical Stats MOO_FanaticOfTheAbsolute_Human Variant 1 Stats MOO_FanaticOfTheAbsolute_HalfElf Variant 2 Stats MOO_FanaticOfTheAbsolute_Elf Variant 3 Stats MOO_FanaticOfTheAbsolute_Drow Variant 4 Stats MOO_FanaticOfTheAbsolute_HalfOrc Variant 5 Stats MOO_FanaticOfTheAbsolute_Halfling Adepts of the Absolute are potent cleric -based spellcasters adhering to the Cult of the Absolute . Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 2.1 Act Two 2.2 Act Three 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.2 Loot 4 Known adepts of the Absolute 4.1 Drow 4.2 Halfling 4.3 Half-elf 4.4 Half-orc 4.5 Human 5 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Adepts are devoted spellcasters and clerics of the Absolute. Like the zealots , and most other members of the broader Cult of the Absolute , adepts are oblivious to the reality of the tadpoles and deceptive nature of the pretend-god, believing or being manipulated into believing that the Absolute is a new goddess. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Adepts of the Absolute appear primarily in the halls of Moonrise Towers , acting as clerical enforcers and soldiers within the Absolute's army. A number of them can be fought during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] A large number of adepts were initially present during the battle for High Hall , with most of them perishing during the City Watch's rout from High Hall. Two adept of the Absolute remains present during the fight within the High Hall's courtyard, one the ramparts above the gate, other one hidden in the sewers. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Adepts are full spellcasters broadly similar to War Domain clerics , with the ability to cast the Hunger of Hadar warlock spell. Buffed with the Death Ward condition, they can survive otherwise fatal attacks once, and are capable of turning their allies' misses into hits through the War God's Blessing reaction. They have the ability to upcast spells ( ) and have the following abilities at their disposal: Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Command: Flee ( + ) Command a creature to flee from you on its turn and do nothing else. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per combat Death Ward ( + ) Protect a creature from death. The next time damage would reduce it to 0 Hit Points , it remains conscious with 1 Hit Point left. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Guardian of Faith ( + ) Call forth a divine guardian that attacks nearby enemies. Every time it deals damage, the guardian loses an equal amount of Hit Points . Range: 9 m (30 ft) Recharge: Per combat Guiding Bolt ( + ) Damage: 4~24 4d6 ⁠ Radiant The next attack roll against this target has Advantage . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Hunger of Hadar ( + ) Damage: 4~24 2d6 ⁠ Cold + 2d6 ⁠ Acid Creatures within this black sphere are Blinded and take damage at the end of their turn and the start of their turn. Creatures starting their turn in the area take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage. Creatures ending their turn in the area possibly take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage. The area is Difficult Terrain . DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per combat Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Quarterstaff Damage: 2~7 1d6 + 1 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Sacred Flame ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Radiant Engulf a target in a flame-like radiance. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Topple ( )   –   Quarterstaff Damage: 1~4 1d4 ⁠ Bludgeoning Swipe at a creature to knock it Prone . DEX Save Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Short rest Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Quarterstaff Scale Mail Known adepts of the Absolute [ edit section | visual editor ] Drow [ edit section | visual editor ] Adept Dorikel Adept Furek Adept Keris Halfling [ edit section | visual editor ] Adept Ghulen Half-elf [ edit section | visual editor ] Adept Bel Half-orc [ edit section | visual editor ] Adept Mola Human [ edit section | visual editor ] Adept Merim Adept Nola Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Some members of this archetype may have slightly different passives, movement speed, weight, and size due to being members of different races. It's possible that the "Adepts" were originally called "Fanatics" at some point in development. Some current dialogue files in the game still refer to certain Adepts as Fanatics, such as MOO_Bazaar_Guard00.html , the dialogue file for Adept Dorikel , who still refers to him as Fanatic Dorikel . It's also more consistent with the naming scheme of the Zealot of the Absolute , as Zealot and Fanatic have closer meanings. v t e Creature Archetypes Absolutists Absolute Questioner Acolyte of the Absolute Adept of the Absolute Inquisitor of the Absolute Zealot of the Absolute Banites Black Gauntlet of Bane Fist of Bane Iron Consul of Bane Bhaalists Death's Head of Bhaal Invoker of Bhaal Night Blade Reaper of Bhaal Myrkulites Mistress of Souls Counting House Counting House Artillerist Counting House Enforcer Flaming Fist Flaming Fist Archer Flaming Fist Guisarmier Flaming Fist Healer Flaming Fist Protector Flaming Fist Wizard Gather Your Allies Gur Hunter Sharpshooter Gur Hunter Warrior (Handaxe) Gur Hunter Warrior (Scimitar) Harper Archer Hellrider Cleric Hellrider Paladin Ironhand Grenadier Watcher Guardian Githyanki Ardent Gish Gish'ra (caster) Gish'ra (melee) Raider Veteran Gish Veteran Raider Veteran Warrior Warrior Youth Gnolls Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Redcaps Redcap Boatswain Redcap Mystic Cannoneer Goblins Goblin Booyahg Goblin Boss Goblin Brawler Goblin Devout Goblin Sapper Goblin Sharp-Eye Goblin Tracker Goblin Warlock Goblin Warrior Sharrans Justiciar Crusader Sharran Fidelian Sharran Novice Sharran Sentry Umberlants Dark Breaker Savage Seawind Untaken

Technical Stats Githyanki_IntelligenceOfficer Githyanki ardents are a class-like archetype of githyanki NPC encountered in Crèche Y'llek . Mages that specialize in psionic combat, ardents are the purest githyanki spellcasters encountered in the game. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Ardents wield a Githyanki Shortsword , though they will always prefer casting a cantrip over swinging their sword, unless forced by silence . Despite this reluctance for swordsmanship, they also benefit from an extra attack . Technical Stats Githyanki_Gish Githyanki gish are an archetype of githyanki character encountered throughout Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] As Battlemages who blend arcane spellcasting with melee combat, gish soldiers are versatile combatants. Regular gish troops are located in many places of githyanki influence. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Blindness ( + ) Limit a foe's sight range. It is easier to hit, and the creature will miss more often. Attack rolls against it have Advantage and the foe attacks with Disadvantage . CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Burning Hands ( + ) Damage: 3~18 3d6 ⁠ Fire Each flammable target is hit with 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: Self Hold Person ( + ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't Move , Act , or React . Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Misty Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Monster_Gnoll Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu are a unique type of gnoll enemy in Act One . They are feral hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger of their demonic creator, Yeenoghu . The closest form of a cleric among gnolls, fangs of Yennoghu tap into the unholy powers of their demonic god to unleash soul sapping magic that weakens their prey. CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Spear Damage: 4~9 1d6 + 3 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Soul Offering ( ) Numb a creature's soul and offer it to Yeenoghu to prevent it from taking Bonus Actions or Reactions . CHA Save Range: 8 m (27 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Hyena Ear Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Yeenoghu is the demon lord that many gnolls worship. It is said that their insatiable hunger comes from this demonic entity. Technical Stats Goblin_Caster Goblin Booyahgs are generic goblin characters found throughout Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] The Booyahgs are the wizards of goblinkind, although their skills and knowledge are primitive compared to more learned spellcasters. Despite these shortcomings, they are still dangerous when ambushing in large groups. Their area of effect and crowd control spells make them high-priority targets in early encounters. Technical Stats Goblin_Ranger_Strong Goblin Sharp-Eyes are a generic goblin NPC and enemy found throughout Act One in the Goblin Camp and Blighted Village . The elite archers of goblinkind, they take to the high ground and snipe enemies from a distance to make up for their physical weakness in close quarters. Their ability to ensnare party members and summon Worgs make them high priority targets in early combat encounters. They can use specialized arrows such as Arrows of Fire , if they possess them in their inventory. Technical Stats Goblin_Ranger Goblin Trackers are generic goblin characters found throughout Act One of Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Hunters and scouts of goblinkind, they favour using ambushes and taking to the high ground to make up for their physical weaknesses in close quarters. Technical Stats END_Inquisitor_Drow Variant 1 Stats END_Inquisitor_Tiefling Inquisitors of the Absolute are ranged combatants of the Absolute army , serving as lookouts and mobile patrollers. “ I strike for Her! „ — Inquisitor of the Absolute Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Inquisitors are long-range combatants and expert marksmen of the Cult of the Absolute . It's not clear if, like the zealots and adepts , the inquisitors are oblivious to the Absolute's standing as a false goddess, or like the Mistresses of Souls , if they are aware of the hoax-like nature of the Absolutist plot. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Inquisitors make their first and only appearance during the battle for High Hall as mobile patrollers and lookouts. Two inquisitors can be observed patrolling the northern-most and southern-most sides of High Hall respectively, escorted by a Mind Flayer and Winged Horror . They join combat whenever they are in range of the party. The third and last inquisitor is immediately encountered upon entering through the main gate, stationed by herself on the southern rampart. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Inquisitors are Dexterity -based rangers , being mobile enemies capable of slowing down and harassing both the party and their Gather Your Allies summons. They are able to disrupt Concentrations through the use of their Arrow of Arcane Interference , and can render characters immobile through the use of Ensnaring Strike . Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Brace (Ranged) ( )   –   Heavy Crossbow +1 Spend 6 m (20 ft) of your movement . For the rest of your turn, roll ranged damage twice and use the highest result. Recharge: Short rest Conjure Barrage ( + ) Damage: 2~16 Normal weapon damage + 2d8 ⁠ Weapon Channel your weapon's essence into a destructive, widespread volley. DEX Save Range: Self Ensnaring Strike ( + + ) Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Piercing Your attack summons thorny vines that possibly Ensnare your target. Ensnared creatures cannot move and take 1d6 ⁠ Piercing damage at the start of each turn. An ally can use their Help action to try and tear away the vines. STR Save Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Spear +1 Damage: 3~8 1d6 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ranged Attack ( )   –   Heavy Crossbow +1 Damage: 6~15 1d10 + 5 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Piercing Shot ( )   –   Heavy Crossbow +1 Damage: 6~15 1d10 + 5 ⁠ Piercing Deal regular damage and possibly inflict Gaping Wounds which cause extra damage on attacks. Undead and constructs can't receive Gaping Wounds. CON Save Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Short rest Rush Attack ( )   –   Spear +1 Damage: 5~8 1d4 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Charge forward and attack the first enemy in your way, possibly pushing them Off Balance . Technical Stats Human_Cultist_Myrkul_MasterOfSouls Mistress of Souls is a title given to certain Myrkul -aligned spellcasters within the Cult of Myrkul . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The necromancers [ 1 ] of Myrkul are technically identical, bearing the same statistics and equipment. For story purposes they differ in personality, aesthetic, and function. Unlike the Zealots, Adepts, and other members of the Cult of the Absolute , the Mistresses of Souls appear to know the truth behind the tadpoles; they are fully aware of what the Absolute is and the religious hoax they're perpetrating. [ 2 ] Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Mistresses of Souls are noted for their use of Incubate Death , which spawns additional Necromites to fight on their behalf. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bone Chill ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Necrotic Prevent the target from healing until your next turn. The target cannot help Downed characters. An undead target receives Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fireball ( + ) Damage: 8~48 8d6 ⁠ Fire Shoot a bright flame from your fingers that explodes upon contact, torching everything in the vicinity for 8d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Incubate Death ( ) Damage: 6~27 3d8 + 3 ⁠ Necrotic Spawn a skeletal involucre. After 1 turn, the involucre explodes, dealing 3d8 Necrotic damage and birthing a necromite. DEX Save Range: 24 m (80 ft) Misty Step ( + ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Tactician [ edit section | visual editor ] Shield ( + ) When you are about to be hit by an enemy, use your Reaction to increase your Armour Class by 5. You also take no damage from Magic Missile . These effects last until the start of your next turn. Technical UID QUEST_GnollBorn_A UUID 4966d89a-45ee-4b8a-855f-433dbfb4736b Stats Gnoll_Newborn Trs. Monster_Gnoll Newborn Gnolls are gnoll enemies found in Act One along The Risen Road . About Newborn Gnolls [ edit section | visual editor ] They are feral, hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger bestowed upon them by their demonic creator, Yeenoghu . Despite being freshly spawned from the body of a Bloated Hyena , they have shocking strength and can coordinate fiercely with each other. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attack and abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 3~6 1d4 + 2 ⁠ Piercing Bite a target. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Sudden Rush ( ) Increase your movement speed to 18 m / 60 ft. Moving no longer provokes Opportunity Attacks. Technical Stats Githyanki_Raider Githyanki raiders are a class-like archetype of githyanki characters encountered throughout Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Raiders are Dexterity -based Battle Master Fighters . They are foot soldiers, who specialise in wielding crossbows. Raiders are equally deadly at close quarters and long distances. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Misty Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Long rest Ranged Attack ( )   –   Githyanki Crossbow Damage: 5~14 1d10 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Manoeuvres [ edit section | visual editor ] Githyanki Raiders can spend up to four Superiority Die on manoeuvres : Rally ( + ) Healing 8 Temporary ⁠ Healing Expend a superiority die to bolster the resolve of a friendly creature. It gains an additional 8 temporary hit points . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Trip Attack (Ranged) ( + ) Damage Normal weapon damage + Superiority Die A powerful shot that possibly knocks the target Prone . Technical Stats Githyanki_Gish_Strong Veteran Gish are a stronger archetype of githyanki Gish characters encountered throughout Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] As Battlemages who blend arcane spellcasting with melee combat, gish soldiers are strong, versatile combatants. They are in the Knights of the Shield Hideout in Baldur's Gate or in the Upper City during Act Three . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Astral Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Blindness ( + ) Limit a foe's sight range. It is easier to hit, and the creature will miss more often. Attack rolls against it have Advantage and the foe attacks with Disadvantage . CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Burning Hands ( + ) Damage: 3~18 3d6 ⁠ Fire Each flammable target is hit with 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. DEX Save Range: Self Counterspell ( + ) Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Hold Person ( + ) Hold a humanoid enemy still. They can't Move , Act , or React . Attacks from within 3 m / 10 ft are always Critical Hits . At the end of each turn, the affected creature can make a Wisdom Saving Throw to end this condition. WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Misty Step ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Long rest Ray of Frost ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Cold Reduces the target's Movement Speed by 3 m / 10 ft. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Shocking Grasp ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Lightning The target cannot use Reactions . This spell has   Advantage on creatures with metal Armour . Contents 1 Overview 2 Involvement 2.1 Act One 2.2 Act Two 2.3 Act Three 3 Combat 3.1 Attacks and actions 3.1.1 Tactician/Honour only 3.2 Loot 4 Known zealots of the Absolute 4.1 Drow 4.2 Dwarf 4.3 Halfling 4.4 Half-Elf 4.5 Half-Orc 4.6 Human 5 Notes Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Zealots are soldiers and followers of the Absolute, forming the backbone of its army. Like the adepts , and most other members of the broader Cult of the Absolute , zealots are oblivious to the reality of the tadpoles and deceptive nature of the pretend-god, believing or being manipulated into believing that the Absolute is a new goddess. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Two zealots of the Absolute can be found dead in the Mountain Pass , perishing after being attacked by githyanki youth as they were escorting Duke Ravengard to Moonrise Towers . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Zealots of the Absolute are found acting as enforcers and soldiers of the Absolute army, and can be found in large numbers in Moonrise Towers as well as in the war camp west of Reithwin . They form the backbone of Absolutist forces in the area, and can be fought against during the ⁠ Assault on Moonrise Towers . As the Elder Brain orders to start the march towards Baldur's Gate , zealots of the Absolute can be seen marching alongside undead and goblins . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] A large number of zealots, such as Lewis Morell , were present during the initial assault on High Hall , pushing the City Watch out of the area at the cost of severe casualties. When the party arrive, only three living zealots remain and can be encountered in the Upper City ; two of which are situated in the courtyard, with the third one hidden in the Upper City Sewers . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Zealots of the Absolute are deadly melee opponents based off a Strength -oriented Oath of Vengeance paladin class. In Act Two, they are some of the most dangerous enemy archetypes that the party can face, boasting high HP pools and capable of dishing large amount of damage through their smites , while being statistically more powerful than any of the potential allies that the party can have. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] These undead nurses are the reanimated workers of the House of Healing , serving Shar's Scalpel Malus Thorm . ## Aasimar
- **来源**: [Aasimar](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Aasimar)
- **分类**: Races

Dame Aylin the aasimar Aasimar are a non-playable race of angel-like humanoids in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Endowed with a divine lineage, aasimar represent the physical and mental experience of other mortal creatures elevated. In the long uncertain night of Faerûnian life, they burn like pale inspiring torches. „ — In-game racial description About aasimar [ edit section | visual editor ] Similar to Tieflings, Aasimar are creatures either descended from or touched by celestials or other good-aligned beings. Notable aasimar [ edit section | visual editor ] Dame Aylin is a special aasimar. Most aasimars have a distant angelic relative which grants them the ability to temporarily summon wings and make their eyes glow. Dame Aylin is in fact a demigod - she is a daughter of Selûne , and because of this she is immortal. Olam is an aasimar spellcaster and Harper that battled Ketheric Thorm more than a hundred years ago, before falling prey to the darkness and effects of the Shadow Curse . ## Aberration
- **来源**: [Aberration](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Aberration)
- **分类**: Races

A spectator aberration. Aberrations are a type of creature that are unnatural, and do not resemble any creature in the natural world in any way shape or form. They can be found throughout Baldur's Gate 3, most notably as the game's main antagonist, the mind flayers. “ Warped, alien beings that have come to Faerûn from beyond the multiverse. „ — In-game racial description Contents 1 Characteristics 2 Types of aberrations 2.1 Spectator 2.1.1 Beholders in Baldur's Gate 3 2.2 Cloaker 2.2.1 Cloakers in Baldur's Gate 3 2.3 Phasm 2.3.1 Phasms in Baldur's Gate 3 2.4 Mind Flayer 2.4.1 Mind flayers in Baldur's Gate 3 3 Other 4 Related items 5 Related spells and abilities 6 Notes 7 External links Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Due to the nature of aberrations, they may be found in a large variety of shapes and forms. They may have large or bizarre organs and appendages, strange abilities and unknown origins. Many aberrations do not come from the Material Plane, and instead arrived there through magical means. As such, aberrations rarely have common features or characteristics, unlike other types of creatures. Types of aberrations [ edit section | visual editor ] Spectator [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Beholder and Beholder on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Aggressive and greedy aberrations that believe their own forms to be the ideal, and hold all others - be it other beholders or 'lesser beings' - in contempt. „ — In-game racial description Beholders are large, floating orb-like creatures with a giant eye in the middle and several eyestalks protruding from the main body. Inherently magical in nature, each eyestalk is capable of firing magical beams of light, inflicting a variety of powerful magical effects. Beholders in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Spectator Cloaker [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Cloaker and Cloaker on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Resembling dark leathery cloaks, these aberrations lurk in caves, waiting to slay lone or injured prey stumbling through the darkness. „ — In-game racial description Cloakers are intelligent floating creatures that resemble large stingrays. When lying on the ground, they appear similar to large cloaks, hence the name. In combat, Cloakers can emit a subsonic moan that paralyzes nearby creatures, as well as create illusory duplicates. Cloakers in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Phantasm Phasm [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Phasm on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Hungry for new experiences, these creatures use any tactic - as well as their ability to polymorph - to sate their curiosity. „ — In-game racial description Phasms are sentient, though amorphous, shapechangers that can take the shape of almost any object or creature. Although they do not have eyes, they can sense creatures through vibrations in the earth and are highly intelligent. Phasms in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Zlorb [ 1 ] Mind Flayer [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Mind Flayer and Mind flayer on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Psionic tyrants, slavers, and interdimensional voyagers that feed off the brains of thinking creatures. Most belong to a hivemind colony devoted to an elder brain, and all work towards achieving the Grand Design - their dream of once more controlling empires that span the multiverse. „ — In-game racial description Highly intelligent, sadistic creatures that possess powerful psionic abilities, Mind flayers – also known as illithids – are amoung the most well-known and feared aberrations. They feed by extracting the brains of other creatures, and create more of their own through a process known as ceremorphosis . ## Adamantine Golem
- **来源**: [Adamantine Golem](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Adamantine_Golem)
- **分类**: Races

An Adamantine Golem in Baldur's Gate 3 Adamantine Golem are non-playable construct creatures in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are terrifyingly resilient creations, able to withstand incredible punishment thanks to their construction from adamantine. “ Unstoppable juggernauts that exist only to follow their creator's orders, even if that creator has long since passed. „ — In-game racial description About adamantine golems [ edit section | visual editor ] Adamantine golems are extremely difficult to damage, often immune to damage from a variety of attacks, both magical and physical. They are very tall and heavy, but can't speak. They can stomp the ground, causing localized quakes that can be felt from far away. Due to their resilience, they will often last far longer than their creators, and continue faithfully executing their duties. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 11m / 36ft Size Large Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Adamantine Skin Made entirely from adamantine, this mass is about as heavy as a dragon, and nearly as indestructible. Only intense heat can soften the metal enough to be shaped. ## Alioramus
- **来源**: [Alioramus](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Alioramus)
- **分类**: Races

Chult Alioramus Alioramus are a type of beast and non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Alioramus are sedulous hunters, their broad jaws capable of crushing a knight's chest through a full inch of iron plate. „ — In-game racial description About alioramus [ edit section | visual editor ] Alioramus, which means "different branch", are a dinosaur beast found in the jungles of Chult , often said to be one of the most dangerous places in Faerûn. They are recognisable by their colourful crests and, characteristic of theropods, three toes and claws on each limb. Alioramus pounce on enemies, using their sharp teeth to bite and deal piercing damage. The alioramus colossa can also drive its pack into a Mating Frenzy to give them additional damage and resistances. Alioramus enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Chult Alioramus Chult Alioramus Colossa Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Alioramus is a real genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur. Alioramus use a similar model to the dilophosaurus used for Crimson and Wild Shape: Dilophosaurus (also a real dinosaur from the same clade, theropoda). The alioramus and dilophosaurus models were designed by character artist Luna Wullaert.
