Animated Armour is a Construct in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are in the Arcane Tower , Grymforge , and Sorcerous Sundries . Animated Armour can be disabled by anti-magic effects. “ Suits of magically animated plate armour. Ponderous and persistent, these constructs are often used as guardians. „ — In-game racial description Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Four (or six, on Tactician difficulty and above) animated armours armed with crossbows are on the top floor of the Arcane Tower with Bernard . Several more defend Grymforge . Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] A unique animated armour, the Hollow Armour , is located in the pit of the House of Healing Morgue . Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Sorcerous Sundries employs several animated armours as guards, some of whom take part in the fight with Lorroakan . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Animated armours are equipped with basic weapons, usually a Greatsword or Heavy Crossbow . Animated armours can be disabled by Sussur Antimagic Field from Sussar Blooms . This works either when the Sussur Bloom is placed near them or held by a nearby character. The number of flowers in the Underdark is enough to disable all animated armours when fighting Bernard. Due to their low Wisdom , animated armours are susceptible to spells or effects targeting a Wisdom saving throws , such as Command However, animated armours are immune to many mental effects like Frightened , Hold Person , and Crown of Madness . Their weight is low at 40 kg / 80 lb. A character with a minimum of 15 strength can attempt to pick up and throw them with the Throw action. In the Arcane Tower and Grymforge encounters, they can be thrown into the surrounding chasms to instantly destroy them. Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Main Hand Attack ( ) Damage Normal weapon damage Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ranged Attack ( ) Damage Normal weapon damage Make a ranged attack with your equipped weapon. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Named Animated Armours [ edit section | visual editor ] Klank Krank Animated Armour enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Hollow Armour Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Early Access. Model variations Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Ordinarily these enemies reward 40 experience each. However, it seems that the 4 found in Grymforge can reward 75 experience each when playing on Honour Mode Difficulty or Custom Difficulty with the Honour Mode ruleset. Only a hit that deals at least 10 damage can damage it. Arcane Turrets are environmental objects found in the Underdark . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Turrets are Constructs , used by Lenore De Hurst to defend her Arcane Tower . They are immobile turrets which fire at any creature that gets near. They fire four times per turn, dealing 1d4 + 1 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage with each shot to the closest target within a radius of 20 m (67 ft), and they always hit. These turrets have the Sturdy condition and are vulnerable to antimagic and ⁠ Lightning damage. Strong non-resisted attacks such as Eldritch Blast with Agonising Blast or Two-Handed ⁠ Bludgeoning weapons can also be used to damage them. The turrets can be dealt with in several ways: Arcane Turrets can be deactivated through restoring the power of the Arcane Tower with a Sussur Bloom . Arcane Turrets can be destroyed by reducing them to 0 HP. Arcane Turrets can be temporarily disabled by a Sussur Bloom , whether it is placed near them or held by a nearby character. If the line-of-sight of an Arcane Turret is broken, such as by using a Fog Cloud spell or taking cover, it is unable to fire. Arcane Turrets do not shoot at invisible targets. Arcane Turrets shoot at Minor Illusions . Arcane Turret enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Arcane Cannon Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Even after being disabled, the turrets can still be attacked, and XP is given upon a turret reaching zero hp. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If a Sussur Bloom is placed nearby a turret and the turret is then destroyed, it immediately revives and can start shooting again once the bloom is removed. This is not an issue if the Arcane Tower has been powered on before dealing with the turrets. The XP reward is only granted after destroying the turret for the first time. ## Automaton

An Automaton in Baldur's Gate 3 Automatons are non-playable construct creatures in Baldur's Gate 3 . They look like mechanical creatures, often with facial features derived from their creator or creature they were trying to emulate. “ Once a blueprint, now an indication of modern technology, this machine can only ever be a facsimile of a real person. „ — In-game racial description About automatons [ edit section | visual editor ] Automatons are simple constructs, usually built to perform manual labour or to act as servants or butlers. They are powered by reserves of magical energy that can last for hundreds of years, and they are often found as heirlooms of noble houses or royalty. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Multiattack: Static Discharge Benard can Multiattack while under the effects of his Static Discharge Aura . CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Once per battle Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Azer Warhammer Shield Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Concept art by Jane Katsubo Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The other options for Conjure Minor Elemental summon creatures of level 7, but the summoned azer remains at level 1. The primary implication of this is that the azer's proficiency bonus is 2 instead of 3. Therefore its attack rolls are lower. The azer's current HP level is visually reflected by his fiery hair (lower health = less fire). ## Bear
- **来源**: [Bear](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bear)
- **分类**: Races

Bears are a non-playable Race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Juggernauts of the animal world, bears are capable of walking on their hind legs, hibernating during colder seasons, and absolutely ruining your mountain hike. „ — In-game racial description About bears [ edit section | visual editor ] Bears are carnivorous mammals with stocky legs, long snouts and small, rounded ears. In combat, bears are notable for their large health pools and slashing claw attacks. Bears can be spoken to using Speak with Animals . Beast Master Rangers may summon a Bear Companion , and Circle of the Moon Druids may turn into a bear with Wild Shape: Bear . Halsin has the unique ability Wild Shape: Cave Bear . ## Bird
- **来源**: [Bird](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bird)
- **分类**: Races

See also: Raven A bird and the valuables it uses to decorate its nest. Birds are a race of beast creature. They can be encountered as NPCs , summoned as allies, or even transformed into using special abilities. “ Their melodies fill the woods of Toril with a mellow sweetness, and their feathers paint brush strokes on even the dullest sky. „ — In-game racial description About birds [ edit section | visual editor ] Though the party encounters birds with varied personalities, all share low intelligence and the ability to fly. NPC birds can be conversed with using Speak with Animals . Transmutation wizards can transform into a bird using the Shapechanger ability, as can Circle of the Moon druids with Wild Shape: Dire Raven , or any character wearing the Corvid Token . ## Blink Dog
- **来源**: [Blink Dog](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Blink_Dog)
- **分类**: Races

A Blink Dog in Baldur's Gate 3 Blink Dogs are a type of Fey and non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are intelligent dog-like creatures so named because of their ability to 'blink', or teleport. “ The flickering, unpredictable magic of the faerie realm courses through the blink dog - allowing it to flit in and out of this plane to avoid harm. „ — In-game racial description About blink dogs [ edit section | visual editor ] Blink dogs are quite fast, and possess the ability to Blink . For a canine, they possess an unusually muscular physique as well as large ears. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 15m / 50ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Bugbears are a non-playable Race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are hairy Humanoids that thrive in battle and are fond of raiding, hunting, and ambushing. “ Hairy humanoids that crave carnage and treasure in equal measure. „ — In-game racial description About bugbears [ edit section | visual editor ] Bugbears often fight alongside Goblins and other members of the Absolute . These hairy humanoids crave carnage and treasure in equal measure, using a mix of brute force and guile to meet their needs. TUT_BackupCambion_Trident Variant 2 Eqp. LOW_HouseOfHope_Cambion Cambions are a race of Fiend and non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . Typically found in the Hells, Cambions are half-fiend, half-mortal, and are resistant to many types of damage. “ Scarlet-eyed and bitter-tempered, cambion are the bastard children of devils and mortals, a fusion of two Planes in one body. „ — In-game racial description Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Prologue [ edit section | visual editor ] Two Cambions appear at the back of the bridge entrance after reaching 10 turns left until the Nautiloid crashes. Their high Hit Points , AC and many Resistances make them very difficult to kill directly. Overall, they are meant to force the party to activate the controls or risk being killed by them. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Six Vengeful Cambions fight the party while they move to escape from the House of Hope . It is also possible to encounter two cambions if a party member is afflicted with the condition Castigated By Divinity . ## Celestial
- **来源**: [Celestial](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Celestial)
- **分类**: Races

A typical celestial creature called a Deva. Celestials are a type of creature that come from or are descended from creatures in the Upper Planes . They are good-natured creatures, and are the counterpart of Fiends . “ Good-aligned creatures native to the Upper Planes. Many of them are servants of deities, employed in the mortal realm. „ — In-game racial description Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Celestials come in a variety of forms and sizes and are united in their common cause to do good. Celestials are usually angelic in appearance and derive their power from the gods. Types of celestials [ edit section | visual editor ] Hollyphant [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Hollyphant and Hollyphant on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Bobbing like corks in the earnest, busy muddle-puddle of their lives, hollyphants are sweet-natured little pachyderms who often serve as helpers to good-aligned deities. „ — In-game racial description Hollyphant are winged miniature elephant-like creatures with golden fur. ## Countermeasure
- **来源**: [Countermeasure](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Countermeasure)
- **分类**: Races

Countermeasures are hostile Aberration creatures in Baldur's Gate 3 that may appear during the fight Atop the Netherbrain depending upon the party's choices during the Confront the Elder Brain quest. A Countermeasure About [ edit section | visual editor ] Four Countermeasures are created by the Netherbrain if the party chose to trust The Emperor and allow him, a Full-Illithid player character, or Full-Illithid Karlach to consume Orpheus . They are designed to both mimic and counter the specific classes of characters in the active party. They only appear during the final battle Atop the Netherbrain . Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Countermeasures are intended to be effective against the classes they mimick. For example, the Spellplague has the Magic Resistance passive, Resistance to fire, cold, and lightning damage, and can cast Counterspell , making them more difficult for Wizards to deal with. It may be advisable to fight different countermeasures with members of the party who are not countered by them. Countermeasure class variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Barbarian: Rage Queller Bard: The Snapping of Strings Cleric: Blasphemous Acolyte Druid: Unnatural Blot Fighter: Breaker of War Monk: Way of the Profane Ki Paladin: Oathless Wretch Ranger: The Darkening Hunt Rogue: Assassin's Folly Sorcerer: Metamage Persecutor Warlock: Pactsplitter Wizard: Spellplague Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] If a character is multi-classed then their countermeasure is randomly selected from among their classes. Countermeasures have 4 character models, each of which is always used during the final battle. Most countermeasures arguably fail to live up to their name, particularly against experienced and well prepared players. Some do not have any abilities or powers that effectively counter a character's class and are simply a variant of that class; e.g., Paladin countermeasure is just a (weak) Paladin , where a more effective 'countermeasure' would have been a Death Knight or something with Radiant Retort. v t e Creatures Humanoids Aasimar Bugbear Changeling Gnoll Goblin Hobgoblin Kobold Kuo-toa Meazel Sahuagin Shadar-Kai Werewolf Aberrations Cloaker Countermeasure Intellect Devourer Mind Flayer Spectator Spectral Flumph Tentacle Beasts Alioramus Badger Bat Bear Bird Boar Cat Crab Deep Rothé Dilophosaurus Displacer Beast Dog Frog Giant Eagle Hyena Owlbear Ox Rabbit Rat Raven Dire Sheep Spider Squirrel Wolf Dire Celestials Deva Hollyphant Moonlight Sliver Constructs Adamantine Golem Animated Armour Arcane Turret Automaton Guardian of Faith Flesh Golem Manifestation of Tyranny Ptaris' Mental Image Scrying Eye Steel Watcher Dragons Red Dragon Undead Dragon Elementals Azer Djinni Elemental Air Earth Fire Grease Lava Mud Water Flaming Sphere Hell Sphere Mephit Grease Ice Magma Mud Myrmidon Air Earth Fire Water Fey Blink Dog Dryad Hag Meenlock Pixie Redcap Fiends Cambion Vengeful Hellsboar Gilded Lesser Vengeful Imp Gilded Lesser Vengeful Incubus / Succubus Merregon Vengeful Orthon Giants Ogre Monstrosities Bulette Ettercap Doppelganger Drider Gremishka Harpy Hook Horror Minotaur Gilded Mimic Phase Spider Shadow Mastiff Slayer Worg Oozes Fetid Ooze Greaseball Ochre Jelly Plants Blight Myconid Shadow Creeper Shambling Mound Wood Woad Undead Conjured Spectre Crawling Claw Dark Justiciar Death Knight Death Shepherd Flying Ghoul Ghast Ghost Ghoul Grim Visage Mummy Mummy Lord Poltergeist Shadow Skeleton Vampire Vampire spawn Wraith Zombie Greater

Technical UID Crawling_Claw UUID 21ac7288-39b8-478f-a827-cf8eb4b824e6 Stats CrawlingClaw Crawling Claws are a type of Undead creature in Acts Two and Three . “ Severed from their owners and skittering along on digits still stiff with rigor mortis, these hands can squeeze the breath from a throat in an instant. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Crawling Claws are the reanimated amputated hands of humanoids. They are often crafted by necromancers to perform menial tasks, or employed as familiars by warlocks and wizards. Crawling Claws do not have a great deal of health or significant attacks, instead overwhelming their foes in swarms known as 'applauses'. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] In Act Two , Marcus summons a horde of crawling claws to cover his escape from the Last Light Inn if the party urges Jaheira to test him with her mind flayer parasite in a jar. This scenario is only possible if Mol dies in Act One and is thus unable to vouch for the party. In Act Three , two named Crawling Claws, Itchy and Scratchy , are near Lucretious at the Circus of the Last Days . Additionally, many Crawling Claws are in the Ancient Lair . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Claws ( ) Damage: 3~17 2d8 + 1 ⁠ Slashing Lash out with deadly claws. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Crawling Claw characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Itchy Scratchy Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Crawling Claws have a unique "Rock On" ⁠ victory animation if they are part of the player character's party, which plays after the end of combat. While they normally cannot be allied with the party, it is possible to observe this behavior by taking control of one with the Control Undead ability. Crawling Claws are the only creature that possess Blindsight without also possessing some value of Darkvision . This means that, in areas of Obscurity , all attacks against it gain Advantage despite the creature "not relying on sight". ## Dark Justiciar
- **来源**: [Dark Justiciar](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dark_Justiciar)
- **分类**: Races

Dark Justiciars are elite warriors of Shar , gifted with supernatural abilities, and carry out her will throughout Faerûn . “ Remnants of the once-living that are trapped between life and death. „ — In-game racial description Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] All Dark Justiciars encountered in Baldur's Gate 3 are dead or undead with the exception of Lyrthindor in Grymforge and Shadowheart herself, if she is anointed as one after she kills Aylin during her personal quest ⁠ Daughter of Darkness . Dark Justiciars were far more numerous in the past, terrorizing Reithwin under the leadership of Ketheric Thorm and building such architectural marvels as the Gauntlet of Shar and Grymforge . They were beaten back by a broad coalition of forces, including Harpers and Emerald Grove druids, suffering significant losses in the process. The remaining Dark Justiciars were finally defeated after an infernal bargain struck between Morfred and Raphael resulted in Raphael ordering Yurgir to decimate Grymforge . Yurgir then proceeded to hunt down and kill virtually every remaining Justiciar in the Gauntlet of Shar . Common abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] Upon defeat, all undead Dark Justiciars leave behind 1.5 m (5 ft) Darkness over their corpses. Undead Dark Justiciars are immune to Bleeding . However, unlike other Undead ; such as Ghasts , Ghouls and Zombies ; it is possible to Poison and Charm them. ## Death Knight
- **来源**: [Death Knight](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Death_Knight)
- **分类**: Races

Death knights are a race of undead in Baldur's Gate 3 . They were once paladins in life, twisted in undeath into powerful and cruel entities. “ When a fallen paladin dies without atonement, it can be brought back from the grave as something entirely different - entirely evil. „ — In-game racial description About death knights [ edit section | visual editor ] Death Knights appear fully clad in armour, such that you cannot see anything beneath. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Improved Extra Attack You can make two additional attacks after attacking with your main-hand weapon. Magic Resistance Has Advantage on Saving Throws against Spells and other magical effects. Revenant's Ire This profane entity's weapon attacks deal an additional 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage. Parry Parry the next melee attack that hits you to reduce the damage by 1d8 + Dexterity Modifier. Riposte When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, expend a superiority die to retaliate with a powerful strike that deals an additional Superiority Die damage. EQP_Greatsword_HalfPlate Death Shepherd is an Undead creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Two Death Shepherds are leading a swarm of ghouls along the Rosymorn Monastery Trail . Another is in the Moonrise Towers Prison during the assault on Moonrise Towers, and a fourth appears in the Necrotic Laboratory within the Mind Flayer Colony . A unique Death Shepherd named Garret Dortmell can appear in the Lower City Graveyard if the player character helps Nina Dortmell resurrect him. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Cleave ( )   –   Greatsword Damage 1/2 Normal weapon damage Swing your weapon in a large arc to attack up to 3 enemies at once. They each take half the damage your weapon usually deals. Recharge: Short rest Lacerate ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 4~14 2d6 + 2 ⁠ Slashing Slash at your target's vital points to make it Bleed . Undead and constructs can't bleed. CON Save Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Short rest Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 4~14 2d6 + 2 ⁠ Slashing Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) No Rest for the Wicked ( ) Death is but a temporary inconvenience - raise a fallen undead with half of its hit points . Range: 3 m (10 ft) Pommel Strike ( )   –   Greatsword Damage: 1~4 1d4 ⁠ Bludgeoning Make a non-lethal attack against an enemy and possibly Daze them. CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Short rest Reach from Beyond ( ) Damage: 2~8 + modifiers 2d4 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Necrotic Defile a target with Myrkul's decaying magic. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Greatsword Half Plate Armour Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] No Rest for the Wicked revives its target with full HP on Tactician and Honour difficulty. The Death Shepherd's No Rest for the Wicked can be countered by picking up the corpses of defeated undead so that they cannot be revived. Counterspell is also effective. The Death Shepherd is able to revive other Death Shepherds using No Rest for the Wicked , and those revived can also use this ability in turn. To avoid an endless cycle of Death Shepherds reviving each other, it is recommended to make sure that there are no downed Death Shepherds when any of them start their turn. One way to achieve this is to reduce each to a few HP remaining but not kill them, and when they all are at a few remaining HP, then eliminate them all in a single turn, for example by hitting them with a Fireball . Death Shepherds lose most of their resistances once the temporary hit points from Necrotic Veil are removed. However, they retain resistance to ⁠ Slashing , ⁠ Piercing , and ⁠ Bludgeoning damage and immunity to ⁠ Poison damage, so it may be wise to use spells of other damage types to defeat them (e.g., Fireball , Lightning Bolt ). Deep Rothé are animals in the Underdark in Act One of the game. Druids can also wild shape into them using Wild Shape: Deep Rothé . About [ edit section | visual editor ] Deep Rothé [ 1 ] are common beasts in Faerûn, mostly used as a beef breed and beasts of burden; one of the common supplies that the party may find around or buy from traders throughout the game is Grilled Rothé Ribs . Deep Rothé are a sub-species of common Rothé, adapted to live in the Underdark. Rothé much resemble herd beasts like musk-oxen or yacks in appearance and probably share similar their temperament and behaviour. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] The Underdark is the only place in the game where the party meets these huge and stately animals. They are sentient and can be spoken to via Speak with Animals , which may offer a way to resolve quests the party is currently involved in or provide certain details about present and future plot affairs. There are six Deep Rothé, which the party can meet and speak with throughout the game: In the Ebonlake Grotto - Deep Rothé at X: 54 Y: -89 In Grymforge - Deep Rothé, Deep Rothé Calf and Elder Rothé at X: -657 Y: 402 In Grymforge - another pair of Deep Rothé clearing the debris at X: -670 Y: 441 Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Dancing Lights ( ) Illuminate a 9 m / 30 ft radius. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Frenzied Charge ( ) Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Piercing Charge forward, attacking all enemies in the way and pushing them back 3 m / 10 ft. Recharge: Per turn Gore ( ) Damage: 18~27 3d4 + 4 ⁠ Piercing + 11 ⁠ Force Impale a target Deals an additional 11 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to targets with   Lesser ,   Medium , or   Greater Toughness . Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Deep Rothé characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Deep Rothé (myconid colony) Deep Rothé Calf Elder Rothé Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find the Mushroom Picker ⁠ Get Past the Rubble Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Deep Rothé is an uninflected term. This means the singular and plural forms are identical. Similar terms include Sheep and Bison. Rothé both fits the English pattern for uniflected plural nouns and in the game files there is only a single occurrence of the word "Rothés" which is presumably erroneous as every single other time the game refers to a group of Rothé, it says "Rothé" . Opportunity Attack Attack an enemy moving out of reach. Displacer beasts are a non-playable race and beast creature, found in the Gauntlet of Shar and the Circus of the Last Days . The Displacer Beast Shape action allows a creature to polymorph into a displacer beast. “ A displacer beast's coat is slick with illusory magic that can bend light, letting it project images of itself and turn invisible. Adventurers say you can never know a displacer beast's true location - until its claws sink into your belly, that is. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Displacer beasts are feline, tentacled creatures resembling panthers. They often live in small groups, preferring sheltered habitats such as caves or tree hollows. Displacer beasts can be spoken to using Speak with Animals , and can be transformed into by partial-illithids with Displacer Beast Shape . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Displace ( ) Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Psychic Teleport yourself and a target to a nearby location, shredding the target's mind and leaving behind an illusory copy of yourself. INT Save Range: 3 m (10 ft) Illusory Copy ( ) Create an illusory displacer beast to attack nearby enemies. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Tentacle Whip ( ) Damage: 8~28 2d6 + 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning + 2d6 ⁠ Piercing Lash out with a sleek, spinous tentacle. Range: 3 m (10 ft) Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Displacer beasts are significant combat threats. 18 strength makes them formidable attackers. while Displace gives them free roam of the arena while leaving behind a double that can still dish out damage. This brute strength can be countered by targeting their low mental abilities, which make them more susceptible to manipulating or controlling effects like Fear or Banishment . Displacer beast characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Nessa Shadow-Whiskers Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Concept art by Tan Bur-Ci Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Displacer Beasts are typed as Large Monstrosities in 5e, but are typed as Medium Beasts in Baldur's Gate 3 . Doppelgangers are a non-playable race and type of Monstrosity in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Capable of morphing their physiology to impersonate other humanoids, doppelgangers have served as cunning spies, political envoys, and assassins. „ — In-game racial description About doppelgangers [ edit section | visual editor ] Doppelgangers can completely transform their appearance to mimic almost any Humanoid creature. They refer to themselves as Shallar . They disguise themselves as other humanoids, then try to Ambush enemies by reverting to their true form. Successfully ambushing an enemy allows them to use their multiattack. ## Dragon
- **来源**: [Dragon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dragon)
- **分类**: Races

A red dragon. Dragons are a type of powerful and magical creature that exists in Baldur's Gate 3. There are many types of dragons, differentiated by their colour and shine of the scales on their skin. “ Immensely intelligent, ancient, and powerful reptiles that covet wealth. Chromatic dragons are selfish, evil, and feared, while metallic dragons are noble, good, and respected by the wise. „ — In-game racial description Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Dragons resemble large, quadruped lizards with massive wings. There are several types of dragons, most commonly metallic and chromatic, and their type usually determines whether they are evil or good. Being magical in nature, dragons have extremely long life-spans, and as they age they typically grow considerably more powerful. Types of dragons [ edit section | visual editor ] Undead Dragon [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Undead Dragon and Undead dragon on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Bones studded with rotting scales and draped with dead tissue, these dragons have been animated by fell necromancy. „ — In-game racial description Undead dragons are an extremely rare type of dragon that are reanimated from the corpse of a deceased dragon. They appear like they did when they were living except most of the flesh has rotted away, leaving behind a skeletal structure. Despite the lack of flesh, they can be just as terrifying as they were when alive. Undead dragons in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Ansur Other dragons [ edit section | visual editor ] Red Dragon Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Arrow of Dragon Slaying - consumable arrow that deals double damage against dragon targets. Staff of the Ram - Knockback not applied against dragons or Huge creatures. ## Dragonborn
- **来源**: [Dragonborn](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dragonborn)
- **分类**: Races

Dragonborn are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They have resistance to a type of energy damage, and are able to make deadly breath weapon attacks. These abilities are affected by their dragonborn subrace. Dragonborn resemble draconic humanoids, can have scales in a variety of colours, and may or may not have a tail. “ A proud race that values clan and skills above all else. Once enslaved by dragons, they strive to be self-sufficient, not wanting to be beholden to anyone, not even the gods. „ — In-game racial description About dragonborn [ edit section | visual editor ] Dragonborn are a race of draconic mortals native to Abeir , the twin world of Toril given over to the primordials in ancient times. [ 1 ] For millennia, their ancestors lived in bondage under draconic overlords until the cataclysmic Spellplague transplanted their nation of Tymanther directly onto Faerûn . [ 2 ] Frequently defined by clan loyalty and individual honor, most dragonborn hold self-reliance as a central virtue. Driven by the history of their enslavement, many abhor dragons and view religious devotion with skepticism. [ 3 ] Whether their scales reflect chromatic or metallic heritage, [ 4 ] dragonborn strive to prove their worth through personal mastery rather than the patronage of higher powers. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Draconic Ancestry The blood of ancient dragons flow through your veins. You are Resistant to ⁠ Acid damage. ## Drider
- **来源**: [Drider](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Drider)
- **分类**: Races

A Drider in Baldur's Gate 3 Drider are a non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Favoured drow that fail the tests of the Webmother Lolth have their forms warped and made wicked - grafted with spiders to serve as symbols of her power. „ — In-game racial description About drider [ edit section | visual editor ] Drider are centaur-like creatures that appear to have the upper body of a Drow, with the lower half replaced by a giant spider. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Improved Critical The number you need to roll a Critical Hit while attacking is reduced by 1. This effect can stack. Multiattack: Wounded Target The drider can Multiattack if its target has fewer than all of its hit points . Sunlight Sensitivity While in sunlight, this creature has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Perception checks that rely on sight. Web Walker Isn't slowed down by Web surfaces, and can't be Enwebbed by them. ## Drow
- **来源**: [Drow](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Drow)
- **分类**: Races

Drow are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3. They are the dark elves of the Forgotten Realms, dwelling in the Underdark , large subterranean caverns beneath the surface. “ Driven to the Underdark, most drow have adopted a ruthless pragmatism. While the Lolth-sworn delight in the goddess' evil tenets, the Seldarine reject Her attempt to overthrow the leader of the elven pantheon. „ — In-game racial description About drow [ edit section | visual editor ] Drow are shaped by life in the subterranean Underdark . Also known as dark elves, they possess keen senses adapted to its bioluminescent shadows and a natural affinity for magic. While many drow are bound to the ruthless, matriarchal society of the Spider Queen Lolth , others – such as the Seldarine drow – reject her cruelty. While surface fear of Lolth-Sworn tyranny is well-earned, Seldarine drow who venture above must still endure that same hostility, forced to overcome a dark legacy they actively oppose. [ 1 ] Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base racial speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Size Medium Drow Weapon Training You have proficiency with Rapiers , Shortswords , and Hand Crossbows . Superior Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 24 m (80 ft). Fey Ancestry The Feywild casts a veil over your mind. You have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Charmed , and magic can't put you to Sleep . Keen Senses You gain Proficiency in the Perception skill. Drow Magic You gain access to the following Spells : Cantrip: Dancing Lights (at character Level 1) 1st Level Spell: Drow Magic: Faerie Fire (at character level 3) Recharge: Long rest 2nd Level Spell: Darkness (at character level 5) Recharge: Long rest NPC features [ edit section | visual editor ] While player-characters do not, certain NPC drow characters have the following passive feature in addition to the above: Sunlight Sensitivity While in sunlight, this creature has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Perception checks that rely on sight. Subraces [ edit section | visual editor ] Lolth-sworn drow [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Lolth-Sworn Drow appearance “ Raised by Lolth's cult in the city of Menzoberranzan, these drow embody the virtues of their corrupt and merciless goddess. Lolth marks Her followers with bright red eyes so those in the Underdark will learn to fear them on sight. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Lolth-sworn Drow do not gain any additional racial features but do gain access to certain locked dialogue choices. By default, Lolth-sworn Drow have red eyes. The dialogue options for Lolth-sworn drow are considerably evil , for example, threatening the pickpocket kids at the Druid Grove of enslavement in the Underdark, or encouraging Kagha to kill the Tiefling child. Seldarine drow [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Seldarine Drow appearance “ Seldarine drow can be found seeking allies from all over Faerûn, aiming to settle their conflict with Lolth - and each other - by any means necessary. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Seldarine Drow do not gain any additional racial features but do gain access to certain locked dialogue choices. By default, Seldarine Drow do not have red eyes. Religions [ edit section | visual editor ] The cult of Lolth [ edit section | visual editor ] The much-reviled matriarch of the drow pantheon, Lolth holds sway over spiders, the Underdark, and the wicked creatures of the Demonweb Pits. Her primary goal is to corrupt all drow, transforming them into heartless cultists. [ 2 ] The clergy of Eilistraee [ edit section | visual editor ] Eilistraee is the goddess of the Seldarine drow, beauty, song, and freedom. The Dark Maiden desires balance between all races, and struggles against her mother Lolth's corrupt aims. The cult of the Absolute [ edit section | visual editor ] Various Lolth-sworn drow and at least one Seldarine drow can be found among the members of the Cult of the Absolute at Moonrise Towers . Cleric deities [ edit section | visual editor ] Due to this split in religions among the drow, Clerics have their deities restricted based on their respective subrace. Lolth-sworn drow can only pick Lolth , whereas Seldarine drow can pick the usual set of deities except for Lolth. Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Items can have unique bonuses when wielded or worn by drow characters. These can also be enabled by using Disguise Self to temporarily appear as a drow. Cruel Sting - a drow wielding this longsword deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage against Restrained targets. The following items are drow-themed, but don't grant any associated bonuses in terms of gameplay mechanics. Dostrealt's Piccolo - a flute themed around Captain Dostrealt , a drow wizard. Handmaiden's Mace - a mace themed around followers of Lolth. Phalar Aluve - a longsword with finesse themed around Eilistraee and the Seldarine drow. Ring of Salving - a healing ring themed around followers of Eilistraee. Shadow of Menzoberranzan - a cowl with a reference to the drow city of Menzoberranzan . Swordmaster Gloves - a pair of gloves themed around Drizzt Do'Urden , a famous drow adventurer. Dryads are a non-playable Fey race found in Baldur's Gate 3 . About Dryads [ edit section | visual editor ] Dryads channel powerful druidic powers , allowing them to entangle their enemies and call forth Wood Woads for help. They can be summoned through the spell Conjure Woodland Being , a level four spell available to level 7 Druids . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Entangle ( ) Create a vine surface, slowing down creatures, possibly   Entangling them. STR Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Fallen Lover ( ) Summon a Wood Woad bound to your tree to fight alongside you. Range: 9 m (30 ft) Recharge: Short rest Spike Growth ( + ) Damage: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Piercing Shape a piece of ground into hard spikes. A creature walking on the spikes takes 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage for every 1.5 m (5 ft) it moves. The spikes are Difficult Terrain , halving a creature's Movement Speed . Range: 18 m (60 ft) Strengthened Shillelagh ( ) Your staff or club becomes magical: it deals 4d8 Bludgeoning damage, and uses your Spellcasting Ability for Attack rolls . Range: Self Dryad characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Zethino Dryad summons [ edit section | visual editor ] Dryad (Conjure Woodland Being) Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] A dryad's default attack deals 3d6+1 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. In addition to Grasp of the Forest , both the default attack and Strengthened Shillelagh have also another passive which can Entangle the target. It does not have a specific name, and the save in battle log is shown as against Main Hand Attack . It uses a DC  13 Dexterity Saving Throw . If spilt, dryad blood turns into Twisting Vines on the ground. ## Dwarf
- **来源**: [Dwarf](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dwarf)
- **分类**: Races

Dwarves are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ As durable and unyielding as their homes of stone, dwarves are some of the finest warriors, miners, and smiths of Faerûn. „ — In-game racial description About dwarves [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwarves are a stalwart and ancient people, shaped by stone, steel, and unyielding tradition. Dwelling in mountain halls and subterranean strongholds, they hold craftsmanship, clan loyalty, and ancestral honor as central pillars of their culture. [ 1 ] Their lives are long, their memories longer still, and every triumph or grievance is etched into song and stone. [ 2 ] Patience and discipline guide them, whether at the forge, the council table, or the battlefield. Dwarven culture is diverse across Faerûn . Shield dwarves and gold dwarves fiercely uphold the legacies of their clans and mountain kingdoms, while duergar – the gray dwarves of the Underdark – embody a harsher existence forged through ancient enslavement by illithids, relying on cunning, secrecy, and iron will. [ 3 ] Across Faerûn, dwarves are respected for their skill, resilience, and loyalty – remaining steadfast allies and formidable foes. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 7.5 m (25 ft) per turn. Size Medium Dwarven Combat Training You have Proficiency with Battleaxes , Handaxes , Light Hammers , and Warhammers . Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Dwarven Resilience You have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Poisoned and you have Resistance against ⁠ Poison damage. Subraces [ edit section | visual editor ] Gold dwarf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Gold Dwarf appearance “ These dwarves are known for their confidence and keen intuition. The culture of their Deep Kingdom values family, ritual, and fine craftsmanship. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwarven Toughness You have 1 extra maximum Hit Point per level. Shield dwarf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Shield Dwarf appearance “ Great losses in ancient wars against goblins and orcs have led these dwarves to adopt a cynical mindset, but they will endure anything to restore their ancestral homelands. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwarven Armour Training You have Armour Proficiency with Light armour and Medium armour . Duergar [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Duergar appearance “ Once enslaved by the eldritch mind flayers, duergar adapted to freedom with harsh practicality. Their cold demeanours and gift of stealth are well-known throughout the Underdark. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Superior Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 24 m (80 ft). Duergar Resilience An affected creature has Advantage on Saving Throws against Illusions and against being Charmed or Paralysed . Duergar Magic You gain the access to the following Cantrips : Level 3: Enlarge ( Recharge: Long rest , does not require Concentration and does not use Spell Slots). Level 5: Invisibility ( Recharge: Per combat, does not use Spell Slots). NPC characters [ edit section | visual editor ] Additionally, non-player duergar characters also have: Sunlight Sensitivity While in sunlight, this creature has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Perception checks that rely on sight. Religions [ edit section | visual editor ] The church of Moradin [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dwarffather inspires dwarven inventions and is constantly seeking to improve his race, encouraging a good-natured, intelligent, and harmonious existence with other good races while battling their pride and isolationist tendencies. Worshipers of Laduguer [ edit section | visual editor ] His clerics are the unquestioned rulers of duergar society, enforcing cold and callous behaviour among his worshippers. Laduguer is a xenophobic god with a doctrine of empowerment through slave exploitation and protection through an unforgiving military program. He is at odds with the other dwarven god Moradin. Cleric deities [ edit section | visual editor ] Due to the position Laduguer takes within duergar society, only duergar Clerics are able to pick him as deity. Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Certain items have unique bonuses when wielded or worn by a Dwarf. These bonuses can be enabled by being disguised as one before equipping the item. Dwarven Thrower : Dwarven Thrower (passive feature) - a Dwarf throwing this warhammer deals an extra 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large, Huge or Gargantuan creature, the strike deals an additional 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. Nimblefinger Gloves : Nimblefinger - a Dwarf wearing this gloves gains +1 Dexterity. Notable dwarves [ edit section | visual editor ] Gold dwarves [ edit section | visual editor ] Baelen Bonecloak Carmen Pennygood Derryth Bonecloak Dolor Entharl Danthelon Figaro Pennygood Hope Helsik Korrilla Nettie Rakath Glitterbeard Redhammer the Diviser Shield dwarves [ edit section | visual editor ] Delverdenn Malek Stones Old Troutman Uncategorized dwarves [ edit section | visual editor ] Manip Nestor Roveer Notable Duergar [ edit section | visual editor ] Brathwen Corsair Greymon Elder Brithvar Gekh Coal Havkelaag Herdmaster Skarjall Morghal Murmath Pistle Sergeant Thrinn Stonemason Kith Stone Guard Kur See also [ edit section | visual editor ] List of all dwarves List of all duergar List of all gold dwarves List of all shield dwarves Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Each Dwarf subrace equates to a specific type of Dwarf subrace in Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition, as they share their unique traits: A Gold Dwarf equates to a Hill Dwarf in 5e A Shield Dwarf equates to a Mountain Dwarf in 5e. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Dwarves are subject to bugs resulting from errors in animation scripting: Due to a timing error, reactions such as Deflect Missiles cannot be used against Dwarves attacking with two-handed crossbows as the attack animation finishes before the reaction can trigger. Due to erroneous animation binding of Off-Hand Melee Attacks initiated from outside melee range, i.e., 1.5 m (5 ft), male Dwarves perform two off-hand attacks from a single off-hand melee attack (1 Bonus Action ) when a specific combination of weapons is equipped: The main-hand weapon must be Small1H (e.g., a Dagger ) The off-hand weapon must be Piercing1H (e.g., a Shortsword ) References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Player's Handbook (5e), Chapter 2: Races, pp. 18–20. ↑ Player's Handbook (5e), Chapter 2, p. 18; Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting (3.5e), p. 11. ↑ Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide (5e), Chapter 3: Races of the Sword Coast, pp. 103–105; Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes (5e), Chapter 3. ## Elemental
- **来源**: [Elemental](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elemental)
- **分类**: Races

A typical elemental creature called an Air Elemental. Elementals are a type of creature that hail from the Elemental planes . They are creatures that embody a single elemental plane. “ Creatures native to the Elemental Planes. They range from simple masses of a specific element to beings infused with elemental energy. „ — In-game racial description Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Elementals come in a wide variety of forms and sizes depending on their element. They don't typically have features typical of other creatures, as they are generally made of the element's plane they come from. They are often, but not always, resistant or immune to the damage type associated with their element. Types of elementals [ edit section | visual editor ] Azer [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Azer and Azer on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Master craftsmen and expert miners made from bronze and fire. „ — In-game racial description Azer are dwarf-like creatures with bronze skin that burns so hot that their weapons and bodies can burn nearby creatures. Mephit [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Mephit and Mephit on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Capricious, vulgar, and rarely endearing - except to their masters. Mephits are curious, impish creatures from the Elemental Planes. „ — In-game racial description Mephits are imp-like creatures that enjoy being tricksters. Mephits in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Grease Mephit Ice Mephit Magma Mephit Mud Mephit Mud Elemental [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Mud Elemental “ These sludgy, muculent elementals come from a Plane intersecting Elemental realms of Water and Earth. „ — In-game racial description Mud elementals are strong, humanoid shaped masses of mud. Lava Elemental [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Lava Elemental “ These superheated sacks of molten slag come from a Plane intersecting Elemental realms of Earth and Fire. „ — In-game racial description Lava elementals are similar in appearance to earth elementals except they are made of lava. ## Elf
- **来源**: [Elf](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elf)
- **分类**: Races

Elves are a playable race . They are long lived, and have an affinity for magic. “ With ethereal countenances and long lifespans, elves are at home with nature's power, flourishing in light and dark alike. „ — In-game racial description About elves [ edit section | visual editor ] Elves are an ancient and long-lived people, their origins entwined with the Feywild and the primal magic of the world. Possessed of keen senses and unearthly grace, they move through life with a patience born of centuries. Elven societies prize art, poetry, and arcane study, preserving traditions that stretch back to lost empires and forgotten ages. To other races, their measured speech and distant composure can seem aloof, yet beneath it lies deep feeling and fierce loyalty. Across Faerûn , elven cultures differ — from reclusive woodland kin who guard ancestral forests to cosmopolitan high elves devoted to scholarship and spellcraft. Though diminished from their ancient heights, elves remain bound to memory and legacy, carrying the weight of history even as they carve careful paths into the future. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Size Medium Keen Senses You gain Proficiency in the Perception skill. Elven Weapon Training You have Proficiency with Longswords , Shortswords , Longbows , and Shortbows . Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Fey Ancestry The Feywild casts a veil over your mind. You have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Charmed , and magic can't put you to Sleep . Subraces [ edit section | visual editor ] High elf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default High Elf appearances “ Heirs of the mystical Feywild, high elves value magic in all its forms, and even those who do not study spellcraft can manipulate the Weave. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Cantrip: Choose 1 Cantrip from the Wizard spell list. Note that this means these cantrips use Intelligence as a casting stat. Acid Splash Blade Ward Bone Chill Booming Blade Bursting Sinew Dancing Lights Fire Bolt Friends Light Mage Hand Minor Illusion Poison Spray Ray of Frost Shocking Grasp Toll the Dead True Strike Wood elf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Wood Elf appearances “ These elves spend their reclusive lives in Faerûn's forests. Decades of training in archery and camouflage are enhanced by an otherworldly swiftness. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Mask of the Wild Proficiency in Stealth checks. Fleet of Foot Your Movement Speed is increased by 1.5 m (5 ft). Interactions [ edit section | visual editor ] A deposit of three oozes lurks at the bottom of a charnel pit in the House of Healing Morgue . The creatures turn hostile and reveal themselves the moment a character touches the bottom floor of the pit. ## Fiend
- **来源**: [Fiend](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fiend)
- **分类**: Races

For the Warlock subclass, see The Fiend . A typical fiend creature called a Cambion. Fiends are a type of creature that are from the Lower Planes . They are creatures born of pure evil. “ Evil, wicked creatures from the Lower Planes that labour under the leadership of lawful archdevils or chaotic demon princes. „ — In-game racial description Contents 1 Characteristics 2 Types of fiends 2.1 Cambion 2.1.1 Cambions in Baldur's Gate 3 2.2 Devil 2.2.1 Devils in Baldur's Gate 3 2.3 Gnoll Flind 2.3.1 Gnoll Flinds in Baldur's Gate 3 2.4 Hellsboar 2.4.1 Hellsboars in Baldur's Gate 3 2.5 Imp 2.5.1 Imps in Baldur's Gate 3 2.6 Merregon 2.6.1 Merregons in Baldur's Gate 3 2.7 Succubus & Incubus 2.7.1 Succubi / Incubi in Baldur's Gate 3 3 Other fiends 3.1 Orthon 3.1.1 Orthons in Baldur's Gate 3 3.2 Quasit 3.2.1 Quasits in Baldur's Gate 3 4 Related items 5 Related spells and abilities 6 Notes and references 7 External links Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Fiends come in a variety of forms and sizes. Some are intelligent, while others are not. They are so long-lived that they have an unknown lifespan; as such they do not grow old. With the possible exceptions of Shovel and Haarlep , most fiends in the game are from the (nine) Hells, rather than the Abyss. [ 1 ] Most fiend creatures are resistant or immune to ⁠ Fire damage, due to coming from the Lower Planes. Types of fiends [ edit section | visual editor ] Cambion [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Cambion and Cambion on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Scarlet-eyed and bitter-tempered, cambion are the bastard children of devils and mortals, a fusion of two Planes in one body. „ — In-game racial description Cambion are half-humanoid half-fiend hybrids. Cambions in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Cirrus Feena Mizora Raphael Vengeful Cambion Zhalk Devil [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Devil on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Both lawful and evil to the bone, devils live to scheme and exploit the rules they follow, be it to climb the hierarchy of the Nine Hells or to lay claim to the souls of the mortals they make contracts with. „ — In-game racial description Devils are highly lawful fiends that believe in order. They differ greatly from demons, who believe only in chaos. Devils in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael In game data, there is no devil race. Raphael is defined as a Cambion instead. Gnoll Flind [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Flind and Flind on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Feral, hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger of their demonic creator, Yeenoghu. „ — In-game racial description Flinds are related to Gnolls, but are particularly strong and vicious and part-fiend themselves Gnoll Flinds in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Flind Hellsboar [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Hellsboar and Hellsboar on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Grafted with infernal iron and burning with hellfire, these porcine brutes are filled with a distinct brand of malice. „ — In-game racial description Hellsboar are fiends that look like large boars, with large boney skulls. Hellsboars in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Gilded Hellsboar Lesser Hellsboar Vengeful Boar The Vengeful Boar is defined as its own race in game data, making it technically not a hellsboar. Imp [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Imp and Imp on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Cackling peddlers of infernal mischief, imps bind themselves to the service of more powerful devils who furnish them with commands. „ — In-game racial description Imps are a small, manipulative fiends that serve their masters as foot soldiers or servants. Imps in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Cursed Imp Cruor Gilded Imp Lesser Imp Vengeful Imp Merregon [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Merregon and Merregon on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ In life, these faceless legionnaires of the Nine Hells were soldiers who served evil without reservation. „ — In-game racial description Merregon are the foot soldiers of the armies of most devils in the Nine Hells and live to serve their masters. They wear masks and can't speak, though they can form a sort of hive-mind when grouped together. Merregons in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Hoarding Merregon Merregon Legionnaire Vengeful Merregon Succubus & Incubus [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Succubus & Incubus and Succubus on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Native to the Lower Planes, succubi beckon those they seduce with soft fingers, concealing their claws beneath. „ — In-game racial description “ Sensual and depraved, these dark-winged fiends from the Nine Hells derive pleasure from enticing and devouring lonely souls. „ — In-game racial description Succubi/Incubi are crafty demons whose purpose is to seduce and tempt mortals in order to take their souls. Succubi / Incubi in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Haarlep Other fiends [ edit section | visual editor ] The following types of fiend don't have their own data entry in the game. The listed creatures are defined directly as fiends by game data, not as any sub-type of it. Orthon [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Orthon on the Forgotten Realms Wiki Orthons are hulking humanoid fiends that serve as heavy infantry in the Nine Hells, fulfilling roles such as formation fighter, brutish berserker, and bounty hunter. Orthons in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Yurgir Quasit [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Quasit and Quasit on the Forgotten Realms Wiki Quasits are a chaotic race of fiend that embody wickedness and cruelty. Quasits in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Conjured Quasit Shovel Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Hammer of the Just - additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage against fiends Holy Water - deals 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage against fiends The Blood of Lathander - blinds nearby fiends The Undead Bane - deals additional damage and applies Bane to fiends Voss' Silver Sword - +1d4 bonus to attack rolls and damage against fiends Related spells and abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] Aura of Hate - nearby fiends deal Charisma modifier additional damage with weapon attacks Divine Sense - grants advantage on attack rolls against fiends Divine Smite - deals an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant to fiends Holy Fire - deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant per turn to fiends Planar Binding - if successful, takes control of enemy fiend Protection from Evil and Good - fiends have disadvantage against the target Turn the Faithless - turns fiends, causing them to flee Turn the Unholy - turns fiends, causing them to flee Undead Ward Aura - allied fiends become resistant to ⁠ Bludgeoning , ⁠ Slashing , and ⁠ Piercing damage. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ In traditional D&D lore, Quasits, Succubus and Succubi are demons, which always hail from the Abyss, but in the game, Shovel is simply referred to as a Fiend. Additionally, in the 5e ruleset, Succubus and Succubi are simply fiends, being neither demon nor devil. There is an entry for demons as a race in game data, but it is not used for any creature that exists in the game. ## Flesh Golem
- **来源**: [Flesh Golem](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Flesh_Golem)
- **分类**: Races

A Flesh Golem in Baldur's Gate 3 Flesh Golems are non-playable Construct creatures in Baldur's Gate 3 . They look like fleshy abominations with various body parts stitched together. “ The powerful enchantments that have stitched together this assortment of body parts have imbued it with both a strong defence and formidable strength. „ — In-game racial description About flesh golems [ edit section | visual editor ] Flesh Golems are a type of construct built from a wide variety of fleshy body parts from once-living creatures. They are usually extremely strong and durable, though very quiet and obey their master. During a long fight, they can sometimes go berserk. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Berserk This entity will go Berserk if its health diminishes. Aversion of Fire If this entity takes Fire damage, it receives Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks until the end of its next turn. Magic Resistance Has Advantage on Saving Throws against Spells and other magical effects. Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Immutable Form Spells that alter someone's form have no effect on the affected entity, and it has a +5 bonus to Saving Throws against spells that would remove it from this plane. ## Frog
- **来源**: [Frog](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Frog)
- **分类**: Races

Addled Frog Frogs are a type of Beast and non-playable Race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ These hopping fellows look terribly unfortunate, which isn't a problem, because they sound absolutely miserable, too. „ — In-game racial description About frogs [ edit section | visual editor ] Frogs are carnivorous amphibians, widely distributed over a range of different climates such as desserts and swamps. They also sometimes serve as familiars to magic users. Frogs can be spoken to with Speak with Animals , and conjured as a familiar with the spell Find Familiar: Frog . It is also possible to be briefly polymorphed into a frog through the condition Toad Mode cast by Dolly Dolly Dolly . ## Full-illithid
- **来源**: [Full-illithid](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Full-illithid)
- **分类**: Races

Full-illithid Stats Size Medium Type Aberration Race Mind flayer Balanced Balanced Difficulty Stats AC 16 Initiative +1 Weight 60 kg (120 lb) Ability scores STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 13 (+1) 12 (+1) 14 (+2) 20 (+5) 18 (+4) 18 (+4) Saving throws STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA +1 +1 +2 +5 +4 +4 Conditions Mind Flayer Form Affected entity has completed ceremorphosis and become a mind flayer. Permanent Mind Sanctuary While in combat, Mind Flayers can use actions and bonus actions interchangeably. Features Ability Drain Once per turn, when you make an Attack Roll , the attack reduces that target's corresponding Ability by 1. The reduced ability score cannot be decreased lower than 1. Charm Can charm an attacking enemy, preventing further attacks until their next turn. Cull the Weak When you bring a creature down to fewer hit points than your number of evolved illithid powers, it dies and all nearby creatures take 1~4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. Favourable Beginnings First attack roll or ability check against any target gains proficiency bonus. Luck of the Far Realms Once per Long Rest , you can change a successful Attack Roll against a foe into a Critical Hit . Permanent Mind Sanctuary You can use actions and bonus actions interchangeably. Psionic Backlash When an enemy casts a spell, can use a reaction to deal 1d4 Psychic per spell level. Psionic Dominance When an enemy within 18 m (60 ft) targets you with a spell of a Level that is lower than or equal to your Proficiency Bonus , you can use your reaction to nullify the spell. A full-illithid is a character who has undergone complete ceremorphosis and become a mind flayer . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] This option only becomes available after travelling to the Astral Plane during the quest Confront the Elder Brain . In order to transform, the player character must offer to do so while in dialogue with the Emperor or Orpheus once they have reached the Astral Plane after travelling to the Morphic Pool . If Karlach is present, she also offers to transform. It is not necessary for the player character or Karlach to have accepted the Astral-Touched Tadpole and become a partial-illithid to become a full-illithid. While all party members may become partial-illithid, only the player character, Orpheus or Karlach may undergo the full transformation. Undoing the transformation is only possible for Gale as an Origin character. If he completes ⁠ The Wizard of Waterdeep and hands over the Crown of Karsus to Mystra , the goddess of magic transforms Gale back into his human self to show her gratitude. Changes [ edit section | visual editor ] The player character and Karlach still have access to their previous set of abilities and proficiencies. However, ability scores, race and type change (see info box). Ability score improvements previously gained through the Ability Improvement feat are not retained (e.g., the character will still have 12 dexterity even if they previously improved it by 2 using the feat). However, improvements gained through the Mirror of Loss and Auntie Ethel's Hair persist and are added on top of the illithid's base abilities. A transformed Orpheus has slightly different stats, and only has access to his illithid powers. Conditions [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind Flayer Form Permanent Mind Sanctuary New abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] After becoming a full-illthid, the illithid power tree becomes locked, [ note 1 ] however most [ note 2 ] abilities, or upgraded versions of abilities, are gained, as well as some new ones: Levitate (Illithid Power) Tentacle Whip (Full-illithid) Extract Brain (Full-illithid) Strengthened Force Tunnel Fierce Perilous Stakes Nebulous Black Hole Synaptic Consumption Augmented Shield of Thralls Potent Concentrated Blast Fracture Psyche (Full-illithid) And the full-illithid upgrade of Mind Sanctuary: Permanent Mind Sanctuary Old abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] If the character does not already have the following powers, they are unlocked: Displacer Beast Shape Stage Fright Psionic Overload Mind Blast Mind Sanctuary Transfuse Health And the following passives, if they do not already have them: Ability Drain Charm Cull the Weak Favourable Beginnings Luck of the Far Realms Psionic Backlash Psionic Dominance See also [ edit section | visual editor ] Illithid powers Partial-illithid Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ As of patch #5 ↑ After becoming full-illithid, cannot gain: Displace , Freecast , Repulsor , Illithid Expertise v t e Creature statistics Ability scores Charisma Constitution Dexterity Intelligence Strength Wisdom Skills Acrobatics Animal Handling Arcana Athletics Deception History Insight Intimidation Investigation Medicine Nature Perception Performance Persuasion Religion Sleight of Hand Stealth Survival Features Conditions Feats Illithid powers Passives Permanent bonuses Spells List Other Armour Class Creature sizes Creature types Hit points Experience Point Buy Proficiency Resistances

Ghosts are a type of Undead creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . They primarily appear in Lady Jannath's Estate and the Murder Tribunal in the Lower City . “ The soul of a once-living creature, bound to the material plane by its desire to resolve some unfinished task from its life. „ — In-game racial description About ghosts [ edit section | visual editor ] Ghosts are a spectral form of undead. They cannot be summoned or controlled by the party in the game. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Ethereal Affected entity is incorporeal and can't be Shoved , Thrown , or used as an Improvised Melee Weapon Fly (class action) Fly to a target position for half movement cost. Incorporeal Movement Opportunity attacks against you have Disadvantage . Ghouls are a type of Undead and Humanoid creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Driven by their insatiable hunger for humanoid flesh, ghouls usually roam the night in packs. „ — In-game racial description About ghouls [ edit section | visual editor ] Ghouls devour the flesh of corpses and hunger for that of the living. They can be created by the level 5 necromancy spell , Animate Dead , which can be learned by wizards and clerics . These ghouls are higher level and have different abilities. ## Giant (creature type)
- **来源**: [Giant (creature type)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Giant_(creature_type))

See also: Giant (barbarian subclass) A typical giant creature called an Ogre. Giants are enormous creatures that are humanoid but often have monstrous properties. “ Though giantkind comes in many varieties, each with its own culture, all of them are huge, loud, heavy, and, most importantly, strong. „ — In-game racial description Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Giants are very large, muscular creatures that may or may not be intelligent. In Baldur's Gate 3 , there is only one giant creature type in the game and they are all of Large size. [ 1 ] Types of giants [ edit section | visual editor ] Ogre [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Ogre , Ogre on the Forgotten Realms Wiki and Giant on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ As stupid as they are gluttonous, these hulking giants are known for their quick tempers. They live by raiding, scavenging, and killing for food and pleasure both. „ — In-game racial description Ogres are quick-tempered, dull creatures that kill for food and for fun. ## Githyanki
- **来源**: [Githyanki](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Githyanki)
- **分类**: Races

Not to be confused with Githyanki (Faction) and Githzerai Githyanki are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ With a ruthlessness borne from mind flayer enslavement, githyanki ride the Astral Sea atop red dragons, bringing their silver swords and psionic might to bear against any trace of the illithid menace. „ — In-game racial description About githyanki [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Githyanki appearances Githyanki are peerless warriors from the Astral Plane , known for their legendary silver blades and red dragon mounts. They seek the total destruction of Mind Flayers , whose ancient empire enslaved the ancestral Gith for millennia. Because the effects of time are nearly suspended in their native Astral Plane, githyanki are hatched from eggs across realmspace in outposts called crèches. Crèches serve multiple functions outside the Astral Plane, acting simultaneously as hatcheries, training grounds, and shelters. [ 1 ] Githyanki society is highly militaristic. [ 2 ] They are ruled by their lich queen, Vlaakith , and are led in battle by her dragon-riding knights, the kith'raki, [ 3 ] who serve as high-ranking commanders and provincial governors of the crèches. Because they are the most powerful warriors in the empire, veteran kith'raki are closely monitored by the Lich-Queen's inquisitors – the Ch’r’ai – and are the most frequent candidates for Vlaakith's revered promise of 'Ascension'. [ 4 ] Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base racial speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn Size Medium Astral Knowledge Gain Proficiency in all Skills corresponding to a chosen Ability ( Recharge: Long rest ) Githyanki Psionics You gain access to the following Spells : Cantrip: Githyanki Psionics: Mage Hand (Character level 1). Your Mage Hand is invisible when cast via Githyanki Psionics. Recharge: Long rest 1st Level Spell: Githyanki Psionics: Jump (Character level 3) Recharge: Long rest 2nd Level Spell: Misty Step (Character level 5) Recharge: Long rest Martial Prodigy A lifetime of relentless training gave you Armour proficiency with Light armour and Medium armour , as well as Proficiency with Shortswords , Longswords , and Greatswords . Religion [ edit section | visual editor ] In Baldur's Gate 3 , Vlaakith can be selected as a deity for githyanki Clerics as part of character creation. Within the broader lore of Dungeons & Dragons , however, githyanki society operates without deities. Their history of enslavement by the illithid empire fostered a deep cultural rejection of servitude, a philosophy they extend to divine worship. Instead of gods, the githyanki are rigidly devoted to their Lich-Queen, Vlaakith CLVII. [ 5 ] It is likely that githyanki clerics represented in-game are lore equivalents to the Ch’r’ai – a caste of inquisitors and zealots who channel arcane power directly from Vlaakith, acting as her enforcers rather than traditional shepherds of a religious flock. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] The Cult of Vlaakith [ edit section | visual editor ] Vlaakith is an undead wizard who demands absolute reverence, though she currently lacks a divine spark. High-ranking githyanki warriors who achieve significant power are summoned to their capital, Tu'narath, for 'Ascension'. While nearly all githyanki view this as a reward and elevation to a higher plane of service, certain in-game choices and cutscenes confirm that Vlaakith actually consumes their souls to fuel her own power and to prevent potential rivals from emerging. [ 8 ] The Pact with Tiamat [ edit section | visual editor ] The githyanki maintain a longstanding alliance with Tiamat , the Queen of Evil Dragons. According to established lore, the original leader, Gith, ventured into the Nine Hells to forge a pact with Tiamat, resulting in the githyanki's use of red dragons as mounts. The exact terms of this pact remain undisclosed within the lore, though there is sustained evidence across multiple sourcebooks and in-game dialogue that Vlaakith I betrayed Gith to Tiamat in order to secure the alliance. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] Githyanki view the resulting use of red dragons more as military assets than as creatures to be revered in their own right. The Afterlife [ edit section | visual editor ] Because githyanki reside in the timeless Astral Plane and reject conventional deities, they do not participate in the standard afterlife cycle, and their souls have no 'reserved seating' in the Outer Planes . Instead, lore reflects that souls not consumed by Vlaakith merge with the Astral Plane itself upon death. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Certain items have unique bonuses when wielded or worn by a Githyanki; their bonuses can be enabled by being disguised as one before equipping them. Aberration Hunters' Amulet : Advantage on Intelligence Saving Throws and Aberrations have Disadvantage on Attack Rolls against the wearer. Boots of Psionic Movement : After the wearer uses Fly , their next melee weapon attack deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. Circlet of Psionic Revenge : Grants +1 to Intelligence , Wisdom and Charisma Saving Throws . Githyanki Greatsword (Psionic) : Attacks with this weapon deal an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. Psionic Ward Armour : Grants Resistance to ⁠ Psychic damage. Soulbreaker Greatsword : Attacks with this weapon deal an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. Silver Sword of the Astral Plane : Attacks with this weapon deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. The holder also has Advantage on Intelligence , Wisdom and Charisma Saving Throws , Resistance to ⁠ Psychic damage, and cannot be Charmed . Notable Githyanki [ edit section | visual editor ] Baretha Jeera Lae'zel Losiir Orpheus Ptaris Stornugoss Therezzyn Varrl Vlaakith - Former Voss W'wargaz See also [ edit section | visual editor ] Githyanki vocabulary Githyanki literature List of all githyanki Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ If Lae'zel is freed from her cage near the Ravaged Beach and asked, "And what exactly is a crèche...?" , she answers, "It is many things. A hatchery, a training grounds, a shelter." ↑ Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes (5th Edition, 2018) , emphasizes the military hierarchy of Githyanki society. It also references the specialized spellcasters and inquisitors who maintain Vlaakith's rule. ↑ A gith dictionary ↑ Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes (5th Edition), Chapter 4, details the githyanki military hierarchy and the roles of the kith'raki and Ch'r'ai. ↑ A Guide to the Astral Plane (2nd Edition) and Mordenkainen’s Tome of Foes (5th Edition) relates the githyanki rejection of deities. ↑ Dungeon Magazine #100 ("The Lich-Queen’s Beloved") outlines how Vlaakith grants spells to her loyalists despite lacking true divinity. ↑ Under 5th Edition rules, clerics must technically serve a deity to gain spells. Since Vlaakith is not a deity, a "Cleric of Vlaakith" is a lore contradiction. Baldur's Gate 3 does allow githyanki clerics, which ensures players have the mechanical freedom to play any class/race combination. While the game does not explicitly label this a concession, it does lack unique reactivity for clerics of Vlaakith – even when meeting Vlaakith herself – which strongly suggests the class was implemented as a mechanical option rather than an integrated lore path. ↑ In-game dialogue with Voss and the events within the Astral Prism confirm the true nature of Vlaakith's Ascension ritual. ↑ Possible dialogue choices with Voss during an evening cut-scene with Lae'zel, after having entered the Astral Prism in Crèche Y'llek and leaving the Rosymorn Monastery Trail. ↑ The betrayal of Gith to Tiamat is heavily implied as a closely guarded secret in Dungeon Magazine #100 and later editions of the Monster Manual (Red Dragon entries). ↑ If Lae'zel is played as origin , she remarks on Losiir's death after escaping the Nautiloid , pronouncing, "Losiir is gone. His spirit now swims the Astral Sea." ↑ A Guide to the Astral Plane details the fate of githyanki souls. ## Githzerai
- **来源**: [Githzerai](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Githzerai)
- **分类**: Races

Not to be confused with Githyanki Githzerai are a mentioned-only race in Baldur's Gate 3 . About githzerai [ edit section | visual editor ] Githzerai ( githyanki language for "those who spurn Gith") are a group of Gith who reside in the plane of Limbo . Their split with the githyanki dates back to philosophical differences that emerged in the wake of Gith's successful rebellion against their mind flayer enslavers. The nascent githzerai (lead by their prophet, Zerthimon ) rejected Gith's desire for conquest, believing it made them no better than their former illithid masters. The division resulted in a civil war that saw Zerthimon killed and the githzerai forced to retreat from their home in the Astral Plane . They retreated to Limbo, where most now spend their lives as ascetics and cultivate their psionic powers, led by their immortal god-king, Zaerith Menyar-Ag-Gith . The Waking Mind of a githzerai can be found at the Mind Flayer Colony , and can be conversed with in that location. It will make a request to the character conversing with it, and will reward the special condition Githzerai Mind Barrier if this request is agreed to. Their brain can also be consumed. In the Epilogue , if Orpheus begins his new rebellion against Vlaakith and Lae'zel joines him, then she tells the player character of her upcoming meeting (taking place the day after the reunion) with Zaerith Menyar-Ag-Gith, who has proposed an alliance between the githzerai and the Prince of the Comet. This potential alliance is also implied in a missive sent to the player character by Orpheus, titled The First Protocol , wherein he proclaims the first new Protocol of the Githyanki is "All who call themselves gith shall unite under one sky".
