## Gnoll
- **来源**: [Gnoll](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Gnoll)
- **分类**: Races

A Gnoll standing over their human victim Gnolls are non-playable humanoid creatures in Baldur's Gate 3 . They closely resemble hyenas and are consumed with a primal bloodlust and hunger. Oftentimes, gnolls worship the demon lord Yeenoghu . “ Feral, hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger of their demonic creator, Yeenoghu. „ — In-game racial description About gnolls [ edit section | visual editor ] Gnolls are a race of carnivorous humanoids, tall and lean with a craving for the hunt. They have a strong affinity for family and blood ties, though this comradery is not always extended to separate packs. Gnolls are fond of hyenas, viewing them as brethren and keeping them as pets or hunting companions. Gnolls can be born from bloated hyenas that are fat off the spoils of a massacre. Flinds [ edit section | visual editor ] Flinds are a stronger and more vicious cousin to gnolls who have become part fiend . They often command war bands of gnolls but are otherwise solitary hunters. A gnoll who vanquishes a flind is said to transform into a flind themselves; however, Baldur's Gate 3 has no such mechanic. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Rampage When a Gnoll Downs a creature with a melee attack, the gnoll can use a Bonus Action to move up to half its Movement Speed and make a bite attack. Gnoll characters [ edit section | visual editor ] 'Barnabus' Flind 'Timothy' 'Tomelia' Gnoll enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Render by Nikolai Chugunov Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Prior to Patch 6, gnolls were categorized as monstrosities rather than humanoids . This change makes Baldur's Gate 3 more similar to 5th Edition D&D (which also categorizes gnolls as humanoids). ## Gnome
- **来源**: [Gnome](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Gnome)
- **分类**: Races

Gnomes are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Small, clever, and energetic, gnomes use their long lives to explore Faerûn's brightest corners and darkest depths. „ — In-game racial description About gnomes [ edit section | visual editor ] Gnomes are a small, long-lived race known for their sharp intellect, innate magic, and boundless curiosity. Distantly related to the fey, [ 1 ] their keen minds and natural mental resilience – known as Gnome Cunning [ 2 ] – allow them to parse complex arcane theory, master intricate engineering, or navigate danger with cleverness rather than brute force. Though many gnomes approach life with cheerful optimism and a delight in discovery, their culture is far from monolithic. In Faerûn , gnomes span a wide spectrum: from the inventive Gondian artificers of Baldur's Gate to the reclusive deep gnomes of the Underdark . Whether crafting bizarre contraptions, unlocking ancient lore, or fighting for survival in shadowy subterranean realms, gnomes rely on resourcefulness and ingenuity to leave an indelible mark on the world. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 7.5 m (25 ft) per turn. Size Small Gnome Cunning You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma Saving Throws . Shortened Stride Your movement speed is 7.5 m (25 ft). Artificer's Lore Add twice your Proficiency Bonus to History checks. Forest gnome [ edit section | visual editor ] Default forest gnome appearances “ Even smaller than their cousins and twice as reclusive, forest gnomes are a rare sight in Faerûn. They master magic and craftsmanship in their distant, idyllic groves. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Speak with Animals Gain the ability to comprehend and communicate with beasts. Recharge: Long rest . Deep gnome [ edit section | visual editor ] Default deep gnome appearances “ More guarded than their surface cousins, deep gnomes survive in the Underdark with darkvision and skilful stealth. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Superior Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 24 m (80 ft). Stone Camouflage You have Advantage on Stealth checks. Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Certain items have unique bonuses when wielded or worn by a Gnome. These bonuses can be enabled by being disguised as one before equipping the item. Nimblefinger Gloves : Nimblefinger - a Gnome wearing this gloves gains +2 Dexterity. Rock gnomes uniquely start with a Music Box . ## Goblin
- **来源**: [Goblin](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Goblin)
- **分类**: Races

A goblin in Baldur's Gate 3 Goblins are a non-playable Humanoid Race in Baldur's Gate 3 . Some Goblins are hostile NPCs to the party, but others can be interacted with. “ Weak, selfish humanoids. Though they often serve stronger races, they crave power and abuse what authority they obtain. „ — In-game racial description About goblins [ edit section | visual editor ] Goblins are small-sized , which is advantageous for ambushing enemies through burrows and tunnels. They are usually lightweight, meaning they are easier to Throw and Shove than larger sized creatures. Goblin skin is usually wrinkled, with skin tones ranging from yellow to brown to green. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Small Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Tactician only [ edit section | visual editor ] Fury of the Small When you damage a creature larger than you, you can choose to deal 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Physical extra. Limited to once per combat. Gremishka are a type of Monstrosity and non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They can be found in Rosymorn Monastery during Act One . “ The vicious product of spells gone wrong, these cat-like creatures delight in tormenting magic-users, relishing in the unstable effect magic has on them. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Gremishkas somewhat resemble a fur-less feline with the ears of a bat, and razor-sharp teeth. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 5~13 1d4 + 3 ⁠ Piercing + 1d6 ⁠ Force Bite a target. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Unique traits [ edit section | visual editor ] Gremishkas have the Magic Allergy condition at all times: whenever a spell or cantrip is cast close to them, they gain the Unstable condition. At the start of its next turn, it triggers a random effect, similar to Wild Magic , through a list of possible effects unique to gremishkas. Ice Bloom Create an ice surface and gain   Armour of Agathys . Chaotic Offence Gain 3   Mirror Images , become   Enlarged , and become   Hastened all at once. Panther Polymorph Turn into a panther. Force Explosion Create an explosion that   Dazes nearby creatures. Gremishka Spawn Burst into pieces. Two new gremishkas are born from your remains. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Gremishkas are not particularly imposing Monstrosities , yet they make up for this through numbers and their chaotic reactions to magic. Using something as simple as Fire Bolt can cause a chain reaction through Wild Magic effects, which trigger other gremishka's Allergy condition. Their Evasion passive also makes it challenging to kill them with AoE spells like Fireball . The simplest approach is to rely on physical attacks and avoid using magic. If no spells are cast, a fight against these cat-like creatures is typically quite easy. ## Grim Visage

The Visage of Guilt Grim visages are a type of undead in Act Two . They haunt the Reithwin Tollhouse alongside its tollmaster Gerringothe Thorm , muttering madness the whole time. Each grim visage resembles a floating skull filled with billowing green smoke. “ These skulls spawned from Gerringothe Thorm's twisted psyche. Manifestations of her worst flaws, they keep the coins of her protective armour intact. „ — In-game racial description About grim visages [ edit section | visual editor ] Each visage guards a portion of the accursed coins that provide Gerringothe with her power. Each visage destroyed will, in turn, remove 100 of her maximum hit points and a piece of her Coin Armour . Outside of combat, each visage is protected by Shadow Visage , preventing the party from preemptively weakening Gerringothe. Racial Features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 12m / 40ft Size Tiny Accursed Coins This cursed visage controls part of the coins protecting the Toll Collector . Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). ## Hag
- **来源**: [Hag](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hag)
- **分类**: Races

A hag in Baldur's Gate 3 Hags are a non-playable Fey Race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are clever, highly magical creatures who delight in the suffering they cause. Their power is further increased by their collections of magical trinkets, created by the Hag over the years. “ Soothsayers, invaders of dreams, dark ritualists, saviours, murderers: hags are all of these and more. „ — In-game racial description About Hags [ edit section | visual editor ] According to The Evil Eye there are three known kinds of hags: Green Hags, Sea Hags, and Night Hags. Night Hags are named after their ability to haunt a mortal's dreams. They slowly devour the mortal's vital essense, collecting it in their soul bag. They are known to be petty and selfish, and prone to bragging. Sea Hags are said to smell of fish, and prefer to eat their victims whole. They can kill with a glance. Green Hags can appear as beautiful mortals, are very dangerous, and are quick to anger. ## Half-Elf
- **来源**: [Half-Elf](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Half-Elf)
- **分类**: Races

Half-Elves are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Curious, ambitious, and versatile, half-elves are welcome everywhere, but struggle without a community to call their own. „ — In-game racial description About half-elves [ edit section | visual editor ] Half-elves walk between two worlds, embodying a mixture of human ambition and elven grace. They inherit keen senses and a longer view of life, tempered by humanity’s adaptability and restless drive. This balance grants them unusual insight, enabling them to read hearts and intentions with quiet clarity. Yet belonging does not come easily. Neither fully claimed by elven enclaves nor entirely at home in human cities, half-elves often define themselves beyond bloodline. In Faerûn , they are wanderers, diplomats, and bridge-builders, shaping identities rooted not in purity, but in choice. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Size Medium Civil Militia You have weapon proficiency with: Spears Pikes Halberds Glaives Light armour Shields Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Fey Ancestry The Feywild casts a veil over your mind. You have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Charmed , and magic can't put you to Sleep . Subraces [ edit section | visual editor ] High half-elf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default High Half-Elf appearances “ A touch of the Feywild remains in half-elves with this bloodline, and even those untrained in magic possess a hint of wild power. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Choose 1 Cantrip from the Wizard spell list. Note that this means these cantrips use Intelligence as a casting stat. Acid Splash Blade Ward Bone Chill Booming Blade Bursting Sinew Dancing Lights Fire Bolt Friends Light Mage Hand Minor Illusion Poison Spray Ray of Frost Shocking Grasp Toll the Dead True Strike Wood half-elf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Wood Half-Elf appearances “ Like their wood elf parent, these half-elves have a quickened stride and an eye for stealth. Yet many break away from isolation in Faerûn's forests to explore the rest of the Realms. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Mask of the Wild Proficiency in Stealth checks. Fleet of Foot : Your Movement Speed is further increased by 1.5 m (5 ft). Drow half-elf [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Drow Half-Elf appearances “ Most half-drow result from liaisons between Seldarine drow and surfacers. While half-drow inherited a few magical gifts, they aren't usually raised in the Underdark. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Drow Magic You gain access to the following Spells : Cantrip: Dancing Lights (at character Level 1). 1st Level Spell: Drow Magic: Faerie Fire (at character level 3; Recharge: Long rest ). 2nd Level Spell: Darkness (at character level 5; Recharge: Long rest ). Note: These spells use Charisma as their casting stat. ## Half-Orc
- **来源**: [Half-Orc](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Half-Orc)
- **分类**: Races

Half-orcs are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are born of both human and orc ancestry, and exhibit a blend of orcish and human characteristics, their appearances varying widely. “ Creatures of intense emotion, half-orcs are more inclined to act than contemplate - whether the rage burning their bodies compels them to fight, or the love filling their hearts inspires acts of incredible kindness. „ — In-game racial description About half-orcs [ edit section | visual editor ] Half-orcs are born of both human and orc ancestry and bear traits of both lineages. Known for fierce strength, resilience, and intense emotion, they are inclined toward action and physical prowess. Half-orcs do not have a culture unique to their bloodline; instead, they often adopt the customs and ways of the settlement they grow up in, making their identities as varied as the places they call home. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Despite suspicion from others, many forge their own paths with unwavering resolve. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Default appearance Base Racial Speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Size Medium Menacing You gain Proficiency in the Intimidation skill. Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Relentless Endurance If you reach 0 hit points , you regain 1 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points instead of becoming Downed . Savage Attacks When you land a Critical Hit with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. ## Halfling
- **来源**: [Halfling](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Halfling)
- **分类**: Races

Halflings are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Small yet capable, halflings prefer the comforts of home and hearth - but their natural luck and dexterity makes them fine adventurers. „ — In-game racial description About halflings [ edit section | visual editor ] Halflings are small in stature but famously resilient, possessing quick reflexes and an uncanny knack for defying the odds. While many cherish home, hearth, and good company, others leverage their unassuming size to master stealth and intrigue, or to satisfy ruthless ambition. Whether tending quiet villages, navigating shadowy underworlds, or braving wild frontier lands, halflings rely on quiet resolve, courage, and remarkable luck to navigate a world built for much larger folk. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 7.5 m (25 ft) per turn. Size Small Halfling Luck When you roll a 1 for an Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw , you can reroll the dice and must use the new roll. Brave You have Advantage on Saving Throws against Frightened . Subraces [ edit section | visual editor ] Lightfoot halfling [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Lightfoot Halfling appearance “ Stealthy but social, these halflings travel all over Faerûn to make names for themselves. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Naturally Stealthy Your nimble nature makes you skilled at concealment. You have Advantage on Stealth Checks . Strongheart halfling [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Strongheart Halfling appearance “ Legend has it that dwarven blood gave stronghearts their hardiness. Resistant to poison and wellsprings of endurance, these halflings easily hold their own. „ — In-game racial description Subrace features [ edit section | visual editor ] Strongheart Resilience You have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Poisoned and Resistance to ⁠ Poison damage. Equipment [ edit section | visual editor ] Certain items have bonuses when wielded or worn by a Halfling. These bonuses can be enabled by being disguised as one before equipping the item. Nimblefinger Gloves : Nimblefinger - a Halfling wearing this gloves gains +1 Dexterity. Harpies are a non-playable race and monstrosity type creature located north of the Emerald Grove in the Secluded Cove . “ Sadistic creatures with the legs and wings of a vulture and the body of an elf. Their sweet song enchants their prey, luring them to their deaths. „ — In-game racial description Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Investigate the Beach A group of harpies can be found singing their alluring song along the Secluded Cove. They have already lured the young tiefling Mirkon close to the water's edge. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Claws ( ) Damage: 3~13 2d6 + 1 ⁠ Slashing Lash out with deadly claws. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Fly ( ) Fly to a target position Range: 18 m (60 ft) Luring Song Charm nearby creatures with a magical melody to   Lure them to you. Multiattack ( ) Damage: 6~26 2d6 + 1 ⁠ Slashing + 2d6 + 1 ⁠ Slashing Aim two attacks at a   Lured creature. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Per turn Sharp Rock ( ) Damage: 3~9 2d4 + 1 ⁠ Bludgeoning Throw a sizable, rugged stone. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] The harpies utilize a combination of the terrain and their Luring Song . One harpy always remains at a distance to perform the song, which can cause the party to waste turns if they fail to resist. Meanwhile, the other harpies fly close to attack the party. Any attempts to approach distant harpies will be slowed because of the cove's Difficult Terrain . The harpies can ignore distance and terrain using their fly ability, which allows them to easily multiattack party members who are lured . It is recommended to use ranged attacks and spells on the singing harpy to break their Concentration . If successful, it is suggested to fight aggressively before another harpy sings again. In preparation for combat, it is possible to bless the party before speaking with Mirkon to improve the party's resistance to Luring Song. Using gnomes , elves , or half-elf characters with Advantage on saves can improve the likelihood of resisting the song. It may also be helpful to utilize the high ground flanking Mirkon. A viable yet violent strategy to protect Mirkon involves throwing or shoving him away from the shoreline and the harpies. Tossing him provides more distance from the enemies to reduce his likelihood of being killed. If a party member can cast Calm Emotions , the fight can be somewhat trivialized. Calm Emotions protects Mirkon and all party members within its casting radius from being affected by Luring Song, which significantly reduces combat difficulty. (The game log will still show a saving throw being rolled, but the characters are unaffected on failures.) Alternatively, the party can use Silence and keep their entire party within the silenced area. In both cases, the party should be careful to prevent the caster's Concentration from being broken. If the party member casting Calm Emotions or Silence is a cleric , they can cast Sanctuary on themselves to prevent broken Concentration. However, note that casting Silence over Mirkon before speaking with him immediately triggers the fight. If the player character decides on this strategy, it is advised to cast Silence over Mirkon and the entire party. The hobgoblin must have an ally who is within 2 m (7 ft) of the target and isn't Incapacitated . ## Human
- **来源**: [Human](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Human)
- **分类**: Races

Humans are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are one of the most populous races in Faerûn , exhibiting a versatile range of skills rather than any one mastery. “ The most common face in Faerûn, humans are known for their tenacity, creativity, and endless capacity for growth. „ — In-game racial description About humans [ edit section | visual editor ] Humans are the most widespread and adaptable people of Faerûn , defined by ambition and versatility rather than ancient tradition. [ 1 ] Their relatively short lifespans drive them to achieve greatness quickly, producing heroes, tyrants, scholars, and explorers in equal measure. Culturally diverse and endlessly resourceful, humans found kingdoms, forge alliances, and reshape history. [ 2 ] They reflect this adaptability by excelling in virtually any role, relying on determination and balance rather than singular strength. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Human appearances Base Racial Speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Size Medium Civil Militia You have weapon proficiency with: Spears Pikes Halberds Glaives Light armour Shields Human Versatility Select an additional Skill to be Proficient in. Your carrying capacity is increased by a quarter. ## Humanoid
- **来源**: [Humanoid](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Humanoid)
- **分类**: Races

A kobold humanoid creature. Humanoids are a type of bipedal creature that can be frequently found throughout Baldur's Gate 3. They are the most common creature type, and include all playable races . “ A collection of bipedal races, ranging from humans, elves, and halflings to goblins, gnolls, and kobolds. „ — In-game racial description Contents 1 Characteristics 2 Types of humanoids 2.1 Bugbear 2.1.1 Bugbears in Baldur's Gate 3 2.2 Gnoll 2.2.1 Gnolls in Baldur's Gate 3 2.3 Goblin 2.3.1 Goblins in Baldur's Gate 3 2.4 Hobgoblin 2.4.1 Hobgoblins in Baldur's Gate 3 2.5 Kobold 2.5.1 Kobolds in Baldur's Gate 3 2.6 Kuo-toa 2.6.1 Kuo-toa in Baldur's Gate 3 2.7 Meazel 2.8 Shadar-Kai 2.8.1 Shadar-Kai in Baldur's Gate 3 2.9 Werewolf 2.9.1 Werewolves in Baldur's Gate 3 2.10 Other humanoids 3 Related items 4 Related spells and abilities 5 External links Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Humanoids primarily consist of non-monstrous, bipedal and intelligent creatures. They have two legs, two arms, a torso and a head. Many humanoids are civilised and social creatures, though some are less so. Types of humanoids [ edit section | visual editor ] Bugbear [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Bugbear and Bugbear on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Hairy humanoids that crave carnage and treasure in equal measure. „ — In-game racial description Bugbears are tall, hairy humanoids related to goblins that thrive in the heat of battle. They can usually be found working with other goblins. Bugbears in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Bugbear Assassin Chop Grukkoh Lann Tarv Gnoll [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Gnoll and Gnoll on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Feral, hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger of their demonic creator, Yeenoghu. „ — In-game racial description Gnolls are large, bipedal hyena-like creatures that are consumed with a primal bloodlust and hunger. Gnolls may be found in hunting packs, and typically worship the god Yeenoghu . Gnolls in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Gnoll Fang of Yeenoghu Gnoll Flesh Gnawer Gnoll Hunter Newborn Gnoll Goblin [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Goblin and Goblin on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Weak, selfish humanoids. Though they often serve stronger races, they crave power and abuse what authority they obtain. „ — In-game racial description Goblins are small humanoid creatures that often live in underground caverns in large numbers. They aren't the brightest or strongest creatures around, however their numbers, proficiency with weapons, and general sneakiness can make them dangerous. Goblins in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Goblin Brawler Goblin Booyahg Goblin Boss Goblin Devout Goblin Sapper Goblin Sharp-Eye Goblin Tracker Goblin Warlock Goblin Warrior Hobgoblin [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Hobgoblin and Hobgoblin on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Large, brutal humanoids that live for martial prowess, war, and glory. „ — In-game racial description Hobgoblins are larger, stronger versions of Goblins and share many features, except for their deep red skin. Hobgoblins in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Dror Ragzlin Blurg Kled Kobold [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Kobold and Kobold on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Clever but craven reptilians that overcome their physical ineptitude by banding together. „ — In-game racial description Kobolds are very similar to goblins except they resemble small scaley lizards that stand on two legs. Like goblins, they aren't especially intelligent or strong but they are very crafty, and specialize in traps and ambushing. Kobolds in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Kobold Inventor Kobold Looter Kobold Scout Kuo-toa [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Kuo-toa and Kuo-toa on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Mad, fish-like denizens of the Underdark. They revere imaginary gods with an insane religious fervour. „ — In-game racial description Kuo-toa are humanoid, fish-like creatures that inhabit the seas but can occasionally come on to land thanks to their webbed feet. Kuo-toa are cruel creatures, but are intelligent enough to converse with land creatures and wield weapons. Kuo-toa in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Kuo-toa Hunter Cursed Kuo-Toa (melee) Cursed Kuo-Toa (ranged) Cursed Kuo-Toa Chief Pooldripp Meazel [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Meazel and Meazel on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Twisted, cruel hermits affected by the Shadowfell. Imbued with magic, they move through the shadows to snatch their victims. „ — In-game racial description Meazel are small, hairy creatures that are recluses. When disturbed, they respond typically by garrotting their victims. Shadar-Kai [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Shadar-Kai and Shadar-Kai on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ These elves were transformed by the Shadowfell, until nothing remained but a mournful, joyless existence between life and death. „ — In-game racial description Shadar-Kai are special elves that are bound to the Shadowfell , and are characterized by pale white skin and hair. Shadar-Kai in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] He Who Was Werewolf [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Werewolf and Werewolf on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Savage predators that spread their curse through biting other humanoids. Most werewolves succumb to their bloodlust, but some learn to control their urges, often under the guidance of Selûne, goddess of the moon. „ — In-game racial description Werewolves are savage predators created by a curse that is transmitted by being bitten by other werewolves. Monster_Hyena Hyenas are a type of beast and non-playable race who can be found travelling with gnolls and the Cult of the Absolute . “ Of all subspecies of hyena, only the spotted ones emit that strange cackling giggle that raises the hairs on the neck of a savanna hunter. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Hyenas are pack hunters and scavengers who often serve as hunting companions or pets to gnolls. The corpsed wombs of hyenas regularly serve as the birthing place for new gnolls. They can be found near a wrecked caravan along the Risen Road during Act One , with members of the Cult of the Absolute in the Shadow-Cursed Lands during Act Two and in the Abandoned Cistern with members of the Stone Lord's gang during Act Three . A Bloated Hyena , stuffed with the spoils of fresh slaughter, violently erupts and gives birth to a Newborn Gnoll if not killed first. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 15m / 50ft Size Medium Pack Tactics When an ally is within 3 m (10 ft) of your target and is not Incapacitated , your Attack Rolls against the target have Advantage . Hyena enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Bloated Hyena Hyena (Shadow-Cursed Lands) Snicker Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 3~9 2d4 + 1 ⁠ Piercing Bite a target. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Notable loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Hyena Ear Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Alternative portraits Render by Jean-Pierre Roy Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] There is a unique hyena in Act One at X: 9 Y: 522 with several improved abilities. It possesses the Alert feat and has an additional +5 to initiative on Tactician , as well as 18 Wisdom . This hyena dashes to alert nearby gnolls at X: -3 Y: 546 of the party's presence, and the boosts to initiative and Wisdom make it much more difficult to catch and restrain. The total +11 bonus to Initiative is the single highest bonus on any character in the game. The in-game tool-tip text for the hyena race implies that they are modelled from the spotted hyena, a very social and matriarchal species of hyena. ## Imp
- **来源**: [Imp](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Imp)
- **分类**: Races

Imps are a non-playable race of Fiend creatures, a small flying lesser devil with a venom stinger tail. Found primarily in the Nine Hells , Imps are the first enemies encountered in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Cackling peddlers of infernal mischief, imps bind themselves to the service of more powerful devils who furnish them with commands. „ — In-game racial description About Imps [ edit section | visual editor ] Imps are found throughout the game as enemies, including as the very first scripted combat encounter. An allied imp can be summoned by Pact of the Chain Warlocks using Find Familiar: Imp . Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft (Flying) Size Small Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Devil's Sight You can see normally in darkness, both magical and non-magical, to a distance of 24 m (80 ft). Monster_IntellectDevourer Intellect Devourers are non-playable Aberrations created by mind flayers . They are in various locations in Baldur's Gate 3 . About intellect devourers [ edit section | visual editor ] Intellect devourers resemble glistening brains with four short clawed legs. They are drawn to, and feed on, Intelligence . Illithids breed intellect devourers by transforming the brain of a thrall. The subjected brain grows legs and becomes independent of its original body. Intellect devourers on the Ravaged Beach have the passive Weakened , lowering Armour Class by 5, Hit Points by 6, and removing Darkvision. However, they can still be dangerous if they group up on a single character. ## Kobold
- **来源**: [Kobold](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Kobold)
- **分类**: Races

Popper the kobold at Circus of the Last Days Kobolds are a type of non-playable Humanoid race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Clever but craven reptilians that overcome their physical ineptitude by banding together. „ — In-game racial description About Kobolds [ edit section | visual editor ] Kobolds resemble small scaley lizards that stand upright, and can be found at the Rosymorn Monastery and in Baldur's Gate . Racial Features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Small Pack Tactics When an ally is within 3 m (10 ft) of your target and is not Incapacitated , your Attack Rolls against the target have Advantage . Sunlight Sensitivity While in sunlight, this creature has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Perception checks that rely on sight. Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Tactician Only [ edit section | visual editor ] Evasion Your agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain spells. When a spell or effect would deal half damage on a successful Dexterity Saving Throw , it deals no damage if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail. ## Kuo-toa
- **来源**: [Kuo-toa](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Kuo-toa)
- **分类**: Races

A Kuo-toa in Baldur's Gate 3 Kuo-toa are a non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are degenerate and sadistic amphibian humanoids, but they can generally be communicated with. “ Mad, fish-like denizens of the Underdark. They revere imaginary gods with an insane religious fervour. „ — In-game racial description About kuo-toa [ edit section | visual editor ] Once inhabiting the shores and islands of the surface world, Kuo-toa now dwell in the Underdark . They are generally cruel and sadistic creatures with a cunning intelligence and have the appearance of fish-like humanoids. Kuo-toa are former mind flayer slaves that have the power to manifest their gods through their own belief. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Sunlight Sensitivity While in sunlight, this creature has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Perception checks that rely on sight. The presence of lava elementals disturbs nearby lava, and they heal while standing in it. “ These superheated sacks of molten slag come from a Plane intersecting Elemental realms of Earth and Fire. „ — In-game racial description About Lava Elementals [ edit section | visual editor ] These elemental creatures can manipulate lava. They rapidly heal while standing in Lava and can use their Create Lava action to summon Lava underneath them if no Lava is nearby. Controlling and removing a Lava Elemental's access to Lava can be key to defeating one, while effects that prevent targets from regaining hit points, such as the Bone Chill spell, prevent regeneration regardless of whether the elemental is in Lava. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] A Lava Elemental wanders within the lava lake near the Abandoned Refuge in Grymforge . This elemental is aggressive and attacks the party on sight. Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] A Lava Elemental is on display in Sorcerous Sundries . It is not aggressive to the party. ## Mephit
- **来源**: [Mephit](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mephit)
- **分类**: Races

A Magma Mephit Mephits are a non-playable race and type of elemental creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Capricious, vulgar, and rarely endearing - except to their masters. Mephits are curious, impish creatures from the Elemental Planes. „ — In-game racial description About mephits [ edit section | visual editor ] Ancient mud and ice mephits can be summoned using the spells Conjure Minor Elemental: Mud Mephits and Conjure Minor Elemental: Ice Mephits respectively. Mephits have a Death Burst action and passive, which allows them to deal explosive damage in an area upon death. Each type of mephit has a different version of this feature dealing an appropriate damage type. These effects do not trigger if the Mephit is knocked unconscious. ## Merregon
- **来源**: [Merregon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Merregon)
- **分类**: Races

A Merregon in Baldur's Gate 3 Merregon are a non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are the foot soldiers of the nine hells, and typically wield halberds. “ In life, these faceless legionnaires of the Nine Hells were soldiers who served evil without reservation. „ — In-game racial description About Merregons [ edit section | visual editor ] Merregon are faceless warriors, and permanently wear a mask and do not speak, instead they communicate telepathically. They can be outfitted in a variety of armor and weapons but typically wield a halberd . Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Devil's Sight You can see normally in darkness, both magical and non-magical, to a distance of 24 m (80 ft). Extra Attack You can make an additional free attack after making an unarmed or weapon attack. Magic Resistance Has Advantage on Saving Throws against Spells and other magical effects. MOO_MimicReward Variant 4 UID S_LOW_CountingHouse_Mimic UUID 8db79e35-7dca-46e4-9602-d17938237dec Stats Mimic Mimics are a type of Monstrosity in Baldur's Gate 3 . They often resemble ordinary chests and devour unaware prey that attempt to open them. “ There is no gold in here! „ — Minsc , expressing his displeasure after exiting a Mimic About [ edit section | visual editor ] Mimics can transform to take on the appearance of ordinary objects, often resembling that of treasure chests. They lie in wait and grow long tentacles and sharp teeth, only revealing them just before feasting on unaware prey that get too close. A total of five Mimics can be encountered in-game, three of them are at Grymforge guarding a Harper Stash and one is at Moonrise Towers in what is presumably Isobel's old room. A fifth one is killed by Minsc during a cut-scene in the Counting House . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Bite ( ) Damage: 5~19 2d8 + 3 ⁠ Piercing Bite a target and possibly swallow its weapon. STR Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Pseudopod Lash ( ) Damage: 6~21 3d6 + 3 ⁠ Acid Lash out with a tongue-like appendage to reduce the target's   Armour Class by 2 and pull it 6 m / 20 ft closer. Range: 12 m (40 ft) Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Mimics are ambushers, using their ability to disguise to take their enemies by surprise. Upon approaching a Mimic while disguised, a DC 20 Perception Check is made. If failed, that character is Surprised as the fight begins. It is advisable to fight Mimics with ranged attacks, as they have only half the movement speed of most enemies, and most of their attacks are made at close range, where their Pseudopod Lash attacks can pull a party member down a chasm or off a cliff face (e.g., while fighting them in Grymforge ). It is also wise to keep extra weapons on hand in case a character is eaten by their Bite attack. Weapons eaten by mimics can be retrieved upon looting their bodies after killing them. Because of their low Intelligence , Wisdom and Charisma , Mimics are vulnerable to the many spells involving such Saving Throws . Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Gold Random mix of common weapons, rings and gems Handaxe +1 (Grymforge Mimic) Spineshudder Amulet (Moonrise Towers Mimic) Wondrous Gloves (Grymforge Mimic) Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Model by Mohamed Abdelfatah Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Mimics cannot climb up discrete vertical objects like ropes and ladders. Mind Flayers or illithids are a non-playable Race of Aberration creatures. In Githyanki language, they are called ghaik . Multiple Mind Flayer characters exist in the game. “ Psionic tyrants, slavers, and interdimensional voyagers that feed off the brains of thinking creatures. Most belong to a hivemind colony devoted to an elder brain, and all work towards achieving the Grand Design - their dream of once more controlling empires that span the multiverse. „ — In-game racial description About Mind Flayers [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind flayers are psionic aberrations with a humanoid-like figure and a tentacled head that communicate using telepathy. They feast on the brains of intelligent beings and can enthrall other creatures to their will. Every mind flayer is connected to an Elder Brain , a colossal and powerful psionic brain that commands the mind flayers it is linked to. Mind flayers reproduce by infecting other creatures with a Mind Flayer Tadpole that consumes its host from the inside, transforming them into another mind flayer in a process called Ceremorphosis . Thousands of years ago, mind flayers were a dominant planar power. Using massive flying vessels called Nautiloids , they traveled to hundreds of worlds, harvesting intelligent humanoids to consume, propagate their race, and use as slave labour. One of their enslaved races, the gith , rose up to destroy their empire, leaving only small pockets of mind flayers behind. Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Mind flayers play a major role as antagonists throughout the game, from the prologue into the endgame. Though most are immediately hostile, in some cases a mind flayer can be friendly or downright ingratiating. Whether their pleasantness is genuine or a self-serving veneer on their psionic charms is often unknown. EQP_Unarmed Minotaurs are monstrosity creatures found in the Underdark during Act One . They have powerful leap attacks and can gain advantage on attacks at the expense of giving enemies advantage. About Minotaurs [ edit section | visual editor ] Minotaurs are large humanoid creatures with bull heads and savage roars. They are known for being able to recall any path they have previously traveled. Minotaurs are native to the Underdark . One of them attempts to rush through the entrance of the Selûnite fort and another two patrol the Underdark. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Brutal Leap ( + ) Leap at a target and possibly knock it Prone . STR Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Recharge: Per turn Charge ( + ) Damage: 8~36 4d8 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Charge forward, attacking all enemies in the way, pushing them back 2 m / 7 ft and possibly knocking them   Prone . STR Save Recharge: Per turn Gore ( ) Damage: 6~24 2d10 + 4 ⁠ Piercing Impale a target and push it back 2 m / 7 ft. STR Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Main Hand Attack ( )   –   Greatclub (Minotaur) Damage Normal weapon damage Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Reckless Roar ( ) Gain Advantage on Attack Rolls . Attackers also gain Advantage on Attack Rolls against you. Recharge: Per turn Tenacity ( )   –   Greatclub (Minotaur) Damage: 4 4 ⁠ Bludgeoning When you miss an attack, deal ⁠ Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier anyway (minimum of 1). Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Amulet of the Unworthy [ 1 ] Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] A safer way to handle the two patrolling Minotaurs north of the Selunite Outpost is to keep most of the party hidden and use a party member with high movement speed and good jumping distance to lure them toward X: 120 Y: -175 . A Bulette is scripted to emerge there for a few turns. Since it is Territorial , it attacks the Minotaurs and engages them in combat before burrowing away. After the Bulette has weakened them, the hidden party members can enter combat from stealth for an advantage and finish off the remaining Minotaurs. See also: Mummy A Mummy Lord in Baldur's Gate 3 Mummy Lords are a non-playable Undead race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Huddled in their sarcophagi like sickly penitents, mummy lords creep out to protect their tombs, their crumbling rags host to fierce ancient fists and skin crawling with curses. „ — In-game racial description About mummy lords [ edit section | visual editor ] The Mummy Lord is a more powerful type of Mummy who are effectively immortal unless their heart is destroyed. They lack resistance to physical damage, but also do not have a weakness to fire. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Permanently Armed Creature can't be disarmed. Magic Resistance Has Advantage on Saving Throws against Spells and other magical effects. Multiattack: Frightened The Mummy can Multiattack if the target is Frightened . Turn Resistance Turn Resistance gives Advantage on Saving Throws against any effect that turns undead. ## Myconid
- **来源**: [Myconid](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Myconid)
- **分类**: Races

Two myconids in the Underdark cheering. Myconids are a non-playable race of ambulatory and sentient fungi in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Intelligent, ambulatory fungi residing in the Underdark. They use spores to both communicate and attack, though they'd rather avoid the latter. „ — In-game racial description About myconids [ edit section | visual editor ] Myconids are a peaceful species of sentient fungi found in the Underdark . Groups of myconids live in communities called circles – a collective consciousness or hivemind that communicate through a song-like telepathy, speaking in visions and music. Other species may communicate with myconids through the ingestion of airborn spores. Circles are lead by a single Sovereign, who determines the song of its people (and thus the temperament of a circle), and is able to spawn more myconid by embedding spores into a corpse and resurrecting it. As the Underdark lacks in food sources or light, myconid have evolved to sustain themselves by drinking the essence of the energy of the Underdark – the faerzress. [ 1 ] As such, myconid cannot leave the Underdark. ## Myrmidon
- **来源**: [Myrmidon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Myrmidon)
- **分类**: Races

Portrait of an Air Myrmidon Myrmidons are a type of elemental creature in Baldur's Gate 3 that are available to be transformed into via Combat Wild Shape and Conjure Elemental . About myrmidons [ edit section | visual editor ] Myrmidons are elementals bound in armour. They have immunity to poison, and resistance to slashing, piercing and bludgeoning damage. Myrmidons are Permanently Armed , and as such cannot be disarmed. Air, fire and water myrmidons are also Ethereal so they cannot be shoved , thrown or used as an Improvised Melee Weapon . Myrmidons can be transformed into by druids, or summoned by wizards, bards and druids. They can be found in The Wyrmway , and during combat with Lorroakan or Ansur . ## Orc
- **来源**: [Orc](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Orc)
- **分类**: Races

Not to be confused with Half-orc Orcs are a race of humanoids that are not present but mentioned in Baldur's Gate 3 . Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Orcs are known for their poor temperaments and tendencies toward anger. The offspring of a human and an orc is known as a half-orc . They have a tense relationship with shield dwarves , having warred against them and taken many of their ancient kingdoms. ## Partial-illithid
- **来源**: [Partial-illithid](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Partial-illithid)
- **分类**: Races

This topic has a community guide . Minthara and default Dark Urge as partial-illithids A partial-illithid is a character who has undergone a transformation and become a partial mind flayer , gaining the passive Partial Ceremorphosis . Partial-illithids gain access to elite illithid powers , but also experience a physical change. Becoming partial-illithid [ edit section | visual editor ] After completing Act Two and travelling to the outskirts of Baldur's Gate , the active party is attacked by Githyanki Monks upon long resting. After the fight, The Emperor offers the player character the Astral-Touched Tadpole . The player character can use the astral tadpole immediately, however other companions may have to be Persuaded , except Minthara , who wants to use the tadpole, but must be spoken to for the option to become available. A character can then choose to open their mind to the tadpole (or eat it) to undergo partial ceremorphosis. If any character chooses to eat the tadpole, it is consumed and no longer available for others to use. When given the astral tadpole, the player character must pass a DC 21 Wisdom Check to refuse using it immediately, though a character who has not used any tadpoles need not pass a skill check. A successful refusal still results in the player character receiving the Astral-Touched Tadpole as an inventory item; it can be destroyed after, if desired. For a more detailed walkthrough, see ⁠ Embrace Your Potential . Partial-illithid powers [ edit section | visual editor ] A partial-illithid gains access to the outer tier of elite illithid powers , which can now be unlocked with Mind Flayer Parasite Specimens : Absorb Intellect Black Hole Displacer Beast Shape Fracture Psyche Freecast Illithid Expertise Mind Blast Mind Sanctuary Psionic Dominance They also immediately obtain the following powers (any regular tadpoles the character might have already spent to unlock these abilities will be refunded): Concentrated Blast Favourable Beginnings Fly Force Tunnel Psionic Overload Transfuse Health Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] During the partial ceremorphosis scene, some of the character's teeth may fall out. However, a full set of teeth are still seen in later scenes with the character. Non-party NPCs do not make any comments about transformed characters. Becoming partial-illithid changes only the character's appearance, access to illithid powers, and a small set of companion comments; it does not consequentially affect story choices. Partial Ceremorphosis is a permanent passive condition. The change in a character's appearance from this passive follows them into any disguise they use. This passive is only removed by undergoing full Ceremorphosis . v t e Creature statistics Ability scores Charisma Constitution Dexterity Intelligence Strength Wisdom Skills Acrobatics Animal Handling Arcana Athletics Deception History Insight Intimidation Investigation Medicine Nature Perception Performance Persuasion Religion Sleight of Hand Stealth Survival Features Conditions Feats Illithid powers Passives Permanent bonuses Spells List Other Armour Class Creature sizes Creature types Hit points Experience Point Buy Proficiency Resistances

Phase Spiders are a type of Monstrosity and non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . They can phase teleport to travel short distances instantly. “ Giant spiders that can phase in and out of the Ethereal Plane, making it seem like they can teleport. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Phase spiders are arachnid-kin who dwell in the ethereal plane. Four of them can be found in the Whispering Depths , where they created Web surfaces that warn them of intruders. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Web Walker Isn't slowed down by Web surfaces, and can't be Enwebbed by them. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Ethereal Jaunt ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Range: 22 m (73 ft) Recharge: Per turn Venomous Bite ( ) Damage: 6~21 1d6 + 3 ⁠ Piercing + 1d6 ⁠ Poison + 1d6 ⁠ Poison Bite a target and possibly   Poison it. Deals 1d4+2 Piercing damage and 1d4 Poison damage, and possibly injects a venom that deals 1d4 Poison damage. CON Save Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Venomous Discharge ( ) Damage: 5~15 2d6 + 3 ⁠ Poison Spit out a venomous substance and possibly   Poison those it hits. CON Save Range: 12 m (40 ft) Web ( ) Expel a thick, flammable webbing that slows creatures within and possibly   Enwebs them. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Silk Gland Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Phase spiders are slippery opponents, capable of striking at great distances and bypassing control and area-denial effects like Spike Growth using their Ethereal Jaunt ability. Unprepared parties will struggle to close gaps if they cannot cross Web surfaces in the spiders' lair. Items like Disintegrating Night Walkers and Spiderstep Boots help melee attackers overcome these obstacles. Poison Resistance goes a long way to boosting survivability, as all their attacks rely heavily on poison damage. Phase spider enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Phase Spider Matriarch Phase Spiderling Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Phase spiders have +1 bonuses to Strength and Dexterity on Tactician with resultant bonuses to Initiative , Armour Class , Attack rolls , and Saving throws , making an already fierce early game enemy even deadlier. ## Pixie
- **来源**: [Pixie](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Pixie)
- **分类**: Races

Dolly Thrice the pixie. A Pixie is a type of Fey and non-playable Race in Baldur's Gate 3 . About pixies [ edit section | visual editor ] Pixies are a tiny Fey creature, infamous for their trickery, which is sometimes playful and sometimes malicious. They enjoy playing pranks, but some also perform more helpful magic. During the events of Baldur's Gate 3, pixies are used to light Moonlanterns , their pixie dust giving off light that provides protection from the shadow curse. However, this comes at the expense of the pixie - the Moonlanterns only work while they are being injured. Two pixies can be encountered; Dolly Dolly Dolly in the Shadow-Cursed Lands and Jelliwig in the Lower City . Several dead pixies can also be found in the Shadow-Cursed Lands, victims of Balthazar's experiments on the Moonlanterns. ## Plant
- **来源**: [Plant](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Plant)
- **分类**: Races

A plant creature. Plants are a type of creature that are plant-like or fungal in nature. They can be found throughout Baldur's Gate 3, most notably in the Underdark in Act One, or in shadow-cursed form during Act Two. “ Vegetative or fungal creatures. Most can walk and move - and some are carnivorous. „ — In-game racial description Contents 1 Characteristics 2 Types of plants 2.1 Blights 2.1.1 Blights in Baldur's Gate 3 2.2 Myconid 2.2.1 Myconids in Baldur's Gate 3 2.3 Shambling Mound 2.3.1 Shambling mounds in Baldur's Gate 3 3 Other 4 Related items 5 Related spells and abilities 6 External links Characteristics [ edit section | visual editor ] Plant creatures are creatures that have plant-like features like wood and bark or fungal features like fruiting bodies, but are able to rapidly move and even attack, unlike typical plants. Most plant creatures are non-sentient, but some of the fungi encountered in Baldur's Gate 3 such as the Myconid are indeed sentient. Most plant creatures usually have an aversion to fire, and as such are vulnerable to ⁠ Fire damage. Types of plants [ edit section | visual editor ] Blights [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Blight (race) and Blight on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ These awakened plants, gifted with intelligence and mobility, plague lands contaminated with darkness. „ — In-game racial description Blights are twisted, corrupted plants that have been tainted by evil. They resemble dead versions of their original plant form. Blights in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadow-Cursed Needle Blight Shadow-Cursed Vine Blight Myconid [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Myconid and Myconid on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ Intelligent, ambulatory fungi residing in the Underdark. They use spores to both communicate and attack, though they'd rather avoid the latter. „ — In-game racial description Myconid are a species of sentient fungi that inhabit the Underdark. They typically form communities called circles, and communicate to each other in song form. For other creatures, they communicate telepathically by releasing spores. Myconids in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Sovereign Glut Mossy Myconid Noxious Myconid Restless Myconid Sovereign Spaw Shambling Mound [ edit section | visual editor ] Main articles: Shambling Mound and Shambling mound on the Forgotten Realms Wiki “ These rotting heaps of animated vegetation absorb all organic matter they come in contact with, and are bloated with the remains of plants, animals, and sewage systems. „ — In-game racial description Shambling mounds are large, rotting masses of plant material that dwells often in swamps. Also known as shamblers , shambling mounds are made of dead plants which can make it difficult for a victim to spot until it's too late. Shambling mounds in Baldur's Gate 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadow-Cursed Shambling Mound Other [ edit section | visual editor ] Wood Woad Giant Shadow Creeper Grasping Vine Shadow Creeper Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Exterminator's Axe - deals 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire extra damage against plant creatures. Nature's Snare - ensnared effect does not work against plant creatures. Related spells and abilities [ edit section | visual editor ] Blight - always deals maximum damage on plant creatures. Charm Animals and Plants - charms plants on success Slam (Zombie) - Crawling Gnaw does not apply to plant creatures. Vampire Bite , Ascendant Bite , and Bite (Mother's Loathing) - cannot be used on plant creatures. Poltergeists are an Undead creature in Baldur's Gate 3 . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Poltergeists can be encountered in the ⁠ Jannath Estate . Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Fly ( ) Fly to a target position Range: 18 m (60 ft) Forceful Throw ( ) Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Bludgeoning Throw an item at a creature, wounding it and possibly knocking it   Prone . Heavier items deal more damage. DEX Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Telekinetic Thrust ( ) Damage: 7~34 3d10 + 4 ⁠ Force Shove a target with your mind. The shove distance depends on your Strength and the target's weight. STR Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) Withering Touch ( ) Damage: 7~35 4d8 + 3 ⁠ Necrotic Touch a nearby creature and pour your fetid magic through its very soul. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Poltergeists initially have the condition Invisible , and cause damage by throwing furniture. If a party member has the condition See Invisibility or Volo's Ersatz Eye , they become Revealed for one turn. Poltergeists are only drawn into battle if they are revealed, otherwise they can be ignored entirely (although they continue throwing furniture). They can fly down from the upper levels of the estate, so it may be best to wait for them to come closer rather then traversing into areas where Cursed Skulls are still active. ## Raven
- **来源**: [Raven](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Raven)
- **分类**: Races

Ravens are a type of bird in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Ravens are often employed as messengers or decorative scene-setting by a certain kind of wizard (the kind that drinks out of skull goblets and owns dribbly candles). „ — In-game racial description About ravens [ edit section | visual editor ] Ravens are a type of bird found in several places, most notably in the Shadow-Cursed Lands in Act Two . Ravens are often associated with the Raven Queen . They are generally low intelligence but higher than other animals, and can often be spoken to with Speak with Animals . A raven companion, Dire Raven Companion , is available to Beast Master Rangers. Circle of the Moon Druids can transform into a raven using Wild Shape: Dire Raven . ## Red Dragon
- **来源**: [Red Dragon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Red_Dragon)
- **分类**: Races

A Red Dragon in Baldur's Gate 3 Red Dragons are non-playable Dragon creatures in Baldur's Gate 3 . They are large, confident, and generally evil dragons. About red dragons [ edit section | visual editor ] Red dragons are distinguished by their very large size and wingspan, possibly the largest out of all the dragons, as well as their crimson red scales that can be recognized from afar. In combat, red dragons often unleash a deadly cone of fire on their enemies, melting flesh and metal alike. They are commonly used as mounts for high ranking Githyanki warriors, having been granted them by the goddess Tiamat . Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Size Huge Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Magic Resistance Has Advantage on Saving Throws against Spells and other magical effects. ## Redcap
- **来源**: [Redcap](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Redcap)
- **分类**: Races

This page is for the Redcap race. For the creature, see Redcap . A Redcap in Baldur's Gate 3 Redcaps are a non-playable Fey race in Baldur's Gate 3 exclusively used by Redcap creatures in the game. “ Small, homicidal creatures. Born of bloodlust, they have to keep their caps steeped in blood to survive. „ — In-game racial description Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] Redcaps appear at several locations throughout the game: ⁠ Sunlit Wetlands - Act One ⁠ Festering Cove - Act One ⁠ Circus of the Last Days - Act Three ⁠ Blushing Mermaid - Act Three ⁠ Old Garlow's Place - Act Three About redcaps [ edit section | visual editor ] Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Small Multiattack: Bloodlust The redcap can make a Multiattack while under the effects of Bloodlust . Steeped in Slaughter Has Advantage on Attack Rolls made against Bleeding foes. Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Scrying Eyes are constructs, typically serving the Cult of the Absolute. They are shaped like giant floating eyes. “ These levitating eyes transmit all that they see to the one who created them. „ — In-game racial description Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Scrying Eyes observe the actions of others and relay them to the secret leaders of the Cult of the Absolute . They can report crimes and attempt to alert their allies, if they are attacked. Scrying Eyes are at outposts of the Absolute, including the Shattered Sanctum , Grymforge , and Moonrise Towers . If a party member is caught committing a crime against the Absolute by a Scrying Eye, then the Steel Watcher guarding the South Span Checkpoint in Rivington becomes hostile if it examines the party. [ verify ] Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Psychic Resonance ( ) As its allies draw near, the creature informs them of its exact location. Range: Self Recharge: Per turn Psychic Scream ( ) The creature cries out in alarm to alert its allies. Range: Self Recharge: Per turn Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Crystalline Lens Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] In Tactician and Honour Mode, Ethereal Form's damage reduction (-8) is applied after resistances. Scrying Eyes are especially vulnerable to Shatter since it deals Thunder damage and additional bonus damage against creatures made of inorganic material. It can easily destroy a Scrying Eye in a single hit. Booming Blade can also be used to destroy Scrying Eyes. Shoving a Scrying Eye into a chasm is another option, and does not use resources. Using Improvised Melee Weapon allows for moving a Scrying Eye to a position which allows other party members to shove or throw them into a chasm. Many shoving points of Moonrise Towers have low walls that prevent successful shoving/throwing of Scrying Eyes. Stacking boxes from nearby can allow a party member to reach a height that permit throwing them over the walls. Characters with sufficiently high Strength can often throw Scrying Eyes directly over these walls without needing to stack boxes. ## Shadar-Kai
- **来源**: [Shadar-Kai](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Shadar-Kai)
- **分类**: Races

He Who Was , a Shadar-Kai Gloom Weaver Shadar-Kai are a non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ These elves were transformed by the Shadowfell, until nothing remained but a mournful, joyless existence between life and death. „ — In-game racial description About Shadar-kai [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadar-kai serve the Raven Queen inside the Shadowfell. They were formerly elves before being trapped in the Shadowfell and transformed. The Raven Queen, who is obsessed with collecting memories and essences (typically of loss and grief), sends the shadar-kai to retrieve mementos of tragic events, whether they are physical tokens, memories, or the souls of the dead. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Fey Ancestry The Feywild casts a veil over your mind. You have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Charmed , and magic can't put you to Sleep . Sunlight Weakness Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws while in sunlight. A Shadow is an Undead creature found commonly in Act Two . They are twisted remnants of humanoids that were transformed by the shadow curse . They are visually similar to Wraiths but are, in fact, in their own eponymous non-playable race . “ Resembling dark exaggerations of humanoid shadows, these undead feed on the vitality of the living creatures they were once part of. „ — In-game racial description Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Attacks and actions [ edit section | visual editor ] Dark Currents ( ) Dissolve into the ground and emerge from the shadows at a different location. Range: 8 m (27 ft) Recharge: Per turn Necrotic Claws ( ) Damage: 7~27 2d8 + 3 ⁠ Slashing + 2d4 ⁠ Necrotic Lash out with cursed claws. Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Strength Drain ( ) Damage: 3~24 3d8 ⁠ Necrotic Claw a foe's heart and possibly leech its Strength by 3. The target dies if its Strength is reduced to 0. If the target is in bright light or daylight, it makes its Saving throw with Advantage . STR Save Range: 4 m (13 ft) Loot [ edit section | visual editor ] Rather than dropping loot, a Shadow leaves behind a Shadow Vestige on death that contains a trace of the life it led before it became transformed by the shadow curse. Each shadow drops a unique vestige. The contained memory is spoken by the game's narrator when the vestige is interacted with. Shadow enemy variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadow Friend Shadow Plush Named shadow creatures [ edit section | visual editor ] The Judge Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadow Lantern - grants Conjure Shadow Lantern Wraith which conjures an allied shadow. ## Shambling Mound
- **来源**: [Shambling Mound](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Shambling_Mound)
- **分类**: Races

A Shambling Mound in Baldur's Gate 3 Shambling Mounds are a non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ These rotting heaps of animated vegetation absorb all organic matter they come in contact with, and are bloated with the remains of plants, animals, and sewage systems. „ — In-game racial description About shambling mounds [ edit section | visual editor ] Shambling mounds are large, masses of dead and rotting plant material that have been given life by a lightning bolt. While moving, they appear vaguely humanoid shaped. They usually reside inside swamps, waiting for unsuspecting victims to approach before attacking. Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Large Superior Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 24 m (80 ft). ## Spider
- **来源**: [Spider](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Spider)
- **分类**: Races

See Phase Spider for the monstrosity. A spider in Baldur's Gate 3 Spiders are a type of Beast and non-playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . “ Eight-legged, spindly, and generally awful. „ — In-game racial description About spiders [ edit section | visual editor ] Spiders are a type of arthropod that can create Web surfaces. Spiders are often kept by Drow , as familiars or mounts. The most influential drow goddess, Lolth , is also known as the Queen of Spiders . Cultures which revere Lolth forbid killing spiders. Non-hostile Spiders can be spoken to using Speak with Animals . A spider companion, Aranea (Wolf Spider Companion) , is available to Beast Master Rangers. Druid characters can transform into a giant spider using Wild Shape: Spider . Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Tiny or Small or Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Web Walker Isn't slowed down by Web surfaces, and can't be Enwebbed by them. ## Steel Watcher
- **来源**: [Steel Watcher](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Steel_Watcher)
- **分类**: Races

This page is for the Steel Watcher race. For the creature, see Steel Watcher (creature) . A Steel Watcher guardian Wyrm's Rock Fortress Steel Watchers are a non-playable Construct race in Baldur's Gate 3 . Steel Watchers are characterised by their imposing size and ability to self-destruct. They almost exclusively appear in the city of Baldur's Gate . “ The operations of these huge steel juggernauts are powered by engines of churning hellfire. „ — In-game racial description About [ edit section | visual editor ] Created by Enver Gortash to serve him, Steel Watchers uphold the law in the city of Baldur's Gate. Steel Watchers are formidable foes with large amounts of health and multiple Resistances . Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed 9m / 30ft Size Large Agile Chassis The lightweight build of this Steel Watcher grants it Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws and an additional 9 m (30 ft) movement speed. Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Failsafe Protocol After losing a significant amount of Hit Points , this creature will begin a Self-Detonation Protocol to eliminate all nearby threats. If it dies, it instantly detonates . Immutable Form Spells that alter someone's form have no effect on the affected entity, and it has a +5 bonus to Saving Throws against spells that would remove it from this plane. [ See: Bugs ] Magic Resistance Has Advantage on Saving Throws against Spells and other magical effects. Perfect Sentry You can't be Surprised . Involvement [ edit section | visual editor ] “ ... they act as a defensive wall of steel, but their true purpose is conquest. Mechanized slaughter. „ — Minthara , on Steel Watchers After arriving in Rivington, if Karlach is present while a Steel Watcher is spoken with, it is revealed that Karlach's heart is a prototype engine for the Steel Watchers. If the party explores the Steel Watch Foundry it is revealed that the Watchers are not fully mechanical; rather, they are hybrids of technology and necromancy. Each unit is built around a zombie whose brain has been removed, infected with a Mind Flayer Tadpole , and preserved in vats at the Foundry, where Banite cultists use them to remotely control the corresponding Watcher. During ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch several Hellfire Watchers and a special Steel Watcher Titan are in Steel Watch Foundry . With the exception of the Steel Watcher Titan , Steel Watchers gain the condition Detonation Impending! when their hit points are low. This is caused by the passive feature Failsafe Protocol . The explosion deals 4d12+26 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage in an area around the Watcher. This attack ignores resistance and immunity to Fire damage. Targets still take half damage on a successful Dexterity Saving Throw . If the party defeats Gortash without dealing with the Foundry but has not defeated Orin yet, the Steel Watchers are taken over by the Netherbrain who makes them ignore the party and not assist the Flaming Fist in combat, in order to aid the party in defeating Orin. Additionally, the Netherbrain blows up the Foundry and the Iron Throne . Once the party also defeats Orin, however, the Netherbrain promptly turns on the party and all the Steel Watchers become hostile to them (arguably fulfilling Minthara's assessment of their purpose, if she survives to Act Three ), which then drags the Flaming Fist into combat as well. Types of Steel Watchers [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Category:Steel Watchers Gondian Steel Watcher Hellfire Watcher Steel Watcher Steel Watcher Titan Related literature [ edit section | visual editor ] How to Build a Watcher Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch ⁠ Get Gortash's Netherstone ⁠ Save the Gondians Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Enriched Infernal Iron Gontr Mael [ 1 ] Hellfire Engine Crossbow Immiscibility of Fluids Infernal Iron Steelwatcher Helmet Watcher Greatsword Watcher Crossbow Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Render by Gino Luka Kölling Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ This bow can be looted from the Steel Watcher Titan. ## Succubus & Incubus
- **来源**: [Succubus & Incubus](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Succubus_&_Incubus)
- **分类**: Races

Succubi and Incubi are non-playable races of the Fiend type. The only character of this type in the game is Haarlep who can change between the two variants at will. About Succubi and Incubi [ edit section | visual editor ] Succubi and incubi are lusty, captivating creatures. They ultimately aim to seduce mortals to take their souls. To better accomplish this they are expert linguists and use their shape changing powers to assume a form most humanoids find stunningly attractive. In this regard Haarlep is no exception, and is the only such creature to be found in the game. Although Baldur's Gate 3 implies having separate races, Haarlep nevertheless adheres to the 5th Edition ruleset, as their gender is interchangeable and in fact may change with the player character during an encounter with them. Prior to the 5th edition, these creatures were considered demons . In the 5e ruleset, they are neither demon nor devil , and are simply labled as fiends , who may ally with – or be used by – either cause in the Blood Wars . Succubi [ edit section | visual editor ] Haarlep in Succubus form. The term succubus refers to the female variant. Its plural is succubi . “ Native to the Lower Planes, succubi beckon those they seduce with soft fingers, concealing their claws beneath. „ — In-game racial description Incubi [ edit section | visual editor ] Haarlep in Incubus form. The term incubus refers to the male variant. Its plural is incubi . “ Sensual and depraved, these dark-winged fiends from the Nine Hells derive pleasure from enticing and devouring lonely souls. „ — In-game racial description External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Succubus on the Forgotten Realms Wiki Succubus (Incubus) on Roll20 Compendium (5e stat block) DnD Beyond - The Blood War, too big, too small, or just right? ## Tiefling
- **来源**: [Tiefling](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tiefling)
- **分类**: Races

Tieflings are a playable race in Baldur's Gate 3 . Touched by the Hells, tieflings are resistant to fire and carry extraordinary Infernal powers. “ Descended from devils of the Nine Hells, tieflings face constant suspicion in Faerûn. Thankfully, their arcane abilities make them natural survivors. „ — In-game racial description About tieflings [ edit section | visual editor ] Tieflings are mortals marked by infernal blood tracing back to the Nine Hells . Born from ancient pacts or distant devilish ancestry, they bear horns, tails, and ember-bright eyes that set them apart. Across Faerûn , they frequently face suspicion, prejudice, and fear, regardless of how they choose to live. [ 1 ] Whether descended from Asmodeus , Mephistopheles , or Zariel , many tieflings by necessity develop a resilient, self-reliant nature as they continually strive to define themselves on their own terms – as survivors, mercenaries, or heroes in an often unwelcoming world. [ 2 ] Racial features [ edit section | visual editor ] Base Racial Speed You can move 9 m (30 ft) per turn. Size Medium Darkvision Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). Hellish Resistance Your blood protects you from flame, abyssal or otherwise. Gain Resistance to ⁠ Fire damage, taking only half damage from it. Subraces [ edit section | visual editor ] Asmodeus tiefling [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Asmodeus tiefling appearances “ Bound to Nessus, the deepest layer of the Hells, these tieflings inherited the ability to wield fire and darkness from the archdevil Asmodeus' infernal bloodline. „ — In-game racial description Subrace Features [ edit section | visual editor ] Infernal Legacy Gain the following Spells : Cantrip: Produce Flame (Level 1). 1st Level Spell: Infernal Legacy: Hellish Rebuke (Level 3; casts as if using a second-level slot; Recharge: Long rest ). 2nd Level Spell: Darkness (Level 5; Recharge: Long rest ). Note: These spells use Charisma as their spellcasting modifier, except for Produce Flame . [ note 1 ] Mephistopheles tiefling [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Mephistopheles tiefling appearances “ Descended from the archdevil Mephistopheles, these tieflings are gifted with a particular affinity for arcane magic. „ — In-game racial description Subrace Features [ edit section | visual editor ] Legacy of Cania Gain the following Spells : Cantrip: Mage Hand (Level 1). 1st level spell: Legacy of Cania: Burning Hands (Level 3; casts as if using a second-level slot; Recharge: Long rest ). 2nd level spell: Legacy of Cania: Flame Blade (Level 5; Recharge: Long rest ). Note: These spells use Charisma as their spellcasting modifier. Zariel tiefling [ edit section | visual editor ] Default Zariel tiefling appearances “ Tieflings from Zariel's bloodline are empowered with martial strength, and can channel searing flame to punish their enemies. „ — In-game racial description Subrace Features [ edit section | visual editor ] Legacy of Avernus Gain the following Spells : Cantrip: Thaumaturgy (Level 1). 1st Level Spell: Legacy of Avernus: Searing Smite (Level 3; casts as if using a second-level slot; Recharge: Long rest ). 2nd Level Spell: Legacy of Avernus: Branding Smite (Level 5; Recharge: Long rest ). Note: These spells use Charisma as their spellcasting modifier.
