## Counterspell
- **来源**: [Counterspell](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Counterspell)
- **分类**: Spells、Reactions

Counterspell is a level 3 abjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to interrupt another caster's spellcasting, causing it to fail and have no effect. Description Try to stop a spell being cast. If it is higher level than the spell slot you used to Counterspell, you must make a check using your spellcasting ability [ See: Bugs ] to prevent it. The check's difficulty is equal to 10 plus the level of the spell you are trying to counter. This spell can be cast while you are Silenced . Properties Cost Reaction + Level 3 Spell Slot At higher levels Counterspell can be upcast to counter spells of higher levels without requiring a check. Technical details UID Target_Counterspell Spell flags IsSpell How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Sorcerer , Warlock , and Wizard Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by items: Staff of Interruption ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Scroll of Counterspell is unobtainable without third party tools. Notes Even a failed Counterspell feeds an Abjuration School Wizard's Arcane Ward . When a scroll is successfully counterspelled the scroll is not consumed. Cantrips can also be counterspelled. Counterspell cannot be counterspelled Bugs When attempting to Counterspell a spell of a higher level, the Counterspell caster's Intelligence modifier is used instead of their spellcasting ability modifier as the tooltip states. [ 1 ] Arcane Ward can only be fed up to 3 charges, regardless of spell Level used, due to how an additional hidden Counterspell is cast based on success/failure. External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Counterspell on the Forgotten Realms Wiki References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ From the definition of TryCounterspellHigherLevel(level) in Mods/Shared/Scripts/thoth/helpers/CommonConditions.khn   : Show code function TryCounterspellHigherLevel(level) local spellPowerLevel = SpellPowerLevelEqualOrLessThan(level) if not spellPowerLevel.Result then local counterspellDC = 10 + context.HitDescription.SpellPowerLevel local st = AbilityCheck(Ability.Intelligence, counterspellDC, false, false, 0, context.Observer, context.Observer) return ConditionResult(st.Result,{},{},st.Chance) end return ConditionResult(true,{},{},1.0) end

Lightning Spells cast on water causes the Shocked condition: Removing their reaction and having a chance to stun. Electrified Water + a Fire Spell causes Electrified Steam , which resets the Shocked and Wet conditions. A Cold spell freezes the water/mist and creates an Ice surface, causing Difficult Terrain (half Movement Speed) and may cause creatures in the area to fall Prone unless succeeding a DEX Save. (e.g. Create Water + Glyph of Warding ). Conjuration School Wizards only receive the Create Water variant of the spell, which can only be cast once per Short Rest and does not consume a spell slot. Rain Dancer only grants the Create Water variant of the spell. A character can only have one version of Create or Destroy Water at a time, even if gained from multiple sources. A hidden character that is out-of-combat can cast the Create Water version of this spell on in-combat characters without using an action. While casting the spell unhides them and likely forces them into combat, the character who created this water will still have an action to use in the first turn of combat, as though they had not cast a spell. This is true even in Honour Mode. The incantations for Create Water are Pluo ( "Rain" ) and Aqua pura ( "Pure water" ). The incantations for Destroy Water are Aresce ( "Become dry" ) and Ares decimos ( "Ten times drier" ). ## Curriculum of Strategy: Artistry of War
- **来源**: [Curriculum of Strategy: Artistry of War](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Curriculum_of_Strategy:_Artistry_of_War)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Curriculum of Strategy: Artistry of War is a level 5 evocation spell . It is a unique spell which fires a devastating barrage of homing projectiles that deal ⁠ Force damage. Only wizards can learn this spell by transcribing it from a unique scroll . Description Summon the apparitions of 6 master strategists. Each apparition strikes a target of your choosing, dealing 2d6 + 6 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage (for a total of 12d6 + 36 ⁠ ⁠ Force ). Properties Cost Action + Level 5 Spell Slot Damage: 48~108 2d6 + 6 ⁠ Force + 2d6 + 6 ⁠ Force + 2d6 + 6 ⁠ Force + 2d6 + 6 ⁠ Force + 2d6 + 6 ⁠ Force + 2d6 + 6 ⁠ Force Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Short rest At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Projectile_CursedTome_CurriculumofStrategy Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold How to learn Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 5 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Artistry of War to their spellbooks. Notes The scroll is obtained by reading The Red Knight's Final Strategem in the vault of Sorcerous Sundries . The book can be found at X: 368 Y: 1057 , behind a wall north of the entry portal to the vault, either locked behind a hidden button (requires a DC 15 Perception check to reveal) or accessed from the Vault button in Ramazith's Tower . This spell can be considered a significantly more powerful version of Magic Missile . When upcast with a Level 5 Spell Slot , Magic Missile does 7d4+7 (14~35) force damage across 7 projectiles, dealing 24.5 force damage on average. Artistry of War does 12d6+36 (48~108) force damage across 6 projectiles, dealing 78 force damage on average. Like Magic Missile, this spell's projectiles hit without any attack roll and can curve around obstacles and terrain to hit targets without line of sight. Unlike Magic Missile, this spell is not blocked by Shield . This spell can only be cast once per short rest and cannot be upcast with a Level 6 Spell Slot . This recharge time cannot normally be avoided, even with a free cast feature like Arcane Battery or Freecast . The incantation for Curriculum of Strategy: Artistry of War is Pario , Latin for "Bring forth" , "Produce" , or "Create" . Bugs Despite originating from a spell, damage from this spell is dealt as if from a non-magical source .

Danse Macabre is a level 5 necromancy spell . It summons 4 uncontrollable Ghouls to fight for you. Description Create 4 ghouls that fight alongside you. Properties Cost Action Details Range: 9 m (30 ft) Recharge: Long rest At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_CursedTome_WakeTheDead Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities , IsSpell Creature: Ghoul (Danse Macabre) STR 16 (+3) DEX 17 (+3) CON 10 INT 11 WIS 10 CHA 8 (-1) Duration Long rest Hit Points 20 Armour Class 17 Claws ( ) Lash out with deadly claws and possibly Paralyse the target. Death Burst Explode and deal 6d6 Necrotic to all creatures within 3 m / 10 ft. Devour ( ) Bite a knocked down, prone, or sleeping target, and deal 3d10 + Strength Modifier ⁠ ⁠ Slashing damage. Heal that many hit points. How to learn Granted by items: Necromancy of Thay Notes This spell can only be acquired by completing the quest ⁠ Unlock the Ancient Tome , in Act Three , which fully unlocks the secrets of the Necromancy of Thay . Unlike Animate Dead: Ghoul Pack (or other Animate Dead spells), this spell does not require corpses to cast. The Necromancy School features Undead Thralls: Additional Undead and Undead Thralls: Better Summons both apply to Danse Macabre. With these features, it can summon up to 5 ghouls each with more hit points and damage. Ghouls summoned by this spell: Explode with a Death Burst when killed, dealing ⁠ Necrotic area-of-effect damage. This can destroy other ghouls as a chain reaction and hurt nearby party members as well. Are immune to Demonspirit Madness . This prevents them from being driven mad due to a failed Wisdom saving throw when the summoner wears Abyss Beckoners . Cannot be controlled by the player, and can sometimes 'split' player-controlled characters into different sections of the Initiative order (e.g. Player character/Gale/Astarion/Ghoul/Shadowheart). This prevents the player from swapping between party members before the ghoul and party members after the ghoul (e.g. they cannot have Shadowheart cast Create Water before Gale casts a spell with ⁠ Lightning damage). This is a potentially large downside to using Danse Macabre. Act simultaneously since they belong to the same swarm group, if in the same section of the initiative order. This can potentially reduce turn times due to the large number of extra creatures on the battlefield. Continue to attack a Knocked Out target for 0 damage and do not switch targets so long as the target remains knocked out. The incantation for Danse Macabre is Surgē , the Latin command "Rise!" Bugs The tooltip incorrectly states it costs a Level 5 Spell Slot . Visuals Play Video Local File https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Danse_Macabre_Visuals.mp4

Effects that grant sight in magical darkness, such as the warlock's Eldritch Invocation Devil's Sight , the Eversight Ring from Act Two , Shar's Spear of Evening from Act Two, the Steelwatcher Helmet from Act Three, Eyes of the Dark , and Born into Darkness , allow ranged attacks into and out of this spell's area. Ranged attacks made from the spell's area have Advantage with the tag "Attacking from shadows", provided that the target does not have Darkvision or the attacker is outside its range. This effect is in spite of Darkvision not allowing attacks into or seeing in Darkness . The incantation for Darkness is "Umbra" , Latin for "Shadow" or "Shade". Exposing Sussur Blooms to light from this spell will not cause them to wither while in the Underdark . Bugs Although the in-game descriptions of both this spell and the spell container list a 20-turn limit for this variant, if applied to a character, the effect will be applied to their held main-hand weapon until long rest and will persist even if the caster is no longer in the active party. Although exposing Duergar , Drow and other NPCs to light within range from this spell does trigger Sunlight Sensitivity , it will not show any status effect for the player to see (e.g., as a passive or condition on their character sheets, if examined), yet one can check the combat logs to see the effects of Disadvantage being applied. This spell cannot be cast on a non-allied creature due to a coding mistake, which would otherwise have required them to make a Dexterity Saving Throw with DC equal to the caster's spell save DC to avoid the effect. ## Death Ward
- **来源**: [Death Ward](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Death_Ward)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Death Ward is a level 4 abjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to prevent a target from dying. Description Protect a creature from death. The next time damage would reduce it to 0 Hit Points , it remains conscious with 1 Hit Point left. Properties Cost Action + Level 4 Spell Slot Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_DeathWard Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Death Ward Death Ward Duration: Until Long rest The next time damage would reduce the affected entity to 0 Hit Points , it remains conscious with 1 Hit Point left. How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Cleric , Life Domain (Domain Spell), and Death Domain (Domain Spell) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Notes Dismissing the caster from the party does not remove the condition. When the creature affected is hit with spells like Magic Missile and receives multiple attacks as part of one spell, assuming the 1st attack was sufficient to down the creature with Death Ward active, the 2nd attack appears to apply before Death Ward activates. This means that after 2 attacks the creature loses Death Ward but remains with 1HP: If the initial attack has 3 applications the creature is downed on the 2nd attack and again for an actual kill on the 3rd attack. In the case of party members with Death Ward applied, they need to receive 6 attack applications to actually die: 2 to break down the ward, 1 to get downed and 3 more to fail 3 Death Saves. This effect seems to apply to all multi-application attacks, like Scorching Ray and Eldritch Blast . If cast by a Cleric , this spell must remain Prepared ; removing Death Ward from the caster's prepared spell list removes the condition from all party members whom the caster applied Death Ward to. If a creature is downed on their own turn, all of their actions are restored after being revived by Death Ward. Death Ward does not protect against being shoved, thrown, or otherwise forcibly displaced into chasms. Death Ward does protect party members from Bhaal's Edict , although in this case they lose all of their current buffs and conditions as if they had briefly died. The incantation for Death Ward is Quod Dico Face , Latin for "Do as I say" . Bugs Death Ward uses Survival Instinct as a Parent condition, and as such inherits the Action point restoration it possesses. This can be exploited by a character casting Death Ward on themselves, allowing them to continuously regenerate Action points so long as they are able to both down themselves and recast Death Ward multiple times per turn. Destructive Wave is a level 5 evocation spell . It allows the caster to create a massive shockwave that damages enemies and can possibly knock them prone. Description Create a shockwave of either divine or malevolent thunder that damages nearby enemies and possibly knocks them Prone . Properties Cost Action + Level 5 Spell Slot Damage: 10~60 5d6 ⁠ Thunder + 5d6 ⁠ Radiant Details CON Save (On Save: Targets still take half damage.) Range: 9 m (30 ft) Targets: Enemies only At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_DestructiveWave Spell flags HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell Variants Destructive Wave: Necrotic Destructive Wave: Radiant Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Classes: Class level 9: Tempest Domain (Domain Spell) and Light Domain (Domain Spell) Other ways to learn: Granted by Markoheshkir with Bone-shaking Thunder active ( Recharge: Short rest ) There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. This spell can only be learned by Tempest clerics and Light clerics despite being a paladin spell in D&D 5e, as paladins do not get access to level 5 spells until level 17 in D&D 5e. Bugs This spell is classified as a ⁠ Radiant or ⁠ Necrotic spell depending on the variant rather than a ⁠ Thunder spell. This means it will not work with Tempest Domain's Destructive Wrath or Bone-shaking Thunder's bonus damage. The ally cannot be larger than Medium . Properties Cost Action + Level 4 Spell Slot Details Range: 50 m (167 ft) Targets: 1 moveable ally, Medium or smaller At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. This teleports them alone at the cost of an Action , equivalent to an Arrow of Transposition . This spell cannot teleport allies who are immobile or immune to forced movement, such as from Steadfast from the Helldusk Boots . Attempting to target such a character displays the message: "This character cannot be moved by force". In Explorer difficulty, non-party allies and summons receive a buff that makes them immune to being shoved. This consequently makes them impossible to target with Dimension Door as well. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Bard , Sorcerer , Wizard , Trickery Domain (Domain Spell), and Draconic Bloodline (Gold/Fire Ancestry) Class level 3: Arcane Trickster , Eldritch Knight , and Gloom Stalker Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Bard Magic Initiate: Sorcerer Magic Initiate: Wizard Ritual Caster: Free Spells Granted by items: Mask of the Shapeshifter Other ways to learn: Granted to Warlocks who choose the Eldritch Invocation Mask of Many Faces at level 2+ Wizards can transcribe a Scroll of Disguise Self to their spellbooks. Notes Given the spell's categorization as an illusion rather than a transmutation, and based on its original description and limitations in Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition, one would expect this spell to behave primarily as illusion-based in Baldur's Gate 3, but this is not the case, as is evidenced further below. While disguised as another race, a character does not gain any of the special feats or properties of that race, such as movement speed adjustments, Fey Ancestry , Halfling Luck , Astral Knowledge , or race-specific actions like the breath weapon attacks of dragonborn races. However, in many other respects, this spell does cause the game to treat the disguised character as fundamentally that of their new presence, including in some race related distinctions. Known examples of this include: Assuming the actual size of the disguised form; if the selected form is a race with a different creature size , it can be used to fit through some entrances with size requirements. The racial descriptor at the top of the character sheet changes to the race the character is disguised into, and idle animations of that race are used. Being able to bypass related restrictions on items such as the Silver Sword of the Astral Plane and Dwarven Thrower . Being able to use Speak with Dead on creatures the caster has killed before changing disguises. Being able to repeat certain dialogue options with companions and NPCs, though this does not allow for changes in approval which already occurred. For Clerics and Paladins of Selûne , being able to safely pray at the Altar to Shar and obtain her blessing, rather than her curse. A separate attitude score is used, and permanently maintained, for each separate disguise used with merchants . Race specific dialogue options in both companion and NPC interactions (e.g., Crèche Y'llek's Antechamber ) often become available. In some cases, there are plot-specific dialogue options specifically related to disguising oneself as another race (e.g., pretending to be githyanki in an attempt to bypass their patrols). In other cases, the dialogue makes no distinction between disguising oneself as a race and actually being a member of it. Characters can use this spell to escape each prison once. By changing appearance after being jailed – either by donning or shedding a disguise – the Fugitive condition no longer triggers guard recognition. However, characters who revert to their "criminal" form before the condition expires will blow their cover, and guards will see through any subsequent attempts to use this trick in the same prison. Origin characters and companions typically bypass unique and / or specific dialogue options available to them when disguised (e.g., Astarion at the Last Light Inn with Raphael and The Dark Urge with Gortash in Wyrm's Rock Fortress). The version granted by Mask of the Shapeshifter and Eldritch Invocation Mask of Many Faces is called Shapeshift and does not consume any spell slots. Disguised companions and hirelings revert to their normal form upon leaving the active party. The appearance of the disguise is fixed and remains unchanged whenever this spell is cast. The selected subrace is likewise fixed; for instance, disguising a party member as a dwarf always produces a gold dwarf disguise. Bugs The player character (selected) and their disguised companions, standing together in camp. If a companion or hireling is disguised while at camp , they will remain where they were last placed when another companion or player character is selected, rather than automatically moving back to their tent, until they are moved again or a long rest is taken. This can be useful when seeking to apply conditions or spells with a limited radius, such as Aid . This bug does not apply to Jaheira if she herself is bugged and recruited to the party. Disguise Self disables effects which require the Brand of the Absolute to trigger, such as Gloves of Power . As of Patch 5, Hotfix 17, it is possible to give the caster racial equipment bonuses for longer than intended by using the Mask of the Shapeshifter , taking the mask off, and long resting without removing the disguise. On waking up, the disguise will be gone, but the racial bonuses on the equipment will still affect the character. This only works for racial equipment bonuses, not racial dialogue options. If the player character is disguised as a githyanki when talking to Shadowheart for the first time on the beach at the start of Act One they are awarded an extra 30 xp. Dialogue options to kiss romanced companions are unavailable while they are disguised. While hirelings are disguised, they cannot be spoken with. While disguised, if companions are slated to speak during cut-scenes, they might not be seen or heard, though if they are not their lines can still be read on-screen. ## Disintegrate
- **来源**: [Disintegrate](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Disintegrate)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Disintegrate is a level 6 transmutation spell . It allows casters to deal devastating ⁠ Force damage to a single target, possibly destroying it completely. Description If the target fails a Dexterity Saving Throw , and the spell reduces it to 0 hit points, it disintegrates into a crumbly ash. Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Damage: 50~100 10d6 + 40 ⁠ Force Details DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Damage is negated.) Range: 9 m (30 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Projectile_Disintegrate Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Sorcerer and Wizard Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 6 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Disintegrate to their spellbooks. Notes Despite possible implications in the description, disintegrated targets can still be looted. The Netherbrain does not disintegrate when reduced to 0 hit points from this spell. Damage can be guaranteed by first applying a condition that stuns or makes the target unconcious, such as Stunned or Hold Person . ## Disrobing Blinkstep
- **来源**: [Disrobing Blinkstep](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Disrobing_Blinkstep)
- **分类**: Spells、Bonus_actions

Disrobing Blinkstep is a level 2 conjuration spell . It allows the user to teleport anywhere within sight without triggering Opportunity Attacks , dropping their armor and clothing in the process. Description You teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. However, your clothes do not teleport with you. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Per turn At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. How to learn Granted by items: Boots of Very Fast Blinking This spell is a variation of: Misty Step Notes When the user teleports, they drop worn items. Specifically, worn items on the left side of the character sheet: Headwear , Cloaks , Armour / Clothing , and Handwear – along with worn Camp Clothing on the right side of the character sheet – drop around the place they teleported from (see gallery below). Weapons and Shields are not deemed clothing by the game and remain equipped on use. Additionally, worn Camp Shoes , Underwear , Amulets , and Rings remain on the user, as do The Boots of Very Fast Blinking themselves. The user does not drop any wearable items which are not equipped. If the user removes their equipment prior to using these boots, they can use this variation of Misty Step without any additional drawbacks - aside from the potential benefits of any worn items removed beforehand. Items dropped by this spell are tossed randomly in an approximate 1.5 meter radius around the place where the caster started. This may be prudent to consider if using this spell near ledges. Bugs Sorcerers are able to twin-cast disrobing blinkstep which allows them to select two teleportation positions. It is unclear if this has any effect aside from the caster teleporting to the second position. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Use in game Character Sheet Appearance

## Divine Favour
- **来源**: [Divine Favour](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Divine_Favour)
- **分类**: Spells、Bonus_actions

Divine Favour is a level 1 evocation spell . It allows spellcasters to empower their Weapons to deal extra Radiant damage. Description Your prayer empowers you with divine radiance. Your weapons deal an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details Range: Self Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_DivineFavor Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell Condition: Divine Favour Divine Favour Duration: 3 turns Your weapons deal an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: War Domain (Domain Spell) Class level 2: Paladin Notes This spell pairs well and early in the game with Luminous Armour to inflict the Radiating Orb debuff to lower enemy attack rolls. As this is a condition it can in turn also trigger the Boots of Stormy Clamour to further debuff enemies by lowering their physical Saving throws . Unlike in Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition, unarmed attacks in Baldur's Gate 3 are not counted as "weapon attacks" and do not benefit from Divine Favour. Description Make a beast fight alongside you. Every time the Beast takes damage, it makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against your domination. ## Dominate Person
- **来源**: [Dominate Person](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dominate_Person)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Dominate Person is a level 5 enchantment spell . It allows spellcasters to force a humanoid to temporarily fight as an ally. Description Dominate a nearby humanoid. Allies are unaffected. Every time the creature takes damage, it may repeat the Saving Throw against your domination. Properties Cost Action + Level 5 Spell Slot Details WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_DominatePerson Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Dominated Dominated Duration: 10 turns WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Affected entity will follow and fight alongside the caster of this spell. Every time it takes damage, it may break the caster's control over it with a successful Wisdom Saving Throw . How to learn Classes: Class level 9: Bard , Sorcerer , Wizard , The Archfey , The Great Old One , Trickery Domain (Domain Spell), and Knowledge Domain (Domain Spell) Granted by items: Nymph Cloak ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 5 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Dominate Person to their spellbooks. Notes Dominated characters follow the caster and fight the caster's enemies, but are not directly controllable like a normal summon or party member. Bugs The level 10 Enchantment Wizard feature Split Enchantment allows the caster to target two humanoids with this spell, but only dominates one - even with failed saves - as the second instance of domination ends the effect of the first. ## Draconic Elemental Weapon
- **来源**: [Draconic Elemental Weapon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Draconic_Elemental_Weapon)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Draconic Elemental Weapon is a level 3 transmutation spell . It imbues a weapon with a chosen energy type, increasing its damage and accuracy. This item spell is similar to the Paladin spell Elemental Weapon . Description Imbue a weapon with elemental power. It receives a +1 bonus to Attack Rolls and deals an additional 1d4 damage of your choice. Properties Cost Action Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_MAG_ElementalWeapon Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsMelee , IsSpell Variants Draconic Elemental Weapon: Acid Draconic Elemental Weapon: Cold Draconic Elemental Weapon: Fire Draconic Elemental Weapon: Lightning Draconic Elemental Weapon: Thunder How to learn Granted by items: Drakethroat Glaive ( Recharge: Long rest ) Notes This spell can be used to enchant a different weapon instead, by either dropping the intended weapon on the ground then casting the spell on it or by having another party member equip that weapon and cast the spell on them. A Sorcerer can target two weapons using Metamagic: Twinned Spell . This spell can target weapons and non-enemy creatures with a weapon in their main hand. This effect does not stack with Elemental Weapon or Elemental Age . It does stack with Magic Weapon and Elemental Cleaver .

## Eldritch Blast
- **来源**: [Eldritch Blast](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Eldritch_Blast)
- **分类**: Spells、Cantrips、Actions

Eldritch Blast is a cantrip (Evocation) . It allows the spellcaster to shoot out an energy beam that deals ⁠ Force damage, and can be upgraded with Warlock abilities. Description Conjure a beam of crackling energy. Deals 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to a target. Properties Cost Action Damage: 1~10 1d10 ⁠ Force Details Attack Roll Range: 18 m (60 ft) Pushes: 4.5 m (15 ft) (with Repelling Blast ) At higher levels Unlike other cantrips whose damage increases at certain character levels, Eldritch Blast, instead, creates multiple beams at higher levels: 1d10 (1~10) ⁠ Force per ray 2 beams at character level 5 3 beams at character level 10 You can either target a single creature or multiple creatures with the beams. Each beam rolls a separate Attack Roll and is affected by the selected Eldritch Invocations (see notes for further details). Technical details UID Projectile_EldritchBlast Spell flags AddFallDamageOnLand , DisplayDamageModifiers , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Warlock Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Warlock Spell Sniper Used by creatures: Absolute Questioner , Bolt , Delverdenn , Goblin Warlock , Greez , Gurk , Helsik , Jasin , Jivin Mizzrym , Pactsplitter , Sumera , Tska'an , Tud , and Z'rell Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Notes The benefits of Potent Robe , as well as various effects like Lightning Charges and Eldritch Invocations (such as Agonising Blast or Repelling Blast ), are applied to each beam. While Repelling Blast applies to each beam, it can only knock back a creature once per cast. A target afflicted by Hex takes additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage from each beam. Can be subject to Counterspell . When interacting with effects like Death Ward and dealing multiple beam attacks to the same creature, assuming the 1st attack is sufficient to down the creature with Death Ward active, the 2nd attack appears to apply before Death Ward activates. This means that after 2 beam attacks the creature loses Death Ward but remains with 1HP: If the initial attack has 3 beams the creature is downed on the 2nd attack and again for an actual kill on the 3rd attack. In the case of party members with Death Ward applied, they would need to receive 6 (beam) attacks to actually die: 2 to break down the ward, 1 to get downed and 3 more to fail 3 Death Saving Throws . This effect appears to apply to all multi-application attacks such Magic Missile and Scorching Ray (as of 4.1.1.3669438). The incantation for Eldritch Blast is Dolor , Latin for "pain/anguish" . ## Elemental Age
- **来源**: [Elemental Age](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elemental_Age)
- **分类**: Spells、Bonus_actions

Elemental Age is a level 3 transmutation spell . It enhances the caster's main hand weapon with a chosen element, increasing its damage and accuracy. Description Give your main hand weapon a +1 bonus to its Attack Rolls and an additional 1d4 ⁠ Acid , ⁠ Cold or ⁠ Fire damage to its strikes depending on the elemental age embodied. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: Self At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_MAG_Self_ElementalWeapon Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsMelee , IsSpell Variants Corrosive Age Glacial Age Burning Age How to learn Granted by items: Flail of Ages ( Recharge: Long rest ) Notes This spell can be used to enchant a different melee weapon as follows: Equipping the weapon to be enchanted to the main-hand and the flail to the off-hand of a party member with the Dual Wielder Feat . Casting the spell to enchant the main-hand melee weapon; the enchanted weapon remains enchanted regardless if transferred to another party member or if the flail is unequipped or transferred to another party member. This spell does not stack with Draconic Elemental Weapon or Elemental Weapon . It does stack with Magic Weapon and Elemental Cleaver . Bugs Casting Elemental Age while standing on top of weapons that are on the ground will enchant both the Flail of Ages and the weapons at the same time. The description states that "The blade can be unequipped and equipped again, but has to stay on the spellcaster's person." but this is simply text inherited from the parent spell Shout_FlameBlade and has no actual function.
## Elemental Retort
- **来源**: [Elemental Retort](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elemental_Retort)
- **分类**: Spells、Reactions

Elemental Retort is a level 5 evocation spell . It is unique to Lorroakan , allowing him to retaliate with elemental damage siphoned from his myrmidons when attacked. Each of Lorroakan's myrmidons adds 3d8 damage to to this spell and an additional Reaction to cast it with. It cannot be learned by party members. Description When you take damage, you can retaliate, blasting your attacker with the elemental damage of each myrmidon currently Siphoned . Properties Cost Reaction Damage: 12~96 3d8 ⁠ Lightning (If Air Myrmidon is alive) + 3d8 ⁠ Poison (If Earth Myrmidon is alive) + 3d8 ⁠ Fire (If Fire Myrmidon is alive) + 3d8 ⁠ Cold (If Water Myrmidon is alive) Details DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Target still takes half damage) Range: 18 m (60 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_LOW_RamazithsTower_Dummy Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsEnemySpell , IsHarmful , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold How to learn Used by creatures: Lorroakan Notes At full power, this spell can be devastating as it deals 12d8 damage and can be used up to 5 times per round. It even penetrates resistances on Tactician because of Lorroakan's Elemental Adept feats. Killing a myrmidon will remove 3d8 damage and one Reaction . Killing all four myrmidons will completely negate the spell. Aside from killing the myrmidons, this spell can be blocked by any of the normal reaction blocking conditions . Actions that successfully inflict a reaction blocking condition don't necessarily trigger elemental retort themselves. [ verify ] Bugs Silence does not prevent Lorroakan from casting this spell despite technically requiring a verbal component. This reaction can trigger off any action that targets Lorroakan, not just ones that damage him as the tooltip claims.

## Enlarge
- **来源**: [Enlarge](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Enlarge)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

See also: Enlarge (Duergar) Enlarge is a level 2 transmutation spell . This spell allows spellcasters to increase a creature's body size. Affected creatures deal more damage with their weapons and gain Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Description Make a creature larger. Its weapons deal an extra 1d4 damage. It has Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Details Range: 9 m (30 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Enlarge Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell Condition: Enlarged Enlarged Duration: 10 turns CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Size is increased. Weapon attacks deal 1d4 more damage. Has Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . How to learn This spell is a variation of: Enlarge/Reduce Notes The Constitution Saving Throw only applies when the spell is cast on a non-party member. When Duergar cast this spell as a racial ability, it can only be cast once per Long Rest but notably does not require Concentration as of Patch 3 . Enlarge increases the target creature's size to the next higher category. For example, a Medium creature becomes Large . This also increases the scale of the creature's model by 33%. Enlarged creatures can Shove significantly heavier objects. Refer to max shove weight for details. On the other hand, Enlarge does not affect the weight of objects that can be Thrown or wielded as a Improvised Melee Weapon . Enlarge also increases the weight of the target creature to 2.35 × original weight. If the new weight is below the minimum weight of the new size category (e.g. 200 kg if increased to Large ), the weight is set to the minimum value for that category. See Creature Size for more information. The incantations for Enlarge are Gigans ("Giant") and Extende ("Extend"). Bugs Despite not being mentioned in the condition description, unarmed attacks, but not those made while transformed by Wild Shape, are affected by Enlarge. Visuals Play Video Local File https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Enlarge_Reduce_Visuals.mp4 External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Enlarge/reduce on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Enlarge/Reduce
- **来源**: [Enlarge/Reduce](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Enlarge/Reduce)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Enlarge/Reduce is a level 2 transmutation spell . It allows spellcasters to alter a creature's body size. The caster can choose to double or halve the size of the affected creature. Description Make a creature larger or smaller. Either option has a duration of 10 turns. This affects their weapon damage and Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Details Range: 9 m (30 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_EnlargeReduce Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell Variants Enlarge Reduce How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Sorcerer and Wizard Class level 8: Arcane Trickster and Eldritch Knight Races: Character level 3: Duergar ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Granted by items: Sethan ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 2 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Enlarge to their spellbooks. Notes The Constitution Saving Throw only applies when the spell is cast on a creature that is not a member of the party. The effects of Enlarge/Reduce on a target creature are as follows: Increases the target's size category by 1 (Enlarge) or reduces it by 1 (Reduce) Increases the target's carrying capacity by +25% (Enlarge) or reduces it by -25% (Reduce) Grants Advantage on Strength saving throws and skill checks (Enlarge) or Disadvantage on them (Reduce) Increases its weapon or unarmed damage by +1d4 (Enlarge) Multiplies its weight by 2.35 (Enlarge) or divides it by 2.35 (Reduce) Increases its visual size by 33% (Enlarge) or reduces it by 33% (Reduce) The change in size from the spell stacks with the change in size from Disguise Self , making it possible to become a tiny creature (small race + Reduce). As a tiny creature it is possible to go through even the smallest of passageways such as pipes or jumping through the bars of a fence, something even small races cannot do. Sethan only grants the Reduce variant of the spell, while Duergar only receive the Enlarge variant of the spell. Both variants are usable once per Long Rest . The incantations for Enlarge are Gigans ( "Giant" ) and Extende ( "Extend" ). The incantations for Reduce are Minimus ( "Smaller" ) and Diminue ( "Diminish" ). Properties Cost Action Cost on hit Bonus Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Damage: 1~6 Normal weapon damage + 1d6 ⁠ Piercing (Per turn) Details Attack Roll STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Concentration At higher levels Upcasting : Ensnared condition deals an extra 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage per level. For the version used by Wood Woads, see Entangle (Wood Woad) . Entangle is a level 1 conjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to conjure magical vines and turn an area within range into difficult terrain. Creatures are possibly Entangled and move at half speed while standing in this area. Description Vines sprout from the ground, turning it into Difficult Terrain and possibly Entangling creatures within. Entangled creatures cannot move. An ally can use its help action to try and tear away the vines. Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Radius Creates Area: Twisting Vines Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Entangled creatures cannot move. Type: Surface Condition: Entangled Entangled Duration: 1 turn STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Cannot move. Attack Rolls against the creature have Advantage , while the creature's Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws have Disadvantage . Condition: Difficult Terrain: Vines Difficult Terrain: Vines Duration: Whilst on surface Movement speed halved. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Druid Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Druid Used by creatures: Harvard Willoughby (Nature's Vengeance) Notes If a character becomes Entangled when this spell is cast, it remains so until the end of its next turn, because Entangled loses duration at the end of the combat turn. Instead, Prone from Grease or Enwebbed from Web do not prevent a character from moving during its next turn (unless they get this condition again when moving). An equivalent spell, Faithwarden's Vines , is provided by Pale Oak . Bugs Entangle has TargetConditions of not Grounded() , which means it cannot be targeted against creatures that have the Grounded attribute (such Ketheric Thorm with Reaper's Rigidity ). Despite this restriction, Entangle does affect creatures that have the Grounded attribute (without any change in functionality), and can be cast against such creatures by indirectly targeting them within the AoE circle. ## Enthrall
- **来源**: [Enthrall](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Enthrall)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Enthrall is a level 2 enchantment spell . It allows spellcasters to capture the attention of a creature, forcing it to focus on them. Description Reduce a creature's peripheral vision and make it look at you. Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Details WIS Save Range: 6 m (20 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Enthrall Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell Condition: Enthralled Enthralled Duration: 10 turns WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Peripheral vision reduced. Will keep looking at the spellcaster. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Bard and Warlock Notes This is not considered a hostile spell and can be cast on NPCs without repercussions. This spell prevents NPCs from investigating crimes, in other words, successfully pickpocketing an Enthralled NPC or Enthralling them after they shout that they have been robbed stops them from investigating or initiating a conversation, ending the investigation entirely. If pickpocketing, ensure the target is Enthralled when they notice something is missing. As long as they have 3 remaining turns of Enthrall after succeeding on a pickpocket attempt, safety is likely. It is recommended the pickpocketer not be the caster of the spell. Additionally, since no investigation is done, the pickpocketer is not marked as suspicious, and the NPC in question will not stare at the criminal, making successive pickpocket attempts easier to set up. Stealing items which belong to an NPC that are out in the open, not on their person, is trickier and requires timing; they must be enthralled after they shout that they have been robbed to interrupt the investigation, then ending it prematurely. Casting too late risks the investigation starting and getting caught in a conversation. In this case the culprit can be the one who casts the spell. ## Evard's Black Tentacles
- **来源**: [Evard's Black Tentacles](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Evard's_Black_Tentacles)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Evard's Black Tentacles is a level 4 conjuration spell . It summons tentacles in an area that make it difficult to move and harm creatures. Description Tentacles sprout from the ground, turning the area into Difficult Terrain , attacking and Smothering creatures within. Properties Cost Action + Level 4 Spell Slot Damage: 3~18 3d6 ⁠ Bludgeoning ( Strength Saving Throw to negate) Details STR Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 6 m (20 ft) Radius Creates Area: Black Tentacles Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_BlackTentacles Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell Area: Black Tentacles Black Tentacles Duration: 10 turns AoE: 6 m (20 ft) Radius Squirming, ebony tentacles fill the area, turning it into Difficult Terrain , and dealing 3~18 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage to all creatures entering it and Smothering them. Type: Surface Condition: Black Tentacles Black Tentacles Duration: Whilst on surface STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Restrained by dark tendrils. Affected entity can't move and takes 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage per turn. Attack Rolls against the affected entity have Advantage , while the entity's Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws have Disadvantage Condition: Difficult Terrain Difficult Terrain Duration: Whilst on surface Movement Speed halved How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Wizard and The Great Old One Granted by items: Strange Tendril Amulet ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 4 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Evard's Black Tentacles to their spellbooks. Notes Black Tentacles condition has two possible effects: it can prevent a character from moving, and it can deal damage. There is a saving throw for restraining, and restraining may happen when the spell is cast at the beginning of a character's turn when re-entering the area. Damage is dealt only at the beginning of the turn when a character fails the save and also had the condition before the turn. An affected character seems to lose all movement speed, but actually the duration of this condition is only applied whilst on its surface ; this means that movement speed is returned if the character escapes the surface, for example by using Misty Step . As a comparison, Enwebbed has duration of 1, so escaping the webbed surface does not return the movement speed. If a character is dealt damage by a weapon (at least, spells and fists do not appear to have this effect) earlier in the same round, it is not affected when the spell is cast. However, if later in the same turn such a character moves in the affected surface, they will need to make the saving throw. ## Eyebite
- **来源**: [Eyebite](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Eyebite)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Eyebite is a level 6 necromancy spell . It allows casters to choose amongst one of three debilitating conditions to impose on a single target. Description Your eyes become black corridors walled in teeth, your gaze capable of inflicting dread, sickness, or putting creatures to sleep. While Concentrating , you may cast Eyebite without expending a spell slot . Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Details WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Eyebite Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell Variants Eyebite: Panicked Eyebite: Sickened Eyebite: Asleep How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Bard , Sorcerer , Warlock , and Wizard Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 6 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Eyebite to their spellbooks. Notes Enemies affected by Eyebite: Asleep do not count as being asleep for the purpose of being vulnerable to Devour (Animate Dead Ghoul) [ verify ] . Eyebite grants three variants to the caster as indicated above: Eyebite: Panicked , Eyebite: Sickened and Eyebite: Asleep . These variants are "granted" spells. Granted spells are issued to the caster after casting the original, and can be cast again without spending another spell slot as long as Concentration is not broken. Granted spells such as this are not directly tied to the casters' repertoire of known spells (i.e., their spellbook icon in the game). Therefore, if a granted spell is cast when multiclassing, subsequent recasts (in this case, for example, Eyebite: Asleep ) use the spellcasting modifier of the most recently acquired spellcasting class rather than the spellcasting modifier that was used for the initial casting of Eyebite. In this case, it may result in an unexpectedly low spell save DC. The incantation for Eyebite is Deminuo Te , Latin for "I lessen/diminish you" . - **分类**: Spells、Actions

False Life is a level 1 necromancy spell . It allows spellcasters to gain Temporary Hit Points . Description Bolster yourself with a necromantic facsimile of life to gain 7 temporary hit points . Can only have temporary hit points from one source. Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details Range: Self At higher levels Upcasting : Casting this spell at a higher level yields an extra 5 temporary hit points for each spell slot level above 1st. Technical details UID Shout_FalseLife Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell Condition: False Life False Life Duration: Until Long rest Gain 7 temporary hit points plus 5 additional for each spell slot level above the first. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Sorcerer , Wizard , and Death Domain (Domain Spell) Class level 3: Arcane Trickster and Eldritch Knight Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Sorcerer Magic Initiate: Wizard Other ways to learn: Also granted to Warlocks who choose the Eldritch Invocation Fiendish Vigour at level 2+. When gained in this way, the spell can be cast at will and doesn't expend Spell Slots . Wizards can transcribe a Scroll of False Life to their spellbooks. Notes If a wizard casts False Life on themselves, this spell must remain prepared . Removing it from the Prepared Spells list immediately removes the applied bonus. If applied by using a scroll directly, instead of transcribing it into a wizard's spellbook, the caster need not keep the spell prepared. The incantation for False Life is Dum Vita Est, Spes Est , Latin for "While there is life, there is hope" . ## Fear
- **来源**: [Fear](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fear)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Fear is a level 3 illusion spell . It allows spellcasters to terrify targets by projecting phantasmal images, forcing enemies to flee. Description Hostile targets drop everything and become Fearful : they have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls . If the target ends their turn where they can't see you, they can make another Saving Throw to shake off their fear. Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Details WIS Save Range: Self AoE: 9 m (30 ft) Cone Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Zone_Fear Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell Condition: Fearful Fearful Duration: 2 turns WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Has Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls . It must run from the source of its fear and cannot take any additional actions. Targets can make a Saving Throw to shake off this effect if they end their turn out of sight from their source of fear. Condition: Weapon Dropped! Weapon Dropped! Duration: 1 turn WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) An enemy has made you drop your weapon to the ground, similar to Disarmed . How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Bard , Sorcerer , Warlock , Wizard , and Trickery Domain (Domain Spell) Class level 9: Gloom Stalker Granted by items: Servitor of the Black Hand Gloves ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 3 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Fear to their spellbooks. Notes This spell does not target allies who are included in the area of effect. This spell is the only ability in the game that applies Fearful (or a variation of) but is affected by effects providing advantage or disadvantage on saving throws against being Frightened , such as Countercharm or Shield of the Undevout . While the initial saving throw to apply Fearful is affected by these effects, the saving throw that occurs each turn to remove Fearful is not. ## Feign Death
- **来源**: [Feign Death](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Feign_Death)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Feign Death is a level 3 necromancy spell . It allows spellcasters to put their allies into a magical, protective coma, feigning death. Description Put an ally in a protective coma. They become Resistant to all damage except ⁠ Psychic . Disease and poison no longer have any effect. Removed when Helped . Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Details Range: 1.5 m (5 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_FeignDeath Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Feigning Death Feigning Death Duration: 10 turns Has sunk into a magical coma deep enough to imitate death Resistant to all damage except ⁠ Psychic damage, and Disease and Poison no longer have any effect Removed when Helped How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Bard , Cleric , Druid , and Wizard Granted by items: Boots of Apparent Death ( Recharge: Short rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 3 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Feign Death to their spellbooks. Notes If the party committs a crime and guards are called on the party, it is possible to cast Feign Death on the party member who committed the crime to avoid being interrogated. The guards typically leave before the spell runs out, and the party can then keep all the stolen goods. Depending on the severity of the crime, the other party members might be interrogated as well and need to roll a Charisma Check. In light of this, use of Feign Death is advised for petty crimes like pickpocketing or for more serious crimes if the other party members are nowhere near. Despite the flavoring of the spell, in combat enemies may not treat someone with this buff as if they were dead and will typically continue to attack them. So it cannot be used to reset or escape fights. Prior to Patch 7, Applying Feign Death on an allied NPC (denoted by a green outline when moused-over) was not considered a hostile action and did not offend the target or nearby NPCs. Moreover, Stealing from an NPC under the effect of Feigning Death did not trigger hostility, provided no other NPCs witnessed the crime and the target NPC did not notice anything had been stolen upon waking. Failing a pickpocket attempt, however, terminated the current pickpocketing session, which could not be resumed until the next turn , yet not wake the NPC. This was particularly effective when used on Traders . However, with the application of Patch 7, only allies can be targeted by Feign Death. Feign Death when cast from a scroll does not appear to have been patched with this limitation. ## Find Familiar
- **来源**: [Find Familiar](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Find_Familiar)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

See also: List of summoned familiars Find Familiar is a level 1 conjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to conjure a fey familiar that can aid them in combat and world exploration. Description Summon a familiar, a fey spirit that takes an animal form of your choosing Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Short rest Ritual At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_FindFamiliar_Ritual Spell flags CannotTargetCharacter , CannotTargetItems , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Wizard and Ranger (via Beast Tamer ) Class level 3: Eldritch Knight , Arcane Trickster , and Warlock (via Pact of the Chain ) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Wizard Ritual Caster: Free Spells Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Scroll of Find Familiar is unobtainable without third party tools. Notes Although listed as a Ritual spell where one might expect otherwise, this spell - as per its description - has the limitation of being cast only once per short rest, per character. The standard (non-racial) version of the cantrip Mage Hand has the same limitation. Find Familiar: Cheeky Quasit and the version of Find Familiar granted from the Ritual Caster feat have separate once per short rest limitations. A character who knows multiple versions of these spells can summon familiars multiple times (once for each version known) without short resting, though they are still limited to one active familiar at a time. Familiars are automatically dismissed when the caster leaves the active party. When cast by a Wizard, a conjured familiar persists if the caster unprepares the spell and unlike most summons, persists even after a long rest. All versions and variants of the Find Familiar spell are mutually exclusive; a character can only have one familiar summoned by any Find Familiar spell at a time, including special summons like Shovel and Scratch , the Raven Gloves spell Summon Quothe the Raven , and the additional options granted to a Warlock with Pact of the Chain . However, this does not include Us , as it does not count as a Find Familiar variant. Casting another version of the spell dismisses any currently summoned familiar. The Beast Master Ranger feature Summon Companion is separate to Find Familiar, and may also be active at the same time. Familiars can drink elixirs and potions by having someone else place elixirs/potions out of their inventory and then have the familiar drink it from the ground by right-clicking them, or by drinking it directly from a companion's inventory as long as the elixir/potion is not inside a container. Even though familiars can drink elixirs, increasing their Strength serves no purpose outside of increasing jump distance, as their attacks always use Dexterity . The raven is the only standard familiar given a specific name: "Quothe". This is a reference to Edgar Allen Poe's poem "The Raven", and probably also the raven Quoth who appears in Terry Pratchett's Discworld novels (himself a reference to "The Raven"). Familiars cannot interact with the environment except to examine and attack. Notably, unlike Mage Hand , they cannot be used to explore burrows or press buttons (though many of the buttons and levers can still be triggered if the Familiar Attacks them). Familiars can drag objects. This includes placing objects onto vents or moving objects off of traps. The incantation for standard Find Familiar variants is Ex Textura , Latin for "Out of the weave" , while that of Find Familiar: Boo is Invoco Te , Latin for "I call you" . Variants [ edit section | visual editor ] Select variant: Find Familiar: Cat Find Familiar: Crab Find Familiar: Frog Find Familiar: Rat Find Familiar: Raven Find Familiar: Spider Variants exclusive to Pact of the Chain : Find Familiar: Imp Find Familiar: Quasit Special separate variants of this spell that can only summon one specific creature: Find Familiar: Boo ( Minsc only) Find Familiar: Cheeky Quasit (Obtainable in the Apothecary's Cellar } Find Familiar: Scratch (If Scratch is in the camp and Scratch's Ball is in possession) Visuals [ edit section | visual editor ] Play Video Local File https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Find_Familiar_-_Cheeky_Quasit_Visuals.mp4 External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Find familiar on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Flame Blade
- **来源**: [Flame Blade](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Flame_Blade)
- **分类**: Spells、Bonus_actions

This article is about the normal spell. For the Mephistopheles tiefling variant, see Legacy of Cania: Flame Blade . For the summoned weapon, see Flame Blade (weapon) . Flame Blade is a level 2 evocation spell . It allows spellcasters to summon a fiery scimitar in their free hand that sheds bright light. Casters can make a melee weapon attack with the blade to deal Fire damage to enemies. Description Conjure a flaming Scimitar in your hand for 10 turns that deals 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. It sheds a bright light in a 3 m (10 ft) radius and a dim light in a 6 m (20 ft) radius. The blade can be unequipped and equipped again, but must stay on the spellcaster's person. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Details Range: Self At higher levels Upcasting : Damage increases by 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire for every two spell slot levels above 2nd (e.g., a total of 4d6 at levels 4 and 5, and 5d6 at level 6). Technical details UID Shout_FlameBlade Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell Item: Flame Blade (weapon) Flame Blade   – Duration: 10 turns Damage: 3~18 3d6 ⁠ Fire Properties Scimitars Melee Martial One-handed Price: 30 gp Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Druid Granted by items: Elixir of Tiefling Vice ( Recharge: Single use) Other ways to learn: Wizards cannot transcribe a Scroll of Flame Blade to their spellbooks. Notes Mephistopheles tieflings gain a racial variant of this spell, but the summoned weapon behaves differently from the one conjured by the normal spell. Refer to Legacy of Cania: Flame Blade for details. On the other hand, the single use variant from the Elixir of Tiefling Vice behaves the same as the normal spell. The blade has no weapon actions tied to it other than basic attack. Attacks with the blade use a melee spell attack roll rather than a normal weapon attack roll. As a result, many features that apply to normal weapon attacks do not apply when attacking with a Flame Blade, while some spell related features apply instead. The attack roll uses the wielder's spellcasting ability . This is normally Wisdom , but when multiclassing it uses the spellcasting ability of the class the caster most recently took a first level in. The attack roll benefits from items and features that improve spell attack rolls like Hood of the Weave or Arcane Acuity , but not weapon attacks like Swordmaster Gloves . Attacks with the Flame Blade do not count as weapon attacks for most features (specifically, anything that checks IsWeaponAttack() ). This includes Arcane Synergy , Band of the Mystic Scoundrel , Colossus Slayer , and many others. The one exception is Extra Attack and its variants which check for weapon attacks a different way. As with most spell attacks, no modifier is added to the damage roll . Attacks with the Flame Blade do not count as "spells" for most interactions, but there are two specially handled interactions: Pyroquickness Hat : Hits with the Flame Blade trigger the effect and grant a Bonus Action . Gloves of Battlemage's Power : Hits with the Flame Blade trigger the effect and grant Arcane Acuity . This item has very unintuitive and buggy behaviour, so refer to its page for more details. The blade can be equipped in either the main hand or the off hand, and can be unequipped, but must stay on the spellcaster's person. This also means it cannot be thrown. When the spell ends, the caster automatically re-equips the weapon they had equipped immediately prior to casting the spell, without costing an Action . If the caster is wielding a Light weapon in their main hand (or has the Dual Wielder feat and is wielding a weapon which is not Two-Handed weapon in their main hand), Flame Blade will be wielded in Two-Weapon Fighting style along with that weapon. The position of these weapons will be as follows: If the caster was already wielding a weapon in their off hand when the spell was cast, Flame Blade will replace the off-hand weapon. When the spell ends like this (with flame blade in the off-hand), the weapon that was previously in the off hand will not be re-equipped, and the off hand will be left empty. If instead the off-hand was empty when the spell was cast, the blade will be summoned in the main-hand , and the weapon previously equipped in the main hand will be moved to the off-hand . When the spell ends like this, the original weapon will be moved back to the main-hand, with the off-hand now empty. While equipped, Flame Blade prevents the wielder from sheathing their weapon(s). Flame Blade has the same two incantations as Shillelagh : Canto Te , Latin for "I enchant you" , and Para Bellum , Latin for "Prepare for war" . Bugs A permanent Flame Blade can be obtained by having a druid hireling such as Danton cast this spell, immediately recalling their soul, and hiring them again. A Flame Blade created this way loses its technical FLAME_BLADE status which causes it to revert to a normal melee weapon. Attacks count as normal melee weapon attacks rather than melee spell attacks. It uses the normal melee attack modifier for the attack roll and damage. Normally this is Strength , but features like Pact of the Blade and Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks can change this. It is no longer bound to the summoner and can be holstered, thrown, and transferred to party members. It no longer interacts with the Gloves of Battlemage's Power or Pyroquickness Hat . It no longer emits light. It loses the flaming visual effect. External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Flame blade on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Flame Strike
- **来源**: [Flame Strike](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Flame_Strike)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Flame Strike is a level 5 evocation spell . It allows the caster to make a pillar of divine flame at a chosen location dealing 5d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage and 5d6 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage. Description Make a pillar of divine fire roar down from the heavens like the wrath of affronted angels. Properties Cost Action + Level 5 Spell Slot Damage: 10~60 5d6 ⁠ Fire + 5d6 ⁠ Radiant Details DEX Save (On Save: Targets still take half damage.) Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Radius At higher levels Deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage and 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage for each spell slot level above 5th. Technical details UID Target_FlameStrike Spell flags CanAreaDamageEvade , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell How to learn Classes: Class level 9: Cleric , The Fiend , Light Domain (Domain Spell), and War Domain (Domain Spell) Notes Flame Strike is often compared with the similar spell Fireball : When cast with a level 5 spell slot, both deal 10d6 damage, though Flame Strike generally has a slight advantage here due to the mixed damage type it has: Fire damage is often resisted, while Radiant damage rarely is. Relatedly, Flame Strike imparts two separate instances of damage to the affected targets, one for each damage type. This has many mechanical benefits, such as forcing all targets who are concentrating to each roll two saving throws to maintain concentration . Fireball requires a direct trajectory between the caster and the target for the Fireball to travel, while Flame Strike can be used within range so long as the caster has sight of the target location. Fireball has a roughly 69% larger area of effect when compared to Flame Strike. Fireball can be cast at 3rd or 4th level if the caster cannot or does not wish to use higher-level spell slots. In D&D 5e, Flame Strike deals only 4d6 Fire and 4d6 Radiant damage at 5th level, and upcasting it only increases one of the damage types by 1d6, rather than both. The incantation for Flame Strike is Torrē , the Latin command "Parch/Scorch/Burn". External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Flame strike on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Flesh to Gold
- **来源**: [Flesh to Gold](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Flesh_to_Gold)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

See also: Flesh to Stone Flesh to Gold is a level 6 transmutation spell . It restrains a target and turns it into gold after 3 turns. Description Restrain a target and, after 3 rounds, the target becomes inactive solid gold until the spell ends. The target will Petrify if it does not succeed its Saving Throw within 3 turns. [ See Notes ] Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Details CON Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_TWN_Tollhouse_FleshToGold Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Turned to Gold Turned to Gold Duration: Permanent CON Save ( Spell save DC ) The affected creature is turned into gold. It cannot move or take actions, bonus actions, or reactions. How to learn Granted by items: Signed Trade Visa Notes This spell can only be cast once by consuming the Signed Trade Visa . Using it might bring unexpected (run-ending) consequences if certain characters cannot die. This spell cannot be copied to a Wizard's spellbook. However, Flesh to Stone , a functionally identical spell, can be learned by level 11 Wizards and Warlocks . As with all scrolls, using this spell does not consume a spell slot when cast, only the scroll itself and an Action . The target must fail four Saving Throws in total in order to turn to gold. Each turn the target fails a saving throw, it progresses to a new stage of the Flesh to Gold debuff, all of which are identical in effect to Restrained : Flesh to Gold: Stage 1: Affected entity cannot move as its body begins to turn to gold over the course of 3 turns. Flesh to Gold: Stage 2: Affected entity cannot move as its body is turning to gold. Flesh to Gold: Stage 3: Affected entity cannot move as its body enters the final stage of goldification. Bugs Despite the description stating the effect lasts 'until the spell ends,' petrification from this spell is indeed permanent until the target is cured by Basilisk Oil or a spell such as Greater Restoration . Flesh to Gold incorrectly uses the icon from Flesh to Stone, which it uses as a parent spell. Despite requiring Concentration to cast, Flesh to Gold's concentration immediately ends once the target has progressed to Flesh to Gold: Stage 2 and is no longer required afterwards. Through use of a khn function named HasFleshToSToneCheck() , Flesh to Stone and Flesh to Gold should be uncastable on a target which is already afflicted with either of these two spells. However, this function only includes checks for the Flesh to Stone conditions, and as such Flesh to Stone is castable on a creature already afflicted with Flesh to Gold.
## Flesh to Stone
- **来源**: [Flesh to Stone](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Flesh_to_Stone)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

See also: Flesh to Gold Flesh to Stone is a level 6 transmutation spell . It allows the caster to Atrophy a foe, Restraining them until they temporarily turn to stone. Description Atrophy a foe, Restraining them until they temporarily turn to stone. The target will Petrify if it does not succeed its Saving Throw within 3 turns. [ See Notes ] Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Details CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_FleshToStone Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Flesh to Stone: Restrained Stage 1 Flesh to Stone: Restrained Stage 1 Duration: 3 turns Affected entity cannot move as its body begins to petrify over the course of 3 turns. Attack Rolls against it have Advantage , while the entity's Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws have Disadvantage . Condition: Petrified Petrified Duration: Permanent CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Turned to stone. Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions . How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Wizard and Warlock Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 6 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Flesh to Stone to their spellbooks. Notes The target must fail four Saving Throws in total in order to turn to stone. Each turn the target fails a saving throw, it progresses to a new stage of the Flesh to Stone debuff, all of which are identical in effect to Restrained : Flesh to Stone: Restrained Stage 1 : Affected entity cannot move as its body begins to petrify over the course of 3 turns. Flesh to Stone: Restrained Stage 2 : Affected entity cannot move as its body progresses toward petrification. Flesh to Stone: Restrained Stage 3 : Affected entity cannot move as its body enters the final bone-stiffening stages of petrification. On the fourth turn, the target becomes Petrified . This spell can be cast on a creature without provoking hostilities during the four petrification saving throws. However, once the creature has turned to stone or succeeded a saving throw, its nearby allies turn hostile and / or a guard response is provoked. Bugs Despite the description stating the effect is 'temporary,' petrification from this spell is indeed permanent until the target is cured by Basilisk Oil or a spell such as Greater Restoration . Through use of a khn function named HasFleshToSToneCheck() , Flesh to Stone and Flesh to Gold should not be castable on a target which is already afflicted with either of these two spells. However, this function only includes checks for the Flesh to Stone conditions, and as such Flesh to Stone can be cast on a creature already afflicted with Flesh to Gold. Fog Cloud is a level 1 conjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to summon a sphere of Fog on an area in range and heavily obscure the area. Creatures within the area are Blinded. Description Create a cloud of dense fog to Heavily Obscure and Blind creatures within. Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 4.5 m (15 ft) Radius Creates Area: Fog Concentration At higher levels Upcasting : When this spell is cast at 2nd level or higher, its area of effect increases by 2 m (7 ft) for each spell slot level above 1st. Technical details UID Target_FogCloud Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold Area: Fog Fog Duration: 10 turns AoE: 4.5 m (15 ft) Radius Heavily Obscures and Blinds creatures within. Type: Cloud Condition: Blinded Blinded Duration: Whilst on surface Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range of attacks and spells reduced to 3 m (10 ft). Attack Rolls against Blinded creatures have Advantage . How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Druid , Sorcerer , Wizard , Tempest Domain (Domain Spell), and Draconic Bloodline (Bronze/Lightning Ancestry) Class level 2: Ranger Class level 3: Arcane Trickster and Eldritch Knight Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Druid Magic Initiate: Sorcerer Magic Initiate: Wizard Granted by items: Hammergrim Mist Amulet Other ways to learn: Wizards can transcribe a Scroll of Fog Cloud to their spellbooks. Notes The incantation for Fog Cloud is Voco Nubes , Latin for "I call/summon smoke" . Bugs The radius of Fog Cloud does not consistently increase by 2 m (7 ft) for each spell slot level cast above the 1st. Instead, the following occurs: Spell slot 1 to spell slot 2 increases the radius by 1.5 m (5 ft). Spell slot 2 to spell slot 3 increases the radius by 2 m (7 ft). Spell slot 3 to spell slot 4 increases the radius by 2 m (7 ft). Spell slot 4 to spell slot 5 increases the radius by 0.5 m (2 ft). Spell slot 5 to spell slot 6 increases the radius by 1.5 m (5 ft). The displayed cast radius of Fog Cloud at spell slot level 1 is 4 m (13 ft), but it instead creates a cloud radius of 4.5 m (15 ft). The displayed cast radius of Fog Cloud at spell slot level 5 is 12 m (40 ft), but it instead creates a cloud radius of 10.5 m (35 ft). The displayed cast radius of Fog Cloud at spell slot level 6 is 14 m (47 ft), but it instead creates a cloud radius of 12 m (40 ft). ## Freedom of Movement
- **来源**: [Freedom of Movement](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Freedom_of_Movement)

Freedom of Movement is a level 4 abjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to imbue an ally with the ability to avoid some slowing effects. Description Snap an ally out of any Stun . Difficult Terrain can't slow them down, and they can't be magically Paralysed or Restrained . If the target is restrained by non-magical means, it can spend 1.5 m (5 ft) of Movement to free itself. Properties Cost Action + Level 4 Spell Slot Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_FreedomOfMovement Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Freedom of Movement Freedom of Movement Duration: Until Long rest The affected creature's Movement Speed cannot be reduced by Difficult Terrain , spells or magical effects. The affected creature cannot be Paralyzed or Restrained . How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Bard , Cleric , Druid , War Domain (Domain Spell), Tempest Domain (Domain Spell), and Circle of the Land (Coast or Grassland) Notes Freedom of Movement only ignores the additional movement cost of Difficult Terrain . Secondary effects of terrain (such as falling Prone on an Ice surface or taking ⁠ Lightning damage on an Electrified Water surface) can still affect a party member who has Freedom of Movement. If cast by a Cleric or Druid who does not have Freedom of Movement as a Domain/Circle Spell, this spell must remain Prepared . Removing this spell from the caster's Prepared Spells list removes the buff from all party members whom the caster applied it to. Bugs Despite the description, there is no differentiation between magical and non-magical sources of Paralysed or Restrained (all are removed/prevented), nor is there any function which allows an affected creature to spend 1.5 m (5 ft) of Movement to free itself from any effects. Ineffective against Maimed . External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Freedom of movement on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
