## Glyph of Warding
- **来源**: [Glyph of Warding](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Glyph_of_Warding)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Glyph of Warding is a level 3 abjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to inscribe a ward that can trigger various magical effects when stepped on by an enemy. Description Inscribe a circle of arcane glyphs on the ground. When stepped on by an enemy the selected magical effect will trigger. The glyph will last until triggered, or until a Long Rest . Only one glyph can be active at a time. Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Details DEX Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) AoE: 4 m (13 ft) Radius At higher levels See each individual variant's page. Technical details UID Target_GlyphOfWarding Spell flags CannotTargetItems , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell Variants Glyph of Warding: Acid Glyph of Warding: Cold Glyph of Warding: Detonation Glyph of Warding: Fire Glyph of Warding: Lightning Glyph of Warding: Sleep Glyph of Warding: Thunder How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Bard , Cleric , and Wizard Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 3 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Glyph of Warding to their spellbooks. Notes When the glyph is triggered, each of those affected by it rolls a Dexterity Saving Throw . If a creature successfully saves, they only take half the damage for the elemental variants of this spell, and suffers no ill effect for the sleep and detonation variants. Only those considered an enemy can trigger the glyph. When the glyph is triggered everyone within the area is affected, regardless of allegiance. Enemies are indicated via a red circle beneath the creature, red outlines when highlighted, and denoted by a red dot in the minimap. Neutral, friendly, and allied creatures (highlighted yellow, green, or blue respectively) can safely traverse the glyph. If the glyph is cast in an area where hostile creatures are already present, it triggers immediately. Only one glyph per caster can be active at a time. If a creature with an active glyph casts the spell again, the previous one vanishes with no effect. Active glyphs also vanish harmlessly if the caster is dismissed from the party. When the spellcaster is surrounded by enemies, it is sometimes worth throwing the glyph down right at their feet. This is true for most AOE spells, but especially so for the sleep variant of Glyph of Warding: The shared Initiative system means an ally can immediately shove/help the spellcaster awake should they fall asleep due to their own glyph. Magical Sleep Immunity is fairly common, either from an Elixir of Peerless Focus or from Fey Ancestry Shadowheart , being a Half-Elf Cleric , can naturally utilize this tactic starting from level 5. The incantation for Glyph of Warding is Ira Et Dolor , Latin for "Anger and pain" . ## Glyph of Warding: Fire
- **来源**: [Glyph of Warding: Fire](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Glyph_of_Warding:_Fire)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Glyph of Warding: Fire is a level 3 abjuration spell . This spell is a variant of the Level 3 Abjuration Spell, Glyph of Warding . It allows spellcasters to inscribe a ward which explodes and deals Fire damage to enemies when triggered. Description The glyph explodes, dealing ⁠ Fire damage to enemies in the vicinity. Creatures who pass the Dexterity Saving Throw still take half damage. The glyph will last until triggered, or until a Long Rest . Only one glyph can be active at a time. Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Damage: 5~40 5d8 ⁠ Fire Details DEX Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) AoE: 4 m (13 ft) Radius At higher levels Upcasting : Casting this spell at a higher level deals an extra 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage for each spell slot level above 3rd. Technical details UIDs Target_GlyphOfWarding_Fire Projectile_GlyphOfWarding_Fire_Trap Triggered effect Spell flags CanAreaDamageEvade , CannotTargetItems , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell , IsTrap How to learn This spell is a variation of: Glyph of Warding Notes Only those considered an enemy can trigger the glyph. When the glyph is triggered everyone within the area is affected, regardless of allegiance. Enemies are indicated via a red circle beneath the creature, red outlines when highlighted, and denoted by a red dot in the minimap. Neutral, friendly, and allied creatures (highlighted yellow, green, or blue respectively) can safely traverse the glyph. If the glyph is cast in an area where hostile creatures are already present, it triggers immediately. Only one glyph per caster can be active at a time. If a creature with an active glyph casts the spell again, the previous one vanishes with no effect. Active glyphs also vanish harmlessly if the caster is dismissed from the party. ## Glyph of Warding: Sleep
- **来源**: [Glyph of Warding: Sleep](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Glyph_of_Warding:_Sleep)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Glyph of Warding: Sleep is a level 3 abjuration spell . This spell is a variant of the Level 3 Abjuration Spell, Glyph of Warding . It allows spellcasters to inscribe a ward which can put enemies to Sleep when triggered. Description The glyph emits a soothing magic that puts everyone within range to Sleep when stepped on by an enemy. Any creatures within the area of effect (that aren't immune to magical sleep) that fail the Dexterity Saving Throw will be put to Sleep. The glyph will last until triggered, or until a Long Rest . Only one glyph can be active at a time. Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Details DEX Save Range: 9 m (30 ft) AoE: 4 m (13 ft) Radius At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UIDs Target_GlyphOfWarding_Sleep Projectile_GlyphOfWarding_Sleep_Trap Triggered effect Spell flags CannotTargetItems , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell , IsTrap Condition: Sleeping Sleeping Duration: 2 turns DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) A sleeping creature cannot move or act. Moreover, the creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attack Rolls against it have Advantage , and any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 1.5 m (5 ft) of the creature. Removed by taking damage, becoming wet , receiving Help or being Shoved . How to learn This spell is a variation of: Glyph of Warding Notes Only those considered an enemy can trigger the glyph. When the glyph is triggered everyone within the area is affected, regardless of allegiance. Enemies are indicated via a red circle beneath the creature, red outlines when highlighted, and denoted by a red dot in the minimap. Neutral, friendly, and allied creatures (highlighted yellow, green, or blue respectively) can safely traverse the glyph. If the glyph is cast in an area where hostile creatures are already present, it triggers immediately. Only one glyph per caster can be active at a time. If a creature with an active glyph casts the spell again, the previous one vanishes with no effect. Active glyphs also vanish harmlessly if the caster is dismissed from the party. When the spellcaster is surrounded by enemies, it is sometimes worth throwing the glyph down right at their feet. This is true for most AOE spells, but especially so for the sleep variant of Glyph of Warding: The shared Initiative system means an ally can immediately shove/help the spellcaster awake should they fall asleep due to their own glyph. Magical Sleep Immunity is fairly common, either from an Elixir of Peerless Focus or from Fey Ancestry Shadowheart , being a Half-Elf Cleric , can naturally utilize this tactic starting from level 5. ## Grant Flight
- **来源**: [Grant Flight](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Grant_Flight)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

See also: Fly (disambiguation) Grant Flight is a level 3 transmutation spell . It allows spellcasters to grant a creature they touch the ability to fly. Description Bestow the ability to Fly upon yourself or an ally. Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Concentration At higher levels Upcasting : Affects an additional target for each spell slot level above 3rd. Technical details UID Target_Fly Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Flight Flight Duration: 10 turns Fly up to target position, up to 18 m (60 ft) each turn using your Movement Speed . How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Sorcerer , Warlock , Wizard , and Circle of the Land (Mountain) Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 3 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Fly to their spellbooks. Notes This spell has been renamed from Fly , the tabletop version's name, to distinguish it from the Fly action that naturally flying creatures have. Affected creatures do not have true flight, and instead have to land at the end of each movement. The incantation for Grant Flight is Tibi Do Penna , Latin for "I give you (a) feather" . Bugs Upcast versions of this spell gain the ability to target multiple creatures, but as the spell lacks the SpellFlag IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities the same creature can be selected multiple times for no additional effect. ## Greater Invisibility
- **来源**: [Greater Invisibility](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Greater_Invisibility)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Greater Invisibility is a level 4 illusion spell . It allows spellcasters to provide a more resilient form of Invisibility for their allies. Description Turn a creature Invisible. Attacks against it have Disadvantage . It attacks with Advantage . Invisibility breaks when you fail increasingly harder Stealth Checks on attacking, casting spells, or interacting with items. Properties Cost Action + Level 4 Spell Slot Details Range: 1.5 m (5 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Invisibility_Greater Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Greater Invisibility Greater Invisibility Duration: 10 turns Entity has Advantage on Attack Rolls . Attack Rolls against it have Disadvantage When interacting with items, casting spells, or attacking, the entity needs to succeed on a Stealth Check to maintain Invisibility. The Check becomes harder with each successful attempt. How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Bard , Sorcerer , Wizard , Circle of the Land (Underdark), The Archfey , and The Hexblade Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 4 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Greater Invisibility to their spellbooks. Notes The Stealth check Difficulty Class for this spell starts at 15 and increases with the number of successes, with the exact scaling determined by difficulty: Outside of Honour mode, the DC scales linearly : DC = 1 5 + ( number of previous successful Stealth checks ) In Honour mode, the DC scales quadratically : DC = 1 5 + ( number of previous successful Stealth checks ) 2 Actions with the Invisible flag can be performed without this Stealth check. They also do not increase the Stealth check DC of subsequent actions. A hidden character who is out of combat can cast this spell on allies in combat without expending their action in this combat. While casting the spell is likely to render the caster unstealthed and add them into the initiative order, the caster still has their action in combat. ## Hail of Thorns
- **来源**: [Hail of Thorns](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hail_of_Thorns)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions、Bonus_actions

Hail of Thorns is a level 1 conjuration spell . It allows the caster to make a ranged attack which creates a ⁠ Piercing damage explosion in addition to dealing normal weapon damage. Description Shoot a volley of thorns. The thorns deal weapon damage to the target and then explode. The explosion deals an additional 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage to the target and surrounding creatures. On miss, the thorns still explode. On save, targets still take half damage from the explosion. Properties Cost Action + Bonus Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Damage: 1~10 Normal weapon damage + 1d10 ⁠ Piercing ( Dexterity Saving Throw to halve) Details Attack Roll (On Miss: Thorns still explode.) DEX Save (On Save: Targets still take half damage from the explosion.) Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 2 m (7 ft) Radius At higher levels When the spell is cast at 2nd Level or higher, the addition AoE damage increases by 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing for each spell slot level above 1st. Technical details UID Projectile_HailOfThorns Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Ranger Granted by items: Gloves of Hail of Thorns ( Recharge: Short rest ) Notes There are two rolls involved with this spell: An Attack Roll to determine if the weapon damage applies to the main target and a Dexterity Saving Throw to determine if the explosion damage is halved. The hit chance shown in the preview when targeting the spell is for the saving throw rather than the attack roll. Despite involving an attack roll and weapon damage, Hail of Thorns does not count as a weapon attack for many interactions, most notably Extra Attack . Bugs Since the primary roll of this ability is not a weapon attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include: Arcane Synergy Gloves of Archery Hunter's Mark Sharpshooter: All In Titanstring Bow If the target fails the initial saving throw, the attack roll always succeeds. ## Harm
- **来源**: [Harm](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Harm)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Harm is a level 6 necromancy spell . It allows spellcasters to greatly enfeeble an enemy. Description Reduce a target's maximum Hit Points , but never below 1. Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Damage: 14~84 14d6 ⁠ Necrotic Details CON Save (On Save: Target still takes half damage, but its maximum hit points are not reduced.) Range: 18 m (60 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Harm Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Harm Harm Duration: Until Long rest CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Affected entity's maximum Hit Points have been reduced by the damage inflicted by the Harm spell This condition is a Disease How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Cleric Bugs On a failed saving throw, Harm reduces the target's maximum hit points by 14d6 but does not actually inflict any ⁠ Necrotic damage. This means that it does not trigger damage riders or other effects which require a damage source. Further, the effective damage dealt (through the reduction in maximum hit points) is reduced by the amount of hit points the target was already missing, potentially to zero . On a successful saving throw, Harm deals 14d6 / 2 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage as expected. Creatures immune to disease receive no damage if they fail their save, but still take half damage if they succeed. ## Haste
- **来源**: [Haste](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Haste)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Haste is a level 3 transmutation spell . It allows spellcasters to allow their allies to become Hastened . Description Target yourself or an ally to become Hastened . The creature has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed is doubled, and can take one additional Action per turn. When the condition ends, the creature becomes Lethargic . Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Details Range: 9 m (30 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Haste Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell Condition: Hastened Hastened Duration: 10 turns Creature has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. When the condition ends, the creature becomes Lethargic . Condition: Lethargic Lethargic Duration: 1 turn Consumed by exhaustion in the aftermath of Haste . Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions . How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Sorcerer , Wizard , Circle of the Land (Arctic or Grassland), and Warlock (via Pact of the Tome once per long rest) Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 9: Oath of Vengeance Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by items: Darkfire Shortbow ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 3 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Haste to their spellbooks. Notes If a creature casts Haste on themselves and then casts another Concentration spell, they immediately gain the Lethargic condition and the new spell ends, resulting in the loss of the spell slot or scroll used. Casting Haste on an already Hastened creature immediately ends their turn, as they become Lethargic, but the duration of Haste on the creature is refreshed. If the caster and the target are on the same turn in initiative, this can be used to "chain" casts of Haste on a creature while delaying the negative effects of Lethargic by casting Haste on the creature after they finish their turn, but before actually pressing "End Turn". Gontr Mael grants Celestial Haste , a variant of this spell which only lasts 5 turns but does not trigger Lethargic when it ends. Recharge: Long rest While the description of Haste states that it doubles the target's movement speed, it only adds 9 m (30 ft) to their total. The granted extra Action is significantly stronger than the one given by the D&D 5e version of the spell; in the tabletop game, that Action can instead only be used to take the Dash , Disengage , or Use an Object actions, or to make a single weapon attack. Honour mode largely returns the granted extra Action to tabletop functionality. The incantation for Haste is Provolo , Latin for "Fly forth" or "Rush out". Visuals Play Video Local File https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Haste_Visuals.mp4 External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Haste on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

Heal is a level 6 evocation spell . It allows spellcasters to substantially heal a target by recovering Hit Points and removing Blindness and Diseases . Description Heals a target's wounds and remove Blindness and any diseases. No effect on undead and constructs . Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Healing: 70 70 ⁠ Healing Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Heal Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsMelee , IsSpell How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Cleric and Druid Notes Range of spell changed from ⁠1.5 m (5 ft) to ⁠18 m (60 ft), similar to DnD 5e, as of Patch 5 If this spell is cast on The Dark Urge while they are in the Lower City , Lower City Sewers , or the Undercity Ruins , it unlocks a unique memory flashback. A childhood recollection plays if Heal is cast before the Urge confronts Orin , while one of two other variations triggers after her defeat, depending on whether the Urge accepts or rejects Bhaal . ## Heat Metal
- **来源**: [Heat Metal](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Heat_Metal)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Heat Metal is a level 2 transmutation spell . It allows spellcasters to heat up a metal weapon or armour on the targeted creature, forcing them to let go or receive damage or suffer various penalties. Description Cause a metal weapon or armour to glow red-hot and force the wearer to let go or receive Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks . If the creature is only wearing metal armour, it always receives Disadvantage. If the creature is still touching the metal, you can use a bonus action on subsequent turns to deal another 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire and force the creature to let go or receive Disadvantage. Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Fire Details CON Save (On Save: Target takes full damage, but suffers Disadvantage on attack rolls instead of being disarmed) Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Upcasting : Casting this spell at a higher level deals an extra 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage for each spell slot level above 2nd. Technical details UID Target_HeatMetal Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Grants: Reapply Heat Metal Condition: Weapon Dropped! Weapon Dropped! CON Save ( Spell save DC ) An enemy has made you drop your weapon to the ground, similar to Disarmed . Condition: Heat Metal: Disadvantage Heat Metal: Disadvantage Duration: 1 turn Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks until the start of the caster's next Turn. Condition: Heat Metal Heat Metal Duration: 10 turns Heats up a metal weapon or armour on a creature with no save (weapon is automatically prioritized). Metal weapons are dropped if the creature holding it fails their initial Saving Throw . If the creature is touching the heated metal item, they receive Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks . Each subsequent turn, if the creature is still touching the metal, the spellcaster can use Reapply Heat Metal to deal another 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage, forcing the creature to pass a Saving Throw again or drop the item (if it is a metal weapon). How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Bard and Druid Used by creatures: Magma Mephit Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Scroll of Heat Metal has been entirely removed from the game. Notes The bonus action cast provided by the Heat Metal condition receives the same upcasting damage bonus as the main cast. The bonus action recast is not available until the caster's next turn. Having resistance or immunity to fire does not prevent the weapon disarm effect. Reapply Heat Metal is a "granted" spell, or one that can be recast . Granted spells are issued to the caster after casting the original, and can be cast again without spending another spell slot as long as Concentration is not broken. Granted spells such as this are not directly tied to the casters' repertoire of known spells (i.e., their spellbook icon in the game). Therefore, if a granted spell is cast when multiclassing, subsequent recasts (in this case, Reapply Heat Metal ) use the spellcasting modifier of the most recently acquired spellcasting class rather than the spellcasting modifier that was used for the initial casting of Heat Metal. In this case, it may result in an unexpectedly low spell save DC. Bugs Due to a coding error, the condition which provides Disadvantage to the target (applied after a successful saving throw) is removed if another unrelated condition is removed from the target. This particular bug only affects the level 2 version of this spell. Due to a coding error, the condition which provides Disadvantage to the target is not automatically removed if the Heat Metal spell is ended early. This particular bug affects all levels of this spell. Heat Metal cast at level 4 deals only 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire , and its tooltip does not display the damage which Reapply Heat Metal deals. It additionally lacks several other functors found in other levels of this spell. Reapply Heat Metal cast at level 4 correctly deals 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire . Reapply Heat Metal cast at levels 5 and 6 incorrectly displays its tooltip damage as the level 3 version. External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Heat metal on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Hellflame Cleave
- **来源**: [Hellflame Cleave](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hellflame_Cleave)
- **分类**: Spells、Cantrips、Actions

Hellflame Cleave is a cantrip . It is a unique attack granted by the Hellfire Greataxe which cleaves through an area, covering it with deadly hellfire. Description Spew hellish flames and strike your foes. Hellfire ignores resistance and immunity to ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. Properties Cost Action Damage: 2~12 Normal weapon damage + 2d6 ⁠ Fire Details DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Targets still take half damage.) AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Cone Creates Area: Hellfire Recharge: Short rest Technical details UID Zone_MAG_Automaton_Human_Steelwatcher_HellfireCleave Spell flags CanAreaDamageEvade , HasSomaticComponent , IsDefaultWeaponAction , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Roiling Hellfire Roiling Hellfire Duration: 1 turn Flames from the heart of Avernus engulf this entity, inflicting 6d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Area: Hellfire Hellfire Duration: 2 turns AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Cone Deals 6d6 Fire damage per turn that ignores Resistances and Immunities . Type: Surface Condition: Roiling Hellfire Roiling Hellfire Duration: Whilst on surface Flames from the heart of Avernus engulf this entity, inflicting 6d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. How to learn Granted by items: Hellfire Greataxe Notes This weapon action does not count as an attack for the purposes of Extra Attack and requires a full Action to use. Instead, this is actually classified as a cantrip which results in some unexpected interactions. It can be Counterspelled . A sorcerer can apply Metamagic to it. The applicable options are Careful Spell , Extended Spell , Heightened Spell , Subtle Spell , and perhaps most importantly, Quickened Spell . It benefits from spell and cantrip specific damage bonuses like Elemental Affinity: Damage and Necklace of Elemental Augmentation . It activates Eldritch Knight's War Magic . It can still be cast while Silenced . It cannot be cast while Raging . The Roiling Hellfire condition is applied by both the weapon action itself and the Hellfire surface it creates. Even if a target saves against the attack, it will still be inflicted with Roiling Hellfire cause by the surface. Bugs Despite the tooltip saying that Hellfire ignores resistances and immunities, it does not. Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include: Arcane Synergy Great Weapon Master: All In Hunter's Mark Prepare Wrath Visuals Play Video Local File https://bg3.wiki/wiki/File:Hellflame_Cleave_Action.mp4

## Heroes' Feast
- **来源**: [Heroes' Feast](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Heroes'_Feast)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Heroes' Feast is a level 6 conjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to summon a bountiful smorgasbord to bolster themselves and their allies and strengthen their resolve. Description You and everyone around can't be Poisoned , Diseased , or Frightened (status group) . Everyone's maximum Hit Points increases by 12, and they make Wisdom Saving Throws with Advantage . Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Details Range: Self AoE: 18 m (60 ft) Radius At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_HeroesFeast Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell , UnavailableInDialogs Condition: Thoroughly Stuffed Thoroughly Stuffed Duration: Until Long rest Immune to Diseased , Poisoned , and Frightened All Wisdom Saving Throws are made with Advantage Maximum Hit Points are increased by 12 How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Cleric and Druid Notes Creates a temporary Feast Supplies container for 10 turns that contains 46-58 Camp Supplies and 1 bottle of Water . These items drop on the floor when the container expires. The buff from this spell disappears if the caster unprepares the spell. Heroes' Feast buffs all party members within range and line of sight, including familiars and summons, meaning that Heroes' Feast should generally be cast after any summons. The 12 HP from Heroes' Feast stacks with the bonus HP from Aid . While this spell does not make affected creatures immune to ⁠ Poison damage in general, Cloudkill deals its damage through the Cloudkill condition which falls under the poisoned condition type . Heroes' Feast does make creatures immune to this condition, and thus Cloudkill as a whole. The incantation for Heroes' Feast is Maior Et Fortior , Latin for "Bigger and stronger" . ## Hex
- **来源**: [Hex](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hex)
- **分类**: Spells、Bonus_actions

Hex is a level 1 enchantment spell . It allows spellcasters to curse a creature and deal additional Necrotic damage to them. The curse also imposes Disadvantage on a chosen ability check. Description Make your attacks deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage to the target and give it Disadvantage on an Ability of your choosing. If the target dies before the spell ends, you can Reapply Hex to a new creature without expending a Spell Slot . Properties Cost Bonus Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Necrotic (Per attack from caster) Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_Hex Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell Variants Hex (Strength) Hex (Dexterity) Hex (Constitution) Hex (Intelligence) Hex (Wisdom) Hex (Charisma) Condition: Reapply Hex Reapply Hex Can cast Hex without expending a new spell slot . How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Warlock Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Warlock Notes "Disadvantage on an Ability of your choosing" only applies to chosen Checks , not all rolls utilising that Ability : the target still rolls normally on Saving Throws and Attack Rolls . If the target dies or is knocked out before spell's duration ends, gain Reapply Hex . While in this state, a glowing shattered crystal appears above the caster's head. Hex damage can be applied multiple times to apply with multiple successful Attack Rolls , as long as the attack is made by the originating warlock caster . Example scenarios: A Warlock hits the target with a melee or ranged weapon attack: additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic . A Level 1 Warlock casts Eldritch Blast and hits the target: additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic . A Level 5 Warlock casts Eldritch Blast and hits the target with both rays: additional 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic , for hitting twice. A Level 3 Warlock casts Scorching Ray and hits the target with all three rays : additional 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic , for hitting three times. A Level 5 Warlock casts Scorching Ray and hits the target with all four rays : additional 4d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic , for hitting four times. Hex is only triggered by hitting the target with a successful Attack Roll , and not by other sources of damage. Example scenarios: A Warlock casts Magic Missile (which does not require an Attack Roll): no additional damage from Hex. A Warlock casts Fireball (which requires a Saving Throw , not an Attack Roll): no additional damage from Hex. Unlike the tabletop version, this spell lasts until the caster's concentration is broken. Hex has two incantations: Te Exsecro , Latin for "I curse you" , and Maledictus , Latin for "speak ill of / abuse" . Bugs If a creature has Hex applied, and lands a Critical Hit against the caster that triggers any "on hit / damage" abilities to damage the hexed creature, the damage of Hex is doubled along with the regular damage. For example, a Goblin Warlock casts Armour of Agathys on themselves, and then Hex on Lae'zel. Lae'zel then lands a Critical Hit on the Goblin Warlock, taking 5 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage from Armour of Agathys in the process. This triggers Hex to deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic to Lae'zel, which is then (erroneously) doubled to 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic due to the Critical Hit. ## Hold Monster
- **来源**: [Hold Monster](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hold_Monster)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Hold Monster is a level 5 enchantment spell . It allows spellcasters to Paralyse a creature, preventing them from acting and making them vulnerable to attacks. Description Paralyse a creature. It can't move , act , or react . Attacks from within 3 m (10 ft) are always critical hits . No effect on undead. Properties Cost Action + Level 5 Spell Slot Details WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Upcasting : Affects an additional target for each spell slot level above 5th. Technical details UID Target_HoldMonster Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Hold Monster Hold Monster Duration: 10 turns WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Affected entity can't Move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions . Attacks against the entity have Advantage . Attacks against the entity are always Critical Hits if the attacker is within 3 m (10 ft). Affected entity automatically fails all Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . At the end of each turn, the affected entity makes a Wisdom Saving Throw . On a successful save, the condition is removed. How to learn Classes: Class level 9: Bard , Sorcerer , Warlock , Wizard , and War Domain (Domain Spell) Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 5 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Hold Monster to their spellbooks. Bugs Upcast versions of this spell gain the ability to target multiple creatures, but as the spell lacks the SpellFlag IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities the same creature can be selected multiple times, requiring a saving throw for each time they are selected. Hunger of Hadar is a level 3 conjuration spell . It creates an area that deals damage and inflicts conditions to creatures in it, including reduced movement speed. Description Creatures within this black sphere are Blinded and take damage at the end of their turn and the start of their turn. Creatures starting their turn in the area take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage. Creatures ending their turn in the area possibly take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage. The area is Difficult Terrain . Properties Cost Action + Level 3 Spell Slot Damage: 4~24 2d6 ⁠ Cold + 2d6 ⁠ Acid ( Dexterity Saving Throw to negate) Details DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 6 m (20 ft) Radius Creates Area: Hunger of Hadar Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_HungerOfHadar Spell flags CannotTargetItems , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell Area: Hunger of Hadar Hunger of Hadar Duration: 10 turns AoE: 6 m (20 ft) Radius A sphere of cold blackness, teeming with unknown horrors. Creatures starting their turn in the area take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage. Creatures ending their turn in the area possibly take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage. The area is Difficult Terrain and creatures within are Blinded . Type: Summoned Condition: Hunger of Hadar (Aura) Hunger of Hadar A sphere of cold blackness, teeming with unknown horrors. Creatures starting their turn in the area take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold . Creatures ending their turn in the area possibly take 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Acid . The area is Difficult Terrain , and creatures within are Blinded . How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Warlock Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by items: Markoheshkir ( Recharge: Short rest ) Notes The spell's cold damage appears to be not dealt by the caster, but the created environment instead. As a result, it does not trigger Winter's Clutches' Encrusted with Frost effect. The incantation for Hunger of Hadar is Ira Et Dolor , Latin for "Anger and pain" . Bugs The spell mistakenly uses a fixed DC 12 Spell Save instead of the caster's, although this only affects the 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage, as the rest of the spell's effects do not require a saving throw. When upcast to Level 4 Spell Slot , no sound effect plays when cast upon an enemy. External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Hunger of Hadar on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
## Hunter's Mark
- **来源**: [Hunter's Mark](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Hunter's_Mark)
- **分类**: Spells、Bonus_actions

Hunter's Mark is a level 1 divination spell . It allows spellcasters to mark a creature as their prey and deal additional ⁠ Weapon damage to the targeted creature. Description Mark a creature as your quarry to deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Weapon damage whenever you hit it with a weapon attack. If the target dies before the spell ends, you can use Reapply Hunter's Mark to mark a new creature. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Weapon (Per weapon attack) Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_HuntersMark Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Grants: Reapply Hunter's Mark Condition: Hunter's Mark Quarry Hunter's Mark Quarry Duration: Until Long rest Affected entity suffers an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Weapon damage if the spellcaster hits it with a weapon attack. Condition: Hunt Completed Hunt Completed Can use a bonus action to reapply Hunter's Mark to another target. How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Ranger Class level 3: Oath of Vengeance Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by items: Grymskull Helm ( Recharge: Long rest ) Hunting Shortbow ( Recharge: Long rest ) Used by creatures: Charismatic Sentinel , Gandrel , Dominica Arsetz , Drar , Ellyka , Fuffi Fuffers , Geraldus , Grundril , Holvik , Kaldani , Lord Shattershield's Attendant , Manus , Murmath , Old Flake-Eyes , Rahir , and Trynn Notes Beast companions for Beast Masters and Gathered Swarm for Swarmkeepers both have a passive feature, Prey's Scent and Prey's Scent (Swarmkeeper) respectively, which causes this spell to improve their damage as well when their Ranger casts it. Otherwise, only the caster benefits from the extra weapon damage. The damage provided by this spell functions more like Sneak Attack than spell damage; as such, it does not provoke effects that activate on spell damage such as The Spellsparkler . Unlike in Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition, unarmed attacks in Baldur's Gate 3 are not counted as "weapon attacks" and do not benefit from Hunter's Mark. The Latin incantations for Hunter's Mark are Es Praedae Mei ( "You are my prey" ) and Mors Certa ( "Certain death" ). ## Invisibility (Duergar)
- **来源**: [Invisibility (Duergar)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Invisibility_(Duergar))
- **分类**: Spells、Cantrips、Actions

See also: Invisibility (disambiguation) Duergar Invisibility is a cantrip . This spell allows users to turn themselves Invisible to the naked eye. Description Become Invisible. Properties Cost Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Per combat Concentration Condition: Invisible Invisible Duration: Until Long rest Has Advantage on Attack Rolls and imposes Disadvantage on enemy Attack Rolls. Invisibility ends early if the invisible entity attacks, casts another spell, interacts with an object, becomes wet, takes an action or bonus action, or is damaged. How to learn Races: Character level 5: Duergar ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Notes This Duergar racial spell counts as a cantrip, but does not fall under any school of magic. This means it interacts with some cantrip-related features like War Magic , but not school-specific features like Illusion Quickening . Although limited to one casting in combat, this version of invisibility can otherwise be cast as often as desired outside of combat. Aside from duration, this racial version functions exactly like the Level 2 Invisibility spell. Refer to Invisibility notes for details. Given its recastability and unlimited duration, this cantrip version is arguably much more powerful than the standard invisibility spell. The only drawback of this version is that the caster may only apply it on themselves. Only Greater Invisibility offers any stealth checks to maintain invisibility when it might otherwise break.

## Karsus' Compulsion
- **来源**: [Karsus' Compulsion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Karsus'_Compulsion)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Karsus' Compulsion is a level 9 enchantment spell . It is granted by the Triune Netherstone and is usable only by Full-Illithids to control the Crown of Karsus . Description Channel the stones' magic to control the Crown of Karsus and dominate the Netherbrain . The caster must channel this spell until their next turn for it to take effect. Ends if caster is Incapacitated , Stunned , Polymorphed , or Knocked Out . Properties Cost Action Details Range: 6 m (20 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_END_Mindflayer_CrownDomination Spell flags IsHarmful , IsSpell , Temporary , Wildshape Condition: Channelling Karsus' Compulsion Channelling Karsus' Compulsion Duration: Until Long rest Affected entity is focussing all their magic and effort on casting Karsus' Compulsion until their next turn. Becoming Incapacitated , Stunned , Polymorphed , or Knocked Out ends the spell. Condition: Chains of Karsus Chains of Karsus The Netherbrain is too powerful for even the Momentary God's magic - Karsus' Compulsion could not dominate it completely. The spell has instead bound the brain's will in place temporarily. To complete the domination, you must strike it down. How to learn Granted by items: Triune Netherstone Notes Granted by holding the Triune Netherstone . This spell may only be cast by a Mind Flayer . This is one of only four 9th Level spells featured in Baldur's Gate 3. The other three are: Wish , cast by Vlaakith at the end of Creche Y'llek if the party doubts her power. Power Word Kill , learned by the Dark Urge after slaying Orin and accepting Bhaal's gift. A special variant is cast by Farslayer of Bhaal Ghislev in the Undercity Ruins . True Resurrection cast by Withers when requesting the return of a fallen companion or via the Scroll of True Resurrection . Unlike Wish , Power Word Kill, and True Resurrection, Karsus' Compulsion was created specifically for Baldur's Gate 3.

## Kereska's Favour
- **来源**: [Kereska's Favour](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Kereska's_Favour)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Kereska's Favour is a level 4 evocation spell . Granted by Markoheshkir , it allows its caster to imbue themselves with an element and unlock resistances and spells associated with it. Description Imbue yourself with elemental energy sourced from the draconic goddess, Kereska. Properties Cost Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Short rest At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_MAG_TheChromatic_ChromaticAttunement Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsLinkedSpellContainer , IsSpell , Wildshape Variants Bolts of Doom Bone-shaking Thunder Deadlier than Arsenic Flame of Wrath Frost of Dark Winter Sizzling Cataclysm How to learn Granted by items: Markoheshkir ( Recharge: Short rest ) Notes There is an associated variant of this spell for each elemental damage type. They boost their respective elemental damage by the wielder's proficiency bonus and grant two spells that can be cast once per short rest and do not use spell slots. The different variants are summarized below. Bolts of Doom Boosts ⁠ Lightning damage Spells generate Lightning Charges Grants Lightning Bolt (as level 3 spell) Grants Chain Lightning (as level 6 spell) Bone-shaking Thunder Boosts ⁠ Thunder damage Spells inflict Reverberation Grants Shatter (as level 5 spell) Grants Destructive Wave (as level 5 spell) Deadlier than Arsenic Boosts ⁠ Poison damage Spells inflict Poisoned Grants Ray of Sickness (as level 1 spell) Grants Cloudkill (as level 5 spell) Flame of Wrath Boosts ⁠ Fire damage Spells generate Heat Grants Fireball (as level 3 spell) Grants Wall of Fire (as level 4 spell) Frost of Dark Winter Boosts ⁠ Cold damage Spells inflict Frost Grants Ice Storm (as level 4 spell) Grants Cone of Cold (as level 5 spell) Sizzling Cataclysm Boosts ⁠ Acid damage Spells inflict Noxious Fumes Grants Melf's Acid Arrow (as level 2 spell) Grants Hunger of Hadar (as level 5 spell) [ 1 ] The conditions granted by these spells do not stack; after taking a short rest and casting a new variant, the old condition is replaced. The user must keep Markoheshkir equipped to keep the spell effects. Unequipping the staff also removes any active Kereska's Favour effect; this includes, for example, temporarily unequipping items when using Shapechanger . For the weapon property, see Light (weapon property) . Light is a cantrip (Evocation) . It makes an object shed light in a small area. Description Infuse an object with an aura of light. Only affects one target at a time. Properties Cost Action Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Technical details UID Target_Light Spell flags HasVerbalComponent , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Light Light Duration: Until Long rest This object has an aura of light with a radius of 7.5 m (25 ft). How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Bard , Cleric , Light Domain (Domain Spell), Sorcerer , and Wizard Class level 3: Arcane Archer , Arcane Trickster , and Eldritch Knight Races: Character level 1: High Elf and High Half-Elf ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Notes When cast on a non-ally creature, a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to the caster's spell save DC is rolled and the Light condition is applied if the creature fails this saving throw. As of Hotfix #25, this spell grants the full Until Long Rest condition duration only when cast on a character. Objects like scenery or gear items lit up while on the ground receive a 20 turn condition duration instead. When cast on a character, it applies the effect to their active weapon . Characters whose Armour Set Visibility setting is set to "Camp" only shed light if they are actively making an attack (since in this mode, the active weapon is not visible when stowed). However, the spell is still active and switching the setting back to Default causes the light to appear again. Light has two incantations: Fiat Lux , Latin for "let there be light" , and Sol Invictus , Latin for "unconquered sun" . Light cannot penetrate Darkness . ## Longstrider
- **来源**: [Longstrider](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Longstrider)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Longstrider is a level 1 transmutation spell . It allows spellcasters to make a creature move farther during a turn. Description Increase a creature's Movement Speed by 3 m (10 ft). Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Ritual At higher levels Upcasting : Affect an additional target for each spell slot level above 1st. Technical details UID Target_Longstrider Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IgnorePreviouslyPickedEntities , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Longstrider Longstrider Duration: Until Long rest Increase a creature's Movement Speed by 3 m (10 ft). How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Bard , Druid , and Wizard Class level 2: Ranger Class level 3: Arcane Trickster and Eldritch Knight Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Bard Magic Initiate: Druid Magic Initiate: Wizard Ritual Caster: Free Spells Granted by items: Blackguard's Greaves Boots of Persistence Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Scroll of Longstrider is unobtainable without third party tools. Notes As this is a ritual spell, it is free to cast outside of combat and persists on all recipients (even in not in the active party) until death or a Long Rest . As such, if having someone in the party who can cast this spell, it is advisable to have it active all party members at all times. If cast by a druid or wizard , this spell must remain prepared by the party member who cast it; removing it from the caster's Prepared Spells list immediately removes the buff from all party members whom the caster applied it to. This is the only ritual spell in Baldur's Gate 3 which has upcasting benefits; the game allows selecting a higher level spell slot when ritual casting this spell out of combat, though all this does is apply the effect to multiple targets in a single casting. The incantations for Longstrider are Properō , the Latin command "Hasten!" , Citium , Latin for "Quick" , and Ocior , for "Faster" .

## Lunar Bulwark
- **来源**: [Lunar Bulwark](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lunar_Bulwark)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Lunar Bulwark is a level 1 abjuration spell . It is granted by the Moon Devotion Robe , which allows the wearer cast the functional equivalent of Mage Armour on themselves once per long rest. [ See: Bugs ] Description Bathe yourself in the shielding magic of Selûne's watchful gaze. The target can't be wearing Armour . Properties Cost Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Long rest At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_MAG_Selunite_MageArmor Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell Condition: Mage Armour Mage Armour Duration: Until Long rest Base Armour Class is 13. How to learn Granted by items: Moon Devotion Robe Notes The normal base Armour Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier , while this spell changes it to 13 + Dexterity Modifier. The recipient still gets bonuses from other sources that do not change their base armour class such as +1 AC robes , Bracers of Defence , Shield of Faith , etc. Gloves and Helmets marked as Light , Medium or Heavy Armour count as armour, and will prevent Mage Armour from working. Mage Armour works while wearing a Shield . Mage Armour , Draconic Resilience , Unarmoured Defence (Barbarian) , Unarmoured Defence (Monk) and Barkskin all change one's base armour class and therefore do not stack. If one has multiple of these they will only get the benefit of the one which gives the most Armour Class . Mage Armour can work while in Wild Shape as long as one has no armour equipped in any slot before transforming. This effect only functions on forms with a base Armour Class lower than 13. Mage Armour does not count as wearing armour for things like Unarmoured Movement , Become the Bulwark and Defence . The incantation for Mage Armour is Mactē Virtutē , the Latin command "honour with virtue!" Bugs Although Selûne's Protection associated with the Moon Devotion Robe should be activated by Lunar Bulwark , it is not; the wearer must instead have the regular version of Mage Armour cast on them for its radiant damage to function.

## Mage Armour
- **来源**: [Mage Armour](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mage_Armour)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Mage Armour is a level 1 abjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to surround an unarmoured creature (including themselves, if unarmoured) with magical protection. Description Surround an unarmoured creature in a protective magical force. Its Armour Class increases to 13 + its Dexterity modifier . This effect does not stack with Unarmoured Defence . The target can't be wearing Armour . Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_MageArmor Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsMelee , IsSpell Condition: Mage Armour Mage Armour Duration: Until Long rest Base Armour Class is 13. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Sorcerer and Wizard Class level 3: Arcane Trickster and Eldritch Knight Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Sorcerer Magic Initiate: Wizard Granted by items: Moon Devotion Robe Other ways to learn: Also granted to Warlocks who choose the Eldritch Invocation Armour of Shadows at level 2+. This version of the spell only targets the caster, and does not expend a Spell Slot . Wizards can transcribe a Scroll of Mage Armour to their spellbooks. Notes This buff persists if the caster is removed from the active party, even if rejoining later. If cast by a wizard , this spell must remain prepared by the party member who cast it; removing Mage Armour from the caster's Prepared Spells list immediately removes the buff from all party members whom the caster applied it to. If applied by using a scroll directly, instead of transcribing it into a wizard's spellbook, then the caster need not keep the spell prepared to maintain the buff. If a party member who has Mage Armour equips a piece of Armour, the buff is removed. Mage Armour is not reapplied when unequipping that Armour; it must to be cast on them once more. The normal base Armour Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier ; this spell changes it to 13 + Dexterity modifier. The recipient still get bonuses from other sources that do not change their base armour class, such as +1 AC robes , Bracers of Defence , Shield of Faith , etc. Gloves and Helmets marked as Light , Medium or Heavy Armour count as armour, and prevent Mage Armour from working. Mage Armour works while a Shield is equipped. Mage Armour , Draconic Resilience , Unarmoured Defence (Barbarian) , Unarmoured Defence (Monk) and Barkskin all change base armour class and therefore do not stack. If the recipient has multiples of these they only get the benefit which provides the best Armour Class . Mage Armour works in Wild Shape as long as the user has no armour equipped before transforming. This effect only works on forms with a base Armour Class of less than 13. Mage Armour does not count as wearing armour for things like Unarmoured Movement , Become the Bulwark and Defence . The incantation for Mage Armour is Mactē Virtutē , Latin for "With great virtue" . ## Mage Hand
- **来源**: [Mage Hand](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mage_Hand)
- **分类**: Spells、Cantrips、Actions

Mage Hand is a cantrip (Conjuration) . It conjures a spectral hand that can interact with objects. Description Create a spectral hand that can manipulate and interact with objects. Properties Cost Action Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Short rest Technical details UID Target_MageHand Spell flags CannotTargetCharacter , CannotTargetItems , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell Creature: Mage Hand (creature) STR 10 DEX 10 CON 3 (-4) INT 2 (-4) WIS 1 (-5) CHA 1 (-5) Duration 10 turns Hit Points 3 Armour Class 5 Size Tiny Shove ( ) Try to push your target away. Your chances depend on your Athletics , and are higher if you're hidden or invisible. Throw ( ) Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Bard , Sorcerer , Warlock , and Wizard Class level 3: Arcane Trickster , Eldritch Knight , and Swarmkeeper Races: Character level 1: High Elf , High Half-Elf , and Mephistopheles Tiefling ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Bard Magic Initiate: Sorcerer Magic Initiate: Warlock Magic Initiate: Wizard Granted by items: Djinni Ring Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Notes This is the only cantrip with a limitation on how often it can be cast (once per short rest). This is somewhat in contradiction with the basic concept of cantrips. While Find Familiar can also only be cast once per short rest, it is a spell, not a cantrip. Githyanki and Arcane Tricksters can cast a special version of Mage Hand that is invisible. The Githyanki version is obtained via a racial ability called Githyanki Psionics: Mage Hand but can only be cast once per Long Rest . With the Mage Hand Legerdemain feature of Arcane Tricksters, the Hand is invisible and the summon duration is extended to be permanent (as shown above, it is normally 10 turns). Although this ability is generally restricted to a single use per short rest, an Arcane Trickster can gain a second casting by acquiring the Mage Hand cantrip through an external source, such as the Magic Initiate feat or by multiclassing into another spellcasting class. Any version of the cantrip cast by an Arcane Trickster benefits from Legerdemain enhancements, including permanency and invisibility. However, this redundancy can only be achieved once; the game's interface prevents selecting the same cantrip a third time through subsequent feats or classes. The specific order in which these versions are learned – whether from the subclass or the external source – does not change the outcome. Hr'a'cknir Bracers allow the wearer to cast Mage Hand as a Bonus Action . If the Hand throws a weapon marked as a Homing Weapon from the ground, the weapon is instantly equipped to the caster of the Hand upon its return, unequipping previous equipment. If the Hand throws a returning weapon from its own inventory, it is equipped to the Hand (except Comeback Handaxe, which returns to inventory). Mage hand can be used to effect in tandem with Spiked Bulbs and BOOOAL's Benediction to give Advantage in combat while not using valuable action resources of party members. Mage Hand has two incantations: Veni Et Iuva Me , Latin for "come and help me" , and Voco , Latin for "I call/summon" . Bugs Mage Hand has Opportunity Attack but cannot use it as it lacks a Reaction . External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Mage hand on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
## Magic Missile
- **来源**: [Magic Missile](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Magic_Missile)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Magic Missile is a level 1 evocation spell . It allows spellcasters to hit enemies with multiple projectiles that deal ⁠ Force damage. Description Create three darts of magical force, each dealing 1d4 + 1 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to its target. The darts always hit their target, and can each be targeted individually. Properties Cost Action + Level 1 Spell Slot Damage: 6~15 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Force + 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Force + 1d4 + 1 ⁠ Force Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) At higher levels Upcasting : Creates one additional dart per level also dealing 1d4 + 1 ⁠ ⁠ Force . Technical details UID Projectile_MagicMissile Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Sorcerer and Wizard Class level 3: Arcane Trickster and Eldritch Knight Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Sorcerer Magic Initiate: Wizard Granted by items: Psychic Spark ( Recharge: Long rest ) Ne'er Misser ( Recharge: Short rest ) Other ways to learn: Wizards can transcribe a Scroll of Magic Missile to their spellbooks. Notes Shield renders its recipient immune to Magic Missile. The level 10 Evocation School Wizard feature Empowered Evocation add the wizard's Intelligence modifier to each missile. Psychic Spark adds an extra dart to each Magic Missile cast (e.g. four total at spell level 1). Callous Glow Ring adds 2 points of Radiant damage to each missile if the target is illuminated. Coruscation Ring provided that the caster is illuminated, inflicts 2 rounds of Radiating Orb on the target for each missile. The Spellsparkler adds 2 Lightning Charges to the caster for each missile. When interacting with effects like Death Ward and dealing multiple missile attacks to the same creature, assuming the 1st attack was sufficient to down the creature with Death Ward active, the 2nd attack appears to apply before Death Ward activates. This means that after 2 missile attacks the creature loses Death Ward but remains with 1HP: If the initial attack has 3 missiles the creature is downed on the 2nd attack and again for an actual kill on the 3rd attack. In the case of party members with Death Ward applied, they need to receive 6 missile attacks to actually die: 2 to break down the ward, 1 to get downed and 3 more to fail 3 Death Saving Throws . This effect appears to apply to all multi-application attacks such Scorching Ray and Eldritch Blast (as of 4.1.1.3669438). The incantation for Magic Missile is Tormentum , Latin for "Catapult" , "Missile" , and "Torment" . - **分类**: Spells、Actions

For other versions of Mapped Terror, see Mapped Terror (disambiguation) . Mapped Terror: Betrayal is a level 4 illusion spell . This spell dominates a target and then frightens their ally with the inexorable terror of betrayal. It cannot be learned by party members. Description Exploit the target's mapped fear to Frighten it and Dominate one of its allies. Properties Cost Action + Level 4 Spell Slot Details WIS Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 18 m (60 ft) Radius Recharge: Per turn At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_LOW_HouseOfGrief_ExploitFear_Betrayal Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsEnemySpell , IsHarmful Condition: Frightened Frightened Duration: 2 turns WIS Save ( DC  16) Cannot move. Frightened entities also have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls . Condition: Dominated Dominated Duration: 2 turns WIS Save ( DC  16) Affected entity will follow and fight alongside the caster of this spell. Every time it takes damage, it may break the caster's control over it with a successful Wisdom Saving Throw . How to learn Used by creatures: Viconia DeVir Notes Cast by Viconia DeVir after using Castigate Heartform on a character who professed to fearing "Betrayal" during the Mapping of the Heart The spell targets one of the party members who did not undergo the mapping of the heart. On a failed save, they are Dominated . If the character who underwent the mapping is within 18 m (60 ft) of that party member, then they make the same save or become Frightened . This spell inflicts a special version of Dominated with a StackPriority of 2. This means that it overwrites any existing Dominated conditions. The target who makes a save against being Dominated still benefits from effects which grant advantage or disadvantage on saving throws against being Frightened, such as Countercharm .

Properties Cost Action Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Technical details UID Target_MinorIllusion Spell flags CannotTargetCharacter , CannotTargetItems , HasSomaticComponent , IgnoreSilence , Invisible , IsSpell , Stealth Creature: Cat (Minor Illusion) STR 0 (-5) DEX 0 (-5) CON 0 (-5) INT 0 (-5) WIS 0 (-5) CHA 0 (-5) Duration 10 Hit Points 1 Armour Class 10 Movement Speed 0 m (0 ft) How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Bard , Sorcerer , Warlock , and Wizard Class level 3: Eldritch Knight , Arcane Trickster , and Way of Shadow Races: Character level 1: High Elf and High Half-Elf ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Notes This cantrip does not require concentration . It does not break invisibility . It has significant utility throughout the entire game: It lasts 10 turns. Illusion School Wizards can cast Improved Minor Illusion as a Bonus Action that lasts 20 turns instead. Outside of combat, this cantrip causes most NPCs to walk towards the illusion and surround it. This can be particularly deadly as a preparation for a first-strike ambush (e.g. luring a number of potential targets into a small area, then hitting them with a Fireball ). During combat, it causes enemies to turn towards the illusion. The illusion activates traps if placed on top of them. If placed on top of a vent, the illusion prevents gas from coming out, just as if a physical item were placed there. If cast again before an existing version ends, observers will not move to investigate the new one. External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Minor illusion on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Moonbeam
- **来源**: [Moonbeam](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Moonbeam)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Moonbeam is a level 2 evocation spell . It allows spellcasters to call down a beam of moonlight which deals Radiant damage to any creature that enters the beam or starts its turn there. Description Call down a beam of light that damages any creatures that enters the beam or starts its turn in the light. You can use an Action to move the beam 18 m (60 ft). Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Damage: 2~20 2d10 ⁠ Radiant (Per turn) Details CON Save (On Save: Targets still take half damage.) Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 1 m (3 ft) Radius Creates Area: Moonbeam Concentration At higher levels Upcasting : When the spell is cast at 3rd level or higher, damage increases by 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant for each spell slot level above 2nd. Technical details UID Target_Moonbeam Spell flags CannotTargetItems , HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsSpell Grants: Move Moonbeam Area: Moonbeam Moonbeam Duration: 10 turns AoE: 1 m (3 ft) Radius Type: Summoned Condition: Moonbeam (Aura) Moonbeam CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Ghostly flames engulf any creature that enters this silvery light or starts its turn inside the light. They deal 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant . On a successful save, targets still take half damage. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Druid Class level 5: Oath of the Ancients (Oath Spell) Granted by items: Selûne's Spear of Night ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Scroll of Moonbeam has been entirely removed from the game. Notes The Moonbeam is considered a summoned entity, separate from the caster. This has the following implications: Casting Moonbeam or Move Moonbeam does not break Sanctuary , even if damage is successfully dealt. Radiant Retort targets the beam itself, leaving the caster unharmed; as the Moonbeam does not actually have hit points, it will not be damaged either. Passives like Radiating Orb Gloves and Radiating Shockwave are not triggered by Moonbeam. Since Patch 6, casting Moonbeam on a blighted area in the Shadow-Cursed Lands leads to the caster losing Concentration over the spell and dispelling it, but damage is still done. Move Moonbeam is a "granted" spell. Granted spells are issued to the caster after casting the original, and can be recast without spending another spell slot as long as Concentration is not broken. Granted spells such as this are not directly tied to the casters' repertoire of known spells (i.e., their spellbook icon in the game). Therefore, if a granted spell is cast when multiclassing, subsequent recasts (in this case, Move Moonbeam ) use the spellcasting modifier of the most recently acquired spellcasting class rather than the spellcasting modifier that was used for the initial casting of Moonbeam. In this case, it may result in an unexpectedly low spell save DC. The incantation for Moonbeam is Ex Textura , Latin for "From the weave" . Bugs Despite being an Evocation spell, Moonbeam does not interact with Sculpt Spells . External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Moonbeam on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Otto's Irresistible Dance
- **来源**: [Otto's Irresistible Dance](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Otto's_Irresistible_Dance)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Otto's Irresistible Dance is a level 6 enchantment spell . It allows spellcasters to force a creature to stay in place, inactive. Description Cause a creature to start dancing, making it unable to take Actions or Move . Its attackers have Advantage on Attack Rolls . The dancer has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws . Properties Cost Action + Level 6 Spell Slot Details WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 9 m (30 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_IrresistibleDance Spell flags CannotTargetItems , CannotTargetTerrain , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Otto's Irresistible Dance Otto's Irresistible Dance Duration: 10 turns Unable to take Actions or Move Attackers have Advantage on Attack Rolls Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Bard and Wizard Other ways to learn: Wizards with a Level 6 Spell Slot can transcribe a Scroll of Otto's Irresistible Dance to their spellbooks. Notes Unlike most other control spells, the target of Otto’s Irresistible Dance does not get to attempt a saving throw when the spell is first cast, meaning its turn is very likely to be wasted. Counterspell is one of the very few ways to prevent this from happening. Until Patch 4 the target of this spell did not get to attempt to make saving throws on subsequent turns, which made it an irresistible 10 round crowd control ability. This bug was fixed in Patch 4. Sorcerers cannot normally learn this spell; they may do so by multiclassing , choosing Wizard as their last class at level 12, and then transcribing a Scroll of Otto's Irresistible Dance . The incantation for Otto's Irresistible Dance is Obēdirē , the Latin command "Obey!" ## Pass Without Trace
- **来源**: [Pass Without Trace](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Pass_Without_Trace)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

For the equivalent Way of Shadow Monk action, see Shadow Arts: Pass Without Trace . Pass Without Trace is a level 2 abjuration spell . It allows spellcasters to grant themselves and nearby allies a bonus to Stealth Checks . Description Call forth a veil of shadow and silence that gives you and nearby allies a +10 bonus to Stealth Checks . Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Details Range: Self AoE: 9 m (30 ft) Radius Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Shout_PassWithoutTrace Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , Invisible , IsConcentration , IsSpell Condition: Pass Without Trace Aura Pass Without Trace Aura Duration: Until Long rest This entity and nearby allies have a +10 bonus to Stealth Checks . How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Druid , Trickery Domain (Domain Spell), and Circle of the Land (Grassland) Class level 5: Ranger Class level 6: College of Lore (via Magical Secrets ) Class level 10: Bard (via Magical Secrets ) Granted by items: Ring of Shadows ( Recharge: Long rest ) Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Notes This spell, especially in conjunction with Cat's Grace , is arguably one of the most useful available to characters focused on stealth. Until the Ring of Shadows becomes available, it may be advantageous for rogues and rogue-focused characters wanting to "go solo" to multi-class for the ability to cast this spell, since it: Gives the single highest bonus to stealth available in the game , bolstering its user's ability to skulk about for various purposes (e.g. moving with stealth , sneak attacking , and stealing from other creatures undetected). Is available early in Act One , at character level three (four, for multi-classed rogues). Remains in effect as long as the caster's concentration is unbroken. The incantation for Pass Without Trace is Evanesco , Latin for "I disappear/vanish" . External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Pass without trace on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Phantasmal Force
- **来源**: [Phantasmal Force](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Phantasmal_Force)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Phantasmal Force is a level 2 illusion spell . It allows spellcasters to flood a target creature's mind with an illusion of the last thing that attacked it, dealing 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage per turn, changing to the last type of damage inflicted upon the target. Description Deal damage to a creature each turn. At the start of its turn, it takes ⁠ Psychic damage. Each subsequent time it takes damage, the damage type of Phantasmal Force changes to match that damage type. Properties Cost Action + Level 2 Spell Slot Details INT Save Range: 18 m (60 ft) Concentration At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_PhantasmalForce Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsConcentration , IsHarmful , IsSpell Condition: Phantasmal Force Phantasmal Force Duration: 10 turns INT Save ( Spell save DC ) Haunted by an echo of the last thing that attacked them. Takes 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage each turn. When the target takes damage from another source, Phantasmal Force changes to that damage type. At the end of each turn, the target makes an Intelligence Saving Throw . On a success, the condition ends. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Bard , Sorcerer , Wizard , The Great Old One , and The Archfey Class level 7: Arcane Trickster Class level 8: Eldritch Knight Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Scroll of Phantasmal Force is unobtainable without third party tools. Notes The individual Phantasmal Force damage conditions all share the same StackID with each other, meaning only one may be active on a character at a time. Due to the way the passive is written, this causes a priority effect where the conditions follow this order of priority (with the earlier conditions taking priority over later conditions): Slashing > Piercing > Bludgeoning > Acid > Thunder > Necrotic > Fire > Lightning > Cold > Psychic > Poison > Radiant > Force For example, if a character casts Ice Knife , which deals both Piercing and Cold damage, on a target that is affected by Phantasmal Force, the enemy will be left with Phantasmal Force: Piercing. ## Power Word Kill
- **来源**: [Power Word Kill](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Power_Word_Kill)
- **分类**: Spells、Actions

Power Word Kill is a level 9 enchantment spell . It kills an enemy, and can only be used once per campaign. Description Compel an enemy with 100 Hit Points or fewer to die instantly. Limited to one use only. Properties Cost Action Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) At higher levels Casting this spell at a higher level grants no additional benefit. Technical details UID Target_LOW_DarkUrge_PowerWordKill How to learn Other ways to learn: This spell can only be learned as the Dark Urge after slaying Orin and accepting Bhaal's gift. There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Notes After using this spell on a creature, it is removed from the player character's common actions and cannot be used again. The spell is not removed if it is cast on the caster themselves and the caster actually dies from it. The spell can be cast on two targets simultaneously through the use of Twinned Spell or Split Enchantment . Using either of these features to target the caster along with another creature allows the spell to be used repeatedly. Sarevok casts this on Dolor if the player character convinces Dolor to take up arms against the Murder Tribunal . ## Produce Flame
- **来源**: [Produce Flame](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Produce_Flame)
- **分类**: Spells、Cantrips、Actions

Produce Flame is a cantrip (Conjuration) . It creates a blue flame in the caster's palm which emanates light and can be thrown at enemies. Description A flame in your hand sheds a light in a 9 m (30 ft) radius and deals 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage when thrown. Throwing the flame immediately after you conjure it does not cost an Action . Extinguishing or throwing it on subsequent turns costs an action. The throw has a range of 9 m (30 ft). Properties Cost Action Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Fire Details Range: Self At higher levels At character level 5, the damage of the hurled flame increases to 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire . At character level 10, the damage of the hurled flame increases to 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire . Technical details UID Shout_ProduceFlame Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent , IsSpell Grants: Produce Flame: Hurl Produce Flame: Dismiss Condition: Produce Flame Produce Flame Duration: Until Long rest A flickering flame sheds light in a 9 m (30 ft) radius around the creature. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Cleric and Druid Races: Character level 1: Asmodeus Tiefling ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Granted by features: Magic Initiate: Cleric Magic Initiate: Druid Granted by items: Moon Devotion Robe Other ways to learn: There are no scrolls available for wizards to transcribe to their spellbooks. Notes Objects such as torches, campfires, and braziers ignite when taking fire damage; this spell provides an easy way to ignite them from a distance. On console, if you did not enter combat with the flame in hand, you can use the Hurl action by casting the spell from the radial menu, then selecting the spell a second time, bringing up a submenu, and selecting Hurl. If you were holding a flame at the start of combat, you may have to create a radial menu option to Hurl the flame. Highlight the radial space you would like to use, then consult the bottom right for the contextual button to "Set Slot". Produce Flame has two incantations: "Fiat Lux" , Latin for "let there be light", and "Sol Invictus" , Latin for "unconquered sun". Bugs The damage on the tooltip for Produce Flame is not marked correctly for the increases at level 5 and 10. The tooltip for the throwing action, Produce Flame: Hurl , is marked correctly, and the damage scales correctly. The version of this Cantrip granted to Asmodeus tieflings uses the character's Wisdom modifier to hurl the flame, rather than Charisma as stated in the Produce Flame: Hurl tooltip. External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Produce flame on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Produce Flame: Hurl
- **来源**: [Produce Flame: Hurl](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Produce_Flame:_Hurl)

Produce Flame: Hurl is a cantrip (Conjuration) . It throws the flame you conjured in your hand by Produce Flame at a target. Description Hurl the conjured flame in your hand at a target and let it sizzle out. Properties Cost Action Damage: 1~8 1d8 ⁠ Fire Details Attack Roll Range: 9 m (30 ft) At higher levels At character level 5, the damage increases to 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire . At character level 10, the damage increases to 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Fire . Technical details UID Projectile_ProduceFlame_Hurl Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , IsHarmful , IsSpell , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold , Temporary How to learn Granted by spells: Produce Flame Notes On the turn that Produce Flame is cast, this ability will not cost an action to use. Bugs The version of this cantrip granted by the Asmodeus tiefling subrace uses the character's Wisdom modifier to hurl the flame, rather than Charisma, like all other racial spells granted to tieflings. For clerics, the tooltip for Produce Flame does not correctly show the damage increases at levels 5 and 10. The tooltip for the throwing action, Produce Flame: Hurl, is marked correctly, and the damage scales correctly. Produce Flame: Hurl only remains available to a character for 99 turns, while Produce Flame: Dismiss remains available until long rest. After 10 minutes of in-game time, a character is only left with the ability to dismiss the flame and cannot hurl it.
