They start Bleeding , and the ensuing gush continuously heals your wounds. Properties Cost Action Damage: 2~20 2d10 ⁠ Slashing Healing: 2~12 2d6 ⁠ Healing (To self) Details CON Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Targets still takes half damage.) Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) At higher levels At Level 10, the damage is increased to 3d10 ⁠ Slashing and the healing is increased to 4d6 ⁠ Healing . Technical details UIDs Target_BloodBath_Slayer Base version Target_BloodBath_Slayer_10 Upgraded level 10 version Spell flags IsHarmful , IsMelee Condition: Bleeding Bleeding Duration: 3 turns CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Takes 2 ⁠ ⁠ Slashing DRS damage at the start of each turn and has Disadvantage on Constitution Saving Throws . Removed by healing. Condition: Revitalising Gore Revitalising Gore Duration: 3 turns CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Affected entity is drenched in its enemies' blood. It regains 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points per turn. At level 10, the healing is increased to 4d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points per turn. How to learn Used by creatures: Slayer Bugs The spell save DC of the Slayer's actions uses the spellcasting ability of the last class you took a first level in, but with the Slayer's ability scores. This results in a very low DC due to the Slayer's low mental ability scores. In particular, Fighters, Rogues, Wizards, Clerics, Druids, Monks, and Rangers have a +0 spellcasting modifier from Intelligence or Wisdom in Slayer form, while Barbarians, Bards, Paladins, Sorcerers, and Warlocks have a -1 spellcasting modifier from Charisma while in Slayer form.

## Symbiotic Entity
- **来源**: [Symbiotic Entity](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Symbiotic_Entity)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

Symbiotic Entity is a Circle of the Spores druid class action. Instead of transforming into a beast, these druids can spend a Wild Shape Charge to enter Symbiotic Entity form. In this form, they gain temporary hit points and deal additional ⁠ Necrotic damage with weapon or unarmed attacks and Halo of Spores . It is lost when the temporary hit points are depleted. Description Gain 4 temporary hit points per Druid level and deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage with weapon or unarmed attacks while you have them. Cast Halo of Spores with double damage. Symbiotic Entity ends early if you use Wild Shape . Can only have temporary hit points from one source. Properties Cost Action + Wild Shape Charge Details Range: Self Duration: Until Long rest At higher levels At level 10, Spreading Spores can be cast while in this form. Technical details UID Shout_SymbioticEntity Condition: Symbiotic Entity Symbiotic Entity Duration: Until Long rest Affected entity has gained 4 Temporary Hit Points per Druid level, its melee weapon or unarmed attacks deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage, and it deals double damage with Halo of Spores . [ See: Bugs ] Ends early if the entity uses Wild Shape . How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Circle of the Spores Notes Symbiotic Entity does not count as being wild shaped for the purposes of Wild Strike , so it does not grant extra attacks in this form. While active, other sources of temporary hit points (such as Vital Conduit Boots ) replenish missing Symbiotic Entity hit points, but cannot exceed its cap. Shapeshifter's Boon Ring is not triggered by Symbiotic Entity, and thus does not provide the bonus to ability checks. Bugs Despite the tooltip warning, the condition which grants the temporary hit points does not use the "TEMPORARY_HP" StackId and thus may be active on a character in addition to other sources of temporary hit points. In this case, the character will receive the temporary hit points from the highest source, while any lower sources will be used to replenish any lost temporary hit points from the highest source. Despite the tooltip saying this ability only affects melee weapon attacks, it affects ranged weapon attacks as well. ## Synaptic Consumption
- **来源**: [Synaptic Consumption](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Synaptic_Consumption)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

This article is about the upgraded full-illithid power. For the base partial-illithid version, see Absorb Intellect . Synaptic Consumption is an action and Illithid Power available to Full-Illithids . This action allows a full-illithid to heal over time by sapping a target's ability scores . Initially, the ability score reduction is -5 and the healing amount is 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points , but this effect grows more potent over 5 turns. On each subsequent turn, the target's ability scores are reduced by a further -1 and the healing amount increases by 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . On the fifth turn, the target is knocked prone. Description Devour your foe, lowering all of their Ability Scores initially by 5, and by 1 each subsequent turn. Additionally, you regain 2~20 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points per turn. This lasts for 5 turns, after which the target is left Prone Properties Cost Action Healing: 30~300 2d10 ⁠ Healing (On initial application) + 4d10 ⁠ Healing (After 1 turn) + 6d10 ⁠ Healing (After 2 turns) + 8d10 ⁠ Healing (After 3 turn) + 10d10 ⁠ Healing (After 4 turns) Details INT Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 9 m (30 ft) Duration: 5 turns Technical details UID Target_MF_AbsorbIntellect Spell flags CannotTargetItems , CannotTargetTerrain , DisableBlood , IsHarmful , Wildshape Condition: Absolute Consumption (Stage 1) Absolute Consumption Duration: 1 turn INT Save ( Spell save DC ) All of the creature's abilities are reduced by 5. When this effect ends, it drops Prone Regain 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points How to learn Used by creatures: Full-Illithid Notes This action is obtained automatically after becoming a full-illithid . The condition Absolute Consumption is lost and regained each round after an initial failed saving throw. Every turn of the effect, the ability score reduction increases by 1, starting as a -5 penalty on the first turn and ending as a -9 penalty on the final turn. Similar to Absorb Intellect , the healing amount increases by 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points each turn.

## Throw
- **来源**: [Throw](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Throw)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

Throw is a common Action which allows the user to throw certain Weapons , Consumables , environmental objects, and even other creatures. Description Throw a character or item from the world or your inventory. Your Strength affects how much weight you can throw. Heavier items deal more damage. The damage of weapons with the thrown property is the same as the weapon's melee damage. Properties Cost: Action Damage: Normal weapon damage Details: Attack Roll Range: 3-18 m (10-60 ft) The range depends on the weight of the object, see below. Range for picking up objects from the ground is AoE: 1 m (3 ft) Radius Damage: For weapons with the Thrown property, the damage and damage type are the same as the weapon's melee damage. For other objects and creatures, damage is determined by the weight [ 1 ] of the object being thrown: Light objects, under Weight: 10 kg (20 lb): 1 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage Medium objects, Weight: 10 kg (20 lb) - 50 kg / 100 lb: 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage Heavy objects, over Weight: 50 kg (100 lb): 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage If the thrown object or creature is over half the target's weight, the target is knocked back 2 m (7 ft). [ 1 ] If the thrown object or creature is heavier than the target, the target becomes Prone ( no saving throw). [ 1 ] A thrown creature always lands Prone ( no saving throw). Throwing a creature requires a successful Athletics check, using the same DC as when shoving a creature , except the check is not made at advantage when hidden. Range The range of the Throw attack depends on the object's weight in kilograms and the thrower's Strength ability, according to the following formula: [ 2 ] round ( 3 + 1 5 ⋅ 1 5 ⋅ Strength 2 − Weight 2 ⋅ Weight ) The formula's output is adjusted to 3 meters if it would have been lower and 18 meters if it would have been higher. Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. Notes Throw is an explicitly defined action with an exhaustive list of interactions in the game's code. Throw is its own type of action, separate from weapon attacks, even when used with Thrown weapons. Weapon actions are explicitly defined to work with weapon attacks, and so cannot be used with Throw. Another major consequence of this is that thrown weapons do not trigger most 'on-hit' passives, except for those mentioned below. In addition, thrown weapons do not apply any innate extra damage (e.g., the 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage from the Shining Staver-of-Skulls ) or any damage from coatings or dipping . The following interactions are explicitly coded to work with Throw: Slinging Shoes deal an additional 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage when thrown. Nyrulna deals 3d4 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage in a ⁠6 m (20 ft) blast when thrown. Lightning Jabber deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage when thrown. Boo can Blind a target that fails a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw when thrown, though the duration lasts for less than one full combat round; ending at the start of the blinded target's turn . Dwarven Thrower deals an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage when thrown by a dwarf , 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning if the target is Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. Creatures marked with Hunter's Mark take an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Weapon damage when hit by a thrown weapon. All variants of Elemental Cleaver infuse a weapon so that it deals an additional 1d6 of the chosen elemental damage type when thrown. Ring of Flinging and Gloves of Uninhibited Kushigo provide an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Weapon damage to all Throw attacks. Any boosts to weapon damage that do not check for melee or weapon attack rolls are applied to thrown weapon attacks. Examples include Rage , Caustic Band , Helldusk Gloves , Crusader's Mantle , etc. A creature can throw items and other creatures weighing up to 0 . 2 ⋅ STR 2 kg. [ 3 ] For example, with a Strength score of 18, the weight limit for Throw is 64.8 kg (129.6 lb). It requires a Strength of at least 20 to pick up a Medium humanoid (75 kg (150 lb)). Throw triggers Extra Attack and can be used without an Action after triggering Extra Attack. Berserker Barbarians have the improved throwing ability Enraged Throw . The Tavern Brawler feat significantly improves throwing damage. Thrown objects and creatures take falling damage (and can inflict crushing damage) if thrown from a sufficient height. Bound Weapons return to their wielder when thrown, but do not receive the Thrown property if they do not already have it. Throwing a homing weapon or Bound Weapon from a character's inventory causes them to equip it to their main hand without expending an action. Bugs A creature killed by a Thrown weapon on high ground may not grant experience upon their death if they do not die from the Throw attack itself, but instead from the crushing damage of the weapon falling; in this case, the game treats the killed target as if they were killed by a neutral entity rather than the attacker. Throwing a Burning object at a target sets the thrower on fire. However, this does not occur if the thrown object impacts only the ground. This also applies to thrown Torchs . Footnotes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 1.2 The weight of living creatures is not influenced by items equipped or inside their inventory; it is connected to their size , and can be seen by clicking "Examine -> Detailed Info" and looking under "Weight:" . ↑ The parameters are determined by ThrowDistanceMin , ThrowDistanceMax , ThrowWeightMultiplier , and ThrowStrengthCapMultiplier , defined in Public/Shared/Stats/Generated/Data/Data.txt . ↑ From the definition of CanImprovisedWeaponWeight() in Scripts/thoth/helpers/CommonConditions.khn .

## Transfuse Health
- **来源**: [Transfuse Health](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Transfuse_Health)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

Transfuse Health is an action and Illithid Power . This ability allows the character to heal a target by half the caster's current hit point value. Description Sacrifice half your remaining hit points to heal a target for the same amount. Properties Cost Action Details Range: 9 m (30 ft) Technical details UID Target_TAD_TransfuseHealth How to learn Used by creatures: Illithid , Partial-Illithid , and Full-Illithid Other ways to learn: Unlock from the illithid power skill tree with a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen Obtained automatically after becoming a Partial-Illithid Obtained automatically after becoming a Full-Illithid Notes Affects any entity (except Undead) — including party members, allies, enemies, and inanimate objects — so long as they have a hit point value. The damage dealt to oneself can break Concentration . Does not take into account Temporary Hit Points when calculating the heal amount, but it will deduct them when hurting the caster. For example, having a character with 50 Hit Points and 10 Temporary Hit Points use Transfuse Health on an ally will heal them for 25 Hit Points, and will damage the caster by 25, reducing their Hit Point value to 35. This skill is particularly noteworthy due to the fact that it is the only heal action in the game that can heal any entity (not Undead). There are some quests in the game (such as Lift the Shadow Curse ) where you are supposed to defend inanimate objects from an onslaught of enemies, and this skill can "heal" the object in question. This skill does not damage the user if used within a Globe of Invulnerability . Bugs Some damage riders such as Lightning Charges and radiant damage from the Callous Glow Ring increase the self-damage.

## Trumpet of Sparkles
- **来源**: [Trumpet of Sparkles](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Trumpet_of_Sparkles)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

Trumpet of Sparkles is a class action unique to Valeria that allows her to deal Radiant damage to bad creatures. Description Blast forth a cone of celestial sparkles. Evil creatures have Disadvantage on the Saving Throw , and Good creatures take no damage. [ See Notes ] Properties Cost Action Damage: 4~32 4d8 ⁠ Radiant Details CON Save ( DC  14) (On Save: Targets still take half damage.) AoE: 6 m (20 ft) Cone Targets: All non-allied creatures in the cone Technical details UID Zone_TrumpetOfSparkles_Hollyphant Spell flags HasVerbalComponent , IsEnemySpell , IsHarmful How to learn Used by creatures: Valeria Notes Baldur's Gate 3 has an extremely limited implementation of D&D alignments. For the purposes of this ability, a "good" creature is anything with the ALIGN_GOOD tag and an "evil" creature is anything with the ALIGN_EVIL tag. These tags are only set for clerics depending on their deities. Any other creature has no alignment. Evil creatures do not technically roll at disadvantage. Instead, they must make two separate saving throws: one at DC 14 and another at DC 19. If either saving throw fails, they suffer the full effects of the ability.

## Unarmed Strike
- **来源**: [Unarmed Strike](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unarmed_Strike)
- **分类**: Actions

Unarmed Strike is a common Action which allows the user to make an attack with their bare fists when no melee weapons are equipped. Description Hit a target with your bare fists. Properties Cost Action Damage: 1 + modifiers 1 + Strength modifier ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Unarmed Attack Roll Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Notes Tavern Brawler adds the attacker's Strength modifier to the attack roll and damage a second time. Monk's Martial Arts: Deft Strikes replaces the 1 base damage of an Unarmed Strike with 1d4. This increases to 1d6 at monk level 3 and 1d8 at monk level 9. Monk's Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks may replace the Strength modifier normally added to the damage of Unarmed Strikes with the Dexterity modifier if it is higher. In either case, the bonus damage from Tavern Brawler always uses the Strength modifier. Many buffs and features which specify that they apply to "weapon attacks", such as Divine Smite , do not apply to Unarmed Strikes. For a comprehensive list of effects that interact with Unarmed Strikes, see: List of features and items that interact with unarmed strikes . Bugs Items and features that add a damage roll to Unarmed Strikes without monk's Martial Arts: Deft Strikes cause the damage tooltip to display as 0d20 + Strength modifier + the additional bonus damage . The base Bludgeoning damage is still dealt correctly. Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Fists of Fury Kill a character with an Unarmed Strike.

## Unshackling Strike
- **来源**: [Unshackling Strike](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unshackling_Strike)
- **分类**: Actions

Unshackling Strike is a weapon action granted by Orphic Hammer . Description Smite the magical bonds keeping a creature Restrained , Paralyzed , and Stunned , freeing it. Properties Cost Action Details Melee Weapon Attack Roll Range: Normal weapon range Technical details UID Target_MAG_OrphicHammer_ChainBreaker Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , HasVerbalComponent How to learn Granted by items: Orphic Hammer Notes This is the only action in the game able to destroy the Infernal Crystals keeping Hope imprisoned. Unshackling Strike does not free Orpheus , instead, the Infernal Crystals ( not the Minor Orb of Domination) need to be struck with a regular attack while wielding the Orphic Hammer . Unshackling Strike uses a melee weapon attack roll, meaning that using it against a friendly character with high Armor Class is likely to result in a miss. The icon for this action is reminiscent of the Dispel Magic icons in Baldur's Gate 1 and 2, and it is in fact labelled Spell_Abjuration_DispelMagic within the game files. However, according to Swen Vincke, Dispel Magic was cut content for Baldur's Gate 3. He relates how Baldur's Gate 3 devs tried to make D&D's Dispel Magic work for a long time, but ultimately abandoned it: "it would've doubled the size of the game."

## Volley
- **来源**: [Volley](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Volley)
- **分类**: Actions

Volley is a Hunter ranger weapon action. This ability allows Hunters to attack every enemy in a large area with a ranged weapon rather than a single target. Description Fire a cascade of magical broadheads and bodkin arrows upon nearby foes. Properties Cost Action Damage Normal weapon damage Details Ranged Weapon Attack Roll Range: Normal weapon range AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Radius Targets: All non-allied creatures and objects Technical details UID Target_Volley Spell flags HasHighGroundRangeExtension , IsHarmful How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Hunter Notes During the beta the description was "Fire a cascade of arrows upon nearby enemies.". In release (Patch #2) the description for this skill was blank and in patch 8 it was finally updated to the current description. This is used essentially in place of a normal ranged attack. It cannot hit party members, but it can hit other friendly NPCs. Otherwise, there is no drawback to using this over a normal ranged attack. Some properties of items are applied to every creature which is hit but some are applied only to a single creature. There does not seem to be a simple rule which creature is affected if only a single creature is affected. It is not obvious which properties apply to every creature and which apply only to a single creature. Properties Cost Action + 2 Ki Points Damage: 3~30 3d10 ⁠ Bludgeoning Details DEX Save ( Weapon action DC ) (On Save: Target still takes half damage but no other effects) Range: 9 m (30 ft) At higher levels At level 9 with Improved Elemental Casting , the damage increases to 4d10 ⁠ Bludgeoning . Technical details UIDs Target_WaterWhip The normal version accessible through Way of the Four Elements Target_WaterWhip_Umberlee Version used by Allandra Grey that does not used Ki points or grant a bonus unarmed strike Spell flags DisableBlood , IsHarmful , IsLinkedSpellContainer Variants Water Whip: Knock Prone Water Whip: Pull Grants: Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Way of the Four Elements Notes Along with Fangs of the Fire Snake (which uses an unarmed attack roll), this is the only other Way of Four Elements abilities that scales with Strength or Dexterity rather than Wisdom. Since this uses weapon action DC, Heightened Manoeuvre from the Gauntlets of the Warmaster will apply. Conversely, bonuses to spell save DC such as Lay Bare Their Weakness from the Hat of Uninhibited Kushigo will not apply. Bugs The combat log will incorrectly show the DC calculation as the base DC + Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus, but the resulting DC will still be based on the higher of the character's Dexterity or Strength modifier.
## Water Whip: Knock Prone
- **来源**: [Water Whip: Knock Prone](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Water_Whip:_Knock_Prone)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

Water Whip: Knock Prone is a class action that allows a Way of the Four Elements monk to deal damage and knock a target prone. Description Use the water whip to knock the target Prone . Properties Cost Action + 2 Ki Points Damage: 3~30 3d10 ⁠ Bludgeoning Details DEX Save ( Weapon action DC ) Range: 9 m (30 ft) At higher levels At level 9 with Improved Elemental Casting , the damage increases to 4d10 ⁠ Bludgeoning . Technical details UID Target_WaterWhip_Prone Spell flags DisableBlood , IsHarmful Grants: Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike Condition: Prone Prone Duration: Until Long rest DEX Save ( Weapon action DC ) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn This spell is a variation of: Water Whip Notes This spell and Trip Attack (Ranged) are the only two sources of an indefinite prone effect. While an enemy can spend movement speed to end the Prone condition and get up, if it is prevented from moving (e.g. with Ensnared , Enwebbed , or Frightened ), it will remain prone indefinitely. Along with Fangs of the Fire Snake (which uses an unarmed attack roll), this is the only other Way of Four Elements abilities that scales with Strength or Dexterity rather than Wisdom. Since this uses weapon action DC, Heightened Manoeuvre from the Gauntlets of the Warmaster will apply. Conversely, bonuses to spell save DC such as Lay Bare Their Weakness from the Hat of Uninhibited Kushigo will not apply. Bugs The combat log will incorrectly show the DC calculation as the base DC + Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus, but the resulting DC will still be based on the higher of the character's Dexterity or Strength modifier.

## Weapon Bond
- **来源**: [Weapon Bond](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Weapon_Bond)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

Weapon Bond is an Eldritch Knight class action. This prevents the Fighter's main hand weapon from being disarmed and makes it automatically return to the Fighter when thrown. Description Ritually bind the weapon in your main hand. The weapon can't be knocked out of your hand, and it automatically returns to you when thrown . Properties Cost: Action Details: Range: Self Duration: Until Long rest Condition: Bound Weapon Bound Weapon Ritually bound to its wielder. The weapon cannot be knocked out of the wielder's hand, and automatically returns to its wielder when thrown . How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Eldritch Knight Notes This applies only to the weapon held in the caster's main hand. Only one weapon can be bound at a time. Attempting to bind another weapon causes the previous to be unbound. Works only with melee weapons. This effect is well-suited to thrown weapons given to characters who utilize the Tavern Brawler feat. Know that binding a weapon does not grant it the Thrown property if it does not already have it. Only weapons with the Thrown property do their full weapon damage, including any added elemental effects (such as from the Flawed Helldusk Gloves ); otherwise they only do basic damage of an Improvised Weapon based purely on their weight. Bugs Bound weapons thrown outside of combat do not return to their owner's hands. The Bound Weapon condition lacks the Attributed(InventoryBound) code that is otherwise found on Bind Pact Weapon and Bind Hexed Weapon . Although this was (apparently) done to allow a bound weapon to be Thrown , it also has the side effect of allowing an Eldritch Knight to give their bound weapon to any other character to use to the same effect. Thus, outside of a long rest , this condition persists even if: the caster is removed from the active party the caster respecs with Withers to another class the caster is dismissed back to the Fugue Plane For example: one can acquire a hireling, select the Eldritch Knight subclass at level 3, apply the bond to a weapon intended for another character, hand it back to them, then respec the hireling to a completely different class, remove them from the active party and / or dismiss them entirely. v t e Fighter Subclasses Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Fighting Styles Archery Defence Duelling Great Weapon Fighting Protection Two-Weapon Fighting Manoeuvres Commander's Strike Disarming Attack Distracting Strike Evasive Footwork Feinting Attack Goading Attack Manoeuvring Attack Menacing Attack Precision Attack Pushing Attack Rally Riposte Sweeping Attack Trip Attack Arcane Shots Banishing Arrow Beguiling Arrow Bursting Arrow Enfeebling Arrow Grasping Arrow Piercing Arrow Seeking Arrow Shadow Arrow Other class features Action Surge Curving Shot Eldritch Strike Extra Attack Improved Critical Hit Improved Extra Attack Improved Combat Superiority Indomitable Magic Arrow Remarkable Athlete: Jump Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency Second Wind War Magic Weapon Bond

This ability allows Hunters to attack every enemy around them with a melee attack rather than a single target. Description Strike out at all nearby foes, making separate Attack Rolls against each target. Properties Cost Action Damage Normal weapon damage Details Melee Weapon Attack Roll AoE: 2 m (7 ft) Radius Targets: All enemies and objects in the AoE Technical details UID Shout_Whirlwind Spell flags IsHarmful , IsMelee How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Hunter Notes Since this attack only hits enemies, it can safely be used in place of a normal melee attack without worrying about friendly fire. This differs from the ranged version of this attack, Volley , which can damage allies. The radius is 2 m (7 ft) while the corresponding ranged attack Volley has a radius of 3 m (10 ft). Extra Reach does not increase the radius of Whirlwind. Some properties of items are applied to every creature which is hit, but some are applied only to a single creature. There does not seem to be a simple rule which is hit if only a single creature is hit. It is not obvious which properties apply to every and which only to a single creature. ## Wild Shape
- **来源**: [Wild Shape](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wild_Shape)
- **分类**: Actions、Class_actions

See also: Combat Wild Shape , the Circle of the Moon Druid enhanced version with extra exclusive forms. Wild Shape is an action gained by Druids at Level 2 that allows them to magically transform into various creatures in order to fight in combat or explore the environment. Description Magically assume the shape of a beast. While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells . You take on the attributes of your beast form -- excluding your Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma scores. When your beast form drops to 0 hit points , you revert to your normal form. Properties Cost: Action  +  Wild Shape Charge Details: Grants access to the forms Wild Shape: Badger , Wild Shape: Cat , Wild Shape: Spider , and Wild Shape: Wolf . Grants access to the form Wild Shape: Bear for Circle of the Moon druids only. Your physical ability scores ( Strength , Dexterity , and Constitution ) become the ability scores of the creature while Wild Shaped. Your hit points and Armour Class also become that of the transformed creature. You retain the mental ability scores ( Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma ) of your original form. Your movement speed is based on your racial movement speed, but some shapes add a bonus. When you reach 0 hit points, you revert back to your original form (with the same hit points you had before Wild Shaping). If you take damage that reduces the Wild Shape form's hit points below 0, the remaining damage is applied to your original form. If the remaining damage is also enough to reduce your original form to 0 hit points, you die instantly, skipping the usual death saving throws. If you cast a Concentration spell before entering Wild Shape, entering Wild Shape does not end your concentration on it. You cannot cast spells while in Wild Shape, and furthermore cannot take any action outside of those available to your Wild Shape. Your equipped items are merged into your beast form and do not have any effect until you revert back. You retain your normal skill and saving throw proficiencies while Wild Shaped, but the total bonuses for Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution-based rolls are influenced by your new animal form ability scores. Your beast form has a fixed number of base hit points that increase every two levels that you advance in the druid class after unlocking each unique creature type. The hit point increase is calculated by a factor depending on the shape you are using: Sabre-Tooth, Panther: 1.15 Myrmidons, Rothe, Owlbear: 1.2 Bear, Badger, Spider: 1.3 Wolf: 1.4 Wild Shape Improvement - The damage dealt by beast form attacks gains additional damage on level 4 depending on the form used: 1d4 damage: Cat (Claws), Bear (Claws), Dire Raven (Beak, Rend Vision), Panther (Bite), Owlbear (Claws, Rupture, Crushing Flight) 1d6 damage: Badger (Bite, Claws), Spider (Bite), Wolf (Bite, Exposing Bite), Deep Rothé (Gore, Charge), Panther (Jugular Strike, Pounce), Sabre-Toothed Tiger (Bite, Jugular Strike, Shred Armour), Dilophosaurus (Bite, Pounce, Corrosive Spit) The damage die for all these attacks increases by one size (e.g., from 1d4 to 1d6) at level 8, and again at level 12. The DC of the special attacks of the Wild Shape forms is determined as follows: 8 + proficiency + WIS modifier. When shapeshifted, speaking to party members (active or inactive, including Hirelings ) in the world or in camp reverts you temporarily to your original form and resumes Wild Shape after conversation ends without expending Wild Shape Charge. This feature also works with Withers and Mizora . To start conversation with any other non-companion NPCs, the shapeshifted character must Dismiss Wild Shape and resume Wild Shape by expending additional Wild Shape Charge afterwards. Being shapeshifted into an animal-type form lets you understand other animals in the world freely, without using spells or potions, even though shapeshifting does not grant the player condition of Speak with Animals . This does not work with the Myrmidon forms from Circle of the Moon Druid's Combat Wild Shape . Many items, feats, and class features do not work while in Wild Shape. See List of features that work in Wild Shape for an extensive list of what does and does not work. At Higher Levels At 4th level grants access to the form Wild Shape: Deep Rothé . At 6th level grants access to the forms Wild Shape: Panther and Wild Shape: Owlbear . At 10th level grants access to the form Wild Shape: Dilophosaurus . Variants Wild Shape: Badger Wild Shape: Bear Wild Shape: Cat Wild Shape: Spider Wild Shape: Wolf Wild Shape: Dire Raven Wild Shape: Deep Rothé Wild Shape: Panther Wild Shape: Owlbear Wild Shape: Sabre-Toothed Tiger Wild Shape: Dilophosaurus Wild Shape: Air Myrmidon Wild Shape: Earth Myrmidon Wild Shape: Fire Myrmidon Wild Shape: Water Myrmidon How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Druid Notes For April Fools 2023, Larian Studios posted a tweet "announcing" a new Wild Shape for Druids: the Waterdhavian Cheese Wheel . Aberrant Shape was an Illithid Power Druid Bonus Action in Early Access that morphed the Druid into an Intellect Devourer . Based on unused icons in the game's files, there are several Wild Shape forms that were cut from the game before release. Notably, there are fully designed icons for rat, bat, and boar Wild Shapes. Rather perplexingly, there also exists a Wild Shape icon for Sights of the Seelie: Summon Deva . An unused spell description in the official Toolkit indicates there was a way to acquire the ability to Wild Shape into a Deva once per short rest. On PS5, a character in Wild Shape, when controlled, changes the light colour on the controller from Blue to Purple. Wild Shape actions which use a non-fixed DC for saving throws use the character's spellcasting ability modifier of the last class the character took a first level in. This may not be Wisdom if the character multiclassed from Druid to another class. Your owlbear shape has a starting health of 65 hit points that increases every two druid levels. Properties Cost: Action  +  Wild Shape Charge At Higher Levels The hit points and damage of the owlbear form increase with druid levels, as shown in the table below: Druid level Hit points Bonus damage Claws Crushing Flight Rupture 6 65 +1d4 +1d4 +1d4 8 78 +1d6 +1d6 +1d6 10 94 +1d6 +1d6 +1d6 12 112 +1d8 +1d8 +1d8 Condition: Wild Shape: Owlbear Wild Shape: Owlbear Wild shaped into an Owlbear Creature: Owlbear (wild shape) STR 20 (+5) DEX 12 (+1) CON 17 (+3) Hit Points 65 Armour Class 15 Movement Speed 12 m (40 ft) Size Large Claws ( ) Lash out with deadly claws and push the target back 1.5 m / 5 ft. Crushing Flight ( + ) Leap at a target to bite it and knock it   Prone . Dismiss Wild Shape Dismiss your Wild Shape and change back to your original form. Enrage ( + ) Give in to the owlbear's base instincts to increase your Strength and Constitution by 2, gain 12 temporary hit points , and possibly make nearby creatures Fearful . Lunar Mend ( + ) Expend spell slots to regain Hit Points while wild shaped. You regain 1d8 hit points per spell slot level. Rupture ( ) Rupture the earth, causing debris to tear through nearby objects and creatures. How to learn Classes: Class level 6: Druid This action is a variation of: Wild Shape Notes The owlbear gains 3 Rage Charges for Enrage . The owlbear loses all Rage Charges if the player character transforms back to normal for a cutscene or conversation. The owlbear uses Crushing Flight to jump by default, including in passive pathing (i.e., when following the main character). This can cause unexpected damage to nearby NPCs, turning them hostile. Thus, it is advised to turn back into Druid form in towns to prevent accidentally provoking the entire populace. Crushing Flight can be used deal large amounts of damage by crushing targets from great heights whilst Enlarged , see Owlbear from the top ropes tactic for an in-depth explanation. v t e Druid Subclasses Circle of the Land Circle of the Moon Circle of the Spores Circle of the Stars Wild Shapes Creatures Badger Bear Cat Spider Wolf Dire Raven Deep Rothé Panther Owlbear Sabre-Toothed Tiger Dilophosaurus Air Myrmidon Earth Myrmidon Fire Myrmidon Water Myrmidon Starry Forms Archer Chalice Dragon Lands Arctic Coast Desert Forest Grassland Mountain Swamp Underdark Other class features Cosmic Omen Fungal Infestation Halo of Spores Improved Wild Strike Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Lunar Mend Natural Recovery Nature's Ward Primal Strike Spells Spreading Spores Symbiotic Entity Twinkling Constellations Wild Strike

## Winter's Breath
- **来源**: [Winter's Breath](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Winter's_Breath)
- **分类**: Actions

Winter's Breath is an Action unique to the Water Elemental . Description Exhale a freezing torrent of ice. Burning creatures undergo rapid cooling and become Brittle . Has no effect on inanimate objects. Properties Cost Action Damage: 4~24 4d6 ⁠ Cold Details CON Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Targets still take half damage.) Range: Self AoE: 6 m (20 ft) Cone Creates Area: Ice Condition: Brittle Brittle Duration: 3 turns CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Affected entity has been rapidly cooled while aflame, making it Vulnerable to Thunder and Bludgeoning damage. Takes 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage at the start of their turn. Area: Ice Ice Duration: 2 turns Difficult terrain - movement speed is halved and creatures may fall Prone. Type: Surface Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn DEX Save ( Spell save DC ) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. Condition: Difficult Terrain Difficult Terrain Duration: Whilst on surface Movement Speed halved How to learn Used by creatures: Water Elemental Notes When the ice created by this attack melts, it leaves behind a water surface that lasts indefinitely. The spell save difficulty class for this action is Strength , which means a consistent way to increase spell save dc for the Conjure Elemental variant is to give them strength-altering potions such as the elixir of Hill Giant Strength or the elixir of Cloud Giant Strength.

Wolf Companion is a variant of Ranger's Companion which is a Subclass Feature of Rangers learned immediately upon choosing the Beast Master subclass. This ability allows the Beast Master to call upon their animal companion to fight and aid them in combat. Description Summon a wolf that can inflict devastating wounds and knock down enemies with its Lunging Bite . Properties Cost: Action Details: Range: 18 m (60 ft) Recharge: Short rest Lupus STR 12 (+1) DEX 15 (+2) CON 12 (+1) INT 3 (-4) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 6 (-2) Hit Points 11 Armour Class 13 Summon a Wolf that can inflict devastating wounds and knock enemies Prone. Bite ( ) Bite a target. Lunging Bite ( ) Lunge at a target to bite it and possibly knock it Prone . Pack Tactics When an ally is within 3 m (10 ft) of your target and is not Incapacitated , your Attack Rolls against the target have Advantage . Prey's Scent You deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Physical damage to creatures marked by your Ranger's Hunter's Mark . Your wolf companion has 11 Hit Points and 13 Armour Class . It is also proficient in Stealth and Perception . At Higher Levels Level 5 Lupus Major STR 12 (+1) DEX 15 (+2) CON 15 (+2) INT 3 (-4) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 6 (-2) Hit Points 31 Armour Class 16 Infectious Bite ( ) Bite a target and possibly turn it Septic . Companion's Bond Your Ranger's Companions receive a bonus to Armour Class and damage equal to its Proficiency Bonus . Your Wolf companion now has 31 Hit Points and 16 Armour Class . Its Constitution increases by 3 and its proficiency bonus increases from +0 to +3. Level 7 Exceptional Training Your summoned companions can now Dash , Disengage , and Help as a Bonus Action . Level 8 Your Wolf companion now has 61 Hit Points and 16 Armour Class . Level 11 Lupus Optumus STR 12 (+1) DEX 18 (+4) CON 15 (+2) INT 3 (-4) WIS 12 (+1) CHA 6 (-2) Hit Points 91 Armour Class 21 New Ability: Lupine Slash ( ) Strike nearby targets within 3 m / 10 ft using a spectral sword that appears between your jaws. Bestial Fury Grants all your companions an extra attack. Your Wolf companion now has 91 Hit Points and 21 Armour Class . Its Dexterity increases by 3 and its proficiency bonus increases to +4. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Beast Master This action is a variation of: Ranger's Companion Notes The summoned wolf companion derives its name from Latin: [ 1 ] Lupus – wolf Lupus Major – great wolf Lupus Optumus – best wolf Footnotes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Notably Major and Optumus are incompatible inflections. Optumus is an alternate form of optimus, the superlative of bonus, while Major is an alternative form of maior, the comparative degree of magnus. The correct sequence would have either been Lupus -> Lupus Maior/Major -> Lupus Maximus , or Lupus -> Lupus Melior -> Lupus Optumus/Optimus . v t e Ranger Subclasses Beast Master Gloom Stalker Hunter Swarmkeeper Favoured Enemy Bounty Hunter Keeper of the Veil Mage Breaker Ranger Knight Sanctified Stalker Natural Explorer Beast Tamer Urban Tracker Wasteland Wanderer ( Cold Fire Poison ) Other class features Bestial Fury Companion's Bond Dread Ambusher Melee Ranged Hide Escape the Horde Exceptional Training Extra Attack Gathered Swarm Cloud of Jellyfish Flurry of Moths Legion of Bees Hide in Plain Sight Hunter's Prey Colossus Slayer Giant Killer Horde Breaker Iron Mind Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Mighty Swarm Multiattack Defence Prey's Scent Spells Ranger's Companion Stalker's Flurry Steel Will Superior Darkvision Umbral Shroud Volley Whirlwind Attack Writhing Tide

All six "Ethels" obtain the condition Hag's Trickery . The location of the original Ethel is randomized. Auntie Ethel will lose all conditions other than Hag's Trickery when this action is used, to maintain the illusion. An illusory copy of Ethel disappears after a single instance of damage. The original Ethel will only lose Hag's Trickery . Any undamaged illusory copies will continue to exist after the original Ethel has been discovered.
## Bardic Inspiration (class action)
- **来源**: [Bardic Inspiration (class action)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bardic_Inspiration_(class_action))
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

This article is about the base bard class action. For other uses, see Bardic Inspiration (disambiguation) . For the unrelated gameplay mechanic that allows rerolling failed skill checks, see Inspiration . Bardic Inspiration is a Bard passive feature and class action. This ability allows a Bard to inspire their allies and influence the outcome of their rolls. At level 5 and onwards this feature is replaced with Improved Bardic Inspiration . Description Inspire an ally to go beyond their capabilities with your performance. They can add a +1d6 bonus to their next Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw . Properties Cost Bonus Action + Bardic Inspiration Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Targets: 1 ally that does not already have Bardic Inspiration At higher levels When the Bard reaches level 5, the bonus increases to +1d8. When the Bard reaches level 10, the bonus increases to +1d10. Technical details UID Target_BardicInspiration Spell flags HasVerbalComponent Condition: Bardic Inspiration Bardic Inspiration Duration: Until Long rest Can use Bardic Inspiration to add a +1d6 bonus to the next Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw . Bonus depends on originating Bard's level How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Bard Notes Helping Alfira play for the tiefling kids at the end of Act 2 allows the use of the unique Improved Bardic Inspiration class action once per long rest, costing only a bonus action. This functions similarly to Bardic Inspiration but uses a d12 and triggers via toggled passives, rather than reactions. Bugs When used to modify an attack roll with a +1d10 bonus, the Bardic Inspiration condition is not removed from the character. Bardic Inspiration may target a character who is already affected by the +1d10 version, wasting the effect as they do not stack. Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Blazer of Benevolence : When you inspire an ally using Bardic Inspiration, you gain 4 temporary hit points. Boots of Brilliance : Play your instrument to restore one of your Bardic Inspiration slots (Recharge: Long Rest). Cap of Curing : When you inspire an ally using Bardic Inspiration, they also regain 1d6 hit points. Wondrous Gloves : Your Armour Class increases by 1. In addition, if you have Bardic Inspiration, you gain 1 more use of it. v t e Bard Subclasses College of Glamour College of Lore College of Swords College of Valour Inspiration Bardic Inspiration Combat Inspiration Font of Inspiration Improved Bardic Inspiration Mantle of Inspiration Blade Flourish Defensive Flourish Melee Ranged Slashing Flourish Melee Ranged Mobile Flourish Melee Ranged Other class features Countercharm Cutting Words Expertise Extra Attack Jack of All Trades Magical Secrets Mantle of Majesty: Command Song of Rest Spells

## Boot of the Giants
- **来源**: [Boot of the Giants](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Boot_of_the_Giants)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Boot of the Giants is a Giant barbarian class action that allows them to send enemies flying with a swift kick. Description Try to kick a target away. Your chances depend on your Athletics , and are higher if you're hidden or invisible. You can kick a target up to twice the weight that Shoving them would allow. [ See Notes ] Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage Unarmed ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Technical details UID Target_BootOfTheGiants Spell flags AddFallDamageOnLand , CombatLogSetSingleLineRoll , IsHarmful , IsMelee How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Giant (barbarian subclass) Notes Like Shove , this ability involves a contested Athletics check. Refer to Shove roll for details on how this is calculated. This ability uses your unarmed damage and can be increased by anything that normally increases unarmed damage such as: Tavern Brawler will add your Strength modifier to the damage. Martial Arts: Deft Strikes will increase it to 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning when multiclassing into Monk . Gloves of Crushing and similar items will increase the damage. This ability cannot target enemies who are too heavy or immune to shoving such as Ethereal creatures. Thus, the kick cannot even be used to deal damage against such targets. As with shove, the maximum weight of a creature that can be moved is Strength score × Multiplier. For Boot of the Giants, this multiplier is 24 always. [ 1 ] For Shove, the multiplier is 12 normally, 5.1 when Reduced , and 28.2 when Enlarged . Properties Cost Bonus Action + 3 m (10 ft) Movement Speed Details STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 9 m (30 ft) AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Radius Recharge: Per turn Technical details UIDs Projectile_MAG_Barbarian_BrutalLeap Version available to players through Bonespike Boots Projectile_Jump_Minotaur NPC-only version Spell flags AddFallDamageOnLand , CannotTargetCharacter , CannotTargetItems , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , IgnoreVisionBlock , Invisible , IsJump , Stealth , Temporary Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 2 turns STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . ## Challenge to Duel
- **来源**: [Challenge to Duel](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Challenge_to_Duel)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

See also: Compelled Duel Challenge to Duel is a unique spell-like action which can be cast when wielding Duellist's Prerogative . It allows spellcasters to compel an enemy to only attack them. Description Challenge an enemy to attack only you, inflicting Bleeding on the target. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details WIS Save ( Weapon action DC ) Range: 9 m (30 ft) Technical details UID Target_MAG_Legendary_CompelledDuel Spell flags HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful Condition: Compelled to Duel Compelled to Duel Duration: 3 turns WIS Save ( Weapon action DC ) Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls against anyone but the caster. Might start Bleeding if struck by the Dueller. How to learn Granted by items: Duellist's Prerogative Notes This action itself does not inflict Bleeding . Instead, every time a target creature with Compelled to Duel is hit with the Duellist's Prerogative , the passive Elegant Duellist triggers a DC  15 Constitution Saving Throw to start bleeding. This saving throw roll is not shown in the combat log. Bugs Despite being listed as a level 1 Enchantment spell (inherited from parent spell Compelled Duel ), this action is not technically a spell (the IsSpell flag and concentration requirement from Compelled Duel has been removed). Thus, it does not interact with any spell-specific effects such as Vivacious Cloak or Split Enchantment . It also uses weapon action DC instead of spellcasting DC and hence benefits from Heightened Manoeuvre .

How to learn Used by creatures: Spiritual Weapon (maul) Notes The attack roll and damage for this attack uses the summoner's spellcasting modifier, but the DC to inflict the condition is based on the summoned weapon's weapon action DC (with an inherent +2 bonus). The once per short rest cooldown of this attack is reset when resummoning a spiritual weapon, so it is effectively once per summon instead. ## Crushing Flight
- **来源**: [Crushing Flight](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Crushing_Flight)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

This article is about the version of the ability used by NPC owlbears. For the version available in Wild Shape: Owlbear form, see Crushing Flight (Owlbear Wild Shape) . Crushing Flight is a class action used by Owlbear creatures which lets them leap at targets and potentially knock them prone. Description Leap at a target to bite it and knock it Prone . Properties Cost Bonus Action + 6 m (20 ft) Movement Speed Details STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 21 m (70 ft) Recharge: Per turn Technical details UID Projectile_Jump_Owlbear Spell flags CannotTargetCharacter , CannotTargetItems , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , IgnoreVisionBlock , IsJump , NoAOEDamageOnLand , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 2 turns Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Used by creatures: Owlbear and Shadow Plush Notes The spellcasting ability used for the DC of this ability is Intelligence . With the owlbear's Intelligence of 3, this provides a modifier of -4 to the DC. The owlbear does not take fall damage upon landing.
## Crushing Flight (Owlbear Wild Shape)
- **来源**: [Crushing Flight (Owlbear Wild Shape)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Crushing_Flight_(Owlbear_Wild_Shape))
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

This article is about the version of the ability available in Wild Shape: Owlbear form. For the version used by Owlbear NPCs, see Crushing Flight . Crushing Flight is a class action available in Wild Shape: Owlbear form. Owlbears use this ability to cover large swaths of ground while attacking opponents. Description Leap at a target to bite it and knock it Prone . Properties Cost Bonus Action + 6 m (20 ft) Movement Speed Damage: 2~16 2d8 ⁠ Bludgeoning Details STR Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Target takes reduced damage [ See: Bugs ] .) Range: 21 m (70 ft) AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Radius At higher levels At Level 4, this attack deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. At Level 8, this additional damage becomes 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning . At Level 12, this additional damage becomes 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning . Technical details UID Projectile_Jump_Owlbear_Wildshape_Lunge Spell flags CannotTargetItems , HasHighGroundRangeExtension , IgnoreVisionBlock , IsJump , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Used by creatures: Armoured Owlbear and Wild Shape: Owlbear Notes This action has two separate, overlapping components which can inflict Prone . Each has a separate Spell Save DC Strength Saving Throw so an enemy must succeed at both or get knocked prone. First is the prone effect built innately into the action which inflicts prone for just one turn. It will show in the combat log as "Saving Throw against Crushing Flight." A secondary explosion is created on landing ( Projectile_Jump_Knockdown_AOE ). it will inflict prone for two turns and show in the combat log as "Saving Throw against a blast from ..." The base range of the jump is 16 m (53 ft). It scales with Strength and benefits from the same modifiers as a normal Jump . With the owlbear's 20 Strength and no other modifiers, the range is 21 m (70 ft). The owlbear does not take fall damage upon landing. Additional damage will be added to the attack depending on the weight of the Owlbear and vertical distance travelled. This uses a similar damage calculation to Throw . Effects like Enlarge that increase weight will increase damage, as will falling from greater heights. Bugs Rather than taking half damage on save (which would be (2d8 + bonus damage)/2 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning ), targets instead take (1d8 + bonus damage)/2 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning which is closer to one quarter damage. This damage is always dealt as magical, regardless whether or not the attacker has Primal Strike .

## Curving Shot
- **来源**: [Curving Shot](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Curving_Shot)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions、Reactions

Curving Shot is an Arcane Archer fighter passive feature/reaction that allows the fighter to redirect a missed ranged weapon attack towards another nearby enemy. Description When you miss with any magical ranged attack, use a Bonus Action to attack the next closest target with the same attack. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Ranged Weapon Attack Roll Range: 18 m (60 ft) Targets: Closest enemy to initial target Recharge: Per turn How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Arcane Archer Notes Despite not stating such on any tooltip, Curving Shot is only usable once per turn due to it requiring and expending a hidden resource. It is not possible to choose the target of the redirected attack. It selects whichever enemy is closest to the original target. If there is not a clear path between the original and redirected targets, the projectile may collide with terrain and be wasted. This feature works with a hardcoded selection of special ranged weapon attacks [ 1 ] , including Arcane Shots. The full list is as follows: Normal ranged attacks, but not offhand attacks All Arcane Shots All magic arrows except Arrow of Many Targets , Arrow of Salving , and Arrow of Transposition . The basic ranged weapon actions Hamstring Shot , Piercing Shot , and Mobile Shot The College of Swords flourishes Defensive Flourish (Ranged) , Mobile Flourish (Ranged) , Slashing Flourish (Ranged) The ranger special attacks Horde Breaker (Ranged) and Dread Ambusher (Ranged) The spells Ensnaring Strike (Ranged) (when cast at levels 1, 2, or 3) and Branding Smite (when cast at level 2 or through Zariel tiefling 's racial ability) Sneak Attack (Ranged) The special weapon actions Bolt of Celestial Light and Illuminating Shot The inaccessible weapon actions Headcrack and Pin Down Any other attack action not listed does not work with Curving Shot. This includes offhand attacks, special weapon actions like Blinding Shot , and any Battlemaster combat manoeuvres (which can be acquired as an Arcane Archer with the Martial Adept feat). If all nearby enemies are incapacitated and the primary target is missed, Curving Shot does not trigger. This is because, SG_Incapacitated is excluded from the HasEnemyWithinRange() function check. This is not a bug, but a deliberate check. If at least one nearby enemy is not incapacitated and the primary target is missed, Curving Shot does trigger. ## Dip
- **来源**: [Dip](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dip)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Dip is a common bonus action that allows the user to dip their weapons into a surface , causing them to deal extra damage. Description Dip a weapon into a surface to alter the surface or enhance the weapon. If you are dual-wielding, you dip both weapons. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: 3 m (10 ft) Targets: Dippable surface or Burning object Technical details UID Target_Dip Spell flags Invisible , IsMelee , Stealth , TargetClosestEqualGroundSurface Condition: Dipped in Fire Dipped in Fire Duration: 3 turns Weapon deals additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. Condition: Coated in Toxin Coated in Toxin Duration: 10 turns Targets take 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage at the end of their next turn, unless they succeed a DC  11 Constitution Saving Throw . Condition: Coated in Serpent Venom Toxin Coated in Serpent Venom Toxin Duration: 10 turns Targets take 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage at the end of their next turn, unless they succeed a DC  13 Constitution Saving Throw . Condition: Coated in Wyvern Toxin Coated in Wyvern Toxin Duration: 10 turns Targets take 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage at the end of their next turn, unless they succeed a DC  15 Constitution Saving Throw . Condition: Coated in Purple Worm Toxin Coated in Purple Worm Toxin Duration: 10 turns Targets take 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage at the end of their next turn, unless they succeed a DC  19 Constitution Saving Throw . Notes The following surfaces allow dipping: Fire , Hellfire , or a Burning object or creature - Dipped in Fire for 3 turns Simple Toxin - Coated in Toxin for 10 turns Serpent Venom - Coated in Serpent Venom Toxin for 10 turns Wyvern Poison - Coated in Wyvern Toxin for 10 turns Purple Worm Poison - Coated in Purple Worm Toxin for 10 turns Water - Washes off existing coating Any other surface such as Electrified Water or Holy Fire are not dippable. Despite the tooltip description stating you can use the Dip ability to "alter the surface", this does not appear to be possible with any surfaces currently implemented. The effect of dipping is similar to Coatings and mutually exclusive with them. Some Coatings can be thrown on the ground to make a surface . This surface will persist between Long Rests Dipping your weapon in the surface will give the coating effect. Weapons can be dipped into any object with the Burning condition, including torches, candles, and burning party members. A character can carry burning objects such as torches, and drop them on the ground (which does not spend actions or bonus actions) just before dipping. Bugs Weapons can be dipped into a Flaming Sphere only if it was created by a non-upcasted Flaming Sphere spell.

## Dirty Trick: Sand Toss
- **来源**: [Dirty Trick: Sand Toss](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dirty_Trick:_Sand_Toss)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Dirty Trick: Sand Toss is a class action available to Swashbuckler rogues. Description Toss a handful of sand at your enemy and possibly Blind them. Gain Advantage on your next attack. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage: 1~6 1d6 ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Weapon Attack Roll CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Technical details UID Target_DirtyTrick_Blind Spell flags DisableBlood , IsHarmful , IsMelee Condition: Blinded Blinded Duration: 2 turns CON Save ( Spell save DC ) Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range of attacks and spells reduced to 3 m (10 ft). Attack Rolls against Blinded creatures have Advantage . Condition: Dirty Advantage Dirty Advantage Duration: 2 turns Gain Advantage on your next attack. How to learn Classes: Class level 4: Swashbuckler Notes The spell save DC for this action is calculated with Dexterity . Despite using a physical ability score, it does not use weapon action DC so it still benefits from anything that improves spell save DC . Unlike Dirty Trick: Flick o' the Wrist , Sand Toss does not require a Finesse weapon. The attack roll for this action uses the same ability modifier as the main hand weapon, such as dexterity for finesse weapons, strength for unarmed or standard weapons, and charisma for warlock pact weapons. Despite not dealing weapon damage, this action does trigger many melee on-hit passives (e.g. Hunter's Dagger or Nature's Snare ), but not weapon functors (such as Silence roll from Sussur Dagger or Blinded roll from Vision of the Absolute ). Bugs When used with a ranged weapon currently active, the attack roll uses the strength modifier. Since this action makes a melee weapon attack roll, it receives -5 penalty from Great Weapon Master: All In but its damage does not increase by 10 when wielding Two-Handed and Versatile (no shield) weapons. v t e Rogue Subclasses Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Cunning Action Dash Disengage Hide Sneak Attack Sneak Attack (Melee) Sneak Attack (Ranged) Rakish Sneak Attack (Melee) Rakish Sneak Attack (Ranged) Other class features Assassin's Alacrity Assassinate: Ambush Assassinate: Initiative Dirty Trick Flick o' the Wrist Sand Toss Vicious Mockery Expertise Evasion Fancy Footwork Fast Hands Infiltration Expertise Mage Hand Legerdemain Magical Ambush Panache Rakish Audacity Reliable Talent Second-Story Work Supreme Sneak Uncanny Dodge

Unlike Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike , this attack does not need to follow a normal weapon or unarmed attack. Description Punch twice in quick succession. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Ki Point Damage Unarmed ⁠ Bludgeoning + Unarmed ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Unarmed Attack Roll Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Technical details UID Target_FlurryOfBlows Spell flags DisableBlood , IsHarmful , IsMelee How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Monk Notes This attack is equivalent to two Unarmed Strikes and is affected by everything that applies to normal unarmed attacks such as Martial Arts: Deft Strikes , Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks , and Manifestation of Body . This attack does not trigger Extra Attack since it does not use an Action . Way of the Open Hand Monks can learn additional variants of Flurry of Blows with extra effects. ## Flurry of Blows: Stagger

- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Flurry of Blows: Stagger is a Way of the Open Hand monk class action. It is an enhanced variant of Flurry of Blows that will stagger the target, preventing it from using Reactions . Description Punch twice in quick succession and Stagger the target, making it unable to take Reactions . Properties Cost Bonus Action + Ki Point Damage Unarmed ⁠ Bludgeoning + Unarmed ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Unarmed Attack Roll Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Technical details UID Target_OpenHandTechnique_NoReactions Spell flags DisableBlood , IsHarmful , IsMelee Condition: Open Hand Technique: Staggered Open Hand Technique: Staggered Duration: 1 turn Took a powerful blow. Can't take Reactions . How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Way of the Open Hand Notes Open Hand Technique: Staggered prevents the target from spending Reactions , not from taking reactions entirely. This is important since many of the legendary actions given to bosses in Honour mode are reactions which do not cost a Reaction resource. This ability is similar to the Mobile: Evade Opportunity Attack feat since it disables a target's Opportunity Attack without a Saving Throw . This attack is equivalent to two Unarmed Strikes and is affected by everything that applies to normal unarmed attacks such as Martial Arts: Deft Strikes , Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks , and Manifestation of Body . This attack does not trigger Extra Attack since it does not use an Action . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. ## Frenzy
- **来源**: [Frenzy](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Frenzy)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Frenzy is a Berserker barbarian bonus action that is a variant of Rage . It turns the Berserker's anger into an uncontrollable fury and grants additional abilities in addition to those from Rage. Wearing Heavy Armour triggers the Rage Impeded condition, removing some benefits of Frenzy. Description Your Rage turns into a frenzy! You gain Frenzied Strike and Enraged Throw . You can also make an Improvised Melee Weapon attack as a bonus action. Deal 2 extra damage with melee and improvised weapons, and throwing. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Available only in combat. Rage ends early if you don't attack an enemy or take damage each turn. You can't cast or concentrate on spells while raging. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Rage Charge Details Range: Self At higher levels At level 9, the bonus damage to attacks granted by Frenzy increases to +3 . Technical details UID Shout_Rage_Frenzy Grants: Frenzied Strike Enraged Throw Improvised Melee Weapon (Bonus Action) Condition: Frenzied Frenzied Duration: 10 turns Deal an additional 2 (increased to 3 at level 9) damage with melee and improvised weapons, and when throwing objects. Also has Resistance to physical damage , and Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws . Cannot cast or concentrate on spells . Condition: Rage Impeded Rage Impeded Duration: Permanent Weighed down by Heavy Armour . Until the armour is removed, Raging won't grant extra damage, resistance to physical damage, or Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Berserker Used by creatures: Abby , Bombasto , Gleeful Clong , Inku Neza , Lord Jannath's Bodyguard , and Morgya Bugs This version of Rage is usable when already affected by Rage once the Barbarian reaches level 9. v t e Barbarian Subclasses Berserker Giant Wild Magic Wildheart Rage Frenzy Giant's Rage Rage Bear Heart Eagle Heart Elk Heart Tiger Heart Wolf Heart Rage: Wild Magic Aspect of the Beast Bear Chimpanzee Crocodile Eagle Elk Honey Badger Stallion Tiger Wolf Wolverine Bestial Heart Bear Heart Eagle Heart Elk Heart Tiger Heart Wolf Heart Bolstering Magic Boon Level 1 Spell Slot Level 2 Spell Slot Level 3 Spell Slot Other Class Features Boot of the Giants Brutal Critical Danger Sense Diving Strike Elemental Cleaver Extra Attack Fast Movement Feral Instinct Inciting Howl Intimidating Presence Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Magic Awareness Mighty Impel Mindless Rage Primal Stampede Reckless Attack Relentless Rage Tiger's Bloodlust Unarmoured Defence Unrelenting Ferocity Unstable Backlash Vaprak's Greed

Giant's Rage is a Giant barbarian class action that is a variant of Rage . This ability channels the barbarian's rage towards throwing objects and people. Like other rage abilities, wearing Heavy Armour triggers the Rage Impeded condition, removing some benefits of Giant's Rage. Description Enter a Rage and increase in size. Your Rage damage bonus is doubled on Throw attacks. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Available only in combat. Rage ends early if you don't attack an enemy or take damage each turn. You can't cast or concentrate on spells while raging. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Rage Charge Details Range: Self At higher levels At level 9, the bonus damage to attacks granted by Giant's Rage increases to +3 for weapon or unarmed attacks and +6 for thrown attacks. Condition: Giant's Rage Giant's Rage Duration: 10 turns Raging and increased in size. Deals an additional 2 damage (increased to 3 at barbarian level 9) with melee and improvised weapons, unarmed strikes, and 4 damage (increased to 6 at barbarian level 9) while throwing objects. Also has resistance to ⁠ Physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Size is increased by one category. Cannot cast or concentrate on Spells . Condition: Rage Impeded Rage Impeded Duration: Permanent Weighed down by Heavy Armour . Until the armour is removed, Raging won't grant extra damage, resistance to physical damage, or Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . ## Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack (attack)
- **来源**: [Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack (attack)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Great_Weapon_Master:_Bonus_Attack_(attack))
- **分类**: Bonus_actions

Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack is a weapon action available to characters with Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack after killing an enemy or landing a critical hit with a melee weapon. Description As a Bonus Action , make a melee attack with your equipped weapon. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage Normal weapon damage Details Melee Weapon Attack Roll Range: Normal weapon range Technical details UID Target_GreatWeaponMaster_BonusAttack Spell flags IsHarmful , IsMelee , Temporary How to learn Granted by conditions: Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack Notes Landing a critical hit or killing blow with any other melee weapon attack grants the condition Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack . While this condition is active, a character has access to this attack. Performing the attack removes the condition. With a source of extra Bonus Actions such as Fast Hands , it is possible to use this attack multiple times in a round since it has no once-per-turn restriction. A kill or critical hit with Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack itself cannot reapply the corresponding condition. Despite being part of the Great Weapon Master feat, this attack can be triggered by and used with any melee weapon, including one-handed weapons. The All In component of the feat is, however, restricted to weapons wielded with two hands.

## Improved Bardic Inspiration (class action)
- **来源**: [Improved Bardic Inspiration (class action)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Improved_Bardic_Inspiration_(class_action))
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

This article is about the class action granted by Alfira. For the passive feature gained by Bards at higher level, see Improved Bardic Inspiration (passive feature) . For other uses, see Improved Bardic Inspiration (disambiguation) . Improved Bardic Inspiration is a class action that can be granted by Alfira if she survives through Act Two . This ability allows a Bard to inspire their allies just like Bardic Inspiration except the die is always +1d12 and can be used once per Long Rest without requiring a resource. Description Inspire an ally to go beyond their capabilities with your performance. They can add a +1d12 bonus to their next Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw . Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Targets: 1 ally that does not already have Bardic Inspiration Recharge: Long rest Technical details UID Target_SCE_TieflingFollowup_BardicInspiration Spell flags HasVerbalComponent Condition: Improved Bardic Inspiration Improved Bardic Inspiration Duration: Until Long rest Can use Bardic Inspiration to add a +1d12 bonus to the next Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw . How to learn Other ways to learn: This class action is only gained if Alfira survives to the end of Act Two, and the talking party member agrees to perform with her for the tiefling children inside the throne room of Moonrise Towers . Alfira must not have been told to give up being a Bard when met in the Emerald Grove in Act One. The talking party member must also be a Bard . All party members with the Bard class can acquire this ability by talking to Alfira one after another. Halsin is an exception this. Even if he has the Bard class, when he moves to speak with Alfira, the Narrator proclaims with the same text as if he is trying to speak with the tiefling children present there: "★ Still rattled by what happened at the Emerald Grove, they'll need time to recover before they'll be ready to talk .★" Notes As this effect triggers via a toggled passive rather than a Reaction , the player has little control over when and how this bonus is used. For example, the bonus to Saving Throws is immediately expended the first time an affected character is targeted by any attack or ability (whether friendly or hostile), rather than only on a hostile attack or ability in which the Saving Throw bonus might prevent or mitigate an incoming effect. This class action survives respeccing with Withers , even if the character moves to a class other than Bard. Internally, this class action is referred to in developer comments as Shining Dawn , a possible reference to her song in Act One which is called Weeping Dawn . Bugs Due to a coding error, this condition also grants the Bardic Inspiration resource and reactions of a d6 Bardic Inspiration. Using one of the reactions expends the Bardic Inspiration charge but does not remove the Improved Bardic Inspiration condition, leaving non-bard characters with an empty, nonreplenishable Bardic Inspiration charge slot until the condition is expended. v t e Bard Subclasses College of Glamour College of Lore College of Swords College of Valour Inspiration Bardic Inspiration Combat Inspiration Font of Inspiration Improved Bardic Inspiration Mantle of Inspiration Blade Flourish Defensive Flourish Melee Ranged Slashing Flourish Melee Ranged Mobile Flourish Melee Ranged Other class features Countercharm Cutting Words Expertise Extra Attack Jack of All Trades Magical Secrets Mantle of Majesty: Command Song of Rest Spells

See also: Improvised Melee Weapon Improvised Melee Weapon is a Berserker Barbarian class action that allows the user to improvise an attack by picking up an item or creature off the ground using a bonus action. Can only be used while Raging . Description Pick up an item or creature and use it to make a melee attack. Your Strength affects how much weight you can lift. Heavier items deal more damage. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage Object ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Attack Roll Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Range for picking up objects from the ground is AoE: 1 m (3 ft) Radius Damage: For weapons with the Thrown property, the damage roll and damage type is the same as the weapon's melee damage For other objects and creatures, damage is determined by the targets weight of the object being thrown: Light objects: under Weight: 10 kg (20 lb): 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. Medium objects: Weight: 10 kg (20 lb) - 50 kg / 100 lb: 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. Heavy objects: over Weight: 50 kg (100 lb): 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. If the thrown object or creature is heavier than half the target's weight the target is knocked back 2 m (7 ft). If the thrown object or creature is heavier than the target's weight the target becomes Prone (no saving throw). Throwing a creature will apply Prone to that thrown creature (no saving throw). Technical details UID Throw_ImprovisedWeaponBerserker Spell flags AddFallDamageOnLand , CombatLogSetSingleLineRoll , IgnoreSilence , IgnoreVisionBlock , InventorySelection , IsHarmful , PickupEntityAndMove , RangeIgnoreVerticalThreshold , Temporary Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Berserker Notes A creature can pick up items and other creatures weighing up to 0 . 2 ⋅ Strength 2 kg (derived from the definition of CanImprovisedWeaponWeight() in Scripts/thoth/helpers/CommonConditions.khn ). For example, with a Strength score of 18, the weight limit for Improvised Weapon is Weight: 64.8 kg (129.6 lb). It requires a Strength of at least 20 to pick up a normal humanoid ( Weight: 75 kg (150 lb)). Improvised Melee Weapon counts as a melee unarmed attack. The Tavern Brawler feat improves Improvised Melee Weapon. The target's weight is not influenced by a creatures equipped items or items inside a creatures inventory or a container. The weight is not how much it weighs to pick up or have in your inventory, but the weight of only the object/creature itself. ## Lacerate (Spiritual Weapon)
- **来源**: [Lacerate (Spiritual Weapon)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lacerate_(Spiritual_Weapon))
- **分类**: Bonus_actions

This article is about the version of the attack used by Spiritual Weapons. For the normal weapon action, see Lacerate . Lacerate is a weapon action available to halberds , greatswords , and greataxes summoned by Spiritual Weapon . Description Slash at your target's vital points to make it Bleed . Undead and Constructs can't bleed. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage: 2~9 + modifiers 1d8 + 1 + Spellcasting modifier ⁠ Force Details Melee Spell Attack Roll CON Save ( Weapon action DC ) Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Recharge: Short rest At higher levels Upcast : The damage of this attack increases by 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage for every 2 spell slot levels above 2 used to cast Spiritual Weapon . Technical details UID Target_Slash_SpiritualWeapon_Greataxe Spell flags IsDefaultWeaponAction , IsHarmful , IsMelee Condition: Bleeding Bleeding Duration: 2 turns CON Save ( Weapon action DC  + 2) Takes 2 ⁠ ⁠ Slashing DRS damage at the start of each turn and has Disadvantage on Constitution Saving Throws . Removed by healing. How to learn Used by creatures: Spiritual Weapon (halberd) , Spiritual Weapon (greataxe) , and Spiritual Weapon (greatsword) Notes The attack roll and damage for this attack uses the summoner's spellcasting modifier, but the DC to inflict the condition is based on the summoned weapon's weapon action DC (with an inherent +2 bonus). Since the weapon has ability scores of 10, this results in a DC of just 12 (at proficiency bonus of 2) to 14 (at proficiency bonus of 4). The once per short rest cooldown of this attack is reset when resummoning a spiritual weapon, so it is effectively once per summon instead. Bugs The in-game tooltip is incorrect - all the damage dealt is ⁠ Force damage. Contrary to other Spiritual Weapon attacks, the damage dealt is non-magical.

## Lightning Blast
- **来源**: [Lightning Blast](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lightning_Blast)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Lightning Blast is a class action granted by The Blast Pendant . This ability allows the wearer to empower a lightning spell or cantrip to deal extra damage equal to the number of Lightning Charges accumulated. Description Focus the electricity in your veins to strengthen your next spell or cantrip . Your spell or cantrip that deals ⁠ Lightning damage [ See Notes ] will deal additional ⁠ Lightning damage equal to your remaining Lightning Charges . On hit, all of your Lightning Charges are consumed. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Long rest Technical details UID Shout_MAG_ChargedLightning_LightningBlast Condition: Lightning Blast Lightning Blast Duration: 2 turns Your next Lightning spell or cantrip deals additional ⁠ Lightning damage equal to your remaining Lightning Charges . On hit, all of your Lightning Charges are consumed. How to learn Granted by items: The Blast Pendant Notes In-game, the description says that this action works specifically with lightning spells, but the conditions are not actually that restrictive. It works with any spell so long as it deals some lightning damage. Since this action requires having Lightning Charges anyway, all damaging spells will deal at least 1 ⁠ Lightning damage. As a result, this action can be used with any damaging spell. Bugs If the wearer has 5 or more turns of Lightning Charges remaining when casting their next spell, both the additional damage from Lightning Blast and the 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning DRS from Lightning Charges will be dealt to the target of the spell.
