## Mantle of Inspiration
- **来源**: [Mantle of Inspiration](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mantle_of_Inspiration)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Mantle of Inspiration is a College of Glamour bard class action that protects allies with a mantle that charms enemies that hit them. Description Imbue 2 allies with your vigour and grant them 5 temporary hit points . If they're hit with a melee attack, the attacker becomes Charmed . Properties Cost Bonus Action + Bardic Inspiration Details Range: 9 m (30 ft) Targets: 2 allies At higher levels At level 6, Mantle of Inspiration can target 3 allies for 8 temporary hit points . At level 10, Mantle of Inspiration can target 4 allies for 11 temporary hit points . Condition: Mantle of Inspiration Mantle of Inspiration Duration: Until Long rest Imbued with bardic vigour and granted 5 temporary hit points . If hit with a melee attack, the attacker becomes Charmed . Condition: Charmed Charmed Duration: 1 turn Cannot attack the spellcaster. The spellcaster has Advantage on Charisma Checks in dialogue. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: College of Glamour Notes The charm effect does not protect against various Multiattack abilities. It charms the attacker after the first hit of the multiattack but this does not prevent the subsequent attacks in the sequence. It works properly against enemies making multiple separate attacks through Extra Attack or similar effects. The healing effect of the Cap of Curing does not trigger when using this variant of Bardic Inspiration. Granting temporary hit points also does not count as providing healing so it does not trigger effects like The Whispering Promise . This action can target Bard themselves. v t e Bard Subclasses College of Glamour College of Lore College of Swords College of Valour Inspiration Bardic Inspiration Combat Inspiration Font of Inspiration Improved Bardic Inspiration Mantle of Inspiration Blade Flourish Defensive Flourish Melee Ranged Slashing Flourish Melee Ranged Mobile Flourish Melee Ranged Other class features Countercharm Cutting Words Expertise Extra Attack Jack of All Trades Magical Secrets Mantle of Majesty: Command Song of Rest Spells

## Perfectly Balanced Strike
- **来源**: [Perfectly Balanced Strike](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Perfectly_Balanced_Strike)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions

Perfectly Balanced Strike is a weapon action granted by Belm . Description Send Belm snaking out with an adder's speed, the very exemplar of swiftness embodied in steel. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage Normal weapon damage Details Melee Weapon Attack Roll Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Per turn Technical details UID Target_MAG_PHB_ScimitarOfSpeed_BonusAttack Spell flags IsAttack , IsHarmful , IsMelee , Temporary How to learn Granted by items: Belm Notes Perfectly Balanced Strike is a variation of Dueller's Enthusiasm , allowing the wielder to make an "offhand-like" attack with Belm while it is in their main hand. The difference is that there are no restrictions on Belm's variation – shields and offhand weapons do not disable the weapon action. When Belm is equipped in the offhand , Perfectly Balanced Strike functions as an additional main-hand weapon attack. This attack uses all the stats and on-hit effects of the equipped main-hand weapon, including adding the wielder's ability modifier to the damage without the need of Two-Weapon Fighting . This effect mimics how additional attacks worked in Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 which used AD&D (i.e., 2e) rules.

## Polearm Clout
- **来源**: [Polearm Clout](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Polearm_Clout)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions

Polearm Clout is a bonus action attack granted by the Polearm Master feat after making an attack with a polearm. It is a bludgeoning attack made with the butt of the polearm. Description Sweep your polearm around, whacking a foe with the weapon's heavy haft. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage: 1~4 + modifiers 1d4 + Strength or Dexterity modifier ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Weapon Attack Roll Range: Normal weapon range Recharge: Per turn Technical details UID Target_PolearmMaster_BonusAttack Spell flags IsHarmful , IsMelee , Temporary How to learn Granted by features: Polearm Master: Bonus Attack Notes The damage modifier of this attack uses Strength or Dexterity , whichever is higher, even if the weapon does not have the finesse property, or Charisma in the case of Pact of the Blade / Bind Hexed Weapon . It does not change to spellcasting modifier in the case of Shillelagh . This attack can only be triggered once per turn. Therefore, a Thief who gains Extra Attack through multiclassing cannot use Polearm Master: Bonus Attack twice, even though they have two bonus actions. This behaviour is different from that of Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike , which can be used twice (e.g., by attacking with an action, making a bonus action attack, then making the attack granted by Extra Attack, then making a second bonus action attack.

This article is about the base barbarian action. For the identically named version used by Beastmaster boars, see Rage (Boar) . For other uses, see Rage (disambiguation) . Rage is a Barbarian bonus action and class feature. Enter a Rage to gain resistance against physical damage, deal extra melee and thrown damage, and Advantage on Strength checks and Saving Throws . Wearing heavy armour imposes the Rage Impeded condition, removing most benefits of Rage. Description Deal 2 extra damage with melee and improvised weapons, and throwing. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Available only in combat. Rage ends early if you don't attack an enemy or take damage each turn. [ See: Bugs ] You can't cast or concentrate on spells while raging. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Rage Charge Details Range: Self Duration: 10 turns At higher levels At level 9, the bonus damage to attacks granted by Rage increases to +3 . Technical details UID Shout_Rage Grants: End Rage Condition: Rage Rage Duration: 10 turns Deals an additional 2 (increased to 3 at level 9) damage with melee and improvised weapons, unarmed strikes, and while throwing objects. Has resistance to ⁠ Physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Cannot cast or concentrate on Spells . Condition: Rage Impeded Rage Impeded Duration: Permanent Weighed down by Heavy Armour . Until the armour is removed, Raging won't grant extra damage, resistance to physical damage, or Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Barbarian Notes "Attacks" to maintain Rage can be any ability targetting a non-allied creature and are not limited to standard weapon attacks. Abilities like Shove or illithid powers like Black Hole also count towards maintaining Rage. Rage cannot be used while being Calmed . In a departure from D&D 5e rules, Rage bonus damage can apply to melee weapons not using Strength (e.g. finesse weapons using Dexterity ). Although not stated in the in-game tooltip, Rage bonus damage also applies to unarmed strikes . Entering a rage automatically ends concentrations from all sources but concentrations from non-spell sources can be started during rage e.g. Blessing of the Trickster and Mantle of Majesty: Command . Bugs Taking damage will not maintain Rage if the barbarian has another passive feature which also triggers on taking damage (more precisely, any passive with an OnDamaged StatsFunctorContext ). Examples include: Uncanny Dodge Grievous Retribution from the Bloodguzzler Garb and Cloth Armour Caustic Reprisal from the Fleshmelter Cloak Countershock from The Jolty Vest Force Conduit (even with insufficient charges to trigger an explosion) If the Rage animation plays while the player does not have control in turn-based mode (for example, by ending the turn with no other characters in the active turn order ), no Rage charges will be consumed. This applies to all other variants of Rage. Rage includes a hidden function which reduces fall damage by half. While this causes Jump tooltips to correctly show half-damage from falling, it stacks with the innate Bludgeoning resistance also granted by Rage and effectively quarters fall damage. This version of Rage is usable when already affected by Rage once the Barbarian reaches level 9. v t e Barbarian Subclasses Berserker Giant Wild Magic Wildheart Rage Frenzy Giant's Rage Rage Bear Heart Eagle Heart Elk Heart Tiger Heart Wolf Heart Rage: Wild Magic Aspect of the Beast Bear Chimpanzee Crocodile Eagle Elk Honey Badger Stallion Tiger Wolf Wolverine Bestial Heart Bear Heart Eagle Heart Elk Heart Tiger Heart Wolf Heart Bolstering Magic Boon Level 1 Spell Slot Level 2 Spell Slot Level 3 Spell Slot Other Class Features Boot of the Giants Brutal Critical Danger Sense Diving Strike Elemental Cleaver Extra Attack Fast Movement Feral Instinct Inciting Howl Intimidating Presence Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Magic Awareness Mighty Impel Mindless Rage Primal Stampede Reckless Attack Relentless Rage Tiger's Bloodlust Unarmoured Defence Unrelenting Ferocity Unstable Backlash Vaprak's Greed

This article is about the action used by Beastmaster boars. For the barbarian action, see Rage . For other uses, see Rage (disambiguation) . Rage is a bonus action gained by the Beast Master ranger's Boar Companion at level 5. It allows the boar to enter a rage once per combat which grants bonus damage, resistance to physical damage, and the ability to make a bonus action attack for its duration. Description Go into a frenzy, increasing your size and becoming stronger through raw anger. While raging, your melee attacks deal an additional 2+1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Slashing [ See Notes ] damage and you are Enlarged [ See Notes ] . You gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Available only in combat. Rage ends early if you don't attack an enemy or take damage each turn. You can't cast or concentrate on spells while raging. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Per combat Duration: 10 turns Technical details UID Shout_Rage_Boar Grants: Frenzied Strike (Boar) Condition: Rage (Boar) Rage Duration: 10 turns Deals an additional 2 + 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Slashing [ See Notes ] damage with melee attacks. Is Enlarged [ See Notes ] . Has Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Can use Frenzied Strike (Boar) . Rage ends early if the boar didn't attack an enemy or take damage since its last turn. How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Beast Master Used by creatures: Verres Calamitosus and Verres Major Notes The rage condition actually incorporates the effects of Enlarged as well which gives an unlisted +1d4 bonus to damage, +1 to size category (increases the boar to Large), and a 1.33 size multiplier. v t e Ranger Subclasses Beast Master Gloom Stalker Hunter Swarmkeeper Favoured Enemy Bounty Hunter Keeper of the Veil Mage Breaker Ranger Knight Sanctified Stalker Natural Explorer Beast Tamer Urban Tracker Wasteland Wanderer ( Cold Fire Poison ) Other class features Bestial Fury Companion's Bond Dread Ambusher Melee Ranged Hide Escape the Horde Exceptional Training Extra Attack Gathered Swarm Cloud of Jellyfish Flurry of Moths Legion of Bees Hide in Plain Sight Hunter's Prey Colossus Slayer Giant Killer Horde Breaker Iron Mind Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Mighty Swarm Multiattack Defence Prey's Scent Spells Ranger's Companion Stalker's Flurry Steel Will Superior Darkvision Umbral Shroud Volley Whirlwind Attack Writhing Tide

This article is about the Wild Magic version of the Rage action. For other uses, see Rage (disambiguation) . Rage: Wild Magic is a Wild Magic Barbarian bonus action. It replaces normal Rage and triggers a random magical effect when entering the rage. Description Enter a Rage that releases all the magic roiling inside you, causing a random magical effect. Gain Resistance to physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Ability Checks and saves . Available only in combat. Rage ends early if you don't attack an enemy or take damage each turn. You can't cast or concentrate on spells while raging. Properties Cost Bonus Action + Rage Charge Details Range: Self Duration: 10 turns Magical Effects Effect Description Weapon Infusion Magic infuses your weapon. It deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage and gains the Light and Thrown properties. If thrown, it immediately reappears in your hand. Magic Retribution You are protected by wild, vengeful magic. Enemies that hit you take 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage in retaliation. Protective Lights You, and any allies within 3 m (10 ft) of you, have a +1 bonus to Armour Class . Intangible Spirit Each turn, as a Bonus Action , choose to summon a spectral flumph within 10 m (33 ft) of you. The flumph explodes at the end of your turn, dealing 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to anyone within 4.5 m (15 ft) on a failed Dexterity Saving Throw . The DC is based on the summoner's Constitution modifier. Bolt of Light Each turn, as a Bonus Action , choose to shoot a Bolt of Light from your chest at a target within 10 m (33 ft) of you. Wild Magic: Bolt of Light deals 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage and Blinds the target on a failed DC  12 Constitution Saving Throw for 1 turn. Vine Growth Flowers and vines spread outward from you in a radius of 4.5 m (15 ft) creating Difficult Terrain for everyone other than you. Teleport Each turn, as a Bonus Action , choose to Teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 18 m (60 ft) Dark Tendrils Shadowy tendrils lash outwards from you. Each creature within 9 m (30 ft) of you must succeed a DC  12 Constitution Saving Throw or take 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage. Additionally, you gain 1d12 temporary hit points . At higher levels At level 9, the bonus damage to attacks increases to +3 . Technical details UID Shout_Rage_WildMagic Condition: Rage Rage Duration: 10 turns Deals an additional 2 (increased to 3 at level 9) damage with melee and improvised weapons, unarmed strikes, and while throwing objects. Has resistance to ⁠ Physical damage, and Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . Cannot cast or concentrate on Spells . Condition: Rage Impeded Rage Impeded Duration: Permanent Weighed down by Heavy Armour . Until the armour is removed, Raging won't grant extra damage, resistance to physical damage, or Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Wild Magic Barbarian Bugs This version of Rage is usable when already affected by Rage once the Barbarian reaches level 9. The condition which is responsible for blocking spell casting while under the effects of Rage is not immediately applied when using Rage: Wild Magic, and is instead applied after the Wild Magic surge occurs. This leaves a very brief moment, before the Wild Magic surge, where a Wild Magic Barbarian can still cast spells while under the effects of Rage. v t e Barbarian Subclasses Berserker Giant Wild Magic Wildheart Rage Frenzy Giant's Rage Rage Bear Heart Eagle Heart Elk Heart Tiger Heart Wolf Heart Rage: Wild Magic Aspect of the Beast Bear Chimpanzee Crocodile Eagle Elk Honey Badger Stallion Tiger Wolf Wolverine Bestial Heart Bear Heart Eagle Heart Elk Heart Tiger Heart Wolf Heart Bolstering Magic Boon Level 1 Spell Slot Level 2 Spell Slot Level 3 Spell Slot Other Class Features Boot of the Giants Brutal Critical Danger Sense Diving Strike Elemental Cleaver Extra Attack Fast Movement Feral Instinct Inciting Howl Intimidating Presence Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Magic Awareness Mighty Impel Mindless Rage Primal Stampede Reckless Attack Relentless Rage Tiger's Bloodlust Unarmoured Defence Unrelenting Ferocity Unstable Backlash Vaprak's Greed

The Cursed creature takes additional damage whenever you hit it with an attack and has Disadvantage on Ability Checks for one Ability of your choosing. ## Relentless Lunge
- **来源**: [Relentless Lunge](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Relentless_Lunge)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Relentless Lunge is a special class action available only to the Slayer . It allows the Slayer to leap through the air, crushing its foes where it lands. Description Leap sinuously and smash into your foes, possibly knocking them Prone . Properties Cost Bonus Action + 3 m (10 ft) Movement Speed Damage: 2~12 + modifiers 2d6 + Strength modifier ⁠ Bludgeoning Details STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: Jump range AoE: 5 m (17 ft) Radius Recharge: Per turn At higher levels At level 10, the damage becomes 4d6 + Strength modifier ⁠ Bludgeoning Technical details UIDs Projectile_TerrifyingLunge_Slayer Base version which deals 2d6 damage Projectile_TerrifyingLunge_Slayer_10 Level 10 upgrade which deals 4d6 damage Spell flags IgnoreVisionBlock , IsAttack , IsHarmful , IsJump Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 2 turns STR Save ( Spell save DC ) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Used by creatures: Slayer Notes The range is equal to the normal Jump and all modifiers that apply to jump range apply to the range of this attack as well. Before level 10, the range is 9.5 m (32 ft) (due to the Slayer's Strength modifier of +5). After level 10, the range increases to 11.5 m (38 ft) (due to the Slayer's Strength modifier of +7). As of Patch 6, this attack can now break Sanctuary . Bugs The spell save DC of the Slayer's actions uses the spellcasting ability of the last class you took a first level in, but with the Slayer's ability scores. This results in a very low DC due to the Slayer's low mental ability scores. In particular, Fighters, Rogues, Wizards, Clerics, Druids, Monks, and Rangers have a +0 spellcasting modifier from Intelligence or Wisdom in Slayer form, while Barbarians, Bards, Paladins, Sorcerers, and Warlocks have a -1 spellcasting modifier from Charisma while in Slayer form. AreaRadius is incorrectly set at 18 m (60 ft), causing the appearance that the area of effect radius is much larger than it actually is.

## Sacred Munitions
- **来源**: [Sacred Munitions](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Sacred_Munitions)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions

Sacred Munitions is a weapon action granted by Gandrel's Aspiration . Description Infuse your crossbow bolts with holy energy. For the rest of your turn, your ranged weapon attacks inflict Turned against undead . Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Short rest Duration: 1 turn Technical details UID Shout_MAG_WeaponAction_UndeadTurningBolt Spell flags IsDefaultWeaponAction Condition: Sacred Munitions Sacred Munitions Duration: 1 turn Affected entity's ranged weapon attacks possibly inflict Turn Undead on a target. Condition: Turned Turned Duration: 3 turns A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from the creature which turned it as possible. It cannot willingly move to a space within 9 m (30 ft) of that creature. It also cannot take Reactions . For its Actions , it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. The condition ends upon taking damage. How to learn Granted by items: Gandrel's Aspiration Notes The in-game description says "Your ranged weapon attacks possibly inflict Turn Undead," but there is actually no saving throw to resist it. A level 5 cleric using this feature will also have the Destroy Undead feature applied to their ranged attacks, dealing 4d6 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant bonus damage to undead targets. ## Scarlet Saturation
- **来源**: [Scarlet Saturation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Scarlet_Saturation)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Scarlet Saturation is a special class action available to the wielder of Rhapsody . After killing three creatures, the wielder can expend all three accumulated Scarlet Remittance charges to deal critical hit damage with the next attack. This action is one of the three variants of Scarlet Feast . Description If you have a +3 bonus from Scarlet Remittance , consume it to make your next attack a Critical Hit . Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Long rest Duration: 2 turns Technical details UID Shout_MAG_Zhentarim_Bloodfeeding_Critical Spell flags IgnoreSilence , Invisible , NoCameraMove , Stealth Condition: Scarlet Saturation Scarlet Saturation Duration: 2 turns Your next attack is guaranteed to Critically Hit . How to learn Granted by items: Rhapsody This spell is a variation of: Scarlet Feast Notes This action does not actually turn an attack roll into a critical hit, but instead makes a hit deal critical damage. It is possible to miss with the attack, though the effect is not expended on a miss. Additionally, the critical hit damage from this effect will bypass critical hit immunity from items like the Adamantine Shield . Bugs This effect is only removed when landing a weapon attack, but it will make any attack deal critical damage, including unarmed, thrown, or spell attacks.

Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: Self Recharge: Per combat Technical details UID Shout_Fury_Gnoll_Boss Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , IsEnemySpell Grants: Frenzied Fury Condition: Seething Fury Seething Fury Duration: 2 turns Rage brews within the gnoll. ## Shove
- **来源**: [Shove](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Shove)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Shove is a common bonus action which allows the user to shove an creature or object, pushing it away (and possibly off ledges or into harmful effects). Description Try to push your target away. Your chances depend on your Athletics , and are higher if you're hidden or invisible. The shove distance depends on your Strength and the target's weight. Properties Cost Bonus Action Details Range: 1.5 m (5 ft) Pushes: Shove distance Technical details UID Target_Shove Spell flags AddFallDamageOnLand , CombatLogSetSingleLineRoll , IsHarmful , IsMelee Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] Shove is a basic, common action available to almost every humanoid. Because of falling damage and chasms, shoving can be an extremely potent action both when used by or against the party. Shove has a dedicated keybind (V) with the keyboard and mouse interface. It can also be used from the ability bar like any other ability. Using Shove shows a percentage chance preview and the trajectory and landing position of the object or character if the push is successful. The odds of success with, and the distance of, the shove depend on a number of factors described below: A valid shove. The goblin will be pushed into the pit and land in a valid location, taking significant fall damage. For a shove to be valid, the target creature must land in a position where it could normally stand, or in a dedicated chasm. Chasms can be identified by the "Chasm" tooltip which appears when hovering the cursor over them. Pushing a creature into a chasm instantly kills it, but the body and any loot it carries is (usually) lost forever. An invalid shove. The goblin would be shoved into the wall, which is not a valid location. Rather than hitting the wall and then falling into the pit, the goblin will not move at all if shoved. Attempting to push a creature into an invalid location (for example, into a wall) shows a red shove preview. While the game does not prevent the player character from making an invalid shove, doing so does not move the target - even if the roll is successful. Roll [ edit section | visual editor ] When attempting to shove a non-allied creature, both the target and the shover make skill checks in a contested roll. The shover makes a normal Athletics check against a DC determined by the target's passive skill using either Athletics or Acrobatics , whichever is higher. [ 1 ] [ See: Bugs ] This passive skill is equal to 10 + skill bonus with Advantage on the relevant skill checks adding 5 and Disadvantage subtracting 5. For example, a barbarian at level 1, with 17 Strength, proficiency in Athletics, and currently Raging has a passive Athletics skill of: 10 + 3 (STR modifier) + 2 (Proficiency) + 5 (Advantage on STR checks) = 20 If the shover's roll meets or exceeds the target's passive skill, the shove is successful. Shove attempts cannot critically fail. Both Hiding and Invisibility grant Advantage on shove's Athletics check. [ See: Bugs ] An example of the erroneous shove DC shown in the combat log. Information on the contested skill check is not readily visible in-game since, in the combat log, the DC of a shove skill check is always erroneously shown as 0. The percentage chance preview before making a shove is accurate, however. Shoving is one of the few cases where skill checks are made in combat. As a result, this is one of the few uses for the component of Hex which imposes Disadvantage on skill checks of a specified ability. Hexing Strength greatly reduces the chance of an enemy successfully shoving you and makes it easier to shove high Strength enemies. Hexing Dexterity makes it significantly easier to shove high Dexterity enemies. Note that it is not possible to see an enemy's skill bonuses in the inspect window. Therefore, in absence of such information, it may be advisable to hex the higher of these two abilities . When targeting an ally, Shove does not require a skill check and always succeeds, provided all other prerequisites for a successful shove are met. This behaviour was added in Patch 6; prior to this, shoving allies required passing a skill check. Max weight [ edit section | visual editor ] The weight of a target object and a creature's Strength score determine whether a shove attempt can be made in the first place. The requirement is: Strength score × Multiplier ≥ Target object weight . Note that this is the full Strength score, not the Strength ability modifier that is usually used. The multiplier is 12 unmodified, but is increased to 28.2 for Enlarged creatures, and decreased to 5.1 for Reduced creatures. [ 2 ] Smaller characters like gnomes do not receive penalties to their maximum shove weights. The multiplier is adjusted specifically by the Enlarged/Reduced conditions and has nothing to do with creature size . Even functionally identical effects like Elixir of The Colossus or Giant Form do not affect the maximum shove weight. If the weight condition is not met, attempting to shove an object or creature displays a message "Too heavy to Shove." Distance [ edit section | visual editor ] The distance an object or creature is shoved depends on the Strength of the shover and weight of the shoved object. This distance is restricted to a minimum of 1 m (3 ft) and a maximum of 6 m (20 ft). [ 3 ] Note, however, that the maximum shove distance assumes level terrain. When shoving an object off a ledge, it can go further than 6 m (20 ft) since it continues its parabolic trajectory as it falls. Tactics [ edit section | visual editor ] Shove is an excellent tool to exploit terrain and environmental hazards. When pushing enemies off ledges, they take damage according to the falling damage rules if falling at least 4 m (13 ft). Additionally, if falling least 8 m (27 ft), they are knocked Prone with no saving throw . Pushing enemies into chasms is even more potent, but results in the loss of any loot they may carry. Aside from the obvious use of pushing enemies to their deaths, Shove has a wide range of creative uses. Shoving can be used to avoid Opportunity Attacks by pushing a threatening enemy out of range before retreating, and opponents of the party may use this tactic. It can be used to rouse a creature from Sleeping or help them shake off the effects of certain spells like Hypnotic Pattern . Shoving (or even just attempting a shove) counts as an attack for the purposes of maintaining Rage . Allies can be shoved out of range of dangerous effects. For example, a player character can shove an ally Garrotted by a Meazel to break the effect. Related features [ edit section | visual editor ] Boot of the Giants - A special shove-like action that additionally deals Unarmed Strike damage to the target. Charger - Grants a special shove ability, Charger: Shove . While this ability costs a full Action and a Bonus Action , it is not actually any stronger or more effective at shoving than the basic shove. Displace - When inflicting falling damage through a shove, this feature adds bonus ⁠ Psychic damage. Throw and Improvised Melee Weapon - Attempting to throw or use a creature as an improvised weapon involves a contested athletics roll, identical to shove except without advantage for hiding. Related items [ edit section | visual editor ] Bracing Band - Gain +1 AC for a turn after shoving an enemy. Also works when pushing an enemy any other way. Corpsegrinder - The special weapon action uses normal shoving distance to determine the pushback. Reaper's Embrace , The Mighty Cloth , Boots of Striding , and Helldusk Boots can prevent you from being forcibly moved by Shove. Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Shove Off Kill a creature with falling damage. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If the target of a Shove has a condition which grants them Advantage on any kind of roll, they cannot use Acrobatics to set the DC for being shoved and use Athletics instead. In this case, the shover no longer gets advantage when hidden, and instead only receives advantage if the target of their Shove is hidden. References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ From the definition of ShoveCheck() in Scripts/thoth/helpers/CommonConditions.khn . ↑ From the definition of CanShoveWeight() in Scripts/thoth/helpers/CommonConditions.khn . ↑ From the definitions of ShoveDistanceMin and ShoveDistanceMax in Public/Shared/Stats/Generated/Data/Data.txt .

## Starry Form: Dragon
- **来源**: [Starry Form: Dragon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Starry_Form:_Dragon)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Starry Form: Dragon is a bonus action available to Circle of the Stars druids. It lets them enter a Starry Form where they gain a radiant breath attack and significant bonus to concentration saving throws. At higher levels, druids in this form additionally gain the ability to hover and fly. Description A constellation of a wise dragon appears on you. When you make a Saving Throw to maintain Concentration on a spell, a roll result of 9 or lower is considered a 10. As a Bonus Action while in this Starry Form, you can cast Dazzling Breath . Properties Cost Bonus Action + Wild Shape Charge Details Range: Self Duration: Until Long rest At higher levels At level 2, Dazzling Breath does 2d6 + Wisdom modifier ⁠ Radiant damage. At level 5, Dazzling Breath does 3d6 + Wisdom modifier ⁠ Radiant damage. At level 10, Twinkling Constellations upgrades this form with the ability to hover and Fly . Dazzling Breath does 4d6 + Wisdom modifier ⁠ Radiant damage. Technical details UID Shout_Wildshape_Star_Dragon Spell flags HasSomaticComponent , UnavailableInDialogs , Wildshape Grants: Dazzling Breath Fly (Starry Form) Condition: Starry Form: Dragon Starry Form: Dragon Duration: Until Long rest In Starry Form. When you make a Saving Throw to maintain Concentration on a spell, a roll result of 9 or lower is considered a 10. As a Bonus Action while in this Starry Form, you can cast Dazzling Breath . How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Circle of the Stars This spell is a variation of: Starry Form Notes This action is listed in the Wild Shape container action along with the normal Wild Shape forms. The level 10 upgrade makes the druid 'hover' while in dragon form. This grants immunity to all surface effects and fall damage ; however, the character still uses normal walking animations and does not visually appear to be hovering. This effect is equivalent to the surface immunity provided by a Swarmkeeper's Writhing Tide . Note that scripted cutscenes and conversations before combat automatically dismiss Wild Shape (e.g., the conversations before the battle of raiding the Emerald Grove ). This could seriously sabotage the fight once combat starts if the player character is unaware. [ verify ] Bugs After taking this action, characters receive both a condition and a passive with the same name, 'Starry Form: Dragon', yet they have different descriptions. Starry Form: Dragon only affects concentration saving throws and does not affect any ability checks or other Constitution Saving Throws despite the passive stating otherwise: When you make Intelligence or Wisdom Checks or Constitution Saving Throws, you can replace rolls of 9 or lower with a 10. v t e Druid Subclasses Circle of the Land Circle of the Moon Circle of the Spores Circle of the Stars Wild Shapes Creatures Badger Bear Cat Spider Wolf Dire Raven Deep Rothé Panther Owlbear Sabre-Toothed Tiger Dilophosaurus Air Myrmidon Earth Myrmidon Fire Myrmidon Water Myrmidon Starry Forms Archer Chalice Dragon Lands Arctic Coast Desert Forest Grassland Mountain Swamp Underdark Other class features Cosmic Omen Fungal Infestation Halo of Spores Improved Wild Strike Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Lunar Mend Natural Recovery Nature's Ward Primal Strike Spells Spreading Spores Symbiotic Entity Twinkling Constellations Wild Strike

Properties Cost Bonus Action Details WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Range: 18 m (60 ft) Targets: 1 creature not recently affected by Stunning Gaze Recharge: Per turn Concentration Duration: 1 turn Technical details UIDs Target_StunningGaze_DeathsHead Normal NPC version Target_StunningGaze_DeathsHead_Hardcore Tactician version that removes the concentration Target_END_AllyAbilities_StunningGaze Dark Urge version with once per short rest limit Spell flags IsConcentration , IsEnemySpell , IsHarmful Condition: Stunned Stunned Duration: 1 turn WIS Save ( Spell save DC ) Affected creatures cannot move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions . Notes The version that can be acquired by The Dark Urge is limited to once per short rest . A creature cannot be affected by Stunning Gaze for multiple turns in a row. Unarmed Strike is a monk class action that allows the user to make an attack with their bare fists using a bonus action. Description Swiftly strike an enemy as a bonus action. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage: 1~4 + modifiers 1d4 + Strength or Dexterity modifier ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Unarmed Attack Roll Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) How to learn Granted by conditions: Martial Arts: Unarmed Strike Notes Tavern Brawler applies just as with regular Unarmed Strikes . Monk's Martial Arts: Deft Strikes replaces the 1 base damage of an Unarmed Strike with 1d4. This increases to 1d6 at monk level 3 and 1d8 at monk level 9. Monk's Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks may replace the Strength modifier normally added to the damage of Unarmed Strikes with the Dexterity modifier if it is higher. Many buffs and features which specify that they apply to "weapon attacks", such as Divine Smite , do not apply to Unarmed Strikes. For a comprehensive list of effects that interact with Unarmed Strikes, see: List of features and items that interact with unarmed strikes . ## Vampire Bite
- **来源**: [Vampire Bite](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Vampire_Bite)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Vampire Bite is a unique action available to Astarion . It can be used without breaking stealth, deals piercing damage, heals Astarion, and increases his abilities while debilitating the target. Origin Astarion gets access to the Vampire Bite action after completing the prologue and waking up on the beach. Companion Astarion gets access to the Vampire Bite action after he is outed as a vampire. Description Suck the blood from a living creature to regain hit points . The target takes 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage, but not if it is Sleeping [ See: Bugs ] or you are Hiding . If the target is humanoid , you become Happy and the target becomes Bloodless . Biting a creature does not break stealth. Properties Cost Bonus Action Damage: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Piercing (if Astarion is not Hiding) Healing: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Healing (if the target is alive and not Gale or Karlach) Details Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Targets: A creature that is not an undead , plant , elemental , ooze , construct , or Petrified Recharge: Short rest Technical details UID Target_VampireBite_Astarion Spell flags CannotTargetItems , CannotTargetTerrain , IsHarmful , IsMelee , Stealth Condition: Happy Happy Duration: Until Long rest Astarion's vampiric hunger has been temporarily sated. +1 to all Attack Rolls , Saving Throws , and most Ability Checks . How to learn Used by creatures: Astarion Notes Attempting to use this action on the following creatures neither heals Astarion nor grants the Happy condition, and also causes an additional effect: Karlach before her heart is upgraded twice – inflicts 3 turns of Burning Gale or Dead creatures – inflicts 3 turns of Poisoned Compared to the unique features and abilities of other origin characters , Vampire Bite stands out for its combat potential and extended buff. Companions confront origin Astarion about his vampirism if he uses this action in front of them without having previously revealed his condition to them. Using this ability on companions causes them to lose some approval, unless the player character is dating them. [ verify ] Bugs The attack uses the wrong condition ( SLEEPING   rather than SLEEP   ) to check if a target is Sleeping , and therefore does not correctly avoid dealing damage to Sleeping targets, unless Astarion is also Hiding .

## War Priest
- **来源**: [War Priest](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/War_Priest)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Passive_features

War Priest is a War Domain Cleric passive feature which allows the cleric to make a limited number of bonus action attacks using War Priest Charges that recharge after a long rest. Description When you make an unarmed or weapon attack, you can spend a War Priest Charge to make an additional attack as a Bonus Action . Details Cost: Bonus Action  +  War Priest Charge At higher levels A War Domain Cleric begins with three War Priest Charges per long rest. This increases to: Four charges at Cleric Level 5 Five charges at Cleric Level 8 Six charges at Cleric Level 11 How to learn Classes: Class level 1: War Domain Used by creatures: Adrielle Notes This ability has been changed slightly from the original tabletop version, where the user instead has an amount of charges equal to their Wisdom modifier, with a minimum of 1 charge (and as such the amount of uses will range from 1 to 5). While it is described as passive ability, it does not show up in the character's passive options (like non-lethal attacks). As long as they have charges and bonus actions available, the ability triggers in the same way Extra Attack works; after making an attack they will see their attack (and compatible actions) highlighted, it does not prompt for a confirmation. The use of War Priest Charges always take place before the attacks of a second action. For example, if a character with available War Priest Charges uses Action Surge then the character first uses the attack(s) of their first Action , then with a Bonus Action via War Priest Charges , and then finally with the attack(s) provided by their second action. v t e Cleric Subclasses Death Domain Knowledge Domain Life Domain Light Domain Nature Domain Tempest Domain Trickery Domain War Domain Channel Divinity Charge Charm Animals and Plants Cloak of Shadows Destructive Wrath Dampen Elements Guided Strike Invoke Duplicity Knowledge of the Ages Preserve Life Radiance of the Dawn Read Thoughts Touch of Death War God's Blessing Divine Strike Radiant (Melee) Radiant (Ranged) Poison (Melee) Poison (Ranged) Cold (Melee) Cold (Ranged) Fire (Melee) Fire (Ranged) Lightning (Melee) Lightning (Ranged) Necrotic (Melee) Necrotic (Ranged) Thunder (Melee) Thunder (Ranged) Weapon (Melee) Weapon (Ranged) Other class features Acolyte of Nature Blessed Healer Blessing of the Trickster Blessings of Knowledge Destroy Undead Disciple of Life Divine Intervention Expertise Improved Warding Flare Inescapable Destruction Potent Spellcasting Reaper Spells Thunderbolt Strike Turn Undead War Priest Warding Flare Wrath of the Storm

Properties Cost: Bonus Action  +  2 Wild Shape Charges At Higher Levels The hit points of the Fire Myrmidon form increase with druid level, as shown in the table below: Druid level Hit points 10 90 12 108 Condition: Wild Shape: Fire Myrmidon Wild Shape: Fire Myrmidon Wild shaped into an Fire Myrmidon Creature: Fire Myrmidon STR 13 (+1) DEX 18 (+4) CON 15 (+2) Hit Points 123 Armour Class 18 Size Small Cinderous Swipe ( ) Create a blooming cone of fire as you swipe at a foe. Elemental Warp ( ) Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see. Fly ( ) Fly to a target position Dismiss Wild Shape Dismiss your Wild Shape and change back to your original form. Lunar Mend ( + ) Expend spell slots to regain Hit Points while wild shaped. You regain 1d8 hit points per spell slot level. Myrmidon's Immolation ( ) Ignite with incandescent, primordial flames that   Hasten you. Scorching Strike ( ) Lash out with a blazing strike and possibly Burn your target. Hellish Rebuke React to your next attacker with flames that deal 2d10 ⁠ ⁠ Fire . Ethereal Affected entity is incorporeal and can't be Shoved , Thrown , or used as an Improvised Melee Weapon How to learn Classes: Class level 10: Circle of the Moon This action is a variation of: Wild Shape Notes This shape consumes 2 Wild Shape charges, and comes equipped with a Scimitar of Cinder that adds + 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire to every attack. There is no reason to use the normal main hand attack over Scorching Strike which deals additional damage and has a chance to Burn targets. Bugs Per Fire_Myrmidon_Wildshape character stats, this form is supposed to use Dexterity as its spellcasting ability modifier. However, due to a bug where, regardless of the SpellCastingAbilityInheritanceType setting from shapeshift rules, SpellCastingAbility from character stats cannot overwrite SpellCastingAbility from class descriptions, this field is not applied and instead the character's spellcasting ability modifier of the last class the character took a first level in is used. This may not be Wisdom if the character multiclassed from Druid to another class. v t e Druid Subclasses Circle of the Land Circle of the Moon Circle of the Spores Circle of the Stars Wild Shapes Creatures Badger Bear Cat Spider Wolf Dire Raven Deep Rothé Panther Owlbear Sabre-Toothed Tiger Dilophosaurus Air Myrmidon Earth Myrmidon Fire Myrmidon Water Myrmidon Starry Forms Archer Chalice Dragon Lands Arctic Coast Desert Forest Grassland Mountain Swamp Underdark Other class features Cosmic Omen Fungal Infestation Halo of Spores Improved Wild Strike Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Lunar Mend Natural Recovery Nature's Ward Primal Strike Spells Spreading Spores Symbiotic Entity Twinkling Constellations Wild Strike

## Writhing Tide
- **来源**: [Writhing Tide](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Writhing_Tide)
- **分类**: Bonus_actions、Class_actions

Writhing Tide is a class action available to Swarmkeepers which lets them use their swarm to fly a short distance and hover to avoid ground-based hazards. This state lasts for 10 turns during which the Swarmkeeper can reuse this ability each turn without consuming additional resources. Description Condense part of your swarm into a mass that lifts you up. Gain a flying speed of 9 m (30 ft) and become unaffected by surface effects. Properties Cost: Bonus Action  +  Writhing Current Details: Range: 9 m (30 ft) At Higher Levels At Level 7 you are granted 3 Writhing Currents . At Level 9 this is increased to 4 Writhing Currents . Condition: Writhing Tide Writhing Tide Duration: 10 turns Your swarm is protecting you from surface effects. How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Swarmkeeper Notes This the only use for Writhing Currents charges. The immunity to surface effects is not applied until after landing. This means you will not be protected from surface effects when flying into them initially. However, once the Writhing Tide condition is active, it is safe to walk over or fly into such surfaces. v t e Ranger Subclasses Beast Master Gloom Stalker Hunter Swarmkeeper Favoured Enemy Bounty Hunter Keeper of the Veil Mage Breaker Ranger Knight Sanctified Stalker Natural Explorer Beast Tamer Urban Tracker Wasteland Wanderer ( Cold Fire Poison ) Other class features Bestial Fury Companion's Bond Dread Ambusher Melee Ranged Hide Escape the Horde Exceptional Training Extra Attack Gathered Swarm Cloud of Jellyfish Flurry of Moths Legion of Bees Hide in Plain Sight Hunter's Prey Colossus Slayer Giant Killer Horde Breaker Iron Mind Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Mighty Swarm Multiattack Defence Prey's Scent Spells Ranger's Companion Stalker's Flurry Steel Will Superior Darkvision Umbral Shroud Volley Whirlwind Attack Writhing Tide

## Absorb Elements
- **来源**: [Absorb Elements](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Absorb_Elements)
- **分类**: Class_actions、Reactions

Absorb Elements is a passive feature/reaction which absorbs half damage from the next elemental attack targeting the user and adds that element type as an additional 1d6 damage on the user's next attack. Description Absorb elemental damage once per Short Rest . Take half damage from the next elemental attack targeting you, and deal an additional 1d6 of that element type on your next attack. Properties Cost Reaction Details Recharge: Short rest Technical details UIDs Absorb_Elements_Passive Passive feature Interrupt_AbsorbElements Reaction Condition: Absorb Elements: Acid Damage Absorb Elements: Acid Damage Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Absorb Elements: Cold Damage Absorb Elements: Cold Damage Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Absorb Elements: Fire Damage Absorb Elements: Fire Damage Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Absorb Elements: Lightning Damage Absorb Elements: Lightning Damage Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Absorb Elements: Thunder Damage Absorb Elements: Thunder Damage Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage the next time it deals damage with a weapon. How to learn Granted by items: Cloak of Elemental Absorption Cloak of the Weave Notes This reaction halves damage by granting resistance to the elemental damage type when triggered. Since resistances do not stack, this will not reduce the damage further if the user already has the applicable resistances. Absorb Elements can apply its damage bonus multiple times to a single weapon attack. Bugs This reaction cannot be used while affected by Starry Form .
## Accursed Spectre (reaction)
- **来源**: [Accursed Spectre (reaction)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Accursed_Spectre_(reaction))
- **分类**: Class_actions、Reactions

See also: Accursed Spectre (passive feature) Accursed Spectre is a reaction granted to The Hexblade warlocks that allows them to raise a spectre from a fallen enemy cursed by Hexblade's Curse . Description Raise an Accursed Spectre from the soul of a fallen cursed target to fight by your side. The size of the fallen creature will determine whether you raise a Feeble Spectre , Mundane Spectre , or Primordial Spectre . Doesn't work with constructs , elementals , oozes , plants , or undead . Properties Cost Reaction Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) Creature: Feeble Spectre STR 11 DEX 14 (+2) CON 11 INT 10 WIS 10 CHA 11 Duration 10 turns Hit Points 17 Armour Class 12 Size Tiny Summoned when used on a Tiny or Small size corpse. Pluck Soul ( ) Pull your warlock's enemy towards you up to 5 m (17 ft). Right Behind You ( ) Materialise next to your summoner's victim. Creature: Mundane Spectre STR 13 (+1) DEX 14 (+2) CON 11 INT 10 WIS 10 CHA 11 Duration 10 turns Hit Points 31 Armour Class 14 Size Tiny Summoned when used on a Medium size corpse. Devour Soul ( ) Consume the soul of your warlock's enemy while healing the warlock for half the damage. Pluck Soul ( ) Pull your warlock's enemy towards you up to 5 m (17 ft). Right Behind You ( ) Materialise next to your summoner's victim. Creature: Primordial Spectre STR 16 (+3) DEX 14 (+2) CON 11 INT 10 WIS 10 CHA 11 Duration 10 turns Hit Points 48 Armour Class 12 Size Tiny Summoned when used on a Large , Huge , or Gargantuan size corpse. Devour Soul ( ) Consume the soul of your warlock's enemy while healing the warlock for half the damage. Seize Soul ( ) Pull your warlock's enemy towards you up to 10 m / 33 ft. Reap Soul ( ) Unsheathe a set of hexed sickles and rip your warlock's enemy to shreds. Right Behind You ( ) Materialise next to your summoner's victim. How to learn Classes: Class level 6: The Hexblade Notes It is not stated anywhere, but spectres get temporary hit points equal to half the summoners level and deal bonus damage equal to the summoner's Charisma modifier. This feature cannot be used on summoned creatures, either allied or enemy. It also cannot be used on any creature with an effect like Death Ward which revives the creature after dropping to 0 hit points. This is true even after the condition is expended. Accursed Spectres are not traditional summons; they cannot be directly controlled by the player and they are immobile. However, they can teleport to creatures hit by the warlock's Hexed Weapon and take an immediately attack through their Right Behind You reaction. This allows for a degree of indirect control over the spectre. Multiple spectres can be summoned simultaneously. Unlike most other summoning abilities, conjuring a new spectre does not unsummon the existing one. Spectres are immune to the Madness effect from the Abyss Beckoners gloves. Bugs The description does not state it, but this cannot be used on undead . Creatures killed by Cull the Weak will not trigger this reaction. The CharacterStats for this summoned creature does not correctly have the proper DifficultyStatuses set, and as a result the creature loses 30% HP from the Explorer difficulty modifier as if it were a hostile NPC. This reaction cannot be used while affected by Starry Form or when Disguised . v t e Warlock Subclasses The Archfey The Fiend The Great Old One The Hexblade Pact Boon Pact of the Chain Pact of the Blade Pact of the Tome Eldritch Invocations Agonising Blast Armour of Shadows Beast Speech Beguiling Influence Book of Ancient Secrets Devil's Sight Dreadful Word Fiendish Vigour Lifedrinker Mask of Many Faces Minions of Chaos Mire the Mind One with Shadows Otherworldly Leap Repelling Blast Sculptor of Flesh Sign of Ill Omen Thief of Five Fates Whispers of the Grave Other class features Accursed Spectre Armour of Hexes Beguiling Defences Bind Hexed Weapon Dark One's Blessing Dark One's Own Luck Entropic Ward Fey Presence Fiendish Resilience Deepened Pact Hex Warrior Hexblade's Curse Misty Escape Mortal Reminder Mystic Arcanum Spells Thought Shield: Psychic Reflection Thought Shield: Psychic Resistance

Aspect of the Elk is a free action gained by Wildheart Barbarians that have chosen Aspect of the Beast: Elk . This ability allows the Barbarian to grant increased movement speed to you and nearby allies. Description Grant yourself and nearby allies a 1.5 m (5 ft) bonus to Movement Speed Properties Details Range: Self AoE: 18 m (60 ft) Radius Technical details UID Shout_AspectOfTheElk Condition: Aspect of the Elk Aura Aspect of the Elk Aura Duration: Permanent Affected entity and nearby allies have a +1.5 m (5 ft) bonus to Movement Speed . Description You and nearby allies gain a bonus to Saving Throws equal to your Charisma modifier. The aura disappears if you fall Unconscious. Properties Details Range: Self AoE: 3 m (10 ft) Radius Technical details UID Shout_AuraOf_Protection Condition: Aura of Protection (Aura) Aura of Protection Duration: Permanent The creature and its allies within 3 m (10 ft) gain the creature's charisma modifier as a bonus to their saving throws . How to learn Classes: Class level 6: Paladin Notes Although the ability is granted automatically, it needs to be 'cast' in order to activate. One may need to drag the class action from the Spellbook onto the custom toolbar to use it. Once activated, the aura lasts for as long as the class action is available to the character. The tooltip in the level-up interface sometimes lists the saving throw bonus as +0 regardless of the Paladin's actual Charisma modifier. This page is about content exclusive to Honour mode . Bhaal's Edict is an action available to the Boon of Bhaal during combat with Orin in Honour mode . Description Force a creature to become your murderer - if it does not kill another during its next turn, it will die instantly. Condition: Bhaal's Edict Bhaal's Edict If you don't kill another creature before the end of your next turn, you will die instantly. How to learn Used by creatures: Boon of Bhaal Notes Using Move Moonbeam does not count as killing another creature and does not remove the condition. This may be true when casting Moonbeam too. ## Bladesong
- **来源**: [Bladesong](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bladesong)
- **分类**: Class_actions

For the class, see Bladesinging . Bladesong is the signature ability of Bladesinging wizards. Description Invoke the Bladesong. You gain a +2 bonus to Armour Class and your movement speed increases by 3 m (10 ft). You also gain Advantage in Acrobatics and a +2 to Constitution Saving Throws . You also unlock Bladesong Climax and the ability to accumulate Bladesong charges in combat. You can't wear Medium or Heavy Armour or Shields while Bladesinging You must be wielding a dagger , longsword , rapier , scimitar , shortsword , or sickle . Properties Cost Bladesong Power At higher levels At Wizard level 5, the bonus to AC and Constitution Saving Throws increases to +3. At Wizard level 9, the bonus to AC and Constitution Saving Throws increases to +4. Technical details UID Shout_Bladesong Grants: Bladesong Climax Condition: Bladesinging Bladesinging Duration: 10 turns Invoking the Bladesong. You gain a +2/+3/+4 bonus to Armour Class and your movement speed is increased by 3 m (10 ft). You also gain Advantage in Acrobatics and a +2/+3/+4 bonus to Constitution Saving Throws . The AC and saving throws bonus is +2, +3, or +4 at Bladesinger levels 2, 5, or 9 respectively. Condition: Bladesong Damage Charge Bladesong Damage Charge A charge that will increase how much damage you deal to enemies by 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Force when using Bladesong Climax . You can accumulate these charges by casting Level 1 spells or above that are not weapon attacks. Condition: Bladesong Healing Charge Bladesong Healing Charge A charge that increases how much you heal yourself and your allies by 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points when using Bladesong Climax . You can accumulate these charges by attacking with weapons. Condition: Bladesong Impeded Bladesong Impeded Bladesinging impeded by armour/shield/weapon. Until the armour/shield/weapon is removed, your Bladesong won't grant any benefits or let you generate Bladesong Charges. How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Bladesinger Notes While Bladesong can be activated outside of combat, Bladesong charges can only be generated in combat. Some recastable spells like Move Moonbeam do not count towards generating Bladesong Damage Charges . However, the list of exclusions is not comprehensive and other free recasts do generate charges such as Activate Call Lightning . [ 1 ] Bugs The requirement to be wielding a dagger, longsword, etc. applies only to the main hand. While "Bladesong Impeded" will be displayed on the Wizard, Bladesong will still be usable even if the off hand is wielding an incompatible weapon. Bladesinger wizards cannot accumulate climax charges if the weapon in their offhand is not compatible, nor can they use the climax. Bulwark Rebuke is a reaction gained from the Rebuke of the Mighty passive feature that allows you to strike back at an enemy that hits you, dealing damage and knocking them Prone . Description When a foe hits you with a melee attack, deal it 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Force and possibly knock it Prone . The creature takes half damage on a successful Saving Throw . Properties Cost Reaction Damage: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Force Details STR Save ( Spell save DC ) (On Save: Target still takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage but is not knocked Prone .) Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Technical details UID Target_Legendary_ShieldBlow_Riposte Spell flags IsDefaultWeaponAction , IsHarmful , IsMelee Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 1 turn Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Granted by items: Viconia's Walking Fortress Notes As the saving throw to apply prone checks the wielder's spell save DC, Bulwark Rebuke is more effective on casters than it is on martial characters.

## Controlled Chaos

Controlled Chaos is a Wild Magic Sorcerer reaction that triggers a Wild Magic effect after an enemy spellcaster casts a spell . Description Foes may suffer a Wild Magic Surge while casting spells near your fluctuating magic. Properties Cost Reaction How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Wild Magic Sorcerer Notes There is no range restriction for this reaction despite what the description suggests. The surges triggered by this reaction are chosen from a smaller list consisting predominately of the harmful effects. Effect Min Level Controlled Chaos Description Action Surge 1 ✓ You gain an additional action this turn. Blur 1 Each creature within 9 m (30 ft) becomes Blurred . Burning 2 ✓ Each creature and item within 6 m (20 ft) starts burning and takes 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire per turn. Cambion 10 ✓ Summon a cambion from the fiery nexus of the Nine Hells. It is hostile to everyone. Cats and Dogs 2 ✓ Each creature within 9 m (30 ft) is randomly transformed into either a cat or a dog. Enchant Weapons 1 Enchant the weapon of each creature within 6 m (20 ft). Their next attack is a Critical Hit and deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Force . Enlarge/Reduce 2 Each creature within 9 m (30 ft) is randomly Enlarged or Reduced . Entangle 2 ✓ Create a vine surface around yourself, slowing down creatures, possibly Entangling them. Explosive Healing 1 When you hit a target with a spell, heal all creatures within 3 m (10 ft) for 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points per Spell Slot level used. Flight 2 You can Fly until the end of the turn. Fog 1 ✓ Create a cloud of fog around yourself. Creatures within are Heavily Obscured and Blinded . Polymorph 2 ✓ You are transformed into a beast. Resilient Sphere 2 ✓ Enclose yourself in an arcane sphere. You cannot be damaged by attacks or effects from outside the sphere, nor can you damage anything outside the sphere. Movement Speed is halved. Shield 2 Armour Class is increased by 5 and you are immune to the effects of Magic Missile Slow 2 ✓ You are Slowed . Sorcery Points 2 Until the end of your next turn, each spell you cast restores Sorcery Points equal to its Spell Slot level. Speak with Animals 2 Gain the ability to comprehend and communicate with beasts. Spike Growth 2 ✓ Shape a piece of ground around yourself into hard spikes. A creature walking on the spikes takes 2d4 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing for every 1.5 m (5 ft) it moves. Summon Mephit 1 ✓ Summon a hostile mephit. Swap 1 Swap positions with a target each time you cast a spell or cantrip . Telekinesis 2 Able to lift and throw objects and creatures with your mind until the end of your turn. In Tactician difficulty and above, this also gives Flesh the effects of Reckless Attack with both its benefits and drawbacks. Properties Damage: 2~8 2d4 ⁠ Thunder Details STR Save ( DC  13) Range: Self AoE: 2 m (7 ft) Radius Pushes: 3 m (10 ft) Recharge: Short rest Technical details UIDs Shout_Berserk_FleshGolem Active ability triggered by the reaction Interrupt_Berserk_FleshGolem Reaction which triggers at 40% HP SHA_FleshGolem_Berserk Passive feature which grants the reaction Spell flags IsEnemySpell Grants: Multiattack (Flesh) Condition: Berserk Berserk Duration: Until Long rest A frenetic rage racks the affected entity's flesh. Its Multiattacks each deal an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage and knocks targets Prone It also gains Resistance to Slashing, Piercing, and Bludgeoning damage, and has Advantage on Strength Checks and Saving Throws . This frenzy ends if the affected entity regains all its hit points. Condition: Reckless Attack Reckless Attack Duration: Until Long rest You have Advantage on Attack Rolls , but enemies also have Advantage on Attack Rolls against you. How to learn Used by creatures: Flesh Notes Flesh cannot use this reaction while Blinded or afflicted with any other condition in that status group . Flesh will attack his allies while Berserk . This effect can be dispelled with Calm Emotions .

## Cutting Words
- **来源**: [Cutting Words](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Cutting_Words)
- **分类**: Class_actions、Reactions

Cutting Words is a reaction available to the College of Lore bards. It allows them to distract and confuse their foes, potentially causing attacks to miss, or ability checks or saving throws to fail. Description Use your wit to distract a creature and sap its confidence. It receives a -1d6 penalty to Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw . Properties Cost Reaction + Bardic Inspiration Details Range: 18 m (60 ft) At higher levels At bard level 5, the penalty increases to -1d8. At bard level 10, the penalty increases to -1d10. Technical details UIDs Target_CuttingWords Ability triggered by the reaction Interrupt_CuttingWords Reaction which triggers the ability Spell flags HasVerbalComponent , IsHarmful How to learn Classes: Class level 3: College of Lore (via Cutting Words ) Notes Unlike in D&D 5th Edition rules, Cutting Words cannot be applied to damage rolls. However, it can be applied to saving throws (which is normally available only to Eloquence Bards). In most cases using this action causes the caster to make a verbal quip or insult the target, drawing on the same pool of dialogue options as Vicious Mockery . These remarks are fully voice acted, including for characters who do not normally have access to the action. Bugs The visual effect and reaction spell are always directed towards the source of the attack, whether the attack has an attack roll or a saving throw. As a result, when Cutting Words is used to the reduce the saving throw roll of an enemy against a spell cast by a non-enemy creature, the visual effect and reaction spell will still be directed towards the caster. The reaction spell is flagged as a harmful spell, and if the caster is a neutral creature it may become hostile towards the bard and its party. Despite being flagged with HasVerbalComponent , Cutting Words may be used even while silenced. Cutting Words is missing the potency of the bardic dice in its description when displayed in the combat log. Cutting Words checks for the bard level of the source of the attack, instead of the bard that is using Cutting Words ( observer ). As a result, unless the attacker is also a bard, the maximum difference in roll value that Cutting Words can trigger on is 6 instead of the expected 8 or 10 for bards that are level 5 or above. v t e Bard Subclasses College of Glamour College of Lore College of Swords College of Valour Inspiration Bardic Inspiration Combat Inspiration Font of Inspiration Improved Bardic Inspiration Mantle of Inspiration Blade Flourish Defensive Flourish Melee Ranged Slashing Flourish Melee Ranged Mobile Flourish Melee Ranged Other class features Countercharm Cutting Words Expertise Extra Attack Jack of All Trades Magical Secrets Mantle of Majesty: Command Song of Rest Spells

This article is about the reaction. For the corresponding passive feature, see Defensive Attack (passive feature) . Defensive Attack is a free reaction that can be taken when making the first attack with the Defender Greataxe in a turn. It temporarily sacrifices one Enchantment level from the axe to grant the wielder +1 AC and saving throws. Description At the start of a round, you can reduce the weapon's additional attack bonus by 1 to increase your Armour Class and Saving Throws by 1. Properties Details Range: Self Recharge: Per turn Condition: Defensive Stance Defensive Stance Duration: 1 turn You have +1 bonus to Armour Class and Saving Throws . How to learn Granted by items: Defender Greataxe Notes This reaction is only triggered when making the first attack with Defender Greataxe in a round. Subsequent attacks do not give an opportunity to activate this action. The -1 penalty to attack rolls from this effect is applied to the attack that triggers the reaction. The confirmation prompt for the reaction shows the attack roll and AC of the target, so one can decline the reaction if turning a hit into a miss.
## Defensive Duellist
- **来源**: [Defensive Duellist](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Defensive_Duellist)

Defensive Duellist is a reaction obtainable by a feat of the same name. If you are attacked while wielding a Finesse Weapon weapon, you can temporarily increases your Armour Class . You must have at least a 13 in Dexterity in order to take this Feat . Description When attacked with a melee attack, add your Proficiency Bonus to your Armour Class , possibly causing attacks to miss. Requires a Finesse Weapon you are Proficient in. Properties Cost Reaction Details Recharge: Per turn How to learn Granted by features: Defensive Duellist (Feat) Notes Though not explicitly stated, the weapon equipped in the main hand is required to have the Finesse property. Defensive Duellist only triggers when it is capable of turning a melee attack hit into a miss. Defensive Duelist does not change the user's Armour Class. Instead, it subtracts the user's Proficiency Bonus from the enemy's attack roll. Bugs Unlike similar reactions ( Shield Master: Block ), the icon for Defensive Duellist in the reactions tab does not "gray out" when the reaction is unavailable due to an incompatible equipped weapon.
## Defensive Protocol: Bulwark
- **来源**: [Defensive Protocol: Bulwark](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Defensive_Protocol:_Bulwark)
- **分类**: Class_actions

Defensive Protocol: Bulwark is a free action used by the Steel Watcher Titan in response to taking significant damage. The Titan enters a stationary, defensive state where it can unleash a devastating barrage of Hellfire Missiles . Description Hunker down into an Unyielding state and Repair yourself. While hunkered, you can launch Hellfire Missiles and Repel combatants. Properties Details Recharge: Twice per battle Technical details UIDs Shout_SteelWatcher_Quadruped_ActivateBulwarkMode First use unlocked when below 75% HP Shout_SteelWatcher_Quadruped_ActivateBulwarkMode2 Second use unlocked when below 50% HP Spell flags IsEnemySpell Grants: Hellfire Missiles Repelling Protocol Condition: Defensive Protocol: Bulwark Defensive Protocol: Bulwark Duration: 2 turns While in this defensive state, the Steel Watcher becomes Unyielding and can use its Repair Matrix , Hellfire Missiles and Repelling Protocol . Also grants 75 temporary hit points . If the Steel Watcher loses these temporary hit points, he automatically uses Terminate Bulwark Protocol and loses this condition. If hit by a Flashblinder , the Steel Watcher loses this condition. Condition: Unyielding Construct Unyielding Construct Duration: 2 turns Only an attack dealing at least 15 damage can harm this Steel Watcher. Condition: Repair Matrix Repair Matrix Duration: 2 turns At the start of its turn, restorative servos heal this Steel Watcher for 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . How to learn Used by creatures: Steel Watcher Titan Notes In total, while in this state, the Steel Watcher Titan has the following effects: Gains 75 temporary hit points , increased to 200 temporary hit points on Honour mode. Heals 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points per round, increased to 6d8+14 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points on Honour mode. Ignores any damage less than 15 points, with the threshold increased to 40 on Honour mode. Note that this does not reduce the damage of an attack that exceeds the threshold. Becomes immobile. Gains access to Hellfire Missiles and Repel . Loses access to all its other actions such as Multiattack , Launch Protocol: Bola , and Hellfire Curse . This action technically has a once per combat limit but the Steel Watcher Titan is given two identical copies of it. As a result, it can can use this action twice per combat. The Steel Watcher Titan unlocks this action after dropping to certain hit points thresholds. Once it is below 75% HP, it can use the first copy of the ability. It unlocks the second use after dropping to 50% HP.
## Deflect Missiles
- **来源**: [Deflect Missiles](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Deflect_Missiles)
- **分类**: Class_actions、Reactions

This article is about the monk reaction to reduce the damage of a missile attack. For the follow up reaction to throw back the projectile, see Deflect Missiles: Redirect . Deflect Missiles is a reaction gained by monk at level 3. Deflect Missiles allows the monk to reduce incoming damage from ranged weapon attacks and optionally return the projectile. Description Reduce the damage from a ranged weapon attack by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level. If the damage is reduced to 0, you can use a Ki Point to Deflect the Missile . You can only reduce damage from the attack - any additional effects can't be negated. Properties Cost Reaction Technical details UID Interrupt_DeflectMissiles Grants: Deflect Missiles: Redirect How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Monk Notes Reducing damage does not negate any other effects of the attack. Conditions such as Gaping Wounds from Piercing Strike are still applied, even if the damage is reduced to 0. This reaction works against any attack that uses a ranged weapon attack roll. Bugs Damage does not need to be reduced to 0 in order to redirect the attack. Against ranged attacks that fire multiple projectiles, such as Multiattack (Ranged) or dual wielded Hand Crossbows , only the last attack can be deflected to reduce its damage. None of the projectiles can be thrown back with Deflect Missiles: Redirect .

Deflect Missiles is a Monk reaction which allows for throwing a ranged weapon projectile back at an attacker after first catching the missile with Deflect Missiles . Description Use your reflexes to catch a projectile from a ranged weapon attack and shoot it back at your attacker. Properties Cost Ki Point Damage Unarmed ⁠ Bludgeoning Details Melee Unarmed Attack Roll Range: 18 m (60 ft) Technical details UIDs Projectile_Deflect_Missiles Actual attack action Interrupt_DeflectMissiles_Return Reaction which triggers the attack Spell flags IsAttack , IsHarmful How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Monk Notes This attack counts as a melee unarmed attack and benefits from everything that normally affects Unarmed Strikes such as Tavern Brawler . If two Monks are hit by a single Volley from the same Ranger, they can both simultaneously redirect the damage back to sender.

Description When you roll ⁠ Thunder or ⁠ Lightning damage, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage instead. Properties Cost Channel Divinity Charge Technical details UIDs Interrupt_DestructiveWrath Reaction DestructiveWrath Passive feature which grants the reaction How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Tempest Domain Notes The reaction prompt will be shown before the attack roll of a triggering action is made. ## Divine Intervention
- **来源**: [Divine Intervention](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Divine_Intervention)
- **分类**: Class_actions

Divine Intervention is a Cleric one-time free action that can perform one of several large-scale actions. Description Call upon your deity in your moment of greatest need. Once they interfere, your deity will never do so again in this manner. The caster can only use this feature once in their adventure. Properties Details Range: Self Options When using Divine Intervention, you have four options to choose from. Arm Thy Servant Main article: Divine Intervention: Arm Thy Servant Call upon your deity to grant you a legendary weapon forged in the fires of your holy bond. This ability creates a legendary mace in the cleric's inventory and immediately equips it. If you respec your cleric, the Devotee's Mace does not go away. If you have multiple cleric characters, or use Withers to respec a character who otherwise would not be a cleric, you can get multiple copies of the Devotee's Mace. Golden Generosity Main article: Divine Intervention: Golden Generosity Call upon your deity to provide you with a rich bounty of potions and Camp Supplies . This ability spawns a chest Bestowed Bounty on the ground next to the cleric, containing Camp Supplies , superior or supreme healing potions , and six to seven elixirs. If you re-spec your cleric, the Bestowed Bounty chest will vanish, but any items that were inside it will drop on the ground in the same location. Opulent Revival Main article: Divine Intervention: Opulent Revival Resurrect fallen companions with half their hit points, and restore all nearby allies as if they had Long Rested. This ability applies to allies within a 60 ft (18 m) radius. Sunder the Heretical Main article: Divine Intervention: Sunder the Heretical Call upon your deity to bring forth a radiant cataclysm upon all nearby enemies. This ability deals 8d10 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage to all enemies in a 50 ft (15 m) radius. Targets can succeed on a Wisdom saving throw to take half damage. Technical details UID Shout_DivineIntervention Spell flags IsLinkedSpellContainer Variants Divine Intervention: Arm Thy Servant Divine Intervention: Golden Generosity Divine Intervention: Opulent Revival Divine Intervention: Sunder the Heretical How to learn Classes: Class level 10: Cleric Used by creatures: Hope Notes A character cannot use Divine Intervention more than once, even by respecing . However, players can use respecing to get Divine Intervention a number of times equal to the number of characters they have available, since each character may use it once. Both Arm Thy Servant and Golden Generosity can be used outside of combat and the items they create stick around indefinitely (although, of course, items created by Golden Generosity are consumable). The items generated in the Bestowed Bounty are tied to each save. The first cast of Bestowed Bounty on a save always gives the same items, the second a different set, and so on. This means that save-scumming to get a better roll on the chest is not possible. The base value of the Devotee's Mace , created by Arm Thy Servant , is 640 gold. It costs 200 gold to respec a character into a cleric, create the Devotee's Mace, and then change back (or to recruit a hireling and respec them into a cleric), keeping in mind that pickpocketing Withers does not have negative consequences. While there are arguably more effective – and less tedious – ways to obtain extra gold, the Devotee's Mace can be sold as a source of income, if (somehow) running low on funds at levels 10 and above. v t e Cleric Subclasses Death Domain Knowledge Domain Life Domain Light Domain Nature Domain Tempest Domain Trickery Domain War Domain Channel Divinity Charge Charm Animals and Plants Cloak of Shadows Destructive Wrath Dampen Elements Guided Strike Invoke Duplicity Knowledge of the Ages Preserve Life Radiance of the Dawn Read Thoughts Touch of Death War God's Blessing Divine Strike Radiant (Melee) Radiant (Ranged) Poison (Melee) Poison (Ranged) Cold (Melee) Cold (Ranged) Fire (Melee) Fire (Ranged) Lightning (Melee) Lightning (Ranged) Necrotic (Melee) Necrotic (Ranged) Thunder (Melee) Thunder (Ranged) Weapon (Melee) Weapon (Ranged) Other class features Acolyte of Nature Blessed Healer Blessing of the Trickster Blessings of Knowledge Destroy Undead Disciple of Life Divine Intervention Expertise Improved Warding Flare Inescapable Destruction Potent Spellcasting Reaper Spells Thunderbolt Strike Turn Undead War Priest Warding Flare Wrath of the Storm

## Divine Smite (reaction)
- **来源**: [Divine Smite (reaction)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Divine_Smite_(reaction))
- **分类**: Class_actions

This article is about the reaction to trigger Divine Smite post-hit. For the action to use Divine Smite directly, see Divine Smite . For general information about smites, see Smite . Divine Smite is a Paladin reaction. The reaction can be done after successfully hitting a target with any melee weapon attack , and can be used multiple times in one attack (e.g. while dual-wielding). It is the reaction version of Divine Smite . Description Your weapon deals an additional 2d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage, increased by 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage when attacking Fiends or Undead . Properties Cost Level 1 Spell Slot Damage: 3~24 2d8 ⁠ Radiant + 1d8 ⁠ Radiant (If the target is undead or a fiend) At higher levels When Divine Smite is cast at 2nd level or higher, damage increases by 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Radiant for each spell slot level above 1st. This damage is capped to 5d8, so using a spell slot above 4th spell level adds no further damage. Technical details UIDs Interrupt_Smite_Divine Interrupt_Smite_Divine_2 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_3 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_4 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_5 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_6 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_Critical Interrupt_Smite_Divine_Critical_2 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_Critical_3 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_Critical_4 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_Critical_5 Interrupt_Smite_Divine_Critical_6 Spell flags IsHarmful , IsMelee How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Paladin Used by creatures: Anders , Zevlor , and Minthara Notes This does not cost a Reaction point. This reaction can be triggered on any melee weapon attack that is not a Divine Smite . This allows for smiting on offhand attacks, weapon actions like Cleave , or special attacks like Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack . It can even trigger when using a Smite spell like Thunderous Smite . Using Divine Smite directly through the action is equivalent to triggering the reaction on a basic attack. The reaction is split into one reaction for normal hits called Divine Smite and one for critical hits called Divine Smite: Critical Hit per spell slot level. This means that with level 2 spell slots, you will have four reactions, two for each level. By default the Divine Smite: Critical Hit reaction is set to auto-confirm and the Divine Smite is disabled. In-game Divine Smite is listed under Class Actions in your spellbook. Divine Smite as a reaction cannot be triggered when attacking from invisibility. See Smite for additional details that apply to all variants of Smite.
