Text [The volume describes the full process of 'Unburdening' in exact detail. Valuable targets are identified from those who seek out the services of the House of Grief . If they are willing to pay, they proceed to the Mapping of the Heart , where the Inquirer of Grief will question them while discreetly probing their thoughts for anything that can be of use to the Lady of Loss . Following this, targets are ushered downwards to stand before the Mirror of Loss. Given the correct prompts by the Inquirer of Grief, the target will surrender memories to the mirror, for the benefit of all of Lady Shar's children. In the same stroke, the mirror can remove memories of what they have seen in the Cloister , as well as whatever they believe to be the source of their troubles. Then they can be turned loose, blissfully ignorant of the offering they made.]
## The Unclaimed
- **来源**: [The Unclaimed](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Unclaimed)
- **分类**: Books

The Unclaimed is a sturdily-bound story of a Cleric of Shar whose soul was never claimed from the City of Judgement . The sturdily-bound story of a cleric of Shar whose soul was never claimed from the City of Judgement. Properties Books Author: Church of Shar Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GEN_Planes_CityofJudgment UUID e8183f9e-217a-49a9-96ae-b61329e78a5f Where to find On a lectern on the east side of the room in Refectory X: -166 Y: -345 Text In life, her service had been impeccable. Daily did she devote herself to the Lady of Loss . Daily did she free herself from the tyranny of memory. All, in time, was lost to her - her relations, her preferences, even her own name. Upon the altar of her devotion placed she the ultimate offering: her emptied mind. And when she died, when she awoke in death and found herself standing in the pale and faded City of Judgement, she waited for the Lady of Loss to retrieve her. A million souls and more passed her in colourless gusts, but no hand materialised in her hand; no voice whispered instruction in her ear; no guidance proffered itself from the bleached and barren sky. Time, immaterial time, passed around her like air, coming and going. And still, the goddess did not come for Her devotee. Kelemvor pitied her, as much as the Lord of the Dead is able, but could not intervene. This cleric of the Lady of Loss, unclaimed despite her worthiness, might yet have one more lesson to learn: that not of forgetting, but being forgotten.

The Thorms are but collectors: collectors of coin, glory, blood, and more yet. I, however, collected that which holds the most value: information. The Mason caught my eye. Straight are his steps and faithful are his words, for as long as drink does not touch his tongue. Two drops of Blackfire whiskey, and he sings his heart's true tune. He calls Father a tyrant, a coward, a traitor. He beseeches the Moonmaiden to shine upon him once more. Dangerous words. I have told Father; he will surely silence the Mason and make him an example. Meanwhile, the Mason drawls his heresy. It is all I can do not to mock him to his very face. --- 6 Flamerule My own methods, used against me! The ale she fed me was poisoned - and by my own hand! My truth serum was all too effective. I professed the lot: the poisoned drinks, Malus' 'treatments', the interrogations - all of it. She means to reveal our 'schemes' to the Baldur's Gate authorities. Unless, of course, I grace her palm with more gold than Gerringothe could muster. Father would have my head if he knew - or worse yet, donate me to Malus. Such is my good fortune that I possess all manner of barrels. She should make a perfect fit. --- 23 Elient The Harpers came too close - they poisoned Father Ketheric himself, yet he professes no ill effects. Malus insists it a fluke. Doctor he may be, but he is no less a foll for it: Father has achieved that of which I can only dream: immortality. I have long suspected. I can guess Father's purpose, but I cannot fathom the means. ## The Watch and the Steel Watch
- **来源**: [The Watch and the Steel Watch](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Watch_and_the_Steel_Watch)

The Watch and the Steel Watch describes the security in the Lower and Upper Cities of Baldur's Gate . This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_GeneralLoreBook_TheWatchAndTheSteelWatch UUID 52aecfcc-11cd-4570-bb8a-406cb38ce95d Where to find Basilisk Gate Barracks X: 156 Y: -6 Baldur's Mouth X: 40 Y: -44 Text Famously - or perhaps notoriously - the mercenary force known as The Flaming Fist handles Baldur's Gate's law enforcement duties in the Lower City and Outer City, including Wyrm's Crossing . But what about the exclusive Upper City , home to the wealthy and powerful? There, order is kept by a highly disciplined force simply called the Watch . Though derrided by the Fists as mere toy-soldier bodyguards to the city's partriars, spit-and-polish phonies who won't get their hands dirty fighting real crime, the truth is quite different - as you'll find in short order if you break the law in the Upper City. The Watch are well-trained and authorised to use lethal force if patriars are threatened. Which brings us to the Steel Watch , those new clanking automatons that share their name with the guardians of the Upper City but to date have only been deployed in support of the Flaming Fist. Their creator, Lord Gortash , has stated that his watchers are intended to help protect all of Baldur's Gate - but it seems the Marshal of the Watch Citadel is sceptical and waiting for proof before admitting them to a role in the Upper City.
## The Way of the Wanderer

The Way of the Wanderer is about the meaning of home without a permanent domicile. This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID S_HAV_TieflingSurvivors_SuperOldMagicBook UUID 2def7912-e561-4d60-a073-ddf64b7d3981 Where to find At the bar in Last Light Inn at X: -75 Y: 141 Text How to convey that which I know, deep within myself, to be true? Would that I could bring each of you reading these words into this head of mine, this heart of mine, feeling as one. perhaps then I could speak what words fail to describe. That home isn't home unless you're far from home. That love isn't love unless it unleashes you. That the sky is infinitely big as long as you can always see it. Do I make sense? I think not. But perhaps the peripatetic patter of these words can create some rhythm approximating the joy of feet on road, with naught but everything ahead.

Properties Books Author: Church of Ilmater Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_UNI_WYR_SaintsOfTheTemple_000 UUID f011da74-438c-4312-a821-a984a1c2e6b3 Where to find On a bookshelf in the Open Hand Temple Cellar X: 8 Y: -1019 Text [The book tells the story of a patriar woman who gave up her fortune to become a cleric of Ilmater in service in the Outer City and now seeks to be canonised after her death.] Herein is the full of true account of my bid to be canonised after my death as Saint Brigid of Ilmater, the Broken God, he of Compassion and Mercy, the One who Endures. I lived a blessed life of every privilege a patriar woman can fathom; my parents were loving and generous, my community warm; our larder was always full to bursting. But in the years after the death of Sarevok , my eyes were opened to the world as it is – a world of pain and danger. A world where evil, if left unchecked, can thrive. I realised that my blessings had a cost – why had I so much where others had so little?. I could no longer remain in the gilded Elysium of the Upper City and sought to see the world as it truly was.

## To Take Control
- **来源**: [To Take Control](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/To_Take_Control)
- **分类**: Books

To Take Control is part of a memoir. This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: Enver Gortash Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp Where to find In the Counting House High Security Vault nº6 at X: -718 Y: 884 Text Gortash Private Memoir Notes, Number 9 To Take Control We were deep in Mephisto's vault, burgling the Crown of Karsus , when I saw next to the crown that the wily archdevil had a portfolio labelled 'Accelerated Grand Design'. I couldn't resist taking that as well. The portfolio contained plans compiled by a mad alhoon known only as Blue Apex for a version of the illithid resurgence, a Grand Design that called for mass tadpoling of both friends and enemies - but not to convert the tadpoled into mind flayers , but rather to suspend that ceremorphosis under powerful magic to create a vast and unconscious hive mind commanded by an enhanced elder brain. My mind, trained in the tyrannical tenets of Bane , instantly saw that this was a means to perpetrate a powerful religious hoax, a mass movement controlled, ultimately, by none other than myself. For who but the Chosen of Bane could master so grand a scheme? Notes See also: Accelerated Grand Design The Astral Prism Heist

## Tombstone Shop Notes
- **来源**: [Tombstone Shop Notes](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tombstone_Shop_Notes)
- **分类**: Books

Tombstone Shop Notes contains observations on the activity around Candulhallow's Tombstones . This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: Alexander Rainforest Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_LOW_SerialKiller_RainforestJournal UUID 2e1d3087-82d8-4e9d-82cb-5958e568815f Where to find On a desk in the basement of Rainforest's Home X: -1420 Y: 1051 Text I'd come across several pointers toward the Candulhallow's Tombstones shop, so I decided to use my spare time for a while to watch it for suspicious activity. Indeed, the place is strange: it seems disconnected from Candulhallow's main mortuary business over in Eastway, in fact they don't seem to sell anything at all. There's one callow shop lad who hangs about looking bored, otherwise there's just the occasional customer who enters and then stays inside for a while, sometimes for hours. When they leave, these customers seem different somehow, I'd swear I saw one go in and out in the same clothes but leave wearing a different face. Must stay alert, I think the shop lad may have noticed me hanging around. I'll give this observation just one more day.

## Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. IV: The Risen Road
- **来源**: [Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. IV: The Risen Road](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Traveller's_Guide_to_the_Sword_Coast_Vol._IV:_The_Risen_Road)
- **分类**: Books

Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. IV: The Risen Road is part of a larger collection of guide books. An old, cheaply-bound book that's starting to fall to pieces. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GEN_World_GuideRisenRoad UUID 2aed64cd-0eb0-4351-9259-183d3f345910 Where to find Sold by Nansi Gretta In the Secluded Chamber at X: -58 Y: 69 At the Risen Road at X: 111 Y: 560 In a the southeastern bookcase inside the atrium of the House of Healing at X: -182 Y: 36 On the first floor of Moonrise Towers Text [The stained, well-thumbed pages filled with travelling advice that seems to be decades out of date] ... those who seek to journey to the coast from the interior regions lying to the east will typically seek out the Risen Road. Running parallel to the River Chionthar , the Risen Road provides an overland route all the way from Elturel to Baldur's Gate , and has proven tempting to travellers seeking an alternate to the river barges that sail the Chionthar. A portion of the road approximately halfway between Elturel and Baldur's Gate has in recent years developed into an enclave for Selûne worship, with a temple of not insignificant splendour lying near the road. Indeed an entire village, Moonhaven , has developed alongside the temple, and can provide food and shelter to weary travellers. Farther east lies the citadel of Moonrise Towers , where a toll is required for onward passage of goods and folk alike. Some are tempted to go off-road in order to avoid the toll, however bandits and other dangers may cause them to pay a much steeper price...
## Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. VIII: The Outer City
- **来源**: [Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. VIII: The Outer City](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Traveller's_Guide_to_the_Sword_Coast_Vol._VIII:_The_Outer_City)
- **分类**: Books

Traveller's Guide to the Sword Coast Vol. VIII: The Outer City is part of a larger collection of guide books. An old, poorly-bound volume that's lost half of its yellowed pages. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GEN_World_GuideOuterCity UUID ea3786b5-2219-454c-87de-31743d34d359 Where to find Sold by Nansi Gretta On a bookshelf in the office at the very back of the Zhentarim Basement X: 302 Y: -171 On a bookshelf in Arfur's Basement Text ... overland travellers nearing Baldur's Gate have been known to smell the city before they clap eyes on it. This is thanks to what is known as the Outer City - the area that houses much of what Baldur's Gate needs to survive and thrive, but at the same time would rather not keep within its walls. Tanneries, stockyards, slaughterhouses, saltworks and less-than-regulated markets abound here, as well shanties and camps for the less fortunate souls who are drawn to the city. It is the author's firm opinion that respectable travellers should never dawdle in such a place, no matter how tempting its base attractions may be after a long journey. Instead they should make way promptly (while paying strict attention to any valuables on their person or in their baggage) then see about presenting themselves to one of the main entrances to the Lower City, such as the famed Basilisk Gate. Once entry has been secured, they can consider themselves in the city proper...
## Treatise on the Antimagic Properties of Sussur Tree Flowers

Properties Books Author: Lenore De Hurst Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID S_UND_ClericResearch UUID 606542f8-af80-4102-b849-84e73d8a7f12 Where to find Near the entrance to the backyard of Arcane Tower X: -27 Y: -292 Text THE ANTIMAGIC PROPERTIES OF SUSSUR TREE FLOWERS By L. De Hurst For those knowing about sussur trees , their magical properties have always been a topic of debate; not only their ability to create an antimagic aura, which is complete enough that even those unattuned to the Weave can feel its effect, but also - and most interestingly to those living in the World Above - the ways its roots, bark, and flowers can be harnessed to make magic items. Rumours of such items are rare, but spread in settlements bordering the Underdark . Their existence, however, has never been confirmed by any of our clerics , nor by any other reputable scholars. I hypothesised that these items are no mere legends, and indeed, in this treatise I will endeavour to explain how I myself created items that have antimagic properties, and that use the magical absorption of sussur tree flowers as a power source. [Lines have been drawn on the following pages, as if the author intended to fill them with writing, but the remainder of the thin book is blank.]
## Tusky Grins
- **来源**: [Tusky Grins](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tusky_Grins)
- **分类**: Books

Tusky Grins is an excerpt of a book written about cannibal Half-Orcs . This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: Joyce Ringwarble Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_GeneralLoreBook_TheHalfOrcCannibalsAmongYou UUID 419084c9-6002-480a-a025-ae1c4580b8fe Text [Excerpt from Joyce Ringwarble's Tusky Grins What I don't understand is why they are not simply rounded up and sterilised. When I confront people with that idea, some nod, and smile, and make placid little comments. Some grimace or laugh and move swiftly on. Some actually recoil. And there are those who grow angry, and it is to them I relate this story: My cousin, Penelope , spent her life championing half-orcs (and all piggy-eyed orc peoples) in her writing. She interviewed and befriended many of their kind, and one day, without warning, one of them took her daughter from her crib, and he ate her. Not gobbled up. Nothing fairytale here. He chewed the child's fingers while she screamed and waved a bloody stump. And he smiled at my cousin. That was what drove her mad, I think. Beware, dear reader. Beware their tusky grins. Notes See also: Adopters of Culture

## Unpublished Portents
- **来源**: [Unpublished Portents](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unpublished_Portents)
- **分类**: Books

The author of Unpublished Portents suggests that the disappearance of fog in Grey Harbour and Baldur's Gate is an omen. This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: Katie Lowlochden Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp Where to find In a row of books in the House of Grief at X: -275 Y: 10 Text Unpublished Portents by Katie Lowlochden. As a blend of aeromancy - the art of divining the future from atmospheric conditions - and hydromancy - diviation through water - fog divination represents an experimental and as yet inconclusive praxis. Take the cases of Grey Harbour and Baldur's Gate. Soothsayers took to crafting masks from the dense, milk-pale fog blanketing these places, the expressions on those masks indicating positive or negative outcomes in the lives of those who originally commissioned them. Now those banks of fog have retreated, presenting an intriguing omen all its own...

Urban Exploration - The Undercity ! describes a sprawling underground beneath Baldur's Gate . This paper is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_Sewers_UrbanExplorationTheUndercity UUID 3fdacf17-1a27-46b8-b12a-24335e5c6ea2 Where to find Bonecloak's Apothecary X: -25 Y: -26 Basilisk Gate Barracks X: 151 Y: -7 Second floor of The Lodge X: -202 Y: -77 On a table in Rainforest's Home X: -99 Y: -112 Text Intrepid hobbyists who pursue the urban exploration of Baldur's Gate will find no greater challenge than that offered by discovering the dark realm beneath the city's streets. Everyone knows, of course, that the city's sanitation needs are served by extensive sewer tunnels through which water flows, carrying wastes downhill into Grey Harbour. Once you find your way into these sewers through one of the round street access hatches, you will enter a noisome but intriguing domain, haunted mainly by the half-civilised kobold tribe that maintains the pipes and culverts. And somewhere, hidden in its far corners, the sewers are said to connect to the long-forgotten tunnels of the truly haunted Undercity Ruins ! It's thrilling to think about exploring that dangerous region, but for liability reasons this author cannot recommend it.

Properties Books Author: Volo Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_Book_B_VoloCGBN UUID f5eb9707-169e-47ce-bb3d-5d25d6fa8aa6 Where to find Near Volo in Sacred Pool X: 186 Y: 545 Near Auntie Ethel's shop in The Hollow X: 195 Y: 547 Text [The book is handwritten in a swinging scrawl. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_GeneralLoreBook_WallOfTheFaithless UUID 517532d1-e1c4-4c89-ae0e-2b191c3e3b5b Where to find In a Stack of Books atop a display case in the Archive of the House of Hope X: -6537 Y: 2904 In a Row of Books in Szarr Palace Ramparts X: -71 Y: -21 Text At the core of the Fugue Plane's barren ash-gray wasteland stands the City of Judgement with its Crystal Spire jutting above the streets and the influx of souls. ## What Abides Below
- **来源**: [What Abides Below](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/What_Abides_Below)
- **分类**: Books

What Abides Below is a common Book which offers a few minor details about the history of Baldur's Gate, and suggests that there may be a mystery to explore within its sewer system. This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_GeneralLoreBook_UndercityLegends UUID 4595eed7-ac54-43e4-b28f-2d574717c2cf Where to find In the basement of Rainforest's Home at X: 1421 Y: 1052 Sold by Nansi Gretta Text Plamondon tells us that Grey Harbour was a small coastal village before Balduran returned with his vast sea-treasure and founded a great city here. But the vast subterranean ruins hidden beneath our modern city's sewer system tell a very different story. There was a city on the bight of the Lower Chionthar ages before Balduran built his Seatower , a metropolis of grand boulevards and granite towers open to the sky before the unknown cataclysm that split them to their foundations and then swallowed them into the bedrock. Who were these forgotten people who lived in the age before Balduran? Perhaps more importantly, who or what still lives in the ruins of that tumbledown port town below? What things, creatures, or creations, lurk deep beneath our streets - and do they have designs on what we like to think of as our world on the surface above? Notes The Undercity Ruins is most likely "the vast subterranean ruins" the text is referring to. Otherwise, the text could instead refer to the The Tourmaline Depths .

## Wizardsbane Oil Recipe
- **来源**: [Wizardsbane Oil Recipe](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wizardsbane_Oil_Recipe)
- **分类**: Books

Wizardsbane Oil Recipe contains a recipe for creating Wizardsbane Oil . This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: Haskinn Xhesilaphin Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_Alchemy_WizardsbaneOil UUID 30d66533-b41f-47cd-a317-c901bcb092b5 Text Yet another good day! They are strung out on a string like pearls, long may they continue. My pain is still bad (a dragonborn without scales is, as most people can tell simply looking at me, immensely ache-worthy and sore, but yes, indeed, another fine and fair day. I sat outside the Elfsong and enjoyed a bit of sun, and there my new friend Deimric found me. Deimric is a human, once naive and now a little wiser. A solid adventurer, much like my old (and perhaps never-to-be-seen-again) friend Nikros. Deimric asked me if he could learn to brew something that would counteract all these spellcasters he's ben coming up against recently in his wanderings and mercenary work. I outlined the following: Prepare Essence of Gremishka Tail with any Suspension and you will derive one does of Oil of Wizardsbane. Very useful against pesky spellcasters. Deimric clapped me on the back, apologising profusely as I winced and grumbled. In truth I did not mind. Friendship and a little sunshine had softened me a touch. Another good day indeed!

## Ye Follye of Karsus

Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp UID BOOK_GLO_SorcerousSundries_KarsusStory UUID ea61964d-fd13-40c9-8b75-9b00e0ee5812 Where to find Sorcerous Sundries , both in the bookshelves and sometimes sold by Tolna Tome-Monger Text [This ancient water-damaged tome is largely illegible except for the following.] ...did Karsus, mystic, autodidact, in all his vainglory, disdainful as ever of received wisdom, proclaim that, crisis-bound, he would safeguard the magic tapestry of all wizardry by supplanting the failing weavegod Mystryl with another immortal guardian, wiser and stronger of mind. Who could that be, asked the Netherese, amazed, and Karsus gave them reply, Who but I? Have I not mastered all spells that are known and divers others that are not? Canst thou but wait, implored Lord Shadow, until... Notes Karsus was a powerful arcanist in the ancient Netheril which by mistake brought its fall. He also forged Crown of Karsus . Mystryl was the previous goddess of Magic, until she sacrificed herself and reincarnated as Mystra . See Karsus , Mystryl and Netheril on Forgotten Realms Wiki.

## You've Got Friends in the Guild
- **来源**: [You've Got Friends in the Guild](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/You've_Got_Friends_in_the_Guild)
- **分类**: Books

You've Got Friends in the Guild is a book supporting Nine-Fingers Keene and The Guild . This book is redolent with the enticing smell of paper and ink. Properties Books Author: unknown Rarity: Common Weight: 0.5 kg (1 lb) Price: 14 gp Where to find Baldur's Mouth at X: 64 Y: -42 In a Backpack in the Lower City Sewers at X: -147 Y: 903 Text [Introduction to this blood-splattered piece of propaganda] Unkind people say to me, 'But how come the Guild carved up the Lower City like so much pumpkin? Slicing it into segments for kingpins to rule from the shadows?' To which I can only shrug, and reply, 'Delegation, mate. How else are they supposed to get anything done?' To carry the analogy a bit, the pumpkin was ripe, and if it weren't cut by the Guild, somebody else would have. Me, I'm grateful it was Nine Fingers and her organisation what got the carving knife out. Unlike a lot of vested interest in this city, the Guild actually want what's best for the city. Their view is this: if you got to have crime, better it be organised crime!

## Basilisk Oil
- **来源**: [Basilisk Oil](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Basilisk_Oil)
- **分类**: Potions

Basilisk Oil is a Consumable ( Potion ). When used, it restores a petrified creature back to its organic form. Extracted from a basilisk's gullet, this thick, grey oil swirls slowly in its container. Properties Potions Single Use Rarity: Common Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 10 gp UID OBJ_Oil_Of_The_Basilisk UUID 212ca846-4766-4370-8847-454e59751598 Stats OBJ_Oil_Of_The_Basilisk Effect Bonus Action Administer the potion Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft) Turn a Petrified creature back to its organic form Action Throw the potion. Range: 18 m (60 ft) Turn a Petrified creature back to its organic form AoE: 1 m (3 ft) Radius Where to find Sold by: Boney at the Circus of the Last Days in Rivington (2 per long rest) Quartermaster Talli at the Last Light Inn (1 per long rest) In the Apothecary's Cellar in the Blighted Village at X: -667 Y: -355 In a heavy chest behind a wall of spiderwebs in the Underdark at X: 81 Y: -206 On a table in the secret basement of the Arcane Tower at X: 146 Y: -421 Usage This item can be administered to the six Petrified Drow ( Arcagh , Artimezt , Dhourn , Izwae , Moy , and Tecothy ) in the Underdark . This item can be administered to the three Petrified Debtors in Hope's Prison . Doing so, however, turns them into dust and lets them disappear. This item can be administered to Efrin Hammerborn in Auntie Ethel's Overgrown Tunnel . However, doing so without killing Ethel first results in him dying from his condition. Notes Unlike most potions, Basilisk Oil cannot be directly consumed by the user, but must instead administered to another creature or Thrown . To get the Basilisk Oil in the Arcane Tower, the party must first obtain Guiding Light to get to the basement of the building. Alternatively, the party can pass a perception check along the eastern wall on the top floor of the Arcane Tower, revealing a lever that unlocks a path to the basement from the ground floor of the tower. Passive features [ edit section | visual editor ] Basilisk Oil has 1 hit point . ## Broken Promises
- **来源**: [Broken Promises](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Broken_Promises)
- **分类**: Potions

Broken Promises is one of Ethel's special potions that grants both a positive and harmful effect. A parasite swims in the bottom of this bottle, fat with strength. Properties Potions Single Use Rarity: Common Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 1 gp UID CONS_Hag_Broken_Promises UUID 3575950d-c41a-448d-bb2d-cd08c78c88c6 Effect Bonus Action Consume the potion to inflict Broken Promises on yourself. Condition: Broken Promises Broken Promises Duration: Until Long rest Strength is increased by 2 until the next Long Rest . Upon resting, Strength is indefinitely reduced by 1. Where to find At the end of the ⁠ Overgrown Tunnel , in the Acrid Workshop Notes This is the only potion in Auntie Ethel's workshop with a short-term benefit and long-term detriment. Attempting to use Remove Curse triggers the detriment immediately. This does not stack with items which set strength to a specific number, such as Elixir of Hill Giant Strength . If the player character wants the potion's short-term benefit, its negative effect can be mitigated with the following strategies: Killing the character who consumed the potion (they must actually be Dead and not rolling death saves) and reviving them with Withers or a Scroll of Revivify removes the effect. However, this also removes certain other 'permanent' effects, such as Loviatar's Love . Respec with Withers into a build which does not utilize strength. Switch to the Club of Hill Giant Strength as a main weapon. If one plans to take a story path which permanently removes one character from the party roster (such as sacrificing someone to BOOOAL ), this potion can be given to them. Similarly, the potion can be given to a hireling one plans to later dismiss. Consume the potion after taking the final long rest at the end of the game. Drinking the potion grants the ⁠ An Acquired Taste to party members with the Guild Artisan background.

## Potion of Angelic Reprieve
- **来源**: [Potion of Angelic Reprieve](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Potion_of_Angelic_Reprieve)
- **分类**: Potions

Potion of Angelic Reprieve is a Consumable ( Potion ). It has a beneficial utility effect. The motion of the shimmering liquid going back and forth in its vial is somnambulant - you know drinking it will bring the comfort of a warm, enveloping blanket. Properties Potions Single Use Rarity: Rare Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 90 gp UID ALCH_Solution_Potion_Rest_Lesser UUID b0ff8d30-5825-49d4-8cd4-ebf3a3d0a024 Stats ALCH_Solution_Potion_Rest_Lesser Effect Bonus Action Consume the potion to apply Potion of Angelic Relief on yourself. Condition: Potion of Angelic Relief Potion of Angelic Relief Duration: 2 turns Affected entity falls asleep for 2 rounds. When it wakes up, it receives the effects of a Short Rest and all 1st and 2nd level spell slots are restored. If interrupted before the duration expires, the effects will not apply. Where to find Sold by: Lann Tarv at Moonrise Towers ( Shadow-Cursed Lands ) Lucretious at the Circus of the Last Days ( Rivington ) Notes This item can only be purchased, not crafted. Although this item should be able to be crafted via Alchemy by combining Essence of Unicorn Horn (procured from Unicorn Horn ) and any Salt , Unicorn Horns are (perhaps somewhat ironically) not to be found in the game. This potion is particularly useful for a Warlock , due to the class regaining all spell slots after a Short Rest . This potion allows Sorcerers to transform their level 1 and 2 spell slots into sorcery points to be used later - for creating more spell slots or metamagic - with the following procedure. The exact number of sorcery points gained varies depending on the number of spell slots spent. Repeatedly Create Sorcery Points using Level 1 Spell Slots and Level 2 Spell Slots until all are spent. Consume this potion to restore all level 1 and 2 spell slots. Steps 1 and 2 can be repeated as long as you have potions. Consume the trove of Sorcery Points as desired. Bugs The potion is not programmed to restore Divination Wizard prophecies , likely an oversight. This potion does not restore abilities granted by items which use the OncePerShortRestPerItem cooldown type, but does restore abilities granted by items which use the OncePerShortRest cooldown type, contrary to Potion of Angelic Slumber which restores both types of Long and Short Rest-cooldown abilities on items. Where to find Carried by Ch'r'ai W'wargaz Carried by Stalker Svignee in the Upper City Sewers Crafted via Alchemy by combining Essence of Planetar Feather (procured from Planetar Feather ) and any Suspension Sold by Koll the Red in High Hall Inside a Rustic Chest downstairs in The Waning Moon at X: -205 Y: -86 Inside a locked Opulent Chest in the boudoir in the House of Hope Inside a locked Gilded Chest in the hallway between the boudoir and the archive in the House of Hope Inside each Gilded Chest near the brain stem in High Hall Notes This potion does not reset the number of short rests that the character can take before their next long rest, although it does restore a bard's Song of Rest , which can provide a short rest. It restores once-per-long-rest item abilities, but only certain illithid powers . [ See: Bugs ] This potion cannot be applied by throwing; it can only be drunk. Bugs After this potion is consumed, unequipping any equipment or saving and then loading the savegame depletes any of the potion-replenished long and short rest abilities on a character's items again. Illithid powers which are not restored by the potion include: Illithid Persuasion , Luck of the Far Realms , Psionic Dominance , and Freecast . The potion does not restore Portent Dice. The potion does not remove the unique buff Rapture or the Dislocated Shoulder condition. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] In-game model

## Potion of Everlasting Vigour
- **来源**: [Potion of Everlasting Vigour](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Potion_of_Everlasting_Vigour)
- **分类**: Potions

Potion of Everlasting Vigour is a unique Potion that permanently increases the imbiber's Strength score by +2 when consumed. A reward received from biting Araj Oblodra. Vampirism has sometimes been called The Dark Gift, or the Dark Kiss , perhaps as an allusion to their forbidden relationship to sunshine. It does provide gifts in abundance; such is the case with this potion. Properties Potions Single Use Rarity: Common Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 10 gp UID CONS_Potion_Blood_Astarion UUID cc426fc4-a82e-4375-8a77-31f2344b71b4 Stats OBJ_BloodPotion_Astarion Effect Bonus Action Permanently increase your Strength by 2. Where to find Given by Araj Oblodra in Moonrise Towers Notes Astarion must be convinced to bite Araj in Moonrise Towers to obtain this item. Consuming this potion grants the recipient a permanent +2 bonus applied on top of their base Strength and can raise it above 20. More specifically, it: Remains after death Remains after changing the character's class with Withers , even if modifying their base Strength score Is always applied after any Ability Score Improvements , but before any capped bonuses, such as from The Mighty Cloth Will always apply, regardless of how high a character's Strength score is, but does not affect modifiers that set Strength to a fixed score, such as an Elixir of Hill Giant Strength or the Gauntlets of Hill Giant Strength Related Permanent Bonuses

## Potion of Speed
- **来源**: [Potion of Speed](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Potion_of_Speed)
- **分类**: Potions

Potion of Speed is a Consumable ( Potion ) with a beneficial utility effect. This solution ripples and splashes of its own accord, almost like it's trying to escape the bottle. Properties Potions Single Use Rarity: Uncommon Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 20 gp UID CONS_Potion_Speed UUID ad9f3f24-d755-48b6-aa7b-c34da068209f Stats OBJ_Potion_Of_Speed Effect Bonus Action Consume the potion to grant yourself Hastened Action Throw the potion to grant Hastened to all creatures in an area Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 1 m (3 ft) Radius Condition: Hastened Hastened Duration: 3 turns Creature has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. When the condition ends, the creature becomes Lethargic . Where to find Sold by various merchants throughout the game with Utility Potion Table ; examples of merchants selling this item include: Cyrel in the Risen Road Toll House Roah Moonglow in the Shattered Sanctum Derryth Bonecloak in the Myconid Colony In the Harper cache hidden beneath the Scuffed Rock on the Ravaged Beach at X: 141 Y: 280 Carried by some Mind Flayers Crafted via Alchemy by combining any Salt with Ashes of Hyena Ear , which are procured from Hyena Ear ) Notes When the Hastened effect ends, affected creatures normally receive the Lethargic condition, causing them to miss their next turn. Using another Potion of Speed while already Hastened can effectively delay the Lethargic condition. When using a new Potion of Speed, the Hastened effect of the old one ends immediately, applying Lethargic right away, but Lethargic only lasts until the end of the current turn; if a creature is ready to end its turn (e.g. all actions are used) before consuming the second Potion of Speed (e.g. using the last Bonus action to drink the new one), then nothing is lost. The Haste Spores condition granted by Haste Spore Grenades is similar to that of the Hastened condition granted by speed potions , but only lasts 1 turn instead of 3, and does not leave users with the Lethargic condition when it expires, possibly increasing the utility of Haste Spore Grenades when Thrown over that of Potions of Speed. The price of a Haste Spore Grenade is 5 higher than that a Potion of Speed. Passive features [ edit section | visual editor ] Potion of Speed has 1 hit point . ## Elixir of Arcane Cultivation
- **来源**: [Elixir of Arcane Cultivation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elixir_of_Arcane_Cultivation)
- **分类**: Elixirs

See also: Arcane Cultivation (disambiguation) Elixir of Arcane Cultivation is an uncommon elixir that grants an additional level 1 spell slot when consumed. A small bottle, filled to the brim with arcane energy. Properties Elixirs Single Use Rarity: Uncommon Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 20 gp UID ALCH_Solution_Elixir_Meditation UUID 6f328fc5-6f54-4aad-959d-0825290a2763 Stats ALCH_Solution_Elixir_Meditation Effect Bonus Action Consume to grant an additional Level 1 Spell Slot . Replaces effects of other elixirs when drunk. Condition: Elixir of Arcane Cultivation Elixir of Arcane Cultivation Duration: Until Long rest Has an additional Level 1 Spell Slot . Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk. Where to find Can be crafted via Alchemy by combining Vitriol of Weavemoss (procured from Weavemoss ) and any Sublimate . Notes When the effect of this elixir is removed (i.e. when drinking a different elixir), the affected character loses a level 1 spell slot, prioritizing an already expended slot. If having expended at least one level 1 spell slot, there is no harm in replacing this elixir (or benefit in keeping it). A warlock still gets a spell slot of the elixir's level and can cast spells up to that level using the elixir's slot instead of a Pact Magic slot. - **分类**: Elixirs

Elixir of Barkskin is an uncommon elixir that increases your Armour Class when drunk. Before your eyes, the elixir firms into a tough, striated twig, then it liquefies once more. Properties Elixirs Single Use Rarity: Uncommon Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 30 gp UID ALCH_Soultion_Elixir_Barkskin UUID cc1a8802-675a-426b-a791-ec1d5a5b6328 Stats ALCH_Solution_Elixir_Barkskin Effect Bonus Action Drink to increase your Armour Class to 16. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk. Condition: Elixir of Barkskin Elixir of Barkskin Duration: Until Long rest Armour Class increased to 16. Where to find Sold by Derryth Bonecloak at the Myconid Colony ( Underdark ) Crafted via Alchemy by combining Salts of Tree Bark (procured from Wood Bark ) and any Suspension Notes This elixir sets your AC to the maximum of 16 or your normal AC after any bonuses are applied. For example, this means combining the Elixir of Barkskin with Shield of Faith (+2 AC) will not increase your AC to 18. Conversely this means any negative AC effects like Acid will not decrease your AC while under the effects of Barkskin. Passive features [ edit section | visual editor ] Elixir of Barkskin has 1 hit point . Elixir of Battlemage's Power is a rare elixir that increases the potency of spells by granting 3 stacks of Arcane Acuity that persist until the next long rest. Derived from the eye of a mage-hunting Nothic, this elixir waxes from within with a piercing light. Properties Elixirs Single Use Rarity: Rare Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 65 gp UID ALCH_Solution_Elixir_ArcaneAcuity UUID 7d1699d9-c3fa-4761-9718-28230f78420b Stats ALCH_Solution_Elixir_ArcaneAcuity Effect Bonus Action Drink to increase the effectiveness of your spells. You gain 3 stacks of Arcane Acuity until your next long rest. Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk. Condition: Elixir of Battlemage's Power Elixir of Battlemage's Power Duration: Until Long rest Affected entity has Arcane Acuity until its next Long Rest . Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk. Gain Arcane Acuity for 3 turns. Arcane Acuity cannot go below 3 turns. Where to find Can be crafted via Alchemy by combining Suspension of Gauth Eye (procured from Gauth Eyestalk ) and any Sublimate . Can be sold by any merchant that has the Elixir Table or Potion Table starting at level 6 . As stock is semi-random, merchants may have anywhere from 0 to 2. Popper in Rivington. Bugs The consumer gains 3 turns of Arcane Acuity at the start of each turn in combat; however, as Arcane Acuity loses a turn of duration at the start of each turn in combat, the duration will immediately be reduced to 2 turns. If all remaining turns of Arcane Acuity are removed due to the consumer receiving damage, 3 turns will be immediately reapplied. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] In-game model

Where to find Crafted via Alchemy by combining Ashes of Worg Fang (procured from Worg Fang ) and any Salt Sold by various merchants throughout the game, including (but not limited to): Act 1 Cyrel in the ⁠ Risen Road Toll House Derryth Bonecloak in the ⁠ Myconid Colony Stonemason Kith at ⁠ Grymforge Act 2 Araj Oblodra on the main floor of ⁠ Moonrise Towers Roah Moonglow on the main floor of ⁠ Moonrise Towers Quatermaster Talli at ⁠ Last Light Inn and on the main floor of ⁠ Moonrise Towers Act 3 Popper at the ⁠ Circus of the Last Days Entharl Danthelon in ⁠ Danthelon's Dancing Axe Derryth Bonecloak [ 1 ] in ⁠ Bonecloak's Apothecary Notes In Honour mode , the extra Action does not benefit from Extra Attack so martial classes only get a single additional attack from the elixir. Replaces effects of other elixirs when applied this way as well. The effect lasts only 10 turns when applied this way. Condition: Elixir of Cloud Giant Strength Elixir of Cloud Giant Strength Duration: Until Long rest Strength increased to 27. Where to find Crafted via Alchemy by combining Salts of Cloud Giant Fingernails (procured from Cloud Giant Finger ) and any Suspension Sold by any merchant who has the Elixir Table or Potion Table starting at level 9 ; as stock is generated semi-random, merchants may have anywhere from 0 to 2: Araj Oblodra on the main floor of Moonrise Towers and in a house north to Beehive General Goods in Lower City Baelen Bonecloak at Bonecloak's Apothecary in Lower City (if healed with the Noblestalk during ⁠ Find the Mushroom Picker ) Derryth Bonecloak at Bonecloak's Apothecary in Lower City (if given the Noblestalk during ⁠ Find the Mushroom Picker ) Entharl Danthelon at Danthelon's Dancing Axe in Wyrm's Crossing Helsik at Devil's Fee in Lower City Hoarding Merregon , the Merregon vendor who is part of Yurgir's retinue in the Gauntlet of Shar Mattis at the Last Light Inn and outside of Requisitioned Barn in Rivington at X: 59 Y: -127 Oliver Tefoco at Beehive General Goods in Lower City Popper the kobold at the Circus of the Last Days in Rivington Quartermaster Talli at Last Light Inn and on the main floor of Moonrise Towers Roah Moonglow at Moonrise Towers Stylin' Horst at The Velveteen Elixir , the floor above Danthelon's Dancing Axe in Wyrm's Crossing Traveller Griska on the ground floor of Fraygo's Flophouse in Wyrm's Crossing Found in the following locations: Inside the sarcophagus belonging to Zina at X: 1225 Y: 790 in the Durinbold Mausoleum Next to Koll at X: 235 Y: 45 in High Hall Inside the display case in the Open Hand Temple Cellar at X: 8 Y: -1024 (has a 1 in 3 chance to contain one; the other options being a Supreme Elixir of Arcane Cultivation or an Elixir of Psychic Resistance ) Notes The earliest vendors to stock Cloud Giant Fingers are Blurg and Derryth Bonecloak at the Myconid Colony in the Underdark , starting at level 6. Thus it is possible to craft this elixir while still in Act One . As the 27 Strength provided by this elixir lasts until long rest, it is arguably the most useful in the game for Strength-based party members. If the party have sufficient quantities of this elixir once it becomes available, characters can be respecced with 8 Strength and have ability score points and feats which would have been used to increase Strength allocated elsewhere. For example: Stat points may be reallocated to Dexterity to increase AC and initiative or Constitution to increase HP. An Ability Improvement feat used on Strength may instead be used on Tavern Brawler , which massively benefits high-Strength characters that primarily use Throw attacks or Unarmed Strikes . Otherwise, characters might take broadly useful feats like Alert or Lucky . - **分类**: Elixirs

The Elixir of Half-Elven Healing is a rare Elixir made up of all of a half-elf's best qualities. Upon consumption, you and surrounding allies regain hit points equal to your Constitution score . One of Blood Vendor Araj Oblodra's elixirs, distilled from a specific sanguine quality, and with properties aligned to an equally specific race. Properties Elixirs Single Use Rarity: Rare Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 10 gp UID CONS_Elixir_Blood_HalfElf UUID 293ffe17-abc1-4842-b338-cd9482e3bcbc Stats OBJ_BloodPotion_HalfElf Effect Bonus Action You and surrounding allies regain hit points equal to your Constitution score . Where to find Given by Araj Oblodra in Moonrise Towers and later in Lower City in exchange for half-elven blood Notes Despite its name this potion does not have any lasting effects Bugs While the description says the heal amount is equal to the character's Constitution score, the actual heal amount is 1d20 + Constitution modifier. For example, a character with a Constitution score of 16 would be expected to heal itself and nearby allies for 16 ⁠ hit points , but it actually heals for 1d20 + 3 (4~23) ⁠ hit points because a Constitution score of 16 is a modifier of 3.

Consuming another elixir overwrites this effect. If higher, this elixir does not lower a character's strength. The alchemy recipe for this potion can be learned by manually extracting 3 Hill Giant Fingers . As the 21 strength provided by this elixir lasts until long rest, it is arguably one of the more useful in the game for fighter types until the Elixir of Cloud Giant Strength becomes available. Upon acquiring sufficient quantities of this elixir, characters can be safely respecced with 8 Strength and have ability score points and feats which might be used on strength allocated elsewhere. For example: Stat points may be reallocated to Dexterity , Constitution , or Intelligence Ability score improvement feats may instead be used on Alert , Lucky or Tavern Brawler Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] In-game model External links [ edit section | visual editor ] Potion of giant strength on the Forgotten Realms Wiki

## Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation
- **来源**: [Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Greater_Elixir_of_Arcane_Cultivation)
- **分类**: Elixirs

See also: Arcane Cultivation (disambiguation) Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation is an uncommon elixir that grants an additional level 2 spell slot. From hedge wizards to high priests, these elixirs are coveted by spellcasters of any ilk. Properties Elixirs Single Use Rarity: Uncommon Weight: 0.1 kg (0.2 lb) Price: 30 gp UID ALCH_Solution_Elixir_Meditation_Greater UUID 8c7656f5-507a-4cee-8e15-320c968539f0 Stats ALCH_Solution_Elixir_Meditation_Greater Effect Bonus Action Consume to grant an additional Level 2 Spell Slot . Replaces effects of other elixirs when drunk. Condition: Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation Duration: Until Long rest Has an additional Level 2 Spell Slot . Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk. Where to find Can be crafted via Alchemy by combining Suspension of Laculite (procured from Laculite ) and any Vitriol . Notes When the effect of this elixir is removed (i.e. when drinking a different elixir), you will lose a level 2 spell slot, prioritizing an already expended slot. If you have expended at least one level 2 spell slot, there is no harm in replacing this elixir (or benefit in keeping it). Drinking multiple Greater Elixirs of Arcane Cultivation in a row will not restore multiple spell slots. However, if you alternate between drinking this and a different elixir, you can restore multiple slots. For example, drinking a Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation, then a Elixir of Arcane Cultivation , and then another Greater Elixir of Arcane Cultivation will restore two level 2 slots and one level 1 slot. If drunk by a Warlock , the extra spell slot will behave like a Spellcasting spell slot rather than a Pact Magic spell slot — i.e., it will always be level 2 regardless of the Warlock's level, and it will not be restored by taking a short rest. However, it is still possible to cast Warlock spells with it. If drunk by a spellcasting character who only has level 1 spell slots at their current level, this elixir will still give them a level 2 spell slot. Although this does not provide access to any level 2 spells, they can still use the extra spell slot to upcast level 1 spells. If drunk by a character with no spellcasting features at all, this elixir will still give them a single level 2 spell slot, though they will not be able to use it for anything. ## Concussion Grenade
- **来源**: [Concussion Grenade](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Concussion_Grenade)
- **分类**: Grenades

Concussion Grenade is a grenade found in Act Three . It explodes for a large amount of thunder damage. Deals Fire and Thunder damage to nearby objects and knocks them back. Properties Grenades Rarity: Common Weight: 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) Price: 10 gp UID PUZ_Trap_Gortash_GrenadeInstantiator_Grenade UUID 98f2cb6a-e268-4f99-aac3-62edabd8774c Stats WYR_Gortash_Grenade Effect Throw a bomb that explodes on impact and deals 5d10+18 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 4 m (13 ft) Radius Dexterity Saving Throw : DC 18 to halve the damage. Area: Fire Fire Duration: 2 turns AoE: 2 m (7 ft) Radius Deals 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Type: Surface Condition: Burning Burning Duration: 1 turn Takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Can be removed with the Help action, using a Healing Potion or gaining Wet . Immune from if Wet . Dip action can be used on Burning characters or objects. Where to find Summoned by Grenade Impellers in Wyrm's Rock Fortress . Notes Gains Quickly Ticking Mine after being left on the ground for one turn. Picking up the grenade in this state will lead to it exploding in the owner's inventory at the start of the next turn. Gains Unstable Ballistics on Tactician or Honour Mode , causing them to explode immediately when interacted with. Due to a script used in the Item Template , kills with this grenade do not reward experience . The explosion knocks targets back 4 m (13 ft) if they fail their saving throw. The knock back originates from the thrower's position, not the impact point of the grenade. Bugs Due to an incorrectly coded DealDamage() functor, the explosion deals 5d10+9 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage instead of half the listed tooltip damage. Due to a peculiar TargetConditions entry, if a character with Sculpt Spells picks up and throws a Concussion Grenade, it will not deal any damage.

Properties Grenades Single Use Rarity: Uncommon Weight: 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) Price: 20 gp UID ALCH_Solution_Grenade_SporesConfusion UUID cbc47f2b-b88a-4bd8-99cd-aacc2dc2ea44 Stats ALCH_Solution_Grenade_SporesConfusion Effect Action Lob this vaporous decoction to Befuddle nearby foes Range: 18 m (60 ft) Creates area: Timmask Spores Area: Timmask Spores Timmask Spores Duration: 2 turns AoE: 2 m (7 ft) Radius Chance to Befuddle creatures. When the grenade explodes, there is also a blast which can deal 2d4 + 1 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage. This is a spell attack. Characters already in a Timmask Spore cloud are not affected by Befuddled from another grenade, although the blast damage still affects them. Properties Grenades Single Use Rarity: Uncommon Weight: 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) Price: 25 gp UID ALCH_Solution_Grenade_SporesHaste UUID 6008231b-9f5a-44f6-8050-14586b7626fd Stats ALCH_Solution_Grenade_SporesHaste Effect Action Explodes in a cloud of invigorating energy Range: 18 m (60 ft) Creates area: Haste Spores Area: Haste Spores Haste Spores Duration: 3 turns AoE: 2 m (7 ft) Radius Creatures have a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , their movement speed is doubled, and they can take one additional action per turn. To obtain this item from Spaw, the party must agree to help kill the duergar invaders the first time they speak with him by selecting, "Sure, I can handle those duergar nearby." , as the flag UND_MyconidCircle_SovereignOfferedSpores is only set for this line of dialogue. Asking Spaw about animating corpses ( "What in the hells did you do to that corpse?" ), going back to the previous dialogue tree ( "Let's talk about something else." ), and then agreeing to help ( "I'll cleanse the rot. Those duergar near the lake will die." ) does not award the grenades since it does not set the flag.

## Smokepowder Bomb
- **来源**: [Smokepowder Bomb](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Smokepowder_Bomb)
- **分类**: Grenades

Smokepowder Bomb is a Consumable ( Grenade ) item which can be thrown and explodes on impact. This explosive gnomish invention is packed tight with smokepowder. Properties Grenades Single Use Rarity: Common Weight: 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) Price: 16 gp UID GRN_Bomb_A UUID 278271f9-3fbc-4cf7-a5dc-b36527f521b2 Stats OBJ_Bomb Effect Action - Throw a bomb that explodes on impact Range: 18 m (60 ft) AoE: 4 m (13 ft) Radius 3d4 + 9 (12~21) ⁠ Force damage ( DC  12 Dexterity Saving Throw to halve) Where to find Sold by multiple traders in the game: Act 1: Cyrel in the Risen Road Toll House Derryth Bonecloak in the Myconid Colony Roah Moonglow in the Shattered Sanctum Act 2: Quartermaster Talli at the Last Light Inn Act 3: Entharl Danthelon in Danthelon's Dancing Axe Bumpnagel in Angleiron's Cellar On the window ledge of the prison cell in the Worg Pens of the Shattered Sanctum; it can be grabbed from inside the cell In a trapped and locked wooden chest in the cave north of the Risen Road Carried by goblins if they are killed before they can throw them Notes The quantity of this item's availability with traders can vary depending on level, however Quartermaster Talli appears to sell at least 2 Smokepowder Bombs. Smokepower Bombs cannot be crafted via Alchemy . In most cases, merely placing Smokepowder Bombs does not turn neutral creatures hostile; they can be used to set up challenging opponents for a fall. Bugs A Smokepowder Bomb detonates and deals its damage when the bomb itself takes damage, regardless of source or type. Normally, this occurs when the thrown bomb hits something (as Throw attacks damage the thrown object). However, the bomb is triggered multiple times if it takes damage from multiple sources at the same time. This can be achieved by stacking multiple damage rider effects that apply to Throw attacks, such as Lightning Charges or Hunter's Mark . Each such effect causes the bomb to simultaneously explode an additional time. This can be used to devastating effect. An example log of a Smokepowder Bomb triggered multiple times would be: Character used Throw on Cave-In. Smokepowder Bomb was hit for 8 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. Smokepowder Bomb was hit for 1 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage. Character destroyed Smokepowder Bomb. Smokepowder Bomb received 2 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning damage from falling. Smokepowder Bomb received 1 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage from falling. Character blasted Cave-In for 32 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage. Character blasted Cave-In for 0 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage. Character blasted Cave-In for 37 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage. Character blasted Cave-In for 0 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage. The Smokepowder bomb blasted twice: the first time provoking 32 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage, and the second time provoking 37 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage. Another consequence of the detonation occurring when the bomb itself takes damage is that dragging a bomb out of an inventory and onto a Fire surface (or any other surface that deals damage) causes the bomb to detonate immediately. Because dropping items does not use an action, this can be repeated as many times in the same turn as one has bombs (although some careful positioning or resistances may be required to prevent the character moving the bombs from blowing up). Unlike other grenades, Smokepowder Bombs do not display an impact radius when targeting a Throw. Gallery [ edit section | visual editor ] Prop designs by Cliff Laureys

## A Familiar Face
- **来源**: [A Familiar Face](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/A_Familiar_Face)
- **分类**: Quests

Nocturne is a lifelong friend of Shadowheart's. A Familiar Face is a sub-quest of both Shadowheart's ⁠ Companion quest and her ⁠ Origin quest . It is acquired if Shadowheart consumes the Noblestalk in the Underdark . Contents 1 Objectives (Companion Quest) 2 Objectives (Origin Quest) 3 Walkthrough 3.1 Obtaining the Noblestalk 3.2 Consuming the Noblestalk 3.3 Finding Nocturne Objectives (Companion Quest) [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions. Find Shadowheart's old friend. "We have entered the Lower City - Shadowheart's old stomping grounds. Perhaps the friend she remembered due to the Noblestalk can still be found with the rest of the Sharrans." Quest Complete "We found Shadowheart's old friend, who now goes by the name Nocturne. She serves as quartermaster for the Sharran cloister, and despite being glad to see Shadowheart again, she could not bring herself to turn from Shar." "We found Shadowheart's old friend, who now goes by the name Nocturne. She serves as quartermaster for the Sharran cloister, and could prove to be a valuable ally to Shadowheart." "Shadowheart's old friend perished before a reunion could take place." "Shadowheart has surrendered the reclaimed memory of her old friend to the Mirror of Loss." "We moved on to other matters, and did not find Shadowheart's old friend." "Shadowheart perished before she could be reunited with her old friend." "Shadowheart abandoned us before we could help her find her old friend." Objectives (Origin Quest) [ edit section | visual editor ] Find your childhood friend. "I have returned to the Lower City of Baldur's Gate. Once I reach the Cloister, I might be able to discover what happened to my childhood friend." Quest Complete "I met my childhood friend, who now goes by the name Nocturne. Though she was glad to see me, she was unable to abandon her faith in Shar as I had done." "My old friend was defeated before a reunion could take place." "At the Mirror of Loss, I sacrificed the memory of a childhood friend that the Noblestalk had restored to me. Perhaps I will never know who that person was, or what came of them." "I continued on my journey without ever seeking out my old friend." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Obtaining the Noblestalk [ edit section | visual editor ] The locations of the Noblestalk and the backpack within the Bibberbang. The party can obtain a powerful curative mushroom known as the Noblestalk in the Bibberbang Grotto at X: -4 Y: -62 in the Underdark . The grotto is also key to the quest ⁠ Find the Mushroom Picker . The delicate mushroom can be destroyed by any damage. If approached, the Bibberbang release poisonous and flammable spores. The lit torch lying in the grotto will readily ignite them, destroying the Noblestalk. However, there are several options to obtain the Noblestalk: A Mage Hand can drag the Noblestalk without triggering the Bibberbang. However, the Noblestalk should not be thrown to avoid accidentally destroying it. After extinguishing the torch (e.g. by throwing Water or casting Create Water ) the Bibberbang can safely be destroyed without endangering the Noblestalk. Imp or Quasit Familiars (including Shovel ) are immune to poison and can walk through the clouds unharmed, or the party can wait for them to dissipate before retrieving the Noblestalk themselves. If Sovereign Glut is an Attached Follower , he does not trigger the mushroom traps. He can be controlled directly, using the move action with the Noblestalk to transport it back to the party. Consuming the Noblestalk [ edit section | visual editor ] After obtaining the Noblestalk, the party must speak with Shadowheart . She then can be offered the Noblestalk as a chance to regain her memories. Shadowheart is hesitant to do this, as she fears that trying to overcome her memory suppression might be construed as defying Shar . However, she can be convinced by passing a DC 12 Persuasion or Intimidation Check . If she consumes the Noblestalk, she regains a childhood memory of a young tiefling boy with short horns and purple hair named Rennald who comforted her when she was being teased by the other initiates. The memory initiates this quest, as Shadowheart hopes to reunite with the tiefling in Baldur's Gate . Finding Nocturne [ edit section | visual editor ] The tiefling in question now goes by a new name – Nocturne . Nocturne is within the quarters of the Cloister of Sombre Embrace at X: -399 Y: -1608 , north of the audience room where Viconia DeVir is fought during ⁠ Investigate the House of Grief . When Shadowheart enters, Nocturne immediately recognizes her and exclaims she was not sure if she would ever see Shadowheart alive again, as her being tasked to pursue the Mysterious Artefact was considered a suicide mission. Whether or not Shadowheart has become an enemy of Shar , she is eager to reminisce with Nocturne about their childhood. She shares some funny stories with Shadowheart, such as how she got a scar on her elbow from a collision with the teeth of a girl named Buddug Vriss . Nocturne acts as a quartermaster for the Sharran cloister. If Shadowheart takes over the cloister, she remains in her position, serving her new mistress. If Shadowheart defies Shar and kills all the cultists, Nocturne says that she is willing to trade while she remains, but intends to soon depart for a new cloister. ## Acquire the Gauntlets for Helsik
- **来源**: [Acquire the Gauntlets for Helsik](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Acquire_the_Gauntlets_for_Helsik)
- **分类**: Quests

Helsik behind her counter Acquire the Gauntlets for Helsik is a Quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking to Helsik in Devil's Fee . “ You put me in a difficult position, mortal. You are almost certain to fail. Almost. And so, there is a chance you might succeed. Fine. I'd like to be able to carry all of my precious stock without the need of a team of oxen. There are Gauntlets of Hill Giant Strength within the House of Hope. Free passage, and you fetch them for me. Deal? „ — Helsik , offering a bargain Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Reach the House of Hope. Helsik the diabolist said she will help us reach the House of Hope if we steal a powerful artefact for her while we're there: Gauntlets of Hill Giant Strength . We agreed to the deal. She gave us a note with precise instructions - we should follow them in the ritual room upstairs. Find and steal the gauntlets for Helsik. We made it to the House of Hope. We should keep an eye out for the gauntlets that Helsik wants. Return to Helsik with the gauntlets. We stole the gauntlets. We should give them to Helsik as promised when we leave the House of Hope. Quest Complete We gave Helsik the gauntlets, upholding our side of the deal. Helsik was defeated. She won't be needing the gauntlets anymore. We decided to keep the gauntlets for ourselves, deciding not to uphold our side of the deal. We decided to keep the gauntlets for ourselves, but to uphold our side of the deal, we paid her in gold instead. We failed to uphold our side of the deal with Helsik. We must press on. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The Devil's Fee [ edit section | visual editor ] Helsik , can be found at the Devil's Fee . Inquiring about Helsik being a diabolist has her revealing that her true business is not in information or hellish curios. She is Mammon's Picklock, Latchkeeper of the Nine Hells. She breaks people into the Hells, for a cost. With a successful DC 20 Persuasion Check , she waives the fee in lieu of the Gauntlets of Hill Giant Strength , which starts this quest. The placement of the ritual items in the circle. If striking a deal with Helsik, she gives the party all the tools needed to open a portal to Avernus . This includes a Grimoire Bound in Imp Skin and a Ritual Pouch with all the necessary items. The party must go upstairs in the Devil's Fee to find a circle in blood, read the Grimoire Bound in Imp Skin to learn the ritual, and then place the ritual items in the correct areas. Starting from the point closest to Helsik's diary and going clockwise: Skull at X: -35 Y: 6 Coin of Mammon at X: -34 Y: 8 Empty spot Diamond at X: -30 Y: 7 Incense at X: -29 Y: 4 Empty spot Empty spot Then the Infernal Marble must be placed in the center of the circle and a portal to hell opens. Meeting Hope [ edit section | visual editor ] A map to the House of Hope. Once inside the House of Hope, a strange dwarf named Hope appears to greet the party. The party can convince her to aid them, which results in her giving each party member a Debtor's Attire so that they can move about the House undetected. The Archives [ edit section | visual editor ] The Gauntlets in the Archive. The Gauntlets are in the Archives, as one of Raphael's newest acquisitions. They are in the northernmost corner of the room at X: -6548 Y: 2939 . The platform the Gauntlets are on is rigged with a pressure plate, so they can either be swapped out with another pair of gauntlets or the trap can be disarmed before the item is stolen. Then, the party can sneak off, as with stealing anything. If intending to steal either the Soul-Sworn Contract in ⁠ Escape the Deal or the Orphic Hammer in ⁠ Deal with the Devil / ⁠ Save Hope , then disarming the trap and sneaking to steal the Gauntlets is unnecessary, as the alarm goes off anyways once the contract or hammer is taken. Returning to Helsik [ edit section | visual editor ] Once returning from Hell, Helsik demands the Gauntlets. The party can hand them over, refuse to do so, or attempt to pass a DC 10 Deception Check to say that they do not have them. If the Gauntlets are handed over, they do not appear in Helsik's trading inventory and cannot be pickpocketed back. If refusing to hand them over, Helsik permanently refuses to trade with the party member who did not fulfill the bargain. However, other party members can begin the same conversation with her from the start. Additionally it is possible to pass a DC 10 Deception Check by saying that the party do not have the Gauntlets. She then says that this invalidates the bargain and demands a 20,000 gold payment for the trip. The party can pay off the gold fee instead of handing over the Gauntlets. At this point it is possible to tell her that the party will leave with the Gauntlets, cannot afford the fee, or attempt a DC 10 Intimidation Check by saying I just killed a devil in his own home. You really don't want to test my patience . Intimidating her allows to the party to keep the Gauntlets and continue to trade with her. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If the gauntlets are equipped on a party member who is currently wild shaped, then the party can agree to give Helsik the gloves and the quest completes saying the party gave them up, but a message that the gloves cannot be unequipped appears and they remain in the wild shaped character's inventory- allowing the party to keep the gloves without making any checks. Helsik acts like the party gave her the gloves. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death...
