## Fulfill the Deal
- **来源**: [Fulfill the Deal](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fulfill_the_Deal)
- **分类**: Quests

Fulfill the Deal is a sub-quest of the quest ⁠ Deal with the Devil in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Sharess' Caress 2.2 Being forced to fulfill the deal 2.3 After defeating the Netherbrain Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Obtain the Crown of Karsus. "According to the terms of our deal with Raphael, we must give him the Crown of Karsus after we've defeated the Absolute threat. But first we must get hold of the relic." Quest Complete "We have destroyed our infernal contract with Raphael. Now we have no obligation to give him the Crown of Karsus." "We obtained the Crown of Karsus, and as per the terms of our contract, we gave it to Raphael." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Sharess' Caress [ edit section | visual editor ] Mamzell Amira can be encountered on the ground floor of Sharess' Caress by the front entrance. When asked what she has to offer, Amira mentions that a devil is in residence Raphael . At the bar, Korrilla can be met, informing the party that Raphael wishes to speak with them. At the top floor Raphael can be found in a room labelled the Devil's Den . If Kith'rak Voss is alive, he is trying to make a deal with Raphael, but Raphael sends him away. He does, however, have a proposition for the party. Raphael is in possession of the Orphic Hammer which can break the cage that holds Orpheus . In return, he wants the Crown of Karsus , which is being used to control the Elder Brain . Raphael's proposal can be rejected or accepted. If rejected, he states that he will remain at Sharess' Caress for some time in case they change their mind. If accepted, he creates a Soul-Sworn Contract and the party instantly feels a pang of regret, starting ⁠ Escape the Deal . Being forced to fulfill the deal [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael arrives in the Astral Prism. If the party does not obtain the Orphic Hammer , either through making a deal with Raphael or stealing it from the House of Hope, then party's hand can be forced to fullfil Rapheal's deal. This occurs during ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain . After the initial confrontation, the Emperor steps in to protect the party from the Netherbrain and shelters them in the Astral Plane . During this time, the Emperor states that only an illithid can hope to take down the Netherbrain in its current form and that the illithid must consume the power of Prince Orpheus in order to succeed. As an illithid, the Emperor says he can do this, and asks the Netherstones be relinquished to him. If choosing to say "I don't believe a word you just said." and then "I will never trust you." , then the Emperor becomes enraged and states that he has no other choice but to reassimilate into the Netherbrain. He leaves the party in the Astral Realm, with seemingly no options left to defeat the brain. In this case, Raphael appears within the Astral Prism. Now the party must sign a contract for the Orphic Hammer in exchange for the Crown of Karsus. Refusing to sign turns the party members into mind flayers who are then assimilated into the Netherbrain, causing a Game Over . After defeating the Netherbrain [ edit section | visual editor ] Fulfilling the deal results in an additional cutscene after the credits roll. Raphael has already begun his conquest of the Hells , with many rulers already seeking to bargain with him. He threatens the prospect of turning to other realms once the hells are united, ending his speech with, "It won't be long before I come knocking at your door. Ta ta, for now." v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Gather Your Allies (quest)
- **来源**: [Gather Your Allies (quest)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Gather_Your_Allies_(quest))
- **分类**: Quests

"Gather Your Allies" redirects here. For the action this quest grants, see Gather Your Allies (class action) . The party's allies have gathered to fight the Absolute. Gather Your Allies is a main Quest spanning all three Acts of Baldur's Gate 3. It is obtained in Act One and completed in Act Three . Its objectives are fulfilled by completing various other quests throughout the campaign. “ Thou art alone, but for thy friends. Didst thou not make allies? I fear thy final confrontation will prove quite a challenge. Hadst thou allies, the yoke of salvation may not have weighed down on thee so. But, since thou didst not convince others to join thy cause, thou wilt face the Netherbrain's assault armed only with thine own faculties. Let us hope they are enough, lest this plane fall to illithid ruin. I wish thee good fortune, and good grace. „ — Withers , if the party failed to recruit any allies Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 3 Consequences 4 Notes and references Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending player decisions and outcomes. Recruit allies in the fight against the cult "Freeing ourselves of the parasite is proving more difficult than we imagined. We should be on the lookout for powerful allies - we'll likely need them in the fight to come." "Volo has become a most loyal ally. His powerful words of encouragement are sure to be at our backs in the trials to come." "Auntie Ethel is grateful for us letting her keep the child. We can rely on her help in the trials ahead." "Halsin is grateful for our help protecting the sanctity of life. We can count on his formidable druidic powers, should the need arise." "Yurgir, pleased to be free of his contract, will lend us the hellish might of an orthon in the trials to come." "Mizora is sure to seek revenge for her abduction to Moonrise Towers. When the time comes to face the Absolute, we'll find her on our side." "Isobel is grateful that, thanks to us, her beloved is safe. We are sure to have the light of Selûne guiding us in the darkness to come." "Dame Aylin, the fearsome aasimar, is now our sworn ally. She'll have our backs in any fight - no matter the enemy." "Lorroakan is more powerful than ever with the Nightsong in his possession, thanks to us. The might of Ramazith's Tower will be at our backs, should we ever need it." "Rolan is grateful for our help securing his position in Ramazith's Tower. We can rely on the tower's full power, should we ever need it." "Arabella is back from learning how to control her powers. We can trust that her magic will be there to help us when we need it most." "The strange creature is thankful that we helped it enter the city. No doubt we'll have a powerful ally when we need it most." "Valeria feels indebted to us for having saved her from an untimely death. She and her City Watch are prepared to support us in the final battle." "Dammon the weaponsmith has become a staunch ally. We can rely on his ingenuity and the owlbear cub's might in our final battle." "Wulbren and the Ironhand Gnomes no longer have to contend with the Gondians. We can rely on their aid, should we ever need it." "The Gondians' lives were saved with our help. We've made loyal allies in them, should we ever need their aid." "Barcus won't forget that we helped him become the new leader of the Ironhand Gnomes. We can count on his support should we ever need it." "Grand Duke Ravengard is grateful for us saving him from the Absolute's clutches. He will stand by our side in the final battle." "Florrick is immensely grateful that we freed her and helped with the threat at Moonrise. We are sure to have her and the Flaming Fist by our side when we need it most." "The Zhentarim don't like to be in anyone's debt - it's bad for business. For helping them, we are sure to have their blades on our side, should it come to protecting the city. It's their new home, after all." "Nine-Fingers is grateful that we helped her retain control of the Guild - she's not one to give away what's hers. We can count on her and her Lady's Court in the final battle." "Mol isn't one to forget those who have helped her along the way. She'll have our back in the fight to come." "We've made an ally of Kith'rak Voss. He and his mighty steed will aid us when the time comes." "Astarion is grateful for us helping him become Vampire Ascendant. We can count on his dark magic in the final battle." "The Gur people are grateful for our role in taking down Cazador Szarr. We are sure to have them by our side, come what may." "Shadowheart is thankful that we helped her gain her rightful position in the Sharran Cloister. We can count on the dark power of the Sharrans in the battle to come." "Viconia is grateful that we helped her establish her rightful position. We can count on Viconia and Lady Shar's faithful in the fight to come." "Jaheira has joined our party. We'll have whatever aid the High Harper can muster in the fight to come." "Bhaal is most pleased we have embraced him. The Lord's slayer will make for a powerful ally in the battle ahead." Updates for Deceased/Abandoned Characters The following objectives are added for characters who leave or are killed: "Halsin has left, forging his own path. He won't help us in the fight to come." "We killed Dammon, so he and the owlbear cub can no longer aid us in the battle to come." "Shadowheart has left, so we will be without her aid in the battle to come." "We killed Viconia, so have lost the aid of her and Lady Shar's faithful." "Auntie Ethel would have lent us her aid, but we killed her before she could." "We killed Ulma, so we will no longer have the help of the Gur people in the final battle." "Astarion is gone, so we will be without his aid in the fight to come." "Counsellor Florrick was ready to support us in battle, but we killed her before she could." "The Guild are leaderless. They're in no condition to help us in our fight." "The Zhentarim are newly victorious, but leaderless. They will be busy with matters of their own, so will not be able to aid us." "Jaheira has left us - and with her, any chance of aid from the Harpers in the fight to come." "With Wyll dead, Mizora has little interest in helping us." "We sent Yurgir, who could have been a powerful ally in our final battle, back to the Hells." "We killed the owlbear cub, despite how far it had come. We will no longer have its support in the battle to come." "The phasm would have aided us in battle, no matter how formidable our foe, but we killed it." "We killed Grand Duke Ravengard, who can no longer help us in the fight to come." "We killed Isobel despite all we did for her and Dame Aylin. She can no longer help us in the final battle." "We killed Dame Aylin despite all we did for her and Isobel. She can no longer help us in the final battle." "We killed Lorroakan, so no longer have his support from the heights of Ramazith's Tower." "We killed Rolan, despite having helped him accomplish his goals. He can no longer aid us when the time comes." "We killed Wulbren. He can no longer aid us in our final battle." "We killed Barcus, an unfortunate gnome until the end. He can no longer aid us in our final battle." "We killed Valeria, despite having saved her so recently. She can no longer aid us in our final battle." "We killed Volo, just a humble bard and documentarian at the core. He can no longer help us in the fight to come." Quest Complete "The allies we've made on our journey have all gathered together - ready to lend us their power in the battle ahead. It is time to finish this - once and for all." For example, siding with Nine-Fingers Keene during ⁠ Aid the Underduke locks the party out of being able to ally with the Zhentarim in the same playthrough. All Companions must be recruited in Act One and their personal story quests must be resolved for their objectives to be completed in Gather Your Allies. Zevlor Act One: Completing ⁠ Save the Refugees , siding with the Tieflings Act Two: Freeing Zevlor from the ⁠ Mind Flayer Colony in ⁠ Find Zevlor [ 5 ] Hellrider Platoon Summon Zevlor and a Paladin and a Cleric. Zhentarim Act Three: Overthrowing Nine-Fingers Keene in ⁠ Aid the Underduke The Zhentarim and the Guild are mutually exclusive as allies. Black Fist Enforcers Summon two elite assassin mercenaries from the Zhentarim's ranks. Consequences [ edit section | visual editor ] Netherese Orb Blast : Gale can also blow himself up. After completing ⁠ Free Orpheus , the final battle begins to ⁠ Confront the Elder Brain . The player character receives the special action Gather Your Allies which summons friendly units or grants buffs during combat based on the characters or factions who have been recruited. The recruited characters also appear in a room in the High Hall , where they give a short dialogue line of support. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ If Raphael is killed, the contract can still be given to Mol, but Raphael's death must not be mentioned, and a successful Persuasion Check must be passed. As a Warlock, a specific dialogue choice is in place of the skill check. ↑ Agreeing to Mizora's ultimatum is not necessary. ↑ Volo's passive buff, Volo's Guide to Monsters , is also a ⁠ manual for the Dungeons and Dragons tabletop game. ↑ If, during ⁠ Kill Raphael's Old Enemy , the party complete the subquest ⁠ Break Yurgir's Contract by defeating Lyrthindor , Yurgir will automatically join them against Raphael . If the party killed Yurgir or persuaded him to kill himself, he can still be convinced to assist them with a DC 30 Persuasion Check . ## Get Gortash's Netherstone
- **来源**: [Get Gortash's Netherstone](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Get_Gortash's_Netherstone)
- **分类**: Quests

Gortash is heavily protected inside Wyrm's Rock Fortress. Get Gortash's Netherstone is a Quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking to Enver Gortash in the audience chamber above Wyrm's Rock Fortress . “ Oh, goodie. Now we can go see Gortash, dangle this stone in front of him, and watch him beg before we slit his throat... right? „ — Karlach , relishing the prospect [ 1 ] Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Full-on Assault 2.2 Disable the Steel Watch 2.3 Gortash's Bargain 3 Quest Rewards 4 Related Quests 5 Achievements 6 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Head west on the road to Baldur's Gate. Gortash left for Baldur's Gate. We should go after him. Find Gortash. Baldur's Gate is near. We should find out where Gortash is. Find Gortash in Wyrm's Rock Fortress. We discovered that Gortash is in Wyrm's Rock Fortress, where he will be sworn in as Archduke of Baldur's Gate. We need to make our way there. Enter the Audience Hall. We made it to Wyrm's Rock Fortress and were invited to Gortash's inauguration upstairs. Confront Gortash. We found the audience hall of Wyrm's Rock Fortress and found Gortash involved in the midst of a ceremony. Gortash is protected by the Steel Watch. If we want to make a move against him, we should figure out how to deal with them first. We destroyed the Steel Watch Foundry. The Steel Watchers are now disabled, making Gortash an easier target. Consider Gortash's bargain. We obtained Orin's Netherstone. We should show it to Gortash if we want to follow through with his proposition. Gortash put forward a proposition. If we kill Orin and take her Netherstone, he will let us rule the city alongside him with the elder brain at our command. Defeat Gortash. The Iron Throne is destroyed. Angered, Gortash will no longer wish to uphold the proposition he put forward to us. Gortash became hostile. If we want his Netherstone, we have to defeat him. We decided not to accept Gortash's proposition and destroyed the Steel Watch Foundry. The Steel Watchers are now disabled, making Gortash an easier target. Meet Gortash at the Morphic Pool. We struck a deal with Gortash to control the elder brain together. We agreed to meet him under the city at the Morphic Pool, where the elder brain feeds. Take Gortash's Netherstone. We killed Gortash. We should take his Netherstone. Quest Complete We defeated Gortash and took his Netherstone. The elder brain killed Gortash and we took his Netherstone. We now have all three Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] After arriving in Baldur's Gate , the party needs to make their way from Rivington to Wyrm's Rock Fortress to get through to the Lower City . When the party completes ⁠ Find a way into Wyrm's Rock fortress , they can enter the fortress. Once they do, a Steel Watcher instantly stops them and tells them they are intruding. However, the Watcher is taken over by the voice of Gortash, who invites them to his coronation where they can speak about the future of the Netherstones . After entering the Audience Hall and approaching Gortash, he speaks to the party and offers an alliance, and then completes his coronation as Archduke of the city. From there, the party must decide what to do with him. Full-on Assault [ edit section | visual editor ] Once the party arrives at Wyrm's Rock Fortress, they can choose to do battle with Gortash at any point after meeting him in the Audience Hall. Gortash can be fought with before his coronation has even ended. If the Steel Watch has not been disabled, then the fight is significantly more difficult. The party can also force Gortash's hand to some extent. If they speak to him without Orin's Netherstone, he gives them one warning not to come back until they have it. Trying to speak to him again causes him to be hostile to the party. If Gortash is defeated without his Steel Watch disabled, then Elder Brain takes over the Steel Watch and uses them to destroy the Steel Watch Foundry . It then takes control of the remaining Steel Watchers. Disable the Steel Watch [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Disable the Steel Watch In order to weaken Gortash's grip on the city, the party can undertake Disable the Steel Watch . Completing this quest results in all the Steel Watchers around the city falling about, making the battle against Gortash easier. If the party goes to the Iron Throne during this quest, Gortash warns them not to go there. If they do, this signals the end of any kind of deal between him and the party. He and the entire Wyrm's Rock Fortress become hostile upon approach. Gortash's Bargain [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Consider Gortash's Bargain On arriving at Wyrm's Rock Fortress, Gortash invites the party to his coronation as Archduke. If the attending and speaking with Gortash, he offers the party a pact - he will not attack them so long as they leave him and his Steel Watch alone. If the party agree to take Orin's Netherstone and return to him, he will rule the city together with them. A DC 15 Insight Check reveals he fully intends to share his kingdom with the party. If taking Gortash up on his offer, he asks the party to give the Netherstones to him. If agreeing, he turns on the party, as he sees them as weak-willed. If the party refuse twice, then he tells them he was simply testing them, making sure they have the backbone to make proper allies. Gortash tells the party to keep the stones and meet him at the Morphic Pool so that they can take control of the Elder Brain. However, in the confrontation with the brain, regardless of what happens, it kills Gortash, forcing the party to take the last Netherstone. In order to ally with Gortash, the party must give up on ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands , ⁠ Save the Gondians , ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke , and ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch . The party also should not have killed his parents in the Lower City at Flymm's Cobblers . If these actions occur, Gortash sees it as a violation of his agreement and turns hostile to the party. Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Cloth of Authority Fabricated Arbalest Gortash's Hand Netherstone-Studded Gauntlet – separates on pick-up into: Gauntlet of the Tyrant Gortash's Netherstone Tyrannical Jackboots Related Quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Consider Gortash's Bargain Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Fancy Footwork Defeat Gortash in Wyrm's Rock without activating any traps. ## Get Help from Auntie Ethel
- **来源**: [Get Help from Auntie Ethel](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Get_Help_from_Auntie_Ethel)
- **分类**: Quests

Ethel wants to help the party. Get Help from Auntie Ethel is a sub- quest of Act One's main quest, Find a Cure . It can be initiated by speaking with Auntie Ethel at the Druid Grove, or running into her south of the Blighted Village . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Meeting Ethel 2.2 Ethel's bargain 3 Consequences Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Get Auntie Ethel's help. We met an eccentric old lady in the Emerald Grove. She's confident she can remove our parasites and invited us to her teahouse. We met an eccentric old lady at a teahouse in the wilderness. She's confident she can remove our parasites - for a price. Ethel named her price for helping us: one of our eyes We agreed to give up an eye in exchange for removing the parasite. Quest Complete We made a deal with Auntie Ethel, but she couldn't remove the parasite, claiming it was Netherese. If a green hag can't help us, who can? Auntie Ethel died before she could help us. We need to find someone else to remove the parasite. Things turned violent with Auntie Ethel. She isn't happy with us. We left the area before finding out whether the old lady could help us. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Meeting Ethel [ edit section | visual editor ] Ethel can be found in two different places. She can first be encountered in The Hollow within the Emerald Grove X: 192 Y: 544 , where she runs a small shop selling lotions and potions. Ethel notices that the party looks ill, and they can reveal that they were infected with a mind flayer tadpole. Ethel states that she can help, but that she doesn't have the supplies at the Grove. She invites the party to visit her at her house in the wetlands. Ethel can also be encountered southwest of the Blighted Village, in the Sunlit Wetlands X: 45 Y: 313 . Here, Ethel is confronted by two men, the brothers Johl and Demir , who accuse her of kidnapping their sister, Mayrina . The party can intervene on behalf of the brothers or Ethel. If the party sticks up for Ethel, she invites them back to her house. Ethel's bargain [ edit section | visual editor ] Ethel removes an eye with her claws. Ethel's house X: -47 Y: 266 is in the southwestern area of the Sunlit Wetlands/Putrid Bog. She greets the party and regardless of whether she was told or not, states she's well aware of the tadpole in their heads. Luckily, she has experience removing them. She offers the party a deal - sacrifice one of their eyes and she will remove the tadpole. If the party agrees, Ethel transforms into her true form, a hag, and asks if she should take the left or right eye. After choosing, Ethel takes the eye and enchants it, giving the party member the trait Hag-Eyed. After this is done, she tries to fulfil her part of the bargain by removing the tadpole. Unfortunately, the tadpole fights against the removal. Ethel is unable to remove it, as it has been enchanted by Netherese magic. If asked about the eye, she says she fulfilled her part of the bargain and that she didn't agree to remove a Netherese tadpole. As a token of rare good faith from a hag, Ethel will give Auntie Ethel's Charm to the party after the attempted removal. Consequences [ edit section | visual editor ] Depending on dialogue choices, a character who still has both eyes can allow Auntie Ethel to attempt to remove the tadpole. This will fail and result in the major, permanent debuff Paid the Price , which gives +1 to Intimidation checks but disadvantage on Perception checks along with disadvantage when attacking Hags. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Get Help from Healer Nettie
- **来源**: [Get Help from Healer Nettie](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Get_Help_from_Healer_Nettie)
- **分类**: Quests

Nettie is a talented healer - but can she cure a tadpole? Get Help from Healer Nettie is a sub- quest of Act One's main quest, ⁠ Find a Cure . It can be started by inquiring about a healer with Nymessa and Damays or various individuals at the Druid Grove . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Being truthful with Nettie 2.2 Not being truthful with Nettie 2.3 Avoiding getting poisoned 2.4 Poisoned and trapped 2.4.1 Getting an antidote from Nettie 2.4.2 Brewing an antidote 2.5 If Nettie is killed 3 Quest rewards 4 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Find the druid's apprentice. "Aradin told us that the druid Halsin has an apprentice. If we can find her, she might be able to help us with the parasite." Find the healer Nettie. "When we asked about healing, we were told to look for Nettie in the Inner Sanctum." "There's a camp nearby where someone named Nettie can supposedly heal any wound. She might be able to help remove the parasite." Follow Nettie. "We told Nettie about the parasite. She seemed concerned and asked us to follow her to another room for treatment." Find an antidote for the poison. "Unable to heal us, Nettie spared us the horror of ceremorphosis - by poisoning one of us with deadly venom. We need to cure the poison immediately." "Nettie's corpse told us of a cure - the Elixir of Silvanus. It seems related to flora of the Dalelands." "To make the lifesaving antidote, we need to mix a bundle of mugwort in a cauldron of theriac, blessed by Silvanus." Quest Complete "Nettie tried to poison us, but we managed to talk her out of it. She let us go, but she made us promise to kill ourselves if we started to turn." "We managed to find a cure for the venom Nettie used - but we're still no closer to a cure for the parasite." "We rescued Nettie's master, Halsin. Now that he's safe, we don't need to ask Nettie for help - we can go directly to the master druid instead." "Nettie was killed before she could help us. We'll need to find another way to cure ourselves." "Nettie's dead - serves her right for trying to poison us. But it's a bittersweet victory: we still need to find a way to deal with the parasite. "We left the area without seeing if the druid apprentice could heal us." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The library where Nettie can be spoken with. Nettie is within the Emerald Grove , in the room beyond the lounge where Kagha and Rath are situated. She does not help until the player character admits to their infection by a Mindflayer Tadpole. She invites them to join her in the library room deeper within the sanctum to talk. Once inside the room, she locks the door behind the party members who have have already moved into the room and Fast Travel is not possible for those party members. Approaching Nettie initiates a conversation. Being truthful with Nettie [ edit section | visual editor ] If the interacting player character informs her of the various symptoms the party have been experiencing, then Nettie is honest in kind. She does not have a cure, and was instead planning to euthanize the party before they could transform. Nettie then offers to let the party go free if they swear to consume a Wyvern Toxin to kill themselves at the first signs of turning. If they agree and swear to Nettie's demands, she informs them of the current situation in the Grove and urges them to ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin . If the party member refuses, she attacks in hopes of stopping the party before they transform and harm others. Not being truthful with Nettie [ edit section | visual editor ] If the player character refuses to provide any details of their symptoms, she asks to touch their hand without explanation. If the player characters offers their hand to Nettie, the Druid slices it with the poisoned plant Kelemvor's Kiss Branch , inflicting the player character with a special Poisoned condition called At Death's Door , which inflicts a -2 penalty to all Ability Scores , and continues to worsen after Resting . If the player character refuses to offer their hand, Nettie tries to slice it regardless. The player character must then pass an ability check to avoid this: [ 1 ] [DEXTERITY]  Dodge when she lunges for you.  (DC 10) [INTIMIDATION]  Don't be a fool. I'd kill you before you could blink. (DC 15)  (if not a Barbarian) [INTIMIDATION]  Try me.  (DC 15  )  (Barbarian only) Avoiding getting poisoned [ edit section | visual editor ] The another check must be passed to get Nettie to stand down: [ 1 ] [PERSUASION]  The drow didn't transform - I won't either. (DC 10) [MEDICINE]  I'm not showing symptoms - that means I have time. (DC 10) [HISTORY]  Try to recall the tenets of her order - she can't support this!  (DC 10)  (if not a Druid) [DRUID] [HISTORY]  Try to recall the tenets of her order - no druid could support this!  (DC 10  ) [INTIMIDATION]  You can't hit me, let alone kill me. Don't make me put you down. (DC 10)  (if not a Barbarian, Monk, or Fighter) [MONK] [FIGHTER] [INTIMIDATION]  I'm trained in combat, you're a druid with a stick. Don't make me kill you. (DC 10  ) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  You won't have to worry about anyone else after I CRUSH YOUR SKULL.  (DC 10  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  I don't need to transform to kill everyone. Stand down.  (DC 10  ) If this is successful, the conversation loops back to her request to the party to swear to drink the poison should they start transforming. Saying yes finishes the quest. Refusing to agree once again leads to combat. Poisoned and trapped [ edit section | visual editor ] Getting an antidote from Nettie [ edit section | visual editor ] The player character has an opportunity to grab the branch and try to identify the poison: [ 1 ] [NATURE]  Examine the branch to identify the poison.  (DC 10)  (if not a Druid or Ranger) [DRUID] [RANGER] [NATURE]  Examine the branch - have you come across this plant before?  (DC 10  ) [NATURE]  Grab the branch and try to identify the poison.  (DC 10)  (if not a Druid or Ranger) [DRUID] [RANGER] [NATURE]  Grab and examine the branch - have you come across this plant before?  (DC 10  ) Doing so reveals the thorn is a plant called Kelemvor's Kiss . The party can walk away from the conversation at this point. Nettie is not hostile, believing that with the doors locked and the player character poisoned, they are no longer a danger. Listed below are options to obtain the antidote, which is on Nettie, at this point: Convince Nettie to give it by passing two ability checks. This is the only peaceful method to obtain the antidote and leave the room at this point. [ 1 ] [DECEPTION]  You can't do this - your leader needs to talk to me. (DC 15) [DECEPTION]  I have important information - your grove will die without it. (DC 10) [DECEPTION]  I'm the only one that can find Halsin. (DC 10) [MEDICINE]  But I'm safe - I'm not showing symptoms, and it's been days. (DC 10) [MEDICINE]  Eventually? That gives me time to find a cure. (DC 10) [MEDICINE]  As long as there's a chance, you're not saving me. You're committing murder. (DC 10) [HISTORY]  Try to recall the tenets of her order - she can't support this!  (DC 15) [DRUID] [HISTORY]  Try to recall the tenets of her order - no druid could support this!  (DC 15  ) [ARCANA]  Magic can cure me if you can't. I know the Weave well! (DC 10) [WIZARD] [WARLOCK] [SORCERER] [ARCANA]  Magic can cure me if you can't. I know the Weave well! (DC 10  ) [ARCANA]  Magic can cure me if you can't. I know the Weave well! (DC 10  )  (if playing as Gale) [INTELLIGENCE]  You said there were others like me - we need to cure this, or your kin will never be safe. (DC 10) Attack Nettie and loot her body for the Elixir of Silvanus . Pick-pocket the Elixir of Silvanus from Nettie. She turns hostile once she discovers it missing. However, this allows the party to fight against her without the At Death's Door debuff. If a party member gets the antidote through dialogue with Nettie, she then offers to let the party go free as long as they swear to commit suicide prior to turning. Refusing once again leads to a fight. Brewing an antidote [ edit section | visual editor ] It is possible to learn to brew an antidote. In the room where the party originally found Nettie healing the bird, there is a book named On Antidotes on a desk by the cauldron. Reading the book teaches how to craft an Antidote . Combining Salts of Mugwort with any suspension allows to brew an antidote. Antidotes found elsewhere also work for curing the poison. Three Mugworts are in the Druid's Quarters, required to extract the salts. The room Nettie locks the party in has three Bullywug Trumpets which allow them to extract a suspension, altogehter providing all the ingredients needed to brew an antidote. Picking up the Bullywug Trumpet nearest to Nettie triggers a dialogue line where she tells the party to stop searching for an antidote as they will not find one. It is possible to brew the antidote ahead of speaking with Nettie or simply bring one found elsewhere in the world. Should the player character get poisoned, they then have the option to cure themselves immediately, which causes Nettie to give up, and loop back to offering the party a chance to leave if they swear to kill themselves should they start to transform. If Nettie is killed [ edit section | visual editor ] The party remain trapped within the library. To escape, they must loot Nettie's Circlet, the Key of the Ancients which opens the stone slab doors. The party can use this to return to the Druid Grove , or head towards the Underground Passage . Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Key of the Ancients Wyvern Toxin Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The Cauldron of Boiling Theriac used to brew the Elixir of Silvanus in early versions. Prior to Patch #1 the party was able to read the book Flora of the Dalelands in the Druid's Quarters to learn that the poison Nettie used on them is known as 'Kelemvor's Kiss'. The book also taught the party how to brew an Elixir of Silvanus by adding a Mugwort Bundle to the Cauldron of Boiling Theriac to cure the poison. This would also have granted the inspiration "The Apprentice Turns Master" for the Guild Artisan background. ↑ 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 Dialogue file: Act1/DEN/DEN_Apprentice_Cyanide v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Get Orin's Netherstone
- **来源**: [Get Orin's Netherstone](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Get_Orin's_Netherstone)
- **分类**: Quests

Orin is a dangerous shape-shifting opponent. Get Orin's Netherstone is a Quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It is started automatically after entering Wyrm's Rock Fortress and long resting, or by entering the sewers for the first time. [ 1 ] “ Another Bhaalspawn, buried by our hand. Bhaal should learn better than to send his offspring against us - they might as well be babes, dropped bare-bottom into the Rashemen winter. „ — Minsc , reflecting after the quest's completion [ 2 ] Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Orin's Kidnapping 2.2 Candulhallow's Tombstones 2.3 Infiltrate the Murder Tribunal 2.4 The Temple of Bhaal 2.5 The Chosen’s Room 2.6 Confronting Orin 3 Quest Rewards 4 Achievements 5 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Head west on the road to Baldur's Gate. Orin, the Lash of Bhaal, is hiding somewhere in Baldur's Gate with a Netherstone. We must find her and take it. Search Baldur's Gate for Orin. We need to scour the city for clues to Orin's location - murder most foul may be the place to start when tracking a Bhaalist. Orin confronted us in a shapechanged disguise - then teleported away. We should keep looking for clues as to her base of operations. Find and gain access to the Temple of Bhaal. Gortash told us Orin resides in the Temple of Bhaal. We must find the temple and a way of getting in. We found the Temple of Bhaal, but the doors are sealed shut. We need to find a way in - Orin may be inside. We found a cruel and deliberately staged murder scene in Baldur's Gate - it could be the work of Orin. We met a Flaming Fist Constable investigating Bhaalist murders in the city. We should investigate - this trail of blood may lead us to Orin and her Netherstone. We found a Bhaalist target list - new recruits are being asked to stage murders as Absolute butchery. We should investigate: successful recruits gain access to the Temple of Bhaal, where Orin awaits. Orin has kidnapped one of our number - we must find the Lash of Bhaal and free our companion. Orin kidnapped Yenna - a young girl we met in Rivington. We must find the Lash of Bhaal and rescue her. We killed Bane's Chosen, just as Orin requested. Now we need to bring his severed hand to the Murder Tribunal - where we will gain access to the Temple of Bhaal and Orin herself. Find a way to access the Temple of Bhaal. We slew Justice Sarevok and his Murder Tribunal - we should search his belongings to find a way into the Temple of Bhaal. We found a Bhaalist Amulet on Sarevok's body. It may help us enter the Temple of Bhaal. We found a map pointing us towards the Temple of Bhaal's hidden Undercity location. Investigator Valeria told us where to find the Temple of Bhaal - Orin awaits us there. Open the Temple of Bhaal and confront Orin. Now we have the Bhaalist Amulet and the Temple of Bhaal's location, we can finally face Orin. Justice Sarevok found us worthy of entering the Temple of Bhaal: he gave us an Amulet to open the doors as well as the Temple's location. We should go there - Orin awaits. Confront Orin in the Temple of Bhaal. We opened the Temple of Bhaal using the Bhaalist Amulet - now we must face Orin within. The doors to Father's Temple opened before us - as the Bhaalspawn's right. We must enter and slay Orin. Defeat Orin. We must slay Orin to claim her Netherstone. Retrieve Orin's Netherstone from her dagger. With Orin dead, we must retrieve the Netherstone from her dagger. Quest Complete We have slain one of Bhaal's fetid spawn and claimed her Netherstone. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin's Kidnapping [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin the Red kidnaps a party member under various circumstances. One event trigger is long resting after arriving in the Lower City . Orin shapeshifts as the party member she abducts and speaks to the party. Orin only abducts characters who are at camp and not in the current party. If there are no eligible companions at camp (for example if only three party members were recruited at all, or by using a party limit extender mod), Yenna is kidnapped instead. If Orin's kidnapping has not been triggered through a long rest, it can also be triggered in the Lower City Sewers . In this case, the event is mostly the same for each person - Orin, disguised as the kidnapping victim, appears grievously injured and begs the party to run away, explaining how they were brutally tortured by Orin. Then, Orin reveals herself and the kidnapping plot. After Orin reveals she has a hostage, she states her demands. Enver Gortash bound her blade when the Chosen Three initially came together, making her unable to harm him. For this reason, she needs the party to step in and kill him. After this, she intends to face the party in a battle to the death - winner takes the Netherstones. As long as the party takes him down, she will not harm her captive. This initiates ⁠ Rescue Orin's Victim . If ⁠ Get Gortash's Netherstone is completed first, Orin sends a blood to letter to camp titled "Congratulations on the Murder of Gortash." She tells the party, that they must now face the Murder Tribunal and become an unholy assassin of Bhaal, before they can face her. She gives the party a location - Candulhallow's Tombstones and a password - 'Sicarius.' This starts ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal . If not pursuing Gortash first, then ⁠ Investigate the Murders (or ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal ) must be completed. Finishing the quest also reveals the location and password for the tribunal. Candulhallow's Tombstones [ edit section | visual editor ] Entrance to Candulhallow's Tombstones Candulhallow's Tombstones is northeast of Elfsong Tavern at X: 74 Y: 25 . Its entrance can either be lockpicked, or opened by a key if the party successfully stopped the serial killings. The party must move into the back office room and remove the Butterfly on Skull painting at X: 87 Y: 15 to find a button. Pressing the button reveals a secret door. The only way to get past this door is to know the passphrase, Sicarius. The painting that hides the button. Within the basement, there is a sign that says " Flaming Fists this Way." This area is heavily trapped with grease barrels that alight if entering that way. Instead, the party can remain on the brick path on the right and enter the door to the Murder Tribunal's antechamber at X: -1302 Y: 519 Infiltrate the Murder Tribunal [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the Murder Tribunal. The party must enter the Murder Tribunal Antechamber and speak to That Which Guards. This entity provides a riddle, "Present me well from gifts thine own, or I shall rend thy flesh from bone." Choose "I killed to be here - and took the victim's hand as proof" to proceed forward. The party can use the hand bag from Dolor, the hands taken from any victims they chose to kill, or the hand of Gortash to gain entry. Choosing any other option results in a fight with the guards, and the Murder Tribunal becomes hostile as well. However, avoiding dialogue and directly attacking the guards does not make the Tribunal hostile. If the party chose not to pursue the serial killer Dolor, then he is at the Tribunal arguing with That Which Guards. That Which Guards states that only one murderer can go forth into the Tribunal. The party can tell Dolor to either go ahead, persuade him to fight against the Tribunal, or fight him to the death. If not fighting their way through, Sarevok Anchev is encountered, along with the Echo of Amelyssan , Echo of Illasera , and Echo of Sendai . The party can ask Sarevok various questions about how he is still alive, his ties to Orin, and about what the Murder Tribunal is. Sarevok states that there is no better mirror, in which to see the true nature of a killer than his victim. Thus, he summons the image of one of the murder victims. The spectre cannot speak, as the murderer stole its voice. Thus, the party must speak for it. Sarevok asks how the pitiful creature was slain: First, I ended its sorry existence. Then, I cut the hand from its corpse. The deed is done - the details don't matter. In combat. Honourably. [DECEPTION]  First, I ended its sorry existence. Then I cut the hand from its corpse. (DC 20) [DECEPTION]  Slowly and painfully. I savoured every scream. (DC 20) [DECEPTION]  With a smile on my face, and pleasure in my heart. (DC 20) (The DC is 10 instead of 20 for Dark Urge characters, or removed if the party actually killed the victim) If the soul was actually slain by the party, then no deception checks are needed. Choosing the first two options or the last option or failing the Deception checks make Sarevok and the echoes hostile. Otherwise, Sarevok leads the party to the Dread Lord's Abattoir, for the next challenge. Inside the abattoir is the hollyphant investigator, Valeria . Sarevok demands Valeria to be killed in order to be baptized as an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal. However the party can turn on Sarevok and attack him and free Valeria. An additional scene plays if either Minsc or Jaheira (or both) are in the party during the tribunal. Sarevok instantly recognizes them and accuses them of meddling in his father's affairs. The party can respond by stating they are sacrifices offered up to Bhaal and kill them or side with Jaheira / Minsc and attack the Tribunal or go through an Intimidation or Performance check to force Jaheira / Minsc to kneel before the Tribunal. Doing the latter satisfies Sarevok enough to allow the Tribunal to continue. Killing Jaheira / Minsc will more than satisfy the Tribunal so the questioning about the murdered victims is skipped entirely and Sarevok starts walking to the abattoir. The Map to Bhaal Temple and the Amulet of Bhaal , which are needed to enter the Temple of Bhaal, can be acquired either as a reward from becoming an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal or looted from Sarevok Anchev . A Wooden Desk at X: -1239 Y: 531 contains A page from Sarevok's book , which if reveals, that Sarevok fathered Orin with his daughter Helena. This adds dialogue options, when talking with Orin and her mother in the Temple of Bhaal. The Temple of Bhaal [ edit section | visual editor ] The hanging corpses in the Undercity Ruins. The entrance to the Temple of Bhaal is at the Undercity Ruins waypoint. A large stone door is blocking entry. It is immune to lock-picking but the doorway can be unlocked in a few other ways. Using a ranged attack on one of the two corpses hanging from the ceiling in the center of the room at X: -142 Y: 934 Casting Knock on it Becoming an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal via ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal Showing Amulet of Bhaal There is a long, winding path east to get to the Temple proper. Close to the entrance, an ambush of several unholy assassins occurs, detectable through a Perception check. Once the door to the Temple is reached at X: 2 Y: 1006 , the Amulet of Bhaal is necessary. The party must place the amulet against the door to gain entry. Orin can be found deep into the Temple. The Chosen’s Room [ edit section | visual editor ] Map of the Temple of Bhaal. The Chosen's Room at X: 96 Y: 991 is down the stairs behind Orin (opposite the Temple’s entrance). It can be reached through a tunnel on the northern path or stealth means such as invisibility. The room contains the corpse of Orin’s mother Helena Anchev . [ 3 ] If Speak with Dead is used on Helena's corpse, additional dialogue check options can be made available when confronting Orin at the altar. To accomplish this, either of the Who - questions must be asked, followed by Why did you try to kill your own daughter and then Did Orin know that Sarevok ordered you to kill her? . Passing these new checks causes a conflict in Orin, resulting in her Slayer transformation being forced on her by Bhaal instead of her choosing to activate it. If an Origin other than the Dark Urge is chosen, then a dead white dragonborn labeled Fallen Bhaalspawn can be found lying on the ground. Confronting Orin [ edit section | visual editor ] Orin’s Netherstone-Pommelled Bloodthirst dagger, before the player removes the Netherstone. Orin's victim is shackled to an altar, which Orin holds the key to. Orin welcomes the party, while she knows if the player character became an unholy assassin or not. She also holds a dagger to the victim, threatening to kill them. Like the salvation your mother offered? She attacked you on Sarevok's orders. Your father's orders...  (if spoken to Helena) You're pathetic. No wonder he tricked you so easily. [DECEPTION]  Sarevok told me the truth himself. He was laughing at you. (DC 25) [PERSUASION]  Sarevok's your father , Orin. He abused your mother. He abused you. (DC 25) [RELIGION]  Bhaal rejoices in such cruel betrayals. You really believed you were the exception? (DC 25) I'm not the one who needs saving. [DECEPTION]  Gortash is dead. I left him rotting on the roof of his fortress. (DC 25) [INTIMIDATION]  Anything you do to him/her, I will inflict on you a hundredfold. (DC 25) [RELIGION]  You said Bhaal wanted us to fight. He will reject this offering. (DC 25) [PERSUASION]  I did what you asked. I killed Gortash, so let him/her go. (DC 25  )  (if Gortash defeated) Their fate is of no interest to me. If any check is failed or a non-check option is chosen, Orin kills the victim on the altar and then transforms into her Slayer form (a level 12 monstrosity) and initiates combat. If any check is passed, Orin still transforms and initiates combat , but ignores the living victim and faces the party. The altar can be lockpicked during combat with a DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check , freeing the victim and allowing them to fight alongside the party. Otherwise, the victim can be freed by looting the Altar Key from Orin's remains; after which they thank the party and return to camp. Once the battle is completed, Orin is reduced to a lootable ‘gore pile’ and a cutscene shows the player character retrieving her dagger with the Orin's Netherstone in it. Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Crimson Mischief Mutilated Carapace Netherstone-Pommelled Bloodthirst – separates on pick-up into: Bloodthirst Orin's Netherstone Ring of Murderous Opportunity Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] First Blood Kill Orin while her cultists are performing their ritual chant. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ This quest is not time sensitive, as long not attempting to infiltrate the Temple of Bhaal. ## Get Past the Rubble
- **来源**: [Get Past the Rubble](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Get_Past_the_Rubble)
- **分类**: Quests

The deep rothé are tired of being abused. Get Past the Rubble is a sub- quest of ⁠ The Adamantine Forge in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Herdmaster Skarjall at Grymforge or using Speak with Animals to speak to the deep rothé. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 With Speak with Animals 2.2 Without Speak with Animals 3 Companion approval 4 Related quests 5 Notes and references Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Clear the rubble. We found a passage buried in rubble that leads to the Adamantine Forge. We should clear it. Quest Complete If the party destroy the rubble: We destroyed the rubble. If the deep rothé destroy the rubble: We got past the rubble. If the party fail to reach the Adamantine Forge: We left Grymforge without reaching the Adamantine Forge. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] After entering Grymforge , the party can climb the stairs and travel north to encounter Herdmaster Skarjall at X: -668 Y: 442 . Skarjall orders the party to whip the Deep Rothé that are clearing out rubble. If asked why, passing a DC 15 Persuasion Check causes Skarjall to show the party a piece of Adamantine Slag , revealing the presence of nearby adamantine. He offers to pay the party in gold if they clear the rubble, but asserts that the Adamantine Forge is clan property. The party's interaction with the deep rothé can impact how the rubble is cleared: If telling Skarjall that the rothé deserve the whip and asking why he cannot crack his whip one more time, then both Skarjall and the rothé become hostile. The rothé can be convinced to either continue working or turn on their duergar masters. The party can whip the rothé themselves, which turns the rothé hostile. With Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 1 ] Hit the rothé. [PERSUASION]  Breathe. Focus. If you strike, your masters will destroy the herd. (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  You were made to serve. This is your meaning. Remove the rubble, as you were told. (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  Give in to your rage and avenge your pain. Don't strike us all, just your masters (DC 10) Without Speak with Animals [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 1 ] Hit the rothé. [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Display your palms and murmur soft, low reassurances.  (DC 15) [ANIMAL HANDLING]  Meet its eyes. Show it how calm you are - all is well.  (DC 15) If the rothé are convinced to continue working, Skarjall turns on the party, saying he wants all the spoils for himself. Then the rothé aid the party in defeating him. If the party convince the rothé to turn on their masters, then they can be asked to clear out the rubble afterwards. The rubble can also be destroyed using bludgeoning or force damage (i.e. spells like Eldritch Blast or Smokepowder Bombs . In combat, Skarjall is joined by Grundril and Morgya . The rest of the fortress remains neutral to the party during and after the battle. The party can earn 80 XP at the start of the fight if the rothé are convinced to turn on their masters. Each duergar rewards 75 XP. Finally, asking the rothé to destroy the rubble rewards another 80 XP. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Convince the deep rothé to clear the path. Breathe. Focus...   -1   +1 Convince the deep rothé to attack the duergar. Give in to your rage...   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ The Adamantine Forge Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] This quest is entirely optional - the Adamantine Forge can be accessed in other ways, such as using Misty Step or Fly . ## Help Kith'rak Voss
- **来源**: [Help Kith'rak Voss](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Help_Kith'rak_Voss)
- **分类**: Quests

Help Kith'rak Voss is a Quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3 that is added after you speak with Voss after he approaches you in the camp. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Encountering Voss 2.2 Obtaining the Hammer 2.3 Showing the Hammer to Voss 3 Quest Rewards Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Meet Voss in Baldur's Gate. "Kith'rak Voss visited our camp and asked us to help him free someone held prisoner within the Astral Prism. We agreed to bring the Prism to Baldur's Gate and meet him there." Find Voss in Sharess' Caress. "We spoke to Lae'zel after finding out that the prisoner in the Astral Prism is Orpheus. She wants to meet Voss in Sharess' Caress." "We learned that the prisoner's chains can be broken with something called the Orphic Hammer. We should find Voss in Sharess' Caress and talk to him about it." "We entered the Wyrm's Crossing district of the Outer City. Sharess' Caress, the tavern where Voss will be waiting for us, should be nearby." Speak to Raphael in Sharess' Caress.. "We learned that the prisoner's chains can be broken with something called the Orphic Hammer. Maybe we can find out more about it from Raphael." "We saw Kith'rak Voss and the devil Raphael having a heated conversation. Raphael must know something about the key to freeing the prisoner from the Astral Prism." Speak to Voss in Sharess' Caress. "Raphael proposed a deal: if he gives us the Orphic Hammer, the key to freeing Orpheus, we give him the Crown of Karsus once we defeat the elder brain. We refused. We should probably talk to Voss, who's waiting in the Sharess' Caress taproom." Retrieve the Orphic Hammer from the House of Hope. "Kith'rak Voss tasked us with finding a way of retrieving the Orphic Hammer from Raphael's House of Hope. We should explore the city - see if we find any leads." "We entered the House of Hope. The Orphic Hammer should be close. We should look around." "We found the Orphic Hammer, but it is protected by a magical barrier. There must be a way to disable it." "We disabled the magical barrier protecting the Orphic Hammer. We can finally get our hands on it." Show the Orphic Hammer to Voss in the Undercity. "We retrieved the Orphic Hammer. We should bring it to Voss, who's waiting for us in the Undercity." Show the Orphic Hammer to Voss in Sharess' Caress. "We retrieved the Orphic Hammer. We should bring it to Voss in the Sharess' Caress taproom." Tell Voss about the deal with Raphael. "We signed Raphael's contact and he gave us the Orphic Hammer. We should tell Voss in the Sharess' Caress taproom." Show the Orphic Hammer to Voss in the Undercity. "We signed Raphael's contract and he gave us the Orphic Hammer, but we lied to Voss and told him that we didn't. He will be waiting for us in the Undercity, where we should bring the Hammer." Show the Orphic Hammer to Voss in Sharess' Caress. "We found the Orphic Hammer. We should bring it to Voss in Sharess' Caress." Quest Complete "We didn't sign the contact with Raphael, but we told Voss we did. As a reward, he gave us a powerful silver sword - the highest grade of weapon in githyanki custom. He left to prepare for the revolution that will follow Orpheus' deliverance." "We showed Voss the Orphic Hammer and he gave us a powerful silver sword - the highest grade of weapon in githyanki custom. He left to prepare for the revolution that will follow Orpheus' deliverance." "We went to Sharess' Caress, but Voss wasn't there. We won't be able to tell him that we found the Orphic Hammer." "Voss is dead. He won't be able to aid Orpheus in his rebellion against Vlaakith." "Voss left after we attacked him. He must be gathering his allies for when Orpheus needs their help." "We entered the Morphic Pool before showing Voss the Orphic Hammer. We should press on - the elder brain awaits." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Encountering Voss [ edit section | visual editor ] Kith'rak Voss initially approaches the party as part of ⁠ Discover the Artefact's Secrets and Lae'zel's personal quest, ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior . He is briefly seen in the Mountain Pass , where he refers the party to seek out the Githyanki Crèche inside Rosymorn Monastery . After meeting Vlaakith , leaving the Astral Prism and discussing with Lae'zel what happened inside, Voss approaches the camp, during a long rest (including a forced one, when moving outside the Rosymorn Monastery Trail ). He tells the party to help the person in the Astral Prism as much as they can. He explains that he and his warriors are going to Baldur's Gate and the party should meet with him at Sharess' Caress . Once reaching Sharess' Caress in Wyrm's Crossing , the party can speak with the proprietor, Mamzell Amira . She can be asked what she has to offer. Amira mentions that a devil is in residence - Raphael . At the bar, Korrilla is also around, informing the party that Raphael wishes to speak with them. They both refer the party to the upper floor of the tavern. At the top floor is the Devil's Den, and Raphael. Kith'rak Voss is inside trying to deal with Raphael, but Raphael sends him away. Voss tells the party that he waits outside to hear how their conversation with Raphael went. Raphael does indeed have a proposition for the party. He is in possession of the Orphic Hammer - a tool which can break the cage that holds Orpheus . In return, he wants the party to retrieve the Crown of Karsus , which is being used to control the Elder Brain . Obtaining the Hammer [ edit section | visual editor ] Raphael's proposal can be rejected or accepted, as part of ⁠ Deal with the Devil . If rejected, he states that he remains at Sharess' Caress for some time in case they change their mind. If accepted, he creates a Soul-Sworn Contract and the party instantly feel a pang of regret, starting ⁠ Escape the Deal . In this instance, Raphael immediately relinquishes the Hammer to the party. There is also the option to steal the Orphic Hammer, by pursuing the quest ⁠ Free Orpheus . Showing the Hammer to Voss [ edit section | visual editor ] If signing the deal with Raphael, the party can show it to Voss immediately. Voss gifts the party a Silver Sword of the Astral Plane , a mighty weapon and a precious cultural item of the Githyanki. He then departs to prepare his forces to take on the Elder Brain. If refusing the deal, Voss relocates to the Lower City Sewers near the Undercity Ruins waypoint. There, he waits for the party and grants them the sword, if they show him the Orphic Hammer: after this he leaves to gather his forces. If Lae'zel has forsaken Vlaakith it is well worth having her in the party while speaking with Voss, as she gets multiple Approval boosts during the conversation and unique dialogue with Voss. ## Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite
- **来源**: [Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Help_Omeluum_Investigate_the_Parasite)
- **分类**: Quests

Omeluum hopes to aid the party in removing their parasite. Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite is a sub- quest of Act One's main quest, ⁠ Find a Cure . It can be initiated by speaking with Blurg and Omeluum at Ebonlake Grotto (the Myconid Colony), and informing them of the parasite. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 The Arcane Tower 2.1.1 Navigating the tower 2.2 Returning to Omeluum 2.2.1 First saving throw 2.2.2 Second saving throw 2.2.3 Third saving throw 2.2.4 Survival Instinct 3 Quest rewards 4 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Let Omeluum examine the parasite. "We mentioned the parasite to Blurg, a hobgoblin. His colleague, a mind flayer named Omeluum, offered to examine it. Perhaps it can cure us?" Ask Omeluum how to negate the tadpole's magic. "The mind flayer couldn't extract the parasite, but offered us a way to negate the magic protecting it." Find the mushrooms Omeluum requested. "To help us, Omeluum requires a Tongue of Madness mushroom and some Timmask Spores. We can find both at the mysterious tower nearby." "We found some Timmask Spores. We'll need to bring them back to Omeluum once we find the Tongue of Madness." "We found the Tongue of Madness. We'll need to bring it back to Omeluum along with the Timmask Spores." Drink the potion Omeluum made for us. "Before Omeluum can start the procedure, we'll need to drink the potion it made from the mushrooms we found." Get the Ring of Mind Shielding from Omeluum. "The potion Omeluum gave us didn't work - it made the parasite even stronger. To calm it down, Omeluum is willing to trade us a ring of mind shielding." Quest Completed! "We left the area before Omeluum could help. We'll need to find a cure somewhere else." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Talking to Omeluum and agreeing to its plan to brew the potion starts the quest. [ 1 ] To complete this quest, the party must obtain Tongue of Madness and Timmask Spores and bring them to Omeluum. These mushrooms are in the Arcane Tower . However, it is also possible to get both mushrooms without entering the tower. For Timmask Spores, the party can approach a Timmask mushroom in turn based mode and pick up the spores before they disappear. Tongue of Madness can be bought from Derryth Bonecloak . The Arcane Tower [ edit section | visual editor ] Navigating the tower [ edit section | visual editor ] The fungus on the south wall serving as jumping platforms. The party can explore the Arcane Tower by restoring power and using the elevator. If party members have access to flight (such as the Fly spell, or the Circle of the Moon Druid's Dire Raven form ), they can completely bypass the need to restore the tower's power. However, this means giving up on 25 Experience and potentially inspiration points for the Guild Artisan background. To successfully finish the quest, party members must visit the first floor (greenhouse), which contains some Tongue of Madness mushroom and Timmask Spores . Once they have obtained these, they can return to Omeluum to finish the quest. Returning to Omeluum [ edit section | visual editor ] Once the party returns to Omeluum, it brews the potion as promised, and attempts to extract the tadpole from the talking party member, granting the inspiration ⁠ Mind Over Mushrooms to party members with the Guild Artisan background. If a party member passes a passive DC 10 Insight Check , they can learn that Omeluum expects doubt and fear from them. If they ask if the experiment is dangerous, it tells them that it does not know what the potion will make them see or feel, but that they may become a danger to themselves. The illithid however reassures them that the potion will not kill them. The party member who drinks the potion can either attempt a series of saving throws or give in to the potion and attempt no saving throws. Declining the saving throws applies the listed negative effects as if failed. First saving throw [ edit section | visual editor ] A passive DC  15 Constitution Saving Throw which, if failed, inflicts Poisoned on the character for 10 rounds. Second saving throw [ edit section | visual editor ] Once Omeluum starts psionically probing, the tadpole resists, and the party member must choose whether to attempt a save: [ 2 ] [MONK] [WISDOM]  Use meditation to clear your mind.  (DC 10  ) [WISDOM]  Draw on your willpower and resist.  (DC 10)  (if not a Monk) [INTELLIGENCE]  Focus on the present, not the illusions.  (DC 10) If the party member fails the saving throw, they gain the Tongue of Madness condition for 5 turns, which gives them Disadvantage on Charisma checks. Third saving throw [ edit section | visual editor ] The interacting party member must finally attempt a second saving throw, this time with a DC 15: [ 2 ] [CLERIC] [WISDOM]  Call to your god for protection.  (DC 15  ) [BERSERKER] [WISDOM]  No fear. ONLY FURY!  (DC 15  ) [BARBARIAN] [WISDOM]  Fear? What's that?  (DC 15  ) [WISDOM]  Drown out the tadpole by focusing on a tune.  (DC 15) [WISDOM]  Resist the panic from within.  (DC 15)  (if not a Barbarian or Cleric) [INTELLIGENCE]  Wall off your mind from the psionic seizure.  (DC 15) The party member gets a unique Dazed condition for 5 turns if they fail this save. [ 3 ] Survival Instinct [ edit section | visual editor ] Regardless of which saves were successful, Omeluum is unable to extract the tadpole. Rather, its intervention has caused the tadpole to become stronger. This results in the party member who drank the potion gaining the Survival Instinct power. [ 4 ] At this point, the quest is marked as complete. As it was unable to help, Omeluum offers the party member its Ring of Mind-Shielding , though it will not normally part with it for free. The interacting party member can either buy this ring or convince Omeluum to give it to them in several variants: [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 2 ] I have gold. Will that suit? I've flown on a mind flayer ship. I can trade you details of the schematics, if you're interested. How about I tell you more about that nautiloid? Every last detail. [PERFORMANCE]  Give a dramatic retelling of your time on the mind flayer ship. (DC 10) [INTELLIGENCE]  Offer a detailed, logical analysis of the nautiloid.  (DC 10) [INTELLIGENCE]  Enrich your story with details from the designs you found on the nautiloid.  (DC 10  )  (if the party read the Rune Slate during the Prologue ) [PERSUASION]  I wouldn't be in this situation if it wasn't for a mind flayer. You owe me. (DC 15)  (if not a Githyanki or Duergar) [DUERGAR] [GITHYANKI] [PERSUASION]  Your people enslaved mine. The debt is yours to repay. (DC 15  ) [INTIMIDATION]  Either give me the ring, or I'll run you through. (DC 20)  (if not a Barbarian) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Something of little value - your life.  (DC 20  ) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  YOUR LIFE. GIVE IT.  (DC 20  ) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  Perform the tale of your adventures so far: 'The Ballad of Brains, Brine Pools and Balderdash.'  (DC 15) Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] The character who drinks Omeluum's potion gains the Survival Instinct tadpole ability. Ring of Mind-Shielding (can be purchased or obtained through checks). Omeluum becomes a trader, with notable items like Pearl of Power Amulet and Creation's Echo in its inventory. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Although Lae'zel , if she is present, will be extremely rude to Omeluum and generally hostile to the idea of working with an Illithid, her Approval is not affected by anything that happens in this quest. ↑ 2.0 2.1 2.2 Dialogue file: Act1/Underdark/UND_MyconidCircle_SocietyOfBrilliance_MindFlayer ↑ This is different from the Dazed condition caused by attacks like the Pommel Strike weapon action. ↑ In the Early Access, the character instead gained the Repulsor Tadpole Power . ↑ During Early Access , the options included: Offering gold - i.e. trade for it just like any other merchant Trading their knowledge / experience of the Nautiloid by passing a DC 15 Intelligence or Performance Check . Intimidating Omeluum - by passing a DC 20 Intimidation Check . Omeluum did not turn hostile in case of a failure. ↑ If the party member failed their previous saves during the extraction process, they can choose to leave the conversation and allow those effects to pass prior to attempting the skill checks to obtain the Ring of Psionic Protection. In Early Access, it seems that the party member was free to try these checks to get the ring for free as many times as they wanted. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Help the Devilish Ox
- **来源**: [Help the Devilish Ox](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Help_the_Devilish_Ox)
- **分类**: Quests

The Strange Ox needs help getting into Baldur's Gate Help the Devilish Ox is a quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with the Strange Ox in Rivington . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Smuggle the ox 2.2 Attack the strange creature 3 Quest rewards 4 Bugs Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Help the strange creature. We met an odd creature. It has the shape of an ox, but is clearly something else. It wants to get into the city. Wonder why? We ran into that strange creature again - the one who was pretending to be an ox. It wants to get into the city. Wonder why? Smuggle the creature into the city. We met an odd creature. It has the shape of an ox, but is clearly something else. We agreed to help it reach the city. It transformed into an apple so we could carry it. We agreed to help the strange creature reach the city. It transformed into an apple so we could carry it. Defeat the strange creature. We angered the strange creature. We're in for a fight. We tried to eat the apple. The creature was furious. We're in for a fight. Quest Complete We brought the creature to the city as requested. Seems it left us a note. We defeated the strange creature. We decided not to bring the strange creature into the city. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] In order to receive this quest, the Strange Ox must have survived in both the Druid Grove and Last Light Inn and must not have been attacked by the party at Last Light Inn. There are also cutoff points for the quest: failed interactions with the Ox, crossing into the Lower City , or progressing the main storyline too far – a recommendation would be to trigger this quest in the earliest stages of Act Three . The Strange Ox can be found in Rivington , inside a stable near the Requisitioned Barn X: 41 Y: -143 . A DC 15 Insight Check indicates that the Ox is indeed the Strange Ox from past encounters. Using Speak with Animals allows its quest to be undertaken. The Ox says that it is delighted to see the party. It then further elaborates that it is trying to get into the city proper. After this, the following options appear: Not until you tell me exactly what you are. I suppose so. What form will you take? [DARK URGE]  Charge, charge through the city streets with me, leaving virgin hearts as smear-stains. Maybe some kind soul might. But not me. Smuggle the ox [ edit section | visual editor ] The Strange Ox transforms into an apple. If the dialogue option, "I suppose so. What form will you take?" is chosen, the Ox transforms into a Strange Apple , which the party must pick up to complete the quest. [ See: Bugs ] This Strange Apple spawns on the ground, making it easy to miss. Forgetting the apple causes the quest to fail upon entering the Lower City , and losing out on its possible reward. The journal reads, "We decided not to bring the strange creature into the city," even though the party can go back, retrieve the apple, and bring it there; the quest remains uncompleted. If properly brought to the Lower City upon entering for the first time, the Ox declares, "Oh-ho! Thank you for the lift, my friend. Thank you very much indeed. Ta-ta!" The quest then ends, and it disappears, leaving behind the Shapeshifter's Boon Ring and a Slightly Slimy Note . Attack the strange creature [ edit section | visual editor ] The Strange Ox transforms into an ooze. If the dialogue option, "Not until you tell me exactly what you are," is chosen, the Ox tells the party they do not want to go down that road. The following choices then appear: I assure you I do. Tell me what you really are, or I'll strike you down myself. Fine. I'll help you. Let us leave it at that. Then you go your way, and I'll go mine. If the dialogue option, "I assure you I do. Tell me what you really are, or I'll strike you down myself," is chosen, the Ox transforms into a level 9 ooze and attacks. If the quest was accepted, the party can still attack the Strange Apple, causing the Ox to reveal its true form and begin combat. This can be done even after the quest has failed. Once defeated (200 xp), it drops the Hat of Fire Acuity , the Shapeshifter's Boon Ring , and two random high-quality gems (e.g., Diamond and Jade ). Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] If smuggling the Strange Ox and safely delivering it to the Lower City: Shapeshifter's Boon Ring – if the ring was obtained earlier, the Ox leaves a random potion of moderate value in place of the ring. [ See: Bugs ] The Strange Ox also becomes an ally as part of ⁠ Gather Your Allies and can be summoned with An Apple a Day during the final battle against The Netherbrain . Because the Strange Ox remains alive, the party cannot receive the Hat of Fire Acuity . Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] In a multiplayer game, the quest reward is not given if the Strange Apple is in the inventory of the avatar character of a player other than the host when entering the Lower City. The reward is still given if the apple is in a companion's inventory, even if the companion is controlled by a non-host player. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death...
