## Reclaim the Blue Jay's Nest
- **来源**: [Reclaim the Blue Jay's Nest](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Reclaim_the_Blue_Jay's_Nest)
- **分类**: Quests

Blue Jay Reclaim the Blue Jay's Nest is a Quest in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Blue Jay at Rosymorn Monastery Trail . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 3 Quest rewards 4 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Kill the eagles. We met a blue jay who asked us to kill the eagles on the monastery roof. He claimed they stole his nest. We found eagles nesting on the roof of the monastery. These must be the ones the blue jay was talking about. Speak to the blue jay. We dealt with the eagles. We should tell the blue jay. Quest Complete The blue jay was thrilled to have his nest back. The blue jay is dead. He won't be needing a nest. We can no longer return to the monastery. The blue jay is on his own. Using the lance scared the birds off, including the eagles and the blue jay. It seems none of them will be needing the nest. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The Blue Jay can be found along the trail leading between the cable car stops X: -57 Y: -19 . If spoken to using Speak with Animals , the Blue Jay asks the party to get rid of the giant eagles that stole its nest on the roof of Rosymorn Monastery . After defeating the Giant Eagle and Ancient Giant Eagle , the party can return to the Blue Jay. At some point later, the Blue Jay relocates to the nest on the roof. When the quest is complete, it marks a treasure location on their map as Blue Jay's Find at X: -5 Y: -29 . Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] 10 XP and a random assortment of low-value items looted from the buried chest at the marked location. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The buried chest can be revealed at any point by passing a DC 25 Survival Check or simply digging at that location. If the Eagles are defeated using non-lethal damage, the Blue Jay swoops in and kills them while they are incapacitated. The Blue Jay can reveal through dialogue that it stole the nest it is currently inhabiting. Additionally, since Giant Eagles are Neutral Good aligned in Dungeons and Dragons 5E , and their nest is too big for the Blue Jay, it is possible that the Jay is trying to steal the Eagles' nest. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Rescue Orin's Victim
- **来源**: [Rescue Orin's Victim](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rescue_Orin's_Victim)
- **分类**: Quests

"Halsin" acts strange at camp. Rescue Orin's Victim is a sub-quest of the quest ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It is started automatically after entering Wyrm's Rock Fortress and long resting, or by entering the sewers for the first time. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 The Kidnapping 2.1.1 Kidnapping at Camp 2.1.2 Kidnapping in the Sewers 2.2 Orin's Demands 2.3 Finding and Confronting Orin 3 Quest Rewards 4 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Save Orin's victim. "Orin abducted Lae'zel. She told us that she'll release her if we kill Gortash." "Orin abducted Gale. She told us that she'll release him if we kill Gortash." "Orin abducted Halsin. She told us that she'll release him if we kill Gortash." "Orin abducted Minthara. She told us that she'll release her if we kill Gortash." "Orin abducted Yenna. She told us that she'll release her if we kill Gortash." Find where Orin is keeping her victim. "We refused Orin's deal to kill Gortash. There must be another way to save her victim - assuming they're still alive. We should find out where she took them." Destroy the Steel Watchers. "We defeated a Steel Watcher - Gortash now has one fewer mechanical lackeys protecting him. Investigating the Steel Watch may be a good approach." Take down the Steel Watch. "We found a letter from Orin explaining that striking down Gortash will be difficult with the Steel Watch protecting him. We should find the Steel Watch Foundry and take it down. Hopefully the abductee is still safe." Find Orin's next instructions. "We destroyed the Steel Watch Foundry as Orin instructed. She seems to enjoy infiltrating our camp and leaving messages for us there - maybe that's where we'll find further instructions." Kill Gortash. "With the Steel Watch destroyed and Gortash vulnerable, Orin left us a message with a clear directive: kill Gortash." Find Orin's final instructions. "Gortash is dead. Orin will surely have left another note for us at camp after learning this." Submit to the Bhaalist Murder Tribunal. "Orin left us a note congratulating us for killing Gortash. Her abductee is thankfully still alive. Before we can seek Orin in the Temple of Bhaal and rescue the victim, she demands that we submit to trial in something called the Murder Tribunal." Find Orin's victim in the Temple of Bhaal. "We were anointed Unholy Assassin at the Murder Tribunal, gaining access to the Temple of Bhaal. We need to find Orin there if we are to rescue her victim in time." "We now know how to gain access to the Temple of Bhaal, but Orin won't be happy that we dismantled the Murder Tribunal. We must reach the Temple and rescue her victim before she learns this." "We found Orin's victim tied to an altar. We should be careful as we approach." Check up on the victim. "With Orin defeated, we can finally see if her victim is all right." Quest Complete "We failed to save Orin's victim from her clutches." "Orin's victim is safe and sound back at camp." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The Kidnapping [ edit section | visual editor ] “ I can't even tell if any of you are acting strange because you've been replaced or because this group is full of weirdos. „ — Astarion , on the prospect of a Doppelganger in camp Orin the Red kidnaps a party member under various circumstances, typically after long resting upon arriving in the Lower City . Orin shapeshifts as the party member she abducts and speaks to the party. Orin only abducts characters who are alive, not romanced , and are not in the current party (i.e., at camp). Alternatively, if the party does not long rest first, Orin confronts them in disguise as the kidnapped victim in the Lower City Sewers . It is not possible to avoid the kidnapping before confronting Orin. She kidnaps the following companions, using the priority below: Lae'zel Halsin Gale Minthara Yenna Approval has no influence on the chosen victim. To avoid a companion being kidnapped they must either be romanced, in the active party, or dead . If all of the companions who could otherwise be kidnapped meet the above criteria, then Orin kidnaps Yenna instead. If no potential victims are available and Yenna is told she is unwelcome at camp, Orin still appears at camp disguised as Yenna to inform the party that the young girl was kidnapped. If the party somehow avoids triggering the cutscene in the sewers or at a long rest (i.e., by using Misty Step to get past Orin in the sewers), Yenna appears chained to the altar in the Bhaal temple. If the party somehow completely avoids talking to Yenna, Orin still takes on her form both in the sewers and at long rest. Kidnapping at Camp [ edit section | visual editor ] If the kidnapped party member is Lae'zel, "she" puts a knife to Yenna and claims that Yenna is a shapeshifter. The party can object, using the following options: [INTIMIDATION]  Let her go, Lae'zel. (DC 25) [PERSUASION]  There's something we're not seeing here. (DC 25) Otherwise, "Lae'zel" kills Yenna by slitting her throat. If Yenna is saved, she runs off and Orin reveals herself. If Gale is the unlucky target, "he" approaches the party about the orb in his chest and states he must sacrifice himself for the good of the many, otherwise Baldur's Gate will be only the first city to fall. As he seems to be exploding, "he" instead transforms into Orin, who reveals her kidnapping. If Halsin is kidnapped during a long rest, "he" appears about to kill Scratch (or Yenna, if Scratch is not present). "He" transforms back into his humanoid self, claiming that the corruption of the city is eating away at him. "Halsin" puts a knife to his chest, which the party can either slap away, try to use medicine to find a way to treat "Halsin", or try to persuade him to stand down. If Halsin's kidnapping is discovered in the sewers, "he" bursts out of a door and says he was forced to kill many people. He breaks down at his apparent guilt. Afterwards, Orin reveals herself and says the party must sharpen their wits to spare Halsin the true blade. If Minthara is captured, "she" is covered in blood and claims that Astarion, Isobel, Jaheira, Karlach, or Wyll was trying to kill her. "She" may show a dead body under a cloth, claiming it to be their corpse, slain in self defense. If neither Astarion, Isobel, Jaheira, Karlach, nor Wyll, is available, "she" claims it is Yenna. "Minthara" says no one at camp is trustworthy and that they must be slain in their sleep. Whatever the response, she then reveals herself to be Orin. If the victim is Yenna, she is cooking a meat skewer when the party member approaches. She tells them to try it, stating there is something special in it. This turns out to be Grub , the cat, who Orin killed and cooked into the skewers. If the party member repeatedly refuses to eat her 'meal', she breaks down in despair. With either result, Orin reveals then herself and the true nature of the meat skewers. Kidnapping in the Sewers [ edit section | visual editor ] If Orin's kidnapping is not triggered through a long rest, it can also be triggered in the Lower City Sewers . In this case, the event is mostly the same for each person - the kidnapped victim appears grievously injured and begs the party to run away, explaining how they were brutally tortured by Orin. Then, Orin reveals herself and her kidnapping plot. This event is triggered at three locations in the sewers - at the door to the room accessed from the Knights of the Shield Hideout , in the area close to the Undercity Ruins waypoint at X: -141 Y: 923 , or near the exit to the Szarr Palace at X: -91 Y: 878 . Orin's Demands [ edit section | visual editor ] After Orin reveals she has a hostage, she states her demands: Enver Gortash bound her blade when the Chosen Three initially came together, making her unable to harm him. For this reason, she needs the party to step in and kill him. After this, she intends to face the interacting party member in a battle to the death - the winner takes the Netherstones. As long as the party kills Gortash, she does not harm her captive. If the party pursues Gortash first and manages to complete ⁠ Get Gortash's Netherstone , Orin sends a bloody letter to camp titled "Congratulations on the Murder of Gortash." She tells the party that they must now face the Murder Tribunal and become an unholy assassin of Bhaal before they can face her. She gives them a location - Candulhallow's Tombstones and a password - 'Sicarius.' If the party does not want to face Gortash first, then ⁠ Investigate the Murders or ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal must be completed, unless the player character is the Dark Urge in which case Sceleritas Fel opens the door for them. Finishing one of these quests also reveals the location and password for the tribunal. Finding and Confronting Orin [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party ventures to the depths of the Temple of Bhaal during ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone , the victim is chained to the Altar of Bhaal. If the player character begins a conversation with Orin and picks the wrong option or fails a check, Orin immediately murders her victim. To save the victim, they must either succeed a check or use information on Orin's mother Helena Anchev . Alternatively, they can begin combat by attacking (with or without surprise), bypassing the dialogue entirely. The Altar can be opened using the Altar Key looted from Orin, lockpicked with a DC 25 Sleight of Hand Check , or opened with Knock . If freed during combat, the victim joins the fight as a controllable character. Stealthily lockpicking the altar before engaging in the battle initiates dialogue with Orin, as if the victim were still restrained, but allows the player character to bypass dialogue checks otherwise requirted to convince Orin to spare her abductee. Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] The rewards of ⁠ Get Orin's Netherstone The victim alive, if the party does not let them die Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] If the kidnapped victim is a companion, their non-equipped inventory is moved into a backpack which is transferred to the player character's inventory. Despite Orin's threats to murder the victim if the party does not accept her deal, she never actually does so before confronting her, regardless of choices or the time passed. If Orin is attacked during the kidnapping reveal, she teleports away after inviting the party to find her at the Temple of Bhaal . If the Dark Urge is chosen as the Origin but sends their companion to confront Orin, she automatically executes her hostage with no skill shecks to prevent her from doing so. If the party defeats Orin, but leaves the Bhaal Temple while the abductee is still chained to the altar, the victim dies as soon as the first party member crosses the temple threshold. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Rescue the Druid Halsin
- **来源**: [Rescue the Druid Halsin](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rescue_the_Druid_Halsin)
- **分类**: Quests

Halsin is imprisoned by goblins. Rescue the Druid Halsin is a sub- Quest of Act One's main quest, ⁠ Find a Cure . It can be initiated after entering the Druid Grove by speaking with various Non-player characters about Halsin's disappearance. This quest is the same as ⁠ Save the First Druid . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Entering the Goblin Camp 2.2 The Shattered Sanctum 2.3 Freeing Halsin 2.4 Priestess Gut 2.5 Minthara 2.6 Dror Ragzlin 2.7 Back in the Worg Pens 2.8 Getting the Rewards 3 Quest rewards 4 Companion approval 5 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Find the druid Halsin. Halsin was last seen leaving the grove with a group of adventurers. Halsin was actively researching the parasite - he might be one of the few people who understand our condition. Search for Halsin in the Goblin Camp We learned that a powerful druid named Halsin hasn't returned from an expedition into goblin territory. He might be able to help us. The druid Halsin was researching the parasite. He might be one of the few people who understands our condition - we need to find him. Halsin's research suggests that the parasite is connected to a Goblin Camp located in an old temple of Selûne. The adventurers were with Halsin when he disappeared. They might know what happened to him. We learned that Halsin transformed into a bear during the chaos of the failed expedition. He might still be in that shape. We learned that the goblins imprisoned the survivors deep within their camp. Halsin could be held captive there - if he survived. We discovered that the druid Halsin was here in the Goblin Camp and he claimed to be able to remove their parasites. If he's still alive, he might be able to help us. Aradin told us the druid Halsin was either killed or captured by the goblins. The only way to find out for sure is to infiltrate their camp. We found a group of goblins massacred by some kind of animal. Could this have been the work of the missing druid Halsin? Defeat the goblin leaders. We found the missing druid Halsin. He can't heal us, but if we help him defeat the goblin leaders, he may help us find answers at Moonrise Towers. We killed Dror Ragzlin, the goblin king. The drow commander Minthara is dead. We killed Priestess Gut, the goblin priestess. Return to Halsin. We defeated all three goblin leaders. We should report to Halsin. The goblins left to attack the grove. We should report to Halsin. Defend the Emerald Grove from the goblins. We found the missing druid Halsin. He can't heal us, but if we help defend the grove from the goblins, he may help us find answers at Moonrise Towers. Halsin has left to fend off the goblins attacking the grove. If the defences hold, we can find him there afterwards. Meet Halsin in the Emerald Grove. With the goblin leaders dead, Halsin and the grove can rest easy. We should meet him there to discuss what comes next. With the raiders dead, Halsin and the grove can rest easy. We should meet him there to discuss what comes next. Halsin has returned to the grove. He should be able to help us with our parasite now. We should speak to him. Halsin thanked us and assured us that Rath would reward us for rescuing him. Meet Halsin at camp. We found the missing druid Halsin. He can't heal us, but we might find answers at Moonrise Towers. He'll meet us at camp to discuss our next move. With the goblin leaders dead, Halsin and the grove can rest easy. He'll meet us at camp to discuss our next move. Learn more about Halsin. Halsin was defeated before he could help us with the parasite. Maybe his research can be of use. Celebrate at camp. Grateful for our help, the tieflings are celebrating our victory. Time to have some fun. Quest Complete We met the druid Halsin. He cannot cure us, but will join us as we embark for Moonrise Towers. There, we may discover more about our infection. With the grove's fate decided, Halsin has joined us as we embark for Moonrise Towers. There, we may discover more about our infection. We found a diary written by the druid Halsin. In it, he talks about the parasites originating in Moonrise Towers. Halsin believed that the parasites are coming from Moonrise Towers. The tieflings and the druids were defeated. It's unlikely Halsin will help us now. We left the area without seeing if the druid Halsin could help us. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Information on Halsin can be found by speaking to Nettie during ⁠ Get Help from Healer Nettie or by speaking to Rath. Both Rath and Nettie are in the Inner Sanctum, which is accessible via the stone door north of the Sacred Pool. Mentioning to Rath that Kagha seems dangerous makes him lament that a snake has replaced their leader. Pressing for more information results in Rath revealing that Halsin disappeared at the goblin camp. Nettie discusses more about Halsin if the party is honest with her about their affliction and symptoms, stating that Halsin could better treat them if he was around. Halsin can be found in the Worg Pens area at X: 393 Y: -60 of the Shattered Sanctum , in the interior area of the Goblin Camp . While in his wildshape bear form, his goblin captors are harassing him, unaware of his identity. Details on how to approach the Goblin Camp and free Halsin are described below. This quest can also be completed successfully by initiating the quest ⁠ Raid the Grove . To accomplish this, the party must reveal the location of the Emerald Grove to Minthara , causing her to lead an assault on the grove. While besieging the grove, the party can betray her. This strategy lures a good portion of the goblin forces from the Goblin Camp to the grove, causing Halsin to free himself and return to the Grove, once the siege defence is successful. Entering the Goblin Camp [ edit section | visual editor ] There are various check-point encounters on the path to the Goblin Camp. There are several methods to approach these, including but not limited to: A frontal assault. This approach may lead to turning the entire camp hostile if an alarm drum is successfully sounded. A mixture of diplomacy checks, such as Persuasion and Deception . Alternatively, it is possible to brute force through all diplomacy checks by utilizing the Tadpole Power during dialogue. Drow , or characters disguised as one via the Disguise Self spell, have special dialogue options to bypass diplomacy checks. Avoiding the check-points through Stealth or finding an alternative path (i.e. approaching the camp from the north-west). Approaching from the north-western path requires the party to deal with some sleeping guards who can be woken accidentally if a jumping party member lands near them. A Silence spell can effectively prevent this. Upon successfully clearing or bypassing the check-points and entering the camp proper, it is possible to freely partake in Goblin Camp activities, converse with the partying goblins, and take on various side quests (more information on the Goblin Camp page). Specifically for this quest, the party must venture into the interior of the temple. The Shattered Sanctum [ edit section | visual editor ] The cracked wall on the second-level of the Goblin Camp. There are three entrances into the Shattered Sanctum - the Heavy Oak Doors at X: 105 Y: 454 , the Passageway at X: 51 Y: 476 , or through the Cracked Wall on the upper level of the camp at X: -106 Y: 481 . The Heavy Oak Doors: This entrance is guarded by Warrior Trinzas , who can be persuaded through diplomacy, Tadpole Powers , or drow specific dialogue like the previous check-points. Violence is always a viable alternative, however, there is a risk the fighting draws the attention of other goblins in the area, leading to the alarms being sounded and all the goblins turning hostile. The Passageway: The path to this entrance is "guarded" by three Blast Mines (two charged with Poison Cloud and one with Explosion). Entering by this way places the party at the southeast corner of the Shattered Sanctum. The Cracked Wall: The wall is an object with 22 Hit Points , Sturdy , and immunity to all damage types except piercing (resistant) and force (vulnerable). This makes force-damage items/spells/abilities that can clear the 10 damage threshold - like Smokepowder Bombs or Eldritch Blast - ideal for breaking this wall. There are sleeping guards situation close to the wall. If using the Silence spell on the explosion or the guards to cover the noise, a confrontation can be avoided. There is technically a fourth entrance to the temple from the Selûnite Outpost in the Underdark , but that door is inaccessible externally, and must be be opened from inside of the Shattered Sanctum first via the Stone Discs or the wall Lever. Freeing Halsin [ edit section | visual editor ] Ornate doors in the Shattered Sanctum leading to the Worg Pens. Once inside, the party must approach the ornate door at the eastern side of the Shattered Sanctum at X: 342 Y: 32 to enter the Worg Pens , where Halsin is held prisoner. As long as the alarm was not raised, no one stops the party, assuming they are either a True Soul or a welcomed visitor. Alternatively, a party member can also get taken to the Worg Pens by getting themselves captured - either by offending the goblins (i.e. getting caught pick-pocketing), or through the potential events of the ⁠ Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help quest (drinking Gut's potion of sleep while not being resistant to it). In this case, the party member is taken to the prison at the Worg Pens, and has the option to break out and find Halsin that way. Regardless, once in the Worg Pen, approaching the cages triggers a cutscene where the goblins harass Halsin, who is disguised in his bear wildshape. Using Speak with Animals allows the interacting party member to understand Halsin in his animal form. There are various dialogue options to react to the scenario. Regardless of what happens, in order to free Halsin, the goblins guarding the area must be fought, including Butcher Vrak and Beastmaster Zurk . The Worg Pens where Halsin is kept captive. At the start of the fight, the goblin youths that were harassing Halsin try to flee and call for assistance. If successful, they draw in the guards outside the doors - Sharp-eye Neem , Sharp-eye Eef , and Sharp-eye Nass . Once freed, Halsin explains he came here with a group of adventurers to learn more about the mind flayer tadpoles, but was captured. He believes the goblin leaders are planning to assault the grove and offers to join the party as a temporary companion to escape. Accepting his offer turns the entire camp hostile. If Halsin's offer is rejected, he remains in the Worg Pens until the leaders are taken care of. Priestess Gut [ edit section | visual editor ] Priestess Gut can be found in front of the giant throne immediately north of the front entrance at X: 297 Y: -18 . She offers to brand the party with the Brand of the Absolute . Regardless of whether the brand is accepted, Gut recognises the party as fellow True Souls. She attempts to probe into the party's minds with her illithid powers. Allowing her to do this causes her to notice something is amiss. Explaining that it is the result of the tadpoles and asking if she can help, commences ⁠ Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help . Gut says that the party should join her in her private chambers. Following her to her chambers, she says that she has a cure for the tadpole and a special cleansing potion must be taken first. However, an Arcana check reveals that it is just a sleeping potion. If called out on this, or if the party member in question is resistant to sleeping potions (i.e. a drow, elf or half-elf), she becomes hostile, triggering several nearby goblins to do the same. However, if the potion is taken, she chains up the party member and says that she intends for them to become her pet squid. It is possible to break free with an Acrobatics or Strength check ( Rogues do not need a check to break free). If nothing is done at all, a special cutscene is triggered where Korrilla appears from a portal and assassinates both Gut and her Ogre guard. She then disappears after a brief conversation, warning the party to be more careful. Minthara [ edit section | visual editor ] The drow Minthara is in the northeastern corner of the Shattered Sanctum at X: 333 Y: 42 . There is a Scrying Eye which must be dealt with before defeating her; otherwise, the entire camp is alerted. Minthara can easily be taken out after speaking with her, as she runs across the bridge to gather the troops. While she is running on the bridge, attack the bridge's posts and she falls into the chasm below. Otherwise, once the scrying eye is dealt with, only Minthara and her minions in the room become hostile, so the other two leaders can still be dealt with stealthily. If Minthara is only Knocked Out instead of killed, she later can be recruited to the party in Act Two . Dror Ragzlin [ edit section | visual editor ] Dror Ragzlin is unique because he is the only member of the trio who cannot be killed without alerting the two other leaders and the rest of the goblins; killing him, no matter how, turns the entire Shattered Sanctum and Goblin Camp hostile. For this reason, it is best to wrap up all business in the Goblin Camp and acquire the waypoint in the Selûnite Outpost in the [Underdark]] below the Shattered Sanctum before killing or knocking him out. Dror Ragzlin is in the throne room to the north, casting Speak with Dead on an illithid corpse at X: 296 Y: 40 . A cutscene automatically plays as the party enter the room, with Ragzlin asking if they would like to speak to a squid. If Ragzlin communes with the illithid without party interference, its killer is revealed to be the party after the second question. This can be avoided by taking control of Ragzlin's questions with a DC 10 Wisdom Check and asking questions other than who is the killer such as "Why was the Nautiloid in Faerûn?" Asking an obvious question like "Who is the Absolute?" causes Ragzlin to be suspicious of the party. Otherwise, if the party is exposed as the illithid's killer, they can talk Ragzlin down through a Persuasion check or by using Detect Thoughts to reveal that he likes being called the Absolute's Right Hand. Back in the Worg Pens [ edit section | visual editor ] Halsin is grateful if the party return and report on the leaders' defeat, and is then willing to answer many questions about his knowledge of tadpoles, as well as the strange movements of Absolutists at Moonrise Towers. He tells the party to return to the Emerald Grove where he will meet them again. Upon returning to the Sacred Pool area, Halsin confronts Kagha about her actions. He either demotes her status to an initiate or casts her out entirely, depending on whether ⁠ Investigate Kagha was completed. Getting the Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] If speaking to Rath in the Inner Sanctum at X: 463 Y: -30 , he rewards the party for their service. In the Enclave Library there is a giant stone wolf statue in the room. There are four plaques surrounding the wolf. The party must combine the rune with the empty socket at X: -463 Y: 24 . After interacting with all four runes simultaneously, a hidden staircase is revealed, which leads to a special treasure room . Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Elixir of Poison Resistance Potion of Animal Speaking - 3x Potion of Greater Healing - 2x Robe of Summer Scroll of Animal Friendship - 2x Scroll of Hold Person Sorrow Wyvern Toxin Halsin joins camp, and can become a potential companion in Act Two. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Release Halsin from the worg pens:   +1 Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Once Dror Ragzlin is killed, the entire goblin camp, inside and out, becomes hostile. If the party spared Sazza from Minthara, Sazza may voice disapproval but does not become hostile. Thus, the She Cannot Be Caged! achievement can still be achieved. Traveling to Rosymorn Monastery Trail and back causes Halsin to die, concluding this quest. This happens even if the party avoid any long rests during the transition, either forced or voluntary. If having travelled to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail before doing a long rest, the celebration does not trigger. Then Halsin can be found waiting at the Sacred Pool , where the party can talk to him; this works after talking to Art Cullagh in the Last Light Inn in Act Two. The "Celebrate at camp" objective is skipped in this case. ## Rescue the Gnome
- **来源**: [Rescue the Gnome](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rescue_the_Gnome)
- **分类**: Quests

Barcus is tormented by goblins. Rescue the Gnome is a Quest in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It is initiated by discovering a group of goblins in the Blighted Village laughing at having tied Barcus Wroot to the blade of a windmill. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Solving the encounter peacefully 2.1.1 Intimidate, deceive, or persuade 2.1.2 Using the tadpole 2.1.3 Demand you be allowed to pass 2.1.4 Approach as a drow 2.2 Attacking the goblins 2.3 Freeing Barcus 3 Quest rewards 4 Consequences 5 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Approach the goblins. We spotted a deep gnome tied to the blades of a windmill. He's being tormented by a group of goblins. Defeat the goblins. The goblins attacked us. Stop the windmill. We've defeated the goblins. If we want to help the gnome, we'll have to stop the windmill. It took some convincing, but the goblins left. If we want to help the gnome, we'll have to stop the windmill. (70 XP Rewarded) Untie the gnome. Now that the windmill has stopped spinning, we should be able to untie the gnome. (15 XP Rewarded) Quest Complete After rescuing Barcus Wroot, we parted ways with him. We invited Barcus Wroot to our camp. The deep gnome was killed. We left without helping the deep gnome. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The only objective of this quest is to free Barcus Wroot . Approaching the windmill at X: 13 Y: 418 automatically initiates a conversation with the goblin leader Fezzerk . There are several options to resolve the situation. Solving the encounter peacefully [ edit section | visual editor ] There are a handful of ways of solving the encounter peacefully without combat: Intimidate, deceive, or persuade [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 1 ] [DECEPTION]  We're allies - I have the Absolute's Brand. Leave the gnome to me. (DC 5)  (if Branded with the Absolute) [DECEPTION]  We're allies, you and I. Servants of the Absolute. (DC 15) [INTIMIDATION]  You dare refuse a githyanki warrior ? (DC 15)  (Lae'zel only) [INTIMIDATION]  I won't let you harm a defenseless being - not without a fight. (DC 15)  (if not Lae'zel) [WISDOM]  Read the goblin's mind. You don't have the stomach for a fight. [PERSUASION]  You've had your fun - it's high time you found someone else to torment. (DC 15)  (non-Barbarian only) [INTIMIDATION]  Negotiations are over. Either leave or die. (DC 15)  (if not Barbarian or Paladin) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  ROAR.  (DC 15  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Mine.  (DC 15  ) [PALADIN] [INTIMIDATION]  I'm not bargaining with you. Free him, or I swear on my oath, you will die.  (DC 15  ) [PERSUASION]  All of you lot against one deep gnome? You should go find a better target. (DC 15) [HALF-ORC] [INTIMIDATION]  Don't utter a word. Just stare down the goblin.  (DC 10) [PALADIN] [INTIMIDATION]  I consider the gnome under my protection. You don't want to fight me for him. (DC 15  ) [BRANDED] [DECEPTION]  Show him your brand and say you're taking the gnome. The Absolute wills it.  (DC 5) [BARBARIAN]  Your skull will make a fine chalice one I plug those beady eye sockets. [FIGHTER]  You're making a mistake. You can think it over in the Fugue Plane. Using the tadpole [ edit section | visual editor ] [ 1 ] [TRUE SOUL]  You will release the gnome. That's an order. [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  You will release the gnome. That's an order. (DC 5) [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  I am a True Soul. Now once again - release the gnome. (DC 5) If convincing the goblins to walk away, the party is rewarded experience as if they defeated the whole group. Demand you be allowed to pass [ edit section | visual editor ] If trying to pass, Fezzerk claims that this is also what Barcus wanted, and demands 1000 gold, leading to several options: [ 1 ] Pay the goblin. [PERSUASION]  I might be willing to part with a more reasonable sum. (100) (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  Here's my counter-offer: a far more reasonable sum. (500) (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  That's a ridiculous amount. I'll make you a realistic offer. (250) (DC 10) [PERSUASION]  Haggle with the goblin, though you lack even a modest sum of gold.  (DC 15) [WISDOM]  Read the goblin's mind. Your price is absurd and you know it. [DECEPTION]  I can pay twice that much. I just have to go and fetch it. (DC 15) [MONK]  This will lead only to pain, not fulfillment. [ROGUE]  Provide directions to a non-existant cache of gold. [BARD]  Not an orator, eh? I could teach you how to talk gold out of any purse, for free passage. [INTIMIDATION]  Here's my counter-offer: you can all live so long as you leave right now. (DC 15)  (non-Barbarian only) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  OR YOU CAN LEAVE. ALIVE.  (DC 15  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Leave. Or die.  (DC 15  ) No matter which of the above checks succeed, Fezzerk lowers the price to 5 because he cannot count. Passing the Illithid Persuasion check can force his group to leave without payment. If paid, the party members are allowed to leave, but if approaching again, a fight breaks out. [ 1 ] Pay the 'higher' sum to the goblin. You do know that's a lower figure, yes?  (if have enough gold) You know that's a smaller sum of gold, yes?  (if doesn't have enough gold) [DEEP GNOME]  I've changed my mind - release the deep gnome and clear off. Or else. (starts a fight) [PERFORMANCE]  Wait! Just let me go... please.  (DC 5) [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  I'm going to pay nothing, and you and your cronies are going to leave. (DC 5) This causes Fezzerk and his group to leave, rewarding experience as if the party defeated them all. Approach as a drow [ edit section | visual editor ] Drow characters (or those disguised as one) can demand an explanation or demand that Fezzerk leaves. This causes Fezzerk to be nervous, and he asks the talking party member if they are a True Soul : [ 1 ] Of course I'm a True Soul. How dare you even question the fact?  (if aware of true souls) [PERFORMANCE]  I don't answer to the likes of you. (DC 5) [DECEPTION]  Naturally - do I look cursed to you? (DC 5) [INTIMIDATION]  Say nothing. Stare down the gibbering coward.  (DC 5)  (if not a Barbarian or Paladin) [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION]  ROAR.  (DC 5  ) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Did I say you could ask questions ? (DC 5  ) [OATH OF THE ANCIENTS] [INTIMIDATION]  I am nature's vanguard, you are but a stench on the breeze. Begone.  (DC 5) [OATH OF DEVOTION] [INTIMIDATION]  I am duty bound to Virtue itself. You are in my way. Leave this place. (DC 5) [OATH OF VENGEANCE] [INTIMIDATION]  I am the fear-dream of disloyal whelps. You are starting to irk me. Leave. (DC 5) [OATH OF THE CROWN] [INTIMIDATION]  I represent the law, which all must obey. And I order you to leave . (DC 5) [ILLITHID]  I am a True Soul. Your prisoner is now mine. (DC 5) [ILLITHID]  I am a True Soul. Your prisoner is now mine.  (if aware of true souls) [BRANDED]  Show them your brand. [BRANDED]  Show them your brand and tell them to carry on. All other options start combat. Attacking the goblins [ edit section | visual editor ] If attacking the goblins without attempting to convince them to stop or let the party pass (it is possible to ask what and why he is doing this first) nets   +1   -1   +5 . If a fight breaks out, he surrenders when nearly killed, causing the rest of his group to flee. It is possible to interrogate him, demand his possessions, or kill him. Experience is not granted for the goblins that run away, so to obtain the most experience while engaging in Fezzerk's surrender requires the party to kill all other goblins first. Barbarians have a unique dialogue path: [ 2 ] [WISDOM]  Ignore the rage. Listen to your head. There is nothing to gain from being rash.  (DC 10  ) [BERSERKER]  Give in. KILL THE MAGGOT. Leave reason to the reasonable. Kill the runt. Otherwise, the party can interrogate him: [ 2 ] I want the gold you took. Now.  (if the player paid him) Give me my gold back - and anything else you have, too.  (if the player paid him) Talk and you might live. If it's worth my while. Your valuables - now.  (if the player paid him) I want everything of value you have.  (if the player didn't pay him) Your valuables are mine now. Hand them over. ... or just kill or release him: [ 2 ] No mercy. Kill the goblin.   +1   -1   +1   +1   +5 Run along, goblin. Before I change my mind.   -1   -1   -5 Freeing Barcus [ edit section | visual editor ] The brake lever that will safely stop the windmill. Once the goblins are dealt with, the party must enter the interior of the windmill to pull the brake, allowing them to free Barcus. There are two levers inside the windmill. The "Brake" lever must be chosen to safely stop the windmill. The "Release Brake" lever causes the windmill machinery to spin faster, which launches Barcus into the sky by inertia, subsequently killing him. His body can be found on the western road leading out of the Blighted Village. If the windmill is stopped properly, the party can free Barcus by interacting with him. Barcus offers the party his luggage in the windmill basement, which contains various goods, including a Smokepowder Satchel . He reasons that lugging the extra weight resulted in the goblins capturing him. Saving Barcus is not required to obtain his possessions, as his luggage is in the basement regardless. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Smokepowder Bomb carried by Fezzerk Smokepowder Satchel The Speedy Lightfeet in the heavy chest next to Barcus' heavy backpack Very Heavy Greataxe carried by Fezzerk 45 XP for saving Barcus Wroot 190 XP for making Fezzerk and his group to leave. 210 XP for defeating all of Fezzerk's group. After one combat round or so, the rest of the group flees slowly. Besides killing the two devouts and Fezzerk, they do not grant any additional XP. 280 XP for making Fezzerk and his group to leave, going turn based mode to attack them, defeating the two goblin devouts and Fezzerk last. Consequences [ edit section | visual editor ] Saving Barcus has far reaching consequences for many quests, including ⁠ Save the Grymforge Gnomes , ⁠ Rescue Wulbren , and ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands . If rescued, he can be encountered again throughout Acts Two and Three . Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Exploring the Blighted Village or the area north of its walls may trigger the appearance of Barcus and the goblin group without triggering the quest. Entering Grymforge without rescuing Barcus (even without initiating the quest) causes the goblins to disappear and Barcus to die, locking the party out of this quest and future quests involving Barcus. ↑ 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 Dialogue file: Act1/Forest/FOR_GnomeGoblin1 ↑ 2.0 2.1 2.2 Dialogue file: Act1/Forest/FOR_GnomeGoblin1_Surrender_NotAtWindmill v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Rescue the Grand Duke
- **来源**: [Rescue the Grand Duke](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rescue_the_Grand_Duke)
- **分类**: Quests

A Flaming Fist attempts to rescue those within Waukeen's Rest. Rescue the Grand Duke is a quest in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by approaching the burning inn on The Risen Road , Waukeen's Rest . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Waukeen's Rest 2.1.1 Through the front door 2.1.2 Through the south-eastern building 2.1.3 If Florrick is saved 2.1.4 If Florrick dies 2.2 Last Light Inn 2.3 Moonrise Towers 2.4 Wyrm's Rock Fortress 2.4.1 Councilor Florrick 2.4.2 After the coronation 2.5 The Iron Throne 3 Quest rewards 4 Notes and references 5 Bugs Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Find a way into Waukeen's Rest. "We approached a burning inn called Waukeen's Rest. Flaming Fists are trying to break down the door - a Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate is trapped inside." "We couldn't get through the door. There must be another way in." Search for survivors. "We managed to get inside. We need to find the Grand Duke and fast." "We found a survivor trapped behind a locked door." "A man is stuck under some rubble. He's not the Grand Duke, but he still needs help." Speak with Counsellor Florrick. "The woman we rescued survived. Maybe she saw the Grand Duke?" Search for Grand Duke Ravengard. "We learned that the Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate was kidnapped." "We learned that the Grand Duke was captured by drow and taken westwards." "We agreed to look for the Grand Duke. We should investigate the area." "Moonrise Towers is a popular location - at least for the cult of the Absolute. Perhaps the Grand Duke was taken there too." "We agreed to look for the Grand Duke. We should head to Moonrise Towers." "We learned nothing from the woman we rescued. Someone else must know what happened to the Grand Duke." "We refused to help Counsellor Florrick. But we should keep an eye out for the Grand Duke - he'd make a powerful ally." "We didn't find the Grand Duke or anyone who'd seen him. We should still keep an eye out, though - he'd make a powerful ally." "We met Counsellor Florrick at Last Light Inn. She urged us to search for Grand Duke Ravengard. She believes he is being held in Moonrise Towers." "We finally reached Moonrise Towers. Grand Duke Ravengard must be here somewhere." Pursue Ravengard's captors to Baldur's Gate. "Grand Duke Ravengard was infected with an illithid tadpole, and taken to Baldur's Gate." Search for Grand Duke Ravengard. "We finally found Grand Duke Ravengard - standing by Gortash's side as he crowned Gortash the new Archduke. He disappeared after the ceremony." Talk to Mizora. "Grand Duke Ravengard is dead. Wyll's patron, Mizora, awaits us in camp. Perhaps she can help." Rest at camp. "Mizora asked us to meet her in camp. She has an important proposal to make regarding Wyll's father, Grand Duke Ravengard." Search for Grand Duke Ravengard. "Wyll severed his pact with Mizora, even after she hinted that she could help locate and rescue Grand Duke Ravengard. It would seem the duke is as good as dead, but perhaps we might still find and save him." Find the secret command centre. "Wyll made a pact with Mizora and the archdevil Zariel in exchange for information about Grand Duke Ravengard's whereabouts. He is being held prisoner at Gortash's secret command centre." Search for Grand Duke Ravengard. "We reached Gortash's underwater command centre, also known as the Iron Throne. We need to find Grand Duke Ravengard." Lead Grand Duke Ravengard to safety. "We found Grand Duke Ravengard. We need to lead him to safety." Speak to Grand Duke Ravengard. "Grand Duke Ravengard is safe at last. We should speak to him at our camp." "In exchange for an eternal pact with Wyll, Mizora resurrected Grand Duke Ravengard. We should speak with him." Quest Complete "Grand Duke Ravengard is dead." "Grand Duke Ravengard is safe, and grateful for our help." "Grand Duke Ravengard has been brought back from the dead and is free from the Absolute's influence, thanks to the Emperor. He will make a formidable ally when the time comes to face the elder brain." "Wyll broke his pact with Mizora, even after she offered to resurrect his father. Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard is no more." "Wyll broke his pact with Mizora. Duke Ravengard is no longer our concern." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Waukeen's Rest [ edit section | visual editor ] Florrick thanks the party for rescuing her from the burning inn. Warning! Approaching Waukeen's Rest closely enough to trigger companion dialogue and then long resting, fast traveling (e.g. to camp) or venturing to Rosymorn Monastery Trail , causes the trapped survivors, including Florrick, to die. If this happens, this quest can still be obtained in Act Three. Waukeen's Rest is an inn located on the Risen Road at X: -65 Y: 609 . As the party approach, they smell smoke and hear shouting. Through the front door [ edit section | visual editor ] At the front entrance there is a group of Flaming Fists trying to bust down the door. Gauntlet Yeva explains that Grand Duke Ravengard could be in there. [ 1 ] What happened to this place? Grand Duke Ravengard? [STRENGTH]  Push against the wreckage.  (DC 10) [PALADIN] [STRENGTH]  Let out a rallying cry as you help the Fists push. ONWARD! (DC 10  ) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  WE CAN DO IT! PUT YOUR BACKS INTO IT! PUSH!  (DC 10) You heard her, Wyll. Get in there.  (auto-success if Wyll is present) If the first two options are chosen, Yeva explains that the inn was raided by drow and goblins. Grand Duke Ravengard was lost during the raid. A successful Strength check smashes the door open and the Fists rush inside. The party must go straight into the room to find a set of stairs, and climb it to find the two remaining survivors Counsellor Florrick and Benryn . Attempting to rescue Benryn starts ⁠ Rescue the Trapped Man . Following the orders to go into the burning inn also grants the ⁠ Chain of Command inspiration to party members with the Soldier background. Florrick is in the northern room at X: -57 Y: 618 , which the Fists swarm as they enter the building. Attacking and destroying the broken door frees her. She then runs out of the inn with the Fists in tow, granting the following inspiration: ⁠ Rescued from the Flames ( Folk Hero backgrounds) ⁠ Protector of the Duke ( Noble backgrounds) Through the south-eastern building [ edit section | visual editor ] In the south-eastern building there's a room filled with crates and barrels. This room has a broken ceiling. Using Misty Step , Fly or utilizing Jump with a combination of stapled crates gets the party on the first floor. The party must head through the door, which has to be smashed or lockpicked. Behind the door is a small bridge that leads to another door that also needs to be smashed or lockpicked. Behind this door is the room where Florrick is found. Approaching her makes her leave the room, head to the bridge and through the second door. She then jumps or climbs to the ground floor and runs to the Flaming Fists at the front door. If Florrick is saved [ edit section | visual editor ] Outside, she requests that the party rescue the Duke, then leave to organize her own efforts. Before she leaves, however, she gives the party three rewards to choose from: The Joltshooter The Sparky Points The Spellsparkler After learning of the Duke's kidnapping, it is also revealed that Ravengard is Wyll's father. This starts part of Wyll's companion quest, ⁠ The Grand Duke . By casting Speak with Dead on a Dead Drow Raider near the entrance of Waukeen's Rest, the party can learn that the Cult of the Absolute is related to the kidnapping, and that the Grand Duke might have been taken to Moonrise Towers . At the Goblin Camp , the party can learn slightly more. If the party do a toast after poisoning the booze tub at X: -99 Y: 442 . As part of the toast, Warlock Gurk says "To tha' duke's face when we gave 'im to the drow!" If Florrick dies [ edit section | visual editor ] If Florrick dies because the party did not rescue her in time, later events in Act Two and Act Three with Florrick will not occur. However, Rescue the Grand Duke can still be obtained in Act Three at Wyrm's Rock Fortress. Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] During Act Two , the party can encounter Counsellor Florrick at the Last Light Inn with an entourage of Flaming Fists. She asks if the party have made any inroads with Moonrise Towers. Regardless of the response, she implores the party to keep looking. Florrick, however, departs for Baldur's Gate to seek reinforcements. Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Duke Ravengard is infected by the Chosen Three. In Moonrise Towers Prison , the party can ask the Warden if she has seen the Duke. However, she responds that he sounds important and that she only deals with the dregs down in the prison. The party can also interrogate the corpse of a dead goblin scout, Sharp-Eye Lora , who reveals that she took prisoners to Moonrise Towers including a duke. The Duke can eventually be found near the end of Act Two, during ⁠ Defeat Ketheric Thorm . In the Mind Flayer Colony , as the party chase after ⁠ Ketheric Thorm , they encounter the Chosen Three - Thorm, Orin the Red , and Enver Gortash , and with them Ulder Ravengard. The party watch in the shadows as the trio infect Ravengard with a mind flayer tadpole and then whisk him away to Baldur's Gate. Wyrm's Rock Fortress [ edit section | visual editor ] Duke Ravengard swears Gortash in as Archduke of Baldur's Gate. In Act Three , Duke Ravengard is encountered once again after completing ⁠ Find a way into Wyrm's Rock fortress . Once the party enter Wyrm's Rock Fortress , Gortash takes control of a Steel Watcher and invites the party to his coronation. Ravengard is in the Audience Chamber with Gortash and officiates Gortash's swearing in as Archduke of Baldur's Gate. Immediately after the ceremony, Ravengard can be spoken to. Councilor Florrick [ edit section | visual editor ] If Florrick was rescued at Waukeen's Rest and the party mention that she sent them, he says that she is a black widow who betrayed the city, and that she was punished. Choosing to connect with Ravengard's parasite to seek information about Florrick reveals that she is imprisoned in Wyrm's Rock Prison and set to be executed, starting ⁠ Free Counselor Florrick . If Florrick died at Waukeen's Rest the ⁠ Free Counselor Florrick quest cannot be obtained. The party can prod Ravengard's mind further, and find out that deep uncertainty and fear of an illithid invasion is within him, indicating his mind has not fully been taken over. After the coronation [ edit section | visual editor ] Once the coronation is complete, Mizora appears and reveals that Duke Ravengard is already being moved to another location to be disposed of. She refuses to elaborate further and tells the party to go to camp. After a Long Rest, Mizora appears before Wyll to present a new contract - an eternity of servitude for Zariel in exchange for rescuing the Duke. If Wyll signs the contract, she reveals that Duke Ravengard is in Gortash's underwater prison, the Iron Throne and promises to keep him from harm. Otherwise, if Wyll breaks the contract, Mizora states that he is as good as dead, but that she plans to stick around to see what happens. Wyll does not have to accept Mizora's new pact to save his father, but must speak to Mizora at camp before traveling to the Iron Throne, or the Duke will be dead. This changes the bargain Mizora offers Wyll at camp from revealing the Duke's location to resurrecting him from the dead in exchange for Wyll's soul, forever bound to her and Zariel, with the alternative remaining the same – to break the pact immediately. If the party ignore the coronation and move into the Lower City , then Duke Ravengard remains in the Audience Hall with Gortash until the ceremony is completed. If the party complete the ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch without attending the coronation, then the entirety of Wyrm's Rock Fortress becomes hostile, including Duke Ravengard. To ensure that the Duke can be rescued, it is advised to attend the coronation, speak to Mizora, and take a long rest to ensure that he can be found in his intended location. The Iron Throne [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Iron Throne After the previous events, Duke Ravengard is moved to the Iron Throne , either alive or dead. The party may find the Iron Throne either by exploring the Lower City, or be led there as part of the quests ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch , ⁠ Save the Gondians , ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands , or ⁠ Avenge the Drowned . Map of the Iron Throne Duke Ravengard is in the block of cells directly east from the ladder to the submersible. He is in the middle cell with only 35 current HP if alive. He also has the Fiendish Obeisance status, unless Wyll is not recruited to the party. Upon opening the door to his cell, the Duke becomes an Attached Follower . If Wyll broke his pact with Mizora, she appears and attempts to kill the Duke: once he leaves the cell, she gives him the Fiendish Obeisance: Kneel status for one turn, preventing him from moving and giving him Disadvantage on Dexterity saves, and summons multiple Combustion Belly Spiderlings next to the Duke which self-destruct using Spiderling Burst on their turn or when killed. The Duke can be helped to survive or avoid the spiders by a variety of means including healing, granting protective effects such as Fire Resistance through Protection from Energy: Fire or throwing an Elixir of Fire Resistance near him, Shield of Thralls , Invisibility , Sanctuary (though this doesn't protect against Spiderling Burst ) or helping him escape quicker with mobility spells such as Haste , Dimension Door , Arcane Gate or Omeluum's unique ability Teleport to Submersible (Omeluum can be found here only as part of ⁠ Retrieve Omeluum ). Mizora does not appear if Wyll died before resigning their pact and so will not summon the Spiderlings or force the Duke to kneel [ verify ] . Mizora cannot force the Duke to kneel if Fiendish Obeisance is removed with Greater Restoration . If Mizora and her witnesses Cirrus and Feena are not first spoken with at camp, the Duke is found dead. After escaping the Iron Throne, the party may be able to make a deal with Mizora to resurrect the duke in exchange for renewing Wyll's pact, or reject the deal in order to break his pact. The availability of this option may depend on Wyll's status and earlier choices. If Gortash is defeated before traveling to the Iron Throne, the prison is automatically destroyed and Duke Ravengard is killed, although only implicitly. But if Wyll made the pact with Mizora, she brings him back to life in camp as if nothing happened. If Duke Ravengard is saved, he stays at camp under the protection of the Astral Prism . If Wyll is recruited to the active party, the pair can reconcile, and Ravengard asks the party to seek out Ansur , Baldur's Gate's guardian dragon who sleeps under the city. If Wyll is killed (e.g., as a result of an altercation with Karlach during Act One ), this detail is NOT shared with Ravengard when sharing the player character's memory via The Emperor . Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] After rescuing her from the burning inn, Counsellor Florrick grants the party a choice between three items, which all have similar abilities: The Joltshooter The Sparky Points The Spellsparkler If Duke Ravengard is rescued, he becomes an ally as part of ⁠ Gather Your Allies . Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ Dialogue file: Act1/Plains/PLA_FlamingFists Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Even if Wyll decides to break Mizora's Pact and allows his father to die for his freedom, Karlach may, if spoken with immediately after Mizora's cut-scene concludes, still comment as if Wyll signed his soul over eternally to Zariel. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Rescue the Illithids' Captive
- **来源**: [Rescue the Illithids' Captive](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Rescue_the_Illithids'_Captive)
- **分类**: Quests

Maybe we should leave her there? Rescue the Illithid's Captive is a quest in the Prologue of Baldur's Gate 3 . It can be initiated by approaching Shadowheart's Mind Flayer Pod on the Nautiloid . This quest is not available if the player chooses Shadowheart as their Origin . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 3 Quest rewards 4 Notes and references Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Find a way to release the captive. "We encountered a survivor, trapped inside one of the pods aboard the nautiloid. Perhaps we can find a way to free her." If the player character found an Eldritch Rune: "We found an Eldritch Rune. It may help us to rescue the captive half-elf." Talk to the half-elf. If the player character used the Eldritch Rune: "We opened the pod using an Eldritch Rune, and freed the captive. We should speak to her." If the player character passed a Strength check as a barbarian : "We forced the pod open using our brute strength, freeing the captive. We should speak to her." Quest Completed! If the player character recruits Shadowheart: "We learned that the survivor aboard the nautiloid is called Shadowheart. She joined us." If the player character does not offer for Shadowheart to join them: "We learned that the survivor aboard the nautiloid is called Shadowheart. We decided to go our separate ways." If the player character does not speak to Shadowheart after freeing her: "We freed the captive aboard the nautiloid from her pod, but left her behind." If the player character does not free Shadowheart: "We left the captive inside the pod, and escaped the nautiloid without her." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] After the first imp fight on the Nautiloid, the party must enter a room with two unconscious victims of the mind flayers, a high elf and human . Towards the north-east side of the room, Shadowheart is trapped in a mind flayer pod. If speaking to Shadowheart, she suggests trying to open the pod by using a nearby panel. The party can try one of the following options to physically free her from the pod: [ 1 ] Grip the pod's lid and pull. [BERSERKER] [STRENGTH]  RIP THE POD OPEN.  (DC 10) [BARBARIAN] [STRENGTH]  Don't give up. Tear this thing open.  (DC 10) Otherwise, the pod does not budge. If examining the nearby console, an empty socket is revealed. Sorcerers, Warlocks, and Wizards can attempt to study it and then inscribe the right runes: [ 1 ] [SORCERER] [WARLOCK] [WIZARD] [ARCANA]  There's magic at work here. Determine what kind.  (DC 7) Inscribe the device with the glyphs you sensed from the pod's warding runes. Otherwise, the party must obtain an Eldritch Rune from a corpse in the far east room at X: 62 Y: -355 which can be inserted into the empty socket in the console to power it up. A further check can be made to reveal that the console controls the release of the pod: [ 2 ] [ARCANA]  Take a closer look at the powered-up console.  (DC 10) Lastly, there is a final ability check to use the tadpole for the first time: [ 2 ] [ILLITHID] [WISDOM]  Will the pod to open.  (DC 2) After opening the pod, the party can recruit Shadowheart or ignore her. If the player character fails the DC 2 Wisdom Check to open the pod using the Eldritch Rune, it is possible try again with Lae'zel . If both characters fail the check, Shadowheart remains trapped in the pod but can be found after the Prologue in Act One . Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart as a temporary companion while on the Nautiloid.
