## Servant of None
- **来源**: [Servant of None](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Servant_of_None)
- **分类**: Quests

Servant of None is a personal quest for Karlach's origin, immediately starting in the Prologue . It has one sub-quest: ⁠ Forging a Heart . “ Ten years ago, I was sold to the archdevil Zariel - she put a hellfire engine in my chest and made me her prize soldier. But I've escaped now - thank you, mind flayers - and I've got a few scores to settle, if this engine doesn't burn me to ash first. I'll need people I can trust. An infernal mechanic. And a serious amount of luck. But you know what? I'm not worried. After ten years in the hells, I can take on anything. I've got my chance at freedom, and believe me - I'm going home . „ — Karlach , introducing herself in the Character Creation Menu Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Escape the Hells. "This is it. I've been trapped in the Hells for a decade - and this nautiloid is my ticket out." Patch up the heart. "I made it. The Sword Coast - I'm home! Almost, anyway. How far is it to Baldur's Gate? And where's the nearest infernal mechanic? This heart of mine is burning hot." "Dammon might be able to fix my engine. Better give him a shot at it." Deal with the paladins. "Those 'paladins' are Zariel's goons. I'll send them back where they came from." Live free. "With Zariel's lackeys gone, I'm free to live the life I want. Finally!" "The champion of the Blood Wars ran away from a few of Zariel's lackeys. No matter - I have more important things to worry about." Find Gortash. "He was right there. Gortash, the man who sold me to Zariel. The reason my heart's burning hotter than Hell's hole. I don't know what he was doing here, but I'm going to find him." Make Gortash pay. "There he is. Time to pay the piper, Gortash." Check Gortash's corpse. "Gortash is dead. I need to see him up close - I need to know he's gone." Save the city. "Gortash is dead. I thought it would feel different. Maybe once the city's safe again." "I need to turn down the heat on this heart. There's got to be an infernal mechanic in the city, right?" "I need to turn down the heat on this heart. Maybe Dammon made it to the city." Quest Completed! "Heart's blazing like a hellstorm and that bastard Gortash still walks the city. My city. Once it's safe, I can deal with the rest." "I would've liked to turn down this infernal heat a little, but I'm ready to save the city. At least Gortash isn't here to interfere." "I've done what I could. Upgraded my heart. Didn't make Gortash pay for his sins, but once the city's safe, nothing else will matter." "I've done what I came here to do. Upgraded my heart, tied up loose ends with Gortash - all that's left for me to do is save the city I love." Playing Karlach as an Origin [ edit section | visual editor ] Playing as an Origin naturally locks the player out of multiple interaction cutscenes which may occur when playing as any other character (including Custom Tav and the Dark Urge ). Many cutscenes concerning various interactions with other companions, NPCs and the environment, are left intact in their core. Most, though, are augmented with Karlach's own feelings and memories, voiced by the Narrator within the dialogue. [ verify ] As a playable character, Karlach also has several unique cut-scenes connected to her involuntary conscription into Zariel's army and to the problems caused by her hellish contraption's effects on herself and, by extension, those around her. ## Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders
- **来源**: [Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Solve_the_Open_Hand_Temple_Murders)
- **分类**: Quests

Sister Yannis is concerned about the veracity of Valeria's investigation. Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders is a Quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Sister Yannis in the Open Hand Temple . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Gather information 2.2 Find the Crime Scene 2.3 The Flower Key 2.4 Report Your Findings 2.5 Valeria's Kidnapping 3 Quest Rewards 4 Related quests 5 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Gather information about the murders. We've been asked to look into the deaths of Father Lorgan and Brilgor at the Open Hand Temple. Sister Yannis, the temple's rector, believes Brilgor's been blamed for the crime too hastily by Investigator Valeria. Sister Rose told us that Father Lorgan's corpse was missing a hand, cut off before he died. We should keep looking for more information. We learned that Father Lorgan was frozen in place by some sort of paralytic poison before he died. We should keep looking for evidence. Brother Donnick told us that Brilgor's body is out back in the cemetery, and Father Lorgan's is in the infirmary. We should check out both corpses for evidence. By speaking with the dead, we learned that a dwarf clad in red killed both Father Lorgan and Brilgor. We need hard proof to exonerate Brilgor, however, and should check out the murder scene. Find the crime scene. We learned that Father Lorgan uses the temple crypt to hide imperilled refugees. We should examine the crypt to learn more. The corpse of Brilgor mentioned that he and Father Lorgan were murdered in a hidden tunnel beneath the Open Hand Temple - we can access it through the temple crypt. Brother Donnick told us that Father Lorgan's corpse was found in the crypt underneath the temple kitchens. We could look there to find more information. The corpse of Father Lorgan mentioned that he and Brilgor were murdered in a hidden tunnel beneath the Open Hand Temple - we can access it through the temple crypt. Investigate the crime scene. A trail of blood ran from the Open Hand Temple crypt into a secret passage through nearby caves. We should follow it to find more evidence. We discovered the name of Father Lorgan's killer - Dolor. A name alone will not be enough to exonerate Brilgor, however. We found the weapon used to slay Father Lorgan and Brilgor - a dagger steeped in paralytic poison. It's good evidence - but we need something else to prove this crime wasn't just a murderous refugee. Find the lock to fit the flower key. One of the doppelganger assassins underneath the Open Hand Temple had a strange, flowery key. We should find what it opens. We found a murder weapon and flowery key underneath the Open Hand Temple. We should check what the key opens. Investigate Fraygo's Flophouse and find a use for the flower key. Fraygo's Flophouse is adorned with flowery motifs matching the key we found underneath the Open Hand Temple. We should see what the key unlocks. A key in Fraygo's Flophouse perfectly matches one we found under the Open Hand Temple. We should see if we can find more evidence about Father Lorgan's murder in the flophouse. We learned from a dead doppelganger assassin that the flowery key we found unlocks something in a flophouse - something that will reveal Dolor's secrets. Report your findings to Investigator Valeria. We found the lair of a Bhaalist murderer in Fraygo's Flophouse. A target list in the lair details the killer's instructions - slay specific Baldurians and frame the Absolute for it. Father Lorgan, priest of the nearby Open Hand Temple, is named on the list. Perhaps we should warn someone. Quest Complete Investigator Valeria wasn't pleased about it, but she accepted our evidence exonerating Brilgor. She asked us to bring the Target List to Gauntlet Devella in the Lower City to help solve another open case. Investigator Valeria is gone for good - as is our chance of clearing Brilgor's name. Investigator Valeria quickly realised Brilgor was not to blame for Father Lorgan's murder after her kidnap by the Bhaalist cult - his name is clear. We didn't have time to clear Brilgor's name before we had to face our ultimate foe. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Gather information [ edit section | visual editor ] Within the Open Hand Temple, Sister Yannis is having a conversation with Investigator Valeria at X: -44 Y: -6 . They are discussing the recent murder of Father Lorgan , which Valeria is investigating. Valeria states that the case is closed, implicating a refugee, Brilgor , as the culprit. Unsatisfied by this conclusion and feeling that the investigation is shoddy, Yannis asks the party if they will investigate. Choosing "If you think the Investigator did a shoddy job, I can look into the murder for you." or "Let me help you - I'll look around, see if there's anything to prove Brilgor innocent." has the party agreeing to investigate the case. She gives the party free reign to investigate any area of the temple, should they agree. Agreeing to investigate grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Assistant to the Extra-Planar Agent ( Sage backgrounds) ⁠ Drama Sleuth ( Entertainer backgrounds) ⁠ Trusting Your Instincts ( Folk Hero backgrounds) Sister Rose at X: -58 Y: -21 is in the same room as Father Lorgan's corpse, which is laying on a bed. If "I'm looking into Lorgan's death. I need to ask you some questions." is chosen, some answers can be acquired from Rose. Choosing "Who do you think killed Father Lorgan?" or "How did he die?" has Rose revealing that she found a paralytic poison on Lorgan's wounds and that his hand was sawed off to the bone. Brother Donnick at X: -57 Y: 11 is in the kitchen, and provides information on the location of Brilgor's corpse. He was buried out back, behind the temple X: -106 Y: -19 , and his casket can be dug up with a shovel. Using Speak with Dead , more information can be gleaned from both Brilgor and Father Lorgan. Lorgan's corpse reveals answers about his murder. Questioning Lorgan: Who are you? Father Lorgan Lorgan... Reverend... Open Hand... Who killed you? Father Lorgan Dwarf... dressed in red... Why did he kill you? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* What were you doing when you died? Father Lorgan Hiding Brilgor... from Fists... Why were you hiding Brilgor? Father Lorgan Must protect... innocents... Ilmater's will Where did you hide him? Father Lorgan Took him to tunnels... with the rest... fool... fool... How did you die? Father Lorgan A poisoned blade... paralysis... Where were you attacked? Father Lorgan Tunnels from the cellar... refuge... Find the Crime Scene [ edit section | visual editor ] Location of the hatch. The crime scene can be found via a hatch in the kitchen at X: -62 Y: 3 . There are pools of blood which can be followed to the exact location of the murders. However, the drops of blood abruptly stops in front of what appears to be a stone wall. There are three ways to get past this and into the secret tunnels beyond: Venturing into the adjoining room to the south and jumping over the cracks in the wall at X: 16 Y: -1026 . Opening the secret door in the crypt by locating the secret buttons in there. These buttons are obscured by heraldry at X: 17 Y: -1000 and at X: 18 Y: -1015 on the walls to the left and right of the stone wall. Using the entrance directly under the bridge of Wyrm's Crossing (on the path which leads the encounter between the Stone Lord's and Nine Fingers' thugs) is a cave entrance; this leads to the tunnels. The heraldry hides buttons to the secret tunnel. Moving into the tunnels, the party can encounter three dopplegangers: Muzz , Rudd , and Zomm . These dopplegangers instantly become hostile to the party. After killing them, Muzz's body holds the Field Report - Deathstalker Zumm , which reveals the name of the murderer, Dolor . Zomm's body carries a Flowery Key . Zomm's body can be spoken to with Speak with Dead , revealing more information about Dolor: Who are you? Zomm Zomm... Faceless... Eater of men... Did you kill Father Lorgan? Zomm No... Dolor did... Splendid... Kill... What were you doing here? Zomm Cleaning up... Dolor... Messy... Zomm Left his dagger... Careless... Who is Dolor? Zomm Our blood-red dwarf... Tricky... Hungry... Where is Dolor now? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Is Dolor one of you? Zomm Yes... But wants... More... What does Dolor want? Zomm Transcendence... Who do you work for? Zomm We... We... Narrator *The corpse tries to speak, but something prevents it.* Why did you want this dagger so much? Zomm Strong... Paralyses... How many more of you are there? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* I found this flowery key. What is it for? Zomm Flophouse... Dolor's secrets... Location of the hole with the murder weapon. Identifying Dolor grants the ⁠ Truth Shines Through inspiration for party members with the Folk Hero background. If passing a perception roll, the party can notice a hole in the ground at X: 67 Y: -1018 , which contains the murder weapon, Stillmaker . The Flower Key [ edit section | visual editor ] The Flower Key opens up a set of hidden doors at the uppermost level of Fraygo's Flophouse at X: -6 Y: :72 . After going up the stairs of the Flophouse, a ladder at X: -12 Y: 87 leads to the top floor where a red wardrobe can be found at X: -17 Y: 82 . Interacting with this door automatically uses the flower key and opens a hidden room. With a perception check, blood can be noticed on the floor near the bed at X: -13 Y: 76 . Choosing to examine the blood leads to an investigation check of 10. If passed, it can be noticed that a body is hidden under the bed. Pulling out the body reveals the corpse of Ffion Goldgrind . As with the other corpses, Ffion can be spoken to with Speak with Dead : Who are you? Ffion Goldgrind Ffion Goldgrind... What is this place? Ffion Goldgrind Landlord...contraband storage... How did you die? Ffion Goldgrind Murdered...by my son... What were you doing when you died? Ffion Goldgrind Seeking...answers... What answers did you seek? Ffion Goldgrind My boy...had a secret... evil secret... Who is your son? Ffion Goldgrind Dolor... Why did your son kill you? Ffion Goldgrind Found... His secret... My sweet boy... Why... What was your son's secret? Ffion Goldgrind Killed...folk...slowly...he liked it... Who has your son killed? Ffion Goldgrind Me...and...and... Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* Who was your son's next target? Ffion Goldgrind Ilmater temple...Didn't see...exactly who... Where can I find your son? Narrator *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.* What does your son look like? Ffion Goldgrind Dwarf...Like me...Dresses in...red... Did your son kill you? Ffion Goldgrind Yes...grinned...whole time... On the table to the right of the room's entrance is a Bloodstained Parchment at X: -21 Y: 79 . This parchment contains a list of murder victims and can be picked up to present to Valeria as hard evidence. Report Your Findings [ edit section | visual editor ] After leaving the Open Hand Temple, Valeria can be found drinking upstairs in Sharess' Caress at X: 24 Y: 92 . Speaking with Valeria and selecting "Afraid so - I've found new evidence, Investigator." allows the party to share the results of their investigation. Selecting "Father Lorgan's murder is just one part of a bigger plot, a Bhaal plot." and then "It's not a theory - I have proof. This document contains information connecting the murders to the Bhaalist resurgence." allows the party to show Valeria the bloodstained parchment. The party member who speaks to Valeria must have the Bloodstained Parchment and Stillmaker in their inventory to get dialogue options about them. If the party successfully finds enough information to exonerate Brilgor of Father Lorgan's murder and picks up the bloodstained parchment in Fraygo's Flophouse, then Valeria refers the party to speak to Gauntlet Devella at the Elfsong Tavern and provides a pass to the Lower City to allow them entrance. Valeria directs the party to the Elfsong Tavern. Valeria's Kidnapping [ edit section | visual editor ] As the party progresses into the Lower City , Valeria is eventually kidnapped by Bhaalists and can be encountered as a part of ⁠ Investigate the Murders and ⁠ Impress the Murder Tribunal . If she is rescued, she accepts that the Bhaalist plot is not a hoax and provides more information on the location of the Bhaalist Temple. Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Lower City Pass Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] The area of the murder leads the party to an area where ⁠ Help the Cursed Monk can also be completed. Additionally, finding the Bhaalist murder list leads to Ffion's corpse, where Mamzell Amira can subsequently be notified for ⁠ Find the 'Stern Librarian' Ffion . Successfully providing evidence of the Bhaalist plot allows the completion of ⁠ Find a way into Wyrm's Rock fortress . Astarion approves, if passing the Investigation check on finding the body on Fraygo's Flophouse To speak with Brilgor's dead body you first need to drag his portrait out of the coffin inventory screen onto the ground. If you free Valeria from the Murder Tribunal before reporting your findings, she will disappear and you won't be able to complete the quest . v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Steal a Githyanki Egg
- **来源**: [Steal a Githyanki Egg](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Steal_a_Githyanki_Egg)
- **分类**: Quests

The githyanki egg is struggling to hatch. Steal a Githyanki Egg is a Quest in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Lady Esther at the Mountain Pass . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Accessing the Monastery 2.2 The Githyanki Crèche 2.3 Acquiring the egg 2.4 Returning to Esther 3 Rewards 4 Consequences 5 Bugs Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Search the Githyanki Crèche for an egg. "Lady Esther has asked that we steal an egg from the githyanki. The Society of Brilliance want to incubate it, raise it, and soothe its so-called violent nature." "We convinced Lady Esther to pay us to steal the githyanki egg up front." Take the egg from the Hatchery. "We learned of an egg being kept in the githyanki Hatchery. It's guarded by a caretaker and two guards. There must be some way to steal it." Take the egg to Lady Esther. "We snatched the githyanki egg from the Hatchery. Lady Esther will pay us handsomely for it." Quest Complete "The githyanki egg has been destroyed." "We kicked the egg off a cliff." "We tricked Lady Esther into taking an owlbear egg instead. She thanked us, and rewarded us." "We gave Lady Esther the githyanki egg. She appreciated our help and rewarded us." "Lady Esther is gone. There's no chance of giving her an egg now." "We tricked Lady Esther into taking an owlbear egg instead." "We gave Lady Esther the githyanki egg. She appreciated our help." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Lady Esther is found northeast of the Trielta Crags Waypoint in the Mountain Pass at X: -43 Y: -128 . There Esther asks the party if they have seen the "stupid little hive" known as the crèche. She explains that she was chased off after trying to buy a githyanki egg. The Society of Brilliance asked her to acquire one of their roe so they can incubate it and, once it hatches, raise the spawn in their tradition. Esther asks the party to acquire an egg for her, and says she will reward the party handsomely for their service. The party can insist on payment upfront with a successful DC 21 Persuasion Check , agree to do the task, refuse, or kill Esther outright. Accessing the Monastery [ edit section | visual editor ] The broken door to the Monastery leads the way in. The Rosymorn Monastery is accessed from the Mountain Pass. The party must find the Cable Car Wheel at X: -47 Y: -74 and succeed a DC 15 Strength Check to summon it. After climbing on the cable car, the party can use the wheel to move toward the Monastery. Following the path east to the doors of Rosymorn Monastery triggers a cutscene where a group of githyanki warriors shoot down some cultists. Unfortunately, the doors are locked and magically enchanted, but there are broken windows that can be climbed through just west of the doors at X: 64 Y: 31 . Once inside, a number of drunk Kobolds can be snuck past or killed. The party must move north to the giant crack in the wall, and then jump up the rocks to get higher up on the Monastery. The Githyanki Crèche [ edit section | visual editor ] Climb the cliffs to access the upper levels of the Monastery. From upper floor, the party must move north up the hall, then jump across the gap to the west. On moving north, then west, the party can find a set of crumbling stairs. Jumping past the gaps allows them to follow the stairs down. After descending the stairs, the party must move north, destroy the barricade on the western wall, and walk through. Moving north through the oak door and west past the statue of Lathander , the party can find a lever on the wall at X: 78 Y: 49 that opens the monastery doors; this makes reentering the monastery easier. After moving west and following the stairs to the north, the party can reach the monastery basement at X: 74 Y: 80 to enter the Crèche Y'llek . The githyanki are suspicious of outsiders. If Lae'zel is present, she can smooth the way without any checks. Otherwise the party can gain access by persuading, intimidating, or deceiving the guards. Acquiring the egg [ edit section | visual editor ] The Hatchery northwest of the Crèche Y'llek Waypoint at X: 1322 Y: -781 is filled with a number of dangerous traps, as well as acid. To avoid getting damaged the party can use the rocks. The overseer, Varsh Ko'kuu , can be met on the cliff overlooking the egg at X: 1289 Y: -759 . Speaking with him reveals that there is only one egg remaining, which has a limited time to hatch before it will be destroyed by Kith'rak Therezzyn . I am here to help you save the egg. I wanted to see the hatchery. I didn't expect it to look so empty. You mistook me for someone. Who were you expecting? I came here to steal an egg. Varsh Ko'kuu wants to see the final egg hatch. If the party choose one of the first three options and pass an DC 10 Insight Check , Ko'kuu explains that the Kith'rak will come any day now to destroy the egg, as it is the last one left to hatch. This seems like an awful lot of fuss for one egg. What will happen to this egg if it doesn't hatch? [PERSUASION]  Why do you care so much about one dud egg? (DC 16) If Ko'kuu is asked why he cares so much, he says he was the last one of his brood to hatch; he wants the egg to have the same chance. Choose " DC 16 Persuasion Check . Let me help - I can take it somewhere safe" and Ko'kuu asks what the party will do with it: I'll raise it as if it were my own flesh and blood. I'll make the best omelette you've ever tasted. I'll find another crèche. One that's more forgiving. [GITHYANKI]  I'll see that it becomes the greatest ghaik -slayer you've ever seen. Depends, how much do you think these things sell for? If the interacting party member states they will raise it or find it another creche, Ko'kuu agrees to relinquish the egg. Claiming their intention to make an omelette or sell the egg turns him hostile. If Ko'kuu is convinced to give up the egg, he provides Varsh Ko'kuu's Boots , which can aid in approaching the egg, and the hidden traps in the room become visible. Once the egg is reached, the party must interact with it to get the chance to pick it up, step on it, or leave it. Stepping on it turns Varsh and the other Githyanki hostile. Returning to Esther [ edit section | visual editor ] Once the party return to Esther, there are several options: Esther can be given the egg, after which she rewards the party, or told the egg was destroyed, which turns her hostile. Esther can be given an Owlbear Egg and convinced to take it with one of the following options: [NATURE]  The curves, the colouration, the size - looks right to me. (DC 21) [DECEPTION]  No, but this owlbear egg is worth much more. And it can be all yours. (DC 21) [PERSUASION]  Of course not. It's from an owlbear. But I bet your employers won't know the difference. (DC 21) The Dark Urge has a unique option to kick the githyanki egg over the cliff right in front of Esther, which turns her hostile and causes Paladins to break their Oath. The party can keep the egg for themselves and return it to the Lodge personally for a reward. The party can refuse to hand the egg over to Esther. If she was persuaded to pay upfront beforehand, she turns hostile. Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] 449 Gold - if the egg is given to Esther 1000 Gold - if the egg is sold to Havkelaag in Act 3 (although the party might not get the full amount if they took the advance from Esther) 466 Gold - if succeeding a DC 21 Persuasion Check to convince Lady Esther to pay upfront (if the player character is a githyanki or in a githyanki disguise , the amount is lowered to 272 Gold) 485 Gold - if the owlbear egg is given to Esther and a DC 21 Persuasion Check to convince Lady Esther to deceive her employers Consequences [ edit section | visual editor ] If Esther is given a genuine githyanki egg, its grown progeny appears up in a portal at the Society of Brilliance Lodge in the Lower City in Act Three . The githyanki is now fully grown, going by the name Ptaris . He reveals that he was raised by Lady Esther and a dwarf named Havkelaag , who sped up his aging. As a result of the Society's rigid upbringing, Ptaris murdered both of them and other Society members including Omeluum ). He becomes aggressive to the party if he is not convinced that the Ptarian code he was raised by was wrong. Additionally, if the egg is given to Esther, the quest ⁠ Retrieve Omeluum does not appear during ⁠ Save the Gondians . If the egg was taken and then given away, regardless of who it was given to, Orpheus confronts the party about their choice if he is freed during ⁠ Free Orpheus . If the egg was not given away and Lae'zel survives until the Epilogue , she reveals that the egg has hatched, and that she has named the boy "Xan" ("freedom" in the Gith language). She notes with pride that he will have the chance to choose whatever path in life which calls to him. If the egg was not given away or left with Lae'zel, but instead left in the camp chest of the Elfsong Tavern before the final battle, then the newspaper clippings in the epilogue have an article title alluding to the egg hatching, and the newborn Gith crawling around the bar. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] When speaking to Lae'zel after picking up the egg, she may demand that the party not give the egg to Esther, even if Esther was killed while Lae'zel was present. v t e Act One quests Blighted Village Destroy the Ancient Tome Finish the Masterwork Weapon Rescue the Gnome Search the Cellar Unlock the Ancient Tome Druid Grove Defeat the Goblins Find Doni Find Your Belongings Investigate Kagha Investigate the Beach Kill Kagha Raid the Grove Return the Locket Save Arabella Save the First Druid Save the Goblin Sazza Save the Refugees Steal the Sacred Idol Goblin Camp Rescue Volo Grymforge Free True Soul Nere Blind the Absolute Find Explosives Get Past the Rubble Help the Cursed Monk Save the Grymforge Gnomes The Adamantine Forge (Quest) Mountain Pass Find the Blood of Lathander Steal a Githyanki Egg Ravaged Beach Explore the Ruins Free Lae'zel Risen Road Find the Missing Shipment Free the Artist Hunt the Devil Rescue the Grand Duke Rescue the Trapped Man Sunlit Wetlands Save Mayrina Underdark Avenge Glut's Circle Cure the Poisoned Gnome Defeat the Duergar Intruders Deliver Nere's Head Find the Missing Boots Find the Mushroom Picker
## Steal the Sacred Idol
- **来源**: [Steal the Sacred Idol](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Steal_the_Sacred_Idol)
- **分类**: Quests

Mol wants revenge. Steal the Sacred Idol is a Quest in the Druid Grove in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be initiated by speaking with Mol after earning her trust by helping the various tiefling children in the Druid Grove . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Stealing the Idol 2.1.1 Combat 2.1.2 Assassination 2.1.3 Peacefully ending the rite 3 Quest Reward 4 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Steal the druids' sacred idol. Mol asked us to steal some kind of idol from the druids. Fight the druids. We took the sacred idol and disrupted the ritual - but now the druids are attacking the tieflings. Give the Idol of Silvanus to Mol. Mol asked us to steal a sacred idol from the druids. Luckily, we already have it. We stole the sacred idol and killed all the druids. Now we just need to deliver the idol to Mol. Even though the ritual to seal the grove had been halted, we stole the sacred idol. Now to deliver it to Mol. Find Mol in Baldur's Gate. We gave the sacred idol to Mol. She promised to repay us in Baldur's Gate. Mol and her crew left for Baldur's Gate before we could speak with her. We should look for her in the city. Quest Complete We gave the sacred idol to Mol. She promised to repay us in Baldur's Gate. We angered Mol and her gang - they won't deal with us anymore. We decided to keep the sacred idol for ourselves. The tieflings were forced out of the grove before we could steal the sacred idol. We left the grove without stealing the sacred idol. We weren't able to return the idol to Mol. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Hatch to the tiefling hideout. In order to receive this quest, the party must be on good terms with the tiefling children in the Grove. A variety of quests influence how Mol sees them: ⁠ Find Your Belongings - Not threatening the tiefling children ⁠ Investigate the Beach - Saving Mirkon from the Harpies ⁠ Return the Locket - Resolving the conflict with Meli keeping the locket ⁠ Save Arabella - Saving Arabella from Teela The most effective way to gain Mol's respect is to rescue Mirkon. He informs the party about the location of the tiefling hideout and the password needed to enter, allowing a simple path forward. Once inside, Mol greets the party and thanks them for all the good deeds they've done for the children. Choosing Thought you might need help with something results in Mol requesting the party steal the Idol of Silvanus as revenge for hurting Arabella and the other tiefling refugees. Agreeing to steal the idol starts the quest. If not choosing the dialogue option to help Mol the party is locked out of the quest and its reward. Stealing the Idol [ edit section | visual editor ] The Idol of Silvanus is in the center of the Sacred Pool X: 243 Y: 507 right in the middle of the Rite of Thorns ritual and surrounded by druids. Combat [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Emerald Grove/Combat Idol of Silvanus in the Sacred Pool. Stealing the idol while the ritual is underway starts a cutscene where a signal is given and the druids commence a pre-arranged slaughter of every tiefling within the Grove. The druids also become hostile to the party with the notable exception of Rath and Silver who side with the tieflings. As the fight happens in real time, careful planning is required to avert a massacre. The final stand takes place in the makeshift prison where all the tiefling civilians are holed up. If enough of them are killed then ⁠ Save the Refugees fails. Assassination [ edit section | visual editor ] If the druids in the ritual circle are killed through Stealth , the party can safely take the idol. The quest says "now the druids are attacking the tieflings" but the massacre cutscene does not trigger and no such attack occurs. Peacefully ending the rite [ edit section | visual editor ] Completing the quest ⁠ Investigate Kagha , ⁠ Save the First Druid , or ⁠ Defeat the Goblins , ends the Rite of Thorns. Once the rite ends, this quest can no longer be started, and stealing the idol no longer immediately triggers grove wide combat – making it significantly easier to finish this quest if it was previously acquired. The idol can be discreetly stolen. Even if the party is caught, combat can be averted with a DC 15 Deception or Intimidation Check . Alternatively it is possible to steal the idol and fast travel away before being confronted about the theft. Quest Reward [ edit section | visual editor ] Ring of Protection ⁠ Heretic ( Criminal backgrounds) ⁠ Idolatry ( Urchin backgrounds) Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] After completing the quest, the idol can be bought back (or pickpocketed) from Mol, allowing the idol's bonuses to be kept. The price depends on the character's Charisma and standing with her. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Stop the Presses
- **来源**: [Stop the Presses](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Stop_the_Presses)
- **分类**: Quests

Vox populi, vox dei. Stop the Presses is a quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Estra Stir in the Lower City or Lens in Rivington or Ettvard Needle in the Baldur's Mouth . If this quest is not picked up before Gortash's death, it is then no longer available because the newspaper then solely reports on the Archduke's death. Ettvard Needle even calls the party "old news" and shoos them away. “ Ink and paper are not as insidious as the voice of the Absolute, but they send out their commands all the same. „ — Minthara , speaking to the player character after their conversation with Baldur's Mouth journalist Estra Stir. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Estra Stir and the Baldur's Mouth Gazette 2.2 Stopping the Hit Piece 2.3 Killing Ettvard 3 Result 4 Inspiration 5 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Talk to the editor of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette. "We met a journalist, Estra Stir, who told us we're set to star in the next edition of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette. We should find out why." Stop the Baldur's Mouth Gazette printing slander. "Ettvard Needle has written an article for the next Baldur's Mouth edition that will ruin our reputation. We must stop it from printing." "We found a test printing of tomorrow's article about us - it'll be disastrous for our reputation. We need to stop it printing." "We found the Baldur's Mouth printing press and it looks like we can change which headline article is printed in tomorrow's edition. To save our reputation, we should do just that." "We befriended Jelliwig, a fey creature within the Baldur's Mouth printing press, who'll swap tomorrow's headline article for us. We just need to find a replacement article." "A discarded article in the Baldur's Mouth building reflects positively on us. If we find the printing press, perhaps we can get it published in place of the planned hit-piece." Print a puff piece in the next broadsheet. "We found a positive headline about us to load into the printer - we just need to figure out how." "We found a positive headline about us for Jelliwig to load into tomorrow's edition before it prints." Check the next edition of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette. "We swapped out the negative headline with a different one we found in the Baldur's Mouth building. Tomorrow's paper should no longer damage our reputation." Quest Complete "We didn't stop the negative headline printing - and our reputation around the city is in tatters." "We destroyed the Baldur's Mouth printing press - preventing the negative headline about us from being printed." "Ettvard threatened to ruin our reputation, so we ruined him. Today's paper should instead cover his demise." "The Baldur's Mouth headlines should be singing our praises - we should see if the city's populace noticed." "The Baldur's Mouth headlines won't be mentioning us at all now - leaving our reputation intact." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Estra Stir and the Baldur's Mouth Gazette [ edit section | visual editor ] The front entrance to Baldur's Mouth Gazette Speaking with Estra Stir , just south of the Basilisk Gate in the Lower City at X: 122 Y: -66 , reveals that the party is the subject of the Baldur's Mouth Gazette's next issue - the juiciest one to date. Estra refuses to elaborate on what the piece intends to be about, nor hear any arguments about the party's consent to be written about. However, her statements start the quest, to investigate Baldur's Mouth by speaking to the editor. The Baldur's Mouth building is south of the Elfsong Tavern at X: 67 Y: -52 . Inside is the editor-in-chief, Ettvard Needle . If Ettvard is spoken with, he reveals that the article being published on the party is negative, and they should have thought about the consequences before disgracing themselves in public. The reason for Ettvard's hatred can vary - if the quest ⁠ Solve the Open Hand Temple Murders has been started, then he states it is due to getting involved in a murder investigation immediately after entering the city. If the ambush at the Circus of the Last Days has been encountered, there is a chance that he instead places the blame for the murder of the circus performers on the party. If the ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch quest is completed, he states that the party members were responsible for destroying the Steel Watch Foundry . Otherwise, he may blame them for a tenfold increase in Absolutist activity, or for the trafficking of Tiefling Refugees into Baldur's Gate . After Ettvard has been spoken with, the party members are kicked out of the Gazette and the door is locked, making entry significantly harder. However, it is possible to freely roam about the public parts of the Gazette before speaking with him. Stopping the Hit Piece [ edit section | visual editor ] Baldur's Mouth's roof has a hole in it that can reach the elevator. In order to stop the hit piece, the party must reach the printing press in the Baldur's Mouth basement. This can be reached by an elevator by the entrance or by metal doors downstairs near Ettvard. There are many ways to sneak into the area. One is to use Misty Step or Fly and jump to the roof of the Baldur's Mouth. Then, above the area where the elevator is, there are barricades which can be destroyed with blunt attacks or spells. After doing this, it is possible to jump down, and use the elevator's lever to sneak into the basement. Alternatively, a party member with Greater Invisibility can sneak in while the rest wait outside. The Gazette Basement. Once inside, two Steel Watchers patrol the corridors. By using Invisibility , Greater Invisibility , or Hiding – combined with Turn-Based Mode and Dash – one or more party members can slip past them without triggering combat. An iron gate separating the two main halls can be lockpicked; alternatively, party members can navigate through the northern side rooms by destroying the wooden barricades connecting them. The printing press lies directly past the gate. Upon arriving in the printing room, the party discovers that the printing press is a machine run magically by a fairy named Jelliwig . If the fairy Dolly Dolly Dolly was freed from the Moonlantern in Act Two, then Jelliwig recognizes the party, and offers to help immediately. Otherwise, it must be persuaded through dialogue choices and skill checks. What 'art' would that be? Are you a talking printer? Take one step further. Choosing the first two options results in the printer speaking up, introducing itself as Jelliwig, the 'artist' in charge of putting ink on the broadsheets. What reputation? [PERSUASION]  I'd love to see an example of your work (DC 7) [PERFORMANCE]  I'm actually a great admirer of your work - may I see? (DC 7) If Jelliwig is asked to change the article or stop the presses, it is reluctant to do so, for fear of angering Ettvard. Then get out of my way. I need to clear my reputation. [DECEPTION]  Help me change the article or I'll banish you from the printer. (DC 15) [PERSUASION]  Wouldn't changing the article be delightfully naughty? (DC 15) [BARBARIAN] [INTIMIDATION]  Do it, you stupid creature. Unless you want to be ripped apart, piece by piece? (DC 10) [SORCERER] [INTIMIDATION]  Do it, or I'll melt you into a steaming pile of iron and regret. (DC 10) If the check is passed and Jelliwig agrees to help, it then states that it needs a new printing block to replace the old one. Appropriate blocks are located throughout the basement, as well as in baskets on the Baldur's Mouth's main floor. Choosing 'Take one step further' and 'Take another step further' results in different checks: [ATHLETICS]  Force the printing press open and clear the loaded headline.  (DC 20) [BARBARIAN] [STRENGTH]  Wrench the printing press open and rip out the loaded headline.  (DC 18) [SLEIGHT OF HAND]  Reach inside and carefully remove the loaded headline.  (DC 20) [ROGUE] [SLEIGHT OF HAND]  Dislodge the current headline with a precise flick of the wrist.  (DC 18) If these checks are failed, then the press starts printing automatically, and is unable to be tampered with further. If Enver Gortash is dead, it is possible to alter the headlines even if the party has not started the quest, or it is no longer available. Doing so affects the world the same way as if the quest was active. Jelliwig is willing to be mischievous if properly motivated. Positive Articles: Adventurers, Our Best Hope For the City - in a wicker basket at X: -1029 Y: 1013 Celebrate the Brave Heroes Who Slew General Ketheric - upstairs, in a wicker basket behind Ettvard at X: 53 Y: -50 Make Big Money by Trading with Adventurers - in a wicker basket at X: -1029 Y: 1058 Neutral Articles: Cutest Cat You've Ever Seen - on a counter at X: -1022 Y: 1066 Graverobbers' Spree - upstairs, in a wicker basket at X: 58 Y: -42 Hear the Finest Shanties at the Blushing Mermaid - upstairs, in a wicker basket at X: 43 Y: -60 Negative Articles: A Public Danger! - on a shelf at X: -1032 Y: 1035 Curse-Breakers or Curse-Makers? - on a desk at X: -1032 Y: 1018 Wolves in Sheeps' Clothing - on a counter at X: -1014 Y: 1016 Killing Ettvard [ edit section | visual editor ] It is possible to end the hit piece by killing Ettvard. This results in the paper covering his demise, rather than the hit piece. Result [ edit section | visual editor ] This quest is time sensitive after speaking to Ettvard Needle - if the quest has not been started or only Estra Stir is spoken with, then no papers are printed about the party. After speaking to Ettvard, the paper is printed after the next Long Rest . If the headline is not altered by the party, a negative one is printed. Positive headline : People around town compliment the party or recognize them positively, and their reputation is improved, resulting in a gain of 10 attitude . Neutral headline : Nothing changes. Negative headline : People around town comment negatively towards the party, and their reputation is tarnished, resulting in a loss of 15 attitude. The following merchants are affected by the attitude change: Alan Alyth Figaro Pennygood Fytz the Firecracker Gloomy Fentonson Nansi Gretta Oliver Tefoco Omotola Thomas C. Quirkilious Tolna Tome-Monger Vicar Humbletoes Inspiration [ edit section | visual editor ] Discovering Jelliwig in the basement of Baldur's Mouth grants the following inspiration: ⁠ Rennaissant Ingenuity ( Sage background) Completing this quest and rigging the news in the party's favour grants the following inspiration: ⁠ A Pressing Heist ( Criminal background) ⁠ Defamed No More ( Noble background) ⁠ Making It Sing to Your Tune ( Entertainer background) ⁠ The News of My Deeds Was Greatly Exaggerated ( Charlatan background) Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Talking to Lens only initiates this quest if she is the real Lens and not a disguised Orin . The latter half of this quest is trivialized if ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch has been completed, as the only guards in the Gazette's basement are Steel Watchers, which are then disabled. The 10 attitude buff for traders appears to apply only to characters who are active members of the party when the quest is completed. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Surrender Shadowheart to Viconia
- **来源**: [Surrender Shadowheart to Viconia](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Surrender_Shadowheart_to_Viconia)
- **分类**: Quests

Viconia demands Shadowheart's return. Surrender Shadowheart to Viconia is a sub-quest of the quest ⁠ Investigate the House of Grief in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Viconia in the House of Grief . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 3 Quest Rewards 4 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Viconia asked that we surrender Shadowheart to her in exchange for her help defeating the Absolute. "We told Shadowheart that Viconia asked us to surrender her to the cult. We should return to Viconia and face her." "We withheld the truth from Shadowheart about what Viconia has planned for her. We should return to Viconia with Shadowheart." Quest Complete "We surrendered Shadowheart to Viconia. We are now in alliance with Viconia." "We decided to not surrender Shadowheart to Viconia." "We wiped out the Sharran cult before Shadowheart could be surrendered to them." "We did not have the time to conclude matters with Viconia. We must press on." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Viconia in the heart of the House of Grief. This quest begins during ⁠ Investigate the House of Grief . Entering the hidden door in the House of Grief transports the party to the Cloister of Sombre Embrace . Deep in the heart of the cloister is Viconia DeVir , with a group of Sharran cultists. She explains she knows the party has the artefact in their possession and that she needs it to destroy the Absolute. Viconia initially attempts to negotiate in a way which keeps blades sheathed: All right, you wish to negotiate? Make me an offer then. As far as the artefact is concerned, there's nothing to discuss. Attack Turn to leave. Selecting the first option has Viconia demanding the artefact in exchange for the party's lives. The party can counter: Shar will allow you to make such an offer? This must be truly important, if Shar would allow you to make such an offer. Why do you want it? [INTIMIDATION]  Not happening. Even if I wanted to give it to you, I can't. The artefact is bound to me. It will kill you. (DC 20) [PERSUASION]  The artefact alone can't save you. Best if we unite against a common enemy - the Absolute. (DC 20) Attack. If the Intimidation or Persuasion checks are passed, then Viconia relents. However, she demands that Shadowheart be handed over. If Shadowheart is present at this moment, giving her over to Viconia resolves the quest. If Shadowheart is not present the party can return to camp and speak to her: I met with your Mother Superior - she expects me to hand you over to her. I met with your Mother Superior. She's willing to negotiate for your parents, if you come with me. I met the Mother Superior. She wishes to see you, and honour your new place at Shar's side. Regardless of the choice, Shadowheart says she must confront Viconia. The party must then return to the House of Grief with Shadowheart. There, Viconia tells the party to make good on their deal: She's all yours. Never If the first choice is selected, the Sharrans take Shadowheart away. Surrendering Shadowheart to Viconia results in her permanently leaving the party. Viconia thanks the party and commits to helping in the final battle against the Absolute. If Shadowheart has left the party permanently before (and is considered dead), Viconia complains she should have the one who killed Shadowheart and then attacks the party, unless they succeed on a DC 30 Persuasion Check . Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] If Shadowheart is given over to the cultists, Viconia and her Sharran subjects become allies in the fight against the Absolute and are added to the list of allies in ⁠ Gather Your Allies . If Shadowheart is a Dark Justiciar of Shar , she replaces Viconia as the Mother Superior. The same support in ⁠ Gather Your Allies is then provided by Shadowheart instead. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Attempting to enter the Threshold of Loss door instantly causes the Sharran guard standing near the door, Fidelian Lamona to become permanently hostile, which also makes Viconia and the rest of the cultists temporarily hostile. It is possible to enter and use the Chamber of Loss, dispatch the hostile guard, evade the rest of the Sharrans, and then come back for dialogue. ## The Blade of Frontiers
- **来源**: [The Blade of Frontiers](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Blade_of_Frontiers)
- **分类**: Quests

The Blade of Frontiers is the Companion Quest for Wyll . It is automatically added to the journal when he joins the party inside the Druid Grove . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Recruiting Wyll 2.2 Hunt down Karlach 2.3 Meeting Mizora 2.4 Rescue Zariel's Asset 2.5 Mizora at Wyrm's Crossing 2.6 The Great Wyrm 3 Rewards 4 Companion approval 4.1 During Mizora's judgment at camp, if Wyll does not kill Karlach 4.2 Freeing Zariel's Asset 5 Achievements 6 Bugs 7 Notes and references Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions. Hunt down Karlach. We recruited Wyll, a monster hunter known as the Blade of Frontiers. He is on a mission to kill Karlach, a powerful devil who is a danger to the entire Sword Coast. We met a group of paladins who seek Karlach, the very same target who Wyll is hunting. They provided us with her exact whereabouts. Talk to Wyll about Karlach. We located Karlach, who was not the treacherous devil Wyll believed her to be. We resolved the situation peacefully, but Wyll owes us an explanation. Rest at camp. Wyll spoke ominously about a penance he must face. We should take a long rest when the opportunity strikes; there's clearly a lot the Blade of Frontiers isn't telling us. Continue travelling with Wyll. We met Wyll's diabolical patron, Mizora, who was none too happy to find that Wyll failed to slay Karlach. She punished Wyll for his disobedience by turning him into a devil and departed - though it seems likely we'll meet her again. Rescue Zariel's asset from Moonrise Towers. Mizora appeared in the form of a projection to inform us that the Absolute cult abducuted an infernal asset of some importance to the archdevil Zariel. We should find and release them - Wyll's very soul hangs in the balance. We've delved deep into Moonrise Towers. We should search the area thoroughly - the devil that Mizora asked us to rescue must be nearby. Wait for Mizora to be in Contact. Zariel's asset turned out to be Mizora herself. In return for our help, she promised to release Wyll from his pact, but only after six months had passed. She disappeared again - but not before promising she'd find us soon enough. We've reach Wyrm's Crossing, on the outskirts of Baldur's Gate. We should keep an eye out for Mizora. Attend Gortash's ordination ceremony. Return to Mizora. The ceremony is over. We should return to Mizora. Rest at camp. Mizora asked us to meet her in camp. She has an important proposal to make regarding Wyll's father, Grand Dule Ravengard. Continue forth with Wyll. Mizora gave Wyll a choice. He could agree to an eternal pact with her and Zariel, and she would reveal where his father's been taken and ensure his safe return. Or he could break his pact with Mizora, dooming his father to die in Gortash's secret command centre. Wyll broke the pact, choosing his freedom over his father's life. Talk to Ravengard. Mizora gave Wyll a choice. He could agree to an eternal pact with her and Zariel, and she would reveal where his father's been taken and ensure his safe return. Or he could break his pact with Mizora, dooming his father to die in Gortash's secret command centre. Wyll broke the pact, choosing his freedom over his father's life. Read The Legend of Ansur. We've retrieved a book called 'The Legend of Ansur'. We should read it. Duke Ravengard told Wyll the only way to save Baldur's Gate from the Absolute scourge is to awaken a powerful wyrm called Ansur who sleeps under the city. A tome called 'The Legend of Ansur' is key to finding the entrance to the wyrm's lair. Find the entrance to Ansur's lair, the Wyrmway. After reading 'The Legend of Ansur', we discovered the great wyrm Ansur resides in a secret lair called the Wyrmway. The entrance is apparently located somewhere within Wyrm's Rock Prison, and the notes inside it hint that opening the way involves lightning sparks and torches. Return to Ravengard. We defeated the resurrected remains of the great wyrm Ansur. We should return to camp and inform Duke Ravengard. Quest Complete We failed Mizora's rescue mission. As punishment for breaking his contract, Wyll was dragged into Avernus, where he will battle demons as a horrid lemure. With his father's blessing, Wyll announced himself the Blade of Avernus. He is devoted to protecting the Sword Coast from infernal threats by hunting devils, both within the Hells and without. With his father's blessing, Wyll announced himself the Blade of Frontiers. He is devoted as ever to his cause: protecting Baldur's Gate and the Sword Coast from the many dangers that plague it, and ensuring its people know a safe and prosperous future. With his father's blessing, Wyll intends to step forward as a Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate. Once we have defeated the Absolute, he is sure the people will welcome another Ravengard to help restore and rebuild the city. We abandoned Wyll's remaining considerations and pressed on towards an uncertain fate. Wyll turned against us. Wyll left our party - for good. Wyll died - as heroes often do. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll’s story spans the entire game. Recruiting Wyll [ edit section | visual editor ] Wyll can be first encountered when he joins the fight outside of the Emerald Grove . Afterwards, the party can find him inside the grove training young Tiefling refugees. He can be recruited to the party, and explains that he is hunting a devil named Karlach . Hunt down Karlach [ edit section | visual editor ] Off with her head! Main article: Hunt the Devil The party can find Karlach down the hill from the Toll House . Karlach can be spoken to and recruited, freed or killed. If Wyll is in the party, the two have a confrontation. If Karlach is recruited to the party before speaking to Wyll, he shows up at camp to confront her. Wyll or Karlach can each be asked to leave, be killed, or the situation can be resolved peacefully. If Karlach is encountered and recruited without Wyll in the party, they have a confrontation the next Long Rest . Meeting Mizora [ edit section | visual editor ] During a long rest, Mizora manifests at camp. If Karlach is killed, she gifts Wyll the Infernal Robe . Otherwise, she punishes Wyll and his appearance permanently changes. Rescue Zariel's Asset [ edit section | visual editor ] Mizora manifests a second time either at camp or near the entrance of Moonrise Towers , this time to request that the party rescue one of Zariel's assets, who has been trapped at Moonrise Towers. During this conversation, she can be persuaded to end Wyll's contract in exchange for rescuing the asset. Zariel's asset cannot be found in Moonrise Towers proper, rather they can only be saved after entering the Mind Flayer Colony . Here, it is revealed that Mizora herself is the asset, being trapped within a pod in the Tadpoling Centre . The party, noticing an opportunity, can try to negotiate Wyll's contract or simply free her: [ 1 ] [INTIMIDATION]  Free Wyll, or I let the cult infect you. I bet you'd make a loyal thrall. (DC 16) [HISTORY]  Remember all you can about devils and their contracts.  (DC 16) 'Abi, diabole, et nunquam redi.' [PERFORMANCE]  Say you know a pact-breaking charm and chant a series of pseudo-Infernal phrases.  (DC 16) Poor thing. I'll let you out of there. Fine, let's get on with it. Convincing Mizora to free Wyll from his pact grants   +10 . The party can then inspect the nearby console and attempt to free her, or even kill her, however killing her also also kills Wyll : [ 1 ] [STRENGTH]  Gather your strength and smash your foot through the pod.  (DC 14) [BARBARIAN] [STRENGTH]  SMASH THE POD.  (DC 14  ) Examine the device on the left. Connect your mind to the device on the left and activate it.   (if passive DC 10 Arcana check failed) Connect your mind to the 'annihilate' device and activate it.   (if passive DC 10 Arcana check succeeded) Examine the device on the right. Connect your mind to the device on the right and activate it.   (if passive DC 10 Arcana check failed) Connect your mind to the 'unleash' device and activate it.   (if passive DC 10 Arcana check succeeded) Saving Mizora nets another   +10 approval from Wyll, however she stipulates that it takes another six months for the pact to end. If Wyll is present, the party can ask Mizora for a reward for going through the trouble of rescuing her: [ 2 ] [PERSUASION]  You'd think we'd get a reward for going through all this trouble. (DC 14) Successfully persuading her causes her to gift the Infernal Rapier to Wyll and grants another   +3 approval. Mizora at Wyrm's Crossing [ edit section | visual editor ] After reaching Wyrm's Crossing in Act 3 , Mizora can be found loitering in Wyrm's Rock Fortress or just before the transition to the Lower City . She asks that the party attend Gortash's ordination. Afterwards, she offers to save Duke Ravengard if Wyll keeps his contract. (See ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke for this sub-quest). The Great Wyrm [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Wyrmway If Duke Ravengard is saved, he gives the party the quest to gather the aid of the great wyrm Ansur . If the Duke perishes, or Wyll breaks his pact, walking around in the Lower City may trigger an encounter with Counsellor Florrick , who confronts the party and accuses Wyll of killing his father. If Florrick is dead or still imprisoned, Cordula Eltan takes her place. If he is in the party, Wyll retorts that this is disinformation being spread by Mizora. Talking Florrick or Eltan down results in her providing the necessary information to begin the quest. If they cannot be dissuaded from attacking, the information can also be claimed from the corpse of either Florrick or Eltan. Ansur can be found by travelling to Wyrm's Rock Prison . Here, the party must travel down the western passage way to find two dragon sconces. The sconces must be hit with electricity damage to light them. Past the new opening is The Wyrmway . After the Wyrmway's trials are completed, Ansur can be found and must be fought against. After defeating Ansur the party should return to camp to inform Duke Ravengard if he lives, and Wyll can come to a decision about his future. Wyll can decide to become the Blade of Avernus, or follow his father's political path of Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate. Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Infernal Rapier - for freeing Mizora in the Mind Flayer Colony, if Wyll is in the party and persuading her to give the party a reward for their troubles. Infernal Robe - if recruiting Wyll and killing Karlach. Mizora will give this on the following Long Rest. Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] During Mizora's judgment at camp, if Wyll does not kill Karlach [ edit section | visual editor ] If Wyll is the origin character: Defending Karlach from Mizora   +5 Giving up Karlach to Mizora   -5 If a character other than Wyll is the origin character: Defending Karlach from Mizora   +1   +5   +1   +1 Offering to give up Karlach to Mizora   -1   -5   -1   -1 Threatening Mizora   +1   +1   +1   +1   +1 Telling Mizora to fuck off   +1   +5   +1   +1   +5 Admiring Mizora - "Well, well. Aren't you a luscious thing?"   -1   -1 Freeing Zariel's Asset [ edit section | visual editor ] Convincing Mizora to anull Wyll's contract   +10 Freeing Mizora from the pod   +10 Convincing Mizora to reward the party for their efforts   +3 Annihilating Mizora in her pod   -1   -1   -1   -1   -1 Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Loophole Break Wyll's pact with Mizora. Crash Landing In the Wyrmway, wait until the dragon is mid-flight, then knock it out of the sky - KAPOW. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] During the scenes where Mizora visits the party camp at night to speak with Wyll, he wears his default camp clothing in its starting color, even if it has been dyed or he has different camp clothing equipped. If the Wyrmway and Ansur are completed before saving Duke Ravengard, Wyll can be stuck saying the party needs to return to camp and tell Ravengard, and has other conversation options. ## The Blade of Frontiers (Origin)
- **来源**: [The Blade of Frontiers (Origin)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Blade_of_Frontiers_(Origin))
- **分类**: Quests

This page is in the process of being constructed or reformatted . You are welcome to contribute as well. Last edited on 2025-08-25. If multiple days have passed since, this template should be removed. The Blade of Frontiers is a personal quest for Wyll's origin , immediately starting in the Prologue . It is titled the same as his Companion quest and has two sub-quests: ⁠ The Grand Duke and ⁠ Wyrmway . “ Seven years ago, I was exiled from Baldur's Gate, the city I call home. My name is Wyll, but the people of the Sword Coast call me the Blade of Frontiers - champion of the meek, defender of the innocent.The truth isn't quite so simple, but they're right about one thing. I hunt monsters, and I always catch my prey. My latest target is a devil, and I'm right on her tail. Once I'm through with her, she'll never escape the fires of the First Hell. „ — Wyll , introducing himself in the Character Creation Menu Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending player decisions and outcomes. Hunt and destroy Karlach. "I woke up upon a nautiloid - a mind flayer ship. The last thing I remember is pursuing my target, a dangerous devil called Karlach, across the fiery hellscape of Avernus. I need to escape this ship and destroy the infernal fiend; if she were to be loosed upon the Sword Coast, there's no telling what havoc she would wreak." "My patron Mizora paid me a visit at my campsite. She reminded me of my mission: hunt and kill the devil called Karlach. If I fail, the consequences could be dire." "I met a group of paladins who know Karlach and want her dead. They provided me with her exact whereabouts." Rest at camp. "Karlach joined the party. I should take a long rest and confront her in camp - this uneasy peace can't last forever." Rest at camp. Your patron will want to have words. "I located Karlach, but she is not the dangerous devil Mizora said she was, but a victim of the archdevil Zariel's schemes. I spared her life in spite of my mission. I'm not sure what punishment I'll be facing, but I won't have to wait long to find out - Mizora is sure to appear in my camp and give me a piece of her mind." "Karlach is done for, and the Sword Coast is safer for it. Mizora will be pleased; I should rest in camp and await her next instructions. I am due a reward for my efforts." Continue your travels. "I now inhabit the guise of a devil, Mizora's punishment for betraying the terms of our pact. I am fortunate she did not cast me into the Hells, but I'm still alive - for now. I can only imagine what she'll demand of me next." "Mizora was pleased to learn I'd dealt with Karlach, and rewarded me handsomely for my efforts. She'll be back, of course; when a devil owns your soul, there is no getting rid of her." Rescue Zariel's asset from Moonrise Towers. "Mizora appeared in the form of a projection to inform me that the Absolute cult abducted an infernal asset of some importance to the archdevil Zariel. I should find and release them - unless I want to be cast into the Hells for good, that is." "I've delved deep into Moonrise Towers. I should search the area thoroughly - the devil that Mizora asked me to rescue must be nearby." Wait for Mizora to be in contact. "Zariel's asset turned out to be Mizora herself. She disappeared again after I released her from her pod, but I've clearly not seen the last of her. She is my patron, and I am her pup - as she is so fond of reminding me." "Zariel's asset turned out to be Mizora herself. In return for my help, she promised to release me from my pact, but only after six months had passed. She disappeared again, but I've clearly not seen the last of her. She is still my patron, and I am her pup - as she is so fond of reminding me." "Mizora gifted me an infernal rapier for my troubles, though she required some convincing." "I've reached Wyrm's Crossing, on the outskirts of Baldur's Gate. I should keep an eye out for Mizora - she must be lurking about somewhere." Attend Gortash's ordination ceremony. "I found Mizora at Wyrm's Rock fortress. She insisted I attend Gortash's ordination and seek her out afterwards." Return to Mizora. "The ceremony is over. I should return to Mizora." Rest at camp. "Mizora asked me to meet her in camp. She has an important proposal to make regarding my father. What is she scheming?" Rescue Ravengard from Gortash's secret prison. "Mizora gave me a terrible choice. I could agree to an eternal pact with her and Zariel, and she would reveal where my father's been taken and ensure his safe return. Or I could break my pact with Mizora, dooming my father to die. I chose my father's life over my freedom; now, it's up to me to retrieve him from Gortash's command centre." "Mizora gave me a terrible choice. I could agree to an eternal pact with her and Zariel, and she would reveal where my father's been taken and ensure his safe return. Or I could break his pact with Mizora, dooming my father to die in Gortash's secret command centre. It wasn't an easy decision - but I chose my freedom over my father's life." Talk to Ravengard. "Mizora gave me a terrible choice. I could agree to an eternal pact with her and Zariel, and she would resurrect my father. Or I could break my pact with Mizora, and father would remain dead for good. I chose my father's life over my freedom, and Mizora resurrected him. I should speak with him about all that's happened." "I've sprung father free from the Iron Throne and he's gone to my camp. I should speak with him there." Continue your travels. "Mizora gave me a choice. I could agree to an eternal pact with her and Zariel, and she would resurrect my father. Or I could break his pact with Mizora, and father would remain dead for good. It wasn't an easy decision - but I chose my freedom over my father's life. If I must see other consequences for my actions, they have not yet come to bear." Check the ambushers' possessions. "Counsellor Florrick and her allies ambushed us, accusing Wyll of killing his father so he could take over the city. We defeated them after Florrick refused to stand down; we should check their possessions for any relevant information." [ 1 ] "Cordula Eltan and her allies ambushed me, accusing me of killing my father so I could take over the city. I defeated them after Eltan refused to stand down; I should check their possessions for any relevant information." Read The Legend of Ansur. "I've been reunited with my father. He told me the only way to save Baldur's Gate from the Absolute scourge is to awaken a powerful wyrm called Ansur who sleeps under the city. A tome called 'The Legend of Ansur' is key to finding the entrance to the wyrm's lair. " "Counsellor Florrick and her allies ambushed me, accusing me of killing my father so I could take over the city, but I convinced them to stand down. Florrick told me that the only way to save Baldur's Gate from the Absolute scourge is to awaken a powerful wyrm called Ansur who sleeps under the city. A tome called 'The Legend of Ansur' is key to finding the entrance to the wyrm's lair." "Cordula Eltan and her allies ambushed me, accusing me of killing my father so I could take over the city, but I convinced them to stand down. Eltam told me that the only way to save Baldur's Gate from the Absolute scourge is to awaken a powerful wyrm called Ansur who sleeps under the city. A tome called 'The Legend of Ansur' is key to finding the entrance to the wyrm's lair." "I've retrieved a book called 'The Legend of Ansur'. I should read it." Find the entrance to Ansur's lair, the Wyrmway. "I discovered a book about the dragon Ansur. This could be the key to finding a way into the Wyrmway - Ansur's secret lair." "After reading 'The Legend of Ansur', I discovered the great wyrm Ansur resides in a secret lair called the Wyrmway. The entrance is apparently located somewhere within Wyrm's Rock Prison, and the notes inside it hint that opening the way involves lightning sparks and torches." Find the way to Ansur. "I've reached the Wyrmway, where the great wyrm Ansur resides. I must make my way to him." Rest at camp and consider your next steps. "The great wyrm Ansur was long dead before I ever reached him. I defeated his resurrected remains - but what's to become of Baldur's Gate without Ansur's might to protect it? I must rest in camp and consider my options." Return to Ravengard. "The great wyrm Ansur was long dead before I ever reached him. I defeated his resurrected remains - but what's to become of Baldur's Gate without Ansur's might to protect it? I must return to father and tell him what's transpired." Quest complete "With my father's blessing, I have chosen to step forward as a Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate. Once I have defeated the Absolute, the people will welcome me - Ulder Ravengard's only son - as a scion of courage and justice who shall help lead Baldur's Gate to the prosperous future it deserves. The Blade of Frontiers is dead. Long live Grand Duke Wyll Ravengard!" "I have chosen to step forward as a Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate. Once I have defeated the Absolute, the people will welcome me - Ulder Ravengard's only son - as a scion of courage and justice who shall help lead Baldur's Gate to the prosperous future it deserves. The Blade of Frontiers is dead. Long live Grand Duke Wyll Ravengard!" "With my father's blessing, I have devoted myself to the cause dearest to my heart: protecting Baldur's Gate and the Sword Coast from the many dangers that plague it, and ensuring its people know a safe and prosperous future. The Blade of Frontiers is on the hunt; let no brute nor beast tear this land asunder!" "I have re-devoted myself to the cause dearest to my heart: protecting Baldur's Gate and the Sword Coast from the many dangers that plague it, and ensuring its people know a safe and prosperous future. The Blade of Frontiers is on the hunt; let no brute nor beast tear this land asunder!" "With my father's blessing, I have vowed to hunt devils wherever they dare to dwell, be that in the fires and demented deserts of the Hells, or the fields and forests of the Sword Coast. The Blade of Frontiers is dead. Long live the Blade of Avernus!" "A new man has been born from the old. My new mission: to hunt devils wherever they dare to dwell, be that in the fires and demented deserts of the Hells, or the fields and forests of the Sword Coast. The Blade of Frontiers is dead. Long live the Blade of Avernus!" "I abandoned my remaining personal duties and pressed on towards an uncertain fate." Playing as Wyll Origin [ edit section | visual editor ] Playing as an Origin naturally locks the player out of multiple interaction cut-scenes that may occur when playing as any other character (including Custom Tav and the Dark Urge ). Many cut-scenes concerning various interactions with other companions, NPCs and the environment, are left intact in their core. Most, though, are augmented with Wyll's own feelings and memories, voiced by the Narrator within the dialogue. [ verify ] As a playable character, Wyll also has several unique cut-scenes which are connected to him being coerced and tricked into a warlock pact, and subsequently being exiled from Baldur's Gate . ## The Chosen of Shar
- **来源**: [The Chosen of Shar](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Chosen_of_Shar)
- **分类**: Quests

A mural at the Emerald Grove depicts fallen Dark Justiciars. The Chosen of Shar is a sub-quest of both Shadowheart's ⁠ Companion quest and her ⁠ Origin quest . It is added to the journal after encountering information on Dark Justiciars . Contents 1 Objectives (Companion Quest) 2 Objectives (Origin Quest) 3 Walkthrough 3.1 The Dark Justiciars 3.2 The Gauntlet of Shar 3.3 The Shadowfell 4 Quest Rewards 5 Bugs Objectives (Companion Quest) [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions. Find the Dark Justiciar's lair. "Shadowheart has shown interest in finding the lair of the Dark Justiciar - an elite force dedicated to the goddess Shar." "We found murals in the grove that seemed to depict an ancient order of Sharran warriors - the Dark Justiciars. Further signs of their presence - historical or otherwise - may lie elsewhere." "We found a finely sculpted idol of the goddess Shar, and decided to gift it to Shadowheart. She was greatly pleased; the discovery of such a piece bolstered her hopes of uncovering further signs of a Dark Justiciar presence." "The Archdruid Halsin described how there was once an entire army of Dark Justiciars that waged war against followers of Selûne, long ago. The rites of becoming a Dark Justiciar are no mean feat - they must have had a substantial lair in order to train and anoint a force of such size." "We found an ancient temple of Selûne that had seemingly been razed by Dark Justiciars in the past. Such a force must have had a stronghold to operate from. Perhaps it can still be found." Explore Grymforge. "We entered the ruins of what may have been a fortress dedicated to the goddess Shar. We could be close to the Dark Justiciar's lair." "We found the corpses of several Dark Justiciars - Shar must have been worshipped here. Shadowheart suggested we search for answers." "We found traces of Hellish fiends.
