Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The Dark Justiciars [ edit section | visual editor ] During dialogue with Shadowheart , she reveals she has always dreamed of becoming a Dark Justiciar of Shar , but the Mother Superior thwarted any attempts at doing so. More information on the Dark Justiciars can be found at various places, starting in Act One . This starts the quest The Chosen of Shar to learn more about the Dark Justiciars and their history. Information on the Dark Justiciars can be found within the Inner Sanctum of the Emerald Grove by examining the murals with Shadowheart in the party. One of the frescos, 'Fallen,' depicts a group of druids standing over a vanquished army - the army of Shar. The druids aided a group of Selunites in vanquishing Shar's army at Moonrise Towers . If Halsin is saved during ⁠ Rescue the Druid Halsin , he can tell more about a war that was fought between the Selunites and the Dark Justiciars. If travelling to ⁠ through the Underdark and exploring Grymforge , several signs of Dark Justiciar remnants can be noticed. In the area near the Deep Rothé in the quest ⁠ Get Past the Rubble , there are several such corpses which Shadowheart can comment on. Additionally, there is an Idol of Shar at X: -645 Y: 366 which can be found on the path past the rubble, through many sets of pressure plate traps and a locked wrought iron gate. The gate can be smashed with force damage or passed with spells such as Misty Step or Gaseous Form . Mage Hand can also be used to switch the lever on the other side of the gate. Speaking to Shadowheart, she can be gifted the statuette (with unique reactions for clerics of Selûne ). Lastly, within the path to the Adamantine Forge , there are several Devilfoil Masks which indicate that Merregons from the hells fought with the Dark Justiciars, and a conversation with Kith while investigating a demolished temple wall highlights the presence of sulphur crystals, suggesting that a huge devil was responsible. Unfortunately, the trail goes cold within Grymforge. Choosing to free Nere as part of ⁠ Free True Soul Nere results in his explaining that he was looking for an entrance to an ancient Sharran Temple , but the way was blocked. The temple is visible from just past the locked double doors where he was trapped, but the bridge leading there has been destroyed. It is not until the latter half of Act Two that the party can find a way in. The Gauntlet of Shar [ edit section | visual editor ] As part of ⁠ Infiltrate Moonrise Towers , the party members are prompted to ⁠ Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic , which leads them to the Grand Mausoleum . After solving a small puzzle in the Mausoleum, it is possible to enter the Gauntlet of Shar . In order to reach the Nightsong in the Shadowfell, the party must obtain four Umbral Gems . Three of them are granted upon completing the Trials of Shar. The fourth one must be acquired from the orthon Yurgir , also residing in the Gauntlet (see below). Once all four Umbral Gems are in the party's possession, if Shadowheart is in the party, the Spear of Night must be obtained from the Silent Library to be able to deal with the Nightsong. If the player character twice refuses to search for the spear before going to the Shadowfell, Shadowheart becomes hostile to the party. Shadowheart does not need to personally be taken through the Gauntlet of Shar, although she does have numerous opportunities for unique dialogue and approval. The Shadowfell [ edit section | visual editor ] Shadowheart must decide whether to slay or spare the Nightsong. To complete the quest The Chosen of Shar, Shadowheart must be taken to the Shadowfell . If not included, she immediately appears after the party returns to the material plane to confront them, saying they prevented her from achieving her destiny. She then permanently leaves the party, saying she hopes she never sees them again and forgets them in time. The quest The Chosen of Shar then fails. Once leaping to the heart of the Shadowfell, it is revealed that the Nightsong is not an object, but an aasimar named Aylin . She has been held captive using Balthazar's necromancy by Ketheric Thorm for over a century, to forcibly share her immortality with him. After this, several events can play out, depending on whether Balthazar is alive and whether the player character convinces Shadowheart to spare Aylin. Shadowheart can be convinced to spare Aylin in several ways, depending on her Approval rating with the player character and her Nightsong Points . If Aylin is spared , she thanks the party after Shadowheart throws the Spear of Night into the abyss of the Shadowfell. Aylin promises to tell Shadowheart more about her history after taking down Ketheric Thorm. Then, she flies off to face him. After leaving the Shadowfell, Shar subjects Shadowheart to great torment before casting her back to the mortal realm, and Shadowheart loses her favour. After completing ⁠ Defeat Ketheric Thorm , and upon speaking to her in camp, Aylin reveals that sometime after being freed, she retrieved the Spear of Night from the Shadowfell, altered it, and now gives it to Shadowheart in its new form as Selûne's Spear of Night . If Aylin is killed , Shadowheart becomes a Dark Justiciar and is rewarded with Shar's Spear of Evening . However, the party lose a valuable ally in Aylin, and there are major consequences for the inhabitants of the Last Light Inn as a result of to Shadowheart's actions: Isobel is overwhelmed and unable to sustain her protection magic over the Inn, causing all within to fall to the Shadow Curse . Shadowheart refers to this as cleansing the resistance to Lady Shar's will. Additionally, unlike instances where Isobel is kidnapped in ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , Jaheira is nowhere to be found and does not aid the party in the fight at the Last Light Inn. Regardless of Shadowheart's choice, one primary goal remains the same: Ketheric Thorm must be faced as part of ⁠ Defeat Ketheric Thorm . This is either mandated by Shar, who sees him as a traitor, or urged by Aylin, who promises to reveal more information on Shadowheart's past if she assists. Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] If Shadowheart kills the Nightsong: Dark Justiciar Boots Dark Justiciar Gauntlets (Rare) Dark Justiciar Half-Plate (Very Rare) Shar's Spear of Evening If Shadowheart spares the Nightsong: Moonlight Glaive Selûne's Spear of Night (granted after completing Infiltrate Moonrise Towers , upon speaking to Dame Aylin in camp) Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] If Shadowheart has equipped the Spear of Night upon going into the final cut-scene, it remains visible on her back in some shots even if she has already thrown it away. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## The Githyanki Warrior
- **来源**: [The Githyanki Warrior](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Githyanki_Warrior)
- **分类**: Quests

The Githyanki Warrior is the Companion Quest for Lae'zel . It is automatically added to the journal when she formally joins the party in Act One . “ Yisk Gith'ka tavki krash'ht - the githyanki will be free. „ — Lae'zel , after affirming the player character's decision to steal the Orphic Hammer from the House of Hope. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Recruiting Lae'zel [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel is first encountered on the Nautiloid in the Prologue , but can only become a full companion in Act One . If Lae'zel survives the Nautiloid crash, she is trapped in a cage north of the Roadside Cliffs Waypoint at X: 224 Y: 372 . If Lae'zel dies on the Nautiloid, her corpse is on the Ravaged Beach and can be revived using a Scroll of Revivify . Lae'zel can also be encountered at Mountain Pass near the Githyanki patrol. Finding the crèche [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Find the Githyanki Crèche Immediately upon recruiting Lae'zel, she insists on traveling to the nearest crèche. She claims the crèche houses a Zaith'isk , a sacred device which can cure the infected of their tadpoles through purification. If ⁠ Free Lae'zel is completed, it is revealed that a Tiefling named Zorru recently encountered a Githyanki patrol. Zorru is in the Druid Grove near the storage barn. If Zorru is spoken to while Lae'zel is present, he admits encountering Githyanki near the Mountain Pass. When party arrive at the Mountain Pass, they can encounter Kith'rak Voss and a squadron of Githyanki. If Voss is spoken with, he interrogates the player character on the location of a stolen Githyanki artefact, polyhedric and inscribed with Githyanki runes. If Shadowheart is present, she realises he is hunting for the Mysterious Artefact she carries. If Voss learns that the party possess the artefact or are infected with tadpoles, the Githyanki become hostile. Otherwise, Voss instructs them to proceed to the crèche, and the encounter ends peacefully. Conflict at camp [ edit section | visual editor ] During a Long Rest after the Githyanki encounter, Lae'zel confronts Shadowheart over the Mysterious Artefact . Lae'zel demands possession of the artefact, but Shadowheart adamantly refuses. Although they state an agreement to a duel at sunrise to settle their conflict, Shadowheart has no intention of leaving her victory to chance and the player character wakes up during the night to her holding a knife to Lae'zel's neck. If nothing is done, Shadowheart slits Lae'zel's neck and smashes her parasite as it crawls out. The player character can defend Lae'zel, causing Shadowheart to become permanently hostile, or persuade Shadowheart to peacefully end the conflict by passing a DC 10 Persuasion Check . Arriving at the crèche [ edit section | visual editor ] Creche Y'llek is in the basement of the Rosymorn Monastery . Ghustil Stornugoss is in the infirmary there, where she claims she can purify the party of infection through use of a Zaith'isk. If the interacting party member agrees to purification, they can learn that the true purpose of a Zaith'isk is to extract the memories of the infected and then kill them. Whoever steps in the Zaith'isk must undergo saving throws to prevent -2 debuffs to Wisdom , Intelligence , and Constitution respectively. These debuffs can be removed by consuming a Tadpole . The Zaith'isk ultimately explodes. Lae'zel questions whether the Ghustil was corrupted, and demands the party report her to Kith'rak Therezzyn . Confronting the Inquisitor [ edit section | visual editor ] Vlaakith wishes to kill the Dream Visitor. In Kith'rak Therezzyn's Chambers, she is berated by Inquisitor Ch'r'ai W'wargaz . A pathway leading through the Captain's Chamber is blocked by a Githyanki Barrier Disruptor at X: 1390 Y: -757 . To open the path, a Gith Shard must be obtained from Kith'rak Therezzyn . Inquisitor W'wargaz recognizes the party and allows them entry. Alternatively, if the Kith'rak is shown the artefact, she demands that the player character speak with the Inquisitor immediately. In the Inquisitor's Chambers, W’wargaz bids the player character to speak with him. If they refuse, he grows impatient and becomes hostile. If the player character speaks with him, he reveals the Githyanki have been following the party's movements because of their involvement with the Absolute . The Inquisitor then demands the artefact. The player character can ask questions or attempt to offer the artefact, which causes Vlaakith to appear through the Planecaster. Vlaakith demands the party kneel before her: [ 1 ] Who exactly are you?  (non-Githyanki only) Stand tall - you are her equal in iniquity.   (Dark Urge only) Remain standing. You shall kneel before no one but the Dark Lady.   (Shadowheart only) Stay standing, just as you are. Wave politely. [DARK URGE]  Kneel: choke down your brutal pride. [GITHYANKI]  Kneel before Vlaakith, your queen. Kneel.   (non-Githyanki only) Vlaakith then questions the player character on how they came to be in possession of the artefact, which is actually an Astral Prism . She reveals that there is someone inside, who she claims is a compromised agent of the mind flayers, and commands the party to enter it and kill them. The player character can respond with any of the following: [ 1 ] [GITHYANKI]  My skills and fate are not subject to your whims. [GITHYANKI]  It is my greatest honour to obey. [GITHYANKI]  The god-queen of my people cannot kill someone herself? [GITHYANKI] [INTELLIGENCE]  Try to peer into your queen's mind. [INTELLIGENCE]  Try to peer into Vlaakith's mind. [ENEMY OF SHAR]  I was bid to safeguard the artefact - not anything or anyone hiding within it. I shall do as you wish.  (Shadowheart only) [ENEMY OF SHAR]  No. I answer to no one but Lady Shar - and anything that benefits you must surely harm her.,  (Shadowheart only) I will do as you wish. Can't you kill the one inside yourself? I thought 'gods' were all-powerful. [WARLOCK]  I'm afraid I don't do the bidding of extraplanar entities for free - bad for business. No way. I don't work for deluded tyrants. So the dream visitor is inside the artefact... I can't kill them. They protect me from the Absolute. Fine. I will go in and kill them. No. In fact, maybe I'll free the one inside. If you're a god, do it yourself. [OATHBREAKER]  I do not 'obey'. You have misjudged me, lich queen. [OATH OF VENGEANCE]  You are confused, Vlaakith - I serve those in need of justice, not some tyrant god. [OATH OF DEVOTION]  I serve those of a loyal heart, not some astral god-queen. I will not obey you. [OATH OF THE ANCIENTS]  My oath is sworn to the ancient magic of this world - not your astral empire. I owe you nothing. [OATH OF THE CROWN]  I obey the just laws of this realm, not the unjust laws of the Astral Plane. If the player character repeatedly mocks her godhood, Vlaakith casts the 9th-level spell Wish , killing the party and causing a Game-Over . If the player character simply refuses her demand to enter the prism, W’wargaz and the other Githyanki in the room become hostile. The Ch'r'ai is joined in combat by Ardent Jhe'rezath , Raider Kyrr'a'ath , Warrior Brelal'reth , and Ardent Qu'th . If the party enters the prism, they can meet the Dream Visitor , who will only speak with the player character. The Dream Visitor explains that the power used to protect the party from the Absolute was stolen from the Githyanki. Additionally, the Visitor knows Vlaakith's empire is illegitimate and she does not possess the same power that Mother Gith did. The Visitor believes this is why Vlaakith wants them dead. The Visitor kneels and offers a blade to the player character, stating they can strike down the Dream Visitor if they believe it is right, but this is merely a test to reveal the player character's true intentions towards them. If fatally struck, the Dream Visitor appears to die from the wound, but then returns and expresses dissapointment at the betrayal. After this conversation, the party returns to the Material Plane. If the Inquisitor is still alive, he immediately attacks them and the entire crèche becomes hostile. The party can fight their way through, attempt to sneak out, or escape through the Secret Stairway from the quest ⁠ Find the Blood of Lathander . Vlaakith or Orpheus [ edit section | visual editor ] The betrayal by the Inquisitor causes Lae'zel to question her loyalty. While she wants to believe that Vlaakith is testing her faith, she can be swayed by Kith'rak Voss, who enters the camp during a Long Rest . If Lae'zel agrees to listen to him, Voss claims that Vlaakith is a pretender and the true Prince, Orpheus , is the key to their race's future. He asks the party to meet him at Sharess' Caress in Baldur's Gate , which initiates ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss . If Lae'zel refuses to listen to Voss, he becomes hostile, and it is revealed that he planned to meet a mysterious contact at Sharess' Caress. An alternative path opens up by avoiding the confrontation with Vlaakith. The simplest way to do this is by avoiding the crèche entirely. However, another option is to avoid the Inquisitor in his chambers and instead move to the western hallway. Here, there are two statues that open the way to a secret stairway. If the party enters this stairway and makes it past the traps (documented in ⁠ Find the Blood of Lathander ), it can obtain The Blood of Lathander . Choosing to do this without first using the Dawnmaster's Crest activates a Solar Machine which destroys the entire crèche (and kills any party members who fail to escape in time). If the creche storyline is not fully resolved (either by destroying the creche or speaking to the inquisitor), then Lae'zel eventually confronts the player character and says that she intends to go back, unless thyey pass a DC 6 Intimidation Check . And because Lae'zel was not betrayed by Vlaakith, she happily obeys her queen. Vlaakith's Final Offer [ edit section | visual editor ] “ Glad to see I'm not the only one on the wrong side of an omnipotent authority figure. „ — Gale , on Lae'zel's rebuke of Vlaakith's demands to slay Orpheus In Act Three , after the first Long Rest upon entering Rivington , Vlaakith appears as a giant projection in the sky above camp. She comments on Lae'zel (depending on if she was betrayed at the crèche), and commands her to return to the Astral Prism and slay Orpheus. In doing so, she states she will reward Lae'zel with the title Baht t'Vlaakith , or Commander of Dragons. If Lae'zel learns the truth from Voss and intends to continue to pledge loyalty to Vlaakith, the party can convince her otherwise: [ 2 ] [ARCANA]  Use the tadpole. Seek Vlaakith's mind through her psionic conveyance.  (DC 18) Link to Lae'zel's parasite, show her Vlaakith's mind. [PERSUASION]  Voss was right, Vlaakith is your slaver. Denounce her - you must walk free. (DC 30) Otherwise, keeping silent or encouraging her to obey reinforces her loyalty to Vlaakith. Conversely, if Lae'zel learns the truth from Voss and becomes intent on betraying Vlaakith, she can be convinced (with a difficult check) to change her mind again: [ 2 ] [PERSUASION]  Kneel, Lae'zel. To be the god-queen's Chosen is an extraordinary honour. (DC 30) [WISDOM]  Connect with Lae'zel's parasite. 'Commander of Dragons. This is your destiny.'  (DC 30) Lastly, if Lae'zel never learns the truth from Voss, the party must pass two or more ability checks to convince her: [ 2 ] [PERSUASION]  Face the facts, Lae'zel. Vlaakith lied to your people. It's time you reject your queen. (DC 30) [PERSUASION]  Poisoned by a life of propaganda. I pity you, Lae'zel. (DC 18) [INTIMIDATION]  So the worm bows to the wyvern. Have some dignity, stand up to Vlaakith! (DC 18) [ARCANA]  Use the tadpole. Seek Vlaakith's mind through her psionic conveyance.  (DC 18) [WISDOM]  Link to Lae'zel's parasite, show her Vlaakith's mind.  (DC 18) Killing Kith'rak Voss [ edit section | visual editor ] If Vlaakith does not betray Lae'zel, Voss does not appear in camp and cannot be found in Sharess' Caress or the sewers. Instead, Vlaakith orders Lae'zel to kill Orpheus, and Lae'zel remains unaware of Voss' betrayal. However, if Lae'zel turned on Voss, she demands the party hunt him down as an enemy of Vlaakith. This can be done either in Sharess' Caress or in the sewers. Freeing Orpheus [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Free Orpheus Lae'zel expresses annoyance and admiration at the player character's intent to steal the Orphic Hammer rather than strike a deal with Raphael. Regardless of whose cause Lae'zel commits herself to, her objective remains the same: Free Orpheus from the Astral Prism; either to liberate him or slay him in Vlaakith's name. Well aware that the Orphic Hammer is the only thing capable of breaking Orpheus' bonds, Raphael approaches the party with an offer as part of ⁠ Deal with the Devil : in exchange for the hammer, which he has in his possession, the party will surrender the Crown of Karsus after defeating the Elder Brain. Gale vehemently opposes the deal, as he has designs on the crown himself, while Lae'zel chastises the player character for sacrificing her people's future if the offer is declined. The quest can proceed in one of two ways, depending on the party's decision with Raphael's offer: If the deal is refused, breaking into Raphael's House of Hope to steal the Orphic Hammer becomes the next objective of the quest Free Orpheus. If the deal is accepted, the quest ⁠ Escape the Deal instead begins, which progresses in much the same way, the only difference being that the contracted party members must steal their contracts instead of the hammer. When shown the hammer as part of ⁠ Help Kith'rak Voss , Voss rewards the party with his Silver Sword of the Astral Plane . Back in the Astral Prism [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Confront the Elder Brain However the party obtain the Orphic Hammer, they must wait for an opportunity to re-enter the Astral Prism. This does not happen until the player character fails to control the Elder Brain, as it has transformed into a much more powerful being, a Netherbrain . The Emperor rescues the party by spiriting them away into the Astral Prism. Here it is revealed that the Emperor plans to assimilate Orpheus to gain his powers, and then take on the Netherbrain. If Lae'zel is still aligned with Vlaakith, she is happy to let the Emperor assimilate Orpheus, as it fulfills her mission for her queen. If the party causes the Emperor to leave and rejoin the Netherbrain, Lae'zel must be convinced to delay her assassination until after the Netherbrain has been destroyed. If Lae'zel abandoned Vlaakith and is brought to the Astral Prism, a DC 30 Persuasion Check must be passed to assimilate Orpheus without her becoming hostile. Otherwise, Lae'zel turns on the party and must be killed. The party can instead refuse the Emperor and free Orpheus. Without an illithid, however, someone must choose to transform - the player character, Karlach or Orpheus himself. Lae'zel becomes distressed with Orpheus if he decides to become an illithid, but does not become hostile as a result. Additionally, if the party seeks to free Orpheus but did not go to the House of Hope, Raphael appears with the Orphic Hammer, but now the party is forced to ⁠ Fulfill the Deal and hand over the Crown of Karsus after the battle. Lae'zel's choice [ edit section | visual editor ] Lae'zel's quest culminates in one final choice after the Netherbrain is defeated. She can choose to either return to the Astral Sea with Orpheus or Vlaakith (or alone to start a rebellion in Orpheus' name), or she can be persuaded to remain with her newly found friends in Faerun. For player characters who chose to romance Lae'zel, they can ride off with her on a Red Dragon . ## The Githyanki Warrior (Origin)
- **来源**: [The Githyanki Warrior (Origin)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Githyanki_Warrior_(Origin))
- **分类**: Quests

This page is in the process of being constructed or reformatted . You are welcome to contribute as well. Last edited on 2026-05-01. If multiple days have passed since, this template should be removed. The Githyanki Warrior is a personal quest for Lae'zel when played as Origin , and starts in Act One . It is titled the same as her Companion quest and has two sub-quests: ⁠ The Prince of the Comet and ⁠ Vlaakith's Will . “ Since I was born in the cold reaches of Wildspace, I have known but one purpose: to wield a silver sword and ride a red dragon in service of my regent, the githyanki queen Vlaakith. My first step on this path is to slay a mind flayer and bring its head to my queen. There is no flesh I will not carve and no barrier I will not shatter to see it done. I am the one who sunders, I am the Undying Queen's most unshakeable warrior. I am Lae'zel of K'liir. „ — Lae'zel , introducing herself in the Character Creation Menu Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions. Act One - Wilderness: Search the Sword Coast for signs of a Githyanki Crèche. "I was infected with an illithid parasite aboard a ghaik nautiloid. Vlaakith's protocol demands I seek a Githyanki Crèche - there, I can be purified of this damnable tadpole." Find Zorru. "I discovered that a tiefling named Zorru has seen other githyanki. I spoke the Rite of Ascension and ascended to the astral plane upon a mighty red dragon to be with my queen. No longer am I Lae'zel of K'liir: I am Lae'zel of Tu'narath." "I defeated the Netherbrain with Orpheus' aid, and I have joined the prince's forces to dethrone Vlaakith. With the Prince of the Comet as my guide, I will liberate my people from the lich queen's talons." "I defeated the Netherbrain with Orpheus' aid - but he has sacrificed himself, unwilling to face a future as a ghaik abomination. I will lead the rebellion against Vlaakith in his stead and liberate my people from the lich queen's talons." "I defeated the Netherbrain. After careful thought, I have chosen to make my home in these lands with someone I've grown fond of - but my mind and blade remain ever sharp. No longer am I Lae'zel of K'liir: I am Lae'zel of Faerûn." "I defeated the Netherbrain. After careful thought, I have chosen to make my home in these lands - but my mind and blade remain ever sharp. No longer am I Lae'zel of K'liir: I am Lae'zel of Faerûn." "I defeated the Netherbrain - yet turned my back twice over: first to Vlaakith, God-regent of the Six Arms of Tu'narath, then to Gith's only son Orpheus, Prince of the Comet. These lands are now my home. No longer am I Lae'zel of K'liir: I am Lae'zel of Faerûn." "I defeated the Netherbrain and face an uncertain future. These lands are now my home. No longer am I Lae'zel of K'liir: I am Lae'zel of Faerûn." Playing as Lae'zel Origin [ edit section | visual editor ] Playing Lae'zel as Origin naturally locks the player out of certain interaction cutscenes that may otherwise occur with other characters (including Custom Tav and the Dark Urge ). Many cutscenes concerning various interactions with other companions, NPCs and the environment, are left intact in their core. However, most are augmented with Lae'zel's own feelings and memories, voiced by the Narrator within the dialogue. [ verify ] As a playable character, Lae'zel also has several unique cut-scenes connected to her gradually unearthing the true story of her people - and to the inevitable and mutually exclusive choice she must make. [ verify ] When Lae'zel is chosen as origin, Losiir becomes a temporary companion on the Nautiloid and is recruited at the same location as Lae'zel would be in a non-origin playthrough. Losiir has almost identical statistics and features to Lae'zel, but instead wields a Scimitar and a Longbow , and starts with the Defence fighting style . ## The Grand Duke
- **来源**: [The Grand Duke](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Grand_Duke)
- **分类**: Quests

The Grand Duke is in serious danger. The Grand Duke is a sub-quest of both Wyll's ⁠ Companion quest and his ⁠ Origin quest . It is added to the journal after arriving at Waukeen's Rest . Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Waukeen's Rest [ edit section | visual editor ] Waukeen's Rest X: -65 Y: 609 is an inn located on the Risen Road. Upon approaching, the party can smell smoke and hear shouting. At the front entrance some Flaming Fists are trying to break down the door. Upon speaking with them Gauntlet Yeva explains that Grand Duke Ravengard could be inside. What happened to this place? Grand Duke Ravengard? [STRENGTH]  Push against the wreckage.  (DC 10) [PALADIN] [STRENGTH]  Let out a rallying cry as you help the Fists push. ONWARD! (DC 10  ) [BARD] [PERFORMANCE]  WE CAN DO IT PUT YOUR BACKS INTO IT! PUSH!  (DC 10) There was no duke inside, just a wood elf. And she's dead.  (if already witnessed deceased) If the first two options are chosen, Yeva explains that the inn was raided by drow and goblins, and Grand Duke Ravengard was taken during the raid. Florrick thanks the party for rescuing her from the burning inn. A successful Strength check smashes the door open and the Fists rush inside. The party must proceed into the room and go upstairs to find the two remaining survivors - Counsellor Florrick and Benryn . [ 2 ] . Attempting to rescue Benryn starts ⁠ Rescue the Trapped Man . Florrick is in the northern room X: -57 Y: 618 , which the Fists swarm as they enter the building. To free her the broken door must be destroyed; she then runs out of the inn with the Fists in tow. After rescuing her from the burning inn, Counsellor Florrick grants the party a choice between three items: The Sparky Points The Joltshooter The Spellsparkler After learning of the Duke's kidnapping, it is also revealed that Ravengard is Wyll's father. This starts this quest. Goblin Camp [ edit section | visual editor ] At the Goblin Camp , the party can learn more of Duke Ravengard's fate. If toasting with the goblins after poisoning the booze tub X: -99 Y: 442 , Warlock Gurk says as part of the toast: To tha' duke's face when we gave 'im to the drow!" Last Light Inn [ edit section | visual editor ] During Act Two , the party can encounter Counsellor Florrick at the Last Light Inn with an entourage of Flaming Fists. She asks if the party have made any inroads with Moonrise Towers . Regardless of the response, she implores the party to keep looking. She herself, however, has to depart for Baldur's Gate to seek reinforcements. Moonrise Towers [ edit section | visual editor ] Duke Ravengard is infected by the Chosen Three. In the Moonrise Towers Prison , the party can ask the Warden if she has seen the Duke. However, she responds that he sounds important and she only deals with the dregs down in the prison. The party can also interrogate the corpse of a dead goblin scout, Sharp-Eye Lora , who reveals that she took prisoners to Moonrise Towers, including a duke. Mind Flayer Colony [ edit section | visual editor ] The Duke can be found near the end of Act Two in the Mind Flayer Colony , while chasing after Ketheric Thorm as part of ⁠ Defeat Ketheric Thorm , the party encounter the Chosen Three - Thorm, Orin the Red , and Enver Gortash , and with them they have Ulder Ravengard. The party can watch in the shadows as the trio infect Ravengard with a mind flayer tadpole and then whisk him away to Baldur's Gate. Wyrm's Rock Fortress [ edit section | visual editor ] Duke Ravengard swears Gortash in as Archduke of Baldur's Gate. In Act Three , Duke Ravengard can be encountered once again after completing ⁠ Find a way into Wyrm's Rock fortress . Once entering Wyrm's Rock Fortress , Gortash takes control of a Steel Watcher and invites the party to his coronation. Ravengard is in the Audience Chamber with Gortash and officiates Gortash's swearing in as Archduke of Baldur's Gate. Immediately after the ceremony, Ravengard can be spoken with. If saying that Florrick sent the party, he replies that Florrick is a black widow who betrayed the city, and was punished. Choosing to connect with Ravengard's parasite to seek information about Florrick reveals that she is imprisoned in Wyrm's Rock Prison and set to be executed, starting ⁠ Free Counselor Florrick . If the party prod Ravengard's mind further, they find deep uncertainty and fear of an illithid invasion within him, indicating that his mind has not fully been taken over. Once the coronation is complete, Mizora appears and reveals that Duke Ravengard is already being moved to another location to be disposed of. She refuses to elaborate and tells the party to go to camp. After a long rest, Mizora appears before Wyll to present a new contract - an eternity of servitude to Zariel in exchange for rescuing the Duke. If Wyll signs the contract, she reveals that Duke Ravengard is in Gortash's underwater prison, the Iron Throne and promises to keep him from harm. Otherwise, if Wyll refuses to sign the new contract, Mizora states that he is as good as dead, but she plans to stick around to see what happens. Wyll does not have to accept Mizora's new pact to save his father (which can be achieved while pursuing ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch , ⁠ Save the Gondians , or ⁠ Avenge the Ironhands ), but must speak to Mizora at camp before traveling to the Iron Throne, or the Duke will be dead. This changes the bargain Mizora offers Wyll at camp from revealing the Duke's location to resurrecting him from the dead in exchange for Wyll's soul, forever bound to her and Zariel, with the alternative remaining the same – to break the pact immediately. If ignoring the coronation and moving into the Lower City , then Duke Ravengard remains in the Audience Hall with Gortash until the ceremony is completed. If completing the questline ⁠ Disable the Steel Watch without attending the coronation, then the entirety of Wyrm's Rock Fortress becomes hostile, including Duke Ravengard. To ensure that the Duke can be rescued, it is advised to attend the coronation, speak to Mizora, and then take a long rest to ensure that he can be found in his intended location. The Iron Throne [ edit section | visual editor ] See also: Iron Throne Map of the Iron Throne Duke Ravengard is in the block of cells directly east from the ladder to the submersible. He is in the middle cell with only 35 current HP if alive. He also has the Fiendish Obeisance status, unless Wyll is not recruited to the party. Upon opening the door to his cell, the Duke becomes an Attached Follower . If Wyll broke his pact with Mizora, she appears and attempts to kill the Duke: once he leaves the cell, she gives him the Fiendish Obeisance: Kneel status for one turn, preventing him from moving and giving him Disadvantage on Dexterity saves, and summons multiple Combustion Belly Spiderlings next to the Duke which self-destruct using Spiderling Burst on their turn or when killed. The Duke can be helped to survive or avoid the spiders by a variety of means including healing, granting protective effects such as Fire Resistance through Protection from Energy: Fire or throwing an Elixir of Fire Resistance near him, Shield of Thralls , Invisibility , Sanctuary (though this doesn't protect against Spiderling Burst ) or helping him escape quicker with mobility spells such as Haste , Dimension Door , Arcane Gate or Omeluum's unique ability Teleport to Submersible (Omeluum can be found here only as part of ⁠ Retrieve Omeluum ). Mizora does not appear if Wyll died before resigning their pact and so will not summon the Spiderlings or force the Duke to kneel [ verify ] . Mizora cannot force the Duke to kneel if Fiendish Obeisance is removed with Greater Restoration . If Mizora and her witnesses Cirrus and Feena are not first spoken with at camp, the Duke is found dead. After escaping the Iron Throne, the party may be able to make a deal with Mizora to resurrect the duke in exchange for renewing Wyll's pact, or reject the deal in order to break his pact. The availability of this option may depend on Wyll's status and earlier choices. If Gortash is defeated before traveling to the Iron Throne, the prison is automatically destroyed and Duke Ravengard is killed, although only implicitly. But if Wyll made the pact with Mizora, she brings him back to life in camp as if nothing happened. If Duke Ravengard is saved, he stays at camp under the protection of the Astral Prism . If Wyll is recruited to the active party, the pair can reconcile, and Ravengard asks the party to seek out Ansur , Baldur's Gate's guardian dragon who sleeps under the city. If Wyll is killed (e.g., as a result of an altercation with Karlach during Act One ), this detail is NOT shared with Ravengard when sharing the player character's memory via The Emperor . Quest Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] If Duke Ravengard is rescued, he becomes an ally as part of ⁠ Gather Your Allies . ## The Hellion's Heart
- **来源**: [The Hellion's Heart](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Hellion's_Heart)
- **分类**: Quests

Karlach's heart was replaced by an infernal engine. The Hellion's Heart is a sub-quest of Karlach's Companion quest , ⁠ Our Fiery Friend . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Finding an Infernal Mechanic 2.2 Infernal Iron Locations 2.3 Upgrading Karlach's Heart 3 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions. Find an infernal mechanic. Karlach needs an infernal mechanic to tune up the engine she has for a heart. There might be one nearby. Talk to Dammon. We should bring Karlach to Dammon, the tiefling weaponsmith we met in the druid's grove. Find infernal iron Dammon inspected Karlach's engine. He said he'll need infernal iron in order to craft a repair. Return to Dammon. We found infernal iron; we should take it to Dammon. Let Dammon sleep on a solution Dammon upgraded Karlach's engine, but couldn't repair it yet. He'll need time to think of a solution. We should find him in Baldur's Gate - and bring infernal iron with us, too. Meet Dammon on the road ahead. We entered the shadow-cursed lands but didn't yet repair Karlach's heart. We can only hope Dammon made it to the city and can help us later. Talk to Dammon. We met Dammon sheltering in Last Light Inn. We should bring Karlach to talk to him. Quest Complete Karlach's heart was upgraded again, but Dammon has more bad news: her heart can't keep going outside of the Hells. Karlach will die if she doesn't return to Avernus. Dammon can no longer help repair Karlach's heart. Karlach left us - she won't be coming back. Karlach is gone forever. We failed to repair Karlach's heart. We never found a mechanic who could help repair Karlach's heart. Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Karlach struggles to control her infernal engine. The Hellion's Heart begins after Karlach is recruited and opens up about her Infernal Engine. For example, if Karlach was taken to defeat the Paladins of Tyr as part of ⁠ Hunt the Devil , she admits that the engine has been running hot since she left Avernus and that she needs to find an infernal mechanic. Finding an Infernal Mechanic [ edit section | visual editor ] It's possible to catch up with the infernal mechanic in three places: At the Druid Grove , in The Hollow . At the Last Light Inn , in the barn. In the Lower City, at the Forge of the Nine Dammon inspects Karlach's engine. The mechanic is a tiefling named Dammon . When the city of Elturel fell to Avernus, Dammon was there and was put to work as a mechanic. Upon meeting Karlach, he recognizes that her heart is from the hells. He believes he can help her, but needs to materials to do so. He has spotted several pieces of Infernal Iron on his travels and believes it is needed to aid Karlach. There are many places Dammon can die. During the raid on the Grove in ⁠ Raid the Grove , Dammon can become a casualty. Dammon can die during an attack on the Last Light Inn by Fist Marcus and his minions. If Dammon reaches Baldur's Gate, he's safe so long as the party doesn't randomly murder him. Infernal Iron Locations [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several different places to find Infernal Iron. Karlach's heart only needs two to get all upgrades from Dammon. Possible locations include: In the basement of the Blacksmith's House in the Blighted Village - in the chest with the Steelforged Sword In the locked room above Dror Ragzlin's throne in the Shattered Sanctum Received or traded from Kith in Grymforge if all three checks are passed about the Ruins Inside the Mason's Guild in Reithwin Town in the Shadow-Cursed Lands In the locked room on the left in the back of the Zhentarim Basement See Infernal Iron for a full list of locations where to find. Upgrading Karlach's Heart [ edit section | visual editor ] To repair Karlach's heart, return to Dammon with Karlach in the party. Karlach must install the upgrades herself, so this only works if Karlach is present. After the first upgrade, Karlach still feels hot, but not as much as before. She feels more powerful than ever, but it's not enough to solve the problem. Dammon commits to keep working and says he'll consider the possibility of enchanted coolant. He advises the party to look for more Infernal Iron on the road for when they meet again. Once the second upgrade is complete, Karlach can touch other people again without burning them up. She is immensely excited and can be hugged. The moment is highly significant for Karlach, who hasn't touched another person in ten years. If the first upgrade is done in the Grove, Dammon says he must think more about how he can help Karlach. He won't have a clear idea until after the party meets him again at the Last Light Inn. If the party initially encounters Dammon at the Last Light Inn, both upgrades can be received after a Long Rest. If Dammon was met in Baldur's Gate, both upgrades can be received at the Forge of the Nine after a Long Rest. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Although the Steel Watchers have unique interactions to Karlach's infernal engine and the Gondians worked with infernal iron, there are no options to pursue more solutions for Karlach past the two upgrades with Dammon. Letting Dammon upgrade Karlach's infernal engine the first time grants her the Heart of Iron passive feature. Later, when Dammon does another upgrade it will further upgrade Karlach's infernal engine, replacing her previous bonus with Heart Ablaze . v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## The High Harper
- **来源**: [The High Harper](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_High_Harper)
- **分类**: Quests

The High Harper is the Companion quest for Jaheira . It is added to the journal if Jaheira joins the party towards the end of Act Two and the player character speaks to her once they arrive at Wyrm's Crossing in Act Three . “ It is every Harper's hope to be a light that drives out darkness. But I've lived long enough to see so many of those lights burn out, while the shadows cling stubbornly on. Knowing that - isn't it our duty to burn on if we can? To fight for as long as we are able? „ — Jaheira , on a Harper's duty to protect and serve others Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Meeting the Harpers 2.2 Entering the Guildhall 2.3 Nine Fingers Keene's Plans 2.4 Entering the Counting House 2.5 Into the Sewers 2.6 Facing Minsc 3 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Meet the Harpers at Danthelon's Dancing Axe. "Jaheira asked us to go to Danthelon's Dancing Axe in Wyrm's Crossing, where her Harper contacts are waiting to report." Meet the Harpers in the basement of Danthelon's Dancing Axe. "Danthelon told us that the Harpers are waiting for us below his shop." Talk to Geraldus. "The Harpers rendezvous turned out to be an ambush by doppelgangers. Only Geraldus, the last true Harper, survived - we should speak to him." Talk to Jaheira. "The Harpers rendezvous turned out to be a trap laid by doppelgangers. We should see what Jaheira wants to do next." Find Minsc. "Jaheira's Harper rendezvous turned out to be an ambush by doppelgangers. She revealed that she was hoping for information on an old friend who was taken by the cult: Minsc of Rashemen. She will search out a new way to find him once we reach the Lower City." Speak to Nine-Fingers Keene at the Guildhall. "Jaheira wants to speak to Nine-Fingers Keene, leader of the criminal Guild. She believes the guildmaster might have a lead on how to find her old friend Minsc." Search the Guildhall for a lead. "Nine-Fingers revealed the Minsc is none other than the Stone Lord, a rival gang-boss who's been stealing her territory for the cult. She's laid a trap to deal with him, and won't tell us where. We'll need to search the Guildhall for clues." Find Minsc at the Counting House. "We found a note indicating that Nine-Fingers plans to ambush Minsc at the city's Counting House. We need to get there first." "Uktar, Guild bursar, revealed that Nine-Fingers plan to ambush Minsc at the city's Counting House. We need to get there first." "Two drunken Guild members let slip that Nine-Fingers plans to ambush Minsc at the city's Counting House. We need to get there first." Find Minsc at the Counting House. "We found Minsc, an old friend of Jaheira's, robbing the vault beneath the Counting House. It seems he's being manipulated by the cult. After escaping a trap laid by the city's guildmaster, Nine-Fingers Keene, he teleported away. We should search the vault for clues as to where he went." "We saw Minsc rob the vault beneath the Counting House, led by a doppelganger wearing Jaheira's face. He escaped Nine-Fingers' trap and teleported away - we should search the vault for clues on where he went." "The lower levels of the Counting House are off-limits to the public. We need a vault pass from Head Clerk Meadhoney to enter." "Head Clerk Meadhoney revealed that a 'Stone Lord' matching Minsc's description was taken down into the vaults by the Head Banker a short time ago." "The lowest level of the Counting House is protected by a great vault door. We need to enter a code to pass." "We found a book of significant dwarven dates in the Head Banker's office. A certain entry was circled - 1356." Search the Sewers for Minsc. "A cultist in the Counting House carried a note mentioning some hideout in the 'Cistern'. We should head down to the sewers to search for Minsc." "A dead cultist in the vault mentioned some hideout underneath the city. We should head down to the sewers to search for Minsc." "We found a trail of muddy footprints in the vault. They reek of the sewer - that's where we should go next to find Minsc." Search the Sewers for the Stone Lord. "We entered the sewers. The Stone Lord must be here somewhere." Confront Minsc. "We found Minsc's hideout and learned that he has been tadpoled by the cult. If he's being brainwashed by the Absolute, then perhaps there is still a chance to take him alive." "We found Minsc's hideout and learned that he has been tadpoled by the cult. It seems he's being brainwashed by the Absolute - Jaheira asked us to take him alive." Speak to Minsc. "We managed to subdue Minsc - for now. We should deal with him before he has a chance to come to his senses." Follow Minsc. "The Emperor extended its protection to Minsc, freeing him from the Absolute's influence. He thanked us... and immediately ran off. We should follow." Speak to Minsc. "Minsc appears to have found what he was looking for. We should speak to him and see if he wants to join our party." Quest Complete "We discovered that Minsc is working for the cult of the Absolute. We fought and killed him." "The Emperor did not extend its protection to Minsc. We had no choice but to kill him." "Minsc has joined our party. (So has Boo.)" "We saved Minsc from the Absolute's influence and sent him on his own way." "Jaheira has left the party. Without her, it seems unlikely we will be able to save Minsc." "We've moved on to confront the Netherbrain. Wherever Minsc is now, he's on his own." "Jaheira is dead." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Meeting the Harpers [ edit section | visual editor ] After Jaheira is recruited at the end of Act Two, she informs the party of a Harper safehouse in Wyrm's Crossing, in a shop called Danthelon's Dancing Axe X: -6 Y: 133 . As the party enters the outer city and passes the shop, party chatter points out the shop, which is on the west end of Wyrm's Crossing, across from Carm's Garms . Upon entering the shop and speaking to the shopkeeper, Entharl Danthelon greets the party, although Jaheira tells him to skip the pleasantries if she is in the party. With Jaheira in the party, Entharl gives the key to a secret room at X: -18 Y: 138 and the Harpers are waiting down the iron ladder. If Jaheira is not in the party, then selecting "Jaheira sent me. I'm to meet some Harpers here" and choosing either subsequent choice has Entharl relinquish the key. This interaction must occur prior to entering the Lower City or Jaheira informs Danthelon that the Harpers have been infiltrated by Doppelgangers entry to the basement is not possible anymore. Jaheira wants to rescue a dear old friend. Once down below, Harper Geraldus greets the party with a strange greeting - "May Selûne's Tears shine on this meeting." He again emphasizes Selûne's Tears a few moments later. A successful Insight check reveals that Geraldus is not nervous, but terrified, and is using Selune's Tears as some sort of code. Jaheira mentions that the Harpers remind her of Marcus , implying that they are traitors laying a trap. Choosing to strike while Jaheira has them distracted makes the enemies Surprised . After the Harpers are defeated, they transform into doppelgangers and Geraldus explains the rest of the Harpers were murdered or dragged away, while he was only kept alive to lay a trap for Jaheira. Jaheira suggests that the life of a Harper might be unsuited for Geraldus, as he endangered Entharl and others by going along with the doppelganger's plans, but she can be persuaded to think otherwise. Either way, Geraldus leaves and Jaheira explains the main reason she sought out the Harpers was for more information on Minsc of Rashemen , who she had sent them after. Previously, Minsc and Jaheira had been investigating the cult together, but were separated and Jaheira had to leave him behind so that she could spread word of the cult to others. Geraldus speaks in code. With the Harpers gone, Jaheira needs a moment to think. She tells the party she has some ideas on how to proceed, but wants to consider whether this is truly her last resort. After arriving in the Lower City , she explains her plan is to enlist the help of the Guild and Nine-Fingers Keene . Entering the Guildhall [ edit section | visual editor ] There are several paths to the Guildhall. The fastest route is to use the manhole X: 127 Y: -30 in the alley north of the Basilisk Gate waypoint and smash through the western wall X: 38 Y: 784 . Follow the path west and there is a locked door to the Guildhall. Lockpicking it (DC 20) grants easy entry. Above ground is an alley X: 57 Y: -101 guarded by Tusgront and several other Guild members. If ⁠ Aid the Underduke was started and the party aided Farlin in Rivington, they are instantly recognized as allies of the Guild and allowed entry. If Jaheira is in the party, selecting "Careful, that's the High Harper Jaheira you're speaking to" smooths the way without any checks. Otherwise, a Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion check allows passage. Keene is in her office, well aware of the Harper's entrance into her territory. She informs the party that she knows of Minsc already, and he is going by the new title of the Stone Lord. He now works for the Absolute and is decimating the members of the Guild. For that reason, she intends to take him down, but refuses to let the party confront Minsc themselves. However, there are plenty of other Guild members with loose lips. Nine Fingers Keene's Plans [ edit section | visual editor ] Uktar X: -30 Y: 754 reveals the plan if "The Quicker I deal with the Stone Lord, the quicker Nine-Fingers gets back to business" is selected Tut Thistlebog X: -14 Y: 740 drunkenly gives away the information, if Jaheira is in the party or if his companion is properly persuaded. The Professor points the party toward Tut when asked about the plan A note X: -37 Y: 763 , From the Desk of Rakath Glitterbeard, Head Banker , in Keene's room can be read which gives away her plans. The Guild intends to ambush Minsc at the Counting House . Entering the Counting House [ edit section | visual editor ] The Counting House is one of the most heavily secured banks in Baldur's Gate, making it a challenge to infiltrate. Entering the building, Head Clerk Meadhoney X: -103 Y: -179 can be asked about the Stone Lord. He explains that the man was brought down by the head banker, Rakath Glitterbeard . The party can use Persuasion, Intimidation, or Deception to convince Meadhoney to write them a bank pass so that they can catch up to Minsc. Book location in the upper floors of the Counting House. Both the bank pass and the code to get further into the vault can be pilfered by sneaking upstairs. The bank pass sits on a side table in the corner of the first room on the left X: -103 Y: -185 . The secret to getting further into the vault is hidden in a book in the second room. A rogue can attempt to sneak past the guards, or there is a pipe which connects the two rooms that a wildshaped druid can pass through. A date is circled in the book - 1356, which provides a valuable hint to enter the deepest vault. After gaining a bank pass, the party can present it to Cashguard Captain Faril who is guarding the way forward near Meadhoney. Down the stairs and to the east is another checkpoint, easily passed with the bank pass. There are a number of traps which are automatically disabled if the party shows a proper pass. Moving forward, the party can enter the vaults. The correct combination to enter the Counting House vaults Once inside the vaults, the deepest area of the room is straight ahead. However, the door is locked and can only be opened by a code. There is a set of nine keys. By stepping on the correct four keys one at a time, the party can move forward. These keys are the top left, top right, the center key, and the middle right key. Alternatively, the party can short-circuit the contraption by soaking the button floor in water and electrifying it with any lightning source. The party must move forward and can finally see Minsc in the flesh. Unfortunately, Minsc leaves before he can be confronted. A group of Bhaalists attack the party as a parting gift. Minsc is nearly swallowed by a Mimic. Once the Bhaalists are defeated, the party must search for clues on where Minsc went. Approaching the large vault at the end of the room X: -691 Y: 873 , which was completely smashed by Minsc, and a successful perception check shows mud from the sewers. Into the Sewers [ edit section | visual editor ] Minsc can be found in the Abandoned Cistern . There are two possible ways to find Minsc: belowground and aboveground. The valves that opens the sluice gate Belowground, the party must traverse the pipes above the caustic water X: -186 Y: 883 and defeat the Bhaalists guarding the area. Going north, is an area with a Sluice Valve, which is stuck. It can be unstuck and opened with a successful athletic check. Otherwise, the party must interact with the temperature valve and the water level valve, timing them properly to open the door. Hitting the water level valve first, then waiting five seconds before hitting the temperature valve and it should successfully open the door. Then, after a walk through the sluice tunnel, the party can find Minsc. Pressure plates in the "Keep Out" room. Aboveground, is a garden area north of the Steel Watch Foundry with a door that simply says "Keep Out." There are two pressure plates on the north and south walls of the room. Moving a party member or one of the crates in the room on each of them at the same time opens the door to a secret area. In this area is an ornate hatch which leads to the area where Minsc is. Facing Minsc [ edit section | visual editor ] After finding Minsc again, he will not see reason, as his tadpole is controlling him. He immediately attacks the party, along with a number of doppelgangers and cultists, as well as one Zhentarim. All Absolutists must be killed. Taking down "Jaheira" the doppelganger elicits some panicked voice lines from Minsc. If the Zhentarim escape, they are found later in the Guildhall. If Minsc dies here, Jaheira massively disapproves, condemns the party, and leaves permanently, concluding the quest. To avoid this, the party must knock Minsc out using non-lethal attacks. The Emperor initially refuses to bring Minsc under his protection, stating that he is too unpredictable to help. However, he can be convinced to bring Minsc under his protection, particularly with Jaheira present. If Jaheira is not present, then Minsc can still be shown images of Jaheira alive and well, allowing him to be recruited. If Jaheira is dead, Minsc cannot be recruited. If Minsc is successfully recruited, he rushes off to find his friend Boo , smashing through several walls to the north. Following him and subsequently talking to Minsc and Jaheira resolves the quest. It is also possible to enter the Stone Lord's hideout before witnessing the Counting House trap for him. In this case, only the pack of Absolutists (including several "common" doppelgangers) is present in the Cistern. Eliminating them preemptively leaves the party to fight only with false Jaheira, Roah Moonglow and Minsc later. Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] As of Hotfix 4, there is a potential issue with visiting Danthelon's Dancing Axe if the party has already moved on to Wyrm's Rock and the Lower City. If this happens, it is possible the dialogue with Entharl will not trigger and the Harpers will not be in the basement. The quest can still be completed by bringing Jaheira to talk to Nine-Fingers in the Sewers, cutting out the bugged portion of the questline. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death...
