## Unlock the Ancient Tome
- **来源**: [Unlock the Ancient Tome](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unlock_the_Ancient_Tome)
- **分类**: Quests

"Ancient tome" redirects here. For the quest to destroy the tome, see Destroy the Ancient Tome . The Necromancy of Thay is opened... Unlock the Ancient Tome is a sub- quest of ⁠ Search the Cellar in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It is initiated upon finding the book Necromancy of Thay in the Blighted Village . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Unlocking the book 2.2 Reading the book 2.3 Fully unlocking the book's secrets 3 Rewards 4 Companion approval 5 Notes Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Unlock the book. "This book is locked tight, and the mechanism isn't shaped for a key. Maybe some kind of stone would work?" "The owner of the tome mentioned a keygem. Could this be the secret to unlocking The Necromancy of Thay ?" "The necromancer's apprentice mentioned a keygem lost in the tunnels. We need to find it." "We found the gem to unlock the book." Read the book. "We've unlocked the book of necromancy. Should we read it?" "The tome is clearly powerful, but we'll need to read further to uncover all of its secrets." Find a way to finish The Necromancy of Thay. "We managed to read most of the book, absorbing some of it's necromatic power, but it snapped shut before we could finish. There must be a way to read the end." "We made it to the final page of the tome, but it's indecipherable. We need to find a way to read it." "Mystic Carrion and his spirits told us that we need the Tharchiate Codex to unlock the true power of The Necromancy of Thay ." Find the Tharchiate Codex in Sorcerous Sundries. "Mystic Carrion and his spirits told us that we need the Tharchiate Codex to unlock the true power of The Necromancy of Thay . We can find it in the Sorcerous Sundries." "We spoke to Tolna, the bookseller in Sorcerous Sundries. She said that rare books, such as the Tharchiate Codex , are not for sale. Instead, they are kept in a secure vault." Enter the vault. "The entrance to the vault, where we can find the Tharchaite Codex , is in Tolna's office." Find the Tharchiate Codex. "We've accessed the vault, and the lower level of Sorcerous Sundries. Now to find the Tharchiate Codex ." Read the Tharchiate Codex. "We have the Tharchiate Codex . To decipher The Necromancy of Thay , we need to first read the codex." Master The Necromancy of Thay. "We read the Tharchiate Codex , and now have the knowledge to finish The Necromancy of Thay " Quest Completed! "We deciphered the final page of The Necromancy of Thay . The power to summon powerful Thayan undead is ours." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Unlocking the book [ edit section | visual editor ] The apprentice's pack holds the key to the Amethyst's location. The Necromancy of Thay can be obtained during Search the Cellar within the apothecary's secret laboratory past the ornate mirror. Removing the book from its trapped room starts a quest to either unlock the Necromancy of Thay's secrets or destroy it forever. Retrieving the tome from the apothecary's cellar is only one part of unlocking it - it also requires a key to open. The Amethyst is under the spider's lair. There are two ways to find the Dark Amethyst needed to unlock the book. One is to enter the blacksmith's basement north of the Blighted Village waypoint (this is also the same basement where ⁠ Finish the Masterwork Weapon is completed). One of the northern walls is cracked and can be destroyed with force damage, which leads to the Whispering Depths. The other way is to investigate the well X: 23 Y: 400 north of the waypoint. Choose "[INVESTIGATION] Peer into the well" and then climb the bucket rope ladder down into the well to arrive at the cave. Inside the cave is an Apprentice's Pack X: -494 Y: -364 which has more information on the stone's whereabouts. The Dark Amethyst is deeper in the cave, in the western area at X: -563 Y: -353 , below the Spider Matriarch's webs. Either sneak past the horde of spiders, or defeat them all. Defeating the matriarch grants the Poisoner's Robe . Reading the book [ edit section | visual editor ] With both the Dark Amethyst and the Necromancy of Thay in the party's inventory, interacting with the Necromancy of Thay starts a dialogue with the interacting party member inspecting the tome. Selecting Place the amethyst in the slot on the book's cover unlocks it. Once unlocked, there are several options for the book: Open and read it Give it to Astarion or Gale Drop it and proceed with ⁠ Destroy the Ancient Tome If opened and read, the reading party member must pass three Wisdom saving throws to avoid being cursed. See the Necromancy of Thay for full details on this interaction. Turning at least one page of the book grants the reader the Speak with Dead spell and the Forbidden Knowledge buff. Once all three saving throws are passed, the book snaps shut. Choosing to give the book to Astarion grants approval points from him and a special cutscene at camp. Reading the book also grants the ⁠ Secrets of the Necromancer inspiration to party members with the Sage background. Fully unlocking the book's secrets [ edit section | visual editor ] To fully unlock the secrets of the Necromancy of Thay , the party must obtain and read the Tharchiate Codex . There are several hints about the Necromancy of Thay and the Tharchiate Codex which can be found throughout Act Two and Act Three : A book on necromantic tomes on the rooftop of Moonrise Towers also makes reference to the Tharchiate Codex . Mystic Carrion in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate can be paid to reveal that the Sorcerous Sundries holds the Codex in its Sorcerous Vault . Gale and Tolna Tome-Monger will also reveal that Sorcerous Sundries holds the Codex in the Sorcerous Vault. The Tharchiate Codex is in the Elminster section of the Vault, which can be unlocked by opening doors in this order: Silverhand -> Evocation -> Wish. If the Necromancy of Thay was given to Astarion or Gale, they must be the controlled character and also hold The Tharchiate Codex in order to fully comprehend the text and unlock its secrets. Reading The Tharchiate Codex curses the reading party member with Tharchiate Withering (see the Codex's page for full details). If reading the Necromancy of Thay once more, the reading party member receives Danse Macabre which completes the quest. Passing the last DC  20 Wisdom Saving Throw is not required, however not doing so will curse the reading party member with Baleful Knowledge . Lastly, fully unlocking the book grants the ⁠ All Knowledge Is Worth Having inspiration to party members with the Sage background. Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Danse Macabre Speak with Dead Forbidden Knowledge ⁠ Secrets of the Necromancer ( Sage backgrounds) - reading the book for the first time ⁠ All Knowledge Is Worth Having ( Sage backgrounds) - finish reading the book Companion approval [ edit section | visual editor ] Open the Necromancy of Thay book for the first time.   -5   -1   -1 Drop the tome, ready to destroy it   -5   -5   +1   +1   +1   +1 Give the book to Astarion   -5   +5 Notes [ edit section | visual editor ] Gale can technically consume the Necromancy of Thay , which destroys it without granting any of its benefits or knowledge. He can also read it like normal. A character can both obtain the Forbidden Knowledge passive and destroy the Necromancy of Thay . This method does not permit a second character to obtain the passive. The method to do so depends on which type of character intends to receive the passive: Origin characters : Initiate dialogue with the book and proceed until given the option " Open the book. " Swap to another character and move the book to their inventory. Place the book in a container on the ground. Return to the origin character, open the book, and proceed as normal. Destroy the container and then the book without picking it up. Be warned, on uneven terrain, this can lead to the book falling through the ground and becoming inaccessible. Companions : Initiate dialogue with the book and proceed until given the option " Open the book. " Swap to another character and move the book to the camp chest. Return to the companion in dialogue, open the book, and proceed as normal. Dismiss the companion from the party. Retrieve the book from the camp chest and destroy it. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Visit the Emperor's Old Hideout
- **来源**: [Visit the Emperor's Old Hideout](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Visit_the_Emperor's_Old_Hideout)
- **分类**: Quests

The Elfsong Tavern Visit the Emperor's Old Hideout is a quest in Act Three of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by approaching the Elfsong Tavern . Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 An ambush 2.2 The Emperor's special items 3 Quest rewards 4 Notes & references Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Continue exploring the Elfsong Tavern Basement. "The Emperor asked us to check its old hideout in the Elfsong Tavern - some of its old items may be of use to us." "We cleared the Elfsong Basement of pests - and were told of a secret door nearby. If we find it, we can enter the Emperor's old hideout." Delve further into the Elfsong Tavern Basement. "We found the secret door in the Elfsong Basement and can explore further." "A githyanki hunting party are using a hidden area under the Elfsong Tavern as a base of operations - to explore further we need to clear them out." Explore the hideout. "With the githyanki hunting party dispatched, we can explore the hideout further - perhaps even claiming some useful items." "While exploring the Lower City Sewers, the Emperor asked us to explore an old hideout. Some valuable items may await us as a reward." Quest Complete "We claimed a valuable weapon from the Emperor's old hideout - but there may even be more to explore." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] This quest starts automatically after approaching the Elfsong Tavern at X: 78 Y: 1 in the Lower City . The Emperor's voice calls out that it was the location of its old hideout and that there may be useful supplies there that the party could take. The button to the entrance The entrance to the hideout is on the ground floor of the tavern, in the kitchen. There is a set of wooden stairs that lead to a storeroom at X: 52 Y: 8 . Upon entering, if the party have not completed Roveer's Storehouse , a large group of rats attack them. After defeating the rats, the party can enter the westernmost door. Near a crack in the wall, a button can be spotted with a successful perception check at X: -868 Y: 544 . Hitting the button opens up a wine cask in the room next door at X: -861 Y: 547 . Going through this cask leads to the door to the hideout. An ambush [ edit section | visual editor ] Ch'r'ai lies waiting... A group of githyanki soldiers are lying in wait in the hideout, led by Ch'r'ai Har'rak . The Ch'r'ai asks questions of the party and what the Emperor offered them in exchange for their servitude, but most of the options lead to combat. The githyanki warriors must be defeated to further explore the hideout. This encounter contains a paladin and two gatemasters, who are capable of summoning more githyanki to the fight. If Lae'zel is present, a successful DC 18 Intimidation Check allows for the githyanki to leave peacefully. The Emperor's special items [ edit section | visual editor ] The button to the storeroom Behind the statue to the north, on the right side of an indent is a hidden button at X: -734 Y: 577 ( DC 13 Perception Check ). This leads to the area where the Emperor kept many precious mementos, some of which can be uncovered by passing additional perception checks. These items include: Special item Location The Emperor's commentary Butter Fork X: -731 Y: 596 "My cutlery set - a gift from my mother. The butter knife is missing, but otherwise it looks to be complete. I don't need it anymore, but the memory stirs something in me still." [ 1 ] Chains X: -739 Y: 594 "The chains I used to bind my meals - villains and lawbreakers. You see I tried to exercise morality, where I could." Dog Collar X: -742 Y: 584 "Rascal's collar...My poor four-legged friend. Their lives are so brief, so simple, and yet - full." [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Emperor's Wardrobe X: -727 Y: 590 "My old wardrobe - the home of all my disguises. We are what we appear to be, and so appearances matter." Empty Brain Jar X: -745 Y: 593 "An old container for brains. Empty - shame. It would have been nice to find one to sustain me now." Recipe for Fiddlehead Soup X: -744 Y: 587 "A recipe for fiddlehead soup - a favourite meal of mine, when I had need of meals like that." [ 4 ] Stelmane's Portrait X: -732 Y: 597 "There she is in all her glory - Duke Belynne Stelmane. My old partner." [ 5 ] Sword of the Emperor X: -734 Y: 589 "My old sword - my first purchase as an adventurer. No use to me anymore. It's yours, if you want it." [ 3 ] Unique Shell X: -726 Y: 586 "A shell - a keepsake from my final voyage. Pinched in a moment of sentimentality." Beyond the area with the chains, there is a secondary room with a hatch, which leads to the sewers. Interacting with the Emperor's sword successfully completes the quest, even if there are some more memorable active items left in the room. Completing the quest does not make these inactive, and the party can still learn about them later. Quest rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Cerebral Citadel Armour , inside the Emperor's Wardrobe Cerebral Citadel Gloves , inside the Emperor's Wardrobe Sword of the Emperor If the player character has an overall 'positive' relationship with the Emperor, then completing this quest allows scenes to trigger on the next available Long Rest in which it will be possible to 'romance' the Emperor. Notes & references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ The name of the item is "Butter Fork", implicitly because of the "missing" butter knife. As Balduran#LegacyForgotten Realms lore claims, that the butter knife was not actually missing. ↑ This item sometimes does not prompt a Perception check, for unknown reason. ↑ 3.0 3.1 Interacting with this item sometimes equips it to the corresponding slot of the controlled character's inventory. It is not known whether this behaviour is a bug. ↑ It may be necessary to pick up the item to trigger this commentary, rather than just interacting. ↑ The game asset used for the portrait item is a renamed version of the painting item "Portrait Of A Woman" . Dialogue with Wyll implies that this portrait is still accurate to what she looked like, albeit at a younger age. v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Vlaakith's Will
- **来源**: [Vlaakith's Will](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Vlaakith's_Will)
- **分类**: Quests

Vlaakith emerges at camp as a projection Vlaakith's Will is a sub-quest of Lae'zel's personal quest, ⁠ The Githyanki Warrior . It is initiated in Act Three if the player character accepts an offer from Queen Vlaakith when she visits their camp. This quest is an alternative path to Lae'zel's other sub-quest, ⁠ The Prince of the Comet , wherein Vlaakith's offer is rejected. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending player decisions and outcomes. Kill Orpheus once he is freed. "Vlaakith appeared to me in camp and made an offer: kill Orpheus, and she will ascend me to the Astral Plane and anoint me as her Chosen. I agreed to honour her command. Orpheus will die by my hand, and I will be named Baht t'Vlaakith ." Kill Orpheus once the Netherbrain is defeated. "I have freed Orpheus, and he lives - for now. I can slay him when the Netherbrain has fallen and the prince is no longer of use to me." Quest complete "Orpheus is no more; Vlaakith's will is done. When I ascend, I will become Baht t'Vlaakith - Vlaakith's Chosen." "The Prince of the Comet lives, and is soon to ride the Astral Plane atop his great dragon. In Vlaakith's eyes, I will be forever Hshar'lak - a traitor." "Orpheus has taken his own life. Vlaakith's will is done. When I ascend, I will become Baht t'Vlaakith - Vlaakith's Chosen." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Early in Act Three, Vlaakith appears at the campsite during the Long Rest upon entering Rivington in the form of an astral projection and demands that Lae'zel kill Orpheus , promising to anoint her as her Chosen. Here, if Lae'zel learned the truth from Voss and became intent on overthrowing Vlaakith, she can be convinced (with a difficult check) to change her mind again: [PERSUASION]  Kneel, Lae'zel. To be the god-queen's Chosen is an extraordinary honour. (DC 30) [WISDOM]  Connect with Lae'zel's parasite. 'Commander of Dragons. This is your destiny.'  (DC 30) Otherwise, Lae'zel has the option to turn Vlaakith down, and continue with the quest ⁠ The Prince of the Comet . Depending on how previous events concerning this part of the plot unfolded earlier in the game (e.g., both learning the truth about Orpheus and being betrayed by Vlaakith upon exiting the Astral Prism at the Crèche Y'llek ), Lae'zel may automatically refuse her demands - without any intervention by the player character. If Lae'zel refuses, no actual consequences occur, although Vlaakith threatens that Lae'zel will be hunted down by her dragon-riding warriors. The sub-quest may be resolved in the final episodes of the game, when the party gain access inside the Astral Prism, or after the fight with the Netherbrain . v t e Quests v t e Main quests Multi-act quests Find a Cure Get Help from Healer Nettie Ask the Goblin Priestess for Help Get Help from Auntie Ethel Rescue the Druid Halsin Help Omeluum Investigate the Parasite Find the Githyanki Crèche Travel to Moonrise Towers Gather Your Allies Find the Nightsong Personal quests Help Your Protector Deal with the Devil Fulfill the Deal Escape the Deal Discover the History of Prince Orpheus Discover the Artefact's Secrets Free Orpheus Embrace Your Potential Help Kith'rak Voss The Urge Open Your Scars Servant of None Forging a Heart Companion quests The Blade of Frontiers The Grand Duke Wyrmway Daughter of Darkness The Chosen of Shar A Familiar Face The Githyanki Warrior Vlaakith's Will The Prince of the Comet Our Fiery Friend The Hellion's Heart The Pale Elf The Wizard of Waterdeep In Case of Death... ## Wake Art Cullagh
- **来源**: [Wake Art Cullagh](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wake_Art_Cullagh)
- **分类**: Quests

Art Cullagh's mind is gripped by the Shadowfell. Wake Up Art Cullagh is a Quest in Act Two of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started by speaking with Fist J'ehlar at the Last Light Inn or by talking to Art. Contents 1 Objectives 2 Walkthrough 2.1 Meeting Art Cullagh 2.2 Halsin's aid 2.3 The House of Healing 3 Related quests 4 Achievements 5 Notes and references Objectives [ edit section | visual editor ] Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes. Find some clues about Art. "We met Art Cullagh, a mysterious man lying unconscious in Last Light Inn." "We heard Counsellor Florrick talking about a Flaming Fist found comatose in Last Light Inn. He may have knowledge about the shadow curse. We should see if we can wake him somehow." "We met Art Cullagh, a mysterious man lying unconscious in Last Light Inn. He's being cared for by a Flaming Fist." Tell Halsin about Art Cullagh. "Art Cullagh whispered the name 'Thaniel' in his sleep - the spirit of the land that Halsin mentioned. We should tell Halsin about this." Note: The player character must speak to Fist J'ehlar to unlock the conversation with Halsin. J'ehlar may not be at Cullah's bedside but patrolling the inside of the Last Light Inn." Investigate the House of Healing. "We found Art's last orders - to investigate the House of Healing. If we follow in his footsteps, we might learn more about him." Show the lute to Art. "We found a lute bearing Art's initials in the House of Healing. Maybe playing it for him will bring him back to his senses." "We met an unconscious Flaming Fist named Art Cullagh in Last Light Inn. The lute we found at the House of Healing bears his initials. Perhaps the two are connected?" Quest Complete "We woke Art. He desperately wants to speak to Halsin about Thaniel - the spirit of the land, who he met in the Shadowfell." "Art despaired when he learned of Halsin's death. Without him, Thaniel is lost to the Shadowfell - and the shadow curse can never be lifted." "We woke Art. He told Halsin that he met the spirit of the land, Thaniel, in the Shadowfell." If Isobel dies or is kidnapped in Resolve the Abduction: "Art Cullagh died before we could wake him." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] Meeting Art Cullagh [ edit section | visual editor ] Art Cullagh is in the Last Light Inn , in a bed on the ground floor in a room to the north. If the quest ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke was completed, a group of Flaming Fists are in the room, as well as Counsellor Florrick [ 1 ] and J'ehlar . Florrick explains that when Isobel cleansed the Inn, Art suddenly appeared. All attempts to talk to him thus far have failed, but he does have on his person his original writ of duty, signed by Eltan , the founder of the Flaming Fists. Cullagh is looked after by Fist J'ehlar , who explains that he has been completely unresponsive, but the party are welcome to try and speak with him. If the quest ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke has not been completed, they can talk to Art directly to begin the quest. [ 2 ] Cullagh repeats the same song: “ "Thaniel and me are climb, climb, climbing up a tree. We, we see what we see and do just what we please, together waiting for the sun forever. We see shadows, they get darker, but our hiding place is brighter. Monsters snuffling and stalking, in the shade where we are walking. We are fearsome, black and red. We are living, they are dead. Two of us safe 'til the end." „ — Art Cullagh Party members can try and observe him with several checks, each offering clues as to what happened to him: [ 3 ] [MEDICINE]  Observe his present condition.  (DC 14) [CLERIC] [WISDOM]  Try to commune with the man's soul.  (DC 14) [ARCANA]  Search for signs of magical influence. (DC 14)  (if not a Sorcerer) [SORCERER] [ARCANA]  Look for any signs of magic afflicting this man.  (DC 14  ) [SORCERER] [ARCANA]  Recall your studies... What could be causing this?  (DC 14  ) [HISTORY]  Try to identify the song . (DC 14)  (if not a Bard) You're a musician, aren't you, Art. [BARD]  Hum the tune he was singing - try to identify it. [BARD]  Examine his body for clues as to a preferred instrument. [DETECT THOUGHTS] [INTELLIGENCE]  Probe his mind. Repeat what you heard in his mind: 'Thaniel'. Passing one or more of these checks results in the interacting party member noticing that his mind has been gripped by the Shadowfell , but not broken by it. They may also notice his hands have calluses, like someone who played a stringed instrument: [ 3 ] [BARD]  Search his body for any indication of a preferred instrument.   (if the song was identified) [BARD]  He seems musically-inclined. Look him over for any related clues.   (if the song wasn't identified) [INVESTIGATION]  Look closer at him. There may be something you missed.  (DC 10) J'ehlar also produces a Worn Letter recovered from his pocket. It indicates Cullagh was tasked with investigating the House of Healing , which was suspected of being corrupted. The party can ask J'ehlar if she has heard the song before, or if she knows who Thaniel is, but she has no idea about either. If the quest ⁠ Rescue the Grand Duke has not been completed and a party member passes a perception check, the letter appears on the bed next to Art. Halsin's aid [ edit section | visual editor ] There is one person who is intimately familiar with the Shadow-Cursed Lands : Halsin . If the Druid Grove was protected during ⁠ Save the Refugees , Halsin follows the party in their camp and, as one of the few living people who was around the area before the curse, admits to knowing much about the land. If a party member speaks to Halsin and asks him about Thaniel, he says he knows the name well and immediately sets off to examine the unconscious Fist. He tells the party member to meet with him at the Inn. Once there, Halsin says there is no way Cullagh could know Thaniel's name without having met him and that it is imperative he is woken up. He suggests finding something to trigger his consciousness, such as a memory or an item. The House of Healing [ edit section | visual editor ] The House of Healing has been tainted by Sharran cruelty. Cullagh's writ of duty references the House of Healing , making it the first stop in finding a way to awaken him. If the party enter through the front door, they are stopped by Sister Sinda , who says they must wait in line until the doctor is available. The party can persuade, intimidate, or use performance to convince Sinda that they need to see the doctor immediately. The Dark Urge origin and Astarion (if he is chosen to talk as a companion, or is an origin as well) have unique dialogue options to be admitted, which results with Sinda admitting the party without any checks. Sinda can also be bypassed by entering the hospital building from multiple other points of entrance, and moving to the operating room. Once they reach it, this line of dialogue with her is not activated anymore. Once inside the House of Healing at X: -199 Y: -16 , the party must move north to the operating room. Here, Malus Thorm is operating on a distressed "patient" [ 4 ] by torturing them. He pauses to tell the party they are welcome to learn from him. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] A student, yes. Do please enlighten me. You will stop this sick spectacle at once. I don’t wish to study, only to lift the curse on this land.  (if not a Druid) [DRUID]  I am no student, I seek knowledge of the curse. It is a blight on this land. What wrong has this man done to deserve such torture?  (if not a Barbarian, Rogue, or Wizard) [BARBARIAN]  Just kill them already - all this torture is pointless. [ROGUE]  In my experience, torture is usually more pain and less proselytising. [WIZARD]  I am a scholar, this is true - just not in the study of torture. Attack. If the party attack Malus outright, he is joined by Sisters Hunna , Vanessa , Anya , and Geanne . Otherwise, Malus explains they have nearly cured the 'patient.' He states that absence is the heart of Shar's teachings, and asks "What is the light of eyes but the cancer that causes one to witness the laceration of being?" With this pronouncement, he slashes his patient's eyes, completing the 'cure.' He then asks the party if they are ready to be cured as well. [ 6 ] [INVESTIGATION]  Examine the sisters and their implements.  (DC 14)  (if not a Rogue) [ROGUE] [INVESTIGATION]  Cast your gaze over the blades of the sisters.  (DC 14  ) [RELIGION]  Recall what you know of Shar’s teachings.  (DC 14)  (if not a Cleric) [CLERIC] [RELIGION]  Recall what you know of Shar’s blasphemous teachings.  (DC 14)  (if not a Cleric of Shar) [PERSUASION]  The sisters aren’t ready. They’ll make me sick instead of curing me. (DC 16) [PALADIN]  You are the cause of the only suffering here - I am duty bound to end you. A successful Investigation check reveals that the sisters' blades are bloodied and dull, and only the most measured hand could make a clean incision. Passing a Religion check lets the party recall a Sharran maxim: "Go forth and sow doubt, but do not compel it - for only the willing may know the Lady's embrace." With the former, the party can suggest that the sisters practice on each other. With the latter, the party can suggest the sisters practice on Malus himself. A unique option is made available if the party sneaks behind Malus before the cutscene and moves to the room to the north. Inside is the book Surgery and Physiology: A Sharran's Primer at X: -199 Y: 77 which explains Malus has a "final lesson" of loss. [ 7 ] [INTIMIDATION]  I have read your treatise. Initiate the final lesson, or die by my hand. (DC 18)  (if Malus' book was read) [PERSUASION]  ‘Only with sacrifice is mastery gained.’ For the sisters to learn, you must submit. (DC 18)  (if Malus' book was read) [FIGHTER] [PERSUASION]  Sparring is vital to progress. Have them practice on each other. (DC 21  ) [PERSUASION]  Why not have them hone their skills on each other? (DC 21)  (if not a Fighter) [ROGUE] [PERSUASION]  Practice - that's how I got good with a blade. They should spar each other. (DC 21  ) [WIZARD] [PERSUASION]  In my years of study, I have found no better teacher than example. Perhaps you could volunteer? (DC 21  ) [MONK] [PERSUASION]  When the fist trembles, sometimes another is needed to steady it. A good master would volunteer themselves. (DC 21  )  (if Malus' book wasn't read) [BARD] [PERSUASION]  I take joy in performing with a master of my craft - I'm sure the sisters are the same. Why don't you volunteer? (DC 21  )  (if Malus' book wasn't read) [PERSUASION]  They need a better subject to practise on first. Not a student, but a master. (DC 21)  (if Malus' book wasn't read, and not a Monk, Bard or Wizard) [BARBARIAN]  I suffer from boredom. The cure is ripping you apart. Once Malus is dealt with, the Battered Lute can be looted from his corpse. This special lute with the initials AC meticulously carved into the body must be played at Art Cullagh's bed in Last Light Inn to wake him up and grant one or more of the following inspirations: [ 8 ] ⁠ Favour for a Favour ( Noble background) ⁠ Strings of Fate ( Entertainer background) ⁠ Waking the Sleeper ( Sage background) He immediately asks for Thaniel, and says Thaniel said to find Halsin. If Halsin is still alive he is eager to track down Thaniel, progressing ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse . He asks the party to meet him by the lakeside to commence this quest. Otherwise, if Halsin is dead, the quest ends without resolution and the region remains locked under the effects of the shadow curse. Related quests [ edit section | visual editor ] ⁠ Lift the Shadow Curse Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Non-Invasive Procedure Kill the Surgeon before he performs surgery on you in combat. ## Wyrmway
- **来源**: [Wyrmway](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wyrmway)
- **分类**: Quests

This article is about the sub-quest and its walkthrough. For the location, see The Wyrmway . The main area of the Wyrmway Wyrmway is a sub-quest of both Wyll's ⁠ Companion quest and his ⁠ Origin quest . It is added to the journal after reading the book The Legend of Ansur . “ Enduring that self-righteous poetry was a greater trial than any of the ones we bypassed. „ — Minthara , reacting to the entrance statue's pompous verses [ 1 ] Contents 1 Objectives (Companion quest) 2 Objectives (Origin Quest) 3 Walkthrough 3.1 The Legend of the Ansur, the Great Wyrm 3.2 Entering The Wyrmway 3.3 Passing the Trials 3.3.1 Chamber of Justice 3.3.2 Chamber of Insight 3.3.3 Chamber of Strategy 3.3.3.1 Lanceboard problems that may be offered 3.3.4 Chamber of Courage 3.4 Failing a Trial 3.5 The Lair of the Great Wyrm 3.6 Fighting Ansur 3.6.1 After fighting the remains of the Great Wyrm 4 Rewards 5 Achievements 6 Notes and references Objectives (Companion quest) [ edit section | visual editor ] Find the Wyrmway. "After reading 'The Legend of Ansur', We discovered the great wyrm Ansur resides in a secret lair called the Wyrmway. The entrance is apparently located somewhere within Wyrm's Rock Prison, and the notes inside it hint that opening the way involves lightning sparks and torches." Explore the Wyrmway. "We've reached the Wyrmway, where the great wyrm Ansur resides. We must make our way to him." Conquer the Wyrmway's trials. "The statue guarding the Wyrmway entrance informed us we cannot reach Ansur's lair until we prove ourselves as worthy heroes." Speak to the Wyrmway's central statue. "We completed the Wyrmway's challenges. We should proceed to the statue at the entrance to Ansur's Lair." Proceed to Ansur's lair. "We've been granted access to Ansur's lair. It's time to see what awaits us there." "We gained access to Ansur's lair without completing the Wyrmway's challenges." Examine Ansur's remains. "Ansur, the great wyrm, is a mere pile of bones. We should investigate further." Quest Completed! "Ansur is no more. Baldur's Gate will have to survive without its great dragon defender." "We have forsaken our tasks in the Wyrmway and won't be able to return." Objectives (Origin Quest) [ edit section | visual editor ] Find the Wyrmway. "After reading 'The Legend of Ansur', I discovered the great wyrm Ansur resides in a secret lair called the Wyrmway. The entrance is apparently located somewhere within Wyrm's Rock Prison, and the notes inside it hint that opening the way involves lightning sparks and torches." Explore the Wyrmway. "I reached the Wyrmway, where the great wyrm Ansur resides. I must make my way to him." Conquer the Wyrmway's trials. "The statue guarding the Wyrmway entrance informed me I cannot reach Ansur's lair until I prove myself as a worthy hero." Speak to the Wyrmway's central statue. "I completed the Wyrmway's challenges. I should proceed to the statue at the entrance to Ansur's Lair." Proceed to Ansur's lair. "I've been granted access to Ansur's lair. It's time to see what awaits me there." Walkthrough [ edit section | visual editor ] The Legend of the Ansur, the Great Wyrm [ edit section | visual editor ] Statues of Balduran marking the progress: successful (right), failed or not initiated (left) If Ulder Ravengard is saved, he gives the party the book and asks that they enlist the aid of the great wyrm Ansur . If the Duke perishes, or Wyll breaks his pact, walking around in the Lower City may trigger an encounter with Counsellor Florrick , who confronts the party and accuses Wyll of killing his father. If Florrick is dead or still imprisoned, Cordula Eltan takes her place. If he is present, Wyll retorts that this is disinformation being spread by Mizora . Talking either Florrick or Eltan down results in their providing the book to the party to begin the quest. If they cannot be dissuaded from attacking, the book can also be claimed from their corpse. Reading the book adds it to the party journal and begins the quest. Entering The Wyrmway [ edit section | visual editor ] Ansur is in the hidden depths of Wyrm's Rock Prison . Here, the party must travel down the western passage way to find two dragon sconces. The party can gain access to the secret passage by first hitting both dragon head torches with any source of ⁠ Lightning damage such as Shocking Grasp , Witch Bolt or Lightning Arrows . Once damaged by these means, the fire in torches becomes blue, and the wall between them reveals an illusion, granting passage. Note that firing arrows or casting spells is considered an attack, and may draw unwanted attention from the prison guards, notably Fist Ivarus , who patrols the inner corridor. Alternatively, the party can access Wyrm's Rock Prison by descending the cliffs outside Wyrm's Rock Fortress to the west side of the prison and entering through a mousehole. Past the new opening is the antechamber. At the far end is a locked door, and a statue of Balduran, resembling those posted throughout the city, beside it. Interacting with the door or statue enacts a dialogue; the statue suggests in poetic verses that the player character is worthy enough to meet Ansur. The Emperor intercedes, trying to talk the player character out of exploring the Wyrmway (likely without success). Calling themselves worthy results in the statue unlocking and opening the door with another proclamation. Also, companions can succeed a DC 15 Arcana Check to find out the statue is charmed with a Magic mouth spell. Interacting with the statue enables a passive DC 15 History Check . The check is common with the another one at the murals on the wall nearby, which tell Ansur's history; it is not rolled again if deciphering of the murals was successful, and vice versa. If Wyll is present, the player character calling themselves worthy gains   +3 from him. Telling Wyll the statue is probably addressing its call to him grants   +7 . Passing the Trials [ edit section | visual editor ] The party must complete four trials to open the Dragon's Sanctum where Ansur , a Bronze Dragon, resides. The purpose of these trials is to prove the party worthy of speaking with Ansur. To do so, they must pass trials titled Courage , Insight , Strategy and Justice (one per each of "four pillars of power", as cited by Wyll in party conversations). Failing any of the trials results in the party facing hostilities. [ 2 ] Four more statues of Balduran stand in a row in the central hall of the Wyrmway. Each depicts the founder of Baldur's Gate holding a symbol of one of the trials: a pair of scales for Justice , a Knight chesspiece for Strategy , a book for Insight , and a sword for Courage . Statues with the corresponding symbols stand also in each trial chamber. Successful completion of a trial has the matching statue in the central hall begin to glow. Chamber of Justice [ edit section | visual editor ] The chamber of justice This trial takes place in the far left area, with no door. The goal of this trial is to dismiss the dishonorable judge and issue a punishment commensurate to the committed crime. The story of the indictee in question is shown in six paintings starting from "The Apple" and ending with "The Judgement", each described by Narrator if interacted with. The paintings depict a man who steals apples to feed urchin children, then is hired to purloin a powerful artifact, chased and detained, and finally judged. In the middle of the chamber is a stone dais with three more pictures on bookstands. These depict possible judgements which can be passed on the culprit by the player character, but are covered in shadow by the dishonorable Judge standing in the middle of a binding circle, covered with a globe-like shrouded area. If spoken with, the Judge barks at the party, saying he has prepared the decision, and none should interfere. To choose and declare their own sentence, the party must first extinguish the shadow shroud covering the paintings. The Judge resembles a common Shadow encountered in Act Two , but is invulnerable to all damage sources and cannot be pushed away by any means; it must be dismissed magically. Known ways to remove the judge: Absorb Intellect Banishment Control Undead Displace (teleporting the judge anywhere outside the circle) Exhort the Risen Greater Restoration Polymorph Power Word Kill ( Exclusive to The Dark Urge ) Remove Curse Turn Undead It is also possible to use spells that exploit the Judge's damage field avoidance behaviour, pushing it out of the circle. However, if the spell area is not sufficient to displace the Judge out of it completely, the shadow stays nearby and floats back to its place once the party member stops concentrating. [ 3 ] Known spells which accomplish this include: Darkness Flaming Sphere (casting it nearby and manually guiding it to make the Judge leave the circle) Fog Cloud Hunger of Hadar Insect Plague Moonbeam Spirit Guardians Wall of Fire Finally, it is possible to interact with the shadowed paintings directly by a Remove Curse spell, but each painting requires an individual casting to be cleared. After lifting the shadows, each of the three shadowed paintings can be picked up or inspected. They are named 'The Cell' , 'Freedom' , and 'The Hanging' and represent the possible sentences for the committed crime. One of them must be placed upon the empty bookstand named "The Waiting Judgement" behind the Judge's back. To solve the trial, the sentence needs to be proportionate to the crime. When interacting with the statue, if Wyll is present, he offers a hint regarding the answer: "The right path (to justice) often lies between the extremes." Hence, the correct solution to the trial is choosing The Cell painting and placing it on the empty bookstand. Inserting Freedom or The Hanging into the niche fails the trial and summons a horde of hostile undead (see below). On a granite bench near the shrouded paintings in the chamber is the Journal of Past Adventurers Nº2 . Chamber of Insight [ edit section | visual editor ] The chamber of insight The way to this trial lies over a nearly invisible path between the two left-hand statues of Balduran. In this trial the party must discern which advice for the city's ruler is not useful and even harmful for further prosperity. The chamber itself is a vast cave resembling a library, with a meandering path leading almost back to the entrance, with multiple bookcases arranged along both sides. At the far end of the path is a stone dais with three blood-red ghosts of the advisors: Paul Amaps , Cristina Suelto , and Alwin Stedd . To ascertain whose assertion is wrong the party must read three books, penned by each advisor: Amaps' Memoirs Suelto's Ethics of War Stedd's Virtues of Unions These books, however, do not lie peacefully on the shelves, but flutter around: one at the start of the path, one within the middle widening, and the last close to the end. Catching the fidgety books manually requires a DC 15 Sleight of Hand Check . Only one attempt can be made for each party member throughout the trial, regardless of their results; therefore, regardless of whether a party member catches a book or fails, they cannot try again on another . The books can be downed or stopped in the flight by using Command: Grovel , Command: Halt , Fear , Hold Monster or similar spells. It is also possible to throw the books to stop them from flying. Activating Turn-based mode when near a book makes interacting with them easier, but still requires a party member to roll a check or use a spell. Attacking the books is not recommended, as they are usually destroyed in doing so. Reading the books reveals Suelto adopted a cruel ideology, actually proposing to raze enemy's lands to the ground despite their surrender, to prevent their ability to go to war once and for all, proving she is the one who should be eliminated. [ 4 ] If Wyll is present, it is possible to speak with him after reading the final book; he also advises that Suelto is the one to attack. All ghosts in the end of the chamber have 1 HP , so a single strike is sufficient. Attacking Suelto at the end of the chamber results in the party correctly passing this test. Failing the trial summons a number of hostile undead . Chamber of Strategy [ edit section | visual editor ] The chamber of strategy, featuring a lanceboard This trial takes place in the lower right-hand room. The way to the actual trial is blocked by several Attuned Crystals, which may be destroyed, walked around (from the left side) or jumped / flown over. In this trial the party must solve a lanceboard problem (a chess-like game common within Forgotten Realms) by delivering checkmate to Black in two moves only. Note that the hint "there is only one rule, the black king must fall in two turns" given by Balduran's statue is somewhat misleading as the king is not actually taken during a checkmate and that there is, in fact, more than one rule: specifically, there are rules which govern how each piece moves. If Gale is present, he offers his help [ 5 ] . Agreeing to use his advice grants the player character a   +1 point of the wizard's approval. There are three [ 6 ] possible lanceboard problems, which might be offered to the party to solve. The particular setup is defined randomly (presumably at the beginning of the game), so it is not possible to re-enter the Wyrmway to change it. The problems and their solutions are as follows: Suggested by Gale: (1) Moving the White Rook one square to the right, thus threatening the Black King. The further decision depends on Blacks' response: (1-1) Option 1 - Black Bishop takes the White Rook, which allows the White Queen to move 3 squares to the right and deliver a checkmate. (1-2) Option 2 - Black King retreats, making one pace to up-and-right square, and moving the White Knight one square up and two squares left causes a checkmate. (2) Moving the White Queen diagonally to the upper right corner of the board checks the Black King. Its only movement to safety is the black square on its forward left diagonal. Afterwards, White Queen goes four squares to the left, directly in front of the White Rook and diagonal to the Black King, which delivers a checkmate. (3) Moving the White Queen all the way across and take the Black Pawn. This checks the Black King as well, forcing him to retreat a square left. The White Queen then takes the other pawn, one square up and left, protected from other black pieces by the White Bishop. An alternative "brawn" solution is to destroy the Black King piece (featuring 50 HP on Balanced) with ⁠ Lightning damage, which it is vulnerable to. 'Killing' it this way also results in passing the challenge. There are three attempts to finish this trial correctly, the reminder indicated by the number of red heart-shared crystals left at the top of the board; each failed attempt results in one 'heart' shattering. Additionally, whenever a party member interacts with one of the Lanceboard pieces, an indicator shows where the pieces can move, according to the ⁠ Rules of chess . If Gale is present and the player character agrees to take his advise, upon choosing an appropriate piece the correct move is highlighted white. Journal of Past Adventurers Nº3 is at located the feet of the statue of Balduran in this chamber. For more information on lanceboard game, see Lanceboard on the Forgotten Realms Wiki . Lanceboard problems that may be offered [ edit section | visual editor ] The player's first move is red, puzzle's response is green, player's winning move is blue. Setup 1 and its first solution. Setup 1 and its second solution. Setup 2 and its solution. Setup 3 and its solution. Chamber of Courage [ edit section | visual editor ] This trial takes place in the right-most chamber. It is a cave with a roundish ground crossed by a water stream, and a Statue of Balduran in the centre. At the statue's feet stands a Cemetery-Blue Torch , its flames glowing cyan. The four stone orbs are standing around the edges of the area. This is a fighting trial which lasts 4 turns. Throughout it, one of the party members holds the torch in their hand (equipped as a weapon) and must withstand the elements' attacks to pass the test. The party member interacting with the Balduran statue becomes the "torch carrier" for the trial and must survive (stay alive and not downed ). Thus, the rest of the party should defend the torch carrier. The torch is bound to its carrier, preventing other weapons from being equipped [ 7 ] and preventing the torch from being passed to others. As such, it is recommended that a spellcaster , or any class not dependent on their main-hand melee weapon, carry the torch. The torch is one-handed; off-hand weapons and shields are unaffected. Elementals will spawn on the following turns: Turn 1: 2x Air Elemental and 2x Water Elemental Turn 2: 1x Air Myrmidon and 1x Water Myrmidon Turn 3: 1x Air Myrmidon and 1x Water Myrmidon Turn 4: None The torch carrier is marked with a Sacred Flame , which prevents them from turning invisible and makes them a prime target for the elementals in this trial. Applying Sanctuary or casting Globe of Invulnerability [ 8 ] on the torch carrier trivializes the entire encounter, as this prevents enemies from targeting the torch carrier. A Potion of Universal Resistance taken by the torch carrier has the same effect without the concentration issue. Two castings of Planar Binding will effectively end the round they are cast in and the bound elementals are available throughout the rest of the combat, vanishing afterwards. The elementals may then be killed by others directly, or shoved over the edge of the arena they spawn near to kill them instantly. [ 9 ] . None of the elementals leave behind loot, so there is no disadvantage to the shove technique. The Attuned Crystals that grow in clusters around the area can be shattered during the battle to give any nearby character resistance to elemental damage for 2 turns, granting them Crystal Skin condition. The four orbs around the ground are merely counters of how many turns elapsed. They start emitting electric charges one by one as the battle proceeds. They do not attack and have no impact on combat. If the torch carrier survives and is not downed by the end of the fourth turn (regardless of how many enemies survived), they pass this trial and may proceed. The trial is failed if the torch carrier is downed, killed, or exits the room before the turn counter elapses. The Journal of Past Adventurers Nº4 is on the stone edge in the southern part of the chamber. Failing a Trial [ edit section | visual editor ] If the party fails any trial or exits it before completion, they are attacked by several groups of undead, one wave in each uncompleted [ verify ] chamber and another in the central area. Once all the undead have been dispatched, the party can proceed despite their failure, and without needing to complete any remaining trials. Failing a challenge is the only way to obtain Journal of Past Adventurers Nº5 and find out what happened to the party's predecessors. The maximal set and number of hostiles to be fought consist of: Fallen Champion - 4x Fallen Fighter - 16x Fallen Ranger - 15x Fallen Wizard - 7x Failing any trial renders the need to complete any remaining trials obsolete, though they can still be taken before proceeding into the Dragon's sanctum. The Lair of the Great Wyrm [ edit section | visual editor ] After successfully completing all four trials (or failing any of them and defeating all the spawned undead) the door in the main hall is unlocked, granting access to The Dragon's Sanctum , where Ansur is said to lie in wait. While exploring deeper in the Sanctum, it is revealed the great protector of the city has long since turned into a rotten carcass, prostrated in the middle part of the Sanctum. All possible companions comment on this, either with regret, irony or admiration with the creature's former magnificence. Ansur awakens Ansur's body can be interacted with, initiating a conversation [ 10 ] between the player character, Ansur and The Emperor , with the player character's body being used as a conduit for the dragon's spirit. Throughout the conversation, it is revealed that the Emperor is actually none other than Balduran , the legendary adventurer who founded the city of Baldur's Gate. Faulting the illithid for murdering him, Ansur calls it "faessi" , meaning "coward" in Draconic language. Breaking the player character off mid-word, the wyrm-spirit calls them "vrak" ("child") or, if they are a Dragonborn , "ux Bahamuti" ("Bahamut's progeny"). [ 11 ] Fighting Ansur [ edit section | visual editor ] Main article: Ansur/Combat If Ansur is spoken with, regardless of chosen dialogue lines, he calls out the Emperor and reanimates as a hostile undead; the party must then inevitably fight the dragon and two Water Myrmidons which spawn in the steam clouds at the far sides of the cave. Defeating Ansur marks the quest as completed. After fighting the remains of the Great Wyrm [ edit section | visual editor ] After defeating Ansur, another conversation with the Emperor is triggered immediately. The Emperor confirms it was Balduran in the past, and once again tells its story as an adventurer being captured and infected by illithids, along with new details on Ansur's role in this part of its existence. Regardless of the player character's reaction, the Emperor expresses few regrets on its deed, offering as an explanation simple necessity and its will to survive. In the northern part of the cave the Helm of Balduran lies on an altar. The altar is a kind of a pressure plate: taking the helm off it opens the illusory wall which leads back to the spelean [ 12 ] tunnel to Wyrm's Rock Prison . The Helm can be taken without interacting with the remains of Ansur at all. After defeating Ansur, it is advisable to return to camp to inform Duke Ravengard (if he lives), and Wyll can come to a decision about his future. Wyll can choose to become the Blade of Avernus, or follow his father's political path as Grand Duke of Baldur's Gate. Rewards [ edit section | visual editor ] Balduran's Giantslayer - looted from Ansur Helm of Balduran Achievements [ edit section | visual editor ] Crash Landing In the Wyrmway, wait until the dragon is mid-flight, then knock it out of the sky - KAPOW. Notes and references [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ This line or similar ones from other companions appear at random if the party failed or bypassed any of the Wyrmway trials ↑ The party is awarded due XP and always allowed to proceed to the Dragon's Sanctum at the end of the trials, regardless of success or failure and any subsequent hostilities. ↑ To prevent a spell from being wasted, remember the Judge drags its shrouding globe with them when seeking to avoid impact, and flies away once the globe has left the binding circle. For example, the diameter of Cloud of Daggers spell area is insufficient to chase the shadow off. ↑ The party may learn of Suelto's ideology earlier in Act Two by recovering a similar book titled, Suelto's Ethics of War from Ketheric's chambers on the first floor of Moonrise Towers . This book appears to serve as Ketheric's ideology on conflict in general and warfare in particular. Also, the text The Five Year War: A Diplomat's Record alludes to the correct choice here. ↑ Gale chimes in when the player character interacts with the Statue of Balduran to know the task at hand. If he is currently the active character, another party member should be chosen and speak to the statue again, to hear the wizard's experienced opinion. If Gale is played as Origin , he utters the solution automatically, and it is shown above his head like a location remark or party banter line ↑ In-game dialogue files imply a fourth board setup that is never run. However, Gale would describe its solution as such: "First, the white queen moves up and right, diagonally, two squares. This allows her to threaten black's king, while protected by her white knight. The king then has no choice but to take the knight, ensnaring himself him between his own pawn and bishop. The white queen can then checkmate by moving one more square up and to the right." ↑ Should the torch carrier throw a homing weapon that re-equips itself, the trial is failed. ↑ Air Myrmidons can stun the concentrating character using Electrified Flail to break concentration ↑ Air elementals are immune to Shove but can be knocked back by other means such as Mobile Flourish (Ranged) ↑ The synopsis to the correspondent dialogue file implies that initially the conversation was prompted by any party member attempting to take the Helm of Balduran from the altar behind Ansur. However, as of Patch 8 it is possible to walk the around dragon's remains, loot the helm and leave the cave without waking up Ansur. In this case, all due inspirational events concerning the helm are granted as usual. The conversation (and consequent fight) now enacts only if the party interacts with the wyrm's corpse. ↑ This is not accurate, because according to Forgotten Realms lore Bahamut is said to be the progenitor of the dragons (and, subsequently, the Dragonborn) of "metallic" subraces only. Progenitors of other subspecies are reputed to be Tiamat ("elemental", or chromatic dragons) and Sardior (extremely rare "gem" dragons). For more information, refer to Dragonborn on the Forgotten Realms Wiki . ↑ "Spelean" is an adjective meaning related to, found in, or inhabiting caves, derived from the Latin word for cave (spelaeum). The term is used in the study of caves and their features, as in "spelean animals" or the "Journal of Spelean History". ## Leave No One Behind
- **来源**: [Leave No One Behind](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Leave_No_One_Behind)
- **分类**: Achievements

Image of the achievement Leave No One Behind is an achievement in Baldur's Gate 3 that requires the party to save a specific subset [ 1 ] of the Tiefling Refugees . If the conditions are met, this achievement is awarded upon completing the game. Contents 1 Act One 1.1 Special mentions 2 Act Two 2.1 Special mentions 2.2 Deceased or missing 3 Act Three 3.1 Special mentions 3.2 Missing 4 Bugs 5 Notes and references Act One [ edit section | visual editor ] Tiefling Refugees (Act 1) The Hollow Alfira Bex Cal Dammon Danis Ide Lakrissa Lia Rolan Umi Zorru Secluded Chamber Zevlor Tiefling Hideout Mol Inner Sanctum Arabella v t e Specific tiefling refugees in the Emerald Grove must survive. This requires the party to complete the ⁠ Save the Refugees questline, siding with the tieflings throughout and, depending on the choices the party made, ensuring their survival against goblins or hostile druids. The Rite of Thorns must also not be completed. See list to the right for a full name list of all tieflings that must be alive at the end of Act One. Special mentions [ edit section | visual editor ] The below must all be accounted for before ⁠ Defeat the Goblins is complete. Rolan : Found in the grove with his siblings. He must be convinced to stay with the rest of the refugees due to events of Act Two. Arabella : Found in the Inner Sanctum , where Kagha must be convinced to spare her. Cerys only appears in this act if Zevlor has died, thus her appearance means the achievement has failed. If the The Dark Urge is chosen as origin , Alfira must be knocked out non-lethally on the day their special long rest event triggers. She is then replaced by a Dragonborn bard Quil during Dark Urge's personal camp event. If successful, Alfira does not disappear from her position in the Emerald Grove. Act Two [ edit section | visual editor ] Tiefling Refugees (Act 2) Last Light Inn Alfira Bex Cerys Dammon Mol Ide Umi Shadow-Cursed Lands Arabella Rolan Moonrise Towers Prison Cal Danis Lakrissa Lia Mind Flayer Colony Zevlor v t e In Act Two, many of the tieflings are - unavoidably - either missing or dead. Refer to the list to the right to see who must be accounted for and kept alive for this achievement. The Last Light Inn must not fall at any point. This includes keeping Isobel safe during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction , where tieflings must survive the raid, as well as ensuring Nightsong is saved in ⁠ Find the Nightsong . Special mentions [ edit section | visual editor ] The below should be accounted for before the party enter the Shadowfell as part of the ⁠ Find the Nightsong , with the exception of Zevlor and Mol . Cerys : Found inside the Last Light Inn . Cerys can easily be mistaken for a member of the Harpers unless the party talk to her and learn that she was a member of the refugees who was busy scouting during Act One. She must be kept alive through ⁠ Resolve the Abduction just like the other Tieflings. Dammon : Found right outside the Last Light Inn . Dammon must be protected if choosing to fight the Strange Ox . Rolan : Initially found in Last Light Inn , but leaves to find his siblings. The party must then save him in the Ruined Battlefield X: -54 Y: -111 . Bex , Ide , and Umi : Found in Last Light Inn , as long as Rolan and his siblings were convinced to stay in the Emerald Grove in Act One. Arabella : Found near the graveyard in Reithwin Town X: -153 Y: 15 . Her quest ⁠ Find Arabella's Parents must be completed. Cal , Danis , Lakrissa and Lia : Imprisoned in Moonrise Towers and must be rescued with everyone surviving. The party must speak to Alfira upon returning to Last Light Inn for completion. The party can also speak to the other rescued tieflings for various rewards. See also ⁠ Rescue the Tieflings . Mol : Will always be captured during ⁠ Resolve the Abduction and does not appear until Act Three. See also ⁠ Find Mol . Zevlor : Must be rescued in the Illithid Colony. See also ⁠ Find Zevlor . Deceased or missing [ edit section | visual editor ] The following can be found deceased in the shadow-cursed lands. Their deaths cannot be avoided and do not have an impact on getting the achievement: Amek , Asharak , Elegis , Ikaron , Kaldani , Komira , Locke , Memnos , Rechel , Toron , Xeph . The following always are missing and do not show up in the game again: Arka , Damays , Doni , Eramas , Gan , Guex , Nadira , Nymessa , Okta , Pandirna , Rikka , Tilses , Zaki . The following are temporarily missing, but show up later in Act Three: Zorru The following are temporarily missing and do not have an impact on getting the achievement, but show up later in Act Three: Silfy Act Three [ edit section | visual editor ] Tiefling Refugees (Act 3) Rivington Bex Cerys Danis Ide Umi Zorru Lower City Alfira Dammon Lakrissa Sorcerous Sundries Cal Lia Rolan Other Arabella (Sewers) Mol (Guildhall) Zevlor (Upper City) v t e Most of the surviving tieflings can be found in the refugee camps in Rivington , though some have made it into the Lower City . At this point in the game, no major events endanger the refugees. Special mentions [ edit section | visual editor ] Rolan : Found at the Sorcerous Sundries . Rolan must not die if the party chooses to fight Lorroakan . Mol : Found in the Guildhall . She must be spoken to for the completion of Find Mol and cannot be allowed to die during the battle between the Guild and the Zhentarim during Aid the Underduke . Zevlor : Zevlor cannot be found in Act Three until the end of the game. He must survive if he is summoned using Gather Your Allies during the final battle. Missing [ edit section | visual editor ] In addition to the list of missing tieflings in Act Two, Meli cannot be found anywhere. Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Achievement may incorrectly unlock early if saving tieflings missed in a previous playthrough. ## Non-Invasive Procedure
- **来源**: [Non-Invasive Procedure](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Non-Invasive_Procedure)
- **分类**: Achievements

Non-Invasive Procedure is an achievement in Baldur's Gate 3 . It requires the player to kill Malus Thorm before he "performs surgery" on a player character. This refers to the four special actions he can perform after using his Request Surgical Instrument special action. See Fighting Malus Thorm for details. Malus is encountered in the House of Healing in Act Two , within the Shadow-Cursed Lands . He and four "sisters" are performing surgery on a helpless victim in an operating theatre. Strategy [ edit section | visual editor ] To get the achievement, combat must be initiated. Convincing Malus to allow the sisters to perform surgery on him, thereby killing him without combat, does not work. In combat, the sisters can stun and hold party members, allowing Malus to perform surgery. Therefore, it is best to eliminate them first. This can be done even before entering combat, by convincing Malus that the sisters need to improve their surgical skills by practicing on each other. During combat, Malus attempts to resurrect the sisters by touching them, so holding or immobilizing him is helpful.
## Pest Control
- **来源**: [Pest Control](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Pest_Control)
- **分类**: Achievements

Pest Control an achievement in Baldur's Gate 3 . It requires the player to kill the Phase Spider Matriarch before her eggs hatch. The matriarch and a number of other phase spiders are found in the Whispering Depths in Act One , which can be accessed from the Blighted Village , either by going down the well in the village's center, or by breaking a wall in the cellar of the blacksmith's workshop. Strategy [ edit section | visual editor ] To get the achievement, the player must kill the spider before she can hatch any of the three clusters of eggs located atop three stone platforms around her nesting spot. This is made challenging by the fact that her first action upon entering combat is often to use Ethereal Jaunt to teleport near one of the egg clusters and hatch it. The easiest approach is to have a party member with good stealth capabilities sneak onto the two platforms that are furthest from the matriarch, and destroy those clusters first. This is possible without it being noticed at all. Attacking the last egg cluster, which is closer to adult spiders in the area, is likely to be noticed and thus initiate combat, but this is not a problem since the cluster is easily destroyed in one attack.
## Punch Drunk
- **来源**: [Punch Drunk](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Punch_Drunk)
- **分类**: Achievements

Punch Drunk is an achievement in Baldur's Gate 3 . It requires the player to defeat twenty opponents with a party member who is drunk, in a single playthrough. Strategy [ edit section | visual editor ] To accumulate kills that count towards this achievement, it is only important for the party member to be drunk during the moment of the killing blow. They can drink any of the alcoholic drinks found in the game before entering combat, or during combat, before they land the killing blow. An easy way to obtain all needed kills at once is by fighting the Shadow-Cursed Ravens that spawn in Act Two , in the Shadow-Cursed Lands . Upon interacting with a dead cursed raven on the ground at X: 29 Y: 118 , a large number of cursed ravens begin to spawn, each with only one hit point. They are killed easily en masse by using a lasting area of effect spell such as Spirit Guardians , or by letting them flock towards one target and then using an ability such as Shatter for area damage. A similar opportunity is found in Act Three during the Roveer's Storehouse side quest, where the player is tasked with killing a large number of rats.

Adrip with Kereska's Acid Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Acid damage. Its acid spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it possibly inflict 3 turns of Noxious Fumes upon the target. While attuned to Kereska's acid it can cast Melf's Acid Arrow and Hunger of Hadar at 5th level once per short rest. Properties Stack ID : MAG_LEGENDARY_CHROMATIC_ATTUNEMENT_FIRE Loses duration : start of turn If already applied : replace current Grants: Hunger of Hadar ( + ) Creatures within this black sphere are Blinded and take damage at the end of their turn and the start of their turn. Melf's Acid Arrow ( + ) Shoot a green arrow that bursts in a spray of acid. Deals ⁠ 4d4 Acid damage immediately and ⁠ 2d4 Acid damage at the end of the target's next turn. If the spell misses, the target still takes half the initial damage, but no damage at the end of its next turn. Condition: Noxious Fumes Noxious Fumes DEX Save ( DC  13) Hostile creatures in a radius of 3 m (10 ft) take 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Acid DRS damage. Notes The in-game tooltip says this effect inflicts Noxious Fumes for 1 turn, but it actually inflicts it for 3 turns. Possibly applying Noxious Fumes can only occur once per attack. A spell hitting multiple targets will still only make a single saving throw for one of the targets to apply the condition. This is the only variant of Kereska's Favour that requires a saving throw to inflict its condition. The ice, thunder, and poison variants all apply their respective conditions without a saving throw. Bugs Additional damage is added solely based on the DamageType flag of the action used. It does not actually check that the action was a spell. ## Arcane Charge (Condition)
- **来源**: [Arcane Charge (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Arcane_Charge_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Arcane Charge While damaging Threatened entities, deal +2 bonus damage with spells. [ See: Bugs ] Properties Stack ID : MAG_GISH_ARCANE_CHARGE Notes If a single attack does multiple independent instances of damage, Arcane Charge boosts each one, so spells like Magic Missile benefit the most. Some damage riders behave as independent sources of damage and get boosted by Arcane Charge. See DRS effects for a comprehensive list of damage riders that work like this. Bugs The in-game tooltip is incorrect based on the way the effect is coded, and reads as follows: "While Threatened, affected entity has a +2 bonus to damage with spells." However, having the Arcane Charge condition causes a creature to deal bonus spell damage against any Threatened creature; the one with the condition does not necessarily need to be Threatened. Volatile Shield Affected entity has been granted temporary hit points by an illithid. If these are removed by incoming damage, the shield bursts, possibly Stunning nearby foes. The shield only bursts after all temporary hit points have been removed. This also removes the condition. When the shield bursts, enemies within 9 m (30 ft) are Stunned for 1 turn, unless they succeed a DC  15 Intelligence Saving Throw . Withering Barrier If the affected entity is hit with a melee attack while it still has temporary hit points, it deals 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing to creatures within 3 m (10 ft).

Barkskin Armour Class increased to 16. Properties Stack ID : BARKSKIN Status groups : SG_RemoveOnRespec Notes If your Armour Class is lower than 16, Barkskin changes your base Armour Class to 16 with no other bonuses allowed from any source. Mage Armour , Draconic Resilience , Unarmoured Defence (Barbarian) , Unarmoured Defence (Monk) and Barkskin all change your base armour class and therefore do not stack. If you have multiple of these you will only get the benefit of the one that gives the most Armour Class . Barkskin can work while in Wild Shape . ## Bhaal's Boon (Condition)
- **来源**: [Bhaal's Boon (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bhaal's_Boon_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Bhaal's Boon Bhaal revels in the affected entity's gift for murder, granting it a +1 bonus to Armour Class per marked kill. 1 point of this bonus Armour Class is lost each time the Slayer avoids an attack. [ See: Bugs ] Properties Stack ID : BHAALS_BOON_SLAYER If already applied : add to duration More properties : MultiplyEffectsByDuration FreezeDuration Bugs Stacks of this condition are removed in far more circumstances than they should be which makes it nearly impossible to accumulate stacks. Whenever a condition of any type is removed from the Slayer, the number of stacks will decrement. Many features involve hidden technical conditions that are applied and removed frequently. In particular, every attack made with Extra Attack involves applying and removing hidden technical conditions which track the extra attacks. As a result, simply attacking causes the stacks to decrement, often immediately after acquiring the first stack. Sources of Bhaal's Boon Let the Slaughter Begin
## Bhaal's Edict (Condition)
- **来源**: [Bhaal's Edict (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bhaal's_Edict_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

This page is about content exclusive to Honour mode . Bhaal's Edict If you don't kill another creature before the end of your next turn, you will die instantly. Properties Loses duration : end of turn Notes Death Ward does protect party members from Bhaal's Edict , although in this case they lose all of their current buffs and conditions as if they'd briefly died. The death effect appears to be applied during Boon of Bhaal 's turn, rather than when the affected party member's turn ends. Sources of Bhaal's Edict Bhaal's Edict

## Black Hole (Condition)
- **来源**: [Black Hole (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Black_Hole_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Black Hole The black hole pulls nearby creatures and deals 3d10+4 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage. The nearby area is Difficult Terrain and can Slow creatures within it. [ See: Bugs ] Properties UID: MF_BLACK_HOLE_SLOW Stack ID : SLOW Loses duration : end of turn Honour mode Slowed creatures cannot be Hastened , and Slowing a creature will end Haste. Stack ID : HASTE Stack priority : 12 Grants: Slow: Actions You can't take both an action and a bonus action. If you take an action, you lose a bonus action, and vice versa. You also can't make more than 1 attack per turn. Slow: Casting If you cast a spell that costs 1 Action , roll a d20. On 11 or higher, you hang in prepare phase and skip turn. On your next turn you must spend an action point and finish casting. If you don't have an action point, the spell is cancelled. Bugs Despite what the tooltip says, the nearby area is unaffected by this condition, and no difficult terrain is created. Only creatures hit directly by Nebulous Black Hole are Slowed by this condition. Slow: Casting is non-functional and spells cast by slowed creatures will never be delayed. Slow: Actions does not prevent a creature from making multiple attacks unless they somehow become Slowed between attacks on their own turn. Permits safe passage through some of the Shadow-Cursed Lands without a light source. Resistant to magical ⁠ Necrotic damage. Properties Stack ID : HAV_SELUNEOINTMENT More properties : IgnoreResting Sources of Blessing of Selûne Obtained by talking to Isobel at the Last Light Inn and receiving her prayer. Affects all party members and inactive companions for the duration of Act Two . Notes This blessing persists even if Isobel dies, including if the player character murders her. Deeper areas of the Shadow Curse require protection from a Pixie Blessing , Moonlantern , or Shadow Lantern . The blessing only grants resistance to magical ⁠ Necrotic damage. Notably it does not apply to Necromites' Reach from Beyond ability.

## Blindness (Condition)

## Bliss Spores (Condition)
- **来源**: [Bliss Spores (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bliss_Spores_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Bliss Spores Affected entity has a +1d6 bonus to Attack Rolls , Ability Checks , and Saving throws until the next Long Rest . Properties Stack ID : BLISS_SPORES Notes Granted as a quest reward from Defeat the Duergar Intruders . Informing Sovereign Spaw of Glut's betrayal before telling him about the duergar's deaths does not result in the player being rewarded with Bliss Spores. Similar to Bardic Inspiration , this condition provides significant bonuses across the board. It survives respeccing with Withers and moving between Regions , as well as Act One and Act Two . As such, it may be advisable to either refrain from defeating Gekh Coal (and, therefore, removing Nere's Head ) or delay speaking to Spaw afterwards to save the Bliss Spores condition for anticipated situations of considerable challenge.

## BOOOAL's Benediction (Condition)
- **来源**: [BOOOAL's Benediction (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/BOOOAL's_Benediction_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

See also BOOOAL's Blessing for an equivalent effect attached to the Sickle of BOOOAL . BOOOAL's Benediction Advantage on Attack Rolls against Bleeding creatures, as long as there are Kuo-toa to worship BOOOAL . Properties UID: UND_BOOOALBLESSING More properties : IgnoreResting ApplyToDead Sources of BOOOAL's Benediction Sacrificing a true companion to BOOOAL Notes There must be at least two companions in the party, one of which can be a hireling , for the dialogue choice to sacrifice a companion to appear. It is possible to get this buff without having to sacrifice a companion with the following steps: Lure Pooldripp away from the altar (for instance: up the path toward the exit to the Underdark) with Minor Illusion or other non-violent means. He goes back to the altar after investigating. If Pooldripp is not lured away, the cutscene for this event begins upon any character approaching the altar, even if Invisible . Pickpocket the Sickle of BOOOAL off Pooldripp, and avoid him until he resumes worshipping. Trigger the cutscene near the altar. Navigate the dialogue choices to either persuade BOOOAL that the player character can "kill many more in your name" ; or identify him as a "rabid little fey creature" and then say [To priest] to "bow before BOOOAL's chosen" . Earning BOOOAL's Benediction grants the party experience as if BOOAL and all his worshipers are defeated. This buff persists through death and is only removed if all of the Kuo-toa in The Festering Cove are killed. Only characters who are present and in the active party at the moment the Benediction is triggered receive the buff. Those at camp or outside the party roster do not, and the effect cannot be reapplied later.

## Bound Weapon (Condition)
- **来源**: [Bound Weapon (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Bound_Weapon_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Bound Weapon Ritually bound to its wielder. The weapon cannot be knocked out of the wielder's hand, and automatically returns to its wielder when thrown . Properties Stack ID : WEAPON_BOND Bugs This condition lacks the Attributed(InventoryBound) code that is otherwise found on Bind Pact Weapon and Bind Hexed Weapon . Although this was (apparently) done to allow a bound weapon to be Thrown , it also has the side effect of allowing an Eldritch Knight to give their bound weapon to any other character to use to the same effect. Thus, others can equip a bound weapon and use it as if they had bound it themselves, even if they are not an Eldritch Knight. For example, one can use an Eldritch Knight Hireling to cast Weapon Bond on a weapon, give it to another character, and then remove the hireling from the active party and / or dismiss them. In this way a bound weapon can be used by any party member – until the next long rest . Sources of Bound Weapon Bloodthirst Netherstone-Pommelled Bloodthirst Woe Weapon Bond
