## Slowed (Black Hole) (Condition)
- **来源**: [Slowed (Black Hole) (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Slowed_(Black_Hole)_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Slowed Affected entity's Movement Speed is halved, and its Armour Class and Dexterity Saving Throws are reduced by 2. The entity can't take Reactions or make more than 1 attack per turn, [ See: Bugs ] and can only take either an Action or a Bonus Action . Spells cast might be delayed for 1 turn. [ See: Bugs ] Properties UID: TAD_BLACK_HOLE_SLOW Stack ID : SLOW Loses duration : end of turn Honour mode Slowed creatures cannot be Hastened , and Slowing a creature will end Haste. Stack ID : HASTE Stack priority : 12 Grants: Slow: Actions You can't take both an action and a bonus action. If you take an action, you lose a bonus action, and vice versa. You also can't make more than 1 attack per turn. Slow: Casting If you cast a spell that costs 1 Action , roll a d20. On 11 or higher, you hang in prepare phase and skip turn. On your next turn you must spend an action point and finish casting. If you don't have an action point, the spell is cancelled. Bugs Slow: Casting is non-functional and spells cast by slowed creatures will never be delayed. Slow: Actions does not prevent a creature from making multiple attacks unless they somehow become Slowed between attacks on their own turn. ## Soul Pillar Proximity (Condition)
- **来源**: [Soul Pillar Proximity (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Soul_Pillar_Proximity_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Soul Pillar Proximity Raphael is surrounded by Soul Pillars, granting Raphael's attacks an additional 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage (per pillar) and a +3 bonus to his Dexterity score (per pillar). Properties UID: LOW_RAPHAEL_PILLARCOUNTER_1 Stack ID : LOW_RAPHAEL_PILLARCOUNTER_1 Stack priority : 1 More properties : DisableOverhead DisableCombatlog DisablePortraitIndicator Grants: Soul Pillar Proximity For each remaining Soul Pillar, Raphael's attacks deal an additional 1d12 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage and he has a +3 bonus to his Dexterity score. Notes The text of this condition will change to reflect the granted benefits, as each soul pillar grants one stack of additional damage and Dexterity bonus. The maximum values are an additional 4-48 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage and a +12 bonus to Dexterity score. Technically each quantity of soul pillars is its own condition: LOW_RAPHAEL_PILLARCOUNTER_1   LOW_RAPHAEL_PILLARCOUNTER_2   LOW_RAPHAEL_PILLARCOUNTER_3   LOW_RAPHAEL_PILLARCOUNTER_4   Bugs The in-game description of this effect says that the bonus is +3 to Dexterity checks and saving throws, but it is actually a +3 bonus to overall Dexterity score. This has a smaller impact on Dexterity checks and saving throws, but also increases AC. Creatures with Soul Pillar Proximity Raphael Brief preview Each nearby soul pillar grants +1d12 Fire damage and +3 DEX .

## Spell Rot (Condition)
- **来源**: [Spell Rot (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Spell_Rot_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Spell Rot Unless you are Undead , each time you cast a spell you receive 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage per spell level. Cursed Properties Stack ID : LOW_ANCIENTLAIR_CURSE Status groups : SG_Cursed If already applied : replace current Sources of Spell Rot Affects characters while they are in the Ancient Lair . Notes For Tactician and Honour difficulty, this damage is increased to 3d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic per spell level. Removed automatically on exiting the Ancient Lair through the passageway. Fast traveling to another area before leaving the Lair does not remove this condition. Remove Curse removes this condition [ 1 ] Astarion [ 2 ] and Jaheira (if she is wearing Khalid's Gift ) are immune to this condition. Cantrips and spells that use class resources (such as Radiance of the Dawn ) do not trigger the damage, as they inherently do not have levels. Shield does not trigger damage. Abilities that the player may not expect to trigger damage, but still do include: Luminous Arrow from Circle of the Stars Druid , which counts as a level 1 spell Divine Smite , which triggers the damage even if the associated attack misses Spells cast for free thanks to features like Arcane Battery Footnotes [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ If it self cast, the caster takes (final) damage on casting. ↑ Although Astarion is not generally considered Undead with respect to most effects, this appears to be an exception.

## Surprised (Condition)
- **来源**: [Surprised (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Surprised_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Surprised Cannot take Actions or Reactions . Properties Stack ID : SURPRISED Loses duration : end of round More properties : OverheadOnTurn Surprised is a special condition that can affect creatures during the first round of combat. Overview [ edit section | visual editor ] When one side of a combat encounter is unaware of the other side, they may be surprised . A surprised creature cannot take any Actions or Reactions for one combat round. Characters with the Alert feat, the Feral Instinct feature or specific items (such as the Elixir of Vigilance ) cannot be surprised . Certain combat encounters, especially ones that occur after an in-game cutscene, are set to always surprise the party. These can usually be countered by utilizing the aforementioned features or else conditions such as Invisible or hiding in heavily obscured areas with spells such as Darkness before triggering them. How to surprise enemies [ edit section | visual editor ] The key to surprising enemies is line of sight: they must have a clear line of sight to the character surprising them. If they do not, then they begin searching for that character and are not surprised once they find them and begin combat. This can make it challenging and counter-intuitive to successfully surprise a group of enemies. Precautions such as the following may aid in the process: Use Hide to put the entire party into stealth, including pets. Ungroup the party, including pets, then select one party member as the ambusher and move them into position to trigger the surprise. Keep the other party members and pets some distance away while the ambusher approaches the enemy from outside their vision cones. If they cross a vision cone in a Clear Area then they are instantly spotted, but if they are Lightly Obscured or Heavily Obscured then they must succeed a Stealth roll against the enemy's Perception check. On a successful roll the enemies do not notice the character, but on a failed roll they initiate combat without being surprised. The ambusher must initiate combat from within line of sight of the enemy. If they do, then the enemy should be surprised. However, if they are out of line of sight then the enemies begin searching for the party member and are not surprised once they find them and begin combat. The way combat is started matters. Here are some key points (but the testing has not been exhaustive): Melee attacks always work. Ranged attacks done on melee range always work. Spell attack rules are either bugged or complicated. Spell attacks work nearly always for melee range and a bit less often for non-melee range. The following examples demonstrate the discrepancies: Eldritch Blast (attack roll) works both for melee and non-melee range. Fireball (Dexterity save) works for melee but not for non-melee range. Fear (Wisdom save) works both for melee and non-melee range. Magic Missile (no attack roll) works neither for melee nor for non-melee range. Witch Bolt (attack roll) works for melee but not for non-melee range. If the attack type (melee, ranged, spell) works, it does not matter whether it hits or misses. Grenades do not work, even if you hit the enemy directly. For Ambushing enemies, every type of attack, even grenades, work, as long as enemies have not spotted the party. This is true even if having failed the Perception check and attack the currently empty location where the enemy will turn out to be. Once the enemy is surprised, the rest of the party can be moved into position to join the fight. They are drawn into the fight once they either enter an enemy's vision cone or attack them. If a character's Stealth is high enough then enemies sometimes fail to notice them even as their allies are being attacked and killed from a distance. This can even work with Area of Effect spells such as Fireball as long as the party member casting it remains hidden. The enemies run around in a desperate search for the party member but cannot find them. This can be accomplished with a high Dexterity score, Proficiency and Expertise in stealth, Advantage in dexterity or stealth checks, and certain spells and abilities such as Pass Without Trace . Triggering Surprised from Invisibility [ edit section | visual editor ] The most reliable way to surprise an enemy is to become Invisible and attack them. This invisibility can come from any source (e.g., Potion of Invisibility , Invisibility , Greater Invisibility , or Shadow of Menzoberranzan ). The Quasit and Imp pets also work, as does Wild Shape: Panther . List of encounters with surprised participants [ edit section | visual editor ] Act 1 [ edit section | visual editor ] Sneaking into the Overgrown Ruins Refectory leaves Andorn surprised. Approaching Nadira surprises the Bugbear Assassin trying to ambush her. Interacting with certain caskets in the cave inside the Apothecary's Cellar causes an Agile Guardian to burst out and surprise the party. Attacking the bloated hyenas along the Risen Road leaves them surprised. In the Underdark , approaching the Petrified Battlefield initiates combat with a Spectator , triggering a cutscene which leaves the party members surprised. Approaching the Underdark Beach triggers a conversation with a Duergar. If attacked immediately, all the Duergar at the beach are left surprised. If Gekh Coal is called and he turns hostile, the party members are surprised instead. In Grymforge , attacking the three Mimics always surprises the party members when interacting with them in their disguised form. Attacking them from range starts the battle without being surprised. Magma Mephits surprise the party members if they approach the mithral vein closest to the Adamantine Forge . Act 2 [ edit section | visual editor ] In the Shadow-Cursed Lands , three separate encounters with Blights can surprise the party members if they get too close to them. In Moonrise Towers , attacking the Mimic always surprise the party members when interacting with them in their disguised form. Attacking them from range starts the battle without being surprised. The meazels encountered in the Ruined Battlefield at X: -43 Y: 7 surprise the party if a DC 18 Perception check is not passed. Act 3 [ edit section | visual editor ] At the end of " Dribbles '" performance at the Circus of the Last Days , the party members are left surprised unless the ambush is noticed through passive Perception checks, in which case the ambushers are surprised instead. In Entharl's basement , for ⁠ The High Harper quest, a group of doppelgangers posing as Harpers can be spoken to. A combination of dialogue checks and choices can lead to either the party members or the ambushers being surprised. - **分类**: Conditions

Swift as Wind Your next weapon attack has Advantage . That attack deals an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Force . Properties Stack ID : MAG_MONK_SWIFT_AS_THE_WIND Bugs This condition is only removed when making a weapon attack that hits, as opposed to the next attack roll. Sources of Swift as Wind Breezeswift Speed
## Sword Spider's Haste (Condition)
- **来源**: [Sword Spider's Haste (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Sword_Spider's_Haste_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

This article is about content that is inaccessible through normal gameplay . It can still be accessed via in-game exploits or third party tools. Sword Spider's Haste Affected entity has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed is doubled, and it can take one additional Action per turn. Properties UID: SPIDER_SWORD_HASTE Stack ID : HASTE Status groups : SG_Surface , SG_Condition Loses duration : start of turn Stack priority : 10 Honour mode A Hastened creature can not use Extra Attack with its additional action. Applying Slowed to a Hastened creature ends this condition, and prevents it from being reapplied as long as the creature is Slowed. [ See Notes ] Notes This condition appears in commented out code to initialise the goblin siege on the Emerald Grove . It would have been applied to two Sword Spiders at the beginning of the battle. The in-game description says it doubles movement speed, but it actually increases it by 12 m (40 ft). Unlike the regular Hastened condition, this condition does not inflict the Lethargic debuff when it ends. Terazul grants a similar condition, The Terazul Jitters , which stacks with this condition. In honour mode only, Slowed and similar conditions end Sword Spider's Haste. This is because for honour mode specifically, these conditions are assigned the HASTE stack ID and a higher stack priority than Sword Spider's Haste. Conditions with the same stack ID Conditions with the stack ID HASTE , only one of these can be applied at the same time: Condition Effects Absorbed Essence: Illasera Sarevok is permanently Hastened and can't be Paralysed , Restrained , or have his movement speed reduced in any way. Black Hole H Honour The black hole pulls nearby creatures and deals 3d10+4 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage. The nearby area is Difficult Terrain and can Slow creatures within it. [ See: Bugs ] Celestial Haste Affected entity has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. Haste Spores Affected entity has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. Hastened Creature has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. When the condition ends, the creature becomes Lethargic . Mind Sanctuary: Haste H Honour Affected entity has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. When the condition ends, the creature becomes Lethargic . [ See: Bugs ] A Hastened creature can not use Extra Attack with its additional action. Mindbroken H Honour Affected entity is Slowed by the Netherbrain's psyche-shattering might. Mud-Drenched H Honour Thick mud halves your Movement Speed , and reduces your Armour Class and Dexterity Saving Throws by 2. Slowed H Honour Affected entity's Movement Speed is halved, and its Armour Class and Dexterity Saving Throws are reduced by 2. The entity can't take Reactions or make more than 1 attack per turn, [ See: Bugs ] and can only take either an Action or a Bonus Action . Spells cast might be delayed for 1 turn. [ See: Bugs ] Slowed H Honour Affected entity's Movement Speed is halved, and its Armour Class and Dexterity Saving Throws are reduced by 2. The entity can't take Reactions or make more than 1 attack per turn, [ See: Bugs ] and can only take either an Action or a Bonus Action . Spells cast might be delayed for 1 turn. [ See: Bugs ] Sword Spider's Haste Affected entity has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed is doubled, and it can take one additional Action per turn.
## Symbiotic Entity (Condition)
- **来源**: [Symbiotic Entity (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Symbiotic_Entity_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Symbiotic Entity Affected entity has gained 4 Temporary Hit Points per Druid level, its melee weapon or unarmed attacks deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage, and it deals double damage with Halo of Spores . [ See: Bugs ] Ends early if the entity uses Wild Shape . Properties Stack ID : SYMBIOTIC_ENTITY Status groups : SG_RemoveOnRespec Grants: Spreading Spores ( ) Seed an area in deadly spores that deal 2d8 Necrotic damage per turn to all creatures that inhale them, except you and your allies. Bugs Despite the tooltip saying this ability only affects melee weapon attacks, it affects ranged weapon attacks as well. Sources of Symbiotic Entity Symbiotic Entity

## Tempestuous Siphon (Condition)
- **来源**: [Tempestuous Siphon (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tempestuous_Siphon_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Tempestuous Siphon A nearby air myrmidon grants the affected entity Immunity to Lightning damage and an additional 3d8 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage to Elemental Rebuke . The affected entity also gains temporary access to Lightning Bolt and an additional Reaction per turn. Properties Stack ID : LOW_LORROAKAN_AIR Stack priority : 5 Notes Prior to Patch #7 , this condition did not grant an extra reaction per turn. Creatures with Tempestuous Siphon Lorroakan Brief preview Immunity to lightning and additional lightning damage to Elemental Retort .
## Temporarily Hostile (Condition)
- **来源**: [Temporarily Hostile (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Temporarily_Hostile_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Temporarily Hostile If the party knock out this entity or flee from it in combat, it may harbour some resentment towards them, but will not remain hostile . Properties Stack ID : HOSTILE Stack priority : 1 More properties : DisableCombatlog
## Temporary Hit Points (10) (Condition)
- **来源**: [Temporary Hit Points (10) (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Temporary_Hit_Points_(10)_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 10 temporary hit points . Properties Stack ID : TEMPORARY_HP Stack priority : 1 Sources of Temporary Hit Points Life Stealing Critical Conditions with the same stack ID Conditions with the stack ID TEMPORARY_HP , only one of these can be applied at the same time: Condition Effects Armour of Agathys Gained 5 × spell level temporary hit points . If hit with a melee attack, the attacker takes 5 × spell level ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage. This effect ends when the temporary hit points are lost. Bear's Endurance Has Advantage on Constitution Checks . Gain 7 Temporary Hit Points . Dark One's Blessing Gained temporary hit points equal to its Charisma modifier and Warlock level combined. False Life Gain 7 temporary hit points plus 5 additional for each spell slot level above the first. Gigantic Endurance Gained 27 temporary hit points . Heroic Affected entity has gained 10 temporary hit points . Heroism Can't be Frightened . Receive 5 temporary hit points per turn. Inspiring Resolve Affected entity has been fortified by courageous words, granting it temporary hit points . Lunar Vitality You have 22 temporary hit points . While having the temporary hit points, all incoming damage is reduced by 1. Mantle of Inspiration Imbued with bardic vigour and granted 5 temporary hit points . If hit with a melee attack, the attacker becomes Charmed . Myrkul's Gift Gained 10 temporary hit points . Until it loses these temporary hit points, this creature deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic with weapon attacks and has Resistance to ⁠ Cold and ⁠ Necrotic damage. Rallied The galvanising word and will of Duke Ravengard runs hot through your veins - granting you 30 temporary hit points. Rallied Granted 8 temporary hit points by a friendly combatant's rallying cry. Refreshed Hit Point maximum increased by 10 until the next Long Rest . Turns into Nauseated after a Long Rest or after Auntie Ethel turns hostile. Stormheart Resolve This creature began Hoarding Energy , gained 100 temporary hit points for 1 round and lost all Incapacitating Conditions after reviving itself. Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 10 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 15 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 3 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 4 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 2d10 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Gained Charisma modifier temporary hit points from Bolstering Smite . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 15 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Affected entity has gained Charisma modifier temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Elixir of Bloodlust granted you 5 temporary hit points . Replaces effects from other elixirs when drunk. Temporary Hit Points Well-Liked and Well-Fortified: instead of dying, you have gained temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier. Temporary Hit Points Gained 4 temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained Constitution modifier temporary hit points . Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 8 temporary hit points . Tharchiate Vigour Granted 20 Temporary Hit Points by The Tharchiate Codex's enervating magic. Volatile Shield Affected entity has been granted temporary hit points by an illithid. If these are removed by incoming damage, the shield bursts, possibly Stunning nearby foes. The shield only bursts after all temporary hit points have been removed. This also removes the condition. When the shield bursts, enemies within 9 m (30 ft) are Stunned for 1 turn, unless they succeed a DC  15 Intelligence Saving Throw . Withering Barrier If the affected entity is hit with a melee attack while it still has temporary hit points, it deals 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing to creatures within 3 m (10 ft).

The shield only bursts after all temporary hit points have been removed. This also removes the condition. When the shield bursts, enemies within 9 m (30 ft) are Stunned for 1 turn, unless they succeed a DC  15 Intelligence Saving Throw . Withering Barrier If the affected entity is hit with a melee attack while it still has temporary hit points, it deals 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing to creatures within 3 m (10 ft).

Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 2d10 temporary hit points . Properties Stack ID : TEMPORARY_HP Stack priority : 1 Sources of Temporary Hit Points Death Drinker Conditions with the same stack ID Conditions with the stack ID TEMPORARY_HP , only one of these can be applied at the same time: Condition Effects Armour of Agathys Gained 5 × spell level temporary hit points . If hit with a melee attack, the attacker takes 5 × spell level ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage. This effect ends when the temporary hit points are lost. Bear's Endurance Has Advantage on Constitution Checks . Gain 7 Temporary Hit Points . Dark One's Blessing Gained temporary hit points equal to its Charisma modifier and Warlock level combined. False Life Gain 7 temporary hit points plus 5 additional for each spell slot level above the first. Gigantic Endurance Gained 27 temporary hit points . Heroic Affected entity has gained 10 temporary hit points . Heroism Can't be Frightened . Receive 5 temporary hit points per turn. Inspiring Resolve Affected entity has been fortified by courageous words, granting it temporary hit points . Lunar Vitality You have 22 temporary hit points . While having the temporary hit points, all incoming damage is reduced by 1. Mantle of Inspiration Imbued with bardic vigour and granted 5 temporary hit points . If hit with a melee attack, the attacker becomes Charmed . Myrkul's Gift Gained 10 temporary hit points . Until it loses these temporary hit points, this creature deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic with weapon attacks and has Resistance to ⁠ Cold and ⁠ Necrotic damage. Turns into Nauseated after a Long Rest or after Auntie Ethel turns hostile. ## Tharchiate Withering (Condition)
- **来源**: [Tharchiate Withering (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tharchiate_Withering_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

Tharchiate Withering Your Constitution score is reduced by 5 while cursed by The Tharchiate Codex's warped arcana. Cursed Properties Stack ID : CURSEDTOME_THARCHIATE_CODEX Status groups : SG_Cursed More properties : ApplyToDead IgnoreResting Notes Curable via Remove Curse . Once cured, and after each Long Rest thereafter, this condition is replaced by Tharchiate Vigour . Can be negated by equipping Amulet of Greater Health which sets your Constitution score to 23 despite the effect of the curse. This amulet allows you to keep the curse and continue to sport the aesthetics of the curse from its accompanying sickly green aura without the health penalty. The Fiend Warlocks especially might prefer the aesthetics of the curse over Tharchiate Vigour considering Dark One's Blessing by this stage of the game provides comparable Temporary Hit Points from every kill. Sources of Tharchiate Withering The Tharchiate Codex

## Threatened (Condition)
- **来源**: [Threatened (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Threatened_(Condition))
- **分类**: Conditions

This article is about the condition. For items that interact with it, see Threatened set . Threatened An enemy is close. Has Disadvantage on ranged Attack Rolls . Properties UID: FLANKED Stack ID : FLANKED Loses duration : N/A More properties : DisableOverhead DisableCombatlog IgnoreResting Sources of Threatened Being within the melee range of a hostile creature in combat. Notes A creature's melee range can be affected by the reach of their melee weapon. The condition itself has no effect on attacks against the threatening enemy; the disadvantage only applies to ranged attacks against other creatures. If multiple enemies are in threatening range, then the Threatened creature will have disadvantage against all of them. However, there is also a separate source of disadvantage ("Target is too close") when making a ranged attack from within 3 m (10 ft) of a target, meaning most creatures will have disadvantage on ranged attacks against a threatening creature. This can be removed by Crossbow Expert: Point-Blank , making it possible to use crossbow attacks without disadvantage against an enemy at close range. This does not work, however, if one is Threatened by multiple creatures. Because of how the "Target is too close" effect is implemented, it is possible for a target to be within an aura with a range of 3 m (10 ft) (such as Aura of Murder ) while not being close enough to grant disadvantage on ranged attacks. This is because the effect measures the distance from the centre of the attacker to the target, while an aura accounts for the size of a creature's hitbox. Bugs When attacking a very large target, like the Dominated Red Dragon , multiple parts of it may threaten the attacker at once, as if surrounded by multiple enemies, causing all ranged attacks to have disadvantage. This makes Crossbow Expert: Point-Blank useless against such targets.

## Unstoppable (Condition)
- **来源**: [Unstoppable (Condition)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unstoppable_(Condition))

Properties Stack ID : DEATHSHEAD_UNSTOPPABLE Loses duration : end of turn Notes For weapon attacks, most sources of additional damage do not consume additional charges of Unstoppable, even when appearing separately in the combat log. Some effects can consume one charge of Unstoppable in addition to the attack or spell that caused said effects. The list is non-exhaustive. Oil of Combustion (when ignited) Cull the Weak Sneak Attack Every Magic Missile projectile counts as a separate attack and therefore takes one charge of Unstoppable for each projectile. Upcasting Magic Missile can effectively remove all charges of Unstoppable from an enemy in one turn. Vessel for Kereska's Poison Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Poison damage. Its poison spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it inflicts 2 turns of Poisoned upon the target. While attuned to Kereska's poison, it can cast Cloudkill and Ray of Sickness at 5th level once per short rest. Properties Stack ID : MAG_LEGENDARY_CHROMATIC_ATTUNEMENT_FIRE Loses duration : start of turn If already applied : replace current Grants: Cloudkill ( + ) Craft a large cloud that inflicts 5d8 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage per turn. Notes The in-game tooltip says this effect inflicts Poisoned for 1 turn, but it actually inflicts it for 2 turns. Applying Poisoned can only occur once per attack. A spell hitting multiple targets like Cloudkill will only apply the condition to a single target. Bugs Additional damage is added solely based on the DamageType flag of the action used. It does not actually check that the action was a spell. Sources of Vessel for Kereska's Poison Deadlier than Arsenic Conditions with the same stack ID Conditions with the stack ID MAG_LEGENDARY_CHROMATIC_ATTUNEMENT_FIRE , only one of these can be applied at the same time: Condition Effects Adrip with Kereska's Acid Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Acid damage. Its acid spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it possibly inflict 3 turns of Noxious Fumes upon the target. While attuned to Kereska's acid it can cast Melf's Acid Arrow and Hunger of Hadar at 5th level once per short rest. Conduit of Kereska's Ice Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Cold damage. Its cold spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it inflicts 2 turns of Encrusted with Frost upon the target. While attuned to Kereska's ice, it can cast Cone of Cold at 5th level and Ice Storm at 4th level once per short rest. Crackling with Kereska's Lightning Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Lightning damage. Its lightning spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it gains 2 Lightning Charges . While attuned to Kereska's lightning, it can cast Chain Lightning at 6th level and Lightning Bolt at 3rd level once per short rest. Gripped by Kereska's Flame Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Fire damage. Its fire spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it gains 2 turns of Heat . While attuned to Kereska's flame, it can cast Fireball at 3rd level and Wall of Fire at 5th level once per short rest. Rumbling with Kereska's Thunder Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Thunder damage. Its thunder spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it inflicts 2 turns of Reverberation upon the target. While attuned to Kereska's thunder, it can cast Shatter and Destructive Wave at 5th level once per short rest. Vessel for Kereska's Poison Affected entity has resistance to ⁠ Poison damage. Its poison spells deal additional damage equal to its proficiency bonus . When it deals spell damage, it inflicts 2 turns of Poisoned upon the target. While attuned to Kereska's poison, it can cast Cloudkill and Ray of Sickness at 5th level once per short rest.

Stack priority : 15 Condition: Mind Sanctuary: Depleted Mind Sanctuary: Depleted Duration: 1 turn You cannot benefit more from Mind Sanctuary this turn. Condition: Mind Sanctuary: Haste Mind Sanctuary: Haste Duration: 1 turn Affected entity has a +2 bonus to Armour Class , Advantage on Dexterity Saving Throws , its Movement Speed increases by 9 m (30 ft), [ See: Bugs ] and it can take one additional Action per turn. When the condition ends, the creature becomes Lethargic . [ See: Bugs ] A Hastened creature can not use Extra Attack with its additional action. ## Ability Drain
- **来源**: [Ability Drain](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Ability_Drain)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Ability Drain is a passive feature and Illithid Power . Once per turn while attacking, this ability reduces the target's relevant Ability score by 1. Description Once per turn, when you make an Attack Roll , the attack reduces that target's corresponding Ability by 1. The reduced ability score cannot be decreased lower than 1. The ability that is reduced is the same as the one used to make the Attack Roll. For melee weapons, this is usually Strength , for ranged weapons usually Dexterity , and for spells usually your Spellcasting Ability . Details Recharge: Per turn Condition: Ability Drain: Strength Ability Drain: Strength Duration: 1 turn Strength reduced by Ability Drain . Condition: Ability Drain: Dexterity Ability Drain: Dexterity Duration: 1 turn Dexterity reduced by Ability Drain Condition: Ability Drain: Intelligence Ability Drain: Intelligence Duration: 1 turn Intelligence reduced by Ability Drain . Condition: Ability Drain: Wisdom Ability Drain: Wisdom Duration: 1 turn Wisdom reduced by Ability Drain . Condition: Ability Drain: Charisma Ability Drain: Charisma Duration: 1 turn Charisma reduced by Ability Drain . How to learn Used by creatures: Full-illithid Other ways to learn: Unlock from the illithid power skill tree with a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen after obtaining the following: Psionic Overload Obtained automatically after becoming a Full-Illithid Notes Weapon attacks using Spellcasting Ability (e.g. via Shillelagh , Bind Pact Weapon or simply by using Sylvan Scimitar or Infernal Rapier weapons) apply Ability Drain for the respective Spellcasting Ability. As of Hotfix #16, Ability Drain does not reduce a target's ability below 1.

## Absolute Night
- **来源**: [Absolute Night](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Absolute_Night)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Absolute Night is a passive feature that lets the weapon blind its targets. Description Blind targets that fail a Dexterity Saving Throw . Deals an additional 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing to certain creatures that sport multiple sets of eyes. Condition: Blinded Blinded Duration: 2 turns DEX Save ( DC  11) Has Disadvantage on Attack Rolls . Range of attacks and spells reduced to 3 m (10 ft). Attack Rolls against Blinded creatures have Advantage . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Vision of the Absolute Notes As implied in the description of Absolute Night, the passive feature deals extra damage to spiders, spider-like enemies, spectators and other creatures with many eyes. This only works with melee attacks. Thrown weapon hits do not trigger this bonus. Likewise, the ability to blind opponents does not function when a weapon with this passive is thrown. Although the combat log shows (if the target succeeds the roll) a breakdown of the roll indicating that Absolute Night uses the Spell DC , the actual DC is fixed at 11. Bugs The saving throw against being Blinded is incorrectly attributed in the combat log against the attacker or the attack which was used, rather than against Absolute Night.

## Absolute's Bane
- **来源**: [Absolute's Bane](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Absolute's_Bane)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Absolute's Bane is a passive feature that penalizes the user's targets with Bane for 2 turns when you hit them with a weapon attack (melee or ranged). Description On a hit with a weapon attack, possibly inflict a -1d4 penalty to the target's Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . Condition: Bane Bane Duration: 2 turns CHA Save ( DC  11) Has a -1d4 penalty to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gloves of Power Used by creatures: Za'krug Notes If the wearer does not have the Brand of the Absolute , Absolute's Bane will not activate. Even if it is noted in the passive effect UI. The Bane effect is also applied by ranged weapons. Confirmed working on Patch 2. Bugs The Bane effect does not activate when the wearer is disguised , even if it is noted in the passive effect UI. The Bane effect's saving throw does not appear in the combat log, nor do reactions like Portent Dice trigger, even though the passive effect UI indicates there is a saving throw, and the effect sometimes does not trigger (presumably because the enemy succeeds at their saving throw). Though not stated as such, the passive applies Bane and thus does not stack with itself or other sources of Bane.

## Adamantine Reverberation
- **来源**: [Adamantine Reverberation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Adamantine_Reverberation)
- **分类**: Passive_features

This page is about content exclusive to Honour mode . Adamantine Reverberation is a legendary reaction available to Grym in Honour mode. Once per turn when struck by an attack, Grym reverberates, granting 10 temporary hit points and doubled movement speed until the temporary hit points are depleted. Description Grym's form vibrates after being struck, providing 10 temporary hit points and doubling its movement speed while the temporary hit points are present. When the temporary hit points are removed, a shockwave pushing targets back 4 m (13 ft) and dealing 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder will explode outward. Details Recharge: Per turn Condition: Adamantine Reverberation Adamantine Reverberation Duration: 1 turn While it has temporary hit points, this creature's movement speed is doubled. Immediately after losing these temporary hit points, the creature knocks back foes 4 m (13 ft) with a shockwave that deals 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder . How to learn (Information not yet added.) Notes This reaction gains DC bonus from Strength ability score; the DC raises to 19 in tactician mode and 21 in honour mode. Grym cannot acquire Adamantine Reverberation condition while Prone . However, if it already has this condition before becoming prone, the shockwave is actived once the temporary hit points are removed. Grym cannot acquire Adamantine Reverberation condition while Muddy . The radius for the blastwave is 3 m measured from the Grym's red circle.

## Adroit Caster
- **来源**: [Adroit Caster](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Adroit_Caster)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Adroit Caster is a toggleable passive feature that allows you to cast a cantrip at a second creature at the same time, once per short rest. Description Cantrips targeting foes and allies can target an additional creature. The same target can be chosen twice. Usable once per short rest. Cantrips require the targets to be close together, unless those cantrips are projectiles. Details Recharge: Short rest Toggleable Condition: Adroit Caster Adroit Caster Cantrips targeting foes and allies can target an additional creature. The same target can be chosen twice. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gemini Gloves Notes Adroit Caster stacks additively with Metamagic: Twinned Spell , meaning that a total of three targets can be chosen if both effects are used jointly. Eldritch Blast only receives one additional blast and not another full set, e.g. a level 10 warlock gets 4 (3+1) blasts and not 6 (3x2) Cantrips that do not use projectiles instead grant the spells an area of effect; the nearest target to the primary target within this area is chosen to take the second attack. For touch range cantrips, such as Shocking Grasp or Guidance , the radius is ⁠2 m (7 ft). For non-projectile cantrips with a range greater than touch, such as Sacred Flame or Thorn Whip , the radius is ⁠6 m (20 ft). When combined with Twinned Spell, this allows these cantrips to hit 4 creatures instead of the expected 3, as the wearer casts the spell twice with its added area of effect.

Condition: Heat Heat Duration: 2 turns Engulfed by a vengeful fire. Takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage each turn, but can use Heat Convergence . Heat Convergence consumes all remaining turns of Heat to deal extra ⁠ Fire damage on their next fire spell or attack. Heat has a maximum Duration: 7 turns. ## Arcane Battery
- **来源**: [Arcane Battery](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Arcane_Battery)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Arcane Battery is a toggleable passive feature which allows the user to cast a spell without using up a spell slot. Description Alleviate the arcane burden of spellcasting with the power of this staff. The next spell you cast doesn't cost a spell slot . You need to toggle this feature on in order to activate this effect. Details Recharge: Long rest Toggleable Condition: Arcane Battery Arcane Battery Affected entity's next spell doesn't cost a spell slot in order to cast. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Markoheshkir Staff of Spellpower Bugs The long rest cooldown restriction on Arcane Battery is per character , rather than per item . As such, Arcane Battery can be used repeatedly by passing the weapon possessing this feature to different characters, activating it once on each. Arcane Battery is still consumed if active when the character casts a cantrip, despite cantrips not being highlighted in the character's cast bar. Toggling Arcane Battery highlights some abilities and items that do not consume spell slots, such as Danse Macabre and spell scrolls ; these abilities and items activate properly, but are still consumed (along with Arcane Battery) in the process.
## Arcane Echomalefaction
- **来源**: [Arcane Echomalefaction](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Arcane_Echomalefaction)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Arcane Echomalefaction is a passive feature which applies Reverberation on enemies after applying a condition. Description When the wearer inflicts a condition upon a hostile creature, they also inflict 2 turns of Reverberation . [ See: Bugs ] Condition: Reverberation Reverberation Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has a -1 penalty to Strength , Dexterity , and Constitution Saving Throws per remaining turn. When the entity has 5 or more turns of Reverberation, it takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder DRS damage and must succeed a DC  10 Constitution Saving Throw or fall Prone . The condition is removed afterward. Creatures Immune to ⁠ Thunder damage can't receive Reverberation. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Boots of Stormy Clamour Notes Arcane Echomalefaction triggers only once for any action or effect which inflicts a condition and affects only one target per trigger. If an action applies a condition to multiple targets simultaneously or sequentially (such as the persistent Blinded aura from Lathander's Light ), the effect triggers only on the first target to receive the condition, even if additional targets become affected later in the turn. Applying Reverberation does not trigger this passive. Bugs Arcane Echomalefaction triggers under many circumstances where it appears it should not, due to hidden technical conditions, such as when a ranged weapon attack misses, when Sanctuary is cast near enemies, or when revealing an invisible enemy with See Invisibility .

## Arcane Ward
- **来源**: [Arcane Ward](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Arcane_Ward)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Arcane Ward is a passive feature of the Abjuration School Wizard. Upon casting an Abjuration spell, [ See: Bugs ] gain a charge in Arcane Ward which blocks incoming damage. Each time damage is taken, it is reduced by the charge count and the charge count decreases by one. Description The residual magic of your spells forms a ward around you that protects you from harm. Each time you cast an Abjuration spell, the intensity of the ward increases by the amount of the spell's Level, up to a maximum of 2x your Wizard level. Each time you take damage, the ward blocks an amount of damage equal to its intensity, and its intensity decreases by 1. After each Long Rest , the ward's intensity resets, and becomes the same as your Wizard level. Condition: Arcane Ward Arcane Ward Your Arcane Ward blocks damage equal to its charges and then loses 1 charge. Casting Abjuration spells will add charges equal to the level of the spell. How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Abjuration School Notes Casting an Abjuration spell restores Arcane Ward charges even if the spell fails, which is possible with spells like Counterspell or Banishment . Upcasting Abjuration spells results in more Arcane Ward charges being added, with the exception of Counterspell [ See: Bugs ] . Arcane Ward gains charges from any Abjuration spell (except Shield [ See: Bugs ] ), including spells cast via scrolls and items. This includes: Non-wizard Abjuration spells (e.g., Sanctuary or Armour of Agathys ). Special items like True Love's Embrace , which grants Warding Bond when the matching True Love's Caress ring is used by an ally. Protection from Missiles , a 2nd-level Abjuration spell only accessible via Abdel's Trusted Shield and Cindersnap Gloves items. Warlock's Armour of Shadows Eldritch Invocation, allowing them to cast Mage Armour on themselves, recharging 1 Arcane Ward. This can even be done repeatedly to charge the ward up to its maximum level without expending any spell slot. It is necessary to equip and unequip armour each time though, a slow process. Bugs The maximum damage reduction from Arcane Ward is always 20, even for a level 11 or 12 Abjuration Wizard with 21-24 charges of Arcane Ward. Despite being an Abjuration spell and consuming a spell slot, Shield does not grant Arcane Ward charges. Counterspell always restores 3 charges, even if upcast. Because Arcane Ward is implemented as a condition with a duration, it counts as a condition being applied by the spell cast to charge it. This means that if Metamagic: Extended Spell – which doubles the duration of any condition applied by the spell – is used when casting an Abjuration spell, Arcane Ward's charge count is also doubled. This doubling occurs after the cap equal to twice the wizard's class level is applied, meaning that this can be exploited to gain charges up to four times the class level. For example, a Sorcerer 2/Wizard 5 with 7 charges of Arcane Ward casting Banishment should be capped at 10 charges, but ends up with 20 charges if Extended Spell is used. However, when Arcane Ward is overcharged in this way, casting any Abjuration spell that would normally charge it without using Extended Spell forces it to be capped again at twice the wizard's class level. This can be used with most limited-duration Abjuration spells, such as Banishment , Sanctuary , or Arcane Lock . However, Glyph of Warding: Sleep cannot be used for this purpose, as the warding trap has no duration limit (despite the tooltip describing it as a 4-turn duration). There is a second bug with Metamagic: Extended Spell , which can be used to acquire infinite Arcane Ward charges, as explained in this Reddit post . To do this, an Abjuration Wizard must have at least 3 charges of Arcane Ward, then if a sorcerer casts a spell which creates a damaging surface or cloud (e.g., Chromatic Orb: Fire , Spike Growth , or Cloudkill ) and then toggles Extended Spell, if the wizard takes damage from the spell, each time they take damage, the number of charges decreases by 1 as usual, but then doubles. This is because each time damage is taken, the Arcane Ward condition is reapplied with one fewer charge and the source of the condition is considered the source of the damage taken. This means that Arcane Ward becomes a condition with a duration (because its charges are represented as "turns remaining") applied by a spell cast by a sorcerer currently using Extended Spell, which causes the duration to double. This bug works whether the spells are cast by the wizard themselves, multiclassed with sorcerer, or by a sorcerer party member. Surfaces which cause damage immediately, such as Spike Growth, charge Arcane Ward much faster than surfaces which cause damage at the end of each turn, like a Fire surface. This doubling effect allows a wizard to amass Arcane Ward charges up to 2,147,483,647, the maximum possible value of a ⁠ 32-bit signed integer , at which point it is sometimes possible to cause an ⁠ integer overflow by exceeding 2,147,483,647 charges of Arcane Ward and end up with a negative amount of charges. With negative Arcane Ward charges, the amount of charges no longer changes from taking damage, and the ward acts as though it has 1 charge, negating only 1 damage. Casting an Abjuration spell resets the ward back to its standard limit. This bug does not require using surfaces or clouds. Any sorcerer who uses a damaging spell (which can be affected by Extended Spell) on an Abjuration Wizard while Extended Spell is toggled triggers the bug, but anything other than surface or cloud spells is highly inefficient, as it quickly uses up Sorcery Points . When an Abjuration Wizard has zero Arcane Ward charges, many actions restore as many charges as the character's wizard level, as seen on this Reddit post . Some examples: Casting some spells, e.g., Booming Blade , True Strike , Fire Shield , or Hex . Equipping some equipment that applies conditions, e.g., Shar's Spear of Evening or Nyrulna . This includes automatically re-equipping these weapons after throwing them. Receiving some conditions, e.g., Lightning Charges , Force Conduit , Heat , or Arcane Acuity . Some class actions , e.g., Barbarian's Rage , Eldritch Knight's War Magic , or War Cleric's War Priest . When an Abjuration Wizard using Arcane Ward attacks a target, and that target reacts by casting the wizard version of the Shield spell, the attacking Abjuration Wizard immediately loses all of their active Arcane Ward charges. v t e Wizard Subclasses Abjuration School Bladesinging Conjuration School Divination School Enchantment School Evocation School Illusion School Necromancy School Transmutation School Spells Abjuration Conjuration Divination Enchantment Evocation Illusion Necromancy Transmutation Other class features Arcane Recovery Arcane Ward Benign Transposition: Teleport Bladesong Empowered Evocation Experimental Alchemy Expert Divination Extra Attack Focused Conjuration Grim Harvest Hypnotic Gaze Illusory Self Improved Abjuration Improved Minor Illusion Instinctive Charm Inured to Undeath Minor Conjuration: Create Water Portent Potent Cantrip Projected Ward Sculpt Spells See Invisibility Shapechanger Song of Defence Split Enchantment Third Eye: Darkvision Third Eye: See Invisibility Training in War and Song Transmuter's Stone Undead Thralls Animate Dead Additional Undead Better Summons

## Aura of Murder (passive feature)
- **来源**: [Aura of Murder (passive feature)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Aura_of_Murder_(passive_feature))
- **分类**: Passive_features

See also: Aura of Murder (disambiguation) Aura of Murder is a toggleable passive feature. It creates an aura which makes enemies Vulnerable to Piercing damage. Description Enemies within 3 m (10 ft) become Vulnerable to ⁠ Piercing damage, unless they are Immune to it. Details Toggleable Condition: Aura of Murder (Bhaalist Armour) Aura of Murder Duration: Permanent Enemies within 3 m (10 ft) are Vulnerable to Piercing damage, unless they are Immune to it. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Bhaalist Armour Notes In patch 8, the radius was increased from 2 m (7 ft) to 3 m (10 ft). It appears that partial piercing immunity, such as that possessed by Cazador , inhibits the Aura of Murder granted by this feature. [ verify ] Bugs It is possible for the Aura of Murder effect to disappear when travelling between the Lower City and Rivington ; this can be remedied by toggling the effect off and on in the passives tab of the hotbar. Due to the way resistances and immunities are handled, enemies resistant to Piercing damage only have their resistance removed (instead of being made vulnerable) by Aura of Murder. This effect does not stack with attacks that bypass piercing resistance, like those made while wearing the Bonespike Gloves .

## Battlemage's Power
- **来源**: [Battlemage's Power](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Battlemage's_Power)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Battlemage's Power is a passive feature that enhances the user's spellcasting whenever they damage a foe with a weapon attack spell. Description When you hit a target with a spell or cantrip that uses a weapon, you gain Arcane Acuity . Details Recharge: Per attack Condition: Arcane Acuity Arcane Acuity Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has a +1 bonus to its spell Attack Rolls and spell save DC for each remaining turn. Reduce the duration by 2 each time the entity takes damage. Arcane Acuity has a maximum Duration: 10 turns. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gloves of Battlemage's Power Notes The spells that can trigger this effect are: Any smite spell (and also Divine Smite ). Casting a smite spell and then reacting with Divine Smite will trigger Battlemage's Power twice. Booming Blade Ensnaring Strike (Melee) and Ensnaring Strike (Ranged) Hail of Thorns Any damage dealt while wielding a normal, non-permanent Flame Blade in the main hand. The damage can be from any source such as weapon attacks, spell damage (including each dart from Magic Missile ), or even damage from status effects like Burning . Battlemage's Power does not trigger if the conjured weapon is in the off-hand, even if attacking with the conjured weapon. Weapon attacks with Shadow Blade (weapon) Bugs The reader is advised that Battlemage's Power appears to have some of the most complex and unintuitive behaviour in the game, making it difficult to distinguish what is actually a bug. Any damage dealt while wielding a normal, non-permanent Flame Blade in the main hand triggers Battlemage's Power. The damage can be from any source such as weapon attacks, spell damage (including each dart from Magic Missile and each blast from Eldritch Blast ), or even damage from status effects like Burning . Battlemage's Power does not trigger if the conjured weapons are in the off-hand, even if attacking with the conjured weapon. This only works with a normal, temporary Flame Blade summoned by the corresponding spell and not with a permanent Flame Blade acquired through hireling exploit . This effect also used to work while wielding a Shadow Blade in the main hand, but this was removed in a hotfix after Patch 8. Battlemage's Power does not function with the Mephistopheles Tiefling version of Flame Blade, as this version has a different condition applied to it which is not listed in the ArcaneAcuityGlovesCondition() .khn script. Throwing Healing Potions and Grenades triggers Battlemage's Power, even without hitting any target. Reaction Smites provide acuity if and only if the triggering attack provided acuity. If the source attack does trigger Battlemage's Power, reaction smite triggers them a second time, for a total of +4 Acuity. All of the following provide Acuity: Persistent AoE spell effects like Cloudkill and Wall of Fire Every status in the game which deals damage attributed to the wearer triggers Battlemage's Power. For example, Burning and Electrocuted . Fall damage caused by the wearer Some miscellaneous effects like the Holy Lance Helm Retaliation effects do not trigger Battlemage's Power. This includes onHit effects such as Armour of Agathys and Fire Shield ; onDamage effects such as Fleshmelter Cloak ; and onMiss effects such as Shield of Scorching Reprisal . Battlemage's Power is meant to have a OncePerAttack restriction, meaning they should only provide Acuity once per damaging event. However, the OncePerAttack limit gets reset every time the player character performs any effect which targets any in-game entity, whether that entity is an enemy, an ally, or the wearer themself. This includes regular attacks as well as self-target abilities like Dash and Rage . This also includes effects the game considers an "attack" (due to underlying code) such as: using the Perform action (including in combat), speaking with the Sentient Amulet (including in combat), targeting someone with the ability check version of Bend Luck , and provoking an attack of opportunity (though if the wearer takes damage from it, they lose 2 Acuity). Explosions also reset the gloves' once per attack limit. This includes the AOE "explosions" from Hamarhraft and Luminous Armour as well as grenades like Alchemist's Fire and Caustic Bulb . References [ edit section | visual editor ] From the definition of ArcaneAcuityGlovesCondition() in Mods/Shared/Scripts/thoth/helpers/CommonConditions.khn : Show code function ArcaneAcuityGlovesCondition() return IsSmiteSpells() | SpellId('Target_BoomingBlade_ClassSpell') | IsSpellChildOrVariantFromContext('Target_BoomingBlade_ClassSpell') | SpellId('Target_BoomingBlade') | IsSpellChildOrVariantFromContext('Target_BoomingBlade') | SpellId('Target_EnsnaringStrike') | SpellId('Projectile_EnsnaringStrike') | IsSpellChildOrVariantFromContext('Target_EnsnaringStrike') | IsSpellChildOrVariantFromContext('Projectile_EnsnaringStrike') | SpellId('Projectile_HailOfThorns') | IsSpellChildOrVariantFromContext('Projectile_HailOfThorns') | HasStatus('FLAME_BLADE',GetActiveWeapon()) | HasStatus('FLAME_BLADE_4',GetActiveWeapon()) | HasStatus('FLAME_BLADE_6',GetActiveWeapon()) | HasStatus('SHADOW_BLADE',GetActiveWeapon()) | (IsSpell() & IsWeaponAttack()) end
## Bear Heart

## Blessed Healer
- **来源**: [Blessed Healer](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Blessed_Healer)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Blessed Healer is a Life Domain Cleric passive feature that heals the Cleric whenever it heals someone other than itself for 2 + the spell's level ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Description Healing others heals you as well. When you cast a healing spell of Level 1 or higher on another creature, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . How to learn Classes: Class level 6: Life Domain Used by creatures: Hope Notes This applies to spells that heal both the caster and someone else, such as Mass Healing Word . Healing spells that target multiple allies will heal the caster for each target that is healed. Bugs (As of Hotfix #11, possible Bug) Blessed Healer seems to activate on much more sources of Healing than the tooltip indicates: Healing Spells of Level 1 and higher that target only the user will trigger both Disciple of Life and Blessed Healer (for a total of 4 + 2 * Spell Level). Healing magic that does not have a level (such as the Channel Divinity Preserve Life , the cantrip Selûne's Dream and the Paladin class action Lay on Hands ) is treated as level 0, and the caster restores 2 HP to themselves. Healing potions (of all strengths) are treated as level 1 (whether consumed or thrown), and the caster restores an additional 3 HP to themselves. v t e Cleric Subclasses Death Domain Knowledge Domain Life Domain Light Domain Nature Domain Tempest Domain Trickery Domain War Domain Channel Divinity Charge Charm Animals and Plants Cloak of Shadows Destructive Wrath Dampen Elements Guided Strike Invoke Duplicity Knowledge of the Ages Preserve Life Radiance of the Dawn Read Thoughts Touch of Death War God's Blessing Divine Strike Radiant (Melee) Radiant (Ranged) Poison (Melee) Poison (Ranged) Cold (Melee) Cold (Ranged) Fire (Melee) Fire (Ranged) Lightning (Melee) Lightning (Ranged) Necrotic (Melee) Necrotic (Ranged) Thunder (Melee) Thunder (Ranged) Weapon (Melee) Weapon (Ranged) Other class features Acolyte of Nature Blessed Healer Blessing of the Trickster Blessings of Knowledge Destroy Undead Disciple of Life Divine Intervention Expertise Improved Warding Flare Inescapable Destruction Potent Spellcasting Reaper Spells Thunderbolt Strike Turn Undead War Priest Warding Flare Wrath of the Storm
## Blessed Mercy
- **来源**: [Blessed Mercy](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Blessed_Mercy)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Blessed Mercy is a passive feature that adds attack bonuses and saving throw bonuses when the wearer heals them. Description When you heal a creature, it gains a +1d4 bonus to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws for 2 turns. Condition: Bless Bless Duration: 2 turns Gains a +1d4 bonus to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . How to learn Granted by the equipment: The Whispering Promise Notes Applies the same condition as the standard Bless spell, and therefore cannot stack with it. Despite also being called Bless , this buff is not enhanced by the Staff of Arcane Blessing . Multi-target healing abilities, such as Mass Healing Word or a thrown Potion of Healing , bless all affected creatures (potentially including the caster). Drinking a Potion of Healing counts as healing oneself and triggers the effect of the ring as well. The Bless effect is applied even if the target being healed is already at full health. Healing effects from the Ring of Regeneration , Helm of Balduran , or taking a Short Rest all count as healing oneself and trigger the effect of the ring as well. The self-healing from Life Domain Cleric's Blessed Healer does not trigger the effect. Gaining temporary hit points does not count as healing and therefore does not trigger the effect.

## Blood-Curdling Emission

- **分类**: Passive_features

Blood-Curdling Emission is a passive feature that allows the weapon to scare its target. It deals extra damage and increases chance to hit against frightened targets. Description On a hit, possibly inflict Frightened ( DC  12 Wisdom Saving Throw ). Gain a +1d4 bonus to attack and damage against Frightened creatures. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Bow of the Banshee Notes Blood-Curdling Emission grants different effects depending on how the wielder attacks: Attacks made with the shortbow have a chance to inflict Frightened . All weapon attacks (not just from the shortbow itself) against Frightened creatures gain +1d4 to damage rolls. All attacks (including unarmed and spell attacks) against Frightened creatures gain +1d4 to attack rolls. The Frightened condition is not actually applied by the passive feature, but by the Bow of the Banshee itself. Bugs The combat log erroneously references the spell save DC of the wielder; it still uses the fixed DC of 12. This ability is not affected by effects providing advantage or disadvantage on saving throws against being Frightened , such as Countercharm or Shield of the Undevout .

Bolstering Smite is a passive feature that gives the wearer temporary hit points when they inflict a condition with a smite. Condition: Temporary Hit Points (Bolstering Smite) Temporary Hit Points Gained Charisma modifier temporary hit points from Bolstering Smite . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Helmet of Smiting Notes The spells that currently work with Bolstering Smite are: Banishing Smite , Blinding Smite , Branding Smite , Searing Smite , and Wrathful Smite . Bugs Bolstering Smite does not function with Thunderous Smite or Staggering Smite . Any application of Frightened by the wearer triggers Bolstering Smite. Though not stated in the description, the temporary hit points only last for two turns. The temporary hit points only have a StackPriority of 1, and as such are overridden by any other source of temporary hit points which have a StackPriority of 1 or higher, even if the new source is of a lesser value.

## Brand of the Absolute
- **来源**: [Brand of the Absolute](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Brand_of_the_Absolute)
- **分类**: Passive_features

The Brand of the Absolute The Brand of the Absolute is an optional permanent bonus that leads to unique dialogue options and powerful item interactions. Contents 1 Appearance 2 Becoming Branded 3 Branded dialogue 4 Item synergy 5 Bugs Appearance [ edit section | visual editor ] The brand is a combination of the symbols of each of the Dead Three : the black hand of Bane , the bloody skull of Bhaal , and the triangle-inset skull of Myrkul . Becoming Branded [ edit section | visual editor ] A party member may become branded by speaking to Gut in the Shattered Sanctum . After branding them, she attempts to mentally connect to their parasite and ask them to join her in her private chapel. After this conversation, Gut no longer offers to brand additional characters, but any party member can receive the brand by speaking to Warlock Greez . Becoming branded has the following consequences: A one-time disapproval from the following Companions :   -1   -1 "Branded" appears in the Tags section of the character's Detailed View. The tag may not show up if the character is disguised. "Branded" Dialogue options become available. Branded dialogue [ edit section | visual editor ] Brakkal recognizes the brand and subsequently refuses to talk to the branded character. Fezzerk obliges and leaves Barcus Wroot alone, leaving the Blighted Village afterwards. Gekh Coal backs down without a dialogue check at the Decrepit Village in the Underdark . Corsair Greymon requires an easier dialogue check, made with Advantage , to back down on the skiff in the Underdark. Lump and his fellow Ogres back down without a dialogue check at the Blighted Village. Item synergy [ edit section | visual editor ] The following pieces of equipment require the Absolute's brand to function at their full potential: Absolute's Protector Absolute's Talisman Absolute's Warboard Gloves of Power Ring of Absolute Force Bugs [ edit section | visual editor ] Tav may not become "Branded" after an attempt in Patch #7 , so it is necessary to check if it has succeeded or failed (verified as of 12/25/2024). The Ring of Absolute Force fully functions even if the wearer is not branded.
## Brave

## Breezeswift Speed
- **来源**: [Breezeswift Speed](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Breezeswift_Speed)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Breezeswift Speed is a passive feature that increases a monk's attacks. Description While using Step of the Wind , your next Attack Roll has Advantage and deals an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage. Condition: Swift as Wind Swift as Wind Duration: 1 turn Your next weapon attack has Advantage . That attack deals an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Force . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Garb of the Land and Sky Notes The effect of Breezeswift Speed is dispelled when landing a successful weapon attack, but can boost attacks other than with proper weapons. The Advantage component of the effect applies to all attack rolls including unarmed attacks, throwing items, and spells. When making one of these (non-weapon) attacks, the effect remains. The damage component applies to thrown weapons as well. Again, the effect is not lost when making a throwing attack, so Breezeswift Speed can be used buff the damage of all throwing attacks in a turn. Bugs Breezeswift Speed provides Swift as Wind , which is only removed when making a weapon attack, as opposed to the next attack roll. Breezeswift Speed states it affects the next "Attack Roll", while Swift As Wind states it affects the next "weapon attack". While active, Swift As Wind affects all attack rolls but only increases weapon damage.

## Brutal Critical
- **来源**: [Brutal Critical](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Brutal_Critical)
- **分类**: Passive_features

See also: Savage Attacks Brutal Critical is a Barbarian passive feature. The barbarian makes their critical hits even deadlier. Description You've trained to strike swift and true. When you land a Critical Hit , you roll an extra damage die as well as the normal additional critical die. How to learn Classes: Class level 9: Barbarian Used by creatures: Baff Elkhorn , Bearclaw , Gilded Minotaur , Lady Flux , Lobo Denysse , Lord Jannath's Bodyguard , Minotaur , Rage Queller , Tusgront , Ulma Notes This feature only applies to main hand melee weapon attacks or unarmed melee attacks. For comparison, Savage Attacks , a similar racial feature, only applies to melee weapon attacks (main hand or offhand) and not unarmed attacks. Weapons that deal multiple damage dice like greatswords or mauls will only receive a single extra damage die from this feature. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Callous Glow Ring Notes The effect requires the target to be standing in a light level of Clear Area . ## Caustic Reprisal
- **来源**: [Caustic Reprisal](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Caustic_Reprisal)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Caustic Reprisal is a passive feature that retaliates against an attacker that hits the wearer. Description Whenever a creature deals melee damage to the wearer, that creature takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Acid Damage. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Fleshmelter Cloak Notes Caustic Reprisal only activates if the wearer takes damage. For example when damage is reduced to 0 by Arcane Ward , Caustic Reprisal does not activate. Acid damage from Caustic Reprisal does not activate the Ichorous Corrosion passive on the Ichorous Gloves . Due to the way Baldur's Gate 3 handles its damage calculations, if the attacker lands a critical hit, "Caustic Reprisal" damage is doubled from 1d4 to 2d4.

Description This creature's attack deals additional 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage and may inflict Paralysed . Condition: Paralysed Paralysed Duration: 1 turn CON Save ( DC  15) Affected entity can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions . Attacks against the entity are always critical hits if the attacker is within 3 m (10 ft). Attack rolls against the entity have Advantage . Affected entity automatically fails all Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . How to learn Used by creatures: Strange Ox Notes This feature still applies when the Strange Ox is one of its alternate forms such as Alternate Form: Dire Wolf . Bugs This feature triggers even on a miss, dealing damage and potentially Paralysing the target.

## Chaos
- **来源**: [Chaos](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Chaos)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Chaos is a passive feature which heals the wielder on every hit. Description On dealing damage with this weapon, regain 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . [ See Notes ] How to learn Granted by the weapons: Sword of Chaos Notes Chaos does not trigger when damaging items. On-heal effects such as Blessed Mercy do not trigger through Chaos either. The wielder is healed upon each instance of damage. This means that in the case of attacks which deal multiple damage types, such as Booming Blade and Divine Smite (as well as other Smite spells), or in the case of attacks which damage multiple targets, such as Slashing Flourish (Melee) , the wielder is healed multiple times. The in-game description says "On a hit, regain 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points .".

Grants: Tadpole Charm How to learn Used by creatures: Dead Mind Flayer (Goblin Camp) , Dream Guardian , Full-illithid , Mind flayer (nautiloid wreck) , Mind flayer (windmill) , Mind flayers , Minthara , Omeluum , Rage Queller Other ways to learn: Unlock with a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen after obtaining the following illithid power : Favourable Beginnings Obtained automatically after becoming a Full-Illithid Notes The saving throw does not always appear in the combat log. ## Cheeky Tipple
- **来源**: [Cheeky Tipple](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Cheeky_Tipple)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Cheeky Tipple is a Way of the Drunken Master monk passive feature that prevents the effects of being intoxicated. Description You are Immune to the negative effects of being Drunk . Once per day, when you drink alcohol, you regain half your Ki Points (rounded down). Condition: Drunk (Drunken Master) Drunk Duration: 5 turns Although drunk, you are immune to the negative effects of alcohol, thanks to your training in the Way of the Drunken Master . How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Way of the Drunken Master Notes When receiving any drunk condition such as Alcohol , this passive will remove it and instead apply a special version of Drunk for 5 turns. This duration does not depend on the duration of the initially applied drunk condition. The extended duration of this harmless drunk effect is particularly useful for items like Punch-Drunk Bastard and Drunken Cloth which rely on being drunk. Normally Alcohol from consumables like Wine lasts only 2 turns while this feature extends it to 5 turns. Amulet of the Drunkard also extends the duration of this special drunk effect by 5 turns. ## Cloud of Jellyfish
- **来源**: [Cloud of Jellyfish](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Cloud_of_Jellyfish)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Cloud of Jellyfish is passive feature available to Swarmkeepers . It turns the Gathered Swarm into jellyfish that deal ⁠ Lightning damage and can shock enemies. This feature can be switched out at level up. Description You gain a swarm of jellyfish that fights on your side. Once per round, the swarm can assist you in one of three ways after you attack an enemy: it can attack and deal additional ⁠ Lightning damage, Shock your enemy, or teleport you to a safer location. Cloud of Jellyfish: Attack - Deal 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage to the target. Cloud of Jellyfish: Teleport - Teleport up to 5 m (17 ft) away. Cloud of Jellyfish: Shocking Sting - Possibly Shock the target for 1 turn. Details Recharge: Per turn At higher levels At level 11, Mighty Swarm upgrades the swarm options to: Cloud of Jellyfish: Attack - Deal 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage to the target. ## Coldbrim Chill
- **来源**: [Coldbrim Chill](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Coldbrim_Chill)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Coldbrim Chill is a passive feature that chills the wearer's target whenever they apply a condition. Description Once per turn, any condition inflicted on a target, also applies 2 turns of Encrusted with Frost . [ See: Bugs ] Condition: Encrusted with Frost Encrusted with Frost Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has Disadvantage on Dexterity Saving Throws . When there are 7 or more turns remaining, the entity must succeed a DC  12 Constitution Saving Throw or take 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Cold DRS and become Frozen . On a successful save, it only takes half damage. Afterward, the frost sloughs away. Removed by Burning . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Coldbrim Hat Notes Coldbrim Chill only affects a single target per turn. The wording of the description may be slightly confusing. Specifically, the fact that the Coldbrim Chill effect only applies once throughout the turn, meaning that an area of effect spell like Hypnotic Pattern only applies to the first target hit and only once that turn, not to all targets. Applying Encrusted with Frost to a target is specifically excluded from conditions that trigger this passive. Bugs Coldbrim Chill triggers under many circumstances even though it appears it should not, due to hidden technical conditions, such as when a ranged weapon attack misses, when Sanctuary is cast near enemies, or when revealing an invisible enemy with See Invisibility .

## Companion's Bond
- **来源**: [Companion's Bond](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Companion's_Bond)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Companion's Bond is a Beast Master Ranger passive feature that enhances your companion. Description Your Ranger's Companions receive a bonus to Armour Class and damage equal to its Proficiency Bonus . Upgraded hit points and abilities for your companion and a new visual look. How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Beast Master Used by creatures: Aranea Aculeata , Aranea Major , Corvus Celer , Corvus Major , Funglesby , Lupus Major , Lupus Optumus , Sharran Spider , Sharran Wolf , Sharran Wolf (Viconia) , Ursa Ingens , Ursa Major , Verres Calamitosus , Verres Major Notes If a companion is already active when the Ranger levels up to level 5, it receives this feature's upgrades and appearance change immediately. The Ranger does not need to re-summon it. Bugs The in-game description says that the bonus scales with "your" (i.e. the Beast Master's) proficiency bonus, but in fact it uses the companion's proficiency bonus. This means the bonus will not increase to +4 until the final level 11 upgrade to your animal companion rather than at character level 9. Prior to the level 5 upgrade, animal companions will incorrectly have a proficiency bonus of 0 instead of +2. After the level 5 upgrade, the proficiency bonus will correctly increase to +3. Effectively, this means that at level 5, your animal companions will also receive an increase to their attack rolls equal to their proficiency bonus, but this is not actually part of this feature, merely a consequence of bugged proficiency bonus progression. Brief preview Receive a bonus to AC and damage equal to its proficiency bonus. v t e Ranger Subclasses Beast Master Gloom Stalker Hunter Swarmkeeper Favoured Enemy Bounty Hunter Keeper of the Veil Mage Breaker Ranger Knight Sanctified Stalker Natural Explorer Beast Tamer Urban Tracker Wasteland Wanderer ( Cold Fire Poison ) Other class features Bestial Fury Companion's Bond Dread Ambusher Melee Ranged Hide Escape the Horde Exceptional Training Extra Attack Gathered Swarm Cloud of Jellyfish Flurry of Moths Legion of Bees Hide in Plain Sight Hunter's Prey Colossus Slayer Giant Killer Horde Breaker Iron Mind Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Mighty Swarm Multiattack Defence Prey's Scent Spells Ranger's Companion Stalker's Flurry Steel Will Superior Darkvision Umbral Shroud Volley Whirlwind Attack Writhing Tide
## Conductive Strikes
- **来源**: [Conductive Strikes](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Conductive_Strikes)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Conductive Strikes is a passive feature that adds lightning charges when performing an unarmed attack. Description On a hit with an unarmed attack, the wearer gains 2 Lightning Charges . Condition: Lightning Charges Lightning Charges Duration: 2 turns Lightning courses through you. You have +1 to Attack Rolls and deal an additional 1 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning damage. If you gain 5 charges, they are consumed the next time you deal damage, and you deal an additional 1d8 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning DRS damage. You lose 1 charge per turn. How to learn Granted by the equipment: The Sparkle Hands Notes Conductive Strikes grants Lightning Charges on any unarmed attack, which includes Throw attacks. Unlike similar passives, Conductive Strikes lacks a OncePerAttack restriction and thus triggers on any source of damage during an attack. For example, a Giant Barbarian: Throwing Lightning Jabber deals damage from the weapon, granting 2 Lightning Charges. Deals lighting damage from Throwing: Lightning Damage , granting an additional 2 Lightning Charges. Deals damage from Elemental Cleaver , granting an additional 2 Lightning Charges. When combined altogether, a total of 6 Lightning Charges have been granted by a single attack.

## Cull the Weak
- **来源**: [Cull the Weak](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Cull_the_Weak)
- **分类**: Passive_features

For the passive feature used by Kar'niss, see Cull the Weak (Drider) . Cull the Weak is a toggleable passive feature and Illithid Power . When a character with this passive active brings a creature down to fewer Hit Points than the character's number of evolved Illithid Powers, the creature dies and all nearby creatures take 1~4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. Description When you bring a creature down to fewer hit points than your number of evolved illithid powers, it dies and all nearby creatures take 1~4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic damage. Details Toggleable How to learn Used by creatures: Full-illithid Other ways to learn: Unlock from the Illithid Power skill tree with a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen after obtaining the following: Concentrated Blast Notes Although the description says "all nearby creatures", the damage actually only applies to enemies. As this inevitably kills the creature that triggers it, this passive and Non-Lethal Attacks are mutually exclusive. Enabling either one will disable the other automatically. This can be triggered multiple times on a single creature in rapid succession, if the effect that brings it below the hit point threshold has multiple distinct sources of damage (e.g. if the creature is hit by more than one dart from a single casting of Magic Missile ). On kill effects like Elixir of Bloodlust and The Deathstalker Mantle will not trigger if killed by this power.
