## Darkveil Precision
- **来源**: [Darkveil Precision](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Darkveil_Precision)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Darkveil Precision is a passive feature that grants a bonus chance to hit while hidden in shadow. Description While obscured in shadow, the wielder has a +1d4 bonus to their ranged weapon attacks . Condition: Darkveil Precision Darkveil Precision As long as it remains obscured, the affected entity has a +1d4 bonus to ranged Attack Rolls . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Least Expected Notes Darkveil Precision, when active, places a condition upon the wielder by the same name which has the following description: "As long as it remains obscured, the affected entity has a +1d4 bonus to ranged Attack Rolls." This may be confusing as it does not specify "ranged weapons" as the passive does, but the 1d4 bonus is indeed limited to ranged weapon attack rolls. Bugs Darkveil Precision is not automatically applied to the wielder when first equipped while already Lightly Obscured or Heavily Obscured . The wielder must first either move to Clear Area and back, or Hide .
## Darkvision
- **来源**: [Darkvision](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Darkvision)
- **分类**: Passive_features

For the Way of the Shadow Monk feature, see Shadow Arts: Darkvision . For the Level 2 spell, see Darkvision (spell) . Darkvision is a passive feature that prevents Disadvantage when attacking creatures in the dark within 12 m (40 ft), or 24 m (80 ft) for Superior Darkvision . Some creatures have darkvision with custom range. Darkvision also affects obscurity mechanics. Description Can see in the dark up to 12 m (40 ft). How to learn Races: Character level 1: Elf , Tiefling , Dwarf , Half-Elf , Forest Gnome , Rock Gnome , and Half-Orc ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Granted by the weapons: Selûne's Spear of Night Notes The actual distance of Darkvision often depends on the creature that has this feature. The values above are the default for playable races. When a hiding creature enters the line of sight of a creature with darkvision, and is within the range of darkvision: Being Lightly Obscured counts as being under Clear Area instead. Being Heavily Obscured counts as being Lightly Obscured instead. The same applies to Superior Darkvision , just with a longer range. Also granted by Sarevok's Horned Helmet and Sunwalker's Gift . More information on Darkvision mechanics and its potential combat implications can be found here . Bugs Normally, a creature gains Advantage when making a ranged attack from within magical Darkness , assuming it can do so via a feature such as Devil's Sight that grants vision in magical darkness. However, if the target of the attack has Darkvision, and the attacker is within the target's Darkvision range, then the attacker gains no advantage. This is despite the fact that Darkvision does not grant vision in magical darkness. Brief preview Can see in the dark up to a certain distance.

## Dazing Smite
- **来源**: [Dazing Smite](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dazing_Smite)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Dazing Smite is a passive feature that dazzles targets you hit with a Smite. Description On a hit infused with one of your Smites , the target must succeed a Constitution Saving Throw or become Dazed . Condition: Dazed Dazed Duration: 2 turns CON Save ( DC  13) Has Disadvantage on Wisdom Saving Throws , can't take Reactions , and loses the Dexterity bonus to their Armour Class . Removed if an ally Helps this creature. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Blackguard's Sword Used by creatures: That Which Guards Notes Dazing Smite will activate when used with the ranged variants of smites when attacking with a ranged weapon. Dazing Smite requires damage to be dealt when attacking with a smite spell, and not simply for a hit to occur. Bugs Dazing Smite will not activate when used with the following smites: Banishing Smite (Melee) when cast at level 6 Blinding Smite when cast at level 4, 5, and 6 Branding Smite (Ranged) when cast at level 4, 5, and 6 Divine Smite (reaction) when cast as an interrupt to a non-smite attack (including the smites mentioned in this list) Staggering Smite when cast at level 5 and 6

## Deadly Derivation
- **来源**: [Deadly Derivation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Deadly_Derivation)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Deadly Derivation is a passive feature that heals the wearer a little when they poison a foe. Description When you Poison a foe, heal yourself for 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Derivation Cloak Notes There are four Poisoned conditions reusing the same icon, which can be confusing. The most general one is Poisoned , and it's the only one considered by this passive. That means there will be no healing via the following similar conditions: Poisoned condition caused by a weapon coated in Basic Poison . But the same item when thrown generates a Poison Cloud , which can cause the correct Poisoned condition, triggering this passive. Poisoned condition caused by drinking or throwing Suspicious Poison . Poisoned condition caused by consuming Spider meat . This passive has great synergy when combined with Poisoner's Gloves and Broodmother's Revenge . Every attack can cause Poisoned , healing the character and refreshing the poison coating.
## Death Burst
- **来源**: [Death Burst](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Death_Burst)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Death Burst is a family of abilities available to mephits that causes them to explode when they die. It has both a passive component that is triggered automatically on death and an active component that lets them manually trigger the explosion, typically dealing twice the damage. Death Burst is available in several different damage types depending on the type of mephit. Fire [ edit section | visual editor ] Action Death Burst Damage: 2~12 2d6 ⁠ Fire Explode in a burst of fire. DEX Save Range: Self Passive Death Burst: Fire When the mephit dies, it explodes in a burst of lava that deals 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage to all creatures within 2 m (7 ft). On a successful save, the creatures still take half damage. This version of Death Burst is available to Magma Mephits . Note that unlike the other versions, the actively triggered explosion does not deal extra damage. Cold [ edit section | visual editor ] Action Death Burst ( ) Damage: 4~24 4d6 ⁠ Cold Explode in a burst of ice that damages all nearby creatures. DEX Save Range: Self Passive Death Burst: Cold When the mephit dies, it explodes in a burst of ice that deals 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Cold damage to all creatures within 2 m (7 ft). On a successful save, the creatures still take half damage. This version of Death Burst is available to Ice Mephits , including those summoned with Conjure Minor Elemental: Ice Mephits . The explosion also creates an Ice surface in the area of effect that can potentially trip anyone caught inside. Force [ edit section | visual editor ] Action Death Burst ( ) Damage: 6~36 4d6 ⁠ Force + 2d6 ⁠ Force Explode in a burst of sticky mud. It dries instantly on any nearby creatures not made of mud,   Restraining and hurting them. DEX Save Range: Self Passive Death Burst: Force When the mephit dies, it explodes with a force that deals 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Force damage to all creatures within 2 m (7 ft). On a successful save, the creatures still take half damage. This version of Death Burst is available to Ancient or Young Mud Mephits . This includes the ones summoned by Conjure Minor Elemental: Mud Mephits . The explosion also creates a Mud surface in the area of effect that impedes movement.

- **分类**: Passive_features

Deepened Pact is a passive feature that grants Warlocks additional bonuses depending on their chosen Pact Boon . Description Pleased with your service, your otherworldly patron added new boons to the terms of your pact. Pact of the Blade Gain an Extra Attack with your pact weapon. Pact of the Chain Find Familiar familiars also gain an extra attack. Pact of the Tome Can cast Animate Dead , Haste , Call Lightning once per long rest. How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Warlock Notes Outside of Honour Mode, the Extra Attack granted to those with Pact of the Blade stacks with other sources of Extra Attack when multiclassing 5 levels into barbarian , fighter , monk , paladin , or ranger , or 6 levels into College of Swords , College of Valour , or Bladesinging . This is the only known way to stack different Extra Attack features, and does not work in Honour Mode. Pact of the Blade also grants an Extra Attack for a Throw or Ranged Attack when wielding the pact weapon. If the Ranged Attack is made first or the character is wielding a ranged weapon when using Throw, then no Extra Attack is granted. Although the description only mentions gaining an Extra Attack with a Pact Weapon , the Hexblade's Hexed Weapon also works. ## Defence
- **来源**: [Defence](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Defence)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Defence is a fighting style passive feature. Description You gain a +1 bonus to Armour Class while wearing armour . How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Fighter Class level 2: Ranger and Paladin Used by creatures: Apostle of Myrkul , Har'rak , Ketheric Thorm , Losiir , Minsc , Minthara , Skoona , Varanna Sunblossom , Zevlor , Zombie Minthara Notes This effect is active while wearing anything marked as light, medium, or heavy armour in any equipment slot. This fighting style is generally considered weaker than other, more specialized fighting styles such as Duelling or Archery . However, it is useful for Champion Fighters who can choose a second fighting style. Since the benefit of Great Weapon Fighting becomes less effective when paired with Savage Attacker or Brace (Melee) , a warrior using two-handed weapons may instead want to take Defence. Bugs For Helldusk Armour and Elven Chain , both of which lack a proficiency group, Defence does not consider them as armour proper. To work around this, these items have a hidden passive which grants +1 AC if the wearer has the Defence passive. However, if the wearer also has another piece of armour equipped which has a proficiency group, the normal +1 AC from Defence is additionally applied, for a total of +2 AC. ## Defensive Attack (passive feature)
- **来源**: [Defensive Attack (passive feature)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Defensive_Attack_(passive_feature))
- **分类**: Passive_features

This article is about the passive feature. For the corresponding reaction, see Defensive Attack . Defensive Attack is a passive feature that lets the wielder of Defender Greataxe temporarily sacrifices one Enchantment level from the axe to gain +1 bonus AC and saving throws. This choice is given when making the first attack with the axe in a round. Description When making your first attack of the round, you can reduce this weapon's enchantment by 1 to increase your Armour Class and Saving Throw bonus by 1. Grants: Defensive Attack Condition: Defensive Stance Defensive Stance Duration: 1 turn You have +1 bonus to Armour Class and Saving Throws . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Defender Greataxe Notes This provided reaction is only triggered when making the first attack with Defender Greataxe in a round. Subsequent attacks do not give an opportunity to activate this action. The -1 penalty to attack rolls from Defensive Attack will be applied to the attack that triggers the reaction. The confirmation prompt for the reaction will show the attack roll and AC of the target so you can decline the reaction if it would turn a hit into a miss.

- **分类**: Passive_features

Demonspirit Aura is a toggleable passive feature granted by the Abyss Beckoners . They impart damage resistance to the wearer's summons at the risk of driving them mad . Description The wearer's summoned creatures have resistance to all damage except ⁠ Psychic damage. At the start of the summoned creatures turn, it must succeed a Wisdom Saving Throw or be driven Mad . Details Toggleable Condition: Demonspirit Aura Demonspirit Aura Affected entity's summoned creature has Resistance to all damage except ⁠ Psychic . At the start of the summoned creature's turn, it must succeed a Wisdom Saving Throw or be driven Mad . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Abyss Beckoners Notes Though not stated ingame, the aura is visible as a red circle; it emanates from the wearer with a AoE: 9 m (30 ft) Radius. Summoned creatures which are otherwise immune to Charmed (such as Calmed or Aura of Devotion ) cannot go mad .

## Devil's Sight
- **来源**: [Devil's Sight](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Devil's_Sight)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Devil's Sight is an Eldritch Invocation from the Warlock class. It allows the wearer to see through both natural and magical darkness. Description You can see normally in darkness, both magical and non-magical, to a distance of 24 m (80 ft). Details UID DevilsSight How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Warlock Used by creatures: Conjured Imp , Cruor , Cursed Imp , Gilded Imp , Helsik , Hoarding Merregon , Lesser Imp , Merregon Legionnaire , Pactsplitter , Raphael , Sceleritas Fel , Tska'an , Vengeful Imp , Vengeful Merregon , Yurgir Notes Devil's Sight negates most effects of magical darkness clouds at all ranges. Only the obscuration effect remains past 24 m (80 ft). Devil's Sight grants immunity to being Blinded by Darkness , but not other sources, such as Blindness , Fog Cloud , or Hunger of Hadar . The in-game tooltip for being Blinded by Darkness shows a duration of " Whilst on surface ", while for Blindness and Hunger of Hadar it shows " Until long rest ". Fog is treated as magical darkness for the purposes of this feature. Creatures with Devil's Sight treat Fog and other magical darkness as lightly obscured areas. For more information on Darkvision mechanics and its potential combat implications, see Darkvision mechanics . Brief preview Can see in the dark, including magical darkness, up to 24 m (80 ft). v t e Warlock Subclasses The Archfey The Fiend The Great Old One The Hexblade Pact Boon Pact of the Chain Pact of the Blade Pact of the Tome Eldritch Invocations Agonising Blast Armour of Shadows Beast Speech Beguiling Influence Book of Ancient Secrets Devil's Sight Dreadful Word Fiendish Vigour Lifedrinker Mask of Many Faces Minions of Chaos Mire the Mind One with Shadows Otherworldly Leap Repelling Blast Sculptor of Flesh Sign of Ill Omen Thief of Five Fates Whispers of the Grave Other class features Accursed Spectre Armour of Hexes Beguiling Defences Bind Hexed Weapon Dark One's Blessing Dark One's Own Luck Entropic Ward Fey Presence Fiendish Resilience Deepened Pact Hex Warrior Hexblade's Curse Misty Escape Mortal Reminder Mystic Arcanum Spells Thought Shield: Psychic Reflection Thought Shield: Psychic Resistance

## Displacement
- **来源**: [Displacement](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Displacement)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Displacement is a passive feature that makes it difficult for enemies to hit the wearer in combat. Description At the beginning of the wearer's turn, the cloak activates, granting enemies Disadvantage on Attack Rolls that target the wearer. This effect lasts until the wearer takes damage. Condition: Displaced Displaced Duration: 2 turns Until you take damage, foes have Disadvantage on Attack Rolls against you. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Cloak of Displacement Bugs Displaced is not removed by anything the game does not consider to be a hit, even if it deals damage. This includes the following: A successful save against a damage dealing spell, even when the spell still deals half damage on a save. Tenacity damage.
## Divine Allegiance
- **来源**: [Divine Allegiance](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Divine_Allegiance)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Divine Allegiance is a passive feature available to Oath of the Crown paladins which allows them to heal an adjacent ally when they take damage, at the cost of taking damage themselves. Description When an ally within 1.5 m (5 ft) of you takes damage, you can use your Reaction to magically substitute your own health for your ally's, healing them by 2 × (Paladin level) ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points at the cost of taking 2 × (Paladin level) ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage yourself. How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Oath of the Crown Notes Taken ⁠ ⁠ Radiant damage can be reduced by resistance and damage reduction. Bugs Some damage riders such as Lightning Charges and radiant damage from the Callous Glow Ring increase the self-damage. ## Dolor Amarus (passive feature)
- **来源**: [Dolor Amarus (passive feature)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dolor_Amarus_(passive_feature))
- **分类**: Passive_features

Dolor Amarus is a passive feature that deals extra damage when a weapon attack lands a critical hit. Description When you land a Critical Hit with a weapon or unarmed attack, [ See: Bugs ] it deals an additional 7 damage. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Dolor Amarus Vicious Battleaxe Vicious Shortbow Vicious Shortsword   (inaccessible) Used by creatures: Dolor Notes Dolor Amarus applies to all weapon attacks while a weapon with the feature is equipped, and it can be activated multiple times if multiple weapons with the passive are equipped. For example, if both Dolor Amarus daggers are equipped – or one dagger and the Vicious Battleaxe on a character with Dual Wielder – together with the Vicious Shortbow , when the wielder lands a critical hit, then +21 damage will be added, instead of +7. Dolor Amarus also stacks on multiple damage riders, which could potentially lead to massive bonuses from different damage sources. The name dolor amarus is Latin for "harsh suffering" or "bitter sorrow". Bugs Despite the description, Dolor Amarus does not deal an additional 7 damage on unarmed attack critical hits (including Throw attacks).

## Draconic Resilience
- **来源**: [Draconic Resilience](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Draconic_Resilience)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Draconic Resilience is a Draconic Bloodline Sorcerer passive feature that raises the Sorcerer 's base Armour Class to 13 when not wearing armour. Description Dragon-like scales cover parts of your skin. When you aren't wearing armour, your base Armour Class is 13. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Draconic Bloodline Used by creatures: Aelis Siryasius , Havkelaag , Klaus Notes The normal base Armour Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier , while this changes it to 13 + Dexterity modifier . You will still get bonuses from other sources that don't change your base armour class like +1 AC robes , Bracers of Defence , Shield of Faith , etc. Helmets , gloves and footwear marked as Light Armour , Medium Armour or Heavy Armour count as armour, and will prevent Draconic Resilience from working. Draconic Resilience works while wearing a Shield . Mage Armour , Draconic Resilience , Unarmoured Defence , Unarmoured Defence and Barkskin all change your base armour class and therefore does not stack. If you have multiple of these you will only get the benefit of the one that gives the most Armour Class . Draconic Resilience can work while in Wild Shape as long as you have no armour equipped in any slot before transforming. This effect only works on forms with a base Armour Class of less than 13. Brief preview Without armour, base Armour Class is 13. v t e Sorcerer Subclasses Draconic Bloodline Shadow Magic Storm Sorcery Wild Magic Metamagic Careful Spell Distant Spell Extended Spell Twinned Spell Heightened Spell Quickened Spell Subtle Spell Draconic Ancestry Red Black Blue White Green Gold Silver Bronze Copper Brass Heart of the Storm Lightning Thunder Resistance Other class features Bend Luck Controlled Chaos Create Spell Slot Create Sorcery Points Draconic Resilience Elemental Affinity: Damage Elemental Affinity: Resistance Eyes of the Dark Eyes of the Dark: Darkness Fly Hound of Ill Omen Shadow Walk Storm's Fury Strength of the Grave Tempestuous Magic Tides of Chaos Wild Magic Spells

## Dreadful Hewer
- **来源**: [Dreadful Hewer](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dreadful_Hewer)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Dreadful Hewer is a passive feature that makes it difficult for enemies to resist your fearful abilities. Description Your foes have Disadvantage on Saving Throws to resist your spells or actions that inflict Fear . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Shield of the Undevout Used by creatures: That Which Guards Bugs Despite misleading tooltips, Dreadful Hewer provides Disadvantage on target's Saving Throws for many effects applying Fearful or Frightened conditions. The passive affects Wrathful Smite , Fear , Menacing Attack (Melee) (and its variants), Dissonant Whispers , Dreadful Aspect , Fey Presence: Disturbing , and Ray of Fear . The passive does not affect Mortal Reminder , Intimidating Presence , Eyebite: Panicked , Blood-Curdling Emission , Command: Flee , Bolt of Celestial Light , and Immolating Gaze . The passive also provides Disadvantage against some non-expected abilities, namely Fey Presence: Beguiling .

## Dual Wielder
- **来源**: [Dual Wielder](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Dual_Wielder)
- **分类**: Passive_features

See also: Dual Wielder: Bonus Armour Class Dual Wielder is a passive feature granted by the Dual Wielder feat . It allows characters to dual wield weapons that are not two-handed even if they aren't Light . Description You can use Two-Weapon Fighting even if the weapons you are wielding aren't Light . You cannot dual wield Two-Handed weapons. How to learn Granted by the feats: Dual Wielder (Feat) Used by creatures: Allandra Grey , Antinia , Arcagh , Elenna Thrinn , Kar'niss , Minthara , Qora , Rycke , Skoona , Zombie Minthara Notes Normally, a character can only dual wield two weapons with the Light property. This feat allows them to dual wield One-Handed and Versatile weapons as well. Prior to Patch #7 , the tooltip stated player characters could not dual wield Heavy weapons, a property that was never implemented in the game. During level up, the selected character will always have only one weapon visible at their back, even if two are equipped. Brief preview Can use Two-Weapon Fighting with any weapons that aren't Two-Handed .

## Duelling
- **来源**: [Duelling](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Duelling)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Duelling is a fighting style passive feature. Description When you are wielding a melee weapon that is not Two-Handed in one hand, and no weapon in the other, you deal an additional 2 damage with that weapon. You can carry a shield in your free hand and still gain this bonus. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Fighter Class level 2: Ranger and Paladin Class level 3: College of Swords Class level 10: Champion Used by creatures: Bareki , Esther , Pollo the Muscle , Robust Guardian Notes This passive adds its damage to Throw attacks with Thrown weapons that hit while wielding a qualifying weapon with the melee weapon set selected. The Thrown weapon cannot be equipped prior to Throwing it, unless it is dual wielded and in the main hand. If the Thrown weapon is in the off-hand, it does not receive the bonus damage unless no ranged weapon is equipped. The bonus damage is added even if the Thrown weapon is Two-Handed . This feature is tedious to use when Throwing homing weapons , as the weapon always returns to the off-hand when being dual wielded. Gaining the bonus damage of Duelling requires a character to unequip the homing weapon after each Throw and then switch back to their melee weapon set before Throwing it again. Prior to Patch 8, the description implied that Versatile weapons could not be used to gain the bonus damage. Bugs A thrown Duelling weapon does not receive any additional damage unless it possesses the Thrown weapon property. v t e Fighter Subclasses Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight ## Duelling Gloves
- **来源**: [Duelling Gloves](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Duelling_Gloves)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Duelling Gloves is a passive feature that grants a bonus to single handed melee weapons. Description While only holding one weapon in your main hand and nothing in your free hand, gain a +2 bonus to melee weapon Attack Rolls . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gloves of The Duellist Notes The description of effect is misleading. Like the Duelling fighting style, the bonus from Duelling Gloves remains active even if the wearer has a shield in their offhand, as long as they do not have a weapon in their offhand. It also deactivates if the wearer uses a versatile weapon alone (in two-hand mode), but remains active if they wield a versatile weapon alongside a shield.

Eldritch Strike is an Eldritch Knight Fighter passive feature. This allows the Fighter to force a creature to have Disadvantage on its next Saving Throw by a mere weapon attack. Description When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, it has Disadvantage on its next Saving Throw against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn. Condition: Stricken with Eldritch Inertia Stricken with Eldritch Inertia Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has Disadvantage on its next Saving Throw against a spell cast by the source of the condition. How to learn Classes: Class level 10: Eldritch Knight Bugs Despite the description stating it affects the "next spell", this condition affects all saving throws caused by the Eldritch Knight until it expires. This applies also to non-spell sources such as weapon actions , weapon passives like Blood-Curdling Emission , illithid powers , etc. v t e Fighter Subclasses Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Fighting Styles Archery Defence Duelling Great Weapon Fighting Protection Two-Weapon Fighting Manoeuvres Commander's Strike Disarming Attack Distracting Strike Evasive Footwork Feinting Attack Goading Attack Manoeuvring Attack Menacing Attack Precision Attack Pushing Attack Rally Riposte Sweeping Attack Trip Attack Arcane Shots Banishing Arrow Beguiling Arrow Bursting Arrow Enfeebling Arrow Grasping Arrow Piercing Arrow Seeking Arrow Shadow Arrow Other class features Action Surge Curving Shot Eldritch Strike Extra Attack Improved Critical Hit Improved Extra Attack Improved Combat Superiority Indomitable Magic Arrow Remarkable Athlete: Jump Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency Second Wind War Magic Weapon Bond

## Elemental Augmentation
- **来源**: [Elemental Augmentation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elemental_Augmentation)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Elemental Augmentation is a passive feature which adds damage to the caster's elemental cantrips. Description When one of your cantrips deals ⁠ Acid , ⁠ Cold , ⁠ Fire , ⁠ Lightning , or ⁠ Thunder damage, add your Spellcasting Modifier to the damage dealt. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Necklace of Elemental Augmentation Notes Elemental Augmentation functions by checking the cantrip being cast for a specific DamageType flag (such as ⁠ Fire or ⁠ Lightning ) rather than the actual damage type listed for the cantrip or the damage type done by the cantrip when hitting a target. This means that 'added' damage – such as that from Lightning Charges – does not trigger the necklace's effect, because these external bonuses lack the necessary flags. Consequently, the necklace only works with cantrips which natively deal the correct damage types, and does not work with cantrips which lack a DamageType flag, like Booming Blade . Elemental Augmentation stacks with the Elemental Affinity: Damage feature for most Draconic Bloodline Sorcerers (though not those with green dragon ancestry, which use Poison damage). In this case, the Charisma modifier will be added to the damage of the relevant cantrips twice. When multiclassing, Elemental Augmentation uses the spellcasting ability modifier of the last class added, not necessarily the spellcasting ability of the class which granted the cantrip. The minimum additional damage is 1, even if the character's spellcasting ability modifier is 0 or negative. Hellflame Cleave deals two instances of damage which both receive the bonus damage from Elemental Augmentation. The following cantrips receive bonus damage from Elemental Augmentation: Name Level Cast time Duration Range/Area Attack/Save Damage/Effect Acid Splash C - 18 m / 60ft 2m / 7ft (Radius) DEX Save 1d6 ⁠ Acid Activate Witch Bolt C - 30 m / 100ft - 1d12 ⁠ Lightning Ensnaring Shock C 4 turns 18 m / 60 ft DEX Save 1d4 ⁠ Lightning Fire Bolt C - 18 m / 60ft Attack Roll 1d10 ⁠ Fire Firebolt? C - 18 m / 60ft Attack Roll 1d10 ⁠ Fire Hellflame Cleave C 1 turn 3m / 10ft (Cone) DEX Save Normal weapon damage 2d6 ⁠ Fire Produce Flame C Long Rest Self - 1d8 ⁠ Fire Produce Flame: Hurl C - 9 m / 30ft Attack Roll 1d8 ⁠ Fire Ray of Frost C 1 turn 18 m / 60ft Attack Roll 1d8 ⁠ Cold Rays of Fire (Cantrip) C - 18 m / 60 ft Attack Roll 3d6 ⁠ Fire 3d6 ⁠ Fire 3d6 ⁠ Fire Shocking Grasp C 1 turn 1.5 m / 5 ft Attack Roll 1d8 ⁠ Lightning
## Elemental Infusion
- **来源**: [Elemental Infusion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Elemental_Infusion)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Elemental Infusion is a passive feature that adds elemental damage to the wearer's next weapon attack, after dealing elemental damage with a spell. Description When you deal ⁠ Acid , ⁠ Cold , ⁠ Fire , ⁠ Lightning , or ⁠ Thunder damage using a Spell or a Cantrip , that element infuses your weapon. Until the end of your next turn, you deal an additional 1d4 damage of that element on your first successful weapon attack. Details UID MAG_ElementalGish_ElementalInfusion_Ring_Passive How to learn Granted by the equipment: Ring of Elemental Infusion Used by creatures: Umr'a'ac Notes Elemental Infusion can apply its damage bonus multiple times to a single weapon attack. The individual elemental damage boost conditions all share the same StackID with each other, meaning only one may be active on a character at a time. However, the conditions also use a StackType of Overwrite , meaning the last condition applied from the passive is the condition that will actually affect the wearer's next weapon attack. Due to the way the passive is written, this causes a priority effect where the conditions follow this order of priority (with the later conditions overwriting the earlier conditions): Acid Infusion < Cold Infusion < Fire Infusion < Lightning Infusion < Thunder Infusion This means that if a character attacks an enemy with a spell that deals primarily Fire damage, but is also dealing bonus Thunder damage, the character will be left with Thunder Infusion. Condition: Acid Infusion [ edit section | visual editor ] Acid Infusion Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Acid the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Cold Infusion [ edit section | visual editor ] Cold Infusion Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Cold the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Fire Infusion [ edit section | visual editor ] Fire Infusion Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Lightning Infusion [ edit section | visual editor ] Lightning Infusion Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Lightning the next time it deals damage with a weapon. Condition: Thunder Infusion [ edit section | visual editor ] Thunder Infusion Duration: 2 turns The affected entity deals an additional 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder the next time it deals damage with a weapon.

## Empowered Evocation
- **来源**: [Empowered Evocation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Empowered_Evocation)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Empowered Evocation is an Evocation School Wizard passive feature which increases the damage of the caster's Evocation spells by their Intelligence modifier. Description Your grasp of Evocation magic has tightened, and you can add your Intelligence Modifier to damage rolls with any Evocation spells. How to learn Classes: Class level 10: Evocation School Used by creatures: Elminster , Illithid Arcanist , Lorroakan , Rolan Notes This damage bonus applies to each instance of a spell's damage, increasing the potency of spells such as Magic Missile , Scorching Ray , and Curriculum of Strategy: Artistry of War . This damage bonus applies to all Evocation spells , even if the spell was not learned via the Wizard class. For example, casting Burning Hands learned via the Sorcerer class still adds the caster's Intelligence Modifier to the damage, despite using the caster's Charisma Modifier for its Spell Save DC. Because this passive works with all spells and not just "leveled spells", the damage bonus applies to damage-dealing Evocation Cantrips as well, such as Fire Bolt , Shocking Grasp , and Eldritch Blast . In the case of Eldritch Blast, the caster's Intelligence Modifier is added to each beam. ## Evasion
- **来源**: [Evasion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Evasion)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Evasion is a Monk and Rogue passive feature that lets them evade area of effect damage which require Dexterity Saving Throws [ See Notes ] , reducing or entirely negating the damage. Description Your agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain spells. When a spell or effect would deal half damage on a successful Dexterity Saving Throw , it deals no damage if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail. How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Monk and Rogue Used by creatures: Addled Frog , Assassin's Folly , Barnz , Bugthimble , Clotilde , Deera , Dhoria , Displacer beast , Dolor , Earspoon , Eglantine , Elliot , Farlin , Fishbait Arno , Flo-Flo , Friol , Gordis , Gremishka , Gruntman , Hiila , Ironhand Grenadier , Kobold Inventor , Kobold Looter , Kobold Scout , Koll (kobold) , Kuo-toa (creature) , Lady Lockjaw , Liya , Mask of Terror (The Blushing Mermaid) , Metamage Persecutor , Nessa , Nine-Fingers Keene , Ogga , Onilla , Orin , Popper , Proselyte of Mahkloompah , Quenora Grisly , Roah Moonglow , Rocky , Shadow-Cursed Raven , Shadow-Whiskers , Shrev , Skoan , Snapbone , Snirr , Terse Torvalt , Vagga , Varneela , Velki , Zerillis , Zhent Elf , Zhent Half-Elven , Zhentmodeus , Zina Notes Refer to this table for a comprehensive list of actions that can be evaded. Despite the description of this feature, it does not strictly matter whether an action has a Dexterity saving throw or whether it is a spell. As a rule of thumb, explosions which involve a Dexterity saving throw can be evaded (e.g. Fireball but not Sacred Flame which uses a Dexterity saving throw but is single target). However, this is not true of every such explosion and there are actions without Dexterity saving throws which can also be evaded. This does not do anything to mitigate any additional non-damaging effects that the triggering spell/effect might apply. ## Executioner
- **来源**: [Executioner](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Executioner)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Executioner is a passive feature that lets the wearer critical hit the next target after getting a kill. Description When you kill a creature, your next Attack Roll will be a Critical Hit . Once spent, this effect refreshes after a Long Rest . Details Recharge: Long rest Condition: Executioner Executioner Spurred on by bloodlust. Next Attack Roll will be a Critical Hit . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Killer's Sweetheart Notes After a creature is killed, the Executioner critical hit can be set to 'Ask' or disabled entirely in the Reactions tab , allowing it to be saved for later. Using it does not consume a Reaction resource . The automatic critical hit from Executioner can be applied to every target hit by a single AOE attack, such as Whirlwind Attack or Razor Gale . Bugs Despite the tooltip suggesting otherwise, Executioner only applies to weapon attack rolls. When using weapon specific abilities that impose a saving throw such as Pushing Attack (Melee) and Lacerate , Executioner attempts to apply its 'Natural 20' effect to the enemy's saving throw as well as the character's attack. This creates a risk of wasting the Executioner condition to help the enemy. If the Executioner reaction is set to 'Automatic': the game forces the character's attack roll to a 20 (a Critical Hit) but also forces the target’s Saving Throw to a 20. This grants the enemy a high probability of resisting the secondary effect (e.g., they take the damage but are not pushed). If the Executioner reaction is set to 'Ask': The game triggers two separate prompts: First Prompt : asks to turn the character's attack roll into a 20. (Recommend: Yes ) Second Prompt: asks to turn the enemy's Saving Throw into a 20. (Recommend: No ) If the character accepts the second prompt, the Executioner condition is consumed, and the enemy receives a large bonus to their save. Note: While Saving Throws do not technically 'critically succeed' on a 20, the high roll often results in the enemy resisting the effect. Wasted Charges : due to a scripting error, Executioner fails to check if the attacking character has already rolled a Natural 20 normally. If the character lands a critical hit on their own, the reaction can still trigger (and be consumed) if they either accept the reaction prompt or have it set to 'Automatic'.

## Expert Divination
- **来源**: [Expert Divination](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Expert_Divination)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Expert Divination is a Divination School Wizard passive feature which grants an additional Portent Die and allows its user to fulfill prophecies to restore any spent Portent Dice each short rest. These prophecies typically entail casting a spell from a specific school or dealing a specific type of damage. Description You gain an additional Portent Die . When taking a Short Rest you receive a set of Prophecies . Complete them to regain missing Portent Dice. How to learn Classes: Class level 6: Divination School Notes This feature increases a wizard's maximum number of Portent Dice to 3. [ See: Bugs ] After short resting, the user receives a random prophecy for each spent Portent Die. Fulfilling this prophecy restores a die with a new, random value. [ See: Bugs ] Altogether, Expert Divination increases the number of Portent Dice a wizard can use from 2 per long rest up to 3 per short rest. The different possible prophecies are: Deal a specific damage type: Prophecy: Burn After Reading Prophecy: Frosty Reception Prophecy: Shocking Revelation Prophecy: Thunderous Applause Prophecy: Forceful Insistence Prophecy: Grave Fate Prophecy: Venomous Words Prophecy: Headache Prophecy: Holy Epiphany Prophecy: Melting Pot Prophecy: A Blunt Tool Prophecy: A Little Prick Prophecy: Cutting Edge Cast a spell from a specific school : Prophecy: Guarded Prophecy: A Little Help Prophecy: Predictable Prophecy: Spellbinding Prophecy: Evocative Prophecy: Feign Surprise Prophecy: Dead Right Prophecy: Changes Prophecy: Well-Read : Learn or cast a spell using a scroll . Prophecy: Delivering Alms : Help an ally. [ See: Bugs ] Prophecy: Reap Rewards : Kill an enemy. Bugs Prophecy: Delivering Alms can never be completed because it references a passive which does not exist in the game code. Divination Wizards can only have one die per value, yet the game only ensures unique values for Portent Dice granted after long rests. This means a fulfilled Prophecy might result in no extra die if a wizard already has a die with the same value. For example, a wizard with 2 remaining Portent Dice has a 10% chance of not getting a new die, while a wizard with a single remaining die has a 5% chance. Casting area of effect spells while not in turn-based mode can make prophecies activated by dealing a certain damage type trigger multiple times, resulting in multiple new Portent Dice, often overcoming the limit of 3. For example, casting a Fireball with Lightning Charges against a group of five enemies while outside of combat and having both Prophecy: Burn After Reading and Prophecy: Shocking Revelation results in up to 10 new Portent Dice for a Divination Wizard, as both prophecies are triggered once per enemy. v t e Wizard Subclasses Abjuration School Bladesinging Conjuration School Divination School Enchantment School Evocation School Illusion School Necromancy School Transmutation School Spells Abjuration Conjuration Divination Enchantment Evocation Illusion Necromancy Transmutation Other class features Arcane Recovery Arcane Ward Benign Transposition: Teleport Bladesong Empowered Evocation Experimental Alchemy Expert Divination Extra Attack Focused Conjuration Grim Harvest Hypnotic Gaze Illusory Self Improved Abjuration Improved Minor Illusion Instinctive Charm Inured to Undeath Minor Conjuration: Create Water Portent Potent Cantrip Projected Ward Sculpt Spells See Invisibility Shapechanger Song of Defence Split Enchantment Third Eye: Darkvision Third Eye: See Invisibility Training in War and Song Transmuter's Stone Undead Thralls Animate Dead Additional Undead Better Summons

## Extra Attack
- **来源**: [Extra Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Extra_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

See also the Warlock version Deepened Pact Extra Attack is a passive feature that allows you to make an additional attack when making an Attack Action . Description You can make an additional free attack after making an unarmed or weapon attack. How to learn Classes: Class level 5: Barbarian , Fighter , Monk , Paladin , and Ranger Class level 6: College of Swords , College of Valour , and Bladesinging Notes The initial attack needs to cost an Action for Extra Attack to trigger; Therefore Bonus Actions (like Off-hand Attack , Flurry of Blows , Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack , Eldritch Knight 's War Magic ) or Reactions (like Opportunity Attack or Riposte ) do not qualify, but Greater Kushigo Counter can trigger extra attack if it is triggered on players turn via an opportunity attack. Any attack that uses a weapon, unarmed, or throwing attack roll can trigger, and be affected by Extra Attack. There are also some other abilities that are explicitly coded to work: [ 1 ] Commander's Strike [ 1 ] Bufotoxin [ 1 ] Smokepowder Arrow [ 1 ] Arcane Shot: Seeking Arrow [ 1 ] Arcane Shot: Piercing Arrow [ 1 ] Once Extra Attack is triggered all affected attacks will glow white and the action point will be removed from their cost. Other resources like bonus actions or class resources will stay. Additional instances of Extra Attack do not stack; a multiclassed Ranger and Fighter with 5+ Levels in each will still only have 1 Extra Attack. Deepened Pact ( Pact of the Blade )'s Extra Attack does stack, but not in Honour mode . Level 11 Fighters gain an improved version of this ability , allowing for 2 Extra Attacks per trigger. Some other Classes have their own version of Extra Attack; Pact of the Blade Warlock's Deepened Pact at level 5 applies only to attacks made with the pact weapon. Pact of the Chain Warlock's Deepened Pact at level 5 enables an extra attack for their familiar. Druid's Wild Strike and Improved Wild Strike at Level 5 and 10. Beast Master Ranger's Bestial Fury at level 11 enables an extra attack for their companion. An attack made with the action gained from Action Surge can trigger Extra Attack, regardless of difficulty. Druids lose Wild Strike's extra attacks if transformed to humanoid form and then back to some animal form. Non-Honour mode The notes below are changed to specifically not work in the Honour mode difficulty. They still work in Explorer , Balanced and Tactician : Warlock's Pact of the Blade Deepened Pact does stack with other sources. Sources of additional actions like Hastened and Elixir of Bloodlust can also have Extra Attack apply. Only Action Surge works in honour mode. For example, a Hastened Level 11 Fighter with Elixir of Bloodlust on Tactician difficulty or below could attack 6 times, then an additional 3 times if they got a kill that round. Brief preview Can make an additional attack after an unarmed or weapon attack. ## Fiery Return
- **来源**: [Fiery Return](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fiery_Return)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Fiery Return is a passive feature that grants extra bonus actions when you deal fire damage with a leveled spell. Description When you deal ⁠ Fire damage with a levelled spell, you Burn yourself and gain an additional Bonus Action this round. Condition: Extra Bonus Action Extra Bonus Action Duration: 1 turn Grants an additional Bonus Action on this turn. Condition: Burning Burning Duration: 2 turns Takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Can be removed with the Help action, using a Healing Potion or gaining Wet . Immune from if Wet . Dip action can be used on Burning characters or objects. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Circlet of Fire   (unobtainable) Pyroquickness Hat Notes The conditions for activating Fiery Return are to deal fire damage with a non-cantrip spell or a melee spell attack roll. Attacks with a Flame Blade conjured by the druid spell count as melee spell attacks, so they trigger Fiery Return. However, this is not true of a Flame Blade summoned by a mephistopheles tiefling's racial feature or a permanent Flame Blade acquired through the exploit described here . The Daredevil Gloves can turn ranged spell attacks into melee spell attacks, so cantrips like Fire Bolt can trigger Fiery Return when paired with the gloves. Bugs If Fiery Return is triggered with a Bonus Action (for example, with Metamagic: Quickened Spell ), the extra bonus action granted by this passive is wasted and consumed immediately. Hellcrawler , a class action granted by the Helldusk Boots , triggers Fiery Return, essentially negating the bonus action cost. Searing Smite does not trigger Fiery Return.

## Fly Trap
- **来源**: [Fly Trap](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Fly_Trap)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Fly Trap is a passive feature that can prevent a target from moving. Description Chance to Ensnare target if it is not a plant or a beast. Condition: Ensnared (Ensnaring Strike) Ensnared Duration: 2 turns STR Save ( DC  12) Cannot move and takes 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage per turn. Attack Rolls against the creature have Advantage , while the creature's Attack Rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws have Disadvantage . Remove when Helped . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Nature's Snare Notes In addition to the combat round, Ensnare also loses a turn of duration at the beginning of the target's turn. Therefore, Fly Trap can prevent an opponent from moving for one turn at most. Piercing damage from Ensnare is applied each turn regardless of whether the save fails or succeeds. There are three different kinds saves: The first is when the condition is applied. The DC for this is 12. The second is at the beginning of the victim's first turn after receiving the condition. The DC for this is Spell save DC. The condition ends if save succeeds. The third is at the beginning of the possible second turn, but this one is redundant, because the condition always ends at the start of the second round (see bugs below) regardless of whether the save fails or succeeds. The DC for this is Spell save DC. The Sharpened Snare passive feature from Sharpened Snare Cuirass affects the second and third save but not the first one.

## Force Absorption
- **来源**: [Force Absorption](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Force_Absorption)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Force Absorption is a passive feature that increases your defenses as you get hit. Description Gain 2 turns of Force Conduit when taking ⁠ Slashing , ⁠ Piercing , or ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. Condition: Force Conduit Force Conduit Duration: 2 turns ⁠ Bludgeoning , ⁠ Piercing , and ⁠ Slashing damage against the affected entity is reduced by 1 per turn remaining. If the entity takes damage while it has 5 or more turns remaining, it deals 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Force DRS damage in a 6 m (20 ft) radius. Maximum Duration: 7 turns. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Rippling Force Mail Notes Force Absorption adds 2 turns as long as at least 1 HP is reduced from ⁠ Slashing , ⁠ Piercing , or ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. It won't add turns if the received damage is reduced to zero due to damage reduction effects (like Force Conduit or Heavy Armour Master ) Force Absorption also adds 2 turns from damage received via fall damage, Warding Bond or self damage effects (e.g Ritual Dagger or Ritual Axe abilities), as long as at least 1 HP is reduced. A character with this passive won't have all the the charges consumed when Force Conduit 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Force area damage is triggered. As the effect happens due to a melee attack, the passive will stack 2 turns again.

## Freecast
- **来源**: [Freecast](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Freecast)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Freecast is a toggleable passive feature and a power available to Partial-Illithids . It allows them to bypass the normal expenditure of spell slots, charges or other similar resource costs for their next chosen Action , once per Long Rest . Description You have discovered a marvellous adaptability within yourself. Spell slots, charges, and similar resource costs for your next action or spell are removed. Refreshes after a Long Rest . Details Recharge: Long rest Toggleable How to learn Other ways to learn: After becoming a Partial-Illithid , unlock from the illithid power skill tree with a Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen after obtaining one of the following: Shield of Thralls Mind Sanctuary Notes If an action takes more than one type of resource (e.g., Metamagic: Quickened Spell with any spell that is not a cantrip), both costs are removed. Prior to Patch 6 , this feature did not remove Channel Oath Charge costs. Arcane Arrow , Bladesong Power , Cosmic Omen , Fungal Infestation Charge , Star Map , and Writhing Current action costs are not affected by Freecast. Bugs Freecast can be easily reset by having another character apply a condition (such as Guidance or Aura of Protection ) on the character seeking to (re)use Freecast. Freecast becomes disabled when equipping or unequipping a weapon from the ranged weapon slot. It can be re-enabled by re-equipping a melee weapon.

## Godswill
- **来源**: [Godswill](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Godswill)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Godswill is a passive feature that boots the user's ability to channel their god's power. Description You gain an additional use of Channel Divinity Charge . Once used, it is restored upon taking a Long Rest . [ See: Bugs ] How to learn Granted by the equipment: Amulet of the Devout Bugs Contrary to the in-game description, the additional Channel Divinity Charge granted by Godswill restores on a short rest . However if the extra charge is expended and the amulet is unequipped, the extra charge does not reappear if re-equipped before a long rest ; at this point it cannot be restored with a short rest. The additional Channel Divinity Charge does not incur the amulet's once-per-rest cooldown if spent on Destructive Wrath , Guided Strike , Touch of Death , or War God's Blessing . If spent in this manner, simply unequipping and reequipping the amulet restores the Channel Divinity Charge.

## Great Weapon Fighting
- **来源**: [Great Weapon Fighting](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Great_Weapon_Fighting)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Great Weapon Fighting is a Fighting Style passive feature. Description When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack with a Two-Handed melee weapon, that die is rerolled once. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Fighter Class level 2: Paladin Used by creatures: Arden , Arensen , Azari , Baretha , Bella (Bloomridge Park) , Bennel , Beorn Wunterbrood , Bradi'ith , Brandella , Brelal'reth , Brinn , Broadhorn , Ch'guth , Corlos , Crosse , Dead Whitburn Servant , Dor'il , Dresten , Duddamoor , Ebber , Elda (Flaming Fist) , Elthira Gossen , Ernestus , Falcäo , Falla , Fernhollow , Fist Attacker , Fry , Goodge , Granitdatter , Gyordi , Halfar , Hextra , Iogar , Ith'dul , Jerbold , Jimi Borleas , Karoline , Kepso , Khunaruth , Klaas , Klen , Krizt , Kuthbert , Lae'zel , Lewis Morell , Leythim , Liara Portyr , Lochan , Ma'aryk , Ma'athal , Malik (zealot) , Matthew , Miller , Munish , Nadi , Nateen , Nephel , Nestor , Ni'ima , Niram , Oathbreaker Knight , Oriona , Pantella , Patrick , Preyn , Qen , Qirahe , Quickstitch , Renan , Rylveth , Samwell Staxford , Saunder , Serrik , Shargil , Silena , Soreni , Starrlet , Taraji , Teth'ka , Thauniel Rusk , Togarr , Ulder Ravengard , Virry , Vu'un , Watcher Guardian , Xon'ar'as , Yeva , Yr'rk , Zira Notes This also applies to Versatile weapons when off-hand is empty. Unlike in 5th Edition rules, added damage dice from sources like Superiority Die , Divine Smite , and a Fire or Simple Toxin -dipped weapon may also be rerolled. This feature increases the average of a dice with x sides by 1 − 2 x , e.g. by 0.5 for a d4, by 0.666... for a d6, and so on. When used in combination with Savage Attacker (Or Brace (Melee) ), Great Weapon Fighting is applied before selecting the highest damage roll. So on the first roll any 1 or 2 is rerolled, then each dice is rolled one more time and uses the highest result. If used with both Brace and Savage Attacker, the dice are rolled one more time at the end and the highest result is chosen. The tooltip is showing 3-4 rolls but it appears to be a bug as of patch 6. Bugs While a two-handed melee weapon is equipped and the melee weapon slot is active, this passive also triggers damage rerolls on all Throw attacks using weapons with the Thrown property that are not equipped (i.e., in the character's inventory, in a container, or on the ground). Brief preview When rolling two-handed melee damage, any die rolling 1 or 2 is rerolled once. For example using the Halberd of Vigilance dipped in fire, this feat would on average add 2 x 0.5 + 0.8 = 1.8 bonus damage. If it is a critical hit it would add 3.6 bonus damage on average. Average bonus damage of Great Weapon Fighting with Savage Attacker (or Brace) [ edit section | visual editor ] Average bonus damage per dice rolled Damage dice Average bonus damage Average damage roll Average bonus damage added by Great Weapon Fighting Average bonus damage added by Savage Attacker 1d4 0.88 3.38 0.25 0.38 1d6 1.27 4.77 0.30 0.60 1d8 1.63 6.13 0.31 0.88 1d10 1.97 7.47 0.32 1.17 1d12 2.31 8.81 0.32 1.48 2d6 2.54 9.54 0.59 1.20 Comparing with the 2 bonus damage of the Duelling fighting style, at least 6 damage dice need to be rolled to be equivalent or better. This fighting style is less efficient when used in combination with Savage Attacker (Or Brace (Melee) ) but it can still be worth taking if: Many damage dice are rolled, which can be achieved with e.g., Divine Strike or when building characters based on critical hits . Someone wants to take a feat other than Savage Attacker, whose efficiency is slightly reduced by using Great Weapon Fighting instead (0.25 to 0.5 less bonus average damage, or 50% to 25% less bonus average damage for a d4 to d12 die) There are no better fighting styles to pick anyway. Average bonus damage of Great Weapon Fighting with Savage Attacker and Brace [ edit section | visual editor ] The average bonus damage is even lower when used with Brace and Savage Attacker: ~0.16 damage/die. However, Brace can only be used once per short rest so it could still be worth taking. ## Great Weapon Master: All In
- **来源**: [Great Weapon Master: All In](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Great_Weapon_Master:_All_In)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Great Weapon Master: All In is a toggleable passive feature provided by the Great Weapon Master Feat that allows Two-Handed or Versatile weapon users to deal extra damage at the cost of reduced accuracy. Description When attacking with a melee weapon you are Proficient with and are wielding in both hands, Attack Rolls take a -5 penalty, but their damage increases by 10. Details Toggleable How to learn Granted by the feats: Great Weapon Master Used by creatures: Baretha , Dead Whitburn Servant , Ebber , Fry , Goodge , Gyordi , Lady Flux , Matthew , Preyn , Watcher Guardian Notes This feature applies to any Two-Handed or Versatile melee weapons when off-hand is empty. Great Weapon Master: All In does not need to be enabled in order to benefit from Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack . Bugs When toggled on, Great Weapon Master reduces Attack Rolls for weapon actions from Two-Handed and Versatile (no shield) weapons that deal a fixed 1d4 damage. These specific 1d4 weapon actions suffer the accuracy penalty and gain the damage bonus despite the weapon action tooltips not displaying the additional damage.
## Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack
- **来源**: [Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Great_Weapon_Master:_Bonus_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack is a passive feature granted the Great Weapon Master Feat . It allows a character to use a Bonus Action to make an additional melee attack during the same turn they land a Critical Hit or kill a creature with a melee weapon. Description When you land a Critical Hit or kill a target with a melee weapon attack, you can make another melee weapon attack as a Bonus Action that turn. Condition: Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack Duration: 1 turn Can make a melee attack as a Bonus Action . How to learn Granted by the feats: Great Weapon Master Used by creatures: Baretha , Dead Whitburn Servant , Ebber , Fry , Goodge , Gravedigger Karcen , Gyordi , Lady Ague , Lady Quinsy , Marcus Falgor , Matthew , Preyn , Watcher Guardian Notes This passive does not require a Two-Handed or Versatile weapon, and allows for a Bonus Action attack with any melee weapon. Great Weapon Master: All In does not need to be enabled for this passive to trigger. Defeating a creature with Non-Lethal Damage also triggers this passive. Can be triggered multiple times in one turn, but cannot be triggered by Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack . Reducing a creature protected by Death Ward to 0 hit points without killing it does grant Great Weapon Master: Bonus Attack.

## Greater Kushigo Counter
- **来源**: [Greater Kushigo Counter](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Greater_Kushigo_Counter)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Greater Kushigo Counter is a passive feature that lets users retaliate against melee attacks that miss. Description The wearer can use a Reaction to make an Unarmed Strike against any attacker that misses. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Vest of Soul Rejuvenation Notes Greater Kushigo Counter triggers Extra Attack , if used during a player character's turn. If this attack is done while Extra Attack (from a normal attack) is activated, both Extra Attacks (from normal attack and Greater Kushigo Counter) are lost. Sentinel: Vengeance attack from an enemy can trigger Greater Kushigo Counter at the wrong moment and cause the loss of both Extra Attacks. On Honour mode, monks with an extra Action (at least from Haste and Elixir of Bloodlust ) can get Extra Attack only once per turn, while characters without extra actions get Extra Attack for both the normal attack and the Greater Kushigo Counter. Thus, both a hasted and a non-hasted monk can get 4 attacks per turn using Greater Kushigo Counter.

Condition: Green Bed Regeneration Green Bed Regeneration When starting your turn on Plant Growth Surface or Vine Surface regain 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Armour of Landfall Notes Hit points can be repeatedly regained outside of combat by entering turn-based mode while standing in overgrowth or vine surfaces and repeatedly ending the turn until it is the wearer's next turn. ## Grim Harvest

Grim Harvest is a Necromancy School Wizard passive feature. It allows the caster to regain hit points every time they kill a creature with a spell. The amount regained is based on the spell slot level used, and is increased if a Necromancy spell is used. Description Once per turn, if you kill a creature with a spell, you regain Hit Points equal to twice the Spell Slot level used - thrice if it's a Necromancy spell. Undead and Constructs are unaffected. How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Necromancy School Used by creatures: Aelis Siryasius , Balthazar , Gekh Coal , Intelligent Sentinel , Lucretious , Moorcombe Notes This ability triggers even if Warlock spell slots are used. Damaging Necromancy Wizard Spells: Blight Circle of Death Dethrone Ray of Sickness Vampiric Touch Bugs Despite the description, there is no restriction in the code to prevent this feature from triggering on undead and constructs. ## Grit
- **来源**: [Grit](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Grit)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Grit is a passive feature that grants the wearer a bonus action if they are severely injured. Description When the wearer has 50% Hit Points or less, they have an additional Bonus Action . Condition: Extra Bonus Action Extra Bonus Action Duration: 1 turn Grants an additional Bonus Action on this turn. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Helmet of Grit Notes temporary hit points are included in the calculation of total hit points required to activate Grit, including with the below listed bug. For example, if the wearer has a hit point maximum of 90, Grit activates once their hit points are reduced to 45 or lower. If they are at 45 hit points and then receive 14 temporary hit points, their total hit points are now 59; Grit then deactivates and only reactivates once their total hit points fall to 45 or below once again. The additional Bonus Action granted by this helmet stacks with those from other sources . Bugs Rather than only replenishing once per turn, Grit activates each time the wearer's total hit points are reduced to 50% or lower. Thus, it is possible for the wearer to gain multiple additional bonus actions in a turn by being healed above and then reduced again to 50% or less Hit Points .

## Halfling Luck
- **来源**: [Halfling Luck](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Halfling_Luck)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Halfling Luck is a passive feature in Baldur's Gate 3 which allows all halflings to reroll any (d20) dice once when it lands on a 1 for an Attack Roll, Ability Check, or Saving Throw. Description When you roll a 1 for an Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw , you can reroll the dice and must use the new roll. How to learn Races: Character level 1: Halfling ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Used by creatures: , 'Suspicious' Foont , 'Zinfandel' Gorse , Anderson , Arron , Babyjowls , Bad Twin Bubbins , Baz Hopbank , Beulla Sandfoot , Blades Bakstir , Bliggerillo , Bloris Meadhoney , Bramble , Brigand Harrold , Brinn , Brinna Brightsong , Burrock , Bustlebury , Chapeau , Cinna Brewcellar , Cora Highberry , Corliss Undertump , Dashkent Moliver , Dead Halfling (Ancient Lair) , Don't-Call-Me-Runt , Doora Thumbfoot , Drana Hoyte , Drussuvissill , Edmundis Magarus , Elindale , Falura , Fernhollow , Fillip , Findal , Flansy Thornwhist , Freddo , Fredrichk , Furbleston , Ghulen , Greymask , Happy Hoarson , Hector Roba , Huido , Impurto Nexim , Ironfinger , Jaryd , Khathi , Korrinna Koreena , Lanni , Linsella , Loic , Lolo Fuzzletoes , Lord Shattershield's Bodyguard , Lugarrio , Mahrin , Mask of Regret (Overgrown Tunnel) , Miklaur , Morgan , Nonabune , Olodan , Ooltheg , Pammella Nortale , Pharbz , Pheebs Splayfoot , Pinta , Randalf , Roah Moonglow , Robbin Datherswick , Roger Gherkins , Roger Highberry , Scarpers , Slarmy , Sleam , Sledge Pettifeet , Slorsha Grommer , Slumgullion , Stivvo , Sylbert , Sylvie Summerworth , Terse Torvalt , Theda Grosz , Thindo Vintervur , Three-Piece , Thyssa Shineboot , Tina Two-Thumbs , Trynn , Tut Thistlebog , Wren , Yannis , Zeffy Softbluff Notes It is possible for the new roll to be another 1. Halfling Luck is unique as a racial feature in that it cannot be replicated by any other item, spell, feat or ability in the unmodified version of the game. Although other racial features and abilities can be replaced (or at least approximated) by some methods, Halfling Luck has no such equivalent. As of patch 6, when rolling with advantage, the following rules apply: If one dice rolls a 1, it is re-rolled, and the higher of the two dice used. If both dice roll a 1, they are both re-rolled, and the highest of them is used. The chance to hit displayed when hovering an attack on an enemy does not take into account Halfling Luck. Halfling Luck is particularly useful to avoid failures for ability checks and saving throws when the roll would only fail on a critical miss. On a normal roll that succeeds on a 2 or more, Halfling Luck reduces the chance to fail from 1/20 to 1/400. On a roll with Advantage that succeeds on a 2 or more, Halfling Luck reduces the chance to fail from 1/400 to 1/160,000, making it practically impossible to fail. With Karmic Dice active, it may be simply impossible to roll 4 critical failures in a row. Lucky is one way to consistently obtain advantage on almost any roll, as such it (arguably) pairs well with this passive. Halflings can pilfer all easy-to-steal items from traders without fear of missing a single roll. Be mindful that uninterrupted stealing can make the character Heavily Encumbered which gives Disadvantage on all ability checks, including further pickpocket attempts. Stealth checks can get pretty much guaranteed to succeed. This passive greatly reduces incidents of Concentration interruptions which result from constitution save critical misses when taking low damage. Brief preview When rolling a 1 on an attack roll , ability check , or saving throw , rerolls once and uses the new result. Math [ edit section | visual editor ] Chances of succeeding a specific roll [ edit section | visual editor ] See Advantage math section for comparison. Chance of rolling a target number or above on 1d20 with Halfling Luck Target on 1d20 Luck Normal Roll Luck with Advantage Luck with Disadvantage 1 100% 100% 100% 2 99.75% 99.9994% 99.5% 3 94.50% 99.7% 89.3% 4 89.25% 98.84% 79.66% 5 84% 97.44% 70.56% 6 78.75% 95.48% 62.02% 7 73.5% 92.98% 54.02% 8 68.25% 89.92% 46.58% 9 63% 86.31% 39.69% 10 57.75% 82.15% 33.35% 11 52.5% 77.44% 27.56% 12 47.25% 72.17% 22.33% 13 42% 66.36% 17.64% 14 36.75% 59.99% 13.51% 15 31.5% 53.08% 9.92% 16 26.25% 45.61% 6.89% 17 21% 37.59% 4.41% 18 15.75% 29.02% 2.48% 19 10.5% 19.9% 1.1% 20 5.25% 10.22% 0.28% Chance to hit comparisons [ edit section | visual editor ] On a normal roll, Halfling Luck multiplies the chance to hit by : 1.05 whatever the target roll is This would be the most noticeable for a target roll of 2 which would add a flat 4.75% chance to hit or almost +1 on a d20. For a target roll of 20 it would add a flat 0.25% chance to hit, which would be a critical success. On a roll with Advantage, Halfling Luck multiplies the chance to hit by : 1.003 for a target roll of 2 or a flat +0.25% chance to hit 1.01 for a target roll of 3 or a flat +0.70% chance to hit ... 1.03 for a target roll of 11 or a flat +2.44% chance to hit ... 1.05 for a target roll of 20 or a flat +0.47% chance to hit, which would be a critical success. On a roll with Disadvantage, Halfling Luck multiplies the chance to hit by : 1.10 whatever the target roll is This would be the most noticeable for a target roll of 2 which would add a flat 9.25% chance to hit or almost +2 on a d20. For a target roll of 20 it would add a flat 0.03% chance to hit, which would be a critical success. Chance to fail comparisons [ edit section | visual editor ] On a normal roll, Halfling Luck divides the chance to fail by : 20 for a target roll of 2 1.82 for a target roll of 3 1.40 for a target roll of 4 ... 1.003 for a target roll of 20 On a roll with Advantage, Halfling Luck divides the chance to fail by : 400 for a target roll of 2 3.31 for a target roll of 3 1.95 for a target roll of 4 ... 1.01 for a target roll of 20 On a roll with Disadvantage, Halfling Luck divides the chance to fail by : 19.52 for a target roll of 2 1.78 for a target roll of 3 1.36 for a target roll of 4 ... 1.0003 for a target roll of 20 External Links [ edit section | visual editor ] Advantage and Halfling luck calculation by Kalaeman

## Heavy Armour Master
- **来源**: [Heavy Armour Master](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Heavy_Armour_Master)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Heavy Armour Master is a passive feature provided by the Feat of the same name. Your mastery over heavy armour increases, granting you damage reduction of incoming non-magical [ See: Bugs ] physical damage by 3. Description Your Strength increases by 1, to a maximum of 20. Incoming damage from non-magical attacks also decreases by 3 while you're wearing heavy armour. Requires Proficiency with Heavy Armour How to learn Granted by the feats: Heavy Armour Master (Feat) Notes This feat only works if the character is wearing heavy body armour. For example, it doesn't apply if the character is only wearing Grymskull Helm which counts as Heavy Armour in terms of required proficiency. Bugs This feat works for all incoming physical damage ( ⁠ Slashing , ⁠ Bludgeoning , or ⁠ Piercing ), no matter magical or not. This feature limitation only works as expected for self-damage. Which means Ritual Axe self-damage doesn't get damage reduction from this feat, as it's the only magical physical self damage effect in the game.

How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gauntlets of the Warmaster Notes The in-game description for Heightened Manoeuvre is arguably incomplete. It affects any action that uses the weapon action DC for its saving throw. This includes: Every manoeuvre Almost every weapon action Stunning Strike (both unarmed and weapon variants) Water Whip Heightened Manoeuvre does not affect weapon actions that do not involve the weapon action DC. These actions include: Every Arcane Shot Dazzling Ray Hellflame Cleave Reposition Malefactor Zephyr Break Zephyr Flash The ability to subject opponents of the wearer's manoeuvres to disadvantage is of significant utility to Battle Masters .

## Illithid Persuasion
- **来源**: [Illithid Persuasion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Illithid_Persuasion)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Illithid Persuasion is a unique illithid power which allows Origin characters, as well as Minthara and Minsc , to impose their will onto others with the Brand of the Absolute through conversation. This ability is unlocked automatically. Description Impose your authority onto those with the Brand of the Absolute . Properties During certain conversations just before dialog choices come up, the Narrator states "As the symbol glows, power courses through you. 'Authority'." This means that a target character has the Brand of the Absolute and can be dominated mentally to submit to the interacting party member. A DC 2 Wisdom Check is usually required, though some interaction may require a higher DC . Despite the low check, having a 1 or having a negative can still result in a failure. The first through seventh times this power is used, a unique comment is made by the Narrator on each specific occasion. Once a character successfully exercises the persuasion power seven times, the dialogue option prompt for this power is changed to True Soul and most uses of it no longer require a check (though some options using the persuasion power may still require one). After this ability is used, the character cannot use it again until their next Recharge: Long rest . Details Recharge: Long rest How to learn Other ways to learn: Available to characters who have been tadpoled Notes In Early Access , the progression of the illithid powers worked differently. Instead, the player character's tadpole grew in power by using Illithid Persuasion options in dialogue. Once the player character had used Illithid Persuasion three times, they received a power unique to their Class . Some of these abilities were reworked into the current Illithid Powers. Normally, this power is automatically granted to all tadpoled companions. However, if a companion is convinced to use tadpole powers, and is not in the active party while being convinced, a bug prevents the ability from being granted. However, not having this ability does not affect a tadpoled character's ability to use Illtihid Persuasion in dialogue. Text lines after using Ilithid Persuasion 1st use : "A shiver runs across your mind... You feel sated." (This line is normally used only after saving Shadowheart on the Nautiloid in the Prologue ). 2nd use : "Something stirs deep within you, hungry and alert... It's taking something you'll never get back." 3rd use : "Your mind lurches, reeling suddenly as if... bitten." 4th use : "A shadow swims across your vision, and a familiar voice tells you to be calm. You are loved." 5th use : "Your blood runs quicker, feeding the gnawing absence at the centre of your mind." 6th use : "The presence deep in your mind is awake, unblinking. This is it. A single word pervades your consciousness: 'Soon'." 7th use : "Your mind is full, bursting with ecstasy and terror. Finally, it is coming. You are becoming." Interactions in the Prologue Saving Shadowheart by using the Eldritch Rune Interactions in Act One Astarion trying to bite during a long rest Talking with Edowin automatically uses this ability on Brynna ; using it here can prevent a fight from breaking out Andrick in the owlbear cave Entering the Blighted Village through the eastern or southern gate; ⁠ Just Passing Through is not granted when used Meeting with Fezzerk at the windmill Entering the Goblin Camp from the front or side entrance; ⁠ Very Important Parasite is not granted when used Lae'zel trying to kill the player character during a long rest; this happens after the Mysterious Artefact cutscene when reaching certain areas like Goblin camp Speaking with Krolla after asking about winnings Convincing Klagga to give the Dwarf's Poem to the party Speaking with Crusher ; ⁠ Anything for a Profit , ⁠ What Price Dignity? , and ⁠ Give Them a Show are not granted when used Convincing with Piddle to give the On Goblins: My Life Among the Conquering Host to the party Speaking with Trinzas when entering Shattered Sanctum Speaking with Spike ; ⁠ Grabbing the Poker with Both Hands is not granted when used Speaking with Gribbo , convincing her to let go Volo Saving Halsin Speaking with Flind during the fight with the gnolls Speaking with Gekh Coal without having Glut with the party Interactions in Act Two Telling Gronag to fetch the bone he threw Telling Barnabus to behave after severing Linsella 's influence Convincing Winged Horrors to eat eachother Speaking with Marls at the Moonrise Towers docks Interactions in Act Three Speaking with Dravo Flymm and Sally Flymm in Flymm's Cobblers Bugs A bug may occur where one may receive the "True Soul" tag early - on the 4th use.

Illusion Quickening is a passive feature that lets the wearer cast illusion or enchantment spells after making a weapon attack. Description After hitting a creature with a weapon attack, you can cast illusion or enchantment spells as a Bonus Action . Details UID MAG_ArcaneTrickster_Ring_Passive Condition: Quickening Incantation Quickening Incantation Duration: 1 turn You can cast Illusion and Enchantment Spells as a bonus action. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Band of the Mystic Scoundrel Notes A character with Quickening Incantation condition cannot cast illusion or enchantment spells that turn as an action anymore, only as a bonus action. Spells from other schools of magic may still be cast using their regular costs. The Quickening Incantation loses duration at the start of the turn, so an Opportunity Attack does not give a character this condition for their next turn. Illusion Quickening also works for illusion or enchantment spell scrolls, including Disguise Kit which effectively counts as a Disguise Self scroll. Bugs Any weapon attack triggers Illusion Quickening, even against world items.

## Impulse Blast
- **来源**: [Impulse Blast](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Impulse_Blast)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Impulse Blast is a passive feature that sends a shockwave when its wielder kills a creature or lands a critical hit. Description Knocks nearby creatures Prone after killing a target or landing a Critical Hit . Condition: Prone Prone Duration: 2 turns DEX Save ( DC  14) Can't move or take Actions , Bonus Actions , or Reactions , and has Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity Saving Throws . Attacks against a Prone creature have Advantage if they're made within 3 m (10 ft) of the creature. A Prone creature must spend half its Movement Speed to stand up. Falling Prone immediately ends Concentration . If a creatures falls Prone on its turn, the turn immediately ends. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Intransigent Warhammer Notes Impulse Blast only activates on attacks made with the Intransigent Warhammer . Only enemies are affected by the blast. Bugs Despite suggesting it automatically knocks nearby enemies prone, Impulse Blast has a hidden DC  14 Dexterity Saving Throw .

## Infernal Legion
- **来源**: [Infernal Legion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Infernal_Legion)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Infernal Legion is a passive feature that makes the wearer a part of the legion. Description Grants the Infernal Legion condition while worn. Condition: Infernal Legion Infernal Legion You are one, you are legion, without personality or individuality - born only to fight. When within 20 m (67 ft) of another creature wearing a merregon's mask, Strength increases by 1 and Intelligence , Wisdom , and Charisma decrease by 1 per nearby mask. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Devilfoil Mask Notes The Infernal Legion condition is only applied if the mask's wearer is within range other creatures wearing a mask. It gains one stack for each mask within range, not including the wearer themself. It is also not displayed on the mask's tooltip in-game. Infernal Legion grants an uncapped bonus to Strength, but takes effect before other items and bonuses which raise Strength to a capped amount. Sometimes, upon a character level up, the Infernal Legion buff disappears; this can be corrected by unequipping and re-equipping the mask. The Infernal Legion buff disappears if a Druid wearing the mask uses Wild Shape .

Infernal Sight is a passive feature that lets the wearer see in normal darkness, and provides immunity against blindness. Description You can see in magical [ See: Bugs ] and ordinary darkness up to a range of 12 m (40 ft). You cannot be Blinded . Bugs Infernal Sight does not see through magical darkness and does not provide the cone of light that is otherwise present with the Darkvision effect from a different source, such as the Darkvision spell, an Elixir of Darkvision , or from having the Darkvision passive innately via race .

## Invisible Weapon
- **来源**: [Invisible Weapon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Invisible_Weapon)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Invisible Weapon is a passive feature that prevents the wielder from being disarmed, until it becomes visible on a missed attack. Description This weapon is Invisible while equipped. It has Advantage on Attack Rolls . It loses this property for 2 rounds on a missed Attack Roll . The weapon also scores a critical hit when rolling a 19. Condition: Invisible Weapon Invisible Weapon Affected entity can't be disarmed. It has Advantage on Attack Rolls . It scores a critical hit when rolling a 19. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Unseen Menace Notes Prior to Patch #6 , this feature did not actually prevent disarming. Although not explicitly stated, as is with most other critical threshold reducing items , the critical hit reduction from Unseen Menace stacks with all other sources of increased critical hit range. This passive is not applied when the weapon is Thrown . Consequently, a miss when the weapon is thrown does not render it visible.
