## Lathander's Blessing
- **来源**: [Lathander's Blessing](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lathander's_Blessing)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Lathander's Blessing is a passive feature that protects the wielder should they fall in combat. Description Once per Long Rest , when your hit points are reduced to 0, you regain 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Allies within 9 m (30 ft) also regain 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . How to learn Granted by the weapons: The Blood of Lathander Notes Lathander's Blessing does not activate if the wielder is not in the active party. For example, a companion who is left at camp and receives damage via Warding Bond which reduces their hit points to zero does not cause this effect to trigger. Lathander's Blessing does not protect against being shoved, thrown, or otherwise forcibly displaced into chasms. Bugs Lathander's Blessing does not heal allies of the wielder, but rather only active party members nearby. Due to the way the heal is coded, the attacker who triggered Lathander's Blessing is considered to be the source of the healing. As a result, the healing will not trigger on-heal effects such as Blessed Mercy from The Whispering Promise when equipped by the wielder. Due to an incorrectly set TargetConditions field, the additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points affects the wielder in addition to the 2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Due to a timing limitation caused by the method in which healing is applied, the wielder may not always receive all of the healing they are stated to have received in the combat log; they often receive only 1 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points (from being stabilized) or 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points , rather than the stated 1d6+2d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . It is also possible for the wielder to receive healing, yet still remain dead, showing their lootable corpse with remaining hitpoints. Due to a missing technical condition ( MAG_LATHANDERS_TRACKER ) resulting from The Blood of Lathander being spawned in-game via a "Local Item", this passive's "Once per Long Rest" cooldown only refreshes for the wielder during a Long Rest. Equipping the weapon on another character that did not wield the weapon during a Long Rest does not allow this passive to trigger. Additionally, Lathander's Blessing is not reset when consuming a Potion of Angelic Slumber or when affected by Divine Intervention: Opulent Revival .
## Lathander's Light
- **来源**: [Lathander's Light](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lathander's_Light)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Lathander's Light is a toggleable passive feature that sheds light and blinds select enemy types. Description Sheds holy light in a 6 m (20 ft) radius. In combat, fiends and undead standing in the light are Blinded if they fail a DC 14 Constitution throw. Details Toggleable Condition: Lathander's Light Lathander's Light Duration: Permanent Sheds holy light in a 6 m (20 ft) radius. In combat, fiends and undead standing in the light are Blinded , unless they succeed a Constitution Saving Throw . How to learn Granted by the weapons: The Blood of Lathander Notes Unlike Light , the Lathander's Light condition works even when wielding a ranged weapon. The light emitted by Lathander's Light has the following properties: It does not apply to allies, meaning you won't blind your own summoned undead. It dispels the Shadow Curse , removing the need to equip a Torch . It enables effects that require the target be illuminated, such as applying the damage from the Callous Glow Ring . It is considered sunlight for the purpose of triggering Sunlight Hypersensitivity but is not for Sunlight Sensitivity . It applies to neutral creatures (including neutral Undead ), potentially making them hostile.

Condition: Those Laid Bare Those Laid Bare Duration: 1 turn Affected entity has a +1 bonus to save against spell DC . ## Legendary Action: Adamantine Reverberation

This page is about content exclusive to Honour mode . Legendary Action: Adamantine Reverberation is a legendary action passive feature available to Grym in Honour mode. Once per turn when struck by an attack, Grym reverberates, granting 10 temporary hit points and doubled movement speed until the temporary hit points are depleted. Description Once per round, Grym can use its Legendary Action to Reverberate when it is struck, doubling its movement and granting it 10 temporary hit points. Losing these temporary hit points triggers a shockwave that knocks targets back 4 m (13 ft) and deals 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage. Legendary Actions restore at the start of each round. Condition: Legendary Action: Adamantine Reverberation Legendary Action: Adamantine Reverberation When struck, Grym's adamantine form Reverberates , doubling its movement and granting it 10 temporary hit points. Losing these temporary hit points triggers a shockwave that knocks targets back 4 m (13 ft) and deals 4d8 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder damage. How to learn Used by creatures: Grym Brief preview Once per round, use your Legendary Action to Reverberate when struck.
## Legendary Action: Beguiling Rebuke
- **来源**: [Legendary Action: Beguiling Rebuke](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Legendary_Action:_Beguiling_Rebuke)
- **分类**: Passive_features

This page is about content exclusive to Honour mode . Legendary Action: Beguiling Rebuke is a passive feature available to Raphael while he is not in his Fiendish Ascension form. It lets him expend a legendary action to use Beguiling Rebuke , after he or his allies are attacked. Description Beguile your attacker and its nearby allies, possibly preventing them from attacking you again. Cambions ascended by this cascade deal Hellfire damage, which ignores Resistance and Immunity to Fire damage. [ See: Bugs ] Legendary Actions restore at the start of each round. Condition: Legendary Action: Beguiling Rebuke Legendary Action: Beguiling Rebuke Raphael can spend a Legendary Action to immediately Beguile a hostile creature and its allies after being attacked. How to learn Used by creatures: Raphael Notes Raphael can spend a Legendary Action to immediately Beguile a hostile creature and its allies after being attacked. Raphael may use this Legendary Action as many times per round as there are Soul Pillars standing at the start of the round. Bugs Beguiled lacks the proper Charmed status group , and as such will not be removed or prevented by typical means. The extra description in this passive appears to be misplaced, as it has no relevance in this case.
## Legendary Action: Bhaal's Edict

Legendary Action: Weird Magic Surge is a passive feature available to Ethel in Honour mode, which lets her use the legendary action Weird Magic Surge immediately after a spell is cast. A higher level spell will produce more illusory duplicates. A higher level spell will result in more illusory duplicates being summoned. Legendary Actions restore at the start of each round. Condition: Legendary Action: Weird Magic Surge Legendary Action: Weird Magic Surge Auntie Ethel can use her Weird Magic Surge immediately after a spell is cast. A higher level spell will produce more illusory duplicates. How to learn Used by creatures: Auntie Ethel

Legion of Bees: Attack - Deal 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing damage to the target. Legion of Bees: Teleport - Teleport up to 5 m (17 ft) away. Legion of Bees: Knockback - Possibly push the target back 5 m (17 ft). Legion of Bees: Mighty Knockback - Possibly push the target back 5 m (17 ft) and knock it Prone for 1 turn. Grants: Legion of Bees: Attack Legion of Bees: Knockback Legion of Bees: Teleport How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Swarmkeeper Notes The different swarm options all share a cooldown. Only one of them can be used in a single round. The damage dealt by the swarm attack is considered non-magical. ## Lesser Infernal Retribution

Lesser Infernal Retribution is a passive feature that retaliates against enemies with a bit of fire. Description When you are hit by a foe within 2 m (7 ft), it might take 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Flawed Helldusk Armour Notes Lesser Infernal Retribution requires a DC  13 Dexterity Saving Throw in order to deal damage. This does not trigger Heat while wearing Thermoarcanic Gloves or having Gripped by Kereska's Flame . Bugs The required saving throw for Lesser Infernal Retribution is attributed in the combat log to the wearer of the armour, rather than the attacker, but is correctly rolled by the attacker. ## Lethal Weapon (Bludgeoning)
- **来源**: [Lethal Weapon (Bludgeoning)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lethal_Weapon_(Bludgeoning))
- **分类**: Passive_features

Lethal Weapon is a passive feature that bypasses defenses against bludgeoning damage. Description This weapon ignores resistance to ⁠ Bludgeoning damage. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Adamantine Mace Foebreaker Notes Lethal Weapon does not bypass immunity to bludgeoning, only resistance . Lethal Weapon applies to unarmed strikes made while it is equipped. The game does not allow most characters to make unarmed strikes while a melee weapon is equipped in their main hand, but Monks who are level 5 and higher can use Stunning Strike to do this; they can also use Unarmed Strike to apply this effect with their off-hand as a Bonus Action . All sources of ⁠ Bludgeoning damage from a character with Lethal Weapon ignore resistance. For example, another dual-wielded bludgeoning damage weapon striking in melee, Dwarven Thrower being thrown , or the spell Ice Storm .

## Life Essence Harvest
- **来源**: [Life Essence Harvest](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Life_Essence_Harvest)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Life Essence Harvest is a passive feature that causes creatures killed by spells to give the wielder Spell Slots. They can only be used for Necromancy Spells. Description When the wielder kills a hostile creature with a spell, they greedily absorb its energy and gain Life Essence until their next Long Rest. Condition: Life Essence Life Essence Duration: Until Long rest Affected entity has absorbed a creature's essence. It can use that essence to cast any Necromancy spell without consuming a spell slot . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Staff of Cherished Necromancy Used by creatures: Mystic Carrion Notes Life Essence Harvest has no cooldown and can be triggered without limit. Killing a creature with a spell granted from Life Essence does not provide a new charge of Life Essence . Indirect spell damage from sources like Spirit Guardians does not provide a charge of Life Essence when killing a hostile creature. Per the GreaterNecromancySpellFilter() .khn script, this effect is intended to allow the casting of an extra Necromancy spell only if the spell level is equal to or lower than the number of Life Essence turns the wielder has. However, this restriction is currently non-functional, and any level of Necromancy spell can be cast using the effect. Though none of the tooltips explicitly mention this functionality, Life Essence displays the number of turns the wielder has on its tooltip. Bugs Casting a Necromancy cantrip consumes the Life Essence Harvest charge, even though the character's cast bar does not highlight the cantrip to indicate it will use the effect.

Life Stealing Critical is a passive feature that deals extra damage on a critical hit and also gives you temporary hp. Description On a Critical Hit , the target takes an extra 10 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic DRS damage as long as it isn't a construct or an undead. You also gain 10 temporary hit points . Can only have temporary hit points from one source. Condition: Temporary Hit Points (10) Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 10 temporary hit points . ## Lucky
- **来源**: [Lucky](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Lucky)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Lucky is a passive feature provided by the Feat of the same name. It grants the user 3 Luck Points , which can be can be used to manipulate either their rolls, or an enemy's rolls. Description You gain 3 Luck Points , which you can use to gain Advantage on Attack Rolls , Ability Checks , or Saving Throws , or to make an enemy reroll their Attack Rolls . Details Recharge: Long rest Grants: Lucky: Reroll with Advantage Lucky: Reroll Attacker's Die How to learn Granted by the feats: Lucky (Feat) Notes Lucky grants a toggleable passive by the same name which, when turned on, provides Advantage on the character's next Ability Check. This feat is one of the few ways to gain Advantage on almost all types of d20 rolls. Player characters in Honour Mode may benefit from this feat in situations where failure has particularly unfortunate results or, conversely, success is deemed essential. This feat stacks with the racial passive feature Halfling Luck . Bugs Due to the way this passive is granted, it defaults to "off" and cannot be toggled "on" the very first time it is acquired until after the character has first made an ability check, has used a reaction, has used a short rest, or has taken a long rest.
## Lunar Bestial Fortitude

Bugs Lunar Protection granted by Lunar Bestial Fortitude incorrectly states it provides a +1d4 bonus to Armour Class; it is a flat +2 bonus. When affected by a Starry Form, the bonus AC is applied a second time, resulting in a total AC bonus of 4.

## Mage Hand Legerdemain
- **来源**: [Mage Hand Legerdemain](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mage_Hand_Legerdemain)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Mage Hand Legerdemain is an Arcane Trickster Rogue passive feature. This ability enhances your Mage Hand , allowing it to remain permanently and granting it invisibility. Description When you cast Mage Hand, the spectral hand is invisible and permanent. Condition: Invisible Invisible Has Advantage on Attack Rolls and imposes Disadvantage on enemy Attack Rolls. Invisibility ends early if the invisible entity attacks, casts another spell, interacts with an object, becomes wet, takes an action or bonus action, or is damaged. How to learn Classes: Class level 3: Arcane Trickster Notes Invisibility ends on nearly any action taken by the mage hand, and is only regained on short rests. Due to a bug, the Mage Hand's invisibility is also broken by any ally with See Invisibility if summoned within their vision range. To avoid this, summon it outside of their vision range. This is probably the best tool to scout safely, as long are there are no creatures nearby with See Invisibility , which is fairly rare. One can scout an entire area thanks to the Mage Hand's ability to fly which allows it to go to places otherwise very difficult to reach, as long as one can make the camera see the ground level of that place. Letting the hand throw objects or potions in battle is very effective, because dropping an item on the ground for the hand to throw does not cost an action. Even while invisible and out of combat, the hand is able to flank an opponent to activate a Rogue's Sneak Attack . Prior to Patch 8, the description stated "When you cast Mage Hand, the spectral hand is invisible and can carry out additional tasks." v t e Rogue Subclasses Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Cunning Action Dash Disengage Hide Sneak Attack Sneak Attack (Melee) Sneak Attack (Ranged) Rakish Sneak Attack (Melee) Rakish Sneak Attack (Ranged) Other class features Assassin's Alacrity Assassinate: Ambush Assassinate: Initiative Dirty Trick Flick o' the Wrist Sand Toss Vicious Mockery Expertise Evasion Fancy Footwork Fast Hands Infiltration Expertise Mage Hand Legerdemain Magical Ambush Panache Rakish Audacity Reliable Talent Second-Story Work Supreme Sneak Uncanny Dodge

## Mage Slayer: Break Concentration
- **来源**: [Mage Slayer: Break Concentration](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mage_Slayer:_Break_Concentration)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Mage Slayer: Break Concentration is a Passive Feature provided by the Mage Slayer Feat . When you attack a creature, they have Disadvantage on any Concentration Saving Throws they make that turn. Description Enemies you hit have Disadvantage when making Saving Throws to maintain their Concentration . [ See Notes ] How to learn Granted by the feats: Mage Slayer Notes The actual effect of this feature is that any enemies you hit with a melee attack are guaranteed to lose concentration. The target still makes a concentration saving throw, but concentration will be broken regardless of the result.
## Mage Slayer: Saving Throw Advantage

Mage Slayer: Saving Throw Advantage is a passive feature provided by the Mage Slayer Feat . When a creature casts a spell near you, you have Advantage on any Saving Throws against it. ## Magic Club
- **来源**: [Magic Club](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Magic_Club)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Magic Club is a passive feature applied to Twisting Branch clubs carried by Wood Woads . It causes the clubs to become magical weapons and deal extra damage. Description In the Wood Woad's hand, a common club becomes magical and deals 3d4 ⁠ ⁠ Bludgeoning DRS damage extra. How to learn Used by creatures: Wood Woad Notes This effect is not applied to the Twisting Branch that can be acquired as normal loot. Bugs Due to a coding error, the 3d4 extra damage from this feature is not magical despite the description saying it is. The 3d4 extra damage applies to all melee attacks instead of just weapon attacks, and it triggers twice if dual wielded. Most damage riders also stack with each instance of this damage.
## Magic Initiate: Bard
- **来源**: [Magic Initiate: Bard](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Magic_Initiate:_Bard)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Magic Initiate: Bard is a passive feature provided by the Feat of the same name. It grants you spells and cantrips from that particular class. Description You have learnt 2 cantrips and a Level 1 spell from the Bard spell list . You can cast the Level 1 spell once per Long Rest . Your Spellcasting Modifier for all 3 spells is Charisma . How to learn Granted by the feats: Magic Initiate: Bard (Feat)
## Magic Initiate: Cleric
- **来源**: [Magic Initiate: Cleric](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Magic_Initiate:_Cleric)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Magic Initiate: Cleric is a Passive Feature provided by the Feat of the same name. It grants you spells and cantrips from that particular class. Description You have learnt 2 cantrips and a Level 1 spell from the Cleric spell list . You can cast the Level 1 spell once per Long Rest . Your Spellcasting Modifier for all 3 spells is Wisdom . How to learn Granted by the feats: Magic Initiate: Cleric (Feat) Bugs This feat has an unlisted effect that increases the maximum AC bonus from Dexterity while wearing Medium Armour from +2 to +3. This effect is equivalent to the Medium Armour Master feat. Also like that feat, this effect will break the Exotic Material feature of certain Medium Armours.

Magical Ambush is a togglable passive gained by Arcane Tricksters at Level 9. Magical Ambush allows the Rogue to circumvent their target's defenses when casting spells while hidden. Description While you are Hiding , your targets have Disadvantage on Saving Throws against your Spells . Condition: Magical Ambush Magical Ambush Affected entity is hidden . Creatures have Disadvantage on Saving Throws against its spells. How to learn Classes: Class level 9: Arcane Trickster Notes Most direct damage saving throw spells like Burning Hands do apply the effect. Most direct control saving throw spells like Hold Person do apply the effect, but on the initial saving throw only. Most ground spells like Wall of Fire and Glyph of Warding do not apply the effect. ## Malefic Funghi
- **来源**: [Malefic Funghi](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Malefic_Funghi)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Malefic Funghi is a passive feature that boosts a druid's spells and damage. Description The wearer gains a +1 bonus to Spell Save DC and when dealing ⁠ Necrotic damage, they deal an additional 1 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Armour of the Sporekeeper Notes Since elemental damage from several sources is additive in one instance, Malefic Funghi only provides 1 extra damage regardless of the number of sources of necrotic damage. For example, a Vampire Ascendant Astarion with Manifestation of Body and Symbiotic Entity active deals only 1 extra necrotic damage with this armour equipped, despite having three separate sources of necrotic damage.
## Man's Best Friend
- **来源**: [Man's Best Friend](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Man's_Best_Friend)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Man's Best Friend is a passive feature which boosts the offence and defence of a hunting dog, according to the proficiency bonus of their master. Description This hunting dog's Armour Class and damage increase by an amount equal to the Proficiency Bonus of its houndmaster. How to learn Used by creatures: Gordis , Pol , Rocky , Zina Notes This passive feature is actually two-in-one: a variant for Houndmaster Pol that adds his proficiency bonus to the dogs, and a variant for the dogs that receives the proficiency bonus. Both of these conditions are named Man's Best Friend.

- **分类**: Passive_features

Mantle of Inspiration is a passive feature that protects the user with a mantle that charms enemies that hit them. Description Imbued with bardic vigour. When a creature hits you with a melee attack, they become Charmed . Condition: Charmed Charmed Duration: 1 turn Cannot attack the spellcaster. The spellcaster has Advantage on Charisma Checks in dialogue. How to learn Other ways to learn: Applied by the Mantle of Inspiration condition. ## Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike
- **来源**: [Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Martial_Arts:_Bonus_Unarmed_Strike)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike is a Monk passive feature that grants a single follow-up Unarmed Strike (Monk) using a Bonus Action . The initial attack must be unarmed or use a melee Monk weapon . Description After making an attack with a melee Monk weapon or while unarmed, you can make another unarmed attack as a bonus action. Condition: Martial Arts: Unarmed Strike Martial Arts: Unarmed Strike You can make an unarmed attack as a Bonus Action this turn. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Monk Used by creatures: Mask of Terror (The Blushing Mermaid) , Sina'zith Notes This feature only triggers on melee attacks, and will not trigger on itself. If the user has multiple bonus actions, such as from Wholeness of Body and Fast Hands , the first use of Bonus Unarmed Strike makes it unavailable to be used again immediately for the second bonus action. To avoid this, the user must perform another monk weapon attack or Unarmed Strike (e.g. level 5 monk with Extra Attack ) before using the second bonus action. ## Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks
- **来源**: [Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Martial_Arts:_Dextrous_Attacks)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Martial Arts: Dextrous Attacks is a Monk passive which makes attacks with Monk Weapons and unarmed attacks scale with Dexterity instead of Strength , if the user's Dexterity is higher. ## Martial Bravery
- **来源**: [Martial Bravery](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Martial_Bravery)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Martial Bravery is a passive feature that grants the wearer increased damage when surrounded by 2 or more enemies. Description Your weapon and unarmed attacks deal an additional 2 damage while surrounded by 2 or more foes. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Scabby Pugilist Circlet Notes Though not mentioned in the description, Martial Bravery also increases the damage of Throw attacks. Bugs Due to faulty exclusionary check within the HasEnemyWithinRange() conditional script, Martial Bravery still functions with nearby unconscious and incapacitated enemies as long as there is at least one conscious enemy nearby (alive and not incapacitated). Despite the description, two or more enemies must be within 3 m (10 ft) of the target , not the wearer of the circlet. This means the wearer does not need to be "surrounded" at all; they need enemies near the target of their attack.

## Mental Debilitation
- **来源**: [Mental Debilitation](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mental_Debilitation)
- **分类**: Passive_features

This article is about content that is inaccessible through normal gameplay . It can still be accessed via in-game exploits or third party tools. Mental Debilitation is a passive feature that mentally exhausts attacking foes. Description When the wearer succeeds a Saving Throw against any foe's spells or actions, that foe gains Mental Fatigue . Condition: Mental Fatigue Mental Fatigue Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has a -1 penalty to Wisdom , Intelligence and Charisma saving throws for every turn remaining. When it fails a Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma saving throw while having 5 or more turns of this condition remaining, the entity takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic DRS damage and is no longer mentally fatigued. Mental Fatigue has a maximum Duration: 7 turns. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Braindrain Cape   (inaccessible)
## Mental Inhibition
- **来源**: [Mental Inhibition](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mental_Inhibition)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Mental Inhibition is a passive feature that tires out a mind targeted by the ring's wearer. Description When a foe fails a Saving Throw against one of your spells or actions, they gain Mental Fatigue for 2 turns. Condition: Mental Fatigue Mental Fatigue Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has a -1 penalty to Wisdom , Intelligence and Charisma saving throws for every turn remaining. When it fails a Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma saving throw while having 5 or more turns of this condition remaining, the entity takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic DRS damage and is no longer mentally fatigued. Mental Fatigue has a maximum Duration: 7 turns. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Ring of Mental Inhibition Notes Mental Fatigue is not applied on saving throws made to shake off an effect . For example, if a creature is under the effect of Hold Person , it makes a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each turn to end the effect . Failing that saving throw does not apply Mental Fatigue. As of Patch 2 Hotfix 5, the condition is not applied to failed saves from weapon passive effects, coatings, clouds, or wall spells, such as Cloudkill , Stinking Cloud , or Wall of Fire . In these cases, the saving throw appears to be against the area of effect instead of the caster. [ verify ] Bugs Despite the description, Mental Inhibition also applies to allies.

Mental Interference is a passive feature that tires out the user's targets when dealing psychic damage to them. Description When you deal ⁠ Psychic damage, you also inflict Mental Fatigue for 2 turns. Condition: Mental Fatigue Mental Fatigue Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has a -1 penalty to Wisdom , Intelligence and Charisma saving throws for every turn remaining. When it fails a Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma saving throw while having 5 or more turns of this condition remaining, the entity takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Psychic DRS damage and is no longer mentally fatigued. Mental Fatigue has a maximum Duration: 7 turns. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Braindrain Gloves Notes In Honour mode , the ⁠ Psychic damage from Flurry of Moths: Attack does not trigger Mental Interference. However, the separate psychic damage from Prey's Scent against a marked target does trigger it. Both damage instances apply Mental Fatigue outside of the Honour mode ruleset.

## Metamagic: Twinned Spell
- **来源**: [Metamagic: Twinned Spell](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Metamagic:_Twinned_Spell)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Metamagic: Twinned Spell is a toggleable passive feature used by Sorcerers . This ability allows Sorcerers to target two creatures with certain Spells . Description Spells that only target 1 creature can target an additional creature. Costs 1 Sorcery Point per Spell Slot level used. Cantrips also cost 1 Sorcery Point . For spells that don't shoot a projectile, the targets need to be close enough together. Details Toggleable How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Sorcerer Used by creatures: Mizora Notes When twin casting a spell, two separate targets must be chosen. The same creature cannot be targeted twice by the same twinned spell. This passive can be used with Drakethroat Glaive to enchant two weapons (requires 3 Sorcery Points ). Spells that are able to target multiple creatures cannot be used with Twinned Spell , even if those spells are only used to target one creature. This includes spells such as Magic Missile and Eldritch Blast (after 5th level). A spell that targets the caster themselves cannot be twinned, even if it only affects the caster. Spells that affect an area cannot be twinned. This includes spells like Ice Knife which are single target but with an additional area of effect. The only exceptions are Hail of Thorns and Lightning Arrow . Summoning spells cannot be twinned. Since Patch 6, Chain Lightning cannot be twinned. However, this restriction does not apply to the version of Chain Lightning granted by Markoheshkir . Bugs Due to the lack of a TargetRadius check for projectile spells, Twinned Spell is compatible with the ranged version of certain spells while also being incompatible with the melee version. An example of this is Ensnaring Strike . - **分类**: Passive_features

Mobile: Evade Opportunity Attack is a passive feature that lets a creature move away from a target without provoking Opportunity Attacks , after they have made a melee attack. Description If you move after making a melee attack, you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks from your target. The effect still works if your attack misses. Condition: Sluggardly Sluggardly Duration: 1 turn Can't make an Opportunity Attack against its most recent attacker. How to learn Granted by the feats: Mobile Used by creatures: Dadger , Erus , Faona , Galleass , Gurira , Heen , Helenia , Jacko , Loretta , Morra , Smathers , Thamberg , The Warden , Theoda , Triava , Yonni Notes Your melee attacks (including melee Attack Roll spells) will inflict Sluggardly on your targets for Duration: 1 turn.

## Mortal Reminder
- **来源**: [Mortal Reminder](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mortal_Reminder)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Mortal Reminder is a passive feature unique to The Great Old One Warlock subclass that Frightens creatures upon a critical hit. Description When you land a Critical Hit against a creature, that creature and any nearby enemies must succeed a Wisdom Saving Throw or become Frightened until the end of their next turn. Details UID ClarifiedMortality Condition: Frightened (Mortal Reminder) Frightened Duration: 1 turn WIS Save Cannot move. Frightened entities also have Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls . How to learn Classes: Class level 1: The Great Old One Used by creatures: Cursed Imp , Kree Derryck Notes The Wisdom save uses the character's spellcasting ability modifier of the last class the character took a first level in. This may not be Charisma if the character multiclassed from warlock to another class. The Wisdom saving throw for Mortal Reminder applies to all enemies within a 3 m (10 ft) radius of the critically hit target. ## Mystra's Blessing
- **来源**: [Mystra's Blessing](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Mystra's_Blessing)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Mystra's Blessing is a passive feature which boosts the wielder's Bless spell. Description Creatures you Bless also gain Mystra's Blessing for an additional 1d4 bonus to spell attack rolls. [ See: Bugs ] Condition: Mystra's Blessing (Staff of Arcane Blessing) Mystra's Blessing Duration: 10 turns +1d4 to Attack Rolls made with spells How to learn Granted by the weapons: Staff of Arcane Blessing Bugs The in-game description of this passive feature is not entirely correct, and reads as follows: Bless grants an additional 1d4 to Saving Throws and Weapon Attack Rolls, and an additional 2d4 to Spell Attack Rolls. Instead, creatures Blessed with the Staff of Arcane Blessing gain two separate conditions: The regular Bless condition , which grants a 1d4 bonus to all saving throws and attack rolls. The special Mystra's Blessing condition , which grants another 1d4 bonus, but only to spell attack rolls. Specifically, it is possible to lose the regular Bless condition (due to the caster losing concentration ) while retaining the Mystra's Blessing condition. In this case, the creature is left with a 1d4 bonus to spell attack rolls, but loses the other 1d4 bonuses, despite the tooltip of the condition claiming otherwise. Mystra's Blessing is only applied when Bless is cast using a level 1 or level 2 spell slot, in addition to the once-per-day version granted by the staff itself.
## Natural Pugilist
- **来源**: [Natural Pugilist](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Natural_Pugilist)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Natural Pugilist is a passive feature that increases the user's unarmed attack rolls and damage. Description You gain a +1 bonus to Melee Unarmed Attack Rolls and damage. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Corellon's Grace Notes Unarmed attack bonuses granted by Natural Pugilist are still useful if a monk is equipped with Corellon's Grace , since monks can perform various unarmed attack actions (e.g., Unarmed Strike (Monk) , Flurry of Blows , and Ki Resonation: Punch ) even when equipped with a melee weapon, as long as it is a monk weapon . When using an Improvised Melee Weapon , which is considered an unarmed melee attack, Natural Pugilist grants the bonus to the attack roll but not to the damage roll.

## Nature's Vengeance
- **来源**: [Nature's Vengeance](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Nature's_Vengeance)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Nature's Vengeance is a passive feature which inflicts extra conditions based on the type of surface the wearer is standing on. Description When the wearer stands on certain surfaces and casts a spell that deals damage, the target also suffers the surface's effects. Qualifying surfaces are Fire , Acid , Caustic Brine , and Simple Toxin . Condition: Burning Burning Duration: 2 turns Takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage per turn. Can be removed with the Help action, using a Healing Potion or gaining Wet . Immune from if Wet . Dip action can be used on Burning characters or objects. Condition: Caustic Brine Caustic Brine Duration: 2 turns Takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage per turn. Condition: Poisoned Poisoned Duration: 2 turns Suffers Disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks . Condition: Acid Acid Duration: 2 turns Reduces Armour Class by 2. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Amulet of Elemental Torment Notes The surface effects applied by Nature's Vengeance are: Fire : Apply Burning for 2 turns. Deals the first tick of 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Fire damage immediately. Caustic Brine : Apply Caustic Brine for 2 turns. Deals the first tick of 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Acid damage immediately. Simple Toxin : Apply Poisoned for 2 turns. Acid : Apply Acid for 2 turns. Nature's Vengeance does not work with any other surfaces. This includes the other basic elemental surfaces like Ice surfaces or Electrified Water surfaces. Valid poison surfaces can be created by breaking Simple Toxin vials or with Chromatic Orb . Surfaces created by breaking stronger poisons like Serpent Fang Toxin are different and do not work.

Night Walker is a passive feature that allows the user freedom of movement without any common restrictions. Description The affected creature cannot be Enwebbed , Entangled , or Ensnared and cannot slip on Grease or Ice . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Disintegrating Night Walkers Notes Night Walker only provides immunity to Ensnared received from Ensnaring Strike cast up to level two, and not from levels three or higher. It additionally does not provide immunity to Grasping Arrow: Entangled or Black Tentacles .

## Nimble Attack
- **来源**: [Nimble Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Nimble_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Nimble Attack is a passive feature that increases the movement speed of the user after hitting a target. Description When the wielder hits an enemy with this weapon, they gain Momentum for 2 turns. Condition: Momentum Momentum Duration: 2 turns Spurred on by a sense of urgency. Movement Speed increased by 1.5 m (5 ft) per remaining duration of this effect. Removed when Restrained , Incapacitated , Prone , or slowed down. Momentum has a maximum Duration: 5 turns. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Speedy Reply Bugs Momentum applies multiple times per attack with spells that are considered weapon attacks and include multiple DealDamage functions, such as Booming Blade and the various Smite spells.
## Nimblefinger
- **来源**: [Nimblefinger](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Nimblefinger)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Nimblefinger is a passive feature that grants bonuses to small size races. Description Gnomes are granted +2 to Dexterity . Halflings and Dwarves gain +1 Dexterity. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Nimblefinger Gloves Notes Being disguised as a Dwarf, Gnome, or Halfling when equipping the item also activates the effect. This effect persists even if dispelled, but doing so does not survive a reload. The Dexterity bonus is uncapped, and can therefore increase Dexterity to 24 in combination with the Mirror of Loss . However, the gloves do not stack with other capped Dexterity bonuses when Dexterity is above any of those caps. Therefore, this does not work if combined with a feat like Resilient: Dexterity , which caps at 20.

Through your acts of mercy, kindness, and forgiveness, kindle the light of hope in the world, beating back despair. Shelter the Light. ## Opportunity Attack
- **来源**: [Opportunity Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Opportunity_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Opportunity Attack or Attack of Opportunity is a common Passive feature / Reaction . This ability allows a creature to make a melee Attack Roll against enemies when they move out of the creature's melee range. Description Automatically attack an enemy moving out of your reach. How to learn (Information not yet added.) Notes The Disengage Action allows creatures to avoid provoking opportunity attacks. When dual wielding melee weapons, both weapons are used for an opportunity attack. First, a Main Hand Attack is made, followed by an Off-Hand Attack (Melee) with the same modifiers and damage as normal. The Polearm Master feat allows an opportunity attack when creatures move into reach if using polearms. Creatures cannot make opportunity attacks when: Wielding ranged weapons Having conditions that prevent the use of Reactions , such as Prone , Incapacitated , or Sleeping Unable to see the target for any reason, such as the target being Invisible or the attacker being Blinded Brief preview Attack an enemy moving out of reach.

## Organ Rearranger
- **来源**: [Organ Rearranger](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Organ_Rearranger)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Organ Rearranger is a passive feature that makes its wielder more deadly. Description Reduce the number you need to roll a Critical Hit while attacking by 1. This effect can stack. When you roll 2 damage or less, reroll the dice, taking the highest result. Details UID MAG_TheClover_Rearrangement_Passive How to learn Granted by the weapons: Knife of the Undermountain King The Clover   (inaccessible) Notes Organ Rearranger stacks with other passive effects that improve critical chance, including ranged attacks and spell attack rolls [1] [2] . Organ Rearranger's damage reroll is only applied to melee weapon attacks. When dual-wielding melee weapons, both weapons will benefit. All damage dice attached to an attack can be rerolled, not just the weapon's base damage die. The damage reroll is not normally applied to any other attack type, including throw attacks using the Knife of the Undermountain King itself. However, Organ Rearranger's damage reroll does stack with itself (via a second Knife of the Undermountain King due to the King's Knife or Invoke Duplicity bugs) or dual wielding with Twist of Fortune . The improvement of the second reroll is smaller than the first one.

## Polearm Master: Bonus Attack
- **来源**: [Polearm Master: Bonus Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Polearm_Master:_Bonus_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Polearm Master: Bonus Attack is a passive feature provided by the Polearm Master Feat . When attacking with a polearm, you can make an additional weaker attack with the butt of the polearm using a Bonus Action . Description When attacking with a Glaive , Halberd , Pike , Quarterstaff , or Spear , you can use a Bonus Action to attack with the butt of your weapon. This attack does 1d4 (1~4) + Strength or Dexterity modifier ⁠ Bludgeoning Grants: Polearm Clout How to learn Granted by the feats: Polearm Master Notes The damage modifier of this attack uses Strength or Dexterity , whichever is higher, even if the weapon does not have the finesse property, or Charisma in the case of Pact of the Blade / Bind Hexed Weapon . It does not change to spellcasting modifier in the case of Shillelagh . It is not stated in-game but Polearm Mastery works with Pikes too. Polearm Master is coded to work with any weapon that is tagged as a SPEAR or STAVE (quarterstaffs), and weapons with Extra Reach (Glaives, Halberds and Pikes ) This attack can only be triggered once per turn. Therefore, a Thief who gains Extra Attack through multiclassing cannot twice benefit from Polearm Master: Bonus Attack , even though they have two bonus actions. This behaviour is different from that of Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike , which can be used twice (e.g., by attacking with an action, making a bonus action attack, then making the attack granted by Extra Attack, then making a second bonus action attack.)
## Polearm Master: Opportunity Attack
- **来源**: [Polearm Master: Opportunity Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Polearm_Master:_Opportunity_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Polearm Master: Opportunity Attack is a passive feature provided by the Polearm Master Feat . When an enemy approaches your melee range, you can spend a Reaction to make an attack. Description When wielding a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear, you can make an Opportunity Attack when a target comes within range. Prerequisite: Must be wielding a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear. How to learn Granted by the feats: Polearm Master Notes Cannot be triggered by moving forcibly an enemy into the range, for example, by shoving. Unlike the regular Opportunity Attack , this feature is able to be used while under the protection of Sanctuary but will immediately break the effect. Bugs This feature is still able to attack targets that have either Panache or Fancy Footwork . Due to a reaction timing issue, this feature does not function with Sentinel: Snare and a weapon with Extra Reach to stop creatures from entering within their 1.5 m (5 ft) melee range. The Opportunity Attack reaction window will prompt at 2.5 m (8 ft), but the attack will not be made until the creature has already moved to within 1.5 m (5 ft).
## Portent
- **来源**: [Portent](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Portent)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Not to be confused with potent Portent is a Divination School Wizard passive feature which offers the user glimpses into the future. They gain two random Portent Dice which they can use as a Reaction to substitute into Attack Rolls and Saving Throws rolled in range. Description Your dreams grant you glimpses that let you influence the future. After each Long Rest , the user gains two random Portent Dice. During the day, they can use their reaction to change the die of an Attack Roll or Saving Throw rolled near them to one of their Portent Dice. Each Portent Die can only be used once; unused Portent Dice are lost at the end of the day. Portent can only change a die in the favour of the caster and their allies. Attack rolls can only be changed from a miss to a hit for allies, and from a hit to a miss for enemies. Saving throws can only be changed from a fail to a success on allies, and from a success to a fail on enemies. Portent counts creatures marked yellow as allies. This means if the user initiates combat by attacking an enemy marked as yellow, the user cannot change the target's saving throw from succeeding to failing, only the opposite. Be careful, as the game may prompt for this. Portent ignores most saving throws not built into actions; see Events ignored by reactions for exceptions one can use with Portent. Details Recharge: Long rest Grants: Portent Die How to learn Classes: Class level 2: Divination School Notes The available Portent Dice and their values appear on the reactions tab of the user's spellbook, and over the hotbar on the right side. Spending a Portent Die is done as a reaction, but does not consume a Reaction . The value shown in the reaction window shows the current roll including modifiers, but Portent Dice replace the value before modifiers. This is why the reaction window may say something like "Rolled 17, needs 18", but the user can change it to a 15 and still succeed because they have a bonus of +3. In the reaction window, the user can hover over the number to see what they rolled, and what the modifiers are. Portent only needs either the target or source of the roll to be within range (18 m / 60 ft) - it does not require line-of-sight. Portent Die can cause an attack to become a critical hit if its value is in the user's critical hit range. The user can long rest or partial rest to replace their portent dice with a new full set. Expert Divination provides one extra portent die each long rest. It also generates Prophecies capable to refresh each spent dice. This means the Divination Wizard can use up to 3 dice per short rest now. A wizard cannot normally have repeated value Portent dice; the game engine grants unique dice values after every long rest, though a bug in Prophecy fulfillment contains a known exception (see bug below). Enemies with Legendary Resistance that do not need it to initially pass a save will not use it to overpower a Portent reaction to the same save. Bugs Portent does not trigger in the following situations: An ally's attack misses due to rolling a natural 1 but the (modified) roll meets or exceeds the target's AC An ally's attack misses and the Portent roll, if used, would be under the target's AC yet would critically hit due to an expanded critical threshold (for Portent Dice below 20) An enemy critically hits but the roll is under the target's AC An enemy save succeeds due to Legendary Resistance Portent sometimes triggers unnecessarily due to misinterpreting critical hits or misses as non-critical, or wrongly assuming Portent Dice of 1 or 20 automatically fail or succeed a saving throw. Divination Wizards can only have one die per value, yet the game only ensures unique values for Portent dice granted after long rests. This means a fulfilled Prophecy (achieved outside of resting) might result in no extra die if the Wizard already has a die with the same value. For example, a Wizard with 2 Portent dice has a 10% chance of not getting a new die, while a Wizard with a single die has a 5% chance. Casting area spells while not in turn-based mode breaks the regular limits of Divination Wizard abilities: The same Portent die can be used against all enemies. Casting crowd-control spells like Hypnotic Pattern before joining combat can easily result in all enemies disabled by forcing a fail on their saving throw by spending a single Portent die. Prophecies activated by dealing some typed damage can be triggered multiple times, resulting in multiple new Portent dice, often overcoming the limit of 3. Example: Casting a Fireball with Lightning Charges against a group of 5 enemies before joining combat under both Prophecy: Burn After Reading and Prophecy: Shocking Revelation results in up to 10 new Portent dice for the Divination Wizard, as both prophecies will be triggered once per enemy. v t e Wizard Subclasses Abjuration School Bladesinging Conjuration School Divination School Enchantment School Evocation School Illusion School Necromancy School Transmutation School Spells Abjuration Conjuration Divination Enchantment Evocation Illusion Necromancy Transmutation Other class features Arcane Recovery Arcane Ward Benign Transposition: Teleport Bladesong Empowered Evocation Experimental Alchemy Expert Divination Extra Attack Focused Conjuration Grim Harvest Hypnotic Gaze Illusory Self Improved Abjuration Improved Minor Illusion Instinctive Charm Inured to Undeath Minor Conjuration: Create Water Portent Potent Cantrip Projected Ward Sculpt Spells See Invisibility Shapechanger Song of Defence Split Enchantment Third Eye: Darkvision Third Eye: See Invisibility Training in War and Song Transmuter's Stone Undead Thralls Animate Dead Additional Undead Better Summons

## Reliable Talent
- **来源**: [Reliable Talent](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Reliable_Talent)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Reliable Talent is a passive feature gained by rogues at level 11. It treats any roll under 10 as a 10. Description When you make an Ability Check with a Skill you are Proficient with, the lowest result you can roll on the die is 10. How to learn Classes: Class level 11: Rogue Used by creatures: Assassin's Folly , Dolor , Elliot , Fishbait Arno , Friol , Lady Lockjaw , Nine-Fingers Keene , Orin , Roah Moonglow , Snapbone Notes This is a very versatile class feature, as it removes the floor principle of bounded accuracy [ 1 ] on all ability checks where a rogue has proficiency. When applied, this passive changes a d20 roll lower than 10 (including a 1) to a 10; modifiers are still applied afterwards. This can make skill checks of low to moderate DC where a rogue has proficiency guaranteed to succeed, and removes the chance to critically fail on those ability checks. This passive works well with the Githyanki racial feature Astral Knowledge . This passive helps in combat with Stealth checks, such as those made while using Greater Invisibility , and Athletics checks to Throw or Shove enemies. For a multiclassed rogue character with this feature, it may be advisable to start as a rogue at level 1 (or respec with Withers to do so) for proficiency in four skills. Bugs When Karmic Dice are enabled, opposed dialog checks have a chance of automatically failing. This includes rolls that would have otherwise been a guaranteed success due to Reliable Talent. The religion checks against the Mirror of Loss are a notable example of where this can be detrimental References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ For a detailed explanation of bounded accuracy, see Understanding Bounded Accuracy on the D&D Wiki. v t e Rogue Subclasses Arcane Trickster Assassin Swashbuckler Thief Cunning Action Dash Disengage Hide Sneak Attack Sneak Attack (Melee) Sneak Attack (Ranged) Rakish Sneak Attack (Melee) Rakish Sneak Attack (Ranged) Other class features Assassin's Alacrity Assassinate: Ambush Assassinate: Initiative Dirty Trick Flick o' the Wrist Sand Toss Vicious Mockery Expertise Evasion Fancy Footwork Fast Hands Infiltration Expertise Mage Hand Legerdemain Magical Ambush Panache Rakish Audacity Reliable Talent Second-Story Work Supreme Sneak Uncanny Dodge

## Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency
- **来源**: [Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Remarkable_Athlete:_Proficiency)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency is a Champion Fighter passive feature that adds half of their Proficiency Bonus to any Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution Checks they are not Proficient in. Description You're a master of your own body, your athletic prowess extended beyond the usual. You can add half of your Proficiency Bonus to any Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution Checks that you are not Proficient in. How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Champion Notes The skills that can be boosted by this feature are Athletics , Acrobatics , Sleight of Hand , and Stealth . There are no skill checks that use Constitution. Unlike the tabletop version, this version does not grant a bonus to Initiative rolls as they are not considered Dexterity checks. As this ability only boosts physical skills, it may be worth considering to prioritize getting mental skills instead, such as Perception or Survival . When calculating the bonus for this feature, the result is rounded down after dividing by 2. This means with a proficiency bonus of 3, this feature will provide a bonus of just +1. As such, this feature will only provide a bonus of +1 until the character reaches level 9, at which point the bonus will increase to +2. The bonus does not appear on your character sheet, but is nevertheless applied when making applicable skill checks. v t e Fighter Subclasses Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Fighting Styles Archery Defence Duelling Great Weapon Fighting Protection Two-Weapon Fighting Manoeuvres Commander's Strike Disarming Attack Distracting Strike Evasive Footwork Feinting Attack Goading Attack Manoeuvring Attack Menacing Attack Precision Attack Pushing Attack Rally Riposte Sweeping Attack Trip Attack Arcane Shots Banishing Arrow Beguiling Arrow Bursting Arrow Enfeebling Arrow Grasping Arrow Piercing Arrow Seeking Arrow Shadow Arrow Other class features Action Surge Curving Shot Eldritch Strike Extra Attack Improved Critical Hit Improved Extra Attack Improved Combat Superiority Indomitable Magic Arrow Remarkable Athlete: Jump Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency Second Wind War Magic Weapon Bond

## Savage Attacker
- **来源**: [Savage Attacker](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Savage_Attacker)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Not to be confused with Savage Attacks Savage Attacker is a passive feature provided by the feat of the same name. Your attacks become more fierce, and you deal damage at a higher level than usual when dealing melee weapon damage. Description When making melee weapon attacks, you roll your damage dice twice and use the highest result. How to learn Granted by the feats: Savage Attacker (Feat) Used by creatures: Bao'ek'nuk , Bugbear , Chop , Fyodor , Gilded Minotaur , Grukkoh , Hairy Henry , Holli Dylford , Lady Ague , Lady Flux , Lady Quinsy , Minotaur , Scrawny Bugbear , Severn , Stimk , Teghun Notes When used in combination with Great Weapon Fighting , Great Weapon Fighting is applied before selecting the highest damage roll with this feat: Great Weapon Fighting will do a first roll and reroll if it is a 1 or 2, while Savage Attacker will then roll one more time for each roll and use the highest result. When making a melee attack roll , this Passive Feature is known to affect damage riders (see Damage Mechanics ) such as Divine Smite . Specifically, damage rolls for these damage riders are rolled twice for the higher result. Unknown if this mechanic interaction is bugged or intended. As of patch 7 this feat does now apply to Sneak Attacks , Blade Flourishes , and Manoeuvres . Each damage die is rolled twice independently, even for weapons that deal 2d6 damage. For example if a 2d6 weapon rolls 1 and 5 rerolled respectively into 3 and 4, the total damage would be 3 + 5 = 8 and not 7. This feat essentially means you have Advantage on your damage rolls. The average bonus to your damage becomes, depending on what dice the weapon uses (for the math, see the math section on the advantage page ): Weapon deals 1d4 damage: average bonus damage is 0.625 (+25.0%) Weapon deals 1d6 damage: average bonus damage is 0.972 (+27.8%) Weapon deals 1d8 damage: average bonus damage is 1.313 (+29.2%) Weapon deals 1d10 damage: average bonus damage is 1.650 (+30.0%) Weapon deals 1d12 damage: average bonus damage is 1.986 (+30.6%) Weapon deals 2d6 damage: average bonus damage is 1.944 (+27.8%) For example, the Halberd of Vigilance (1d10 slashing damage and 1d4 force damage) which was dipped in fire (1d4 fire damage) will, on average, do 1.65 + 0.625 + 0.625 = 2.9 (+27.6%) more damage with Savage Attacker. When throwing weapons with the Thrown property, Savage Attacker will apply to the roll for the base weapon damage, but not any additional damage riders such as Ring of Flinging .
## Savage Attacks
- **来源**: [Savage Attacks](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Savage_Attacks)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Not to be confused with Savage Attacker See also: Brutal Critical Savage Attacks is a passive feature available to half-orcs . When they score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, they can roll one of the weapon’s damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit. Description When you land a Critical Hit with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. How to learn Races: Character level 1: Half-orc ( Character level is the sum of all class levels for a multi-classed character.) Used by creatures: Kerz , Skoona Notes Off-hand weapons also roll an extra damage die on critical hits. In additional to the one extra weapon damage die provided by this feature, it also adds a second extra damage die to a Divine Smite or Sneak Attack critical hit (although for Sneak Attacks, this is only true when triggered as a reaction). However, in either case, the second extra damage die is not applied in honour mode. Specifically, in honour mode, if a player character has this passive feature and scores a critical hit, savage attack will not add a second extra damage die to that of Divine Smite or Sneak Attack . This is likely due to the DRS mechanic , which has mostly been removed from honour ruleset. Under the honour ruleset, Sneak Attack damage (when triggered as a reaction) and Smite damage are considered separately from the base attack. This feature does not work with unarmed attacks or Wildshape melee attacks. Both Savage Attacks and Brutal Critical can activate at the same time on a critical hit. Although previously stated in the main description, for clarity it is expanded upon here: weapons with multiple damage die will only gain one die of extra damage, not the full dice set. For example, a great sword's normal critical hit does 4d6; this passive will add 1d6, totalling 5d6. A great axe's normal critical hit damage is 2d12; this passive will add 1d12, totaling 3d12. Brief preview Upon landing a melee critical , rolls an extra damage die.

How to learn Granted by the equipment: Moon Devotion Robe Used by creatures: Isobel Bugs Although Selûne's Protection should be activated by Lunar Bulwark , it is not; the wearer must instead have the regular version of Mage Armour cast on them for its radiant damage to function. - **来源**: [Sentinel: Snare](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Sentinel:_Snare)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Sentinel: Snare is a passive feature obtainable by the Sentinel Feat . Users of this feature are able to stop enemies in their tracks if you hit them with an Opportunity Attack . Description When you hit a creature with an Opportunity Attack , it can no longer move for the rest of its turn. Condition: Sentinel Foe Sentinel Foe Duration: 1 turn Can't move. Restrained by an Opportunity Attack from a Sentinel. How to learn Granted by the feats: Sentinel Used by creatures: Blythe , Cirian , Derysia , Eni , Feona , Fustian , Glyria , Hoarding Merregon , Kevo Phogge , M'alice , Merregon Legionnaire , Mitchia , Nov Shmoz , Rycke , Spaulder , Vengeful Merregon Bugs When used by unarmed characters, such as monks and druids in Wild Shape, the Damage Roll is empty in the combat log as this passive forces a melee weapon attack via Target_Sentinel_AttackOfOpportunity instead of the typical UseAttack() function. Unarmed Strike damage will still be correctly dealt.
## Sentinel: Vengeance
- **来源**: [Sentinel: Vengeance](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Sentinel:_Vengeance)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Sentintel: Vengeance is a passive feature obtainable by the Sentinel Feat . Users of this feature can attack enemies who attack an ally within your melee range. Description When an enemy in melee range attacks an ally, you can use a Reaction to make a weapon attack against that enemy. Target ally must not have the Sentinel feat. How to learn Granted by the feats: Sentinel Used by creatures: Blythe , Cirian , Derysia , Eni , Feona , Fustian , Glyria , Hoarding Merregon , Kevo Phogge , M'alice , Merregon Legionnaire , Mitchia , Nov Shmoz , Rycke , Spaulder , Vengeful Merregon Notes If two player characters, A and B, are simultaneously active in combat (due to initiative order) and character A has the Sentinel feat, then character B can trigger a Sentinel: Vengeance attack by forcing an enemy close to character A to make an Opportunity Attack . Character A may also receive Extra Attack for this attack. Sentinel: Vengeance attacks with both weapons if dual wield attacks is toggled on. If a character uses their reaction attack outside of their turn, they will attack with both weapons. If a character uses their reaction attack during their turn (character A as detailed in the example above), they must still have a bonus action available to get the two attacks. Given this, it may be advisable to save a bonus action for anticipated reaction attacks. Unlike Opportunity Attack, Sentinel : Vengeance attack is triggered even while wielding a ranged weapon. Sentinel: Snare does not apply to this attack, and an enemy hit with this attack can still move. This can be used to avoid getting stuck against enemies with the Sentinel feat. While the other Sentinel feats apply to druids in Wild Shape, this only applies to the Wild Shape forms that wield weapons: Air, Fire, and Water Myrmidons. Bugs Despite the description stating a weapon attack is made, and that it only functions with Wild Shape forms that wield weapons, there is no restricton for non-Wild Shape creatures to be wielding a weapon. Unarmed characters will make an unarmed attack.

## Skinburster Force
- **来源**: [Skinburster Force](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Skinburster_Force)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Skinburster Force is a passive feature. Description When the wielder deals melee damage with this weapon, they gain 2 turns of Force Conduit . Condition: Force Conduit Force Conduit Duration: 2 turns ⁠ Bludgeoning , ⁠ Piercing , and ⁠ Slashing damage against the affected entity is reduced by 1 per turn remaining. If the entity takes damage while it has 5 or more turns remaining, it deals 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Force DRS damage in a 6 m (20 ft) radius. Maximum Duration: 7 turns. How to learn Granted by the weapons: The Skinburster Notes Skinburster Force can stack multiple times per attack when using Cleave or similar multi-hit abilities. Bugs Skinburster Force triggers multiple times per attack with spells that are considered weapon attacks and include multiple DealDamage functions, such as Booming Blade and the various Smite spells. After successfully dealing damage with an attack, this passive's code incorrectly checks the target of the attack for turns of Force Conduit instead of the attacker , and applies certain technical conditions to the target instead of the attacker. As a result, this passive triggers effects such as Coldbrim Chill from Coldbrim Hat against the target.

## Slayer's Extra Attack
- **来源**: [Slayer's Extra Attack](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Slayer's_Extra_Attack)
- **分类**: Passive_features

This article is about the base version of the passive used in Slayer form. For the improved version granted at level 10, see Slayer's Improved Extra Attack . For the normal class feature, see Extra Attack . Slayer's Extra Attack is a passive feature available to the Slayer , granting it two additional attacks. Description You can make one additional attack after attacking with your main-hand weapon. How to learn Used by creatures: Slayer Notes Normally, Extra Attack only works with actions which use weapon or unarmed Attack Rolls , but this version of the feature is triggered by any of the Slayer's unique abilities which consume Actions , even the ones that are not attacks. These are: Multiattack - Attack Roll Slay - Attack Roll Let the Slaughter Begin - Constitution Saving Throw Sumptuous Blood Bath - Constitution Saving Throw While the non-attack roll actions trigger Slayer's Extra Attack, they cannot be used as the free follow up attack. In order to use them with Slayer's Extra Attack, they must be the initial action. For example, it is possible use Sumptuous Blood Bath and then Slay as the free Extra Attack action, but not vice versa. At level 10, this passive grants two additional attacks. Bugs The in-game description for this passive is copied from Slayer's Improved Extra Attack and states that it grants two additional attacks, but it actually only grants one. It also does not require an attack with a main-hand weapon.

## Slow: Actions
- **来源**: [Slow: Actions](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Slow:_Actions)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Slow: Actions is a passive feature applied to a target afflicted with Slowed and is a component of the Slow effect. Description You can't take both an action and a bonus action. If you take an action, you lose a bonus action, and vice versa. You also can't make more than 1 attack per turn. How to learn Other ways to learn: Applied to creatures afflicted with Slowed . Notes The resource limitation component of this effect does not function exactly as described. Instead, a single resource of one type will be removed after consuming all the resources of the other type. For example, a Thief with 1 Action and 2 Bonus Actions will not lose the action point until consuming both bonus actions. Conversely, using the action will only remove a single bonus action. Also, since the the resources are not removed until afterwards, consuming both resources simultaneously such as with Searing Smite will bypass this effect. Bugs This passive does not prevent a creature from making multiple attacks unless they somehow receive it between attacks on their own turn.

On 11 or higher, you hang in prepare phase and skip turn. On your next turn you must spend an action point and finish casting. If you don't have an action point, the spell is cancelled. As such, it does not trigger effects like Blessed Mercy from The Whispering Promise . The healing occurs when Bardic Inspiration is given to a creature, not when they actually use it. ## Soul Catching
- **来源**: [Soul Catching](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Soul_Catching)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Soul Catching is a passive feature granted to the wearer of the Gloves of Soul Catching . After landing an unarmed or throwing attack, the wearer can heal 10 hit points or gain a +5 bonus to a single attack roll or saving throw. Only one of these options can be used each turn. Description Once per turn, on an unarmed hit, you regain 10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points . Alternatively, you may forego healing to gain a +5 bonus on an Attack Roll or Saving Throw until the end of your next turn. [ See: Bugs ] Details Recharge: Per turn Grants: Soul Catching Boon Soul Catching Prowess Soul Snare: Heal Condition: Grasp Essence Grasp Essence Duration: 2 turns When you hit a creature with an unarmed attack, you can regain 10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points or choose to gain Advantage on Attack Rolls or Saving Throws before the end of your next turn. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gloves of Soul Catching Bugs Soul Catching has numerous errors: It states it requires an 'unarmed hit' while the Grasp Essence condition states "hit a creature with an unarmed attack". Functionally, any damaging unarmed attack will trigger the effect, even against world items. It states the wielder regains 10 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points , but instead it grants an a free action that, when used, provides the healing. It states the wielder may gain Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of their next turn, while the Grasp Essence condition states the wielder may gain Advantage on attack rolls or saving throws before the end of their next turn. Advantage is not actually gained, but rather a free reaction is granted that provides the wielder with a choice of either adding a +5 bonus to a single attack roll or to a single saving throw, at which time the Grasp Essence condition is removed. Due to a coding error, Grasp Essence is removed from the wielder if they take damage and do not have any temporary HP.

## Spell Sniper
- **来源**: [Spell Sniper](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Spell_Sniper)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Spell Sniper is a passive feature obtainable by a Feat of the same name. Users with this feature have learned an additional cantrip, and are more likely to critical hit with a spell. Description You learn a cantrip, and the number you need to roll a Critical Hit while attacking with a Spell is reduced by 1. This effect can stack. The cantrip must be one of: Bone Chill Eldritch Blast Fire Bolt Ray of Frost Shocking Grasp Thorn Whip How to learn Granted by the feats: Spell Sniper (Feat) Used by creatures: Ellice , Elminster , Ghislev , Grice , Grimlark , Hivune , Horriss , Notar Esojac Notes The critical hit roll bonus applies to all spells with a spell attack roll. Spells like Booming Blade and Searing Smite which make weapon attack rolls do not benefit. These cantrips do scale with character level. So a Level 5 Fighter with Spell Sniper will send two rays with Eldritch Blast, or roll two damage dice for Ray of Frost. These cantrips use the character's Spellcasting Ability for the class selected when gaining this feat. For example, if a Cleric class level is selected when gaining this feat and the character chooses Eldritch Blast with this feat, their Wisdom modifier is used, not their Charisma modifier.

Spellmight is a toggleable passive feature that allows a caster to steady their hand, dealing excellent damage if it hits, Description When casting a spell that requires an Attack Roll , you can take a -5 penalty to the roll to deal an additional 1d8 damage. - **分类**: Passive_features

Stillness of Mind is a Monk passive feature that automatically calms the user if they are Charmed or Frightened. ## Stirring Execution
- **来源**: [Stirring Execution](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Stirring_Execution)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Stirring Execution is a passive feature which grants allies temporary hit points based on their respective Charisma modifiers when the wielder of Duke Ravengard's Longsword kills an enemy. Description When you kill an enemy, allies within 9 m (30 ft) gain temporary hit points equal to your [ See: Bugs ] Charisma Modifier (minimum 1). Condition: Temporary Hit Points (Stirring Execution) Temporary Hit Points Affected entity has gained Charisma modifier temporary hit points . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Duke Ravengard's Longsword Used by creatures: Ulder Ravengard Bugs The temporary hit points are actually based on the Charisma modifiers of the characters receiving them, not the character delivering the killing blow with this sword. The minimum of 1 still applies. The temporary hit points only have a StackPriority of 1, and as such are overridden by any other source of temporary hit points which have a StackPriority of 1 or higher, even if the new source is of a lesser value. Used by creatures: , Aminah , Anouk , Argram , Barcus Wroot , Beldron , Belub , Bonna , Brathwen , Brithvar , Brounce , Bumpnagel , Dalthar , Danna , Drar , Duergar Spore Servant (guard caster) , Dulbers Frint , Dunnol , Elenna Thrinn , Fonmara , Fuffi Fuffers , Fulguro , Garmor , Gekh Coal , Gergerann , Gipkins Jared , Greymon , Grumm , Grundril , Havkelaag , Hogi Nuners , Holvik , Hurk , Jerris , Kettel , Kirgrath , Kith , Kree Derryck , Kur , Laridda , Lava Elemental , Lorlarrio , Lunkbug , Lurgan , Magmar , Meerna , Minthara , Mirthis , Moorcombe , Morghal , Morgya , Murmath , Orgarth , Philomeen , Pistle , Shadow-Cursed Needle Blight , Shadow-Cursed Shambling Mound , Shattered Duergar , Skarjall , Skickpit , Thudd , Thulla , Ver'yll Wenkiir , Viss , Welso , Wicky , Wrint Sprigley , Zombie Minthara Notes When a hiding creature enters the line of sight of a non-allied creature with superior darkvision, and is within the range of superior darkvision: Being Lightly Obscured counts as being under Clear Area instead. Being Heavily Obscured counts as being Lightly Obscured instead. Bugs The passive vision cone from Superior Darkvision is non-functional for Duergar. They possess both the 'Darkvision' and 'Superior Darkvision' passives, and because of how the conflict between these two is resolved by the game-engine for this race, the smaller vision cone from standard Darkvision always overwrites the larger one from Superior Darkvision. However, Superior Darkvision still prevents Disadvantage from a larger distance (24 m (80 ft)) compared to standard Darkvision (12 m (40 ft)).

## Tavern Brawler
- **来源**: [Tavern Brawler](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tavern_Brawler)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Tavern Brawler is a passive feature granted by the feat of the same name. It increases the accuracy and damage of Unarmed Strikes , Throw attacks, and Improvised Melee Weapon attacks. Description When you make an unarmed attack, use an improvised weapon, or throw something, your Strength Modifier is added to the damage and Attack Rolls an additional time. How to learn Granted by the feats: Tavern Brawler (Feat) Notes This feat always adds the Strength modifier. For example, if an Unarmed Strike is made with Dexterity , both Dexterity and Strength modifiers will be added a single time. Druids in Wild Shape receive the bonus, except when wild shaped as a Fire , Water , or Air Myrmidon . Characters (and Wild Shape forms) with negative Strength modifiers have their attack and damage rolls reduced an additional time by this feat. This does not apply to damage from Throw and Improvised Melee Weapon attacks, [ 1 ] however, because Tavern Brawler adds a separate damage source which cannot deal less than 0 damage. When a creature is Thrown , it takes extra damage from Tavern Brawler when it lands. [ 1 ] This feat, especially in conjunction with high Strength, is considered to be one of the strongest in the game, as it significantly increases both the likelihood of a hit and the damage dealt. [ 2 ] It also benefits from a number of synergies: Halfling Luck , which significantly reduces the odds of a critical miss when an attack roll would succeed on a 2 or higher, as Tavern Brawler enables. Normally, there is a 1 in 20 chance of a miss on such an attack, but for halflings there is only a 1 in 400 chance (or 1 in 160,000 with Advantage ). When making a Throw attack or Improvised Melee Weapon attack, the additional damage of Tavern Brawler is treated as a DRS . [ 1 ] Bugs As of Patch 8, bonus damage from this feat bypasses Sturdy and similar conditions when attacking with Throw . [ 1 ] As of Patch 8, this feat applies to the damage of several spells and effects while the caster is in Wild Shape , including spells like Spike Growth and items like Noxious Spore Grenades . Wild Shapes with low Strength have a penalty applied to the damage rolls of these spells and effects. Additional elemental damage from attacks while in Wild Shape , such as ⁠ Acid damage from Corrosive Spit or ⁠ Thunder damage from Grounded Thunder Strike , will receive an additional damage bonus, even in Honour Mode. The additional damage of Tavern Brawler applied to Throw attacks, Improvised Melee Weapon attacks, and certain attacks in Wild Shape [ verify ] has no damage type and therefore can never be resisted, [ 1 ] even by an Elixir of Universal Resistance or Warding Bond (In this case, both the caster and target take full damage). Flat damage reduction effects still apply. In Honour Mode, Improvised Melee Weapon attacks do not receive extra damage from Tavern Brawler. They receive a bonus to attack rolls as expected. Although using Throw on anything but Thrown weapons behaves similarly to Improvised Melee Weapon , Throw attacks always benefit from both the attack roll and damage benefits of Tavern Brawler. However, when throwing a creature in Honour Mode, the creature will not receive extra damage from Tavern Brawler when landing. References [ edit section | visual editor ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 1.4 Except in Honour Mode. ↑ This is arguably a significant deviation from the bounded accuracy principle [ url 1 ] of D&D 5e, which aims to keep ACs, DCs, and roll modifiers within a certain range to ensure that the outcome of an action is determined by a d20 roll, rather than many flat modifiers stacked together. To put this feat's bonuses into better context, imagine the DM gives a player character the +10 damage from the Great Weapon Master Feat, but then also gives them a +5 to attack rolls instead of the normal -5 . ↑ YouTube: @exoethan (2023-11-27). (BG3) Why exactly is Tavern Brawler so OP? . Retrieved 2025-12-26.

## The Comeback
- **来源**: [The Comeback](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Comeback)
- **分类**: Passive_features

The Comeback is a passive feature that grants a creature temporary HP when you heal them. Description When the wearer heals a target, it gains an additional 3 temporary hit points . Can only have temporary hit points from one source. Condition: Temporary Hit Points (3) Temporary Hit Points Kept from death's door by a brief magical boost. Gained 3 temporary hit points . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Boots of Aid and Comfort Notes The target of the healing, not the healer, gets the temporary hit points from The Comeback . Healing multiple creatures at the same time (e.g. via Mass Healing Word ) will grant temporary hit points to all of them. Taking a Short Rest counts as healing oneself and grants the temporary hit points to the wearer, but not to other characters benefiting from the same short rest. The temporary hit points will still be granted if the wearer directs a healing effect at a target that's already at full hit points. However, they will not be granted if the target can't be healed for some other reason, such as being under the effect of Bone Chill .
