## The Scourge Mistress' Bane
- **来源**: [The Scourge Mistress' Bane](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Scourge_Mistress'_Bane)
- **分类**: Passive_features

The Scourge Mistress' Bane is a passive feature that can apply Bane but will hurt the wielder if they are too healthy. Description Chance to inflict upon the target a 1d4 penalty to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . If the attacker still has 50% or more hit points , they take 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Piercing themselves. A Baned creature receives a 1d4 penalty to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws. Condition: Bane Bane Duration: 2 turns Has a -1d4 penalty to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws . How to learn Granted by the weapons: Ritual Axe Notes The Bane condition applied by this weapon is the same as the Bane spell and does not stack. Because of the bug listed below, the Battle Master Fighter's Sweeping Attack applies this debuff to every target within the cone's area of effect, hit or miss. Many situations increase the self-damage dealt by this passive feature: The Savage Attacker feat results in secondary damage being re-rolled higher. A critical hit with this axe doubles the self-damage. Some damage riders such as Lightning Charges , radiant damage from the Callous Glow Ring and Psionic Overload increase the self-damage. Effects which reduce incoming piercing damage reduce the self-inflicted damage. However, as the self-damage is classified as magical, Heavy Armour Master damage reduction does not apply. If at 50% health or higher, the wielder suffers self-damage even if the target dies from the axe blow. Bugs While the item description says 'chance,' Bane is always inflicted on a hit. If the wielder of this axe is at 50% health or higher and they use Non-Lethal Damage to knock out an enemy with it, they will also be knocked out, even if at full HP.
## The Shadow Itself
- **来源**: [The Shadow Itself](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/The_Shadow_Itself)
- **分类**: Passive_features

The Shadow Itself is a passive feature that cloaks the wearer in invisibility whenever they kill an enemy. Description Once per turn when you kill an enemy, shroud yourself in primeval darkness to become Invisible for 2 turns. Details Recharge: Per turn Condition: Invisible Invisible Duration: 2 turns Has Advantage on Attack Rolls and imposes Disadvantage on enemy Attack Rolls. Invisibility ends early if the invisible entity attacks, casts another spell, interacts with an object, becomes wet, takes an action or bonus action, or is damaged. How to learn Granted by the equipment: The Deathstalker Mantle Notes The Shadow Itself only triggers once per turn, and only does so if the character kills an enemy directly while in combat mode. Examples of kills that do not trigger this effect include, but are not limited to: Indirect kills, such as attacking an incendiary barrel that then burns a nearby enemy to death. [ verify ] Killing an opponent by sniper-shot with a bow, out of combat. A creature killed from the wearer's casting of Cloud of Daggers Sneak Attack as a reaction . [ verify ] If a 'homing' weapon such as Returning Pike deals the killing blow to an enemy, then the weapon's return animation will cause the invisibility to end early. If the Dark Urge is played as origin and either Alfira or Quil are killed in camp by another (e.g., Astarion ) before finishing the Long Rest, conversation options in camp next morning proceed as if the player character killed them, and Sceleritas still meets with them upon their next Long rest, but does not reward the cape. Bugs There is a bug involving this item with the Illithid power Cull the Weak . If the equipping character has The Shadow Itself activated and kills a target, the effect does not activate (or immediately gets cancelled).

## Throw Damage Immunity
- **来源**: [Throw Damage Immunity](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Throw_Damage_Immunity)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Throw Damage Immunity is a passive feature exclusive to Boo which prevents him from receiving any damage when thrown. Description Creature is immune to being damaged by being thrown. How to learn Used by creatures: Boo Bugs When thrown, characters receive one turn of a hidden technical condition PRONE_AFTER_THROW that is removed on taking damage, and when removed applies Prone to the character. Normally, the damage taken from being thrown would trigger the removal of this technical condition and apply Prone, but this passive prevents that damage. Instead, the technical condition remains and ticks down at the start of the thrown character's turn, causing a delayed application of Prone.

Thunderbolt Strike is a Tempest Domain cleric passive feature that pushes Large or smaller creatures 3 m (10 ft) that are dealt ⁠ Thunder or ⁠ Lightning damage from the cleric. Description When you deal ⁠ Thunder or ⁠ Lightning damage to a creature that is Large or smaller, you can also push it up to 3 m (10 ft). ## Thunderous Conversion
- **来源**: [Thunderous Conversion](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Thunderous_Conversion)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Thunderous Conversion is a passive feature that disorients the user's target whenever they deal thunder, lightning or radiant damage. Description When the wearer deals ⁠ Thunder , ⁠ Lightning , or ⁠ Radiant damage, inflict 2 turns of Reverberation upon the target(s). Details Recharge: Per attack Condition: Reverberation Reverberation Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has a -1 penalty to Strength , Dexterity , and Constitution Saving Throws per remaining turn. When the entity has 5 or more turns of Reverberation, it takes 1d4 ⁠ ⁠ Thunder DRS damage and must succeed a DC  10 Constitution Saving Throw or fall Prone . The condition is removed afterward. Creatures Immune to ⁠ Thunder damage can't receive Reverberation. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gloves of Belligerent Skies Notes The ⁠ Lightning damage originating from Lightning Charges does not seem to trigger the item and thus does not apply Reverberation effect to targets unless on Honour difficulty rules. The ⁠ Radiant from Morninglord's Radiance , however, does trigger Reverberation - both on weapon and spell attacks. (as of 4.1.1.3648072) The ⁠ Thunder damage from Phalar Aluve: Shriek does not activate Thunderous Conversion unless on Honour difficulty rules. If the wearer's attack adds a 5th stack of Reverberation, the resulting Thunder damage re-applies two more stacks of Reverberation. Thunderous Conversion does not work with Moonbeam . Bugs Though stated "upon the target(s)", Thunderous Conversion can only trigger once per attack. This means that AoE spells (e.g., Radiance of the Dawn or Flame Strike ) can only apply Reverberation to the first target in the log order, leaving the rest without the effect. This also means that dealing multiple instances of damage in a single attack (e.g., with Lightning Arrow ) will still only apply 2 turns of Reverberation .
## Tides of Chaos (passive feature)
- **来源**: [Tides of Chaos (passive feature)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tides_of_Chaos_(passive_feature))

This article is about the toggleable passive to use Tides of Chaos before a roll is made. For the reaction to use it after a roll, see Tides of Chaos . Tides of Chaos is a Wild Magic sorcerer toggleable passive feature which grants Advantage on the sorcerer's next ability check. After this feature is triggered, the next spell cast has a greatly increased chance of a creating a Wild Magic surge (50% chance instead of the normal 5%). Alternatively, this feature can be triggered after a roll is failed with the corresponding reaction . Description Activate to gain Advantage on your next Attack Roll , Ability Check , or Saving Throw . Increased chance of Wild Magic surge afterwards. Details Cost: Tides of Chaos Charge Grants: Tides of Chaos Condition: Tides of Chaos Tides of Chaos Duration: Until Long rest Increased chance of Wild Magic surge (to 50%). Lost immediately after casting a Level 1 or higher Spell and rolling a Wild Magic Check. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Wild Magic Sorcerer Used by creatures: Jacelyn Notes Wild Magic Sorcerers receive 1 Tides of Chaos Charge which is replenished on every Short Rest or Long Rest . Normally, a  d20 is rolled each time a levelled spell is cast. If the result is 20, a Surge is triggered. Tides of Chaos reduces the Difficulty Class (DC) to 11 (i.e. a 50% chance). Bugs Tides of Chaos grants a toggleable passive by the same name which, when toggled on, provides Advantage on the character's next Ability Check. Due to the way this passive is granted, it defaults to "off" and cannot be toggled "on" the very first time it is acquired until after the character has first made an ability check, has had a condition applied to it, has used a short rest, or has taken a long rest. v t e Sorcerer Subclasses Draconic Bloodline Shadow Magic Storm Sorcery Wild Magic Metamagic Careful Spell Distant Spell Extended Spell Twinned Spell Heightened Spell Quickened Spell Subtle Spell Draconic Ancestry Red Black Blue White Green Gold Silver Bronze Copper Brass Heart of the Storm Lightning Thunder Resistance Other class features Bend Luck Controlled Chaos Create Spell Slot Create Sorcery Points Draconic Resilience Elemental Affinity: Damage Elemental Affinity: Resistance Eyes of the Dark Eyes of the Dark: Darkness Fly Hound of Ill Omen Shadow Walk Storm's Fury Strength of the Grave Tempestuous Magic Tides of Chaos Wild Magic Spells

## Titan Weapon
- **来源**: [Titan Weapon](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Titan_Weapon)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Titan Weapon is a passive feature that adds your Strength modifier to your ranged weapon attacks. Description This weapon deals additional damage equal to your Strength Modifier . The weapon only adds the modifier if it improves your chance to hit. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Titanstring Bow Notes Titan Weapon adds a minimum of +1 to the damage roll, even if the attacker has a Strength of 11 or lower. The bonus damage is in addition to the normal Dexterity bonus for ranged weapons. The bonus damage can be applied multiple times to a single ranged weapon attack. For example, special arrows with additional damage will receive the bonus to its additional damage, e.g. the additional Necrotic damage from Arrow of Ilmater will also receive bonus Necrotic damage equal to your Strength modifier. Another example is a rogue's Sneak Attack when used as a reaction. This is mostly changed in Honour mode , but the bonus damage can still apply to special arrows. The bonus damage applies to most Arcane Shots . Notably, Arcane Shot: Seeking Arrow and Arcane Shot: Piercing Arrow do not apply the bonus damage due to the lack of attack rolls for these actions. Bugs Titan Weapon has an extra description that states "The weapon only adds the modifier if it improves your chance to hit." but this has no actual function/relevance. The bonus damage from Strength is not reflected on the character sheet or Ranged Attack tooltip.
## Toggle Non-Lethal Attacks
- **来源**: [Toggle Non-Lethal Attacks](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Toggle_Non-Lethal_Attacks)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Toggle Non-Lethal Attacks is a common toggleable passive feature that allows users to knock targets out instead of killing them. Toggling on/off will apply to the entire party of playable characters, but not to summons such as familiars. While this passive is turned on, when an Unarmed Strike or melee weapon attack reduces a creatures hit points to zero or one, it becomes Knocked Out or Knocked Out (Temporary) . Description Knock someone Unconscious instead of killing them. Must be unarmed or using a melee weapon. Does not work undead , constructs or oozes . Details Toggleable Condition: Non-Lethal Damage Non-Lethal Damage Non-lethal damage does not kill creatures if it reduces their hit points to 0, it just leaves them unconscious. How to learn Used by creatures: Amphol , Augur Harxkellan , Drybeldiyx , Fallen Bhaalspawn , Gaheid Slickjaw , Klarrvox , Pritt Yellowbreath , Pythonicus , Surixana , Thomas C. Quirkilious , Zgorrellik Notes While in combat with a creature, if they have the condition Temporarily Hostile , they become Knocked Out (Temporary) ; after a long rest they regain consciousness. If the creature does not have this condition, it disappears permanently after a long rest, and in some cases may be treated as dead by the game. Healing a knocked-out character does not restore them to consciousness; only a long rest does so. It is still possible to loot most things from a Knocked Out except tadpoles, heads, etc. The feature can be found under the "Passives" section of the hotbar (or by expanding the action radial if using a controller). The icon that shows "Toggle Non-Lethal Attacks" must be pressed. Curiously enough, some non-melee attacks, like Monk's Deflect Missiles: Redirect are capable of taking benefit from this passive, knocking targets out instead of killing them. Most forms of damage caused by a melee attack still knock the creature out instead of killing it ( Smite , thunder damage from Cacophony , etc); but all spell damage kills it. Damage boosts that are directly added to the melee weapon or unarmed attack damage will knock the entity unconcious but any boosts that add to the damage calculation are not considered non-lethal and will still kill the damaged entity. Under most circumstances, the game treats Knocked Out characters as if they are Dead . However, there are a couple of instances where the game treats knocking out characters as a legitimate outcome. Normally, while playing as the Dark Urge , Alfira is to be unwittingly murdered upon Long Resting, after she she arrived at the camp. If Alfira is killed or knocked out before, Quil Grootslang appears in her stead. If Alfira survives until the end of the game, which is only possible by knocking her out before the murder event, she recognizes that the Dark Urge has stayed their hand and is grateful to them for sparing her. In both circumstances where Auntie Ethel is fought, her Mask servants can be knocked out and after a Long Rest after Ethel is killed, they are shown to be free from her control. It is possible to recruit Minthara while siding with the tiefling refugees by knocking her out. This allows her to show up in Moonrise Towers where she can be recruited, while the party can still complete ⁠ Save the Refugees . If demanded by Kethk to kill Varrl , the player character can spare him by knocking him out, allowing him to be healed after he is dragged out of the classroom. Marcus and his Imps always try to knock out Isobel when attempting to capture her in the Last Light Inn . Helping them kidnap her makes Ketheric grateful for bringing her back to him, and allows the player character to be rewarded by the Absolute. Should Isobel be killed, however, Ketheric instead is greatly upset, and sends the party to the Absolute as punishment. When fought in the sewers, Minsc must be knocked out in order to recruit him as well as to prevent Jaheira from permanently leaving the party. As long as Auntie Ethel has Vanra in her stomach, killing her leads to Vanra's death as well, unless the player character threw a Hag's Bane on her beforehand. Alternatively, Vanra can still be freed by knocking Ethel out, which allows the player character to cut her stomach open to release the child from her confinement. If Korilla is knocked out rather than killed during the fight against Raphael in the House of Hope , Hope is grateful to the player character for sparing her.

## Tranquillity
- **来源**: [Tranquillity](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Tranquillity)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Tranquillity is a Way of the Open Hand Monk passive feature that prevents enemies from directly harming the monk until the first time they attack each day (effectively a free use of Sanctuary ). Description Long Rests surround you with an aura of peace, granting you Sanctuary permanently until you attack. Condition: Sanctuary Sanctuary Affected entity can't be targeted by enemy attacks or spells. However, it can still take damage from spells that influence a larger area. Condition ends if the affected entity attacks or harms another creature, and will receive Sanctuary Blocked for 1 turn. Twist of Fortune is a passive feature that increases the consistency of the wielder's weapon damage. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Twist of Fortune Notes The Twist of Fortune passive appears to affect all melee damage rolls while equipped, not just damage with Twist of Fortune itself. ## Two-Weapon Fighting
- **来源**: [Two-Weapon Fighting](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Two-Weapon_Fighting)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Two-Weapon Fighting is a Fighting style passive feature. It allows characters to effectively dual-wield two weapons with the Light property, adding damage. Description When you make an offhand attack, you can add your Ability Score Modifier to the damage of the attack. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Fighter Class level 2: Ranger Class level 3: College of Swords Granted by the equipment: Gloves of the Balanced Hands Used by creatures: Antinia , Lord Shattershield's Attendant , Qora , Rycke , Skoona , Zurk Other ways to learn: Wielding Crimson Mischief in the off-hand Notes Multiple sources of Two-Weapon Fighting do not provide additional damage to off-hand attacks. Not to be confused with the Dual Wielder feat. During level up, the character will always have only one weapon visible at their back, even if two are equipped. Unlike tabletop 5e, the Two-Weapon Fighting Style provides no benefit to Thrown weapons in Baldur's Gate 3. While dual-wielding still allows for an off-hand throw attack via Bonus Action , BG3's game engine automatically adds the user's Ability Modifier to throw damage by default. Therefore, this Fighting Style – which grants the same modifier to off-hand strikes – is redundant for throwing. In tabletop D&D, this style is required to add Ability Modifier damage to an off-hand throw (PHB, p. 195). v t e Fighter Subclasses Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Fighting Styles Archery Defence Duelling Great Weapon Fighting Protection Two-Weapon Fighting Manoeuvres Commander's Strike Disarming Attack Distracting Strike Evasive Footwork Feinting Attack Goading Attack Manoeuvring Attack Menacing Attack Precision Attack Pushing Attack Rally Riposte Sweeping Attack Trip Attack Arcane Shots Banishing Arrow Beguiling Arrow Bursting Arrow Enfeebling Arrow Grasping Arrow Piercing Arrow Seeking Arrow Shadow Arrow Other class features Action Surge Curving Shot Eldritch Strike Extra Attack Improved Critical Hit Improved Extra Attack Improved Combat Superiority Indomitable Magic Arrow Remarkable Athlete: Jump Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency Second Wind War Magic Weapon Bond v t e Ranger Subclasses Beast Master Gloom Stalker Hunter Swarmkeeper Favoured Enemy Bounty Hunter Keeper of the Veil Mage Breaker Ranger Knight Sanctified Stalker Natural Explorer Beast Tamer Urban Tracker Wasteland Wanderer ( Cold Fire Poison ) Other class features Bestial Fury Companion's Bond Dread Ambusher Melee Ranged Hide Escape the Horde Exceptional Training Extra Attack Gathered Swarm Cloud of Jellyfish Flurry of Moths Legion of Bees Hide in Plain Sight Hunter's Prey Colossus Slayer Giant Killer Horde Breaker Iron Mind Land's Stride: Difficult Terrain Mighty Swarm Multiattack Defence Prey's Scent Spells Ranger's Companion Stalker's Flurry Steel Will Superior Darkvision Umbral Shroud Volley Whirlwind Attack Writhing Tide

## Unarmoured Defence (Barbarian)
- **来源**: [Unarmoured Defence (Barbarian)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unarmoured_Defence_(Barbarian))
- **分类**: Passive_features

Unarmoured Defence is a Barbarian passive feature that adds a character's Constitution modifier to their Armour Class in addition to their Dexterity modifier when not wearing armour . Description Your body is as resilient as any armour. While not wearing armour , you add your Constitution Modifier to your Armour Class . Wearing Heavy Armour impedes all positive effects of your Rage . This effect does not stack with Mage Armour. How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Barbarian Used by creatures: Abby , Arthus , Baff Elkhorn , Bearclaw , Bedi , Bombasto , Bor , Dror Ragzlin , Eldra Luthrinn , Garmor , Gleeful Clong , Haseid , Inku Neza , Kled , Lady Flux , Lobo Denysse , Lord Jannath's Bodyguard , Mask of Vengeance (The Blushing Mermaid) , Morgya , Rage Queller , Shiv Dahlia , Tusgront , Ulma , Vol , Zombie Dror Ragzlin Notes The normal base Armour Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier , while this changes it to 10 + Dexterity modifier + Constitution modifier . Characters with this passive still receive bonuses from other sources that do not change their base armour class like +1 AC robes , Bracers of Defence , Shield of Faith , etc. Helmets , Gloves and Footwear marked as Light , Medium or Heavy Armour count as armour, and prevent Unarmoured Defence from working. This works while wearing a Shield , unlike its Monk counterpart . Mage Armour , Draconic Resilience , Unarmoured Defence (Barbarian) , Unarmoured Defence (Monk) and Barkskin all change a character's base armour class and therefore do not stack. If a character has multiple of these they only benefit from the one that gives the most Armour Class . Unarmoured Defence works while in Wild Shape as long as the user has no armour equipped in any slot before they transform. This effect only works on forms with a base Armour Class less than this passive gives. ## Underdog's Bravery
- **来源**: [Underdog's Bravery](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Underdog's_Bravery)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Underdog's Bravery is a passive feature that improves the user's attacks while surrounded. Description The wearer gains Advantage on melee Attack Rolls while surrounded [ See: Bugs ] by 2 or more foes. How to learn Granted by the equipment: Gloves of the Growling Underdog Notes The enemies must be within 3 m (10 ft). This passive is limited to weapon attacks and does not function with Unarmed Strikes or melee spell attacks. Bugs Two or more enemies must be within 3 m (10 ft) of the target , not the wearer of the gloves. This means the wearer does not need to be 'surrounded' at all; they need enemies near the target of their attack. A character using a weapon with Extra Reach can gain Advantage without even having the Threatened condition. Incapacitated enemies, which are not supposed to count towards qualifying for this passive, will do so – as long as at least one enemy is not incapacitated. This feature may work against Ansur and the Dominated Red Dragon even when no other enemies are nearby, due to their hit proxies counting as separate enemies.

## Unstable Blood
- **来源**: [Unstable Blood](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Unstable_Blood)
- **分类**: Passive_features

See also: Unstable Blood (surface) Unstable Blood is a permanent passive feature which causes a creature's blood to explode when in contact with fire. Description Your blood is now highly flammable and will explode when in contact with fire. How to learn Other ways to learn: The player character must find Araj Oblodra in Moonrise Towers and give her a sample of their blood. When meeting her again in the Lower City , they must do so again and then drink the potion she offers to receive this passive feature. Notes When the player character would normally generate a Blood surface around them, they instead create Unstable Blood ; it becomes Fire if it receives fire damage. Total damage from surface can be increased by Lightning Charges , and Callous Glow Ring .

Bugs Unwavering does not prevent Difficult Terrain: Deep Water .

You also have a + 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage bonus to weapon and unarmed attacks. Grants: Ascendant Bite Misty Escape (Vampire Ascendant) How to learn Other ways to learn: Only available to Astarion after becoming an ascendant vampire. Notes Does not seem to apply when wild shaped , except for forms that attack with weapons. Bugs The in-game description states Astarion gains a + 1d10 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage bonus to Attack Rolls . ## Venomous Revenge
- **来源**: [Venomous Revenge](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Venomous_Revenge)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Venomous Revenge is a passive feature that coats the wearer's weapons with poison whenever they are healed. Description Whenever the wearer is healed, their weapon becomes coated in magic and deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Poison damage. Condition: Venomous Revenge Venomous Revenge Duration: 2 turns Affected entity has been recently healed, and its weapon attacks deal an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Poison . How to learn Granted by the equipment: Broodmother's Revenge Used by creatures: Kagha Notes Venomous Revenge applies to both melee and ranged weapons, but, as with all poison coatings , its effect does not work when a weapon is Thrown . The effect is triggered even with full health or when being picked up from a Downed state. The effect is triggered by: being targeted by any healing spell, like Healing Word . consuming any healing items, like a Potion of Healing , a Goodberry , or a Raspberry . all equipment with continuous regeneration effects: the Helm of Balduran and Ring of Regeneration . healing effects from the Derivation Cloak and Armour of Landfall . The effect is not triggered by: Most self-healing effects from equipment: Shattered Flail , Sword of Chaos , Woe , Robe of the Weave , Psionic Ward Armour , Vest of Soul Rejuvenation , Circlet of Mental Anguish , or Wapira's Crown . Healing from Transfuse Health . This effect interacts in the following ways with dipping and coatings: The effect overwrites Dipped in Fire and vice versa. The effect does not trigger for an already coated weapon (e.g. Drow Poison ). Coatings overwrite the effect.

## War Magic
- **来源**: [War Magic](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/War_Magic)
- **分类**: Passive_features

For the passive feature only available to githyanki NPCs, see Githyanki War Magic . War Magic is an Eldritch Knight Fighter passive feature. This allows the Fighter to make an attack after using a Cantrip by using a Bonus Action . Description You have honed your body and magic for war. After you cast a cantrip, you can make a weapon attack using a Bonus Action . How to learn Classes: Class level 7: Eldritch Knight Notes War Magic activates only once per round. However, each time it activates, it allows a character up to two Bonus Action attacks if they have multiple bonus actions (e.g., Fast Hands or Helmet of Grit ). Even if a character has three or more bonus actions, War Magic only allows for two attacks to be made. The bonus action attack can be any attack that normally works with Extra Attack , such as a Throw or Booming Blade . The bonus action attack does not activate Extra Attack. War Magic only triggers when casting a cantrip which costs an Action . It does not trigger on Bonus Action cantrips like Shillelagh or Sorrowful Lash . It does trigger when casting Booming Blade, but only if it is an initial attack; if Booming Blade is cast with Extra Attack, War Magic does not trigger. It triggers on certain weapon actions classified as cantrips, namely Hellflame Cleave and Moonmote . v t e Fighter Subclasses Arcane Archer Battle Master Champion Eldritch Knight Fighting Styles Archery Defence Duelling Great Weapon Fighting Protection Two-Weapon Fighting Manoeuvres Commander's Strike Disarming Attack Distracting Strike Evasive Footwork Feinting Attack Goading Attack Manoeuvring Attack Menacing Attack Precision Attack Pushing Attack Rally Riposte Sweeping Attack Trip Attack Arcane Shots Banishing Arrow Beguiling Arrow Bursting Arrow Enfeebling Arrow Grasping Arrow Piercing Arrow Seeking Arrow Shadow Arrow Other class features Action Surge Curving Shot Eldritch Strike Extra Attack Improved Critical Hit Improved Extra Attack Improved Combat Superiority Indomitable Magic Arrow Remarkable Athlete: Jump Remarkable Athlete: Proficiency Second Wind War Magic Weapon Bond

## Wild Magic (passive feature)
- **来源**: [Wild Magic (passive feature)](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Wild_Magic_(passive_feature))

For the Barbarian subclass, see Wild Magic (barbarian subclass) . Wild Magic is a passive feature which can trigger a random magical effect when casting a Level 1 or higher Spell. An effect is triggered when rolling a 20 on a  d20 (i.e., a 5% chance). Description Unruly magic sparks and fizzes through your veins. Each time you cast a spell of Level 1 or higher, your magic might surge and trigger a random magical effect . How to learn Classes: Class level 1: Wild Magic Sorcerer Used by creatures: Jacelyn Notes A  d20 is rolled each time you cast a leveled spell. If the result is 20, then a Wild Magic Surge is triggered (i.e., 5% chance). ## Willing Whip
- **来源**: [Willing Whip](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Willing_Whip)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Willing Whip is a passive feature that grants resistance to Necrotic damage but deals Necrotic damage to every creature nearby. Description Grants Resistance to ⁠ Necrotic damage. Deals an additional 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic DRS damage to nearby targets, including the wielder. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Loviatar's Scourge Used by creatures: Abdirak Notes Due to the resistance granted by this passive, fractional damage received by the wielder is rounded down, and they take only 0~3 ⁠ ⁠ Necrotic damage. However, nearby allies take full damage. Helldusk Armour , if used in conjunction with the above resistance, effectively negates all Necrotic damage otherwise inflicted upon the wielder by this passive. The area of effect is centred on the creature that is hit, and the radius is 2 m (7 ft). This feature is particularly useful against groupings of low-hit-point enemies that may otherwise have many opportunities to score critical hits against the party. If Lae'zel is in the party while fighting the murder of Shadow-Cursed Ravens on the Ruined Battlefield in Act Two at X: 30 Y: 114 , the area of effect damage from this passive may easily earn the Soldier 's ⁠ Pentacrush Inspiration , while taking little to no damage in the process. Attacks which deal multiple instances of damage, such as the various smite spells or Booming Blade , trigger multiple instances of Willing Whip. Similarly, weapon attacks that target multiple creatures, such as Tiger's Bloodlust , cause this passive to activate separately on each successful attack, potentially causing the wielder and all nearby creatures to take significant damage. Bugs Some damage riders like Lightning Charges and Callous Glow Ring are added both to regular attacks and to the Willing Whip area effect, so they also hurt the mace wielder. Creatures close to the one struck by this weapon take damage every time, but those on the border of its AoE radius sometimes do not. This is especially noticeable with wide area attacks, such as Slashing Flourish (Melee) .

## Yeenoghu's Gift
- **来源**: [Yeenoghu's Gift](https://bg3.wiki/wiki/Yeenoghu's_Gift)
- **分类**: Passive_features

Yeenoghu's Gift is a passive feature which requires the wielder continue attacking or go mad. Description Hitting an enemy with this weapon heals the wielder for 1d6 ⁠ ⁠ Hit Points - but they can go Mad if they don't continue hitting an enemy each turn. Healing through this item doesn't trigger other passives that react to healing. Condition: Yeenoghu's Blessing Yeenoghu's Blessing Duration: 1 turn Indulged its lust for violence. Yeenoghu's Gift won't turn the affected creature Mad . Condition: Yeenoghu's Gift Yeenoghu's Gift Duration: 6 turns Famished for slaughter. Affected entity can go Mad for 2 turns if it doesn't deal damage to an enemy by the end of its turn. How to learn Granted by the weapons: Shattered Flail Notes After hitting a creature with the Shattered Flail , the wielder gains Yeenoghu's Gift for 6 turns. For the duration, they must succeed a DC  10 Wisdom Saving Throw at the end of any turn on which they do not hit an enemy, or go Mad for 1 turn. The Saving Throw rolls made by the wielder of this weapon do not appear in the combat log, but they are in fact being rolled at the end of each turn where the wielder does not damage an enemy . The duration of Yeenoghu's Gift is not refreshed by hitting enemies again; it only lasts the base 6 turns, after which it can be re-applied. While Mad , the wielder is uncontrollably hostile to all nearby creatures, including allies, and uses any and all tools at their disposal to inflict harm. This could include using powerful Ammunition or Consumables from their inventory, casting high level Spells , or shoving allies to their deaths. Although the combat log states "Tav healed self...", this healing does not trigger other items which activate on the character's healing such as Boots of Aid and Comfort , The Whispering Promise or Broodmother's Revenge . The wielder is healed upon each instance of damage . This means that in the case of attacks which deal multiple damage types, such as Booming Blade and Divine Smite (as well as other Smite spells), or in the case of attacks which damage multiple targets, such as Slashing Flourish (Melee) , the wielder is healed multiple times.
